ID: UQ-20261015-01
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Cultural evolution; food studies; island biogeography
Question (canonical): Does the number of distinct traditional dishes in a regional cuisine scale with region area and population as a species–area-style power law, with island and mainland curves differing?
Alternative formulations: Is there a "cuisine–area curve" S = cA^z? / Do larger, less isolated regions accumulate dishes as island biogeography predicts for species?
Motivating gap: cultural evolution borrows ecological models, but dish richness vs. area appeared unfitted.
Presuppositions: dishes countable consistently (contested); comparable regional units; documentation effort controllable (contested).
What would count as an answer: regression of standardized dish counts on area, population and isolation, with a documentation-effort control and island/mainland contrast.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 18 in Gate 2 + 6 and 29 in Gate 4; full list in batches/2026-10-15-1605/C1-record.md and C1-adversary-2.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): Łuczaj et al. 2019, "The ethnobotany and biogeography of wild vegetables in the Adriatic islands", J. Ethnobiol. Ethnomed. 15:18 (PMC6440087; tests island biogeography on island food-plant repertoires, null); Kline & Boyd 2010, Proc. R. Soc. B (tool repertoire vs. island population); Barbosa & Fontanari 2009, arXiv:0902.1346 (culture–area relation).
Novelty — how this differs from each: Łuczaj: same test with food-plant taxa instead of dishes; Kline & Boyd: tools, population not area; Barbosa & Fontanari: theoretical culture count, not food.
Novelty confidence: Low (revised from Medium at Gate 4)
Significance — consequence: if documentation effort explains counts, recipe-count comparisons of cuisines are confounded.
Significance — audience: computational gastronomy, cultural evolution.
Significance — fecundity: repertoire-size laws across cultural domains.
Significance — anchoring: cultural repertoire–population debate (Kline & Boyd; Acerbi et al. 2017).
Reason for silence: offered "dishes can't be counted" explains why answering is hard, not why no one asked (Unresolved).
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): first adversary all Partial (judged too gentle; batch rejection rate was 40%, so Gate 4 was rerun harder). Second adversary: Triviality Resolved | Disguise UNRESOLVED (asked and answered null in ethnobotany: Łuczaj 2019; Insular Pharmacopoeias 2021) | Combinatorial Partial | Presupposition Partial | Vagueness Partial | Significance Partial | Silence UNRESOLVED | Dissolution Partial. Full logs: batches/2026-10-15-1605/C1-adversary.md, C1-adversary-2.md.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 1/3

ID: UQ-20261015-02
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Combinatorics (van der Waerden numbers); SAT
Question (canonical): At the extremal length n = w(2;3,t)−1, what fraction of good 2-colourings are palindromic, and how does it behave as t grows?
Alternative formulations: Are extremal off-diagonal vdW colourings increasingly forced to be symmetric? / Does the palindromic solution count dominate, track or vanish relative to all solutions at threshold?
Motivating gap: this repo's local search found palindromic seeds far stronger than unrestricted search (research/problems/vdw-w23t-lower-bounds).
Presuppositions: exact w(2;3,t) known for small t; counts computable (both established).
What would count as an answer: enumeration/#SAT counts N(t), P(t) at n = w−1 for all known t.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 16 queries, 10 pages; batches/2026-10-15-1605/C2-record.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): Ahmed, Kullmann & Snevily, arXiv:1102.5433 (palindromic numbers pdw(2;3,t), palindromic gap, OEIS A198685; open problem "does the gap attain 0 infinitely often?"); Heule 2017, "Schur Number Five", arXiv:1711.08076 (palindromic share of extremal certificates, Schur case); Kouril & Paul 2008, W(2,6)=1132 (all extremal partitions, symmetric structure).
Novelty — how this differs from each: AKS data already fix the fraction at 0 wherever the palindromic gap > 0 (t = 4–8, 10, 11, 13–16, 19) and at 1 for t = 17 (unique solution), refuting "increasingly symmetric"; the asymptotic part is AKS's own open problem; Heule asks it for Schur numbers.
Novelty confidence: Low (as posed)
Significance — consequence: guides symmetry-restricted search for vdW bounds.
Significance — audience: SAT/Ramsey computation community (small).
Significance — fecundity: whether gap-0 t have small, mostly palindromic solution sets.
Significance — anchoring: AKS open problems 2, 4, 5.
Reason for silence: not reached.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): not run; failed at Gate 2.
Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 1/3
Strongest remaining objection: mostly answered by published pdw/w data.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): n/a (rejected). The residue (N(t) and P(t) for gap-0 t = 3, 9, 12, 18, 20) may be re-submitted as a fresh candidate; AKS cite a Kouril reference for solution counts that was not opened.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): asymptotic part = AKS open problem 2, routed to routed-open-problems.md.

What would count as an answer: cross-city regression of weekly UHI amplitude on commuter share with size/density/climate controls, checked against lockdowns.

(weekly UHI cycles, Australian cities); Liu et al. / Zhan et al., GRL 2022 (UHI drop in 300+ cities under lockdown and 31 cities in the Chinese New Year exodus).

ID: UQ-20261015-04
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Information science (reference rot); Wikimedia research; scientometrics
Question (canonical): In English Wikipedia, does the hazard of a cited external URL becoming unreachable differ by article topic after conditioning on when the citation was added and on the cited domain's type, and which topics lose live verifiability fastest?
Alternative formulations: Is Wikipedia citation half-life field-dependent once link age and site type are controlled? / Is any topic difference in Wikipedia link rot more than a by-product of topic-specific source mixes?
Motivating gap: Wikipedia link rot is measured only overall (Tzekou 2011: 18%; Pew 2024: 11% of references dead) or mechanically (IMC 2022).
Presuppositions: topics assignable (WikiProjects, articletopic model); citation-add dates recoverable; liveness measurable (noisy: soft-404s, paywalls); editor replacement censors decay and must be modelled (flagged).
What would count as an answer: survival model of URL death on citation-addition events with topic, addition year, domain type, domain popularity, and censoring for editor replacement; secondary outcome "dead with no archive".
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 18 in Gate 2, 6 and 26 more in Gate 4; batches/2026-10-15-1605/C4-record.md, C4-adversary.md, C4-adversary-2.md. No topic-stratified Wikipedia dead-link figure found in Wikimedia research, Wiki Workshop, Signpost, IABot, Lewoniewski or Arquivo.pt material.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): Bowers, Stanton & Zittrain 2021, "What the ephemerality of the Web means for your hyperlinks", CJR (link rot by NYT section); Hennessey & Ge 2013, BMC Bioinformatics 14(S14):S5 (link survival across 20 disciplines); Nyayachavadi, Zhu & Madhyastha 2022, "Characterizing 'Permanently Dead' Links on Wikipedia", ACM IMC.
Novelty — how this differs from each: CJR: same design, one publisher's journalist-chosen links, no bot archiving or editor repair; Hennessey & Ge: scholarly papers, no domain-type control; IMC 2022: Wikipedia, but mis-tagging and archive lag, not topic.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: yes → verifiability risk is uneven by domain and archiving/patrol could be prioritised by topic; no → target source types, not topics.
Significance — audience: Wikimedia Research, Internet Archive/IABot engineers, WikiProject coordinators, researchers using Wikipedia citations as data.
Significance — fecundity: whether editor attention per topic offsets decay (maintenance-vs-hazard race); cross-language replication; whether unrecoverable loss concentrates in local/ephemeral-source topics.
Significance — anchoring: Pew 2024 level without structure; CJR's unresolved age confound; IMC 2022 mis-tagging anomaly.
Reason for silence: remediation crowded out diagnosis after IABot (2016+); the join of revision history, topic labels and live crawls falls between scientometrics, web archiving and Wikimedia reference-quality work.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): first adversary: Triviality Resolved, Presupposition Resolved, Dissolution Resolved, rest Partial (rerun harder). Second: Triviality | no stratified figure exists | checked Tzekou, IMC'22, Pew, Baigutanova | Resolved. Disguise | Wikimedia Research Fund grant "Improving the Persistence of External References on Wikipedia" unread (Meta-Wiki blocked from here) | 26 new searches found nothing | Partial. Combinatorial | CJR design × Wikipedia | Wikipedia-specific element (repair censoring) treated as nuisance | UNRESOLVED. Presupposition | consequence assumes topic-blind rationed archiving, but save-at-citation exists | topic-as-unit testable | Partial. Vagueness | threshold arbitrary | hazard model settles it either way | Resolved. Significance | tooling largely unchanged given prospective archiving | still matters for pre-2016 backlog and unarchivable sources | Partial. Silence | open data exist; insiders may expect "source mix" | crowd-out story fits | Partial. Dissolution | a "no" may only mean coarse taxonomy | secondary outcome survives | Partial.
Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: it is a transplant of the CJR design to a new corpus (combinatorial novelty, Unresolved).
Promotion requires: (1) read the Wikimedia Research Fund grant page and outputs with working access; topic-stratified rates there → Rejected; (2) reframe the primary question around the Wikipedia-specific maintenance-vs-hazard race by topic; (3) replace the archiving-allocation consequence.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): sample citation-addition events per articletopic from the Wikipedia Citations dataset and revision history; crawl liveness.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a.

ID: UQ-20261015-06
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Provisional (not Rejected: no Unresolved status on attacks 1, 2 or 4, and Disguise is now Resolved by adversary #3; not Validated: attacks 6 and 7 remain Partial on both adversaries who ran them and adversary #3's Disguise-only sweep supplies no evidence on either, while novelty stays Medium with a close neighbour)
Domain(s): AI systems / computer architecture (LLM inference energy); neighbours: GPU power modelling, EDA power analysis, hardware security (power/EM side channels)
Question (canonical): For dense decoder-only LLMs on a fixed serving engine, with the same numeric format, batch size and forced input/output token counts, does measured GPU board energy per token differ between trained weights and shape-identical untrained weights ((b) per-tensor moment-matched Gaussian; (c) the engine's "dummy" weights) by more than run-to-run noise, and does any difference sit in prefill, in decode, or in both? [R1, adopted at Gate 1; V0 left "materially" undefined, left a gap between its yes and no bars, and admitted MoE routing confounds.]
Alternative formulations: (1) Is shape-only energy modelling of LLM inference missing a data-dependent term, shown by swapping trained for random weights with every tensor shape and kernel held identical? (2) Do the bit-level statistics of trained LLM weights, and the activations they induce, make inference cheaper or dearer in joules than an untrained model of the same shape?
Motivating gap: Gregersen, Patel & Choukse 2024 (arXiv:2409.18324) show input values move GEMM power up to ~38–40% at fixed shape, on synthetic 2048x2048 matrices only, and leave NN-weight sorting as future work. LLM energy predictors (WattGPU 2607.02391; Tokens to Watt-hours 2607.26571) and measurement studies (Prompts to Power 2511.05597) model energy from shape and token counts; Prompts to Power fixes lengths on the grounds that the operation count is then equal. vLLM's dummy loader fills float weights U(±1e-3) (±1 for 8-bit floats) and int8/FP4 weights with random bytes, with a source comment "for accurate performance evaluation" (generator read weight_utils.py and dummy_loader.py; adversary #2 found the comment absent from weight_utils.py and did not check the other). No trained-vs-random energy comparison was found in 64 searches.
Presuppositions: P1 value-dependent switching power survives into fused LLM kernels at board level (contested; part of what is asked; Hot Pixels, USENIX Sec'23, shows board-level operand-dependent power on an RTX 3060 at small magnitude with element-wise kernels). P2 identical kernels across conditions (established for dense, fixed shapes; verify by kernel-name logs; FP8 dynamic scaling, non-finite activations, prefix caching and speculative decoding must be controlled). P3 dummy/random weights appear in published energy or power figures (UNVERIFIED; no instance in 64 web searches and 8 issue-tracker searches; MLPerf inference rules mandate reference weights and forbid weight replacement; every energy paper opened, including the 2026 set Where Do the Joules Go 2601.22076, Watt Counts 2604.09048, 2605.11999 and 2603.20224, uses trained checkpoints or does not say; bears on significance only). P4 decode is bandwidth-bound and dilutes compute switching power (contested; bus-toggle energy is value-dependent, Fallin & Burtscher MCHPC'22). P5 lengths and batch can be held identical (established). P6 ~1% resolvable with interleaved repeats (established with caveats: NVML windows, thermal drift; external metering preferred). P7 trained and moment-matched Gaussian weights differ in bit statistics (partly contested; Yang et al. 2510.02676: trained exponent entropy ~2–3 bits vs Gaussian bound 1.6–2.67; differences would come from tails, outlier channels, correlation and induced activations; vLLM dummy fills differ far more).
What would count as an answer: controlled measurement on ≥2 GPU types, ≥3 dense model sizes, ≥2 formats (e.g., bf16 plus fp8 or int4); arms (a) trained, (b) per-tensor moment-matched Gaussian with norm gains and embeddings at trained scale, (c) engine dummy, (d) consistently row/column-permuted trained weights (mechanism probe: distribution kept, adjacency changed); fixed batch, forced lengths, logged kernels and clocks or a recorded power cap; prefill and decode measured separately; ≥10 interleaved repeats per cell; Δ = E_cond/E_trained − 1 per phase with 95% CI, plus run time (under a cap a value effect appears as time). Pre-registered bands for (b) and (c): YES if the CI lies wholly beyond ±3% (about the best shape-only predictor error) in some phase on both GPU types; NO if within ±1% in every cell; otherwise small-but-real with size and phase reported. Every outcome is settled by data.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 64 web queries executed (29 Gate 2; 20 adversary #1; 15 adversary #3), plus 10 pages opened and 8 GitHub issue searches by adversary #3. Adversary #2 ran 0: its 4 attempts, and 2 by the earlier judge, were refused by the exhausted shared search budget; adversary #3's 2 curls (Semantic Scholar citation graph; Google Patents) were refused by the egress proxy, the patent then being opened by fetch. Full lists: batches/2026-10-15-1633/UQ-20261015-06-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-3.md. Most informative: "Input-Dependent Power Usage in GPUs" Gregersen → N1, synthetic GEMMs, weight sorting only as future work · "power virus" GPU tensor core toggle rate worst-case data pattern → NVIDIA CUTLASS measurement guideline: fill pattern changes dynamic power, "particularly for narrow precisions"; recommends U[-1,1] · H100 FP8 matmul power input distribution zeros throttle → AMD ROCm "Measuring Max-Achievable FLOPs Part 2": toggle rate moves clocks; FP8 MI300X median clock 1792 MHz zero fill vs 1188 MHz trig_float; asserts, unmeasured, that a normal fill approximates real weights and activations · Gregersen cited by, LLM weights power 2025–2026 → citers CompPow 2605.21847, FinGraV 2412.12426, Newkirk et al. 2506.14551 cite it in passing; no follow-up on NN or LLM weights · vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM issue trackers, "dummy weights" throughput/power → loader bugs only (vllm #54712; sglang #25767, #25653); nothing on power or real-vs-dummy throughput · answer-side phrasing, random vs pretrained weights "less power"/"more power" watts → no source states a figure · "toggle-aware" / "glitch power" / "operand isolation" LLM weight values GPU power → EDA vocabulary surfaces no LLM-level work · "energy per token" dummy/random vs trained weights → Where Do the Joules Go, Watt Counts, 2603.20224, TokenPowerBench: none varies weights · vllm initialize_dummy_weights → source confirms U(±1e-3) / random bytes · MLPerf inference power rules random weights → reference weights mandatory · "energy per token" weight permutation HBM decode → 2605.11999 (H200 phase-split energy; weights and content never varied) · reorder/sort LLM weights to reduce GPU power → nothing executed; US 11487342 opened: qualitative · Chinese and Japanese vocabularies (two adversaries) → only English mirrors of N1 and shape-based energy work.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): N1 Gregersen, T., Patel, P., Choukse, E. (2024), "Input-Dependent Power Usage in GPUs", arXiv:2409.18324, Sustainable Supercomputing workshop at SC24 (opened by generator and adversaries #1–#3; https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~patelp1/papers/inputpower-sssc24.pdf). The earliest statement of its future-work item, sorting NN weights to cut switching power, is US 11487342 B2, "Reducing power consumption in a neural network environment using data management", Microsoft Technology Licensing LLC; Ambardekar, McBride, Petre, Cedola, Wall; priority 19 Dec 2017, granted 1 Nov 2022; https://patents.google.com/patent/US11487342B2/en (opened by adversary #3). N2 Vendor fill-representativeness guidance: AMD ROCm Blogs, Sander, Masters, Poursartip & Ho, "Measuring Max-Achievable FLOPs – Part 2", 28 Feb 2025, https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/software-tools-optimization/measuring-max-achievable-flops-part2/README.html (opened by adversaries #1 and #3), with its NVIDIA counterpart, CUTLASS "GEMM Performance Measurement Methodology Guidelines", section "Matrix Fill Methodology", https://docs.nvidia.com/cutlass/latest/media/docs/cpp/gemm_performance_measurement_methodology_guidelines.html (opened by #1 and #3). N3 Petri, Zhang, Chen, Schlichtmann & Li (2023), "PowerPruning", arXiv:2303.13997 (opened), with its unexecuted LLM extension, TU Darmstadt thesis topic "Efficient LLM Inference with Weight Selection", https://www.etit.tu-darmstadt.de/media/hwai/thesis_1/Efficient_LLM_Inference_with_Weight_Selection.pdf (opened; undated). Also close: PyTorch Forums thread 30254 (22 Nov 2018) and sibling 43377 (Apr 2019), a CPU denormal time effect; thonking.ai "Strangely, Matrix Multiplications on GPUs Run Faster When Given 'Predictable' Data!" (He, 29 Apr 2024; synthetic, power-limited); Fallin & Burtscher, MCHPC'22; Kraken, arXiv:2603.02891 (trace-level); Hot Pixels, USENIX Sec'23.
Novelty — how this differs from each: N1: synthetic GEMMs, no trained weights, no end-to-end inference, no phase split, no trained-vs-untrained contrast; its future work asks how to arrange weights to save power, which presupposes rather than tests the effect; the 2017 patent likewise presupposes value-dependent buffer switching and proposes sorting as a remedy, with no measurement, on a DNN module rather than a GPU, and no LLM. N2: poses, at GEMM-benchmark level, whether synthetic fill is representative of real-model power and answers by prescription: CUTLASS recommends U[-1,1] and warns that fixed-power tests are fill-sensitive; AMD measures only zero vs trig_float fill on a synthetic FP8 GEMM (50.8% clock gap) and asserts without measurement that a normal fill approximates real weights and activations; neither, nor any material they link, measures trained weights, runs an LLM, reports energy per token or splits phases. N3: per-value MAC power in a simulated 15 nm systolic array for quantized CNNs, used to choose low-power values; the Darmstadt topic asks which weight values to choose for a decoder-only LLM, not whether trained and untrained weights differ end to end; no GPU board measurement, no random baseline, no phases.
Novelty confidence: Medium. Search record complete: 64 web queries, 8 issue-tracker searches and 10 opened pages across lay, ML-energy, architecture, EDA, hardware-security, stress-test, vendor, answer-side, Chinese and Japanese vocabularies, with adversary #3's Disguise sweep in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try. Not High: AMD's unmeasured assertion that a normal fill approximates real weights is adjacent to an answer; N1's future work and the 2017 patent show one group holding the value-dependence idea near this question for nine years; and Gregersen's citer graph could not be pulled (Semantic Scholar refused), so citer coverage rests on one extended search and three opened citers.
Significance — consequence: YES: shape-only predictors (WattGPU, Tokens to Watt-hours, Prompts to Power regression) carry a systematic, model-specific error term; dummy-weight performance runs are biased, under a power cap as throughput (practice exists in vLLM's loader and vllm-ascend configs, but no published figure using it was found); value-aware LLM power work on GPUs (patent, N1 future work, Darmstadt topic) gets an empirical basis on commodity hardware. NO: N1's GEMM anomaly does not survive into end-to-end LLM inference; shape-only modelling and dummy-weight benchmarking are justified at board level; the premise of the N1/patent/Darmstadt line closes for commodity GPUs. Small (1–3%): bounds the term below current predictor error and caps value-aware savings. Dropped: Deng 2026's 8.3x cross-language gap (a ≤40% value effect cannot explain it); bias in published dummy-weight energy figures (no instance).
Significance — audience: ML-energy measurement groups (ML.ENERGY, MLPerf Power, TokenPowerBench, Watt Counts, the 2605.11999 group), who already run phase-split, repeated-run instrumentation; power-prediction modellers (WattGPU, analytical estimators); serving-engine benchmark maintainers (vLLM, SGLang); the Microsoft (Gregersen/Patel/Choukse) and TU Darmstadt groups pursuing value-aware power reduction. Whether any of them acts depends on magnitude, and no one in the first three groups currently uses dummy weights for energy figures.
Significance — fecundity: which weight statistics drive any gap (exponent entropy, signs, outlier channels, activations; arm d); whether a function-preserving permutation of trained weights cuts joules at zero accuracy cost (the patent's and N1's proposal, testable on real models); whether energy per token drifts along training or after fine-tuning or quantization at fixed shape; whether prompt content moves power at fixed token counts; interaction with power caps, where the effect appears as throughput.
Significance — anchoring: N1's 38–40% GEMM anomaly; AMD's 1188 vs 1792 MHz FP8 clock gap between fills; thonking.ai power-limited matmul observation; CUTLASS fill-pattern doctrine; Fallin & Burtscher value-dependent bus energy (memory-bound decode); Kraken trace-level weight leakage from tensor cores; Hot Pixels board-level operand-dependent power; shape-only predictor error budget (WattGPU ≤3.4% / ≤13.5% MAPE); PowerPruning per-value MAC power (simulation, CNN).
Reason for silence: claimed mechanism: a disciplinary and instrument boundary (architecture and power researchers use synthetic matrices, gate-level simulation or traces and name LLMs as motivation; ML-energy researchers treat the GPU as a black box, model from shape and load trained checkpoints), plus a sampling habit (dummy weights are used for throughput runs, where energy is not recorded), plus recency (N1 Nov 2024; phase-split LLM energy instrumentation 2025–26). Contested by adversaries #1 and #2: vendors did cross the boundary and settled fill by prescription; the test is cheap; and the group best placed to run it announced the agenda and published nothing, so absence of stakes explains the silence as well as a boundary does. Adversary #3's findings do not discriminate: the 2017 patent lengthens the near-miss to nine years, and Gregersen's citers take it up only in passing, which fits either account.

ID: UQ-20261015-07
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected — Gate 4, attack 2 (Disguise), Unresolved: the question has already been asked and answered in the candidate's own direction, in print, under room-temperature serial-crystallography vocabulary. Günther et al. 2025 (Nat. Commun. 16:9089) compare an AlphaFold3 prediction of FosA^KP against their paired cryogenic and room-temperature structures, report that the room-temperature conformation of the K+-binding loop (residues 92–101) "is also not predicted by AlphaFold3", and attribute this to "a current strong prediction bias of the algorithm towards cryogenic temperatures" caused by PDB training data of which "about 94% are derived from structures collected at temperatures below 220 K". Per LEDGER Gate 4, Unresolved on attack 2 is fatal. Novelty falls Medium → Low.
Domain(s): Structural biology (X-ray crystallography, cryocooling artefacts); AI for protein structure prediction (AlphaFold 2/3, open AF3-class models)
Question (canonical): In proteins crystallised in the same crystal form and measured at both cryogenic (~100 K) and room temperature (≥270 K), at residues whose major conformer differs between the two temperatures by more than coordinate error, do AlphaFold 2, AlphaFold 3 and open AF3-class predictors (sampled over several seeds) reproduce the cryogenic major conformer more often than the room-temperature one, and does any such preference persist when proteins are stratified by training-set exposure? [v2, adopted at Gate 1. v1 left "differ", "AlphaFold-class" and "reproduce" undefined and folded a mechanism into the question.]
Alternative formulations: (1) Has training on a ~95%-cryocooled PDB taught structure predictors cryocooling artefacts, so that "near-experimental accuracy" partly means accuracy to 100 K structures? (mechanistic; not canonical) (2) When the cryogenic and room-temperature crystal structures of one protein disagree, which one do AF2/AF3 predictions match, and do pLDDT or seed spread flag the temperature-sensitive residues?
Motivating gap: AF accuracy is benchmarked against PDB structures that are ~95% cryocooled (St Jude summary of Bradford 2021; Günther 2025 gives ~94% below 220 K as of July 2025). Cryocooling remodels side-chain distributions (Fraser et al. 2011 PNAS, ~30 pairs, >35% of side chains; Keedy et al. 2014 Structure; Bradford et al. 2021 Chem. Sci., T4L L99A, where temperature artefacts biased docking). Garman (Chemistry World, 2021) expects cryo structures to be a poorer training set for "AI-based computational modelling tools". The record's closing claim — "no source tests AF-class predictions against paired cryo/room-temperature structures at residue-conformer level" — is FALSIFIED at Gate 4: Günther et al. 2025 does exactly that for one protein and one loop, and states the bias as a general property of the algorithm. The motivating gap was real as recorded and is retained for the record; it did not survive an executed Disguise search.
Presuppositions: P1 enough same-sequence, same-crystal-form pairs exist (established for dozens of proteins; CONTESTED for power once restricted to major-conformer switches, because most cryo/RT changes are occupancy shifts or added alternates). P2 cryo/RT differences are real, not refinement artefacts (largely established; residual risk from resolution mismatch, since RT members are usually lower resolution; mitigated by one-pipeline re-refinement). P3 the PDB collection temperature is reliable (flagged; check against primary papers). P4 a single predicted conformer can be compared with the major conformer of a multi-conformer model (contested; mitigated by multi-seed sampling plus an occupancy readout). P5 memorisation can be separated from learned bias (contested; the "neither in training" stratum may be near empty because the classic pairs predate the 2018/2021 cutoffs — Günther 2025 independently raises the same confound, noting "cryo structures of FosA^KP were likely included in the training dataset"). P6 a cryo preference reflects learned cryo states (interpretation only; contested, because rotamer priors are themselves cryo-derived). P7 RT is closer to physiological conformations (contested; needed for significance only). No presupposition was found false; the candidate dies on novelty, not on its premises.
What would count as an answer: curate same-sequence, same-space-group pairs (cryo ≤110 K, RT ≥270 K) and re-refine both members through one multi-conformer pipeline. Pre-define temperature-sensitive residues (major-conformer χ-bin change, peptide flip or loop state beyond resolution/DPI error) and temperature-insensitive controls. Predict with AF2, AF3 and ≥1 open reproduction, ≥5 seeds × samples, templates on and off. Classify each sample as cryo, RT or neither. Primary test: H0 P(cryo | matches one) = 0.5, benchmarked against a most-probable backbone-dependent rotamer comparator. Secondary: Jensen–Shannon divergence to the cryo vs RT occupancy vectors. Stratify by training exposure and by ligand and lattice proximity. "Yes" = cryo preference beyond the comparator, especially outside memorised strata; "No" = no preference or an RT preference. [Gate 4 note: by this criterion Günther 2025 is a single realisation of the n=1 case — one protein, one loop, one predictor, server defaults, no comparator, no strata, no test — answering the question's direction without quantifying it.]

Strongest remaining objection: stated here against the verdict, since the verdict is Rejected. The best case for the candidate is that Günther 2025 is n=1 — one protein, one loop, one predictor, one AlphaFold-Server run of unstated seed count, no prior-only rotamer comparator, no multi-seed sampling, no training-exposure strata and no statistical test — with the authors' own hedges ("presumably hinting", "likely caused", "likely included in the training dataset") and with the probable memorisation of FosA^KP cryo structures leaving learned bias and lookup unseparated; so the candidate's effect-size question is untouched by it, and adversary #3's query 14 found no systematic multi-protein benchmark. This objection is rejected because it misidentifies what the ledger tests. The gate is whether the question has been posed, not whether it has been answered well: Günther 2025 poses the comparison at residue level, answers it in the candidate's direction, asserts the mechanism as a general property of the algorithm, and does not frame any of it as open. A question whose answer is already asserted in the peer-reviewed literature is at best an open problem about magnitude, and here not even that, since no source poses the magnitude as a question. A weaker secondary objection: Supplementary Fig. 8 was ROBOTS_DISALLOWED and its caption unread, and the 43 citers of Bradford 2021 were never enumerated — but the main-text sentences are sufficient on their own and have been independently re-verified against the paper by the run session, so neither gap can rescue the candidate.

Routing applies to asked-but-unanswered problems; this one was asked and answered in the candidate's direction by Günther et al. 2025 for one protein (FosA^KP, residues 92–101), with the cryogenic prediction bias asserted as a presumption rather than posed as an open problem, so under LEDGER ENVIRONMENT ("Answered or disguised-known rejections are not routed") no row is appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Alternative formulations: [V0, as submitted] Do cross-model LLM capability correlations and latent factors survive phylogenetic correction for fine-tune/merge genealogy, and how much phylogenetic signal do benchmark scores carry? / Treating leaderboard entries as taxa, which correlations and general-factor findings survive PGLS, and does a tree covariance change them more than flat family clustering? / How much apparent LLM capability structure is pseudo-replication from derivatives of a few bases, and how phylogenetically conserved is each score under fine-tuning?
Motivating gap: comparative biology corrects cross-species correlations for shared ancestry (Felsenstein 1985); leaderboard capability-structure studies pool thousands of fine-tunes and merges of few bases and use only flat corrections (contributor RE, base-model strata, de-duplication). No source found estimating phylogenetic signal of benchmark scores or refitting capability structure under a tree covariance with depth, branch lengths or reticulation.

P3 ancestors in sample (established; handled as sampled ancestors, non-standard). P4 BM/OU/lambda adequately describes score change under directed optimisation (contested). P5 branch lengths meaningful (contested; three schemes). P6 one harness (established). P7 target studies pool related models (established for leaderboard studies; false for Burnell 2023, Ruan 2024, hence removed). P8 evolutionary-correlation estimand is the right target (contested). P9 no uncorrectable survivorship/selection (contested, flagged).

Robust only if it holds in ≥2/3 merge treatments and ≥2/3 branch-length schemes. "No bias": lambda upper CI < 0.2 for most benchmarks, or phylogenetic estimates inside both independence and contributor-RE CIs. "Yes": lambda lower CI > 0.5 for most AND ≥1 headline estimate outside the best coarse correction's CI. "Signal but harmless" and "model-dependent" are also closed outcomes.

Question (canonical): [R1, adopted at Gate 1] In human-written Lean blueprint projects (about 2020-2025), is a node's intrinsic de Bruijn factor (compressed size of its linked Lean declarations plus project-local helpers used only by it, over compressed size of its blueprint statement and proof) lower when a larger share of its formal prerequisites were already in mathlib at the node's first-formalised commit, holding project, field, dependency depth and Lean 3/4 era fixed? (v0, superseded: does the per-lemma factor fall as total mathlib size grows? Not identifiable apart from calendar time.)
Alternative formulations: (a) Has formalising mathematics in Lean become measurably cheaper per unit of informal proof as mathlib grew from 2017 to 2026, and does this differ by field? Motivating gap: de Bruijn's "constant loss factor" (quoted by Wiedijk, 10 hand-picked passages, 0.44-8.8) against Blanqui's (FOM 2018) and Kontorovich's (arXiv:2510.15924) untested claims that libraries cut cost. Blueprints newly pair informal and formal text node by node, with git-dated mathlib pins.

Else INCONCLUSIVE.

Question (canonical): [R1, adopted at Gate 1] In open knockout-based characterisations of commercial antibodies (YCharOS, about 1,200 antibodies / about 120 human proteins by Dec 2024), analysed separately for WB, IP and IF: (i) what share of variance in antibody pass/fail lies between target proteins after adjusting for antibody-level factors (recombinant/monoclonal/polyclonal, vendor, host, disclosed immunogen features) and assay context (abundance in the parental line, research attention)? (ii) do six pre-specified target features (TM segment count, primary compartment, disorder fraction, maximum paralog identity, PTM-site density, length) account for that share? (V0, superseded: which intrinsic target properties, abundance included, predict knockout-validation pass independently of antibody type and vendor? Had no decision rule and treated abundance as intrinsic.)
Alternative formulations: (a) Are some human proteins systematically "hard targets" for commercial antibodies once reagent type and vendor are fixed, and is the hardness carried by topology, disorder, paralogy or modification? (b) In knockout-validated antibody data, do target-level differences in pass rates exceed what antibody-level factors explain, and which protein features carry that variance?
Motivating gap: YCharOS analyses report antibody- and vendor-level predictors only (Ayoubi et al. 2023, eLife RP91645; Biddle & Virk 2023, F1000Research 12:1344). Biddle & Virk note all-fail targets and list candidate causes without testing them. About 40% of Ayoubi targets lacked a successful IF antibody; never explained at target level. Class-level hints: GPCRs (Michel 2009) and TM enrichment among HPA-uncovered proteins (Waury 2025).
Presuppositions: P1 knockout pass/fail is valid ground truth (ESTABLISHED; FLAGGED for truncated or downstream-ATG products). P2 enough distinct targets (PARTLY ESTABLISHED; about 120, current count unverified). P3 about 9-10 antibodies per target (ESTABLISHED). P4 target separable from assay context and vendor immunogen choice (CONTESTED; immunogens often undisclosed). P5 target set spans the features (CONTESTED; charity-nominated, neuro-heavy, mostly intracellular, IF on intracellular targets only). P6 pass/fail comparable across targets within an application (ESTABLISHED). P7 no prior target-level analysis (PARTLY CONTRADICTED; see Gate 4 attack 2). Unflagged, raised at Gate 4: host-conservation/immune tolerance missing from the feature set; OEM clones resold under several vendor names (no deduplication); disclosure-dependent immunogen adjustment makes the estimand differ across antibodies.
What would count as an answer: per-antibody, per-application outcomes from YCharOS Zenodo and F1000 data notes, joined to UniProt, HPA, AlphaFold disorder and Ensembl paralog data; mixed logistic or ordinal model with antibody-level fixed effects, target random intercept and crossed vendor intercept. (i) YES if latent-scale target ICC CI lower bound > 0.10 in at least one application; NO if CI upper bound < 0.05 in all; else "small or uncertain". (ii) a feature is a carrier if its Holm-corrected CI excludes 1 and it cuts target variance by >= 25%; "inconclusive" if underpowered against OR 2. Sensitivity: drop measurement-failure targets, restrict to disclosed immunogens, leave-one-class-out.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a. Rejected at Gate 4 (Disguise Unresolved from both adversaries), not as asked-but-open. The protein-level feature question is asked and partly answered in HPA data (Waury 2025). The all-fail remark in Biddle & Virk 2023 is not posed as an open question. Not routed.

ID: UQ-20261015-11
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine / clinical microbiology (antimicrobial susceptibility testing); measurement methodology (variance components); bacterial population biology (heteroresistance)
Question (canonical): [R1, adopted at Gate 1] In broth-microdilution AST read from per-well raw optical density, with a skip defined as a well below the growth threshold while the next-lower and at least one higher concentration exceed it: (a) in a crossed design of N isolates x k>=5 replicate panels x >=2 panel lots x >=2 laboratories, what is the isolate-level ICC (95% CI) for skip occurrence (binary, per drug) and skip position (ordinal, dilution steps below the MIC), with plate lot, run, reader and laboratory as separate random effects; and (b) does estimated skip propensity rank-correlate with the resistant-subpopulation frequency measured for the same isolate and drug by population analysis profiling (PAP)?
Alternative formulations:
- Are skipped wells in MIC panels random technical error, as the reading rules assume, or a strain-level phenotype carrying information about subpopulation structure?
- Does an isolate's skip pattern replicate across runs, panel lots and laboratories, and does skip propensity track PAP-measured heteroresistance?
- [V0, superseded at Gate 1 for an undefined "skip", no estimand and no model for skip position; subject matter unchanged. Full text in batches/2026-10-15-1833/UQ-20261015-11-record.md.]
Motivating gap: Anomaly mining. EUCAST's BMD reading guide instructs that a single skip be retested or read as the highest MIC and that >1 skip voids the drug, so occurrence and position are overwritten at the moment of observation. The two papers that study skips frame them as method failure in their titles (Elias 2021, colistin; Bixby 2024, fosfomycin), and Elias states the cause "is unknown". Heteroresistance, which routine AST is known to miss, is referenced only to PAP ("gold standard but labour-intensive and costly"). Claimed enabler: instrument and imaging readers now retain per-well raw OD.
Presuppositions:
1. Skips recorded/recoverable per well. ESTABLISHED for instrument/imaging; CONTESTED for visual reading. FAILED at Gate 4 as framed (see 5 and the log, attack 4).
2. Enough isolates testable repeatedly for an isolate-level variance component. CONTESTED; rare binary outcome, k=5 binary ICCs poorly estimated; partly mitigated by base rates (11-13% colistin; up to 38.1% fosfomycin/E. coli).
3. PAP an adequate heteroresistance reference. CONTESTED; PAP poorly reproducible, HR definitions vary. Arm (b) secondary.
4. Skip propensity not merely inoculum/plate-manufacturing artefact. CONTESTED, and partly what is asked.
5. The fosfomycin inconsistency report is drug/species-specific, not general. UNCLEARED by Gate 2 and still uncleared after Gate 4: neither reader could obtain Bixby 2024 full text (PMC reCAPTCHA).
What would count as an answer: The crossed replication design above read from instrument raw OD, spanning high-skip drugs (colistin, fosfomycin) and low-skip comparators, with mixed models for skip occurrence and position. YES = ICC CI lower bound >0.10 for at least one drug AND a pre-specified rank correlation with PAP subpopulation frequency whose CI excludes zero. NO = ICC CI upper bound <0.05 for every drug and no PAP association. The 0.05-0.10 band is a pre-registered third verdict. Secondary: incremental prediction of in vitro regrowth beyond the reported MIC.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 14 queries + 9 fetches at Gate 2; 12 queries + 8 fetches by adversary 1 in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use; 26 in total, none refused. Full lists in batches/2026-10-15-1833/UQ-20261015-11-record.md and UQ-20261015-11-adversary-1.md. Most informative: ("skipped well" broth microdilution reproducibility isolate AST -> only Elias 2021 and Bixby 2024, no isolate-level reproducibility); (skipped wells AST heteroresistance subpopulation -> no paper joins skips to HR); (detect heteroresistance from routine AST / ML predict PAP -> EBioMedicine 2025 predicts HR from WGS, not well patterns); (fosfomycin "inner colonies" disk diffusion heteroresistance reproducibility same isolate -> Bixby et al., JAC-AMR 2025: the same question in disk-diffusion vocabulary, with an effect estimate — the kill); ("gauge R&R"/generalizability theory applied to MIC variance, lab and lot -> Turnidge 2018 JAC strain-vs-laboratory MIC variance decomposition, missed by Gate 2); (CRyPTIC UKMYC plate reproducibility across laboratories -> 7 labs, 2 plate lots, archived plate images, mixed-effects models, since 2018).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Bixby ML, Collins LB, Daley EC, Salay JM, Oliver S, Bryson AL, Hirsch EB, "Heteroresistance associated with the production of fosfomycin-resistant inner colonies during disk diffusion testing among a geographically diverse collection of Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates", JAC-Antimicrobial Resistance 7(1):dlaf013, 2025 — PMC11840249 (PMC redirect served no content; read at mirror dbpia.nl.go.kr/jacamr/article/7/1/dlaf013/8026053). With Bixby et al. 2023 (PMC10101107) and the Salay/Bixby/Hirsch 2025 converse-direction poster (UMN Conservancy, opened).
2. Elias A, Nunes MT, et al., Diagnostics 2021, colistin BMD/agar dilution/MIC strips and the "skipped well" phenomenon — PMC8700027 (opened). With Salay et al., abstract P-2116, OFID 2025 — PMC11778549 (opened). Bixby ML et al., Microbiology Spectrum 12(8), 2024 — PMC11302225: record verified twice, full text NOT readable by either reader.
3. Guliaev, Hjort, Rossi, Jonsson, Nicoloff, Guy, Andersson, "Machine learning detection of heteroresistance in Escherichia coli", eBioMedicine 113:105618, 2025 — PMC11893328 (opened, verified). Adjacent: Turnidge, "Variation of MIC measurements: the contribution of strain and laboratory variability to measurement precision", JAC 73(9):2374-9, 2018 (abstract only); "Dilution-and-Delay (DnD)" preprint bioRxiv 2025.08.11.669743.
Novelty — how this differs from each:
1. Decisive. Same lab, same drug, same species, same logical shape: a reading anomaly the rule says to disregard, treated as an isolate-level producer trait and associated with heteroresistance (IC producers 1.71 greater odds of screening HR, 95% CI 1.24-2.34, P<0.01; 95.3% vs 64.3%). The candidate differs only by observable (OD hole in a dilution series vs colonies inside an inhibition zone), HR reference (PAP vs disk-elution screen) and estimator (crossed-random-effects ICC, estimated for neither). That is a modality/instrument swap on an asked and partly answered question.
2. Elias 2021 holds nearly the needed data (141 colistin BMDs in triplicate; multiple skips in 15/19/19 isolates, and 3/8/13/2 of 26 undetermined isolates with multiple skips in 3/2/1/0 replicates) and reports no per-isolate statistic, no PAP, no lot/lab decomposition. Bixby 2024 and P-2116 quantify skip frequency under an error frame with the method, not the isolate, as the unit. The candidate's estimand is genuinely unestimated here — but these same papers, plus CRyPTIC, defeat the claim that the data require a new instrument.
3. The ML-HR paper predicts HR from whole-genome data against PAP labels and does not mention skips; DnD reaches PAP-grade frequencies with a purpose-built assay. Both occupy the cheaper-surrogate niche with new substrates; the candidate asks whether the signal already sits inside the routine panel.
Novelty confidence: Low (downgraded from the record's Medium: a near-duplicate of the same question in an adjacent modality was found, by the same research group, and the one piece of counter-evidence remains unread).
Significance — consequence: If YES, a quantity standards instruct readers to discard carries strain-level information: the reading rule becomes a known information-destroying step needing a flag-and-record branch; vendors could emit an HR-suspicion flag from data already captured; and method-evaluation work that scores skips as "scientific error" would be penalising the method for a property of the organism, which bears on the live fosfomycin BMD endorsement dispute. If NO, the rule is vindicated on evidence and the colistin/fosfomycin anomaly literature redirects to plate manufacture and inoculum preparation. Discounted at Gate 4: the headline claim that a disregarded AST artefact carries HR information is already published in the disk-diffusion modality, so the YES branch shrinks toward "also true in liquid medium".
Significance — audience: CLSI AST subcommittee and EUCAST steering committee / development laboratory, who own the skip rule and the pending fosfomycin BMD decision (non-endorsement attributed in P-2116 to no-growth wells before the MIC); AST instrument and reader manufacturers, who hold the per-well data and the regulatory channel; heteroresistance researchers needing a PAP surrogate; the Hirsch lab and colistin AST groups as natural executors — the same group that already published the adjacent result.
Significance — fecundity: Whether skip position encodes the subpopulation's MIC; whether skip flags can be back-applied to vendor panel archives for population-scale HR surveillance; whether the "read the highest value" branch biases MIC distributions and hence ECOFFs; mapping onto known HR mechanisms (gene amplification, mgrB/pmrB, uhpT/glpT); prediction of regrowth or clinical failure.
Significance — anchoring: Routine AST's documented blind spot for heteroresistance; irreproducible polymyxin MICs; the explicitly unresolved cause of the skipped-well phenomenon; the standing refusal to endorse fosfomycin BMD.
Reason for silence: Claimed as a measurement rule that overwrites the variable plus a disciplinary split (QC/method-evaluation error frames vs PAP-based population biology), with retained per-well OD as a new enabler. Gate 4 defeated this: the exactly parallel disregard-inner-colonies rule did not suppress the analogous question, which was asked and published twice by visual disk diffusion with no instrument enabler, and skip tallies across replicates already exist in print (Elias 2021, P-2116) alongside CRyPTIC's multi-lab, multi-lot, image-archived plate design from 2018. What remains is low salience, recency, or that the broth version sits in that lab's pipeline — none of which the ledger accepts as a mechanism.
Adversarial log (adversary 1, fresh context, 12/12 searches and 8/8 fetches used, Disguise searches executed in new vocabularies; verbatim log at batches/2026-10-15-1833/UQ-20261015-11-adversary-1.md):
| Attack | Objection | Response | Status |
| 1 Triviality | Answerable in a page; isolate-trait answer implied by Elias 2021's replicate tally | No published table yields a variance component with a CI decomposed over lot/run/reader/lab; Elias is single-site, single-drug, confounded with run | Resolved |
| 2 Disguise | In disk-diffusion vocabulary this is published: are fosfomycin inner colonies an isolate-level producer trait and do they mark heteroresistance? Bixby et al., JAC-AMR 2025 dlaf013, with OR 1.71 (1.24-2.34), plus the 2023 frequency paper and 2025 converse poster; Gate 2's 14 queries never left the word "well" | Observable, HR reference and estimator differ, and no crossed-random-effects ICC exists for either modality; true but thin — a modality transposition of a live question in the same lab's programme | Unresolved |
| 3 Combinatorial novelty | AST metrology x population biology with nothing at the interface | A real and demonstrably productive interface, as the 2025 result shows | Resolved |
| 4 Presupposition failure | (i) The destroyed-at-observation / new-instrument-enabler claim is false: Elias 2021 tabulated skips per replicate by visual reading, P-2116 logged no-growth-well rates across technical triplicate and biological duplicate, and CRyPTIC's UKMYC study (7 labs, 2 plate lots, archived images, logistic mixed models) predates it by years; (ii) presupposition 5, the record's own leading evidence for the null, still unread | The record flags (i) as contested and concedes (ii); neither concession repairs them, and (i) is load-bearing for the reason-for-silence story while being contradicted by the record's own cited priors | Unresolved |
| 5 Vagueness | "Reproducible property" claimable either way | R1 fixes estimand, random-effects structure, 0.10/0.05 bounds and a pre-registered indeterminate band | Resolved |

Strongest remaining objection: Attack 2. In the vocabulary of the same subfield and the same research group, the question has been asked and partly answered — fosfomycin inner colonies as an isolate-level producer trait associated with heteroresistance (JAC-AMR 7(1):dlaf013, 2025) — so the candidate is that question with the observable swapped from agar to broth and the reference swapped from a disk-elution screen to PAP: a disguised known, Rejected under the operating rules even though the broth ICC itself is unmeasured. Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not to be pursued as an un-asked question. ID: UQ-20261015-12
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine / molecular diagnostics (cfDNA fragmentomics, multi-cancer early detection); neighbours: chromatin biology, biospecimen science, prenatal cfDNA, transplant dd-cfDNA.
Question (canonical): [R1, adopted at Gate 1] In a within-donor randomised processing-delay series from one venipuncture (K2EDTA + a stabilising tube; plasma separated at 0/2/6/24/48 h, RT and 4 °C) with deep WGS plus methylation deconvolution per aliquot: (i) does delay-associated loss of ~190 bp coverage periodicity amplitude and dyad-vs-linker phase-resolved coverage differ in magnitude between tissue-specific marker windows, beyond within-donor reproducibility; and (ii) do deconvolved non-haematopoietic tissue fractions and an openly re-implemented arm-level DELFI-type score plus the 100–150 bp proportion leave pre-specified equivalence bands with delay, after adjustment for a measured leukocyte-lysis covariate and with an exogenous tracer separating degradation of pre-existing cfDNA from newly released genomic DNA?
Alternative formulations: (1) Is part of the fragmentomic tissue-of-origin / MCED signal generated in the tube rather than in the body? (2) Under randomised within-donor delay, do deconvolved tissue fractions and published fragmentation scores move enough to mimic or mask disease signal, and is any movement distinguishable from added white-cell DNA?
Motivating gap: Fragmentomics presupposes that post-collection degradation is tissue-nonspecific — a nuisance that shortens fragments without changing tissue attribution. Preanalytical work measures yield, size, integrity, arm-level profiles and end-motif entropy; standards (NCI BEBP, P3) govern delay as a clock window and name no fragmentomic or deconvolution outcome. CORRECTION TO INTAKE: the intake's claim that no preanalytical study has done tissue-of-origin/cell-type deconvolution under delay is false — P2 did it across 0/24/72 h and reported movement. Surviving un-asked content is only (i) the nucleosome-phase mechanism, (ii) non-haematopoietic fractions and a clinical-type score as outcomes, (iii) a design separating lysis from differential degradation.
Presuppositions: P-1 tissue-specific phasing resolvable at depth used (established deep WGS / contested at deployed shallow depth); P-2 deconvolution references valid under partial degradation (contested, partly undermined by P2); P-3 within-donor randomised delay feasible (established); P-4 non-zero nuclease activity in EDTA within clinical windows (established, but EDTA partly inhibits DNases, so effect may be small); P-5 lysis-added leukocyte DNA separable from differential degradation of pre-existing cfDNA (contested — central confounder; covariate alone non-identifying, hence tracer); P-6 proprietary scores faithfully re-implementable outside originating labs (contested); P-7 the outcome half is unanswered (PARTLY CONTRADICTED by P2 and by the prenatal fetal-fraction precedent in P3).
What would count as an answer: Within-donor randomised time course (0/2/6/24/48 h; RT and 4 °C; EDTA + one stabilising tube), healthy donors and donors with known tumour burden; per aliquot deep WGS (phase), methylation sequencing (deconvolution), exogenous nucleosomal tracer at draw. Three-way decision table: YES = fractions/score leave pre-registered bands, departure survives lysis-index adjustment and is corroborated by the tracer, and phase-coverage loss differs between marker sets; NO = all departures inside bands after adjustment (licenses current windows); CONTAMINATION-ONLY = departures explained by the lysis index with no differential degradation. Sensitivity: in-silico degradation of the deconvolution reference (P-2); score recomputed at deployed shallow depth (P-1).
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 15 queries across fragmentomics, preanalytics, chromatin-biology, prenatal and transplant vocabularies; full list with per-query results in batches/2026-10-15-1833/UQ-20261015-12-record.md. Most informative: (2) "cfDNA fragmentomics preanalytical variability time to plasma separation DELFI fragmentation score" → P1 as top hit; (3) "nucleosome positioning ex vivo nuclease digestion plasma cfDNA phasing chromatin" → MNase digestion-level positioning bias known in chromatin biology, never transferred to tube time in plasma; (13) prenatal/historical phrasing → fetal-fraction decline under storage treated as a known lysis-driven dilution to engineer around (Prenat Diagn 2010; Clin Biochem 2013/2015, titles only, not opened); (14) exact conjunction "nucleosome footprint" + "time to centrifugation"/"processing delay" → nothing new, P1 still top; (15) "effect of blood collection tubes on cell-free DNA methylome … cell type deconvolution processing time" → found P2, the near-duplicate of the outcome half.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 "The effect of pre-analytical and physiological variables on cell-free DNA fragmentation", bioRxiv 10.1101/2021.09.17.460828 (PDF opened; published Clin Chem 2022, doi 10.1093/clinchem/hvac029, journal page not opened) — processing time recorded not randomised in 30 healthy EDTA donors; size, P100–150, 5-Mb/arm profiles, end-motif entropy; "no significant difference of the processing time on cfDNA fragmentation pattern" yet "a moderate impact … on the genome-wide cfDNA fragmentation patterns" with no statistics; no nucleosome or deconvolution analysis. P2 "Genome-wide study of the effect of blood collection tubes on the cell-free DNA methylome", bioRxiv 10.1101/2020.04.23.055293 (PDF opened; published Epigenetics 2021 per DOAJ record; author list not retrieved, so cited by title/DOI) — 5 tubes, T0/T24/T72 h RT, 3 donors, RRBS, NNLS + CelFiE deconvolution; sharp NK rise and neutrophil fall in EDTA at 72 h, mean absolute change 13.81%, read by its authors as a cell-type composition shift. P3 "Cell-Free DNA: Biospecimen Collection and Processing", NCI Biospecimen Evidence-Based Practices, rev. 1.0, 5 Feb 2025 (PDF opened) — EDTA centrifuge within 2 h, up to 4 h RT / 24 h at 4 °C; effects reported after as little as 4 h; no fragmentomics, nucleosome, end-motif or deconvolution outcome; notes fetal fraction declining after delayed centrifugation.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same nuisance variable, but P1 is observational, healthy-only, dsDNA-only, with no phase estimand, no deconvolution and no lysis covariate; its one positive signal sits in the arm-level feature space DELFI-type scores use and is reported without statistics, so P1 leaves that component asked and unresolved rather than answered. vs P2 — NEAR-DUPLICATE of the outcome half: P2 already asks whether delay moves deconvolved fractions and answers yes. Remaining differences are all narrowing: leukocyte subtypes rather than non-haematopoietic tissues, n=3/3 timepoints/one temperature/RRBS/no fragmentomic score, no nucleosome-phase analysis, and no separation of differential degradation from newly released leukocyte DNA (P2's own interpretation is the candidate's contamination arm). vs P3 — P3 is the audience's evidence base and sets the window the candidate questions; it names no fragmentomic outcome, and its fetal-fraction datum is the prenatal precedent for the candidate's outcome half. Neighbouring vocabularies: the MNase/DNase digestion-level positioning artefact is the same physics in a different vessel but asked only of in-vitro chromatin; prenatal and transplant literatures treat a moving tissue fraction as dilution to engineer around.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: YES would make processing delay an effect modifier rather than a quality metric, biasing multi-site trials where delay tracks site, case/control status or screening arm, and forcing handling windows to be set from fragmentomic endpoints. NO would positively confirm the field's central presupposition and license current windows. CONTAMINATION-ONLY implies a cheap remedy (measure and adjust a lysis index, not tighten the clock). Marginal consequence is reduced by P2: that fractions move is no longer news.
Significance — audience: MCED developers (analytical-validation delay arm; regulator actively reviewing such claims in 2026); preanalytical standards bodies (P3 is maintained and contains no fragmentomic outcome; BloodPAC/CLSI/IFCC alike); designers of multi-site screening trials (delay as per-sample covariate); biobank custodians holding legacy plasma with heterogeneous processing times.
Significance — fecundity: a sequencing-derived "delay clock" as a QC covariate; whether phase-selectivity operates in vivo via DNASE1L3/DNASE1 variation; whether deconvolution references must be degradation-matched (P-2); ranking feature families (end motifs vs tissue-of-origin) by delay robustness; unifying the prenatal fetal-fraction decline with the cancer fragmentomics literature.
Significance — anchoring: nuclease- vs cell-death-driven fragmentation; the MNase/DNase digestion-level footprinting artefact; the lab-to-lab reproducibility gap in fragmentomic classifiers; the prenatal fetal-fraction precedent in P3; P2's unexplained 72 h leukocyte-subtype shift, attributed to composition change with no test against differential degradation.
Reason for silence: (1) disciplinary boundary with mismatched endpoints — preanalytical groups own the exposure but report yield/integrity/size/MAF, fragmentomics groups own the machinery but hold delay constant by design and exclude variable-delay samples; P2 is the exception that proves it, reaching deconvolution but stopping at blood cell types. (2) Incentive gap — a YES is costly to the parties best placed to test it, and the clinically relevant scores are proprietary, so outsiders must pre-register a re-implementation the developer can disown. (3) Cost/instrument threshold — deep WGS plus matched methylation sequencing on every timepoint is an order of magnitude beyond any preanalytical study on record, and phase-resolved coverage analysis post-dates the windows still in force. These are credible mechanisms, but they explain silence about the phase mechanism only; they do not explain the outcome half, which was not silent.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status):
  1 Triviality | not run | — | Not run
  2 Disguise | not run | — | Not run (UNVERIFIED)
  3 Combinatorial novelty | not run | — | Not run
  4 Presupposition failure | not run | — | Not run
  5 Vagueness | not run | — | Not run
  6 Significance inflation | not run | — | Not run
  7 Reason for silence | not run | — | Not run
  8 Dissolution | not run | — | Not run
  Note: no adversary was spawned — the candidate failed at Gate 2 before Gate 4. No Disguise searches were executed, so Disguise counts as unverified and this entry could not have been Validated on this record even had novelty been higher. Rejection here rests on Gate 2 and Gate 1 alone, not on any adversary finding.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The outcome half is a disguised known — P2 asked and answered "does processing delay move methylation-deconvolved fractions?" (yes, 13.81% mean absolute change in EDTA at 72 h), and what the candidate adds to it is a covariate, a tracer, a depth upgrade and a swap of readout (non-haematopoietic rather than leukocyte fractions, a re-implemented score rather than none) on that same asked question; the genuinely unasked remainder, the nucleosome-phase mechanism, is bundled into the same study and is the half whose own feasibility premise (P-5 identifiability of lysis vs differential degradation) is unvalidated, which also holds well-posedness at 2/3. Under the LEDGER rules a found near-duplicate forces Low novelty, and Low novelty is Rejected at Gate 2; the Gate 1 reformulation may not be used to escape it.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): re-pose the phase-mechanism component alone, stripped of the outcome half, and check whether existing deep-WGS cfDNA sets with recorded (even if non-randomised) processing times permit a phase-amplitude-by-marker-window contrast before any new collection is designed; separately, read P2's published Epigenetics version and P1's Clinical Chemistry version in full, neither of which was opened for this record.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): One component is asked-but-still-open and is routed: whether processing delay changes chromosome-arm-level cfDNA fragmentation profiles (the DELFI feature space). P1 reports a "moderate impact" with no statistics in 30 healthy observational donors and recommends no action — bioRxiv 10.1101/2021.09.17.460828 / Clin Chem 2022 doi 10.1093/clinchem/hvac029. Row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The P2-duplicated deconvolution component is answered, not routed; the nucleosome-phase component is un-asked, not routed.

ID: UQ-20261015-13
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine / drug safety, pharmacovigilance, regulatory science (target); ecology and statistics of unseen richness (Chao1, Good-Turing coverage, rarefaction–extrapolation) (source); neighbours: software defect-content capture-recapture, linguistics (Heaps, Efron–Thisted), medical informatics (code vocabularies)
Question (canonical): For new active substances approved by FDA or EMA in a fixed window (e.g. 2010–2018), does the estimated unobserved adverse-event-type count derived from the pooled pre-approval MedDRA preferred-term frequency spectrum (bias-corrected Chao1 minus observed richness; Good-Turing coverage deficit f1/n) predict the number of distinct preferred terms added to the label's adverse-reactions section within five years of approval, with discrimination and calibration beyond a pre-specified baseline of pre-approval patient-years, observed richness, drug class, biologic status and accelerated-approval status; and, secondarily, are label-added terms enriched among terms seen exactly once pre-approval? (R1 adopted at Gate 1; V0 in the record asked for identity prediction and exposure-point extrapolation, both dropped.)
Alternative formulations: (1) Can an adverse-event "species-accumulation curve" over patient exposure be extrapolated to a drug's post-marketing adverse-event repertoire? (2) Is the completeness of a pre-approval safety database estimable from its singleton/doubleton adverse-event-term spectrum, and does that estimate calibrate against what regulators later add to the label? (3) Lay: does the share of side effects seen only once in a drug's trials tell you how many more will turn up after launch?
Motivating gap: Ecology, sequencing-library complexity (preseq) and software inspection estimate what remains unobserved from the singleton/doubleton spectrum; drug regulation sizes the pre-approval safety database by fixed exposure rules (ICH E1, detectable-frequency rationale) with no estimate of how many reaction types the database has missed, although ~32% of novel therapeutics approved 2001–2010 acquired a post-market safety event at a median 4.2 years (Downing 2017) and trial sample size did not predict later boxed warnings (Schick 2017). Pharmacovigilance capture-recapture targets under-reporting of known reactions; label/structure-based AE prediction uses other drugs' data, not the drug's own spectrum. PT-level AE tables now exist (ClinicalTrials.gov results, EMA Policy 0070 CSRs, FDA reviews).
Presuppositions: P1 MedDRA PTs are countable, stable types — contested (granularity, synonymy, twice-yearly versions; mitigated: PT pre-specified, HLT sensitivity, version lock). P2 pre-approval sampling draws from the same type-abundance distribution as post-market use — contested, the premise the result would quantify. P3 label additions are a usable readout of realised richness — contested (Croteau 2022: 17.5% of changes class-labelling-triggered, FAERS volume dominates year 1; mitigated by PRAC-signal and serious-subset secondary readouts). P4 term-with-count data exist for enough approvals — OVERSTATED in record: ClinicalTrials.gov reports non-serious "other AEs" only above a sponsor-chosen 0–5% threshold, so f1/f2 need CSR appendices, EMA Policy 0070, FDA reviews or data-sharing platforms. P5 post-approval detection effort is commensurable with trial exposure — contested (R1 uses asymptotic and coverage quantities, not exposure-point extrapolation). P6 programme trials can be pooled as one sample — contested (unsolicited TEAEs from controlled trials only). P7 estimators are informative at these sample sizes — established in principle. P8 (ADDED at Gate 5; raised independently by both adversaries; absent from record): the sampled community is all-cause treatment-emergent types while the readout is causally attributed reactions — unlisted and uncontrolled in the current design.
What would count as an answer: Pre-registered retrospective cohort of FDA/EMA new active substances. Per drug: reconstruct the pooled pre-approval PT spectrum (f1, f2, n, S_obs) from unsolicited treatment-emergent AEs of controlled trials at a locked MedDRA version; compute bias-corrected Chao1, f1/n and (secondary) Chao–Jost extrapolation at 2× the sample; outcome = distinct PTs added to US PI section 6 / SmPC 4.8 within five years at the same MedDRA level, serious subset separately; nested models baseline (log patient-years, S_obs, class, biologic, accelerated approval, psychiatric indication) vs baseline + completeness quantities; discrimination (C-index or AUC for ≥k additions) and calibration against a pre-specified margin. Positive control: phase-2 spectrum predicting new PTs in phase 3. YES = improvement beyond margin, calibrated. NO + passing control = sampling-frame shift (P2) quantified. NO + failing control = estimators uninformative on AE spectra. Partial = works for established classes, not first-in-class/biologics. Gate 5 defect: on an all-cause spectrum the positive control passes on background-morbidity richness alone, so a NO is not attributable to P2 as designed; a placebo-arm covariate or serious/drug-excess spectrum restriction is needed.

(2017) "Postmarket Safety Events Among Novel Therapeutics Approved by the US FDA Between 2001 and 2010", JAMA 317(18):1854–1863 (opened via Healio summary; JAMA page not opened; figures consistent per Adv-2). Novelty — how this differs from each: N1 predicts boxed warnings/withdrawals from sample size, review time, prior boxed warning and priority review; no AE frequency-spectrum statistic; its null for sample size is the anomaly the candidate would explain (size should matter only through coverage). N2 predicts any safety event from biologic status, indication, pathway and review timing; no internal safety-data statistic; supplies the base rate and baseline model. N3 prescribes exposure by a detectable-frequency rationale; no drug-specific completeness estimate; never validated against label additions. Pharmacovigilance capture-recapture estimates incidence or under-reporting of a known reaction across sources, not the count of never-observed types.
