ID: UQ-20261015-20
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology / molecular methods — PCR primer and multiplex-panel design. Neighbours: clinical and environmental diagnostics (surveillance panels, tiled amplicon sequencing, oncology MRD), bioinformatics tool building, DNA data storage (random-access PCR), CRISPR guide-activity prediction (structural analogue).
Question (canonical): For a designed library of N >= 3,000 distinct primer pairs on identical synthetic templates, with per-pair efficiency defined as log2 relative yield at a fixed cycle number against a common spike-in set and estimated within each (chemistry x multiplex-density) cell for >= 3 polymerase/buffer systems (thermal profile fixed) and >= 2 densities: (a) what are the variance components for pair, chemistry, pair-by-chemistry, density and pair-by-density, and (b) what is the out-of-sample r^2 and Spearman rho of a sequence-feature model trained in one cell and tested in every other? (V1, the scored version; pre-committed bands TRANSFERABLE / NOT TRANSFERABLE / RANK-ONLY TRANSFER as in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) Is primer-pair amplification efficiency a transferable property of sequence and template context, predictable across polymerase/buffer systems and multiplex contexts, or is it specific to the panel and chemistry in which it was measured?
- (lay) Would a public atlas of measured primer-pair efficiencies be useful outside the exact assay it was measured in, or does efficiency simply not transfer?
Motivating gap: Silence mapping — primer design is dense with how-answers (Tm matching, GC clamp, 3'-end stability, dimer avoidance; repeated empirical ARTIC revisions) and thin on measured accounts of why thermodynamically equivalent pairs differ by orders of magnitude. Gate 2 falsified the gap's second clause in two directions: the qualitative transferability question was asked and answered in 2018 across ten polymerases (P3), and the 10^4-scale sequencing-readout version with a cross-condition transfer test was executed in 2024-25 in template space (P1). Only the crossed pair-level decomposition with chemistry and multiplex density remained unlocated.
Presuppositions: P1 pooled sequencing readout yields an interpretable per-pair efficiency, i.e. pool-level competition separable from intrinsic efficiency — CONTESTED, load-bearing (P1-source validates 4 sequences by singleplex qPCR, F(4,10)=252, p=5e-10, but under one shared primer pair, so inter-primer competition is untested). P2 "efficiency" is a scalar per pair — established in singleplex qPCR, contested in multiplex; V1 defuses it by indexing to the cell, making pair efficiency a vector. P3 thermodynamic matching defines a real contrast set — established but tool-relative (strata depend on the nearest-neighbour model chosen). P4 identical pool runnable across >= 3 chemistries and >= 2 densities — feasible, in routine use. P5 template structure variable independently of primer sequence — partly; needs synthetic templates. P6 (added at Gate 2) chemistry factors separable — P1-source confounds polymerase with anneal (54 vs 60 C) and denature (95 vs 98 C) temperature; the candidate inherits the confound unless the thermal profile is held fixed. Not presupposed: that a transferable predictor exists.
What would count as an answer: the pool above measured in >= 3 chemistries x >= 2 densities with singleplex qPCR validation on >= 24 calibration pairs spanning the efficiency range, yielding (a) a crossed-random-effects variance decomposition with CIs and (b) cross-cell out-of-sample r^2 and rho against a permutation null, scored by the pre-committed bands. Statable, which is why the question fails on novelty rather than well-posedness.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 web searches (cap reached), 5 fetches (3 pages opened); full list in batches/2026-10-15-2033/UQ-20261015-20-record.md. Most informative: (4) "machine learning model predicts PCR amplification efficiency from primer sequence training data measured efficiencies" -> the two decisive hits, Nat Commun 2025 s41467-025-64221-4 / bioRxiv 2024.09.20.614030 and PrimerCast (NeurIPS 2025); (7) "multiplex PCR panel amplicon uniformity compared across different polymerases master mixes same primer panel dropout reproducibility" -> Witte et al. 2018 plus vendor datasheets, no multi-pair x multi-chemistry matrix; (8, answer-side) "public database atlas of measured primer pair amplification efficiencies reusable across assays" -> qPrimerDB (thermodynamic) and PrimerBank (pass/fail only), confirming no measured-efficiency atlas exists; (3) "is PCR amplification efficiency transferable across polymerase buffer systems variance decomposition primer by chemistry interaction" -> vendor tech notes and US20090176232A1, no decomposition study; (10, cross-field analogue) "sgRNA guide activity prediction fails to transfer across datasets platforms" -> PMC10485023, the same portability problem treated as transfer learning. Ledger duplicate check: 15 entries read, none touches PCR; UQ-20261015-15 is a structural sibling (variance decomposition plus predictor refitting), not a duplicate. Not obtained: PMC12533003 (302 then reCAPTCHA) — preprint PDF read instead. Nine vocabularies named but not searched (metrology/commutability, ISO 20395, CLSI MM-series, amplicon balancing, LAMP and capture-probe portability, forensic STR cross-platform, MRD panel patents, "primer pair" x random effect/ICC, non-English) were left for the Disguise pass, which never ran.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1. bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.09.20.614030 (preprint PDF opened; method CluMo; published version appears in search as Nat Commun 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-64221-4 — page not opened, author list NOT verified): two Twist pools of 12,000 random 108-nt sequences under shared 0F/0R primers, six iterations of 15 cycles with iSeq readout, per-sequence efficiencies fit to an exponential PCR model, ~2% poor amplifiers, singleplex qPCR validation on 4 sequences, two workflows (KAPA SYBR FAST/54/95 vs Q5 Hot Start/60/98), five external DNA-storage datasets; cross-condition transfer AUROC/AUPRC 0.87/0.17 to 0.43/0.02; conclusion: bias is oligo-sequence-driven rather than pool-driven, with "strong workflow dependence"; no variance decomposition. P2. PrimerCast, "Predictive Modeling of PCR Amplification with an AI-Ready Experimental Dataset", Baek, Hsu, Ektefaie, Sabeti; poster, NeurIPS 2025 "AI for Science" workshop (abstract page opened): 50,760 primer-target reactions, 141 targets, 360 primer sets, quantitative efficiency labels; no stated chemistry contrast, density contrast, transfer test or decomposition (workshop abstract only). P3. Witte, Sickha, Mester, Fister, Schoder, Rossmanith, "Essential role of polymerases for assay performance — Impact of polymerase replacement in a well-established assay", 14 Nov 2018, DOI 10.1016/j.bdq.2018.10.002 (page opened; journal name not printed in-session): ten polymerases on one primer pair (LIP1/LIP2) and two amplicons; 3/10 enzymes amplified the full prfA range, sensitivity losses up to 10^6-fold, explicit target-by-polymerase interaction "remains unclear", conclusions that polymerase replacement "can destroy a well-established assay" and that the authors "cannot provide a universal strategy".
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — the varying unit is the template under one fixed primer pair, so primer-primer competition, dimers, cross-priming and panel composition are absent; two confounded workflows rather than >= 3 clean chemistries; no density series; binary poor-amplifier AUROC rather than a decomposition. But P1 poses the candidate's transferability question at the candidate's scale with the candidate's readout and validation design, and reports an answer. vs P2 — distinct pairs, quantitative labels, 10^4 scale: the atlas premise is already built; one apparent chemistry, no transfer or decomposition limb. The candidate is the control experiment P2's own dataset needs — an increment on a published artefact. vs P3 — n = 1 pair, 2 amplicons, pass/fail and sensitivity rather than a variance split; but P3 asks and answers the weak form in its title.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: TRANSFERABLE licenses pooling efficiency labels across chemistries, a shared atlas, and reduced revalidation on chemistry change; NOT TRANSFERABLE retires the atlas programme, converts design into panel-local calibration, caps every sequence-only predictor's accuracy as a within-chemistry number, and gives standards bodies grounds to require revalidation on master-mix change; RANK-ONLY TRANSFER keeps atlases for triage only. The decision content is the magnitude, not the sign — P1 and P3 already make "interaction exists" the expected answer.
Significance — audience: primer-design tool builders (Primer3 / qPrimerDB / PrimerBank / PrimerCast lineage), who must choose pooled vs chemistry-stratified training labels; multiplex-panel developers (pathogen and wastewater surveillance, ARTIC-class tiling, bespoke oncology MRD); reagent vendors holding the only cross-chemistry per-pair data as internal QC; standards bodies (MIQE/dMIQE successors, CLSI MM-series, ISO 20395) that require efficiency to be reported but specify no domain of validity. Risk conceded in the record: panel developers may treat the answer as already known from P3 and act no differently.
Significance — fecundity: whether the portable component is only what thermodynamic predictors already capture; whether pair-by-chemistry interaction is low-dimensional enough for few-shot anchor calibration; whether density dependence is pairwise (dimer-driven) or collective (depletion); whether one estimand covers capture probes, LAMP primer sets and CRISPR guides instead of five folk literatures.
Significance — anchoring: ARTIC V4/V4.1 dropout and the publish-the-fix-not-the-measurement pattern; P3's unattributed target-by-polymerase interaction; the unresolved tension inside P1 between "sequence-driven, not pool-driven" and an out-of-workflow transfer at AUROC 0.43 / AUPRC 0.02 — the sharpest anchor; the documented non-transfer of sgRNA-activity models, handled as transfer learning; the standards gap on efficiency's domain of validity.
Reason for silence: cost and incentive on top of a recent instrument, with the instrument clause only partly intact. Pooled synthesis plus NGS made 10^4-scale efficiency measurement possible only in the last few years, and the instrument was promptly spent twice (P1 2024-25, P2 2025) on within-regime predictors: a crossed design multiplies cost by (chemistries x densities) while risking the headline r^2 of the paper being written. The only parties who routinely run one panel across master mixes are reagent and panel vendors, for whom publishing such a matrix is a commercial liability, so the data stay in internal QC; and the question straddles method developers and tool builders. P3's title-level conclusion then functions as received wisdom that makes the quantitative version look settled. Conceded in the record and accepted here: the question was askable in 2018 and answerable since ~2023, so this is received wisdom plus cost, not an instrument barrier — a mechanism, but a weak one that sits beside two papers that came within one design choice of answering it.

ID: UQ-20261015-21
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine (clinical informatics, patient safety, quality measurement); AI (deployed clinical early-warning / decision-support models)
Question (canonical): At sites with staggered go-live of a real-time EHR alert triggered by a threshold on a discretionary (non-device-captured) charted vital sign, with documented threshold awareness among charting staff: (a) does the charted value's discrete mass function shift at go-live — deficit in the first k integers at/above the trigger, excess in the k below, on integer support against the site's own pre-period heaping, with a pre-registered equivalence band; (b) is the shift absent in two negative controls (device-auto-populated values at the same numeric threshold; discretionary values at no-alert thresholds); and (c) if (a) is outside the band, what fraction of that site's own measured PPV/sensitivity change from first to later post-deployment year is reproduced by re-scoring the later cohort under the pre-go-live charting mass function, label definition and case mix fixed? (Intake form V0 reformulated once at Gate 1; both versions in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) Do the numbers clinicians type move away from an alert's threshold once the alert goes live, and does that movement explain why deployed early-warning scores get worse with age? (2) Is Goodhart's law measurable in the input layer of EHR decision support — does threshold-based triggering change the measurand that feeds it?
Motivating gap: Manually charted respiratory rate heaps at 18/20 and is a trigger term in qSOFA/NEWS/sepsis alerts (Badawy 2017); deployed early-warning systems decay after go-live; SEP-1-style threshold measures provoke documented coding-level response. Intake asserted that no published test asks whether the charted numbers themselves shift away from a live threshold. Gate 2 refutes that gap: such a test is published and answered (Carey 2009). Full record: batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-21-record.md.
Presuppositions: (1) trigger value known to charting staff — contested at intake, moved into R1's inclusion criteria; (2) value partly discretionary — established for RR, contested for SpO2/HR (used as controls); (3) pre/post charting comparable apart from the alert — contested (go-live itself changes charting behaviour: McBride 2005, RR recording ~30%→~91%); (4) deployed performance truly decays — contested, made dependent limb (c); (5) go-live dates, exact thresholds and per-observation metadata recoverable at usable N — feasibility, unverified; (6) post-go-live discontinuity in a discretionary variable implies behaviour not physiology — contested, the identifying crux; (7) (added Gate 1) support permits a well-defined "immediately above/below" contrast — partly false as intake assumed: RR mass sits at 18/20, the common trigger is 22, and ordinary heaping already empties 21/23.
What would count as an answer: A pre-registered multi-site staggered-go-live study delivering (a) excess/missing-mass estimates on integer support with the equivalence band, (b) both negative controls, and (c) conditional on (a), the re-scoring decomposition of the site's own PPV/sensitivity change. Three pre-committed verdicts: distortion present and sufficient; present but insufficient; absent within band. Minimum disconfirmation: distortion inside the band at every threshold-aware site, or distortion present in the device-captured control (which would indict the design).
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 of 11 WebSearch calls plus 5 of 5 fetches used, none refused; full list in batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-21-record.md. Significance — consequence: If present and sufficient, post-deployment recalibration and external-validation estimates computed on charted inputs downstream of a live threshold are contaminated by an endogenous measurand, retraining on recent local data encodes the distortion, and threshold triggering is self-undermining by construction; part of reported EWS decay moves from a property of models to a property of measurement, with an ambiguous safety reading (missed deterioration vs appropriate local correction of an over-sensitive alert). If insufficient, a bounded nuisance term. If absent within band, a folk mechanism is killed with a number and Carey is shown not to transport from payment targets to real-time alerts.
Significance — audience: Model-governance/assurance teams (would add input-distribution surveillance at the trigger value with go-live as the event); quality-measure designers at CMS/NQF; EWS/CDS vendors choosing threshold vs continuous triggers and how much of the cut-point to expose; regulators of adaptive clinical software, for whom an endogenous input distribution breaks the premise that post-market data can validate a locked or updating model. Honest discount: the required change is one added monitoring chart, and the data holders are the parties a positive result would embarrass.
Significance — fecundity: Optimal visibility policy for a trigger value; distortion-robust triggers built on the invariant part of a heaped distribution or device-captured surrogates; whether suppressed triggers carry prognostic information (do suppressed-trigger patients deteriorate less?); whether distortion decays, persists or grows with alert tenure and transfers when the threshold moves; which incentive structures distort a measurand at all.
Significance — anchoring: Goodhart / performative prediction (Mendler-Dünner et al., NeurIPS 2022); EWS post-deployment decay literature (Epic-sepsis critiques; medRxiv 2025.07.31.25332542); digit heaping and measurement reactivity in vital signs (Badawy 2017); bunching, McCrary density tests and manipulation-robust RDD from public economics (arXiv 2009.07551); P4P gaming at register and exception margins (Gravelle 2010).
Reason for silence: Not silent, which is the finding. The question was asked and answered one disciplinary step away (Carey 2009: payment target, primary care, BP) and has not crossed into inpatient real-time alerting. Credible mechanism: a disciplinary boundary (bunching/density estimators live in health economics; charted inputs are classed as "data quality" in informatics) reinforced by an incentive gap (the holders of go-live dates and charting metadata are those a positive result would show gaming their own safety alerts). "No one thought of it" is not available and is not claimed — Carey's group thought of it in 2009.

ID: UQ-20261015-22
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine / clinical pharmacology (PBPK, model-informed drug development); regulatory science. Neighbour vocabularies searched: metrology (GUM correlated inputs), environmental-modelling pedigree analysis (NUSAP), evidence synthesis (sample overlap / double counting), HTA decision modelling, regulatory toxicology (OECD GD 331), radiological-protection reference physiology.

Question (canonical) — R1 (one reformulation used at Gate 1; V0 in the record): Within openly documented platforms only (PK-Sim/OSP, published system-parameter compilations, EMA/FDA submission annexes; proprietary libraries out of scope, the coverage gap itself reportable), for a pre-specified list of PBPK *system* parameters (MPPGL, CPPGL, hepatocellularity per gram liver, hepatic/renal blood-flow fractions of cardiac output, organ volumes, and the Rodgers–Rowland / Poulin–Theriault tissue-composition inputs): (a) under a pre-registered rule for "mutually independent primary human measurement" (distinct subject sample AND assay AND laboratory, with a stated adjudication procedure), how many independent primary human sources, pooled subject N, year range and demographic/procurement composition underlie each default value and each default uncertainty distribution, and what is the shared-source incidence matrix across the parameter set (which parameter pairs descend wholly or partly from the same subject series)? (b) For five decision-bearing published PBPK analyses reproducible in an open platform, does Monte Carlo propagation under provenance-corrected uncertainty — each parameter's uncertainty-on-the-mean rescaled to its effective independent-source count plus the shared-source correlation from (a), population variability left at platform defaults — move the decision metric across a boundary fixed in advance (predicted victim AUC ratio leaving 80–125% or crossing the ICH M12 no-effect boundary; paediatric predicted exposure leaving the adult exposure-matching band)?

Alternative formulations:
1. (Lay) How few people's bodies are actually inside the physiology defaults used to justify doses and interaction labelling without a trial — and if the same bodies recur across several parameters, does the justification hold?
2. (Technical) Are PBPK system-parameter uncertainties traceable to mutually independent primary data, or do they share so few primary subject series that intervals computed under independence are too narrow for the decisions built on them?
3. (Metrology) Treating a PBPK platform as a GUM measurement model, what covariances between its physiological input quantities are induced by shared primary sources, and what do they do to the combined standard uncertainty of its decision-bearing output?

Motivating gap: presupposition inversion of the settled claim that PBPK uncertainty is dominated by drug-specific parameters "because system parameters are known physiology" — a claim that licenses FDA/EMA acceptance of PBPK in place of clinical DDI and paediatric studies (EMA PBPK guideline Annex 6 is literally the system-parameter documentation slot). Single parameters have been meta-analysed (Barter 2007; Leeder 2022); parameter-set-wide provenance, effective subject N, demographics and shared-source correlation have not been audited, and no decision-bearing analysis has been re-run under such a structure.

Presuppositions: (1) defaults traceable to primary sources — CONTESTED, handled by open-scope restriction; (2) "mutually independent primary measurement" operationalisable — feasible by precedent (Leeder 2022 stratified by tissue source and procurement route); (3) decision-bearing analyses reproducible outside sponsors — CONTESTED, mitigated by OSP qualification models, leaving a convenience case set; (4) workflows propagate system parameters as independent — CONTESTED, positively evidenced for correlation neglect by CONFIRMS D3; existing population covariances encode between-subject physiological covariation, a different object from shared-source epistemic correlation; (5) decisions are sensitive to system-parameter uncertainty — UNKNOWN, this is limb (b), not an assumption; (6) thin provenance is a defect — CONTESTED, refused: limb (a) is descriptive, decision impact is the criterion; (7) a source count maps to a corrected distribution — CONTESTED, the weakest joint; one mapping pre-registered plus a sensitivity analysis over it.

What would count as an answer: (1) a machine-readable provenance graph — per parameter, independent primary source count under the registered rule, pooled N, years, demographics, procurement route, plus the cross-parameter shared-source incidence/correlation matrix, every chain traced to the primary report or marked untraceable; (2) Monte Carlo propagation for five decision-bearing analyses, default-independent vs provenance-corrected-correlated, reporting boundary crossings and sensitivity to the mapping. Four pre-committed verdicts, all informative: thin AND ≥1 decision flips / thin but all five robust / provenance adequate as documented / not traceable (bounded census plus matrix for the traceable subset, limb (b) declared not estimable).

Full lists: batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-22-record.md and -adversary-1.md / -adversary-2.md). If adequate as documented, the presupposition is vindicated and the graph becomes a reusable traceability artefact. If untraceable, the most consequential outcome and one no present framework reports: a checkable claim about the evidentiary base of model-informed drug development.

Honest deflation carried from the record and sharpened by both adversaries: the likely response is a documentation column on checklists that already exist (EMA Annex 6, OECD GD 331), which is cheap and modest.

Mechanism 1 as written (disciplinary boundary — pedigree analysis confined to environmental modelling, correlated-input propagation to metrology) is contradicted by evidence from both adversaries: participant double-counting is a named concern in medicine's own evidence-synthesis literature, citation-chain provenance audits of decision-bearing reference physiology have been executed inside clinical medicine (eGFR, spirometry), regulatory PBK guidance already templates parameter-source documentation (OECD GD 331), and P3 ran limb (a) inside PBPK itself. Mechanism 2 (wrong-pocket incentive gap: archival tracing is unrewarded, benefit accrues to regulators and to a non-commercial regime) is an acceptable mechanism on the ledger's list but explains why the work is not *done* more than why it is not *asked*. Mechanism 3 (a better-rewarded substitute route — qualification by demonstrated predictive performance, P1) is genuine and evidenced, but it is a reason the question is *correctly* unasked where clinical anchoring exists; its force is the asymmetry — P1's instrument cannot operate where the clinical comparator was never collected, which is where waivers are granted. Mechanism 4 (the "system parameters are known physiology" background assumption, reinforced by sensitivity rankings read as confirming it when they only rank within assumed ranges) addresses non-asking but is asserted, and P3 is partial evidence against it. Net: one asking-mechanism survives, weakly; mechanism 1 should be dropped.

Gate 5 verdict reasoning (terse): novelty Medium with a complete search record (29 documented queries; Disguise verified by both adversaries, 9 queries each, above the required 8); significance 2/3 meets the bar; no Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4 from either adversary, so not Rejected; not a disguised known — both adversaries searched for and failed to find the composite, and the nearest named failure mode (sample overlap / double counting) is a within-parameter object, not the cross-parameter shared-source object at issue, so this is not a corpus or covariate swap on an asked question. Strongest remaining objection: limb (b) is aimed at the smaller error term, and the record's own benchmark prior proves it — R1 rescales uncertainty-on-the-mean and imposes correlation while leaving population variability at platform defaults, yet the boundaries it adopts (80–125% / ICH M12 no-effect; paediatric exposure-matching band) are variability-dominated interval comparisons, and P1 measures this platform class underpredicting BSV ~2-fold (AUC) and ~3-fold (Cmax) against total between-study imprecision of only 18–31% with mean bias −6% to −4%. ID: UQ-20261015-23
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology (single-cell and spatial genomics, human cell atlases) — target; transplant source: observational astronomy (injection-recovery completeness / survey selection functions)
Question (canonical): For each of K published human cell atlases that release raw reads plus pipeline code, inject real foreign cell populations into the atlas's own raw data at controlled frequencies f and pre-specified distinctness levels d, re-run the atlas's own published pipeline at its own published resolution (recovered = >=50% of injected cells in one cluster of purity >=p reported as distinct), and report (a) the recovery-probability surface R_atlas(f,d) with its 50% contour and bootstrap bands, (b) whether contours coincide across atlases after conditioning on cells profiled and on what dissociation delivered, and (c) the expected number of recoverable-in-principle populations the atlas did not report, from integrating 1-R against a stated (f,d) prior. (Intake V0 reformulated once at Gate 1 — R1 adopted; both versions in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) What is a cell atlas's detection limit, stated the way a sky survey states completeness, and how many cell types does it imply remain unseen at that depth? (2) What is the limit of detection of a cell atlas as an assay for cell populations, with population frequency as the concentration axis and separability from matrix as the second axis?
Motivating gap: Every sky survey publishes a completeness/selection function derived by injecting synthetic sources into real data and re-running the pipeline; atlases publish cell counts and comprehensiveness language instead (HCA white paper, arXiv:1810.05192) while downstream users treat them as reference denominators and as the adjudicator of "new cell type" claims. Intake asserted that no one measures a published atlas's own recovery function. Gate 2 found the missed-count half already asked and provisionally answered (P1) and the two axes already in print as predictors of method performance (P2); Gate 4 found the pipeline-level two-axis recovery question asked and answered in 2019. Full record: batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-23-record.md; adversary log: batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-23-adversary-1.md.
Presuppositions: (1) raw data and the exact published pipeline available and re-runnable — partly contested, constrains atlas selection; (2) "transcriptional distinctness" admits a pre-specified cross-atlas parameterisation — contested (P2 already uses a separability construct); (3) injected populations realistic enough that recovery transfers to real biology — contested, central methodological risk; (4) "number of populations missed" is meaningful — contested, cell-type ontology disputed, so the primary estimand is recoverable clusters at a fixed resolution rule; (5) atlases are used as if comprehensive — established by usage; (6) detection depends mainly on frequency and distinctness rather than dissociation/capture bias — contested, forces the function to be declared conditional on what dissociation delivered; (7) added at Gate 1: the published pipeline is mechanically re-runnable — contested and fatal in combination (see adversary attack 4), since published atlases are human-curated artefacts and an injection run measures the automated pipeline plus a surrogate annotation rule.
What would count as an answer: Per-atlas injection-recovery curves through each atlas's own pipeline plus the declared surrogate annotation rule, reported as a 50%-recovery contour with bands in (frequency, distinctness) space; plus a missed-population forward estimate from integrating 1-R against a stated prior, with prior sensitivity and explicit dissociation conditioning. Pre-committed outcomes: (i) contours differ materially, so cross-atlas rare-population claims are not comparable and releases need a completeness statement; (ii) contours similar and shallow, so comprehensiveness language and sampling-only calculators are vindicated; (iii) the integral is prior-dominated, so only the contour is reportable; (iv) the human-adjudication subsample shows the surrogate rule misstates recovery by more than the contour's bands, so artefact-level completeness is not estimable without curators.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 of 11 WebSearch calls and 5 of 5 fetches used at Gate 2, none refused; 9 further Disguise queries and 4 fetches at Gate 4. Full lists in batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-23-record.md and -adversary-1.md. Most informative: "how many human cell types remain undiscovered ... saturation" -> the decisive hit, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.08.631769 (P1), which asks and answers the missed-count half; "spike in known rare cell population into real scRNA-seq data re-run clustering pipeline recovery probability detection limit" -> P2 (rs-10583472), the recurring nearest neighbour on axes; "single-cell atlas 'selection function' OR 'completeness function' ... astronomy analogy" -> astronomy only, the two literatures do not meet at this phrasing; "detectability threshold cluster size separation high-dimensional mixture model" -> the asymptotic (size, separation) boundary exists as theory (arXiv:1806.00118, arXiv:1607.05222), never instantiated on a published artefact; "'injection-recovery' ... transplanted to genomics" -> no transplant found. Adversary Disguise additions that changed the verdict: D1 "spike-in cell line into PBMC scRNA-seq 'detection limit' ... recovered as distinct cluster" -> CellSIUS (Genome Biology 2019), a real-cell two-axis (frequency x diluted distinctness) recovery test under standard pipelines; D6 "'probability of detecting' a cell type as a separate cluster depends on number of cells and number of marker genes power simulation" -> ncells (bioRxiv 706481) plus a whole design-power genre. Ledger duplicate check: all 20 prior entries read; no duplicate; structural siblings UQ-20261015-13 (richness-estimator transplant), -16 (audit a published artefact), -01 (species-area transplant).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (P1) Miihkinen M., Chu Y., Vakkilainen S., Akimov Y., Aittokallio T., "Completeness estimation of large-scale single-cell sequencing projects", bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.08.631769, v1 2025-01-08 / v2 2025-03-04 / v3 2025-06-04, unpublished preprint (full text opened by Gate 2; authorship and versions verified by the adversary via api.biorxiv.org) — rejects cell counts as completeness, fits a lognormal abundance model to Tabula Sapiens, benchmarks Chao2/ICE/Jackknife, applies Chao2 to cluster incidence in mouse isocortex (29.3 estimated vs 29 observed, concluding "fully profiled"), derives a ~3% coverage threshold. (P2) Liu K., Jin X., Fu C., "A systematic benchmark and practical guide for rare-cell detection in single-cell RNA-seq data", Research Square rs-10583472 v1, 2026-09-16, under review (record page opened; resurfaced independently in adversary D1 and D9) — ranks eleven rare-cell detectors on real data downsampled by cell type, reports rare-cell abundance and transcriptional separability as method-dependent predictors of performance. (P3, found by the adversary and the most damaging) Wegmann R. et al., "CellSIUS provides sensitive and specific detection of rare cell populations from complex single-cell RNA-seq data", Genome Biology 2019;20:142, doi:10.1186/s13059-019-1739-7 (opened, adversary F2) — eight-cell-line benchmark with rare populations at 2/5/10 cells (0.08-0.16%) and distinctness diluted 0-99.5% by gene replacement, run through standard pipelines (Seurat, SC3, mclust, pcaReduce), concluding that none of the tested methods identified rare types below 1%. Also real and opened: ncells, bioRxiv 706481 (detection power as a function of proportion, cell number, marker fraction and fold change); poem/subpopulation-detection metrics, bioRxiv 2024.11.28.625845. Sensei (BMC Bioinformatics 2022) and bioRxiv 218370 carried as UNVERIFIED by name; scPower (10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7), SCOPIT, PMC12840603 and PMC6180488 named from listings, not opened.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same target field and the same missed-count question, opposite epistemics: P1 extrapolates unseen richness backward from clusters already reported, which is blind by construction to a population undetectable at any abundance, whereas the candidate measures the detection function forward; but P1 occupies the missed-count slot in print, so that limb is neither un-asked nor merely open. vs P2 — shares both axes and real-data recovery experiments; differs only in unit of analysis (published artefact at its own resolution vs eleven tools), in injection construction (foreign populations mixed at read level vs downsampling resident types), and in deliverable (contour with bands vs association). vs P3/CellSIUS — the closest formulation on the record and missed by Gate 2: it already varies frequency and distinctness jointly on real cells through standard pipelines and states a one-point detection limit; the candidate differs in that the pipeline is a named atlas's own and the target is a tissue atlas rather than a cell-line mixture, which is an instance swap, not a new question. vs ncells/scPower/Sensei/SCOPIT — these answer sampling-step or power-step detection probability without a pipeline re-run; the candidate adds QC, integration, clustering and annotation. vs neighbouring-field practice (metagenomic internal standards, flow/CyTOF LOD, astronomy injection-recovery) — routine there, absent here, one-dimensional in concentration there; vs planted-structure theory — gives the asymptotic shape of the contour, never instantiated on a real artefact.
Novelty confidence: Medium (as recorded at Gate 2, on 11 queries across seven vocabularies with five sources opened). The adversary's 9 fresh-vocabulary Disguise queries did not find the exact object — no per-named-atlas own-pipeline recovery contour exists in any vocabulary tried — but surfaced two prior formulations the record had missed (CellSIUS 2019, ncells 2019) which, with P2, make the two-axis pipeline-level recovery question a known question renamed. Medium novelty survives for the artefact-level object only, and that object is the one presupposition 7 concedes is unmeasurable, so the surviving novelty and the surviving well-posedness do not overlap.
Significance — consequence: If contours differ materially (i), every cross-atlas claim about a rare population's presence, absence or frequency is confounded by the reporting artefact's detection function, completeness-corrected frequency replaces reported frequency, releases acquire a completeness statement, and P1-style richness extrapolations must be redone with unequal detectability. If similar and shallow (ii), a specific worry about the reference infrastructure is retired on evidence and sampling-only calculators are vindicated. If prior-dominated (iii), only the contour is deliverable. If the surrogate rule breaks (iv), artefact-level completeness is shown not to be estimable without the curators.
Significance — audience: atlas consortia and data platforms (HCA, CZI CELLxGENE, Human Lung Cell Atlas, Tabula Sapiens, Gut Cell Atlas, BICCN) who decide what accompanies a release; reviewers and editors adjudicating novel-cell-population claims, who today have no denominator; Cell Ontology curators deciding when absence from an atlas is evidence; rare-cell method developers wanting an artefact-level baseline; groups using atlases as deconvolution, label-transfer and power-calculation denominators; funders trading depth against breadth. Honest limit, pressed and left standing at Gate 4 attack 6: the appetite for a contour is inferred from the astronomy analogue, and P1 is evidence that when this community voiced the need it wanted a count, accepted one, and that reference-mapping novel-type detectors already serve the operational use.
Significance — fecundity: completeness-corrected cross-tissue and cross-condition frequency comparison; optimal design as a contour-lifting problem (cells vs donors vs protocol vs resolution rule); protocol-level completeness as a comparable quantity across dissociation, single-nucleus and spatial assays, turning dissociation bias from caveat into axis; calibration of richness extrapolators against a measured detection function (a repaired P1); completeness-weighted multi-atlas integration; an operational definition of "new cell type" relative to a stated contour; empirical vs theoretical comparison against planted-structure thresholds.
Significance — anchoring: how many human cell types exist (P1, the immune-cell counting debates); the unsettled definition of a cell type, deliberately sidestepped by fixing a resolution rule; reproducibility of rare-population claims; known-but-uncomputed dissociation and capture bias; the gap between proved detectability thresholds and anything measured on real catalogues; the astronomical selection-function norm whose absence is the motivating anomaly.
Reason for silence: Claimed mechanism — a disciplinary boundary between resample-impossible and resample-cheap sciences (astronomy must characterise its catalogue's blind spots; single-cell biology sorts, enriches or builds a better detector instead), reinforced by a benchmarking convention that evaluates methods rather than datasets, plus a recent feasibility threshold (public raw reads, containerised pipelines, compute for hundreds of re-runs). Gate 4 reduced this to Partial: the question demonstrably was asked, of tools and of design (CellSIUS, ncells, scPower, P2, Weber & Robinson 2016 in cytometry) and of datasets by subsampling (bioRxiv 218370, PMC6180488), so the silence is confined to the per-named-atlas injection instance; and the "no venue for a deficiency curve on someone else's atlas" claim is undercut by the existing genre of ambient-RNA and doublet re-analyses of published atlases. Only the feasibility-threshold limb stands.

ID: UQ-20261015-24
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI (large-scale training systems; compute governance and verification); STEM — power systems measurement (PMU/synchrophasor, point-on-wave, electrical-network-frequency forensics). Neighbours: non-intrusive load monitoring, hardware power side channels, media forensics. Source method: new-instrument question.
Question (canonical): For a single-cluster AI training campaign of known power profile and phase schedule, measured simultaneously inside the facility and outside its fence: (a) in the 0.05–55 Hz band, what is the ROC for discriminating "training active" from "facility energised but not training" using (i) utility PMU and point-on-wave records at the point of interconnection and at buses one, two and >three electrical nodes away, and (ii) a publicly recordable wall-socket ENF trace on the same interconnection — as a function of job size in MW and of local grid strength (short-circuit ratio at the PCC, local inertia), with a stated floor below which the test is at chance; (b) which of four pre-named job attributes (training/idle state, checkpoint-restart cadence, dominant collective-communication oscillation frequency, scale-up/scale-down events) are estimable from each measurement class on held-out jobs, with per-attribute error bars; and (c) what is the confusion rate against other large flexible loads (electrolyser, arc furnace, crypto mining, pumped load) and against the same facility running its own power-smoothing hardware?
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) Do the sub-second synchronised power swings of a large AI training job leave a signature detectable outside the facility, at what MW threshold, and which job attributes are recoverable?
- (lay) Can an observer outside a datacentre tell from grid measurements alone whether a large model is being trained inside it, and at what scale does that become possible?
Motivating gap: The forward problem is documented (arXiv:2508.14318, synchronised multi-MW oscillations driven by collective-communication phases) and mitigation hardware ships for it; compute-governance verification proposals rest on on-site, cooperation-dependent mechanisms (attestation, chip telemetry, billing-level energy accounting). An externally measurable non-cooperative channel with a stated detection floor would be a different instrument. Gate 2 found the inverse problem is no longer untouched: a utility-side simulation detector and a chip-level workload classifier both appeared in 2026.
Presuppositions: P1 training-induced oscillations survive aggregation at the PCC and stay above background at the nearest external point — CONTESTED and part of what is asked (utility limits of 3.5–25 MW p-p imply visibility at those amplitudes; on-site batteries/supercapacitors/firmware smoothing exist to remove them). P2 adequate-rate external measurements are lawfully and non-intrusively obtainable — PARTLY CONTESTED and instrument-bounded: PMU validated bandwidth 2 Hz (P-class) / 5 Hz (M-class) regardless of reporting rate, aliasing above half the reporting rate, PMU feeds access-restricted, ENF open to anyone on the interconnection. P3 other large flexible loads do not produce confusable signatures — UNKNOWN; a required arm, not a premise. P4 facility load at the relevant timescale is dominated by one coherent job — CONTESTED (mixed training/inference fleets, multi-tenancy); load-bearing, since the near-duplicate's statistic is itself a coherence measure. P5 field ground truth (MW, phase schedule, parallelism) obtainable for ≥1 instrumented campaign — FEASIBILITY; neither 2026 prior met it. P6 someone would act — grid planners clearly; the governance use is CONTESTED on legal and ethical grounds. Not presupposed: that the channel is open, that any attribute is recoverable, or that mitigation is incomplete.

Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: if the channel is open with a quantified floor, grid planners gain the attribution step their compliance limits presuppose but do not provide, and governance gains a non-cooperative verification primitive together with a confidentiality problem (job-level leakage to anyone with PMU access, and to the public if ENF carries it). If open only for episode detection with no job-level content — the outcome N2's coherence statistic makes most plausible — the reliability use stands and the governance use is refuted, removing an argument that grid monitoring could substitute for on-site attestation. If mitigation closes the channel, a class of proposed non-cooperative mechanisms is retired and smoothing hardware acquires a second, unpriced dimension: signature suppression.
Significance — audience: (1) reliability bodies already acting on adjacent work — NASPI/DOE-OE and the PNNL group, ERCOT large-load modelling, ESIG 2026, and the utilities setting MW oscillation limits — who would learn where to site POW recorders and whether a PMU fleet can support compliance at all; (2) compute-governance verification researchers (arXiv:2604.04712 / 2506.15867 / N1), whose menu of mechanisms a negative answer prunes; (3) datacentre operators and counsel, facing a load-data disclosure question and a new argument for or against smoothing hardware; (4) the ENF forensics community, for whom load-driven ENF content is both a new signal and a new interference source.
Significance — fecundity: whether mitigation's own switching leaves a distinct suppression marker; how coherence and hence detectability degrade with fleet mixing and multi-tenancy; whether public ENF-based auditing of large-load behaviour is possible, and what the restricted/public measurement asymmetry implies for governance design; whether generator- and IBR-oriented oscillation source-location methods transfer to loads; whether load-side signature sanitisation becomes a standard as interconnection oscillation limits did; whether inference fleets separate from training fleets at facility scale as N1 achieves at device scale.

Reason for silence: proposed mechanism is an instrument-and-institution mismatch with a short fuse — the band straddles an instrument boundary only documented in 2026 (PMUs validated to 2–5 Hz and aliasing above half the reporting rate, so the answering data are mostly POW records that are not continuously archived); the institution holding the data is chartered for reliability compliance and barred from publishing customer-attributable load data, while the institution wanting the inference comes from the chip-telemetry tradition and has no PMU access. But the mechanism is expiring, not holding: N2 crossed this boundary from the power-systems side in 2026 and N1 from the security side, which fits "newly asked and barely answered" rather than "un-asked", and is itself part of the ground for the Low rating.

ID: UQ-20261015-25
Date: 2026-10-15
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI — training practice; evaluation methodology; safety evaluation and assurance. (Methodological neighbours: statistical selection inference; lot-release metrology.)
Question (canonical): For open training runs with dense terminal checkpoints, define the shippable set as terminal checkpoints whose held-out validation loss lies inside a pre-registered equivalence band (delta fixed in advance from the measurement error of the loss) around the released checkpoint's loss. Over that set: (a) what is the across-checkpoint spread of each decision-relevant measured quantity (fixed capability suite; refusal rate on a fixed harmful-request set; attack success rate under a fixed jailbreak suite; long-horizon agentic success), with checkpoint and eval item as separate variance components; (b) how does that across-checkpoint component compare with the item-level / paired-bootstrap interval reported for the same eval on a single checkpoint; and (c) under argmin-validation-loss and argmax-on-a-later-reported-dev-suite selection, what is the optimism of the published number, E[score | selected] minus E[score of a uniformly drawn in-band checkpoint on a fresh eval draw]?
Alternative formulations:
- Is a released model's reported score a property of the training recipe or of which checkpoint happened to be shipped?
- How much of the reported gap between two models could be reproduced by shipping a different, equally-trained checkpoint of the same run?
- Does a published safety or capability number attach to a run or to a file — and by how many eval-error-bar widths?
Motivating gap: Silence mapping. Checkpoint selection/averaging is a literature (EMA, best-on-dev, soups); eval error bars are a literature (item- and seed-level); open releases (Pythia, OLMo, LLM360) display jagged terminal eval curves and treat the jaggedness as noise to smooth. The record found no source drawing the inference from that jaggedness to the published number of the single artefact that ships, even though safety cases, threshold commitments, procurement and scaling-law fits are written about that artefact. Gate 4 falsified the "no source" premise (see Adversarial log, attacks 1-2).
Presuppositions:
P1. A loss-equivalence band identifies the legitimately shippable set. CONTESTED — handled by modelling two selection rules; both adversaries note loss is documented to disagree with downstream checkpoint preference (Nishida et al.; Xu/Li/Salas 2605.18852).
P2. Enough dense terminal checkpoints are public. ESTABLISHED for pretraining; UNVERIFIED for post-training — no adversary or the record could confirm any open family publishes dense terminal post-training checkpoints, which is exactly where refusal/jailbreak/agentic behaviour lives.
P3. Eval resampling noise is separable from checkpoint variation. ESTABLISHED.
P4. Third parties treat reported scores as model properties. Asserted from practice; supporting policy documents listed, never opened.
P5. In-band checkpoints are not simply equivalent. This is the question, not an assumption.
P6. A spread, if found, would be acted on. CONTESTED.
P7 (surfaced at Gate 4, fatal to well-posedness as written). "Band width delta fixed from the within-checkpoint measurement error of the loss itself" is near-degenerate: a forward pass at fixed weights on a fixed validation set is deterministic (A2), and read as validation-set resampling SE the band is ~1e-3 nats, below the per-1000-step loss movement during LR annealing, so the shippable set is plausibly a near-singleton (A1).
What would count as an answer: For >=3 open runs with dense terminal checkpoints, including >=1 post-trained family: the across-checkpoint spread inside the band, against paired-resampling noise on the same checkpoint, plus best-of-K optimism. Pre-committed bands: (i) spread <= eval noise — worry retired; (ii) spread > noise but under published safety-case and leaderboard margins — reporting recommendation; (iii) spread crosses a published decision threshold or leaderboard gap — reported numbers are artefact-specific and selection-biased.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 29 total — 11 at Gate 2 (full list: batches/2026-10-15-2233/UQ-20261015-25-record.md), 9 by adversary 1 and 9 by adversary 2, 8 of each adversary's being new-vocabulary Disguise queries (full lists: UQ-20261015-25-adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md). Most informative: (Gate 2, #8) "checkpoint-to-checkpoint variation larger than evaluation error bars bootstrap LLM benchmark reporting recommendation" -> the deliberate answer-search; returned only item-/seed-level error-bar proposals, read by the record as "no answer found" — FALSIFIED at Gate 4. (A1, #1) "'signal and noise' benchmark 'final checkpoints' standard deviation language model evaluation decision" -> Heineman et al., arXiv:2508.13144, NeurIPS 2025: "noise" is DEFINED as the relative SD of scores over the final n checkpoints of a single run (n=30 at 13B), measured on 30 benchmarks over OLMo 2 1B-32B and 73 open models, with a reporting recommendation (average last k) and a scaling-law-fit consequence attached — i.e. the candidate's central quantity is already named, measured and published. (A2, #1-#3) Rashomon/model-multiplicity vocabulary -> Ganesh et al., arXiv:2501.14959, Table 1 already names the estimand ("Std. of Scores", "Unfairness Range" over the near-optimal set), §5.3 asks the metric-hacking/covert-selection question the record filed under fecundity, §7 lists "Multiplicity and LLMs" as the program's open frontier. (A2, #6) early-stopping vocabulary -> Rajabi et al., NeurIPS 2024 workshop, "Amplified Early Stopping Bias": part (c)'s estimand asked and answered generically. (A2, fetch of 2406.10229 full text) -> "the 7B seed variance is well below the 95% CI for the same benchmark" — the spread-vs-printed-interval comparison the record claimed nobody makes. (A2, #8) hardware "golden sample"/silicon-lottery vocabulary -> the unit-vs-product-line inference is folk-standard outside ML. Disguise VERIFIED: both adversaries ran their 8 new-vocabulary Disguise searches; no call refused.

N1'. "Noise" = SD of benchmark scores across the final n checkpoints of one run; measured at scale; averaging last k recommended; noise conjectured to bound scaling-law fit error.
N2'. Ganesh, Gohar, Chen, Liu, Shen et al. (2025), "Systemizing Multiplicity: The Curious Case of Arbitrariness in Machine Learning", arXiv:2501.14959 — opened by A2. N3'. Madaan, Singh, Schaeffer, Poulton, Koyejo, Stenetorp, Narang & Hupkes (2024), "Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks", arXiv:2406.10229 — full text opened by A2. Variance components for LLM benchmark scores compared directly against per-benchmark 95% CIs ("well below"), plus a monotonicity statistic over training checkpoints.
(Record's own three nearest — Nishida et al. 2510.04848 [A1 and A2 confirm: across-terminal-checkpoint SDs, no noise baseline], Madaan 2406.10229, Lu et al. 2607.25063 — plus N4 Xu et al. 2605.05973 and N5 Shen & Li 2609.11490, are in the record. 2607.25063 remains unverified by either adversary. Also named by A2 and never by the record: Rajabi et al. 2024; Xu/Li/Salas 2605.18852; Bouthillier et al. 2021.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs N1' — the candidate's band is a loss-equivalence band rather than a fixed last-n window, and it adds the item-CI comparison, the two-rule optimism and the safety/agentic suites; but the quantity, the object (one run's terminal checkpoints) and two of the three claimed consequences (reporting practice, scaling-law fits) are N1's. vs N2' — the candidate's set is one run's terminal cloud rather than independently trained near-optimal models, so it is a cheaper instantiation of N2's set, not a different estimand; the asking community, the metric and the metric-hacking question pre-exist it. vs N3' — N3's component is cross-seed with data order fixed, not the within-run terminal cloud, and it has no safety/agentic suites; but it already performs the spread-vs-printed-CI comparison the candidate's part (b) was built around.

Significance — consequence: Unchanged as argued (band (iii) would break threshold commitments, scaling-law fits over per-checkpoint scores, and sub-spread leaderboard gaps; band (i) licenses current practice; band (ii) yields a reporting recommendation) — but the capability arm's answer is now largely foreseeable from N1' and N3' (small spread, likely band (i)), so the live consequence narrows to the safety/agentic arm, which P2 may not be able to supply.
Significance — audience: Real and already acting on the quantity — the AI2 eval line publishes it (N1'), the multiplicity community owns the estimand (N2'), the error-bar community revises intervals on variance findings (N3'). This strengthens audience and weakens novelty: these are the communities that already asked.
Significance — fecundity: Sibling-spread scaling with model size or post-training length; whether safety behaviours have systematically wider clouds than capability scores; whether averaging inside the band lands safety behaviour at the cloud mean; whether "which sibling ships" is an auditable covert-selection channel (already asked as metric-hacking in N2' §5.3); replication rate of a third-party safety finding on a different in-band sibling.
Significance — anchoring: Eval-reliability/error-bar programme (N1', N3', Miller 2411.00640); checkpoint-instability and weight-averaging (Nishida 2510.04848; soups); model multiplicity / Rashomon sets (N2'); classical selection-bias-in-performance-evaluation and early-stopping bias (Cawley & Talbot 2010; Dodge 1909.03004; Rajabi 2024; Xu 2605.05973); version-vs-process attachment of measured properties in frontier safety frameworks; emergence/scaling fits over per-checkpoint scores.
Reason for silence: The record's role-and-data boundary plus incentive gap is partly falsified. The group holding the cloud did ask about terminal-checkpoint spread and published it (N1'), and a Meta team asked about tied late checkpoints (2605.18852). A2 supplies the better-evidenced mechanism and it cuts against novelty: the multiplicity community believes the LLM case is out of reach because "training multiple models is often infeasible at this scale" (N2' §7) and pivoted to prompt multiplicity — they did not notice the terminal-checkpoint cloud is free. That is a program standing one step from the question, not a question nobody posed. The data-boundary story survives only for the post-training safety arm.

ID: UQ-20261016-01
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI (large-scale training systems / AI architecture); computer-engineering reliability (silent data corruption, fleet reliability). Source method: anomaly mining.
Question (canonical): (V1, the version assessed) In large-scale neural-network training runs, (a) within a defined population of instrumented runs, what is P(hardware-fault-coincident | loss spike or divergence not explained by batch replay or optimizer state), with a confidence interval and a false-attribution rate measured on fault-free control periods; and (b) can a reference-free weight-space statistic — computable from a released checkpoint alone, with no clean twin of that run — detect, above a stated detection floor, that an uncaught corruption event occurred during the run that produced it?
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake, superseded at Gate 1) What fraction of undiagnosed loss spikes and run divergences in large training runs is attributable to silent data corruption in accelerators or interconnect rather than to data or optimization, and do released checkpoints retain detectable weight-level traces of corruption events that were never caught?
- (lay) Are the loss spikes that frontier runs resolve by rewinding and skipping batches actually hardware faults, and can a shipped model's weights be audited for corruption that went undetected?
- (technical) What is the attributable share of silent arithmetic faults in the unexplained instabilities of large training runs, and what weight-space signature would such a fault leave in a final checkpoint?
Gate 1 note: one reformulation used (permitted). V0 left the conditioning direction and reference class unspecified and was trivially satisfiable on limb (b) by differential methods needing a clean reference; V1 fixes the estimand, the control-period requirement and reference-freeness. Novelty was scored against both versions; V1 does not escape pre-emption.
Motivating gap: Intake's gap — that fleet-scale SDC work and large-run instability reports "never meet" — is **falsified by the record's own Gate 2**. An SDC-in-LLM-training subfield exists as of 2025-26 (AEGIS, OSDI '26; SDCHunter, OSDI '26; Ma et al., ACL 2025; Altenbernd et al., arXiv:2604.00726; plus OCP/NVIDIA and semiconductor-test supply-side work). What survives is narrower: the existing work builds in-flight catching and terminates at rollback, and none reports the reverse conditional, a control-period false-attribution rate, or any inspection of a shipped checkpoint's weights.
Presuppositions: (1) unexplained spikes occur — established (PaLM arXiv:2204.02311). (2) SDC occurs at measurable rates on datacentre GPUs — established 2026 (AEGIS: 18 incidents / 13 GPUs / 3.5e7 GPU-hours; SDCHunter: 23 confirmed defective GPUs, 40 in production); intake's "contested" is out of date. (3) a silent fault can perturb weights durably — substantially established (Ma et al. weight drift / "different optima"; Altenbernd et al. persistent parameter divergence); its establishment *reduces* the candidate's novelty. (4) attribution achievable by replay + telemetry — established forward, contested reverse (SDCHunter: loss, gradient-norm and hardware telemetry do not correlate with SDCs; AEGIS: SDCs masked by normal loss fluctuation). (5) released checkpoints are the deployed artifact — established, trivially. (6) some reference-free weight statistic separates a corruption trace from training noise — **contested**; BitFlipScope's only quantified detector is differential, its self-referential mode reaches block granularity with no stated detection limit, and a "verified fault-free" null population may be unconstructible since AEGIS cannot rule out undetected SDCs in its own fleet. (7) (added at Gate 1) "undiagnosed spikes" is a stable, portable reference class — **contested**: the population is defined by what one team's diagnosis pipeline failed to explain, so the estimand is pipeline-relative.
What would count as an answer: Three separable deliverables. (a) Attribution — an instrumented run with fingerprint/replay-class checking (not ABFT, which Ma et al. find unreliable in bf16) classifying spikes as fault-coincident, reporting the reverse conditional with a CI plus a false-attribution rate on fault-free control periods; **asked, open**. (b) Calibration — fault injection at known rates yielding P(spike), P(silent absorption) and residual perturbation after N steps; **largely pre-empted** by Altenbernd et al., who inject into GPU matmuls across 60M/350M/1.3B runs, sweep injection frequency (eval loss 7.38 / 4.77 / 4.33 / 4.30 at every / 1-in-10 / 1-in-100 / 1-in-1000 steps) and decline recall because "many SDC are masked during training"; only the absorption probability is unreported. (c) Checkpoint audit — a pre-registered reference-free weight statistic (per-tensor tail outliers, mantissa/exponent patterns, update-residual structure) with a null from verified fault-free runs and a stated detection floor, applied to public checkpoints; **un-asked**, and the only limb that is. A negative result (a detection floor) is informative by construction.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 distinct web queries and 5 verified fetches; search budget exhausted, none refused. Full list: `batches/2026-10-16-0033/UQ-20261016-01-record.md`. Most informative: (1) "loss spike attribution silent data corruption large language model training hardware fault" → surfaced the whole 2025-26 subfield; intake's gap falsified on the first query. (3) "what fraction of training loss spikes are caused by hardware faults versus data attribution replay" (answer-search) → no source reports any such fraction. (4) "audit released model checkpoint weights for undetected bit flip corruption forensic weight-level signature" → only adversarial/security work (BitFlipScope, ROBBIN, SILK, OneFlip); nothing on accidental training-time corruption. (6) "soft errors supercomputer silent corruption attributable fraction of unexplained application anomalies HPC" → ~20 years of detection work, no attributable share. (9) "reference-free detection corrupted weights released model no clean copy anomaly statistic mantissa distribution" → backdoor/trojan nulls only. (10) "PaLM loss spikes cause never determined hardware silent corruption" → PaLM plus a well-developed optimizer-side account (Adam instability, arXiv:2304.09871) raising the prior on the non-hardware branch. Verified by reading: osdi26-lei.pdf, osdi26-zheng.pdf, arXiv:2502.12340, arXiv:2512.22174, arXiv:2604.00726v1. Named but **not opened, not citable**: arXiv:2604.10390, 2608.30769, 2605.04213, 2508.01786, 2405.02803, 2503.20263, 2304.09871, 2605.21146, 2508.00161, 2604.26505, OCP/NVIDIA whitepaper.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Altenbernd, Wiesner, Kao, "Exploring Silent Data Corruption as a Reliability Challenge in LLM Training," arXiv:2604.00726v1, 1 Apr 2026 (opened).
2. Lei, Zheng, Li et al. (Tsinghua + ByteDance), "Safeguarding LLM Training at Scale: Online SDC Detection and Insights from 35 Million GPU Hours," OSDI '26 — AEGIS (opened).
3. Zheng et al. (SJTU + ByteDance Seed), "SDCs in the Wild: Characterizing and Diagnosing SDC-defective GPUs in Production LLM Training," OSDI '26 — SDCHunter (opened).
(Also opened, limb-specific: Ma, Pei, Lausen, Karypis, "Understanding Silent Data Corruption in LLM Training," arXiv:2502.12340 / ACL 2025; Karamat, Saif, Chamon, "BitFlipScope," arXiv:2512.22174.)
Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs Altenbernd et al.: inference direction (they inject and observe: P(spike | fault); the candidate wants P(fault | spike)), prospective online detector vs retrospective artifact audit, and no absorption probability or null. **The calibration limb is a near-duplicate of their stated problem; only the curve is unreported.**
- vs AEGIS: answers the forward conditional at fleet scale (3 of 18 incidents observable as training failures) and is evidence that the candidate's limb (a) is *hard*, not an answer to it; never conditions on the spike, reports no measured false-positive rate on fault-free periods, stops at rollback, and concedes undetected SDCs may remain — the audit limb stated as a limitation rather than a question.
- vs SDCHunter: its polluted-checkpoint count is modelled from an assumed SDC rate, never measured on weights; its layer-wise signatures need a healthy concurrent reference group and its replay needs the run's own seeds, kernels and communication order, so nothing transfers to a third party holding only weights.
- vs Ma et al.: establishes presupposition 3 but reports no attributable fraction and proposes no checkpoint statistic.
- vs BitFlipScope: inference-time, adversarially motivated, differential (needs a clean twin) for any quantified detection, block granularity without one, no stated detection limit, never run on public checkpoints — the clearest demonstration that the audit limb is un-asked.
Novelty confidence: Low
Low because a near-duplicate exists for the calibration limb (Altenbernd et al. 2026) and the attribution limb is the explicit organising premise of a five-paper 2025-26 subfield, so it is asked and only two summary statistics are unreported. The LEDGER's own grade for "likely asked; a near-duplicate was found" applies, in both V0 and V1. Narrowed to the checkpoint-audit limb alone, the record's own assessment is Medium — that is a different candidate and must be re-intaken, not rescued here.
Significance — consequence: If the attributable share is non-trivial, rewind-and-skip-batches is partly mis-specified (the correct action is device quarantine and re-verification), and the most-cited piece of evidence in these reports — that replaying the same batches produced no spike — is diagnostically ambiguous rather than exculpatory for the data. If it is near zero with a tight interval, that licenses the optimizer-side account as default and quantifies what AEGIS and SDCHunter already assert qualitatively. If the audit limb returns yes, a released checkpoint becomes auditable for the hardware history of its run by a third party, which no existing method allows; if no, the deliverable is a bounded detection floor.
Significance — audience: (i) frontier pretraining/reliability teams, who demonstrably price reliability information precisely (4.3% overhead for 5.65% coverage vs 683.9% for kernel-level checks); (ii) model evaluators and auditors, who have no notion of hardware provenance for a checkpoint; (iii) accelerator vendors and semiconductor-test/fleet-reliability engineering, who need the workload-level cost to justify in-field screening; (iv) weaker and flagged speculative: model-release governance, which has no accidental-corruption construct.
Significance — fecundity: whether a surviving perturbation predicts any evaluation-level deficit or merely a different optimum of equal quality; whether fine-tuning, merging or quantization launders the trace; whether any public checkpoint was produced under verification strong enough to serve as a null (probably none, itself a finding); whether training-run reproducibility claims are falsifiable given that bitwise replay needs locked kernels and communication order; the optimal spike-response policy given P(fault | spike).
Significance — anchoring: training-instability (hardware vs optimizer branches argued with no shared attribution framework); SDC-at-scale (rates and detectors, no workload-attributable cost); semiconductor test escapes; model provenance and artifact integrity (adversary-focused); reproducibility of training runs.
Reason for silence: For the attribution and calibration limbs, **silence has ended** — the mechanism that kept them quiet (no instrument at fleet scale) broke in 2025-26, when per-kernel fingerprinting and cross-replica checksums at 1e7 GPU-hour scale plus the cost of one corrupted frontier run made the question both answerable and expensive enough to ask. This is a finding against the candidate, not a defence of it. Three mechanisms remain for the checkpoint-audit limb only, all of acceptable kinds: an incentive/liability gap (means and motive sit on opposite sides of the artifact boundary — the lab alone can build the null and gains nothing, the evaluator benefits and holds only weights); a disciplinary boundary at the checkpoint (reliability engineering's success criterion ends at rollback, ML evaluation treats weights as hardware-provenance-free); and vocabulary capture (every weight-level forensic tool found presupposes an adversary, hence a clean reference or a known trigger, which accidental corruption lacks).
