ID: UQ-20261016-02
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — clinical informatics / clinical decision support; pharmacoepidemiology; patient safety.
Question (canonical): Treating each of K commercial interaction compendia (Lexicomp, Micromedex, First Databank) as a classifier whose severity label is the configuration surface for EHR alert firing, on a pre-specified sample of interaction pairs stratified by severity class and over-sampling pairs the compendia grade discordantly, every pair estimated in two or more linked databases under one pre-registered design family (active-comparator new-user cohort, plus SCCS where its assumptions hold), with the estimand harm attributable to the combination rather than to either drug alone and a commensurable pre-specified primary outcome (ADR-coded or all-cause hospitalisation, or death, within 90 days of co-exposure initiation), and pairs failing pre-specified identifiability diagnostics reported as a named "unidentifiable" stratum rather than dropped: (a) what is the distribution of pair-level attributable risk within each compendium's severity class, and what share of between-pair variance in measured harm does class membership explain; (b) does severity class rank pairs by measured harm better than chance, against a pre-specified minimum, and equally across the K compendia; (c) in real alert logs, holding sensitivity for total measured harm fixed, what alert volume fires under compendium-derived versus outcome-derived classes, as a reclassification table? (This is R1, the single Gate 1 reformulation; V0 left the estimand, the commensuration rule and the disposition of unidentifiable pairs undefined. Full V0/R1 text: batches/2026-10-16-0033/UQ-20261016-02-record.md)
Alternative formulations:
1. Do the "major"/"contraindicated" labels in Lexicomp, Micromedex and First Databank predict excess adverse outcomes in linked claims or EHR data, and do the three gradings rank the same pairs in the same order of measured harm?
2. What is the PPV for harm of the severity class that triggers an interruptive DDI alert, and how much alert volume could be removed at fixed sensitivity for harm if the class were outcome-derived?
3. (Lay) Are the drug-combination warnings that stop a prescriber mid-order sorted by how often patients are actually hurt, and would sorting them by measured harm change which ones appear?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion of "compendium severity grades encode risk of harm" — the basis on which EHRs fire interruptive alerts on top classes and P&T committees set firing rules. Anchoring anomaly: the compendia disagree with each other on severity for the same pair (Vitry 2006: 33%/29% major-vs-moderate cross-disagreement, Spearman 0.546; Malone 2023: Fleiss kappa median 0.11), so at most one ordering can be right, yet no ordering has been audited against measured outcomes. Gate 2 corrected the intake twice: PMC2000587 is Vitry 2006 (not Abarca 2004), and "no outcome-validation found" is false for one slice (P1).
Presuppositions: 1. Severity grades determine which alerts fire — ESTABLISHED (AHRQ report: a site re-tiered 103,486 DDIs, alerts ~17.1 → ~1.8 per 100 orders). 2. Compendia disagree materially on severity — ESTABLISHED (Vitry; Malone kappa 0.11). 3. Combination-attributable harm estimable at scale with acceptable confounding control — CONTESTED (confounding by indication/frailty; handled by the named unidentifiable stratum). 4. Class-level harm rate is meaningful — CONTESTED, answered by limb (a)'s variance decomposition rather than assumed. 5. "Harm" commensurable across pairs well enough to rank — CONTESTED; the hospitalisation/death composite under-weights non-hospitalised lab-abnormality harm, so (b) tests discrimination for serious harm only. 6. Alert-volume reduction is a goal because fatigue causes harm — FLAGGED (>90% override rates documented, harm link inferential); limb (c) is stated at fixed sensitivity and does not depend on it. 7. Enough pairs carry sufficient co-exposure counts — TESTABLE, UNVERIFIED; worst for the over-sampled discordant stratum, which may be rare precisely because a warning suppressed co-prescription. 8. Combination-vs-single-exposure is the right estimand — ESTABLISHED by P1 (aORs fall 76.5%/83.0% on switching the reference group from non-exposure to single-drug exposure).
What would count as an answer: Per-compendium class-level harm distributions plus (a)'s variance decomposition; a rank-discrimination statistic per compendium against its pre-specified minimum from (b), with the unidentifiable stratum named and sized; and (c)'s reclassification table of alert volume and harm capture at matched sensitivity. Three pre-committable verdicts: (i) classes discriminate serious harm and the K orderings agree — grading vindicated; (ii) classes discriminate but orderings diverge — at most one grading usable, the table says which; (iii) classes do not discriminate measured serious harm in the identifiable stratum — the configuration surface carries no information about serious harm (see Strongest remaining objection: this reading needs narrowing). Minimum disconfirmation: the unidentifiable stratum swallows most sampled pairs, reported as "not feasible at pair level with current data".
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 distinct queries (minimum 8), 5 fetches; full list with per-query results in batches/2026-10-16-0033/UQ-20261016-02-record.md. Most informative: "drug interaction compendia severity rating validated against patient outcomes attributable risk claims data" → compendium-comparison and checker-accuracy material only, no outcome validation of severity classes; "Hansten Horn drug interaction significance rating history evidence documentation level clinical importance classification" → confirms the grading axes are editorial-evidential (severity-if-it-occurs × documentation quality), never outcome-rate-based; "machine learning re-grade drug interaction severity from real-world outcomes electronic health records reclassify alerts" → contextualisation and rule logic only, no re-grading by observed outcomes; "drug interaction severity ratings criticized based on expert opinion not evidence of harm alert thresholds pharmacy and therapeutics committee" → the decisive hit, the Pharmaceutical Journal report of the CPRD antibiotic-DDI study (P1). Fetch failures recorded, not papered over: DOI 10.1002/cpt.2807 CLIENT_ERROR and PMC3706355 redirect-only, so at Gate 2 P1 stood at news-report standard and Phansalkar at metadata only. Adversary #2 later opened P1's primary (see below). A further 18 queries in 13 vocabularies Gate 2 did not try were run by the two adversaries (adversary-1.md, adversary-2.md).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. van Staa TP, Pirmohamed M, Sharma A, Buchan I, Ashcroft DM, "Clinical relevance of drug-drug interactions with antibiotics as listed in a national medicines formulary", Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics 2023;113(2):423-434, DOI 10.1002/cpt.2807 — VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY by adversary #2 (research.manchester.ac.uk record opened; PMC10107602 blocked by redirect/reCAPTCHA). Two case-control studies in linked English primary-care/hospital data, ages 65-100: 51 BNF severe-warning antibiotic DDIs vs ADR-related admission (121,546 cases / 638,238 controls) and 89 DDIs vs emergency admission; 38/51 (mean aOR 3.96) and 75/89 (mean aOR 2.40) significantly raised against non-exposure, but aORs fell 76.5% and 83.0% against single-antibiotic exposure; conclusion "no evidence of substantial risk", with a call to strengthen the evidence base for formulary DDI listings. One formulary, one warning category, no cross-tier comparison, no compendium comparison, no alerting limb.
P2. Vitry AI, "Comparative assessment of four drug interaction compendia", Br J Clin Pharmacol 2007;63(6):709-714, DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2125.2006.02809.x, PMC2000587 (OPENED). 1,095 unique major interactions, 50 drugs, four compendia; 14-44% of one compendium's majors absent from the others; Spearman 0.546 severity, 0.430 evidence quality; compendia compared only to each other.
P3. Malone DC et al., "Meaningful Drug Interaction Alerts", AHRQ R01HS25984 final report, University of Utah, 2023 (OPENED). Fleiss kappa median 0.11 across Lexicomp/Micromedex/Hansten-Horn; per-pair association estimates; 52.4% of alerts filtered by rule logic; 103,486 DDIs re-graded by pharmacist review cutting alerts ~89%. States it did not evaluate whether severity grades matched measured harm and that the reclassification was by clinician judgement, not outcome data.
Cited but NOT opened, flagged: Abarca 2004 (JAPhA 44(2):136-141, PMID 15098847; title/venue confirmed by two independent results); Phansalkar 2013 (BMC MIDM 13:65, PMC3706355; metadata only, re-surfaced in adversary #1's queries). Tatonetti 2012 carried from intake, NOT verified — do not cite as verified. Adversary-found neighbours: Far E et al., "Validation of a transparent decision model to rate drug interactions", BMC Pharmacol Toxicol 2012;13:7, PMC3598205 (OPENED by adversary #1) — validates rating against rating, disclaims gold-standard status; Andersson M, "Drug-drug interactions: from knowledge base to clinical impact", Karolinska 2014 (OPENED by adversary #2) — builds/evaluates SFINX, never tests the A-D classes against harm; "Predictive Validity of Inappropriate Prescribing Criteria for ADEs, Hospitalizations, and ED Visits: A Time-To-Event Comparison of the Beers and STOPP Criteria", Value in Health 17(7) (found independently by both adversaries, not opened) — the homologous question on a sibling classifier.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 (the real threat): P1 is a genuine outcome test of one formulary's top warning category and returns a null-leaning answer, so the intake's "no outcome validation" claim is conceded as false for that slice. But with a single warning category no discrimination statistic is computable inside P1's design; it does not compare compendia, does not sample on disagreement, and has no reclassification limb. What it supplies is presupposition 8, the estimand on which the answer turns. The candidate is the classifier-level generalisation of P1, with P1 as one cell of stratum (a) and a strong prior of a null. vs P2: same anomaly, opposite direction — P2 establishes the gradings disagree and names missing epidemiological evidence as the cause; it is the premise inverted and has no outcome data. vs P3: closest in intent and the clearest demonstration of the silence — it held claims, EHR, FAERS and N3C data and still routed severity through concordance, per-pair estimates and pharmacist re-grading, cutting 89% of alerts without measuring the harm the removed alerts would have caught, which is limb (c) left unasked by the project best placed to ask it. vs the Beers/STOPP predictive-validity work (adversary-found): the same question form on a different object — PIM criteria flag single drugs, so the contrast is exposed-vs-unexposed and the design never confronts the combination-vs-single-exposure estimand (which reverses P1's conclusion) or a classifier that suppressed its own exposure counts. The novelty is of instance, not of question form, and both adversaries say so.
Novelty confidence: Medium (leaning low). Distinct in object from all nearest priors, and no source in 29 queries across 15 vocabularies asks the discrimination or reclassification question of DDI compendia. Not High: P1 is a close neighbour that answers one cell and would plausibly generalise; the question template is routine in geriatric-PIM research; and two promising leads (East-Asian claims items, two Bordeaux DDI theses) went unopened on budget. Not Low: no near-duplicate found, and P3 shows the best-resourced group in the field declining to ask it. Not asked-but-open: the asked slice (P1) is answered rather than open, so nothing routes to the open-problems handoff.
Significance — consequence: If classes discriminate and the K orderings agree, the configuration surface is vindicated and attention moves to contextualisation with the severity axis settled. If they discriminate but orderings diverge, at most one grading is usable and the table names which — directly relevant to every health system's knowledge-base contract. If they do not discriminate within the identifiable stratum, the label firing interruptive alerts carries no information about serious harm, so current alert burden is a cost with unmeasured benefit rather than a sensitivity/specificity trade-off; P&T committees gain an evidence basis for outcome-derived configuration and P3's 89% cut would read as plausibly harmless rather than merely bold. A null also converts P1 from an antibiotic curiosity into the first cell of a general finding.
Significance — audience: (i) P&T and CDS governance committees, who today pick a firing threshold on a vendor scale with nothing to calibrate against; (ii) knowledge-base vendors (Wolters Kluwer/Lexicomp, Merative/Micromedex, FDB), who would have to state whether their scale is an evidential-documentation scale or a harm-rate scale — currently conflated in the Hansten/Horn axes; (iii) pharmacoepidemiology networks (Sentinel, OHDSI/EHDEN, CPRD), for whom auditing a deployed classifier is a new, well-defined use of machinery they already run; (iv) regulators and policy bodies setting alert-burden expectations. HONEST DISCOUNT: P1 published a null-leaning result on 51 flagged pairs with an explicit call to reduce indiscriminate flagging, and nothing opened shows any formulary entry or alert configuration changed; the binding constraint on switching alerts off is medicolegal cover, which an observational audit does not supply. Scored 2, not 3, on that evidence.
Significance — fecundity: Whether the severity and documentation axes should be separated with only one wired to firing; whether discordant pairs are discordant because effects are heterogeneous or because graders read different evidence; whether harm concentrates in patient strata rather than pairs, which would give contextualisation work an outcome target it lacks; what the suppression bias is worth, turning presupposition 7's failure mode into its own estimable question; whether the audit method transports to the other opinion-graded classifiers wired into EHRs (PIM lists, allergy cross-reactivity tables, duplicate-therapy rules).
Significance — anchoring: the compendia-discordance anomaly (P2, Abarca 2004); the alert-fatigue/override literature whose central quantity, harm per alert, has never been measured; the expert-consensus high-priority DDI list (Phansalkar 2013) as the field's substitute for measurement; large-scale population-level estimation with negative-control calibration (OHDSI SCCS tooling, ALCAPONE) as the enabling instrument; the open methodological problem of confounding by indication in co-exposure studies, which limb (a) reports rather than solves.
Reason for silence: Four mechanisms were offered; after adversarial testing two survive as asking-level. SURVIVING: (2) incentive and liability asymmetry — the graders sell the grading, data holders gain nothing from a null, and committees need a defensible label for medicolegal protection, so the rational institutional move is not to measure; it also binds limb (c) specifically, which needs a health system's alert logs and licensed vendor content in one analysis, and researchers formulate questions they can get data for. (4) problem reframing — the field named its problem "alert fatigue", a volume problem whose natural solution is consensus triage, rather than "classifier validation", a measurement problem; once the high-priority-list framing prevailed (2012-2013) the validation study had no venue or funding line, with P3 as the direct demonstration. WEAKENED BY ADVERSARIES: (1) "the grading-as-a-classifier is nobody's unit of analysis" is falsified as stated — the same community made exactly this classifier its unit of analysis for Beers/STOPP head-to-head against measured outcomes; (3) instrument recency explains why answering is expensive, not why no one asked, and is dated wrong, since the sibling predictive-validity work ran on claims data around 2014.

ID: UQ-20261016-03
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected (Gate 4, attack 2 Disguise Unresolved on the merits — fatal; novelty downgraded Medium to Low at Gate 5)
Domain(s): Biology — plant pathology / plant-disease epidemiology; regulatory science and administrative law (plant biosecurity). Source method: cross-field transplant (cancer-screening overdiagnosis methodology → statutory plant-health eradication).
Question (canonical): (V1, the version assessed — one Gate 1 reformulation used) Taking *Xylella fastidiosa* in Apulian olive under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/1201 as the index programme, and defining the estimand on the TEST-POSITIVE subset only: among hosts destroyed because they themselves tested positive, what proportion would not have reached a stipulated endpoint — (E1) successful acquisition by a competent vector, or (E2) a stipulated damage threshold — within a stipulated horizon T (e.g. 10 years) under the counterfactual of no destruction; and, treating that proportion as a parameter in a stated loss function over destroyed hosts versus averted onward transmissions, what removal radius does that loss function select? Separate, non-overdiagnosis quantity: among untested neighbour hosts felled by the radius rule, what proportion were uninfected or likewise would not have reached the endpoint within T.
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake, superseded at Gate 1) In statutory plant-health eradication programmes where a positive test triggers mandatory destruction of the host and its neighbours, what fraction of destroyed hosts carried infections that would never have become transmissible or damaging within a stated horizon, and what destruction radius would an overdiagnosis-aware policy choose?
- (lay) How much of the detected disease burden in a *Xylella* or citrus-greening eradication zone is disease that would never have mattered?
- (technical) What is the number-needed-to-destroy per averted onward transmission as a function of removal radius, and has it been estimated for any statutory programme?
Gate 1 note: V0 pooled three disjoint categories the screening literature keeps apart — (i) false positives, (ii) untested precautionary radius culls, (iii) true positives whose infection would never have mattered. Only (iii) is overdiagnosis; (i) and (ii) are already named, measured and litigated in plant health, so V0 was answerable by restating known numbers. V1 restricts to (iii), stipulates T and splits the endpoint into transmissibility (E1) and damage (E2), which can diverge.
Motivating gap: Cancer screening built an estimand-and-counterfactual apparatus (excess incidence, unscreened-arm follow-up, lead-time modelling) for exactly the question "what share of detected cases would never have progressed". Plant biosecurity destroys hosts at large scale on individual test positivity plus a radius rule, and the ingredients of a plant analogue — latent and asymptomatic hosts, host-species differences in titre and vector acquisition efficiency, vector phenology, climate suitability, remaining host lifespan — are separately reported and separately modelled, but the record found no source assembling them into one estimand with a horizon and an endpoint attached. Caveat: the gap is asserted from the intake's prior searching only; this run's Gate 2 did not run, so the gap is not independently established.
Presuppositions: P1 destruction triggered by individual-host positivity plus a radius rule — established in the cited regulation per intake, NOT re-verified; adversary 1 narrows it: it holds in eradication zones, while in the containment-area infected zone positives are monitored rather than felled (Lincei 2018 reports infection rates rising in the Zona di Contenimento) and monumental/historic plants may be retained under testing and monitoring. P2 a non-trivial fraction of test-positive hosts never becomes transmissible or damaging within a decade — CONTESTED, the substantive scientific claim; the record itself concedes it is "plausibly small" for subsp. *pauca* in Apulian olive, i.e. for the chosen index system. P3 a counterfactual is obtainable — CONTESTED; the record claims the cleanest design (hold positives and watch) is legally foreclosed, and adversary 1 shows this is false for the index programme, since containment-zone and monumental-tree cohorts of held positives have existed since c. 2015. P4 the quantity is definable once T and an endpoint are stipulated — established methodologically; V1 discharges it. P5 regulators and growers would act — plausible; the radius is a tunable legal parameter and was litigated. P6 the welfare structure differs from screening (the owner bears the loss, third parties and the public interest take the benefit), so "overdiagnosis" is not readable as a welfare loss without an explicit external-benefit term — CONTESTED-as-framing.
What would count as an answer: The stated proportion for named endpoint E and horizon T, plus at least one of (a) an excess-incidence or natural-experiment estimate from areas where destruction was delayed, refused or replaced by containment, with counterfactual cumulative incidence modelled from pre-programme spread; (b) a cohort of test-positive hosts held rather than destroyed and followed to the endpoint, giving progression hazards stratified by host species, titre and vector pressure (adversary 1: such cohorts are legally available in the index programme's containment zone, not foreclosed); (c) a programme-level model calibrated to (b) returning number-needed-to-destroy per averted transmission as a function of radius, with the loss function and the external-benefit term written out. Horizon and endpoint must be stated with the number. A near-zero estimate settles it in the regulators' favour and counts as an answer. Reporting only false-positive rates, or only the uninfected share of radius culls, does not answer it.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): **Gate 2 did not run in the generating pass** — all 11 permitted queries were refused for that session by a conversation-level safety classifier reacting to prior conversation content, not to query content; searching was stopped rather than reworked. It was **completed in a fresh context in a follow-up pass**, where all 14 queries ran normally, which establishes the refusal as context-specific rather than topic-specific. Vocabularies covered across Gate 2 and the two Gate 4 sweeps: Italian and Spanish regulatory/academic, French (Corse/PACA), veterinary test-and-cull and bovine-TB occult progression, FMD wasted-cull and "number needed to cull", forestry sanitation felling, cancer-screening jargon (overdiagnosis / pseudodisease / non-progressive infection), dead-end-host and inoculum-source, HLB psyllid acquisition from asymptomatic trees, invasive-species eradication economics, optimal-control removal-radius. Query lists: `UQ-20261016-03-record.md` (Gate 2, including the refused first pass), `UQ-20261016-03-adversary-1.md` (9 issued, 4 returned), `UQ-20261016-03-adversary-2.md` (9 executed in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try, 3 further refused and recorded, 8 fetches), and `UQ-20261016-03-prior-art-sweep.md` (16 searches, 6 fetches).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
N1. Hyatt-Twynam SR, Parnell S, Stutt ROJH, Gottwald TR, Gilligan CA, Cunniffe NJ, "Risk-based management of invading plant disease", *New Phytologist* 2017. Abstract read verbatim at https://www.repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/263425 (the PMC copy returned only a redirect from this environment); corroborated at https://ponteproject.eu/?p=6761. The method "preferentially removes **hosts expected to cause a high number of infections in the remaining host population**" — a per-host expected-onward-transmission quantity, in a model the repository record keywords as *stochastic* — and this "motivates a variable radius strategy, which approximates risk-based control via **removal radii that vary by location**", with strategies "judged by the estimated number of citrus trees eliminated".
N2. Tildesley MJ et al., "The impact of spatial clustering on disease transmission and optimal control", *PNAS* 2010;107:1041–1046, doi 10.1073/pnas.0909047107. Objective verified through the fetched commentary Riley S, *PNAS* 2010;107(3):957–958, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2824299, which states it verbatim: "the overall number of infected and culled farms (epidemic impact) can be minimized", and in the Figure 1 caption "epidemic impact (infected plus culled farms)". The same commentary names the overdiagnosis concept qualitatively — aggressive culling causes "the loss of many never-to-have-been-infected farms" — without a fraction.
N3. Parnell S, Gottwald TR, Gilligan CA, Cunniffe NJ, van den Bosch F, "The effect of landscape pattern on the optimal eradication zone of an invading epidemic", *Phytopathology* 2010;100(7):638–644, doi 10.1094/PHYTO-100-7-0638, abstract fetched from https://apsnet.org/publications/phytopathology/2010/July/Pages/100_7_638.aspx. Identifies the removal radius that "minimizes the total number of hosts removed during an eradication campaign that is effective in eradicating the pathogen".
(Loureiro et al. 2025, Preprints.org 202509.2405 — ~412,500 plants uprooted in the Balearics under the 50 m rule, "only four trees were confirmed as infected", 91.1% of infections asymptomatic — was Gate 2's nearest prior and is one step short of the candidate: it reports the raw counts without defining an overdiagnosis fraction or optimising the radius. It is now the fourth-nearest, behind N1–N3.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs N1 — **it does not differ enough, and this is what killed the entry.** The record's only stated ground for distinguishing itself from N1 was that in N1 "every infected host is a future source by construction of the model, so the fraction of infected hosts that would never reach an endpoint is *not representable*", and that N1's "risk" means only probability of being infected given position and dispersal. N1's own abstract contradicts both clauses: the quantity it ranks hosts by is expected onward transmissions *per host*, whose zero class is exactly the candidate's E1 estimand, and it already selects a removal radius from it. What survives is residue — conditioning on an individual positive test, stating a horizon T, reporting the quantity as a fraction, estimating it empirically rather than inside a fitted model, and the E2 damage endpoint — i.e. a difference of label, conditioning set and estimation route, not of question. vs N2 — the candidate's radius half has an objective function identical to N2's (hosts removed plus hosts lost to the epidemic), so that half is established in veterinary epidemiology and the novelty there would be the system, not the objective. vs N3 — the closest *plant* version, and a constrained variant: it minimises removals subject to eradication succeeding, which handles the epidemic-loss term as a success constraint rather than a summand. The unconstrained sum is the one thing the candidate adds, and N2 already has it.
Novelty confidence: **Low** (Gate 2 raised it from Unverified to Medium in the follow-up pass; Gate 4 downgraded it to Low on N1 and N2, which Gate 2 did not reach).
Asked-but-open: **No.** Rejected as a disguised known — the quantity is representable and already computed inside the risk-based-removal formalism, and the radius objective is already optimised in two systems — not as a question posed in print and left unanswered.
Significance — consequence: Bidirectional and in both directions it moves an editable legal parameter. Near-zero at T=10 for the index pair vindicates the rule on its own terms. Substantial in some stratum — tolerant cultivars, low-titre positives, hosts outside vector phenology or climate suitability, ornamental and wild hosts with no economic endpoint, hosts near end of productive life — would imply destruction with no epidemiological return in an identifiable subset. The number also enters compensation and proportionality review, where its absence currently works as a default in the programme's favour. This score survived Gate 4 intact: significance is the one attack both adversaries scored Resolved or near it, and it is not why the entry failed.
Significance — audience: (1) EFSA Plant Health Panel rapporteurs, who already fit the spatial spread models; (2) DG SANTE and national plant protection organisations, for whom radius and demarcated-area dimensions are the editable text; (3) grower associations, their counsel and courts applying proportionality under the precautionary principle; (4) USDA APHIS and the Florida/California citrus programmes, which face the same structure for huanglongbing and faced it for citrus canker; (5) the plant-epidemic modelling community. Evidenced discount from adversary 1: *Pesce* (CJEU C-78/16, C-79/16) upheld felling host plants "whatever their health status", so an argument that some *infected* hosts were harmless is legally weaker than the uninfected-neighbour argument that already lost, and audiences (1)–(2) are the parties least incentivised to commission the estimate.
Significance — fecundity: A methodological cascade with a screening counterpart each — lead time of statutory detection; length-biased sampling, since symptom-led and proximity-led surveys preferentially catch fast-progressing infections; the status of "incidentaloma" positives in wild vegetation; the endpoint hierarchy when E1 and E2 diverge; the overdiagnosis-aware re-survey interval; whether compensation should be indexed to an estimated fraction; and the same estimand in animal health.
Significance — anchoring: The contested *Xylella* removal radius; detection sensitivity and latency, which is the lead-time term the estimand needs; EFSA host-status lists, which concede that host identity governs transmissibility; the eradication-versus-containment decision, already resolved toward containment in places; and the proportionality test courts apply to precautionary destruction. Gate 4 adds the one that mattered: risk-based and variable-radius removal optimisation (N1, N3) and ring-cull radius optimisation in livestock (N2).
Reason for silence: Three legs were claimed and **all three are now gone or hollow.** (i) Disciplinary boundary — claimed on the ground that the plant-health formalism treats every infected host as a future source by construction and so never needs to name the fraction that is not. N1 falsifies this: that formalism ranks hosts by expected onward transmissions, so the fraction is nameable and named inside it. (ii) Structural, "the identifying design is prohibited by the instrument under evaluation" — knocked out by adversary 1, since containment-zone positives and monumental-tree derogations have been legally held and monitored for roughly a decade. (iii) Incentive — survives, but explains only why a *regulator* would not commission the measurement, which is not why a modelling community that already computes the quantity would not report it as a fraction. What is left is the competing explanation both adversaries converged on: in susceptible Apulian olive the answer is presumed ~0, there is no puzzle, and the field asks the question in its own units instead.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3
Well-posedness 2/3: after reformulation the estimand, horizon, endpoints and subset are stated and three answer routes are describable, so Gate 1 passes; it does not reach 3/3 because the question does not choose between E1 and E2 as the policy endpoint, the external-benefit term is named but not written, and the counterfactual is model-dependent. Significance 3/3 stands — it is not why this failed.
Strongest remaining objection: the one that rejected it. The candidate's own stated ground for novelty is factually wrong about its nearest neighbour. Risk-based removal already ranks hosts by expected onward transmissions in a stochastic model and already derives location-varying removal radii from that ranking (N1), and the candidate's radius objective — hosts removed plus hosts lost to the epidemic — is already the objective minimised in livestock ring-culling (N2) and, in constrained form, in plant eradication-zone optimisation (N3). The candidate is that question conditioned on an individual positive test, given a horizon, reported as a fraction and relabelled with the screening term.
Residue worth a fresh intake, stated for the record rather than as a promotion path: the *empirical* estimate is genuinely absent. The independent prior-art sweep (16 searches across English, Spanish, Italian and French, veterinary, forestry, screening and eradication-economics vocabularies) found no source reporting the fraction for any plant **or animal** statutory programme — the FMD literature names it only qualitatively ("never-to-have-been-infected farms") though it is implicitly computable from those simulations, the word "overdiagnosis" has not crossed into population-level veterinary or plant eradication at all, and bovine-TB "no visible lesions" reactors are the nearest real-data analogue with no published fraction. A candidate restricted to measuring that quantity in the field, on a tolerant-cultivar or non-crop stratum, graded from the start against N1–N3, would be a different and defensible intake. It would have to be filed as new, not as a revision of this one.
Honesty notes on this run, recorded rather than smoothed over: (1) both of the record's own Gate 4 pointers come back negative — Tildesley et al. 2009's outcome measure is "fewer farms losing livestock", not the "farms culled per outbreak averted" the record attributed to it, and the Frontiers sanitation-felling paper treats felling intensity as an input with felled trees counted as damage, optimising no removal distance. (2) The two fetches that would have settled presupposition P2 directly — Lee et al. 2015 *PNAS* "Asymptomatic spread of huanglongbing and implications for disease control" (PMC4475945) and PMC6835679 on *Xylella* acquisition from asymptomatic plants — were refused by the fetch tool itself and are recorded as unread; the Lee title alone points against P2's negation for huanglongbing. (3) The classifier that blocked Gate 2 in the generating pass also refused 5 of A1's 9 searches and 3 of A2's 12; none was retried or reworked. The rejection does not rest on anything a refused call would have supplied — it rests on N1's own abstract, read verbatim.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable; rejected.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): **None.** Rejected as a disguised known, not as asked-but-still-open; per the operating rules, answered and disguised-known rejections are not routed. No row appended to `ledger/routed-open-problems.md`.

ID: UQ-20261016-04
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — infectious-disease epidemiology (variant surveillance); environmental microbiology (wastewater genomics); statistical phylodynamics. Source method: new-instrument question.
Question (canonical): For a designated variant's invasion window in a given sewershed, is the per-lineage sewage-to-clinical frequency odds ratio constant in time, and does its measured time-drift displace the fitted logistic growth advantage by enough to change a designation or strain-selection decision? (Gate 1 reformulation; one reformulation used.)
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) Using quantitative wastewater lineage deconvolution as a severity-independent denominator, do respiratory-virus lineages differ systematically in clinical ascertainment rate, and how much of the published relative growth advantage of designated variants is ascertainment artefact rather than transmission?
- (lay) Are variant growth-rate estimates from clinical sequencing biased by lineage-dependent probability of being tested, and can paired wastewater lineage frequencies measure that bias directly?
Motivating gap: Relative growth advantage, measured as a frequency ratio among people who sought testing, drives variant designation and feeds vaccine strain composition; lineage-dependent severity, illness duration or care-seeking could enter it as if it were transmissibility. Claimed new instrument: multi-year city-level quantitative lineage deconvolution from wastewater (Freyja and successors) as a severity-agnostic denominator. Gate 2 falsified the gap claim as intaken: Dreifuss et al. (N1) perform exactly that propagation analytically, state the conclusion for differential clinical testing explicitly, and compare wastewater- against clinical-derived logistic growth rates for Omicron BA.1 across six Swiss sewersheds (close agreement). What survives is only the time-varying residual, which N1 defers in print.
Presuppositions: P1 wastewater lineage frequencies unbiased w.r.t. clinical severity — CONTESTED and central; partly refuted as stated (N3: variant-specific shedding rates differ, highest in the Delta period, lowest in Omicron), weakenable to "the shedding component of the ratio is time-constant over the invasion window", itself untested. P2 deconvolution accurate with quantified uncertainty at the relevant frequencies — partly established; error model limiting at low frequencies. P3 clinical and sewage samples matchable on catchment and window — established where sewershed boundaries and residence-level case data align (Swiss, Quebec). P4 published growth advantage is used as transmissibility — established in practice, caveated in the papers. P5 designation and strain-selection committees would respond to a correction — plausible, not verified against committee minutes. P6 (surfaced at Gate 2, binding defect) the shedding and ascertainment components of the composite sewage-to-clinical odds ratio are separately identifiable from paired frequency series — CONTESTED; attribution of drift requires an external within-host shedding anchor, absent which the answer is not identified.
What would count as an answer: for lineage pairs with multi-month paired series in ~10+ sewersheds, a per-lineage time-resolved sewage-to-clinical odds ratio with an explicit shedding-model sensitivity analysis, plus a refit of published logistic growth advantages carrying that ratio as a time-varying offset; the answer is the magnitude and sign of the shift in the slope (not the midpoint, which provably absorbs the constant part) and whether any actual designation or strain-selection decision would have flipped. P1 failing by a comparable amount answers it in the negative and is equally actionable. Non-identifiability of the two components would dissolve rather than answer it.

Domain(s): Medicine — clinical epidemiology, biostatistics, missing-data methodology; secondary: survey methodology / official statistics; meta-science of simulation-validated methods. Source method: silence mapping.
Question (canonical): For pre-specified (dataset, variable, estimand) triples in which missingness was real and present in a frozen analysis file and the true values were later recovered from a source independent of the analysis file and of the imputation model's predictors, what fraction of recovered values fall inside their nominal 95% multiple-imputation predictive intervals, and what is the bias and interval coverage of the target estimand under MI relative to the complete-after-recovery analysis, with complete-case and a pre-specified MNAR pattern-mixture model as comparators? (Gate 1 reformulation; one reformulation used.)
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) In clinical datasets where values recorded as missing were later recovered from an independent source, what is the empirical coverage of MI predictive intervals and the residual bias in the target estimand — does the MAR assumption that licenses routine imputation hold where it can finally be checked?
- Where record linkage retroactively fills in missing clinical values, how large is the bias standard MI leaves in the analysis it was used for?
- (lay) When a medical study fills in blanks statistically and the real numbers turn up later, how often was the fill-in right, and how wrong was the study's conclusion?
Motivating gap: Dense how-literature, empty why-literature — hundreds of imputation methods validated almost entirely in simulation, where the analyst specifies the mechanism the method is then shown to recover, because MAR is non-identifiable from observed data alone. The record's claim is that the non-identifiability theorem was over-read as a prohibition on measurement, and that national linkage, registry back-fill and LLM-assisted chart retrieval have only now made the licensing assumption checkable where it is relied on. Gate 2 already softened the gap by finding the same design executed on real nonresponse in official statistics in 1988–89 (prior 1); Gate 4 removed it, finding the design executed with real missingness and independently recovered administrative truth in labour economics, with MAR explicitly rejected and imputation bias measured.
Presuppositions: P1 recovery sources exist at usable scale for clinically relevant variables — partly established, LIMITING; weak support from Lotspeich et al. 2025, unproven at the per-variable sample sizes coverage estimation needs. P2 the recovered value is the value that was missing, measured comparably — CONTESTED; registry/chart values may be a different assay, time or observer, and Lotspeich et al. call chart review an "alloyed" gold standard, so the truth set carries its own error; proposed check is a concordance substudy, which (adversary 4c) is runnable only in the non-missing stratum and leaves concordance in the missing stratum unidentified. P3 recovery is not so selective that the recovered subset misrepresents the missing set — CONTESTED; bounded by a recovery-propensity model plus worst-case bounds, and the mechanism-vs-misspecification decomposition is valid only conditional on it. P4 the MI predictive distribution is the right object to calibrate — stated as a choice, not a claim; Rubin's MI defines no per-cell interval with a coverage guarantee, which the adversary pressed as presupposing an object MI does not supply. P5 analysts and regulators would change practice given a calibration curve — plausible; ICH E9(R1) mandates sensitivity analyses whose magnitudes are set by convention. P6 analysis files are frozen early enough, with retained version history, that "what was missing at analysis time" is recoverable as a fact — flagged; silently back-filled registries destroy the design.
What would count as an answer: across registered triples, with the triple list and comparators fixed before recovery data are examined — (i) coverage of nominal 95% MI predictive intervals against recovered values, per triple, reported alongside a recovery-propensity model and the P2 concordance substudy; (ii) bias and interval coverage of the target estimand under MI versus the complete-after-recovery analysis, with complete-case and a pre-specified MNAR pattern-mixture comparator; (iii) attribution of miscalibration to MAR failure versus imputation-model misspecification, separable by refitting the imputation model with recovered data in hand, conditional on P3; (iv) explicit bounds over the unrecovered stratum. Nominal coverage is an informative answer, not a null: it would be the first real-data defence of current practice and would anchor sensitivity-analysis magnitudes. Both directions are distinguishable, so the question is not answerable-whatever-the-evidence.

What separates the candidate is a corpus swap into clinical variables plus a set of readout refinements — MI predictive-interval coverage, estimand-level bias and coverage, the mechanism-vs-misspecification decomposition, an MNAR comparator, recovery-selectivity bounds — and the ledger's disguised-known rule rejects a corpus or covariate swap on an asked question even where the exact variant is unmeasured. The refinements are also the candidate's weakest ground, since the record concedes per-value coverage is not the quantity MI optimises and makes the estimand-level readout primary, and that readout is the one N1 already reports in substance. Secondary and unclosed: PMC5487067 ("Validity of using multiple imputation for 'unknown' stage at diagnosis in population-based cancer registry data", PLoS ONE 2017) states the candidate's question in a clinical registry by title and could not be opened, so the possibility that the question has been asked and answered inside medicine is live and unexamined rather than merely suspected; and only one adversary ran, so no independent Disguise pass checked that conclusion.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable to this ledger — the prior step is bibliographic, not empirical: open PMC5487067 and the HRS "testing the missing mechanism" item, and read N1's imputation-bias section against the Gate-1 readouts, to establish whether anything beyond a readout refinement remains. Any future candidate in this area must be posed as an explicitly incremental question about the MI predictive-interval readout, with N1 cited as the asked precedent, not as an un-asked question.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Rejected at Gate 4 (adversarial inspection) — attack 2, Disguise, Unresolved from the only adversary that ran, which is fatal under the ledger's Gate 4 rule; attack 7 is independently Unresolved, which would have capped the entry at Provisional on its own. Gate 2's novelty rating of Medium is downgraded to Low at Gate 5 on the adversary's opened evidence. Not routed: this is a disguised-known rejection (a corpus swap on a question asked and answered in labour economics, with a title-level clinical instance unverified), and ENVIRONMENT excludes answered and disguised-known rejections from ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Full record: batches/2026-10-16-0033/UQ-20261016-05-record.md; adversary log: batches/2026-10-16-0033/UQ-20261016-05-adversary-1.md. Process note for the batch file: only one Gate 4 adversary ran for this candidate (adversary 2 not spawned); it did complete the required 8+ Disguise searches (9 queries in untried vocabularies), so Disguise is verified-and-failed rather than unverified, but its decisive clinical hit PMC5487067 remains content-unverified after a WebFetch redirect and two proxy-refused curl retries.
Verification by the run session (not by an adversary): the adversary's Disguise kill rested partly on a prior it could identify only by title, so it was checked directly. CONFIRMED — "Validity of using multiple imputation for 'unknown' stage at diagnosis in population-based cancer registry data", *PLoS ONE* 2017 (PMC5487067; the PMC page is behind a browser check from this environment, so the abstract was read at https://doaj.org/article/be7945f372f44399ab413171edd6ec5c). It linked New South Wales Cancer Registry records to a cohort study and, for cases whose registry stage was "unknown", extracted the true stage from clinical notes — independently recovered truth on genuinely missing records, which the abstract explicitly contrasts with earlier simulation studies that induced missingness on fully observed stage. It found the missing-at-random assumption held only when the imputation model included primary treatment, and that imputed-stage Cox models gave similar hazard ratios with wider confidence intervals. So the candidate's premise — that this audit "has not been done in clinical biostatistics" — is false in the candidate's own field, on a clinical variable, with MAR tested against recovered truth; the economics prior is not the only instance, and reason-for-silence mechanism 1 fails in clinical biostatistics too. Residue, stated: PMC5487067 reports MAR-conditional-on-treatment and estimand-level agreement, not per-value predictive-interval coverage, which remains unreported — a readout refinement of an asked question, which is exactly what the adversary charged.

ID: UQ-20261016-06
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI — inference systems / evaluation methodology (AI architecture); neighbours: numerical reproducibility (HPC/climate), Monte-Carlo arithmetic, software-testing flakiness, psychometric measurement theory
Question (canonical): On long-horizon agentic benchmarks run with greedy decoding, recorded-and-replayed tool responses, fixed seeds and a fixed harness, (i) how large is the residual run-to-run variance in task success attributable to batch-composition-dependent floating-point nondeterminism in the serving stack — measured as the gap between replicate variance under default kernels with batch composition deliberately varied and replicate variance under batch-invariant kernels — and (ii) is the default-kernel mean success rate equal to the mean over pinned numeric paths, or systematically lower, with any gap scaling in rollout horizon? (Gate 1 reformulation of the Gate 0 original, which asked for numerics' "share" of variance; that share is 1 by construction once all other sources are pinned, so the estimand was degenerate. Original recorded in batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-06-record.md.)
Alternative formulations:
1. Is serving-stack numerical nondeterminism a zero-mean noise source for agent benchmark scores, or a biased one whose bias grows with rollout horizon?
2. When two otherwise identical greedy rollouts diverge because kernel reduction order depended on what else was in the serving batch, how often does the divergence change the final outcome, and in which direction?
Motivating gap: Anomaly mining. The mechanism (batch-variant attention/matmul reductions) is identified and patched in open-source kernels (Thinking Machines Lab, Sept 2025; vLLM batch invariance as a documented feature); temp-0 run-to-run variance on agentic benchmarks is separately reported as a validity problem (arXiv:2602.07150: pass@1 swings 2.2–6.0 pp, SD >1.5 pp; arXiv:2608.04714: ~39% of variability attributed to the backend). The second-order question — noise (zero-mean, widens intervals) or bias (shifts the point estimate, plausibly down, because failure states in long rollouts are more absorbing than recovery states) — is not posed for agent scores. Stated so it can be refuted: under default kernels a rollout walks across numeric paths step to step, under batch invariance it follows one; if absorbing failure is asymmetric with non-absorbing success, extra chances to touch an outcome-flipping token lower the mean, and the deficit should grow in horizon. A flat or zero gap refutes it.
Presuppositions:
P1. Batch-invariant kernels compute the same function up to a fixed reduction order — CONTESTED in the way that matters: not bit-identical to default, so no arm is a priori unbiased; the reference must be a *set* of pinned paths whose spread bounds path choice. (Adversary #2: 2506.09501 shows path choice alone moves single-turn means, so the reference spread may be the same order as the contrast.)
P2. The harness can be deterministic apart from model numerics — CONTESTED; requires record-and-replay of tool responses plus a leakage check (replicates under one pinned path must collapse to one trajectory). (Adversary #1: vLLM #55131, #58899 report VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 is not batch-invariant for several kernels and greedy output changes across restarts, so the check may fail as the tool stands.)
P3. Long-horizon tasks have asymmetric outcome dynamics (failure more absorbing than success) — CONTESTED, deliberately: an output, entering only as the predicted direction. Not a theorem off the shelf (Markov perturbation theory gives bounds without sign; arXiv:2604.24579 models both success and failure as absorbing).
P4. Harnesses reporting deterministic scores actually decode greedily — must be audited; bears on external validity only.
P5. Run-to-run variance under fixed configuration is reported or recoverable — PARTLY; the numerics-specific decomposition is in no released log, so this limb must be generated.
P6. First-divergence point is identifiable — holds for self-run experiments.
P7. Batch composition is manipulable — ESTABLISHED self-hosted, FALSE for hosted APIs (co-tenant traffic), so the hosted case is extrapolation. Unflagged in the record and raised by adversary #2: arm (a) deliberately randomises composition, which brackets rather than samples deployment.
What would count as an answer: A paired experiment on ≥2 agentic benchmarks (one SWE, one terminal/computer-use, to vary horizon and failure structure) and ≥2 model scales, each task set run K times under (a) default kernels with batch composition randomised across replicates, (b) batch-invariant kernels, (c) ≥2 distinct pinned configurations within (b); tool responses replayed, seeds fixed. Must report: the P2 leakage check (arm (b) replicates collapse); residual variance in (a) and the variance gap (a)−(b), against separately unpinned sampling and environment components; the paired mean difference between (a) and the (b)-path distribution with CIs; the rate and direction of first-divergence→outcome-change propagation; and the mean gap × horizon interaction as a pre-registered trend. Mean difference indistinguishable from zero with an interval tight against typical reported gaps (~1–3 pp) and no horizon trend → "noise". A deficit growing with horizon → "configuration-dependent deficit": batching/kernel configuration becomes part of what a benchmark must specify. A double null (negligible residual variance and no mean shift) is a complete answer and closes the question.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 documented queries in total — 11 at Gate 2 (plus 5 fetches, 1 failed), 9 + 2 GitHub issue searches and 4 fetches by adversary #1, 9 and 4 fetches by adversary #2. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-06-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "bitwise reproducibility reduction order does it bias the ensemble mean climate model" → the same logical form is a named, solved problem in climate/ocean ensemble-consistency testing, never transplanted to LLM evaluation. "floating-point reassociation fast-math nondeterministic GPU reductions changes LLM benchmark accuracy 'systematic' not just variance" (adversary #1) and "numerical precision bf16 fp16 inference changes benchmark score systematically lower long rollout … mean not just variance" (adversary #2) → both independently surfaced arXiv:2506.09501 (NeurIPS 2025 oral), absent from the Gate 2 record. "enabling 'batch-invariant' vLLM benchmark accuracy … deterministic mode" (answer-search) → no published accuracy comparison of batch-invariant vs default serving exists. GitHub: EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness #879, #1645, #3055, #3357 → practitioners have asked the variance limb since 2023. "Monte Carlo arithmetic … CESTAC verificarlo random rounding systematic bias" and the numerical-neuroimaging line (arXiv:2108.03129) → standing machinery for "does randomised rounding move the centre", but never a discrete pass/fail estimand. "non-differential misclassification attenuation … measured pass rate downward" → symmetric outcome-flip noise already predicts a downward-biased measured rate for any pass rate above 50%, with no horizon dependence.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. "Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference", arXiv:2506.09501, NeurIPS 2025 oral (author list not recorded by either adversary and not verified here — do not fill it in from memory) (neurips.cc/virtual/2025/oral/130305) — nearest prior, missed by Gate 2 and found independently by both adversaries. Greedy decoding across 12 numeric configurations (2 GPU types × 2 GPU counts × 3 batch sizes): Std@Acc up to 9.15 pp on AIME'24 under BF16 vs ≈0 under FP32; 96.6% of MATH500 examples diverge under BF16 vs 2.2% under FP32; uses FP32/LayerCast as a pinned high-precision control; reports per-configuration means in tables but analyses stability, divergence and top-1 probability variance, never bias. Single-prompt reasoning/coding only.
B. Bjarnason, Silva & Monperrus, "On Randomness in Agentic Evals", arXiv:2602.07150v1, 6 Feb 2026 (ICLR 2026 workshop; OpenReview UFukKhqCpr) — ~60,000 SWE-Bench-Verified trajectories; single-run pass@1 varies 2.2–6.0 pp; SD >1.5 pp at temperature 0; early token divergence; recommends multiple runs, power analysis, pass@k/pass^k. Verified by both adversaries; characterisation accurate.
C. He / Thinking Machines Lab, "Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference", thinkingmachines.ai, 10 Sept 2025 — opened at first hand by both adversaries, closing the record's own caveat. Batch-variant RMSNorm/matmul/attention reductions as mechanism; 1000 temp-0 samples → 80 unique completions, identical under batch-invariant kernels; consequence drawn for RL sampler/trainer mismatch only; no benchmark accuracy, mean or bias.
(Recorded, not ranked: arXiv:2608.04714 (backend ≈39% of variability, non-agentic); arXiv:2601.07239 (Stochastic CHAOS — same conclusion shape, sampling-breadth mechanism); arXiv:2511.17826 (tensor-parallel-invariant inference); arXiv:2604.24579 (absorbing-Markov agent reliability); arXiv:2605.19537, 2606.08998, 2604.06543.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — A varies numeric configuration *between* runs on single-turn prompts and measures spread; the candidate varies batch composition *within* one serving stack across a multi-step rollout and measures a mean gap plus a horizon trend. A has no tool use, no replayed environment, no horizon estimand, and does not treat its own per-configuration means as bias. On limb (i) the candidate is a replication-and-extension of A into the agentic regime, not an un-asked question; on limb (ii) A is silent. vs B — B sizes agentic variance and shows it survives temperature 0, but runs no kernel arm, performs no numerics/sampling/environment decomposition, and never tests the mean; its remedy (run K times) is the right answer to noise and no answer to a shifted mean. vs C — C establishes mechanism and fix and stops at RL training; the candidate uses C's shipped kernels as an experimental control on a question C does not pose.
Novelty confidence: Medium — but on an incomplete search record. The distinctive limb (ii) survived all 29 queries across eval-harness, RL-mismatch, fault-injection, compiler-reassociation, chaos, tensor-parallel, Monte-Carlo-arithmetic, neuroimaging-pipeline, climate, epidemiological, Chinese and French/German vocabularies, and the answer-search found no published batch-invariant-vs-default accuracy comparison. Not Low: no opened source poses or answers the noise-versus-bias question on agent scores. Not High and not Validated-grade: Gate 2's 11 queries missed the nearest within-field prior (2506.09501), and limb (i) is asked-and-partly-answered there and in three years of lm-eval-harness issues.
Significance — consequence: Under a deficit growing with horizon, every published agentic pass@1 is a point estimate conditional on an unreported variable (batch composition and kernel configuration) with a known error direction, and extra replicates cannot fix it because averaging over a shifted distribution converges to the shifted mean; benchmarks would have to specify batching/kernel configuration as they specify prompts and scaffolds, with the gap scaling into the long-horizon regime evaluation is moving toward. Under "noise", the result retires a live hypothesis and bounds how much of B's 2.2–6.0 pp is chargeable to the serving stack, but largely re-derives advice already in circulation. Adversary caveat: effect size is bounded above by the residual variance under full pinning, which 2506.09501 puts at ~0.1–1 pp on 500-item sets (its 9 pp figure is a 30-problem set).
Significance — audience: (a) Benchmark maintainers and third-party evaluators — would add batching/kernel configuration to the reported configuration surface and, under a deficit, re-qualify headline numbers; B's existence shows this community already acts on variance findings. (b) RL practitioners — a horizon-scaling deficit says the reward signal is biased in the same direction as the eval, bearing on whether batch invariance is worth its throughput cost in the rollout path. (c) Procurement and vendor comparison — a contractual agentic score becomes meaningless without specifying serving configuration. (d) Serving-engine maintainers (vLLM, SGLang) — changes the case for batch invariance as a default rather than opt-in. Independent evidence the audience is live: practitioner posts already advise bucketing runs by system fingerprint and refusing cross-bucket comparison.
Significance — fecundity: Makes askable whether the same channel biases LLM-as-judge scoring; whether quantisation, speculative decoding, prefix-cache hits and tensor-parallel degree form a family of batch-composition-like channels with a shared signature (arXiv:2511.17826 suggests the family is real); whether a numeric-path ensemble is a cheap uncertainty estimator for agent tasks, turning the nuisance into an instrument; whether the absorbing-failure asymmetry, once measured, predicts task fragility independently of numerics; and whether published horizon-scaling laws for agent success are partly measurement artifacts.
Significance — anchoring: (i) agentic-eval validity (prior B, arXiv:2605.23950 on harness disclosure); (ii) RL sampler/trainer mismatch (prior C, arXiv:2511.17826, arXiv:2510.26788); (iii) ML reproducibility, where nondeterminism is a known confound always as variance, never as bias; (iv) ensemble-consistency testing in climate and the CESTAC/Verificarlo tradition, which supply the statistical form of an answer; (v) whether agent failure is compounding-error-driven (arXiv:2609.01660, arXiv:2608.06663).
Reason for silence: As recorded — new-instrument plus disciplinary boundary — the primary mechanism is falsified by adversary #2: 2506.09501 (June 2025) built a pinned numeric arm from FP32/LayerCast under greedy decoding across 12 configurations *before* batch-invariant kernels shipped, and still did not ask whether the mean moves; that paper also already crossed the eval-to-kernel boundary the record says is uncrossed. What survives is conceptual and unargued in the record: bias needs a privileged reference and numerics supplies none, so the field has an estimand for configuration-dependence (handled by bucketing and averaging) but none for bias, while the absorbing-failure asymmetry that makes a sign prediction possible sits in a third literature, making the bridge three-way. Plausible; no evidence found for it. Per Gate 4's own rule, a falsified silence story makes the novelty finding suspect and returns the candidate to Gate 2 — which the missed prior independently requires.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent fresh-context adversaries, 9 Disguise-vocabulary queries each (both executed; Disguise verified). Status below is the worse of the two; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-06-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.
| # | Attack | Objection | Best response | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Triviality | Limb (i) is largely in print: 2506.09501 measures greedy Std@Acc across batch-size/GPU-count configurations and collapses it to ~0 under FP32. The direction in limb (ii) is textbook twice over: non-differential outcome misclassification attenuates any rate above 50% downward, and a pinned path meets exactly as many near-tie tokens as a jittered one, so the "more chances" argument is a counting error with zero expected gap. | The agentic residual after environment replay exists in neither prior; attenuation theory predicts a deficit of unknown size with *no* horizon dependence while the absorbing-state mechanism predicts growth, so the two are distinguishable and the horizon trend is not derivable. A null is an accepted complete answer. But the record cites neither textbook result. | Partial |
| 2 | Disguise | Limb (i) is a renamed/regime-swapped known across eval-harness, RL-mismatch, chaos, fault-injection, TP-reproducibility, Monte-Carlo-arithmetic, neuroimaging, climate and Chinese vocabularies — and inside the candidate's own field is asked and partly answered by 2506.09501, which Gate 2 missed; lm-eval-harness users have asked it since 2023. | No vocabulary surfaced limb (ii): a kernel-attributable mean gap against a pinned-path class with a pre-registered horizon trend on agent rollouts. MCA/CESTAC has no discrete pass/fail estimand, the neuroimaging line is variance-framed, Markov perturbation theory gives bounds without sign, and the answer-search found no batch-invariant-vs-default accuracy comparison. Limb (ii) survives 18 new vocabularies; limb (i) does not and must be restated as replication-and-extension. | Partial |
| 3 | Combinatorial novelty | Kernel numerics × agent evals with an empty interface: the only interface-specific content is P3, and 2604.24579's standard model makes success absorbing too; the asymmetry acts in both arms. | The arms differ in perturbation correlation structure (fixed-per-path vs re-drawn per step), which only matters when the outcome depends jointly on a long decision sequence — i.e. only agentically. Evidence the seam is unoccupied rather than unfashionable: 2506.09501 had every per-configuration mean in its tables and did not read them as bias; C stops at RL; B stops at variance and prescribes more runs. Adversary #2 Resolved, #1 Partial (plausible but unevidenced). | Partial |
| 4 | Presupposition failure | P1 is load-bearing and conceded: "mean over pinned paths" is an experimenter-constructed reference class, and 2506.09501 shows path choice alone moves means, so its spread may be the order of the contrast. The shipped instrument may not deliver the pinned arm (vLLM #55131, #58899). Arm (a) randomises batch composition, which brackets rather than samples deployment. | P1 is handled by design (≥2 pinned configs bounding path choice; a swamped contrast yields an uninformative interval, not a false positive); P2 has an explicit falsification check and 2506.09501's FP32 Std@Acc ≈ 0 is independent evidence collapse is achievable; P3 is an output; P7 flagged. Instrument failure makes a run uninterpretable, not the question ill-posed. The "more chances" premise should be dropped; the deployment-bracketing gap is unflagged. | Partial |
| 5 | Vagueness | Could "bias vs noise" be declared either way, or never? | No. Each limb names an estimand (variance gap; paired mean difference with CI against a pre-specified pinned set; pre-registered horizon trend); the decision rule and the double null are written in advance; the leakage check can fail the experiment outright. Both adversaries' strongest section. | Resolved |
| 6 | Significance inflation | The practical delta is bounded by a residual variance put at ~0.1–1 pp on 500-item sets; a sub-1 pp deficit moves no leaderboard and no procurement decision. | Audience is demonstrably real and already acting without a measurement (three years of harness issues, prior B, a NeurIPS oral, vLLM shipping the feature, fingerprint-bucketing advice), and the horizon claim is precisely that long rollouts amplify a sub-pp per-step effect — but no opened source shows the amplified effect is large. Consistent with Significance 2/3. | Partial |
| 7 | Reason for silence | The new-instrument mechanism is falsified: a pinned counterfactual existed and was used in June 2025 (2506.09501, FP32/LayerCast), pre-dating the kernel fix, and that paper already crossed the claimed disciplinary boundary; the variance limb was asked for years. What is left is close to "no one framed it that way", which the ledger rejects. | The surviving account is conceptual and non-circular — no privileged reference means the field has no estimand for bias, only configuration-dependence it already manages — plus a three-way bridge to the long-horizon-failure literature; and FP32 pinning is impractical at agentic scale, so batch-invariant kernels do make the experiment feasible. Explains why answering was hard more than why nobody asked; unevidenced and unargued in the record. | Partial |
| 8 | Dissolution | With no ground-truth numeric path, "is the default mean biased?" collapses into "scores depend on configuration" — already known and already acted on; what remains is a convention to pick, not a question to answer. | It does not fully dissolve: "the jittered–pinned gap grows with rollout length" is well-defined for *any* reference class and is false if the trend is flat, and exchangeability across arms is a hypothesis, not a theorem (within-path-correlated vs per-step-independent perturbations are different joint distributions). The "bias" wording should be retired for "configuration-dependent deficit", or the objection keeps biting. | Partial |
Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The novelty finding rests on a search that missed the nearest within-field prior — arXiv:2506.09501 (NeurIPS 2025 oral) already quantifies batch-size/GPU-count-induced greedy accuracy spread, collapses it with a pinned high-precision arm, and tabulates per-configuration means — so limb (i) as stated is a benchmark-regime extension of a published question rather than an un-asked one, and the question is carried only by limb (ii). Close second, and the one that threatens limb (ii) itself: under P1 there is no privileged numeric reference, so "bias" risks reducing to the already-acted-on fact that scores depend on configuration, leaving only the horizon trend as substantive content.
Promotion requires: a redone Gate 2 (≥8 queries in the eval-harness, numerical-precision/reassociation, Monte-Carlo-arithmetic and chaos vocabularies) that ranks arXiv:2506.09501 as nearest prior and records the lm-eval-harness issue trail; the canonical question narrowed to limb (ii) alone — a kernel-attributable mean gap against a pinned-path class plus a pre-registered horizon trend — with limb (i) restated as replication-and-extension and the "bias" wording replaced by "configuration-dependent deficit"; the "more chances" mechanism argument repaired or dropped and non-differential-misclassification attenuation cited as the competing null that predicts a deficit without a horizon trend; and a reason for silence that does not rest on the new-instrument claim 2506.09501 falsifies. With those in place and novelty still ≥ Medium on a complete record, Gate 5 would support Validated.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Run the P2 leakage pilot before anything else — K replicates of one benchmark at a single pinned configuration under batch-invariant kernels, checking trajectory-level collapse — because vLLM #55131 and #58899 report the pinned arm is not reliably pinned in the shipped tool, and until it collapses neither limb is measurable.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None — not rejected.
Verification by the run session (the prior both adversaries used to demote novelty was checked directly, not taken on their characterisation): **arXiv:2506.09501 is real and is correctly described as a close within-field neighbour Gate 2 missed** — Yuan, Li, Ding, Xie, Li, Zhao, Wan, Shi, Hu & Liu, "Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference", submitted 2025-06-11 (v2 2025-10-24), read at https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09501. It names evaluation batch size, GPU count and GPU type as sources of differing outputs, traces them to "the non-associative nature of floating-point arithmetic", and reports up to 9% accuracy variation on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B under bfloat16 greedy decoding. So the variance limb is asked and partly answered, and the candidate's "new instrument" reason for silence is false as stated. But three things the adversaries' demotion would imply are **not** in it, which is why the verdict stays Provisional rather than Rejected: it does not isolate batch *composition* in the serving stack, its mitigation is LayerCast (16-bit storage, FP32 compute) rather than batch-invariant kernels, and it neither establishes that the *mean* score moves nor studies long-horizon agentic tasks or any growth of the effect with rollout length. To reconcile this with the Gate 2 summary above, which credits it with tabulating per-configuration means: tabulating a mean per configuration is not the same as establishing a mean *deficit* against a pinned-path reference class, and it is the deficit — limb (ii) — that carries this candidate. Medium novelty with one close neighbour is the Provisional definition, and that is where this lands. Correction to the record: the "NeurIPS 2025 oral" venue attached to this citation in the Gate 2 summary was **not** verifiable from the arXiv listing and should be treated as unconfirmed; the arXiv identifier and content above are what is verified.

ID: UQ-20261016-07
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — radiology reporting quality/QA, clinical informatics; AI — medical-imaging dataset construction, label noise, device validation
Question (canonical): In a paired report–image corpus with intact patient/study series order (e.g. MIMIC-CXR), restricted to carry-forward-eligible assertions (a positive assertion of finding class F in follow-up report R_t where F was also positively asserted in the immediately preceding report R_{t-1}, and F is adjudicable from a single image; pure change-descriptors such as "stable"/"improving"/"resolved" excluded from the numerator and reported separately): (a) what fraction of such assertions does a blinded multi-reader panel (>=3 readers, current image alone, no report, no prior) call absent, after subtracting a reader-noise floor estimated on positively-asserted findings in index exams under identical blinding; (b) is the report-label false-positive rate higher on follow-up than on index exams at equal case-mix for the same finding classes, and is the excess concentrated in high-resolution-rate classes (consolidation, effusion, oedema, pneumothorax, line/tube position) rather than persistent structural classes (cardiomegaly, chronic fibrosis); and (c) how much does measured performance of a standard classifier trained and evaluated on report-derived labels change when follow-up exams are excluded or panel-re-labelled, versus a matched random equal-sized exclusion?
Alternative formulations:
1. Does a radiology report describe its own image, or partly the previous one — and how much of the "ground truth" in report-labelled datasets is inherited rather than observed?
2. When report-derived labels disagree with blinded image re-reads, how much of the disagreement is explained by the exam being a follow-up rather than an index study, and does it skew toward findings that had already resolved?
(Gate 0 intake version and the Gate 1 reformulation rationale are recorded in batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-07-record.md; one reformulation used, no scope change.)
Motivating gap: Every large report-labelled imaging corpus (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, PadChest) and part of device-validation reference standards derive labels by NLP over free-text reports. The unstated load-bearing presupposition is that a report describes the study it is attached to. Radiologists read serial exams with the prior report in hand; clinical-documentation research establishes forward content propagation between notes; the imaging-AI label-noise literature partitions total label error into NLP extraction failure and reader disagreement, so cross-exam inheritance is not a category in the dataset-label error taxonomy (radiology's own QA taxonomy does carry a related but opposite-sign category — see adversary 1, attack 2). The predicted consequence is directional, not symmetric: a resolved-but-restated finding persists as a positive label on a negative image, so error should concentrate in follow-up exams and resolving classes. MIMIC-CXR's ICU weighting maximises exposure.
Presuppositions:
- Current image alone suffices to adjudicate presence — CONTESTED for change-defined findings; FIXED by excluding pure change-descriptors (hybrids such as "decreased effusion" remain unresolved — see attack 5).
- Study-series linkage available — ESTABLISHED for MIMIC-CXR-style corpora (subject_id/study_id, order-preserving date shift); per-corpus check required.
- Blinded re-read is an adequate reference standard — CONTESTED; FIXED only partly by >=3 readers plus an index-exam noise floor. Conspicuity/severity matching is NOT in the design (central objection, attack 4).
- Report-derived labels are used as ground truth in artefacts whose measured performance would change — ESTABLISHED for training corpora and public benchmarks; PARTLY CONTESTED for regulatory validation sets.
- Carry-forward distinguishable from genuine persistence — CONTESTED and central; FIXED by restricting the numerator to blind-absent assertions, but see attack 4 (subthreshold residua).
- Mechanism-agnostic by design: measures inheritance as an outcome (report asserts, image does not support, prior asserted); template reuse, anchoring and clinical-context inference all land in the numerator.
What would count as an answer: Blinded multi-reader adjudication on a stratified index-vs-follow-up sample from a paired report–image corpus, reporting (a) per-class carry-forward rates with inter-reader agreement and CIs, netted against the index noise floor; (b) the index-vs-follow-up difference in report-label false-positive rate, with its direction and class concentration (excess in high-resolution-rate classes = predicted signature; symmetric or null pattern = falsifier); (c) the classifier-performance delta under follow-up exclusion/re-adjudication, differenced against a random-exclusion control. A rate indistinguishable from the noise floor, or excess with no class structure, answers it negatively and closes it.

Significance — consequence: If YES and the net rate is material, a correctable defect with a known sign is identified in the reference standard of the field's most-used imaging corpora: published sensitivity/specificity on these benchmarks partly measures inheritance-reproduction rather than image reading; models are trained toward what a radiologist would write given the prior rather than what is on the film; and the bias is exam-position-dependent rather than symmetric, so the standard "label noise attenuates but does not bias" defence fails. Remedies are cheap: series-position flags, index-only splits, re-adjudication. If NO (rate within the noise floor, or excess with no class structure), that closes a live worry, licenses indiscriminate mining of serial exams, and redirects label-quality effort to the non-mention/false-negative channel (arXiv:2608.10084).
