ID: UQ-20261016-26
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — airborne environmental DNA / molecular biodiversity monitoring; neighbouring: palynology (pollen source area), atmospheric source–receptor modelling, screening-test epidemiology

Question (canonical): For a standardized airborne-eDNA sampling protocol, what is the locality specificity of a detection — the probability that a detected vertebrate taxon was actually present inside the pre-specified survey unit during the sampling window — and how does detection probability for an independently verified point source decay with distance from it?
(Gate 1 reformulation retained in the record: for a named protocol in a named landscape class, (i) the fitted P(detect | taxon at distance d, meteorology m) with half-distance and CI per taxon group, and (ii) conditional on that function and an enumerated off-unit source inventory, the proportion of a survey's taxon list attributable to off-unit sources, with CI.)

Alternative formulations:
- When an air sample yields a species' DNA, how far away could that animal have been?
- What is the spatial support of a single airborne-eDNA sample, as a calibrated detection-probability-versus-distance curve against verified animal locations, plus the share of the taxon list from off-unit sources?

Motivating gap: Airborne-eDNA metabarcoding recovers taxa absent from the sampled enclosure (Clare et al. 2022; Lynggaard et al. 2022), reportedly treated as "unexpected" or possible transport/contamination without quantifying rate or source distance, while eDNA is being standardized for regulatory biodiversity work (CEN/TC 230/WG 28; EN 17805:2023). Gate 2 finding, as corrected on the judge's post-Gate-5 verification (2026-10-16; independent fresh-context checker, 10 queries, 2 refused, log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-26-verification.md): the gap is refuted on its own decisive test, because Clare et al. 2022 — the motivating paper the gap says left distance unquantified — did run read count against distance from the enclosure as a named model (LR = 2.51, df = 1, p = 0.113) over 0-276 m with the 27 in-enclosure points excluded, confirmed to the decimal. The record's wider claim that BOTH limbs are addressed is struck: the distance limb is answered in a literature with numbers, while the off-unit-share limb is posed and NOT answered (see Novelty - how this differs and Routing).

Presuppositions: (1) per-taxon detection probability estimable — partly established for a single qPCR target (Kroos et al. 2026: three distance levels, coefficients only, no fitted curve), contested for metabarcoded assemblages; (2) survey-unit boundary pre-specifiable with in-unit presence verified — established at zoos/captive parks, contested in open landscape (Kroos could not exclude free-living wallabies at 1 km); (3) off-unit sources enumerable — CONTESTED and binding; published work substitutes a modelled wind catchment for an inventory; (4) detections not dominated by distance-independent lab/field contamination — contested (Westerduin et al. 2023, origin inconclusive); (5) decay modellable as a function of distance and meteorology — split by readout: significant negative distance effect for targeted qPCR (Kroos), no read-count/distance relationship for metabarcoding (Clare, LR = 2.51, p = 0.113); (6) regulatory use of airborne eDNA for presence/absence — contested, current regulated use is aquatic, no air-specific standard verified in draft; (7) a protocol-stable "sample" exists — contested, falsified by sampler dependence (active 64.4% vs passive 11.1% at 10 m).

What would count as an answer: a calibration experiment with independently verified source locations and samplers at pre-specified distances, yielding (i) a detection-probability-versus-distance curve per taxon group with half-distance and CI and (ii) the off-unit share of a taxon list with CI; a flat curve would be a decisive negative. Against this criterion, as corrected on verification: design (i) is executed only in part. Kroos et al. 2026 used a captive source and samplers at three distance classes (10/100/1000 m, plus an in-enclosure proof-of-concept arm that is not a distance class with a reported detection rate) over 108 analysed samples (88 distance + 20 proof-of-concept; 110 is the planned total), and fitted binomial GLMs and a Bayesian logistic model with distance as a predictor, reporting coefficients and observed frequencies. It does NOT fit a detection-probability-versus-distance function, so no curve, half-distance or per-taxon-group kernel is in hand; what is in hand is a signed three-level effect. Limb (ii) is NOT answered at all: Clare et al. 2022 label residency (17/25 detected mammal and bird species resident; the 32% non-resident figure is this ledger's own arithmetic, 8/25, not Clare et al.'s wording, and they hedge several of the eight as possible zoo stock or food), Stewart et al. 2026 report model-catchment agreement, and the UK national survey attributes exotics to contamination - none partitions a taxon list by whether a taxon's source lay inside or outside a defined survey unit. What is missing is therefore the whole of limb (ii) plus the curve, not only a half-distance transform.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 web searches + 5 fetches; full list in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-26-record.md. Most informative: "airborne environmental DNA detection probability declines with distance from source animal" (own-field mandatory query) → Kroos et al. distance-decay study as top hit, on-point; "air eDNA spatial scale of detection vertebrate zoo distance samplers" → Stewart et al. 2026 wind-catchment paper plus Clare et al. 2022; "Lynggaard Clare airborne eDNA zoo percentage of detected species resident versus non-resident" ("what fraction" limb) → Clare et al. full text containing the resident/non-resident counts; "proportion of air eDNA detections species absent from sampled site false positive" → Westerduin et al. 2023 posing the non-local-detection problem explicitly; palynology (RSAP/Sugita) and bioaerosol source–receptor queries → both modelling traditions mature in the neighbouring fields; "CEN TC 230 ... air samples" → WG 28 and EN 17805:2023 real, no air-specific eDNA standard found.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Kroos et al. (2026) "Targeted Airborne eDNA of an Invasive Wallaby: Effects of Sampler Type, Distance, and Environmental Conditions," Environmental DNA 8(1):e70240, DOI 10.1002/edn3.70240 (preprint full text: biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.26.684691) — 108 analysed samples (88 distance + 20 in-enclosure proof-of-concept; 110 is the planned total) at distance classes 10/100/1000 m, in a park reported to hold 27 Notamacropus rufogriseus with no verification method stated; detection 53.3%/23.3%/14.3%; GLM distance effect −1.0715 (p = 0.00226), Bayesian active-sampler estimate −0.91 (95% CI −1.73 to −0.10). Figures confirmed verbatim on verification; the sample count, the in-enclosure arm and the word "verified" are corrected here, and the paper fits no distance-decay function.
2. Stewart et al. (2026) "Local Transport of Vertebrate Airborne eDNA Is Captured by Wind-Directed Catchment Area Models," Environmental DNA, DOI 10.1002/edn3.70329 — Rotterdam Zoo, passive samplers, 24 resident species, Circular Sector and Footprint models; 100% of detections within 100 m inside predicted catchments, 62% to 655 m.
3. Clare et al. (2022) "Measuring biodiversity from DNA in the air," Current Biology 32(3) — 25 mammal/bird species, 17 resident; negative-binomial read-count models against distance over 0–276 m found no relationship once in-enclosure samples were excluded (LR = 2.51, p = 0.113); authors state read counts should not be used to locate a DNA source.

Novelty — how this differs from each: (1) this is limb (i) executed; differences are cosmetic — one target taxon, three distance strata, a logit-scale coefficient rather than a named half-distance (a one-line transform). (2) this is limb (ii) in its strongest available form, with "outside the modelled wind catchment" substituted for "outside a pre-specified unit with an enumerated inventory"; the 38% outside-catchment figure at 655 m is not the candidate's estimand and carries no CI — real but narrow residue. (3) the candidate asserts Clare et al. left distance unquantified; it did not, and the candidate's stated decisive negative (a flat curve) is already on record for the read-depth readout. The live question is the readout discrepancy, which is not the question asked.

Novelty confidence: Low

Significance — consequence: steep decay with a long right tail means regulatory use must attach a distance-conditional probability rather than a presence assertion; the readout split (targeted detection decays, read depth does not) already says read abundance cannot localise. The marginal consequence of the candidate is right-tail quantification, not the existence of decay.
Significance — audience: real — CEN/TC 230/WG 28, ISO/TC 147 counterparts, agencies running eDNA protected-species determinations, biosecurity programmes (Kroos is an agency wallaby-surveillance use case), zoo and port operators. The audience is already acting on this literature, which argues against novelty rather than for the un-asked framing.
Significance — fecundity: separability of the kernel into sampler aerodynamics × transport × shedding; quantitative transfer of palynology's Relevant Source Area of Pollen (now an obvious next paper, Stewart et al. having already imported wind-footprint modelling); whether the Clare/Kroos readout discrepancy reflects index-hopping and template competition. The third is live and downstream of the candidate.
Significance — anchoring: eDNA false-positive and confidence-in-absence work (CIADM, bioRxiv 2024.05.12.593768); aquatic transport distance (Deiner & Altermatt, PMC3921251); palynological source-area theory; bioaerosol source–receptor modelling. Strong anchoring is why the field got there first.

Reason for silence: offered mechanism was a disciplinary boundary plus new-instrument lag. Falsified by the record: the boundary was crossed in both directions within four years (Stewart imported gridded-meteorology footprints; Kroos ran the captive-source design) and Clare ran a distance analysis in the field's founding paper. The field decomposed the composite into two limbs and answered them separately.

7. Reason for silence | not executed; Gate 2 record already falsifies the offered mechanism | — | Not run
8. Dissolution | not executed | — | Not run

Strongest remaining objection: the distance limb is asked and answered in the candidate's own literature, and the candidate's motivating gap is refuted on its own decisive test. Clare et al. 2022 ran the distance analysis the gap says it omitted (LR = 2.51, df = 1, p = 0.113, 0-276 m, 27 in-enclosure points dropped), and three further primary sources answer the same limb at widening scope: Kroos et al. 2026 to 1000 m with a signed coefficient, Stewart et al. 2026 to 655 m with a modelled catchment and a "likely originate less than 200 m downwind" conclusion, and the UK national airborne-eDNA survey (Sci Rep s41598-025-03650-z) with an estimated 18.6 km median and a 400 m to 75.6 km range. Verification narrowed the ground and the rejection is re-grounded accordingly: NOT "both limbs are executed" (the off-unit-share limb is posed and unanswered, and is routed below), but the distance limb asked-and-answered plus the off-unit-share limb asked-and-still-open - either way the composite question is not un-asked, and the residue on the answered limb (a half-distance transform, cross-sampler per-taxon-group curves) is an increment on a live publishing programme. Well-posedness 2/3 independently bars Validated: the intake limb (i) asks for a protocol-intrinsic "locality specificity" that is in fact a positive predictive value depending on off-unit source base rate, and presupposition 3 is unsatisfiable outside captive settings.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable to a rejected entry; a future run wanting the residue should re-pose it as the Clare-vs-Kroos readout discrepancy (read depth flat in distance, targeted detection not), which is the more promising formulation.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTED, one limb only, on the verification finding that reversed this field. The off-unit-share limb — what share of a detected taxon list originated outside the survey unit — is posed in print and unanswered: Stewart et al. 2026 make source provenance the paper's object and stop at modelled-catchment agreement; the UK national survey (Sci Rep s41598-025-03650-z) warns that "the true source origin(s) of these species' DNA could be missed" and that its estimated distances "should be interpreted with caution", and that "a dedicated experimental design will be necessary to further rigorously test eDNA transport distances"; Lynggaard et al. 2026 (Commun Biol s42003-026-09950-y) call for "investigations into the state, transportation, and persistence of vertebrate airborne eDNA". None of them partitions a taxon list by source location. Row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md, narrowed to the share and naming the distance analyses not to redo. The distance limb is answered and is not routed.

ID: UQ-20261016-27
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — vaccinology; vaccine-effectiveness methodology; regulatory lot/batch release (OCABR/OMCL, FDA CBER); pharmaceutical quality (CMC) as neighbouring field
Question (canonical): Among recipients of a single vaccine product in a registry recording manufacturing lot number and linked to outcome ascertainment, fitting outcome (infection, or severe outcome) on lot-level random intercepts nested within shipment block and conditioning on vaccination date, time since dose, dose number, geography and recipient characteristics: is the between-lot SD of the lot random effect distinguishable from zero, and what one-sided upper bound do the data place on it? (Gate 1 version B; the as-intaken version A and the reformulation record are in the record file.)
Alternative formulations:
- Lay: Do different manufactured batches of the same vaccine protect people to measurably different degrees? (The record itself concedes this form is asked, not un-asked.)
- Technical: Treating manufacturing lot as a random effect in a test-negative or cohort VE analysis, what is the between-lot SD of log VE and its upper confidence limit? (Mislabelled — see Strongest remaining objection.)
- Regulatory: Does national lot release, which certifies identity, potency and sterility against in-vitro specifications, bound between-lot variation in field effectiveness, and by how much?
Motivating gap: Every published VE estimate pools lots, i.e. assumes lots exchangeable with respect to effectiveness; no release criterion is an effectiveness measure; the one paper asking whether official batch control earns its keep (Kretzschmar et al. 2018, Vaccine) answers from in-vitro specification failures with no clinical outcome data. Lot-linked individual records did not exist before the COVID-19 registries. The record's framing claim — that lot-linked registry analyses "are all on the safety-reporting side" — is imprecise rather than false: one of them (prior 1) uses a national-registry hard endpoint rather than spontaneous reports, but its endpoint is all-cause mortality, which is the safety side. On the protection axis the claim holds (see Novelty confidence).
Presuppositions: (1) individual-level lot capture linked to outcomes — CONTESTED, unaudited by the record, upgraded to demonstrated-in-principle by adversary 2 (Czech record-level batch-per-dose data; 244 Comirnaty batches in PEI's app sample); (2) lots spread across enough geography/time to separate lot from era and place — CONTESTED and the live identification hinge: neither record nor adversary found a source showing multiple lots in use at one site in one week; (3) the variance component is estimable with usable precision — CONTESTED, may yield only an upper bound; (4) in-vitro potency release is not already a sufficient surrogate for protection — CONTESTED, survived testing; (5) post-release cold-chain handling recorded or exchangeable across lots — CONTESTED, a candidate mechanism that shifts the referent to distribution; (6) the estimand is a dispersion, not an allegation about particular lots — established by construction; (7) outcome ascertainment does not itself vary with lot — CONTESTED.
What would count as an answer: a hierarchical fit in at least one lot-linked registry reporting the between-lot SD with an interval, plus a pre-registered falsification check (permuting lot labels within shipment block and calendar window must reproduce the null distribution). Both directions informative: a tight null supplies the first direct evidence for the exchangeability assumption every pooled VE estimate makes; a positive finding obliges lot release to add an effectiveness-correlated criterion. An upper bound wider than the VE estimate itself is a negative result about registry data, to be reported as such.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 58 total across three adversaries, the Gate 2 record and the verification pass (29 at batch time, 15 verification queries with 0 refusals, 14 searches and 6 fetches by the third adversary) — 11 Gate 2 searches plus 5 fetches (full list: batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-27-record.md), 9 new-vocabulary searches plus 4 fetches by adversary 1 (UQ-20261016-27-adversary-1.md), 9 new-vocabulary searches plus 5 fetch attempts by adversary 2 (UQ-20261016-27-adversary-2.md). Most informative: (a) Gate 2 `vaccine effectiveness by manufacturing batch lot BNT162b2 registry heterogeneity between batches` → only the safety-side batch literature plus Pfizer's multi-lot immunogenicity SAP; (b) Gate 2 `official control authority batch release OMCL potency assay not predictive of clinical protection` → Kretzschmar 2018, the value-of-batch-release question, never answered with outcome data; (c) adversary 1 `fractional dose vaccine non-inferior immunogenicity dose-response plateau` → PMC9595080, the intended Triviality kill, which inverted (dose-response "non-linear", fractional-dose predictions unvalidated); (d) adversary 1 French/trial-registry sweep → PMC10796506, seven commercial-scale lots, post-approval phase IV, falsifying the record's "3-4 lots, pre-licensure" characterisation of the lot-consistency paradigm; (e) adversary 2 `"clinically relevant specifications" OR "patient-centric specifications" batch-to-batch variability linked to clinical outcome biologic` → the QbD/ICH Q6B framework exists, the estimate does not; (f) adversary 2 `Czech record-level vaccination data vaccine batch lot number COVID-19 infection outcomes analysis by batch` → the decisive hit, below. Disguise was executed by both adversaries (9 new queries each, 13 untried vocabularies: German, Spanish, French, QbD/ICH Q6B, BCG/TB, generic-drug pharmacoepidemiology, IVIG, antivenom, levothyroxine, cold-chain, potency-recall natural experiment, econometric IV, national open data), so Disguise is verified, not unverified.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Schmeling M, Fürst T, Manniche V, Hansen PR, Gilthorpe MS. "A Batch-Dependent Safety Signal Related to All-Cause Mortality Associated with COVID-19 Vaccination." preprints.org 202603.0908.v3, DOI 10.20944/preprints202603.0908, posted 27 Apr 2026 — Czech nationwide record-level data, Dec 2020–Sep 2022, batch recorded per dose for four products; batches "clustered according to their three-month age- and sex-adjusted ACM rates"; opened by adversary 2 (via the rendered page, not the PDF; not peer-reviewed). Companion trace at title level only: PMID 38937903, "Batch-dependent safety of COVID-19 vaccines in the Czech Republic and comparison with data from Denmark" (PubMed blocked, not opened).
2. PMC10796506 — "Immunogenicity, safety and consistency of seven lots of an inactivated COVID-19 vaccine", phase IV; seven commercial-scale lots from three workshops, post-approval; neutralising-antibody GMT at day 28, lots as fixed effects, equivalence criterion 95% CI of the GMT ratio within 0.67–1.5; per-lot GMTs 118.78–134.97; no variance component reported. Opened by adversary 1.
3. Manniche D, Schmeling M, Gilthorpe MS, Hansen PR. Medicina 2024;60(8):1343 — batch-level suspected-AE rates per 1,000 doses, Denmark and Sweden; cross-country correlation across 12 shared batches 0.682 mild, 0.685 severe, 0.078 deaths; explicitly hypothesis-generating, passive surveillance. (Also load-bearing: Kretzschmar et al. 2018, Vaccine 36(17):2364-2370, PMID 29580639 — ~5,850 batches, 13 withdrawn, no clinical outcome data, not spot-checked by either adversary; PEI statement 18 Aug 2023, 1,179,877 vaccinations / 401 batches, safety axis only; MMWR 1984;33(24):349, the historical allegation form.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: 1 — same unit of analysis, same registry substrate, now the same class of endpoint (a clinically ascertained national-registry outcome rather than voluntary reports); what remains distinct is only the infection/effectiveness endpoint, the variance-component estimand rather than cluster analysis of batch-level rates, the within-shipment-block identification and the permutation null. That is an outcome swap plus an estimand swap on a question already posed and worked on the same data. 2 — equivalence of means on an immune surrogate, lots as fixed effects, no dispersion parameter; but its existence (seven commercial post-approval lots) removes the record's claim that lot-consistency testing is confined to 3-4 pre-licensure lots. 3 — reporting-rate outcome, differential reporting the dominant confounder; the record's sharpest stated distinction from this prior no longer separates the candidate, because the same group has since moved to a hard registry endpoint.
Novelty confidence: Medium, restored from the record's Low on the judge's post-Gate-5 verification (2026-10-16; independent fresh-context checker, 15 queries, 0 refusals, log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-27-verification.md) — Medium with a close neighbour, not High.
The Low grade was awarded by the record's own tripwire ("it would fall to Low if an adversary finds any registry analysis with lot as a covariate on a clinical outcome"), read as tripped by prior 1, which adversary 2 located and opened. Verification confirms prior 1 exists and is cited accurately, and refutes the inference drawn from it on three independent grounds. (i) Axis mismatch, decisive: its endpoint is three-month all-cause mortality, titled by its own authors "A Batch-Dependent Safety Signal" and cross-validated against adverse-reaction rates, with no infection endpoint, no comparator and no VE estimate anywhere in it — a safety-axis analysis is not prior art for a protection-axis question. (ii) No variance component: per-batch rates plus cluster analysis, no random effect, no ICC, no variance decomposition, so the candidate's estimand is absent from it on any endpoint. (iii) Not peer-reviewed — the page says so explicitly — and carrying real defects (an impossible date, R² = 1 on a one-batch cluster, post-hoc exclusion of a high-rate batch, undisclosed outlier counts). The tripwire as the record worded it was too broad; applied to the protection axis it is not tripped, and prior 1 is a close neighbour on the same registry substrate by the same author group. The nearest protection-axis items remain prior 2 (equivalence of means on an immune surrogate, lots as fixed effects, no dispersion parameter) and the 1984 MMWR allegation. One record claim is corrected rather than falsified ("the lot-linked analyses run on those registries are all on the safety-reporting side": prior 1 is registry-based rather than spontaneous-report-based, but is on the safety side), and the differential-reporting distinction still separates the candidate from prior 3 while no longer distinguishing it from the group's work as a whole. Record-integrity demerit, found independently by both adversaries on the same primary page: the MMWR 1984 sentence quoted twice in the record as "detailed lot information was not available from the providers" actually reads "Although detailed vaccine information was not available from providers of vaccine" — lot substituted for vaccine inside quotation marks, and the following clause, in which MMWR uses provider diversity as an argument against a cohort effect, dropped. Substance of the reason-for-silence strand survives; the verbatim claim does not.
Significance — consequence: if the SD is distinguishable from zero, lot release acquires a criterion it lacks and VE estimates an omitted variance component; if a tight null, the exchangeability assumption behind pooled VE gains its first direct support and the hot-lot hypothesis is retired on the protection axis by design. Adversary 2 sized and restricted one claim: lot effects average out in pooled estimates, SE inflation being tau/sqrt(L), negligible at L = 244 (0.064·tau) and material only in small-L settings, so the "published intervals are too narrow" consequence holds only for single-site or early-rollout cohorts.
Significance — audience: real and better evidenced than the record claimed — OMCLs and the EDQM OCABR network plus FDA CBER lot release; national programme epidemiologists holding the lot-linked data; VE methodology networks; manufacturers' CMC teams; pharmacovigilance bodies answering batch claims in prose. Adversary evidence: Kretzschmar 2018 is PEI's own staff, and batch questions reached the German federal legislature (Bundestag Drucksachen 20/7534, 20/7813). Overstated branch: that a null settles the public dispute — PEI published a batch-level safety null in Aug 2023 and German batch commentary continued into 2024 and 2026.
Significance — fecundity: which release-assay values predict a lot's deviation (the study that would make release assays genuine surrogates); how much cold-chain excursion explains, separating manufacture from distribution; whether dispersion differs by platform; scale-up era versus steady state; whether safety-axis and effectiveness-axis lot deviations correlate, which has opposite predicted signs under a potency versus an immune-response mechanism.
Significance — anchoring: unexplained between-study VE heterogeneity with no manufacturing term; primary-versus-secondary vaccine failure; the live hot-lot dispute; correlate-of-protection and immunobridging validity; and whether biologics process controls are validated against clinical outcomes at all.
Reason for silence: strand 3 (pre-emption by the lot-consistency paradigm) is the one both adversaries accepted and adversary 1 strengthened with PMC10796506 — practitioners believe a named design already settles "do lots differ?". Strand 2 (CMC and field epidemiology share no journals, reviewers or data) holds. Strand 1 (new data) covers only pre-2021: the registries have existed for five years and a group was mining them, which is what killed the novelty claim. Strand 4 (incentive/taboo) is inference, partly corroborated by adversary 2: every batch-level clinical-outcome analysis located comes from one advocacy-adjacent group while institutional responses are statements and parliamentary answers.

A3 1. Triviality | Partial — and this is now the entry's strongest objection. The potency channel is bounded in a page by the fractional-dose literature: a five-fold dose cut in yellow fever vaccine moved day-28 seroconversion by -0.90% to +1.82% across four manufacturers, in batches deliberately chosen near minimum release potency that still assayed at "6-43 times the minimum specification established by WHO", all CIs excluding the -10% margin. A3's own arithmetic, labelled as such, puts the proposed design's best achievable one-sided limit at tau ~ 0.03 on the log(1-VE) scale (K = 400 lots, 2,500 per lot, 5% incidence), about 0.3 VE points at VE 90%. Not fatal because no public distribution of commercial lot-release potency results exists to complete the bound (its search 14 found none), because the mRNA dose slope is not sign-determined once the Qatar 10 ug / 30 ug confidence limits are carried through (roughly -0.16 to +0.28 per log-dose unit on log(1-VE), A3's arithmetic from the published CIs, and confounded with age by construction), and because the non-potency channels (%intact RNA, LNP attributes, excursions) have no published outcome mapping at all.
A3 2. Disguise | Partial. Eleven new-vocabulary searches across pharmaceutical quality, operations management, transfusion medicine and device vigilance. The nearest prior A3 opened is Bercu et al., "Establishing Patient Centric Specifications for Drug Substance and Drug Product Impurities", J Pharm Innov 2019;14:76-89, which poses the candidate's PARENT question in the quality field's own words — clinically relevant specifications "take into consideration the clinical impact of variations in the critical quality attributes", and "The 'process experience based' approach does not answer the question whether the predicted variability will impact product safety/efficacy" — and A3 checked directly that it neither discusses between-batch variability in clinical response nor proposes linking post-marketing outcomes to batch; it builds limits from toxicology, in-silico work and the TTC. Park et al., Production and Operations Management (DOI 10.1177/10591478251319691), links manufacturing LOCATION to serious adverse-event reports, not lot to effectiveness, and states no variance decomposition on the page A3 opened. Fourteen searches across nine vocabularies returned no analysis of any kind with lot as a term on a clinical effectiveness outcome.
A3 3. Combinatorial novelty | Resolved. The interface problem is identification rather than computation — lots are allocated in shipments to places at times, so the grouping variable is nearly nested inside the nuisance structure and conditioning hard enough to defeat era-and-place confounding may remove the variation being measured — and a second interface problem belongs to neither parent field: a variance component on protection is interpretable as a manufacturing quantity only through a release-assay bridge that, as Bercu shows, the quality field currently builds from toxicology rather than from outcomes.
A3 4. Presupposition failure | Partial, and it derived the scale defect independently for the third time: with log risk = alpha + u_j + X·beta among recipients of lot j against a common unvaccinated alpha_0 + X·beta, SD(u_j) = SD(log RR_j) = SD(log(1-VE_j)), so at VE 90% a tau of 0.1 means VE 89.0-90.9%, not the 81.4-99.5% the record's reading implies. It adds a second defect nobody had stated: identification from the vaccinated stratum alone holds only on the log-relative-risk scale, so the unvaccinated reference does NOT fully cancel for a percentage-point statement — converting to VE points needs the baseline risk.
A3 5. Vagueness | Partial. The sharpest new point: the permutation null does not do what the record claims. Permuting lot labels within shipment block and calendar window destroys the labelling but preserves nothing about which clinic, session or vaccinator received which vial, so it tests "lot labels carry information beyond block", not "that information is manufacturing" — and at national scale, with the design resolving to ~0.03 log units, anything travelling with a lot inside a block loads onto tau.
A3 6. Significance inflation | Partial, and sourced, which is why Gate 3 is marked down below. The named primary action is unavailable: OMCLs and CBER cannot add an effectiveness-correlated release criterion because no such assay exists, and Bercu shows the quality field's live method for clinically relevant limits runs through toxicology and in-vitro work rather than field outcomes. The VE-interval correction is numerically negligible at resolvable magnitudes: at tau = 0.03 the added variance of 0.0009 sits against a pooled log-RR variance of 0.0025-0.01, moving the SE by a few per cent (A3's arithmetic). What survives: the data holders are finite and named (SSI, FoHM, UKHSA, Israeli HMOs), the ECDC VE protocols they work from are standing documents a stratum could enter, the parent regulatory agenda is demonstrably live (ICH Q6(R1) under revision, an ECA ATMP position paper, an EMA industry session), and the null branch would supply the first direct empirical support on a clinical endpoint for an exchangeability assumption every pooled VE estimate makes.
A3 7. Reason for silence | Resolved, and better evidenced than the record: individual-level lot-to-outcome linkage is a COVID-era artefact (the same capability is still only an aspiration in device registries), and the boundary mechanism sharpens — the field that owns the parent question answers it with toxicology, in-silico work and the TTC and does not propose batch-to-outcome linkage at all, which is a stronger mechanism than "the two fields do not talk".
A3 8. Dissolution | Partial. Once lot is nested in shipment block what remains is the dispersion of lot-labelled deviations conditional on block — manufacture, distribution, handling and session clustering in unknown proportions — and the manufacturing component people mean cannot be isolated: if lots rarely cross blocks the contrast is near-degenerate, and without block nesting the estimate is confounded with era and place. Held Partial because a composite is still the variance pooled VE sets to zero, and because the decomposition is tractable by fitting clinic and session effects and excursion records alongside the lot term.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness marked down from the record's 3/3: the canonical estimand as written is not the parameter the stated model yields (attack 4, derived independently by all three adversaries), and the record's own informativeness threshold is therefore stated in mismatched units. The defect is repairable, so the question is not ill-posed; it does not meet 3/3. Significance marked down from 3/3 to 2/3 on A3's sourced deflation: the headline action is unavailable because no effectiveness assay exists for a release criterion to use, and the VE-interval correction is a few per cent of the SE at magnitudes the design can resolve. What holds 2/3 up is the null branch — the first direct test on a clinical endpoint of the exchangeability assumption behind every pooled VE estimate — plus named data holders and a live parent agenda in regulatory quality.
Strongest remaining objection: the dose-response prior bounds the potency channel in a page, and the design cannot resolve anything consequential. A five-fold cut in yellow fever vaccine dose moved day-28 seroconversion by -0.90% to +1.82% across four independent manufacturers, in batches chosen near minimum release potency that still assayed at 6-43 times the WHO minimum; against that plateau, between-lot potency variation has little room to move a clinical endpoint, while the best achievable one-sided limit at national scale is about tau = 0.03 on the log(1-VE) scale, roughly 0.3 VE points at VE 90% (A3's arithmetic, labelled as its own). The candidate's value therefore lies almost entirely in the null branch, as confirmation of an already strong mechanistic prior rather than as a discovery, and it should be recorded only with a pre-registered consequence threshold. It is not fatal because no public distribution of commercial lot-release potency results exists to complete the bound, because the mRNA dose slope is not sign-determined once the published confidence limits are carried through, and because the non-potency channels have no outcome mapping at all. Two older objections stand behind it: presupposition 2, the identification hinge, remains asserted and unsourced — no source found by the record or by any of three adversaries shows two or more lots of one product concurrently in use at one site in one week, and if lot is effectively nested in site-week the design returns a wide bound rather than a lot effect; and the canonical estimand is written on the wrong scale, log(1-VE) = log(RR) being the canonical one (VE is bounded at 1, so log(VE) has a vanishing derivative and a near-degenerate variance exactly where vaccines operate) with the discrepancy factor exactly VE/(1-VE) — 9.0 at VE 90%, 19.0 at VE 95%, verified to four decimals by the checker and derived independently by all three adversaries.
Provisional at: Gate 5. Three independent fresh-context adversaries, 24 attacks, not one Unresolved, so the fatal rule never fires; the batch's Gate 2 rejection is withdrawn as a novelty regrade that did not survive verification. Well-posedness 2/3 bars Validated independently, as does Medium novelty with a close neighbour.
What would promote it, merging A3's required amendments: (i) restate the estimand as the SD of the lot random intercept on log risk, equal to SD(log(1-VE)), give the back-transformation to VE points at a named pooled VE, and drop the claim that the unvaccinated reference cancels for a percentage-point statement — it cancels only on the log-relative-risk scale; (ii) rename the estimand in the question as the dispersion of lot-labelled deviations CONDITIONAL ON shipment block, which is a manufacture-plus-distribution-plus-session composite, and add a decomposition arm (clinic and session random effects, cold-chain excursion records) so a positive tau is not reported as manufacturing variance; (iii) report a feasibility gate before any estimate — lots per shipment block, the proportion of lot pairs actually contrasted within block, events per lot — so a degenerate within-block design is visible as such, which is also how presupposition 2 gets sourced; (iv) pre-register a consequence threshold, such as the tau corresponding to one VE point, because at national scale the design resolves far below any consequential value and "distinguishable from zero" would otherwise be graded against zero; (v) record the dose-response prior explicitly as the background against which a null is informative, so the null is reported as confirmation of a strong mechanistic prior rather than as a surprise. With (i) and (iii) done, well-posedness reaches 3/3; (iv) and (v) are what would make the result worth the registry access.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED — the entry is Provisional, not rejected as already-asked, and ledger/routed-open-problems.md is by its own header a file of rejected candidates. Recorded here instead, because verification established it precisely: the protection-axis question is posed in print exactly once, in MMWR 1984;33(24):349, in a measles outbreak among vaccinated high-school students — "This finding suggested a cohort effect, such as a faulty vaccine lot or particular provider, but none was found", with the reason it could not be pursued given as "Although detailed vaccine information was not available from providers of vaccine" — so it was raised, could not be checked for want of lot-level exposure data, and was closed by inability rather than by evidence, 42 years ago. It is posed in none of the other cited sources: Bundestag 20/7534 asks about Qualitätsunterschiede, not potency or protection, and touches neither Wirksamkeit, Schutzwirkung, Immunogenität nor Impfdurchbrüche; 20/7813 answers on Verdachtsfälle only; the PEI statement of 18 Aug 2023 and its 2024 follow-up are adverse-event reports only. If this entry is ever regraded to Rejected-as-asked, that MMWR instance is the row to route.

ID: UQ-20261016-28
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — laboratory medicine, clinical epidemiology; method source field: climatology (station-record homogenization). Source method: cross-field transplant.
Question (canonical): For a pre-specified frame of multi-site laboratory records (>=K sites, >=15 years, analytes restricted in advance to those with documented commutability across the method generations present) and a pre-registered list of published secular-trend claims resting on them: (a) what breakpoints and offsets does a pairwise-reference procedure transplanted from climate-station homogenization (contemporaneous co-catchment sites as reference series; SNHT / pairwise comparison / ACMANT-style detection on differenced series) detect per site-analyte; (b) against independently retrieved analyzer/method/calibrator change logs, what are the sensitivity and specificity of detection and the agreement of estimated with documented offsets; and (c) on the homogenized record, what fraction of each published trend's magnitude is attributable to breakpoint offsets, and how many trends retain sign and significance? [R1, the one Gate 1 reformulation, adopted. V0 as intaken, and the three under-specifications R1 fixed, are in the record.]
Alternative formulations:
1. (lay) How much of the long-term change we think we see in patients' blood test results is actually the laboratory's equipment changing?
2. (technical) Can a homogenized version of a multi-site decades-long laboratory record be constructed, and does it change the sign or magnitude of reported secular trends in haemoglobin, creatinine/eGFR, albumin or total cholesterol?
3. (the narrow residue surviving Gate 2) Do contemporaneous co-catchment laboratories function as valid reference series for each other in the climatological sense — does the differenced series between two sites' same-analyte distributions isolate instrument change from population change well enough that blind detection beats chance against independently retrieved logs?
Motivating gap: Climatology treats an un-homogenized station trend as uninterpretable and repairs it as a matter of routine (neighbour-referenced breakpoint detection and correction, adjustment uncertainty propagated into the published trend). Multi-decade clinical laboratory series in EHRs, biobanks and registries have the same event structure — analyzer replacement, reagent/calibrator lot and method-generation changes are station-history events — and are used raw to support secular-trend claims; IFCC/JCTLM standardization acts forward on new methods and reconstructs no historical series. Gate 2 held the gap PARTLY FALSE, on the ground that two of the three limbs have executed precedent in the candidate's own literature (multi-site blind detection — Poh/de Lusignan; correction plus trend re-estimation with a published magnitude — ARIC/Parrinello). That ground did not survive, and it was overturned twice independently: by the judge's post-Gate-5 verification (2026-10-16; fresh-context checker, 15 queries, 0 refusals, log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-28-verification.md) and, separately, by the Gate 4 adversary, which opened Poh for itself. What stands: ARIC/Parrinello's magnitude is published and real (CKD prevalence 21.7% -> 1.3% at visit 1; creatinine bias 49%/47%/13% against the paper's own >10% threshold). What falls: Poh/de Lusignan is not station-record breakpoint detection and ARIC has no detection step at all — see Novelty - how this differs.
Presuppositions: P1 method/calibrator change dates recoverable — CONTESTED (Poh: no Read code for the creatinine assay, no ground truth in a 127-practice extract; non-retention is the normal case). P2 enough contemporaneous sites share the true population signal to serve as reference series — CONTESTED, load-bearing, untested by any opened source. P3 method changes give offsets/scale changes, not a change of measurand — CONTESTED (R1 narrows to commutable analytes rather than establishing it; ARIC's HDL precipitation-to-direct-enzymatic case is a counter-instance). P4 published trends retrievable in re-estimable detail — PLAUSIBLE, untested at frame level. P5 offsets detectable above within-site noise — PARTLY ESTABLISHED for creatinine (ARIC >10% bias for creatinine and uric acid), unknown elsewhere. P6 climatological pairwise methods transport to irregular, censored, indication-driven sampling — CONTESTED. P7 the site's patient population is not itself discontinuous at the method-change date — CONTESTED (analyzer purchase co-timed with a service-line change confounds detection and correction alike, and does so identically in the differenced series). P8 (added at Gate 1) "specificity" is well-defined, i.e. a period with no documented change is a true negative — CONTESTED AND NOT REPAIRED BY R1; incomplete logs (P1) mean absence of a documented change is not absence of a change. P9 (added at Gate 4, on the adversary's requirement) breaks are assumed SITE-IDIOSYNCRATIC — CONTESTED AND FALSE FOR A SUBCLASS, and this is the entry's sharpest objection: a pairwise-reference procedure tests the differenced series d_ij(t) = x_i(t) - x_j(t), so if every site in the frame shifts by the same amount at the same time — a national reagent reformulation, a calibrator re-traceable to a new reference material, IDMS-traceable creatinine calibration propagating through a country's laboratories, a guideline-mandated equation swap — the break cancels identically in every pair and is invisible to relative homogenization by construction (the adversary's own derivation, labelled as such, and an identity rather than an empirical claim). Laboratory method changes are MORE synchronised across sites than weather-station relocations, because manufacturers, standardisation programmes and guideline committees act on a whole country at once; Poh's inferred method change in 80 of 127 practices inside a 2006-2010 window and ARIC's HDL method-generation change (magnesium-dextran precipitation to direct enzymatic) are both of that class. Full markings in the record.
What would count as an answer: an implemented homogenization on a defined multi-site record and pre-specified analyte set reporting (i) detected breakpoints and estimated offsets, validated against independently retrieved change logs as sensitivity/specificity with the true-negative frame defined per P8, and (ii) trends re-estimated with and without correction, with the breakpoint-attributable fraction and a CI. Three decision-relevant outcomes: trends unchanged within CI licenses raw-series claims; trends materially changed obliges correction before any secular claim; detection no better than chance is a negative answer about the transplant itself.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 12 web searches (against a cap of 11 — the overrun is recorded, not concealed) and 5 fetches; no search refused. Full list with per-query results in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-28-record.md. The two that decided the gate: (1) the mandated own-field title form, "secular trends in clinical laboratory test results confounded by assay method changes over decades" -> Poh et al. on automated identification of creatinine-assay changes in longitudinal renal-function data, top hit, opened; (5) the mandated fraction-already-computed query, "how much of the observed decline in population cholesterol trend attributable to laboratory assay standardization recalibration rather than real change" -> ARIC/Parrinello recalibration of blood analytes over 25 years, opened — THE QUANTITY EXISTS AND IS PUBLISHED. Also informative: (2) "homogenization clinical laboratory time series breakpoint detection reference series climate station methods" -> climatology only, no clinical hit; (7) "pairwise homogenization algorithm neighbour reference series applied outside climatology" -> climatology only, no transplant out of the field in any domain; (10) "detect analyser reagent lot change from patient result data validated against instrument change records sensitivity specificity" -> lot-verification SOPs only, no study reporting detection operating characteristics against instrument logs. Queries 3, 6, 9, 11, 12 (PBRTQC; OHDSI/OMOP network DQ; official-statistics series linking; econometric panel change-point; EQA-as-reference-station) returned no clinical analogue of a reference station. Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (50 entries); nearest neighbours UQ-20261016-16, UQ-20261015-19, UQ-20261016-17; no duplicate. Added after the batch: 15 verification queries (0 refusals) and the Gate 4 adversary's 15 searches and 6 fetches, 14 of the searches in vocabularies Gate 2 had not tried (hydrology and water quality, neuroimaging, monitoring-programme operations, Nordic patient-median clinical chemistry, patient-based EQA, psychometrics and test equating, metabolomics batch effects, sensor-network blind calibration, biobank curation, federated EHR data quality, PISA trend linking, newborn-screening surveillance, hydrology and geodesy change-point attribution) — so Disguise is verified rather than unverified, 42 searches and 11 fetches in total across the three passes, with one adversary cap overrun and two technical fetch failures recorded in the adversary log and nothing refused anywhere.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): 1. Poh N, McGovern AP, de Lusignan S, "Improving the measurement of longitudinal change in renal function: automated detection of changes in laboratory creatinine assay", J Innov Health Inform 2015;22(2):293-301, doi 10.14236/jhi.v22i2.81, https://informatics.bmj.com/content/22/2/293 (preprint/TR-14-03, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.1542) — 127 primary-care practices, 951,764 records; method change found in 114/127 practices and 23.7% of patient series. 2. Parrinello CM et al., "Recalibration of blood analytes over 25 years in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study: impact of recalibration on chronic kidney disease prevalence and incidence", Clinical Chemistry 2015;61(7):938-947, doi 10.1373/clinchem.2015.238873 — 8 analytes remeasured from stored samples across 25 years; creatinine and uric acid >10% bias; CKD prevalence 21.7% -> 1.3% at visit 1 after recalibration. 3. Sternberg MR, "Multiple imputation to evaluate the impact of an assay change in national surveys", Stat Med 2017;36(17):2697-2719, doi 10.1002/sim.7302, https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/49987 — NHANES 25-hydroxyvitamin D, bridging-adjustment estimator for a known, dated, single assay change. All five sources opened; fetch list in the record.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Poh — CORRECTED, and it is a weaker prior than Gate 2 conceded; both the verification checker and the Gate 4 adversary opened it and agree. Its unit of analysis is the individual patient's paired series ("We shall call this paired measurement time series the renal function time series of the patient"), its reference is internal and exists only for a DERIVED quantity — it maps a self-recalculated MDRD eGFR onto the laboratory-reported eGFR and counts how many mapping functions are needed — and peer practices are explicitly NOT a reference: "As all practices sent laboratory samples to a single laboratory this change will affect all eGFR measurements reported by that practice." There is no ground truth ("No codes were identified in the Read code system which enable recording of creatinine assay method"), no sensitivity or specificity, no correction ("Identification of these changes in eGFR calculation method is the first step towards backwards calibration") and no trend re-estimation. So it detects a change in the eGFR REPORTING EQUATION, an event class visible only where a derived quantity exists, and it cannot run on haemoglobin, albumin or total cholesterol at all. Limb (a) for equation-free analytes is therefore substantially less occupied than the record allowed, and limb (b) was found uncovered in every vocabulary either reviewer searched. vs ARIC — already produces the magnitude the candidate asks for, for one corpus, so the magnitude cannot be claimed unmeasured; differences are that ARIC has no detection step (visit times are the candidate change dates), its reference is a physical gold standard (banked aliquots reassayed) not a neighbouring site, it is a scheduled-visit fixed cohort with one central laboratory, and it re-estimates within its own cohort rather than a pre-registered frame of external claims. vs Sternberg — change known, dated and singular; subject is the estimator for a given bridge, no detection, no multi-site structure, and it needs the stored specimens routine records lack. Net, as corrected: limb (c) is occupied for one corpus by ARIC/Parrinello under the physical-bridge paradigm (banked aliquots, known dates), and the known-date-offset-then-trend design has a cross-field twin the record did not find (Chesapeake Bay Program appendix 2.7a, opened by the adversary: a "LabChange" term that "takes values of zero before the Laboratory Change and values of one afterwards", with no detection, no reference station, no split samples and the historical record not rewritten). Limb (a) is occupied only for analytes carrying a reporting equation. Limb (b) — operating characteristics of blind detection scored against independently retrieved hardware change logs — was found nowhere, in either reviewer's sweep, in clinical chemistry or in any of the five neighbouring vocabularies tried. The design itself is less singular than the record concluded: pairwise referencing with no reference instrument is a named, mature problem family in signal processing ("blind drift calibration of sensor networks", arXiv 1707.03682 / 2111.09417 / 2205.01988, titles and snippets only, not opened), so the record's queries 2 and 7 conclusion that no transplant exists in any domain is an artefact of searching in climatology's words.
Novelty confidence: Medium (low confidence), restored from the record's Low by two independent findings and pulled back down in one respect. Upward, from both the verification checker and the Gate 4 adversary, each having opened the paper: Poh detects equation changes with a within-patient reference, not analyzer or calibrator changes against neighbouring sites, and validates nothing against change logs; Parrinello has no detection step, its breakpoints being known visit dates and its correction coming from re-assaying stored frozen samples from 200 participants by Deming regression; and the co-catchment-laboratories-as-mutual-reference-series design was not found anywhere in clinical chemistry, the adjacent peer-group literature (Percentiler/Flagger, NOPAM, PBRTQC) comparing each laboratory to a peer-group distribution or an external target while treating patient-population differences as noise to suppress rather than as a shared signal to exploit. Loh et al. 2020 (CCLM, doi 10.1515/cclm-2019-1024) does name limb (b)'s parameters (ANPed, false-positive flag rate, bias detection curves) but verifies them against INJECTED error in silico — "To simulate a positive shift, the magnitude of error under examination is added to the original results" — and instructs that real change events be discarded: "Any known periods with potentially erroneous results due to laboratory error should be excluded." That is the inverse of validating detections against retrieved logs. Downward, and why this is not High: the method is a known method under at least three other names (blind sensor-network calibration; item-parameter and scale drift against anchor items in educational measurement, with PISA already adding a link error to every cross-cycle comparison; laboratory-change terms in environmental monitoring), so methodological novelty is lower than the record thought even as question novelty rises.
Significance — consequence: if a material fraction of trend magnitude is breakpoint-driven, secular-trend claims from routine multi-decade laboratory data require homogenization first and a body of prevalence-trend literature needs re-examination — ARIC shows this is not hypothetical, having moved one visit's CKD prevalence by more than an order of magnitude; if trends are unchanged within CI, raw-series claims are licensed and a standing worry retires cheaply; if blind detection is no better than chance, the transplant fails and the failure mechanism (P7 patient mix moving with the instrument, P6 indication drift) is itself the finding.
Significance — audience: EHR/claims methodologists (the OHDSI data-quality line, whose instrument is a plausibility flag, not an offset estimator); biobank and registry curators — CORRECTED on a checkable point: the record asserted they "ship assay-era indicators but no corrected values", and the adversary fetched UK Biobank Data-Dictionary coding 165, "Assay correction level", which indicates "the type of assay correct that was applied to a biochemistry result" with values 0 None / 1 Date and aliquot correction / 2 Date correction only and is attached to 30 biochemistry fields including creatinine and cholesterol, so a flagship biobank already distributes corrected values with a per-result correction flag. The mitigation is narrow — single central laboratory, one assay campaign with injected QC, so it is within-campaign drift correction under the physical-bridge paradigm — but the claim as written was wrong, and what it shows is that curators act when a bridge exists; clinical-chemistry metrology, which has no retrospective arm; epidemiologists publishing analyte trend papers; the authors of the pre-registered claims. Real and identifiable; what is weak is how much would change, since ARIC made the general point and it did not propagate.
Significance — fecundity: what the clinical analogue of a reference station actually is (co-catchment site, EQA peer group, within-patient serial results, banked aliquots) and which is strictly better; whether estimated offsets can reconstruct the lost metadata of P1; whether adjustment uncertainty can be propagated into prevalence estimates as climatology propagates it into temperature trends — which the adversary notes is already routine in two other fields, climatology reporting adjustment uncertainty in trend CIs and OECD's PISA adding a link error to the standard error of every cross-cycle comparison, so this is a transplant rather than an invention; what share of fifteen-year laboratory breakpoints are network-synchronised versus site-idiosyncratic, which P9 makes the gating empirical quantity and which neither reviewer could source; whether a non-commutable change should be chain-linked as a new series rather than offset-corrected; whether detection sensitivity sets a floor on the smallest claimable secular trend at given site density.
Significance — anchoring: the un-generalised ARIC recalibration result; the IDMS creatinine-standardization boundary and MDRD/CKD-EPI equation changes, handled ad hoc; Poh's unexecuted back-calibration; reproducibility of EHR-derived trend claims; capped eGFR values (exactly 60 or 90) as a censoring artefact currently handled by deletion.
Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary (comparability is owned by forward-acting clinical-chemistry metrology; the long records are held by EHR methodologists whose quality vocabulary has no notion of an offset estimated against a reference; the homogenization literature sits in journals neither community reads) compounded by an incentive gap (a homogenization result mainly invalidates others' published findings; ARIC did the work only under an internal cross-visit obligation and did not generalise it) and by missing metadata (P1). Graded Resolved at Gate 4, where the adversary sourced the material half for itself rather than taking the record's word: Poh et al. state flatly that "No codes were identified in the Read code system which enable recording of creatinine assay method" in a 127-practice, 951,764-record extract, so the station-metadata half of the climatological method has no retrievable counterpart and an investigator who tried would stop at the feasibility step — a material barrier, not an attitude. The boundary half sharpens rather than weakens now that the method is known to have two homes (NCEI/ASCMO climatology and sensor-network signal processing), neither read by laboratory medicine, while the clinical community's own peer-comparison tool grew up inside a quality-control frame whose purpose is to tell a laboratory to fix itself today, not to rewrite its past. Credible — but it explains the silence of the narrow residue, not of the broad question, which was not silent.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): RUN LATE AND SEPARATELY. The batch killed this candidate at Gate 2 and spawned no adversary, so the eight rows were unexecuted when the batch returned; once verification refuted the Gate 2 ground, one fresh-context adversary was run at the strict standard on the Gate 0-3 record alone (15 searches against a cap of 14, the overrun recorded by the adversary rather than concealed, 14 of the 15 in vocabularies the record had not tried; 6 fetches, 4 returning content, 2 failing technically on an NCBI redirect and a PMC reCAPTCHA, so PMC6133026 remains unopened and no claim rests on it; no safety-classifier refusals). Verbatim log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-28-adversary-1.md.
1. Triviality | the direction is already in print — ARIC moved a prevalence estimate by an order of magnitude, the newborn-screening literature attributes incidence trends to assay and cutoff change, Poh found a step in most practices — so limb (c) is a one-paragraph inference and limbs (a) and (b) are engineering | none of that yields the quantities asked: limb (b) is an operating characteristic that depends on the unmeasured autocorrelation and magnitude of differential case-mix drift between co-catchment sites, and limb (c)'s per-claim arithmetic depends on where breaks fall relative to each trend window, which ARIC's scheduled-visit structure cannot inform for an open-cohort EHR series; even "the logs do not exist, stop" is an unpublished empirical finding | Resolved (with the caveat that limb (c)'s SIGN is largely foreseeable, so the surprise value rests on limbs (a) and (b))
2. Disguise | five renamings: blind drift calibration of sensor networks; item-parameter and scale drift against anchor items, with PISA's link error as the trend-propagation version; environmental-monitoring laboratory-change terms; metabolomics batch correction with intrastudy QC; and clinical chemistry's own peer patient medians and patient-based EQA | each renaming is missing the same thing — blind calibration assumes nodes do not move, and the clinical analogue of a moving node is a shifting sampled population (P7); anchor items, QC samples and banked aliquots are all physical bridges, whose absence is the candidate's premise; Chesapeake, ARIC and Sternberg all take the change date as given, verified from the Chesapeake document itself; patient medians are prospective single-analyte QC against a peer group with a known current method, not retrospective breakpoint dating in a fifteen-year record. Limb (b) was found under none of the five names | Partial (the method is a known method under at least three other names, which lowers methodological novelty; the question as posed was not found)
3. Combinatorial novelty | "apply SNHT to lab data" is method shopping; the interface contributes nothing | three interface problems, each sourced or derived: the differencing identity assumes the signal is shared and the breaks are not, and laboratory medicine inverts both halves (weak slow shared signal, strongly synchronised breaks — P9); a station relocation does not change the weather, but an analyser purchase bundled with a new service line changes the sampled patients, so break and signal move together at the same site at the same instant, which neither climatology nor blind calibration has; and the detection-power threshold has to be re-derived rather than imported, since Lindau & Venema's regime (ASCMO 4:1-18, 2018) has a different variance decomposition from a clinical site's | Resolved (and sharper than the record, whose P2 asks only whether sites share the SIGNAL and never whether they share the BREAKS)
4. Presupposition failure | (A) the unlisted assumption that breaks are site-idiosyncratic, false for the vendor and standardisation class; (B) "documented commutability across the method generations present" may select an empty analyte set | (A) analyser replacement, reagent and calibrator lot turnover, maintenance and platform consolidation are idiosyncratic in timing and are what service logs are full of, so the blindness covers a subclass; a competent execution declares it in advance, partitions the log into synchronised and idiosyncratic events, estimates sensitivity separately within each, and reports that the synchronised class needs an absolute method or external metadata — which converts a hidden assumption into a required design element rather than voiding the question. (B) read as "analytes whose method generations are known to measure the same measurand", creatinine, haemoglobin and total cholesterol qualify, and ARIC's creatinine was standardised and commutable and still carried >10% bias, so the restriction does not select the effect away | Partial — the adversary considered Unresolved on (A), which would have been fatal, and stopped short on its own standard of proof because it could not source the synchronised-versus-idiosyncratic share; it states that a reviewer with that number could make this a kill, and requires P9 before the entry is recorded
5. Vagueness | specificity is not an identified estimand while logs are incomplete (the record concedes this at P8); worse and unconceded, "the fraction of each published trend's magnitude attributable to breakpoint offsets" is detector-dependent, so naming SNHT, pairwise comparison and ACMANT as alternatives guarantees three answers with no principled choice; and K and the size of the claim list are left free | the attribution limb is identified CONDITIONAL on the detected break set, and reporting it conditionally with limb (b)'s operating characteristics in hand and sensitivity analyses across detectors is what climatology and PISA both do; detection with partial information on change-point times is a studied problem, so P8 is a design gap rather than an impossibility; and K being free is a pre-registration template, not vagueness | Partial
6. Significance inflation | the audience is partly mis-described (UK Biobank coding 165 falsifies the biobank bullet) and partly already served by patient-based EQA; and the record itself concedes ARIC made the general point with a larger effect than anyone would claim and it did not propagate | UK Biobank's correction is within-campaign single-laboratory drift correction, evidence that curators act when they have a bridge and silent on the multi-decade multi-site case; patient-based EQA is prospective and dates no step; the audience that would act is narrower than the record's five bullets but real — the authors of the pre-registered claims and the journals that would inherit a methods requirement — and the negative outcome is cheaply useful | Partial (the record's own ARIC-did-not-propagate concession is the strongest evidence against action)
7. Reason for silence | if the method has four homes, "nobody could see it" is unavailable and what remains is "nobody bothered", which the gate rules out | the mechanism survives and the adversary sourced its material half itself: no Read code exists for recording creatinine assay method, so the metadata half of the climatological method has no retrievable counterpart and an investigator stops at feasibility; plus two disciplinary boundaries and an incentive structure in which the product is the invalidation of other people's published trends | Resolved
8. Dissolution | (a) restricting to commutable analytes may select for cases where the correction is a nuisance rather than a threat; (b) the P9 blindness could reduce limb (a) to "we found the small local breaks and were blind to the big national ones", making limb (c) an artefact of the detector and the real conclusion "you cannot do this without metadata" | commutable does not mean unbiased, and ARIC's standardised creatinine is the counterexample; and a study landing on "pairwise referencing recovers idiosyncratic breaks with sensitivity s and is blind to synchronised ones" has answered a real question with a real number, telling curators which breakpoints they must document because no statistic will recover them | Partial (path (b) is live: the question's most likely outcome is a feasibility statement plus a structural impossibility result, which is publishable but is not its stated deliverable)
Note: Gate 2 found the on-point own-field priors an adversary would have been expected to find, which is the gate working; what Gate 2 then got wrong was what those priors do, which is what verification and this adversary both corrected.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: P9, the unlisted presupposition. A pairwise-reference design can only see breaks that are NOT shared across the frame, because a simultaneous common shift cancels identically in every differenced series — and in laboratory medicine the largest and most consequential breaks are precisely the shared ones, since manufacturers, standardisation programmes and guideline committees change a whole country's laboratories at once, whereas weather stations are re-sited one at a time. This inverts the condition that makes the climatological transplant work, it appears nowhere in P1-P8, and it biases the study's most quotable deliverable in the most dangerous direction: limb (c) will systematically under-attribute published trend magnitude to breakpoints, which manufactures the record's own first decision-relevant outcome ("trends unchanged within CI licenses raw-series claims") for the wrong reason. It stands at Partial rather than Unresolved only because the blindness covers a subclass and because no source was opened quantifying the synchronised-versus-idiosyncratic share of fifteen-year laboratory breakpoints; the adversary states plainly that a reviewer with that number could make this a kill. Second, from attack 5 and not conceded in the record: the attributable fraction is detector-dependent, so it is identified only conditional on a detected break set and must be reported that way with sensitivity analyses across detectors. Well-posedness stays 2/3 on P8 plus this.
Provisional at: Gate 5. One fresh-context adversary ran the full eight attacks at the strict standard and none of attacks 1, 2 or 4 reached Unresolved, so the fatal rule does not fire; five Partials stand, well-posedness 2/3 bars Validated independently, and Medium novelty with close neighbours is the Provisional criterion on its own. The batch's Gate 2 rejection is withdrawn as a novelty regrade that did not survive verification and was then overturned a second time by the adversary's own reading of the same prior.
What would promote it: (i) add P9 to the record as a declared design element and require limb (b) to report sensitivity separately within synchronised and idiosyncratic event classes, naming what external anchor (reference materials, EQA survey data, a split-sample bridge) would be needed for the synchronised class, since no relative method can reach it; (ii) repair P8's true-negative frame — either restrict specificity to a subframe where log completeness can be audited, or adopt the change-point-with-partial-metadata formulation that treats documented dates as partial information rather than ground truth; (iii) pre-commit limb (c) to a detector-conditional estimand with a stated sensitivity analysis across SNHT, pairwise comparison and ACMANT; (iv) source the synchronised-versus-idiosyncratic share, which is the quantity that decides whether the whole design is worth running. With (i)-(iii) done, well-posedness reaches 3/3 and nothing would stand Unresolved.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): settle P9's empirical share before anything else — partition one site's retrievable fifteen-year service log into events that are shared across the frame and events that are site-local, because the design's reach is bounded by that ratio and it is cheap to count where a log exists. P2 remains the second thing to test, and the entry should not be executed on its canonical wording until P9 and P8 are repaired as above.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED, and the record's earlier claim that a row was appended is withdrawn — no row was ever written, and the entry is Provisional rather than rejected-as-asked, so it is not a routing candidate (ledger/routed-open-problems.md is by its own header a file of rejected candidates). The verification pass also found the narrower residual is NOT posed in print: limb (b)'s parameters exist as named quantities in Loh et al. 2020 but are verified against injected error in silico with documented error periods explicitly excluded, and the shared-population half (P2) is not posed at all — where population comparability appears in the peer-group literature it is as a per-laboratory nuisance to suppress. Poh's "first step towards backwards calibration" is a stated next step for its own within-patient equation-change method, not for this question, so it is not routed either.
