ID: UQ-20261016-29
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — research-reagent integrity, molecular cloning, repository QC; neighbouring: metascience/reproducibility (literature-contamination counting), cell-line authentication (ICLAC), software supply chain (reproducible builds/SBOM drift), metrology (reference materials), culture collections

Question (canonical): In a plasmid repository holding, per plasmid, (a) a depositor-supplied map, (b) its own full-construct sequencing of the distributed material and (c) a citing-publication list: over the sequenced catalogue, what is the joint distribution of (discrepancy class: ORF-altering / regulatory / backbone / selection marker / silent) x (number of distinct citing publications whose methods describe the construct by map rather than by catalogue number), with CIs; and in a pre-specified subsample, does orthogonal re-sequencing plus a function assay of discrepant and as-mapped constructs confirm the predicted consequence and establish whether the discrepancy predates or postdates the depositor's publication?
Gate 1 version note: V1, adopted at Gate 1; V0 superseded (see the line below).
(V0, superseded at Gate 1: among research plasmids whose repository sequencing differs from the depositor's published map, what is the joint distribution of discrepancy class by functional consequence and citing-publication count — how many published results were built on a construct other than the one their methods describe? V1 names the three data objects, demotes the bare discrepancy rate because it is published, restricts the exposure denominator per P8, and makes direction-of-error an experimental arm.)

Alternative formulations:
- (lay) When the plasmid in the freezer isn't quite the plasmid in the paper, how often does the difference matter, and whose results rest on it?
- (cross-field) What is the plasmid-catalogue equivalent of the "ghosts of HeLa" count — how much of the literature rests on deposited material that differs from its own description, and in what way?

Motivating gap: Intake held that repository full-construct sequencing newly makes map-versus-reality measurable at catalogue scale while the same repositories count per-plasmid citations, making downstream exposure countable. Gate 2 held that the first half was falsified by Bai et al. 2024 and McGuffie & Barrick 2024. Verification (2026-10-16; independent fresh-context checker, 21 queries, 2 refused, log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-29-verification.md) overturns that for Bai and leaves it standing only for the classification limb: NEITHER paper is map-versus-material at catalogue scale, so the candidate's own premise is not established by the cited work either (see the P3 note below). What stands is that the catalogue-scale discrepancy classification has been run over 51,384 fully sequenced Addgene plasmids — McGuffie & Barrick 2024 — and that the same paper explicitly names publication tracing as deferred labour, which is the ground this rejection now rests on.

Presuppositions: P1 repository sequences accurate enough to be ground truth — CONTESTED at repeats/low-complexity (Bai et al. treat independent sequencing as arbiter but do not quantify their own error rate); P2 deposited material is the material used in the published work — CONTESTED and part of the question (Bai et al. propose the common 11-bp AAV 5' ITR deletion arose independently in several labs and spread, with some labs possibly adopting the mutant as reference, so the direction can run either way or be circular); P3 depositor maps retrievable in machine-comparable form at scale — PARTLY SUPPORTED, UNVERIFIED IN DETAIL (multiple per-plasmid sequence records inferred from result titles; no sequences page opened); DOWNGRADED TO CONTESTED on verification — neither cited paper performs a map-versus-material comparison at catalogue scale (Bai et al.'s true map-versus-material arm is the 49-plasmid Addgene AAV subset; McGuffie & Barrick compare sequences against canonical part databases and sequenced no material themselves), so nothing opened establishes that a repository holds depositor maps joinable to its own full-construct sequencing across a catalogue; P4 per-plasmid citing lists reasonably complete — CONTESTED (self-reported plus text-mined); P5 functional consequence coarsely stratifiable from sequence class — DEFENSIBLE, but a variant of a published scheme (Bai et al. Table 1 tiers: destroy / compromise / context dependent); P6 discrepancies not confined to unused plasmids — ESTABLISHED against the candidate's favour (5' ITR mutated in 34/49, 69%, of >100-request Addgene AAV plasmids); P7 catalogue composition informative about wider practice, or finding scoped to deposited material — CONTESTED (Bai et al.'s vendor-intake arm is the wider-practice evidence); P8 NEW, load-bearing: published methods describe the construct in a way that *can* disagree with the repository sequence — where a paper cites only "Addgene #X" the described construct IS whatever the repository distributes, so no mismatch exists to count and the exposure denominator collapses toward map-stating papers; unquantified anywhere opened, the weakest link; P9 NEW: maps are depositor-supplied, usually not published in the paper, correcting V0.

What would count as an answer: (i) the joint table over the sequenced catalogue — per discrepancy class, plasmid counts and distinct citing publications inside the P8 denominator, with CIs, plus a class-by-consequence cross-tab; (ii) pre-committed bands so a negative is real (NEGLIGIBLE / MARKER-ONLY / SUBSTANTIAL ORF EXPOSURE); (iii) a validated subsample assaying discrepant and as-mapped constructs; (iv) a direction-of-error arm comparing the archived original deposit against an independently obtained depositor-lab aliquot, orthogonally re-sequenced, so pre- versus post-publication origin is assigned rather than assumed. Without (iii) and (iv) the result reduces to the rate-plus-annotation exercise already published.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 12 web searches (cap 11 — one over cap, recorded, no searching continued after it) plus 5 fetches (at cap); no call refused. Full list in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-29-record.md. Most informative: "plasmid repository quality control sequence errors deposited constructs do not match published sequence" → Addgene QC pages, VectorBuilder press release on Bai et al., "Serious errors plague DNA tool that's workhorse of biology" — THIS found the near-duplicate; "full plasmid sequencing reveals discrepancies between deposited plasmids and depositor-provided maps" (mandatory own-field obvious-title query) → McGuffie & Barrick 2024 twice over, no map-versus-material audit by title alone; "Addgene full plasmid sequencing what percentage of plasmids differ from depositor map" (mandatory pre-computed-fraction query) → same PLOS ONE paper, no repository-published rate in its own words; "Bai Lahn 'Prevalence of errors in lab-made plasmids'..." → bioRxiv full PDF, still a preprint as served; "how many publications affected by plasmid sequence errors downstream reproducibility citing papers reagent" (answer-side) → aptamer sequence-alteration review, "Errors in genetic sequences mar hundreds of studies", none joining map-versus-material to citing counts; "reproducible builds measured fraction of packages where published binary does not match source code SBOM drift study" (neighbour 2) → arXiv 2410.08427, AROMA+, ICSE 2025 — the structural analogue is routinely measured there, raising disguise risk; "Addgene citation data metascience analysis plasmid reuse how many publications per plasmid" (exposure limb) → per-plasmid citing-article lists exist and are promoted as a depositor incentive, no QC-joined analysis. Neighbour sweeps over cell-line authentication, culture collections and metrology returned the counting template but no analogue result.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
(A) Bai X, Hong JF, Yu S, ... Lahn BT. "Prevalence of errors in lab-made plasmids across the globe." bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.06.17.596931, 2024 (full PDF opened; no peer-reviewed venue located). MATERIALLY MISDESCRIBED IN THE RECORD, corrected here on verification: it is a VectorBuilder preprint over the vendor's own client submissions, not an Addgene map-versus-sequencing study; its functional-consequence tiering (Table 1: destroy / compromise / context dependent) covers DESIGN errors only, not sequencing discrepancies; the >100-requests figure is a sampling filter for a 49-plasmid Addgene side analysis, not an exposure axis; and citing publications are absent from it entirely. Its figures as reported stand: ~15% (384/2,521) significant design errors; direct sequencing ~35% (91/259) with sequence variations; AAV both-ITRs consistent in only 63% (173/274); 5' ITR mutated in 34/49 (69%) of the >100-request Addgene AAV subset. Direction discussed, not determined.
(B) McGuffie MJ, Barrick JE. "Identifying widespread and recurrent variants of genetic parts to improve annotation of engineered DNA sequences." PLOS ONE 19(5):e0304164, 2024 (PMC11132462 opened). 51,384 fully sequenced Addgene plasmids, 983,436 parts annotated, "171,828 examples of parts that did not match their canonical sequences", 3/5 of plasmids carrying an uncatalogued variant. Ground truth = canonical part databases, not depositor maps, and no physical material was sequenced by the authors, so its "discrepancy classes" are part-variant classes — a different object from a map-versus-material discrepancy. Publication tracing explicitly declined and booked as deferred community labour, verbatim in the Discussion: "It may be possible to trace more of our variants of interest to existing publications", "this will require analyzing hundreds or thousands of publications", "Such efforts will take years of expert curation and laboratory experiments by a community of scientists", with the ideal named as being "able to track the provenance of plasmids and their parts using the scientific literature and/or metadata"; the Results record a failed instance — "none of the five publications associated with the plasmids containing this derivative mention its provenance".
(C) Horbach SPJM, Halffman W. "The ghosts of HeLa: How cell line misidentification contaminates the scientific literature." PLOS ONE 12(10):e0186281, 2017 (abstract opened via RePEc). 32,755 articles using misidentified cells, cited by an estimated half a million papers; closes with a call for a notification system.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
(A) Differs in corpus, scale and object, more than the record allowed: (A) runs on a vendor's client submissions, its true map-versus-material arm is the 49-plasmid Addgene AAV subset rather than a catalogue, its tiering is of design errors rather than of sequencing discrepancies, and it has no publication axis at all. It does not build the class-by-exposure joint distribution, assay discrepant versus as-mapped constructs, or determine direction. The candidate's stratification remains a variant of (A)'s published scheme, and (A) is a close neighbour at small n, not an execution of the candidate's comparison.
(B) Differs in ground truth: catalogue-scale and class-resolved but measured against canonical part sequence, so it cannot speak to "a construct other than the one their methods describe" — and it names the candidate's exposure limb as the analysis it did not perform. The candidate is (B)'s stated next step with (A)'s ground truth substituted in.
(C) Differs in material and defect type: identity failure in cell lines, no sequence-level classes; it supplies the counting design and the notification policy conclusion the candidate transplants.
Stated plainly, as corrected: candidate = (A)'s comparison, which exists only at n = 49 on repository material, at (B)'s scale, which is sequence-versus-canonical-part rather than versus a depositor map, with (C)'s exposure axis, which no plasmid paper has. The components are published in weaker forms than the record claimed; the join is not, and (B) names it as deferred labour.

Novelty confidence: Low — re-grounded, not re-graded, on verification. The record's ground was that (A) performs the candidate's core comparison with an exposure axis; that is struck (see above). The surviving ground is narrower and sufficient under this ledger's rules: (B) poses the citing-publication join in print and books it as multi-year community labour, which is the deferred-labour condition, and an own-field paper posing the question is a successful Gate 2 rather than a novel candidate. Two findings cut the other way and are recorded: no paper computes anything resembling the candidate's joint distribution, and the citation-modality axis (publications describing a construct by map versus by catalogue number alone) was found posed by no one — but a residual nobody has posed is not a routable open problem, and it does not restore novelty for the question as written.

Significance — consequence: if ORF-altering discrepancies carry substantial citing-publication exposure, the acting parties have a ready template — per-plasmid notification on the Horbach & Halffman model, construct-versus-map diffs on repository pages, a materials-verification clause in journal policy. If the mass is silent or marker-only, current partial-confirmation practice is justified. Marginal consequence is reduced: (A) already produced alarming headline rates and public recommendations without the exposure axis, so the exposure axis changes how many papers get flagged, not whether repositories are being pressed to tighten QC.
Significance — audience: real and organised — plasmid repositories (per-plasmid diffs, author notification), journals and publishers (verification policy, notices), the AAV vector community specifically, reusing labs deciding whether to re-sequence, ICLAC-style standing bodies as institutional model, and commercial full-plasmid sequencing providers, whose market case this quantifies — a non-trivial conflict of interest, since (A)'s authors are at such a provider.
Significance — fecundity: does exposure concentrate in a few heavily cited constructs (a power law of risk) or spread thinly; do plasmid discrepancies predict discrepancies in results, testable against replication corpora; does the ITR deletion's apparent independent recurrence mean selection rather than error; can diff data date a construct lineage's divergence; what does the equivalent audit show for cell lines, antibodies, mouse lines and recombinant proteins once each has a full-sequence ground truth.
Significance — anchoring: (A)'s unresolved direction-of-error puzzle; (B)'s explicitly deferred publication-tracing step; the cell-line contamination estimate and its unimplemented notification proposal; the wrongly-identified-nucleotide-sequence reagent literature and the aptamer sequence-alteration review, both tracing reagent-description errors through the literature in neighbouring reagent classes.

Reason for silence: mostly NOT silent — the core comparison was asked and answered in 2024, which is the Gate 2 finding. For the residual exposure limb the offered mechanisms are (1) an institutional-function boundary inside the only party able to do the join (sequencing sits in QC; the citing-article list is built and promoted as a depositor incentive); (2) an incentive/reputational gap on top of it — INFERRED and unevidenced, no refusal or policy located; (3) plain labour, the only evidenced mechanism ((B): hundreds or thousands of publications); (4) a genuine conceptual obstacle — P8: once a paper cites a catalogue number instead of a map there is no paper-versus-material mismatch to count, so the exposure denominator is ill-defined in exactly the cases where reuse is best documented. (4) is strongest and is not a "no one thought of it" mechanism.

ID: UQ-20261016-30
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI — large-scale training systems and training-data provenance (AI architecture); neighbours: distributed-systems recovery semantics, data attribution/memorization auditing. Source method: silence mapping.

Question (canonical): (V1, assessed) For training runs whose restart history and data pipeline are auditable (open runs, or a deliberately instrumented replication under shipped recovery semantics), taking the run's *claimed* training sequence as an artifact (a manifest with an order, or, where order is only procedural, the sequence (seed, loader version, world size) would have produced absent faults): (a) what is the divergence between claimed and realized token sequence induced by dataloader-state recovery at each restart and in total, reported both as a multiset divergence (tokens/documents never consumed; consumed more times than claimed, as a fraction of nominal) and as an ordering divergence (displacement from claimed position); and (b) under a pre-registered test with a stated detection floor, does per-document memorization or trajectory-specific influence differ for documents adjacent to a restart boundary relative to matched documents away from any boundary?

Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake, superseded at Gate 1) In large-scale runs with documented restarts, what fraction of the nominal token sequence is actually skipped or re-consumed by dataloader-state recovery, and is the deviation detectable in the trained model as a dated discontinuity in memorization or influence?
- (lay) When a big training run crashes and resumes, how much data gets quietly dropped or seen twice, and does it leave a mark on the model?
- (neighbour vocabulary) What are the delivery semantics (exactly-once / at-least-once / at-most-once) of a production training dataloader across failure recovery, and what is that recovery's coverage measured on the model rather than on the run?
One Gate 1 reformulation used (V0 to V1): fixed the claimed-sequence artifact, split the single "fraction" into multiset + ordering divergence, and required a pre-registered detection floor so a null is bounded. Full note in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-30-record.md.

Motivating gap: The fault-tolerance how-literature (restartable/deterministic dataloaders, distributed checkpointing, elastic training) is dense and denominates success in goodput; public chronicles report interruption counts and effective training time (OPT-175B arXiv:2205.01068; Llama 3's 466 interruptions, arXiv:2407.21783; 504-GPU operational analysis arXiv:2605.09370, "median retry interval of 11 minutes") but no source was found reporting tokens or documents skipped or re-consumed per restart. Meanwhile consumers of exactness have multiplied: influence/attribution, memorization audits, provenance protocols, and an explicit auditability tier (OPEN-1B, arXiv:2609.17380).

Presuppositions (7, all flagged contested in the record): (1) a run exists with both a restart log and reconstructable data order — contested for frontier runs, satisfiable for open/instrumented runs; (2) a nominal sequence exists as a claim — contested, some runs define order only procedurally; (3) skips/duplications large enough to matter — contested; (4) memorization/influence sensitive to single-pass presence and position — contested, partially supported by arXiv:2412.09538; (5) restart counts/timings recoverable from logs — contested; (6) recovery semantics stable within a run — contested and sharpest (resharding changes what "resume" means); (7) shipped framework behaviour representative of frontier runs — contested, bounds the audit to what is observable. Adversary 2 re-tested (2), (3) and (4) against literature and found all three survive — (3) strengthened.

What would count as an answer: either an audit of real auditable runs reporting per-restart and total multiset + ordering divergence with the recovery semantics in force at each restart named and resharding separated out; or an instrumented run with injected restarts (loader that checkpoints state, one that does not, one world-size change) reporting both divergences plus the pre-registered per-document test against matched controls at a stated floor. A finding that the claimed sequence is not reconstructable at all for most public runs answers the provenance limb directly.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 web searches + 5 fetches; 9 + 4 (adversary 1); 9 + 4 + 1 GitHub issue search (adversary 2) = 29 searches, 13 fetches at batch time; plus 13 verification queries (3 refused or failed on access) and A3's 12 searches and 7 fetches, with one repository-scope access denial recorded — 54 searches and 20 fetches in total, all logged. Most informative: (3, mandatory "what fraction") "'how many tokens' OR 'fraction of tokens' lost or repeated per restart" → no published per-restart token figure; returned only time/goodput quantities (OPEN-1B, arXiv:2605.09370, Checkmate, PHOENIX). (6, mandatory own-field title) "effect of data ordering on language model performance and memorization" → only *designed* order (curriculum/shuffling), none on fault-perturbed order. (4) "exactly-once versus at-least-once semantics data loader" → delivery-semantics vocabulary never applied to training dataloaders in the literature. (8) "elastic training world size change resharding dataloader resume samples skipped or repeated" → systems that *assert* the property (MosaicML "Elastic Determinism", Cerebras, MindSpore), none measuring its violation. (9) Llama 3 466 interruptions → goodput only. Adversary 1's decisive query: PaLM loss-spike rewind → arXiv:2204.02311 §5.1 publishes the skip. Adversary 2's decisive probe: GitHub issue search on NVIDIA/Megatron-LM → #7645/#7646. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-30-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. ElasWave: An Elastic-Native System for Scalable Hybrid-Parallel Training — https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00606v3 (Kang et al., 2025). §7.5 injects a failure (8→7 NPUs, Llama2-7B LoRA/GSM8K) and reports loss deviation 0.2% → 0.045%. Verified verbatim by adversary 2.
2. Tools for Verifying Neural Models' Training Data — https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00682 (Choi, Shavit, Duvenaud; NeurIPS 2023). Not re-verified by either adversary (abstract only).
3. Capturing the Temporal Dependence of Training Data Influence — https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09538 (Wang, Song, Zou, Mittal, Jia; ICLR 2025). Not re-verified by either adversary.
Added by adversaries, and load-bearing against the candidate: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM issues #7645 and #7646 (opened 2026-09-24, open) — https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/7645; PaLM arXiv:2204.02311 §5.1; Hubble arXiv:2510.19811; Jagielski et al. arXiv:2207.00099; Krasheninnikov et al. arXiv:2509.14223. (OPEN-1B arXiv:2609.17380 — the record and both batch adversaries state it makes no mention of restarts, and A3 REFUTES that from the paper itself: §2.3 derives a canonical batch stream from the training seed and corpus manifests whose "complete position of the stream is captured by a small, rank-independent record ... the number of documents consumed from each source, the per-source epoch counters, the exact bit-generator state of the mix RNG, and the partial window left in the packing buffer at save time", which "does not depend on world size, rank, number of nodes, or any other property of the mac[hine]", and §3.4 validates each of seven restarts "using hash comparisons on the steps which were repeated against the prior segment". It is therefore a partial performance of limb (a)'s verification on exactly the auditable-run class V1 scopes to, not merely enabling infrastructure. Added by A3 as prior art: arXiv:2406.05546, "Effects of Data Consistency in Parallel Machine Learning Training" (2024), which poses the candidate's question in-field and was missed by all eleven Gate 2 queries — though A3 opened it and found a small CNN on FashionMNIST on one M1 Max, an accuracy-over-time endpoint, and as its closest accounting figure the "number of gradients processed after killing and recovering twice": gradients, not sample IDs, with no count of skipped or duplicated samples and no per-sample analysis; and arXiv:2505.22042.)

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs ElasWave — its estimand is aggregate loss deviation as a system-quality metric; the candidate's is the document multiset and ordering itself, which loss neither bounds nor reveals; no per-document model test, no real-run audit. vs Choi/Shavit/Duvenaud — same concern, opposite direction: their seed pre-commitment presupposes an honest trainer's realized sequence matches the committed one; the candidate asks what the honest-trainer residual is. vs Wang et al. — supplies the mechanism (influence is iteration-dependent) without asking the question; its perturbations are researcher-chosen counterfactuals, not fault-imposed ones at known timestamps. vs Megatron-LM #7645/#7646 — these do *not* differ enough: they pose limb (a) for the resharding case, state exactly-once as the expected property, and compute exact duplicate/drop counts from the sampler code.

Novelty confidence: Medium — held at Medium by three adversaries, but on a narrower basis than the record argued. A3's finding is the material one: OPEN-1B already performs the stronger version of limb (a)'s check on the auditable-run class the question targets, hash-matching the repeated steps across seven restarts, so what remains genuinely unoccupied is the never-consumed term in loaders that do not checkpoint loader state, sample-level continuity under per-rank resharding, operator-driven data-position edits of the OPT-logbook kind, and whether any public release's claimed sequence is reconstructable at all. Its Disguise sweep also found the estimand's templates in four other fields — per-protocol versus intention-to-treat analysis of delivered exposure in clinical trials; frame coverage error decomposed into undercoverage and duplicate listing inside Total Survey Error; planned-versus-actual material reconciliation with mandatory deviation investigation in GMP batch records — none applied to a training run and none with any analogue of limb (b).
(Record's grade, partly contested on verification. Two of its negative claims failed: PaLM §5.1 publishes the skip in a frontier run — "skipped roughly 200-500 data batches", ~20 times, which adversary 1's own labelled arithmetic puts at ~1.6-5% of steps/tokens — so "no source reports tokens skipped per restart, as a fraction or otherwise" is false; and limb (a) is posed in public discourse for the resharding case by #7645/#7646, which the ledger's own definition of un-asked counts. Novelty is not Low: the conjunction — a whole restart chronicle audited for multiset *and* ordering divergence with a pre-registered per-document test keyed to boundaries — was not found posed, and both adversaries graded Disguise Partial, not Unresolved. The verdict therefore does not turn on Gate 2.)

Significance — consequence: If divergence is non-trivial, every "document D was in the training set, seen once, at position p" claim acquires an unreported error bar and the single-epoch premise becomes an approximation of stated size. If parts-per-million, that licenses the exactness assumption quantitatively for the first time. A non-null model signature would mean published data-ordering and memorization results on restarted runs carry a dated confound — and would make restart history readable out of weights. A bounded null gives attribution methods a tolerance budget.

Significance — audience: data-attribution/influence researchers (would report sequence-error sensitivity or stop worrying with a citation); memorization/extraction/privacy auditors (would condition on restart proximity or justify not doing so); provenance/verification work (OPEN-1B's auditability tier, Proof-of-Training-Data — an auditor replaying a restarted run must distinguish fault recovery from fraud). The EU AI Act training-data-summary audience is STRUCK on the Commission's own words, which A3 opened: the summary should be "generally comprehensive in its scope instead of technically detailed", it "does not require disclosure of the details for the specific data and works used to train the model" (para. 16) nor "the exact mix and composition of data sources" (para. 22), scraped content is reported at the granularity of the "top 10 % of all domain names", and the AI Office supervises without "performing a work-by-work assessment" (para. 26); the ML-BOM and attestation literature A3 sampled (TAIBOM, AIBoMGen, OWASP) attests datasets rather than consumption sequences. Litigation-side analysis does not inherit that self-restraint and stays; training-infrastructure teams (weakest limb — they treat the property as solved by construction); litigation/copyright analysis. Adversary 2's challenge stands partly: the deliverable is a per-config table, not a citable constant (#7645 reports zero divergence for Megatron's *default* loader and non-zero for a non-default combination), and no filing or standard turning on restart-induced consumption error was cited.

Significance — fecundity: delivery semantics of each major stack's dataloader stated as a property; whether restart history is recoverable from a released checkpoint alone (live adjacent field — WARP, arXiv:2607.01686; training-order recency linearly encoded, arXiv:2509.14223 — but not this question); the minimum sequence-error floor at which influence estimates destabilise; whether a realized "data consumption log" should be a release artifact; whether divergence correlates with fault type; whether curriculum results replicate on fault-free runs.

Significance — anchoring: OPT-175B logbook restarts with data-position adjustments (arXiv:2205.01068); Llama 3's 466 interruptions (arXiv:2407.21783); 504-GPU operational analysis (arXiv:2605.09370); OPEN-1B (arXiv:2609.17380); Proof-of-Training-Data (arXiv:2307.00682); ElasWave's 0.2% loss deviation (arXiv:2510.00606); the permutation-invariance violation in arXiv:2412.09538; PaLM's documented rewind-and-skip (arXiv:2204.02311). In-ledger: adjacent to UQ-20261016-01 (fault attribution/weight corruption) and UQ-20261015-25 (checkpoint equivalence); no duplicate.

Reason for silence: Record claimed two structural mechanisms — a disciplinary boundary with a success-criterion asymmetry (those who can compute it are measured on goodput; those who need it work from released checkpoints and have no restart chronicles), and a disclosure-incentive gap (labs would be publishing imprecision in their own provenance claims; vendors would be measuring how far an asserted feature falls short). Both adversaries rejected this as a reason for *non-asking*: practitioners ask it constantly in public (HF, OpenNMT, PyTorch and torchdata threads in English, Chinese and Japanese; #7645/#7646 pose it in its sharpest form and answer it), and engineers answered by building step-indexed stateful loaders. The mechanisms explain non-measurement and non-publication, which the gate explicitly excludes. Adversary 2 graded this Unresolved and invoked the gate's own instruction to treat the novelty finding as suspect.

A2: the record's named defence — "resharding is not derivable from code inspection" — is refuted verbatim by Megatron-LM #7645/#7646, which derive the mechanism from reading MegatronPretrainingRandomSampler and exact counts from a CPU script needing no GPU, no run and no logs ("58 duplicated, 58 never drawn in epoch 0" for DP 4→2 at step 5; checked against main @ ec806b2); given a restart log, per-restart divergence is a lookup. Limb (b) is interpolable between published points: Hubble (arXiv:2510.19811) already inserts documents at chosen training positions at controlled exposures ("inserted in only the first quarter ... does not memorize"; last quarter → "more data is memorized") and Jagielski (arXiv:2207.00099) reports the recency and exposure gradients. | Record's three defences: resharding not code-derivable (refuted); ElasWave's 0.2% loss deviation shows recovery is measurably non-null (verified true, but concerns loss, not the document multiset, and is a LoRA fine-tune, so it does not rescue derivability); "not reconstructable at all" is itself a finding (genuine survivor, but a *different* question — a survey of release documentation, not either limb as posed). | A1 Partial · A2 Partial (**downgraded from Unresolved — fatal** on the judge's post-Gate-5 verification, 2026-10-16: independent fresh-context checker, 13 queries, 3 refused, log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-30-verification.md). Two of A2's three legs survive: the question is not silent, being posed routinely in public issue trackers across the major stacks, and the two cited issues are real, do contain exact duplicate and drop counts for a changed-DP resume, and did obtain them on a CPU with no training run and no logs. The load-bearing leg fails. A2's claim is that the quantity is derivable by reading the sampler's code rather than requiring measurement, and #7646 states the opposite in its own words: the mechanism was read from the sampler's formulas but "the numbers themselves are not derived analytically" — they came from running a script and tallying every drawn ID with `Counter` against an uninterrupted enumeration. The generalisation fails too: analytic enumeration holds for step-indexed deterministic samplers (Megatron legacy cyclic, Mosaic by design) and provably not for HuggingFace datasets' buffered shuffle, where the buffer contents are absent from the checkpoint by documented design, nor for accelerate's `RandomSampler`, where the permutation is drawn before the RNG is saved, nor for DeepSpeed's curriculum sampler, which checkpoints the global numpy RNG instead of its own generator; and for torchtitan the question cannot be asked without patching the framework, because `load_state_dict` asserts the DP world size is unchanged and the state is an opaque per-rank pickle. Third adversary (A3), run after the verification pass because the batch's fatal Triviality grade did not survive it, and a rejection rate that falls that way is not a result until the survivor has been attacked at full strength. Fresh context, Gate 0-3 record only, strict standard; 12 searches and 7 fetches, no safety-classifier refusals, one access failure recorded (a read of Megatron-LM's data_samplers.py was denied because the repository is not in this session's scope, so A3's sampler claims rest on the published issues and documentation rather than on the source). Verbatim log in batches/2026-10-16-1033/UQ-20261016-30-adversary-3.md. No attack reached Unresolved, so across three independent adversaries the fatal rule never fires.
A3 1. Triviality | Partial. Megatron checkpoints consumed_train_samples and skipped_train_samples and constructs its sampler with consumed_samples, so for that stack the restart offset is a restored integer and the accounting is a subtraction; and the dominant divergence term is a rollback artefact, since samples delivered in (checkpoint, crash] updated weight states that were then discarded. Headline for state-checkpointed loaders at fixed world size: zero for the effective sequence, replayed steps times global batch for the delivered one — a paragraph and a table. Held Partial because the residue is real research (per-rank sharded streaming loaders under world-size change have no code-readable answer; loaders that do not checkpoint loader state produce a never-consumed term that is weight-relevant; operator-driven data-position edits are not recoverable by code inspection) and because A3's own attempted arithmetic kill from frontier numbers FAILED: Llama 3 §3.3.4 gives "466 job interruptions" in 54 days and "higher than 90% effective training time" but no checkpoint interval and no quantified lost work, so published figures bound re-delivered tokens only at <=10% of nominal, with that remainder also absorbing detection, requeue and checkpoint-load time — a ceiling, not an answer (A3's arithmetic, carrying the source's looseness).
A3 2. Disguise | Partial. Templates in four other fields (per-protocol versus intention-to-treat; frame coverage error in Total Survey Error; GMP planned-versus-actual reconciliation; device-vigilance lot tracing) supply estimands, not values, and none has been applied to a training run or has any analogue of limb (b). The one in-field posing, arXiv:2406.05546, is weak where it matters, as above — and A3 notes its existence corroborates the silence claim, since even the paper named for data consistency under failure does not do the accounting.
A3 3. Combinatorial novelty | Partial, and it dissolves the record's sharpest presupposition: OPEN-1B §2.3 makes stream position rank-independent by design, so presupposition 6 (resharding changes what resume means) is a design choice rather than a finding, and Megatron's global consumed_train_samples does the same more coarsely. What survives as genuine interface work is one object neither parent field owns — the distinction between the DELIVERED sequence (what the loader handed to accelerators; an at-least-once quantity the systems side measures as goodput) and the EFFECTIVE sequence (what survived into the released weights; the exactly-once quantity provenance and attribution claims rest on). No systems paper A3 opened says which of the two its guarantees cover, and no attribution paper says which it assumes: OPEN-1B's hashes speak to the effective sequence, goodput papers to the delivered one, ElasWave's loss deviation conflates them.
A3 4. Presupposition failure | Partial — the entry's strongest objection, and an eighth presupposition the record does not list. The question assumes the restart-induced divergence enters the trajectory that produced the released weights, so a per-document boundary signature is possible in principle; for the dominant shipped path that is false, because under rollback-replay with loader state in the checkpoint the duplicated deliveries belong to a discarded branch, and OPEN-1B's hash-matched repeated steps are the published instance of the exactness holding across seven restarts. "Realized token sequence" does not distinguish delivered from effective, so limb (a) can report a percentage that is mechanically an accounting of wasted compute while limb (b) is null by construction rather than by evidence — and a bounded null with no mechanism licenses nothing. Held Partial because the question's own answer criteria require a loader that does not checkpoint its state, where the never-consumed term is real and does shape the weights, and a world-size change, where per-rank sharded loaders can lose sample-level continuity in ways nobody has measured.
A3 5. Vagueness | Resolved. Pre-registration closes the displacement-statistic hole by construction, and the version-relativity of the answer is a design feature — the output is a labelled table of (loader, version, world-size change) -> divergence, which is how any claim about an instrument is reported.
A3 6. Significance inflation | Partial, with the EU AI Act audience sourced away on the Commission's own words (see Significance - audience). One audience would change practice on the branch that matters: if per-rank sharded or state-less loaders produce a non-zero never-consumed term, every "document D seen exactly once at position p" claim built on such a run needs an error bar nobody reports.
A3 7. Reason for silence | Partial, where A2 had Unresolved. A3 partly overturns the record's mechanism (1) with a paper the record cites but did not read: OPEN-1B treats claimed-versus-realized data position as a first-class audited property, which is the infrastructure community doing the thing the mechanism says nobody does. It offers a simpler and less flattering mechanism — in the configurations that matter the answer is zero by construction and known to the people who build the loaders, so there is nothing publishable, and elsewhere the runs are proprietary or the loader is simply fixed rather than measured. Against that it holds mechanism (2) intact, with Llama 3 §3.3.4 as the exhibit: 466 interruptions and an effective-training-time figure reported, and not one word about the data loader, consumed samples, or data repeated on restart.
A3 8. Dissolution | Partial. It separates into four questions, three of which are not research: each shipped loader's resume semantics (read the code); compute wasted re-executing rolled-back steps (already instrumented as goodput, the delivered-sequence number in a provenance costume); whether the claimed sequence is reconstructable at all for public releases (real, but a survey of release practice); and the per-document signature (null by construction wherever loader state is checkpointed). Held Partial because the decomposition is itself a contribution — no existing source states which of the four it answers — and because limbs three and four stay open, four for per-rank-sharded and state-less loaders.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Marked down from the record's 3/3 at Gate 1, on a defect A1 raised and A3 showed to be load-bearing: "realized token sequence" does not distinguish the DELIVERED sequence from the EFFECTIVE one, and which is meant decides whether limb (a) is zero by construction for the dominant shipped recovery path. A1 called the repair a single sentence; it is still not in the record, and until it is the canonical question has two readings with different answers. Significance holds at 2/3 with the EU AI Act audience struck and the attribution limb thin. Gate 2 stands at Medium.)

Verdict reasoning (Gate 5): Provisional. Three independent fresh-context adversaries, 24 attacks, not one Unresolved after verification — A2's fatal Triviality grade did not survive it (see attack 1), and A3, which attacked the Gate 0-3 record cold at the strict standard, graded Triviality Partial on its own evidence and reached no fatal grade either. So the fatal rule does not fire. What caps the entry is well-posedness 2/3 on the delivered-versus-effective ambiguity, A2's Unresolved on attack 7 (Unresolved on a non-fatal attack is Provisional at best), and Medium novelty with OPEN-1B now established as a partial performance of limb (a)'s verification. Disguise was verified across 30 new-vocabulary queries in three adversaries and graded Partial by all three, so this is not a disguised-known rejection. The thing that keeps the entry alive is the same in all three logs: for a real large-model run that restarted N times, how far the data it actually consumed diverges from the sequence it claims was found posed nowhere — and the end-to-end form is distinct from the per-stack correctness-bug form that is posed constantly.
Strongest remaining objection: the delivered-versus-effective collapse. "Realized token sequence" is ambiguous between the tokens a loader handed to accelerators and the tokens that shaped the released weights, and under the dominant shipped recovery path — rollback to a checkpoint carrying the loader's own position, as in Megatron's checkpointed consumed_train_samples and OPEN-1B's rank-independent stream record — those differ by exactly the discarded branch of the optimisation. The duplicated-deliveries half of limb (a) would then score as "consumed more times than claimed" updated weights that were thrown away, and OPEN-1B has already published the stronger check on the auditable-run class the candidate targets, validating each of seven restarts by hash comparison on the repeated steps (§3.4). So on the main branch limb (a) measures wasted compute under a provenance name, and limb (b)'s null is a null without a mechanism, which licenses nothing. What survives is narrower than the record claims but real: the never-consumed term in loaders that do not checkpoint loader state, sample-level continuity under per-rank resharding, operator-driven data-position edits of the OPT-logbook kind, and above all whether any public release's claimed sequence is reconstructable at all. Second, surviving from A2 and graded Partial by A3: the reason for silence is contested, because the question is asked constantly in public issue trackers and OPEN-1B shows the infrastructure community treating claimed-versus-realized data position as a first-class audited property — what remains is mechanism (2), evidenced by Llama 3 reporting 466 interruptions and an effective-training-time figure without one word about the data loader.
What would promote it, merging A3's required amendments: (i) split the estimand explicitly into the delivered sequence (at-least-once) and the effective, weight-shaping sequence (exactly-once under rollback), require both to be reported separately, and concede in the question that for state-checkpointed loaders at fixed world size the effective divergence is zero by construction and has been hash-verified across OPEN-1B's seven restart segments; (ii) scope limb (b) to configurations where the effective sequence actually moves — loader state not checkpointed, per-rank sharded streaming loaders under world-size change, operator-driven data-position adjustments and rollbacks — and pre-register the power analysis for those, since elsewhere the null is mechanical rather than empirical; (iii) name the ordering-divergence statistic in the pre-registration (mean absolute displacement in samples, Kendall's tau, fraction displaced beyond a threshold); (iv) restate significance as attribution and memorization researchers plus litigation-side analysis, the regulatory-summary audience having been struck on the Commission's own words; (v) add arXiv:2406.05546 and arXiv:2505.22042 to the prior-art set, re-grade OPEN-1B as a partial performance of limb (a)'s verification rather than enabling infrastructure, and re-examine the reason-for-silence mechanism in that light. With (i) done the question reaches Well-posedness 3/3; with (ii) it stops being null-by-construction; (v) is what decides whether novelty holds at Medium.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not applicable for a rejected entry. The one survivor both adversaries independently identified — across public releases with restart histories, is the claimed training sequence reconstructable at all from published artifacts, and what is the per-stack delivery-semantics table — is a different question and would need its own Gate 0-2 as a fresh candidate.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None. Not routed, and now for a second reason: the entry is Provisional rather than rejected, and ledger/routed-open-problems.md is by its own header a file of rejected candidates. Recorded here instead, since verification established it: the per-stack correctness-bug form of limb (a) is posed and answered in public (Megatron-LM #7645/#7646, with a still-open gap named in the thread — switching from sharded to unsharded on resume is "still accepted silently", 55 duplicated and 55 never drawn in that commenter's test), while the end-to-end accounting question for a real run was found posed nowhere. The asked-and-open residue is therefore a framework bug report, not a research problem for the research run.

Status: Provisional
Domain(s): STEM — radio astronomy / spectrum engineering and satellite regulation; neighbouring: EMC and measurement-system metrology, RF emitter characterisation, optical satellite photometry
Question (canonical): For a cohort of individually identified LEO satellites (NORAD IDs) of one hardware model, observed with one instrument in fixed bands and a fixed beam/elevation configuration, with multiple passes per satellite per epoch and >=2 epochs >=6 months apart: (a) how does the variance of per-satellite band-limited radiated power (normalised to 1000 km) partition into pass-within-epoch, epoch-within-satellite, between-satellite-within-model and between-model components; (b) with model fixed, does epoch-level per-satellite emission change with on-orbit age; (c) what fraction of previously-detected satellites still in orbit fall below a stated, sensitivity-matched per-satellite upper limit at the later epoch? (Gate 1 reformulation; intake version asked whether UEMR is a fixed property of a hardware model or varies over a satellite's operational life, biasing snapshot-based aggregate forecasts.)
Alternative formulations: (1) Does a satellite's radio-noise leakage drift as it ages on orbit (thermal cycling, degradation, payload state, software updates), or is UEMR set per hardware generation at launch? (2) Are UEMR non-detections of previously-detected, still-in-orbit satellites explained by emission variability and duty cycle rather than by survey sensitivity?
Motivating gap: Anchor anomaly in Grigg et al. 2025 (arXiv:2506.02831): of 68 Starlink satellites detected by Di Vruno et al. 2023, "None of these 68 satellites were detected in our work even though 55 of them were still in orbit during this survey", with the emitting component stated to be unknown; the same null recurs for Starlink-3618 in Yang et al. 2026 (arXiv:2603.07631). Existing designs are snapshot-by-generation (Di Vruno 2023; Bassa et al. 2024), and the one within-satellite study (Dong et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.17150) explicitly declines the variance decomposition. NOTE (Gate 4, then corrected): the intake built this gap on a half-quote and never opened the anchor, which stands. But the stronger claim — that the anchor's own next sentences explain the non-redetections, so the gap does not exist — was checked against the primary papers and withdrawn. Grigg's two mechanisms are frequency non-overlap for the v1.0 narrowband lines and EDA2 sensitivity for the v1.5 broadband, assigned one per model class and covering 58 of the 68; they assert that the two campaigns are NOT COMPARABLE, which makes the non-redetection uninformative about emission change rather than evidence that the emission was unchanged; and no numerical upper limit is published for any of the 55 still-in-orbit non-redetections. The gap as written overstated the anomaly; what survives is that the episode is uninformative in both directions and that nobody has published the per-satellite limits that would make it informative.
Presuppositions: [established] individual emitters are trackable across epochs by NORAD ID (Bassa 2024 Tables B.1-B.3; Dong 2026 on the Grigg catalogue). [established] 55 of 68 were in orbit at the later epoch, so re-entry does not explain the nulls. [contested] per-epoch sensitivity can be made commensurable so a non-detection becomes a usable per-satellite upper limit. [contested] hardware is fixed on orbit, so within-satellite change is state, degradation or software (sub-model revisions inside a launch group would break the model-level control). [established] aggregate UEMR forecasts feed real decisions (IAU CPS/SKAO, ITU-R WP 7D, WRC-27 1.16/1.18); per-satellite limits are being proposed (arXiv:2608.11659, unopened). [contested] operator telemetry is needed only for attribution, not measurement — strained: Dong 2026 state operational state "is not directly observable from the ground". [flagged] the estimand is per-satellite radiated power, not the astronomer-facing aggregate; the two diverge if fleet composition changes concurrently (Mallama 2026). [contested — graded FAILED at Gate 4 on adversary 1's kill, re-graded after verification] that the 68 non-redetections are an unexplained anomaly, i.e. that variability versus sensitivity is an untested dichotomy. The dichotomy is indeed untested, but not because the anomaly is unexplained: Grigg offers two instrumental mechanisms that make the campaigns non-comparable, so the episode cannot discriminate between variability and sensitivity either way. The presupposition survives only in the weaker form that no published work bounds the non-detections, which adversary 2 re-derived independently.
What would count as an answer: A matched-sensitivity repeated-epoch campaign — one instrument, fixed bands and beam/elevation configuration, individually identified cohort, >=2 epochs months-to-years apart, multiple passes per satellite per epoch, publishing per-satellite flux densities and a stated upper limit for every non-detection — delivering (a) the four-level variance decomposition, (b) an age test with model fixed, (c) the upper-limited non-detection fraction. Either direction is informative: large epoch-within-satellite variance invalidates snapshot-derived forecasts and forces duty-cycle-aware monitoring and percentile-form limits; stability vindicates the snapshot design and per-satellite limits. A null at stated power is publishable.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 queries + 5 fetches (full list: batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-31-record.md), plus 9 new-vocabulary adversary queries + 4 fetches (UQ-20261016-31-adversary-1.md). Most informative: "temporal variability of unintended electromagnetic radiation from Starlink satellites repeated epochs same satellites" → no repeat-epoch study; surfaced Dong 2026. "RF fingerprint drift over time same transmitter aging unintentional emissions signature stability" → emitter-signature drift is a mature named problem, but terrestrial and framed as classifier degradation. "repeated measures variance components same unit radiated emission long-term stability within-unit between-unit EMC measurement reproducibility" (method-owning vocabulary) → the variance partition is standard in EMC measurement-system assessment, applied to instruments and test setups, not to a fleet of emitters over service life. "'fraction of' previously detected satellites not detected later survey unintended emission upper limits still in orbit" → the raw count (68/55/none) is already in print; no sensitivity-matched bounded fraction. Adversary additions: "EMI increase with component aging electrolytic capacitor degradation radiated emissions drift" → an uncited mechanism literature (HAL hal-01225352 cluster, DC-DC converter ageing EMI), lab-bound; Chinese and German sweeps → nothing new; ITU-R WP 7D regulatory sweep → no per-satellite temporal-variability monitoring item.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): A. Dong, Wang, Cai & Akan 2026, arXiv:2605.17150 — unit: individual satellite pooled to per-satellite medians within one 5-month EDA2 campaign; endpoint: per-detection UEMR flux density 72-234 MHz; comparator: the same satellite in its other solar-illumination state; estimand: median illuminated/eclipsed ratio 0.886, CI [0.441, 1.598]. B. Bassa et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.11767 — unit: individual satellite at one epoch, aggregated to generations; endpoint: flux density in RAS bands corrected to 1000 km; comparator: hardware generation; estimand: generation-level mean difference, 15 dB for v2-Mini. Also reports v1.0/v1.5 signals "consistent in flux density and spectral properties" with the 2022 Di Vruno observation (adversary Fetch D). C. Mallama 2026, arXiv:2604.13145 — unit: constellation/generation aggregate in 0.1-yr bins, individuals explicitly not followed; endpoint: optical magnitude normalised to 1000 km; comparator: calendar time and launch cohort; estimand: secular slope in mag/yr. Opened late by the adversary: Indermuehle & Lourenco 2026, arXiv:2608.12999 (SNIFFLES I, 1-26 GHz, 4,629 tracked observations) — reports a per-version detection fraction ("unintended radiation was detected in 76.9 percent of all observations of the relevant satellite version"), a duty-cycle-like statistic, but no epoch comparison and no per-satellite time series.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A, same object and state-dependence intuition, but A's contrast is a reversible geometric covariate on an hours-to-days timescale inside one campaign, uses detections only, publishes no upper limits, and declines the variance decomposition; the candidate's contrast is epoch separated by months-to-years with on-orbit age as regressor. vs B, B is the snapshot-by-generation design whose bias the candidate questions — one epoch, no re-observed NORAD IDs, no age term, no formal non-detection limits — but B's version-level 2022-to-2024 consistency does answer the first-order question in the direction of stability. vs C, right question, sibling observable, wrong level (population slope and cohort contrast, not per-unit repeated measurement) and a different physical regime (passive reflectivity versus powered electronics with a duty cycle). vs the method-owning fields, neither emitter-signature drift nor within-unit/between-unit variance partition has been pointed at orbiting emitters' radiated power over service life; the gap survived searching in the method's vocabulary, not only the data's.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If epoch-within-satellite variance is comparable to between-model variance, snapshot-based aggregate forecasts estimate the wrong quantity, generational contrasts are partly confounded with operating-state sampling, monitoring must characterise a distribution rather than a level, and per-satellite limits must be written as percentiles over operational states. If per-unit emission is stable, the snapshot design and per-satellite limits are vindicated. Discounted at Gate 4, then partly restored: Bassa 2024's "stability" is a population-distribution consistency remark about first-generation satellites as a group, demonstrated only above a bright floor (LBA S_nu < 10 Jy at 3 sigma against detections of 15 to 1300 Jy) in a paper that never links a single spacecraft across the two epochs and reports in the same breath that brightness varies from satellite to satellite — so the first-order version is not settled at version level, and the discount was too large. What replaces it is sharper and comes from adversary 2: "biased" is the wrong word, because aggregate band power is a sum and within-unit variance does not shift its mean; but the regulated functional under RA.1513-2 is an exceedance share of samples, not a mean, so per-satellite duty cycle and variance enter the regulated quantity directly. The practical stake is therefore real and sits in the monitoring specification — whether compliance can certify a unit from one pass or must sample its states to a percentile — rather than in restating aggregate forecasts.
Significance — audience: IAU CPS and SKAO spectrum-management staff; ITU-R WP 7D under live WRC-27 RAS-protection items; observatory RFI groups holding the instruments (MWA/EDA2, LOFAR/ASTRON, DRAO), for whom the answer decides one-off campaign versus standing per-emitter cadence; constellation EMC engineers, for whom an age trend or a fleet-wide step is a fault-localisation signal. Audience real and verified, but no evidence any of these bodies has asked for distributional per-unit specifications.
Significance — fecundity: duty-cycle distribution of the emitting subsystem; UEMR as a remote proxy for payload loading; whether a software update appears as a synchronised fleet-wide step (the sharpest handle on the unknown-component problem without operator data); emission versus thermal-cycle count rather than calendar age; how to write protection criteria for a time-varying emitter.
Significance — anchoring: on the unidentified-emitting-component problem; on Dong 2026's unresolved illumination dependence and its stated non-separability; on Mallama 2026's unexplained optical secular trends. The primary anchor — the 68/55/none anomaly — does not survive Gate 4.
Reason for silence: Claimed: a disciplinary boundary (data owned by astronomy, method owned by EMC metrology and emitter-signature drift), instrument economics (one-off impact assessments whose deliverable is the aggregate level), fleet turnover faster than a longitudinal baseline accrues, and a data regime only one year old. Gate 4 supplies a simpler and better-evidenced mechanism: there was no puzzle to ask about, because the field's own non-redetections were already explained in print by frequency coverage and sensitivity, and the first-order stability check came out flat. Under the Gate 4 rule that an absent credible reason for silence makes the novelty finding suspect, the inverse applies here — the silence is explained, but by the question's premise being void rather than by a boundary.

Verification then checked that kill against the primary papers and found its load-bearing leg unsupported: Grigg's two mechanisms establish that the two campaigns are not comparable, which makes the non-redetection uninformative about emission change rather than evidence that the emission was unchanged, and no numerical upper limit is published for any of the 55 still-in-orbit non-redetections. What would restore Rejected: a sourced Unresolved on attack 1, 2 or 4 — most plausibly from opening arXiv:2608.11659, arXiv:2512.07341 or arXiv:2412.14483, or from showing that the vehicle-remote-sensing isomorph (SAE 940582, the Denver FEAT series) has already answered the stable-unit-versus-intermittent-state question in a form that transfers.
Verification by the run session (the Gate 4 kill was fatal and sourced, so its three legs were checked against the primary papers; independent fresh-context checker, 14 searches and 6 fetches, both fully used, no refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-31-verification.md). Leg 2 is confirmed; the other two are not supported as stated.
(i) CONFIRMED, with one correction. Grigg et al. 2025 does attribute the non-redetections to frequency non-overlap and to EDA2 sensitivity and nowhere proposes that the satellites' own emission changed: verbatim, "In the first paper by Di Vruno, F. et al. (2023), 68 Starlink satellites are detected", "None of these 68 satellites were detected in our work even though 55 of them were still in orbit during this survey", "the narrowband emission at 125, 135, 143, 150, and 175 MHz does not overlap any of the frequencies in our work", and the v1.5 broadband "being ~1 Jy, which is below the EDA2's sensitivity level in these observations". The correction: the two mechanisms are assigned one per model class rather than jointly to all 68 — "Of these, 12 were model v1.0" and "the other 46 were v1.5 satellites" is 58, leaving 10 of the 68 with no stated class and therefore no stated mechanism (the checker's arithmetic, with 12 and 46 cross-read from the HTML and the PDF conversions to rule out a single OCR slip; the A&A version of record is blocked to this environment). The checker independently re-derived the non-overlap claim from the paper's Table 1 channel centres: the nearest band to Di Vruno's 150 MHz line is centred at 150.78 MHz, roughly 150.32-151.24 MHz, which excludes 150.0 MHz.
(ii) NOT SUPPORTED, and this is the leg the rejection rests on. No formal upper limit or detection threshold in Jy is reported for any of the 55 still-in-orbit non-redetected satellites; the only Jy figure is the ~1 Jy *expected* v1.5 signal, so the sensitivity mechanism is an unquantified plausibility argument rather than a measurement placing each satellite below a stated limit. More decisively, both mechanisms assert that the two campaigns are NOT COMPARABLE, and non-comparability makes the non-redetection uninformative about emission change — it does not establish that the emission was unchanged. The anomaly is defused as evidence, not resolved against the candidate's hypothesis, so "explained in the anchor paper itself" overstates what Grigg does.
(iii) OVERSTATED. Bassa et al. 2024's epoch, instrument and direction are right — two one-hour LOFAR observations on 19 July 2024, the first-generation HBA detections "consistent in flux density and spectral properties" to those detected in the 2022 observation — but that is a population-distribution consistency remark about first-generation satellites as a group, not a per-version stability measurement with an uncertainty budget and not per spacecraft. The paper never states that any individual NORAD ID was observed in both epochs, reports in the same breath that brightness "varies in brightness from satellite to satellite", and demonstrates consistency only above a bright floor: the only stated limit is LBA S_nu < 10 Jy (3 sigma) at 50 and 75 MHz, against detections of "15 Jy to 1300 Jy". A satellite falling from about 1 Jy to well below it in HBA is outside anything this comparison constrains.
(iv) Dong et al. 2026 (arXiv:2605.17150), the record's third paper, names on-orbit age only to control it away — "the reversal could in principle reflect satellite age or commissioning state rather than the DTC payload", handled by restricting the comparison to satellites launched in the same 2024 window — and its design is cross-sectional, with no tracking of individual NORAD IDs over months or years. It supplies no estimate of an age effect in either direction, so it is not a negative answer to the candidate either.
(v) The residual question — whether an individual satellite's UEMR varies over its operational life, so that a prior detection can fall genuinely below a later detection limit — is NOT FOUND posed in print. The nearest printed gestures are Dong's age-as-confound sentence and its recommendation of multi-year monitoring spanning a solar minimum, which is illumination-state seasonality rather than per-spacecraft ageing. Four arXiv items remain unread on an exhausted fetch budget and are recorded as could-not-read rather than absent: 2608.12999 (SNIFFLES I), 2603.07631, 2512.07341 and 2608.11659.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness: the Gate 1 reformulation fixes units, epochs, estimands and a publishable null, and both outcomes are admissible. Held at 2/3 because the canonical question's consequence clause does not follow from its premise — within-satellite variance does not bias an aggregate mean, by linearity — so the question as intaken asserts something its own design cannot deliver, and the bias channel that does survive (truncation at unpublished non-detection thresholds) is a different claim about reporting practice. Fixing the wording is the cheapest promotion step and is listed below.
Significance: the audience is evidenced and is actively building the dependent infrastructure, and adversary 2 supplied the missing link the record lacked — the regulated functional under RA.1513-2 is an exceedance share rather than a mean, so per-satellite duty cycle and variance enter the regulated quantity directly. 2/3 rather than 3/3: the stable branch triggers little action, and the per-satellite limits the consequence leans on sit in a paper nobody has opened.
(Judge's note: well-posedness held at 2/3 as in the record — the intake estimand is not identified by the intake design without the pass-within-epoch replicate level, "matched sensitivity" is never defined as a condition, and "operational life" bundles age, state and software. Significance reduced from the record's 3/3 to 2/3: consequence and audience survive, but the stake is deflated by the published version-level stability result and limb (c)'s dissolution, and no named body is shown to require a distributional per-unit specification. Either score alone would bar Validated (which needs 3/3 well-posedness); the verdict does not turn on them. Disguise was verified — the adversary ran its 9 new-vocabulary searches and returned Resolved — so no unverified-Disguise caveat applies here.)
Strongest remaining objection: the question's consequence clause is not derived and its minimal design is misidentified. Within-satellite temporal variance does not bias an aggregate mean — by linearity of expectation over a sum of per-satellite powers, and a cross-section sampled at arbitrary duty-cycle phases consistently estimates the mean under stationarity — so "aggregate forecasts built from as-launched snapshots are biased" does not follow from variability alone. The one bias channel that could be evidenced, that Grigg publishes no numerical upper limit for any of the 68 non-detections so levels estimated from published detections are truncated at roughly the 1 Jy campaign sensitivity, indicts survey reporting practice rather than satellite ageing, and is fixable by a reporting convention rather than a campaign. Meanwhile the forecasting side is already moving away from the assumption attacked: arXiv:2609.01995 computes measurement-based EPFD distributions scored as an exceedance share against the 2% data-loss criterion of RA.1513-2. And a substantial part of limbs (a) and (b) is purchasable from existing public data today — 112,534 detections of 1,806 identified satellites over four months, about 62 detections per satellite, with launch dates available — which supports the pass-within-epoch term and a cross-sectional age contrast. The candidate survives, but only as the Gate 1 reformulation.
Promotion requires: (i) retiring the canonical "fixed property versus varies" wording, whose first horn is already falsified in print (SNIFFLES I: unintended radiation in 76.9% of observations of one version at 2700 MHz; Grigg: spectral structure changing in time, XX/YY anti-correlated, signal strongest at closest approach); (ii) replacing "aggregate forecasts are biased" with the specific channel asserted — truncation at unpublished non-detection thresholds, a non-stationary fleet age distribution, or non-representative sampling of operating states — and stating that the decision-relevant functional under RA.1513-2 is an exceedance share rather than a mean; (iii) making the first deliverable a re-analysis of the existing public catalogue (pass-within-epoch variance, and a cross-sectional age contrast with model and launch cohort as covariates), with a new two-epoch matched campaign justified only for the epoch-within-satellite term the catalogue cannot identify; (iv) operationalising "sensitivity-matched" with a minimum passes per satellite per epoch, a per-pass detection-efficiency and beam-geometry model and a stated range normalisation, since Grigg's range dependence makes the censoring threshold covariate-dependent and informative; (v) pre-specifying the variance-ratio threshold that counts as a positive result, before data; (vi) adopting the censored-data estimator from exposure science or dynamic-occupancy modelling explicitly, with a stated repair for informative censoring, rather than treating the variance decomposition as novel method; (vii) opening and grading arXiv:2608.11659, arXiv:2512.07341, arXiv:2412.14483 and the full text of arXiv:2609.01995. With (i), (ii) and (vii) done, well-posedness reaches 3/3 and the entry could be Validated.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): re-analyse the existing public Grigg/Dong catalogue rather than proposing a campaign — 112,534 detections of 1,806 identified satellites over four months, with launch dates, gives the pass-within-epoch variance component and a cross-sectional age contrast immediately, and it is the cheapest way to find out whether the epoch-within-satellite term is worth a second epoch at all. Open arXiv:2608.11659, 2512.07341, 2412.14483 and the full arXiv:2609.01995 first; arXiv:2608.12999 has now been graded (abstract) by adversary 2.
Routing: not routed. The entry is Provisional, so it is not an already-asked rejection at all, and the residual question was independently confirmed NOT FOUND posed in print by both the verification checker and adversary 2 — the nearest printed gestures are Dong's age-as-confound sentence, which names age only to exclude it, and its recommendation of multi-year monitoring across a solar minimum, which is illumination-state seasonality rather than per-spacecraft ageing. Nothing for ledger/routed-open-problems.md.
