ID: UQ-20261016-42
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — critical care/anaesthesiology; medical-device validation and regulatory science. Adjacent: biomedical signal processing; measurement-comparison statistics/metrology.
Question (canonical): For continuous or intermittent noninvasive blood-pressure devices evaluated against a fluid-filled intra-arterial reference under a named standard (ISO 81060-3:2022 for continuous automated measurement; per-class analogues declared per dataset), restricted to datasets with retrievable per-pair records and per-line dynamic-response characterisation: (a) for systolic, diastolic and mean pressure separately, how do the device's bias, SD of paired differences and mean squared paired disagreement differ between non-resonant and resonant reference strata, expressed as the fraction of pooled mean squared disagreement contributed by the resonant stratum in excess of its sampling share; and (b) for how many devices does the standard's pass/fail statistic cross its threshold when the analysis is restricted to the non-resonant stratum? (Gate 1 v2; the single permitted reformulation. v1 is in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
1. Is the fluid-filled arterial catheter-transducer system a fit reference standard for BP device validation, given that ~a third of in-service radial lines are underdamped? — NOTE: graded Low at Gate 5. This is Mikhailov & Fabián 2021 nearly verbatim (found by adversary 1, missed by Gate 2).
2. How much of the published cuff/continuous-NIBP-versus-invasive disagreement is the reference's error rather than the device's? — Low (Romagnoli 2014 reports this contrast at one site: systolic IBP−NIBP bias 28.5 vs 4.1 mmHg).
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion on "invasive arterial pressure is the reference". Romagnoli et al., Crit Care 2014;18:644 classed 30.7% (92/300) of radial lines resonant by Gardner fast-flush and derived a waveform-only detector (dP/dt_max 1.67 mmHg/ms; sens 77%, spec 97%). The prevalence limb is answered; the claimed un-asked object was the reference term in device-validation error budgets. Gate 4 showed the gap as stated is not there (see Presuppositions 4/6).
Presuppositions:
1. A nontrivial fraction of in-service arterial lines are dynamically distorted — established at one figure, one setting (30.7%); CONTESTED for generalisability, site and overdamping (prevalence unreported anywhere found).
2. Resonance is identifiable post hoc from a recorded waveform — CONTESTED; detectors exist (Romagnoli dP/dt_max; Rinehart overdamping, sens 98%/spec 92%) but derivation cohorts were sampled far faster than 125 Hz archived monitor data. Adversary 1 adds that f_n moves "by tens of Hz" with every irrigation, so a per-patient label is not even constant.
3. Validation datasets retain, or can regenerate, per-pair records permitting stratification — CONTESTED, untested by anyone; the binding feasibility risk.
4. The standard's pass/fail statistic is a function of the reference, so reference quality can move the verdict — the statistic is, but the framing limb FALSIFIED: ISO 81060-3:2022 cl. 4.3.1 c) is normative on reference dynamic response (adversary 2, primary text).
5. MAP is less distorted than systolic by a second-order catheter system — CONTESTED in the adverse direction (P2: positive and negative errors can cancel into a small mean error). v2 correctly tests SBP/DBP/MAP separately.
6. Device-validation studies do not currently check reference fidelity — FALSIFIED as a statement about the governing requirement (cl. 4.3.1 c), "shall", "for each subject"). Whether studies comply is unmeasured and is a different question.
What would count as an answer: A stratified re-analysis over a pre-specified frame of validation datasets with retrievable paired records, every reference line labelled by a pre-registered fidelity rule (fast-flush where available, waveform-derived otherwise, classifier error propagated), reporting bias, limits of agreement and the standard's pass/fail statistic within strata — the resonant stratum's excess share of pooled MSE, and the devices, if any, whose verdict flips. A prospective validation with fast-flush characterisation of every line answers it directly. Full apportionment requires a declared pseudo-truth (fast-flush-identified inverse-filter reconstruction with propagated uncertainty), and the answer must say which estimand it reports. A null is admissible.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 13 at Gate 2 (against a cap of 11; overrun recorded, minimum-8 met), 9 by adversary 1 and 9 by adversary 2, all new vocabularies — full lists in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-42-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: (Gate 2 q7, mandatory own-field obvious title) "impact of arterial line quality on validation of continuous NIBP accuracy stratified damping" → no paper with this object; nearest hit (JCMC 2024) opened, does not address device validation. (Gate 2 q10, mandatory fraction query) prevalence of resonant/underdamped ABP waveforms over MIMIC → no published fraction over any waveform corpus; only Romagnoli's single-centre figures. (Gate 2 q13, method-owning field) Grubbs estimator / apportioning variance between instruments without a gold standard → mature literature, never applied to the arterial-line reference. (A1 q1, standards/clinical-engineering) AAMI SP10 / ISO 81060 invasive reference damping requirement → surfaced Mikhailov & Fabián 2021, on-point prior Gate 2 missed. (A2 q1, standards/regulatory) ISO 81060-3:2022 reference requirements → sample PDF of the standard itself, containing clause 4.3.1 complete. Access failures of record: ISO 81060-3:2022 full text COULD NOT READ by Gate 2 and adversary 1 (vde-verlag robots-disallowed; iso.org/IEC/national stores paywalled); clauses A.2 and 4.3.4 COULD NOT READ by adversary 2 (sample truncated); NCT06518980 COULD NOT READ by all three (JS shell; API refused/robots-disallowed) — neither prior art nor absence.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Mikhailov Y, Fabián V. "The use of fluid-filled catheters as reference blood pressure monitors." Lékař a technika/Clinician and Technology 2021;51(1-4):5-14, doi:10.14311/CTJ.2021.1.01 — OPENED in full by adversary 1. Unit: two bench catheter systems; endpoint: reference error in mmHg vs dynamic parameters ("tenths of mmHg" at f_n 38.8 Hz/ζ 0.130; "tens of mmHg" at 6.5 Hz/ζ 0.281); comparator: known applied pressure; estimand: fitness of the fluid-filled system as the ISO 81060-2:2018 reference gauge.
P2. "Intra-Arterial Blood Pressure Measurement: Sources of Error and Solutions." medRxiv 2020.08.29.20184275 — OPENED (authors not captured). Unit: simulated waveform per (f_natural, Z) configuration, ranges from fast-flush tests in 121 ICU patients; endpoint: SBP/MAP/DBP error in mmHg vs simulation truth; estimand: the catheter system's own error as a function of its dynamic parameters. No device, no patients' paired records.
P3. Bland JM, Altman DG. "Comparing methods of measurement: why plotting difference against standard method is misleading." Lancet 1995;346:1085-7 — OPENED (www-users.york.ac.uk/~mb55/meas/diffplot.htm; page's own bibliographic line internally inconsistent, volume corroborates the standard citation). Unit: subject measured by two methods; estimand: how to display method-comparison data when both methods err; states within-method error is estimable "only by making repeated measurements by the same method".
P0 (intake anchor, not re-opened; corroborated to title level by both adversaries). Romagnoli et al., Crit Care 2014;18:644. Unit: patient (300 radial lines); endpoint: resonance prevalence and systolic IBP−NIBP bias (28.5 mmHg, LoA −2.9 to 59.6 resonant vs 4.1 mmHg otherwise); estimand: prevalence and magnitude in one population.
P4 (decisive primary text, not a prior formulation but the document the question names). ISO 81060-3:2022 cl. 4.3.1 "Reference invasive blood pressure monitoring equipment", item c) — read in the reseller sample PDF (cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/71161/.../ISO-81060-3-2022.pdf) by adversary 2; clause heading independently confirmed in the ANSI preview TOC.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — P1 qualifies one instrument on a bench with no device under test, no validation dataset, no strata, no apportionment, no pass/fail re-run, and governs the intermittent class (81060-2); but it is this entry's own Alternative formulation 1 asked and partly answered, in a vocabulary Gate 2 never tried. vs P2 — simulation truth, no device, no standard, no strata; parameterises a sensitivity analysis rather than answering. vs P3 — generic method-comparison statistics; names no arterial line, classifier, standard or device class, and is what forces v2's stratified contrast in place of v1's non-identified apportionment. vs P0 — differs on all four attributes and reverses the attribution direction, but performs the stratified bias contrast on exactly the paired difference at one site. vs P4 — the candidate's limb (b) presupposes the move it proposes is not already made by the certification regime; P4 says it is mandated per subject.
Novelty confidence: Medium as graded at Gate 2, not sustained at Gate 4. Downgrade to Low–Medium: the Gate 2 record is demonstrably incomplete in the vocabulary nearest the question (adversary 1 found an on-point standards-facing prior in its first query), and both Disguise sweeps closed Partial rather than Resolved with two near items unread. Not the decisive ground for the verdict.
Significance — consequence: If yes, validation protocols gain a cheap pre-specified inclusion criterion (record and archive the fast flush), part of the standing "noninvasive monitors miss hypotension" conclusion becomes reference artefact, and perioperative-hypotension thresholds inherit a quantified distortion term. If no (metrics indistinguishable across strata for SBP, DBP and MAP alike), the concern is retired with evidence and committees have a reason not to add QC burden. Both directions are actionable.
Significance — audience: Manufacturers and notified bodies for continuous noninvasive BP devices (volume-clamp, pulse-decomposition, cuffless) whose claims rest on invasive-reference validations; FDA reviewers (live cuffless-BP document, surfaced but not opened); developers of cuffless algorithms trained on archived invasive waveforms, whose labels inherit the catheter transfer function — a quantity both adversaries confirm nobody has measured. The flagship claim, that the ISO/IEC committee "must decide whether to specify reference-system dynamic response at the next revision", is inverted: it specified it in the 2022 edition.
Significance — fecundity: Whether cuffless models trained on archived arterial waveforms have partly learned the catheter's transfer function; whether inverse-filter reconstruction should be mandated and how its uncertainty enters a validation budget; whether ±5/±8 mmHg-class criteria are attainable at all given reference uncertainty; site-specific (radial/femoral/brachial) prevalence, where no data exist; whether overdamping moves verdicts the opposite way. Adversary 2 names a further one the kill creates: compliance with cl. 4.3.1 c) in published validations, and residual resonance surviving good-faith compliance.
Significance — anchoring: The cuffless-BP validation-standards controversy, where choice of reference is the central contested methodological point; the unexplained magnitude of cuff-versus-invasive disagreement; the perioperative-hypotension threshold debate.
Reason for silence: Offered mechanism (disciplinary boundary + incentive gap, with an unarchived stratifier underneath) does not hold as written. Its strongest clause — that the standards put reference fidelity "outside the analysis frame by construction" — is contradicted by the text of the standard the question names, and the joint IEC/ISO committee spans both communities and legislated at this seam in 2022. What survives is narrower and explains non-answering rather than non-asking: the fast flush is not machine-recorded and its parameters shift with every irrigation, so the stratifying label was unrecoverable in retrospective datasets until waveform classifiers existed; a passing manufacturer has no reason to reopen the reference and a failing one cannot attack the standard it must certify against. Both adversaries judged this a substitution of "why unrewarding to answer" for "why unasked".
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two adversaries, sequential, fresh contexts, Gate 0–3 record only; A1 9 searches/3 fetches, A2 9 searches/4 fetch attempts; Disguise executed by both (9 new-vocabulary queries each), so Disguise is verified, not unverified. Verification by the run session (two independent fresh-context checkers, because the kill rests on a paywalled standard and a claim that strong should not stand on one reading; 27 searches, 13 fetches, 3 refusals between them; full logs in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-42-verification.md and -verification-standards.md). THE KILL IS CONFIRMED IN THE PRIMARY STANDARD, by both checkers independently, and the scope of what it establishes is narrower than the kill needs it to be — which does not save the candidate, because the premise it falsifies is the candidate's own.
(i) CONFIRMED, in ISO's own official preview of the primary standard (cdn.standards.iteh.ai sample for catalogue record 71161), clause 4.3.1 c), page 5: "The natural frequency and damping coefficient of the reference invasive blood pressure monitoring equipment" ... "shall be examined and optimised to meet dynamic requirements for each subject." All four elements of the claim hold and each was checked separately. It is NORMATIVE — "shall", sited in clause 4, "General requirements for the clinical investigation", not in the informative Annex A. It is PER SUBJECT — "for each subject", not per study. It names BOTH quantities. And it requires BOTH acts, examination and optimisation, not characterisation alone. Conformance for the clause is checked "by inspection of the clinical investigation report". The second checker reached the same text independently and confirmed the modality is "shall" and not "should".
(ii) The standard exists as described and the clause sits where the record says. ISO 81060-3:2022, "Non-invasive sphygmomanometers - Part 3: Clinical investigation of continuous automated measurement type", published 2022-12-16, edition 1, 36 pp, ISO/TC 121/SC 3, stage 90.92. Clause 4.3.1 runs a) to f), not a) to c): b) requires conformity to IEC 60601-2-34, d) levelling to the right atrium, e) removal of air bubbles and clots, f) permits modification of equipment that does not output waveform or beat-to-beat data. Those are adjacent normative requirements on the same reference line and belong in the record.
(iii) THREE LIMITS ON WHAT THE CLAUSE ESTABLISHES, all refutations of things the record implies. The clause prescribes NO METHOD: "resonance", "fast flush", "flush test" and "intra-arterial" appear nowhere in the readable text, so "ISO 81060-3 mandates a square-wave test per subject" would be an overreach. It states NO NUMERIC THRESHOLD, only "to meet dynamic requirements", deferring the numbers to IEC 60601-2-34, to bibliography Reference [1], and to informative clause A.2 — none of which could be read. And the finding belongs to Part 3 ALONE among documents actually verified: ISO 81060-2, ANSI/AAMI SP10, the 2018 Universal Standard, the AHA and ESH statements, IEEE 1708 and IEC 60601-2-34 were all COULD-NOT-READ, so nothing here licenses a statement about what "the standards" require. Part 2's reference is auscultation, for which natural frequency and damping are meaningless, and a secondary source asserting otherwise is flagged as doubtful.
(iv) THE CONFORMITY GAP IS REAL AND IS NOT THE SAME AS THE PREMISE. The requirement appears to go unevidenced in practice. The one ISO 81060-3 validation study opened (Lai et al. 2026) reports no dynamic-response characterisation of any kind and yet marks clause 4.3.1 PASS on the strength of naming the bedside monitor; a medRxiv source states that routine clinical practice performs no quantitative characterisation at all; and no publication was found that apportions a validation study's error between the device under test and the reference line, or that re-analyses a validation dataset restricted to non-resonant lines (NOT FOUND, not refuted). So three things separate cleanly, and the record should keep them apart: the STANDARD requires it normatively and per subject; the CLINICAL literature supplies the square-wave method the standard omits, as good practice; VALIDATION STUDIES, on a sample of one, do not report doing it. The gap between the first and the third is an informative absence about conformity assessment. It is not evidence that the standard is silent, which is what the candidate's framing needed.
(v) Prior 1 confirmed on its numbers and corrected on its reading. Romagnoli et al., Crit Care 2014;18:644: systolic invasive-minus-noninvasive bias 28.5 (SD 15.9) mmHg in the resonant stratum against 4.1 mmHg in the non-resonant one, 92 and 208 patients of 300. Four corrections travel with it. Per-stratum MEASUREMENT counts are not reported — only totals (11,610 IBP pulses, 1,200 NIBP measurements) — so no measurement-level count may be quoted by stratum. The resonance classification is a graphical three-region criterion in Figure 3 with no numeric cutoff printed; the Figure 2 values (AR 0.43, beta 0.28, 12.5 Hz) are a worked example and the dP/dt(MAX) 1.67 mmHg/msec figure is a proposed detector, neither being the grouping rule. The paper assigns no pass/fail verdict under any device standard and names none; its ">10 mmHg clinically relevant / >20 mmHg clinically unacceptable" threshold is a cited clinical-relevance claim, not a conformity criterion. And its direction of inference runs OPPOSITE to a device validation: the invasive line is the object under scrutiny and the oscillometric reading is the comparator, so 28.5 mmHg is evidence about resonant arterial lines, not evidence that a noninvasive device failed. Two internal defects worth carrying: the printed limits-of-agreement formula "bias x 1.96 SD" is a typo for bias +/- 1.96 SD (the non-resonant LoA -6.19 to 14.40 has midpoint 4.105 and half-width 10.295, giving SD 5.25 against the printed 5.3), and the Results text's "30%" resonant in the vascular surgery theatre disagrees with Table 1's 20/70 = 28.6%.
(vi) Fidelity caveats. The decisive sentence came back as two contiguous verbatim excerpts rather than one uninterrupted rendering, because the fetch tool caps quotations at about 125 characters and a second pass declined full reproduction on copyright grounds; both fragments were returned on two independent passes and the modality was separately confirmed, but a word-for-word transcription would need the purchased PDF. The ISO preview stops inside clause 4.3.3, so clause 4.3.4, all of clause 5 and its acceptance criteria, and all of Annex A including A.2 — which NOTE 1 names as the home of the guidance on this very requirement — are unread. One checker overran its fetch budget by one call, spent on the second pass at the decisive clause.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete. The fatal attack-4 ground was tested against the primary document it rests on, by two checkers independently, and held.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 (v2 fixes identifiability for the stratified limb and names standard, endpoints and error propagation, but the headline apportionment is identified only under a pseudo-truth whose validity is itself contested, feasibility presupposition 3 is untested, and limb (b)'s framing premise is now contradicted by the named standard's text) · Significance 2/3 (consequence actionable in both directions and fecundity ample; the flagship standards-committee audience claim is inverted, leaving manufacturers, notified bodies, FDA and cuffless-label developers)
Strongest remaining objection: ISO 81060-3:2022 clause 4.3.1 c) makes examination and optimisation of the reference invasive system's natural frequency and damping coefficient a normative, per-subject requirement of the very standard the canonical question names. That falsifies presupposition 6 and the reason-for-silence mechanism, and structurally empties limb (b): in a compliant dataset the resonant stratum is supposed to be empty by protocol, so restricting to it is either a no-op or a compliance audit of 4.3.1 c) — an already-askable and different question — rather than the error-apportionment question posed. The one soft spot, stated by the adversary against its own kill: it read a reseller's sample rather than the purchased document, the full item was not transcribed verbatim, and clauses A.2 and 4.3.4 were unreadable, so no numerical meaning of "dynamic requirements" was established. Reading A.2 and 4.3.4 is the cheap check that would settle whether this drops to Partial — but it would not promote the entry above Provisional, since attack 7 is Unresolved independently and well-posedness is 2/3.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Buy and read ISO 81060-3:2022 clauses 4.3.1, 4.3.4 and A.2 in the purchased document, and determine whether any published 81060-3-era validation reports compliance with 4.3.1 c) or retains resonant lines. That settles whether anything of this candidate survives, and in what form.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The rejection ground is presupposition failure at Gate 4, not asked-but-still-open: the question's framing premise is contradicted by the governing standard, and the nearest prior (Mikhailov & Fabián 2021) partly answers the fitness formulation rather than leaving it open. Per ENVIRONMENT, answered and disguised-known rejections are not routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The residual question the kill creates — does a compliant reference line still ring, and do published validations report 4.3.1 c) compliance — is a fresh candidate for a later batch, not a routed open problem.

ID: UQ-20261016-43
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): STEM — electrocatalysis / energy materials (OER durability reporting). Method fields: biostatistics (censored survival analysis), reliability engineering (life data with suspensions, competing risks). Also metascience.

Question (canonical): Treating each published electrocatalyst durability run as a right-censored lifetime observation whose censoring time is the author's chosen test duration: what lifetime distribution does the published corpus actually support, and is the censoring informative — does the stopping time depend on the degradation the experimenter was watching? (Gate 1 reformulation, the graded version, adds a pre-specified frame (OER, pH class, current-density band, cell type), one pre-fixed failure definition (overpotential at fixed current exceeds its run-initial value by a pre-fixed Delta), and four limbs: (i) stopping-time distribution and mass on convention values (10/12/24/100/500/1000 h); (ii) Kaplan-Meier plus Weibull/lognormal fit with pre-registered sensitivity over the comparability restriction and a stated publication-selection model; (iii) does end-of-run degradation rate predict stopping time given design covariates, which under non-informative censoring it should not; (iv) test duration needed to separate two catalysts at 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05. Both versions are in the record.)

Alternative formulations:
1. Are headline claims such as "stable for 100 h at 10 mA cm-2" statements about catalysts, or about the conventional durations at which this field stops testing?
2. Read as censored life data, how many reported "stable" results carry lifetime estimates distinguishable from one another, and what duration would separate two candidates at stated power?

Motivating gap:
Reported durations cluster on human-convenient values; the field's documented response has been metric invention and shorter surrogates (S-number, accelerated stress tests) rather than treating its own stopping times as a statistical object with a censoring distribution. The transplanted machinery (right censoring with suspensions, competing risks, tests for informative censoring) is mature, and the interface friction is real: here the censoring time is set by the person watching the outcome, the case independent-censoring assumptions exclude.

Presuppositions:
P1 durations and "degrading at stop" recoverable at scale from reports — CONTESTED (figure reading; extraction error must be measured on a hand-coded subsample). P2 stops are experimenter-chosen, not imposed — CONTESTED (equipment/shift/protocol-fixed stops are non-informative by construction; censoring-reason taxonomy required). P3 one comparable failure definition can be pre-specified — CONTESTED (frame may shrink severely; shrinkage is a reportable result). P4 publication selection acts on which tests are reported — CONTESTED, weakly identifiable. P5 "lifetime" is a meaningful latent quantity for a material-plus-conditions pair — CONTESTED (non-monotone/recoverable degradation forces a competing-risks fallback). P6 (Gate 1) the failure definition is reached often enough for a non-degenerate estimate — CONTESTED (near-degenerate KM is an admissible answer).

What would count as an answer:
A pre-registered extraction over a defined frame yielding: the stopping-time distribution with heaping quantified; a Kaplan-Meier plus parametric fit under the stated failure definition with sensitivity bands; a direct test of informative censoring conditioned on design covariates; and the power-based duration number. Plus a measured extraction-error rate and a censoring-reason taxonomy with its missingness rate. A null on (iii) with a degenerate (ii) is an admissible, pre-declared answer.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result):
42 distinct queries in total: 11 at Gate 2, plus 8 / 11 / 9 from adversaries 1-3 (28 of those in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use: perovskite-PV and ISOS/T80, thermal-catalysis time-on-stream, LLM/text-mined catalysis corpora, optional-stopping metascience, Type I/curtailed/sudden-death reliability, econometric endogenous stopping, PEM-electrolyzer testing reviews, reporting-bias metascience, Chinese-language). Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-43-record.md and UQ-20261016-43-adversary-{1,2,3}.md. Most informative: "trends in reported stability test durations OER electrocatalysts literature survey" -> stability reviews only, no duration distribution; "fraction of papers reporting OER stability histogram of test durations 10 h 24 h 100 h" -> no published histogram or fraction; "Spori Strasser 2017 stability challenges of oxygen evolving catalysts literature survey test duration statistics" -> the one partial hit on limb (i) (below); "Perovskite Database stability test duration T80 right-censored survival analysis" -> Graniero et al. 2023, which holds test length plus end state for ~42,400 devices and declines to extrapolate; "treating published experiments as censored observations meta-analysis follow-up duration dependent censoring" -> clinical estimand literature only; "informative censoring experiment stopping time depends on observed degradation reliability life data" -> mature named method family, never applied to a publication corpus. No query in any vocabulary returned a survival function, a censoring model or an informative-censoring test over any published stability corpus.
COULD NOT READ (grounds nothing in either direction): Spori et al. 2017 Supporting Information (the runtime histograms themselves); Ligorati et al. 2026 CEJ full text by abstract only at Gate 2 but read in full by adversary 1 via the Augsburg OPUS PDF (doi.org, linkinghub and sciencedirect all failed); Chem. Soc. Rev. 2024 d3cs00010a; PMC11434886 and PMC11613331 (PMC hard-blocked, no publisher DOI in hand); Knoppel et al. 2021 Nat. Commun. full paper (authors' Behind-the-Paper post read instead); Khenkin et al. 2020 ISOS consensus statement; Holzhey & Saliba 2018; Nankai 2023 "big data perovskite stability analysis" press item.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
PRIOR 1 (closest; own field, limb (i)) — Spori, Kwan, Bonakdarpour, Wilkinson & Strasser (2017), "The Stability Challenges of Oxygen Evolving Electrocatalysts", Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 56, 5994-6021, DOI 10.1002/anie.201608601. Opened (TU Berlin repository full text; SI unread). Unit: a published test parameter in a surveyed report. Endpoint: frequency of reported test parameters, runtime among them ("We summarize the most frequently occurring test parameters, reported in the literature in frequency histograms"; runtimes "either 24 or 100 h"; Table 3 spans 2 h to 60,000-80,000 h). Comparator: none; descriptive. Estimand: modal/typical reported conditions, PEM single-cell subset.
PRIOR 2 (closest sibling-field lifetime corpus) — Gevorgyan et al. (2016), "Baselines for lifetime of organic solar cells", Adv. Energy Mater. Opened (UAB PDF). Unit: one aged device (983 devices from 303 articles). Endpoint: T80/TS80; for unfinished runs Tfinal-T0 is substituted as "the minimum possible lifetime" — de facto right censoring, never named. Comparator: none; log-binned histograms, averages and maxima. Estimand: descriptive lifetime baselines per technology. Adjacent: Graniero et al. (2023), Front. Energy Res. 11:1118654 (opened twice independently) — ~42,400 devices from >15,000 papers, only 1,834 with measured T80, declines imputation from test length because "the wide variety of aging behaviors would make such extrapolation highly uncertain"; estimand is predictive R2, not survival.
PRIOR 3 (neighbouring energy-materials corpus modelling) — Ligorati, Geyer-Klingeberg, Gunther & Rathgeber (2026), "Degradation of lithium-ion batteries: a meta-analysis", Chem. Eng. J., DOI 10.1016/j.cej.2026.174528. Full text opened by adversary 1 (Augsburg OPUS PDF). Unit: one degradation-rate effect size nested in study (917 from 146). Endpoint: %/cycle rate. Comparator: meta-regression covariate levels. Estimand: conditional mean DegRate. Quoted: "We excluded moderators with substantial missing numerical data, such as experimental duration"; ~55% of observations extrapolate the slope past the observed window. (The record's Prior 3, arXiv:1805.01834, was verified real by adversary 2 — patient-level time-to-AE estimands under varying, administratively set follow-up — and is retained as a structural analogue, not a near prior.)

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs PRIOR 1: Prior 1 publishes a descriptive runtime frequency histogram for the PEM single-cell subset, so limb (i) is not wholly unmeasured in the candidate's own field — this is the sharpest novelty erosion in the record and refutes the Gate 2 claim that the quantity is uncomputed for that subset. It has no heaping statistic, no aqueous-cell counterpart, no censoring indicator, no survival object; limbs (ii)-(iv) are untouched by it.
vs PRIOR 2: shares the lifetime estimand and reaches censoring in substance (lower-bound substitution; stored test length plus end state) but never names it, fits no survival function, analyses no duration distribution, and never asks whether the stop depends on observed degradation; Graniero et al. stopped precisely at the threshold of limb (ii) and said why.
vs PRIOR 3: endpoint is a rate measured during the test, not time to a failure definition; test length is explicitly excluded as a moderator and unfinished runs are linearly extrapolated, with no stopping or censoring model — so it does not collapse limbs (i) or (iii), which the record named as its main vulnerability and adversary 1 settled by reading it.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: 42 queries across the candidate's own words, the method-owning fields' words and six neighbouring literatures found no survival, censoring or stopping-time analysis of any published stability corpus; three independent agents reached that negative. Not High: limb (i) is partly pre-empted in the field's own literature by Prior 1 (SI unread, so how far is unmeasured); Prior 2's corpora already hold the censored data structure; and several plausibly on-point own-field and sibling-field items remain unread (Spori SI, d3cs00010a, two PMC OER-stability reviews, Khenkin 2020, Holzhey & Saliba 2018, the Nankai 2023 item).

Significance — consequence:
If censoring is informative, every literature-derived durability ranking is biased with an estimable sign, benchmark tables need a censoring indicator, and literature-trained stability predictors are fitting censored times as if they were outcomes. If uninformative, the field gains a legitimate pooled lifetime estimate conditional on the publication filter and a design number ("N hours to separate A from B at 80% power") that currently no committee can produce. The pre-declared negative — the corpus supports no lifetime statement beyond the modal stopping time — would itself mean a decade of durability claims measures community convention.

Significance — audience:
(1) Electrocatalysis groups: a censoring-reason field, a "degrading at stop" flag, run-to-failure for headline claims. (2) Journals and referees setting stability-reporting requirements: an auditable checklist item in place of "test longer"; such bodies demonstrably convene on this axis (ISOS consensus statement in the sibling field; PEM testing-procedure reviews; active OER work on shortening stress tests). (3) Electrolyzer developers and funders setting 40,000-80,000 h targets — discounted: the field's own specialists find aqueous model-cell stability off by orders of magnitude from MEA operation, so extrapolation value is limited whatever the censoring structure. (4) Materials-informatics groups whose literature-mined stability labels exist only as free text ("excellent stability of 100 h", "more than 250 h").

Significance — fecundity:
A competing-risks formulation separating dissolution, reconstruction, substrate corrosion and bubble-induced loss; a censoring-reason taxonomy as a new covariate class; informative-censoring-corrected rankings; whether accelerated protocols shift the censoring distribution rather than the lifetime distribution; heaping structure by journal, year or lab as measurable sociology; direct transfer to perovskite T80, membrane fouling and thermal-catalysis time-on-stream.

Significance — anchoring:
The activity-stability trade-off; the metric debate the S-number was invented to settle; the lab-to-stack durability gap and the extrapolation it forces on reliability engineering; electrocatalysis benchmarking and reproducibility; and lifetime inference under heavy censoring set by the observer.

Reason for silence:
An incentive gap across a disciplinary boundary. Confirmed and narrowed by adversaries: three statistically literate neighbouring teams (OPV 2016, perovskite 2023, LIB 2026) held exactly the needed data — stop time plus reached-threshold-or-not — and each handled unfinished runs with an unnamed ad hoc fix (minimum-possible-lifetime substitution; declined imputation; moderator exclusion plus linear extrapolation) without using the word censoring. Modelling the material is rewarded; auditing the corpus's own stopping behaviour yields no new material and implicates referees' own headline claims. The record's "the field's data model has no slot for the stopping point" is demoted: the sibling field has the slot and the question is unasked there anyway. A rival deflating explanation stands unexcluded: the answer is presumed known as an open secret.

Verification by the run session (one fresh-context checker over the nearest prior and the informative-censoring literature; 14 searches, 6 fetches, 3 refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-43-verification.md). The verdict stands at Provisional and the novelty finding strengthens materially. The access failure in the record was not a paywall: the full text is CC-BY and was found on the first search.
(i) ACCESS: the prior is open. Ligorati et al. 2026 is freely readable at https://opus.bibliothek.uni-augsburg.de/opus4/files/128353/128353.pdf (OPUS Augsburg docId 128353), CC-BY 4.0. doi.org, linkinghub and ScienceDirect were never needed. The DOI, journal, authors and year all check out.
(ii) THE PRIOR'S ENDPOINT IS MATERIALLY MISCHARACTERISED IN THE RECORD, AND THE CORRECTION CUTS BOTH WAYS. DegRate is not "a rate observed during the test, not a time to failure". The paper defines it by a failure threshold — "we define the DegRate as a capacity loss leading to 80 % of the initial capacity" — and states "Therefore, DegRate is an end-of-life benchmark, not a local slope at a specific cycle number". It is 20 percentage points divided by cycles to that threshold, i.e. a reciprocal transform of a failure time. So the prior is CLOSER to the candidate on endpoint than the record allowed, and further from it on method, which is the distinction that matters.
(iii) AND THE PRIOR CONTAINS THE CANDIDATE'S OWN ANOMALY, UNNAMED. By its own account, "Approximately 55% (344 out of 627) of DegRates in the regression dataset are estimated using partial cycling data because the 80% end-of-life threshold was not reached", computed by "dividing the observed capacity fade by the number of cycles up to the last reported cycle" under an acknowledged linear extrapolation. That is 54.9% of the estimation sample consisting of right-censored failure times, handled by extrapolation, under a name that never mentions censoring. The paper bounds it only with a 90%/80% ratio sensitivity check it calls "conservative" and "worst-case", never states a direction of bias, and never asks whether cells that failed to reach 80% differ systematically from those that did. One number is worth carrying: its upper range of 8 %/cycle implies an end-of-life of 2.5 cycles, which is not a physically meaningful cell lifetime and suggests the right tail is dominated by short-window extrapolations rather than observed threshold crossings. The paper does not comment on this; it is an inference from its own figures.
(iv) THE DECISIVE ABSENCE IS CONFIRMED AND UNDERSTATED. Every censoring and survival term is absent from the full text — censor in any form, right-censored, survival, time-to-failure, Weibull, Kaplan-Meier, hazard, informative censoring, competing risks — with no censoring indicator, no statement of how long any test ran, and no statement of why any test stopped. And the paper does not do the weaker thing either: test duration is not even a covariate, having been dropped for missing data ("We excluded moderators with substantial missing numerical data, such as experimental duration, battery mass, and electrolyte composition."). It raises publication bias and runs no test of it, by its own admission, and contemplates selection on reported results but never on stopping time.
(v) Three counting corrections. The 917 effect sizes across 146 studies are the full sample; the meta-regression that the record's comparator and estimand describe runs on 627 observations across 88 studies, a listwise-deletion loss of 290 and 58. The record's covariate "groups" are not the paper's: it names five categories in section 2.2 and four in its conclusion, chemistry is not a group but sits under "battery differences", and cut-off voltage and temperature are individual moderators. The paper also contradicts itself on moderators — "67 moderator variables" in five categories in section 2.2 against "46 moderators ... categorized into four groups" in the conclusion — so any citation of a moderator count must say which section it came from. And "pooled" is the checker's word, not the paper's; "conditional mean" is the paper's own and is confirmed.
(vi) THE CENTRAL NEGATIVE HOLDS, WITH A TELLING COMPARATOR. Fourteen targeted queries found nothing treating a corpus of published durability tests as right-censored lifetime data whose censoring time is the experimenter's chosen stop, nor any test of whether that censoring is informative. The three adjacent things separate cleanly: ordinary reliability life-data analysis of engineering test data, where censoring is designed and the analyst owns the stopping rule, is abundant and textbook; meta-analysis of published degradation rates exists, including this prior, an Augsburg photovoltaics sibling, NREL's PV compendium and a Nature Communications perovskite database analysis; and treating the literature's own stopping decisions as a possibly-informative censoring mechanism was NOT FOUND. The sharpest evidence for the gap is that perovskite paper: it analyses 7,419 literature devices with a true time-to-failure endpoint (TS80), uses no censoring methods at all, extrapolates by exponential decay instead, and never mentions that the experimenters chose the test durations.
(vii) Method limitation on the absence findings: the proxy refused both raw curl and urllib to the PDF host, so the keyword absences are the fetch tool's reader scanning the full extracted text, corroborated across two independent passes, rather than a grep the checker ran itself.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete. Nothing fatal was dissolved — three adversaries, no Unresolved attack — and the Gate 1 well-posedness re-grade to 2/3, not novelty, is what bars Validated.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness is re-graded down from the record's 3/3 at this gate: limbs (i), (ii) and (iv) state the evidence that settles them, but limb (iii) — the limb carrying the question's distinctive content — states a null that is false under time-varying mean degradation, a premise sourced to opened own-field texts by adversary 3 and reached independently by adversaries 1 and 2. A mis-specified null is not a vagueness complaint: as written the test would reject under fully non-informative censoring. Significance holds at 2/3: consequence and audiences (1), (2), (4) survive with sourced evidence of standing committees, discounted for audience (3)'s conceded inflation, for severe frame shrinkage under P3, for P4's weak identifiability, and because the likely delivered output is a negative plus a modal stopping time.

Strongest remaining objection: Limb (iii)'s informative-censoring test is invalid as specified — because the end-of-run degradation rate is measured in a window whose position and length are determined by the stopping time, any time-varying mean degradation rate (sourced for this regime: MEA "stabilization ... after several hours", stability "strongly dependent on the time of measurement") makes the regressor a function of the regressand under fully non-informative censoring, so the pre-registered null would be rejected and read as informative censoring even if no author ever looked at the curve; and the record's own mechanism for informative stopping (crop at the convention value) removes the signal, making a null uninterpretable in the other direction.
Promotion requires: re-specify limb (iii) as a landmark / hazard-of-stopping analysis (degradation rate measured in a common absolute window among runs surviving to it, predicting the subsequent stop hazard, or within-run slope change against a fixed terminal window), declare the one-sided cropping asymmetry and define the unit as the reported trace rather than the test, which restores well-posedness to 3/3; and read, via publisher routes only, the Spori et al. 2017 Supporting Information (to reposition limb (i) as the aqueous-cell complement to an existing PEM runtime histogram rather than a first measurement), Chem. Soc. Rev. 2024 d3cs00010a, PMC11434886 and PMC11613331 by converted DOI, Khenkin et al. 2020, Holzhey & Saliba 2018 and the Nankai 2023 item, confirming none reports a stopping-time distribution, a survival fit or a stopping-behaviour analysis. Novelty is then Medium with limb (i) partly pre-empted, which is sufficient; High is not required.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open the Spori et al. 2017 Supporting Information to see what the existing runtime histogram already covers, then draw the frame on a small hand-coded pilot of OER reports and report the frame-shrinkage count and the extraction-error rate before any model is fitted.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected.

ID: UQ-20261016-44
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine/biology — surgical pathology, archival-tissue molecular profiling, cancer epidemiology; adjacent: external/historical-control trial methodology, FFPE pre-analytics. Source method: new-instrument question.
Question (canonical): Within a single pathology archive, for one diagnosis held fixed by re-review of every era's slides under one contemporary protocol and by re-staining from the block, and on one pre-specified molecular panel assayed in a single batch-randomised run: (a) what is the accession-era effect on the tumour's molecular profile across >=3 eras, (b) what is the block-age/fixation-era artefact estimated from era-matched internal controls (paired non-neoplastic tissue from the same blocks; same-era blocks of other diagnoses), and (c) does the era effect in (a), net of (b) and reported with its interval, exceed the between-cohort molecular distance that external- and historical-control borrowing already tolerates? "No era effect distinguishable from artefact at achievable sample size" is a pre-specified admissible answer. (R1, the one Gate 1 reformulation, adopted.)
Alternative formulations: (V0, as intaken) Now that decades-old FFPE blocks are profilable, is the molecular phenotype of a histologically and immunophenotypically identical diagnosis constant across accession eras, or has it drifted enough that historical patients are not biologically exchangeable with contemporary ones? (lay) Is a 1975 cancer the same disease, on the inside, as a 2020 cancer a pathologist would give the same name? (trial-methods) Is the exchangeability assumption behind historical and external control arms testable at the molecular level in archival tissue, and does it survive the test?
Motivating gap: Historical/external controls and Bayesian dynamic-borrowing priors justify exchangeability from clinical covariates; the molecular layer went unchecked because archival material was treated as unreadable, a constraint now removed (Osaki 2026 decade-resolved FFPE proteomics 1972-2022; Krieger 2018 CNV back to the 1980s). Known secular findings (stage/grade migration, Will Rogers, subtype-mix shifts) are all between-class; this asks whether the inside of a fixed class changed. Correction from Gate 4: the premise is not "silent" — the FDA externally-controlled-trials guidance (fda.gov/media/164960/download, opened by adversary 2) names changing diagnostic criteria, changing natural history, changing standard of care and assay comparability explicitly. It is named and unquantified, not unnoticed; the gap is narrower than the record claimed.
Presuppositions: P1 era artefact separable from era biology (CONTESTED, the crux; rests on an unmeasured artefact-transport assumption across tissue types). P2 a histologic/immunophenotypic class can be held fixed across eras (CONTESTED; re-staining depends on era-decaying antigenicity, so class-fixing is itself artefact-exposed). P3 archives retain early-era blocks with outcome data (partly established, archive-specific, retention is itself selection). P4 molecular-level exchangeability is currently untested (search-based negative only). P5 a panel exists on which "same disease" should be era-invariant (CONTESTED; pre-specification required). P6 drift would be attributable to era biology rather than archive composition (CONTESTED; R1 disclaims cause). Gate 4 added P7: for classes now defined molecularly, fixing the class conditions on part of the profile being measured. P8 (adversary 3, decisive): that a between-cohort molecular distance tolerated by borrowing exists at all.
What would count as an answer: within one archive, grade- and marker-matched cases of one diagnosis from >=3 accession eras, re-reviewed under one contemporary protocol, profiled on one pre-specified panel in a single batch-randomised run alongside era-matched internal controls, with an estimand separating era effect from block-age artefact; the era effect reported with its interval against the measured artefact magnitude, and against what borrowing tolerates. A null at achievable n is admissible and informative.

Significance — consequence: if drift exceeds artefact, the covariate-only justification for external/historical controls loses an unquantified molecular premise and part of cross-era survival improvement reassigns to within-class case-mix change; if drift is not distinguishable from artefact at achievable n, borrowing gains its first molecular-level check and the measured artefact becomes a published ceiling on hidden drift. Both branches survive Gate 4; the headline comparative claim does not, because limb (c)'s benchmark has no referent.
Significance — audience: real and evidenced, against the record's own caveat — the FDA guidance (opened, adversary 2) treats historical controls as a subset of external controls, does not require contemporaneity, and names time-related threats, so trialists/regulators are a genuine audience; cancer epidemiologists running 40-50-year historical-cohort comparisons and FFPE pre-analytics groups are unaffected by the horizon objection. Weakened: borrowing in practice spans a few years, the regulated analogue (toxicology) already handles drift by a 2-7-year contemporaneity window rather than by measuring anything, and no interpolation from a 50-year estimate to a 3-5-year gap is supplied.
Significance — fecundity: whether drift concentrates in treatment- vs exposure-selected pathways; whether prognostic models of a fixed class need an accession-era covariate; whether old-cohort-derived signatures are miscalibrated on contemporary patients; whether stage/grade migration is partly molecular; what an era term does to borrowing operating characteristics. The proposed import of palaeogenomic damage-index machinery is no longer novel fecundity — it has been done (AMP 2025).
Significance — anchoring: Will Rogers phenomenon and stage/grade migration; the live external-control regulatory debate; unexplained decade gradients inside the archival-feasibility literature (P3's CNV counts, P2's antigen-integrity losses); and, newly, the toxicologic-pathology HCD problem of separating diagnostic from biological drift, which that field states it has not solved.
Reason for silence: mechanism (3) survives and is the one doing the work — era variation IS artefact by professional definition to the field that owns the material, so a quantity one field is obliged to normalise away is not one it will propose as a signal; independently corroborated in biobank serology (storage-artefact studies exist only to subtract it) and by Barnes 2008, which met an era difference in a molecular readout and attributed it wholly to handling. Mechanism (1) "new instrument" survives only in restricted form (decade-resolved multi-omics of 50-year-old blocks is 2026-vintage; large-scale FFPE expression profiling was mature by 2012 and two-marker era contrasts by 2008). Mechanism (2) disciplinary boundary is falsified for toxicologic pathology.

Verification by the run session (one fresh-context checker, principally an access task over the three closest own-field papers plus the borrowing-tolerance question; 10 searches, 13 fetches, 8 refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-44-verification.md). The verdict stands. The fatal attack-4 ground is confirmed and its supporting detail is struck; the novelty picture narrows sharply, because two of the three "closest own-field papers" turn out not to be priors at all.
(i) THE FATAL GROUND IS CONFIRMED. No published tolerance threshold for historical or external control borrowing is expressed as a MOLECULAR or biomarker DISTANCE — NOT FOUND. Published tolerances are denominated in other units entirely: calendar recency, outcome-parameter drift, and covariate balance. So limb (c)'s comparator is a construct the study would have to invent, which is what attack 4 says.
(ii) BUT THE ADVERSARY'S SUPPORTING FIGURE IS STRUCK. There is no published 2-to-7-year recency limit — NOT FOUND. The only numeric recency rule of thumb located in a primary source is hedged and indication-specific: "more than say 10 years old for docetaxel in this indication should be avoided". Two further precision points belong with it. The per-year drift figures in Hatswell et al. (0.3% ORR, 0.5% PFS, 0.9% OS) and the "5% better than historical controls" figure are OBSERVED MAGNITUDES, not tolerances anyone proposed as a bound, and treating them as thresholds would overstate the literature. And Pocock's recency criterion is qualitative ("recent", "roughly the same time period"), with no numeric cutoff on covariate balance at all — no standardised mean difference, no propensity-overlap bound — so any claim that borrowing has an established quantitative covariate-balance tolerance is unsupported.
(iii) TWO OF THE THREE "CLOSEST OWN-FIELD PAPERS" ARE NOT PRIORS. Chaturvedi et al. is identified exactly as "Human Papillomavirus and Rising Oropharyngeal Cancer Incidence in the United States", J Clin Oncol 29(32):4294-4301 (2011), and it is the excluded prevalence-trend case: its estimand is the trend in HPV prevalence across four calendar periods and the annual percent change in incidence by HPV status, with the marker defining the subtype whose frequency is tracked, and no era-matched or same-era ageing control in the readable text. Its settling sentence: "Trends in HPV prevalence across four calendar periods were estimated by using logistic regression." The "Western Poland" item is Majewski et al. 2026, Front Oncol 16:1651941, read IN FULL, and it is not the candidate's design either.
(iv) AND MAJEWSKI CARRIES THE CANDIDATE'S OWN ARTEFACT, UNRAISED. It is misdescribed by the shorthand "two-decade comparison": it compares two five-year windows, 1998-2002 and 2016-2020, about eighteen years apart. Its older cohort's blocks were roughly 24-28 years old at analysis against 6-10 years for the newer, and antigen decay in older blocks biases Ki-67 downward in the 1998-2002 arm — the same direction as its headline result, Ki-67 higher in 2016-2020 at p = 0.02. That is precisely the artefact this candidate's question is about, present in a published comparison that never raises it. Ninety-two patients across the two periods, confirmed.
(v) THE ONE REMAINING UNREAD PAPER CANNOT BE READ BY ANY ROUTE, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A FAILURE. Osaki et al. 2026, Proteomics, DOI 10.1002/pmic.70161, page identifier e70161, PMID 42363772, has NO open-access copy in existence: OpenAlex and Unpaywall report is_oa false, best_oa_location url and pdf_url both null, pmcid null. The repeated access failures across three agents were not a routing defect — there is nothing to route to, and any further attempt should be an interlibrary or paywall request rather than another mirror hunt. What the abstract does establish: it is NOT purely an assay-stability paper, since it carries a same-case, same-era internal ageing reference ("The muscle layer exhibited the highest stability, serving as a structural reference for evaluating archival ageing"), and it does decompose era variance. But its endpoint is detectability and fidelity, era is framed as a shift to absorb ("storage- and archival-era-associated shifts should be explicitly accounted for in analysis and interpretation"), and its biological claim is era-INVARIANCE, that "a core set of differentially expressed proteins ... were consistently preserved across the evaluable year groups". Whether a formal era-by-biology interaction was fitted sits in paywalled Methods. It is not graded from the abstract, in either direction.
(vi) So the record's "three closest own-field papers remain unread and so ground no grade" becomes: two are read and excluded, one is unreadable anywhere and stays ungraded. The novelty risk is one paper, not three. The verdict does not move, because it rests on Gate 4, not on Gate 2.
(vii) Two route notes for later runs, both worth more than this entry. api.openalex.org is reachable through the fetch tool even though identical requests by raw curl are refused by the egress proxy with a 403 on CONNECT, so an agent concluding "OpenAlex is blocked" from a curl failure is wrong; that single route supplied one abstract and one authoritative citation here. And ascopubs.org is blocked at the network layer, not merely bot-walled — the proxy's own failure log records a 403 on CONNECT — so for an article whose only location is ascopubs, "bronze open access" in OpenAlex does not mean a readable copy exists from here. Related trap: the TMC DigitalCommons record for Chaturvedi is dated 2023, volume 41, issue 17, because it indexes the 2023 JCO republication; the PDF behind it is a cover page with no Methods or Results, and that year must not be propagated.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete. The fatal ground was tested and held; what fell was one illustrative figure inside it.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3 (judge's revision from the record's 3/3: consequence and audience survive on opened evidence, but the comparative limb carrying the headline claim has no referent)
Strongest remaining objection: Limb (c) presupposes something that does not exist. The "between-cohort molecular distance that external- and historical-control borrowing already tolerates" has never been published — the record concedes it, three independent adversaries failed to find it, the FDA guidance adjudicates comparability on covariates, diagnostic criteria, standard of care and assay concordance rather than biological distance, and the only published era tolerance anywhere (toxicologic pathology: EPA 2-3 years, EMEA 5 years, OECD 5/2-3) is denominated in years on lesion incidence. So the comparison that supplies the question's significance must be manufactured by the answerer, who picks both metric and threshold, and either answer can be engineered by that choice; conceded P6 removes the causal reading the significance argument trades on, and (a)-net-of-(b) is identified only under an artefact-transport assumption the design measures nowhere and that the pivotal neighbour is cited as evidence against. Per the operating rules this is Unresolved on attack 4 and fatal.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not taken. If the question is to be rebuilt rather than abandoned, the pointer is to drop limb (c) and re-enter at Gate 0 with (a)+(b) alone, stating the era effect in units of the measured artefact, with a pre-specified MDE; that version must then clear the Disguise attack against Barnes 2008, the toxicologic-pathology HCD literature and the U Chicago AMP 2025 archive work, and Osaki et al. 2026, Chaturvedi 2011 and the Western Poland gastric comparison must be read by publisher route first — all four are currently unread and none of their absences is a check that passed.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None. Rejected at Gate 4 on presupposition failure, not as already-asked or as a disguised known, so no row is appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Noted for the curator, not routed on this candidate's behalf: the separation of diagnostic-criteria drift from true biological drift in historical control data is a distinct question that the toxicologic-pathology consensus document states it has not solved, and would need its own intake.

ID: UQ-20261016-45
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Rejection — gate and reason: Gate 2 — novelty Low: read near-duplicates in the candidate's own field; confirmed at Gate 4 by Unresolved Disguise, a fatal attack.
Domain(s): STEM — computer-assisted mathematics and formal methods; computer-architecture reliability (silent data corruption, soft errors). Source method: silence mapping.

Question (canonical): (V1, Gate 1 reformulation, adopted) Over a defined frame of published computer-assisted mathematical results, (i) what interval on each result's hardware-fault exposure follows from its reported core-hours, hardware and re-check history combined with a stated fleet SDC rate carried at its own order-of-magnitude uncertainty; and (ii) under a pre-registered fault model, what is the fail-silent fraction of a formally verified certificate checker — the share of injected faults under which it outputs "verified" where no valid derivation exists — against the shares that crash or correctly reject?
(V0, intake: "what is the probability that a published computer-assisted result is wrong for hardware rather than logical reasons…". Reformulated because presupposition 6 concedes hardware-caused and logical wrongness are not separable in the historical record, while the answer criteria ask for an exposure interval, not a probability of wrongness. Reformulation does not rescue novelty.)

Alternative formulations:
1. Does re-checking a certificate with a small verified checker reduce a computer-assisted proof's hardware-fault exposure, or concentrate it into one long unreplicated run?
2. Once the executing machine is admitted to have a measured, core-local, reproducible corruption rate, what does a machine-checked theorem's trusted base actually contain?

Motivating gap: As intaken — the formal-methods trust literature is dense with how-answers (minimal kernels, de Bruijn criterion, independently implemented and verified checkers) and silent on the machine they run on, while the architecture community now measures production-fleet corruptions that are often core-local, data-dependent and reproducible, the regime in which "run it again" and "check the certificate" do not help. After Gate 2 — the mapped silence is real for the kernel/TCB how-literature (independently confirmed by adversary 1: Lean 4.29 "Validating Proofs" enumerates its trusted base with no hardware item) and false for the candidate's field taken as a whole: the question is named and twice quantitatively estimated in the mathematics-of-trust literature. The silence mapping surveyed the wrong shelf.

Presuppositions: (1) published fleet SDC rates transfer to the machines these computations ran on — contested; rate families differ by orders of magnitude and academic/consumer rates are not established. (2) corruption is often core-local and reproducible rather than independent-transient — reported by fleet studies, share contested, load-bearing, and the one presupposition that genuinely post-dates the priors: it invalidates Lam's remedy (re-run affected cases) and Hales' reassurance (E8 repeated ~5x). (3) a verified checker's correctness theorem is conditional on a machine model SDC violates — established by inspection, but already said aloud (Hales §3.4; FOM 2000/Bauer), so the candidate's "rarely said aloud" claim fails. (4) fault injection is a valid proxy for field corruption — contested, and the sharpest part of limb (ii). (5) core-hours, hardware and replication history of published results are recoverable — partly established; Hales demonstrates it anecdotally for E8, the projective plane of order 10 and the four-colour theorem. (6) hardware-caused wrongness is distinguishable from logical/software error — inside the injection experiment yes; in the historical record contested, and Lam already performs a design-time version of the separation.

What would count as an answer: Two measurements reported together. (i) A census over a defined frame recording, per result, core-hours, hardware and whether the certificate check was ever repeated on independent hardware or a different architecture, combined with a stated fleet SDC rate to give an exposure interval carrying that rate's order-of-magnitude uncertainty. (ii) A fault-injection campaign against one or more verified certificate checkers under a pre-registered fault model, reporting the fail-silent fraction against the crash and correct-reject fractions, with sensitivity analysis over the fault model. A fail-silent fraction effectively zero (corruption derails control flow) is an equally admissible settlement.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 web searches (cap 11, min 8), plus 9 further queries in six untried vocabularies by adversary 1 — full lists in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-45-record.md and batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-45-adversary-1.md. Decisive ones: (a) mandatory own-field own-words query "soft errors and the trustworthiness of machine-checked proofs hardware fault tolerance proof assistant kernel" → Hales arXiv:1302.2898, which contains a section titled "Soft errors" — this set the grade; (b) mandatory answer-search on the quantity, "probability a computer-assisted proof is wrong because of hardware error cosmic ray four colour theorem Kepler conjecture reliability" → Lam's projective-plane-of-order-10 reliability section plus three FOM threads; (c) adversary's distributed-number-theory query "GIMPS double check hardware error rate bad residues Gerbicz" → Woltman & Kurowski, Fibonacci Quarterly 46/47(3), a published hardware-dominated error rate for long computations; (d) limb (ii) negatives from three dependability-vocabulary queries ("fault injection proof checker bit flip accepts invalid proof SAT DRAT checker soft error"; "architectural vulnerability factor / fail-silent … theorem prover SMT solver"; "fault injection campaign silent output corruption verified checker certificate validator") plus the adversary's HPC-resilience query → routine masked/crash/SDC taxonomies, no campaign targeting a proof checker, no published fail-silent fraction. Search gap stated, not glossed: the arXiv full-text sweep for limb (ii) hard-failed four times (proxy 403 on a long query, ROBOTS_DISALLOWED x3), so limb (ii)'s negative is search-grounded, not exhaustive. Wasserman & Blum, JACM 44(6) 1997 — the field owning the method behind alternative formulation 1 — is COULD NOT READ in both the record and adversary 1 (catalogue records only) and grounds nothing in either direction.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): PRIOR 1 — Hales, "Mathematics in the Age of the Turing Machine", arXiv:1302.2898 (2013), §3.5 "Soft errors"; read. Unit: one long computation or proof-assistant run (E8, 77 h, 64 GB). Endpoint: expected soft errors during the run and whether the claim is trustworthy. Comparator: software bugs; the same hardware at different elevations. Estimand: E[N] = FIT rate x memory x wall time ≈ 40 memory soft errors for E8, with the explicit claim that exposure "can be much higher" inside a proof assistant. PRIOR 2 — Lam, "The Search for a Finite Projective Plane of Order 10", Amer. Math. Monthly 98 (1991) 305–318; reliability section read at the CECM mirror (two displayed probability expressions are images and did not render). Unit: one published computer-assisted non-existence result. Endpoint: probability the published conclusion is wrong because undetected hardware error deleted the branch containing a plane. Comparator: software error, handled separately by two independently written programs. Estimand: that compound probability, from a measured CRAY-1A rate (~1 error/1000 h, implying "two to three errors" over the computation); called "infinitesimal", the result "only an experimental result" that "desperately needs an independent verification". PRIOR 3 — FOM list thread "Computer-verified theorems", Nov 2000, cs.nyu.edu/pipermail/fom/2000-November/004532.html (+/004537.html); read, and independently resurfaced by adversary 1. Unit: a computer-verified theorem. Endpoint: whether it should be believed and which error source binds that belief. Comparator: repetition ("100 different machines"); design error vs random transient. Estimand: none numeric — a qualitative ranking left unresolved between Bauer (random hardware error "a non-issue"), Kanovei and Shipman.
Also on point, found by adversary 1: Woltman & Kurowski, Fibonacci Quarterly 46/47(3) (2008/09) 194–197 — "our error-rate for first-time tests is roughly 2%", attributed to "memory corruption, overheating, overclocking, and other hardware errors", with cross-hardware double-checking already the community norm.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Hales — same object, not an adjacent one: he asks limb (i) in the candidate's own field and answers it to an order of magnitude, and states the hinge claim (exposure grows with proof-assistant run time) outright. Three refinements remain: an exposure interval over a census frame rather than an expected count per named computation; 2021–2026 fleet-measured rate families rather than one 2013 FIT point value; and a possibly reproducible fault model, under which his own reassurance fails. No limb (ii). vs Lam — executes limb (i) at n=1 from a measured machine rate, performs the hardware/software separation the candidate lists as contested, and reaches the candidate's structural conclusion. Differs in frame (many results vs one), rate provenance and the reproducible fault model, under which his re-run remedy fails. No limb (ii). vs FOM 2000 — is the candidate's second alternative formulation plus its does-re-running-help sub-question, debated and left unresolved; supplies no estimand, so the quantitative deliverables are unmet — which makes the candidate asked-but-open in refined form, not un-asked. vs Woltman & Kurowski — different workload (Lucas–Lehmer on consumer PCs, not a verified checker), but it supplies the published empirical quantity and the practice reversal the candidate proposes as novel.

Novelty confidence: Low
Grounds: two read near-duplicates of limb (i) in the candidate's own field and own words, one produced by the mandatory obvious-title query and one by the mandatory answer-search, plus a third adjacent community with the quantity published. Limb (ii)'s quantity was not found published and no injection campaign aimed at a proof checker was found across four dependability-vocabulary queries — a moderate search-grounded negative with the arXiv full-text route blocked, not a verified absence, and not a novelty grade for the question as posed.

Significance — consequence: If the fail-silent fraction is materially above zero, the de Bruijn criterion delivers a guarantee conditional on an unaudited machine model, and the right hygiene for a 100 TB certificate is re-checking on a different microarchitecture rather than a yet smaller kernel. If it is effectively zero, a worry standing since Lam 1991 retires with evidence and the FOM "non-issue" position acquires support it has never had. Against: Hales put essentially this argument to a wide mathematical audience in 2013 and practice did not move.
Significance — audience: proof-assistant kernel and SAT/SMT certificate-checker maintainers (ACL2 and CakeML DRAT/LPR checkers, Lean/mathlib, HOL Light), groups publishing terabyte-certificate results, and the HPC centres running the checks. Real and identifiable; their revealed response to the same argument was no change.
Significance — fecundity: whether architecture-diverse re-checking becomes a reporting norm; whether certificate formats should carry per-chunk digests so checks shard across heterogeneous machines; whether SDC-hardened checkers beat plain duplication on cost; what a correctness theorem conditional on a corrupting machine would state.
Significance — anchoring: de Bruijn criterion and TCB enumerations (CompCert TCB, arXiv:2201.10280; seL4's admitted hardware assumptions; Lean's "Validating Proofs" list); the 2021–2026 fleet-SDC literature; Lam's standing call for independent verification; this ledger's UQ-20261016-01.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary with an incentive gap on each side — a fault class not expressible in a kernel's logic has no slot in a reduction-to-kernel trust argument and is handed off as an assumption; and fleet-SDC vulnerability studies are indexed by commercially weighty workloads, which machine-checked mathematics is not. Partly void, and this is the Gate 2 finding: the question was asked (Lam 1991, FOM 2000, Hales 2013), so what needs explaining is why an asked question with two published estimates produced no measurement programme in 35 years. A silence mechanism cannot rescue a question that was not silent.

Verification by the run session (one fresh-context checker over both near-duplicates and the fault-injection question; 14 searches, 7 fetches, 6 refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-45-verification.md). The Gate 2 kill holds on the source that carries it. The second source is weaker than the record states in three of four respects, and the routing row the batch proposed is withdrawn.
(i) HALES IS CONFIRMED ON EVERY CLAIM, including the arithmetic. Section 3.5 is titled "Soft errors" and concerns cosmic-ray-induced transient hardware error in computer-assisted mathematics. It carries out the attributed computation — 77 hours, 64 GB, 10^3 FIT/Mbit, 1 FIT = 1 error per 10^9 hours — and both quoted sentences appear verbatim: "In software that has been thoroughly debugged, soft errors become the most significant source of error in computation", and the claim that the probability of a soft error inside a proof assistant can be much higher because soft errors scale with execution time. The Denver-versus-Boston 3x elevation comparison appears, in footnote 15 rather than the body. Its estimand is a single point expected value of the form FIT rate x memory x wall time, with no uncertainty interval, no measurement of the actual machine, and no link from an error count to the probability that the mathematical conclusion is wrong.
(ii) Three corrections to how the record quotes Hales. The paper's own printed figure is approximately 39.4 errors, in a displayed equation; "about 40" is its rounded prose, not a second independent estimate. Redoing the arithmetic gives 39.42 with decimal GB (64 x 8000 = 512,000 Mbit) and 40.37 with binary GB (524,288 Mbit), which pins the paper to the decimal conversion. And the 77-hour E8 character-table computation is attributed in Section 3.5 to the Atlas Project, cited [Ada07], not to Vogan.
(iii) LAM 1991 NEEDS NARROWING ON THREE OF FOUR POINTS, and the record leans on it harder than it will bear. The CRAY-1A rate is literature-reported — the machine is "reported to have such errors" — not a rate the authors measured; and the run length is explicitly unrecorded ("we did not keep track of the computer time used on the CRAY"), a guess of 3,000 hours later revised to about 2,000, so "a measured error rate over a known run" overstates both inputs. The cross-check is "two different programs to cross check selective sample cases", not two independently written programs, not a full independent re-run, and not framed by Lam as separating hardware from software failure modes. And "infinitesimal" is scoped to the probability of hardware errors affecting ALL the A2's that a real plane would generate, not to an unqualified probability that the result is wrong. What does hold verbatim is the fourth point: Lam declines the word proof ("these are not proofs in the traditional mathematical sense") and asks for independent verification. Lam's two printed probability values are rendered as inline images in the available edition and could not be read, so no specific numeric probability from Lam is verified here.
(iv) THE SECOND LIMB IS CONFIRMED UN-ASKED. No published fault-injection study of a formally verified proof checker or proof-assistant kernel was found — nothing measuring what fraction of injected hardware faults make such a checker report success on an invalid certificate rather than crash or reject. That is an absence, not an answer, and it is what makes limb (ii) a candidate for fresh intake rather than material for this entry.
(v) Route note for later runs: ar5iv's conversion of arXiv:1302.2898 is incomplete — it ends mid-subsection 1.18 and Section 3 is absent — so it is not a usable route to Section 3.5. The arXiv PDF is. All raw curl was refused at the proxy and the working fetch path caps verbatim quotation at about 125 characters, so the quotes above were verified as short exact strings sentence by sentence, with explicit "does not appear" checks, rather than by transcribing either section.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete. The Disguise ground was tested against Hales directly and held; the Lam narrowings touch a supporting source, not the ground.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Disguise (Unresolved, fatal) — as canonically posed the question is the one Hales 2013 asks and estimates and Lam 1991 answers at n=1, in the candidate's own field and its own words, with a third community (GIMPS) having published the empirical rate and already adopted the cross-hardware re-check the candidate offers as a reversal; nothing but limb (ii) survives, and limb (ii) alone is a different question from the one on the ledger.

For the re-intake of limb (ii) alone — the fail-silent fraction of one named verified certificate checker under a pre-registered core-local, reproducible, data-dependent fault model, the class under which Lam's re-run and Hales' repetitions both fail — read Wasserman & Blum, JACM 44(6) 1997 in full first (COULD NOT READ in both the record and adversary 1; route via doi.org, not PMC), since run-time result-checking owns the method and is the likeliest remaining pre-emption.
Routing (rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED. The batch proposed a row and the run session withdrew it; no row was appended, and this line records why. The rejection is a read-near-duplicates one — Hales asks limb (i) in the candidate's own field and answers it to an order of magnitude — and answered or disguised-known rejections are not routed. The refined corpus-scale version the row proposed (an exposure interval over a constructed frame of published results, from reported core-hours and fleet-measured SDC rate families) is not asked by anyone either: Hales computes it for one case and Lam for another, and neither poses the corpus version, so it falls under the rule that a quantity nobody has asked for is not an open problem. Limb (ii) is the genuinely open thing here and it is also un-asked — verification found no fault-injection study of a formally verified proof checker at all — so it belongs in a fresh Gate 0 intake rather than in this file.
