ID: UQ-20261016-46
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Status change (post-batch): Rejected → Provisional. The batch rejected this candidate on a number that the cited paper does not contain.
Domain(s): AI architecture — data layer (web-scale pretraining corpora, dataset distribution and reproducibility). Neighbours searched: information science / digital preservation, social-media research methods, survey methodology, econometrics, ML security.
Question (canonical): For corpora distributed as URL manifests (LAION-2B-en/Re-LAION, DataComp CommonPool, YFCC100M, OBELICS), pinned to an archived manifest revision and a resolution date T: (i) is the still-retrievable subset a selective rather than random thinning, selective on covariates the manifest itself records (registrable domain, TLD, language, caption length, licence, aesthetic and NSFW deciles, dimensions, shard), measured as per-covariate retention ratios with CIs plus out-of-fold AUC and calibration of a retention model against a pre-registered null band on N = 200k rows per corpus; and (ii) at fixed compute, does a model trained on the retrievable-at-T subset differ from one trained on a size-matched random subsample of the same archived manifest by more than a ±2 SD within-arm seed-to-seed equivalence band on the dataset's own suite (k ≥ 5 seeds per arm)?
Alternative formulations: (1) Has "trained on LAION-2B" stopped naming a fixed distribution — do two labs that train on it years apart train on measurably different data and get measurably different models? (2) Is link attrition in URL-distributed corpora ignorable given what the manifest observes? (3) Do URL-distributed training corpora suffer persistence bias in Elmas's sense, and does it propagate to a trained model rather than only to a descriptive statistic?
Motivating gap: The artifact a lab obtains is whatever the web still serves on download day, while papers, model cards and licences cite the dataset as a fixed object. Attrition is large and dated (Hong et al.: 21.4% of 12.8M CommonPool URLs failed, April 2025; mlfoundations/datacomp #3 ~91% success May 2023, #41 0.884 July 2023); manifests are edited (Re-LAION, 2024-08-30). The intake claim that the silence is total was withdrawn at Gate 2: Hong et al. compared 1,000 failed vs 1,000 successful URLs on three image-derived attributes and called the differences "slight". Distinct from UQ-20261016-38 (robots.txt publisher-side exclusion in Common Crawl text) and UQ-20261015-04 (Wikipedia citation hazard by topic), both read in full.
Presuppositions: P1 manifests archived as published — supported via pinned HF commits (LAION-400M mirror 404 in Jan 2026, img2dataset #476). P2 retention measurable from HTTP status — contested, repaired content-side with an audited error interval; the repair is shown insufficient (see adversarial log, attack 4). P3 attrition large enough — supported (~9-12% 2023, 21.4% 2025). P4 fixed-compute small track probes materiality — contested, left contested; UQ-20261016-38's kill paper found no benchmark gap from an 8% token loss at 1.5B/100B. P5 the suite registers a shift of this size — contested; no published seed-variance table (confirmed "not found" at DataComp §3.2). P6 manifest covariates accurate — aesthetic/NSFW are model outputs; domain, TLD, shard, caption length carry the limb. Significance — consequence: If yes (selective and material), "trained on LAION-2B" denotes a distribution indexed by date — breaking interpretation of failed replications, the fixed-pool premise of DataComp-style filtering leaderboards (the fairness consequence voiced verbatim in datacomp #3 and never studied), and the model-card practice of naming a dataset as a fixed object; download date becomes a required reporting field. If no, URL-manifest distribution is licensed as reproducibility-preserving at the scales tested and attrition becomes a sample-size cost, and the measured seed-to-seed band is a reusable instrument nobody has published. Discounted: the content-hash remedy is already DataComp practice (per-image SHA256, §3.2) and was already recommended corpus-wide by D in 2023; the modal outcome is selectivity on observables with an immaterial small-scale effect.
Significance — audience: (a) manifest publishers (LAION e.V., mlfoundations/DataComp, HF maintainers, PD12M) — but this audience has already declined the proposed remedy under stronger pressure than this question would generate (D notified maintainers in 2023 and flagged that integrity checks "can significantly degrade the utility of a dataset"); Re-LAION was a CSAM-driven link removal, not a content-integrity change. (b) fixed-pool benchmark organisers — evidenced by datacomp #3. (c) reproduction, audit and model-card review teams. (d) information scientists and digital-preservation researchers, who own the method. (e) regulators and litigants reasoning from a dataset name. (a) also has a disincentive to publish instability in its own artefact, and none of (a)-(c) is obviously willing to fund limb (ii)'s compute.
Significance — fecundity: Surviving items — the retention-weighted corpus (IPW on manifest covariates to reconstitute the t0 distribution); differential decay by licence field, inverting what licence filters were built to produce; whether attrition and robots.txt exclusion (UQ-20261016-38) compound or offset on the same domains; the same analysis for WARC-pointer text and video-ID corpora; and the missing measurement of seed-to-seed spread for the standard multimodal suites. Struck as pre-empted: "attrition as an adversarial surface / a poisoning channel that requires no poisoning" is split-view poisoning (D, 2023), published, costed and disclosed; steering by withdrawal rather than substitution is a strictly weaker attack than the published one.
Significance — anchoring: Reproducibility of ML results (Cherti et al.'s reproducible scaling laws presuppose reproducible data); the data-exhaustion debate (if corpora shrink as they grow, the usable web is a flow, not a stock); provenance and consent work (Data Provenance Initiative, Consent in Crisis, arXiv:2511.08637); the absence of a sampling frame for the web in corpus linguistics; and the Re-LAION edit as a dated natural experiment.
Reason for silence: Surviving mechanism — the question is pre-classified as engineering: the quantity lives in issue trackers as a "success rate" with a folk cause (img2dataset #277 taxonomy, #400 resolved as DNS), and datacomp #3 states the fairness consequence out loud and is answered as a throughput problem; #68 asks only what rate is "healthy". Both adversaries verified these bodies independently and both graded this mechanism credible. Secondary: a disciplinary boundary — the move is 2018-2023 vintage in social-media research (B), whose datasets are ID-distributed by platform policy, while ML's manifest distribution is a choice whose cost is deferred. Struck: mechanism 1 (CSAM liability) is unsourced and cannot explain silence on CommonPool, YFCC100M or OBELICS; mechanism 4 (instrument timing) is undercut because Multimedia Commons has held YFCC100M bytes for years and any 2021-22 download is a t0 archive, so the experiment has been cheap and executable since about 2022. Also note the silence is partly broken: the mutability was asked in-field in 2023, in a security frame (D).
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two adversaries, fresh context, sequential, handed the Gate 0-3 record only. Status = worst of the two.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-46-verification.md): the Gate 4 kill is REFUTED at its load-bearing figure.
The rejection rested on “substitution is 59-65% of surviving URLs (adversary arithmetic on Carlini et al.'s stated CC-3M counts, arXiv:2302.10149)”. That paper states no such counts. A checker handed only the claim and the identifier reports: it gives about 1.04% of CC-3M images on expired domains (Table I, DNS record absent), at least 0.08% buyable for $1K, and in Section IV-D a domain-level content check — “Among all domains hosting more than 10 images, we find just one domain has our attack signature” “when comparing images with perceptual similarity”, and “If we instead compare cryptographic hashes of images, we find two additional domains that have been repurchased”, both judged benign (lapsed DNS, re-encoded images). The unit is the domain, not the URL; the estimand is a count of domains, not a fraction of surviving URLs; and no date is attached to the content-change analysis (DNS lookups ran May and August 2022). There is therefore no published majority-substitution rate to derive 59-65% from, in this paper or, as far as the checker could establish, anywhere.
What survives from the kill: the paper does treat dead links and content substitution as two different measurements, so the confound the adversary pointed at is real — its magnitude is simply unknown, and on the only published measurement it is small rather than dominant. The entry is re-based accordingly.
Also re-read: Hong et al. (arXiv:2506.17185) remains the nearest prior — 21.4% download failure on CommonPool-small in April 2025, with a descriptive 1,000-versus-1,000 comparison of failed against successful URLs on image size, face count, CLIP similarity and caption PII, differences called “slight”, no retention ratios, no CIs, no model trained.
Status of the unrun checks: adversary #2 executed 0 of its 9 Disguise queries (shared search budget) — UNVERIFIED under the amended Gate 4 rule. A late strict adversary has since run 12, and found no prior.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness downgraded from the record's self-assessed 3/3 by this gate: the operational definition of RETRIEVABLE does not separate substitution from retention, so limb (i)'s estimand is misnamed and limb (ii)'s contrast is confounded with content drift, and the audited-residual repair does not reach an open-ended population. Significance 2/3 stands, net of the struck fecundity item and the pre-empted content-hash consequence. Disguise is unverified — adversary 2 executed 0 of 9 new-vocabulary queries because the shared search budget was exhausted — so under the ledger's rules this entry could not have been Validated in this run even on a clean adversarial log; Provisional would have been the ceiling. The verdict does not rest on that: attack 4 is substantive and sourced, and Unresolved on attack 4 from any adversary is fatal.)
Strongest remaining objection (restated after verification and a late strict adversary; no sourced kill survives): the attrition-versus-substitution confound is real in kind but unmeasured in degree. Carlini et al. (arXiv:2302.10149) document that URL content substitution happens — among CC-3M domains hosting more than 10 images, one showed substituted content under perceptual similarity, two more were flagged by cryptographic hash and judged benign — but publish no rate at which surviving URLs serve different content. So the candidate's definition of “retrievable” does count a substituted image as retained, and the design still carries no instrument to separate the two populations; that is a fixable specification gap (add a caption-image agreement check and report intact / substituted / gone separately), not a presupposition failure. The late adversary found no kill it could source, over 12 new Disguise queries.
Largest open risk to limb (i): an MMM 2023 best-paper thesis on link rot and dataset shrinkage in web-URL multimedia datasets, found via the UZH DDIS blog. Only the blog was read; the paper itself was NOT opened, so whether it pre-empts limb (i) is UNVERIFIED and is promotion condition 1 — its unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand have to be stated before this entry's novelty grade can be trusted. Partly repaired: P7 (an archived ground truth exists) holds for YFCC100M, whose content is archived in the Multimedia Commons S3 bucket with a small reported fraction missing — but that is a 2014 Flickr corpus, not LAION or DataComp, so the presupposition is supported for one named corpus of the five and unsupported for the rest.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): repair before measurement — measure caption-image agreement, not just HTTP success, on a sample of aged manifest rows for one of the five named corpora, and report the three populations (intact / substituted / gone-or-blocked) separately before any selectivity or materiality estimand is defined. Then open the MMM 2023 link-rot paper and the seven Disguise vocabularies still unreached (video and audio ID-distributed corpora, archival content drift, CC3M/CC12M decay, econometric attrition and IPW/MNAR, Chinese, Japanese, AI-data-commons), plus arXiv:2308.02231 and the TU Darmstadt content-removal-bias record, both still unopened.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed — the entry is Provisional, and a Provisional entry's own question is never routed while the ledger still claims it as un-asked. Priors A-D each differ from both limbs on unit, endpoint, comparator or estimand. Two Gate 2 sentences are struck regardless of the verdict: “not done at all for LAION, YFCC100M or OBELICS” and search 9's “no published figure” (both falsified by arXiv:2302.10149, Table 1: LAION-2B-en 0.29%, OBELISC 0.09%).

ID: UQ-20261016-47
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — tokenization and the pretraining data layer. Neighbours searched: metrology, psychometrics (standard error of equating), evaluation methodology / variance components, data compression (dictionary training), vector quantization.
Question (canonical): Holding corpus, algorithm, pre-tokenizer and vocabulary size fixed, draw k ≥ 5 independent fitting samples of size S from one pretraining corpus and fit one tokenizer per draw: (a) what is the between-draw divergence of the resulting tokenizers — vocabulary Jaccard, merge-sequence agreement, per-domain fertility SD on held-out text — as a function of S; and (b) when one model per draw is pretrained on identical text at matched byte and FLOP budgets, how large is the between-draw SD of validation bits-per-byte and of downstream scores, relative to two reference quantities fixed in advance — the seed-only SD under a single fixed tokenizer, and the published algorithm-choice / vocabulary-size gap? (Gate 1 reformulation, version B; version A, with "identical token budgets" and "loss-per-FLOP", is recorded in the record file.)
Alternative formulations: (1) Is a tokenizer a reproducible artifact of a recipe, or a sample statistic with a standard error nobody has reported? (2) When a paper reports that tokenizer A beats tokenizer B, how much of that gap lies inside the noise of refitting either tokenizer on a fresh sample of the same data?
Motivating gap: Pretraining recipes name two tokenizer design dimensions (algorithm, vocabulary size) and report the fitting sample's provenance and replication not at all, while BPE/Unigram fitting is a sample-dependent greedy estimation run on a slice chosen by a library default (SentencePiece `input_sentence_size` / `shuffle_input_sentence`). TokEval fits all 44 custom tokenizers on 10GB with no sampling or replicate detail; TokSuite puts from-scratch fits out of scope. Corrected by adversary #1: fitting-data *size* is in fact commonly reported (Dagan 10B chars; Schmidt et al. MiniPile 6GB; TokEval 10GB) — the defensible gap is that the sampling procedure and replicate count are unreported.
Presuppositions: (1) Tokenizer fitting is sample-dependent — true by construction; magnitude partly measured in bias form by arXiv:2502.20273, and now also in variance form (see Gate 4). (2) Published algorithm-choice and vocabulary-size gaps each come from one fit and one seed — VERIFIED (Ali et al. 2310.08754: 24 tokenizers / 26 models, one seed, no CIs, seeds explicitly dropped; TokEval; TokSuite). (3) Differently-tokenized models are comparable on one loss scale — contested; handled by bits-per-byte at matched bytes and FLOPs; TokEval's 46-model BPB comparison is precedent. (4) Compute suffices for k refits × ≥2 scales — the binding constraint (Ali et al.'s single-seed grid ≈ 59k GPU-hours). (5) Merge-sequence distance and vocabulary Jaccard are meaningful divergence measures — contested (2508.06621; 2305.03029), so fertility carries limb (a) and merge divergence is descriptive only. (6) The fitting sample is drawn from the same corpus as the pretraining data — design requirement, and the point of difference from tokenizer-transfer / mixture-composition work. Adversary corrections: (4') as written, "identical text" plus matched bytes AND matched FLOPs is over-constrained, since fertility differs between draws — one of the two budgets must be fixed and the other reported; (5') tokenizer fitting is not even deterministic given its input (huggingface/tokenizers #1794; frequency ties, Hayase App. C.7), so the within-draw control is non-trivial.
What would count as an answer: A variance-component decomposition with CIs. Limb (a): k ≥ 5 fits per cell on disjoint samples S ∈ {0.1, 1, 10} GB, everything else fixed; between-draw vocabulary Jaccard, merge agreement and per-domain fertility SD vs S, each against a within-draw control. Limb (b): one model per draw at ≥2 scales on identical text at matched byte/FLOP budgets, plus seed replicates under one fixed tokenizer; between-draw SD of BPB and downstream scores against (i) seed-only SD, (ii) the published algorithm-choice gap (Ali et al.'s ≈1.7-point monolingual average-accuracy gap; ≈9% best-vs-worst on ARC-Easy). Decision rule: "sample matters" = between-draw SD of the same order as the design gap; "does not" = at or below seed SD at the smallest S.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 web searches and 5 fetches (all 5 papers opened, no COULD NOT READ); full list in batches/2026-10-16-1833/UQ-20261016-47-record.md. Most informative: (1) mandatory own-field own-words title query "effect of tokenizer training data on language model performance / tokenizer training corpus size" → arXiv:2502.20273, opened; (3) "tokenizer choice gap within random seed noise pretraining ablation confidence interval" → TokSuite, TokEval, 2609.19145, Dodge et al., no refit-variance study; (6) method-owning-field query on variance components / multiverse analysis of preprocessing → the method family is mature (neuroimaging, EEG, LLM annotation, autointerpretability) and has never been pointed at a tokenizer; (7) "stability of BPE merges across corpora" → 2305.03029, opened; (11) answer-directed "tokenizer sampling variance / between-draw SD" → nothing. Mandatory "what fraction of X" check: the quantity exists in bias form (2502.20273: shared vocabulary with a 900GB reference 58%→97% BPE, 40%→97% UnigramLM, 4%→92% WordPiece as the fit grows 1GB→900GB at vocab 40,960; English intrinsic plateau 120–150GB). Gate 4 added 9 web queries + 4 fetches (adversary 1), 0 web queries + 4 fetches + 2 GitHub searches (adversary 2, budget exhausted), and 0 web queries + 4 fetches + 43 GitHub issue/code searches (adversary 3, budget exhausted); see the three adversary files. **The vocabulary Gate 2 never tried was "stability".**
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): **Prior 1** — "How Much is Enough? The Diminishing Returns of Tokenization Training Data", arXiv:2502.20273 (ICML 2025), opened by Gate 2 and independently re-opened by adversaries #2 and #3: one tokenizer per (algorithm, vocab size, data size) cell, strictly *nested* subsets of one shuffled 900GB corpus, intrinsic endpoints only, no replicates/seeds/CIs, no LMs trained; App. B's pairwise overlap is across sizes (0.57 for 30GB vs 900GB), and it names the candidate's phenomenon in one untested sentence about rare tokens. **Prior 2** — Ali et al., "Tokenizer Choice For LLM Training: Negligible or Crucial?", arXiv:2310.08754 (NAACL 2024): 24 tokenizers / 26 models at 2.6B, one fit and one seed per design cell, ≈59k GPU-hours, downstream accuracy + fertility; source of the candidate's reference gap and the verification of presupposition 2. **Prior 3** — Sälevä & Lignos, "What changes when you randomly choose BPE merge operations? Not much", arXiv:2305.03029: merge-*rule* randomisation on a fixed unresampled corpus, 10 seeded replications per cell, BLEU/chrF, effects −0.98 to +0.56 against seed SEs of 0.02–0.2. **Prior 4, found at Gate 4 and decisive** — Tempus, Whittington, Schmidt, Komm & Pimentel, "Tokenisation via Convex Relaxations", arXiv:2605.22821 (2026-05-21), Fig. 3 "Vocabulary Stability Across Training Subsets": k = 5 independent same-size samples × 4 sample sizes × ≥2 vocabulary sizes from one corpus (ClimbMix), BPE vs ConvexTok, pairwise vocabulary Jaccard with min/max — BPE mean Jaccard 0.807 → 0.856 → 0.886 → 0.914 across the four sample sizes in one block. Evidence: the authors' repository (github.com/JanTempus/tokenisation_lp — `sampling_jaccard.py`, `sampling_experiment.py`, `experiment_climbmix_sampling/ss_*/jaccard/results.txt`, read as code-search snippets) plus three independent summaries of Fig. 3. **COULD NOT READ the paper itself** (fetch cap exhausted; arXiv listing routes ROBOTS_DISALLOWED; proxy CONNECT 403; publisher route https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22821 untried).
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Prior 1 — same object, different estimand (bias toward an asymptote under nested subsets vs variance across independent draws at fixed S); the candidate adds merge and fertility endpoints and the model-level limb Prior 1 declines to run. vs Prior 2 — Prior 2 varies the named design dimensions and holds the fitting sample fixed and undescribed; the candidate inverts that, and Prior 2 cannot answer it even in principle (one fit, one seed, no error bars). vs Prior 3 — merge-rule randomisation on a fixed corpus vs corpus resampling under a fixed rule, and NMT/BLEU vs pretraining/BPB; Prior 3 is nonetheless a published partial null that acts as a prior on limb (b). **vs Prior 4 — it does not differ on limb (a)'s headline.** Prior 4 executes exactly the candidate's design for vocabulary Jaccard vs sample size at k = 5, with a length-conditioned breakdown the candidate does not even propose; what remains unmeasured is merge-sequence agreement, held-out fertility SD, a within-draw control, and all of limb (b). That is a narrowing of an executed measurement, not a new question.
Novelty confidence: Low — Gate 2's Medium is withdrawn. A near-duplicate of limb (a) was found at Gate 4 (arXiv:2605.22821) in a vocabulary Gate 2 did not try. Limb (b) alone would grade no better than Unverified here, because both later adversaries had their web-search budget exhausted and ran 0 of the required 8 Disguise queries: corpus-linguistics frequency-list stability, psychometric equating, ASR sub-word lexicons and non-English literatures are untested.
Significance — consequence: If between-draw SD is of the order of the design gap, every single-fit tokenizer ablation (Ali et al.'s ≈1.7-point averages, TokEval's 46 one-model conditions, TokSuite's 0.10-wide robustness spread) is reporting a design effect confounded with an unestimated variance term, and replicate counts plus a reported fitting corpus become mandatory. If it is at or below seed SD, current practice is licensed explicitly and a standing reviewer objection is retired. Either way the S-curve with its knee answers "how many bytes should I fit on?" in variance terms. Discounted by the verdict: Prior 4 already supplies the vocabulary-Jaccard half of that curve, and Schmidt et al. (arXiv:2402.18376, EMNLP 2024) report that even whole-algorithm swaps are "within the noise" at 350M–2.4B, which disputes the yardstick the consequence is stated against.
Significance — audience: Pretraining data/infrastructure teams choosing the fitting slice by default; the active comparative-tokenizer line (Ali et al. 2024; Dagan et al. 2024; Schmidt et al. 2024; TokSuite 2025; TokEval 2026; "Objective vs. Search" 2026), which states the missing comparison in its own limitations; evaluation-methodology researchers who publish variance budgets for seeds, data order and benchmark items but not for preprocessing artifacts; SentencePiece and HF `tokenizers` maintainers who expose subsampling knobs with no documented consequence. Adversary caveat: what those papers ask for is *model-run* noise estimates; none asks specifically for the fitting-sample component.
Significance — fecundity: How many refits must an ablation average over before a gap is publishable? Does the variance scale with morphological richness or low-resource status? Can it be engineered away (bagged or regularised fitting)? Is between-draw divergence a cheap screen for brittleness under domain shift, avoiding model training? Should a shipped tokenizer carry a stated uncertainty?
Significance — anchoring: The unreported fitting-sample-procedure gap; the contested cross-tokenizer loss-comparison problem; the ML variance-reporting programme (seeds, data order, benchmark items — not preprocessing artifacts); TokEval's unexplained instability of math/code tokenizer rankings under continued training; the mature standard-error-of-equating and finite-training-set-codebook literatures.
Reason for silence: As claimed at Gate 3: determinism illusion plus artifact framing (a checksummed `tokenizer.json` does not look like an estimate; the randomness sits in the library default that picks the slice); a disciplinary boundary (variance-component methodology lives in statistics, the tokenizer in the data-engineering layer); and an incentive/cost gap (limb (a) publishes as a negative that licenses other people's runs; limb (b) costs k× a 59k-GPU-hour grid). **Failed at Gate 4.** For limb (a) there was no silence at all — it was asked and run in 2026 under the word "stability", and practitioner tooling computes "multi-seed vocabulary stability across 5 bootstrap runs". The determinism-illusion mechanism is also undercut by engineers filing tokenizer-fit nondeterminism as a bug (huggingface/tokenizers #1794). Per Gate 4 attack 7's own rule, a reason-for-silence failure sends the novelty finding back to Gate 2, which is where this entry died.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-47-verification.md): the Gate 4 kill is UPHELD, with its citation corrected. arXiv:2605.22821 resolves to "Tokenisation via Convex Relaxations" (Jan Tempus, Philip Whittington, Craig W. Schmidt, Dennis Komm, Tiago Pimentel; v1 2026-05-21), which formulates tokeniser construction as a linear program (ConvexTok) and compares it with BPE and Unigram. No figure carries the caption "Vocabulary Stability Across Training Subsets" that the adversary gave it. The real locus is Figure 3, in the section "Stability of Tokenisers to Randomness on the Training Sample": average Jaccard similarity between vocabularies when a tokeniser is retrained on INDEPENDENTLY sampled subsets of the same data, across numbers of documents and vocabulary sizes, for BPE and the ConvexTok rounding variants (Det, Bias, Int). The design is independent same-size draws, not a nested series of growing subsets — which is what the kill turns on, and it holds. Attack 2 therefore stands against limb (a) on verified evidence; the ground is a published figure read directly, not an absence.

ID: UQ-20261016-48
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — evaluation methodology (pre-deployment testing, external red-team cohorts, safety cases) is the TARGET field deciding novelty. Method imported from ecology/biostatistics (closed-population capture-recapture, Chao-type richness under heterogeneous catchability) and software-inspection defect-content estimation. Neighbour vocabularies searched: security (vulnerability rediscovery), epidemiology (MSE, list dependence), HCI (evaluator effect), software inspection, audit sampling.

Question (canonical): For pre-deployment exercises in which two or more institutionally independent teams evaluated the SAME model checkpoint under documented access, affordances and time budget: (a) under a pre-registered equivalence relation that maps each documented finding to a failure-mode class at a declared granularity, what is the pairwise and joint rediscovery rate of classes across teams, reported with inter-rater reliability on the matching itself and with sensitivity to one looser and one stricter relation; and (b) does that overlap support a non-vacuous estimate of the classes the exercise missed, where the estimand is declared as the discoverable-at-that-effort-and-scaffold population rather than "all failure modes", estimators are fitted in at least two families (one admitting heterogeneous catchability, one admitting positive list dependence), and the estimate counts only if a pre-specified vacuity test passes (finite upper confidence bound, CI excluding "unboundedly many") under explicitly declared non-closure? (R1, adopted at Gate 1; intake version V0 and the three changes R1 made are in the record.)

Alternative formulations: (1) Lay: when two red teams test the same model, how often do they find the same thing, and what does that overlap license us to say about what neither found? (2) Cross-field: can the rediscovery statistics used in the vulnerability-stockpiling debate be computed for frontier-model evaluations, and do their assumptions survive the move from a fixed code artifact to a model whose failure population is created by elicitation? (3) Method-field: is a red-team cohort a valid multiple-recapture sample of a defect population, or is each team sampling a population its own scaffolds bring into existence?

Motivating gap: Safety cases, deployment decisions and emerging adequacy-of-testing language rest on an implicit coverage claim, and no quantity in the field expresses coverage — findings are reported as lists of what was found. Two ingredients are newly present: the same checkpoint is routinely handed to several independent teams and some exercises publish (UK AISI / US AISI joint testing; UK AISI pre-deployment evaluations), and the method homes are mature. The claimed live problem is at the interface: a code artifact has a fixed, individuable defect population, whereas a model's failure classes are produced by elicitation effort and by whichever scaffolds a team brings.

Presuppositions: P1 failure modes admit an equivalence relation stable enough to match two teams' findings — CONTESTED, never demonstrated (no concrete relation named, no pilot IRR). P2 two or more teams tested the same checkpoint with comparable access, affordances and time budget — NOT ESTABLISHED FOR THE FLAGSHIP INSTANCE: adversary 3 opened the UK AISI page and found "separate but complementary tests", different suites (US 40 public challenges; UK 47 apprentice-level tasks), biology published by one institute only, and no tester count, hours or access level; the NIST joint-testing document remains unopened by Gate 2 and all three adversaries. P3 comparable documentation granularity across teams — CONTESTED, confounded with genuine non-overlap. P4 approximate closure over the exercise window — CONTESTED and probably false; run as a declared bound instead. P5 per-team finding-level lists obtainable and shareable — BINDING FEASIBILITY RISK, no supporting evidence; corroborated against: the Anthropic/CAISI/AISI collaboration page attributes findings to "government red-teamers" collectively, i.e. the published output destroys the who-found-what matrix. P6 teams independent in the sense the estimator needs — CONTESTED, now doubly corroborated from opened sources (competition paper: "participants may have converged on similar attack template due to shared familiarity with known techniques"; course module: "红队成员之间互相启发（非独立采样）"). P7 "independent evaluation" is institutional, not statistical, independence — flagged.

What would count as an answer: (1) an empirical overlap matrix from >=2 institutionally independent teams on one checkpoint, each finding mapped to a class by >=2 blinded raters, with IRR on class assignment and on the cross-team match decision, recomputed under a looser and a stricter relation; (2) estimates with CIs from >=2 estimator families (one heterogeneous-catchability, one dependence-admitting) on the incidence matrix, with sensitivity to effort covariates; (3) a pre-specified vacuity test (finite upper confidence bound; CI excluding "unboundedly many") under declared non-closure, which decides whether (2) counts at all. A clean negative counts equally: overlap collapsing toward chance once shared-scaffold and shared-taxonomy strata are conditioned on, or the dependence-corrected bound going unbounded. Not answers: overlap without IRR; an estimate with no dependence model; any estimate without scaffold/effort conditioning.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 searches + 5 fetches (2 opened, 1 abstract-only, 1 ROBOTS_DISALLOWED); adversary 1, 9 searches (8 Disguise) + 4 fetches (4 opened); adversary 2, 0 of 9 web searches (tool refused: turn budget exhausted) + 10 GitHub substitutes + 4 fetches (2 blocked, 2 opened); adversary 3, 0 of 8 web searches (refused) + 34 GitHub substitutes + 4 fetches (1 opened, 1 HTTP 429 COULD NOT READ, 2 rejected before transfer). Added by adversary 1 and missed entirely by Gate 2: Hertzum & Jacobsen, "The Evaluator Effect: A Chilling Fact About Usability Evaluation Methods", IJHCI 15(1) 2003 (OPENED: eleven studies, any-two agreement between evaluators "ranges from 5% to 65%", causes include "vague problem criteria"), and Jacobsen, Hertzum & John, HFES 1998 (OPENED: "Only 20% of the 93 detected problems were detected by all evaluators, and 46% were detected by only a single evaluator"). Leads never executed: N-fold inspection (Martin & Tsai lineage), Böhme's STADS/species-discovery line, bug-bounty platform duplicate rates, qualitative-saturation estimation.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs N1 — same field and the closest thing in it to an overlap statistic, but deduplicates by MD5 and clusters at an unvalidated cosine 0.8, samples ~130–160 individuals rather than institutionally independent teams (four of the top five clusters one contributor each; top 50 users ~88% of activity), reports no IRR, and explicitly declines to extrapolate to a remaining count. vs N2 — the analogue of limb (a) in a field where individuation is supplied free by patch/CVE assignment; reports a rate, never estimates the unseen population, so limbs (b) and the vacuity test have no counterpart. vs N3 — the method home, whose population is closed by construction and whose comparator is a seeded ground truth; its own text, read by adversary 3, also carries the small-k caveats Gate 2 omitted while describing the field as "converging on Mh-JK". vs Hertzum & Jacobsen — this is limb (a)'s structure (independent evaluators, one artifact, pairwise overlap, matching reliability as the known weak link) on a different target (interfaces, human evaluators) and reports agreement proportions, not a dependence-corrected population estimate; its existence nevertheless withdraws the record's claim that evaluator-generated, elicitation-created problem populations are unprecedented ("software inspection never faced" this).

Novelty confidence: Medium, on an INCOMPLETE search record. Medium not Low: no source located anywhere computes a cross-team overlap statistic on one checkpoint with a declared equivalence relation and IRR, and limb (a) remains unlocated after three adversaries. Not High and not a complete record: Gate 2 never searched HCI, the field that has studied this exact structure for 25 years; all arXiv listing routes were blocked; the NIST joint-testing document and the UK–US testing report PDF were never opened; and adversaries 2 and 3 could not run a single Disguise web query. Disguise is therefore only partly executed — one adversary's 8 queries, graded Partial — and counts as UNVERIFIED overall, which independently bars Validated status regardless of the rest of the record.

Significance — consequence: if YES (a finite, dependence-corrected bound with passing IRR), the field gets its first computable coverage quantity and two decisions now made by intuition become computable — commission an Nth external team, or extend an existing team's budget. If NO in the clean-negative form, coverage claims in safety cases are shown unmeasurable by this route and the intervention shifts from "more teams" to deliberately decorrelated scaffolds and taxonomies. If IRR fails, the field learns it cannot count its own findings, which indicts every report format that presents findings as an enumerable list.

Significance — audience: AISI/CAISI-type testing programmes designing joint and sequential exercises; lab external-red-team coordinators choosing cohort size versus per-team depth; safety-case authors and their reviewers; drafters of adequacy-of-testing language; and the method-owning communities, for whom a non-closed, elicitation-generated population is a hard new test case. The audience demonstrably runs the exercises and writes the coverage caveat itself ("These tests were conducted in a limited time period with finite resources"; expanded time and resources "could expand the scope of findings"), but no document found shows any of these parties asking for a coverage statistic; demand is inferred from their decisions, not evidenced.

Significance — fecundity: marginal return per evaluator-hour across teams versus scaffolds; a cohort diversity metric predicting joint coverage; whether failure-class accumulation follows a Heaps-type law in elicitation effort; whether cross-team rediscovery predicts post-deployment incident discovery; whether the same machinery bounds what automated pipelines miss relative to humans; and whether "failure mode" admits any counting-stable equivalence relation, a prerequisite for several other proposed coverage metrics.

Significance — anchoring: the vulnerability-rediscovery/stockpiling debate (N2); software inspection's unresolved small-k accuracy and stated application gap (N3); HCI's evaluator effect and its unresolved problem-matching reliability; documented non-reproducibility of red-teaming headline numbers (arXiv:2606.05233); the qualitative coverage deficit in safety-case confidence work; and the concentration and template-convergence of attack discovery in public competitions (N1), the candidate's own list-dependence mechanism appearing as an untreated anomaly.

Reason for silence: mechanism (1) as written is WITHDRAWN. The record's primary mechanism — "absent construct: with no unit, the missing-mass question does not present itself as a measurable one, so it is not asked" — is contradicted by two sources adversaries opened in the candidate's own field: a safety-evals course module that asks it in so many words ("怎样把'还剩多少'算出来而非靠眼睛" — how do we compute how many are left rather than going by eye), computes Chao1 as a lower bound, pools several red-teamers by rarefaction against one person at triple effort, sets a saturation stopping rule and names both violations (non-independent sampling; model patched mid-campaign) — while supplying no individuation criterion, only "去重"; and a public machine-generated research idea proposing Lincoln-Petersen/Chao estimation of undiscovered jailbreaks across two or more independent samplers (June 2026). Mechanism (2), disciplinary boundary, is weakened: capture-recapture is being imported into LLM evaluation and reviewer tooling routinely in 2026, including five independent repositories citing N3 to build overlap-based stopping rules. What survives is mechanism (3), the incentive and confidentiality gap — NDAs, pre-deployment timelines, system-card summarisation, and a number that is unflattering in both directions — plus genuinely new data (same-checkpoint joint institute testing only since late 2024). Mechanism (3) explains why the measurement has not been MADE; it does not explain why the question was not ASKED, which is what this attack tests. Ruling on the grey-literature question: unvetted teaching material and an automated idea pipeline are not "the literature or public discourse" in the sense that makes a question asked, so adversary 2's Unresolved on this attack is taken at its own stated downgrade condition to Partial — but half the record's silence account falls either way.

7 Reason for silence | mechanism (1) "absent construct" is contradicted by opened material in the candidate's own field that poses and computes the missing-mass question without any individuation criterion; mechanism (2) is crossed routinely in 2026 | unvetted course material and a machine-generated idea are not the literature, and neither touches limb (a); mechanism (3) plus new data survive, but they explain why the measurement is not made, not why the question was not asked | Partial (A1, A3; A2 graded Unresolved and specified the downgrade to Partial if a verifier rules unvetted teaching material out of scope — this judge so rules, and strikes mechanism (1))
8 Dissolution | overlap is a monotone function of granularity, so the "rate" may dissolve into a choice of relation; both opened sources pick the relation arbitrarily in practice (unvalidated cosine 0.8; criterion-free "去重") | the looser/stricter arms expose granularity-dependence instead of hiding it, and an IRR failure is itself a reportable answer about report formats; but the record does not pre-commit to what follows if the verdict flips qualitatively between the arms | Partial (all three)

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-48-verification.md): the load-bearing empirical leg is CONFIRMED and the methods leg is only PARTLY SOURCED.
Confirmed: the published UK AISI account of the joint US AISI / UK AISI pre-deployment evaluation of the upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet describes separate but complementary tests rather than one shared suite, and the per-domain detail bears that out — in cyber, US AISI used 40 public challenges while UK AISI used 47 (15 public, 32 private); in software and AI development, US AISI used public ML-improvement challenges while UK AISI used private evaluations; only US AISI's biology findings are published; both red-teamed safeguards, US AISI with public jailbreaks and UK AISI with public and private ones. Access is described once, as a "limited period of pre-deployment access", with no per-team access levels. Findings are reported by institute with no item-level or shared-item results. So no finding-level overlap can be reconstructed from the published record even for the one exercise with k = 2, which is the presupposition this candidate's limb (b) needs. The referenced technical report was not opened; if it carries item-level results the presupposition could be partly rescued, and that is the one route to re-filing.
Partly sourced: the capture-recapture leg. Chao (1987) confirms the estimator "can be regarded only as a lower bound" and rests on mutual independence, and a Chao 1987 scan gives Schnabel-type estimators as "negatively biased by heterogeneity of capture probabilities"; arXiv:1703.03022 confirms the Lincoln-Petersen independence assumption and that dependence between two captures is poorly studied. But no primary source was found for the specific statement about what is estimable at exactly two lists — the checker's two-list reasoning is its own, and Brittain and Bohning (2009) was blocked (Anubis access denied). This entry therefore rests the rejection on the verified data-availability failure, not on the unsourced identifiability claim, which is recorded as reasoning.
Status of the unrun checks: adversary #2 executed 0 of its 8 required Disguise queries (shared search budget) — UNVERIFIED under the amended Gate 4 rule, blocking Validated but not grounding the rejection.

Scores: Well-posedness 1/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness falls from the record's self-scored 2/3 because the failure is not only the deferred equivalence relation: limb (b) as worded requires two estimator families on a ">=2-list" matrix that cannot carry either of them at k=2, and its vacuity test is non-diagnostic in that regime. Limb (a) alone is well-posed. Significance stays 2/3: consequence argued in both directions with a real decision (cohort size versus per-team depth) and an audience that demonstrably runs the exercises and writes its own coverage caveat, against unevidenced demand and the unresolved P5 data-sharing constraint.

Strongest remaining objection: Rejected at Gate 4, attack 4 (presupposition failure), Unresolved from adversary 3 and sourced to opened text in the candidate's own regime rather than asserted — and separately barred from Validated because Disguise is unverified (two of three adversaries ran zero Disguise web queries) and because the Gate 2 record is incomplete (HCI never searched; NIST joint-testing document and UK–US report PDF never opened; all arXiv listing routes blocked). The single strongest objection: the question's own frame defeats its own limb (b). At the only k it has a verified instance for — two institutes on one checkpoint — list dependence is not estimable from a three-cell incomplete table, the identifying assumption is untestable and estimates under different assumptions can be "arbitrarily different ... even when the models have identical fits to the observed data" (arXiv:2101.09304, opened), the heterogeneous-catchability family the record names is "non-robust in the case with two reviewers and produces underestimates" (N3, hosted primary), and the declared vacuity test passes by construction whenever the both-found cell is non-empty. So "does that overlap support a non-vacuous estimate" is decided by the analyst's assumption, not by the overlap; and the one exercise anybody opened is not even the same test on both sides ("separate but complementary tests", different suites, undocumented access and hours), so P2 is unmet where it was supposed to be strongest. This is NOT a disguised-known rejection: limb (a) — a cross-team rediscovery rate under a declared equivalence relation with IRR on the match decision — remains unlocated after three adversaries, and a re-posed k>=3 version with a concrete, pilot-tested relation is a different candidate that would have to run the whole pipeline again, Disguise included.

Pointer only; not taken here.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The rejection ground is presupposition failure at Gate 4, not already-asked-and-still-open, so routed-open-problems.md gets no row. The two public articulations of limb (b) that adversaries found — a machine-generated research idea and an unvetted course module — are grey or synthetic rather than literature, and this judge has ruled them out of scope for "asked"; they are recorded here so a later reviewer can weigh them, not routed as an open problem.

---
ID: UQ-20261016-49
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — numeric formats and large-scale pretraining systems. Neighbour vocabularies reached: signal processing (block floating point / shared exponent / flush-to-zero), compression fairness (PTQ and QAT disparate impact), differential privacy (gradient-noise disparate impact), multilingual NLP, CV long-tailed recognition, rare-word ASR.

Question (canonical): For matched pretraining runs differing only in numeric format (BF16 control vs MXFP8 vs MXFP4/NVFP4; identical data, order, seed, token count), what is the slope beta of the per-stratum held-out loss gap to the BF16 control against log training-corpus frequency, and does that slope (i) differ from zero against a seed-variance baseline and (ii) track the per-block flush-to-zero rate of gradient entries resolved by the same strata? (Gate 1 reformulation, one allowed; Version A — "is the low-precision loss penalty uniform across the data distribution or does it grow with rarity?" — recorded in batches/2026-10-16-1833/UQ-20261016-49-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
1. Does 4-bit block-scaled training cost the same everywhere in the corpus, or does it quietly delete the long tail?
2. Is the published aggregate penalty of low-precision training an average hiding a frequency-dependent gradient?
3. (Neighbour's words) Is aggregate validation loss a sufficient statistic for accepting a training numeric format, or does the format have a disparate impact on under-represented strata?
(Gate 4 note: formulations 1-2 still carry the "deletes the tail" thesis that the opened evidence puts in doubt; they should be neutralised before any promotion.)

Motivating gap: Block-scaled sub-8-bit pretraining reached production hardware in 2025-26, so the question can for the first time be put to the training process rather than to post-hoc compression, and the decision it bears on (which format for a nine-figure run) is being made on aggregate loss alone. NVIDIA's 10T-token NVFP4 report (arXiv 2509.25149) contains one visible non-uniformity — Code 59.52→56.67, HumanEval+ 59.93→57.43, MBPP+ 59.11→55.91, Winogrande 80.58→78.77 — disposed of with "We suspect the difference could be due to noisy evaluations": an anomaly reported and not asked about. Adversary #3 verified these numbers in the PDF and added a correction the record omitted: on the paper's only data-side strata NVFP4 beats FP8 (Multilingual 77.93→80.24, Global MMLU 74.00→74.94, MGSM 81.87→85.53), which weakens the anchoring anomaly and leaves the sign genuinely open.

Presuppositions:
1. Established — block-scaled sub-8-bit pretraining is in production (2509.25149; ICML 2026 NVFP4 scaling study; vendor recipe).
2. Established — per-block FTZ is instrumentable in a real stack (2602.02047 defines and computes it); verified independently by adversaries #2 and #3.
3. Established — frequency-binned per-token loss is a working instrument (2410.11985).
4. Scope limit — requires an open corpus to compute frequencies.
5. CONTESTED — detectability at affordable scale transfers to frontier scale.
6. CONTESTED — tail effect exceeds seed noise.
7. CONTESTED — rare-stratum estimator is not noise-dominated. (Adversary #2 notes this is milder than stated: both runs score the same held-out tokens, so a paired per-token difference cancels most eval-sampling noise.)
8. CONTESTED, newly undermined — that "rare = small gradient entries". Bagdasaryan 2019: under-represented data "produces larger gradients"; adversary #3: a poorly predicted rare token has |p-y|≈1 at the output.
9. NEW, raised at Gate 4, unaddressed — that per-stratum FTZ is well defined under the named recipe. 2509.25149 applies stochastic rounding to gradients in both Dgrad and Wgrad and a 16x16 Random Hadamard Transform to Wgrad inputs, and keeps embeddings, the output head, norms and 16% of linear layers in BF16/FP32. Cross-token co-location exists only in the Wgrad path, which is exactly where the RHT mixes 16 tokens per quantized entry.

What would count as an answer: matched runs at >=2 scales in BF16/MXFP8/MXFP4; pre-registered stratification (primary: token log-frequency bins; secondary: entity-frequency deciles, language tier); primary readout = per-stratum loss gap fitted against log frequency, beta with CI; decision rule fixed in advance ("tail-differential" = beta != 0 against a >=3-seed BF16 null; "uniform" = beta ~ 0 with CI excluding a pre-stated practically relevant magnitude); per-bin standard errors reported and the fit weighted; mechanism check = per-stratum FTZ tracking beta; intervention check = block size / stochastic rounding / block-layout permutation must move beta if the block-scale story is right. A flat, tightly bounded slope is a publishable answer. Gate 4 adds two requirements the record does not meet: the normalization of the gap (absolute nats vs ratio to the aggregate gap) must be pre-registered, and a capacity-matched BF16 control (or capacity-normalized beta) is needed so a positive slope is not pre-explained by reduced effective parameter count.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 web searches across four agents (11 Gate 2 + 9 adversary #1; adversaries #2 and #3 were refused all 17 of their attempted searches by an exhausted run-wide budget), plus 5+7+4+4 fetches and 31 free GitHub probes. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-1833/UQ-20261016-49-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
- `MXFP4 NVFP4 pretraining loss degradation uneven across data distribution` → Priors 1 and 2; the two most on-point in-field items, both opened.
- [obvious-title] `arxiv "low-precision training" rare token frequency stratified loss "not uniform" quantization block size` → TARQ (2605.27808) and RSQ (2503.01820), both post-training methods using rarity as a knob; nothing asks the candidate's question.
- `"quantization-aware training" ... disparate impact underrepresented subgroups ... "tail" accuracy` (adversary #1) → ICML 2025 *Understanding the Unfairness in Network Quantization* — training-time (QAT), class-imbalance-driven disparity. Falsifies the record's claim that the compression-fairness family is "all post-hoc".
- `"differential privacy has disparate impact" ... quantization noise training long tail` (adversary #1) → Bagdasaryan et al. 2019, opened: "accuracy of DP models drops much more for the underrepresented classes"; same page says those data "produce larger gradients", which inverts the candidate's mechanism.
- `"double bind" pruning "low-resource" quantization compression languages` (adversary #3, GitHub) → Ahia, Kreutzer & Hooker 2021 (arXiv 2110.03036) abstract: "sparsity preserves performance on frequent sentences but has a disparate impact on infrequent ones" — a training-time compression, frequency-stratified, from 2021.
- `"What Matters for NVFP4 Training"` → icml.cc abstract only; OpenReview id jlkIyaG32w. COULD NOT READ (routes failed: icml.cc full text, openreview.net/pdf CLIENT_ERROR, web search). Four attempts across three agents.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. *Pretraining LLMs with NVFP4*, arXiv:2509.25149 (NVIDIA 2025), opened and re-verified by adversary #3. Unit: the run / the finished model. Endpoint: aggregate validation loss plus category-grouped accuracy. Comparator: FP8 (BF16 at smaller scale). Estimand: average quality gap of the format.
2. *Dissecting Outlier Dynamics in LLM NVFP4 Pretraining*, arXiv:2602.02047 (2026), opened; existence and headline numbers re-verified by adversaries #1 and #2. Unit: tensors, 16x16 blocks, channels, operators. Endpoint: kurtosis, top-k magnitude, per-block FTZ ratio, MSE; loss gap to BF16 (0.939% vs 0.588% CHON, GLA-1.3B / 60B tokens). Estimand: average gap plus architecture-conditioned correlations.
3. *The Fair Language Model Paradox*, arXiv:2410.11985 (2024), opened. Unit: tokens in log-frequency bins. Endpoint: per-token loss / accuracy / learning speed against the conventional average. Comparator: weight decay = 0. Estimand: disparate depreciation of low-frequency tokens under weight decay.
Supporting / raised at Gate 4: *Lost in Quantization* (PROPOR 2026, abstract only; +18% EN vs +3.9% PT-BR under naive FP8 — opposite sign to the candidate's premise); ICML 2025 *Understanding the Unfairness in Network Quantization* (QAT, weights only, CNNs; disparity attributed to group gradient norm and Hessian trace); Bagdasaryan et al. 2019 (arXiv 1905.12101); Ahia, Kreutzer & Hooker 2021 (arXiv 2110.03036); Kumar et al. 2411.04330 (precision reduces "effective parameter count", 465 pretraining runs, abstract only).

Novelty — how this differs from each:
1. Same intervention and comparator family, different unit and estimand: Prior 1's estimand is an average parity claim, the candidate's is the derivative of the gap with respect to log corpus frequency. The candidate partly asks whether Prior 1's acceptance statistic is sufficient.
2. Closest work; shares intervention, comparator and the FTZ instrument. Differs on the conditioning variable: Prior 2 indexes by tensor/channel/operator, never by data stratum. Limb (ii) is a change of index on an existing instrument — which is why combinatorial novelty is only Partial.
3. Identical readout, different intervention and mechanism: weight decay is a regularizer on parameter norms and makes no prediction about block size, stochastic rounding or block layout.
vs ICML 2025 / Bagdasaryan / Ahia: all establish that a training-time perturbation (QAT on weights with full-precision gradients; clipping plus isotropic noise; magnitude pruning) can disparately harm under-represented data. None quantizes backward-pass GEMM operands under a shared block scale, none stratifies by corpus token frequency in an LLM pretraining run, none fits a slope, none measures FTZ by stratum. That residue is what is unasked; the general question is not.

Novelty confidence: Medium — held, but suspect. Medium rather than High because Prior 2 is one index away and Prior 3 supplies the method; not Low because no opened source states the candidate's estimand or conditions a training-format loss gap on any data stratum. Suspect because Disguise was never verified by search (below), the record's self-named largest hole is still unread after four attempts, and adversary #3's reason-for-silence attack is Unresolved, which under the ledger's own rule sends the novelty finding back to Gate 2.

Significance — consequence: If beta > 0, the statistic now used to accept a numeric format for a nine-figure run integrates over exactly the strata carrying the penalty, and the mitigations (block size, stochastic rounding, selective high-precision tensors, layout permutation) are already in vendors' hands — the intervention check says which to buy. If beta ~ 0 with a tight CI, aggregate loss is licensed as sufficient and the post-hoc-compression intuition is shown not to transfer to training arithmetic. If the slope is real but unrelated to per-stratum FTZ, the phenomenon survives and the block-scale account is falsified.

Significance — audience: pretraining leads choosing a format (MXFP8 vs MXFP4 at equal aggregate loss is the live, dated decision); hardware vendors and recipe authors, whose published artifact is an evaluation table; multilingual/low-resource NLP, who currently have no instrument to demand; compression-fairness researchers, who get a boundary condition on their own claim. Discounted at Gate 4: several named mitigations are already standard ablation axes, so a "yes" changes a reported table more than it changes a practice, and audience 3 can demand but not decide.

Significance — fecundity: per-stratum precision scaling laws; whether training-format and post-hoc-quantization tail taxes compound; whether magnitude-aware block assignment is a free mitigation; whether "precision-aware data mixing" is coherent; whether the published Code-category regressions are instances of the same effect; FTZ-by-stratum as an online tail-health monitor; whether optimizer-state rather than GEMM precision carries the effect.

Significance — anchoring: the unexplained Code and Winogrande regressions in 2509.25149 (verified, but offset by that paper's favourable multilingual deltas); the aggregate form of precision scaling laws (Kumar et al. 2411.04330, abstract only); the compression-forgetting family; the Ahia et al. low-resource double bind (verified real this run); the sign anomaly in PROPOR 2026; Prior 2's open question of what the flushed "small-but-nonzero signals" carried.

Reason for silence: Claimed — (1) new instrument, block-scaled sub-8-bit training only producible on Blackwell-class hardware in 2025-26; (2) a disciplinary boundary in the expensive direction, between those who can buy a matched control run and those who own the disparate-impact method; (3) vendor-authored format evaluations have no incentive to look for a losing slice; (4) corpus access. Gate 4 leaves this Unresolved: matched low-precision-vs-BF16 runs at academic scale were plentiful from 2024 (Kumar et al.'s 465 pretraining runs; Prior 2's own 1.3B/60B-token gaps on RedPajama), and the frequency-stratified readout of a training-time compression has existed since Ahia et al. 2021, so method and a cheap object sat in the same academic hands for years. Mechanisms 2-4 explain why no one could answer or publish, not why no one asked; only the block-scaled-object leg survives, and it narrows to the Wgrad path.

Verification (post-batch: a 12-query prior-art sweep, log UQ-20261016-49-disguise-sweep.md, and a 6-query neighbours check, log UQ-20261016-49-neighbours-verification.md): Disguise is RESOLVED on executed evidence, and the neighbour claim that pressed this entry is confirmed in general and refuted for the instance.
Nothing in print asks or answers this question. Its three ingredients exist in three separate literatures and no source joins them. (1) Matched-control block-scaled sub-8-bit pretraining exists and is reported only in aggregate: “Pretraining Large Language Models with NVFP4” (arXiv:2509.25149, 12B hybrid Mamba-Transformer, 10T tokens) compares against a higher-precision FP8 run of the same recipe with the unit of analysis the benchmark CATEGORY — General, MMLU-family, Math, Multilingual (Global MMLU and MGSM aggregates), Code, Commonsense — never decomposed by rarity: no token-frequency bucketing, no per-language split inside the multilingual aggregate, no long-tail-knowledge split. The only deficit it discusses is coding (“The exception is the coding task, where NVFP4 falls slightly behind”), attributed to possibly noisy evaluation. The MXFP8 recipes paper (arXiv:2506.08027) was never opened, so a rarity ablation inside it is unlikely but unchecked. (2) Rarity-stratified loss measurement exists, aimed at a different knob: “The Fair Language Model Paradox” (arXiv:2410.11985) bins per-token loss by corpus frequency in powers of 3 and shows aggregate loss staying flat while low-frequency-token loss degrades — exactly this question's uniform-versus-graded contrast — but the intervention is weight decay, and precision appears only as a setup detail. (3) Non-uniform degradation from numeric compression exists post-training: “How Does Quantization Affect Multilingual LLMs?” (arXiv:2407.03211, unit = language and script class, Japanese -1.7% automatic against -16.0% human), “The Uneven Impact of Post-Training Quantization in Machine Translation” (arXiv:2508.20893), and the compression-fairness lineage (arXiv:1911.05248, arXiv:2010.03058); with DP-SGD's disparate-subgroup result (arXiv:1905.12101) alongside. Every one of those treats an already-trained network or private training, so none can speak to a penalty accumulating during pretraining, which is where the shared-exponent mechanism would act.
So the record's “general question already asked and answered in three other vocabularies” is correct as stated and does not reach the instance: none of the three concerns block-scaled low-precision pretraining with a shared per-block exponent, and the one pretraining paper that does reports aggregates only. Mechanism-side searches returned nothing on point — block-floating-point and shared-exponent vocabulary gave hardware documentation with no data-distribution endpoint; heavy-tailed rate-distortion results (arXiv:2411.08549, arXiv:2212.14562) are about sources, not a model's loss on rare data; “Stochastic Rounding for LLM Training” (arXiv:2502.20566) has no subpopulation endpoint; the closest mechanistic framing (arXiv:2608.08188) is weight-only PTQ at 2-4 bits with no rarity axis. One informal signal that the framing is circulating unstudied: a May 2026 blog post on an int4 quality cliff on the long tail — not print, not block-scaled, no controlled comparison.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness reduced from the record's 3/3 by attack 5: the primary estimand's normalization is unfixed and the record's two statements of it conflict. Significance reduced from 3/3: the anchoring anomaly is partly offset by Prior 1's favourable multilingual deltas, the mitigations are already shipped, and decision-relevance rests on an unstated magnitude.)

Strongest remaining objection (Disguise is now verified, so the objection is the mechanism one): adversary #3's reading of the actual NVFP4 recipe. The cross-token co-location that makes the instance format-specific exists only in the Wgrad path, where a 16x16 Hadamard transform mixes 16 tokens into every quantized entry and stochastic rounding is already applied to gradients. If that dissolves the residue, what is left is an instrument swap on an asked question. Second, unchanged: the primary estimand's normalization is left unfixed and self-contradictory, which is what holds well-posedness at 2/3 and caps this entry.
What is no longer an objection: that Disguise was never run. ID: UQ-20261016-50
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — data layer (pretraining quality filtering, data-exhaustion forecasting); method from measurement/reliability theory (inter-rater reliability, G-theory, no-gold-standard latent-class accuracy).
Question (canonical): Treating each published pretraining quality filter as a measurement instrument applied to one fixed Common Crawl sample at a matched keep rate, how much do the filters agree on which documents are "high quality" — pairwise agreement, the size of the all-filters intersection, and the share of the keep decision attributable to the document rather than to the filter — and by how much does the field's estimate of how much high-quality text the web still holds move across equally defensible filters?
Alternative formulations: (1) Is "high-quality web data" a property of documents or of the classifier that picked them? (2) If two teams filter the same crawl with their own published classifiers at the same keep rate, what fraction of the kept corpus is common, and do models trained on each keep-set and on the intersection differ beyond seed noise?
Motivating gap: Curation discards most of the web on a classifier's say-so; the intake held that no one treats filters as instruments with a reliability, and nominated Nemotron-CC as ensembling scorers in a way that presupposes material disagreement "while never reporting how much". Verified by reading: that central claim is false — quantifying the disagreement is the paper's stated justification for ensembling, and the number is in its Table 8. The "comparisons rank filters by downstream score" claim survives.
Presuppositions: P1 filters publicly runnable on a common sample — supported (DCLM fastText and two NVIDIA scorers released; FineWeb-Edu carries a licence question, excluded from Nemotron-CC's ensemble for that reason). P2 matched keep rates are the right footing — contested; all priors operate at native rates. P3 agreement interpretable with no gold standard — contested, conceded as part of the point. P4 exhaustion forecasts depend on a variable quality criterion — mixed: Villalobos defines quality by downstream performance via a filter-retained fraction (10–40%), but its 95% interval [22T, 490T] (~22x) is already built from inter-filter disagreement, so a per-filter spread is pre-absorbed. P5 one snapshot generalises — untested by any prior. P6 document-level is the right unit — contested. P7 (added at Gate 2) chance-corrected agreement computable from published data — partially refuted: Nemotron-CC Table 8 is union-restricted (cells sum exactly to the printed total), so it supplies no true-negative cell.
What would count as an answer: (1) an agreement matrix on one fixed stratified CC sample at matched and native keep rates (pairwise agreement, kappa, |∩K| as a share of each keep-set, document-vs-filter variance decomposition, with CIs); (2) per-filter sensitivity/specificity against a latent quality class under a no-gold-standard latent-class model, or demonstrated unidentifiability; (3) the remaining-high-quality-token stock recomputed per filter as a max/min spread against the forecast's declared uncertainty; (4) optionally, fixed-compute models trained on each keep-set, the intersection and the symmetric difference against a pre-registered seed-variance band. High agreement answers as firmly as low. Gate 2 finding against this list: (1) is published for K=2 at native rates; (3) is absorbed by the forecast's own ~22x interval; (2) and (4) are untouched.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 searches + 5 fetches at Gate 2, all reached on the first arxiv.org route, none refused; full list in batches/2026-10-16-1833/UQ-20261016-50-record.md. Significance — consequence: Heavily discounted. The dramatic branch ("filters barely agree") is already the published state of the world, and the high-agreement branch is effectively closed. What stays unsettled is narrower: whether 10.1% is near chance or far above it, whether it survives rate-matching, and whether the keep decision is mostly filter variance (every single-filter corpus an instrument artefact) or document variance with filters measuring different real properties (benign, and recommending the opposite action).
Significance — audience: Real but largely already served on the headline — NVIDIA computed the overlap and acted on it by ensembling; HuggingFace FineWeb, AI2/Dolma, DCLM authors and Epoch AI would act on a matched-rate reliability figure or an attribution of the [22T, 490T] interval. The method-owning audience (psychometrics, no-gold-standard diagnostic accuracy) has no stake in web corpora.
Significance — fecundity: Moderate — internal disagreement of A's ensemble, line- vs document-level agreement, stability across dumps and languages, whether "the high-quality web" can be an estimand at all. Weakened because the most striking limb is compute-bound for the method-owning field and unincentivised for the corpus-owning one.
Significance — anchoring: Data-exhaustion scaling literature and its ~22x interval; the IR assessor-disagreement result (Voorhees, SIGIR 1998, revisited arXiv:2502.20937) as the verified isomorph; the web's absent sampling frame; identifiability limits on latent-class models with correlated errors.
Reason for silence: Not applicable to the headline, which was not silent (A 2024, B 2024). For the residue, two unevidenced mechanisms: an incentive gradient inside the data-owning field — A reads its own number as a recall deficit to be fixed by ensembling, under which disagreement is a resource and no kappa, rate-matching or decomposition is called for; and a disciplinary boundary with no traffic inward, corroborated in four method-owning vocabularies (LCA, crowdsourcing/Dawid-Skene, ensemble diversity, G-theory: zero transplant), plus one licence artefact barring the best-resourced group from a K≥3 comparison including FineWeb-Edu. Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Attack 4. The filters are not competing instruments for one construct — FineWeb-Edu scores "educational", DCLM instruction-likeness, the Nemotron scorers their own annotators' taste — so inter-filter agreement is not a reliability coefficient, low agreement is the predicted and uninformative outcome, and this objection bites the surviving residue (matched-rate kappa, K≥3, variance decomposition) as hard as it bites the published headline. Attack 8's confounding of the document×filter interaction with residual error in a deterministic single-observation design runs a close second, since it attacks the one limb the residue's consequence rests on.

That separates "filters disagree" from "filters agree no better than chance" — and it belongs to a new candidate's Gate 0, not to this entry.

It needs its own Gate 0 and inherits no status from this entry.
