ID: UQ-20261016-51
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Status change (post-batch): Rejected → Provisional. Both legs of the disguised-known kill failed on checking: the tooling said to measure answer disagreement measures answer presence, and the claim about MMLU's keys is contradicted by MMLU's own paper. A late strict adversary with 12 executed Disguise queries returned Provisional and could source no kill.
Domain(s): AI architecture — evaluation methodology and the training-data layer (benchmark contamination, decontamination practice). Method neighbours: data poisoning / misinformation dose-response; knowledge-conflict QA; educational measurement (item compromise).

Question (canonical): For a pre-registered item frame and an open-data model whose pretraining corpus is indexed (OLMo/Dolma, Pythia/Pile, LLM360, DCLM), retrieving every corpus occurrence of an item stem above a fixed fuzzy-match threshold and classifying each into {states gold, states non-gold, states no answer, gold itself erroneous}: (a) what are the occurrence- and item-weighted class fractions, with CIs and a reported extractor precision/recall on a human-adjudicated sample; and (b) conditioning on difficulty estimated from zero-occurrence models, is accuracy on non-gold-dominated items (>=50% of answer-stating occurrences disagree with gold) below accuracy on matched occurrence-free items — i.e. is the contamination correction to a reported score signed, and how many points does it move when non-gold-dominated items are removed rather than retained? (Gate 1 version 2; intake version 1 in the record.)

Alternative formulations:
- When a benchmark question leaks into pretraining data, does the leak carry the right answer — and what happens to the score when it does not?
- Is decontamination removing a penalty as well as a bonus: what share of leaked items teaches a non-gold answer, and what does that do to the measured score?

Motivating gap (source method: anomaly mining): contamination retrieval tools (WIMBD, infini-gram, OLMoTrace) report occurrence counts and score inflation; the record held that none reports what the retrieved occurrence asserts. Decontamination filters delete by string match regardless of the answer carried, presuming a one-signed effect. Sat beside MMLU-Redux's ~6.5% gold-label error rate, the wrong-key quality of web copies, and the unexplained GPQA non-improvement in arXiv:2508.13180.

Presuppositions: (1) items are retrievable in an open corpus — established; (2) occurrences usually state a parseable answer — contested; (3) "gold label" well-defined — contested (MMLU-Redux 6.49%, verified by adversary 3 at aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.262.pdf, which also prints ">9%" unreconciled); (4) difficulty-matched comparison items constructible — contested; (5) corpus occurrence proxies exposure — established for open-data models only; (6) occurrence frequency measurable — established. Unflagged and now falsified: (7) the field presumes a contaminated score is an upper bound; (8) the content/label of a contaminating copy has never been a variable.

What would count as an answer: a study over open-data models that retrieves every above-threshold occurrence for a pre-registered frame, classifies each into the four classes with a human-adjudicated sample and reported extractor P/R, reports class fractions with CIs, and estimates the accuracy contrast between non-gold-dominated, gold-dominated and zero-occurrence items under a pre-specified design. YES: measurable disagreement share and accuracy delta below matched clean items, CI excluding zero. NO: disagreement <~2%, or null within a stated MDE.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 web searches + 5 fetches, all logged in batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-51-record.md; most informative: own-field obvious title ("contamination with incorrect answers ... can lower accuracy rather than inflate") → surveys only; "already-computed fraction" probe → returned MMLU-Redux's label-error rate, not any occurrence-level disagreement rate; method-field probe (poisoning dose-response) → Alber et al. Nature Medicine, corpus-level injected documents only. Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full, 79 entries, no near-duplicate. Gate 4 added: adversary 1, 9 searches + 4 fetches (UQ-20261016-51-adversary-1.md; opened Magar & Schwartz arXiv:2203.08242 — gold-label injection only, "beyond the scope" footnote; PhishBencher arXiv:2505.18102; Soft Contamination arXiv:2602.12413). Adversary 2, 0 of 9 searches executed (web budget exhausted), 2 of 4 arXiv routes robots-blocked (UQ-20261016-51-adversary-2.md). Adversary 3, 0 of 7 searches executed, 4 arXiv listing fetches ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, 23 GitHub issue/code probes + 4 successful publisher fetches (UQ-20261016-51-adversary-3.md); the decisive probes were `"input-and-label" repo:open-compass/opencompass` and `repo:liyucheng09/Contamination_Detector`.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): the three that now decide the grade (record's priors A/B/C/D are in the record file).
P1 — Li, "An Open Source Data Contamination Report" line, as shipped in liyucheng09/Contamination_Detector and open-compass/opencompass (repo text read as GitHub code-search snippets by adversary 3; papers COULD NOT READ, budget). Unit: a benchmark item. Endpoint: accuracy on clean / input-only-contaminated / input-and-label-contaminated subsets (clean_dirty_comparison.py). Comparator: the clean subset. Estimand: per-class accuracy gap. Quoted: "Input-only contaminated set: the question appears online, but not its answer. Input-and-label contaminated set: both question and answer appear online"; search.py decides the class by matching the retrieved page against `query['label']`. OpenCompass docs show an input-contaminated subset BELOW clean (qwen-7b-hf, ceval-humanities 50.00 vs 67.44 clean; subset n small).
P2 — Gema et al., "Are We Done with MMLU?", NAACL 2025 long.262 (OPENED by adversary 3). Unit: an MMLU item. Endpoint: model agreement with an erroneous gold key. Estimand: label-error rate (6.49%) and memorisation inference — "this may be evidence of memorisation, suggesting that these MMLU instances were learned during the pretraining". Provenance quoted: items "collected from freely available online sources" (Quizlet, crackap.com, Oxford Learning Link, Electrical4U).
P3 — Palavalli, Bertsch, Gormley, "A Taxonomy for Data Contamination in LLMs", arXiv:2407.08716 (OPENED by adversary 3). Unit: a contaminated test instance under continued pretraining. Endpoint: downstream metric. Estimand: effect by contamination type; the label slot is already a variable (Masking, Noising "by using silver rather than gold labels"). Quoted sub-baseline result with no wrong label anywhere: "The MASKED setting generally performs around or worse than the BASELINE" (SQuAD EM 38.77 vs 41.76).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — the candidate splits P1's "input-only contaminated" class into {no answer stated, non-gold answer stated}, swaps the exposure instrument (Bing/web retrieval → indexed open pretraining corpus) and adds a gold-is-erroneous class; the partition, the per-class accuracy comparison and the answer-carried variable already exist. vs P2 — P2's wrong answer is the benchmark's own key, not a corpus document's assertion, and it reports no corpus-side fraction; but it supplies the provenance that makes the candidate's key class structurally thin and already treats key-agreement as a contamination signal. vs P3 — P3 injects rather than retrieves and has no counterfactual-label arm, but it falsifies the candidate's framing premise by showing sub-baseline contamination with no wrong label at all. The candidate's load-bearing negative — "none found reports what the retrieved occurrence asserts" — is false as stated.

Novelty confidence: Medium, restored from the Gate 4 downgrade to Low. The downgrade rested on P1 already partitioning retrieved copies by whether they carry the gold answer; a checker found that its “input-and-label contaminated” class means a question and an answer co-occur in the matched pages, with no comparison against the gold label anywhere in it. The closest neighbour is now infini-gram mini (arXiv:2506.12229), which scores contamination as the share of 50-character question substrings found in the corpus (clean under 20%, dirty 80% or more) and then has a gpt-4o-mini judge categorise dirty entries by whether “the correct answer” appears — answer presence, again, with no gold-agreement check and no accuracy split by contamination class. Medium rather than High because that pipeline shows the machinery for corpus-scale answer classification already exists, so the step to disagreement is small; and because 7 of the late adversary's 12 hit lists went unopened, with MMLU-Redux, Deng et al. (arXiv:2311.09783), Madness of Crowds and Barz and Denzler still unread.

Significance — consequence: if YES, the sign of the contamination correction becomes empirical and decontamination gains an answer-aware design axis; if NO (<~2% disagreement, null contrast), the one-signed assumption gets its first direct licence. Both are weakened by P1/P3: per-class contamination accuracy is already reported, negative gaps included, and deletion-based decontamination is polarity-blind by design — any exposure invalidates the item, so no maintainer needs the sign.

Significance — audience: harness and benchmark maintainers (lm-evaluation-harness — verified by adversary 2 as 13-gram, answer-blind, with no answer slot; OpenCompass — already ships the per-class report); open-data pretraining groups (AI2/Dolma, EleutherAI/Pythia, LLM360, DCLM) who own the indexes; eval-integrity auditors. Real audience, but the action attributed to it ("they would add an answer-polarity field") is asserted, not evidenced, and the expected score movement is sub-point.

Significance — fecundity: answer-aware decontamination and its calibration; whether wrong-answer and right-answer leakage differ in detectability; disagreement share by benchmark, subject and source genre; the mirror case (gold wrong, copies right); whether imitative falsehoods and contamination are one phenomenon at two scales.

Significance — anchoring: the non-monotonic contamination literature (prior A's U-shape; P3's MASKED sub-baseline); prior C's GPQA non-improvement; MMLU label error (6.49%, verified); poisoning dose-response (Alber et al.); the string-match filter primitive.

Reason for silence: offered as instrument shape plus disciplinary split plus an incentive asymmetry. Two legs fail: the content/label of a contaminating copy has been a variable since the input-vs-input-and-label partition (P1) and TS-Guessing's masked-distractor method, and the incentive argument inverts ("our scores are depressed" is highly publishable). What survives — the index tools return counts and spans, annotation is costly, and no maintainer owns an answer slot — explains why answering is expensive, not why no one asked. Adversary 3's alternative, that the non-gold class is expected to be tiny and the causal limb unidentifiable, is a reason the question is not worth asking, which Gate 4 routes back to Gate 2.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — merged across three adversaries, worst status per attack; verbatim logs in UQ-20261016-51-adversary-{1,2,3}.md:

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-51-verification.md): the disguised-known kill is REFUTED in the part it rested on, and its second leg is contradicted.
Confirmed: the three categories do exist. Li et al. (arXiv:2310.17589, “An Open Source Data Contamination Report for Large Language Models”) define clean, input contamination and input-and-label contamination, and the OpenCompass contamination harness uses them as column labels (“accuracy - clean”, “accuracy - input contaminated”, “accuracy - input-and-label contaminated”) without formal definitions. Published contaminated-below-clean results are real: Li's Tables 2 and 3 show them for MMLU with LLaMA 65B, Mistral 7B and Baichuan2 7B, for HellaSwag with Llama-2 13B, Mistral 7B and Yi 6B, for ARC with LLaMA 7B and 13B, and for C-Eval with Mistral 7B.
Refuted: neither source records whether a matched copy states an answer that DISAGREES with the gold label. “Input-and-label contaminated” means only that the question and an answer both occur in the matched pages. The candidate's class is therefore not a sub-partition of an existing class — it is a different variable, and this is the ledger's dominant error mode (a real tool, accurately described, doing a different thing) recurring.
Contradicted: no primary source was found for “MMLU's keys were scraped from the very pages that would constitute its occurrences”, and the late adversary then found MMLU's own paper saying the opposite — that most questions came from sources where questions and answers are on separate pages. The thinness objection survives in a different form (keyless copies may dominate) and is recorded above as a risk to limb (a).

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3 (the Gate 4 downgrade to 1/3 rested on the one-signed presumption having been “shown false” by the same tooling claim that has now failed; published contaminated-below-clean results do exist in Li et al.'s Tables 2 and 3, but with no wrong-answer condition in the design and, per the late adversary, against a released-BERT baseline rather than a matched clean run, so they establish that the sign is not uniformly positive without explaining why)

Strongest remaining objection (restated; the late adversary's, and it is about identification rather than novelty): limb (b) cannot be answered observationally. Wrong-answer contamination and intrinsic item difficulty are not separable in corpus data — items whose web copies disagree with the gold key are plausibly also items the key is wrong about, or items the web is confused about — so a signed correction needs an injection arm, not a conditioning design, and no source was found showing that a corpus majority answer drives the model's answer at all. Second, the reason-for-silence mechanism is weaker than the record claims: infini-gram mini already runs an LLM judge over corpus hits for answer presence, and Magar and Schwartz (arXiv:2203.08242) state “We assume that test instances appear in the pretrain corpus with their gold labels” and put the unlabelled case “beyond the scope of this paper” in a footnote. Together those suggest the case was noticed and set aside, not unseen — which is a weaker silence than an instrument gap. Third, and now the live risk to limb (a) rather than a kill: MMLU's own paper (arXiv:2009.03300) says its questions were “manually collected by graduate and undergraduate students from freely available sources online” and that most came from PDFs or websites where questions and answers sit on separate pages (summariser paraphrase, not an exact-string check). So keyless copies may dominate the occurrence population and make limb (a)'s answer-stating denominator thin — which the record already treats as a reportable NO.

Promotion conditions: (1) pre-register the injection arm, since the observational design cannot sign the effect on its own; (2) open the four unread neighbours — MMLU-Redux, Deng et al. (arXiv:2311.09783), Madness of Crowds, Barz and Denzler — and the five unopened hit lists from the late sweep; (3) report the answer-stating share of occurrences for one named item frame before anything else, since a thin denominator is the cheapest way this question dies.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The entry is Provisional, so its own question stays with the ledger. No adjacent posed question qualifies: the one asked-and-open fragment found in the file sits on an unauthored hypothesis page, which is not a posing source.

ID: UQ-20261016-52
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Status change (post-batch): Rejected → Provisional. The Gate 2 kill rested on four properties attributed to arXiv:2503.20783; a checker that opened the paper found two of them false and a third only hypothesised. The surviving overlap is narrow and capability-side, and it does not reach this candidate's safety-side endpoints.
Domain(s): AI architecture — pretraining/post-training pipeline design; construct validity of the released "base" checkpoint as the pre-post-training control. Method-owning neighbours: causal-inference/trial methodology (control-arm contamination, attenuation), ML metascience.

Question (canonical): Across the released "base" checkpoints that research uses as the pre-post-training control, how much post-training-like behaviour (refusal on harmful requests, chat-template preference, zero-shot instruction following, assistant-persona self-reference) is already present relative to a documented pre-instruction-era reference base, how far does that presence track instruction-formatted content in the pretraining corpus where the corpus is open, and by how much does it bias published estimates of what post-training adds?

Alternative formulations:
- Are "base" models still base — and if not, is every chat-minus-base comparison measuring a shrunken difference?
- What is the degree of post-training-like behaviour in the released pretraining-stage artifact, and what happens to published "alignment tuning does X" effect sizes when a cleaner control is substituted?
(Gate 1 reformulation retained in the record: pre-registered dated frame of base/instruct sibling pairs; limb (i) behaviour rates with CIs as a fraction of the base-to-chat gap, trended against release date and disclosed mid-training practice; limb (ii) instruction/chat-format token share on the open-data subset under a detector with reported precision/recall; limb (iii) re-estimation of >=2 published "post-training adds X" effects under a cleaner control. The reformulation separates PRESENCE from PROVENANCE; the intake phrase "post-training contamination" was dropped as presupposing provenance. Full text: batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-52-record.md.)

Motivating gap (source method: presupposition inversion): AlignmentForum "Base LLMs refuse too" scores 100 JailbreakBench harmful instructions under greedy decoding and reports released BASE models refusing ~48% on average vs ~90% for chat siblings, ~3% on harmless prompts in both, across Qwen1.5-0.5B, Gemma-2-9B and LLaMA-1-7B; it declines to attribute a cause. Meanwhile labs run curated mid-training/annealing stages with instruction-like data before releasing the base, and a large literature (superficial alignment, crosscoder/model diffing, "fine-tuning removes safety", "what RL adds") uses that released base as the untreated arm. Adversary #2 read the post in full and found the record understates it: the post's OWN limitations section already states that pretraining opacity "could blur the line between 'base' and 'chat' models" (the record attributed this to commenters), it already observes base chat-template behaviour, and its comment thread already names the clean test (Pythia) without running it.

Presuppositions (record's six, as re-graded here):
1. A credible "clean" reference base exists — CONTESTED; handled by posing the question as a gradient. Adversary #2 refutes the stronger form of the record's artifact-unavailability claim: the OLMo-2 model card documents Stage 1 (OLMo-Mix-1124, 3.9T) and Stage 2 (Dolmino-Mix-1124, 843B) separately and publishes intermediate pretraining revisions, so a stage-1 arm is public today (no revision is *labelled* a pre-Dolmino control).
2. The named behaviours are measurable above a stated null — record graded ESTABLISHED; DOWNGRADED to PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED. The anchor's detector is a refusal-phrase prefix match with authors' admitted incomplete recall and no reported precision on base continuations; n=100 per model gives ~+/-10 pp (adversary #2's own arithmetic, labelled as such), and "~48%" averages three such estimates. The 3% harmless-prompt rate remains real specificity evidence against pure degeneracy.
3. Instruction/chat-format content is detectable by corpus search with reportable precision — PLAUSIBLE, UNVERIFIED. The WIMBD/Dolma corpus-search line was never opened by any of the three agents. OLMo-2's card does state the stage-2 mix is "50% high-quality data + academic/Q&A/instruction/math content", which is disclosure, not a token share.
4. Published studies do use released bases as the untreated control — ESTABLISHED (arXiv:2312.01552, arXiv:2507.10532, arXiv:2406.05946, arXiv:2503.20783 all do).
5. Behavioural presence implies control bias in a direction that matters — CONTESTED and probably mis-stated by the record: adversary #1 argues (unsourced, so not weighed as a kill) that under genre provenance the base IS the correct counterfactual and chat-minus-base is unbiased, so validity does depend on provenance. Adversary #2 supplies the surviving descriptive core: a chat-minus-base contrast is arithmetically smaller than chat-minus-clean whenever the base already exhibits the outcome.
6. Base and chat siblings are otherwise comparable artifacts — CONTESTED, unchanged.

What would count as an answer: (i) a pre-registered behavioural battery across a dated frame of base/chat sibling pairs, rates with CIs as a fraction of the base-to-chat gap, trended against release date and disclosed mid-training practice; (ii) on the open-data subset, instruction/chat-format token share with detector precision/recall, tested against (i); (iii) re-estimation of >=2 published "post-training adds X" effects under a cleaner control, reporting movement against stated uncertainty. YES: presence rises with release date, tracks corpus share, re-estimation moves published effects beyond their intervals. NO: flat across eras, uncorrelated, substitution moves nothing. Specification defect found at Gate 4 and not repaired in the record: limb (iii)'s criterion "relative to its own stated uncertainty" has no referent for targets that publish no interval — including the record's own nominated target, URIAL, recorded as stating no percentage. No threshold is pre-specified for what share of the gap would count as invalidating a control.

vs P1': the difference is the endpoint set (refusal/persona/template-preference instead of template-free answering and math accuracy), the frame (a dated cross-releaser frame instead of three families), and provenance measured instead of hypothesised. Significance — consequence: unchanged in kind but reduced in increment. If YES, every chat-minus-base quantity is a shrunken difference with an era-dependent shrinkage factor, converting a qualitative worry into a correction term. If NO, refusal is a pretraining-distribution/genre property and base-vs-chat diffing measures style and format rather than acquisition. Both adversaries note the RL-side half of this consequence is already delivered by P1' and P2', and that the "cheap ask of the labs" (publish a pre-mid-training checkpoint, state the stage) is already satisfied by the releaser the record nominates as audience (d): OLMo-2 publishes stage boundaries, both datasets and intermediate revisions. What is not yet in place anywhere is the reporting NORM ("which base stage was the control?").
Significance — audience: real and already attentive — interpretability/model-diffing groups, safety-fine-tuning researchers, RL-for-reasoning researchers (who have demonstrably acted on exactly this control-validity argument, via P1'), base-checkpoint releasers, eval-methodology reviewers. Not inflated; its increment is narrowed to the safety/diffing side.
Significance — fecundity: reduced — the first-named opening (dose-response of mid-training instruction-like data on measured post-training gains) is P2'. Surviving: de-contamination of a base for control purposes; "base" as a disclosed graded stage with a published behavioural fingerprint; which other "alignment" behaviours are genre properties predictable from corpus composition; behaviour-based third-party audit of undisclosed mid-training practice.
Significance — anchoring: superficial-alignment dispute (arXiv:2312.01552, arXiv:2502.04602); shallow-safety-alignment work (arXiv:2406.05946); the RL-capability-boundary argument (arXiv:2503.20783, arXiv:2507.10532, arXiv:2601.11061); refusal-direction mechanistic work; benchmark-contamination methodology; emergent-abilities-as-measurement-artifact.

Reason for silence: NOT ESTABLISHED — and this is what sent the novelty finding back to Gate 2, as the gate instructs. Mechanism (1), "ML lacks the control-contamination vocabulary", is false for the capability endpoint (P1', in ML's own words) and circular as argued (it explains the Gate 2 null with the Gate 2 null). Mechanism (2), "the cleaner artifact does not exist publicly", is refuted for at least one releaser (public OLMo-2 stage-1 revisions, documented stage boundary, open corpus). Mechanism (3), the incentive story, is unevidenced and sits badly against the record's own cited P2, a published paper whose contribution is deflating other groups' effect sizes by a control-validity argument. The only mechanism left standing in either log is recency/lag: openly curated mid-training is two or three release generations old, and the safety community has not yet imported the RL-side result. That explains why the trend limb is newly measurable and why the full three-limb study is laborious — not why the question went unasked, which it did not.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-52-verification.md): the Gate 2 kill is PARTLY REFUTED. arXiv:2503.20783 is “Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective” (Zichen Liu, Changyu Chen, Wenjun Li, Penghui Qi, Tianyu Pang, Chao Du, Wee Sun Lee, Min Lin; v1 26 Mar 2025, v2 6 Oct 2025). Checked property by property: (a) it DOES test six base checkpoints from three families (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and 7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-Math-7B, DeepSeek-V3-Base) under an R1 template, a Qwen-Math template and no template, recording an “answering rate” on 500 MATH questions; (b) it only HYPOTHESISES that Qwen2.5-Math may have been pretrained on concatenated question-answer text, and does not test it or claim instruction data as the cause; (c) it does NOT re-estimate what post-training adds against the “nearly pure base model” — that checkpoint is used to ask whether the Aha moment pre-exists RL; (d) it does NOT conclude that published post-training gains are overstated. Unit: base checkpoint crossed with prompt template. Endpoint: answering rate, plus math accuracy, RL reward, response length, AIME 2024. Estimand: how much template-free answering and reasoning the base models already have before RL, and how much of the RL length growth comes from the GRPO objective. No safety-side endpoint appears anywhere in it.

Domain(s): AI architecture — pretraining-recipe and architecture ablation methodology. Method source: industrial statistics / design of experiments (alias matrices, estimability, split-plot handling of hard-to-change factors).

Question (canonical): Over a pre-registered frame of published pretraining-recipe and architecture ablation studies with sufficient configuration disclosure, reconstructing each headline comparison as a design matrix over a fixed twelve-factor list under a stated model including two-factor interactions: (i) in what share of headline claims is the claimed factor's main-effect column not estimable — exactly or near-collinear (above a pre-registered VIF / alias-coefficient threshold) with another factor's column or an interaction column — with inter-coder agreement and the insufficient-disclosure share reported separately; and (ii) for claims whose artifacts permit it, how large is the de-aliased effect relative to the reported effect against a pre-registered equivalence band from a same-configuration seed-variance study?
(Gate 1 reformulation, one permitted reformulation used; intake version asked for "design resolution" and judged limb (ii) against reported intervals, neither well defined for irregular single-seed ML designs. Both versions in batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-53-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
1. Are the field's pretraining "best practices" identified in the experimental-design sense, or are their main effects confounded by construction with whatever moved to hold a budget fixed?
2. What is the alias structure of the deep-learning ablation, and what do the recipe literature's conclusions look like after de-aliasing?
3. (lay) When a pretraining paper says "this change helped," how often did something else have to change with it, and does the claim survive changing them one at a time?

Motivating gap: Reported recipe/architecture gains routinely fail to transfer (Narang et al. 2021; Melis et al. 2018); the field's standing diagnosis is "the baseline was under-tuned." The DoE diagnosis — ML ablations are compute-constrained designs in which factors are deliberately co-moved to hold a budget fixed, the constrained/split-plot case for which DoE has an alias calculus — had never been counted as a measurable property of the literature. NOTE: Gate 4 falsified the stronger half of this gap (see attack 7).

Presuppositions: (1) enough configuration disclosure to reconstruct factor matrices — CONTESTED, exclusion rate reportable; (2) a separation criterion exists for irregular OFAT designs — resolved by the reformulation (alias matrix / column estimability, not a resolution integer); (3) co-moved factors have non-negligible effects — established for LR/batch size (Choi et al. 2019), contested for tokenizer and precision; (4) audited conclusions propagate into frontier recipes — plausible, unverified; (5) de-aliased re-runs feasible for a non-trivial subset — CONTESTED, limb (ii) confined to small-scale artifacts; (6) "co-moved with" is separable from "legitimately re-tuned for" — CONTESTED and load-bearing; this is the presupposition that failed at Gate 4.

What would count as an answer: (i) a coded frame under a pre-registered inclusion rule giving the non-estimable share, the alias-coefficient distribution for the correlated remainder, inter-coder kappa on the estimability verdict, and the undecidable share separately; (ii) for a sample with artifacts, de-aliased re-runs reporting effects with and without de-aliasing against a seed-variance equivalence band. YES: large non-estimable share, de-aliased effects shrinking below the band or reversing. NO: most designs separate their factor, or de-aliased estimates stay inside the band.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 searches + 5 fetches (both caps reached); adversary #1 added 9 searches + 4 fetches in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try; adversaries #2 and #3 could run 0 searches (shared 200-call budget exhausted before their first query) and 4 fetches each. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-53-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative: "experimental design resolution machine learning experiments aliasing" → DoE pedagogy only, no ML target; "split-plot design hard-to-change factors applied to deep learning training" → split-plot methodology only, no transplant; "trends in experimental design quality of machine learning ablation studies audit of papers" (mandated own-field journal-title form) → Troubling Trends (narrative), AbGen, the Wuppertal announcement, no on-point audit; mandated share-already-published probe → only Bouthillier/Varoquaux practice prevalences, no published share of non-estimable ablation claims; adversary #1 "scientific/nuisance hyperparameters tuning playbook confounded comparison" → located and opened the tuning playbook (decisive); adversary #1 Taguchi/orthogonal-array and Chinese-language probes → DoE-for-HPO tooling exists, no audit of published ablations; adversary #1 "fair comparison / are we really making much progress" → the re-run-under-uniform-protocol genre exists in other subfields.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Choi et al. 2019, "On Empirical Comparisons of Optimizers for Deep Learning", arxiv.org/pdf/1910.05446 (opened). Unit: optimizer x workload; endpoint: final error / steps-to-target; comparator: other optimizers under narrower tuning protocols; estimand: best outcome per optimizer at a fixed tuning budget and the induced ranking.
P2. Bouthillier & Varoquaux, ML experimental-methods survey, NeurIPS 2019 / ICLR 2020, gael-varoquaux.info (opened). Unit: a surveyed author's self-reported practice; endpoint: practice counts (tuning method, seeds, fits, baselines); comparator: none; estimand: practice prevalence in a venue-year population.
P3. Google "Deep Learning Tuning Playbook", github.com/google-research/tuning_playbook (opened independently by all three adversaries, same verbatim lines). Unit: a planned experimental round; endpoint: prescriptive protocol; comparator: none; estimand: none — doctrine, not measurement. Verbatim: "Nuisance hyperparameters are those that need to be optimized over in order to fairly compare"; "fixed hyperparameters create caveats for any conclusions we draw from the experiments"; "The more a given nuisance hyperparameter interacts with the scientific hyperparameters, the more damaging it is to fix its value"; "we may not be able to disentangle the separate effects on the results". Terms "alias", "fractional factorial", "design resolution", "split-plot" absent from the ~100k chars read.
Also opened by adversaries and bearing on Disguise: Kaddour et al. 2023 (arXiv 2307.06440) — efficient-training gains "vanish compared to a baseline with a fully-decayed learning rate" at fixed compute; Porian et al. 2024 (arXiv 2406.19146) — Kaplan/Hoffmann discrepancy resolved into "last layer computational cost, warmup duration, and scale-dependent optimizer tuning"; Yang et al. 2020 (arXiv 1912.12522) — "tricks in the evaluation protocol has a predominant impact"; Fostiropoulos & Itti 2023 ABLATOR (PMLR v224, opened, tooling not audit); Wuppertal "Ablation Survey" thesis announcement (opened; endpoint transparency/depth labels, no DoE content). Narang et al. 2021 opened by adversary #1 and says what the record attributed to it; Melis et al. 2018 COULD NOT READ (budget, no route refused).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1, same worry, adjacent object — Choi re-runs one factor family on workloads it chooses; the candidate codes other people's design matrices and estimates a population share. vs P2, same metascience genre, different endpoint — self-reported practice prevalence vs a reconstructed design property (column estimability) per headline claim. vs P3, measurement vs doctrine — the playbook states the diagnosis prescriptively in ML's own words but counts nothing and has no alias calculus. The census (share + kappa + alias-coefficient distribution) remains unmeasured in everything opened; the instance re-runs (Kaddour, Porian, Yang) de-confound particular claims rather than survey the literature.

Significance — consequence: YES (large non-estimable share, effects shrinking or reversing) would partly replace the under-tuning diagnosis for non-transfer with a structural one computable before compute is spent, and supply a per-table alias statement reviewers could check from released configs. NO would be a substantive defence of practice, relocating the anomaly to implementation/seed variance or scale-dependence. The undecidable share is a reporting-standards finding either way.

Significance — audience: pretraining teams planning ablation suites (would spend compute on alias-breaking points); reviewers and checklist maintainers (a config-verifiable item, unlike "tune your baselines"); ML metascience; AutoML/HPO. Honest discount, and adversaries pressed it: frontier teams already follow the playbook's scientific/nuisance/fixed discipline, and ML prevalence findings are cited rather than acted on.

Significance — fecundity: compute-optimal de-aliased designs under a FLOP budget (constrained D-optimal / split-plot with hard-to-change whole-plot factors); cheapest augmentation that breaks a named alias versus re-tuning the baseline; whether scaling-law fits inherit the alias bias of the ablations that set their fixed factors; automatic alias extraction from released configs; whether non-estimability predicts later non-transfer.

Significance — anchoring: the non-transfer anomaly (Narang 2021; Melis 2018); optimizer-ranking instability (P1); the compute-optimal-scaling discrepancy and its resolution (Porian 2024); hyperparameter-transfer work (muP), which is an engineering answer to the same co-movement.

Reason for silence: as filed — disciplinary boundary (ML's "ablation" descends from lesion studies, not from DoE; statisticians who own the alias calculus do not read pretraining configs), incentive gap (computing your own design's resolution can only weaken your claim; auditing others' has no ML venue), a compute-constraint framing effect (co-movement experienced as physical necessity, not design choice), and a new-data enabling condition (dense config disclosure only in the last few years). Gate 4 falsified the strong form of mechanism 1: the concept travelled into ML's own doctrine; only the calculus did not. Mechanisms 2 and 4 survive and explain why nobody COUNTED, which is why novelty stayed Medium rather than falling to Low.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-53-verification.md): the kill's evidence is CONFIRMED as quoted, and its reach is narrower than the adversary implied.
Confirmed: both fragments are in the Deep Learning Tuning Playbook (github.com/google-research/tuning_playbook), in "Identifying scientific, nuisance, and fixed hyperparameters" under "Designing the next round of experiments" — "need to be optimized over in order to fairly compare" is the definition of a nuisance hyperparameter, and "would not be very insightful" is the weight-decay example, that comparing model sizes at one fixed weight-decay value tells you little. It does prescribe re-optimising nuisance hyperparameters separately for each scientific option, running one tuning study per option and comparing the best trial from each, and it frames the risk it is guarding against as under-tuning producing unfair comparisons.
Narrower than claimed: the playbook says NOTHING about confounding, estimability, or bias of the scientific factor's main effect under per-arm re-tuning — the checker searched the page text and found none of those terms in that connection. And no published position in machine learning was found that treats per-arm re-tuning as a confound rather than as fair comparison; the nearest paper opened, Choi et al. 2019 (arXiv:1910.05446), argues for fuller per-optimiser tuning, i.e. the same way. So the objection is not "the field has already settled the aliasing question against you"; it is that the field has never adopted the separable factorial main effect as its estimand, and states a different comparison target in its own guidance. That is still a presupposition failure — the candidate's headline share is fixed by whichever estimand the coder imposes rather than measured from the literature — but it rests on one guidance document plus a bounded absence, which is recorded here rather than dressed up as a proof.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 (downgraded from the record's 3/3: the estimand is not fixed by the question — the P6 coding rule and the effect-vs-treatment parameterization jointly determine limb (i)'s headline number, which the record itself concedes is "protocol-determined rather than measured") · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection: The question presupposes that the separable factorial main effect is the estimand and that a co-moved nuisance factor is therefore a defect, but ML's own fair-comparison doctrine prescribes exactly that co-movement (tuning playbook, opened verbatim by all three adversaries: nuisance hyperparameters "need to be optimized over in order to fairly compare"; one weight decay across model sizes "would not be very insightful"). Coding per-arm re-tuning as aliasing drives limb (i) to ~1 by construction; coding it as alias-breaking collapses it toward 0; adopting the field's doctrine as the rule converts the question into a compliance audit inside the existing fair-comparison genre. So the headline quantity is selected by the protocol rather than measured from the literature — a presupposition failure (Gate 4, attack 4), not a fixable vagueness.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): if the question is ever re-filed, it must first fix the estimand rather than the frame — state whether the target is the factorial main effect or the field's conditional-optimum comparison, and run the nine Disguise queries listed in batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-53-adversary-3.md plus the unopened near-frame audits (Eimer et al. 2306.01324; CAIN 2023 hyperparameter-usage audit; Leech et al. 2407.12220) before any coding pilot.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. This is a Gate 4 presupposition-failure rejection, not an asked-but-open one, so no row is added to routed-open-problems.md. If re-filed after the estimand is fixed, the relevant neighbours are ML metascience's fair-comparison line (Kaddour 2023; Porian 2024; Yang 2020) and the P2/Wuppertal coded-survey line, not the research workstream; the motivating anomaly (non-transfer of reported gains) is asked-but-open and already represented there independently of this candidate.

ID: UQ-20261016-54
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Status change (post-batch): Rejected → Provisional. The batch rejected this candidate on an Unresolved attack 2 that neither adversary had been able to execute, and on a characterisation of Model Pulse that a checker did not find in its pages. A 12-query sweep and a late strict adversary have since both been run; Disguise is now Resolved on evidence and the entry is capped by an identifiability defect in its own primary weight instead.
Domain(s): AI architecture — open-weight derivative ecosystem (third-party quantizations, fine-tunes, merges, abliterations); method fields: survey sampling, fleet in-service-conformity metrology, software-supply-chain registry measurement.

Question (canonical) — R1, adopted at Gate 1: For a pre-specified set of open-weight releases R, over the population A(R) of publicly available derivative artifacts whose lineage includes R — partitioned in advance into (i) format-only requantizations, (ii) fine-tunes, (iii) merges, (iv) behaviour-modification derivatives (abliterated/"uncensored"), with a declared rule for multi-class artifacts and for merges with parents outside R — and with the PRIMARY weight being each artifact's cumulative hub download count at a pinned census date (per-file where exposed, per-repo with a stated within-repo allocation rule otherwise): how large is D = E_w[m(a)] − m(ref), where m is each of a pre-specified capability suite and a pre-specified refusal/jailbreak-resistance measure, m(ref) is measured on the pinned reference weights through the SAME inference engine and precision path as the class being compared (format-matched control), each component of D is judged against a pre-declared decision margin, and D is reported with CIs, a stated census coverage error, sensitivity across >=3 alternative weightings, and a variance decomposition into between-class and within-class (uploader) components?

Alternative formulations:
- [V0] For a given open-weight release, what is the download-weighted distribution of decision-relevant metrics over the derivative artifacts actually obtained, and how far does that population expectation sit from the value reported on the reference weights?
- What is the gap between the model that is evaluated and the models that are run?

Motivating gap: New-instrument claim — the derivative graph became enumerable (base_model lineage, weight-similarity recovery) and weightable (hub download counts) only recently, so a POPULATION quantity is estimable where the literature reports only reference-weight or author-produced-quantization properties. Release decisions and open-weight safety cases are made about reference weights. Cited as evidence of silence: the ATOM Report (arXiv:2604.07190) uses hub downloads but excludes GGUF/MLX re-uploads from derivative counts and never mentions merges; TMLR 2026 asserts "thousands of open-weight text models have been specifically fine-tuned to disable safeguards" with no measurement and no citation. NOTE: adversary 3 showed the new-instrument half of this gap is overstated (see Adversarial log, attacks 2 and 7).

Presuppositions: P1 downloads proxy use (CONTESTED; R1 defuses the well-posedness half by defining the estimand ON downloads, leaving a significance risk). P2 population enumerable with measured coverage error. P3 hundreds of artifacts evaluable comparably under pinned engines per format. P4 reference weights are a fixed artifact (CONTESTED — inherits UQ-20261016-12's post-release mutation hazard). P5 within-class between-uploader spread exists (partly posed in llama.cpp #13736/#5856 and partly measured by practitioners; subordinate). P6 a population gap would be decision-relevant. P7 suite metrics meaningful on narrow fine-tunes and foreign-parent merges (CONTESTED).

What would count as an answer: (a) a census of A(R) with download weights and measured coverage error; (b) a pinned evaluation of a class- and weight-stratified sample, each artifact in its format's engine against the format-matched reference control; (c) D per metric with CIs; (d) sensitivity across >=3 weightings; (e) a between-class / within-class variance decomposition. YES: some component of D exceeds its pre-declared margin with mass in a nameable class. NO: every component falls inside the reference measurement's own interval and the between-class term is negligible, vindicating reference-weight evaluation as a population proxy. Both branches close the question.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 of a 15 cap at Gate 2 (full list and 5 fetch records: batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-54-record.md). Most informative: [own-field obvious title] "download-weighted evaluation of open-weight model derivatives: quantizations, fine-tunes and merges on Hugging Face" -> no on-point paper; [MANDATORY fraction limb] "what fraction of Hugging Face model downloads are quantized GGUF derivatives" -> recorded as NO published figure (REFUTED at Gate 4 — see attack 2); "empirical study Hugging Face model ecosystem derivative lineage graph download counts" -> ATOM (2604.07190) and Anatomy (2508.06811); "quantization degrades safety alignment refusal rate jailbreak resistance" -> dense controlled-quantization literature, no population, no weights; [method-owning field] "download-weighted prevalence vulnerable package versions registry npm PyPI" -> routine practice in software-supply-chain measurement. Gate 4 added 0 web queries (budget refused all 8 attempted across two adversaries) plus 2 abstract reads by adversary 1, 4 by adversary 3, and ~35 GitHub searches: batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-54-adversary-1.md, -adversary-3.md.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) ATOM Report, "Measuring the Open Language Model Ecosystem", arXiv:2604.07190 (2026) — unit: the release; endpoint: adoption shares, Elo, intelligence index; estimand: descriptive share; excludes GGUF/MLX re-uploads by rule. (2) "Anatomy of a Machine Learning Ecosystem: 2 Million Models on Hugging Face", arXiv:2508.06811 — unit: model/family tree; endpoint: documented card traits; estimand: within-family trait similarity and drift; no evaluation, no weights. (3) "Open Technical Problems in Open-Weight AI Model Risk Management", TMLR 2026 — unit: safeguard/model card (n=15); endpoint: disclosure depth; no comparator, no estimand. Also recorded: Alice.io abliteration report (author-produced, n=6 families, 96-100% compliance) and arXiv:2511.21437 In-the-Wild Merging (controlled factorial). FOUND AT GATE 4, not at Gate 2: tardellirs/modelpulse (Model Pulse, 2026; HF Space tardellirs/model-pulse, built on cfahlgren1/hub-stats back to July 2024) — unit: the derivative artifact, partitioned quantization / fine-tune / adapter / merge; endpoint: download mass; estimand: class and per-family download share (derivatives 43% of all hub downloads Sept 2026, up from 8% July 2024; quantizations 28%; GGUF 11%; Qwen3-8B 6,283 derivatives, 37% of family downloads). Also arXiv:2512.03073 "Economies of Open Intelligence" (abstract opened): weekly download history of 851k models, 2.2B downloads, quantization growth 5X, does NOT scope quantizers out.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs ATOM — same instrument pointed at the release, not the artifact, and excluding this population by rule; no safety metric. vs Anatomy — same object, documented traits rather than measured behaviour, no weights, no reference comparator. vs TMLR — names the loose worry in prose with no estimand, population or number. vs Alice.io and the per-quantization literature — same endpoints, wrong unit: artifacts manufactured by the authors, so a METHOD effect, not a population expectation. vs ModelPulse — ModelPulse supplies component (a) of "what would count as an answer" (census plus download weights with the same class partition) and runs no evaluation at all; the residue claimed as unposed is the behavioural join, components (b)-(e).

Novelty confidence: Medium as graded at Gate 2 — but not safe to rely on, and not confirmable here: the Disguise sweep was never run (0 of 8 required queries at both adversaries), and the one Gate 2 negative that was tested (query 3, the mandatory fraction limb, "no published figure found") was refuted by a public instrument the record missed.

Significance — consequence: YES (a component of D exceeds its margin, mass in a nameable class) converts a rhetorical governance objection into a quotable quantity and puts a population-conformity line item into release-time safety cases, by analogy with vehicle in-service conformity. NO vindicates reference-weight evaluation as a population proxy and retires a live worry cheaply. Both branches informative.
Significance — audience: open-weight releasers writing safety cases and tampering evaluations; national safety institutes (UK AISI); evaluation-infrastructure maintainers; on-prem/procurement teams choosing one quantized artifact; marginal-risk policy analysts. Adversary 3 found the motivating claim "essentially all use is of derivatives" contradicted by the hub's own counts (43%, not essentially all), and both adversaries noted the mean is the wrong functional for the safety audience, who need the tail.
Significance — fecundity: which class carries the download mass; whether D widens with time since release (a release-decay curve); whether uploader identity predicts within-class deviation better than the nominal quant setting; whether first-party reference quantizations shrink D (a testable intervention with an obvious owner); whether population-conformity reporting could be required at release.
Significance — anchoring: open-weight marginal-risk debate; tamper-resistance and fine-tuning-removes-safeguards literature; quantization-activated backdoors (Egashira et al., NeurIPS 2024 — not opened); leaderboard validity; ATOM's exclusion rule; in-ledger siblings UQ-20261016-12 (temporal) and UQ-20261015-08 (dependence correction).

Reason for silence: claimed as a unit-of-analysis norm (ML evaluation is keyed to the release, with no sampling frame or in-service-conformity concept) reinforced by a disciplinary boundary (the method is owned by survey sampling, fleet metrology and registry measurement), an incentive gap, and new-instrument lag. Gate 4 damaged two of the four: daily hub-stats snapshots exist since July 2024, EOI released a weekly download history, and a practitioner has already computed derivative download mass by class and family, so the lag mechanism fails; and the method-plus-data claim is contradicted by software-supply-chain-decay authors (ChenhaoZhang01/supply-chain-decay-artifact, 2026-06) who hold both and chose a loadability endpoint. The surviving mechanism is narrower: the endpoint join was thought obvious or thought a tracker's job.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two adversaries, worst status shown; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-54-adversary-1.md and -adversary-3.md:

The substitute route (17 GitHub searches, 4 abstract reads) found ModelPulse already enumerating and download-weighting this exact population under the same class partition — a component-level prior and a direct refutation of the record's query-3 negative | none available: the attack could not be run as specified, and the reachable substitute produced a hit | UNRESOLVED (both adversaries) — FATAL
3 | Combinatorial novelty | "download-weighted sample of public HF models" already exists as a working method (supply-chain-decay census.py, 2026-06); the candidate swaps the endpoint | the interface problems (format-matched control, DAG-to-partition rule, per-repo-to-per-file allocation) are real and specific, but that they are hard rather than clerical is asserted, not shown | Partial (both)

A3 holds well-posedness should be 2/3 until an allocation anchor exists | Partial (both) — strongest substantive objection

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-54-verification.md): the Model Pulse characterisation that carried the batch's novelty downgrade is PARTLY CONFIRMED, and in the part that mattered it is wrong.
Confirmed: a public tracker called Model Pulse does exist — run by Tardelli Stekel, independent of Hugging Face, Apache-2.0, at github.com/tardellirs/modelpulse with a site at modelpulse.ifsp.dev and a Hugging Face Space. It builds derivative family trees from base_model links and reports how much of a model's reach comes from quantizations, fine-tunes, adapters and merges, over daily snapshots of the hub-stats parquet (rolling 30-day series from 2024-07-29, all-time totals from 2025-02-27).
Not confirmed: the three figures the entry quoted as its evidence — derivatives 43% of hub downloads, quantizations 28%, Qwen3-8B 37% — appear nowhere in the README or repo pages the checker opened, and no census date accompanies them. A report linked from the README was not opened, so they may exist there; until it is read, those numbers are not attributable and have been struck from this entry.
Decisive: Model Pulse measures downloads, likes, ranks and milestones ONLY. It records no capability score, no refusal measure and no jailbreak-resistance measure. So it instruments the census half of this question and has no behavioural endpoint at all, which is the half the candidate's estimand D is about. "A public instrument already does exactly this" was therefore a prior that does a different thing — the dominant error mode on this ledger, found again here.
Also established, and adverse: Hugging Face counts a download as a server-side request (GET or HEAD) to a query file, and for GGUF repositories every .gguf file counts as a query file; per-file counts are not documented as exposed. That is now the entry's second standing objection rather than a footnote.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 (contested to 2/3 by adversary 3, unresolved) · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection (restated after verification; the late adversary's, sourced): the headline estimand D is a NET difference of means, and on-regime evidence says a net delta is the least informative summary of exactly the artifact class that carries this population's download mass. arXiv:2608.15046, "Certifying Compressed Language Models: An Audit and a Statistical Toolkit", over 1,707 compressed-versus-original model-by-task cells, reports that median per-item churn is about five times the median net accuracy delta, and that the net quantity "is least informative when two models are most alike". That paper's scope is compression against the original on capability benchmarks at 1.3B-405B — this candidate's class (i) and its capability metric — and does NOT cover fine-tunes, merges, abliteration, the refusal endpoint or any download weighting, so the refusal limb and the magnitude limb survive it. What it kills is the question's NO branch: a null D would not "vindicate reference-weight evaluation as a population proxy", because per-item churn can be large while the means coincide. Half the claimed significance goes with that inference, and the entry no longer rests on it.
Second objection, compounding and absent from the record's P1: the primary weight is a per-file server-side request counter, and for GGUF repositories every .gguf file counts as a query file while per-file counts are not documented as exposed, so weight multiplicity differs systematically between the GGUF class and single-file safetensors classes — contaminating the very comparison that decides where the download mass sits.
Gate 5 note: attack 2 is now RESOLVED on executed evidence, not unverified. Two sweeps were run post-batch, 12 queries each, across machine-learning, software-supply-chain, survey-weighting, quantization-noise, fleet in-service-conformity, large-scale-audit and leaderboard vocabularies plus answer-searches. Neither found any work whose unit is a release's public third-party derivative population, whose weight is download counts, whose endpoint is capability together with refusal or jailbreak resistance, and whose comparator is the evaluated reference weights. Nearest found: an unfunded Manifund proposal covering quantized, fine-tuned and refusal-removed variants on a refusal endpoint with no weighting, no capability endpoint and no merges; "Anatomy of a Machine Learning Ecosystem: 2 Million Models on Hugging Face" (arXiv:2508.06811), whose endpoint is card and licence metadata over 1.86M derivatives; an ICSE 2026 model-supply-chain study whose body could not be read, so its silence is not evidence; and the ATOM Report (arXiv:2604.07190), whose endpoint is adoption share for about 1.5K mainline models. Per-mechanism controlled studies (quantization versus safety, merging versus safety, fine-tuning versus safety) supply the premise, one researcher-made variant at a time, never a population. Non-academic incidental partials exist and are not citable as prior art: GGUF KL-divergence comparisons across uploaders on localbench, a blog benchmarking eight refusal-removed variants, and a derivative-share-of-trending-page count.
What would promote this entry: fix the estimand so the NO branch is defensible — report a per-item churn or disagreement measure alongside D, since arXiv:2608.15046 shows the net delta alone cannot support the population-proxy conclusion — and settle the weight. Either anchor a within-repository GGUF allocation rule with stated bounds, or re-define the estimand on per-repository weights and publish the resulting coverage error. Validated also needs the two unread items opened: arXiv:2511.21437 (in-the-wild model merging) and the ICSE 2026 supply-chain body.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not a step toward the answer but toward a resubmission — re-run Gate 4's Disguise sweep with search budget, opening first ModelPulse and arXiv:2512.03073 in full, plus Open LLM Leaderboard analyses of community fine-tunes and merges; then re-scope the question to the behavioural join alone, crediting the census to existing trackers, and settle a within-repo GGUF allocation anchor before any component of D is called a measurement.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed, and now for the plain reason that the entry is not rejected. A Provisional entry's own question is never routed, since the ledger is still claiming it as un-asked. No adjacent posed question was found either: no source opened states the behavioural estimand as a posed, unanswered problem, and the census component is instrumented rather than posed.

ID: UQ-20261016-55
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Status change (post-batch): Rejected → Provisional. The batch's fatal grounds did not survive checking in the form they were given: arXiv:2508.17076 asserts the mismatch rather than posing or measuring it, arXiv:2601.21682 only stipulates a predefined stream and concedes in its Limitations that real requests may differ, and both adversaries' Disguise attacks were recorded Unresolved after running 0 web queries on an exhausted shared budget — which the amended Gate 4 rule now classes as Unverified. A late strict adversary with 12 executed queries returned Provisional, and the objections below are its sourced ones.
Domain(s): AI architecture — training-data governance (LLM machine unlearning, benchmark design)
Question (canonical): Over a pre-specified window and a pre-registered set of enumerable public records of removal demands against LLM training data (Lumen DMCA notices naming dataset/model hosts, court-ordered and voluntary dataset withdrawals, documented consent withdrawals, DOI-resolvable retractions), what is the joint distribution of (legal basis, demands per unit time, retrievable artifacts per demand, and — for the subset resolvable to a named open corpus such as Dolma or peS2o — document count, token share and co-document entanglement with retained material), with the unobserved confidential fraction explicitly bounded; and do the published forget sets of TOFU, MUSE, WMDP and DUSK fall inside or outside the support of that distribution?
Alternative formulations: Who actually asks for what to be removed from a training corpus, and does the unlearning literature's benchmark design resemble those requests at all? · What is the size and shape of the forget set in the wild, and is it the shape the methods were built for? (V0, pooling four legal bases with an unnamed sampling frame, failed Gate 1; V1 above is the one permitted reformulation.)
Motivating gap: Silence mapping — a dense how-literature (TOFU, MUSE, WMDP, DUSK, RWKU and hundreds of methods) in which every forget set is stipulated, with no measurement of the demand stream the field exists to serve, even though several demand sources became enumerable after 2023 (Lumen, Crossref/Retraction Watch, infini-gram-scale corpus membership tooling).
Presuppositions: (1) Recorded removal demands against training corpora exist in enumerable form — CONTESTED, biased sample, bound required. (2) A demand can be mapped onto corpus documents — CONTESTED; mapping is non-unique (CleanSlate: same request → 2,432 vs 67,323 windows across curators). (3) Benchmark forget sets can be characterised on the same axes as real demands — asserted ESTABLISHED at Gate 2, BROKEN at Gate 4 (see adversarial log row 4). (4) Forget-set size/structure changes method performance — ESTABLISHED (CleanSlate Table 3; coreset effect), hence demoted out of the question. (5) "Removal demand" is one category across copyright, privacy, retraction, defamation — CONTESTED; V1 stratifies. (6) Corpus membership checkable for open corpora — ESTABLISHED (4,596/4,663 works matched in Dolmino-mid).
What would count as an answer: A measured joint distribution over the stated axes from the pre-registered sources, with coverage stated and the unobserved fraction bounded, set beside the same statistics computed for TOFU, MUSE, WMDP and DUSK. YES = the real mass sits where benchmarks do not sample (many small, identifier-level, legally heterogeneous, sequential demands vs coherent topical blocks). NO = distributions coincide within the coverage bound.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2: 11 distinct web searches + 5 fetches (at cap); full table in batches/2026-10-16-1916/UQ-20261016-55-record.md. Most informative: own-field obvious title ("do machine unlearning benchmarks reflect real-world data deletion requests forget set realism LLM") → the forget-set-critique literature (CleanSlate arXiv:2608.14855, arXiv:2609.00605, arXiv:2410.02879), nothing demand-side; "fraction of retracted articles present in peS2o" → no published figure; "deletion request workload characterization right to be forgotten real requests distribution" → Bertram et al. (CCS 2019, NOT OPENED), the nearest census method; "Consent in Crisis … token share C4 Dolma" → Longpre et al. arXiv:2407.14933. Gate 4: adversary #1 ran 0 of 9 web searches (shared budget exhausted at first call) + 7 GitHub MCP searches; adversary #3 ran 0 of 9 web searches, 12 arXiv listing fetches all ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, and 15 GitHub code-search Disguise queries (D1–D15) plus 6 answer-searches of the github/dmca archive. Full lists in UQ-20261016-55-adversary-1.md and UQ-20261016-55-adversary-3.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 CleanSlate, "What to Forget in Unlearning? Forget Set Curation for Language Models", arXiv:2608.14855 (ICML 2026) — FULL TEXT OPENED; unit = works and matched windows in Dolmino-mid, endpoint = net reduction in extractable windows, comparator = 4 curators × 3 unlearners, estimand = suppression selectivity. P2 Longpre et al., "Consent in Crisis", arXiv:2407.14933 (NeurIPS 2024) — ABSTRACT OPENED; unit = ~14k web domains, endpoint = ex ante restriction signals, estimand = restricted share of C4 (>5% tokens fully restricted, 45% under ToS). P3 Cooper et al., arXiv:2412.06966 — HTML OPENED (tail re-opened by adversary #1 at offset 95,000); conceptual, no unit, endpoint or estimand; §7/appendix still unread by adversary #3. Gate 4 adds two priors Gate 2 never reached: P4 Lubitzsch et al., "Towards a Real-World Aligned Benchmark for Unlearning in Recommender Systems", arXiv:2508.17076 (FAccTRec@RecSys 2025) — abstract read verbatim from mirrors, body COULD NOT READ; P5 FIT/PCH, arXiv:2601.21682 — abstract read verbatim from two mirrors, body COULD NOT READ.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — P1 takes the request as given (researcher-drawn sample of 50 extractable works) and studies the downstream mapping; it counts no demands and has no arrival rate, legal basis or source, but it has already banked corpus entanglement for a stipulated target set and the ordering sensitivity the candidate offered as payoff. vs P2 — same corpus-side method, opposite mechanism and direction in time (ex ante opt-out at domain granularity vs ex post demand at artifact granularity); no unlearning connection. vs P3 — argues the mismatch, declines the measurement; the adversary-opened tail confirms it does not call for the census either. vs P4 — the same question in recommender-systems vocabulary ("benchmarks … fail to reflect real-world operational demands … simulate unrealistically large unlearning requests … the sequential, time-sensitive nature of real-world deletion requests"); the candidate is that question with the corpus swapped to LLM pretraining data plus corpus-measurement axes. vs P5 — the candidate's YES answer asserted and built into a benchmark ("the continual and high-volume nature of real-world deletion requests … Personal information, Copyright, and Harmful content in sequential deletion scenarios"), with the three strata echoing the candidate's legal-basis stratification. MUSE's own abstract already scores "scalability with respect to the size of removal requests" and "sustainability over sequential unlearning requests" (configs scal, sust).
Novelty confidence: Low (revised at Gate 4 from the Gate 2 grade of Medium, on P4/P5, which 11 Gate 2 queries missed; and the Disguise check that would have settled it is itself unverified — 0 of the required web queries ran for either adversary)
Significance — consequence: If YES, published method rankings are established on a region of forget-set space that practice rarely visits, and the live regime is continual, per-demand unlearning rather than one-shot topical blocks; regulators gain a first denominator for deletion-duty feasibility. If NO, benchmarks are vindicated on the axes that matter and the Cooper-style critique narrows to end-state guarantees.
Significance — audience: Unlearning benchmark authors; model providers' data-governance teams; regulators (GDPR Art. 17, EU AI Act training-data duties, EDPB 2025 erasure action); open-corpus curators (AI2 Dolma/peS2o, EleutherAI); Crossref/Retraction Watch as a downstream consumer.
Significance — fecundity: Demand-weighted benchmarks; the arrival process of demands; per-demand compute cost models; "share of a corpus under live demand" as a corpus-design statistic; whether the four legal bases require different end-states and so whether unlearning is one research problem.
Significance — anchoring: Can unlearning satisfy legal deletion duties (arXiv:2412.06966; arXiv:2606.27379); the forget-set sensitivity anomaly (coreset effect; CleanSlate); the consent/robots.txt measurement line; benchmark construct validity (arXiv:2511.04703).
Reason for silence: Claimed as disciplinary boundary (legal/metascience registers vs a methods community rewarded for benchmark numbers) + incentive gap (providers settle confidentially) + new instrument (Retraction Watch open on Crossref since 2023; infini-gram-scale membership tooling). Gate 4 finding: there is no silence on the question — it is asked in recsys (P4) and presupposed across LLM continual unlearning (P5; arXiv:2512.02657, 2604.12526, 2603.19302). The mechanisms explain why the measurement is hard or private, not why nobody asked.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two adversaries, fresh context, Gate 0–3 record only (A1 and A3; A3 a harder rerun that read no earlier log). Verbatim logs: UQ-20261016-55-adversary-1.md, UQ-20261016-55-adversary-3.md.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-55-verification.md): both priors resolve, and neither does what the kill said.
arXiv:2508.17076 is “Towards a Real-World Aligned Benchmark for Unlearning in Recommender Systems” (Lubitzsch, Ovcharenko, Chen, de Rijke, Schelter; v1 2025-08-23, v2 2025-09-18), a position and benchmark-design paper. It argues that existing recsys unlearning benchmarks — CURE4Rec at 5% or more, NeurIPS 2023 at 2% — “simulate unrealistically large unlearning requests” and that the setup should “reflect the sequential, time-sensitive nature of real-world deletion requests”. It ASSERTS that; it does not measure it and does not pose it as a question. Its own experiment uses a 0.1% forget set on Instacart (about 1,000 users for alcohol, about 650 for meat), with Recall, nDCG, PHR, KL divergence against retraining from scratch.
arXiv:2601.21682 is “FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models” (Xu et al.; v1 2026-01-29, v2 2026-05-07). It stipulates a sequential request stream over 600 GPT-4o-generated samples (200 each personal, copyright, harmful; 0 to 300 requests in steps of 60) and its Limitations state that the streams are predefined and that real requests may differ.
Neither measures a real, enumerable stream of removal demands — counts, legal basis, size per demand — against any corpus. So the two papers support this candidate's gap claim rather than closing it: a sibling field believes the mismatch exists and has not measured it. What they do establish is that the FRAMING is published outside this corpus, which is why attack 2 lands at Partial rather than Resolved.
Not verified: the claim that GitHub's DMCA archive holds only single-digit notices naming machine-learning training datasets could not be checked by the checker's one web search (it returned mirrors of individual notices). The counted GitHub code-searches behind it are in adversary #3's log and are treated here as bounding the stratum, not settling it.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 (V1 scored 3/3 at Gate 1, reduced at Gate 4: presupposition 3 fails for two named benchmarks and the support test is unoperationalised) · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection (restated after a late strict adversary, 12 executed Disguise queries, every Unresolved claim sourced): a defect in the sampling frame itself. V1 pre-registers retractions as one of four “enumerable public records of removal demands”, but COPE's retraction guidelines make a retraction close to the opposite of a removal demand: “the online version of the article should be retained with a clear notice of retraction”, because “Retaining the original work ensures transparency of the published record”, with removal reserved for “extremely limited cases” (defamation, privacy violation, court order, serious health risk) and even then “the metadata (title and authors) should be retained”. So a quarter of the frame contributes demands no claimant made — and the record's new-instrument reason for silence leans on exactly that stratum, Retraction Watch having been open on Crossref since 2023. The defect is severable by dropping the stratum, which is why it caps rather than kills.
Second, on support, carried over from adversary #3 and still standing: the benchmark side is partly degenerate by construction — TOFU's forget set is drawn from “200 diverse synthetic author profiles” (arXiv:2401.06121, opened), so its corpus footprint is zero and its position outside any real-demand distribution is settled without a census; WMDP is a hazardous-knowledge safety proxy per its own README; and MUSE already spans request sizes, its own abstract naming “scalability with respect to the size of removal requests” and “sustainability over sequential unlearning requests”, with scal and sust configs. On the demand side, 6 counted answer-searches of the github/dmca archive (fifteen years of notices) returned notices naming machine-learning training datasets in the single digits — one wikiHow notice in 2025 being the only one targeting a scraped-content training dataset, with LAION and “Common Crawl” returning zero — and the largest in-frame real demand, the Bartz v. Anthropic order, is an order to destroy torrented files rather than an unlearning request. That is one host and a code-search index that may be incomplete, so it bounds rather than settles the stratum; but unless a census of Lumen or of developers' own disclosures finds a non-trivial stratum, the joint distribution this question asks for has too little support to estimate.
Third, on significance: xAI's mandated CCPA disclosure already publishes real removal-demand counts for a frontier model developer — for 1 January to 31 December 2025, 65 requests to delete received, 65 completed, 0 denied — so the “first denominator for deletion-duty feasibility” partly exists already, as a recurring legal disclosure rather than as research.
Why this is not a rejection: no source opened measures, counts or stratifies a population of real removal demands against a named training corpus, and the obvious own-field position paper that could have posed it (arXiv:2410.02879, opened) argues forget/retain dependency and target ambiguity instead. Attack 2 is Partial, not Unresolved: the framing is in print in a sibling field as an assertion, not as a measurement.
Promotion conditions (what would move this entry, in order): (1) open arXiv:2603.08341, “ERASE — A Real-World Aligned Benchmark for Unlearning in Recommender Systems”, which the late adversary could not fetch within budget and which is the closest candidate for a renaming of this question — recorded as UNVERIFIED, not as a check that passed; (2) read the tail of Cooper et al., arXiv:2412.06966 §7, also unread (a fetch at offset 96000 returned only bibliography); (3) drop the retraction stratum from the frame, or re-justify it against COPE; (4) establish from Lumen itself, and from developers' own CCPA and GDPR disclosures rather than from GitHub, whether the dataset-naming demand stratum has even hundreds of members. If (4) comes back in the single digits across sources, this question dies for want of a population rather than for want of novelty.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The entry is Provisional, and a Provisional entry's own question is never routed while the ledger still claims it as un-asked. No adjacent posed question qualifies either: arXiv:2508.17076 asserts the benchmark-versus-reality mismatch without measuring it and does not pose it as a question, and arXiv:2601.21682 only notes in its Limitations that its streams are predefined and real requests may differ. For the record, the live literature on this line: Lubitzsch et al. 2025 (recsys), FIT 2026, MUSE scal/sust, CleanSlate 2026; census method, Bertram et al. CCS 2019 and Urban/Karaganis/Schofield 2016. Note for a later pass: Bertram et al. has now defeated four agents (doi.org, dl.acm.org) and remains unread.
