ID: UQ-20261016-64
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — clinical documentation and diagnostic error; primary care and clinical informatics; health equity. Method-owning neighbours: summarization evaluation (NLP), clinical risk prediction, measurement-bias/fairness methodology, ASR evaluation.
Question (canonical): In a corpus of ambulatory encounters retaining both the verbatim transcript and the final signed note, with a pre-specified set of index diagnoses/outcomes established independently from the EHR at a pre-specified lag L (adjudication rule fixed in advance; the index encounter's own coding excluded), what is the difference in out-of-sample discrimination, calibration and decision-curve net benefit between a transcript-input predictor and a note-input predictor — under (a) length- and summary-matched input controls, (b) a human-transcribed reference subsample isolating ASR loss from documentation loss, and (c) pre-specified subgroup-by-artefact interactions (interpreter use, limited language proficiency, dysarthria/cognitive impairment, speech rate, accent/first-language group) — and does the difference persist on pre-ambient, human-written notes from recorded encounters?
Alternative formulations: (A2, lay) "Now that what was actually said in consultations is recorded at scale, which artefact predicts what turned out to be wrong with the patient better: the transcript or the note written from it?" · (Intake version) "How much clinically predictive information does the record discard relative to what was said, and is that gap distributed unevenly across patient groups?" (graded at 2/3 well-posedness; estimand, lag and predictor class unfixed) · (A1, dropped at Gate 1) "…content that no downstream reader, human or algorithmic, can recover" — quantifies over an unbounded reader class, not settleable.
Motivating gap: The instrument that first makes the spoken encounter auditable at scale is used almost only to ask whether the machine writes as well as the clinician (Foo et al., Aust J Gen Pract 2026;55(4):226–232 — PDQI-9-style rater scores, omissions as one Likert item, no outcome). Gate 2 narrowed the gap materially: the omission-against-transcript limb is now closed by Fox et al. (arXiv:2608.31016, 2608.31017). What remains open is outcome-anchoring of documentation loss and its stratification by patient attributes.
Presuppositions: P1 paired transcript–note corpora exist at research-usable scale under permissive governance — CONTESTED and LIMITING (Fox et al. recorded 142 consultations themselves; a 98,331-pair production ambient corpus, arXiv:2606.00019, holds drafts and finals but no transcripts; adversary 2 found no retained-transcript corpus linked to outcomes in 9 queries). P2 an independently established later outcome exists at lag L — CONTESTED on a ground the record does not raise (see attack 4). P3 predictive performance proxies clinically relevant information — CONTESTED (paralinguistic/style channel; vocal-biomarker work is live), so the content/style ablation is load-bearing. P4 the note, not the encounter, is what downstream decisions and note-trained models consume — plausible, partly checkable. P5 loss is non-random across patient attributes — the hypothesis, not an assumption; presupposes stratifiers are recorded, weak for accent/first language and interpreter use. P6 the comparison is not an artefact of input length or predictor capacity — requires the matched controls. P7 transcription is not the dominant error source — CONTESTED; requires the human-transcribed subsample. P8 clinicians/vendors/standard-setters would act — plausible. P9 (added by adversary 2, unlisted in the record) the note is a lossy compression of the transcript — FALSE as stated: Khan 2012 found 103 concepts in notes absent from the reference, Weiner et al. report nearly half of notes carrying content with no transcript counterpart. The graded estimand (a signed difference between two inputs) survives P9; the Gate 3 "sufficient statistic"/"quantified ceiling" framing does not.
What would count as an answer: On a paired corpus under a pre-registered protocol — (i) the signed predictive gap (discrimination, calibration, net benefit) for pre-specified later-established diagnoses, transcript vs note, with length/summary-matched controls, a human-transcribed subsample isolating ASR loss, and human adjudication of discordant cases establishing content rather than style; (ii) an inventory of recoverable content — largely pre-empted by Fox et al. 2608.31016, so replication plus outcome-anchoring, not discovery; (iii) the gap's interaction with pre-specified patient attributes; (iv) the same analysis on human-written notes from pre-ambient recorded encounters. A null is publishable in advance as a defence of documentation practice and of note-trained models.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 documented queries in all — 11 at Gate 2, 9 by adversary 1, 9 by adversary 2 — plus 13 fetches; full lists in batches/2026-10-16-2337/UQ-20261016-64-record.md and UQ-20261016-64-adversary-1.md / -2.md. Most informative: "percentage clinically significant omissions AI scribe notes real-world audit published rate" → the fraction limb is already computed and published (Fox et al., 31.3% of 565 notes, 95% CI 27.0–35.6). "visit audio transcript predicts subsequent diagnosis better than clinician note" and "spoken input outperformed clinician-written note on a downstream prediction task" → nothing in either direction; the answer is unpublished. "summarization information loss downstream prediction task summary versus source" → the method field (COSMIC, arXiv:2402.19457) and, inside written text, arXiv:2502.10388 (full discharge notes vs LLM summaries for 30-day psychiatric readmission) and TRACE (arXiv:2604.16364, note-internal bloat reduction vs three outcome predictions). "differential information loss across patient subgroups … measurement bias fairness documentation" and "documentation completeness disparity by patient race/language" → model-behaviour and note-language studies only (arXiv:2606.00019 names patient-attribute stratification as unaddressed future work); no study stratifies documentation loss against a recording. Vanderbilt residual risk resolved by both adversaries: Khan NA 2012 is a master's thesis referenced to standardized-patient scenario descriptions, not transcripts, with no outcome endpoint. COULD NOT READ: JMIR Med Inform 2026;e88734 (empty publisher page, no retry in cap); Weiner et al. 2024 read only via the Regenstrief institutional release, by record and adversary 2 alike; Foo et al. AJGP 2026 unread; unopened near-priors arXiv:2010.03574, JMIR Aging 2023;6:e44037, one Göttingen dissertation. No PMC/Europe PMC route attempted anywhere.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 Fox S, Markham L, Lail R, Karotsieris M, "LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence: Omission Blindness in AI Clinical Notes and What Recovers It", arXiv:2608.31016v1 (read in full) — unit: note pair (495 pairs / 112 consultations, simulated+authored corpora); endpoint: an LLM judge's omission-detection rate; reference: transcript-derived clinician-audited fact sheet, comparator the verified-clean twin note; estimand: detectability of omission, severity-graded. P2 Fox et al., "One note in three: a verified census of three deployed AI scribes", arXiv:2608.31017 (abstract read; figures independently confirmed by adversary 2) — unit: the note (565 notes, 3 deployed vendors, 142 recorded consultations); endpoint: verified failure rate per note after adjudication; reference: the encounter recording; estimand: population failure rate, 31.3% (27.0–35.6), elastic to review standard (9.3%→79.0%). P3 Weiner M et al., "Accuracy, thoroughness, and quality of outpatient primary care documentation in the VA", BMC Primary Care 2024 (NOT OPENED; read via institutional release, PubMed 39026167 confirms it is real) — unit: the discussed topic within an audio-recorded visit; endpoint: whether a discussed topic appears in the note; reference: the recording, comparator who initiated the topic; estimand: proportion documented, 45% patient-initiated psychosocial vs 92% clinician-initiated. Method-owning negative: COSMIC (arXiv:2402.19457, read) — source–summary mutual information as a bound on downstream classifier error, non-clinical. Closest outcome-anchored source-vs-summary comparison: arXiv:2502.10388 (read) — written notes vs LLM summaries, AUROC 0.54–0.59, no transcripts, no subgroups.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same reference artefact and object, different estimand: detectability of omission by a judge against a severity rubric, versus loss of predictive signal about an externally established outcome; P1's corpus has no linked outcomes and could not answer this in principle. vs P2 — answers the plain-language "how much does the record discard" limb with a published number, but differs in endpoint (later-diagnosis prediction with calibration and net benefit, not fact presence/absence), in unit (the encounter with a linked outcome), and in carrying a pre-specified patient-subgroup interaction P2 explicitly lacks; P2's rubric elasticity is itself an argument for an outcome anchor. vs P3 — same loss, pre-AI, human notes; differs in endpoint (documented/not vs predictive performance) and stratifier (topic initiator vs patient attributes). vs COSMIC/TRACE/2502.10388 — the method move exists and is named, but never with a spoken encounter as source, the legal record as summary, a later-established diagnosis as the task, and differential loss across the people being summarized; Khan 2012 is limb (ii) in 2012 vocabulary with neither transcript nor outcome.
Novelty confidence: Medium (verification opened three of the four near-priors adversary 1 had left unread and none is on the candidate's estimand: arXiv:2010.03574 compares notes against the structured record rather than against a transcript, JMIR Aging 2023;6:e44037 compares survey against chart abstraction, and the Göttingen dissertation could not be identified at all. The grade stays Medium only because JMIR Med Inform 2026;e88734 cannot be opened by any route and a NeurIPS 2026 title, "Beyond Facts — What AI Clinical Notes Leave Out", surfaced unread — see Verification.)
Significance — consequence: If the gap is large, the note is not predictively sufficient for outcomes clinicians act on, with three attached decisions: transcript retention becomes a governance and medico-legal question; documentation targets shift from "faithful and readable" to a scorable retained-signal objective that does not move by a factor of eight when the review instruction changes (per P2); note-trained models acquire a measured rather than speculative input ceiling. If null: a currently unavailable defence of documentation practice, and the retention argument retires. If large and differential by patient group: documentation becomes an identified mechanism of inequity upstream of every model-fairness intervention in the field. Scope discipline required: a single-site, single-predictor-family result bounds nothing about other models, sites or tasks, and the "quantified ceiling for every note-trained model" claim overreaches (adversary 2, attack 6).
Significance — audience: Scribe purchasers and health-system informatics teams; documentation standard-setters and specialty bodies; clinical-AI developers training on notes; health-equity and language-access programmes; medico-legal reviewers and regulators. Evidenced rather than asserted: health systems and vendors already fund and publish paired-artefact audits of live scribes (Fox et al. on three deployed products; arXiv:2606.00019, 66,297 paired sections across two vendors), and deployers are reported to have built proprietary incomparable evaluation pipelines and to be asking for a shared benchmark (arXiv:2609.17355).
Significance — fecundity: What is a predictively sufficient note, and can a documentation target be optimized against retained signal rather than rater score? Should the record be two-tier (transcript + note), and what does that do to clinician and patient behaviour once both know it is kept? Does loss concentrate in P2's content classes (allergies, medications, history written up as examination) or in P3's (patient-initiated psychosocial content)? Does a transcript-trained model's advantage decay once clinicians know the transcript is read? What is the analogous gap for handover notes, discharge summaries and radiology reports (cf. UQ-20261016-07)?
Significance — anchoring: Diagnostic error and missed/delayed diagnosis; the note-bloat debate, which has volume metrics and no loss metric; input-degradation ceilings for EHR-trained models; language-access and interpreter-use disparities, where the instrument has been missing; the summarization-sufficiency problem (COSMIC/TRACE), whose first clinical outcome-anchored instance this would be.
Reason for silence: Mechanism as graded by the record was three-part; adversary 2 struck part of it on evidence. STRUCK: "the instrument is new" — Khan 2012 asked an encounter-to-note information-loss question fourteen years ago using standardized-patient scenarios, needing no ambient scribe. SURVIVES and corroborated: a disciplinary-endpoint boundary. Across five loss studies located (Khan 2012, Weiner et al. 2024, Fox et al. ×2, arXiv:2606.00019) there are five different fidelity endpoints and not one prediction or outcome endpoint, and in all five the recording is used as a gold standard rather than as a rival input — the people with transcripts have never owned an outcome, and the people with outcomes have only ever had notes (P4). PARTIALLY SURVIVES: an incentive-and-retention gap that destroys the comparator (Fox et al. recorded their own encounters; the largest production ambient corpus keeps no transcript) — this explains why answering is hard more than why asking did not happen. For the equity limb the honest mechanism is weaker still: arXiv:2606.00019 names patient-attribute stratification as future work in 2026, which is recency rather than silence.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two independent fresh-context adversaries, logs verbatim in UQ-20261016-64-adversary-1.md and -2.md; 18 new-vocabulary Disguise queries between them (9 each, cap 9, minimum 8 met) and 8 fetches.
1 Triviality | Omissions are known (31.3% of notes with a verified failure; 45% of patient-initiated psychosocial topics documented), so the gap's sign is foreordained and only its size is at issue | The sign is open on opened sources: notes add non-transcript content (Khan 2012: 103 concepts absent from the reference; Weiner: nearly half of notes), and summarization can raise downstream performance — in the only clinical outcome-anchored source-vs-summary comparison found (arXiv:2502.10388), summaries matched or exceeded full notes at three of four sites, point estimates in a 0.54–0.59 band the authors call highly challenging; TRACE shows prediction can be insensitive to large content removal | Resolved (A1), Resolved (A2)
2 Disguise | A renamed known: summarization sufficiency, validity of the medical record, clinical information flow, value of information in medical notes, source-vs-summary utility, ASR fairness | 18 queries in information theory, epidemiological measurement error, communication research (RIAS), speech biomarkers, German and French, clinical NLP, triage safety, historical record-validity jargon, documentation bias, answer-side, inpatient summary and ASR fairness. Every renaming found covers one limb only: TRACE and 2502.10388 have the estimand but inside written text with no transcript and no subgroups; Khan 2012 is limb (ii) with no outcome; JMIR Aging e44037 is survey-vs-chart as rival model inputs; ASR fairness stops at word error rate by accent. Nothing poses the transcript-vs-note predictive gap; nothing stratifies documentation loss by patient attributes. Unverified residue on the equity limb: JMIR Med Inform 2026;e88734 COULD NOT READ (empty publisher page) and a Göttingen dissertation unopened; A2 adds arXiv:2010.03574 and JMIR Aging e44037 unopened | Partial, with an Unverified unread-prior item (A1); Resolved (A2)
3 Combinatorial novelty | Summarization evaluation × clinical documentation × fairness auditing; once the corpus exists the analysis is off the shelf, and data access is not an interface problem | A problem specific to the interface, evidenced: the source artefact is destroyed by the system that creates it (98,331 paired ambient sections with no transcripts; Fox et al. had to record their own), so "is the summary sufficient?" is a retention question, not a benchmarking one; and the differential arm must decompose ASR channel, summarization channel and subgroup case-mix. Conceded: the main effect alone would be a cross-product, and TRACE occupies the clinical × sufficiency pairing one step away | Partial (A1), Resolved (A2)
4 Presupposition failure | A1: P2's "independently established" outcome is not independent — the label is reached through the care pathway the note initiates, so an omission can suppress the very workup that would produce the label, and transcript-only signal is then scored as a false positive; excluding the index encounter's coding does not remove this, and the reformulation does not state it. A2: unlisted P9 (the note is a lossy compression of the transcript) is false, and P1 is unevidenced in the form the question needs | A1: restrict to outcomes reached outside the note's causal pathway (unplanned admission, lab/pathology-confirmed diagnoses, registry cancers, death), lengthen L, state the residual bias — plausible but unevidenced, and the objection is itself a differential-verification-bias argument the adversary could not source within budget, hence Partial not Unresolved. A2: the graded estimand is a difference in a performance functional between two inputs and is well defined whatever the generative relation, so P9's falsity retires the Gate 3 framing rather than the question; P1 is a feasibility cap the record itself prices into a single-site first instantiation | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)
5 Vagueness | Any result absorbable — a null blamed on predictor capacity, a gap on style, a differential gap on ASR; and five stratifiers against a multi-outcome set is a forking path | Named functionals, pre-specified lag and adjudication rule, length/summary matching, human-transcribed subsample, content/style ablation and a pre-declared publishable null close each escape. Unfixed and unaddressed in the record: no multiplicity plan, no minimum clinically meaningful difference, no power statement for a five-stratifier interaction on a single-site corpus — the limb carrying the significance claim | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)
6 Significance inflation | Nobody changes a decision on an AUROC delta; retention policy is driven by liability, and procurement already has 31.3% | The procurement and evaluation audience is evidenced and already consuming this genre (deployed-product censuses, two-vendor production audits, explicit calls for a shared benchmark), and the scorable-target consequence is supported by P2's review-instruction elasticity. The retention/medico-legal and "ceiling for every note-trained model" consequences are asserted and overreach | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)
7 Reason for silence | Paired recording–note corpora are decades old (BMJ 2002 standardized-patient audio, RIAS corpora, VA recordings, Khan 2012), so "new instrument" explains the 2023–26 scribe wave, not thirty years of recordings without this question | The endpoint-boundary mechanism survives and is corroborated across five loss studies with five fidelity endpoints and no outcome endpoint; mechanism #1 should be struck and replaced by "the instrument's owners have never owned an outcome". The retention/incentive mechanism is supported indirectly and explains difficulty of answering more than absence of asking; for the equity limb the mechanism is recency | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)
8 Dissolution | The AUROC difference decomposes into omission, addition, ASR error and style, leaving no single quantity called "what the record discards" — only a two-arm benchmark specific to one model family, site and outcome set | The reformulation already drops the "discard" framing for a signed difference with controls; what survives decomposition is the net predictive difference between the two artefacts the system actually keeps or consumes, which is decision-relevant; the equity limb is a difference-in-differences and so less hostage to predictor capacity. Flagged, unsourced: subgroup AUROC contrasts are sensitive to subgroup case-mix and outcome prevalence, so the interaction is not automatically capacity-invariant, and the record is silent on this. What dissolves is the channel-capacity rhetoric | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)
Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261016-64-verification.md and UQ-20261016-64-verification-2.md): the proximity cap is WITHDRAWN, three of the four unread near-priors are now read and none is on the candidate's estimand, and one unreadable article plus one newly surfaced unread paper are all that still block Validated on attack 2.
The Fox et al. pair does not pre-empt limb (ii). Paper A is arXiv:2608.31016 (31 Aug 2026), "LLM Judges Verify Presence, Not Absence": a judge benchmark on 500 note pairs with constructed omissions, scoring how well LLM judges detect an omission, with category breakdowns by surviving trace and severity. Paper B is the NeurIPS 2026 abstract "One note in three": an audit of three deployed scribes over 142 consultations and 565 notes, reporting 31.3% [27.0, 35.6] of notes with at least one verified failure, omissions 23.1% of errors, failures clustering in allergy and medication fields, invented identity, and history recorded as examination in phone consultations. Neither compares how well a transcript predicts a later outcome against how well the note written from it predicts the same outcome, and neither breaks results down by interpreter use, limited language proficiency, impaired speech or accent. So the neighbour that Gate 5 called "very close and three months old" is close in object and not in estimand: omission detection and omission prevalence are not a predictive-performance gap, and the Gate 5 clause about Fox et al. owning answer-criteria limb (ii) is struck. Paper B was read at abstract level only and paper A's page may have been truncated.
Of the four sources adversary 1 left unopened, three are now resolved and none poses the question. arXiv:2010.03574 is "Characterizing the Value of Information in Medical Notes" (Hsu, Karnwal, Mullainathan, Obermeyer, Tan): structured data alone against structured data plus notes, for readmission and in-hospital mortality, with no transcripts and no speaker or patient-attribute breakdown — the nearest thing on the ledger to the candidate's design, and it compares note against structured record rather than note against transcript. JMIR Aging 2023;6:e44037 is Bernstein et al. on diabetes life-expectancy estimation (Lee index) from patient survey against EHR chart abstraction, n = 75, with no recordings and no language attributes. The Göttingen dissertation could not be identified at all over two searches in English and German; the one Göttingen item opened (Tolle 2023, analogue against digital surgical protocols in a clinical workstation system) is not it, so that near-prior is recorded as NOT FOUND rather than unread, and it grounds nothing.
What still blocks Validated: JMIR Med Inform 2026;e88734 is COULD NOT READ — the article page returned empty content twice and doi 10.2196/88734 redirects to that same empty page, with PMC and Europe PMC blocked — so attack 2 keeps one Unverified component, which under Gate 4's rule caps this entry at Provisional without rejecting it. Verification also surfaced a new unread item that belongs in the same slot: a NeurIPS 2026 listing titled "Beyond Facts — What AI Clinical Notes Leave Out", found in passing and not opened. Neither absence is treated as a check that passed.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 3/3
Verdict reasoning (Gate 5): No attack is Unresolved from either adversary, so the entry is not Rejected; the two fatal-family attacks (1, 4) are Resolved and Partial respectively. Both adversaries ran their Disguise sweeps in full (9 queries each, in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try), so Disguise is not an unrun check — but adversary 1's Disguise carries an explicitly Unverified component on the equity limb: JMIR Med Inform 2026;e88734 COULD NOT READ and a Göttingen dissertation unopened, with arXiv:2010.03574 and JMIR Aging 2023;6:e44037 unopened per adversary 2. An unread paper is not a check that passed, so Validated is blocked on attack 2 for that limb. Independently, Gate 5's own rule caps Medium novelty with a close neighbour at Provisional — and that clause as written is WITHDRAWN. Verification opened both Fox papers: one is an LLM-judge benchmark on constructed omissions, the other an audit of omission prevalence in deployed scribes' notes, and neither compares a transcript's predictive performance against the note's or pre-empts answer-criteria limb (ii), so the neighbour is close in object and not in estimand (see Verification above). What caps the entry is the unread component of attack 2, now reduced from four items to one article that cannot be opened at all plus one newly surfaced unread title. Not a disguised known: no prior shares the estimand or the subgroup contrast, and the named residual risk (Khan 2012) was opened by both adversaries and retired. Not asked-but-open: the predictive-gap and differential-loss formulations were not found posed, so nothing routes.
Strongest remaining objection: The later diagnosis is not independent of the artefact under test — it is reached through the care pathway the note initiates and that later clinicians read, so an omission in the note can suppress the workup that would have established the label, scoring transcript-only signal as a false positive and biasing the measured gap in the note's favour; dropping the index encounter's own coding does not remove this, and neither the reformulation nor the record acknowledges it (adversary 1, attack 4; Partial only because the adversary could not source the differential-verification-bias argument to a primary text within budget).
Promotion requires: (i) opening the two items that remain unread — JMIR Med Inform 2026;e88734, which needs a route other than the journal page and the DOI redirect (both return empty), and the NeurIPS 2026 paper "Beyond Facts — What AI Clinical Notes Leave Out" — and showing that neither poses the transcript-vs-note predictive gap nor stratifies documentation loss by speaker or patient attribute, which would close attack 2 to Resolved for both adversaries; and (ii) amending the reformulation to restrict the outcome set to labels generated outside the note's causal pathway (or to state that verification bias as a limitation), to drop the "lossy channel / sufficient statistic" framing that P9's falsity retires, and to add a multiplicity, minimum-effect and power plan for the five-stratifier interaction.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Test P1 before designing anything — audit one health system's ambient-scribe contract and configuration for transcript retention duration and research permissions, and check in parallel whether any existing recorded corpus (Fox et al.'s 142 consultations, PriMock57, ACI-Bench) can be linked to any outcome at all; if not, the honest first study is a prospectively consented, locally retained paired corpus with a pre-registered outcome window.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None — not rejected. The asked-but-open neighbour noted in the record (consequence-calibrated severity grading of note omissions, named as the next experiment in Fox et al., arXiv:2608.31016 §9) is not routed, since this candidate is not a rejection.

Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — radiology care delivery, diagnostic quality and safety; clinical informatics; imaging protocol governance

Question (canonical): In sites whose viewer/PACS logs emit series-level display events, and under a provenance map and series taxonomy declared before any data are pulled: (i) what proportion of *diagnostically intended* series (excluding localizers/scouts, dose reports, failed/repeated acquisitions and auto-generated reformats/parameter maps) carry no display event attributable to any reader in the interpreting chain between study-available-in-PACS and report signature, counting a displayed derived series as coverage of each source series the provenance map says it encodes; and (ii) in a stratified sample of those never-displayed series, what is the per-series rate of actionable findings under a pre-specified actionability taxonomy, read by >=2 blinded readers with adjudication and the original report withheld? (Gate 1 reformulation; intake version — "what fraction of diagnostically intended archived series are never displayed to any interpreting reader before signature, and what is the blinded re-read yield in those series?" — recorded in the record, substantively identical.)

Alternative formulations:
- Does anyone look at all the images we acquire, and does it matter if they do not?
- Treating the PACS display log as the instrument, how much acquired image data is unexamined, and is the unexamined fraction diagnostically empty?

Motivating gap: The literature is dense on acquisition (protocol, dose, contrast timing) and dense on reader search behaviour (eye tracking, satisfaction of search), and silent on the join — whether an acquired series was opened at all. The logs exist in every PACS but are kept for access control and compliance, owned by IT/privacy rather than radiology research, and often purged on a short cycle; hanging protocols routinely display a subset of what was acquired. Confirmed at Gate 2: the one opened account of a department mining its own PACS audit logs (Maine Medical Center, SCAR 2003) used them for suspicious-access detection, VIP review and turnaround benchmarking, with vendor purge at 30 days.

Presuppositions: P1 series-level display events exist, are reader-attributable and timestamped against signing — CONTESTED, vendor-dependent; handled as an explicit scope restriction, not a hidden assumption (adversary 2's read of DICOM PS3.15 A.5 found no display event in the standard's audit schema, confirming P1 is viewer-proprietary, while logged instance UIDs plus NumberOfInstances make series-level reconstruction feasible where instance logging is on). P2 series can be partitioned in advance into diagnostically intended vs technical/derived — NECESSARY for non-triviality (the localizer re-read family owns the uninteresting answer). P3 non-display implies non-examination — CONTESTED; two-sided error (brief tiling counts as display; second-workstation/logged-out viewing counts as non-display); reconciliation substudy asserted but never demonstrated. P4 blinded multi-reader re-read can establish actionability — plausible, needs adjudication and report withholding. P5 report signature is the cut-off — flagged; later MDT/referrer views are a separate question (this is what separates the candidate from the "unreviewed reports after signature" family). P6 enough series are never displayed for the quantity to be interesting — CONTESTED, unbounded in either direction; limb (i) measures it and near-zero closes the question. P7 someone would act — evidenced. P8 not already published as a vendor/operational metric — WEAKLY CHECKED, NOT CLEARED in three vocabularies; vendor analytics documentation is largely non-indexed.

What would count as an answer: In >=2 sites with series-level display logs, a pre-registered estimate of the never-displayed proportion with distribution by modality, protocol, shift and reader workload; plus blinded multi-reader actionable-finding yield with an interval in a stratified sample; plus the P3 reconciliation substudy. All three outcomes act: near-zero fraction closes the question; substantial fraction with near-zero yield argues for stopping the acquisition; substantial fraction with non-trivial yield defines a prospectively detectable, series-attributable missed-finding class.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries in 13 vocabularies — 11 at Gate 2 (record), 9 by adversary 1, 9 by adversary 2; plus 13 fetches and one off-budget GitHub code search. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-2337/UQ-20261016-65-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "proportion of imaging series never viewed by radiologist PACS audit log before report" (own field, own words) → no study of unviewed series; only the referrer-reviews-after-signature family. "percentage of MRI sequences not reviewed by radiologist unviewed series diagnostic yield" (the fraction limb, searched as already-computed) → no published fraction; nearest is the MR-localizer family. '"never opened" OR "were not opened" image series percentage radiologists PACS log analysis found that' (searching for the answer as a results sentence) → no number; surfaced one new log-file neighbour, "Providers' Access of Imaging Versus Only Reports: A System Log File Analysis" (wrong actor, study-level, post-signature, no diagnostic endpoint). 'PACS "unviewed" series indicator ... thumbnail checkmark feature' (vendor-UI) → shipped three-state per-series viewed indicators (AHI PACS help, opened: "If a check mark is next to a bold-text series, you have seen all the images in the series"; F8 guard "All Images in study have not been viewed"), no logs, counts or percentages. 'IHE ATNA DICOM audit trail granularity series instance level "view" event' → DICOM PS3.15 A.5 (opened) defines no display-specific event, grouping by SOP Class "for one Study" under generic "Access or Use". 'eye tracking volumetric CT what proportion of slices never fixated' → the within-displayed-series version IS asked (Drew et al.; "radiologists actively search less than half of lung CT"); unread, not graded on. Film-era reject/repeat, clinical-trial core-lab QC, digital-pathology viewport telemetry, storage prefetch access-pattern, error-taxonomy, medico-legal and German-language sweeps all returned analogues with different units (coverage inside displayed images; evaluability of submitted data; discarded exposures; retrieval demand) and no analogue of limb (i).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. Forsberg D, Rosipko B, Sunshine JL, "Factors Affecting Radiologist's PACS Usage", J Digit Imaging 2016, 10.1007/s10278-016-9881-1 (abstract opened via link.springer.com; full text paywalled; sibling "Analyzing PACS Usage Patterns by Means of Process Mining", 10.1007/s10278-015-9824-2; conference account via auntminnieeurope.com/clinical-news/article/15649334). Unit: the command trace per examination (one attending, one exam; 567 single-view chest exams / 14 radiologists in the conference account, 8 weeks of command logs in the journal version). Endpoint: number of commands, number of command classes, bigram repetitiveness, time to read. Comparator: between-radiologist, between-specialty, time-of-day. Estimand: association of reader/specialty/time with command counts and reading time. "Series" does not occur in the abstract.
B. "Magnetic resonance spine localizers: the forgotten treasure", mss-ijmsr.com (pictorial review with small audit; not re-verified by either adversary). Unit: the localizer set of one whole-spine MRI (100 sets). Endpoint: count of incidental findings on localizers (9 tallied). Comparator: none; no blinding, no reader count, no adjudication. Estimand: none — a descriptive tally.
C. Maine Medical Center PACS/web audit-log warehouse (Coleman, SCAR 2003), auntminnie.com/.../article/15566409. Unit: the audit record and the user (~1,600 users, 25–30k records/week). Endpoint: suspicious-access detection, VIP review, turnaround benchmarks. Comparator: exam type / body part / day / physician. Estimand: none — compliance surveillance and operational reporting; logs purged at 30 days.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — same instrument family (viewer logs), different object: A's unit is the examination command trace with an interaction-count/time estimand, the candidate's unit is the series with a binary display event attributed to the interpreting chain and cut at signature; A's corpus (single-view chest radiographs) cannot express a never-displayed-series fraction and A carries no diagnostic endpoint, so it cannot carry limb (ii). The record's named demotion condition was tested: the journal abstract reports no per-series display metric, so the condition is substantially reduced but not eliminated (full text unread). vs B — same question shape applied to exactly the class P2 excludes by construction; no denominator, no log measurement, no blinding, no actionability taxonomy, no estimand. vs C — the custodial use of the very instrument the candidate needs: different unit (user/record), different estimand (compliance/throughput), and a 30-day purge that forces any study to be prospective; documentary evidence for the reason-for-silence rather than a prior answer. Not graded on, recorded unread: Drew/Rubin volumetric visual search (gaze coverage within displayed series, no archive denominator, no signature cut-off); the MR-localizer PMC paper (PMC hard-blocked); French TL & Langer SG, "Tracking PACS Usage with Open Source Tools", 10.1007/s10278-010-9337-y (an instrumentation paper that could plausibly carry a per-series usage metric); vendor analytics specifications. US8566122B2 ("navigation to unseen radiology images") and US7698152B2 (Siemens; viewing processor "generates a viewed indicator associated with the individual image and the particular user", claim 15 covering a retrievable log of which images were accessed before a report; background cites no prevalence figure) show the concept is deliberate engineering prior art without being a published measurement.

Novelty confidence: Medium
(13 vocabularies including the candidate's own field in its own words, both mandatory query types, the two method-owning fields, and eight adversary vocabularies Gate 2 never tried. No prior found with the candidate's unit, endpoint and estimand. Not High: one neighbour (A) is close in instrument and is read only at abstract level; a second novelty-bearing paper (French & Langer 2010) is unread; P8 remains uncleared against non-indexed vendor analytics. Demotion condition if any of those reports a per-series display or unviewed-series rate: Low.)

Significance — consequence: Three distinct actions, no uninformative outcome. Near-zero never-displayed fraction retires a recurring hanging-protocol worry with a number. Substantial fraction with near-zero blinded yield means scanner time, dose, contrast and archive cost are spent on data that never enters a diagnostic decision, converting protocol pruning from expert opinion into an audited exercise. Substantial fraction with non-trivial yield defines a missed-finding class that is measurable and attributable at the series level and detectable prospectively from logs, before harm — which no current QA instrument does, since discrepancy meetings and peer review act on reports, not on unopened data.
Significance — audience: (1) Protocol committees and modality leads, who already prune sequences without display-coverage evidence (opened RSNA QI project "Reducing Unnecessary Scan Acquisitions at Abdominal MRI"). (2) Radiology QA/patient-safety and medico-legal functions, for whom "acquired, archived, never opened, finding present" is a new documentable exposure (trade-press terrain confirmed by title only, not opened). (3) PACS/enterprise-imaging vendors: two issued patents and at least two shipped per-series viewed indicators show the feature side has invested but has no population evidence on whether a pre-signature gate is worth the interruption. (4) Compliance/IT custodians, for whom a positive result justifies longer retention and a series-level schema.
Significance — fecundity: Does the fraction rise with workload, shift and list length (a dose-response test of workload on coverage, independent of report error)? Is display coverage a better leading indicator of diagnostic error than turnaround time? Can AI triage be aimed at series the reader did not open — a far smaller, better-defined target than second-reading everything? Does hanging-protocol design explain between-site variance, making coverage a configuration-level rather than reader-level defect? Does a declared series taxonomy become a reusable coverage denominator for other display-log questions?
Significance — anchoring: Satisfaction of search and volumetric visual-search coverage (the within-series version of the same deficit); the unread-examination and follow-up-never-reviewed literatures (the same failure one and two levels up, P5's separate question); incidental findings on localizers/scouts (the same failure one level down, excluded by P2); dose and throughput optimization; and the DICOM/ATNA audit-trail standard, where the instrument's schema is actually decided.

Reason for silence: A custodial split across three owners, a retention wall, and no reporting hook. CORRECTED at Gate 4: the record's "incidental by-product of access control" claim does not survive — US7698152B2 (opened) is a purpose-built per-image viewed indicator with a retrievable pre-report viewing log from 2005, and at least two products ship three-state per-series viewed indicators, so the gauge was built deliberately and has been in products for ~20 years. What survives: those implementations are real-time per-reader UI aids, not exportable or aggregated metrics (vendor help describes no logs, reports, percentages or counts); DICOM PS3.15 A.5 defines no display event, so any aggregate is vendor-proprietary; the acquisition decision, the display decision and the log belong to three functions none of which is funded or credited for the join; retention closes the door even where the schema suffices (30-day vendor purge in the one opened account), forcing a prospective, compliance-negotiated study; and no quality measure, accreditation item or billing code makes "series displayed" reportable. Secondary: the localizer/scout sub-case has absorbed this question's attention for two decades, which lets the general form look already asked. Residual: the answer-side half is evidenced, the ask-side half (no credited owner; sub-case absorption; possible liability deterrence) is plausible but not evidenced.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent adversaries (A1: 9 queries/4 fetches, 7 of the 8 required Disguise vocabularies; A2: 9 queries/4 fetches, 8 Disguise vocabularies). Verbatim logs: batches/2026-10-16-2337/UQ-20261016-65-adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. No attack is Unresolved from either adversary.
1 | Triviality | Answerable in a page: hanging protocols are designed to show a subset and reformats re-encode sources, so "most series are never shown and none of it matters" is a priori; or an informatics lead would say "near zero, we look at everything" | The a priori answer conflates the limbs; the provenance map removes redundant reformats from the numerator by construction, and 29 queries in 13 vocabularies produced no estimate of either limb; the Siemens patent background justifies the feature by a capability gap and cites no prevalence figure; vendors shipping a per-series viewed indicator and an "All Images in study have not been viewed" guard show the industry does not treat the fraction as known-zero; limb (ii) has no existing-knowledge answer at all | Resolved (A1) · Resolved (A2)
2 | Disguise | A renamed version of the vendor unviewed-images feature, the scout/localizer re-read literature, within-image gaze/scroll coverage (Drew; DBT eye-tracking; pathology WSI viewport telemetry), storage access-pattern work, core-lab QC, or the referrer-never-reviews family | Each searched in its own vocabulary: vendor-UI yields shipped features and two patents but no measurement; localizers are the P2-excluded sub-case; pathology and vision science measure coverage inside displayed objects with no archive denominator; core labs measure evaluability of submitted data; film-era work measures discarded exposures; the referrer family is post-signature and report-level. The one new log-file neighbour (Providers' Access of Imaging Versus Only Reports) has the wrong actor, wrong unit and no diagnostic endpoint. A1 ran 7 of the 8 required vocabularies and self-marked Partial on that shortfall plus the then-unread neighbour; A2 ran the full 8 and additionally routed the unread neighbour through Crossref to the publisher and read its abstract | Partial (A1, 7/8 queries) · Resolved (A2, 8/8)
3 | Combinatorial novelty | Informatics x QA re-read glued together; no real problem at the interface | The interface carries its own problems, seen in the primary standard: the audit schema groups objects by SOP Class for one Study under a generic access/use code with no display event, so the join needs a provenance map, an attribution rule for the interpreting chain, a signature-time cut and a retention change that none of the three owning functions builds; display is not examination (the patent defines viewed by proportion of image data displayed; vendor indicators carry a "some but not all" state) | Resolved (A1) · Resolved (A2)
4 | Presupposition failure | P1, P3, P6, P8 contested; the question dies if P1 is false | No presupposition shown false. P1 is an explicit scope restriction and the standards check supports rather than inverts it (no display event in the schema, but instance UIDs plus NumberOfInstances make series reconstruction feasible where instance logging is on). P6 is measured by limb (i), so it is falsifiability. Costs remain: sites whose viewers emit series display events are self-selected (newer, larger), and the record does not say how it would bound limb (i)'s external validity; P3's two-sided error is assigned to a substudy with no evidence such a reconciliation has ever been done; P8 uncleared | Partial (A1) · Partial (A2)
5 | Vagueness | "Diagnostically intended", "displayed", "actionable" elastic enough to produce any answer | All three are declared before the pull and auditable; "displayed" has a concrete operational definition in shipping systems; near-zero genuinely closes the question, so it is falsifiable. But that pre-declaration makes the number *meaningful* is plausible and unevidenced: nothing shows any one provenance map is defensible or how far the fraction moves across maps | Resolved (A1) · Partial (A2)
6 | Significance inflation | Audiences rhetorical; nobody commissions a study whose positive result is discoverable evidence their readers did not look | Audiences evidenced, not asserted: an opened protocol-pruning QI project; two issued patents and at least two shipped per-series viewed indicators on the vendor side; live medico-legal terrain (titles only, nothing rested on their content); three pre-named actions keyed to the three possible outcomes | Resolved (A1) · Resolved (A2)
7 | Reason for silence | The mechanism explains why answering is hard, not why nobody asked — and it is partly false: the gauge was purpose-built by vendors 20 years ago | Two sub-mechanisms are genuinely ask-side (no reporting hook, so the metric has no owner even in radiology informatics; the localizer sub-case absorbing the general question) and the standards check corroborates the answer-side half; but the ask-side half is unevidenced, the strongest candidate (liability deterrence) rests on unopened items, and "vendors built the instrument and nobody aggregated it" needs its own explanation. The record's "incidental by-product" wording is corrected above | Partial (A1) · Partial (A2)
8 | Dissolution | Dissolves into site configuration or into an auditing convention: concede that hanging protocols show a sufficient subset and that briefly tiled series count as displayed, and limb (i) becomes a fact about how generously the provenance map credits coverage, leaving the already-asked protocol-pruning question | A configuration-determined fraction is still measurable, attributable and actionable (reconfigure or stop acquiring), the design already requires >=2 sites with protocol strata, and a zero result in auto-tiling sites is the P6 closing outcome. The selection is the contribution: a log-defined, prospectively detectable, series-attributable sample is one no protocol-pruning study (expert judgement) and no re-read study has used, and limb (ii) is a diagnostic endpoint no convention defines away. Unanswered: how far the headline number moves with the map | Resolved (A1) · Partial (A2)

Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261016-65-verification.md and UQ-20261016-65-verification-2.md): both unread near-priors are still unread, the headline that looked like a demotion is not one, and the instrument presupposition is now evidenced rather than argued.
Neither of the two novelty-bearing papers could be opened. doi 10.1007/s10278-016-9881-1 and doi 10.1007/s10278-010-9337-y both failed at the DOI resolver; link.springer.com served abstract pages only, with full text paywalled. From the abstract pages: Forsberg et al. measure PACS usage as a "sequence of computer commands" per reading session — unit one command trace (one attending radiologist, one exam), endpoints command count, command classes, bigram repetitiveness and time to read, over eight weeks of logs, modelled by GLMs on radiologist, exam category and time of week — with no statement of series-level granularity and no never-viewed fraction; whether the log distinguishes series cannot be confirmed or excluded from the abstract. French & Langer is "Tracking PACS Usage with Open Source Tools", on workstation-fleet utilisation for purchasing decisions, with metrics not visible on the page and no indication of per-series display logging; its one visible line is "Lacking a vended solution for this challenge, we developed our own." So promotion condition (a) is untouched, and under Gate 4's rule the unread pair keeps attack 2 Unverified for the novelty limb, which caps this entry at Provisional without rejecting it.
The "40% of images, radiology reports requiring follow-up are never reviewed" headline that surfaced in the first pass is not about this candidate's quantity, and the second pass pinned down why. In the Radiology Business report (6 Nov 2018) of the Yousem neuroradiology dataset, "approximately 8.4 percent had neither images or imaging reports viewed in PACS or EMRs" across more than 8,200 studies, and of the 124 never-viewed studies "20 percent were classified as normal, 40 percent were minor unimportant findings," while "40 percent were classified as findings that require intervention or follow-up and less than 1 percent were critical." The 40% is therefore a severity split within 124 studies — about 50 studies, roughly 0.6% of the series the article covers — not 40% of follow-up-requiring studies. Its unit is the study or order, its endpoint any access to images or report in PACS or EMR logs, and the reader whose access is counted is on the requesting side, not the interpreting radiologist before signature. The same holds for the SIIM audit-log work reported by AuntMinnie: unit the ED exam, endpoint whether the referring physician ever viewed it ("Exam was never viewed by the referring physician: 5,236 (21%)" for CT, 5% for CR, 54% for US). Neither is the candidate's unit, reader or endpoint, so the demotion condition is not triggered — and Yousem supplies this entry with a published consequence anchor it did not have, at the study level, for the shape of limb (ii).
Promotion condition (b) comes back negative and is restated accordingly. Six further searches across vendor and enterprise-imaging material found no product documentation of a per-series display or view report: Intelerad's InteleViewer help documents how a user opens series but reports no view tracking, and Carestream's analytics dashboard material is study-level operational metrics. Study- and exam-level viewing is documented; series-level viewing is not, in anything that could be opened. That does not falsify P8, since absence over six searches is weak, but it moves the burden: the entry should now be read as presupposing an instrument whose existence is attested only by the DICOM audit schema's object-level granularity and by the scope restriction in the question itself.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 3/3

Strongest remaining objection: Limb (i)'s headline fraction is a free parameter of the pre-declared provenance map, and the map choice is adversarial to limb (ii) — crediting a displayed thick reformat as coverage of an unopened thin-slice source stack writes off precisely the series where actionable yield would concentrate, so a map generous enough to be clinically defensible pushes the fraction toward zero and closes the question by convention, while a strict map inflates it with informationally redundant series; nothing in the record or either adversary log bounds that sensitivity in either direction, and all three pre-named actions are keyed to a threshold on a number that moves with the convention.
Promotion requires: (a) the paywalled full text of 10.1007/s10278-016-9881-1 and a read of French & Langer 10.1007/s10278-010-9337-y, each confirmed to report no per-series display or unviewed-series rate — still open after verification spent five fetches on them, since the DOI resolver failed on both and link.springer.com serves abstracts only; (b) positive evidence from one named viewer's audit or logging specification that per-series display events are actually recorded, which is a harder condition than the batch wrote: six further searches across vendor and enterprise-imaging material found study- and exam-level viewing documented and nothing at series level, so P8 is uncleared and the instrument's existence rests on the DICOM audit schema's object-level granularity plus the scope restriction in the question itself; (c) a pre-declared sensitivity analysis bounding how far the limb (i) fraction moves between a strict and a generous provenance map, with limb (ii) sampling that does not depend on the map choice; and (d) one further Disguise-vocabulary query to complete adversary 1's 8-query minimum. Novelty would then stand at Medium-with-neighbour-read rather than Medium-with-unread-neighbour.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): establish which viewer/PACS products emit exportable, reader-attributable series-level display events at all — that is a product-capability survey, not a measurement — and, at a site with one, agree a prospective log-retention extension with compliance before writing the series taxonomy and provenance map.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected.

ID: UQ-20261017-01
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — physical chemistry / porous-materials characterisation (adsorption metrology). Adjacent: measurement science, metascience.
Question (canonical): Over a pre-declared frame of archived N2/Ar isotherms (NIST/ARPA-E ISODB plus journal SI) each linkable to a source paper reporting a BET area computed from that same isotherm, with the reference fixed by one pre-registered consistency-criteria implementation (BETSI-class, tie-breaking and no-admissible-window rules declared in advance): is E[Δ] positive, where Δ = (reported area − reference area)/reference area, and does E[Δ] increase with proximity-to-frontier — proximity computed from the RECOMPUTED reference area against the highest area published to date for that material class in a declared journal set — after adjustment for material class, publication year and isotherm quality? (R1, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V0 and the reasons for R1 are in the record.)
Alternative formulations: Is the analyst's freedom in choosing the BET pressure range exercised directionally — upward — when the number is close to a record, rather than symmetrically as noise? · Does a published BET area depend on how ambitious the claim it supports is, with the isotherm held fixed?
Motivating gap: Osterrieth et al. (chemRxiv 10.26434/chemrxiv.14291644; Adv. Mater. 2022, 34, 2201502) gave 18 raw isotherms to 61 labs and found "a wide range of values", releasing BETSI as an unambiguous assignment. Its estimand is dispersion across analysts on a fixed isotherm; nobody found here asks whether that dispersion is signed and incentive-linked against an enumerable record frontier (MOF record series, JACS 2012, 134, 15016). Newly computable via source-linked machine-readable isotherms plus a mechanical reference computation.
Presuppositions: 1. archive carries both reported area and source paper — CONFIRMED FALSE as an archive field (ISODB canonical_keys has no BET/surface-area key and strips non-canonical keys on ingest; adversary 1 E1), so the frame must be hand- or text-mined. 2. archive coverage is itself selected — contested, handled by declaring the frame. 3. one criteria procedure yields a reproducible reference — contested; ~10% tolerance needed for NU-110x, UiO-66 fails criterion 4 (Ambroz 2018). 4. a dated per-class frontier is enumerable — mildly contested. 5. the reported value came from the deposited isotherm — contested and unverifiable by inspection given 7. 6. upward window shifts mechanically raise the area — FALSE as stated (see adversarial log row 4). 7. the authors' implied window is not uniquely identified from (isotherm, reported area) — contested, demotes strengthening element (i) to a set-valued quantity. 8. BET area is a competitive figure of merit — established, but contested as an incentive covariate once 6 fails. ADDED BY ADVERSARY 1 and missing from the record: the archived curve must resolve the low-pressure BET window finely enough to recompute a reference (many ISODB records are figure-digitised: articleSource "Figure 4", tabular_data false, digitizer UNKNOWN). NOT presupposed: that any inflation is intentional.
What would count as an answer: Pre-registered recomputation over the declared frame; primary answer is the signed coefficient of proximity-to-frontier in a model for Δ with material-class and year effects and isotherm-quality controls, with a CI; declared null retires the hypothesis. Strengthening elements: window-offset scales with proximity (subject to 7); negative control (BET C-constant / low-pressure residual) shows no proximity effect; falsification if Δ is centred at zero.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 12 at Gate 2 (one over its 11 cap, recorded) + 26 new-vocabulary Disguise queries across three adversaries (9 + 8 + 9) + free GitHub code/issue searches. Most informative: own-field journal-title form "'Are published BET surface areas' MOFs overestimated systematically higher than recalculated" → AIChE 2016/2019 abstracts only, no such paper; mandated already-computed-quantity query "fraction of published BET areas failing Rouquerol criteria" → no published fraction exists; answer-form "recalculated BET areas of published MOF isotherms from NIST ISODB exceed author-reported values percent BETSI applied to literature corpus" → only Osterrieth and repository copies, decisive negative; metrology ISO 9277 proficiency-test sweep → BAM CRMs, NanoValid BET comparison, NIST SRM 1898, all laboratory-vs-certified with no literature frame or claim-magnitude covariate; forensic-econometrics caliper/threshold sweep → applied to test statistics, never to a measured physical quantity; ECSA/Tafel sweep → Limaye/Zeng, Nat. Commun. 12 (2021), the same method on a different figure of merit, null, no record covariate; crystallography recompute-from-deposited-data audits (IUCr, titles only) → contradicts the record's rhetoric that the method has never touched physical-science instrument data; German and Chinese sweeps → nothing but Osterrieth copies. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0059/UQ-20261017-01-record.md and -adversary-1.md / -adversary-2.md / -adversary-3.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 Osterrieth et al., "How Reproducible Are Surface Areas Calculated from the BET Equation?", chemRxiv 10.26434/chemrxiv.14291644 / Adv. Mater. 2022, 34, 2201502 — FULL TEXT COULD NOT READ by any of four agents (failed: doi.org, Wiley onlinelibrary via WebFetch and via proxy curl 403, eprints.gla.ac.uk 403, Cambridge CC-BY bitstream SERVER_ERROR, api.crossref.org CONNECT 403; abstract-level records read at core.ac.uk/outputs/558625868, chemRxiv 6206264b2168676d4d72a29a, repository.cam.ac.uk/handle/1810/337403). P3 Bingel, Walton & Sholl, "Experimentally Verified Alkane Adsorption Isotherms...", opened at osti.gov/pages/servlets/purl/1881147 — unit: replicate sets of published isotherms in the same archive; endpoint: outlier flag / consensus isotherm; comparator: internal consensus among replicates; estimand: unsigned disagreement rate (~15–16%). Adversary-found near neighbour: Ambroz, Parkin et al., Small Methods 2018 (OPENED, discovery-pp.ucl.ac.uk/10056236/1/Ambroz_et_al-2018-Small_Methods.pdf) — recomputes a handful of literature-derived BET values under criteria and states their direction case by case, with no corpus, no statistic and no incentive covariate.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same reference computation, different unit (published paper in the wild, not a participant), endpoint (the original authors' printed number, signed), comparator and estimand (a regression coefficient on an incentive covariate P1 cannot construct, since a round-robin isotherm supports no record claim). vs P2 — P2 is method-vs-geometric-truth on simulated data with no author and no reported value; its direction-of-error finding is a confound the candidate must control, not a prior answer. vs P3 — same archive and same literature-meta-analysis move, but loadings not BET areas, internal consensus not the authors' number, unsigned rate not a signed coefficient; strongest evidence the frame is buildable and the adjacent study was done without asking this. vs Ambroz — case-by-case direction, no corpus, no estimand; but it is the source of the fatal objection below.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If positive and non-trivial, the published porosity frontier is partly an artefact of analysis freedom concentrated at the frontier, with a computable correction and a cheap policy follow-on (deposit the BET window and a criteria-checked value alongside any near-record claim); it converts a reproducibility finding into a bias finding, which has different remedies. If null, BET dispersion is licensed as noise to propagate as an uncertainty interval on the record series — but see the adversarial log: the null branch is not identified under R1's own estimator.
Significance — audience: Porous-materials synthesis groups competing on this number; NIST/ARPA-E ISODB curators and the Sholl/Walton data-quality line (reported-value fidelity as a new quality axis); ISO 9277 / IUPAC and the certified-BET apparatus confirmed real and funded (BAM CRM BAM-PM-101/102 and gas-adsorption reports, NanoValid BET interlaboratory comparison, NIST SRM 1898); editors at venues printing record claims; metrology, which models bias as a property of a laboratory and never of the claim it supports; metascience, which owns the recomputation-audit method — though crystallography has run that genre on deposited data for ~15 years, so the record's "never in the physical sciences" is overstated.
Significance — fecundity: Generalises to every figure of merit read off an analyst-chosen window over a raw curve (t-plot/DFT pore volume, ECSA, Tafel fitting range, uptake extrapolation, capacity at a chosen rate, thermal-conductivity fit windows); makes askable whether the criteria-based reference itself drifts as software defaults change, and what a frontier claim must deposit to be audit-stable. Sibling: UQ-20261016-43.
Significance — anchoring: The live BET-validity debate for micropores (P2; NU-110 satisfies all four criteria yet disagrees ~33% with its accessible area, Ambroz p. 11); the MOF record series and its press treatment; ISODB archive-quality work (P3's ~15–16% outlier rates); the Osterrieth round-robin and the standardisation push it triggered; researcher-degrees-of-freedom metascience, which has no physical-science case with both a mechanical reference and an enumerable record frontier.
Reason for silence: Claimed mechanisms: new tools and data (BETSI 2021/22 plus source-linked archives); a disciplinary boundary (dispersion framed as metrology and handed to a round-robin; the directional/incentive estimand has no owner inside physical chemistry); and an incentive/taboo gap, since the unit of analysis is a named paper and the interesting stratum a handful of named groups, making the deliverable accusation-shaped even when null. Adversarially weakened: the tool mechanism is contradicted — pyGAPS automated the Rouquerol rules by 2019, SESAMI's lineage predates BETSI (AIChE 2019 631b, opened), the BETSI repository was created 2020-05-04, and ISODB predates all of them, while the Sholl group ran the adjacent corpus study without asking; the taboo mechanism is weakened by this field publishing named-paper literature audits ("one in 5 materials chemistry papers may be wrong"); and the record concedes the suspicion "floats free in the field's informal talk", which is nearer un-answered than un-asked. Only the disciplinary-boundary mechanism survives on evidence.

Verification and late Gate 4 (post-batch: two fresh-context readers, logs UQ-20261017-01-verification-ambroz.md, UQ-20261017-01-verification-osterrieth.md and UQ-20261017-01-verification-fig5.md; then a fourth adversary run cold on the Gate 0-3 record with the refutation handed to it, log UQ-20261017-01-adversary-4.md): the kill that decided this entry is REFUTED, the entry is nonetheless Rejected, and it is Rejected on different, better-sourced ground.
The refutation first. Ambroz et al., Small Methods 2018 (doi 10.1002/smtd.201800173) contains no pore-size-dependent sign change in the habitual-minus-criteria BET difference. Read through the UCL open-access copy, the text says the standard range "should not be used for MOFs with pore sizes below 7 Å" and that the resulting areas "can be incorrect", and its ONE directional statement runs the opposite way to the kill: for the sub-7 Å IRMOFs the criteria-selected values are expected to be higher than standard-range ones ("we expect the values would be higher"), which makes the habitual window an underestimate there, not an overestimate. The word "underestimate" does not appear anywhere in the paper, and the sentences the adversaries read as overestimation are about micropore pore filling and about NU-1103/1104's inflated monolayer loading ("the monolayer loading is overestimated resulting in excessive surface area") — a different mechanism from pressure-window choice. Figure 5, which holds the per-material numbers that would settle the direction, could not be read: the Wiley page and the DOI both returned fetch errors, the open-access PDF returned the caption and Table 2's ranges but no bar values, a second fetch was rate-limited at HTTP 429 and curl was refused by the proxy at 403. What the caption and Table 2 do establish is that the criteria ranges for IRMOF-9, -11 and -13 sit far below the standard window (N2 at 77 K: 0.0001-0.0499, 0.00005-0.01, 0.00005-0.01, against 0.05-0.30), which is consistent with the paper's stated expectation and with no sign flip. So the ground recorded as fatal — "the sign flips with pore size, Ambroz pp. 6 and 9, quoted independently by two adversaries" — is struck, and with it the claim that the declared adjustment set cannot work because of a documented reversal.
The novelty side moved the other way. Osterrieth et al., Advanced Materials 2022, is a round robin on SUPPLIED data: 18 previously measured raw N2 isotherms, anonymised with arbitrary scaling factors, sent as csv files to 61 laboratories, each computing a BET area its own way (90% reporting Rouquerol criteria, 23% commercial software, 6% self-written code), compared with each other and against the authors' BETSI implementation. Nothing read of it compares a published paper's own reported area against a value recomputed from that paper's isotherm, and nothing relates a discrepancy to how high the reported area is or to record-holder status. Its estimand is between-analyst spread with the isotherm held fixed; the candidate's is the coefficient of an incentive covariate on a published-versus-recomputed signed offset. So the nearest prior does not do what the Gate 2 grade needed it to do, and this entry's novelty is better than the batch recorded. Recorded limit: that reading is from a repository PDF through a page summariser after the publisher, chemRxiv and Wiley routes all failed, no string was verbatim-checked, and the record-status question was never put to it as a query, so it is "not seen" rather than "confirmed absent".
The late adversary. With the sign-flip ground removed and the three established facts handed over so it would not re-derive them, a fourth adversary ran all eight attacks cold on the Gate 0-3 record, completing 8 new-vocabulary Disguise queries (text-mining, porous-carbon theoretical limit, compliance survey, computational geometric-area databases, econometric bunching, record-claim reassessment, multiverse and specification-curve analysis). Disguise came back Partial: no corpus recomputation and no claim-ambition covariate exists anywhere it looked, which again supports novelty rather than undermining it. Attack 4 came back Unresolved, on a ground no earlier adversary had found and which does not depend on Ambroz at all. Three legs: the NIST/ARPA-E ISODB stores isotherms but has no reported-BET-area field, so the frame must be hand-harvested from papers and its achievable size is unknown; nothing opened shows that the frontier papers' raw isotherms are deposited anywhere, and the frontier stratum is a handful of materials; and the frontier papers themselves say they applied the very procedure the candidate would audit them against — Farha et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2012;134:15016 (NU-110E, 7140 m2/g) states its areas are "subject to well-defined 'consistency criteria'". That last leg is the decisive one: it makes a near-zero offset the expected result exactly in the stratum where the incentive hypothesis carries all of its weight, so the primary estimand is uninformative where it matters most and the record's answer — declare an exclusion rule — is procedural rather than evidence that the frame can be built. Attack 7 came back Unresolved as well and concurs: consistency criteria for MOFs date from 2006-2007 and the record concedes that hand recomputation per paper was feasible, so "the tools are too recent" does not explain the silence, and the remaining mechanisms are inferred from the absence of search hits.
Unresolved on attack 4 is fatal by the Gate 4 rule, so the verdict is Rejected — the fourth adversary's own summary verdict field said Provisional, which the rule overrides, and that disagreement is recorded rather than resolved in the candidate's favour. The practical difference from the batch's rejection is the gate's content: this entry is not rejected because a published paper shows the measurement cannot be adjusted, but because the frame cannot be assembled and the frontier stratum is expected to be null by the frontier authors' own stated practice. Both the strongest objection and the first-step pointer below are rewritten to match.
Residual checks left open and not counted as passed: Figure 5's numbers (the publisher PDF, read directly rather than through a summariser, would settle the offset's direction and size by pore regime); Osterrieth's full text on whether discrepancy size tracks the height of a reported area; and five near-neighbours the late adversary saw by title only and did not open (a carbonaceous virtual-model paper, AIChE 2006 abstract 381a, a Springer correction, RSC d1ta08021k, arXiv:1506.08219).

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The frame cannot be assembled where the question needs it, and the stratum that carries the whole incentive hypothesis is expected to be null by the frontier authors' own stated practice. The NIST/ARPA-E ISODB holds isotherms but no reported-BET-area field, so every reported value must be hand-harvested from its paper and the achievable sample size is unknown; nothing opened shows that the raw isotherms behind the record-holding materials are deposited anywhere, and that stratum is a handful of materials; and Farha et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2012;134:15016, reporting NU-110E at 7140 m2/g, states that its areas are "subject to well-defined 'consistency criteria'". A paper that already applied the audit procedure cannot show an offset against it, so the primary estimand is uninformative precisely at the frontier, and declaring an exclusion rule is a procedure rather than evidence that the frame exists. Attack 7 concurs independently: consistency criteria for MOFs date from 2006-2007 and the record concedes per-paper hand recomputation was feasible, so the offered reason for the silence does not hold and the remaining mechanisms are inferred from the absence of search hits. (Superseded ground, recorded in Verification above: the sign-flip reading of Ambroz et al. that decided the batch verdict is refuted, and the pore-size confound it rested on remains a confound to adjust for rather than an identification failure.)
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Before any recomputation, settle whether the frame exists at all: count how many record-or-near-record porous materials have a raw isotherm retrievable in machine-readable form AND a reported BET area in the depositing paper, and check what fraction of those papers already state a consistency-criteria procedure. If that count is small or those papers mostly state criteria, the primary estimand is dead on arrival and no recomputation is worth running. Only then do the identification work: a pore-filling-pressure covariate derived from each isotherm, with the comparator switched from a criteria window to the same mechanical habitual window, to see whether any within-class variation in proximity-to-frontier survives. Neither step is taken here.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None. Not rejected as already-asked and not a disguised known — 38 documented queries found no prior formulation and no published value of the quantity. Rejected at Gate 4 on attack 4 Unresolved — from a fourth adversary run late and cold after verification refuted the batch's ground, with attack 7 Unresolved concurring — so nothing is routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The late Disguise sweep (8 new vocabularies) again found no prior formulation, so the novelty finding stands and it is the frame, not the question's originality, that fails.
