Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-06-verification.md, -verification-companion.md, -verification-threeseed.md): all three Unverified Disguise checks are now discharged, and the strongest objection is substantially refuted — the 500x overlap is a different object from limb (i).
**The cap.** arXiv:2604.14419 ("Equifinality in Mixture of Experts: Routing Topology Does Not Determine Language Modeling Quality", Ternovtsii & Bilak) was opened through to its cross-seed section. The architecture is an ST-MoE decoder-only transformer with cosine routing to learned 64-dimensional centroids, top-k=4, 3 hops, 1024 singleton experts, 37.6M and 76-84M parameters, WikiText-103 with a 32K BPE vocabulary, seeds 42, 137 and 7. The "500x-above-random functional overlap" is a **Jaccard similarity between the top-20 projected-vocabulary word sets** of an expert and its best match in the other seed: "Jaccard similarity of top-20 projected vocabulary words (best-match across 1024 experts)", averaging "0.15 (Wide) and 0.13 (Deep)" against "the random baseline of ~0.0003". Weight space shows nothing: "best-match cosine similarity averages 0.107 for both architectures".
That is an output-side **function** overlap, not an agreement between the two runs' token-to-expert partitions. Four further differences, each from the opened text: matching is "best-match across 1024 experts", with no Hungarian, assignment or one-to-one constraint found, so many experts may share a best match and the statistic is a per-expert maximum; the comparison is one seed pair (42 vs 137) at **converged checkpoints only** — nothing at 1% of training, where limbs (i) and (iv) are posed; no cross-seed quantity is related to held-out loss or downstream score; and the ~0.0003 null is not derived in the paper and looks like a single-pair expectation rather than a max-over-1024 null, which would make the 500x ratio an overstatement in the paper's own favour. So limb (i) is not "in substance" measured there, the Gate 2 miss is a real miss of a relevant neighbour rather than of a prior, and novelty is not reduced to Low. The entry's attack-1 leg that Equifinality "predicts limb (iv) near-null" is correspondingly weakened and restated: its cross-seed measure is never connected to quality, so it forecasts nothing about limb (iv).
**The two residuals.** Companion arXiv:2604.14434 ("Geometric Routing Enables Causal Expert Control in Mixture of Experts") is an intervention study on single converged checkpoints — Semantic Dictionary projections, knockout, steering, output-vector rewriting — on Wide 1x12 (PPL 33.93) and Deep 3x4 (PPL 34.62). It carries **no cross-seed overlap statistic at all**; its only permutation null is 200 label permutations for a silhouette score, and its Jaccard figures (14.3-33.3%) compare contexts within one model. The "15 runs across 3 seeds" it mentions belong to 2604.14419. REFUTED as a prior. arXiv:2607.28308 ("Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing") has three seeds only for a matched-compute Top-1 versus Top-2 validation-loss comparison in a six-layer MoE (delta = 0.1016 +/- 0.0025), and its "expert subspaces overlap substantially" is a **within-model** measurement: each expert gets its own centred rank-128 subspace and the index compares inter-expert separation against within-expert dispersion inside one model. The adversaries' attack-6 use of that phrase as a pre-empted branch is therefore struck — it says nothing about agreement across runs. Appendix S6.3 and S7.1 text was still not served, but S6.3 is headed "Matched-compute Top-1 versus Top-2" and keyword sweeps for routing agreement, across-runs and Hungarian matching returned nothing, so the residual is now a known-contents section rather than an open Disguise risk.
**What this changes and what it does not.** Promotion condition (a) is discharged in full: all three named reads were made and none contains a cross-run matched routing-agreement measurement. Novelty is Medium and no longer capped by an unread section. The verdict does not move, because well-posedness stands at 2/3 on its own grounds — ARI/NMI are undefined on a top-8 multi-assignment until a reduction is declared, and limb (iv) is not estimable at k >= 3 — and 3/3 is required for Validated. Conditions (b), (c) and (d) stand unchanged and are now the whole of what blocks promotion.
Caveats recorded: all three readers worked through the page summariser rather than raw PDF text, so the absence claims rest on keyword sweeps of summarised text; 2604.14419's definition of "vocabulary projection" and the derivation of its 0.0003 baseline could not be located and may sit in an appendix the summariser omitted.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness reduced from the record's 3/3: limb (i) is well-posed only once a reduction of the top-8 multi-assignment to a partition-comparable object is declared — ARI/NMI are undefined as written — and limb (iv) is not estimable at the stated k >= 3, which two adversaries landed independently, one with its own simulation. Both are repairable by pre-registration, not defects in the question, which is why this is 2/3 rather than a Gate 1 rejection. Significance 2/3 holds but is not secure.)

Strongest remaining objection (REPLACED on verification; the Disguise objection it previously carried was refuted): limb (iv) is not estimable at the stated k >= 3 and ARI/NMI are undefined on a top-8 multi-assignment until a reduction is declared, so the question as written is 2/3 well-posed and cannot be Validated however the literature falls. Two adversaries landed limb (iv) independently, one with its own 20,000-draw simulation giving null R^2 mean 0.499 at n=3, p=1 and R^2 identically 1.000 at n=3, p=2, falling below 0.10 only at n >= 11 — so the limb carrying the quality stake silently needs seeds in the tens, which collides with the cost mechanism that explains the silence. Behind it stands attack 8 at Partial for one adversary: neither declared null preserves each run's expert-mass marginals while destroying correspondence, and with routing mass at Gini ~0.90-0.95 the high-mass experts match first, so a positive headline can be driven by concentration that any two runs of any recipe share. The former strongest objection — that arXiv:2604.14419's "500x-above-random functional overlap" was limb (i) in substance — is withdrawn: on reading, that overlap is a best-match Jaccard between experts' top-20 projected-vocabulary word sets at converged checkpoints, not an agreement between two runs' token-to-expert partitions.
Promotion requires: (a) DISCHARGED on verification — all three Disguise checks were run and none of the three papers contains a cross-run matched routing-agreement measurement, so novelty is Medium and no longer capped by an unread section; the only residual is arXiv:2607.28308 App. S6.3/S7.1, whose heading ("Matched-compute Top-1 versus Top-2") says what it holds and whose keyword sweeps returned nothing; (b) restating limb (iv) with k in the tens or dropping it, and declaring the top-1 or set-overlap reduction that makes ARI/NMI defined, restoring Well-posedness to 3/3; (c) adding a marginal-preserving null (expert-mass / token-frequency-preserving shuffle, or a run matched against a bootstrap of itself) so the headline cannot be manufactured by routing-mass concentration, and separating the unrelated-run null's two confounded factors; (d) recording arXiv:2401.12181 (Gurnee et al.), arXiv:2604.14419 and its companion arXiv:2604.14434 as named neighbours and re-grading with the cross-seed-universality vocabulary included. With (a) discharged, (b) is now the binding condition: it alone separates this entry from Validated.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): read the unread sections of arXiv:2604.14419 and its companion to settle whether limb (i) has already been measured at small scale; only if it has not, verify on FLAME-MoE's released 38M-1.7B ladder that OLMoE's saturation curve reproduces, then pre-register M, the reduction and the three nulls before launching seeds.

ID: UQ-20261017-07
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — pretraining data layer (model-based quality filtering) x architecture/recipe evaluation methodology. Method source: design of experiments (two-factor factorial, interaction variance components, replication). Source method: presupposition inversion ("a corpus is exogenous, so a comparison on a fixed corpus measures the architecture").

Question (canonical): For ONE fixed Common Crawl source pool re-filtered at a matched keep rate by T >= 2 quality classifiers whose positive labels come from different annotator ("teacher") models — chosen capability-matched across families so teacher IDENTITY is not confounded with teacher CAPABILITY — crossed with A >= 3 pre-declared architecture/recipe arms at matched FLOPs and matched token budget, with S >= 2 seeds per cell and one evaluation suite declared before any run: (i) how large is the teacher x arm interaction variance component relative to the within-cell seed variance (ratio with CI), and (ii) how many of the A(A-1)/2 pairwise architecture contrasts reverse SIGN between teachers at a pre-registered minimum effect size?

Alternative formulations:
1. Are published architecture comparisons corpus-conditional, because model-filtered corpora are selected to suit the annotator model that filtered them?
2. If one Common Crawl pool is re-filtered by two different annotator models at the same keep rate, do the two corpora preserve the same ordering of candidate model designs?
3. (lay) When a paper says "this model design is better", is it reporting a fact about the design or a fact about whichever AI graded its training data?
(Intake version, recorded: "does the measured ranking of architectures depend on which teacher produced the quality labels — is the teacher x architecture interaction distinguishable from seed noise?" One permitted Gate 1 reformulation used, to fix the estimand, the comparator, the effect-size band and the identity-vs-capability identification condition.)

Motivating gap: Standard open corpora since 2023-24 are built by classifiers traceable to named teachers — VERIFIED by reading arXiv:2412.02595 (FineWeb-Edu classifier "trained with annotations from Llama3"; DCLM a fastText classifier on OpenHermes-2.5 + ELI5 positives; Nemotron-CC's own labels from "annotations from Mistral 8x22B-instruct and Nemotron-340B-instruct", max-ensembled with DCLM's fastText). Every architecture comparison run on such a corpus is conditional on those teachers, a conditional no recipe paper states. The same paper shows the gap ("All experiments use the same 8B transformer configuration"; its classifier comparisons "vary only the filtered data"). The teacher-comparison literature holds architecture fixed; the architecture literature holds the corpus fixed. Gate 4 correction: the gap is narrower than the record claimed — the data-centric side does cross classifier variants with a model factor and seeds (DataDecide), and the architecture side does cross dense/MoE with data-side factors (arXiv:2609.11917). The uninstantiated factor is the architecture axis crossed with teacher identity, not the whole design.

Presuppositions:
P1. Major open corpora are model-filtered with identifiable teachers. ESTABLISHED by reading arXiv:2412.02595, but OVERSTATED as written (A3): of the three, only FineWeb-Edu has a single identifiable LLM teacher of per-document labels; DCLM's "teacher" is a positive set, Nemotron-CC's a three-scorer max-ensemble.
P2. Architecture rankings are measurable precisely enough for the interaction to clear seed noise at affordable scale. CONTESTED, load-bearing, unresolved. Against: DataDecide reports run-to-run SD "as high as 2% points" at 1B and that it is "difficult to distinguish evaluation variance from true crossovers"; arXiv:2604.20549 reports 0.3-0.8% shifts from the filter's own sampling seed alone. A2's df arithmetic: the exact 95% interval for the variance ratio spans ~285x at T=2/A=3/S=2 and still >10x at T=3/A=5/S=3 (45 matched-FLOP runs).
P3. Keep rate and token budget can be matched across teacher-filtered corpora. ESTABLISHED (threshold on a score; Nemotron-CC Table 9 keep shares 8%/11%/25%; DataDecide matches at 10%).
P4. There exists architecture/recipe variation the field acts on. ESTABLISHED.
P5. Teachers' notions of quality are at least partly idiosyncratic. WEAKENED. The 10.1% keep-set intersection (Nemotron-CC Table 8, 1,152,821/11,359,655 — the ledger's own arithmetic, re-reproduced by A2 and A3) is keep-rate confounded: with 8% and 25% shares the Jaccard ceiling is 0.32 (A2), and the three pipelines also differ in rubric and classifier family, so the figure does not evidence a teacher effect at a FIXED rubric and MATCHED keep rate. A3's query 5 found no inter-teacher agreement figure at fixed rubric in either direction.
P6. Comparison is FLOP-matched, not step-matched. DECLARED.
P7. Any interaction is attributable to teacher IDENTITY rather than capability. CONTESTED; capability is multidimensional, so matching on a declared suite leaves "identity" a residual category. Deployed teachers are capability-mismatched, so the design must commission teachers.
P8. A pre-registered minimum effect size for a "sign flip" is agreeable. CONTESTED by construction (with small true gaps, signs flip for free), which is why the reformulation requires a declared band.
New, from Gate 4 (A3): matched-FLOP arms need a pre-declared per-arm per-corpus tuning protocol, or teacher x arm is confounded with tuning x corpus. WEAKENED on verification: no source quantifies a corpus-induced optimal-LR shift, and the only direct evidence runs the other way — Step Law (arXiv:2503.04715) claims "The HP scaling law demonstrates statistical invariance across linguistic and structural changes in the dataset" and "strong invariance across dense and sparse (MoE) LLMs". Melis et al. 2018 did tune per corpus by black-box optimisation; Narang et al. 2021 deliberately held hyperparameters "constant for each architectural variant" and says only that "Not tuning hyperparameters handicapped other methods". Step Law is one transformers-only preprint and does not cover recurrent or state-space arms, so this is unevidenced rather than refuted.

What would count as an answer: A pre-registered factorial — 2-3 corpora filtered from one pool by different teachers at a matched keep rate, crossed with 3-5 arms at matched FLOPs and tokens, >= 2 seeds per cell, suite fixed in advance. Deliverables: (i) teacher x arm interaction with CI against within-cell seed variance; (ii) the count and identity of pairwise architecture contrasts flipping sign at the declared band; (iii) keep-set overlap between the teacher corpora, so the interaction is readable against how different the corpora were. A null inside the declared band licenses current practice with a number attached; a non-null means an architecture claim must name its corpus's annotator and that results across differently filtered corpora are not poolable. Nothing opened across the record or three adversary logs delivers (i), (ii) or (iii) on the architecture axis.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 38 distinct queries — 11 at Gate 2, plus 9 + 9 + 9 from three independent adversaries, all 27 in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use (NAS, proxy/data-pruning, CLIP self-preference, GxE/AMMI, reference-model perplexity, German, Chinese LM-data, LLM-judge self-bias, IR assessor effects, weak supervision, distillation, data-mixture laws, answer-side caveat hunts). Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-07-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
- "does the choice of quality filter change the ranking of architectures in language model pretraining" (mandatory own-field own-words title form) -> no paper on filter-identity x architecture ranking.
- "'Scaling Laws for Data Filtering' data curation cannot be compute agnostic" -> Goyal et al., arXiv:2404.07177: filter x COMPUTE interaction with an explicit reversal, architecture fixed at ViT-B/32.

- "knowledge distillation teacher identity determines best student architecture" (A2 q5) -> Liu et al., CVPR 2020: "no student architecture produces the best results across all teacher networks"; teacher-identity x architecture ranking asked and answered in distillation.

No architecture-axis flip count across differently filtered corpora exists.

COULD NOT READ, grading nothing: arXiv:2510.00866 Appendices D and F (heading only; defeated arxiv.org/html incl. an offset read, and the machinelearning.apple.com mirror); arXiv:2609.11917 Appendix B.1 seed sensitivity (page opened, appendix not served); arXiv:2605.23721; arXiv:2608.02705. No search or fetch call was refused in any of the four agents; Disguise was fully executed by all three adversaries (9/9, 9/9, 9/9), so Disguise is verified, not unverified.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): REORDERED at Gate 4; the record's own three are demoted.
P1'. Magnusson et al., "DataDecide", ICML 2025, arXiv:2504.11393 (OPENED by A1 and A3, re-opened twice at verification). Unit: pretraining runs over 25 recipes x 14 scales (4M-1B), seeds as replicates. Endpoint: downstream benchmark accuracy and decision accuracy. Comparator: run-to-run variance across seeds at 1B. Estimand: whether a small-scale recipe ranking predicts the large-scale one. CORRECTED on verification: the three named recipes exist in Table 1 but do not form the set claimed — QC Orig 10% and QC Tulu 10% share the Falcon+CC pool and a 10% rate yet differ in the classifier's TRAINING DATA (the original Li et al. 2024 filter against one retrained on pre-release Tulu-v3), while QC FW 10% sits on the DCLM-Baseline pool; the 25 recipes "differ in sources, deduplication, and filtering" at thresholds of 3%, 7%, 10% and 20%; the word "teacher" never appears and Table 1 gives no annotation provenance; and seeds are not 3 across the ladder — "All 1B (target size) models have 3 full reruns with different seeds, while other model sizes have second and third seed runs that are terminated early after 25% of the target compute budget." The 1,050-run figure was a summariser's arithmetic; the paper's own count is "more than 30K model checkpoints in total".
P2'. Liu et al., "Search to Distill: Pearls are Everywhere but not the Eyes", CVPR 2020 (OPENED by A2, openaccess.thecvf.com). Unit: 8 teachers x 5 student architectures from the MNAS space. Endpoint: student top-1. Comparator: none — single runs, no replicates or variance. Estimand: qualitative — "each teacher model could potentially have its own best student architecture"; Table 3 "different teachers have different best students".
P3'. Jha et al., "Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: MoEs Overfit More to Repeated Data", arXiv:2609.11917 (OPENED by A1, A2, A3 — the record's flagged unread lead). Unit: compute-matched dense vs MoE at 80M/200M/1B active. Endpoint: loss/accuracy under repetition R. Comparator: seed sensitivity relegated to Appendix B.1, not visible. Estimand: the repetition x sparsity interaction, with an explicit reversal "at R=32, where dense models outperform MoEs", plus a filter-SHARE x architecture statement.
Also graded on: Goyal et al. arXiv:2404.07177 (filter aggressiveness x compute, sign flip, architecture fixed); Nait Saada et al. arXiv:2510.00866 (HQ reference set x evaluation TASK, no model factor, no seeds); Su et al. arXiv:2412.02595 (teacher-filtered corpora head to head at one fixed 8B configuration); Clarke & Dietz arXiv:2412.17156 and WRENCH (NeurIPS D&B 2021) as the labeler-identity analogues.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1' (DataDecide): the crossed model factor is SIZE on a monotone ladder, not matched-FLOP architecture arms; no teacher x model interaction is estimated and no flip count on a model axis is reported. The claim that it falsifies two of the record's four "Not Low" grounds is WITHDRAWN on verification: no DataDecide subset matches keep rate across corpora differing in the annotating MODEL (Orig and Tulu differ in the classifier's training data; QC FW 10% is a different pool), and crossed-factor cells are seed-replicated only at the 1B target. What does stand is that the crossover-vs-variance problem the candidate poses is already named there, and that classifier provenance is varied at a fixed rate on a fixed pool — which is why attack 3 is Partial rather than Resolved.
vs P2' (Liu): the teacher supplies per-example training TARGETS, so the loss depends functionally on it; the candidate's teacher supplies only a binary keep decision over human text at a matched keep rate. Liu is vision/NAS, reports no statistic, no flip count and no replicates, and its teachers span 78.31-84.4 top-1, so it cannot separate identity from capability — the exact confound the reformulation exists to remove. The interaction class and its affirmative answer are nonetheless six years old and in print.
vs P3' (Jha): varies repetition and filter SHARE, never teacher identity; its seed comparison exists only as an unserved appendix. It establishes that a data-curation factor x architecture interaction with a sign flip is already published in LM pretraining, which is what triggers the record's own pre-committed downgrade.
vs the labeler-identity analogues (IR, weak supervision): IR's assessor effect is evaluation-side with training data fixed and its mechanism is judge bias; WRENCH's label models produce training targets, not a selection filter, and it never poses the end-model-ranking question.
vs the rank-instability genre: counts flips from evaluation-side nuisances with the corpus fixed; the candidate's nuisance sits upstream of training.

Significance — consequence: If YES (interaction outside seed noise with sign flips): "architecture X beats Y at this scale" is not well formed without naming the corpus's annotator; using FineWeb-Edu or DCLM-baseline as a neutral control becomes hidden conditioning; architecture results trained on differently filtered corpora are not poolable in meta-analyses or leaderboards; labs selecting an architecture by single-corpus ablation have been partly selecting for fit to an annotator. If NO (inside a pre-set band): current practice is licensed with the first published noise-floor figure for corpus-conditionality. Deflated at Gate 4: the non-null CLASS is already published (Goyal, Jha, Liu), so only the magnitude and the flip count are at stake, and the consequence chain leans on P5 and P1, both weakened above.

Significance — audience: (a) pretraining teams choosing architectures from single-corpus small-scale ablations (DCLM/FineWeb/Nemotron/OLMo/Marin) — would stratify ablations by teacher or report the conditioning; (b) corpus builders (HuggingFace, AI2, NVIDIA) — teacher provenance becomes a dataset-card field and a teacher-invariant construction becomes a validity device rather than a recall trick; (c) data-centric benchmark designers, whose premise is that fixing the model makes data comparable; (d) reviewers who accept a single-corpus ablation as evidence about an architecture. All three adversaries graded this Partial: the audiences are real and DataDecide proves actors at this scale invest in this decision class, but no evidence was produced that any of them would act differently for a factor isolated this narrowly. On verification the card claim is half right: FineWeb-Edu's dataset card does name its annotator ("using annotations generated by LLama3-70B-Instruct"), while DCLM-Baseline's names no model (only OpenHermes 2.5 and r/ExplainLikeImFive data) and Nemotron-CC's annotators are named in the paper rather than on its project page. Against the entry, arXiv:2504.08716v2 already argues that comparisons across models trained on different data "make it difficult to determine whether these gains are due to architectural improvements or differences in training data" and builds a matched-data comparison for that reason — so the corpus-conditionality problem is recognised in print and already answered by matching the corpus, leaving the candidate only its narrower claim that matching the corpus is not enough.

Significance — fecundity: Is the interaction predictable from keep-set overlap, so a cheap set statistic substitutes for a factorial? Does it shrink with scale (small-ablation pathology vs frontier problem)? Is there co-design — an optimal teacher per architecture class, making filter and architecture joint design variables? Can a teacher-invariant corpus be built, and what does training on the intersection cost? Does the same interaction appear in post-training and reward modelling, where the teacher is explicit? Methodologically: what per-cell replication makes an interaction of the observed size detectable (direct descendant of UQ-20261016-06/-49), and how is teacher identity decomposed into the corpus properties it induces?

Significance — anchoring: The standing anomaly that recipe and architecture gains fail to transfer between labs (Narang et al. 2021; Melis et al. 2018), currently diagnosed as under-tuned baselines. Goyal et al.'s compute-conditional curation result. DataDecide's crossover-vs-variance problem. The data-centric-benchmark premise of DataComp-LM. The evaluation-side rank-instability genre, which has never looked upstream of training. In the ledger: UQ-20261016-50, -53, -06/-49.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary, surviving only in narrowed form after Gate 4. The data-centric side fixes the model to make corpora comparable ("All experiments use the same 8B transformer configuration" is the protocol, not an oversight) and the architecture side fixes the corpus, so no venue owns the crossed cell — but A3 showed both sides do cross their own factor with the other's (DataDecide: classifier variants x 14 scales x 3 seeds; Jha: dense/MoE x data-side factors), so the convention explains only the architecture axis specifically. Cost compounds it: each side's publishable unit is T or A runs, the interaction needs T x A x S plus per-arm tuning. The factor is young: a nameable, re-runnable teacher dates from roughly 2023-24. A2's correction stands: the "new conceptual bridge" strand fails — the bridge is six years old and published (Liu et al. 2020), and the field asked the compute version within months (Goyal 2024), so cost explains why nobody ANSWERED, not why nobody ASKED, and A3's simpler alternative — a rational prior that teacher-at-fixed-rubric is a small factor — is a significance problem masquerading as a silence mechanism.

Verification (post-batch, five fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-07-verification.md, -verification-recipes.md, -verification-crossed.md, -verification-agreement.md, -verification-tuning.md, -verification-pooling.md): the only Unresolved attack rested on a mischaracterised prior and falls to Partial; the verdict does not move, because the Gate 5 condition that holds this at Provisional is a different one, which verification confirms.
**DataDecide is not what either the record or the adversary said it was.** Both described it as one source pool re-filtered by different teacher-derived classifiers at a matched 10% keep rate across 14 scales with 3 seeds, and A3 built its Unresolved attack-3 kill on that: that the candidate is the unrun cell of DataDecide's data axis crossed with arXiv:2609.11917's architecture axis. Two independent readers opened the paper. Table 1's 25 recipes "differ in sources, deduplication, and filtering", with thresholds at 3%, 7%, 10% and 20% and several recipes carrying no classifier filter. The three named recipes exist, but they do not form the set claimed: QC Orig 10% and QC Tulu 10% share the Falcon+CC pool and a 10% rate yet differ in the classifier's TRAINING DATA — "the original (Li et al., 2024) filter" against one "retrain[ed] ... on pre-release version of Tulu-v3 (Lambert et al., 2024)" — while QC FW 10% sits on a different pool (DCLM-Baseline). The word "teacher" does not appear in the paper and Table 1 gives no annotation provenance at all. Seeds are not 3 across the ladder: "All 1B (target size) models have 3 full reruns with different seeds, while other model sizes have second and third seed runs that are terminated early after 25% of the target compute budget." And the second parent is not a data-quality factorial: arXiv:2609.11917 crosses dense against MoE with data REPETITION (R from 1 to 1024), reporting "the catastrophic effect of data repetition leads to a reversal at R=32", with the data-side factor being scarcity, not filter identity.
So neither parent supplies the teacher axis, and the "unrun cell of two public factorials" kill is not sourceable. Per the ledger's rule that an adversary's claims are held to the same standard, **attack 3 drops from Unresolved to Partial**: the interface is less novel than the record's defence implied, since DataDecide does vary classifier provenance at a fixed rate on a fixed pool, but the candidate is not the cross-product of two existing designs. Consequently the entry's own concession that "two of the record's four stated 'Not Low' grounds are factually wrong" is **withdrawn**: no published design matches keep rate across corpora differing in the annotating model, and no design replicates crossed-factor cells across seeds except at DataDecide's 1B target. The record's P1' is corrected accordingly.
**A fourth independent novelty sweep found the conjunction nowhere.** Nine new queries, none refused, turned up no study crossing an upstream data-selection factor with a matched-FLOPs architecture factor and reporting an interaction effect or an architecture-axis flip count. Two neighbours the batch never named are added: arXiv:2502.12120 (Wiedemer et al.) varies corpus, tokenizer and architecture (Llama-3 417M against Mamba 420M) but one factor at a time, states no FLOP matching, reports no interaction statistic, and concludes that pretraining data determines the loss-to-loss trend while architecture has "limited impact"; and arXiv:2605.19407, a filter-aggressiveness x compute x size study whose abstract reports that "with enough compute, the best data filter is no data filter". Both are recorded as neighbours, and 2605.19407's full text is UNREAD, so an architecture axis inside it is not excluded.
**P5 stands as corrected, and the matched-rate figure exists nowhere.** Nemotron-CC's Table 8 numbers are confirmed — of 11,359,655 documents kept by either classifier, 1,152,821 (10.1%) are kept by both, "only 10% of the documents are predicted as high quality by both classifiers" — and the keep rates are confirmed unequal at 8% and 11%, so the entry's keep-rate confound correction is right. A further figure from the same paper's appendix is added: of each classifier's top 1,000 domains, "only 368 domains are in the intersection". No matched-keep-rate cross-filter overlap figure was found in anything that could be opened, with Zyda-2, arXiv:2510.00866 and arXiv:2512.24265 checked and a named list left unopened. That is a found-nothing, not a none-exists — and it is the point: deliverable (iii) is the instrument that would settle whether the factor is near-null by construction, and the adversaries' worry on that remains unevidenced in either direction.
**One Gate 4 presupposition is weakened and one significance leg loses its support.** The addition from A3 — that matched-FLOP arms need a per-arm per-corpus tuning protocol or teacher x arm is confounded with tuning x corpus — is not established by the literature and the only direct evidence points the other way: Step Law (arXiv:2503.04715) claims "The HP scaling law demonstrates statistical invariance across linguistic and structural changes in the dataset" and "strong invariance across dense and sparse (MoE) LLMs". Melis et al. 2018 tuned per corpus with black-box optimisation; Narang et al. 2021 deliberately "held constant" hyperparameters across variants and notes only that "Not tuning hyperparameters handicapped other methods". No source quantifies a corpus-induced optimal-LR shift, and Step Law is a single transformers-only preprint that does not cover recurrent or state-space arms, so the objection is downgraded to unevidenced rather than refuted. Against that, attack 6 gains the source it lacked: arXiv:2504.08716v2 already argues that comparisons across models trained on different data "make it difficult to determine whether these gains are due to architectural improvements or differences in training data" and builds a matched-data comparison for exactly that reason — the field does recognise the corpus-conditionality problem in print and already answers it by matching the corpus. The candidate's narrower claim, that matching the corpus is not enough because the annotator must be matched too, is untouched by it. The entry's assertion that cross-paper pooling of architecture conclusions is "real and unconditioned" is **struck as unsupported**: no survey, leaderboard or model card was opened that does it, and the one relevant document found conditions rather than pools. P1 is confirmed exactly as the batch corrected it — FineWeb-Edu's dataset card names "annotations generated by LLama3-70B-Instruct", DCLM-Baseline's names no model (only OpenHermes 2.5 and r/ExplainLikeImFive data), and the Nemotron-CC annotators (Mistral 8x22B-instruct, Nemotron-340B-instruct) are named in the paper and not on the project page.
**Why the verdict stays Provisional.** With attack 3 at Partial no attack is Unresolved, so the stated cap is gone. But Gate 5 requires for Validated "Novelty >= Medium **with the complete search record**", and the record is demonstrably incomplete and grew more so: arXiv:2510.00866 Appendices D and F, arXiv:2609.11917 Appendix B.1, arXiv:2605.23721, arXiv:2608.02705 and now arXiv:2605.19407's body are all unread, and 2605.19407 is the one whose abstract leaves an architecture axis possible. Gate 5 also names this entry's exact situation as the Provisional case — "Medium novelty with a close neighbor" — and there are now five close neighbours. So Provisional is where the rule puts it, independently of the refuted attack, and the promotion conditions are rewritten below.
Caveats recorded: every read in this pass went through the page summariser, which caps quoted strings near 125 characters; the DataDecide appendix was never served, so annotation provenance for its QC recipes is unestablished rather than absent; the Nemotron-CC Table 8 figures could not be re-fetched for a second check; and the crossed-design negative rests on nine queries with abstracts only for most hits.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness: estimand, comparator, effect-size band, matching conditions and the identity-vs-capability identification condition are all explicit and both versions recorded; the declared minimum design's imprecision is a power defect, not ill-posedness. Significance downgraded from the record's 3/3: consequence is argued in both branches and the audiences are real and named, but attack 6 is Partial in all three logs and the consequence chain leans on P1 and P5, both weakened at Gate 4.)

Strongest remaining objection (REPLACED on verification; the attack-3 objection it previously carried was refuted and regraded to Partial): the design cannot bound its own primary estimand. A2's degrees-of-freedom arithmetic, reproduced by bisection on the F CDF, gives an exact 95% interval for the variance-component ratio spanning about 285x at the declared minimum (2 teachers x 3 arms x 2 seeds) and still more than 10x at 3 x 5 x 3, which is 45 matched-FLOP pretraining runs — so limb (i) is close to uninformative at any affordable design, and the entry rests on limb (ii), the flip count, which is a weaker deliverable than the one the question leads with. Compounding it, deliverable (iii) is the instrument that would show whether there is anything to detect at all, and no matched-keep-rate cross-filter overlap figure exists in any source that could be opened; the one published overlap figure, Nemotron-CC's 10.1% intersection of the union, is confounded by unequal 8% and 11% keep rates, so whether two capability-matched same-rubric annotators produce measurably different corpora is unevidenced in either direction. Second, on significance: arXiv:2504.08716v2 shows the field already matches corpora when comparing architectures, so the candidate must carry the narrower claim that corpus matching is insufficient without annotator matching, and no instance of a survey, leaderboard or model card pooling architecture results across differently filtered corpora was found to anchor it.
Promotion requires (REWRITTEN; the DataDecide-based condition is void with the objection it served): (a) a matched-keep-rate keep-set overlap for two capability-matched same-rubric annotators — the figure that decides whether the factor is near-null by construction, which four independent sweeps have now failed to find in either direction, and which deliverable (iii) would supply for the first time; (b) a power statement showing the planned design can bound the variance ratio informatively against the 285x-at-minimum and >10x-at-3x5x3 arithmetic, or an explicit demotion of limb (i) to descriptive with limb (ii) as the primary; (c) the search record completed — arXiv:2605.19407's body (which may carry an architecture axis), arXiv:2510.00866 Appendices D and F, arXiv:2609.11917 Appendix B.1, arXiv:2605.23721 and arXiv:2608.02705 — since Gate 5 requires a complete record for Validated; and (d) one documented instance of architecture conclusions being pooled across differently filtered corpora as comparable, to anchor the significance claim the entry previously asserted without one. (d) is the cheapest and (a) the most decisive.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Before any pretraining run, measure the thing the design presupposes — take one fixed CC sample and one fixed quality rubric, have two capability-matched cross-family teachers label it, and report the keep-set overlap at a matched keep rate. That is deliverable (iii) alone, it is cheap, and it decides whether the factorial has anything to detect.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected; the question was not found posed. The neighbouring asked-and-partly-answered cells (filter x compute; recipe x scale; repetition x sparsity; distillation teacher x student architecture) are prior art, not routing targets.

ID: UQ-20261017-08
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — open-release artifact engineering and the data layer (method transplanted from federated-learning / DP privacy auditing)

Question (canonical): For open model releases that ship optimizer state alongside weights, how much more does an adversary learn about the final phase of training — document membership, presence of a data source, or reconstructable content — from (weights + Adam moment tensors) than from weights alone at matched attack strength, and what fraction of major open-weight releases ship that state?

Alternative formulations:
1. Are Adam first/second-moment tensors a disclosure channel, or does their EMA aggregation over millions of tokens destroy the signal gradient-inversion attacks exploit?
2. Does the reproducibility norm of releasing resumable checkpoints widen the attack surface of an open release relative to releasing weights alone?
(Gate 1 reformulation retained, one permitted, spent on pinning the comparator: limb (a) CENSUS over a pre-declared frame; limb (b) MEASUREMENT of delta = AUC(P | theta,m,v) - AUC(P | theta) under one fixed pipeline P with (m,v) ablated at identical compute/shadow-model/query budgets, plus delta(k) decay and stated power of the null. Full text in batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-08-record.md.)

Motivating gap: In FL and DP auditing, "what does the shared update disclose about the data?" is a routine question with a mature method family; in open-release engineering the shipped artifact increasingly includes optimizer state for resumability and nobody asks what it discloses beyond the weights. Two instruments that would own the fraction (Model Openness Framework arXiv:2403.13784 I.5; Foundation Model Transparency Index arXiv:2310.12941) have no such field, indicator or count.
Gate 5 corrections to the record's own picture, both sourced by adversaries:
- CENSUS UNDERCOUNT (strengthens the premise): the record knew only OLMo (by construction) and had LLM360/Amber as a declared negative. Adversary #1 and #3 found three further public shippers from primary READMEs — EleutherAI/gpt-neox "[Full weights] ... (Including optimizer states, 268GB)" (Feb 2022); EleutherAI/pythia "final-step checkpoints+optimizer states downloadable from the Hugging Face Hub"; bigscience/bloom-optimizer-states and bigscience/bloomz-optimizer-states (Megatron-DeepSpeed format).
- STRUCK: the record's two-timescale motivation ("v horizon ~1000 steps aggregating 1e9-1e10 tokens at beta2=0.999"). Adversary #3 read the configs: EleutherAI/pythia models/*.yml, gpt-neox configs/20B.yml and allenai/OLMo configs/peteish7-s3.yaml / peteish13-s3.yaml all use betas [0.9, 0.95], i.e. ~10 vs ~20 steps, not 10 vs 1000. The sharp asymmetry that motivated the "ship v, zero m" mitigation does not hold for any release the candidate leans on. The estimand and delta(k) are unaffected; the motivation and mitigation story are.

Presuppositions: P1 some major releases ship optimizer state — NOT assumed, it IS limb (a); now supported by four families (above), falsified for Amber. P2 Adam moments retain per-coordinate information about recent batches — established by the update rule. P3 canary-insertion auditing can be replicated in a purpose-built run — established. P4 "more than weights alone" needs a matched-strength weights-only arm — contested; the reformulation answers it. P5 decision-relevant in both directions — contested (see Gate 3 / attack 6). P6 measurement only on released artifacts and synthetic canaries — declared constraint. P7 released moments are coordinate-aligned with released weights — flagged as a census field, not assumed; live, since OLMo needs unshard.py and BLOOM's shipped state is ZeRO-sharded.

What would count as an answer: (i) a published fraction with the frame stated, per release: optimizer state yes/no, step granularity, format, licence, layout alignment; (ii) on at least one shipping release and on a purpose-built canary run, matched-strength membership / source-presence / reconstruction attacks with and without (m,v), reporting the signed AUC and fixed-FPR extraction-rate difference with CIs and the delta(k) decay. A credible null at stated power is an answer and settles the release-norm question permissively.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 Gate 2 web queries (the cap) + 4 free GitHub code searches + 3 failed curl routes; 26 further new-vocabulary queries across three adversaries (8 + 9 + 9), all logged. Most informative: "privacy leakage from released optimizer states Adam moments reveal training data" -> DP-training/DP-auditing only, nothing on inference from a released optimizer state; "fraction of open-weight model releases that publish optimizer state resumable checkpoints survey Hugging Face openness" -> MOF and FMTI, no census; "empirical study mining Hugging Face repositories files optimizer.pt how many models include" -> the HF-mining corpus (PeaTMOSS, reuse and versioning studies), no file-inventory statistic; "differential privacy releasing optimizer state post-processing momentum accountant leaks more" -> hidden-state/last-iterate DP asks about releasing ITERATES, never the state object; adversary sweeps in unlearning, Fisher-information, momentum-buffer, forensics/provenance, supply-chain-security, TDA/influence, FL stateful-optimizer (Mime/SCAFFOLD), practitioner-discourse, Chinese and Japanese vocabularies -> optimizer state appears as an unlearning tool, a defence ingredient, a DP-mechanism design object, an attribution input and a storage cost, never as the attacker's observable in a released artifact. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-08-record.md and UQ-20261017-08-adversary-{1,2,3}.md.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
NP1. Zanella-Beguelin et al., "Analyzing Information Leakage of Updates to Natural Language Models", ACM CCS 2020, arXiv:1912.07942 (opened, full text). Unit: a token sequence added in the update. Endpoint: differential score/rank. Comparator: single-snapshot analysis. Observable: two WEIGHT snapshots, black-box.
NP2. Wan, Fang, Ma, Wang, "Gradient Inversion Attacks Beyond SGD", ICML 2026, https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/64051 (venue page opened; FULL TEXT COULD NOT READ). Routes that failed across four agents: arXiv API (DNS), arxiv.org/search (proxy 403, then ROBOTS_DISALLOWED), openreview.net/forum?id=RNDJpm1kUW (verification interstitial), openreview.net/pdf?id=RNDJpm1kUW (client error), ICML page (no PDF link).
NP3. Michel, Basu, Kaufmann, "Sequential Membership Inference Attacks", arXiv:2602.16596v2 (abs page opened and confirmed by adversary #3). Unit: the insertion step of a canary. Endpoint: a step-localised insertion test. Comparator: snapshot-independent baselines. Observable: a sequence of models, white-box gradients or black-box loss; no optimizer state.
Census-limb negatives opened: MOF arXiv:2403.13784 (optimizer state only parenthetical in I.5 / Sec. 5.16; no count, no disclosure analysis); FMTI arXiv:2310.12941 (no indicator); the largest HF security scan opened by adversary #2, arXiv:2410.04490 (4,023 of 555,755 repos), enumerates serialized model files by extension and reports no optimizer-state file statistic.
Further neighbours surfaced by adversaries, none posing the question: arXiv:2605.18814 (AdamW-influence consumes {m_t,v_t} as per-step caches recorded during training, explicitly no privacy framing); arXiv:2604.23046 (second-order optimizer state retains residual information after unlearning; qualitative, no adversary); arXiv:2509.14223 (training-order recency linearly encoded in ACTIVATIONS — a weights-only recency prior the record missed, which raises the bar for the matched baseline).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs NP1, same structure ("an artifact pair discloses more than one artifact") but the second channel is the stored optimizer state at ONE checkpoint rather than a second weights snapshot, with a different decay law and a census limb NP1 has no analogue of. vs NP2, the closest METHOD prior: NP2's observable is an update the attacker must invert, in a small-batch image FL round; the candidate's is the stored (m,v) of a public artifact aggregating ~2e7 tokens, with membership/source-presence/text-extraction endpoints and a matched-compute weights-only arm an inversion paper has no reason to run — but because NP2's full text is unread, that NP2 contains no released-checkpoint stored-moment experiment is UNVERIFIED, and this is what caps the grade. vs NP3, NP3 pre-empts the shape of the recency sub-question but its information source is the model sequence, not the moments; the candidate's delta holds the checkpoint fixed and varies only (m,v). vs MOF/FMTI/2410.04490: these are the instruments that would own the fraction and none has computed it.

Novelty confidence: Medium
(11 Gate 2 queries plus 26 adversary new-vocabulary queries, so not Unverified; no opened source in either literature treats released moment tensors as the disclosure channel, defines the weights-only matched baseline, or reports the publication fraction. Not High because NP2 sits directly on alternative formulation 1 and its full text defeated five routes across four agents, and NP3 sits on the recency-decay structure. Not Low because no near-duplicate was found in any of 37 documented queries, and nothing opened is a rename of this question.)

Significance — consequence: a positive, non-trivial delta puts resumability and disclosure in direct tension at the artifact level, with cheap specific mitigations (withhold or zero m, coarsen the step offset, publish state at a lag); a credible null at stated power removes a speculative privacy objection to the strongest form of open release. Note the Gate 5 correction: with betas [0.9, 0.95] in the actual releases, the "withhold m, ship v" mitigation loses the clean 10-vs-1000-step asymmetry the record claimed for it, so the mitigation space is narrower than argued.
Significance — audience: open-release engineering teams that ship resumable state (AI2/OLMo at ~1000-step granularity; EleutherAI for gpt-neox and Pythia final-step; BigScience for BLOOM/BLOOMZ) and hub-side policy; openness-framework authors (MOF I.5 has the component with no disclosure guidance, FMTI has no indicator); privacy auditors, who gain a white-box threat model strictly between weights-only and full trajectory that exists in the wild. This is the weak limb: all three adversaries graded attack 6 Partial, and adversary #3 showed from primary sources that every verified shipper also publishes its training data (and Pythia's README guarantees "preservation of the data order seen by the Pythia models"), while EleutherAI's stated reason for not serving state at all steps is "size ... and anticipated lower demand", not privacy. No opened source shows a release team or framework author asking for this.
Significance — fecundity: data-order and curriculum recovery; unlearning- and removal-compliance verification; whether publishing (m,v) voids hidden-state/last-iterate DP accounting (arXiv:2405.14457); whether a sanitisation of (m,v) preserves resumption while provably destroying per-coordinate recency; the same question for structurally richer optimizer state (second-order, orthogonalised-momentum).
Significance — anchoring: hidden-state DP accounting and the last-iterate question (arXiv:2405.14457, 2410.06186); the gradient-inversion family's open question of what survives aggregation (NP2, survey arXiv:2206.07284); MOF I.5's unresolved "(when applicable)"; what "open-weight" release means in artifact terms. Amber's inability to save optimizer state is reported as a reproducibility failure with no suggestion it was a disclosure mitigation.

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary with a mismatched threat model on each side, plus an incentive gradient. The method-owning communities (FL privacy, gradient inversion, DP auditing, unlearning, TDA) demonstrably know the object carries information — they decouple it, entangle it, privatise it, and feed {m_t,v_t} into attribution — but each frames it as in-transit, in-training or in-accounting, never as a published object; the artifact-owning side frames it as storage cost and demand (Pythia README) or reproducibility (Amber), and has no field in which the gap could be stated (MOF, FMTI). Adversary #2 searched specifically for dismissive folklore ("aggregation obviously destroys it") and found none, so "asked and dismissed informally" is unevidenced. Gate 5 correction, from adversary #3: the record's claim that the object "only became common with the ~2023-onward full-openness releases" is FALSE — gpt-neox shipped optimizer states in Feb 2022 and BLOOM in 2022, and Pythia, the standard substrate of LLM membership-inference work, has had them on the Hub throughout. The object has sat in front of the method-owning community for 3-4 years, which weakens the artifact-novelty leg of the mechanism and leaves the boundary and incentive legs doing the work.

Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers plus a direct read, logs UQ-20261017-08-verification.md and -verification-np2.md): NP2 is still unread, but its abstract has now been read three times independently and it excludes the released-checkpoint framing at abstract level. The verdict does not move; the cap narrows from "the one thing that would make this a disguised known is unverified" to a residual confined to the paper's body.
**What the abstract settles.** "Gradient Inversion Attacks Beyond SGD" (Wan, Fang, Ma & Wang; ICML 2026 poster 64051; OpenReview RNDJpm1kUW) frames its threat as federated learning in which an adaptive optimizer is used, so that "the observable signal is not raw gradients but momentum-based parameter updates" — updates exchanged during training and seen by a server or eavesdropper, not tensors read out of a published checkpoint. Its contributions are an analytical label-recovery rule from those updates and an update-matching objective over dummy inputs, said to strengthen plain-SGD attacks as well. Experiments are on "datasets such as ImageNet and PACS", both image datasets; no text or language-model experiment appears in the abstract. A keyword sweep of the abstract on a third read returns ABSENT for every one of checkpoint, released, published, optimizer state, moment (as a word), second moment, m_t and v_t.
That bears directly on the entry's strongest objection. NP2's observable is a sequence of updates during training; the candidate's is a single released checkpoint's stored first and second moment buffers, with a weights-only arm at matched attack strength. NP2's regime is small-batch image reconstruction; the candidate's is an un-noised EMA over ~2e6-token text batches with membership and source-presence endpoints. On the abstract, NP2 is a neighbour in the FL gradient-leakage line rather than the candidate's question in other words.
**What stays Unverified.** The body was never served. Ten distinct routes failed across seven agents and a direct attempt: the OpenReview forum and a second forum id found under the same title (uLdGZhxlxV) both return a bot-verification wall; openreview.net/pdf?id=RNDJpm1kUW, the OpenReview API and the Semantic Scholar API all return fetch errors; no arXiv identifier exists for it after five searches; proceedings.mlr.press carries no copy that two extended searches could surface; the first author's page (horseee.github.io) lists no entry for it. So a released-checkpoint stored-moment experiment inside the body is not excluded, only made unlikely. Per the ledger's own rule this is Unverified, not Unresolved: it blocks Validated and names the promotion condition, and it does not reject.
**Net effect.** Promotion condition (i) is narrowed but not discharged — what remains is reading the body, not establishing the paper's object, which the abstract now gives three times over. Novelty moves up within Medium. Conditions (ii) and (iii) are untouched, and (iii) — the audience limb, where every verified shipper also publishes its training data and the decision-relevant population of releases that ship state while withholding data has no verified present instance — remains what actually holds this at Provisional rather than Validated. The struck beta2 = 0.999 premise and the corrected census stand as the batch recorded them.
Caveat recorded: all three abstract reads went through the page summariser, which caps quoted text near 125 characters, so the sentences above are its wording rather than verbatim transcription; the "such as" in the dataset sentence leaves open that the body uses datasets the abstract does not name.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 3/3: both limbs have a stated frame, a stated estimand and a comparator that ablates one input within a fixed pipeline at matched compute; the null is specified with a power requirement; the struck beta2 premise and the undercounted census change the motivation and the mitigation, not what is being asked or how it would be settled. Significance 2/3 after the adversaries, not downgraded to 1/3: consequence, fecundity and anchoring hold on opened sources (MOF I.5's empty component, hidden-state DP accounting, the aggregation question), while the audience limb is the one that fails — for the verified shipper population the extra disclosure is of already-public data, and the decision-relevant population (state shipped, data withheld) has no verified present instance. The question therefore clears Gate 3 but does so on prospective rather than present decision relevance.

Strongest remaining objection (NARROWED on verification; the two legs have swapped weight): for every release verifiably shipping Adam state the training data and, for Pythia, its exact order are already public, so a positive delta may measure a channel whose content nobody needs protected — the one objection all three adversaries graded Partial unanimously, and the one verification could not repair. The NP2 leg behind it is much weaker than the batch recorded: its full text is still unread after ten routes across seven agents, so a released-checkpoint stored-moment experiment in its body is not formally excluded, but three independent reads of its abstract put the observable at updates exchanged during federated training ("the observable signal is not raw gradients but momentum-based parameter updates"), the experiments on "datasets such as ImageNet and PACS", and every one of checkpoint, released, published, optimizer state, moment, second moment, m_t and v_t absent from the abstract.
Promotion requires: (i) NARROWED — NP2's object is now established at abstract level three times over, so what remains is reading its body for a released-checkpoint stored-moment experiment the abstract does not mention; the routes still untried are proceedings.mlr.press once ICML 2026 posts it, a HuggingFace-papers copy, and the pages of Gongfan Fang and Xinchao Wang (OpenReview returns a bot wall on both forum ids, its PDF and API return fetch errors, Semantic Scholar's API errors, no arXiv id exists after eight searches, and the first author's page lists no entry); (ii) object-level confirmation of one downloadable, weight-aligned optimizer-state artifact for a major release (an HTTP GET/HEAD on an OLMo step*-unsharded/optim.pt or a Pythia neox-ckpt optimizer file from an unblocked route), since the only instances inspectable so far are a declared negative (Amber) and a repo whose maintainer could not locate its states (bloom-560m); and (iii) either verification of one release that ships optimizer state while withholding training data or data order (BLOOM/ROOTS is the candidate), or re-posing the significance case explicitly as prospective norm-setting with the audience named accordingly. All three met in full would lift this to Validated; (i) alone lifts novelty toward High but does not by itself repair the audience limb, and (iii) is now the binding condition.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): fix and pre-register the census frame, then run the file-inventory limb over it — the one cheap, uncontested limb — recording per release: optimizer-state present y/n, step granularity, format and sharding, licence, and whether coordinates are weight-aligned without a reconstruction step. Do not begin limb (b) before the census says whether the shipper population includes any release that withholds its training data.

Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — agent scaffold design and evaluation methodology. Neighbours searched: quality-cost accounting (COPQ, scrap/rework), serving goodput, process mining (rework/self-loop metrics), context pruning, causal attribution.
Question (canonical): In publicly released agent-benchmark run traces carrying per-LLM-call usage fields (HAL, `agent-evals/hal_traces`), under a rework rule pre-declared and validated against hand coding — rework defined by counterfactual non-use (removal from every later step's context would not change any later action) rather than "no later step reads it" — (i) what share of consumed tokens and recomputed dollars is rework, reported separately for solved and unsolved runs; (ii) on the cells HAL actually identifies (generalist-vs-benchmark-specific scaffold within benchmark for one model, ~24 model comparisons; BrowserUse-vs-SeeAct on Online Mind2Web), how much of the variance in the rework share sits with scaffold, model and task, with CIs; and (iii) does re-ranking cost-effectiveness by net-of-rework cost reorder the published ordering BEYOND the reordering total-cost-aware scoring already produces (SWE-Effi, arXiv:2509.09853)? (Gate 1 reformulation, the one permitted; Gate 0 original and rationale in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) What is an agent run's scrap-and-rework rate in the sense of manufacturing quality accounting, and does the harness or the model own it? (2) If leaderboards reported useful tokens rather than total tokens, would the cost-effectiveness ordering change by more than total-token-budget scoring already changes it?
Motivating gap: New-instrument question. Instrument verified (HAL, arXiv:2510.11977, 21,730 rollouts, ~$40k, 2.5B tokens of logs released); HAL runs no waste/rework category in its log-inspection taxonomy and never mentions useful-vs-total tokens. Partly falsified at Gate 2 and load-bearing: HAL is a PARTIAL grid (most benchmarks run one scaffold), and the intake's motivating anomaly — same-model cost-per-solved-task spread between scaffolds — is not in HAL (its ~9x headline is between models). Full accounting in batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-09-record.md.
Presuppositions: P1 per-call usage fields on the release — UNVERIFIED at Gate 2, then SUPPORTED at Gate 4 from five third-party parsers (`summary.usage`, `output.usage.{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}`, `inputs.model`, `weave_task_id`), with the pitfall that the turn stream is double-logged (litellm wrapper over openai leaf), so naive sums double-count. P2 "discarded" definable without reading intent — CONTESTED; counterfactual non-use needs replay, and action-invariance under stochastic decoding is left undefined. P3 the release supports a three-facet decomposition — LARGELY FALSE as posed; scaffold is mostly nested in benchmark, hence the restriction in the reformulation. P4 published orderings are close enough to reorder — ESTABLISHED, and it cuts against novelty (SWE-Effi separates pairs tied at 28.0% resolve to 17.3% vs 26.8% EuTB). P5 run-time prices recoverable — only approximately: hal-harness carries a harness-time `MODEL_PRICES_DICT` (~190 keys) and silently skips absent models. P6 rework is not simply necessary search — CONTESTED (Agentless's many patches are deliberate redundancy).
What would count as an answer: (i) a pre-declared rework measure applied to the released traces with inter-rater agreement against hand-coded steps, share split solved/unsolved; (ii) a variance decomposition with CIs on the identified cells, naming the unidentified facets; (iii) rank changes under net-of-rework cost reported as an increment over the published total-cost-aware ordering. A null (share roughly constant, so net-of-rework is a monotone rescaling of total cost) answers it; so does a measure-dependence failure, negatively.

Significance — consequence: if the rework share is large and scaffold-owned, a leaderboard's cost column is partly a measurement of harness retry and compaction policy, and operators would report decomposed cost while scaffold designers would get a target total cost hides (it conflates deliberate redundancy that works with loops that do not). If the share is roughly constant, total cost is a sufficient statistic and current reporting needs no change. Deflation the record concedes: a buyer pays total cost, so the reordering is diagnostic, not transactional.
Significance — audience: scaffold/framework designers (retry, compaction, branch pruning); leaderboard operators (HAL already publishes accuracy-vs-cost frontiers; 2605.23950 shows the community acts on reporting-surface findings); serving-capacity planners, for whom discarded tokens are still served tokens; procurement only if the share varies with a harness they can change. Real, but already served by working waste targets (anti-patterns, no-action turns, pruning ratios).
Significance — fecundity: whether the rework share is a controllable scaffold parameter with an accuracy frontier; whether early rework share beats existing failure triage (2606.01365 gives the comparator); whether the share scales with model capability as a cheap competence proxy; whether serving should schedule by predicted goodput; whether benchmark design induces rework.
Significance — anchoring: cost-controlled evaluation (SWE-Effi; "AI Agents That Matter", unopened); harness-vs-model attribution (2607.22585, 2609.11987, 2605.23950); failure-aware observability (2606.01365); process-mining rework metrics (2512.02393, companion tool 2608.17195); context pruning (Squeez 2604.04979, SWE-Pruner Pro 2607.18213); serving goodput. In-ledger: UQ-20261016-06 shares the corpus type only (residual run-to-run variance in success); INDEX.md checked in full, no near-duplicate.
Reason for silence: no credible mechanism survives. (i) Measurement-rule resistance explains why the field reached for heuristic and outcome-preserving rules, not why nobody asked — and it did ask, with those rules (AgentDiet, context pruning). (ii) Disciplinary boundary is falsified: process-centric loop and anti-pattern analysis is in print in the field's own vocabulary (2512.02393 plus companion tool). The narrow residual silence the record claimed — nobody has partitioned the cost of SOLVED runs — is contradicted by 2512.02393's own statement about resolved instances. Only "new data (HAL, Oct 2025)" remains, and new data offers a new place to repeat a measurement, not a reason for silence. Per Gate 4 rule 7, this sends the novelty finding itself back to Gate 2, which is where the Low grade lands.

Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-09-verification.md, -verification-waste.md, -verification-counterfactual.md): the disguised-known ground is withdrawn — neither cited paper does what the kill said — and the entry is Rejected again, on a sourced presupposition failure that the batch's single adversary never reached. The verdict does not move; its whole basis does.
**The original kill does not stand.** A checker opened both papers. arXiv:2512.02393 (Liu et al., "Process-Centric Analysis of Agentic Software Systems") does build Graphectory graphs over 4,000 trajectories (500 SWE-bench Verified issues x 8 agent-model pairs) and its solved-run sentence is verbatim — "An important observation is that inefficiencies, although to a lesser extent, are prevalent in resolved instances as well." But its measures are counts of ACTIONS: Loop Count is the "Number of times the agent decides to repeat a previously executed action", Average Loop Length "The average number of actions involved before an agent decides to repeat". It defines no single inefficiency rate, its anti-patterns are prevalence percentages over trajectories, and **the words token, tokens, dollar and waste do not appear in it**. arXiv:2607.22585 (Vats & Golev) reports tokens — not dollars — per solved task across 2 models x 3 harnesses on 50 tasks, with 95% paired-task bootstrap CIs, amortised as "the cell-wide sum of tokens_total divided by the cell's solved count" with "Failed and infrastructure-error trials ... included in the numerator"; it is a descriptive side-by-side, not a variance decomposition, and it presents no re-ranking, only a recommendation "that coding-agent leaderboards adopt harness-model pairs as the unit of evaluation". Asked directly whether either reports the fraction of token or dollar spend that was discarded rework, and whether either re-ranks a leaderboard net of rework, the checker answered NO to both for both. So the attack-2 Unresolved is not sourceable and **falls to Partial**, and the Gate 2 regrade to Low that rested on it is withdrawn; novelty returns to Medium.
**The region is nonetheless much more crowded than the entry knew.** A second sweep of nine queries in cost, observability and context-engineering vocabularies found four 2026 papers the batch never surfaced, each nearer than the two it killed on. arXiv:2509.23586 (Trajectory Reduction, Trae Agent) says waste is "widespread in almost all trajectories" from a manual review of 100, gives a worked case where "the waste costs 1714 tokens out of 1995 tokens", and reports that its reflection module "removes 69.2%-77.4% of the content it processes", cutting input tokens 39.9-59.7% and net cost 21.1-35.9%. arXiv:2607.12161 (Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction) bounds an addressable cost share at about 4% conservative, 12% central and 25-30% upper, and reports an unattributed billing residual of 8.7% [7.2, 10.1] which it does not call waste. arXiv:2608.01347 (Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents) defines waste operationally — a paired median reasoning ratio above 1.5 with a CI lower bound above 1.1 and no success gain — and reports about 1.9x median cost for runs carrying one unused branch. arXiv:2604.22750 reports that "around 50% of them are repeated actions on the same file" for three models. None is the candidate's estimand: removal rates by an LLM judge, scenario bounds, prompt-variant ratios and action shares are each a different quantity from the share of a run's consumed tokens that is rework under a counterfactual rule, and none re-ranks a leaderboard net of rework. But the candidate is no longer sitting in an empty region, and arXiv:2606.01365 ("Early Diagnosis of Wasted Computation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems") could not be opened within budget and is recorded as UNVERIFIED — a live Disguise risk, not a resolved one.
**The new rejection ground: the rework rule names no well-defined quantity on the instrument the question proposes.** The canonical question deliberately replaced the decidable rule ("no later step reads it") with counterfactual non-use — removal from every later step's context would not change any later action — and proposes to apply it to released HAL traces. Both halves of that fail against opened sources. First, the counterfactual is not decidable from a recorded trace: every published step-attribution method obtains it by re-executing the agent. Causal Agent Replay (arXiv:2606.08275) "re-executes the trajectory forward under the same stochastic policy" with K forward rollouts per intervention and Shapley coalitions exponential in the worst case; CausalFlow (arXiv:2605.25338) replaces each candidate step with K=3 proposals and recomputes downstream steps; Credit Without Ground Truth (arXiv:2608.19760) audits credit signals against executed-replay ground truth. Second, and worse, the rule's predicate is almost never literally true even with nothing removed. "On Randomness in Agentic Evals" (arXiv:2602.07150, ICLR 2026, about 60,000 SWE-Bench-Verified trajectories, 10 runs per configuration) finds that single-run pass@1 estimates "vary by 2.2 to 6.0 percentage points depending on which run is selected", with SDs above 1.5 points at temperature 0 (Devstral-2/r2e-gym 35.4% +/- 1.7, range 32.0-37.8), and that trajectories diverge within tens of tokens at temperature 0 — median first divergence at token 56 for DeepSWE-preview and token 32 for Qwen3-32B, with two temperature-0 runs on django-9296 matching for 93 tokens, diverging at token 94, and ending in opposite outcomes. So an ablated re-run shows changed later actions whatever the removed step contributed, and the rule's yes/no has no fixed value unless the continuation is deterministic. Credit Without Ground Truth adds that the replay target is undefined at 13.1%-26.8% of decision points across two policies and that only 30.5% of points with defined ground truth show a nonzero replay contrast at achievable resolution.
That is a presupposition failure on attack 4 — the question needs counterfactual non-use to be determinable from the released traces it names, and it is not — compounded by vagueness and dissolution on attacks 5 and 8: the quantity becomes well defined only if restated as a distributional contrast against a noise floor, estimated from K rollouts per arm with a stated equivalence margin, or under a fixed-seed local model where replay is exact. Every one of those requires re-executing the agent, which the released-trace instrument cannot do, and none of the three published methods implements removal from later context, the exact intervention the rule names. **Unresolved on attack 4 is fatal, so the Rejection stands on that ground alone**, with Low-to-Medium novelty no longer load-bearing and well-posedness 2/3 independently barring Validated as the batch already recorded.
**Not routed**, and the ground for that changes too. The earlier reason — a disguised-known rejection is not routable — is withdrawn with the kill. The operative reason is now routing rule (f): a question the ledger's own Gate 4 has shown to be non-identifiable on the data it names is not routable. Recorded for a successor candidate rather than routed: the decidable version ("what share of consumed tokens went to steps whose output no later step reads"), which is computable from released traces and which the Gate 1 reformulation discarded; and arXiv:2607.12161's unattributed 8.7% [7.2, 10.1] billing residual, which looks like a posed-and-open question but whose posing sentence was not read at first hand, so under the routing test it is not written as a row.
Caveats recorded: all three checkers read through the page summariser; arXiv:2512.02393's per-pair figures sit in figures that could not be read; arXiv:2607.22585's Table 2 and Table 4 solved counts appear mutually inconsistent (Goose/Qwen 46% against 48%); the waste sweep is a negative over five opened sources, not over the literature, with arXiv:2606.01365 and the leaderboard candidates unread; and the counterfactual sweep left arXiv:2609.06445, arXiv:2606.08998, arXiv:2608.14711 and AgenTracer unopened.

Scores: Well-posedness 1/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness reduced from 2/3 on verification: the batch scored it 2/3 for an unstated rater-agreement threshold and an open leniency band, which are repairable by pre-registration. What verification established is worse and not repairable within the design — the primary estimand's defining predicate has no fixed value on the data the question names, so the frame and the comparator are stated but the estimand is not evaluable. Significance 2/3 is unchanged and is no longer load-bearing.)
Strongest remaining objection (REPLACED on verification; the disguised-known objection is withdrawn with the kill that rested on it): the pre-declared rework rule names no well-defined quantity on the instrument the question proposes. The Gate 1 reformulation deliberately replaced the decidable rule ("no later step reads it") with counterfactual non-use — removal from every later step's context would not change any later action — and proposes to apply it to released HAL traces. Both halves fail against opened sources. The counterfactual is not decidable from a recorded trace: Causal Agent Replay (arXiv:2606.08275) "re-executes the trajectory forward under the same stochastic policy", CausalFlow (arXiv:2605.25338) replaces each candidate step with K=3 proposals and recomputes downstream steps, and Credit Without Ground Truth (arXiv:2608.19760) audits credit signals against executed-replay ground truth — and none of the three implements removal from later context, the exact intervention the rule names. Worse, the predicate is false in the baseline: "On Randomness in Agentic Evals" (arXiv:2602.07150, ICLR 2026) finds single-run pass@1 varying "by 2.2 to 6.0 percentage points depending on which run is selected" with SDs above 1.5 points at temperature 0, and trajectories diverging at median token 56 and token 32 for two models, with a temperature-0 pair on django-9296 matching for 93 tokens then ending in opposite outcomes. So an ablated re-run shows changed later actions whatever the removed step contributed, and the rule's yes/no has no fixed value unless the continuation is deterministic. That is a presupposition failure on attack 4, which is fatal, with attacks 5 and 8 Unresolved alongside it.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable to this verdict. Recorded for whoever reopens it: the rule must be restated before the data is touched — either as the decidable "no later step reads it" version, which the released traces can answer and which this reformulation discarded, or as a distributional contrast estimated from K rollouts per arm against a resampled-but-unablated noise floor, which needs a re-executable agent rather than a trace archive. Only then do the HAL mechanics matter: one `agent-evals/hal_traces` shard's schema, the count of (model, benchmark) cells holding two or more scaffolds, and de-duplication of the double-logged litellm/openai turn stream before summing usage.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed, on a different ground than the batch gave. The disguised-known characterisation is WITHDRAWN on verification — neither cited paper reports a wasted token or dollar share or re-ranks net of rework — and with it the Gate 2 regrade to Low, so novelty returns to Medium. The operative reason is routing rule (f): a question the ledger's own Gate 4 has shown to be non-identifiable on the data it names is not routable. Recorded for a successor candidate rather than routed: the decidable share ("what fraction of consumed tokens went to steps whose output no later step reads"), computable from the released traces and discarded by the Gate 1 reformulation; and arXiv:2607.12161's unattributed billing residual of 8.7% [7.2, 10.1], which looks posed-and-open but whose posing sentence was not read at first hand, so the routing test keeps it out of the file. Procedural notes: one adversary ran and its Disguise sweep was executed (8 new-vocabulary queries, 4 hits opened); verification added 14 queries across three checkers. The fatal ground is an Unresolved attack 4, with attacks 5, 7 and 8 Unresolved alongside it. Well-posedness 2/3 would independently have barred Validated.
