ID: UQ-20261017-13
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — spatial transcriptomics / tissue genomics (target field, whose literature decides novelty); method transplanted from geography/geostatistics (MAUP, change of support). Neighbours checked: landscape ecology, spatial econometrics, image analysis, signal processing.
Question (canonical): For a pre-declared set of Visium HD / Stereo-seq datasets re-binned to a ladder of square supports, and for outputs well defined on an arbitrary areal support (SVG rank list; spatial-domain partition at fixed k), (a) what is the variance decomposition of each output into a tissue-identity component and an aggregation-support component, estimated against a within-support resampling noise floor, and (b) does a support s* exist above which the support component falls below that floor by a criterion declared before any data are pulled? (Gate 1 reformulation, carried forward; the intake version asked how much of spatial-transcriptomics output is determined by bin size/segmentation unit rather than by the tissue. Segmentation-based pipelines and cell-level cell-cell communication are quarantined as a separate limb, since they presuppose cells.)
Alternative formulations: Do spatial-transcriptomics conclusions survive a change of support, in the sense geostatistics means it? / What is the modifiable-areal-unit sensitivity of published spatial-omics analyses, and can a support-stability criterion be defined for them?
Motivating gap: The aggregation unit became a free user parameter only in 2024 (Visium HD 2 um bins, 8 um recommended, 16 um common; OSTA publishes parallel "binned" and "segmented" workflows), while the downstream stack — SVG tests, domain detection, ligand-receptor scoring — was inherited from the fixed-support era and takes the support as given. Gate 2 destroyed the conceptual half of this gap: the gap is real empirically and false conceptually, because the question is posed in print by name, and the 2024 posing itself says the answer is "completely unknown and ignored".
Presuppositions: (1) Re-binning stands in for capture at that support [CONTESTED — real coarse capture also changes sensitivity/diffusion, so any measurement is a LOWER BOUND]. (2) Outputs well defined at every support [CONTESTED; acted on at Gate 1 by splitting the segmentation limb]. (3) Stability definable without ground truth via a within-support resampling floor [CONTESTED, load-bearing; the owning field already has a formal instrument, S-maup, PLOS ONE 2018]. (4) A non-trivial body of published conclusions rests on a default support [UNESTABLISHED — a limb, not shown]. (5) MAUP not already imported into this field [CHECKED AND FALSE — imported under its own name]. (6) Tissue has a characteristic length scale [CONTESTED but harmless].
What would count as an answer: A support-output curve with a resampling noise band over the pre-declared datasets/methods/outputs, yielding either (i) a support or range above which outputs are stable by the declared criterion — a number usable as a reporting standard — or (ii) a demonstration that outputs keep moving across the whole accessible range, making support part of the result and cross-support comparison unlicensed. Both branches substantive.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 documented searches (11 Gate 2, cap 11; 9 adversary, all in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use) plus 9 fetches. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-13-record.md and UQ-20261017-13-adversary-1.md. Most informative: "modifiable areal unit problem spatial transcriptomics aggregation" → DECISIVE; top hit Cell 2023 "Mapping the transcriptome", plus AGILE-GISS 2024 "Lessons from spatial transcriptomics and computational geography" — MAUP already attached to this field by name. "bin size affects spatially variable gene detection and spatial domain identification in Visium HD" (own-field, own-words title form) → no support-dependence paper, only vendor/tutorial material. "fraction of spatially variable genes change with bin size ... quantified" (mandatory fraction query) → the quantity has NOT been published; four SVG benchmarks all at fixed support. "robustness of spatial domain clustering to re-binning Stereo-seq bin20 bin50 bin100 ARI" → no re-binning concordance study; comparators are methods, platforms, organs. Adversary S7/S9 (grain-extent and Nyquist/signal-processing vocabularies) → arXiv 2602.02825, which contains an incidental 8-vs-16 um Visium HD cross-resolution SVG comparison. Adversary S1/S2/S5/S6/S8 (change-of-support, coarse-graining, ecological fallacy, Chinese, image downsampling) → no renamed duplicate in any of them.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) Comber, Zormpas, Queen & Cockell 2024, "Lessons from spatial transcriptomics and computational geography in mapping the transcriptome", AGILE: GIScience Series 5:21, DOI 10.5194/agile-giss-5-21-2024 — READ IN FULL; position piece, no data unit, no endpoint, no estimand; verbatim: "The choice of aggregation unit will influence process understanding through scale (MAUP) driven distortions but this is completely unknown and ignored", plus "there are well established approaches for quantifying the impact of the MAUP". (2) STExplorer, Zormpas et al., bioRxiv 2025.01.17.633539 — READ; unit = bin at one fixed support; endpoint = geographically weighted model outputs; estimand = local non-stationary association, not support-sensitivity; names MAUP and Visium HD binning ("may introduce artificial ecotones by binning"), then fixes the support. (3) arXiv 2602.02825 "On the consistent and scalable detection of spatial patterns" (adversary F2) — READ; unit = gene, fixed method, two supports (8 vs 16 um Visium HD, rasterize_bins), endpoint = SVG statistic displacement, comparator = the other support, Fig S2f with identity-line Z-score outliers and a gene "dampened at the 16 um Nyquist limit"; no formal stability metric, no noise floor, no decomposition, no mention of MAUP. Also relevant: FICTURE (bioRxiv 2023.11.04.565621, adversary F1) reports qualitative grid-size dependence ("Making the grid smaller slightly improved the resolution but led to extremely noisy cluster assignments") as motivation for going segmentation-free. COULD NOT READ: Cell 2023 "Mapping the transcriptome" body — cell.com fulltext and PDF both CLIENT_ERROR; White Rose eprint 218767 landing page read (keyword list includes "modifiable areal unit problem"), PDF not opened within budget; PMC correctly never attempted. It grounds no part of this grade in either direction, and can only harden the rejection.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs (1) — it does not differ as a question; it is a protocol for the question Comber et al. pose, adding a pre-declared ladder, a noise floor, a variance decomposition, a declared s* criterion and the segmentation quarantine. Those are design choices inside an already-posed question, i.e. substantially overlapping. vs (2) — different estimand, so STExplorer would not answer it; but it shows the same group carrying the named problem into the field's own literature and still not measuring it, which strengthens the asked-and-open finding. vs (3) — the candidate generalises it (a pre-declared ladder, a noise floor, a variance share and a declared criterion against a single cross-resolution check), so the candidate is an extension of an illustrative comparison already run inside a methods paper, not a new question. Verification narrowed this: the 8-vs-16 um contrast there is one qualitative sanity check with no stability metric, not a study of support-dependence, so (3) weakens the already-executed reading while leaving the asked-and-open ground on (1) untouched. The SVG/domain benchmark family (Genome Biology 2024, 2025; Bioinformatics 2025; NAR 2025) differs in unit (method, not support) and endpoint (performance, not displacement) and is explicitly NOT the ground for the grade.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: Branch (i) gives a number for a reporting standard and licenses cross-study comparison above s*; branch (ii) makes bin size part of the result, obliges a support-sensitivity panel on every Visium HD paper, and unlicenses 8-vs-16 um and binned-vs-segmented comparison. Either way a live convention gains or loses its justification.
Significance — audience: Spatial-omics method and benchmark authors (support is absent as an axis); OSTA/Bioconductor and Seurat/scverse workflow authors publishing parallel binned and segmented chapters without an argument; 10x Genomics, whose "8 um recommended" would acquire or lose an evidential basis; reviewers and editors; and the GIScience group that demanded the work in print. Against: two years of stated demand with no supply.
Significance — fecundity: Does s* vary by tissue, output class and process grain? Is there a Krige's-relation analogue letting SVG statistics be converted between supports rather than recomputed? Does optimal support track a measurable tissue length scale? Could data-adaptive regionalisation replace square bins? If segmentation and binning disagree, which error is ecological and which individualistic?
Significance — anchoring: The segmentation-free vs segmentation-based dispute (currently argued on cell purity, not support); reproducibility of domain partitions across studies; niche definitions; and the MAUP literature, which would gain an arena where one capture can be re-aggregated at many supports — something census geography cannot do.
Reason for silence: Not accepted. The record's mechanisms (new instrument 2024; GIScience-venue disciplinary boundary; incentive gap against an audit that invalidates defaults) are well evidenced but explain why the question is UNANSWERED, not why it is UNASKED — and it was asked. The record concedes this itself. Per the Gate 4 rule a missing mechanism returns the novelty finding to Gate 2, where it already stands at Low.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): One adversary, fresh context, Gate 0–3 record only, Low grade handed as a prior finding not a verdict; 9 searches and 4 fetches run, none refused; 9 Disguise queries in new vocabularies, so the Disguise sweep was executed and is verified. Verbatim log: batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-13-adversary-1.md.
1 | Triviality — geostatistics already predicts smoothing and short-wavelength loss; F1/F2 show the field sees it | Direction is predictable, magnitude and s* are not; 20 queries surface one illustrative two-support comparison with no stability metric and one qualitative three-rung one; no published number exists | Resolved
2 | Disguise — is it a known question renamed? | No renamed duplicate in change-of-support, coarse-graining, ecological fallacy, grain/extent, image downsampling, Nyquist or Chinese vocabularies — but it is a known question under its OWN name (Comber et al. 2024; STExplorer 2025; MAUP as a Cell 2023 keyword), and the field has already observed the phenomenon incidentally (FICTURE grid-size dependence; arXiv 2602.02825 8-vs-16 um SVG displacement). The only differentiator is protocol, and the owning field already ships the sensitivity instrument (S-maup) | **Unresolved (fatal)**
3 | Combinatorial novelty — geography x spatial omics with nothing at the interface | A real interface exists (one capture, many supports) and the effect bites in practice; it is simply not unoccupied | Resolved
4 | Presupposition failure — P1, P3, P5 | P5 false and conceded; P1 defensible as a lower bound (F1 reproduces the sparsity mechanism in re-binned fine grids); P3 plausible but unevidenced — a within-support resampling floor is not obviously well defined for a spatial partition, since resampling bins breaks the graph the clustering runs on, and count-splitting or replicate sections are not named | Partial
5 | Vagueness — answerable whatever the data show? | Two pre-committed substantive branches, but the threshold is "to be declared" and the branch depends on it and on the floor's construction; F2 shows a two-rung outlier plot readable either way | Partial
6 | Significance inflation — is the audience real? | Yes, evidenced: live 10x and OSTA defaults, two field-internal papers volunteering cross-support comparisons unprompted, published demand from the GIScience group. Against: demand without supply for two years | Resolved
7 | Reason for silence | The mechanism explains non-answering, not non-asking, because the question was asked; rule sends novelty back to Gate 2 | **Unresolved**
8 | Dissolution — segmentation-free and multi-granularity methods engineer the support away | Those methods still carry scale parameters (FICTURE hexagon side 7–14 um; oversmoothing at low anchor density) and the installed base of binned analyses remains, so the question survives in weakened form | Partial
Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261017-13-verification-comber.md): the rejection stands and the routing row holds, with one claim softened — the "two-rung comparison" is a single illustrative example inside a methods paper, not a study of support-dependence.
**The posing sentence is verbatim.** Comber, Zormpas, Queen & Cockell (2024), "Lessons from spatial transcriptomics and computational geography in mapping the transcriptome" (AGILE-GISS 5, 21), contains the string exactly, in the PDF body at Section 3, Example 1 — not on the abstract page, which matters for anyone re-checking it: "The choice of aggregation unit will influence process understanding through scale (MAUP) driven distortions but this is completely unknown and ignored." The preceding sentence fixes what "this" refers to: "Sub-cellular observations are aggregated in different ways (grid, image-segmentation etc) to at least cell level." Section 6 adds the general form: "Despite the MAUP being a core consideration in all analyses of spatial data, its effects are rarely tested for". It is a short position piece: it runs no analysis, tests nothing, and proposes testing as future work. That is precisely the asked-and-still-open shape the routing file takes.
**The second mention is confirmed and also untested.** STExplorer (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.17.633539) repeats the MAUP concern in its introduction — "high-resolution platforms, like Stereo-seq or Visium-HD, may introduce artificial ecotones by binning data" — and runs no test of support-dependence: its analyses use Visium spots only, Visium HD and Stereo-seq appear in background, and the only varied parameter is the GWPCA/GWR bandwidth, with no sensitivity analysis reported.
**The third claim is softened.** arXiv:2602.02825 (Su, Fung, Wang, Yang, Knowles, Rabadan, "On the consistent and scalable detection of spatial patterns") does compare 8 um against 16 um Visium HD — "comprising 164,800 bins at 16 um resolution, and 656,788 bins at 8 um" — but the comparison appears only in the full HTML text, not the abstract, and is one qualitative example: per-gene spatial-variability Z-scores at the two supports plotted against the identity line, with outliers picked out, including that "the 'Swiss roll' pattern introduced during sample preparation was preferentially detected at 8 um resolution" and attributed to "signal dampening at the 16 um Nyquist limit". The entry's "has already run a two-rung 8-vs-16 um comparison" overstates it: it is a cross-resolution sanity check inside a paper whose purpose is a consistent, scalable spatial-pattern test, with no noise floor. The rejection does not depend on the stronger reading — the ground is that the question is posed in print and unanswered, not that it is answered.
**The gap the row claims is intact.** No published systematic measurement of how spatially-variable-gene calls or spatial-domain partitions change across a ladder of aggregation supports, with a within-support resampling noise floor, was found. That negative is bounded and recorded as such: 7 searches, 6 fetches, no SVG-method benchmark opened, and PMC, Europe PMC and PubMed all unavailable. Four benchmark candidates surfaced as titles only (PMC12445034, bioRxiv 2023.12.02.569717, bioRxiv 2024.07.04.602147, PMC10506280) and a Bioinformatics paper btae546 could not be identified. So the row goes in as asked-and-open with its unread items named, per the routing test.
Caveat recorded: the Comber quotes came through the page summariser, which caps verbatim strings near 125 characters, so the two sentences above were checked as separate short strings rather than reproduced as one contiguous passage; anyone citing them should re-check against the PDF.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The candidate is a measurement protocol for a question someone else already asked by name — Comber et al. 2024 pose MAUP-in-spatial-transcriptomics and call it "completely unknown and ignored" — verified verbatim in the PDF body — arXiv 2602.02825 already plots per-gene spatial-variability Z-scores at 8 um against 16 um as an illustrative cross-resolution check, and the formal sensitivity criterion is off-the-shelf in the field that owns the method. A ledger of un-asked questions cannot admit a well-designed protocol for an asked one; the correct destination is the open-problems handoff.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Open the Cell 2023 review body (White Rose PDF eprint 218767/1, since cell.com routes fail) to fix how far the posing already reaches into the target field's flagship venue, then treat it as an open problem in the research workstream rather than a ledger candidate; any answer must cite and extend arXiv 2602.02825's 8-vs-16 um comparison.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md as an OPEN PROBLEM (asked, unanswered — not a disguised known, since the import is explicit and under its own name). Problem: quantify the support-dependence of spatial-transcriptomics outputs (SVG calls, domain partitions) under change of support and test for a stability support s*. Source showing it is open: Comber et al. 2024, AGILE: GIScience Series 5:21 — "completely unknown and ignored"; corroborated by STExplorer 2025 naming it without testing it and by the absence of any published fraction under re-binning. Tier A — public Visium HD and Stereo-seq data exist at 2 um, re-binning is arithmetic, methods are installed, S-maup (PLOS ONE 2018, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0207377) supplies the criterion; the binding constraint is pre-declaration discipline, not compute.

Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — somatic mutagenesis, DNA repair, epigenomics (single-molecule, single-strand-resolved sequencing with per-read 5mC calling). Adjacent: cancer genomics/liquid biopsy, plant epigenomics, sequencing methodology.
Question (canonical): Do the individual DNA molecules that carry a somatic mutation differ in their own local methylation state from matched molecules without a mutation at the same locus in the same sample? (V1, as intaken.)
Alternative formulations:
- V2 (the one Gate 1 reformulation, for well-posedness): in single-molecule, single-strand-resolved sequencing of non-clonal somatic tissue, is local 5mC density over a pre-specified window **excluding the mutated base and every CpG the mutation creates or destroys** associated with a molecule's mutation status, versus mutation-free molecules matched on locus, sample and strand (matched conditional logistic, stratified by mutation class, with a negative-control class and a per-read methylation-call error model)?
- Is the methylation–mutation association a molecule-level fact or only a regional correlation?
Motivating gap: everything the field believes about methylation shaping mutation rate rests on **regional** density-vs-density correlation, which cannot separate a cis, molecule-level mechanism from regional confounders (replication timing, chromatin, repair access) that covary at the same scale; per-molecule mutation+5mC co-measurement (MethylSaferSeqS 2023; duplex/single-strand designs) now exists. The intake's claim that nothing pairs a mutation with the modification state of its own molecule is false — Gate 2 found that pairing in print.
Presuppositions: (1) per-read 5mC calls accurate enough — CONTESTED, no measured per-read error rate obtained; (2) current methylation informative about state when the mutation arose — STRONGLY CONTESTED, false in general (mark at a mutated CpG is physically destroyed), so the claim is an association only; (3) matched mutation-free molecules at the same locus/sample/strand are a valid comparator — partly contested, operational in P1; (4) per-molecule mutation calls are not damage/chemistry artefacts — addressed in principle by single-strand-resolved designs, harder under conversion chemistry; (5) enough mutant molecules at CpG-containing loci for power — UNDEMONSTRATED (P1: 11 and 65 mutant UIDs at two loci); (6) sample is non-clonal.
What would count as an answer: a matched per-molecule odds ratio (conditional logistic; matched on locus, sample, strand) for local 5mC density on mutation-bearing vs mutation-free molecules over a pre-declared window excluding the mutated base and mutation-created/destroyed CpGs, stratified by mutation class, with a pre-specified per-read error model and a negative-control class. A bounded null (tight CI around OR=1 at adequate power) would be equally informative.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 documented queries (11 at Gate 2 across cancer genomics, plant epigenomics, liquid biopsy, germline/evolutionary genomics, sequencing methodology, WGBS analysis; 9 fresh adversary queries in single-cell multi-omics, immunology/SHM, bacterial SMRT methylomics, Chinese-language, ASM/cis-variant read-level, epiallele/epigenotype, clonal haematopoiesis, historical methylation-mediated-mutagenesis, per-read joint-caller tooling). A late Gate 4 (below) added 16 more Disguise queries in two fresh contexts. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-14-record.md, -adversary-0-firstpass.md (the first-pass adversary) and -adversary-1.md / -adversary-2.md (the late Gate 4). Most informative:
- `Methyl-SaferSeqS simultaneous methylation and mutations in the same DNA molecules` → the on-point paper (P1), PNAS 2023 / medRxiv preprint — mutant vs wild-type molecules, same locus, same sample, per-molecule 5mC.
- `reads carrying a somatic mutation show different methylation than reads without the mutation at the same position ... read-level analysis` (mandatory own-field/own-words query) → WGBS methodology only (BSmooth, BEAT); read-level mutation-conditioned methylation is not a named analysis.
- `local DNA methylation at and around somatic mutations ... neighbouring CpG` → Kusmartsev et al. 2020 (P2), the site-level form of V2's neighbourhood estimand.
- `read-level analysis bisulfite ... variant-allele reads vs reference-allele reads cis effect` and `software jointly calls SNVs and 5mC per read` (adversary) → every near-renaming bins reads by a **germline** heterozygous label (ONT haplotype-resolved workflow, longphase, ASM literature), not by a rare somatic event.
- Chinese-language query returned P1 again; no non-English prior.
COULD NOT READ — HiDEF-seq (Liu et al., Nature 630:752, 2024, 10.1038/s41586-024-07532-8): nature.com fetch error; PMC/Europe PMC hard-blocked, not attempted. Its silence is recorded as unverified, not as a check that passed; no grade rests on it in either direction.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
- P1. Wang Y, Douville C, … Vogelstein B, "Detection of rare mutations, copy number alterations, and methylation in the same template DNA molecules" (MethylSaferSeqS), PNAS 2023, PMID 37014860; medRxiv 10.1101/2022.12.06.22283116 (full text read by generator and adversary). Unit: individual template molecule (duplex-barcoded UID family), plasma. Endpoint: bisulfite 5mC on that same molecule. Comparator: wild-type UIDs at the same amplicon in the same sample. Estimand: fraction methylated, mutant vs WT (PIK3CA H1047R 82% of 11 mutant UIDs vs 1.3% of 398 WT C's; TP53 R248W 98% of 835 WT UIDs vs 3.1% of 65 mutant C's).
- P2. Kusmartsev V, Drożdż M, Schuster-Böckler B, Warnecke T, "Cytosine methylation affects the mutability of neighboring nucleotides in germline and soma", Genetics 214(4):809–823, 2020, 10.1534/genetics.120.303028 (read; adversary spot-check passed). Unit: genomic position (matched methylated/unmethylated CpG pairs). Endpoint: rare-variant incidence in ±1–3 bp neighbourhoods. Comparator: matched unmethylated CpGs. Estimand: RR_met (human RR_met = 0.886).
- P3. Akbari V, … Jones SJM, "Megabase-scale methylation phasing using nanopore long reads and NanoMethPhase", Genome Biology 22, 2021, 10.1186/s13059-021-02283-5 (abstract-level only; nothing rests on it). Unit: read assigned to a **germline** haplotype. Estimand: allele-specific methylation between haplotypes.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same unit, same comparator, same endpoint family and same instrument; differs only in which cytosines are read (P1 interrogates the CpG the mutation creates or destroys, i.e. the degenerate base itself; V2 reads a flanking window) and in statistical apparatus (OR, strand matching, class strata, error model, negative control, power — all absent from P1, which is a descriptive check at 2 loci in 2 patients). The adversary verified by full-text reading that P1 contains **no** flanking-CpG analysis. vs P2 — P2 conditions on a site's methylation and asks about mutability, aggregated over molecules and often across samples; V2 reverses the conditioning and moves the unit to the molecule, matching out regional confounders by design. P2 nevertheless already publishes the neighbourhood estimand at site level. vs P3 — its conditioning variant is germline and present on ~half of molecules, used only as a pooling label; a somatic mutation cannot define a haplotype.
Novelty confidence: Low
(Low for the question as intaken: V1 is asked and answered in print by P1, in the candidate's own field and own words, on a single-molecule platform matched on locus and sample. The sharpened V2 was not found in 20 queries across nine vocabularies and would grade Medium — but V2 keeps P1's unit, comparator, sample frame and instrument and swaps only the read-out cytosines, taking its neighbourhood estimand from P2; that is a covariate/measurement-window swap on an asked-and-answered question, which the operating rules reject even when the exact variant is unmeasured. Adversary 1 agreed the Low grade is correct for the question as intaken and recommended Provisional on the strength of V2; the judge does not follow that, because promoting V2 requires narrowing the candidate to a limb the record itself calls a narrowing.)
Significance — consequence: yes (OR away from 1 for C>T classes but not the control class) would make the methylation–mutation relationship a molecule-level fact and license cis mechanisms (5mC deamination, TET intermediates, MBD occlusion of repair); a bounded no would show the large regional correlation is regional in nature and withdraw warrant from models attributing SBS1-like CpG>TpG burden to the individual molecule's methylation. Dented by structure: at the cleanest class the mark at the mutated base is destroyed, so the test runs on correlated neighbours and speaks to the molecule's current microenvironment, not the deaminated cytosine's state.
Significance — audience: mutational-signature modellers (COSMIC/SBS, PCAWG-lineage); DNA-repair biochemists (MMR, BER/TDG, MBD, TET); single-molecule/somatic-mosaicism method developers (duplex, single-strand-resolved), for whom this is a reanalysis of data they already hold plus a per-read error model as a methods deliverable; liquid-biopsy developers in the P1 lineage.
Significance — fecundity: same design for other per-read marks (6mA, oxidative damage, abasic sites, nick position); strand asymmetry on single-strand-resolved reads; repair-tract footprints as methylation discontinuities; a clonal-haematopoiesis analogue at driver loci; and a reusable template — condition on a rare per-molecule event, compare matched molecules within locus and sample.
Significance — anchoring: SBS1/CpG>TpG attribution to 5mC deamination; the regional methylation/chromatin-vs-mutation-rate literature and its replication-timing confounding; kb–Mb variation in somatic mutation rate; per-read modification-call accuracy as an unmeasured methods quantity.
Reason for silence: (1) new instrument used for the job it was built for — P1's authors used the joint readout for assay validation and tumour-fraction estimation, and their one mutation–methylation comparison is a positive control at the mutated base; (2) each field's standard QC discards the molecules in question (methylation pipelines filter mismatch-bearing reads; mutation pipelines treat conversion/methylation as nuisance and regress it out at window level). The adversary strengthened (1) with P1's own parameters (11 and 65 mutant UIDs, 77% conversion, mutations and methylation read off physically separated strands linked by UID), making a flanking matched OR out of reach on that instrument. But a reason for silence that must explain away an existing partial instance is, per the operating rules, a signal to treat the novelty finding as suspect — and here the suspicion resolved toward Low.

Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-14-verification-methylsafer.md and -flanking.md): **the batch's Gate 2 ground does not stand.** MethylSaferSeqS does not answer the candidate's question, the sharpening the judge dismissed as a mere measurement-window swap is what separates an informative question from a tautology, and the second prior the entry leaned on is not prior art at all. That withdrawal did NOT promote the entry: it triggered the late Gate 4 below, which rejected it on a different and better-sourced ground. **The verdict stays Rejected, on new grounds.** Everything in this section stands as the reason the original kill was wrong; the reason the candidate still fails is in the Late Gate 4 section.
**What MethylSaferSeqS actually reports.** Read at first hand from a repository copy of PNAS 120(15):e2220704120 and cross-checked against the medRxiv preprint (10.1101/2022.12.06.22283116), which agreed on every string checked. The method does link sequence and methylation for one original molecule: barcoded adapters carry 5-methylcytosine so they survive bisulfite, each strand is linearly copied about three times with a biotinylated dU-containing primer, the unmethylated copies carry the sequence into the mutation library while the original strands keep their methylation and go to the methylation library, and a shared UID joins them. So the instrument exists. But the mutant-versus-wild-type methylation comparison is reported **in two patients only, as a demonstration that the method works**, and the authors chose those two because the mutation sits "in a CpG dyad that affected the methylation status of the strands" — that is, the mutation itself creates or destroys the very CpG being measured, which is why the text reads "As expected". The numbers: for PIK3CA p.H1047R, "Of those, 11 (2.7%) contained the PIK3CA p.H1047R mutation", and "a high fraction of mutant UIDs (82% of 11) were methylated in the CGT trimer" against "only 1.3% of the 398 C residues in the analogous CAT trimer in the wild-type UIDs"; for TP53 p.R248W, 65 of 900 shared UIDs (7.2%) were mutant, with 98% of 835 wild-type UIDs methylated in the CCG trimer against 3.1% of mutant CCA trimers, the latter attributed to "incomplete bisulfite conversion".
**Why that is not the candidate's question.** The read-out is **the mutated base itself**, the cytosine of the CpG dyad, in a CGT/CAT or CCG/CCA trimer. The paper describes no flanking window and the preprint contains no comparison of flanking CpGs. A methylation difference at a cytosine that the mutation converts is a restatement of the sequence change, not independent epigenetic information. So the judge's reasoning inverts: moving the read-out window off the mutated base to flanking CpGs is not "a measurement-window swap ... keeping the same unit, comparator, sample and instrument" — it is the move that makes the quantity carry information the genotype does not already determine. The Gate 2 regrade to Low is withdrawn and novelty returns to Medium.
**The second prior is struck.** The entry credited the sharpened version with "borrowing its neighbourhood estimand from Kusmartsev 2020". Kusmartsev et al. 2020 (Genetics 214:809, "Cytosine Methylation Affects the Mutability of Neighboring Nucleotides in Germline and Soma") runs the other way: it is a population-level association in which methylation of a CpG predicts the incidence of flanking SNPs — "nucleotides in the close vicinity (+/-3 bp) of methylated cytosines mutate less frequently", measured as "the incidence of singleton SNPs" at each surrounding base. Different unit (population site, not molecule), different endpoint (mutation incidence, not methylation), and the opposite direction of inference. It is background on how methylation shapes mutation risk, not prior art for whether mutation-bearing molecules differ in their own flanking methylation. The attribution is removed.
**The gap, bounded.** Nine queries across single-molecule joint genetic-epigenetic analysis, long-read somatic calling with simultaneous methylation, allele- and haplotype-specific methylation around somatic variants, and mutation-methylation co-occurrence on one read found no report of the flanking-CpG, same-locus, mutant-versus-wild-type single-molecule comparison. The nearest items do something else: Akbari et al. (bioRxiv 2024.02.26.582089) mentions simultaneous genome-and-epigenome measurement only in its introduction and runs no methylation analysis; a Nanopore ASHG 2023 tumour-normal poster calls differential methylation **between samples** and phases germline haplotypes, never splitting reads by somatic-variant status. The negative is bounded and recorded as such: about five pages opened, with a biomodal poster, MethPhaser, PacBio pages and a Genome Research long-read cancer review unread, and no citation search of the MethylSaferSeqS literature possible.
**The conversion leg of the entry's own strongest objection, checked separately (logs -verification-conversion.md and -hidefseq.md).** That objection had a second, quantitative leg that the first verification pass had not checked, so it was checked before any promotion. Its numbers are where it puts them and its inference is not. Confirmed in the preprint: "average conversion efficiency of 77% (IQR: 75% to 79%)" for the LM libraries, and the 50C/3h protocol was chosen by trial and error for yield — "with 80% of unmethylated C's converted to U's", about 70% of input molecules retained — because 50C/16h gave over 98% conversion at the cost of "loss of half of the original DNA template molecules". So the trade-off is real and deliberate, and 23% of unmethylated cytosines going unconverted follows arithmetically from the library average. What is not supported is the step that made the objection fatal. The unit of that figure is the **library**, with the IQR taken across libraries; the paper reports no per-molecule conversion rate and no per-read or per-molecule methylation-call error rate anywhere in the text read, and defines fractional methylation as "the ratio of the total number of unconverted cytosines in CpG sites to the total number of CpG sites", aggregated across molecules per marker. The claim that conversion failure is a per-molecule event whose error is therefore correlated across the whole window is the adversary's own derivation, and the source measures neither the per-molecule rate nor its correlation structure. The magnitude is also overstated against the only in-paper measurement of it: at the TP53 mutant CCA trimer — a cytosine the mutation has already taken out of CpG context, so any apparent methylation there is pure conversion artefact — 3.1% of C residues read as methylated, not ~23%, a sevenfold gap the entry's arithmetic does not account for. Two further points of reasoning, labelled as reasoning rather than as sourced findings: a library-level conversion deficit is common to both arms of a comparison matched on locus, sample, strand and library, so it attenuates a contrast and costs power rather than manufacturing one; and conversion artefact is in principle per-read detectable from the non-CpG cytosines on the same molecule, which is standard bisulfite QC. Per the ledger's rule that a kill which cannot be sourced is Partial at best, **the conversion leg drops to Partial**: a real and material measurement problem, not a fatal objection. Caveat: the preprint was read through the page summariser and the PNAS version of record could not be opened by any route (DOI and pnas.org both client-errored, PMC returned reCAPTCHA), and the summariser warned its text may have been truncated, so the absence of a per-molecule error rate is bounded rather than proven.
**The conversion-free escape does not exist in HiDEF-seq, which is now read.** The same objection's closing clause held that the escape "is exactly the limb neither Gate 2 nor the adversary could verify, because HiDEF-seq could not be read". It has now been read, at nature.com (doi 10.1038/s41586-024-07532-8) and in the bioRxiv preprint, and it does not supply the escape — for a reason that cuts the other way from the objection's. HiDEF-seq is a PacBio single-strand-resolved method for mismatches and DNA damage; it "achieves single-molecule fidelity for base substitutions" and "also detects cytosine deamination — a common type of DNA damage — with single-molecule fidelity", and its polymerase kinetics are used to characterise ssDNA damage ("a distinct kinetic signature for ssDNA C>T calls"), not to call methylation. **It does not call 5mC at all**: the only "methyl" match on the published page is a reference title, and neither source reports a per-read methylation error rate or any comparison of methylation between mutant and non-mutant molecules. So presupposition (1) — per-read 5mC calls accurate enough — remains undemonstrated, which caps the entry and is already its promotion condition; and the finding tells against the candidate's feasibility while telling for its novelty, since the only platform shown to co-measure sequence and methylation per molecule does so on conversion chemistry, in two patients, at the mutated base itself. A dedicated search for any conversion-free chemistry with a published per-read 5mC error rate on unmethylated and fully-methylated controls returned only candidate sources (PacBio pages, a 5mC benchmarking PDF, a Genome Research 2025 supplement, Brief Bioinform bbae413) that the checker had no fetch budget left to open, so that residual is unread rather than absent.

**Where the verification pass left it.** On the first-pass record alone it would have been Provisional: that adversary returned no Unresolved attack across all eight, well-posedness stayed at 2/3, and the search record was explicitly bounded. That is why Gate 5's rule matters here — an entry whose Gate 2 ground falls cannot simply be re-judged into a survivor, and running Gate 4 properly is what found the ground below.
Caveats recorded: the second checker could not open MethylSaferSeqS at all (DOI fetch error, PMC and PubMed blocked, budget exhausted), so the account above rests on the first checker's repository copy and the medRxiv preprint rather than the PNAS version of record; its first summariser pass gave mutant fractions of 3.1% and 9.3% against the quoted 2.7% and 7.2%, and the quoted text was preferred; and that checker used 7 fetches against a limit of 6. From the late pass: the epialleleR reference manual is ROBOTS_DISALLOWED and the GigaScience paper was opened by adversary 1 but not by the independent checker, so the per-read methylation measure and its threshold are UNVERIFIED; the epialleleR paper's own three named user papers and the forward citations of both epialleleR and MethylSaferSeqS are unopened, which bounds the central negative; Beaulaurier et al. (PMC4490391) defeated adversary 2's fetch cap and keeps its attack 2 at Partial rather than Resolved; PacBio's own primrose/jasmine per-read figures could not be opened; and every page in this entry was read through the summariser, which caps quoted strings near 125 characters.

**Late Gate 4 (ran separately, as Gate 5 requires when a Gate 2 ground is withdrawn): two cold adversaries on the Gate 0–3 record, 16 further Disguise queries, logs -adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.** Both were told the Gate 2 verdict was void and handed the facts the verification pass had established, so neither inherited the "already answered" framing and neither re-derived MethylSaferSeqS. They converged on the same finding and graded it differently, and the finding is what decides the entry.
**The finding: the question is posed and shipped, in a vocabulary Gate 2 never searched.** epialleleR (Nikolaienko, Lønning, Knappskog, *GigaScience* 12:giad087, 2023; Bioconductor) has a documented function, `generateVcfReport`, that "calculates frequencies of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) within epialleles" and "tests for the association between SNV and epiallelic status using Fisher Exact test"; its Features list says "The association of methylation with single-nucleotide variations within epialleles can be tested using generateVcfReport", and the README puts it as a "test for the association between epiallele methylation status and sequence variations". A third fresh-context checker opened the vignette independently (log -verification-epiallele.md) and confirmed the strings and, decisively, the output's own shape: per-strand Fisher p-values (`FEp+`, `FEp-`) over per-strand reference/alternate read counts prefixed methylated and unmethylated (`M+Ref U+Ref M-Ref U-Ref M+Alt U+Alt M-Alt U-Alt`). That is the candidate's unit (the read), endpoint (the read's own methylation status), comparator (reads carrying the other base at the same position, same sample, same strand) and estimand (association between variant status and read methylation) in one function, with Fisher exact on a single locus's 2×2 being the exact conditional test that matched conditional logistic generalises. Independently, two readers opened the epialleleR preprint and found the conditioning stated as intent in its own words — the framework "allows to connect DNA methylation status with potential underlying cis-factors" "such as single-nucleotide variation or mutations within the immediate proximity" — with no such analysis run.
**Where the two adversaries differ, and how the rule resolves it.** Adversary 1 graded attack 2 **Unresolved** on that basis, reasoning that what V2 adds — somatic rather than any variant, the exclusion rule, class strata, a negative control, an error model — is design hygiene on an asked question. Adversary 2 graded attack 2 **Partial**, because no sweep found the contrast *executed* and its most promising cross-field hit (Beaulaurier et al., bacterial single-molecule methylome phasing, PMC4490391) could not be opened; it rejected the germline-ASM analogy as "machinery, not an answer". Both are honest readings of the same facts, and the ledger's verdict rule settles it two ways at once: Unresolved on attack 2 from any adversary is fatal, and Gate 0's definition makes a disguised known — "a covariate/instrument/corpus swap on an asked question" — "Rejected **even if the exact variant is unmeasured**", which is precisely this case. A germline-to-somatic swap on a question that ships as a documented test is that swap. **Rejected at Gate 4 on attack 2.**
**Attack 7 is Unresolved from both cold adversaries, independently, and would cap the entry even without attack 2.** The record's silence mechanism was that the quantity "is not in anyone's results tables even when it is in their raw reads". It has been a documented function call since 2023, and the conditioning is in print as stated intent in at least two tool papers and partly executed in a third (P1). Adversary 2's wording is the right one: the field's silence here is **unexecuted intent, not an unposed question** — and the only rescue, that V2's sharpened estimand was never posed in exactly those terms, is circular, because that rescue is available for any question whatever. By the ledger's own rule a failed reason-for-silence returns the novelty finding to Gate 2, which is where this ends.
**What the late pass did NOT find, recorded so the negatives stay countable.** No published result compares the methylation of somatic-variant-carrying reads with same-locus non-carrying reads in the same sample — a bounded negative over 8 searches and 6 fetches, with epialleleR's three named user papers (Lønning, *JAMA Oncol* 2022; Nikolaienko, *Genome Med* 2023; Nikolaienko, *Clin Epigenet* 2025) unopened and the forward citations of both epialleleR and MethylSaferSeqS unverified. The vignette's own worked example returns no association. A 2026 clonal-haematopoiesis preprint (medRxiv 2026.04.03.26350108, DNMT3A R882 and TET2) compares across individuals and edited cells on per-CpG beta values, "Individual beta values, represented as the ratio of methylated reads to total coverage" — not mutant versus wild-type reads. So the question's answer is unpublished for any variant class, germline or somatic; what is published is the question and the tool.
**Two corrections to the late pass's own claims, applied to it rather than inherited.** First, adversary 1 attributed a "minimum average methylation beta value of 0.5 for CpG sites" threshold and a per-read CpG-average measure to the epialleleR paper. The independent checker could not find that string in the vignette, found no threshold stated for this function, and could not open the reference manual or the paper, so **how a read is classed methylated or unmethylated is UNVERIFIED**; it does not change the four-attribute match, which rests on the output's own columns, but it is a user inference and is labelled as one. Second, that checker reached the paper by a DOI it recalled wrongly (giad060, an unrelated paper) and used 7 fetches against a limit of 6; both are recorded, and the paper itself (PMC10622323) remains unread by it, though adversary 1 did open it at the correct OUP URL and adversary 2 opened the preprint.
**One genuine scope limit on the kill, confirmed verbatim and twice.** The tool is blind to the candidate's headline mutation class on the strand that matters: the vignette's own code comment reads "# NA values are shown for the C->T variants on the \"+\" and G->A on the \"-\"" "# strands, because bisulfite conversion makes their counting impossible", and output is "currently limited to SNVs only". A study of C>T at CpG — the deamination class the candidate's motivating gap is built on — would need its own approach for those variants on bisulfite data. That is a real limitation of the implementation, and under the ledger's rule it does not rescue the question: the question is still asked, and the unmeasured class is exactly what "even if the exact variant is unmeasured" covers. It is, however, the sharpest thing the routed problem has to say.
**The pre-tabled conversion objection was declined by the adversary that was invited to use it**, independently of this judge's own reading above: adversary 1 wrote that the per-molecule correlation step "is asserted, not sourced; I found no primary source for it within budget and I will not score a kill on it", and that inferring a per-molecule rate from a library average "is a unit substitution ... contradicted by the same paper's own observations" of 1.3% and 3.1% apparent methylation at cytosines the mutation had moved out of CpG context. It added, sourced, that read-level conversion state is a modelled quantity in this very package — Figure 1 describes an epiallele that "represents the product of incomplete bisulfite conversion", simulated at ~99.75% conversion — so per-read conversion QC is constructible rather than absent. Two adversaries reaching that conclusion independently of each other and of this judge is the strongest form the finding takes.
**Presupposition (1) is better off than the record had it, which matters for the routed problem rather than for the verdict.** A per-read 5mC error rate is a routinely estimated quantity on fully-methylated and unmethylated controls: the nanopore benchmark (Yuen et al., *Nat Commun* 12:3438, 2021) computes it per read — "The predictions were performed on individual reads, and then summarized per CG site", "using reads from 0% and 100% methylated sets" — with AUCPR "above 0.8", and ccsmeth (*Nat Commun* 2023, PacBio CCS) reports per-read "accuracies of 0.9232, 0.8788, and 0.8765" against M.SssI and PCR controls. Both are floors rather than tight bounds, and the same literature says per-read accuracy "remains largely unknown" and calls per-read recovery "a major limitation"; PacBio's own primrose/jasmine figures could not be opened. So the presupposition is unmeasured on a co-measuring instrument rather than false.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: the question is already posed, and shipped as a documented statistical test, in the read-level methylation-tooling vocabulary that eleven Gate 2 queries and nine first-pass adversary queries never searched. epialleleR's `generateVcfReport` "tests for the association between SNV and epiallelic status using Fisher Exact test", returning per-strand Fisher p-values over methylated and unmethylated read counts split by reference and alternate allele at the same position — the candidate's unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand in one function — and its paper names "single-nucleotide variations or mutations within the immediate proximity" as cis-factors for epimutations without running the analysis. What V2 adds is design hygiene on that asked question: somatic rather than any variant, exclusion of the CpG the mutation creates or destroys, mutation-class strata, a negative control and a per-read error model. Under Gate 0's definition that is a covariate swap on an asked question, which the ledger rejects even where the exact variant is unmeasured — and unmeasured it is, since no published result reports the comparison for any variant class. The entry's two earlier objections are both withdrawn and should not be cited: the "answered by P1" ground (P1 reads out the mutated base itself, two patients, "As expected") and the bisulfite-conversion ground (its numbers hold, its per-molecule correlation step is unsourced and its magnitude is contradicted sevenfold by the paper's own residuals).
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable to a rejected candidate; the work belongs in the research workstream, where it is now routed. For whoever picks it up: the first step is not new chemistry but reading the three epialleleR user papers the README names (Lønning, *JAMA Oncol* 2022; Nikolaienko, *Genome Med* 2023; Nikolaienko, *Clin Epigenet* 2025) plus the forward citations of epialleleR and MethylSaferSeqS, to establish whether any `generateVcfReport` result has in fact been published — none of those was opened here, and a published result would close the problem rather than open it. After that, the binding constraints are the two the late pass sourced: the tool cannot count C>T on '+' or G>A on '-' under bisulfite, which is the candidate's own headline class, and no per-read 5mC error rate exists for any instrument demonstrated to co-measure sequence and methylation on one molecule.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): **Routed** to ledger/routed-open-problems.md as an open problem. The batch's original routing decision is reversed along with its ground: the "answered by P1" reading is withdrawn (P1 reads out the mutated base itself in two patients as a method demonstration), and P2 was struck as running the opposite direction of inference, so this is not an answered or disguised-known-because-answered rejection. What the late Gate 4 established instead is that the question is **asked and not answered**: posed in print as a cis-factor hypothesis, shipped as a documented Fisher-exact test since 2023, and reported by nobody for any variant class on a bounded negative of 8 searches and 6 fetches. That is the routing file's own case. The row carries the two constraints the late pass sourced — the C>T/G>A blind spot under bisulfite chemistry, and the absent per-read 5mC error rate on any co-measuring instrument — and names the unopened items that could close it instead of answering it.

ID: UQ-20261017-15
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — interactomics / systems biology (PPI mapping, interactome coverage estimation). Method-owning neighbours: biophysical chemistry and pharmacology (equilibrium binding, assay window), analytical metrology (LOD, working range).
Question (canonical): For each assay class in current interactome-mapping use (HT-Y2H, AP-MS of lysates, binary recomposition assays of the MAPPIT/LUMIER/PCA type, proximity labelling, in-cell crosslinking MS), taking each assay's working concentration regime and detection limit from published protocols as bounded intervals and taking detectability to mean that a law-of-mass-action equilibrium complex fraction exceeds the assay's LOD at that working concentration: (a) where does each assay's detectability boundary lie in the (Kd, intracellular concentration) plane for one declared cell type; (b) what is the union of those regions, and hence the complement invisible to the whole toolkit; (c) what share of pairs falls in the complement under two declared denominators — a reference set with independently measured affinities, and all pairs among proteins expressed in that cell type weighted by a stated Kd prior; and (d) restated under the window, what does at least one published "fraction of the interactome mapped" figure become?
 [v1 at intake was the same question without a declared denominator or detectability criterion; v2 above is the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation and is the version graded.]
Alternative formulations:
 1. What is the detection window of the interactome-mapping toolkit, in Kd and copies per cell, and how much of the interactome lies outside it?
 2. Is the published "fraction of the human interactome mapped" a coverage figure for the interactome, or for the part of it the assays can physically reach?
 3. (metrology) What is the working range of the interactome-mapping method in the analyte's own units, and what is its coverage error as distinct from its sampling error?
Motivating gap: Silence mapping. The field's assay-sensitivity parameter is measured by running each assay against a literature-curated positive reference set — i.e. against previously detected interactions — so it is estimated from inside the detection window and has no slot for what lies outside. Absolute copy numbers per cell line and documented protocol parameters now make the window computable rather than estimable. The intake's claim that there is "essentially no literature asking what its instruments can see" is STRUCK: Hein 2015 reads its own plot's borders as method-set dynamic-range limits; Heo/Maslov/Shakhnovich 2011 imposes an explicit detection threshold on a proteome-wide mass-action solution; Huang/Jedynak/Bader 2007 splits Y2H false negatives into systematic and sampling terms; Lalonde 2008 states the window qualitatively per method. What survives is the narrower gap: no opened source computes the boundary in the cell's units from protocol parameters, unions the assay classes, or restates a coverage figure conditional on a window.
Presuppositions:
 1. Each assay class has a working regime and LOD recoverable from protocols — PARTLY CONTESTED (Y2H nuclear and AP-MS lysate effective concentrations poorly documented); v2 requires intervals.
 2. Abundances convert to concentrations with a defensible volume — CONTESTED (compartments, condensates); v2 requires a compartment model plus sensitivity analysis.
 3. Equilibrium occupancy is adequate to define detectability — CONTESTED, and narrowed by Gate 4: covalent, time-integrating classes (proximity labelling, in-cell XL-MS) accumulate signal over an exposure, and AP-MS is a dilution-and-wash kinetic survival problem, so (Kd, C) are not the governing coordinates for several listed classes.
 4. Reference positive sets are drawn from previously detected interactions — VERIFIED from Venkatesan et al. 2009 (17,297 curated pairs narrowed to 188 then 107; "It is impossible to generate a set of negative interacting pairs with absolute confidence"). Circularity limb stands.
 5. The invisible band is non-empty — CONTESTED and partly what is asked. Supported qualitatively (Hein: weak interactions "frequently gone undetected"; Heo: "missed weak functional interactions") but no interaction has been independently placed inside a computed region.
 6. "The interactome" is a population a share can be reported of — CONTESTED at intake, repaired in v2 by declaring two denominators; Gate 4 attack 5 shows the repair is declaration without a usable denominator.
What would count as an answer: A computed (Kd, abundance) map marked by which assay classes reach each region, with the invisible region's boundary and its uncertainty; the share inside it under both declared denominators; and at least one published coverage figure restated as coverage of the reachable region (e.g. Venkatesan's ~8% of ~130,000). A null stands on its own: if the union substantially covers the plausible plane, coverage statements are sound as stated and the silence was justified. Axes are measurable, so neither answer can be reached by rhetoric — but see the strongest remaining objection on limb (c).
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 38 distinct queries — 11 at Gate 2, 9 per adversary across three adversaries, all in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-15-record.md and the three adversary files in that folder. Most informative:
 - `"fraction of the human interactome" mapped estimate sensitivity reference positive set circular calibration` → Venkatesan et al. 2009, the coverage framework the candidate proposes to re-interpret (own-field key hit).
 - `Hein 2015 "human interactome in three quantitative dimensions" ... detection limit which interactions detectable` → the closest prior; full text opened.
 - `what fraction of protein interactions are too weak or too low abundance to be detected ... interactome` (mandatory already-computed-quantity query) → no published share of the interactome below a detection window; nearest number is Hein's 80,000–180,000 AP-MS-detectable interactions in HeLa.
 - `distribution of dissociation constants ... what fraction weaker than micromolar ... below assay sensitivity` (answer-side, run independently by all three adversaries) → no proteome-wide Kd distribution exists; measured-affinity sets are small and structure-selected.
 - `Nachweisgrenze Affinität Interaktom ... limite de détection interactome affinité couverture` (German/French) → no non-English prior; surfaced Huang/Jedynak/Bader 2007, a coverage paper Gate 2 missed.
 - `Malmquist bias selection function survey completeness ... applied to proteomics interactome incompleteness` (astronomy) and `detection probability occupancy model capture-recapture ... imperfect detection` (ecology) → both fields own the formalism for "what fraction lies outside the survey limit"; neither has been transplanted to molecular interactomes.
 - `proteome-wide mass-action ... which complexes form from copy numbers and Kd, fraction bound in vivo` → Heo/Maslov/Shakhnovich arXiv 1007.2668, opened; the record's "not assay detection" dismissal of this line is withdrawn.
 Access routing: PMC/Europe PMC links appeared in most result sets and were never attempted. COULD NOT READ at the time of the batch: Luck et al. 2020 (HuRI, Nature) — doi.org and nature.com both returned client errors, search budget exhausted before a third route; recorded then as an unread same-field neighbour, with no absence claimed from it. **Since opened** by the verification pass through the PMC author manuscript (PMC7169983) — see the Verification section; the typeset Nature text and Supplementary Note 2 remain unread. Abstract only: Estojak et al. 1995 (adversary 1 read the abstract by a non-PMC route; adversary 2 could not read it at all). Zhang & Shakhnovich 2006/2008: abstract only.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
 P1 — Hein MY et al., "A Human Interactome in Three Quantitative Dimensions", Cell 2015 (read in full, ir.xtbg.ac.cn mirror). Unit: bait–prey pair by quantitative AP-MS (1,125 baits, HeLa). Endpoint: enrichment significance, interaction stoichiometry, interactor copy number. Comparator: per-protein background sets, reciprocal pull-downs, CORUM. Estimand: the joint distribution in stoichiometry × abundance space and the AP-MS-detectable interactome in HeLa (80,000–180,000), plot borders read as method- and proteome-set dynamic-range limits.
 P2 — Heo M, Maslov S, Shakhnovich E, "Protein abundances and interactions coevolve...", arXiv 1007.2668 / PNAS 2011 (opened by adversary 3; ADDED at Gate 4). Unit: protein pair in a model proteome of 3,868 coupled LMA equations. Endpoint: binary complex concentrations above an explicit pull-down cutoff relative to bait. Comparator: functional vs non-specific complexes. Estimand: fidelity of pull-down detection vs abundance — "can detect functional interactions with high fidelity only for high abundance proteins", with "missed weak functional interactions". Kd values "assigned by formula".
 P3 — Venkatesan K et al., "An empirical framework for binary interactome mapping", Nat Methods 2009 (read in full, rothlab PDF). Unit: assay × reference-set pair, aggregated. Endpoint: screening completeness, assay sensitivity (Y2H-CCSB 17%, MAPPIT 21%), sampling sensitivity, precision. Comparator: hsPRS-v1 vs hsRRS-v1. Estimand: interactome size ~130,000 (95% CI ~73,500–199,700) and mapped fraction ~8%. Contains no Kd, no copy numbers, no concentration-based detection limit.
 Also now flanking, from Gate 4: Huang H, Jedynak B, Bader JS, "Where Have All the Interactions Gone?", PLoS Comput Biol 2007 (opened) — splits Y2H false negatives into systematic (55–85% of them) and sampling terms, but the systematic term is construct functionality, with no affinity, abundance or concentration content, and the Discussion defers "varying effective nuclear concentrations and binding constants" to future work. Ivanic J et al., PLoS ONE 4(5):e5815, 2009 (read in full) — log-degree vs log-abundance association only; retained as adjacent-object, not prior art.
Novelty — how this differs from each:
 vs P1: Hein's axes are assay-internal stoichiometry × abundance, not Kd × concentration; one assay class, not the union; its detectable count is extrapolated from detected data, i.e. estimated inside the window; it restates no published mapped-fraction figure. Enough to strike the intake's silence claim and to cap novelty below High.
 vs P2: same physics, different estimand and inputs. Heo assigns Kd by formula in a model proteome and uses a modelled stoichiometric cutoff, not protocol working concentrations and LODs; no declared cell type with measured copy numbers, no union over assay classes, no share outside the window, no coverage restatement. It does establish that the qualitative answer ("weak and/or rare is what we cannot see") has been in print since 2011 — which is what reduces attack 1 to Partial.
 vs P3: same object (coverage), opposite instrument. Venkatesan's mapped fraction is computed from empirically measured sensitivity; the candidate computes the reach boundary in physical units and conditions the fraction on it. P3 supplies the candidate's premise, not its answer.
 vs Huang 2007: same systematic-vs-sampling split, different systematic term (construct quality, not a region of a physical plane) — and it names the candidate's physics as its own undone next step, which both damages the record's "no slot in the field's accounting" framing and leaves the candidate's estimand unoccupied.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If a large region is invisible to the whole toolkit, every published "fraction of the interactome mapped" is a statement about coverage of the reachable region — a coverage-error problem, not a sampling-error problem — and assay-development priorities shift from throughput inside the window to extending it, with a named target region; network statistics on interactome maps acquire a physically specified missingness model in place of uniform-sampling assumptions. If the union substantially covers the plane, the result is a clean null: coverage statements are sound and the inherited-sensitivity circularity is harmless in practice. Gate 4 correction: the coverage-vs-sampling distinction is not wholly blurred by the field — Huang 2007 made it in 2007 — so the novel part of the consequence is the *physical* relabelling, not the distinction itself.
Significance — audience: Interactome-mapping consortia and their coverage arithmetic (CCSB/HuRI lineage, quantitative AP-MS groups); assay developers, for whom a computed blind region is a specification in biophysical units (the proximity-labelling literature already aims at the weak/transient corner without a map of it); database curators and PRS/RRS benchmark builders, since a window implies the positive reference set samples only the reachable region; ML PPI prediction, where a computed window converts "generalises poorly" into a quantified domain-shift term. The audience is real and already contesting adjacent claims; Gate 4 doubts whether it would adopt a prior-dependent share, not whether it exists.
Significance — fecundity: What the degree distribution looks like after correction for a physically specified window (P4-at-Gate-2's question with the threshold measured rather than fitted); whether disease-gene hub enrichment survives window correction or is an abundance artefact; which structurally or genetically evidenced interactions sit inside the invisible region and whether they share properties (IDR-mediated, avidity-driven, condensate-resident); a principled negative set built from the visible region only; the analogous window of a computational predictor; and transfer of ecology's detectability/occupancy estimators to molecular networks, which three adversaries independently confirmed has never been attempted.
Significance — anchoring: The interactome-completeness problem (P3); the low overlap between datasets from different assays, which a window would partly explain as geometry rather than noise; the "weak and transient interactions are under-appreciated" thread (P1, P2); the compartment/condensate problem, which enters as a contested presupposition; benchmark bias in structure-prediction-era PPI inference; and non-identifiability of population size under heterogeneous detection (Link, Biometrics), which an adversary checked and found cuts for the candidate.
Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary compounded by an instrument that cannot see its own blind spot. The field operationalises sensitivity as a hit rate against a literature-curated positive set, so its calibration instrument is structurally unable to sample outside the window and returns a sensitivity number whether or not a blind region exists — the quantity has no slot in the accounting and its absence produces no anomaly. The quantities needed live in biophysics, pharmacology and metrology, which own the method but not the data; the method-owning literature parameterises these assays by labelling radius and reactive-intermediate half-life and, verbatim from a review opened at Gate 4, "does not describe these methods in terms of affinity", so the question cannot be stated in its variables. Gate 4 weakened this twice: Huang 2007 did state roughly the right next step in the field's own flagship computational journal and nobody did it for ~19 years, and a plain input-availability explanation (no measured proteome-wide Kd distribution; Heo had to assign Kd by formula) fits the evidence at least as well. The ledger does not accept difficulty-of-answering as a reason for silence, so the mechanism survives only in its narrower form — why the units were never adopted — and the record's stronger version is withdrawn.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Three independent fresh-context adversaries (A1, A2, A3), 9 web searches each, all executed; full logs in batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-15-adversary-{1,2,3}.md. Status below is the worst across adversaries.
 1 Triviality | Limb (a) is a textbook isotherm — bound fraction above floor f gives a slope-1 line in log Kd vs log C (A1's and A2's own labelled arithmetic, checked against v2's declared 1:1 equilibrium regime) — and the qualitative answer is already in print (Heo 2011, Hein 2015, Lalonde 2008 per method). | The quantitative content is uncollated: no opened source puts the boundary in the cell's units, unions the classes, or restates a coverage figure; Huang 2007 ran a whole modelling paper and still deferred the physics. But the *direction* of the answer is known in advance, which is why limb (c)'s number carries the load. | Partial (A2, A3; A1 Resolved)

Partial, not Unresolved: the repair is concrete rather than circular, nobody has shown a time-integrated criterion reduces to (Kd, C), and the one paper that would decide it is unread (A2 COULD NOT READ; A1 abstract only). | Partial (all three)

Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-15-verification-huri.md and -huri2.md): the verdict is unchanged, but the COULD NOT READ residual that independently blocked Validated is discharged — and what HuRI actually says supports the candidate's novelty rather than capping it.
**HuRI opened on the second attempt**, through the PMC author manuscript (PMC7169983); the Harvard DASH PDF, doi.org and nature.com all returned fetch errors, so the typeset Nature text is still unread. A first checker had reached only the 2019 bioRxiv preprint.
Three findings, each bearing directly on the entry. First, the paper **does** publish the "fraction of the interactome mapped" figure the candidate proposes to restate: "HuRI is estimated to represent 2-11% of the binary protein interactome", with the derivation in Supplementary Note 2 and Extended Data Fig. 3j (unread), varying minimum publications per gene and minimum Lit-BM evidence, and with the main text conceding that "Accurate estimation of the total size of the interactome remains challenging." Second, and decisively for novelty, that figure has **no affinity or abundance basis**. Sensitivity is framed purely empirically, as recovery of PRSv1 and RRSv1 reference pairs by Y2H assay version; no dissociation constant, affinity or concentration language is tied to sensitivity anywhere in the main text returned, the only neighbouring phrase being "a continuum of binding strength or stability". Third, the paper does **not** map a systematically invisible region: the closest statements are that "many PPIs remained undetected as Y2H, like all characterized assays" and that weak or transient interactions are difficult to detect — qualitative remarks, not a boundary. On complementarity it says "The Y2H versions were complementary", with three versions roughly doubling detected PPIs against one and MAPPIT and GPCA used as orthogonal validation, but it never quantifies how much of any space the union covers.
So the same-field neighbour that was blocking Validated as unread turns out to own the candidate's target rather than its answer: it supplies the percentage the candidate wants restated against a detection boundary, and it states the boundary only in assay-recovery terms. The Unverified cap is discharged, and the entry's "closest neighbours each own only a restricted sibling" judgement is confirmed for HuRI specifically.
**The verdict does not move.** Attack 5 (Vagueness) remains Unresolved from adversary 3 — the headline limb, the share of plausible interactions falling in the invisible region, is non-identifiable under both declared denominators, since neither the set of plausible interactions nor the joint distribution of dissociation constants and intracellular concentrations is observable without assuming the thing being estimated. That is a non-fatal attack, so it caps at Provisional, and well-posedness 2/3 caps independently. Attack 2 (Disguise) was Resolved by all three adversaries on 27 executed new-vocabulary queries, so it is verified rather than unverified, and 38 queries in total found no duplicate.
Promotion requires, restated now that HuRI is read: (a) replacing the share-invisible limb with an identifiable one — for instance, the detectable fraction of a named, enumerated reference set of interactions with measured dissociation constants and measured cellular concentrations, which makes the denominator a list rather than an unknown population; (b) a published or derived detection limit in affinity and concentration units for at least two assay families, since HuRI gives none and the boundary is the entry's own object; and (c) HuRI's Supplementary Note 2 and Extended Data Fig. 3j read, to establish how the 2-11% was derived and whether its assumptions already imply a sensitivity model.
Caveats recorded: the PMC copy is the author manuscript, read through the page summariser; Supplementary Notes, Extended Data and most figure legends were not read, so the absences above are "not found in the main text returned" rather than established for the whole publication; and the harness's standing note that PMC is blocked did not hold on this attempt, which is worth remembering as a route.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Limb (c) — the share, which is what gives the question its force — is non-identifiable under both declared denominators: unweighted, denominator (ii) returns ~99.9% invisible by construction because under 0.1% of expressed pairs interact at all; weighted, it returns whatever the analyst's Kd prior says, and no measured proteome-wide Kd distribution exists; denominator (i) survives only on a few hundred structure-selected pairs drawn from inside the visible region, reimporting the circularity the candidate indicts in the coverage literature. Declaring the prior makes the answer auditable, not settleable, and dropping limb (c) leaves a boundary whose direction (weak and/or rare is invisible) was already published by Heo 2011, Hein 2015 and Lalonde 2008.
Promotion requires: Validated needs (i) attack 5 resolved — replace limb (c) with a quantity that does not reduce to an assumed Kd prior or to a visible-region-selected reference set, or drop (c) and re-argue significance on limbs (a), (b), (d) alone; and (ii) well-posedness raised to 3/3 — declare whether the abundance axis is the cell's or each assay's and give the per-assay transport, replace the single occupancy criterion with per-class criteria including a time-integrated one for covalent capture, and bound the Y2H ectopic and AP-MS lysate effective working concentrations to better than a decade. Also required before any Validated grade, independently: read Luck et al. 2020 (HuRI) by a third route and add it to the nearest-prior list, and keep Heo 2011 and Huang 2007 in that list with the record's "not assay detection" dismissal of the Maslov/Shakhnovich line withdrawn.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Pointer only — extract documented working concentration and LOD intervals for the single assay class whose regime is best documented, and see whether the resulting boundary interval is narrower than a decade in Kd. If it is not, the union has no informative edges and the question's quantitative limbs are not yet answerable.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not applicable — not rejected. The canonical question is not asked-but-open; restricted siblings (AP-MS-detectable interactome in one cell line; Y2H systematic vs sampling false negatives; detection-threshold effects in a model proteome) were asked and partly answered, which is a close-neighbour finding, not a routing case.
