Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. R. H. Zhang, S. Dey, A. Mishra, H. Wu, B. Li, R. Zhang, "Batch Speculative Decoding Done Right", arXiv:2510.22876v1 (opened, html). Unit: greedy completions on Vicuna/Qwen3/GLM4. Endpoint: exact match ("full-sequence equivalence with non-speculative decoding") and partial match. Comparator: Table 1 carries BOTH arms — Spec-1 vs non-spec batch 1 (97.1/94.6/96.0% exact; production rows vLLM+Spec 96.9, SGLang+EAGLE 69.8/47.7) AND Non-Spec-Batch, target-only at batch 4 vs batch 1 (53.8/92.9/93.3% exact). Estimand: point-estimate mismatch rates attributed to "floating-point non-determinism and argmax tie-breaking". No CI, no test, no KL.
B. vLLM issue #54506, "[RFC]: Batch invariance for speculative decoding needs to cover the forward pass (M=1 vs M=k+1)", 2026-08-31, open, body read verbatim. Unit: bitwise tensor parity and greedy-token parity on SM70/V100 TP4, FP16, 125B MoE with MTP head. Endpoint: verify↔decode bitwise parity, divergent-token index, acceptance rate. Comparator: plain decode (M=1) against the verification pass (M=k+1), explicitly distinguished from the batch-composition axis VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT covers. Estimand: whether parity should be a documented guarantee or an explicit non-guarantee. Corroborated on three further stacks: #41758 (ngram, A100), #53436 (Blackwell: target-logits SHA differs between runs at fixed seed and identical drafts, acceptance CV 14.2%, "final text is stable, throughput is not"), #54785 (XPU MTP k=4: "outputs cycle between 2-3 variants" at temperature 0), #39273.
C. Param Chordiya, "Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware", arXiv:2607.17283v1, 2026-07-19 (opened: abs + html). Unit: ~9,200 tokens per method. Endpoint: chi-squared two-sample test on token-frequency bins (chi2=162.5, dof=200, p=0.976) plus bit-exact greedy agreement on mock models. Comparator: target-only decoding in the same implementation. Estimand: accept/reject of H0 "token distribution under spec decoding equals target-only"; no magnitude, CI, power analysis or baseline-vs-baseline arm. Concludes "the overall output distribution is mathematically identical to sampling the target model alone".
Also recorded: dev.to/marcuswwchen (read in full; 1.2% of 2,000 greedy vLLM outputs differ with a 1B draft, 0.6% with a 3B, a 500-prompt canary flagging an upgrade at 2.1%; attribution asserted, no test, no baseline, unreviewed); arXiv:2410.20247 (the instrument, exposures weight-level only); arXiv:2609.18005 (calibrated instrument with a declared null condition, measures quantization and early exit); arXiv:2605.29979 (component fingerprinting, abs only); arXiv:2601.11580 (speedup only); arXiv:2511.20621 DiFR (opened: honest-config null, "We have not evaluated our approach on other sampling procedures such as speculative decoding"); NeurIPS 2026 #171257 (opened: replicate baseline with bootstrap CI versus between-method gap, on a sibling vLLM switch).
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — A tabulates the candidate's treatment contrast and its composition-varied non-speculative control in one table, on the candidate's own engines, with the candidate's own attributed mechanism; the record had asserted that no source ran the nuisance arm. The remainder is instrumentation only: MMD at non-zero temperature, a permutation null, a CI, a declared yardstick, and request-mix rather than batch-size variation. On A's point estimates the excess (i)−(ii) is <= 0 on every pair reported (adversary 1's own arithmetic on A's figures, labelled as such). vs B — B is the candidate's question, including its treatment/nuisance decomposition (M-axis as treatment, cross-request composition as nuisance) and its normative payload, asked in the engine-maintainer vocabulary the Gate 2 sweep never searched; its units are bitwise and token-parity, not a distance, so the estimand is not answered there. vs C — C asks and answers the canonical first limb in the candidate's own field and own words with a hypothesis test and no magnitude. The record's escape hatch from C, that C "sampled in float32 on CPU" and so removes the GPU channel, is STRUCK: adversary 2 checked the abstract and found a device-agnostic CUDA/MPS/CPU implementation on an Apple-silicon laptop with a quantized Metal backend, so what is verifiable is only that C is single-stream and not a production engine. Deleting that hatch makes the rejection stronger, not weaker.
Novelty confidence: Medium (raised from Low at post-batch verification; the Gate 2 near-duplicate finding does not survive a read of the paper, which asks one limb and answers it as a non-rejection at an unstated resolution, on a laptop with a hand-rolled engine). The grade no longer carries the rejection: the entry is rejected at Gate 4 on attack 4, not on novelty. Not above Medium: the question is posed in its own field and own words by an open RFC on the candidate's own engine, and a weak late search negative (titles only, no issue trackers read) cannot raise it further.
Significance — consequence: If the excess is non-zero and of the reported order (~1-3% of greedy outputs), every offline evaluation run through a non-speculative path measures a different sampler from the one served, and a model-equality audit would flag a provider as serving a changed model when it had only enabled a documented-lossless optimization — so the auditing instrument's false-positive rate depends on an unmeasured quantity. If indistinguishable from the composition baseline, the vendor claim is vindicated as served and harnesses need not match the serving path. Weakened by what the adversaries opened: if batch size alone flips 7-46% of greedy sequences while the spec switch flips ~3%, the spec channel is the minor one inside an envelope practitioners already treat as real.
Significance — audience: Model-equality auditors and inference-verification builders (arXiv:2410.20247, DiFR, IMMACULATE); evaluation-harness maintainers; serving-engine maintainers, who are being asked to settle exactly this in #54506 ("Should verify↔decode bitwise parity be an explicitly documented guarantee ... or an explicit non-guarantee"); teams running offline-to-online qualification. Audience real and demonstrably acting — which is also why the question is not unasked.
Significance — fecundity: Whether prefix-cache hits, tensor-parallel degree, chunked prefill and continuous-batching scheduling form a channel family with a common nuisance envelope; whether an engine can ship a measured, bounded residual alongside a losslessness claim; whether the sampler-testing tradition (Barbarik lineage) transfers to LLM decoding paths to give engine CI a formal fidelity test rather than a greedy-equality smoke test.
Significance — anchoring: Batch invariance and serving reproducibility; model-equality testing and inference verification; eval validity and the benchmark noise floor; the live contradiction between C's null and the practitioner 1.2%; this ledger's UQ-20261016-06, whose fecundity field named speculative decoding as the next channel — so this is a derived question of an existing Provisional entry.
Reason for silence: Not applicable as stated — the question is not silent. Voiced in vendor documentation, answered in a preprint, answered differently in practitioner writing, and as of 2026-08/09 raised as an open vLLM RFC plus four corroborating issues. The record's offered mechanism (losslessness treated as settled by theorem, measurement budget spent where the credit is, method-owning communities sharing no venue with kernel engineers) explains why answering well is unrewarded, not why no one asked — the failure mode the gate names. The one sourced near-mechanism is a tooling boundary: DiFR states verbatim it skipped speculative decoding because "vLLM version 0.10.0 does not yet support it", which defers the measurement, not the question.

- P1 (arXiv:2607.17283, Chordiya) — numbers CONFIRMED, status as near-duplicate REFUTED. Its figures are right: a two-sample chi-squared of 162.5 on 200 degrees of freedom, p = 0.976, over 201 frequency bins binned so every expected count is at least 5, on 9,209 speculative against 9,214 baseline tokens from 100 prompts of 100 tokens at temperature 1.0. But FIVE features that would make it this candidate's study are absent: no deviation magnitude with a confidence interval or standard error; no power analysis or minimum detectable effect; no permutation or bootstrap null; NO baseline-versus-baseline arm, so it never compares two non-speculative runs with each other; and no calibration against effect sizes the field treats as findings. Its own limitations say "All results are single-stream, batch-size-one, on one consumer machine;" and "The sampled-leg equivalence test has the statistical resolution of about 9,200 tokens per method". Its engine is a from-scratch implementation on an Apple-silicon laptop, and the sentence concluding identity is a THEORETICAL claim about the marginal process. It also discounts its own KL figure: "the reported smoothed symmetric KL (0.471) is dominated by add-0.5 smoothing". So it is a non-rejection at a resolution it does not state, not an answer.
- P2 (arXiv:2510.22876, "Correctness Forensics for Batch Speculative Decoding: Diagnosing the Ragged Tensor Problem") — CONFIRMED, and it carries a datum that reframes the whole question. Table 1 gives same-engine spec-on against spec-off exact-match rates: vLLM+Spec 96.9 (Vicuna), 65.6 (Qwen3), 72.7 (GLM4); SGLang+EAGLE 69.8 and 47.7; SGLang+EAGLE+Deterministic 85.0 and 50.6. It ALSO carries a non-speculative batched control, Non-Spec-Batch at batch 4: 53.8 on Vicuna, 92.9 on Qwen3, 93.3 on GLM4. On Vicuna the NON-speculative batch-composition control (53.8) therefore diverges far more than the speculative contrast (96.9) — the nuisance is larger than the treatment. Every figure is a single-run point estimate with no test, interval or repeated-run variance, while the paper's own account of residual divergence is floating-point non-determinism, so no noise floor is established; and the only engine-against-itself comparison under varied batch size is a THROUGHPUT figure, not an agreement one.
- vLLM RFC 54506 — CONFIRMED verbatim and open. Title: "[RFC]: Batch invariance for speculative decoding needs to cover the forward pass (M=1 vs M=k+1)". It states "nothing in the current stack guarantees those two produce identical bits" and "At temperature 0, enabling speculative decoding can change the generated sequence relative to plain decoding.", and asks that "the target model's verify pass over rows `[t..t+k]` must reproduce, bit for bit, what plain `M=1` decode would produce". No maintainer has ruled; the only two responders are non-maintainers, so it evidences a believed gap under discussion, not a conceded one. Its own control experiment is the most useful thing in it: two launches of the NON-speculative engine differed by up to 5.25 nats in logits while producing identical 64-token greedy output. Metadata beyond the number and title COULD NOT BE READ — this session's GitHub access is scoped to one repository and the issue page's markdown drops its header.
- The two purpose-built instruments both exclude this axis, CONFIRMED. arXiv:2410.20247 (Model Equality Testing) uses a Hamming string kernel with a median 77.4% power at about 10 samples per prompt over 25 prompts, and evaluates quantization (nf4, int8, fp16 against fp32), watermarking, finetuning, substitution of 13 other models and 31 real API endpoints; speculative decoding, batch size, concurrency, engine version and kernel choice are absent from 98% of its text as read. arXiv:2511.20621 (DiFR) states "We have not evaluated our approach on other sampling procedures such as speculative decoding" and "We do not evaluate speculative decoding scenarios," citing lack of vLLM 0.10.0 support, with Appendix F a sketch carrying no experiments.
- Late Gate 4, survey A (Disguise) — WEAK SEARCH NEGATIVE, so Disguise is Partial and not a rejection ground. Nine searches and four fetches found no study reporting the excess over a composition-matched baseline with an interval, and nothing applying a two-sample distributional test to a serving-stack axis with speculation as the treatment. One near miss it did open: arXiv:2609.04748, "Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving", which does run a serving-stack axis (prefix cache on or off) against a disabled-cache repeat baseline — 36.2% trajectory change at 16-bit against 75.0% at 4-bit — but at batch size one, serially, with no speculation. The survey disclosed its own limits in terms: most results were titles only, no issue tracker or maintainer blog was read, so this is "not found" rather than "does not exist".
- Late Gate 4, survey B (presupposition and significance) — UNRESOLVED ON ATTACK 4, and this is now the rejection. The candidate's estimand is the excess of speculation-on deviation over a composition-matched speculation-off baseline. That baseline cannot be held fixed: enabling speculation submits k+1 query rows per request where decoding submits one, which changes the kernel path and reduction order even for a request alone in its batch, and the accepted-token count varies per request, so trajectories, context lengths and co-residency drift apart across the two arms in a data-dependent way. Composition is therefore a POST-TREATMENT variable on the path speculation to shape to output, and matching on it is matching on a mediator. In exact arithmetic the algorithmic effect is zero by the sampling proof, so every observed deviation is a numerics-through-shape effect and the direct algorithmic component is not identified in a production engine at all. The same survey establishes two further things. The literature does distinguish algorithmic from served losslessness, so the candidate's framing is fair: P1 separates bit-exact greedy comparison as "a backend property" and ran its greedy leg on an fp32 CPU backend because bit-exactness on its quantized backend was unattainable. And the significance branch weakens: where the nuisance exceeds the treatment, the result is not a null about speculation but a statement about the instrument's resolution, because a null needs power and an equivalence margin and the candidate declares neither.

Scores: Well-posedness 1/3 · Significance 2/3 (well-posedness lowered from 2/3 at the late Gate 4: the central estimand is not identified, because the quantity it conditions on is changed by the treatment)
Strongest remaining objection: the estimand is not identified — attack 4, Unresolved at the late Gate 4, and this is the rejection. "Excess deviation net of a composition-matched non-speculative baseline" requires batch composition to be holdable fixed across the two arms, and it is not: speculation submits k+1 query rows per request where decoding submits one, changing the kernel path and reduction order even for a request alone in its batch, and the per-request accepted-token count varies, so trajectories, context lengths and co-residency diverge in a data-dependent way. Composition is a post-treatment mediator on the path from speculation to output, so matching on it is matching on a mediator and the residual is not an effect of speculation. The 2510.22876 figures make the same point from the data: its non-speculative batch control agrees with itself on 53.8% of Vicuna outputs while its speculative contrast agrees on 96.9%, so the nuisance is larger than the treatment and no amount of subtraction recovers a clean quantity. For the record, the Gate 2 and first-pass Gate 4 ground is WITHDRAWN: the own-field near-duplicate asks one limb and answers it as a non-rejection at a resolution it does not state, on a laptop with a hand-rolled engine, and the late Disguise sweep was a weak search negative by its own account.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not as posed, because the quantity is not identified. The identified question in this space is the one the RFC itself poses and nobody has measured: hold the input fixed and compare the target model's forward pass over k+1 verification rows against the same model's M=1 decode pass on the same prefix, teacher-forced, under varied co-resident load — that is a shape contrast at fixed input, not a composition-matched contrast, so it has an estimand. Reconciling arXiv:2607.17283's null with arXiv:2510.22876's non-zero mismatch rates on one pinned stack is worth doing in passing, but it inherits the same identification problem the moment it runs through a scheduler.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): routed, but NARROWED at the late Gate 4, because a question the ledger's own Gate 4 has shown to be non-identifiable is not routable as posed. The rejection ground is no longer Gate 2 novelty — that fell on a first-hand read — but attack 4: composition is a post-treatment mediator, so the "excess over a composition-matched baseline" has no estimand in a production engine. What IS identified, asked, and unmeasured is the narrower forward-pass parity question the vLLM RFC poses in its own title: whether the target model's verify pass over k+1 rows reproduces bit for bit what plain M=1 decode produces on the same prefix, at fixed input. That is the row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md, and the broad composition-matched version is explicitly not.

ID: UQ-20261017-27
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — distributed training systems (secondary: scaling methodology). Method transplanted from industrial metrology (variance components / gauge R&R).
Question (canonical): For one pretraining recipe at a scale where several parallelism configurations are feasible, run a crossed design of C ≥ 3 configurations × S ≥ 3 seeds — holding global batch size, global-batch membership and order, seed, numeric formats and token count fixed, and restricting C in advance to a matchable set of changes that provably do not alter the mathematical objective (excluding e.g. Megatron-LM #7464 vocab-parallel label smoothing on the local vocabulary, #1754 non-divisible vocab) — what are the between-configuration and between-seed variance components with confidence intervals, what interval covers σ²_config/σ²_seed for (a) held-out loss at fixed token count and (b) each member of a pre-registered downstream metric set, is the upper confidence limit of that ratio below 1 (the invariance verdict), and which axis (rank count, micro-batch count, sharding style) carries any excess?
Alternative formulations: (1) Is "same recipe, different GPU layout" the same experiment, and by how much is it not? (2) How much of the difference between two training runs is attributable to how the run was sharded rather than to the recipe? (3) The elastic-training literature ships a binary "accuracy consistency" predicate — what is the magnitude behind it, and where does it sit relative to seed noise?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion on the knob every distributed-training paper treats as throughput-only. The field already disbelieves invariance and still does not measure it: FlexTrain (MLSys 2026) names "accuracy inconsistency" as why elastic training has little production use and offers DP scaling only "when accuracy consistency is relaxed"; NVIDIA NeMo-RL's DTensor guide reports reward-model validation loss 0.6035/0.6010/0.5864/0.6021 at TP=1/2/4/8 (n=1 per TP, no seeds, no interval), attributing it to partition/aggregation order and FP non-associativity; Tenplex (arXiv:2312.05181) asserts "the convergence of the DL job is unaffected" from eyeballed curves, one run per arm. Adversary #2 independently re-established the mechanism from NVIDIA's Megatron-core determinism glossary, which scopes bitwise determinism to a *fixed* "parallelism layout (TP, PP, DP, EP, CP, VPP)" and defines no cross-layout tolerance at all. The retrospective/disclosure limb is demoted to a labelled secondary: (Mis)Fitting (arXiv:2502.18969), opened, reports no parallelism or hardware disclosure rate and no device counts.
Presuppositions: (1) Non-invariance mechanisms real in deployed stacks — ESTABLISHED (NeMo-RL guide; Megatron-LM #1754/#7464; NVIDIA determinism glossary). (2) A layout change can be made holding seed, data order, batch and formats fixed — CONTESTED and now worse than the record stated: Megatron's `megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py` keys RNG streams to `tp_rank` (`tensor_model_parallel_seed = seed + 2718 + tp_rank`; default state "different across different model parallel groups"), so for any dropout-bearing recipe a TP/DP change also re-draws realised randomness. (3) Seed divergence is an appropriate yardstick — CONTESTED; the seed floor is itself layout-dependent (DeepSpeed #5717: identical loss curves across seeds under multi-GPU ZeRO), so it must be estimated within each configuration, as the crossed design does. (4) Divergence does not self-cancel over training — OPEN; both endpoints measured for this reason. (5) Published ladders change parallelism with scale and disclose enough to tell — CONTESTED, disclosure half answered negatively; secondary limb only. (6) Not UQ-20261016-53 in new clothes — HELD on the primary estimand (unit: training run vs published claim; endpoint: loss/downstream vs column estimability; comparator: within-configuration seed component vs alias threshold; estimand: variance ratio from new runs vs literature share). Adjacency checked against UQ-20261016-06, -49, -30, UQ-20261017-06, UQ-20261015-25; no duplicate.
What would count as an answer: A crossed C × S paired experiment with the matchable set held fixed, reporting σ²_config, σ²_seed and an interval on their ratio for held-out loss at fixed token count and for each pre-registered downstream metric; invariant iff the ratio's upper confidence limit is below 1 on all endpoints, otherwise the magnitude plus the axis decomposition (rank count vs micro-batch count vs sharding style), per endpoint. Secondary and labelled: the disclosure rate of per-rung parallelism in published scaling ladders.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 web queries + 5 fetches + 2 GitHub issue searches; 18 further adversary queries (9 + 9) in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use, with 8 further fetches. Most informative: "reproducibility of LLM training under different parallelism configurations…" (own-field own-words title form → nothing on *training*; only inference-side analogues arXiv:2511.17826, arXiv:2506.09501); "same global batch size different number of GPUs final model accuracy differs" (→ VirtualFlow, the nearest prior, plus informal practitioner threads); "gauge repeatability reproducibility ANOVA variance components … computational experiment" (method-owning vocabulary → only Six Sigma pedagogy; clean negative); "numerical reproducibility results depend on number of MPI ranks reduction order climate ensemble consistency test" (mature named problem family in HPC/climate, never transplanted); "elastic training changing parallelism degree mid-run convergence equivalence" (→ Tenplex, ElasWave, DynaTrain, LiveR, FlexTrain: the genre whose central correctness claim *is* this invariance); adversary additions: "Nondeterminism and Instability in Neural Network Optimization" (→ Summers & Dinneen ICML 2021), "Randomness in Neural Network Training: tooling" (→ Zhuang et al. MLSys 2022), Chinese-language 切分策略/loss 对齐 (→ arXiv:2602.14462), deterministic-reduction vocabulary (→ DASH ICLR 2026; NVIDIA determinism glossary), "accuracy-consistent elastic training" (→ EasyScale arXiv:2208.14228, UNREAD). Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-1128/UQ-20261017-27-record.md and UQ-20261017-27-adversary-1.md / -adversary-2.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 VirtualFlow (arxiv.org/pdf/2009.09523, opened; unit = one job per hardware configuration, n=1; endpoint = final validation accuracy; comparator = a literature target within an asserted ±0.5%; estimand = closeness to target; reports top-1 75.68–76.01 across six configurations at global batch 8192). P2 Tenplex (arxiv.org/pdf/2312.05181, SOSP 2024, opened; unit = one job reconfigured at step 100; endpoint = loss trajectory; comparator = same job without a change; estimand = a qualitative invariance predicate judged from Fig. 16). P3 FlexTrain (MLSys 2026; abstract at mlsys.org/virtual/2026/oral/3776, body READ IN FULL at post-batch verification through the proceedings PDF; unit = a real LLM training job on a cluster of 1,000-plus eight-GPU Hopper machines, three MoE models from 1B to 30B active, elastic over 32 to 1,024 GPUs; endpoint = throughput, predicted-versus-measured speedup, scaling overhead and job completion time, plus a training-loss overlay as a consistency check; comparator = no-scaling baseline against scaling-PP and scaling-DP; estimand = a binary type-level consistency predicate, "FlexTrain provides accuracy consistency if only adjusting the degree of PP.", with NO final-model metric of any kind and no replicates or seeds). Adversary additions, opened: Summers & Dinneen (arXiv:2103.04514, ICML 2021 — unit = one CNN run; endpoint = accuracy SD over ~100 runs; factors = init/shuffle/cuDNN/single-bit flip; hardware fixed at two V100s, parallelism not varied) and Zhuang et al. (arXiv:2106.11872, MLSys 2022 — ALGO vs IMPL noise, churn 14.68% vs 14.89%, scope "a non-distributed setting", distributed training named as future work). PolyPythias (arXiv:2503.09543), opened by adversary #1: seeds varied, layout not reported or held, no ANOVA — a seed-only yardstick, not a prior on the estimand. COULD NOT READ: EasyScale arXiv:2208.14228, OPEN-1B arXiv:2609.17380, full text of arXiv:2408.05148, Megatron-core deterministic-training page; Megatron/DeepSpeed issues could not be re-opened by adversary #2 (`issue_read` denied for that repo).
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same measured object (accuracy across device counts at fixed global batch) but differs on comparator (literature target, not the within-configuration seed component), estimand (tolerance closeness, not a variance ratio with an interval), design (n=1, so its ~0.33-point spread cannot be separated from run-to-run noise — the exact comparison this candidate exists to make) and treatment axis (device count/type under a layer built to erase the effect, not crossed sharding style and micro-batch count). vs P2 — same treatment factor and endpoint family, opposite posture: asserts invariance as its own system's correctness property from one run per arm; its comparator cannot answer "is the change smaller than the seed". vs P3 — converts the question into a design constraint (change PP, not DP) and routes around it; endpoint is throughput, consistency a binary predicate. vs Summers & Dinneen / Zhuang — the right *contrast* (one noise source against another) in the wrong regime: CNN-scale, non-distributed, parallelism degree never a factor, no variance components, no intervals; they constrain the expected answer without supplying it. vs UQ-20261016-49 — same comparator architecture, non-overlapping treatment factor (numeric format vs parallelism layout): precedent, not duplication. vs UQ-20261016-53 — disjoint on all four attributes for the primary estimand; the overlapping ladder/disclosure limb stays secondary.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: Invariant ⇒ the field's eyeballed regression-test practice is calibrated for the first time: framework teams get a published tolerance for "loss curves match" gates, cross-configuration comparisons become defensible, FlexTrain's "relaxed consistency" tier can be declared free. Not invariant ⇒ every comparison whose arms differ in layout carries a treatment-correlated nuisance factor, biting hardest where layout moves with the treatment (scaling ladders; recipe ablations run at one sharding and shipped as general advice), and release notes asserting "no convergence impact" become unquantified claims. The axis decomposition says what to fix: micro-batch count → fixed accumulation tree; rank count → deterministic collectives; sharding style → the invariance claim must be weakened in the frameworks' own docs.
Significance — audience: (i) Framework teams (Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, TorchTitan, MaxText, NeMo) — NVIDIA has already shipped a determinism developer guide with tiers, golden values "compared bit-exactly by DeterministicTest" and a determinism certificate, built up to the edge of this question and defining no cross-layout tolerance. (ii) Elastic-training researchers, who currently ship a binary predicate or an eyeballed curve as their correctness argument. (iii) Scaling-law practitioners, who would have to report per-rung parallelism. (iv) Reproducibility methodologists assembling a total error budget, who hold the seed term (PolyPythias, Signal-and-Noise) and the inference term (UQ-20261016-06) and no training-layout term.
Significance — fecundity: Does the component grow with scale (large ladders worse than they look)? Is it monotone in rank count? Does it concentrate on one axis, so one invariant-collective change buys invariance? What does bitwise-invariant *training* cost in throughput (DASH reports up to 37.9% for a deterministic backward pass; Zhuang et al. up to 746% for determinism)? Should the layout be part of a model's identity for reproducibility claims? Does the component predict downstream rank reordering at equal loss? Is the seed floor itself layout-dependent (DeepSpeed #5717), making "seed variance" a per-layout quantity?
Significance — anchoring: Elastic-training consistency claims (Tenplex, FlexTrain, ElasWave's 0.2% loss deviation, DynaTrain, LiveR, EasyScale); NeMo-RL's DTensor TP accuracy guide; NVIDIA's Megatron-core determinism glossary and rank-keyed RNG; Megatron-LM #1754/#7464/#5176/#1494; the gradient-accumulation normalisation defect family; batch-invariant inference (arXiv:2506.09501) and deterministic inference across TP sizes (arXiv:2511.17826) — the inference side has a literature, the training side does not. In-ledger: UQ-20261016-49, -06, -53.
Reason for silence: A definitional move plus a disciplinary boundary with an incentive gap. The vendor defined the question out of scope: NVIDIA's determinism contract classes the parallelism layout as part of "everything else held constant", so a cross-layout difference is an expected non-event rather than an open quantity, and because the framework's RNG is rank-keyed practitioners can treat a cross-layout comparison as a different random draw — meaningless rather than unanswered. The systems community owns the knob but needs only a pass/fail gate (one run per arm, compared by eye) and a null result is unpublishable for a throughput paper; the ML-science community varies seeds but treats layout as scheduler infrastructure, so it never enters the design matrix; the method that would settle it belongs to a third field (metrology variance components; climate/HPC processor-count ensemble-consistency testing) whose vocabulary has never been pointed at training runs. Qualification from Gate 4: the *asking* half is weaker than the record claimed — Zhuang et al. (MLSys 2022) names parallelism as the suspected driver of implementation noise and distributed training as future work, and FlexTrain names the unmeasured quantity as its motivation.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand): seven checks ran on this entry's priors and on the four unread titles its own promotion condition named. The verdict does not move, promotion item (1) is discharged in full, and two priors closer than anything in the record were read for the first time.
- Promotion item (1) is DISCHARGED. All four named items, plus FlexTrain's body, were opened, and not one of them reports per-configuration replicates against a within-configuration seed floor. EasyScale (arXiv:2208.14228, "EasyScale: Accuracy-consistent Elastic Training for Deep Learning", SC '23) — READ AT FULL TEXT, and a CLOSER prior than any in the record: it claims exactly this entry's invariance, in bitwise terms ("producing bitwise-consistent models regardless of different numbers and types of GPUs allocated"; "elastic training should generate model parameters bitwise identical compared to the data parallel training"), with three determinism levels (D0 fixed-DoP, D1 elasticity, D2 heterogeneity). But its evidence is single-run TRAIN-LOSS curves over 100 mini-batches per stage across three scripted stages, one run per configuration, with seeds deliberately FIXED and never varied ("we fix the random seeds of RNGs at the beginning of the training"), and only two of its eight models plotted. No bitwise parameter diff, no tolerance band, no replicates, no seed-to-seed figure. Its mechanism inventory is the most complete in anything read here and the record should adopt it: rank-keyed RNG streams, reduction and aggregation order, kernel selection, BatchNorm rank dependence, data-loader ordering, per-GPU batch scaling. OPEN-1B (arXiv:2609.17380) — REFUTED as a prior: one released run on a single global seed of 42, varying only data-parallel node count from 1 to 6, reporting throughput and efficiency only, with bit-exactness across device counts ASSERTED rather than measured; its two runs per configuration differ in whether state hashing was on, so they are throughput repeats, not training replicates. arXiv:2408.05148 — REFUTED as a prior: its single trained-model experiment is a two-layer SAGEConv graph network on Cora, one GPU, fixed seed, and its distributed-setting remarks are untested assertions. The Megatron-core deterministic-training page — SILENCE, not a guarantee: it promises run-to-run bit-exactness for "identical inputs", never defines that scope, and never mentions changing tensor, pipeline or data-parallel sizes, device count or micro-batch count (the words seed, random, rank and data-parallel do not appear). It does name the mechanisms that break bit-exactness: NCCL Tree reduction order, fused cross-entropy, tensor-parallel communication overlap, Transformer-Engine kernel selection.
- FlexTrain (MLSys 2026) — READ AT FULL TEXT for the first time, through the proceedings PDF, and it is the CLOSEST thing in print to this entry's question, at production scale. Unit: a real LLM training job on a cluster of more than 1,000 machines of eight Hopper GPUs each, on three mixture-of-experts models (1B active / 7B total; 6B/60B; 30B/600B) scaled elastically from 32 to 1,024 GPUs. Its consistency claim is a BINARY, TYPE-LEVEL predicate rather than a measured quantity: "FlexTrain provides accuracy consistency if only adjusting the degree of PP." and, in a table caption, "FlexTrain achieves bitwise consistent accuracy when scaling PP, but not when scaling DP+PP." The mechanism is structural — pipeline parallelism "inherently preserves consistency in model weights and activations" through "the maintenance of an identical accumulation order", while for data-parallel changes "accuracy consistency cannot be guaranteed". The evidence is one 200-iteration training-loss overlay at the 1B-active scale ("the loss curves of baseline and scaling-PP are exactly identical") plus two unlabelled relative-difference plots at the two larger scales. DECISIVE: it reports NO final-model metric of any kind — no validation loss, no accuracy, no perplexity, no downstream benchmark — and no replicated runs, no seeds and no variance. So its own scaling-DP loss gap of about 0.031 at 200 iterations is a configuration-to-configuration difference with no seed floor to compare it against. That is this entry's question, unanswered, in print, at the largest scale anyone has published.
- P1 VirtualFlow (arXiv:2009.09523) — CONFIRMED, with one correction the record must take. All six top-1 figures are right (75.92, 75.96, 75.99, 75.83 and 75.68 on 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 V100s, and 76.01 on two RTX 2080Ti) at a fixed global batch of 8192 against a literature target of 76.26; so is the absence of seeds, repeated runs, standard deviations and intervals; and so is the treatment axis being device count and type rather than sharding style or micro-batch count. The correction: the ±0.5% tolerance is stated as reproducing "the target accuracy for all runs (±0.5%)" against a target given loosely as 76%, not against the tabulated 76.26 — and the 16-GPU result of 75.68 sits 0.58 below 76.26, outside ±0.5 if centred there. VirtualFlow must not be cited as supplying a statistically derived tolerance. For scale, its own naive baseline, batch scaled with device count and nothing retuned, gives 69.25, 67.30, 70.68 and 73.04.
- P2 Tenplex (arXiv:2312.05181) — CONFIRMED verbatim. "the convergence of the DL job is unaffected." appears in the Introduction under item "(2) Transforming DL job state", and the section supporting it rests on three qualitative loss-curve panels with no replication, no numbers and no variance.
- Net effect on novelty: Medium stands, and is better founded than the record's version of it. Two priors now claim this entry's invariance outright, which is why it cannot grade higher. But both claim it as an engineering guarantee they BUILT, evidenced by coinciding loss curves in single fixed-seed runs, and neither measures a configuration effect against a seed floor. The entry's own estimand — how large the configuration-to-configuration difference is relative to the seed-to-seed difference the field already tolerates — is unoccupied by every source any agent on this record has opened.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3
Strongest remaining objection: The canonical estimand does not measure the quantity its own motivation names. Summers & Dinneen (ICML 2021, opened) find a single flipped weight bit yields run-to-run variability within 20% relative of random-seed variability, and Zhuang et al. (MLSys 2022, opened) find implementation noise from parallel FP accumulation order — the exact named mechanism — statistically indistinguishable from algorithmic noise and non-additive with an apparent ceiling; so any layout change that is not bitwise neutral is expected to behave as a seed re-roll, landing in the config×seed interaction that Version B omits, and "UCL(σ²_config/σ²_seed) < 1" would read "invariant" precisely in the regime where practitioners experience layout changes as mattering. Both papers are CNN-scale and non-distributed, so this is a strong prior and not a proof — which is why it is Partial rather than fatal.
Promotion requires: (1) DISCHARGED at post-batch verification: EasyScale (arXiv:2208.14228), OPEN-1B (arXiv:2609.17380), arXiv:2408.05148, the Megatron-core deterministic-training page and FlexTrain's body were all opened, and none reports per-configuration replicates against a within-configuration seed floor. The Disguise sweep is now complete on its named items, and the record must cite EasyScale and FlexTrain as the two nearest priors — both claim this invariance and neither measures it; (2) restating the estimand to report σ²_config, σ²_config×seed and σ²_seed with a per-configuration mean-shift test against a seed-based SE, and raising the design floor (≈C=5 × S=10) so the pre-registered "invariant" branch is actually reachable — these two restore well-posedness to 3/3; (3) tightening the matchable set to exclude rank-keyed RNG re-draws (dropout-free recipe plus a materialised init checkpoint and fixed stream assignment), so σ²_config is a layout effect rather than a second seed. With (1)–(3) and novelty still ≥ Medium on re-search, the entry is promotable to Validated; VirtualFlow remains the close neighbour that keeps novelty at Medium.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Settle the specification before any run — fix a dropout-free recipe with a materialised initial checkpoint, enumerate the matchable set with an operational bitwise-neutrality test per axis, and compute the design size at which the pre-registered interval can fall below 1 on both branches.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected. The weaker engineering form (does layout change the outcome, and by how much) is asked and open in the systems literature, but the stated estimand is not, so nothing is routed; if (1)–(3) are not met on the next pass, the Zhuang et al. future-work item and FlexTrain's motivation are the sources to route on.

Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — training systems and optimization (batch formation, batch-size selection, gradient-noise-scale instrumentation). Method transplanted from complex-survey statistics (cluster-sample design effect, Kish effective sample size). Source method: cross-field transplant.
Question (canonical): At a fixed pretraining checkpoint theta, what is the design effect deff(theta, B) of a stack's shipped batch formation (shard assignment + shuffle buffer + rank sharding) — the variance of the minibatch gradient's scalar projection on the full-corpus gradient direction under the real sampling scheme divided by the same variance under i.i.d.-with-replacement resampling of the same corpus at identical nominal B, the two arms differing in nothing but design — what within-batch gradient ICC rho does it imply under deff = 1 + (m-1)rho for a declared m, does multiplying tr(Sigma) by deff move B_simple = tr(Sigma)/|G|^2 and the critical-batch-size prescription past a pre-registered band (NULL <= 1.1 / MODEST 1.1-2 / MATERIAL > 2), and is the correction stable across checkpoints and shuffle-buffer sizes? (V1, the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V0 and the reason for reformulating are in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) How much does shard-and-shuffle-buffer clustering inflate pretraining gradient variance, and does the inflation bias the batch-size rules read off measured gradient noise? (2) What is the design-corrected effective batch size of a large pretraining run — how many i.i.d. examples is a nominal batch of B worth? (3) When a GNS tracker reports B_simple, is it reporting the noise of the run's actual sampling design or of a counterfactual i.i.d. one?
Motivating gap: Survey methodology corrects clustered sampling with deff = 1 + (m-1)rho; pretraining has the structure and not the correction. McCandlish et al. (arXiv:1812.06162, opened) defines B_simple/B_noise and states in fn. 6 that Sigma/B "is strictly true only when training examples are sampled independently from the same data distribution", adds that the conclusions "can be altered straightforwardly to account for correlated samples", and does not carry it out. Merrill et al. (arXiv:2505.23971, opened) finds "the gradient noise scale underestimates the CBS by several orders of magnitude" without touching sampling design; Gray et al. (arXiv:2411.00999, opened) ships a production GNS tracker driving a batch-size schedule and records "Changes in the batch size do not have the predicted effect".
Presuppositions: (1) real loaders cluster-sample — FLAGGED at Gate 2, no loader source read; FALSIFIED at Gate 4 for the flagship open stacks (adversary 1, E1); (2) attribute clustering implies gradient-space clustering — CONTESTED, measured directly by V1, unmeasured anywhere; (3) the noise-scale variance term is estimable and its i.i.d. assumption load-bearing — ESTABLISHED from 1812.06162 fn. 6 / Eqs. 2.8-2.9 / App. A.1; (4) deff is well defined for a vector estimator — DISCHARGED by the declared scalarization; (5) batch-size decisions are taken from measured GNS — ESTABLISHED (arXiv:2411.00999) but contracting (P3); (6) the i.i.d. ideal is the right comparator — CONTESTED, and broken at Gate 4 (adversary 2, Finding B).
What would count as an answer: on >= 2 open stacks and >= 1 corpus, at >= 3 checkpoints: (a) deff and implied rho from two arms differing only in sampling design at frozen theta, bootstrap intervals; (b) design-corrected vs uncorrected B_simple, and the share of P3's GNS-to-CBS gap it closes; (c) implied prescribed-batch-size change, i.e. B/deff in i.i.d.-equivalent units; (d) stability across checkpoints and buffer sizes. deff indistinguishable from 1 at stated power is a publishable null. No retraining required.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand, then a late Gate 4 of two literature surveys): four checks and two surveys ran. BOTH fatal grounds FALL - attack 2's disguised-known and attack 4's sign claim - so the entry moves from Rejected to Provisional, capped by a newly sourced attack 6.
- h_D is a BOUND, not the candidate's quantity, so attack 2 falls to Partial. The definitional quotes are confirmed verbatim: "we use the factor h D to characterize the upper bound of a block-wise data variance" (Sec. 4.2), "h D is an essential parameter to measure the 'cluster' effect within the original data blocks", "Therefore, the larger h D , the more 'clustered' the data.", with h_D = 1 (fully shuffled) and h_D = b (fully clustered) given as hypothetical extremes and h_D carrying the rate term in Theorems 1 and 2 and the definition of beta. But across all three papers there is NO numeric value, table or plot of h_D for any dataset and NO measured gradient variance; "gradient noise scale", "critical batch size" and "large-batch training" do not occur anywhere read; and no workload is an LLM pretraining run (CorgiPile: higgs, susy, epsilon, criteo, yfcc, cifar-10, ImageNet, yelp-review-full; the VLDBJ adds YearPredictionMSD and mini8m; Corgi^2 uses proprietary Mobileye crops, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet). Corgi^2's h'_D = 1 + (1/n - 1/(nb))h_D is confirmed. The explicit comparator the adversary leaned on is also version-dependent: "the common assumption is that data is sampled uniformly and independently with replacement in each epoch" is in the VLDBJ extension, while "uniformly and independently with replacement" does not occur in the arXiv/SIGMOD version at all (Corgi^2 writes "(i.i.d with replacement)"). So the field owns the vocabulary and a worst-case bound in data space; the candidate asks for a measured gradient-space ratio on a shipped loader, tied to the noise scale. A prior that defines a quantity without measuring it is not a disguised known.
- The deferred-proof route is closed, and one read failed. RESOLVED: the "technical report" the VLDBJ extension defers its proofs to ("Due to the space limitation, we detail the proof of the following theorems in Appendix of our technical report", ref. [46]) IS arXiv:2206.05830 itself, so there is no separate document where a measurement could hide, and both papers describe that appendix as theorem proofs plus Appendix-A I/O micro-benchmarks. h_D occurs ZERO times across Sections 6 to 7.3.2, the whole evaluation range, which is where a measurement would belong. The appendices themselves COULD NOT BE READ: three full-text routes all truncate inside Section 7 (alphaxiv 67,284 chars, ar5iv 64,458, arXiv PDF 73,277) and the raw e-print download is refused at the proxy. That read is Unverified, not a check that passed, and it stays in the promotion condition.
- Attack 4's sign claim is REFUTED, so the second fatal row falls to Partial. The McCandlish equations are confirmed: B_simple = tr(Sigma)/|G|^2 is Eq. (2.9), Sigma is Eq. (2.3), cov(G_est) = Sigma/B is Eq. (2.2), and Appendix A.1 gives (A.1) E[|G_est|^2] = |G|^2 + (1/B)tr(Sigma) with the two estimators of (A.2) and the line "We can verify with Equation A.1 that E[|G|^2] = |G|^2 and E[S] = tr(Sigma)." Footnote 6 is verbatim and is the sixth footnote in the PDF numbering: "This is strictly true only when training examples are sampled independently from the same data distribution." and "but our conclusions can be altered straightforwardly to account for correlated samples." The bias, however, is not signed a priori. Writing h(B) for the ratio of realized to independent per-example variance, the two-batch estimator's bias in |G|^2 is tr(Sigma)(h_b - h_s)/(B_b - B_s): exactly ZERO when h is constant in B (batches spanning many whole clusters, h = 1 + (m-1)rho, the whole effect landing in S instead), POSITIVE when both batches sit inside one cluster, and NEGATIVE for without-replacement or stratified designs (h = 1 - B/D gives -tr(Sigma)/D exactly). The adversary's determinate downward sign holds only under whole-batch exchangeable correlation, and the paper derives no sign at all. So the clause does not break the estimand: which way a given loader biases a reported noise scale is a property of that loader's design, which is the thing the candidate proposes to measure.
- Yin et al. is confirmed and the identification is exact. In arXiv:1706.05699, Definition 5 "B S (w) := n * Delta S (w)", the Appendix B.1 identity B_S = M^2/G, and the sampling statement "each index s i is drawn uniformly at random from [n] with replacement" are all verbatim, and under the uniform-empirical identification B_S = B_simple + 1 exactly. Two caveats: their operative admissible batch size is delta*B_S + 1 with delta a free slack parameter, coinciding only at delta = 1; and B_simple is itself an approximation to B_noise that matches B_crit only to order of magnitude.
- Late Gate 4, survey A (Disguise) - one closer framing prior, still no measurement. scDataset (arXiv:2506.01883) is the closest thing found to the candidate's own framing and was unknown to the record: "Block sampling is equivalent to cluster sampling (Cochran, 1977)", a variance "larger than the IID estimator sigma^2/m by a factor of b", and an effective sample size that "drops from m to B=m/b". But it measures only a proxy - minibatch plate-label entropy, 1.76 +- 0.33 at fetch factor 1 against 3.61 +- 0.08 at f = 256 and about 3.62 for random access, at minibatch 64 - on single-cell data with linear and MLP models, and reports no gradient-variance number. MosaicML Streaming documents py1b/py1br/py1e/py1s/py2s qualitatively with no metric. Nine searches returned titles only for most hits, so this is "not found", not "does not exist".
- Late Gate 4, survey B (significance and estimator algebra) - attack 6 is now the cap, UNRESOLVED and sourced, and non-fatal, so the ceiling is Provisional. The prescription the significance case rested on has been abandoned by the community it names: arXiv:2505.23971v3 states "the noise scale cannot be used reliably as a proxy for the CBS" and that "the gradient noise scale underestimates the CBS by several orders of magnitude" (Sec. 3.3), and sets batch size by empirical branched training instead; Shallue et al. (arXiv:1811.03600) report "We were unable to find reliable support for any of the previously proposed heuristics for adjusting the learning rate as a function of batch size" and tell practitioners to "tune all optimization parameters anew when they change the batch size", never mentioning the noise scale in the portion read and treating sampling as method only ("we actually follow the common practice of cycling through permutations of the training set"). The arithmetic compounds it: on the paper's own cost tradeoff a 1.1x batch-size error moves total cost about 5% and a 2x error 25-50%, so the optimum is flat, while B_crit spans 20 to over 10 million across tasks and a deff of 1.1-2 is 0.04-0.3 orders of magnitude. Neither survey found any published analysis of the noise-scale estimator under correlated sampling; the closest statement in print remains footnote 6's unproved assertion that the conclusions are "straightforward" to adapt.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3 (significance raised from 1/3 at the late Gate 4: the stake relocates from the batch-size prescription, which attack 6 shows the field has abandoned, to the validity of the reported noise scale itself - Appendix A.1's estimator is computed on the real training step's batches, so every published figure is design-effected by a factor nobody has measured, and the bias formula above says the direction is loader-specific. Capped at 2/3 because attack 6 is Unresolved.)
Strongest remaining objection: significance inflation, Unresolved and now sourced. The audiences the record named have moved off the quantity. The critical-batch-size community reports that the noise scale "cannot be used reliably as a proxy for the CBS" and "underestimates the CBS by several orders of magnitude" (arXiv:2505.23971v3, Sec. 3.3) and now sets batch size by branched empirical training; the large-batch literature tells practitioners to "tune all optimization parameters anew when they change the batch size" (arXiv:1811.03600) without reference to a noise scale at all. On the batch-size cost curve a 1.1-2x error in the target moves total cost by roughly 5-50% against a quantity spanning five to six orders of magnitude across tasks, so a deff of 1.1-2 changes no decision anyone is currently taking. What survives is a measurement-validity claim rather than a prescriptive one: a reported noise scale is a statement about an unnamed sampling design. Whether anyone would act on that is exactly what is unresolved. Two secondary objections also stand, unresolved and non-fatal: the flagship open stacks (Megatron-LM `_build_shuffle_index`, OLMo `_build_global_indices`) globally permute, read from source, so the affected population is the streaming and shard-buffer stacks rather than training at large; and the reason-for-silence mechanism is narrower than filed, since two independent literatures already name and bound the inflation (CorgiPile's h_D, scDataset's factor b) and only the measurement is missing.
Promotion requires: (1) resolving attack 6 by naming one decision a factor of 1.1-2 would change - a documented case where shuffle-buffer size or shard granularity was chosen on a variance argument, or a measured loader whose deff is large enough that the flat cost optimum stops protecting it; (2) closing the read that failed, the appendices of arXiv:2206.05830, where three full-text routes truncate inside Section 7 and the e-print download is refused at the proxy (untried: the ACM DL version of the SIGMOD'22 camera-ready), so that "h_D is never measured" rests on a read rather than on its zero occurrences across Sections 6-7.3.2; and (3) reading the three papers still unread from Gates 2 and 4 - arXiv:2609.12584, arXiv:2604.00260, and arXiv:2603.02417 Sections 8-9 - any of which could supply the measurement and move the entry the other way.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only - do not take it): the cheapest decisive move is algebra plus one frozen-checkpoint measurement. Derive h(B) for the shipped two-stage design (shard order, then a shuffle buffer of size S) and evaluate tr(Sigma)(h_b - h_s)/(B_b - B_s) at the actual B_small = per-device, B_big = global pair that Appendix A.1's zero-overhead estimator uses; then measure the two resampling arms at one frozen theta on one open streaming stack, with a global-permutation stack as the deff = 1 control. No retraining, and existing LayerNorm-only per-example-gradient instrumentation suffices.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): WITHDRAWN. The row drafted at Gate 5 is not appended, because the entry is no longer Rejected and a Provisional entry's own question is not routed - routing it would file the ledger's own open candidate in the research queue as an already-asked problem, which it is not. The verification residuals above belong to this entry's promotion condition, not to research.

ID: UQ-20261017-29
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — post-training data layer (curation, mixture design); method from data management (repository-scale redundancy/overlap analysis)
Question (canonical): On a dated, pinned frame F of the public post-training data pool (enumerable snapshot of public instruction-tuning and preference datasets, inclusion rule declared before any pull), under a pre-declared normalization N to a canonical (instruction, [context], response-or-preference-pair) form and a pre-declared ladder of three near-duplicate thresholds t1<t2<t3: (a) what is the example-level cross-dataset duplication graph — pairwise overlap shares, the pool's de-duplicated count |F|_dedup(t) as a curve in t, and the distribution over distinct examples of how many named datasets each appears in; (b) for at least three published mixtures, what are the realized distinct-example proportions of the components against the declared weights under a pre-declared multi-component attribution rule (fractional / first-wins / set-of-origins), with component rank order before and after; and (c) what is the retrievability-adjusted version of (a), stating the unretrievable share of F at the snapshot date?
Alternative formulations: (1) How many distinct post-training examples does the open ecosystem contain, as opposed to how many dataset records it distributes? (2) When a recipe mixes k named datasets at declared proportions, how far are the realized proportions of distinct examples from the declared ones once cross-dataset re-export is removed? (Gate 0 original and the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation are both in the record; the reformulation only pinned F, N, the ladder and the attribution rule.)
Motivating gap: New-instrument question. Hub-scale queryability plus cheap billion-scale near-duplicate detection make the UNION of public post-training datasets addressable as one object, while recipes are published as weighted mixtures of NAMED datasets and the field's dedup effort is within-corpus or against benchmarks. Two leading artefacts attest the re-export phenomenon and decline to quantify it: Data Provenance Initiative §2 ("Some collections have overlapping datasets and examples, but we choose not to deduplicate") and Tulu 3 ("many publicly released datasets are compositions of other datasets, we have to manually track the provenance").
Presuppositions: (1) the pool is enumerable/retrievable as a dated frame — contested in degree, handled by limb (c); (2) "the same example" is definable across differing templates — contested, the main design obligation, handled by declared N plus a threshold ladder; (3) declared mixture weights are meant as weights on distinct content — CONTESTED, conceded, the question reports a bookkeeping discrepancy and imputes no intent; (4) duplication at this level changes training outcomes — NOT ASSUMED, it is the stake; (5) DPI did not already compute example-level cross-dataset overlap — verified by reading the paper; (6) pool-scale near-duplicate detection is feasible — now evidenced by adversary 1 (joint MinHash-LSH at ~180B-token scale, arXiv:2512.18834).
What would count as an answer: On frame F at date T — (a) pairwise cross-dataset overlap shares, |F|_dedup(t) as a curve over t1,t2,t3, and the datasets-per-example multiplicity distribution; (b) for >=3 published mixtures (a Tulu-class SFT mix, a preference mix, a large aggregated collection), realized distinct-example component proportions vs declared weights under the declared attribution rule, with rank order before and after; (c) (a) adjusted for retrievability with the unretrievable share stated. Either direction answers: a near-duplicate-free pool at every rung licenses current practice; a largely re-exported pool tells curators their declared weights are not the weights they apply.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct web queries (11 Gate 2, 9 adversary 1, 9 adversary 2) and 13 fetches; full lists in batches/2026-10-17-1128/UQ-20261017-29-record.md and batches/2026-10-17-1128/UQ-20261017-29-adversary-1.md / -2.md. Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 Tracing the Roots (Li et al., arXiv:2604.10480, Apr 2026; read) — unit: the dataset as lineage node, 83 seeds expanded to 430 datasets / 971 inheritance edges, with example-level checks by "exact (instruction, input, output) triplet matches"; endpoint: per-dataset unintended redundancy rates along lineage edges plus lineage-propagated benchmark leakage; comparator: a dataset's own ancestors; estimand: redundancy and leakage attributable to ancestry ("Lineage analysis shifts the unit of comparison from samples to ancestry"). P2 Mix, MinHash, and Match (Alrashed & Orabona, arXiv:2512.18834, Dec 2025; read) — unit: the document/token within Arabic/Turkish/Hindi web PRETRAINING corpora; endpoint: pairwise near-duplicate overlap matrices, union de-duplicated sizes, multiplicity by number of sources, per-source survival; comparator: the other sources in the union; estimand: cross-source redundancy of a pretraining union. P3 On Inter-dataset Code Duplication and Data Leakage in LLMs (arXiv:2401.07930, FSE 2025; read) — unit: the code snippet across CodeSearchNet vs five code fine-tuning sets; endpoint: pairwise near-duplicate shares (Type-3 clones, SourcererCC, Jaccard 0.7/0.8) and the performance inflation they cause; comparator: one pretraining corpus vs each fine-tuning set; estimand: eval-leakage prevalence and its effect on reported performance. (The record's own P1–P3 — DPI arXiv:2310.16787, WIMBD arXiv:2310.20707, Tulu 3 arXiv:2411.15124 — remain real and are superseded as nearest priors by the three above; both adversaries independently re-surfaced them, and DPI's quoted line is existence-checked but not re-quote-verified.)

Novelty confidence: Medium

Medium and not High because the record's central novelty claim — that no prior takes the post-training pool as unit with example-level overlap as endpoint — is FALSE as written: P1 does, on the same object, and P2 executes the limb-(a) design elsewhere. Not Low because neither is a near-duplicate of the canonical question and the two documents that could make it Low (WIMBD App. B.4, P1 App. C) are unread, and an unread paper grounds no grade in either direction.
Significance — consequence: Premise-free: the pool's de-duplicated size becomes the honest denominator for post-training data-scarcity claims, and curators gain a concrete action (add cross-dataset dedup; publish distinct-content weights beside declared ones). A near-duplicate-free pool at every rung retires, with a number, a worry DPI recorded and set aside and Tulu 3 handled by manual provenance tracking. CORRECTED at Gate 5 per adversary 2: the record's consequence (i) — that mixture-ablation conclusions are partly about multiplicity — is struck as stated, since it needs the training-effect premise the record declines to assume (presupposition 4); it stands only as an explicitly conditional corollary.
Significance — audience: Mixture curators publishing weighted recipes (Tulu/OLMo-class teams, BAAI Infinity-Instruct, SmolTalk-class collections); preference-data and reward-model builders, for whom duplicate prompts across sources inflate apparent agreement; data-provenance auditors with an explicit open methodological choice (DPI's "we choose not to deduplicate"); hub/dataset-infrastructure teams who would expose pool-level duplicate structure as metadata. Demonstrably live: an Apr 2026 Shanghai AI Lab / OpenDataLab paper builds redundancy and lineage-contamination accounting over exactly these datasets.
Significance — fecundity: Does cross-dataset multiplicity act on training like epoch repetition? Does an example's multiplicity predict its influence on the trained model? Should mixture optimization be re-parameterized over content clusters rather than named datasets — i.e. is "dataset" the wrong unit for mixture search? Does contamination accounting double-count when a contaminated example enters through several components? Is the multiplicity distribution heavy-tailed enough that a few examples are the de facto backbone of all public post-training?
Significance — anchoring: Within-corpus dedup (Lee et al. 2022); DPI's non-dedup choice; Tulu 3's manual provenance tracking and its stated difficulty distinguishing paraphrase from distributional similarity; mixture-weight optimization (declared weights are its decision variables); data-constrained-scaling/repetition; in-ledger UQ-20261016-46 (manifest frames and retrievability, inherited by limb (c)) and UQ-20261016-51 (per-item occurrence counts, the pretraining analogue of multiplicity).
Reason for silence: Three mechanisms survive. Ownership and incentive: no actor is accountable for the union, each curator is accountable for their own release, and quantifying re-export deflates the record and download counts datasets are credited by — DPI's documented choice not to deduplicate "to preserve the original design choices" is that locally rational non-ownership in writing. Disciplinary boundary: the design is a named problem family under vocabularies ML curation does not share — data-lake redundancy, overlap/unique-coverage analysis, non-redundant set compilation, double counting / covered area, multiple systems estimation, inter-dataset duplication, text reuse — which is why the field's own "deduplication" searches return within-corpus work. Unit mismatch inherited from corpus-cleaning-before-a-run. STRUCK at Gate 5 per adversary 2: mechanism (1) "new instrument" as stated — near-duplicate clustering was already published at four to five orders of magnitude more text (The Pile's 139M documents in 64.6M duplicate clusters, 2023) while Tulu 3's whole mix is 354,192 records, so the instrument was not the binding constraint.

Two record figures are confirmed with a caveat: "430 distinct datasets connected by 971 inheritance edges" INCLUDES the 83 seeds, and the 46.48% unintended redundancy rate for open-instruct-v1 is defined nowhere - neither Section 4.2, Table 3 nor Appendix C states its numerator or denominator - so it is a headline of unknown construction. Union sizes: Arabic 177.8B tokens and 178.9M documents, Turkish 167.6B and 219.1M, Hindi 76.2B and 59.6M. Multiplicity by overlap degree (Table 1), Arabic: 2-way 28.9B tokens, 3-way 16.4B, 4-way 7.1B, 5-way 1.3B, 6-way 32.4M. Per-source survival after dedup (Table 4), Arabic: FinePDFs 98.5%, ArabicWeb24 93.8%, FineWeb-2 56.0%. Near-duplicate rule: character 5-gram shingles, signature length 112, LSH of 14 bands by 8 hashes, MinHash-estimated Jaccard threshold 0.8, union-find over verified pairs. Pairwise overlap is present only partly: Figure 1 is an image of percentages and the numeric pairs sit in Appendix B, Tables 9-12, rather than as a full numeric matrix per language in the main text. Decisively, NO declared mixture weight exists anywhere in it: "mixture weight" and "sampling weight" do not occur, and the sentence the record leaned on, "We then allocate tokens to sources according to their document fractions." (Section 6.1.2), allocates by REALIZED document counts within whichever pool is being sampled, described as preserving that pool's "natural source mixture". The object is web and PDF pretraining corpora; instruction, preference, SFT, RLHF, DPO and alignment do not occur anywhere in it, Related Work and appendices included. Newly found version caveat: v1 is a different, Arabic-only paper (AraMix) with no document-fraction sentence and no Jaccard value, so threshold 0.8 and the sampling rule are v2 properties only.

But on the post-training side the comparator that limb needs is only partly available. The Tulu 3 SFT mixture card states "It contains 939,344 samples from the following sets." while its 18 per-source counts sum to 889,344 - 50,000 short, unexplained, against dataset metadata of 939,343 - and carries no dedup or decontamination statement; SmolTalk's card gives counts in prose for 9 of 13 components (about 876K against a stated 1M) and says only "using tuned ratios", withholding the ratios. Strongest remaining objection: presupposition failure on limb (b), newly sourced and unresolved. The limb asks for realized distinct-example proportions against the DECLARED weights for at least three published mixtures, and verification could not establish that three such declarations exist in numeric form. Tulu 3's card publishes 18 per-source counts that sum 50,000 short of the 939,344 total it states, with no dedup or decontamination statement; SmolTalk publishes "using tuned ratios" and withholds the ratios, with counts for 9 of 13 components; arXiv:2512.18834 allocates by realized document fractions and declares nothing. Limb (b) is therefore answerable as written only where a mixture both declares a weight vector and ships a recoverable example-to-source map, and no three such mixtures have been named. The first pass's objection stands too, narrowed rather than withdrawn: the design is now executed on pretraining corpora by two independent groups - WIMBD's all-pairs text and URL overlap figures, arXiv:2512.18834's matrix, union sizes, multiplicity and survival tables - so what is unasked is the object plus three items (the near-duplicate threshold ladder, the datasets-per-example multiplicity distribution, and limb (b)), not the design.

ID: UQ-20261017-30
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — evaluation methodology (harness and leaderboard design). Neighbours searched: clinical-trial methodology, IR incomplete-judgment evaluation, missing-data statistics, psychometric missing-response scoring, AutoML benchmarking, solver competitions, software-testing flakiness, reporting-standards metascience.
Question (canonical): In published LLM and agent evaluations that release per-item logs with error fields, on a pre-declared frame: (a) what share of the nominal denominator carries a harness-side failure, by class, under a hand-validated taxonomy; (b) holding the estimand fixed, how far apart are the drop-the-item (per-protocol) and score-as-failure (ITT) estimators in score, rank correlation and counted pairwise rank reversals; (c) separately, as a distinct estimand, what does retry-to-completion give; (d) does harness-failure probability correlate with model identity (making the drop estimator biased, not merely lossy); and (e) what fraction of published evaluations state their convention at all? (Gate 1 reformulation, the one permitted; Gate 0 original in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
1. What is an evaluation's intention-to-treat score as opposed to its per-protocol score, and do the two rank models differently?
2. How often does a reported benchmark number depend on how the harness handled its own errors?
Motivating gap: Intake (silence mapping): the harness layer is dense with how-answers (retry policies, timeouts, answer-extraction, exception handling) and empty of why-questions about what the denominator is; a reported gap smaller than the harness-failure share cannot be read as a capability gap. Gate 2 confirmed the how-answer density but falsified "empty of why-questions": the question is posed and partly answered in the field's own words (retry bias, infrastructure noise, fault-side localisation), and both adversaries found further occupied vocabularies.
Presuppositions: P1 harness-side failure separable in logs — SUPPORTED, and the instrument already exists (arXiv:2607.28802, Cohen's kappa 0.76), which cuts against novelty. P2 a usable share of evaluations release error fields — UNVERIFIED (unrun; cannot kill, cannot pass). P3 rankings close enough to move — ESTABLISHED independently (MathArena reversal; Anthropic 6 pp spread, 3 pp skepticism floor). P4 the three conventions exhaust practice — FALSE: at least six in evidence (Inspect default drop-with-unscored-count, score_on_error, abort-on-first-error, listwise deletion to tasks completed by all systems, numerator inclusion per Vats & Golev, AMLB constant-predictor imputation). P5 no standard fixes the convention — SURVIVES for standards (Rollout Cards spec has no such field) but fails for harnesses (Inspect publishes a "Counts in denominator?" column and a default). P6 failure rates large enough to matter — ESTABLISHED AND PUBLISHED (5.8%/2.1%/0.5% by resource config, ~6% pod errors; 23.7% of one theoretical grid lost, adversary's own arithmetic).
What would count as an answer: the failure share by class with hand-coded validation and the unclassifiable share; each evaluation's score under both same-estimand estimators with rank correlation and a pairwise-reversal count; retry-to-completion labelled separately; a test of failure-rate correlation with model identity; the disclosure fraction. Null: "convention-insensitive" if no reversal survives resampling. Statable and falsifiable, so Gate 1 clears; residual looseness is frame size (P2) and the absent equivalence margin.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 (WebSearch cap), plus 8 Disguise + 1 locating by adversary 1 and 8 Disguise + 1 spot-check by adversary 2 = 29 distinct queries; full lists with per-query results in batches/2026-10-17-1128/UQ-20261017-30-record.md and UQ-20261017-30-adversary-1.md / -2.md. Most informative: (own field, own words) "how harness errors and failed API calls change reported LLM benchmark accuracy and model rankings excluded versus scored as incorrect" -> MathArena retry study, decisive; (the "what fraction of X" limb) "SWE-bench agent run infrastructure error excluded from denominator rank reversal scoring convention" -> Anthropic infrastructure-noise post, publishes the share; (P1) "taxonomy distinguishing agent failure from harness failure per-item error field" -> arXiv:2607.28802; (adversary 1, harness-native) "inspect_ai fail_on_error sample errors scored incorrect vs excluded denominator" -> Inspect AI Scoring Policy, documents both estimators; (adversary 1, null-response) -> Rollout Cards 50-repository convention census; (adversary 2, AutoML) "AutoML benchmark framework failures imputed constant predictor effect on framework ranking" -> AMLB, JMLR 25, section 5.1.3. ITT/per-protocol as a NAME is genuinely absent from AI evaluation (Gate 2 query 3); the name's absence is not the question's absence.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. MathArena, "The Hidden Effect of Retrying Requests in LLM Evaluation", https://matharena.ai/retry/ (opened at Gate 2 and re-verified first-hand by adversary 2). Unit: model-problem run (8,855 pairs). Endpoint: accuracy, with stability = P(success | output tokens). Comparator: retry-until-success vs a fixed retry budget where "If all attempts fail, the solution is marked as incorrect". Estimand: expected accuracy under simulated retry-to-completion. Claims: overestimation "up to 5 percent"; GPT-5.1/DeepSeek-v3.2 ranking "reverses at lower stability under a maximum-time failure model". No measured failure share, no drop arm, no disclosure count.
B. AMLB, Gijsbers et al., JMLR 25:101 (2024), section 5.1.3, https://jmlr.org/papers/v25/22-0493.html (PDF opened by adversary 2; section 6.4 COULD NOT READ, route tried: that PDF). Unit: framework x dataset x fold. Endpoint: imputed performance, then ranking. Comparator: constant-predictor imputation vs ignoring the failure vs random-forest imputation. Estimand: mean performance per framework. Claims: dropping is rejected in terms because frameworks "may fail on harder tasks or folds and consequently obtain higher average performance estimates"; "Failures correlate with data set properties"; penalising imputation is "fairer towards the well-behaved frameworks". No sensitivity analysis, no ranking-movement figure, no system-identity test.
C. Anthropic, "Infrastructure noise", https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/infrastructure-noise (opened at Gate 2; not re-opened by either adversary). Unit: task run across six resource configurations. Endpoint: success rate and infra error rate. Comparator: 1x vs 3x vs uncapped enforcement. Claims: infra error rate 5.8%/2.1%/0.5%; "as many as 6% of tasks were failing because of pod errors"; 6 pp most- vs least-resourced spread (p < 0.01); distrust leaderboard gaps below 3 pp. Does not state its own scoring rule and compares no conventions.
Also opened and load-bearing: Inspect AI Scoring Policy, https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/scoring-policy.html — a public harness documenting BOTH candidate estimators with a literal "Counts in denominator?" column, the default named, unscored samples reported separately, and a worked example moving accuracy from 1/2 to 1/3 between them. Rollout Cards, arXiv:2605.12131 — 50-repository census of de facto conventions: "None of the 50 repositories reports how often rollouts failed alongside the accuracy or score", 11 absorb, 31 drop with no counter, 9 log without surfacing. arXiv:2605.21404 (limb (e)'s nearest hit, read by both adversaries) — no field on how errored runs enter the denominator, but categorized failure-count disclosure measured at 3/12 full, 4 partial, 5 absent, same unit (the benchmark paper) and same endpoint type as limb (e). arXiv:2607.09510 — applies the drop convention plus listwise deletion, environment root cause 9.4% of failures.
