ID: UQ-20261017-40
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — diagnostic safety; measurement of diagnostic error; chart-review methodology. Method-owning neighbours: diagnostic-test-accuracy methodology (review/incorporation bias, QUADAS-2), psychometrics (criterion contamination), patient-safety record-review methodology (hindsight bias), clinical informatics (copy-forward propagation), and — found only by the adversaries — radiology/pathology peer-review QA and forensic blind verification.

Question (canonical): On one case set reviewed twice under a pre-registered protocol, what is the signed difference in the classified diagnostic-error rate between (A) standard unblinded chart review with the full record available, and (B) review in which the index encounter's own diagnostic assertions and every downstream repetition traceable to them are redacted, while subsequently generated findings, test results and diagnoses not traceable to the index assertion are retained — reported with its uncertainty, a measured index of blinding success, and the same contrast computed on a subset whose diagnosis is anchored to an index-independent reference (autopsy, mandated external re-adjudication, or a registry with independent ascertainment) to fix the bias direction?

Alternative formulations:
- (lay) Does diagnostic momentum hide diagnostic error from the very instruments built to count it?
- (counterfactual) If the same cases were re-adjudicated with the initial diagnosis redacted, how far would the published diagnostic-error rate move, and in which direction?
- (method field's words) Is the reference standard of diagnostic-error chart review conditionally dependent on the index assertion it is used to judge, and what is the magnitude of the resulting review/incorporation bias in the estimated error rate?
(Gate 1 reformulation used once, for well-posedness only; intake version and rationale in the record.)

Motivating gap: The field is dense with instruments for measuring diagnostic error (Safer Dx and Revised Safer Dx, e-triggers, Global Trigger Tool, SPADE look-back/look-forward, missed-opportunity and care-transition reviews) and thin on whether the measurement is identified. All take later recorded diagnoses as truth. The field names the mechanism that would corrupt that truth in its own journal (Blume, "The inherited diagnosis and diagnostic error", Diagnosis 2026) without drawing the measurement consequence. The Safer Dx validation paper (opened) names hindsight bias in its limitations, does not estimate it, and blinds its reviewer to the error outcome while supplying up to a year of subsequent EHR — blinded to the wrong variable for this purpose. No validation paper found reports a redaction arm.

Presuppositions:
- P1. Diagnostic labels propagate, so the later diagnosis is not independent of the index one. ESTABLISHED as a named phenomenon in the candidate's own literature (Blume 2026, abstract opened); magnitude unmeasured and is the thing at issue.
- P2. Chart-review instruments use subsequent documentation as their reference standard. PARTLY ESTABLISHED, and narrowed at Gate 4: holds by construction for look-back/look-forward and coded-diagnosis e-trigger designs; overstated for Safer Dx, whose items judge the appropriateness of the index diagnostic process and use later EHR "to help determine the clinical context" (adversary 1, opened).
- P3. A redaction protocol can remove index assertions and their inheritance while leaving the presenting features reviewers need. MOST CONTESTED and conceded circular: tagging text as "inherited" presupposes knowing what was independently ascertained, the quantity at issue. If the later diagnosis IS the inheritance, arm B has no reference. Bracketed, not solved, by pre-registered tagging rules, reported inter-annotator agreement, and arm B with and without borderline text.
- P4. Some subset has an index-independent reference to fix direction. PARTLY ESTABLISHED; such subsets are small and selected, so direction is fixed only locally.
- P5. Reviewers can be kept blind in practice. CONTESTED; style, test ordering and referral patterns leak the index impression, so blinding success must be measured, not asserted.
- P6. The classified error rate is the quantity consumers of this literature use. PLAUSIBLE; burden estimates, dashboards and instrument-validation accuracy are built from per-record classifications.
- P7 (added at Gate 4, adversary 2). That a "true" error rate exists for the arms to be biased relative to. CONTESTED: the field's own position is that there is no gold standard for diagnostic error, so the arm difference may be a difference between two conventions. Answered only by the anchored subset.

What would count as an answer: A paired re-adjudication on one case set with two blinded arms — full chart versus chart with index assertions and traceable repetitions redacted — reporting the difference in classified error rate with uncertainty, a measured blinding-success index, inter-annotator agreement on the inheritance tagging, and the same contrast on an index-independent anchored subset; plus restatement of at least one published rate as a bound with stated tightness. A null licenses existing rates against this channel. A large difference converts every published rate into a bound. A sign reversal between anchored subset and full set indicates redaction removes diagnostic evidence rather than contamination — it falsifies P3 rather than answering the question (flagged by both adversaries as rhetorical insurance; see attack 5).

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 12 at Gate 2 (record) plus 8 Disguise + 1 verification (adversary 1) plus 9 new-vocabulary (adversary 2) = 30 distinct queries; 12 fetches, 5 failed. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-1619/UQ-20261017-40-record.md, UQ-20261017-40-adversary-1.md, UQ-20261017-40-adversary-2.md. Most informative:
- (Gate 2, no. 8, mandated own-field obvious-title) "randomized trial review method blinded versus unblinded reviewers measured diagnostic error rate redacted initial diagnosis" -> nearest hit randomises the wrong a priori diagnosis handed to the TREATING clinician; record concluded "Nothing randomises what the REVIEWER sees". FALSIFIED at Gate 4 by adversary 2.
- (Gate 2, no. 12, mandated fraction limb) "proportion of diagnostic errors identified only from subsequent documentation final diagnosis used as gold standard" -> no published decomposition of any measured error rate by detectability without the downstream record; the quantity has not been computed.
- (Gate 2, no. 11, method-owning field) "criterion contamination ... medical record review diagnosis adjudication" -> psychometric sources only; the term is live outside medicine and absent inside this problem.
- (A1, no. 8, radiology QA) -> Wu et al., Radiology 2014;270(3), OPENED: blinding of the reference radiologist stratifies the measured major-discrepancy rate, 2.0% unblinded vs 12.1% blinded, authors call blinding the priority for further research. Missed entirely by Gate 2.
- (A2, no. 5/7, image- and specimen-reading fields) -> Elmore et al., JAMA Dermatol 2022;158(9):1040-1047, OPENED: randomised trial whose manipulandum IS the prior diagnosis shown to a re-reviewer.
- (A2, no. 2, forensics) -> NIJ/NCFS contextual-bias programme; blind verification and linear sequential unmasking are a mature named remedy family.
- (A1, no. 9 / F4) Banham-Hall & Stevens, Clin Med 2019;19(1):16-21 via journal-club digest -> randomised the OUTCOME only, no arm altered the initial diagnosis; the record's "drop to Low" trapdoor is NOT triggered.
- COULD NOT READ by any of the three agents: Zwaan & Singh, "The challenges in defining and measuring diagnostic error", Diagnosis 2015 (10.1515/dx-2014-0069) — doi.org CLIENT_ERROR, degruyterbrill CLIENT_ERROR, PMC hard-blocked. Not a check that passed in either direction.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): Re-ranked at Gate 5; the two nearest were found by the adversaries, not by Gate 2.
P1'. Elmore JG, Eguchi MM, Barnhill RL, et al., "Effect of Prior Diagnoses on Dermatopathologists' Interpretations of Melanocytic Lesions: A Randomized Controlled Trial", JAMA Dermatol 2022;158(9):1040-1047, doi:10.1001/jamadermatol.2022.2932 — OPENED (abstract/article page; full text not read). Unit: a pair of diagnoses of a case by the same dermatopathologist across two phases. Endpoint: adjusted RR of shifting diagnostic class. Reference: index-independent 3-pathologist modified-Delphi consensus panel. Estimand: the causal effect on a re-reviewer of being shown a more or less severe prior diagnosis (upward shift RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.34-1.73; downward RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.19-1.59; reviewers swayed away from the correct diagnosis even when their own blinded read matched consensus). Does not discuss adjudication studies or error-rate measurement.
P2'. Wu MZ, McInnes MDF, et al., "CT in Adults: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Interpretation Discrepancy Rates", Radiology 2014;270(3), pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/radiol.13131114 — OPENED (abstract). Unit: CT examination (58 studies, 388,123 exams). Endpoint: discrepancy rate vs the initial report. Reference: a second radiologist's read of the same, index-independent image. Estimand: pooled discrepancy rate, stratified by whether the reference reader was blinded (major 2.0% unblinded, 43 studies, vs 12.1%, 95% CI 4.4-29.4%, 5 studies; the ~6x ratio is adversary 1's own arithmetic on two point estimates and inherits that interval). Across-study, not paired; mechanism not stated in the abstract.
P3'. Singh H, Giardina TD, Meyer AND, et al., "Accuracy of the Safer Dx Instrument to Identify Diagnostic Errors in Primary Care", J Gen Intern Med 2016, link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11606-016-3601-x — OPENED AND READ by generator and adversary 1. Unit: the record/episode around an index primary-care visit (n=389, mostly trigger-positive; authors note selection bias). Endpoint: binary diagnostic error per record. Reference: a prior two-independent-physician-reviewer determination, the Safer Dx reviewer "blinded to the diagnostic error outcome" and given "EHR data up to 1 year after the index visit". Estimand: concurrent criterion validity of the instrument (117/389 vs 129/389). Limitations name hindsight bias and do not estimate it.
Demoted from the record's top three: Blume 2026 (one patient, no estimand, supports P1 only; could not be re-opened by adversary 1, citedrive abstract unrefuted) and the wrong-a-priori-diagnosis simulator trial (PMC7922172, title-only on all three sides, grades nothing).

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1' (Elmore). Unit differs (record vs pathologist-case diagnosis pair), endpoint differs (signed difference in an instrument's classified error RATE vs RR of class shift), reference differs (contaminated downstream record, partly redacted, vs an uncontaminated consensus panel), estimand differs (bias magnitude of a measurement instrument vs an anchoring effect on a reader). The decisive structural difference, verified from the paper: the slide does not change because of the first diagnosis, so Elmore faced no inheritance problem and needed no redaction rule. Adversary 2 checked the paper rather than its title and confirms it "does not discuss implications for adjudication studies or error-rate measurement".
vs P2' (Wu). Same shape as the candidate's full-set contrast — blinding the reference reader moves the measured error rate — but across-study rather than paired, on a reference (the image) independent of the index report, with no inheritance channel and no anchored subset. It bounds the reviewer-anchoring channel and is silent on the record-inheritance channel.
vs P3' (Safer Dx). Holds the reference standard fixed and measures the instrument against it; the candidate makes the reference standard the object. P3' blinds to the error outcome and deliberately supplies downstream documentation — the opposite manipulation. This is why novelty was Medium and not High even before Gate 4: the worry is named in the field's own validation paper and only the estimand is new.
vs the hindsight-bias case-note-review line (Banham-Hall 2019, digest only): same experimental grammar, different regressor (outcome, not index assertion), opposite predicted sign.
vs the method-owning fields: DTA/epidemiology own the concept (QUADAS-2's reference-standard-blinding item, incorporation and differential-verification bias), psychometrics owns criterion contamination, forensics owns the remedy (blind verification, linear sequential unmasking). The surviving negative must therefore be stated as a transplant, narrowly: not "nobody has asked whether reviewer knowledge of the index interpretation suppresses a measured error rate" — that is asked, and answered twice in index-independent substrates — but "it has never been asked of chart-review error measurement, where the reference is made of the same document as the index assertion."

Novelty confidence: Medium — at the bottom of the band, and on an incomplete search record. Gate 2's 12 queries missed the two nearest priors and stated a ground ("Nothing randomises what the REVIEWER sees") that adversary 2 falsified from an opened primary. Not Low: 30 queries across lay, diagnostic-safety, cognitive-bias, DTA, psychometric, autopsy-pathology, radiology-QA, surgical-pathology, forensic, structured-implicit-review, clinical-informatics, German and answer-side vocabularies returned no formulation of this estimand and no computed value for the fraction limb; both adversaries declined to grade it Low and neither could source a kill on attack 2. Not Medium-as-recorded: the generic question is answered one substrate away, so what survives is a transplant into a harder identification structure, not an unasked question.

Significance — consequence: If the difference is large, every chart-review-derived diagnostic-error rate becomes a bound of newly estimated looseness in a known direction, and burden estimates and institutional dashboards inherit the correction; the usual defence that reviewer noise attenuates rather than biases fails, because contamination by the index assertion is signed. Remedies are then cheap and specifiable: a redaction arm as a required validation element and a reported blinding domain in diagnostic-safety measurement reporting. A null licenses existing rates against this channel and replaces a ritual caveat with an estimate. A sign reversal indicates the instruments are not identifiable from available records at all and must be anchored externally.
Significance — audience: AHRQ's diagnostic-safety measurement programme; the Safer Dx / Revised Safer Dx developers, whose own limitations section names the worry and who already hold a suitable case set; SPADE and e-trigger developers, whose designs take the later coded diagnosis as truth by construction; Global Trigger Tool and missed-opportunity reviewers, who could add a blinding-success measure at near-zero cost; editors applying STARD/QUADAS-style appraisal, who have no signalling question for this instrument class. Evidenced rather than asserted at Gate 4: a leading measurement group ran exactly this methodological experiment on its own instrument in another substrate and placed it in a top specialty journal (Elmore 2022 [CITATION NOT LOCATABLE — see Verification V2]).
Significance — fecundity: Is contamination larger where label propagation is heaviest (primary care, psychiatry, chronic-disease labels) than where each encounter re-derives its assessment (emergency medicine, pathology)? Does ambient AI documentation increase or decrease inheritance, making pre- and post-ambient rates incomparable? Can inheritance be tagged programmatically, turning the redaction arm into a corpus-scale instrument? Is the reviewer's noise floor itself index-dependent, which would recast this literature's inter-rater-reliability results? Does the anchored-subset contrast yield a transportable correction factor or only a local one?
Significance — anchoring: (a) STRUCK at Gate 4 — the record read the ~5% outpatient vs ~30% Safer Dx spread as an unexplained anomaly the candidate explains; adversary 1 opened the paper and showed the 389-record sample was mostly trigger-identified with the authors naming selection bias, so that spread is explained by case enrichment. (b) The autopsy-versus-chart-review gap, reframed from case mix to reference-standard independence. (c) The standing complaint that there is no gold standard for diagnostic error, which has been a reason to stop rather than a question to answer. (d) QUADAS-2's reference-standard-blinding domain, with no instrument in this literature to attach to. (e) The inherited-diagnosis line (Blume 2026), at clinical-warning status with no measurement consequence drawn. (f) Added at Gate 4: radiology QA's own open call for research on blinding the reference reader (Wu 2014).

Reason for silence: Strongest and directly evidenced — caveat absorption: hindsight bias is a ritual limitations line, and naming a bias discharges the obligation to estimate it (visible in the opened Safer Dx limitations). Second — a disciplinary boundary between the field that owns the DATA and the fields that own the METHOD (DTA, psychometrics, forensics, radiology/pathology QA); strengthened at Gate 4, since radiology QA did measure the blinding effect while chart review did not, and the paper that performs the design does not discuss error-rate measurement. Added by adversary 1 and adopted as the best asking-side mechanism: in chart review the index assessment IS the object being graded, so "blind the reviewer to it" reads as structurally ill-formed to practitioners — which is precisely why radiology, where the image is separate from the report, could pose it. The record's mechanisms 3 (incentive asymmetry) and 4 (reviewer cost) explain why answering is unattractive, not why nobody asked, and are retained only as secondary.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status). Two independent adversaries, neither shown the other's log; both ran their full Disguise sweep (8 and 9 new-vocabulary queries), so Disguise is verified, not unverified. Worst status across the two is carried; verbatim logs in UQ-20261017-40-adversary-1.md and UQ-20261017-40-adversary-2.md.
1 | Triviality | A1: Wu 2014 (2.0% vs 12.1%) gives direction and rough magnitude in a page. A2: Elmore 2022 [CITATION NOT LOCATABLE — see Verification V2] (RR 1.52/1.38) gives sign and effect size for the live mechanism; with a year of downstream documentation, "undercounting, probably substantially" follows in a page. | Both substrates have a fixed, index-independent reference (image, slide); neither yields a classified-error-rate difference where the evidence itself is partly a product of the index label. Direction is obtainable in a page; the magnitude, which is what consumers of these rates need, is not. | Resolved (both)
2 | Disguise | A1: this is radiology QA's own question ("does knowledge of the initial report suppress the discrepancy rate a peer-review instrument measures?") renamed; it is a formal design variable there and meta-analytically quantified, and the record's central negative is false as stated. A2: Elmore 2022 [CITATION NOT LOCATABLE — see Verification V2] randomises the index assertion shown to a re-reviewer against an index-independent panel, falsifying Gate 2's ground "Nothing randomises what the REVIEWER sees"; forensics owns the remedy as a named practice, so the candidate is a third instantiation of a standing method. | Both parent designs blind a reader whose reference is independent of the index assertion; the candidate's defining difficulty is a reference contaminated by the index label, which is why it needs traceable-repetition redaction and an anchored subset. A2 checked the primary rather than the title: Elmore does not discuss adjudication or error-rate measurement, so the estimand is unposed. Novelty must be downgraded and restated as a transplant claim; neither adversary could source a kill. | Partial (both)
3 | Combinatorial novelty | DTA methodology x diagnostic safety with nothing at the interface; QUADAS-2's blinding item pointed at chart review and called a question. | The crossing generates an identification problem the parent fields do not have: in DTA and in Elmore the reference is a separate measurement, so blinding is operational; here the reference is the same document as the index assertion, so blinding requires deciding which text is inherited — which presupposes the quantity at issue. Wu 2014 also shows the interface effect is real and large in a neighbouring instrument class, so the interface is not empty. | Resolved (both)
4 | Presupposition failure | A1: (a) P2 overstated — Safer Dx judges the index diagnostic PROCESS and uses later EHR for context, not as mechanical truth (opened); (b) an inherited-and-never-corrected label is undetectable in BOTH arms, so the full-set contrast measures reviewer anchoring, not the propagation channel that motivates the question; (c) redacting the index assertions removes part of what Safer Dx-type items evaluate, so arm B runs a modified instrument. A2: (d) P3 circular by concession; (e) unstated P7 — that a true error rate exists, which the field denies. | (a) conceded and P2 narrowed to look-back/look-forward and coded e-trigger designs. (b) anticipated by the record, which assigns identification to the anchored subset and marks the full-set sign as assumption; the concession is that the novel channel rides on a small selected subset. (c) not addressed by the record and unresolved as a design matter, though A1 flags it as its own unsourced reasoning. (e) answered by the anchored subset, with Elmore's consensus panel as published proof the device works. Neither adversary could source a kill on P3. | Partial (both)
5 | Vagueness | All three outcomes are declared informative and the sign reversal is reclassified as falsifying P3, so no result can embarrass the question; "every downstream repetition traceable to them" has no operational definition, so two teams could both report "the answer" with different numbers. | The paired difference, its uncertainty, a blinding-success index and tagging agreement are pre-specified and a null is a usable positive, so this is not unfalsifiable; but the bracketing is a promise rather than a demonstrated property and the sign-reversal clause is real rhetorical insurance. | Partial (both)
6 | Significance inflation | A1: anchoring (a) is inflated — the Safer Dx ~30% is a trigger-enriched sample, so the rate spread is explained by case selection, not by how much downstream record the method consumes. A2: the named audiences have had this caveat for a decade and chose a limitations sentence. | Anchoring (a) struck; (b)-(e) stand. A2 upgrades to Resolved on evidence: Elmore 2022 [CITATION NOT LOCATABLE — see Verification V2] shows a leading measurement group running precisely this self-directed methodological experiment and publishing it prominently, and the add-on here is cheap on a case set already held. | Partial (A1) / Resolved (A2)
7 | Reason for silence | Three of the record's four mechanisms explain why answering is hard, not why nobody asked; Elmore 2022 [CITATION NOT LOCATABLE — see Verification V2] shows the question is thinkable and fundable, so "nobody conceived it" is unavailable. | Caveat absorption is directly evidenced in the opened Safer Dx limitations; the disciplinary boundary is strengthened by radiology QA having measured the effect while chart review did not. A1 supplies the best asking-side mechanism — in chart review the index assessment is the object being graded, so blinding to it reads as ill-formed — and labels it its own unsourced reasoning. | Partial (both)
8 | Dissolution | A1: splits into two existing literatures — reviewer anchoring (Wu 2014) and record-versus-independent-truth discrepancy (autopsy, Shojania) — with the anchored subset essentially the latter and the full-set contrast the former transposed. A2: "diagnostic error" is a reviewer judgement under a stipulated definition, so the two arms measure two constructs and the difference is a definitional artefact. | Neither literature runs the paired design on a chart-review instrument or isolates the inheritance channel by traceable-repetition redaction; the anchored subset scores both arms against something no reviewer wrote, which converts a definitional difference into a signed bias. The dissolution bites on the full-set contrast, which the record already marks as signed by assumption, and the entry must present the question as a synthesis rather than as unanticipated. | Partial (both)
No Unresolved status on any attack from either adversary, so no fatal objection; the verdict is capped below Validated by novelty, by the incomplete search record and by well-posedness.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17, three independent fresh-context readers plus two late reads, each handed one source and the claim made of it; logs in batches/2026-10-17-1619/UQ-20261017-40-verification-wu.md, -verification-elmore.md, -verification-zwaan.md, -late-elmore.md and -late-zwaan.md): Provisional stands, but the strongest objection loses BOTH of its quantified legs and is rewritten below, and one citation that ran through four of the eight attacks does not exist.
V1. Wu 2014 IDENTIFIED and its design corrected: Wu MZ, McInnes MDF, Macdonald DB, Kielar AZ, Duigenan S, Radiology 2014;270(3):717-735, doi 10.1148/radiol.13131114, a meta-analysis of 58 studies and 388,123 CT examinations, read at ABSTRACT level only (the RSNA full text is paywalled; 6 fetches). Overall discrepancy 7.7% (95% CI 5.6 to 10.3) and major discrepancy 2.4% (1.7 to 3.2). The entry's contrast is real but is a BETWEEN-STUDY subgroup comparison, not a manipulation of blinding within one case set: 2.0% (1.4 to 2.7) over 43 studies in which the reference radiologist was NOT blinded against 12.1% (4.4 to 29.4) over 5 studies in which it was, Q = 10.65, P = .001. The reference standard there is a second radiologist's read, which is NOT independent of the index interpretation in the sense this candidate requires, and no direction-of-bias statement, major-discrepancy definition or within-study comparison could be read from the abstract. So the entry's claim that the question is "asked and quantified twice in index-independent substrates" is wrong on both counts for this source: once, weakly, and not index-independent.
V2. The 2022 Elmore citation DOES NOT EXIST as given, established by two independent readers in sequence (6 searches and 6 fetches each; the second searched the two figures themselves by any author and any year). No paper reports relative risks of 1.52 for upgrading and 1.38 for downgrading a diagnosis against a consensus panel. The nearest real paper, opened, is Elmore JG et al., "Diagnostic Concordance Among Pathologists Interpreting Breast Biopsy Specimens", JAMA 2015;313(11):1122-1132: 115 pathologists, 6,900 interpretations against a consensus reference diagnosis, 75.3% overall agreement (95% CI 73.4 to 77.0), with over- and under-interpretation given as percentages by reference category (benign 87% concordant / 13% over; atypia 48% / 17% over / 35% under; DCIS 84% / 3% over / 13% under; invasive 96% / 4% under) and NO relative risks and no upgrade/downgrade wording anywhere. The only 2022-dated candidates Crossref offers under that author are a metacognition paper (Clayton et al., Med Decis Making, doi 10.1177/0272989x221126528, read to about 100,000 of 102,500 characters: the two figures are absent and there is no manipulation of a previous interpretation) and a viewing-processes paper in J Pathol Inform. The citation originated in adversary 2's Gate 4 log and is load-bearing in FOUR of the eight attacks (1, 2, 6 and 7) as that adversary's strongest evidence; every remaining use of it in this entry is flagged inline. Effect on the verdict: none, because no attack was Unresolved and the worst status on each of those four was already set by adversary 1's independent limb — but attack 2's A2 limb (that this paper "randomises the index assertion shown to a re-reviewer against an index-independent panel, falsifying Gate 2's ground") and attack 6's A2 upgrade to Resolved both rested on it and are struck. Nothing in this entry may cite it as a prior.
V3. Zwaan & Singh 2015 (Diagnosis 2(2):97-103, doi 10.1515/dx-2014-0069) remains COULD NOT READ after a second attempt on six fresh routes, so eleven routes in total have now failed: doi.org, degruyter.com HTML and PDF, degruyterbrill.com HTML and PDF, research.vu.nl, and a PMC copy (PMC4779119) that is hard-blocked here; the Houston Methodist scholars page, an AHRQ PSNet summary, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar each return ABSTRACT or metadata only. From the abstract alone the paper's named challenges are a diagnosis that evolves over time or across settings, underdiagnosis against overaggressive workup, and judging error given disease likelihood and severity and hindsight bias; it does NOT mention a reference standard there. That is not evidence that the body lacks the reference-standard dependence this entry needs it to lack, so promotion item (1) is UNDISCHARGED, with the failed routes recorded so a later pass does not repeat them.
V4. One new unread lead bearing directly on the candidate's object, surfaced by the second Elmore search: Whiting P et al., "Evidence of reference standard related bias in studies of plain radiograph reading performance: a meta-regression" (PubMed 17151064), blocked from this environment. It names reference-standard-related bias in its title, which is this candidate's own mechanism in the parent methodology, so it must be opened before any promotion; it is added to the promotion conditions below.
V5. Net effect: Provisional stands, and what changed is the shape of the cap. The entry is no longer capped by a twice-quantified prior; it is capped by well-posedness 2/3, by an incomplete search record (Zwaan unread after eleven routes, Whiting unread, Wu abstract-only), and by adversary 1's design-internal attack 4(b) and 4(c), which verification did not touch and which remain the real objection.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 - Significance 3/3

Strongest remaining objection: adversary 1's attack 4(b) and 4(c), which are design-internal and unrefuted — an inherited, never-corrected wrong label is invisible in BOTH arms, so the headline full-set contrast measures reviewer anchoring rather than the propagation channel that motivates the question, leaving the novel inheritance channel identified only on the index-independent anchored subset, which is small, selected and non-transportable; and redacting the index assertions may leave arm B scoring a modified instrument rather than the same one. The PRIOR-ART half of this objection has collapsed at verification and is withdrawn. The adversary's citation of a 2022 Elmore paper reporting a relative risk of 1.52 for upgrading and 1.38 for downgrading a diagnosis against a consensus panel could not be located by two independent readers across twelve searches and twelve fetches, by that author or any other, in any year; the closest real paper, Elmore et al., JAMA 2015;313(11):1122-1132, reports 115 pathologists and 6,900 interpretations against a consensus reference with 75.3% concordance (95% CI 73.4 to 77.0) as percentages only, with no relative risks and no upgrade/downgrade wording, so those two figures do not look like outputs of that design at all. And Wu 2014 is not an index-independent quantification of the candidate's contrast: it is a between-study subgroup comparison inside a meta-analysis (2.0%, 95% CI 1.4 to 2.7, over 43 studies where the reference radiologist was unblinded, against 12.1%, 4.4 to 29.4, over 5 studies where it was blinded; Q = 10.65, P = .001), the reference is a second radiologist's read rather than a standard independent of the index read, and no within-case-set manipulation of blinding is performed. So the generic question has been quantified ONCE, weakly and between studies, not twice in index-independent substrates. The entry is still capped at Provisional, by well-posedness and by an incomplete search record rather than by this objection, and one unread lead on exactly this object now stands ahead of it: Whiting et al., "Evidence of reference standard related bias in studies of plain radiograph reading performance: a meta-regression" (PubMed 17151064), blocked from this environment.

Promotion requires: read Zwaan & Singh 2015 (10.1515/dx-2014-0069) via a non-PMC publisher route and confirm it does not pose the reference-standard dependence as an open measurement problem — if it does, this is asked-but-open and must be re-routed rather than promoted; open Whiting et al. 2006 (PubMed 17151064, "Evidence of reference standard related bias in studies of plain radiograph reading performance: a meta-regression") by a non-PMC route, since it names this candidate's object in its title and is the closest unread lead in the record; install Wu 2014 as a nearest prior with its real attributes (a between-study subgroup contrast, reference = a second radiologist's read, no within-case-set manipulation) and NOT as an index-independent quantification; and restate the Gate 2 negative as the narrow transplant claim; and resolve instrument compatibility by showing that Safer Dx-type process items can be scored with the index assessment redacted, so the paired contrast is one instrument on two records rather than two instruments. With those three done and no new prior found, Validated would still require well-posedness to reach 3/3, which needs the bias direction identified off the anchored subset.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): ask the five blinded primary studies inside Wu 2014 and the Elmore phase-1/phase-2 design what a paired, index-redacted re-adjudication looks like when the reference is index-independent, then specify the inheritance-tagging rule and its agreement metric on an existing diagnostic-error case set before any re-adjudication is run.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. Not rejected, and not asked-but-open on the present record: no source found poses this estimand as an open question. The routing decision is contingent on Zwaan & Singh 2015, unread by all three agents.

Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — aerospace / space-systems engineering; spacecraft reliability; space-debris and post-mission-disposal modelling. Method-owning neighbours: frailty / mixed-population reliability and warranty statistics; proliferated space-vehicle qualification.

Question (canonical): For a pre-declared frame of NORAD-identified Starlink satellites labelled by launch group, design generation and target shell, under a failure proxy declared before any data pull (decay onset within T days of launch with no operator decommissioning signature) plus two pre-declared alternative proxies as a sensitivity axis, fit a discrete-time competing-risks hazard model with a launch-group random intercept, conditioning on each unit's cumulative geomagnetic exposure over its own orbit-raising window, its target shell and its design generation: what is the interval estimate of the between-launch-group intercept variance tau^2 (and the implied median hazard ratio between two randomly drawn launch groups), and what does propagating that tau^2 through a standard debris-environment / PMD-compliance model do to the predicted distribution — not merely the mean — of non-disposed objects? (V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, scored as canonical; V1 named the manufacturing lot, which no public record identifies. Both in the record.)

Alternative formulations:
- Are mega-constellation satellite failures exchangeable across production batches, or are some batches "lemons" in a statistically identifiable sense?
- How much of the observed between-launch dispersion in Starlink early deorbit rates is attributable to batch-level manufacturing/screening variance rather than to environment, operations and design revision?

Motivating gap: Mega-constellations are the first case with per-unit public outcomes for thousands of nominally identical spacecraft, and batch-level dispersion is already reported. The academic state of the art on fleet failure is a pooled, unstratified Kaplan-Meier (arXiv 2603.25835, READ: mean daily failure probability 0.0128%; McDowell starlife, READ). The one batch loss with an accepted cause (Group 4-7, Feb 2022) is environment-level, which is why a residual group-level component is the un-asked part. Debris and PMD-compliance models propagate a single scalar reliability parameter (ISO 24113-style 95% PMD success), so a variance component would change the predicted tail, not only the mean. Correction carried from Gate 4: a published per-launch tabulation of early-life survival does exist (see priors) — the gap is the conditional variance component, not the absence of per-launch data.

Presuppositions:
1. Public element sets plus status records identify, per satellite, launch batch and a datable failure. PARTLY DISCHARGED at Gate 4 — McDowell's per-launch stats table classifies per-unit outcomes with stated rules, and SpaceX's FCC semi-annual reports (Star2212.pdf, READ by A2) carry per-satellite maneuverability and reentry rows; but those are disposal-phase signatures without causes, not labels for orbit-raising-phase loss.
2. Launch group proxies the manufacturing lot. CONTESTED, partly discharged by making the launch group itself the estimand; continuous-flow production attenuates any true lot effect toward zero. A3 adds that the launch group is primarily a shared-EXPOSURE unit (same ride, insertion altitude, raising window, software), not a production unit.
3. Per-unit space-weather exposure constructible from element sets. ESTABLISHED in kind (Frontiers 10.3389/fspas.2025.1572313, READ, builds per-satellite histories and stratifies 523 reentries by Dst).
4. tau^2 estimable with useful precision. CONTESTED in the record; Gate 4 (A2, A3) finds the record's own counter-evidence mis-scoped — McDowell's unestimable fleet MEDIAN bears on the right tail, not on early-life variance, and ~200-300 launch groups is a large cluster count, if thin per cluster. Net: this presupposition is in better shape than recorded.
5. Fleet-mean hazard non-stationary across generations. SUPPORTED by both papers read.
6. Retirement policy not correlated with batch. FALSIFIED as stated — in Feb 2024 SpaceX announced controlled deorbit of ~100 first-generation satellites after identifying "a common issue" that could increase failure probability (TechCrunch, OPENED by A1). A batch-level latent defect removed by PLANNED deorbit is a non-event under the primary proxy.
7. A group-level variance component is actionable. PARTLY CONTESTED, now with two sourced negatives: Aerospace OTR-2025-00583 (READ, record) has no lot concept, and Aerospace ATR-2024-02064 (READ by A2) states "The assets are assumed to be identical" and propagates no parameter uncertainty into constellation results.

What would count as an answer: a competing-risks model on an enumerated fleet with a launch-group random intercept, reporting tau^2 with an interval after conditioning on per-unit space-weather exposure, shell and generation, plus the implied median hazard ratio and the propagated effect on the predicted distribution of PMD success / non-disposed objects. Two pre-declared outcomes both count: tau^2 indistinguishable from zero under all three proxies (licensing the scalar parameter debris models assume), or materially non-zero with identified outlier groups. Proxy sensitivity is a required output, not a caveat.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 38 web searches in total (11 Gate 2 + 9 + 9 + 9 across three adversaries) plus 4 GitHub searches and 16 page fetches; full lists in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-41-record.md and the three adversary logs. Most informative:
- [Gate 2 Q1, mandatory own-field own-words title] "Starlink satellite reliability on-orbit failure rate statistical analysis early deorbit by launch group" -> arXiv 2603.25835 plus trade press; concluded "no academic paper on per-launch failure rates" — THIS CONCLUSION IS STRUCK, see A2 Q8.

- [A1 Q1, observer/answer-table vocabulary] -> planet4589.org/space/con/star/stats.html, OPENED: per-launch-group table with "Early Deorbit", "Reentry after Fail", "Failed, decaying", "Anom." and explicit definitions; counts only, no rates, variance or intervals.

COULD NOT READ: seradata.com batch headline (302 to slingshot.space front page, three agents, no archive route) — grounds nothing either way. PRIOR 4 unverified by A1 and A3 but corroborated by A2 via a companion Aerospace document. No PMCID appeared on any path; PMC / Europe PMC never used.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Guarnieri, Tsurutani, Hajra, Echer, Lakhina, "NORAD Tracking of the February 2022 Starlink Satellites", arXiv 2307.02923 — READ by A2. Unit: the individual satellite, aggregated per launch. Endpoint: early loss / entry into working orbit. Comparator: the 34 preceding v1.5 launches (97.05% is the Table 1 TOTAL over 35 launches, not a 34-launch figure — corrected at verification; the prose gives a rounded 97%) against Group 4-7 (22.45%, i.e. 11 of 49 satellites). Estimand: descriptive per-launch efficiency ratios, no model, no uncertainty.
2. J. McDowell, "Starlink statistics", planet4589.org/space/con/star/stats.html — OPENED by A1. Unit: the satellite within its launch group. Endpoint: a four-way classified outcome (early deorbit / reentry after fail / failed-decaying / anomalous) with stated operational rules. Comparator: none. Estimand: counts per launch group; no rates, intervals or variance.
3. "Starlink Constellation: Deployment, Configuration, and Dynamics", arXiv 2603.25835 §3.3 — READ. Unit: the individual satellite. Endpoint: deorbit inferred from TLE presence. Comparator: none (pooled). Estimand: fleet survival function and a scalar 0.0128% mean daily failure probability; its own n is not reported (confirmed at verification: nowhere in Section 3.3, nor the decayed or censored counts, nor the averaging method), the 0.0128% is over the first 1,000 days of operation, and it names batch/generation heterogeneity as "likely" and tests none of it.
Also recorded and read: Frontiers 10.3389/fspas.2025.1572313 (per-unit Dst-stratified reentry timing, n=523, marginal correlations, no batch dimension); McDowell starlife (pooled lifetime KM); Aerospace OTR-2025-00583 and ATR-2024-02064 (practice guidance, no lot-variance object); Ahmad et al. 2025 and ESA SDC9 papers 48 and 182 (opened, not priors).

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs 1 and 2: same population, same launch-group labelling, overlapping endpoint family — these are the close neighbours, and they answer the candidate's V1 headline descriptively. They are tallies: no exposure covariate, no shell or generation conditioning, no random effect, no variance, no interval. The candidate's estimand is the conditional between-group variance after that conditioning, plus its propagation into a debris-model output distribution. A2's own binomial arithmetic from source 1 (labelled as its own: P(X>=38 | n=49, p=0.0295) ~ 1e-48) shows the unconditional exchangeability null is already refuted in print, so the novel content is the conditional residual only.
- vs 3: shares population and substrate and already publishes the fleet-mean hazard the candidate wants to decompose; differs on estimand (mean versus conditional variance) and on conditioning (none versus space weather, shell, generation).

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: nothing found in any of ~38 queries across eleven vocabularies fits a group-level random effect or variance component to spacecraft on-orbit failure hazard, and the method-owning fields have the machinery with no spacecraft application. Not High: two close neighbours (priors 1 and 2) publish per-launch early-life outcome tables, and prior 3 publishes the fleet mean and names the batch hypothesis untested. Not Low: all three were opened and none estimates dispersion, let alone a conditional one. Two Gate 2 statements are struck as falsified — "no academic paper on per-launch failure rates" and "no per-launch academic tabulation surfaced"; only the narrower negative (no published per-launch dispersion estimate) survives. Asked-but-open: no — the descriptive limb is asked and answered in print; the conditional variance-component question is posed nowhere found, so nothing is routable.

Significance — consequence: if tau^2 is materially non-zero, the single scalar reliability / PMD-success parameter that debris-environment and compliance models propagate is mis-specified in its tail, not its mean, so collision-risk and compliance forecasts understate the bad cases, and outlier groups become screening targets; if it is indistinguishable from zero under all three proxies, that licenses an exchangeability assumption no source found anywhere tests. Gate 4 discount, sourced to A3's own labelled arithmetic: for exchangeable launch effects at CV=1 (MHR ~2.2), the fleet-level 97.5th percentile of non-disposed count moves ~5% (per shell, spread widens from ~13% to ~20%), against ~67% for a 2-point change in the mean rate — so the tail payload is real in direction and modest in magnitude, and a design-level correlated defect, which a random intercept does not estimate, would dominate it.

Significance — audience: debris modellers (ESA MASTER/DELTA, NASA ODPO/LEGEND), regulators conditioning licences on PMD success, constellation reliability and qualification engineers, insurers (who already carry a "generic/serial defect" vocabulary). Discount, now doubly sourced: the operator holds the true lot labels, needs no TLE inference and acted in Feb 2024 without one; and the receiving guidance for this audience assumes identical assets with no uncertainty on the mean (ATR-2024-02064, READ), so there is as yet no slot for a variance about it.

Significance — fecundity: is a group-level effect predictable from pre-launch screening or early-orbit telemetry; does tau^2 shrink across generations (an in-orbit manufacturing learning curve); does the decomposition replicate on OneWeb, Kuiper and Guowang, whose launch groups are smaller and lots plausibly cleaner; should spares and insurance be priced per batch; and how much does any mixture parameter move a long-term debris projection's tail.

Significance — anchoring: the Feb 2022 storm batch loss (the one batch event with an accepted cause, environment-level); the published-but-unstratified fleet hazard; the Feb 2024 operator-identified common-issue cohort deorbit; unmodelled uncertainty on PMD success in debris models; and the open qualification-strategy problem for proliferated vehicles.

Reason for silence: (1) New data — per-unit public outcomes for thousands of identical spacecraft are ~5 years old, and before mega-constellations lot variance was not estimable ("Production quantities < 10 space vehicles/system", OTR-2025-00583, READ). Weakened by Gate 4: the per-launch table has been in print since 2023 and the fleet mean since 2026, so the data existed and a tabulation was made, and still no group-level model was fitted. (2) Disciplinary boundary — the sourced mechanism, and the weight now rests on it: the communities holding the orbital record carry no manufacturing covariate (priors 1-3 all unstratified or environment-stratified), two Aerospace documents hold the decision and have no lot-variance object, and the fields owning the estimator (CCF, frailty, credibility theory, batch-effect industrial statistics, all searched) have no spacecraft application. (3) Incentive gap — only the operator can label lots and a per-batch quality signal is commercially adverse. Competing mechanism raised by A1 and A3 and not refuted: the field explains batch outliers causally and individually (storm, common-issue recall, upper-stage failure), so an anonymous residual variance looks low-yield. "No one thought of it" is not invoked; prior 3 shows someone did think of it and declined to test it.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17, two independent fresh-context readers, each handed one source or source set and the claim made of it and neither shown the adversaries' reasoning; logs in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-41-verification-dynamics.md and -verification-perlaunch.md): Provisional stands. Three corrections, two of which cut against the entry and one for it.
V1. arXiv 2603.25835 CONFIRMED on every load-bearing point, read as full text. Section 3.3.2 does apply Kaplan-Meier to decayed satellites, lifetime is "the duration between its first and last appearance in the TLE dataset", and the figure appears three times (abstract, introduction, 3.3.2) as "a mean daily failure probability of 0.0128%" over the first 1,000 days of operation. The n is NOT STATED anywhere in Section 3.3, and neither are the decayed or censored counts, nor the method for averaging the daily values — so the entry's "its own n is not reported" is right and now first-hand. NOT FOUND, each checked separately and in two independent summariser passes over the whole of 3.3: stratification by launch, launch group, batch, shell or generation; any random effect, frailty, mixed model or variance component; and any mention of solar, Kp, Dst or geomagnetic activity in the survival section (solar storms appear only in 2.2, outside it). The conjecture is verbatim and untested — "likely reflecting different satellite batches or generations with different planned lifetimes" (3.3.1), attached to the spread of operational-phase durations (median 864 days, mean 901.4), with "batches" occurring nowhere else in 3.3 and no follow-up test.
V2. CORRECTION, against the entry: the paper DOES state how it separates unexpected from planned deorbits, and the method is a TIME CUTOFF rather than nothing. It treats the first 1,000 days as a baseline of "true in-orbit failures — satellites that deorbit unexpectedly" and says planned end-of-life deorbits "begin to dominate only after day 1,395". So the record's "never states how the data separate them" is withdrawn: the separation is stated and is cruder than unstated — no individual deorbit is classified by cause, which is a different and more useful criticism. Also noted from the same read: the abstract's 4-6 year lifetime claim is never reconciled with S(t) of about 0.83 at day 1,395, and the paper does not connect the two.
V3. CORRECTION to the Gate 2 repair the entry prescribes: arXiv 2307.02923 is thinner prior art than the entry's promotion item implies. Table 1 is per-launch satellite counts (Mission Number, Mission Name, Deployed, Working, Efficiency) over 35 v1.5 launches plus a TOTAL row, compiled from Wikipedia, purely descriptive with no model, no interval and no test. The 97.05% is the TOTAL row (1,765 deployed, 1,713 working) pooled over those 35 rows, NOT the efficiency of "the 34 preceding launches" — the prose gives only a rounded "97% successful for the last 34 launches", so the entry's "(97.05% efficiency)" attaches the table total to the wrong population and is corrected. The 22.45% is confirmed and is satellites working over satellites deployed for one launch (Group 4-7: 49 deployed, 11 working). Decisively for novelty: the words batch, production, manufactur and design flaw do not occur anywhere in that paper, which attributes the loss to the February 2022 storm and drag and says the cause is unknown — so it is a per-launch descriptive prior and not prior art on a lot effect. McDowell's stats page CONFIRMED as counts only: a per-launch-group table with about twenty outcome columns and stated category definitions ("Failed to orbit (f): Launch vehicle failed to reach orbit."), with NOT FOUND for rates, percentages, intervals or any variance measure.
V4. The anti-selection mechanism is CONFIRMED as an event and UNSOURCED as a batch fact. SpaceX's "Commitment to Space Sustainability" plan of 12 February 2024 does report deliberately deorbiting about 100 working first-generation Starlink satellites after the team "identified a common issue" that could "increase the probability of failure" (read in two secondary reports, 13 and 14 February 2024; the SpaceX document itself was not opened). But NOT FOUND in either report: whether those satellites came from one launch, one manufacturing batch or several. The entry's anti-selection argument therefore stands as a mechanism — operator-detected defective cohorts leave the failure frame by controlled deorbit — while the claim that the cohort was a batch is not sourced, and the promotion item's pre-declared proxy has to be defined without assuming it.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness held at 2/3, not lowered: Gate 4 falsified presupposition 6 but also repaired presuppositions 1 and 4, and no attack reached Unresolved. 2/3 alone forecloses Validated.)

Strongest remaining objection: The primary failure proxy anti-selects the signal the question is for — a competent operator removes a detected defective cohort by controlled deorbit, documented for ~100 first-generation satellites with an identified "common issue" in Feb 2024, which the "no decommissioning signature" rule scores as a non-event — while the launch group is primarily a shared-exposure rather than a production unit (the one documented batch loss turning on injection altitude, storm timing and local-time sector), so the conditional tau^2 that the design can actually estimate is an unattributable launch-event variance, and its stated payload is a few-percent shift in a debris-model tail that the receiving guidance has no slot for.
Promotion requires: re-scope the canonical text off "manufacturing-lot" onto the launch group / shipset as the decision unit and add a pre-declared proxy that captures operator-initiated controlled cohort deorbits (the two repairs that would take well-posedness to 3/3 by removing the attenuation ambiguity and the anti-selection), correct Gate 2 to cite arXiv 2307.02923 Table 1 and planet4589.org/space/con/star/stats.html as priors and confine the novelty claim to the conditional variance component, and open at least one debris-environment paper to show the propagated tail shift is material next to the compliance-rate scenario sweeps those models already run — or drop that payload and rest significance on the sampling-frame limb.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open and reconcile the two per-launch outcome tabulations now identified (planet4589.org/space/con/star/stats.html and arXiv 2307.02923 Table 1) against the operator's FCC semi-annual disposal rows, and settle whether their classification rules can separate operator-initiated cohort deorbits from passive early decay, before any model is specified.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed — not rejected. The descriptive per-launch dispersion limb is asked and answered in print (priors 1 and 2), so it is not a routable open problem; the conditional variance-component question is posed nowhere found.

ID: UQ-20261017-42
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — computational materials science / electronic-structure methods / scientific data infrastructure. Method-owning neighbours: missing-data statistics (MNAR, selection models), UQ of computer experiments, HPC workflow failure analysis. Source method: presupposition inversion.

Question (canonical): For a declared, version-pinned high-throughput DFT attempt frame (every structure submitted, with per-task terminal states retained, or a frame re-run from scratch) and a pre-registered recovery protocol applied to a random sample of terminally failed tasks (escalated mixing/preconditioner, smearing, k-grid, initial magnetic configuration, symmetry, step limits) plus cross-code recovery: (a) conditional on composition and structure under a pre-declared featurization, is the distribution of formation energy, band gap, magnetic moment/ordering and dynamical stability the same among recovered-failed as among retained entries (the ignorability null), and what is the hand-adjudicated split of failures into numerics-driven and physics-driven (the latter a declared outcome category, not a missing value); and (b) when the recovered set is reinstated, by how much does at least one published downstream statistic move — a screening hit rate, the count of entries on or within X meV/atom of the convex hull, or the held-out error of a universal MLIP retrained with the recovered entries included? (V2; V1 and the Gate 1 reformulation rationale in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-42-record.md)

Alternative formulations:
1. Are the materials a high-throughput workflow fails to converge a random subset of the ones it attempts, with respect to the quantities the database is used to predict?
2. How much do property distributions, convex hulls and MLIP training sets change when the non-converged tail is recovered, by re-runs or by cross-database recovery?

Motivating gap: The unstated presupposition is that a database's entries are a representative sample of what was attempted, so only chemistry selection (what anyone tried) needs discussing. The chemistry half is quantified (Trezza & Chiavazzo 2023); the numerics half is not. Workflows are built to make failures disappear (custodian: retry, then MaxCorrectionsError and abandon — verified in src/custodian/custodian.py by two adversaries) and the terminal FAILED state exists in the schema but not in consumer-facing documents (emmet-core TaskState, "VASP Calculation State", emmet-core/emmet/core/types/enums.py). JUDGE'S CORRECTION: the record's stronger framing — that failed tasks are "structurally absent" and that there is "no venue and no credit" for a failure inventory — is false as written. MC3D (Huber et al. 2025, opened) publishes an enumerated 38,739-structure frame, an 85.5% success rate, failures broken down by covariates and the full provenance graph; Kingsbury 2022 and Hilgers 2023 publish completion rates. The gap that survives is narrower and real: every such report takes success as the endpoint and none compares the properties of failed against retained units or recounts a downstream statistic.

Presuppositions: (1) attempted-but-failed tasks enumerable — DISCHARGED (MC3D frame + provenance; Hilgers' 6660-system frame; schema TaskState); (2) version-pinned failure criterion — established in principle; (3) recovery gives near-truth for a sample — supported (Hilgers 64.8%→94.3%); (4) target properties defined for dropped entries — CONTESTED, handled by declaring an outcome category, which is the hypothesis, not a fix; (5) numerics- vs physics-driven failure separable by hand — CONTESTED, the identification crux, and part of the failure mass is wall-time/cell-size driven (Kingsbury: incomplete SCAN runs "may have simply run out of wall time"); (6) downstream consumers traceable to entry sets — UNVERIFIED, untested by any adversary; (7) maintainers/MLIP builders would act — UNVERIFIED. Two further filters sit outside the frame: converged-to-unintended-state results that are RETAINED (Horton 2019: spontaneous loss of magnetism "a common failure mode"), and pre-submission numerics exclusions (MC3D dropped all lanthanides/actinides for "a significant failure rate"), so the estimate is a lower bound on numerics selection — which V2 does not say.

What would count as an answer: for a declared frame with a pre-registered recovery protocol, (a) the measured property-distribution difference between recovered-failed and retained entries with the adjudicated numerics/physics split; (b) the implied movement in a named published statistic on reinstatement; (c) an explicit null — no detectable difference after conditioning — which would license current practice for the first time. A report that the frame is unobtainable is not an answer. GAP: as written, (a) names the null over the failed set while (b)/(c) can identify it only over the ladder-recovered stratum.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 38 distinct queries total — Gate 2: 11 web + 2 GitHub code + 5 fetches; Gate 4: 9 new-vocabulary Disguise queries per adversary x3 (all three met the 8-query floor; Disguise executed, not unverified). Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-42-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Demoted from the record's list, still real and still distinct: Lu/Li/Reimers 2508.07204 (between-workflow discrepancy among converged calculations — every unit on the retained side of the filter) and Trezza & Chiavazzo 2311.09891 (chemical-space selection bias with MP as the unbiased reference).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — P1 publishes the frame, the rate and a covariate breakdown but never compares the properties of failed against retained structures ("all structures are considered to be magnetic and metallic in behavior in the initial geometry optimization") and recounts no downstream statistic; the candidate's estimand is P(property | failed, composition, structure) and the movement of a published number, so it is the one unperformed step on top of P1's frame rather than a new frame. vs P2 — shares the frame construct and answers the fraction limb for one workflow; endpoint is success as engineering cost, P(success | inputs), not P(property | failed, X); its recovery was read by the batch as demonstrating the candidate's presupposition 3 — STRUCK at verification, which found fixed solver limits, an explicit assumption that calculation parameters do not change between batches, and recovery by ML-predicted starting inputs rather than by escalation rather than estimating the candidate's quantity. vs P3 — same missing-data vocabulary, different object and endpoint: surrogate accuracy for one simulator, no community database, no recoverable-by-escalation stratum, no physics-driven outcome category, and counts/extremes (hull membership) are not the functional it protects. Judge's finding: the record's claim that the missing-data framing had never been pointed at simulation failure is wrong — it is a decade old in UQ of computer experiments (P3; Higdon 2015's 9% discarded; Bollapragada 2021 on the Fayans EDF "not likely MCAR"; Lucas 2013) — but no opened source in any of those literatures asks the candidate's two limbs.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: 38 queries across roughly thirteen vocabularies (HT-DFT's own words; missing-data statistics; UQ/computer experiments; climate PPE crash analysis; AiiDA/Materials Cloud provenance; MP maintainer docs; phonon databases; quantum-chemistry and OC20 dataset construction; molecular failure-prediction ML; wet-lab negative results; FAIR/dark data; Chinese-language HT-DFT; survivorship) returned exactly two shapes of work — endpoint "will it converge" (propensity) and endpoint "how accurate are the ones that did" (precision of the retained) — and nothing estimating property differences between dropped and retained entries or reinstating them into a hull count, hit rate or MLIP error. Held at Medium, not raised: the Gate 2 prior set missed its two closest neighbours (P1, P3), which an adversary had to find; the fraction limb is already published (P2); and the strongest potential disguise (Duan et al. 2019) remains unread in all three runs.

Significance — consequence: if the filter is non-ignorable, published screening hit-rates and "N newly predicted stable compounds" counts are statistics on a numerics-conditioned subpopulation, and universal MLIPs inherit the filter in both training and held-out splits, so reported errors are optimistic precisely where coverage fails; if ignorable, current exclusion practice is licensed for the first time with a number attached. Magnitude is now evidenced rather than assumed: 14.5% terminal failure in a 2025 production database (MC3D), ~31% incomplete for SCAN against 4% for r2SCAN (Kingsbury 2022), 35.2% baseline in Hilgers' frame. The directional story (failures cluster where interesting physics lives) remains unevidenced, and part of the failure mass is wall-time- and cell-size-driven.
Significance — audience: database maintainers (MP/atomate2/emmet, OQMD, AFLOW, Materials Cloud/AiiDA, Alexandria), for whom publishing a failed-task inventory is a release decision on a field that already exists — and MC3D shows the venue exists; MLIP builders (MACE-MP, CHGNet, M3GNet, GNoME-style), action = stratify or reweight on a failure-propensity score and re-run the cheap tail; benchmark designers (Matbench Discovery), action = report the attempt denominator with the hit numerator; screening authors, action = a sensitivity analysis bounding the hit rate over the unrecovered tail. Not fully evidenced: no maintainer statement about what they would do with a non-ignorability result, and presupposition 6 untested by any adversary; the revealed response to failure so far is to engineer it away (P2, Duan), which is still one of the named actions.
Significance — fecundity: a failure-propensity model becomes a reusable covariate (weighting, uncertainty, active-learning acquisition); the numerics/physics adjudication labels a dataset for the inverse question — is abandonment itself a measurement of instability; Manski-style bounds on hull membership under worst-case tails become computable; attempt-frame reporting becomes askable as a norm; the design transfers to every other simulate-filter-publish pipeline.
Significance — anchoring: the HT-DFT reproducibility and numerical-QC programme (2508.07204; 2008.10402, opened: no failure or hull analysis), the database-bias literature that quantified only the chemistry half (2311.09891), the 2026 coverage roadmap's "blank zones" (2609.19833), the NOMAD dark-data thesis that looked at wasted computation and never mentioned failed calculations (1805.05039, opened), the wet-lab failed-experiment programme (Raccuglia et al.), and distribution-shift complaints about MLIP benchmarks.

Reason for silence: disciplinary boundary plus framing, with the record's incentive clause struck. Struck on evidence: there IS venue and credit for failure statistics (MC3D publishes an inventory with a covariate breakdown; NOMAD accepts "Results... in their raw format as produced by the underlying code"; Hilgers and Duan put failure in the title), and the missing-data treatment of simulation failure is a decade old one field over. What verifies and survives: every materials paper that reports failures takes success as the endpoint, so the question that gets asked is "how do we fail less", never "what does failing hide"; the missingness is manufactured in workflow infrastructure whose success metric is throughput, while the unit screening papers and MLIP trainers consume is the entry document, downstream of a best-of-task selection and carrying no attempt denominator; and the UQ community that owns the method calibrates single simulators, not community databases — so the two communities holding the pieces do not share an object. Corroborating negative: zero GitHub issues across org:materialsproject on failed-calculation selection bias, and the field's own FAIR manifesto on wasted computed data never names failed runs.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — three independent fresh-context adversaries (A1, A2, A3), each 9 Disguise queries; worst status across the three is recorded; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-42-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md:
1 | Triviality | Direction is textbook (failures pile up in open-shell, magnetic, near-metallic, soft-mode systems), so non-ignorability is foregone; Duan's AUC>=0.95 shows the filter is not random | A propensity highly predictable from exactly the conditioning covariates is what MAR looks like, and says nothing about residual dependence given them; the two largest opened real frames stop short of the estimand (MC3D breaks 5,597 failures down by species count and cell size but by no property; Kingsbury: "the data in Figure 4a reflect only successful calculations"); limb (b) cannot be written down at all without the re-runs; A1 and A3 both noted their own "textbook direction" claim was unsourced | Resolved (A1, A2, A3)

But the record's framing does not survive: its prior set missed the two closest neighbours and its "the calculation side never did this" claim is false outside materials. Residual: Duan et al. full text unread in all three runs | Partial (A1 Partial, A2 Resolved, A3 Partial)
3 | Combinatorial novelty | Missing-data statistics x HT-DFT with the interface doing no work: import MNAR, apply to a new dataset | Real obstruction the method-owning side does not have: the missing value may not exist (a task that will not relax may have no minimum), the output is recoverable for a sample so recovery is itself the treatment, failures are a mixture of missing and outcome, and the downstream functionals are counts and extremes where ignorability of a mean gives no protection. A3's caveat: this argument is the adversary's reconstruction, not the record's, because the record did not know the UQ literature | Partial (A1 Resolved, A2 Resolved, A3 Partial)
4 | Presupposition failure | (i) the null presupposes a stochastic outcome given covariates, but at full structural resolution the property is near-deterministic, so ignorability holds by construction and the estimand has content only relative to a coarsened featurization; (ii) the frame sees only terminal failures — Horton 2019 shows a common MP failure mode is converging to an unintended state and being RETAINED, and MC3D excluded lanthanides/actinides pre-submission for high failure rates; (iii) much "failure" is wall-time, not physics (Kingsbury); (iv) the declared category "no local minimum / imaginary modes at the escalated endpoint" asserts physics a non-converged run cannot establish, since imaginary modes need a successful force-constant calculation on a converged reference | No presupposition shown false: (i) is repaired by pinning the featurization to the downstream consumer's, which makes the estimand consumer-relevant rather than tautological, and settings-dependence means Y|X is not strictly degenerate; (ii)-(iii) make the estimate a lower bound on numerics selection rather than ill-posed; (iv) is a labelling fix. All three adversaries recorded these as their own definitional objections, not sourced kills | Partial (A1, A2, A3)
5 | Vagueness | "At least one published downstream statistic" invites picking whichever moves most; "the distribution among the dropped set" is whatever the ladder rescues, so any result can be declared | Frame demonstrably constructible; limb (b) returns a signed number that bounds a published statistic's sensitivity from below under any declared ladder; pre-registration plus one pre-declared primary statistic closes the forking path. A2's residual, the sharpest finding in the batch: the null is stated over the failed set while the design compares retained against the ladder-recovered stratum only, and P(Y|X,failed) is a mixture over recovered and unrecovered — so a difference on the recovered part neither establishes nor refutes the null as worded without bounds on the remainder, and bounds appear in the record only under fecundity, not in "what would count as an answer" | Partial (A1 Resolved, A2 Partial, A3 Resolved)

Fatal-attack check: no Unresolved status on any attack from any adversary (attacks 1, 2 and 4 are Resolved/Partial throughout), so the entry is not Rejected.
