Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17, two independent fresh-context readers, each handed one prior and the claim made of it; logs in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-42-verification-mc3d.md and -verification-hilgers.md): Provisional stands, and the candidate's increment is CONFIRMED intact — neither prior compares the properties of failed against retained systems, and neither recomputes any downstream statistic. Four corrections, one of them to a presupposition the entry claimed as demonstrated.
V1. MC3D (arXiv:2508.19223) CONFIRMED, read as full text through the Figure 10 caption. The attempt frame is real and the figures are exact: "Out of the 38 739 structures that have been processed, the relaxation workflow successfully completed 33 142 structures", a success rate of 85.5%, with "About 14.5% of workflows fail to complete successfully despite the error handling mechanism", and "The vast majority of errors come from the failure to converge to the required precision" verbatim, the commonest errors being pw.x failing ionic or electronic convergence within the iteration limit. Two denominator cautions the entry must carry: 38,739 is the relaxation-workflow frame only, not a submitted pool (a 46,964 non-lanthanide/actinide pool is mentioned separately), and the abstract's frame is different again — 72,589 unique structures and 32,013 in the final database, the latter after removing 1,129 duplicates, so a naive 32,013/72,589 of about 44% is not a success rate and must not be quoted as one. DECISIVE, checked across Introduction, Results, Discussion and most of Methods: NOT FOUND for any comparison of failed against succeeded structures on formation energy, band gap, magnetism or stability; the only property check (relaxed against experimental volume, 78.1% within 5%, 436 structures moving by over 50%) is computed on successes alone. NOT FOUND for any downstream recomputation — a hull count, a screening statistic or a machine-learned-potential error — with machine learning appearing only as motivation.
V2. CORRECTION to how MC3D's covariate breakdown may be cited: the variation of failure with number of species and cell size exists ONLY as Figure 2 and Figure 3 histograms (green success, red unrecoverable failure), whose bar values could not be read, and the text states no failure rate by species count, atom count or chemistry. So "its variation with number of species and cell size" is a figure, not a published number, and this entry must not quote a rate off it. One genuinely new and candidate-favouring fact from the same read: lanthanide and actinide pseudopotentials "often lead to numerical instabilities and a significant failure rate", and those elements were EXCLUDED from the frame with no figure attached — a chemistry-correlated exclusion made before the workflow ran, which is the candidate's own premise appearing as a design decision in its nearest prior.
V3. Hilgers (arXiv:2311.15430) CONFIRMED on the figures, with units corrected. 6,660 counts FILM STRUCTURES — substrate element plus layer occupancy, up to three 3d transition-metal layers on five FCC noble-metal substrate layers — not calculations; the calculations are FLAPW relaxations in FLEUR through AiiDA-FLEUR. 64.8% is 4,316 of 6,660 converging in batch 0 on the initial guesses, and 94.3% is 6,282 of 6,660 after the ML batches. The "-17%" is one of THREE unreconciled figures: 17% of total required SCF iterations in Section 3.3 (and "17% less computational time for each successful relaxation" in the abstract), about 27% for force iterations, and 29% for relaxation steps in the conclusion, with no reconciliation; the entry should say which. DECISIVE: NOT FOUND for any property comparison between failed and converged systems — the roughly 378 never-converged systems are never characterised, the only convergence breakdown is by element and site (Cr and Mn at site A, Fe and Co at site B, Mn and Fe at site C named as hard), and the single magnetic result (about 10% of converged systems ferromagnetic) covers converged systems only. NOT FOUND for any downstream recomputation over recovered systems.
V4. CORRECTION, and this one matters for the design: Hilgers does NOT recover failures by escalating settings, so it does not demonstrate presupposition 3. Its limits are FIXED — at most 100 relaxation steps, 100 SCF iterations per step, nine SCF restarts, fixed charge-density and force criteria (5e-5 Ha/a0) — and the paper lists as an explicit assumption that "Calculation parameters do not change from batch to batch" except for the predicted input quantities. Recovery works by better STARTING INPUTS: ML-predicted magnetic moments first (batch 1, +570 systems), then also predicted interlayer distances. It is iterative batch learning, not an escalating-cost ladder. Nor does it adjudicate why a calculation failed in the candidate's sense: it names two failure patterns (muffin-tin spheres crashing into each other, and drifting into the vacuum outside the film) and attributes SCF failures to "the complex energy landscape and a difficult initial setup", without classifying any individual failure as numerical against physical. The entry's claim that "its recovery demonstrates the candidate's presupposition 3" is struck, and the promotion item's "ladder-recovered stratum" has no published precedent in either prior — which makes the ladder the candidate's own instrument to justify, not an established one to borrow.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3 (judge's regrade from the record's 3/3, on A2's identification gap): the frame, version-pinned criterion, recovery protocol, property set, adjudication procedure, downstream statistic and explicit null are all named, and limb (b) is cleanly falsifiable — but limb (a) names an estimand over the failed set that its own answer definition identifies only over the recovered stratum. That is a fixable mismatch, not ill-posedness, so it caps rather than rejects. Significance 2/3: consequence and anchoring are argued from evidenced magnitudes and two currently-published statistic families, while the audience-action limb rests on presupposition 6 and on maintainer behaviour that no adversary could test.

Strongest remaining objection: MC3D (Huber et al., arXiv:2508.19223 — opened and quoted by A3, missed entirely by Gate 2) already publishes an enumerated 38,739-structure attempt frame, an 85.5% success rate, failures broken down by covariates and the full provenance graph that retains the failed workflows, while the missing-data treatment of simulation failure that the record presents as an uncrossed boundary is a decade-old standard in UQ of computer experiments (Chan-Plumlee-Wild; Higdon 2015; Bollapragada 2021; Lucas 2013) — so the candidate's motivating premise is false as written and what remains is the single unperformed step on an already-published frame, which is a narrower and more fragile novelty claim than Medium-on-the-record's-priors suggests.
Promotion requires: re-run Gate 2 with the four-attribute check against MC3D (2508.19223) and the computer-experiments missing-output literature (2304.09372 and the works it cites) as nearest priors, read Duan et al. 2019 (10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00057) to close the one unread Disguise residual, restate limb (a) as ignorability over the ladder-recovered stratum plus Manski-style bounds over the unrecovered remainder with one pre-declared primary downstream statistic as the endpoint, and rewrite the motivating gap and Reason for silence without the struck "structurally absent" and "no venue and no credit" claims — if the regraded prior set still leaves no property-comparison or reinstatement study, the entry promotes to Validated; if MC3D or Duan turns out to contain either, it is Rejected as a disguised known.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): nothing on the question itself; the pointer is to establish whether the Materials Cloud MC3D provenance archive exposes its ~5,597 failed workflow nodes with their inputs, since that would settle whether any new compute is needed to build the attempt frame.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected.

ID: UQ-20261017-43
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Verdict history: Gate 4, attack 4 (presupposition failure) Unresolved from adversary #3; attacks 3 and 7 also Unresolved from #3. Gates 0–3 passed (novelty Medium, well-posedness 2/3 self-scored, significance 2/3) and three adversaries ran, so this is a Gate 4 kill, not a Gate 2 one. (The trailing clause was moved off the Status line after the batch: a Status line carrying a qualifier is the recurring defect that breaks the index parser.)
Domain(s): Other STEM — structural integrity / non-destructive evaluation / risk-based inspection (target field). Method imported from diagnostic epidemiology and veterinary test validation (Hui–Walter latent-class estimation without a gold standard).
Question (canonical): Using existing multi-method inspection records on the same in-service welds and components (radiographic, conventional UT, phased-array UT, eddy-current calls) with no destructive ground truth, and under a pre-declared flaw-size-class stratification and a pre-declared conditional-dependence structure: is a latent-class (Hui–Walter-type) model identifiable for method-specific probability of detection and false-call rate per size class and stratum, and — where identifiable — how do those field estimates compare with the POD basis actually consumed by the assessment route in question, that route and its POD source being named and verified before the analysis rather than assumed? (V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V1 as submitted is in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) What is the field POD of standard NDT methods, estimated from agreement among methods on the same components rather than from seeded-flaw trials? — this weaker form is asked and acknowledged open in the field's own literature, not un-asked. (2) Can diagnostic epidemiology's no-gold-standard machinery be identified in weld-inspection archives, and does it confirm or contradict the detection assumptions inspection intervals rest on? (3) How many physically distinct methods and prevalence-differing strata are needed before method-specific POD and false-call rate are identified at all, and if the answer is "more than exist", which added method, stratum or partial-truth sample would identify them?
Motivating gap: Inspection intervals and fitness-for-service decisions rest on detection performance whose empirical basis is laboratory seeded-flaw and round-robin work; the field's own authority (P1, opened) states that field records cannot yield POD by the standard routes and that "special statistical methods" are required, naming none; epidemiology solved the formally identical no-gold-standard problem decades ago. Gate 4 damaged this gap: the slot P1 leaves empty was in fact filled in 1995 by a different estimator (N2, opened independently by two adversaries), and the no-gold-standard latent-class family had already crossed into engineering inspection by 2008 (N1, opened independently by two adversaries).
Presuppositions: (1) a linkable multi-method corpus on the same locations exists and is obtainable — contested, binding, unevidenced by any of 39 queries; (2) calls from different methods align to a common spatial unit; (3) the latent state can be binarised at a declared severity threshold — contested, and the crux of the kill; (4) conditional independence given the latent state is tenable or modelled (UT and PAUT share physics); (5) ≥2 strata with differing prevalence and shared method accuracy; (6) inspector/vendor effects absorbable into "method"; (7) a POD basis exists to compare against and committees would act on it — demoted into the question at Gate 1 after the one opened code-side source (Cenosco API 581 handbook) showed a categorical inspection-effectiveness selection, not a POD curve.
What would count as an answer: identified estimates with intervals of per-method POD and false-call rate at declared size classes from a pre-registered latent-class model; a dependence-structure sensitivity sweep; comparison against the documented basis the named route actually consumes; a validation arm on any dig- or teardown-verified subset. A demonstration of non-identifiability counts, if it names the added method, stratum or partial-truth sample that would identify the model.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 39 documented queries (13 at Gate 2 + 26 across three adversaries, 25 of them in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try) and 23 fetch attempts, 12 pages actually read. Q4 ("Hui-Walter ... applied engineering inspection detection rate") → zero engineering results — this negative is FALSIFIED by adversaries #2 and #3. Q6 → statistical-engineering.com "Field Finds" (fetched): MIL-HDBK-1823A methods on field finds "can lead to gross errors in POD", "special statistical methods" required, none named. Q11 (capture-recapture) → software inspection only. Q13 (API 581 effectiveness → POD) → Cenosco 581 handbook (fetched): categorical effectiveness, no POD curve traced. Adversary #1 Q2/Q9 → Amaya-Gómez, Schoefs et al., RESS 223 (2022) 108520: POD and false alarms derived from matched/unmatched defect sets of two ILI runs on a real 45 km pipeline, abstract mentioning no excavation — full text COULD NOT READ (doi route 302 only; open-access copy hal-03647292 unfetched). #1 Q6 and #3 D8 → Brewer, FAA/Volpe DOT-VNTSC-FAA-94-04 (OPENED twice, trid.trb.org and rosap.ntl.bts.gov): field POD from Service Difficulty Report data, misses inferred from crack-growth simulation and fitted by maximum likelihood. #2 Q1 and #3 D1 → van Wieringen & de Mast, Technometrics 50(4):468–478 (OPENED): "pass-fail inspections", "no reference values can be obtained", "model the results ... as a latent class model"; Akkerhuis 2016 UvA thesis (abstract OPENED): without a gold standard the error probabilities "can only be estimated with unrealistically strict assumptions". #2 Q2 → ecological false-positive occupancy models (Royle & Link 2006) estimate per-method detection and false-positive probability against an unobserved site state — the candidate's parameterisation under a third name, with no engineering application found. #2 Q3/Q8 → SEMI M50, a standard whose deliverables are per-tool capture rate and false-count rate "by the overlay method"; method clauses paywalled, scope text points at deposited PSL reference spheres — UNVERIFIED either way. #2 Q7 → ORNL "Probability of detection curves for dissimilar metal welds as input to probabilistic fracture mechanics code" — title-level evidence that a numerical POD consumer exists on the nuclear side; NOT OPENED, grounds nothing. #3 D6 → the medical-physics "ROC without truth" family (Henkelman; Beiden/Wagner) with no NDT traffic, which supports the boundary claim from the medical side.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same field, quantity and data class, but P1's unit is a found flaw, so misses are missing data; the candidate's unit is a location scored by ≥2 methods, so misses enter as discordant cells. P1 refutes the regression route, not the agreement route. vs N1 — one inspection system measured repeatedly in a designed R&R experiment, no size dimension, no physically distinct modalities, no NDE audience and no field-versus-certified-basis comparator; its negative verdict is an input to the candidate rather than an answer. But N1 falsifies the record's claim that the no-gold-standard family "has never crossed into engineering": it crossed in 2008 and was judged unreliable there. vs N2 — same regime and same truth-free data class, but misses are recovered from a crack-growth model plus a single-crack assumption rather than from inter-method agreement, and no false-call rate is co-estimated. N2 nonetheless falsifies the claim that the field left the "special statistical methods" slot empty. Unresolved residual: whether Amaya-Gómez et al. 2022 derive POD and false-alarm rate truth-free from two-run agreement, or treat the later run as a de facto reference — the full text was unread by every agent, and it is the one place a genuine near-duplicate would sit.
Novelty confidence: Medium — the specific conjunction (latent-class estimation of per-method POD and false-call rate per size class over physically distinct NDT methods on archival in-service records, against the consumed basis) was unfound across 39 queries in the target field, two method-owning fields and eight further vocabularies; but two of the record's load-bearing novelty arguments are falsified by opened sources (N1, N2) and the grade would fall to Low if Amaya-Gómez et al. 2022 turns out to be truth-free. The verdict does not rest on this grade: the kill is at Gate 4. Disguise was executed, not unverified — 25 new-vocabulary Disguise queries across three adversaries (9 / 9 / 8, #3's ninth refused by the shared budget after the required eight).
Significance — consequence: if identified and field POD is materially below the basis in use, intervals are too long and remaining-life claims too generous, and the correction is computable; if identified and consistent, the community's folk belief that real POD is far worse is retired with evidence and the laboratory transfer programmes are vindicated; if not identified, the answer is a derived data requirement (one more physically distinct modality, one more prevalence-differing stratum, or a small partial-truth sample). Discounted twice: the route into code arithmetic is unverified, and the field-versus-laboratory comparison is confounded by the unknown field flaw-size spectrum (see strongest objection), so a low field number is equally explained by smaller field flaws than the specimen set.
Significance — audience: API RP 581 (4th ed. 2025) and API 1163 maintainers; ASME Section XI / NRC / PNNL / ORNL probabilistic-fracture-mechanics programmes, the likeliest numerical POD consumer; the MIL-HDBK-1823A and ENIQ/JRC qualification community, which would have to accept a truth-free estimator and whose doctrine is built on known-truth specimens; pipeline operators and ILI vendors, who hold the multi-run archives and run the dig-verification programmes that would supply the validation arm. Discount: the parties holding the data are the parties least served by a published field POD below the certified basis.
Significance — fecundity: whether inspector and vendor identity rather than method carries most accuracy variance; value of information for commissioning one additional physically distinct modality purely to buy identifiability; what implied POD sits behind the categorical effectiveness scales in RBI; a Grubbs-type continuous analogue for sizing error without a reference; stability of agreement-based POD across fabrication eras as a test of the Hui–Walter constant-accuracy assumption; behaviour of no-gold-standard dependence diagnostics at very low prevalence with two near-duplicate physics.
Significance — anchoring: the documented laboratory-versus-field POD gap (Spencer 1998; Sharma et al. 2026 naming cross-modality benchmarking as still open); P1's statement of an unsolved missing-data problem; MAPOD's standing as the funded substitute and its reliance on simulated truth; API 1163 ILI qualification and its dependence on dig verification; identifiability limits of latent-class models under correlated errors.
Reason for silence: two of the record's four mechanisms are struck by opened sources. STRUCK — "a definitional block: the possibility of recovering detection performance from agreement rather than truth is not among the options considered" (N2 shows the field building a records-based miss-inference estimator in 1995). STRUCK — "a disciplinary boundary with no traffic, verified in both directions" (N1 shows the latent-class no-reference method inside engineering inspection since 2008, where it was judged to need unrealistically strict assumptions: informed refusal, not silence). SURVIVING — owner and vendor ownership of the archives plus the liability and procurement exposure of the number; and demand absorption by MAPOD, the funded substitute that manufactures truth in simulation. Both survivors explain why the question is hard or unwanted to answer, not why it was never asked; per Gate 4's attack-7 rule that makes the novelty finding itself suspect.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Three adversaries, each fresh-context, each handed the Gates 0–3 record only and no earlier log. Statuses below as A1 / A2 / A3; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-43-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md.
1 Triviality | the identifiability limb is a parameter count settled generically in the method-owning literature, and A2 adds a published negative the record missed (Akkerhuis: without a gold standard the error rates need unrealistically strict assumptions) | identifiability in principle is textbook, estimability in the archive regime (very low prevalence, two near-duplicate ultrasonic physics, strata co-varying with geometry and access) is empirical, and the named remedy and the comparison cannot be written in a page; A1 and A2 both declined to press the arithmetic because neither opened an identifiability source | Resolved / Partial / Partial.
2 Disguise | A1: Amaya-Gómez et al. 2022 derive POD and false alarms from two ILI runs with no excavation mentioned, and Brewer 1995 fills P1's empty method slot. A2: three namesakes the record never saw — the UvA/Waterloo binary-measurement-system programme, ecological false-positive occupancy models, and SEMI M50's overlay capture-rate/false-count-rate method. A3: in quality-engineering vocabulary the core question is asked and answered (Technometrics 2008); the record's "zero engineering applications" and "boundary with no traffic" are false | none restates the candidate's conjunction: Amaya-Gómez is single-modality with the later run as de facto reference and no latent variable (full text unread), N1 is one gauge in an R&R design with no size dimension or modality physics, occupancy models were never pointed at engineering inspection, SEMI M50's scope text points at deposited reference spheres and its method clauses are paywalled, and Brewer infers misses from growth physics with no false-call rate | Partial / Resolved / Partial.

A3: after N1 the candidate is an existing engineering-inspection method applied to a new archive; the named pathologies are the standard pathologies of latent-class accuracy estimation in its home field, and the only thing new at the interface is data access, which is a feasibility fact | the laboratory comparator and the size-class estimand are NDT-specific and give the interface a genuine problem | Resolved / Resolved / UNRESOLVED (A3: that genuine problem is the one attack 4 shows cannot be posed as declared).
4 Presupposition failure | A3 (fatal): the pre-declared flaw-size-class stratification V2 relies on cannot be built. Size comes from the calls, so a location missed by every method is unsized and cannot be placed in any size class — every class loses its all-negative cell and the per-class false-call rate has no denominator; or size comes from an external covariate, in which case the stratum is not a size class, the estimand is a size-averaged POD, and comparing it with a size-indexed laboratory POD(a) requires integrating that curve over the unknown field flaw-size distribution, so the pre-committed reading "below the lab basis → the basis is a laboratory artefact" does not follow. Plus the motivating premise that the field has no field-record POD method is contradicted by N2. A1 and A2 raised the same estimand defect at attacks 8 and 5. A1 adds that the methods are usually applied at different times, so they do not probe one latent state. A2 adds that presupposition 1 remains unevidenced | make the latent variable polytomous (no flaw / class 1 / class 2 ...) with each method's called size as an ordinal indicator, so undetected locations fall in a shared cell; reroute the comparison to the decision the route makes and carry the within-class size distribution as a declared sensitivity parameter | Partial / Partial / UNRESOLVED. A3's ground is not an unsourced assertion: its first limb is a deduction from two premises the record itself concedes (POD is size-dependent; undetected flaws are unsized) and from P1's opened line, it is independently reached by both other adversaries, and its second limb rests on a primary source two adversaries opened separately. The repair — a polytomous latent class with ordinal size indicators and a harder identifiability problem — is a different question from the one posed, which is why the status is Unresolved rather than Partial.
5 Vagueness | the three pre-committed readings cover every outcome, "materially" is undefined, the dependence sweep is analyst-chosen, the comparator is to be discovered, and the size-class boundaries are unfixed, so two analysts could report different quantities and both call them field POD | identifiability given a declared model is a determinate mathematical property and the negative branch is falsifiable; the threshold, sweep and boundaries are declarable before analysis — but none of them has been declared | Partial / Partial / Partial.
6 Significance inflation | the one opened code-side source shows categorical effectiveness rather than a POD input; the qualification community's doctrine is built on known-truth specimens; the data holders are the parties least served; and A3 notes a regulator already commissioned a field-POD-from-records estimate thirty years ago, so the marginal value is the difference from Brewer's assumptions, not "the first field POD" | the audiences are live and named independently of this candidate, ORNL publishes POD curves as PFM inputs (title level only), and the not-identified branch yields an actionable data requirement with no committee vote | Partial / Resolved / Partial.
7 Reason for silence | mechanisms 1 and 3 are falsified by opened sources (N2 1995; N1 2008); the survivors explain why answering is hard or unwanted, not why nobody asked, and no mechanism is offered for why the industrial statisticians who held the method and the aerospace analysts who held the field-record problem never wrote the other half down | data ownership plus MAPOD's absorption of the laboratory-to-field demand is a credible pair, and informed refusal next door explains why the NDE literature contains no attempt | Partial / Partial / UNRESOLVED.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17, three independent fresh-context readers — the unread potential duplicate, the two negatives the novelty argument rested on, and the identifiability question as a methods question; logs in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-43-verification-amaya.md, -verification-negatives.md and -verification-identifiability.md): Rejected STANDS. The fatal ground is attack 4, a reasoning argument about the estimand reached independently by all three adversaries, and verification did not touch it. What falls is the SECOND-strongest objection: both citations behind it are now unsupported, one misattributed and one not locatable at all.
V1. The unread potential duplicate is IDENTIFIED and is not a duplicate on its stated object. Amaya-Gomez R, Schoefs F, Sanchez-Silva M, Munoz F, Bastidas-Arteaga E, "Matching of corroded defects in onshore pipelines based on In-Line Inspections and Voronoi partitions", Reliability Engineering & System Safety 223 (2022) 108520, doi 10.1016/j.ress.2022.108520. It matches corrosion defects between two CONSECUTIVE in-line inspection runs over time, as a point-matching problem using Voronoi cells to filter candidates and an iterative best-affine-transformation search, tested on a real 45 km pipeline and on synthetic defects; detection probability and false alarms are a SECONDARY use of the matched output, fitted with exponential and log-logistic models on experimental data. That is two passes of the same tool type separated in time, matched geometrically — not several DIFFERENT methods scoring the same locations at one time and estimated by latent class. READ LEVEL: ABSTRACT ONLY (IDEAS/RePEc paraphrase plus Crossref and Semantic Scholar metadata; ScienceDirect is robots-blocked here and the HAL record hal-03647292 sits behind bot protection), so questions about its body are COULD NOT READ and the re-submission prerequisite is only partly discharged: its object is settled, its internals are not.
V2. "van Wieringen & de Mast 2008" is MISATTRIBUTED as the entry uses it. The real paper is van Wieringen WN and de Mast J, "Measurement system analysis for binary data", Technometrics 50(4):468-478, 2008, doi 10.1198/004017008000000415 — and it is about REPEATABILITY AND REPRODUCIBILITY of binary measurement systems when no reference values exist, modelled with a latent class model, with maximum-likelihood and method-of-moments estimators, model checking and sample-size guidelines. Its abstract mentions no sensitivity, specificity or correct-classification probability, and states no impossibility or non-identifiability result; if anything it treats estimation as possible under the model. The accuracy-versus-latent-class paper is a DIFFERENT one with a different co-author — van Wieringen & van den Heuvel, Quality Engineering 17(4):495-507 (2005) — which says "We argue that a latent class model is the most promising candidate", i.e. it endorses this candidate's approach rather than refuting it. The claim that this source "answered the generic no-reference binary-inspection question negatively" is therefore WITHDRAWN, both in the objection and in the routing paragraph. Read level: abstract only (the DOI and publisher routes errored), so nothing is asserted about the 2008 body either way.
V3. "Brewer 1995" COULD NOT BE FOUND. Six searches — the author and year with field and in-service POD terms, with QNDE, eddy-current and ultrasonic terms, with aircraft, nuclear and pipeline terms, and by the title "Development of POD from in-service NDI data" — located no such item. The one near-match opened is Fujimoto, Iwata and Swilem 1990 (J. Soc. Naval Arch. Japan 168), which does estimate POD and false-indication probability from field visual inspections combined with follow-up inspections, and has no author named Brewer. This is the second unlocatable citation in two consecutive batches, and like the first it was load-bearing: here it supplied half of the second-strongest objection. Recorded as NOT LOCATABLE rather than non-existent, and it may not be cited as a prior.
V4. The identifiability argument the kill rests on is PARTLY SUPPORTED and PARTLY UNVERIFIED, which leaves the kill standing on the adversaries' own reasoning rather than on the literature. What the methods literature does say, from opened secondary sources: a single population needs at least three conditionally independent tests, Hui-Walter with V strata has 2L+V parameters so two tests suffice given two strata of different prevalence, and the condition is degrees of freedom at least the parameter count — but Jones et al. 2010 (Biometrics 66(3):855-863, abstract only) state that meeting that count does not itself guarantee identifiability, following Goodman 1974. So the BINARY four-method single-population version of this design clears the standard minimum, which is why the kill correctly aims at V2's size-stratified version rather than at the design as such. Conditional independence given the true state is assumed throughout; violating it risks biased accuracy estimates, though one cited result holds the bias small when accuracy is near 100%, and "Attempting to fit too many conditional dependence terms results in an unidentifiable model" — which supports adversary 3's point about two methods sharing ultrasonic physics. NOT FOUND, after five searches: any published treatment of a polytomous or ordinal latent state whose size indicator is missing precisely for the latent class of interest. The kill's specific claim is therefore unrefuted and unsupported in print; it stands as argument, and the entry now says so.
V5. One finding that cuts FOR the candidate and changes nothing: NOT FOUND, across a dedicated search, for any application of a latent-class or no-gold-standard model to non-destructive evaluation, weld inspection, probability of detection or industrial inspection. The transplant really is unoccupied. That is why this remains a presupposition-failure rejection rather than a disguised-known one, and why the routing paragraph's exclusion is now narrower: the ground is not that the question was asked and answered, but that the estimand as declared cannot be built.
Scores: Well-posedness 1/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The estimand cannot be built as declared. V2's pre-declared flaw-size-class stratification requires sizes for locations that, by construction, no method called — so each size class loses its all-negative cell and the per-class false-call rate has no denominator; and the only fallback, stratifying on an external covariate, yields a size-marginal sensitivity that is not commensurable with the size-indexed laboratory POD(a) basis without the unknown field flaw-size spectrum, which collapses the pre-committed inference from "field estimate below the laboratory basis" to "the basis is a laboratory artefact". All three adversaries reached this defect independently; adversary #3 is right that the repair (a polytomous latent state with called sizes as ordinal indicators, over four methods of which two share physics) is a harder and different question, not this one. Second-strongest, and separable: the record's novelty argument rests on two negatives now falsified by opened primary sources (van Wieringen & de Mast 2008 — MISATTRIBUTED, see Verification V2: that paper is about repeatability and reproducibility, not accuracy, and does not answer the question negatively; and Brewer 1995 — NOT LOCATABLE, see Verification V3), and the nearest potential duplicate (Amaya-Gómez et al. 2022) was unread by every agent.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): nothing on this question; the re-submission pointer is a different question — identifiability of a polytomous latent-class model (no flaw / declared size classes) with each method's called size as an ordinal indicator over physically distinct NDT modalities, with the laboratory comparator either dropped or made commensurable through an explicitly assumed field size spectrum. Before any such re-submission, read Amaya-Gómez et al., RESS 223 (2022) 108520 in full via hal-03647292, the Waterloo "Assessing Binary Measurement Systems" theses (10012/6469, 10012/15394) by a route that clears the bot-check, SEMI M50's method clauses, and the ORNL dissimilar-metal-weld POD-as-PFM-input paper.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): No row for ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The decisive ground is presupposition failure at Gate 4, not already-asked-and-open; and the parts shown to be asked were also answered (van Wieringen & de Mast 2008 answered the generic no-reference binary-inspection question negatively; Brewer 1995 answered the field-POD-from-service-records question with a different estimator), which the routing rule excludes. Noted for the curator without routing: the weaker alternative formulation 1 — the field POD of standard NDT methods, and whether field records can supply it — is asked and explicitly left open in the field's own literature (P1 declines to name a method; Sharma et al. 2026 names cross-modality benchmarking as a gap), but it is not this candidate and it is not what this rejection turns on.

ID: UQ-20261017-44
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — mathematics: formalization, metamathematics, mathematical practice. Instrument: mathlib-scale machine-checked libraries with mechanical axiom tracking (`#print axioms`) and unused-binder / typeclass-generalization linting. Novelty decided by: autoformalization statement-fidelity evaluation, reverse mathematics, proof mining, deductive-verification specification coverage.

Question (canonical): [V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation] Over a pre-declared frame of theorem-level declarations in human-authored machine-checked libraries and blueprint projects that carry an attribution to a specific published theorem (library source attributions, docstring references, blueprint-to-paper node maps), and comparing each against the published statement read under a declared blanket-hypothesis rule (standing conventions such as "all rings here are commutative Noetherian" count as stated hypotheses of the published theorem): what is the signed rate of logical-strength divergence — the share formalized strictly weaker (hypotheses dropped or generalized, or a strictly weaker axiom set) against the share formalized strictly stronger (the formalization had to assume more) — decomposed into mechanically detected divergences (axiom set via `#print axioms`, declared-but-unused binders, typeclass weakening relative to the published hypothesis) and hand-adjudicated substantive ones on a random sample with inter-adjudicator agreement; and does the weaker-side rate vary with the source's publication age, length or subfield?

Alternative formulations:
1. How often does formalization reveal that a published theorem's stated assumptions were unnecessary — and how often the reverse?
2. Now that axiom use and hypothesis use are mechanically checkable at library scale, what is the measured logical slack between published mathematics and what its proofs actually require?
(V1, superseded at Gate 1 on three defects — indeterminate "the published statement", a one-sided "fraction weaker" limb, and "over-hypothesization" prejudging attribution — is in the record.)

Motivating gap: Axiom footprint and binder use are now mechanically ascertainable per declaration at library scale; formalizers report generalization-on-formalization as constant anecdote and the community's public case for formalization partly rests on it. Gate 2 narrowed the gap to the join: the mechanical instrument plus library-scale counts ARE published (Best, FMM 2021: 2,877 hits on one ~80,000-declaration mathlib pass), and a signed formal-vs-source fidelity rate IS published for adjacent corpora (arXiv:2606.14000). Gate 4 narrowed it further and struck part of it: a mathlib-wide axiom partition is published (arXiv:2606.28572, 471,260 declarations partitioned by transitive dependence on choice), so "the axiom-usage fraction appears unpublished" is withdrawn; and the detector genus is 15 years old in three further ecosystems (TPTP Axiom Reduction / Tipi 2012, ontology axiom weakening 2017, Isabelle `find_unused_assms`, Metamath per-theorem axiom tracking), so "newly measurable" survives only for source-attributed human formalization at blueprint scale. No measurement found anywhere uses published-paper-attributed human library declarations as its frame.

Presuppositions: P1 a source-attributed frame is constructible (CONTESTED; frame size unverified — mathlib `docs/references.bib` could not be read, and the library has ~308,000 declarations, so the frame may be a sub-1% selected slice). P2 "strictly weaker" is adjudicable by declared protocol (mechanical part established by Best 2021 with admitted false positives; hand part contested). P3 unused-binder detection is sound at scale (CONTESTED: binders exist for type-checking, downstream interfaces, omitted corollaries). P4 formal statements are faithful renderings not convenient variants (CONTESTED and quantified against the candidate in adjacent frames: 18–42% "Different" vs 1–4% "Stronger"; 218 bespoke definitions and a six-category mismatch taxonomy in arXiv:2608.28997). P5 library selection is not so purposive that the rate says nothing about the literature (CONTESTED, and now sourced against: mathlib's own contributor values page states "we try hard to write our definitions and lemmas in great generality", so the library arm's weaker-side rate partly measures a documented API-stability policy). P6 the published hypothesis set is determinate once blanket conventions are ruled on (CONTESTED, probably the dominant error source; V2 makes the rule explicit, not non-arbitrary). P7 discovered slack is distinguishable from deliberate expositional choice (CONTESTED, not mechanically decidable; V2 declines the attribution). P8 someone acts on the rate (partly supported; the autoformalization-scoring link is the firmest and is the one Gate 4 attack 6 left Unresolved).

What would count as an answer: A signed rate with CIs over a pre-declared, pre-registered frame, decomposed into (i) mechanical divergences (axiom set, unused binders, typeclass generalization against the published hypothesis) and (ii) hand-adjudicated substantive divergences on a random sample with inter-adjudicator agreement; both arms reported in both directions so the pre-declared symmetric null can fire; plus covariate analysis by source age, length and subfield with pre-declared strata; plus a sensitivity analysis over the blanket-hypothesis reading rule (P6) and an audit of frame selectivity (P1, P5). Admissible either way: a material weaker-side rate concentrated in older or longer sources; or a rate inside a pre-registered equivalence band with the strengthening rate, or one that collapses under the reading-rule sensitivity analysis. Gate 4 adds a condition the record lacks: without a root-cause arm (discovered slack / library generality policy / later-published generalization / formalizer error) the number is not interpretable as being about the literature.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 34 distinct queries — 11 at Gate 2 (full list, with the 5 fetches and the COULD NOT READ list, in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-44-record.md) and 23 new-vocabulary Disguise queries across three adversaries (9 + 9 + 5-of-8; full lists in UQ-20261017-44-adversary-1/-2/-3.md). - "formalization reveals unnecessary hypotheses in published theorems Lean mathlib" [mandatory own-field own-words] → no study of the endpoint; surfaced PRIOR 1 and PRIOR 2.
- "\"formalization\" audit whether formal statement is weaker or stronger than the paper statement fidelity rate theorems" → PRIOR 2 (opened; the published signed rates) plus arXiv:2610.20573, the named kill lead that no agent could open.
- "mathlib Classical.choice dependency analysis how much of mathlib is constructive axiom usage count" [adversary 1] → arXiv:2606.28572 partitions 471,260 declarations by choice dependence; the record's "axiom fraction unpublished" claim is false as stated.

Significance — consequence: If a material weaker-side rate separates from the strengthening rate, from the blanket-hypothesis artefact and (per Gate 4) from library generality policy, formalization gains a measured, citable by-product beyond verification — a generalization yield per formalized paper — where it now has anecdotes and 2,877 unaudited hits; and citation practice is shown to under-use the literature at a quantified rate. If the rate sits inside the equivalence band or collapses under the reading-rule sensitivity analysis, the generalization-on-formalization anecdote is deflated with evidence, and PRIOR 2's and PRIOR 3's finding that divergence is dominated by the formalizing process is confirmed as the whole signal. Both arms change something; the magnitude is modest either way.

Significance — audience: (i) autoformalization and benchmark evaluators — named firmest by the record, and the one Gate 4 broke: PRIOR 3 and miniF2F-Revisited both score every deviation from the given source, including logical strengthening, as unfaithfulness to correct, without invoking any literature base rate, so the claimed scoring-rule change is unevidenced. (ii) mathlib maintainers and blueprint leads, who would change attribution policy, not detection — and who the record concedes already act on the mechanical signal without the rate. (iii) formalization funders and journal editors — diffuse. (iv) reverse-mathematics and proof-mining researchers, for whom a corpus rate is a sampling frame for case selection, not a result in their idiom.

Significance — fecundity: slack as a function of time since publication (is it found, or written out?); corpus-scale reverse-mathematics-lite on choice/classical-logic use with the per-theorem programme as validation set; whether over-hypothesization predicts citation under-use; whether removable hypotheses are predictable from paper text, with this rate as base rate; whether blanket conventions dominate, converting the finding from one about mathematical content into one about mathematical prose.

Significance — anchoring: the "what is formalization for" debate; reverse mathematics and proof mining as the per-theorem programmes; mathlib's generalization-linter practice (PRIOR 1); autoformalization fidelity evaluation and benchmark-faithfulness auditing (PRIORS 2 and 3), where the same comparison is already scored for a different purpose; specification coverage/vacuity in deductive verification; and UQ-20261015-09, whose cost side this pairs with.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary with an incentive asymmetry on both sides. The METHOD-owning communities (reverse mathematics, proof mining; and, for the detector, deductive verification, ATP and ontology engineering) ask necessity per theorem, where a corpus rate is not a result the subfield rewards — a rate is not a theorem. The DATA-owning community has the instrument and fires it routinely but reads each hit as a local engineering fact and a pull-request title; mathlib's contributor values page documents maximal generality as a deliberate design value, so insiders have no reason to read a weakening as an observation about the paper, and vivid anecdotes serve the advocacy case better than a rate that might come back small. A politeness/incentive gap discourages framing a colleague's hypothesis as removable — ASSERTED, uncited, and weakened by adversary 2's finding that the prose genre for publishing exactly such findings is lexicographically standard. STRUCK on verification: the "~3-year-old instrument" limb. Unused-assumption and axiom tracking are 15 years old in Mizar (2011), standard in Isabelle (`find_unused_assms`), Metamath (per-theorem axiom tracking), TPTP (Axiom Reduction, Tipi 2012) and ontology engineering (axiom weakening, 2017); only source-attributed human formalization at blueprint scale is recent. Adversary 3 adds an unrefuted deflationary alternative the record does not consider: the question is not asked because formalizers believe its answer is known in kind — divergence is their own curation.

READ LEVEL: ABSTRACT ONLY plus the project README; the OpenReview forum (5c0RSYyIWW) is behind a browser check, its PDF fetch failed, and three searches found no arXiv version. CONFIRMED from the abstract: 367 ProofNet formalizations; 104 (28%) mathematically false plus a further 100 (27%) unfaithful-but-not-false, giving 204 (56%); and the three axes verbatim, "provability, logical strength, and root cause", so logical strength is a named axis. CORRECTED: the 4.8% to 60.0% range is the unfaithful rate across the SIX OTHER benchmarks and does NOT include ProofNet's 56%, which the entry conflates. UNVERIFIED: the sentence "absolute quality is dominated by curatorial process" appears in neither the abstract nor the README, and the body was never opened — so the entry's strongest objection rests on a quote nobody in this batch or this pass has read, and every use of it is now flagged inline. COULD NOT READ: whether any covariate of the source material is analysed, and whether axioms are tracked at all. The comparator is the benchmark's own shipped informal statement rather than a published theorem, which is what the entry claims — but that now rests on the README's data schema (informal_stmt paired with formal_stmt, labels including "Ambiguous NL" and "Misunderstanding of informal statement"), an inference from a secondary source rather than a finding from the paper. One internal inconsistency to carry: the README's own table gives 194 unfaithful where the abstract's arithmetic gives 204.
V2. PRIOR 1 (Best, FMM 2021) CONFIRMED on every figure with its units intact, read as the CEUR PDF. About 80,000 mathlib declarations at one commit excluding core Lean, in a single pass; 2,877 RESULTS for the full run; 183 results from 475 declarations in a single-file run on topology/ordered/basic.lean. The comparator is decisively the declaration's own elaborated proof term — the tool reads typeclass requirements off the proof, and inspecting only the existing proof is listed as a limitation — with NOT FOUND for any comparison against a published paper or textbook, NOT FOUND for any fraction or rate (the words percent, %, and proportion do not occur), NOT FOUND for axiom tracking, and NOT FOUND for any measurement about the published literature. Two cautions for anyone citing it: 2,877 counts results and not declarations, so 2877/80000 is not a valid rate, and 183/475 is a single-file subset not comparable with the library-wide run.
V3. PRIOR 2 (Meek et al., arXiv:2606.14000v1) CONFIRMED to exist and read as full text, with four corrections that all move it AWAY from the candidate. (i) The triples are in TABLE 2, not Table 1 — Table 1 is "Number of open sorries and unnecessary axioms across formalization systems" (RepoProver 5 sorries / 0 axioms, M2F 12 / 4, OpenMath 0 / 0) — so the entry's "Table-1 figures" is mislabelled. (ii) The figures are percentages with entity counts: Faithful / Stronger / Different = OpenMath 54% (51) / 4% (4) / 42% (40), M2F 73% (1,359) / 2% (42) / 25% (463), RepoProver 82% (1,173) / 1% (12) / 18% (253), with a separate round-trip row at 46/14/40, 61/13/26 and 69/11/19. (iii) The counts 175, 4,636 and 6,960 are NOT the units of this analysis: 175 is the statement count of the Butcher ODE textbook (the denominator of a 54.9% coverage figure), while 4,636 and 6,960 are proof counts in the separate Table 3 Mathlib-overlap analysis; the Table 2 n are about 95, 1,864 and 1,438, derived by summing cells because the paper does not state them. (iv) DECISIVELY, "Stronger" does NOT explicitly include dropping a redundant hypothesis: the rubric defines it as "a sound generalization, acceptable for a formalization audit", and the one worked case that drops hypotheses (Theorem 523A, positive-semi-definiteness) was labelled DIFFERENT, with the paper noting "The judge correctly flagged this as Different" even though the authors regard the Lean identity as mathematically correct. The attribute that made PRIOR 2 close to the candidate is therefore not in it. Also: for M2F, the largest corpus, the direct comparator is largely M2F's own generated docstring, so 73% is a self-consistency figure and not faithfulness to a textbook; labels come from LLM judges (DeepSeek-V4-Pro direct, gpt-oss-120b round-trip) with human checking only on a stratified sample of 20 OpenMath entities (agreement on 18); the judged statements are agent-produced throughout ("we keep only the Lean theorem statement and discard the proof"); and NOT FOUND for confidence intervals, for any covariate analysis of the source material, and for any audit of the sampling frame, with the paper itself stating in Section 5.3 that its drops are not missing at random.
V4. Net effect: the verdict does not move, but two of the three promotion conditions are now better specified. Condition (ii), the Disguise completion, is unchanged and still blocks Validated on its own. The novelty risk from PRIOR 3 is live but unmeasured: it cannot be graded against this candidate until someone opens its body, and that read is added to the promotion conditions below.

Strongest remaining objection: the question presupposes that a formal-vs-source divergence carries information about the published literature, and the nearest measurements point the other way — "Ground False" (ICML 2026, 7 corpora, 4.8–60.0% unfaithful) concludes that "absolute quality is dominated by curatorial process" [QUOTE UNVERIFIED — see Verification V1; the full text could not be opened], and the one human-authored corpus audit opened (miniF2F-Lean Revisited: >50% of problems divergent, >300 statements corrected) attributes divergence to formalizer simplification — while the protocol has no root-cause arm separating discovered slack from library generality policy (mathlib's own values page makes maximal generality a documented design value), from adoption of post-publication generalizations (which also confounds the age covariate), or from error; and the axiom sub-limb compares against a paper-side axiom set that papers never declare.

---
ID: UQ-20261017-45
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — civil/environmental engineering; LCA; construction-materials standardisation (EN 15804 / ISO 21930 and its PCRs); public procurement policy. Method-owning neighbours: metrology (variance components / MSA), composite-indicator sensitivity analysis (rank reversal).

Question (canonical):
On a pre-declared, machine-extracted frame of published EPDs for construction products, partitioned into functional classes by a normalisation fixed before any data pull (declared unit, performance/strength class, reference service life, stage set A1-A3 minimum), with the method-effect estimator declared in advance as the within-product contrast across repeated declarations of the SAME product under differing method configurations (PCR version, allocation rule, background-database identity and vintage, declared-unit conversion, programme operator, verifier): (i) what share of within-class variance in declared GWP is attributable to method/background-data configuration versus producer/plant identity; (ii) under harmonised recomputation at one declared reference configuration, what fraction of pairwise within-class comparisons reverse sign and what fraction of compliance determinations against the threshold in force at declaration date (e.g. a Buy Clean maximum acceptable GWP) cross the threshold; (iii) what fraction of the frame was dropped for missing method metadata, by field?
(V1 intake wording and the Gate 1 reformulation rationale are in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-45-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
- Do EPDs measure factories or methods, and does the answer change who wins a Buy Clean procurement?
- For products carrying multiple declarations, how large is the method-induced component of declared GWP relative to the plant-to-plant component, and does it exceed the margin at which procurement thresholds are set?

Motivating gap:
Silence mapping. The standards regime specifies how to compute and verify a declaration; every declaration prints a non-comparability caveat; procurement then compares declared values against numerical thresholds anyway. California DGS's statutory *Buy Clean California Act GWP adjustment study* (1 Jan 2025) names programme-operator plurality, inconsistent review periods, modelling assumptions and datasets/software as what its own discrepancies "could be attributed to", quantifies none of them, and selects industry-wide EPDs for "consistency"; EC3, which mediates most US low-carbon material selection, assigns a flat 3% LCIA-method uncertainty term with allocation "not modeled" and states its methodology "has not been extensively peer-reviewed". The corpus is now machine-readable at the scale of tens of thousands of declarations.

Presuppositions:
1. Enumerable, linkable corpus with extractable method metadata and adequate per-class n. CONTESTED and binding (metadata completeness, not corpus size).
2. Functional equivalence enforceable by declared normalisation. Supported.
3. Harmonised recomputation / identified method-correction possible; EPDs publish results not inventories, so identification may rest on the repeat-declared subset, which may be unrepresentative. CONTESTED — binding threat to limb (i).
4. Plant-level production differences real and non-negligible. Supported (DGS facility counts).
5. Thresholds known, binding, applied to declared values as published. Supported (BCCA limits statutory and changed 1 Jan 2025; rebar 890->755).
6. Declared values not already strategically selected by producers (PCR, verifier, declaring plant). CONTESTED — makes part of the "method component" behavioural.
7. PCR committees, programme operators and agencies would act on a measured split. CONTESTED.

What would count as an answer:
(i) a within-class variance decomposition of declared GWP into method/background-data and producer/plant components, estimated from repeated declarations of the same product under differing configurations, with transportability from the repeat-declared subset reported as a sensitivity rather than assumed; (ii) the share of pairwise within-class comparisons and of threshold determinations that reverse under harmonised recomputation, with uncertainty; (iii) frame dropout by metadata field. An explicit null — small method component, few reversals — counts as an answer.

29 distinct queries (11 Gate 2; 9 adversary 1; 9 adversary 2) plus 13 fetches. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-45-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative:

- "statistical analysis large EPD database drivers of variation in declared embodied carbon concrete steel benchmark study" (own field, own words) -> CTU Prague cement/concrete EPD analysis; CLF "Carbon in construction materials"; unibz "Role of Environmental Product Declarations" record — surfaced and NOT OPENED at Gate 2; this is P4 (see below).
- "EC3 database concrete EPD regression analysis drivers of GWP variation program operator PCR version mix design explained variance" (A1 D4) -> re-surfaced the same unibz/DOAJ record, which A1 then opened at the publisher as P4.
- "'program operator' effect on declared GWP EPD statistically significant difference same product category regression study" (A1 D7, answer-side) -> P4 again, plus P1 and the DGS BCCA compliance regime.
- "rank reversal sensitivity to methodological choices ranking of products environmental indicator share of pairs reversed" (composite-indicator vocabulary) -> JRC/EPI sensitivity canon; mature method family, not applied to EPDs or thresholds.

P1. Konradsen et al. (2023), "Same product, different score: how methodological differences affect EPD results", *IJLCA*, DOI 10.1007/s11367-023-02246-x. Endpoint: category average declared GWP and compliance counts. Comparator: the limit in force vs candidate alternative limits. Estimand: whether to lower each limit (rebar 27/27 at 890, 18/27 at 755, 13/27 at 689.1; adopted 890->755). Significance — consequence:
Unchanged by the rejection and genuine in outline: if method components dominated and determinations crossed under harmonisation, Buy Clean-style limits would be sorting producers partly by LCA consultant, PCR vintage and database licence rather than by kiln, furnace or grid — fixable by harmonised recomputation as a procurement requirement or method-robust threshold bands. If the null held, the printed non-comparability caveat would be shown over-conservative in practice and EC3's assigned factors replaceable by measured ones. The opened corpus evidence (P4, Anderson & Moncaster, AzariJafari) already points toward the null for the A1-A3 stage set that Buy Clean regulates, which is what deflates the magnitude case built on P1's 12-50% swings.

Significance — audience:
Real and statutory: threshold-setting agencies (California DGS under PCC s.3502(c), which revised limits by ~15% in 2025 while declining to quantify the confound; GSA, FHWA; EPA under IRA s.60503/60506 and its open RFI on "substantially lower" thresholds; EU CPR/GPP analogues); PCR committees and programme operators (IBU, EPD Denmark/Norway/International, UL, NSF, ASTM, EPD Australasia); tool and database operators whose adjustment factors are currently stipulated (Building Transparency / C-Change Labs); producers and trade bodies (AISC, CRSI). Both adversaries graded audience reality Resolved or conceded it; the inflation is in the claimed magnitude, not the audience.

Significance — fecundity:
Would open: a repeat-declaration panel as a standing measurement-system audit of the declaration system; method-effect correction as a verified field on the declaration; strategic responsiveness of producers' PCR, verifier and plant choices to the threshold in force (a behavioural elasticity, and threshold gaming as an empirical question in a procurement literature that has none); method-robust threshold design; the same decomposition for the other declared indicators.

Significance — anchoring:
The EN 15804 / ISO 21930 non-comparability caveat and what it claims; the unvalidated status of EC3's uncertainty factors; DGS's explicit non-attribution; the mature but barely transplanted rank-reversal / composite-indicator sensitivity literature and metrology's variance-components framework.

Reason for silence:
As recorded: (1) the printed caveat discharges the question; (2) the parties able to compute the split are the parties it would impugn; (3) the method lives in a field that does not read this one; (4) only recently answerable. Mechanism (3) is falsified by opened evidence — P4 ran ANOVA with operator and database as factors on the corpus in 2025, so the transplant has happened — and (4) is undercut by the same paper having mined the corpus already. Adversary 1 graded this attack Unresolved on that basis; adversary 2, which never saw P4, graded it Partial and noted that mechanisms (2)-(4) explain why answering is hard rather than why asking did not happen, leaving the whole load on (1). The better explanation of the residual silence is that the first-pass corpus answer looked null, so the decision limb seemed moot.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17, one fresh-context reader handed the single paper the kill rests on and the claim made of it, and not shown the adversary's reasoning; log in batches/2026-10-17-1823/UQ-20261017-45-verification-asdrubali.md): Rejected STANDS, on a narrower reading than the kill wrote. The paper exists, all five of its quoted test statistics exist, and it does pose and answer limb (i) on a published-EPD corpus — but it answers it by SIGNIFICANCE TESTING, not by the attribution of spread the candidate asks for, it tests two of the candidate's four methodological factors, and its own headline is contradicted by its own concrete result.
V1. CONFIRMED, read as full text (MDPI HTML; the PDF route returned 403, and table cell values were not visible). The corpus is as described: EPS 97 EPDs, stone wool 41, bricks 60, ready-mix concrete 79 GWP values, cement 64 GWP values, natural stone 58 certifications, steel sections 59 plus rebar 20, windows 70 valid EPDs giving 178 GWP values, wood 101, plus PV 24 and heat pumps 7 excluded as too few; Section 2.1 lists 25 sources plus the ECO Platform umbrella, with no stated total, and the concrete and cement counts are GWP VALUES rather than EPDs. The paper does test programme operator, background database, country and producer organisation against physical and process variables, per product class, using t-tests, bootstrapped t-tests, ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Spearman, linear regression with R-squared, a White heteroscedasticity test and k-means. All five quoted statistics are present in the running text: concrete strength class F = 15.03, p = 3.57e-15; cement strength class F = 8.4, p = 0.0006; steel basic-oxygen-furnace against electric-arc-furnace Kruskal-Wallis p = 2.73e-8; concrete programme operator F = 6.84, p = 0.0002; concrete country F = 4.42, p = 0.0008. The concluding sentence is there, in the Discussion's final paragraph: the programme operator and the LCA background database "did not play a very relevant role in determining embodied climate change impacts of all products considered", attributed to European methodological harmonisation. So the kill's central claim — that this question is asked and answered in the candidate's own literature, on the candidate's own corpus type — is CORRECT and first-hand, and the adversary that found it had genuinely read it.
V2. CORRECTION: the paper performs NO VARIANCE DECOMPOSITION. Checked across the whole body: NOT FOUND for any share of variance, eta-squared, or split of the declared-GWP spread into a methodological and a real-performance component; the only R-squared is single-predictor (stone wool density against GWP, 0.818). So it answers "is this factor significant?" and not "how much of the difference is attributable to it?", which is the candidate's estimand. That is an estimand difference, not merely an estimator one.
V3. CORRECTION: it tests TWO of the candidate's four methodological factors. Product category rule version is NOT tested as a factor — Section 2.1 treats EN 15804 +A1 and +A2 as substantially equivalent — the allocation method is not examined at all, and the declared-unit conversion appears only as a harmonisation STEP the authors perform (tonnes via density, square metres via thickness, insulation at 1 m2 and R = 1 m2K/W over 50 years), never as a factor whose effect is estimated. Procurement appears only as an Introduction citation to EU Green Public Procurement, with no conclusion that methodological choices change a procurement decision.
V4. CORRECTION, and the most useful one: the paper's headline does not hold for concrete, and the paper does not say so. For ready-mix concrete the programme operator (F = 6.84, p = 0.0002) and the country (F = 4.42, p = 0.0008) ARE significant; Section 3.3 explains this by an overlap between programme operators and geography and does not test that explanation or control for it, and the Discussion's "all products considered" sentence carries no carve-out for concrete. The paper also calls the result "substantial equivalence" immediately after reporting significance. So within the very corpus the kill cites, the one highest-volume product class shows a significant methodological-factor effect that is left unexplained and unquantified.
V5. Effect on the verdict: NONE. Limb (i) is asked and answered in print, which is what attack 2 needed, and an estimand upgrade from significance to variance share plus two additional factors is the covariate-and-estimator swap this ledger rejects. But the entry's closing judgement — that the limb (ii) residue "belongs back in this ledger as a narrower candidate" — now has concrete content, and it is recorded here so a later batch does not have to rediscover it: the unoccupied question is the share of within-class declared-GWP spread attributable to PCR version, allocation choice and declared-unit conversion, which this paper never tests, in the one product class where its own data show a programme-operator effect it declines to explain. That is a narrower question than this candidate and must clear Gate 2 on its own.
Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness stands at 3/3 on V2 and was attacked only to Partial on vagueness and presuppositions, not below. Significance reduced from the Gate 3 self-score of 3/3 to 2/3: audience and consequence survive, fecundity survives, but the magnitude argument rested on P1 effects that the question's own normalisation removes, while three opened corpus sources point to the null for the A1-A3 stage set the policy regulates. Both scores are moot — the entry fails on novelty.)

Strongest remaining objection:
Limb (i) is a disguised known. Asdrubali, Grazieschi & Gandola 2025 (*Energies* 18(5):1308) already pose the candidate's central contrast on a 25-operator published-EPD corpus, binned by product class, testing programme operator and background database against producer organisation, country and physical/process variables, and answer it — physical and process variables dominate, "the PO and the background database used in the LCA did not play a very relevant role". The candidate's additions are a sharper within-product estimator, two further factors and a decision limb; by the ledger's own rule an estimator or covariate swap on an asked question is Rejected even where the exact variant is unmeasured. That the record surfaced this paper twice, labelled it a review and never opened it is the failure mode the Gate 2 rules warn about in terms: the kill came from an on-point paper in the candidate's own literature, found by query choice rather than query count.

ID: UQ-20261017-46
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected — Gate 2 (novelty Low; asked-but-open). Gate 4 ran anyway, twice, on the Gate 0-3 record only (per the operating rule that every candidate draws two adversaries, including a Gate 2 kill); neither adversary returned an Unresolved attack, so Gate 4 does not itself reject and the verdict rests wholly on the Gate 2 ground, which both adversaries independently re-graded as Low.
Domain(s): AI architecture — evaluation methodology and inference-stack engineering (secondary: model compression). Method-owning neighbours: psychometrics, reliability engineering (common-cause failure), MLOps (prediction churn / predictive multiplicity), metrology (ISO 5725), SE DNN-testing ("disagreements").
Question (canonical): For one fixed open-weight checkpoint and one fixed exact-match / multiple-choice benchmark under a pinned extraction rule, run at batch size 1 offline under P >= 4 independently-mechanised perturbations the field treats as leaving the nominal model unchanged (quantization family at matched bit width: GPTQ / AWQ / RTN; release-dtype cast bf16 <-> fp16; attention kernel: eager / SDPA / FlashAttention; decode seed at fixed T > 0), is the set of items whose correctness flips shared across perturbation TYPES beyond what item-specific independent Bernoulli flipping predicts — does the benchmark carry a common "fragile stratum" — and what share of the headline score sits inside it?
  Reformulation R1 (the one permitted at Gate 1, both versions recorded): cross each type with k >= 5 exchangeable instances and ask whether the BETWEEN-TYPE component of per-item flip propensity is non-zero once the WITHIN-TYPE component has fixed each item's own rate p_i, whether it survives conditioning on the measured top-two logit margin, and what share of the headline score the top fragility decile contributes.
Alternative formulations:
1. Do independent, semantically meaningless changes to how a model is run flip the same benchmark questions, or different ones?
2. What fraction of a reported benchmark score is carried by items whose correctness is decided by numerics rather than by the model, and is that set a property of the item or of the perturbation?
Motivating gap: arXiv:2407.09141 ("Accuracy is Not All You Need") introduced "flips" and reported double-digit flip rates for compressed LLMs at near-unchanged aggregate accuracy, without any item-level flip-set analysis, cross-method concordance statistic, independent-Bernoulli null, or non-compression arm. That reading of 2407.09141 verifies. The implied wider claim — that the item-level question is therefore open — does not: Gate 2 found a published fragile-share figure in an adjacent perturbation family, a fitted and calibrated per-item margin -> flip model in the quantization family, and the shared-unstable-item existence claim already in print qualitatively in the numerics family.
Presuppositions: P1 per-item correctness deterministically extractable — established only within the stated exact-match/MCQ restriction, and the extraction rule is itself a perturbation axis (2608.21382), so it must be pinned. P2 the arms are treated as nominally semantics-preserving — contested for quantization (openly lossy); the design separates the lossy arm from nominally lossless ones, and 2609.04748 affirmatively supports the attitude-vs-property gap (a nominally lossless cache change moved 36.2% of episodes at batch size 1). P3 the arms are mechanistically independent — STRONGLY CONTESTED and made worse by Gate 2: all arms act through the same final logit margin, and 2608.06564 shows pre-perturbation margin predicts flips well. P4 heterogeneous per-item flip propensity, so the null is non-trivial — supported. P5 batch-size-1 offline execution removes batch-composition mediation — checkable, and the candidate's one clean advance over the opened priors; adversary 2 found a second mediator (prefix/KV-cache state) that survives batch size 1 and the design never pins, repairable but unstated. P6 per-item flip rates estimable at achievable replicate counts — false for V0 and fatal to it (see Gate 1).
What would count as an answer: pairwise and P-way concordance of flip sets (Jaccard, Fleiss' kappa, tetrachoric common-factor fit) against the pre-registered within-type null; the between-type variance component with a CI; the share of the headline score from the top fragility decile; and the residual concordance after conditioning on measured top-two logit margin. "Shared stratum exists" if concordance exceeds the null's upper 95% bound AND survives margin conditioning; "it does not" if concordance collapses to null once per-item rates are free; "margin explains it" if the residual vanishes. All three are answers.
