VERDICT UNCHANGED: Provisional. Every one of the three nearest prior formulations was confirmed to be what this entry said it was, on the clause that matters in each case, and the strongest objection survives in sharper form. One promotion condition is discharged, one number was wrong, one characterisation was overstated, and three quotations needed repair; all are corrected in place above.

PROMOTION ITEM (i) IS DISCHARGED. Salvà-Serra et al., "Beware of False 'Type Strain' Genome Sequences", Microbiology Resource Announcements 8(22):e00369-19 (2019), doi 10.1128/MRA.00369-19, is about MISLABELLING: five strains in five Genome Announcements papers reported as type strains while not descending from the designated nomenclatural types under ICNP rule 18a, with one, Lelliottia nimipressuralis SGAir0187, additionally misclassified at species level. It makes no claim anywhere that two AUTHENTIC holdings of one type strain differ from each other, and its Table 1 ANI values compare a mislabelled strain against the authentic type — different organisms, not divergent holdings — so they must not be cited as divergence figures. It gives a count of five with NO denominator, no rate and no share. Borgers et al., BMC Genomics 20:561 (2019), doi 10.1186/s12864-019-5909-5, is framed as the specific history of one vaccine and generalises no further than TB vaccines; asked un-primed, it does not pose divergence between institutions' holdings in general as open or future work. So the existing "type strain" literature is about identification error rather than material divergence, which is the gap this candidate occupies.

THREE FINDINGS THAT STRENGTHEN THE CASE, all first-hand. (1) NO MEASUREMENT-LEVEL FLOOR EXISTS IN EITHER ATCC SOURCE: nothing in the paper or the poster says how much of the median 7 SNPs and 8 indels is expected noise, which is precisely what limb (b)'s internal comparator exists to supply. (2) THE BCG PAPER ENCOUNTERS THIS CANDIDATE'S PHENOMENON AND ANSWERS IT WITH A REPORTING NORM: its own BCG Danish disagrees with Abdallah et al.'s published BCG Danish at two loci — an 894 bp deletion not found, and a leuA insertion of 399 bp rather than 118 bp — a disagreement between two laboratories' accounts of the SAME substrain, to which its response is to "demand for the specification of the exact origin of the BCG strain(s) used". That is a field hitting the phenomenon and institutionalising provenance hygiene instead of measuring a rate, which is direct evidence for this entry's reason-for-silence answer. (3) TWO UNRELATED SYSTEMS NOW SIZE THE EFFECT, by my own arithmetic on their printed numbers: BCG gives 1 SNP within one laboratory's own lineage (the sapM knockout against its parental wild type) against 42 SNPs between two institutes' substrains, a 42-fold gap; Desroches gives a de facto within-NCTC spread of 0 to 17 SNPs against 164, 803 and 878 across collections, 9.6-fold at the nearest point and 52-fold at the extremes. Both floors are confounded — platform varies with material in one, an engineered knockout in the other — so this sizes what limb (b) would measure and does not substitute for measuring it. A NECESSARY CAVEAT ON THE BCG FIGURE: that divergence was deliberately ARRESTED, a 1956 frozen seed-lot system and a 1966 WHO passage-limit recommendation having "halted the accumulation of additional genetic changes", so 42 SNPs is a frozen historical figure and bounds nothing about ongoing drift in collections with no such regime — which also strengthens this entry's existing point that BCG substrains are not catalogue cross-references asserting equivalence.

THE STRONGEST OBJECTION SURVIVES AND SHARPENS. Its substance was that the frame is built from link EXISTENCE while limb (b) needs link MEANING, and verification establishes both halves more strongly than the entry argued. NCIMB describes NO PROCEDURE for establishing a cross-reference at all: it describes how overlap ARISES and how the claim TRAVELS — "Culture collections share this information on equivalency, where it is known, and most publish a list of 'equivalents' in other collections within their catalogues" — with no laboratory comparison of the two holdings, no inter-collection agreement and no provenance audit anywhere on the page, its own hedge being "where it is known". So the cross-reference is an inherited bibliographic and provenance assertion, not a result of comparing material. And DSMZ makes NO CLAIM AND NO DENIAL about equivalence, a full-text-level absence across the field guide read field by field AND all 44 FAQ items, which never discuss strains held by other collections at all: its cross-reference field is UNDEFINED AS TO MEANING rather than merely minimal.

PROMOTION ITEM (ii) NEEDS A THIRD STRATUM. This entry names two provenance routes, isolator co-deposit and inter-collection re-shipment. NCIMB names three, the third being a collection ITSELF acting as depositor — "in some cases the depositor of the strain to the NCIMB collection was in fact another culture collection", and in the worked example "the company that deposited the strain with NCIMB was the American Type Culture Collection". Add it. The Campylobacter prior also supplies a FEASIBILITY PRECEDENT for that stratification, having split its own frame into ten isolates obtained directly from NCTC against thirteen that came via another laboratory, with signal along exactly that axis: "All three hyper-motile strains were passed between at least two laboratories before entering our collection."

A VERIFICATION POLICY DISTINCTION NOT TO BLUR: DSMZ documents AUTHENTICITY, not genomic verification — "All lots of our strains are checked for strain authenticity with strain-specific methodologies" (per lot) and "Viability and authenticity of each strain is routinely tested at the DSMZ" (per strain) — with the methodologies never named and nowhere stated to be sequencing. JCM is the only dated, mechanism-specific policy found: 16S rRNA GENE sequencing of newly deposited strains since 2011, checked against depositor-supplied data, with strains deposited before 2011 (JCM 12229T among them) not checked that way and JCM working through those lacking confirmation — a single locus, not whole-genome, with an explicit pre-2011 coverage gap. Note that this entry's second JCM example, JCM 1633T, reached SEARCH SNIPPETS ONLY and its page was never opened, so it remains UNVERIFIED.

WHAT GATE 5 STILL CAPS, stated so it is not mistaken for a clear run. With item (i) discharged this entry reads as novelty Medium, well-posedness 3/3, significance 3/3, no Unresolved attack from any of three adversaries, and a search record now complete in the one respect it had declared incomplete. Gate 5's Validated line ("Novelty >= Medium with the complete search record") is then satisfied on its face, while its Provisional line independently catches "Medium novelty with a close neighbor" — and this entry names three nearest prior formulations. The two lines conflict for any entry in exactly this position, and the established reading on this ledger holds it at Provisional, as it held UQ-20261017-07 and UQ-20261017-50. So items (ii) to (iv) are NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and they are design repairs its author would make rather than anything a reading pass can discharge: what would actually lift this entry is an estimand distinct enough from (A), (B) and (C) to regrade novelty above Medium.

RESIDUALS. Appendix S1-equivalent supplements were not reached anywhere in this pass; Table S5 and Fig. S4 of the ATCC paper, where a distribution might be tabulated, are unread, so its absent numeric IQR is a main-text finding only. The DSMZ field guide's canonical URL sits under /archive/ while the page itself carries no archived or superseded notice, and whether a current non-archive field guide exists with different wording is UNCHECKED — anyone resting on that field definition should treat it as possibly superseded. Neither collection page prints any publication or last-updated date. NCIMB's quality-management and accreditation pages were not read, so the absence of a sequencing policy is established for the one page read and is UNCHECKED for ncimb.com as a whole.

ID: UQ-20261018-17
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — biochemistry / in vitro reconstitution and quantitative cell biology; secondary: biophysics of biomolecular condensates. Neighbour vocabularies swept: regulatory toxicology / IVIVE, nutrition and chemoprevention ("physiologically achievable concentration"), ecotoxicology (free concentration in in vitro systems), metabolic systems-biology enzymology, macromolecular crowding, bottom-up synthetic biology, HPS.
Question (canonical): Across the published in vitro reconstitution literature for a declared process family, what is the distribution of the ratio between each component's concentration in the reconstitution and its measured concentration in the cell where the process is claimed to occur, and in what fraction of reconstitutions does the demonstrated sufficiency fail when every component is held at its cellular concentration?
Alternative formulations: Does the reconstitution literature show that purified components are sufficient for a cellular process, or only that they are sufficient at concentrations the cell never reaches? / For each published reconstitution, how far above cellular concentration was each component pushed to make the process run, and does that fold-excess predict whether additional cellular factors were later found to be required? (One Gate 1 reformulation, V2, recorded in the record: one pre-declared process family and registry-defined frame, a declared comparator ladder — cell-average, compartment-average, bounded local-enrichment allowance of ≤10^2 — log10 ratios with two-sided uncertainty, thresholds at 10^0.5 / 10^1 / 10^2, and a bench subset re-run at rung (a) against a pre-declared detection limit with buffer/crowding/temperature as declared arms.)
Motivating gap: Intake held that the sufficiency claim of a reconstitution rests on an untested concentration presupposition, that absolute proteomics (PaxDb) now makes the comparison checkable at literature scale, and — load-bearing — that the worry is argued only qualitatively inside the condensate subfield and "nowhere quantified as a distribution over a frame". That central negative is false as stated: the fold-excess distribution was published in 2021, over a declared frame, with PaxDb as the comparator, in the candidate's own declared secondary subfield (Prior 1).
Presuppositions: (1) reconstitution papers report component concentrations in extractable units — contested and evidenced biased (Prior 1 could form the ratio for 75/89 frame proteins and 30 of those 75 had no usable Csat); (2) a matched cellular concentration exists per component — contested (absolute proteomics covers a minority well; copy-number→concentration needs an uncertain volume); (3) cell-average total concentration is the right comparator — contested and against the candidate's interest (Prior 1's authors call PaxDb values "theoretical lower limits"); (4) "sufficiency fails at cellular concentration" is decidable with a declared detection limit — must be designed in, and Prior 2's conditions were chosen post hoc against the in-cell target with no held-out test; (5) the in vitro process is the same process as the cellular one — contested case by case (Prior 2's endpoint is partitioning and FRAP, not function); (6) later discovery of a required factor is codable without hindsight bias — no precedent found anywhere; (7) buffer, crowding and temperature are secondary to concentration — contested and probably false (Prior 2's best match needed pH 5.8, 30 °C, 300 mM KOAc, ATP).
What would count as an answer: a pre-declared frame; per (paper, component) in-vitro concentration paired with a matched cellular concentration carrying its own uncertainty; the log-fold-excess distribution and the fraction of reconstitutions above pre-declared thresholds; for a pre-specified subset, a bench re-run with all components at cellular concentration against a declared detection limit with buffer/crowding as declared arms; and a pre-registered test of association between maximum fold-excess and subsequent identification of additional required factors. Small fold-excesses with sufficiency surviving the drop would be an equally decisive answer. Gate 2 finding: for the condensate family that answer is already partly on the record and it is mixed.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 31 distinct queries across three agents (Gate 2: 11 searches + 5 fetches; adversary 1: 9 + 4; adversary 2: 11 + 3), full lists in batches/2026-10-18-0945/UQ-20261018-17-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: "do proteins phase separate at physiological concentrations in vitro saturation concentration compared to cellular concentration" (own field, own words, answer-side) → the near-duplicate, Prior 1, the in-vitro-vs-PaxDb comparison itself; "ratio of in vitro assay concentration to in vivo exposure across published studies distribution meta-analysis nominal concentration" (method-owning field) → the ratio method is named and routine in regulatory toxicology, no transplant into reconstitution biochemistry; "meta-research what fraction of studies used supraphysiological concentrations" ("what fraction of X" already computed) → no published fraction except Prior 1's 33.3 / 22.7 / 44 split; adversary 2 query 1 (nutrition/clinical pharmacology) and query 7 (ecotoxicology) → the corpus-ratio analysis is a named method in both, records only, not opened; adversary 2 query 4 → the cellular-over-in-vitro-critical-concentration ratio is computed proteome-wide as "supersaturation" (not opened, endpoint is solubility not assay concentration); adversary 1 D7 (chromatin assembly) and adversary 2 queries 6 and 8 (motility assays, PURE/bottom-up) → no ratio formed in any non-condensate family; "reconstitution physiological concentrations additional factors required later discovered" and eleven further vocabularies → nothing at all on limb 3. No PMC or Europe PMC route attempted (hard-blocked). Its subject is "The LATTER values", fixed by the preceding sentence as the PaxDb-DERIVED values specifically, which that sentence contrasts with the authors' own local-niche estimates and says the local estimates "represent effective (local) concentrations much better than PaxDb-derived values": so it demotes PaxDb RELATIVE TO local estimates rather than cautioning generally about cellular concentrations. Prior 2 — "Quantitative reconstitution of yeast RNA processing bodies" (Rosen lab; PNAS 2023; read as bioRxiv 2022.08.13.503854, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.08.13.503854.full.pdf); READ by Gate 2, not re-opened by either adversary. Unit: individual in vitro condensates/micrographs in an eight-component reconstitution. Endpoint: partition coefficient, FRAP recovery and exchange, fractional overlap. Comparator: previously published in vivo yeast P-body partitioning and dynamics. Estimand: in vitro vs in vivo agreement against a ~2-fold threshold with every protein at its estimated cellular concentration. Prior 3 — "Cytosolic concentrations of actin binding proteins and the implications for in vivo F-actin turnover", J Cell Biol 2023;222(12):e202306036 (https://rupress.org/jcb/article-pdf/222/12/e202306036/1919319/jcb_202306036.pdf); READ. Comparator: internal cross-method, S. pombe values, cell-cycle stage — not in vitro concentrations. Estimand: population-mean cytosolic concentration and the ABP-to-binding-site ratio; runs no reconstitution.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Prior 1 — this is the near-duplicate and it duplicates the limb the candidate leads with: same fraction-above-threshold shape, on a declared frame, in one of the candidate's own declared domains — but NOT, on verification, the same comparator and NOT a ratio at all. Prior 1's cellular value is each protein's MAXIMUM across tissues and cell lines ("the highest of its PaxDb-derived cellular concentrations"), where this candidate's estimand presupposes a cell AVERAGE; and the prior forms no ratio, binning order-of-magnitude excess instead, while posing no open question about the in vitro-to-cellular ratio anywhere. THE DIRECTION OF THAT DIFFERENCE STRENGTHENS THIS REJECTION RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT: measured against the maximum, the excess is SMALLER than it would be against an average, so the prior's "33 proteins (44%) above by more than one order of magnitude" is a CONSERVATIVE LOWER BOUND on the candidate's own quantity. Running limb 1 against a cell average could only move the fraction up, so it would strengthen the prior's published conclusion rather than test anything the prior left open. The verifier put this at "at least 30 of the 75" while itself flagging the denominator of the "30" as textually unresolved between 78 and 75; under the 78 reading the 30 may include up to all three proteins excluded from the 75 (LAT, SYN2, YTHDF3), so the defensible figure is AT LEAST 27 OF 75 (36%), reaching exactly 30 of 75 (40%) only if "these proteins" means the 75. ID: UQ-20261018-18
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — systematics/taxonomy and biodiversity informatics (target field). Method transplanted from forecast verification / calibration of verbal probability expressions and from diagnostic-test predictive value.

Question (canonical): For specimen and occurrence records bearing an open-nomenclature qualifier ("cf.", "aff.", "sp.", "?"), drawn only from sources in which qualifier survival from original label to delivered record has been verified end-to-end, and under a resolution rule declared before any data pull: what is the per-qualifier agreement rate with an independent later determination at a declared rank (reported separately for a revision-based arm and a sequence-backed arm), does that rate order the qualifiers in the sequence their published usage guidance implies, and does the between-stratum spread of that rate across determiner, institution, higher taxon and decade stay inside a pre-declared tolerance — the tolerance being the criterion for whether an aggregator may read the mark as a transferable probability?

Alternative formulations:
- Do taxonomy's hedging marks carry a reproducible probability — does "cf." mean the same chance of being right in two collections, two taxa or two decades?
- Treating each qualified determination as a probabilistic forecast and each later revision or barcode-backed determination as its resolution, how well calibrated are open-nomenclature qualifiers, and how is the miscalibration distributed across determiners and higher taxa?
(V1, as intaken, and the Gate 1 reformulation rationale are in batches/2026-10-18-0945/UQ-20261018-18-record.md; V2 is scored as canonical.)

Motivating gap: Open nomenclature is a formalised convention with published usage guidance and an asserted ordinal confidence axis (Sigovini et al. 2016, read: "the degree of confidence essentially increases from the top down"), which itself records that authors rank "aff." and "cf." in opposite orders and defers numbers to a prospective [0,1] field. The marks propagate at scale into aggregated data, where consumers drop or keep qualified records by convention and the backbone silently lifts unmatched qualified names (Waller 2022, read). The resolution machinery already exists and has been used for the unconditional quantity (Goodwin et al. 2015, read: "at least 58%" wrong names; "29.1%" inter-herbarium disagreement) without conditioning on a qualifier. Three decades of listserv-level complaint that workers use the marks differently, never measured.

Presuppositions: (1) qualifiers retrievable at scale with the mark preserved — CONTESTED, evidenced contested by Waller 2022; (2) independent later determinations exist for enough qualified records — CONTESTED; (3) later determination as ground truth — CONTESTED and conceded (revision arm yields agreement, not predictive value; arms never pooled); (4) resolution not selected on prior doubt — CONTESTED, principal validity threat, requires wholesale-revision or whole-drawer-barcoding resolutions; (5) "confirmed" declared per rank — ESTABLISHED as a declaration; (6) determiner identifiers present for the by-determiner limb — CONTESTED, else reported unestimable; (7) determiners used the marks with documented meanings — NOT ASSUMED, this is the object; (8) that a probabilistic reading is the right reading — CONTESTED, flagged as dissolution risk, V2 phrased so the answer bears on whether users' reading is licensed.

What would count as an answer: a pre-declared frame of qualified determinations with qualifier survival verified end-to-end; a pre-declared resolution rule naming which determinations count and at which rank, revision and sequence arms separate; then (a) per-qualifier agreement rates with intervals, (b) a reliability curve against the qualifiers ordered as Sigovini 2016 Fig. 1 implies, (c) a variance decomposition across determiner, institution, higher taxon and decade against the declared tolerance, (d) a sensitivity analysis using only selection-free resolutions. Correct ordering at stratum-specific levels licenses a recalibration layer; no reproducible ordering establishes that the flag carries no transferable information.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 31 distinct queries in total — 11 at Gate 2, 9 by adversary 1, 11 by adversary 2 (full lists with per-query results in batches/2026-10-18-0945/UQ-20261018-18-record.md and -adversary-1.md / -adversary-2.md). Most informative: mandatory obvious-title query "Do open nomenclature qualifiers predict identification accuracy in natural history collections" -> Sigovini 2016 and the Goodwin 2015 record only, no qualifier-conditional paper; mandatory fraction query on the share of GBIF records carrying identificationQualifier -> no published count found (reported not-found, not zero); "words of estimative probability" / verbal-probability calibration applied to specimen determination -> mature method family, no transplant; misclassification-aware multispecies distribution models -> Adjei et al. estimate the confusion matrix inside the model and ignore reported hedges; zooarchaeological blind test + ZooMS -> Morin et al. 2023 and Hawkins et al. 2022, a real evaluative tradition reporting unconditional agreement with no qualifier breakdown; PBDB "cf."/"aff." modifiers -> the marks are a filter switch in divDyn and paleotree and nobody has measured what the filter removes; TDWG/Taxacom traffic on how far qualified records should be trusted -> TG2 (BISS 4:e58982) and Chapman's 2006 Taxacom thread, both normative; thesis "variation in the identification of the same specimens in different herbaria" -> Wang 2024, 2,713 Mitrephora records, ~52.58% misidentified or unidentified, no qualifier conditioning (the hit Gate 2 feared most, now tested and not a prior).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 Sigovini M., Keppel E. & Tagliapietra D., "Open Nomenclature in the biodiversity era", Methods in Ecology and Evolution 7:1217-1225 (2016), doi 10.1111/2041-210X.12594 (read in full) — unit: the qualifier term; endpoint: recommended usage and an ordinal confidence ranking — only PARTLY supported on verification. Figure 1's caption asserts the ordering ("The degree of confidence essentially increases from the top down"), but THE FLOW CHART'S OWN CONTENT, the actual qualifier sequence, was never reproduced, and a complete most-certain-to-least-certain ranked list is NOT FOUND in the main text; Appendix S1 is alphabetical rather than ranked AND is itself unread, so for the appendix this is COULD NOT READ and not an absence. What the text carries is contested PAIRWISE orderings and a floated proposal that confidence "could be quantified, for instance by assigning them a value in the [0,1] interval". The caption quotation itself runs ~128 characters, at or over the summariser's cap, and an independent search returned no corroborating hit, so it is summariser-relayed and not certified; comparator: prior authors' conventions; estimand: none. P2 Goodwin Z.A. et al., "Widespread mistaken identity in tropical plant collections", Current Biology 25:R1057-R1069 (2015) (read in full via Oxford ORA) — unit: the specimen (~4,500 Aframomum sheets, 40 herbaria in 21 countries) — correct for the Aframomum limb, which this entry names, but verification establishes that THE PAPER'S UNIT IS NOT UNIFORM and the estimand below is therefore one limb's, not the paper's: its three analyses count three different objects. Aframomum counts the individual SPECIMEN with its determination history; Dipterocarpaceae counts the COLLECTION or gathering (9,222 collections, each with at least two duplicate sheets, drawn from 58,860 specimens in NINE herbaria) and yields the 29.1% discordance; Ipomoea counts the NAME, explicitly — "we measured the accuracy of names rather than specimens" — over 560 names, yielding 40% and 16%, while the 11% in the same paragraph is a share of SPECIMENS, so those three are not slices of one denominator. Two further properties of the source: the Aframomum N is internally unreconciled, 4,500 specimens in the abstract against "N = 1,779" in the Figure 1B caption with no reconciliation in text, the headline 58% resting on the 4,500 framing and the time series on 1,779; and the much-quoted "more than 50%" of tropical specimens is the paper's own EXTRAPOLATION with NO stated denominator, not a measurement. DOI as printed, which this entry lacked: 10.1016/j.cub.2015.10.002. Format: a Current Biology MAGAZINE item with "Correspondence" as a running header and NO numbered or titled body sections at all — the only printed headings are SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION, ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS and REFERENCES — so nothing should cite its Introduction, Methods, Results or Discussion as sections; endpoint: name on sheet vs current name; reference: the 2015 monograph, or a duplicate elsewhere; estimand: unconditional prevalence of wrong names. P3 Adjei K.P., O'Hara R.B., Finstad A. & Koch W., "Accounting for Misclassification in Multispecies Distribution Models", arXiv:2204.03708 (read in full) — unit: the observation at a site; endpoint: reported category vs true species; reference: community verification; estimand: a confusion matrix estimated within the model under Dirichlet priors. Fourth close neighbour, found by adversary 2 and MISSED by Gate 2, inside the candidate's own literature: Belbin L., Chapman A., Wieczorek J., Morris P.J. & Zermoglio P.F., "Task Group 2 - Data Quality Tests and Assertions", BISS 4:e58982 (2020) (opened) — unit: the candidate data-quality test; endpoint: whether a test over dwc:identificationQualifier can be specified; estimand: none, it reports "the most recent dropping of the two tests related to dwc:identificationQualifier" because "rules of open nomenclature are unevenly adopted across data records" — BOTH strings VERBATIM and confirmed un-primed on verification, each independently recovered twice, but THE SECOND IS CLIPPED IN A WAY THAT CHANGES WHAT IT CLAIMS, here and at both of its other occurrences in this entry. The printed sentence runs on past the cut: "...and rules of open nomenclature are unevenly adopted across data records TO RELIABLY PARSE AND DETECT dwc:identificationQualifier FOR THESE TESTS TO BE EFFECTIVE." So the claim is about whether AUTOMATED TESTING over the field is tractable, not a free-standing empirical finding about how unevenly the conventions are adopted in practice. Verification also establishes the framing: the two dropped tests are named (TG2-VALIDATION_IDENTIFICATIONQUALIFIER_DETECTED and TG2-AMENDMENT_IDENTIFICATIONQUALIFIER_FROM_TAXON, both record-level), and the dropping is A DECISION TAKEN AND CLOSED, stated in the past tense ("This decision resulted from...") and offered as an "e.g." illustrating that "The core tests have proven to be far more complex than any of the team had anticipated" — with no future work, no research question and no referral onward, although the group does refer other work onward explicitly (Parameters to Task Group 4, the Annotations Interest Group). So it drops the field from scope rather than posing the question, which makes it a weaker neighbour than "fourth close neighbour" implies. Also opened as near-misses: Waller 2022 BISS 6:e91312; Smith, Johnston & Lücking 2016 PLOS ONE 11(3):e0151232; Wang 2024 (MSc, Edinburgh/RBGE, record page); Morin et al. 2023 Sci Rep 13:18825. NOT READ, grounds nothing: Bengtson 1988, Palaeontology 31(1):223-227 (citation verified at palass.org by adversary 2, no route attempted).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same object, no shared estimand; P1 ranks the marks and defers quantification to prospective recording, the candidate measures retrospectively what marks already on existing records delivered and tests P1's ordering as a hypothesis. vs P2 — same reference machinery and substrate, but the estimand is unconditional and the categories exclude qualifier status; P2 shows the resolutions exist at scale without computing the conditional rate or decomposing variance. vs P3 — closest method-side prior, but its predictor is the reported category and its classification probabilities are internal to the model; the candidate's predictor is the determiner's own declared hedge and its output is the externally estimated, stratum-resolved quantity P3's priors lack. vs TG2 — same term, same community, but TG2 decides whether a test can be written and reports no rate; it is a novelty discount and a feasibility objection, not the candidate's question.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: 31 queries across systematics, palaeontology, biodiversity informatics/TDWG, barcoding, zooarchaeology, clinical hedging, biosecurity diagnostics, citizen science and misclassification-aware SDMs, in four languages; nine sources opened. No paper found anywhere that conditions an accuracy or agreement rate on an open-nomenclature mark, and no published count of qualifier-bearing records. Not High because there are two close neighbours on the same object (P1, and TG2 which Gate 2 missed), and because the "share of records carrying a qualifier" limb was searched for and not found rather than shown not to exist.

Significance — consequence: if the rates order as the guidance implies and the spread falls inside tolerance, aggregated records acquire a principled per-record weight and misclassification-aware models get the informative priors they currently invent; if they order at stratum-specific levels, a keyed recalibration layer is licensed; if they do not order at all, a flag carried on an unknown share of records is established as carrying no transferable information, retiring a class of informal filter and telling standards bodies the term cannot be read quantitatively. The null is as actionable as the positive.
Significance — audience: aggregator data-quality teams (GBIF, OBIS, iDigBio, ALA, PBDB), TDWG / Darwin Core maintainers, SDM and macroecology practitioners plus the false-positive-occupancy community, collection managers and monographers, and regulatory/biosecurity identification programmes. Adversary 2 evidenced audiences 1-2 with a document: the Darwin Core data-quality establishment reviewed the term's GBIF values and dropped two planned tests in exactly this evidentiary vacuum — re-based on verification: the vacuum is REAL but it is established by ABSENCE, not by anything TG2 states. A full-main-text read returns NOT FOUND for any measurement of qualifier usage, survival or agreement, and the review the decision rests on is itself unquantified; but NO sentence says a reliability or agreement rate is unknown or unmeasured, and the adjacent sentence asserts something different in kind, about the tractability of machine parsing. Reading it as TG2 flagging a missing rate would be the reader's inference rather than the document's claim; and IPPC/APHIS run a preliminary-ID -> official-confirmation pipeline with regulatory consequence and no published confirmation rate for the preliminary stage.
Significance — fecundity: whether qualifier use is itself informative missingness; human marks versus machine confidence (CV scores, barcode posteriors) head-to-head on the same specimens; whether a recalibration layer validates out of sample; whether determiner-level calibration can be estimated and fed back; whether information content drifted across the barcoding transition; whether marks on fragmentary material behave differently.
Significance — anchoring: the misidentification-rate literature's unanswered "what to do about >50%" (Goodwin 2015 ends in a call for taxonomic effort); the identifiability problem in misclassification-aware distribution models; GBIF backbone name-matching, where qualified strings are a documented failure mode; and the 32-year normative record on this exact object (Bengtson 1988, Chapman/Taxacom 2006, Sigovini 2016, TG2 2020).

Reason for silence: incentive gap on the consumer side (drop/keep is cheap by policy, auditing is costly, and a published rate creates an obligation to recalibrate) plus a disciplinary boundary with a track record: adversary 2 dated four passes over the same object across 32 years, every one proposing a better recording instrument and none measuring the one in hand. Adversary 1 damaged two of the record's three mechanisms — evaluative audit traditions that use "cf." daily do exist (NMBAQC ring tests since 1994, zooarchaeological blind tests), and Goodwin 2015 and Wang 2024 computed unconditional agreement from determination slips by hand, so the "new instrument" mechanism is weaker than claimed. The surviving explanation is the incentive gap plus the boundary's documented normative habit; those are mechanisms, not "no one thought of it".

Domain(s): Biology — functional genomics (genome-scale single-cell perturbation atlases; GRN inference; virtual-cell modelling). Neighbour vocabularies: causal discovery, statistical design/power, identifiability, yeast deletion genetics, ML perturbation benchmarking, genetical genomics/eQTL, prokaryotic promoter screening, DE meta-analysis.
Question (canonical): In one genome-scale CRISPRi single-cell atlas (index case: K562 genome-wide Perturb-seq, ~9,600 primary-transcript perturbations), what fraction of the declared measured gene set is moved by no perturbation at all — reported as a function of a declared log-fold-change grid δ under a union-over-perturbations FDR with k ≥ 2, with RESPONSIVE / UNRESPONSIVE-AND-POWERED / UNDERPOWERED held strictly separate — and does the unresponsive-and-powered set recur in a second line (RPE1) above a declared null? (Scored version = V2; V1 as intake lacked the union rule and the power-coverage rule.)
Alternative formulations: How much of a cell's transcriptome is reachable by perturbing one gene at a time, and is there a part no single-gene knockdown touches? / Reading a Perturb-seq response matrix along the GENE axis rather than the perturbation axis, how many measured genes show no detected response to any perturbation once each gene's own detection power is accounted for, and do the same genes recur in a second line?
Motivating gap: Genome-scale Perturb-seq made the full perturbation × gene matrix measurable; every published analysis reads the perturbation margin (31.1% of perturbations have a transcriptional phenotype) and the gene margin was claimed unread. Gate 4 falsified the second half of that claim: the measured-unit margin is read, named and published in at least two adjacent literatures (see priors). The surviving gap is narrower than intake stated — the per-gene power three-class partition, not the gene-axis reading itself.
Presuppositions: (1) an atlas with enough cells per perturbation to declare per-gene power — established for one line; (2) per-gene power is computable so "not moved" separates from "not measurable" — LOAD-BEARING, unvalidated, no opened source does it on this object; (3) CRISPRi is an adequate instance of perturbing a gene — contested, scoped into the estimand (and confirmed as a live failure mode: "CRISPRi did not work well for weakly expressed TF genes", Nat Commun 2023); (4) declared expression filter excludes unexpressed genes — fine, but the atlas filter is "expressed >0.05 UMI per cell", so G is dominated by near-zero-power genes; (5) the library is dense enough that "any perturbation" ≈ "any single gene" — contested (yeast redundancy ≈29%); (6) non-response is not a compositional-normalisation artefact — contested, no spike-in arm available retrospectively; (7) reachability rather than invariance is what matters — flagged, significance re-routed off it; (8) FALSIFIED: that the measured-gene margin is unread in the literature.
What would count as an answer: the declared filter, δ-grid, union FDR + k ≥ 2 rule and per-gene power function; the three class counts and fractions as functions of δ, never merged; the second-line replication with the overlap of unresponsive-and-powered sets tested against a declared null; and the covariate characterisation (expression, housekeeping status, chromatin state, half-life, library membership).

Significance — consequence: unchanged as argued — near-zero unresponsive-and-powered at a meaningful δ licenses the reachability premise of GRN inference and virtual-cell training; a large recurring set is an identifiability ceiling no model capacity recovers; most non-responders landing in UNDERPOWERED converts the answer into a cells-per-perturbation design number. Are unresponsive genes the buffered genes, tested against stoichiometry-conservation architecture as a pre-declared covariate? THE SURVIVING FRAGMENT IS CONFIRMED OPEN ON BOTH PRIORS, which strengthens this entry's Suggested first step. Neither paper analyses its own non-responders. Albert's 77 get one sentence and no per-gene power, expression-level or detection-limit analysis. Han's main text makes no per-promoter power analysis either, and the one place such an argument could live - Supplementary Note 2, which the paper cites as the BASIS for the 936 call - COULD NOT BE READ. So that limb is UNCHECKED rather than settled either way.

ROUTING STILL DECLINED, and now on checked ground rather than inference. The routing test needs the question POSED in print, and both readers return NOT FOUND on exactly that: Albert never raises a no-eQTL or unmovable fraction as an open question and reports its 77 as a finding; Han's Discussion never poses the fraction responding to no perturbation, and characterises the 29% constant class FUNCTIONALLY instead, by COG enrichment in "inorganic ion transport and metabolism", read as housekeeping. Open but unposed is not routed.

Conduct of this check: no raw read was achievable for either prior, so every quotation is summariser-mediated and subject to a ~125-character cap; a curl 403 at this container's proxy is tool-scoped rather than a host block, and Crossref answers via WebFetch, which is how both author lines were obtained; and one reader's attempt to fetch the published eLife XML from a GitHub repository outside this session's scope was refused, recorded, and not reworked.

---
ID: UQ-20261018-20
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — cell biology (regulated cell death, tissue homeostasis; non-clinical). Method-owning neighbours: quantitative histology / tissue kinetics, quantitative image cytometry, whole-body turnover accounting.

Question (canonical): For one declared tissue in a declared species, strain, sex, age and housing condition, assayed in a declared physiological state with a pre-declared in situ marker panel whose per-modality sensitivity and specificity have been measured in that same tissue against induced positive controls: what is the per-modality prevalence of marker-positive dying cells per unit tissue (with intervals, an explicit multi-positive fraction and an explicit unclassified residual), and — where a modality's corpse-persistence time is independently measured or bounded in that tissue — the implied per-modality death incidence per unit tissue per day, reconciled against an independently measured total turnover? (V2, the graded version; V1 as intaken: what share of in vivo physiological cell death is apoptotic and what share proceeds by each non-apoptotic regulated modality.)

Alternative formulations:
- The field has defined a dozen ways a cell can die; which ones actually kill cells in a normal body, and in what proportions?
- For a declared tissue and a declared modality-marker panel, what is the per-modality incidence of cell death per unit tissue per day once each modality's corpse-clearance time is accounted for?
- (lay) Of the cells a body loses per day, how many die by each named death programme, and on what measurement does that attribution rest?

Motivating gap: The regulated-cell-death literature is dense with how-answers and thin on how-much for declared solid tissues. The authoritative whole-body accounting (Sender & Milo 2021, read: 0.33 +/- 0.02 x 10^12 cells/day, 80 +/- 20 g/day) splits the total only by disposal route, in one Methods sentence (CORRECTED ON VERIFICATION: "assigns no death modality anywhere", as this entry first put it, is wrong at the sentence level — the sentence names apoptosis and phagocytosis, and a flat no would be false; what holds is the narrower claim that the paper's ACCOUNTING is modality-blind, since Figs. 1b and 2b, the two panels that are the turnover accounting, are split by cell type and tissue and by nothing else. The sentence reads "About half of cells replaced daily go through apoptosis and phagocytosis by tissue macrophages", with "the other half" being gastrointestinal and skin cells "which are shed"; it sits in the last of nine Methods subsections, on power consumption, among costs left OUT of the energy estimate, carries no citation, and is followed by the authors' assumption that these processes "do not have a dramatic effect on the overall calculation". A request to transcribe that paragraph raw was refused by the summariser, so whether it is an assumption or a claim is summariser-characterised and is the weakest link in this reading); the field's own in vivo methods introduction (Newbold et al. 2014, read; re-verified un-primed by adversary 3 and again by a third independent reader on post-batch verification) attributes "billions of cells per day" to apoptosis. CORRECTED ON VERIFICATION: the verbatim string is the document's, and its construction is "the loss of billions of cells per day by apoptosis in the human body" — whole organism, per day, an order of magnitude with no number, range or uncertainty attached, and whether it is measured, calculated or cited cannot be determined, because it is a bare background premise in the abstract's third sentence and the body is paywalled. But the clause built around it was this entry's gloss and not the document's claim. The document writes "the number of apoptotic cells found in healthy tissue is surprisingly low and reflects the efficiency of this process", where "this process" refers back to the phagocyte recruitment and clearance of its preceding sentence. So the referent is clearance, but "clearance efficiency" is not the document's phrase; "rather than the death rate" appears nowhere and is an inference from the concessive "Despite"; and "conceding" is this entry's framing — the document presents the point as unremarkable background and immediately pivots to using it to explain why apoptotic cells become visible in treated tumours. What the document does do, and what matters here, is set a whole-body per-day RATE against a per-tissue COUNT without reconciling them numerically, which is this entry's own prevalence-versus-incidence problem appearing unremarked in the field's own methods introduction. The partition is the denominator of every claim that a modality matters physiologically and of every modality-knockout phenotype read in healthy tissue.

Presuppositions: (1) modalities mutually exclusive per dying cell — CONTESTED, handled by construction (declared, possibly overlapping marker partition; multi-positive fraction and unclassified residual reported); (2) modality-specific markers specific enough to classify a single dying cell in situ — CONTESTED, the binding feasibility constraint; residual worry that calibration on induced death may not transfer to spontaneous death; (3) per-modality corpse-clearance times estimable, so prevalence converts to incidence — CONTESTED, incidence made conditional; (4) 'physiological' declarable by stated criteria — ESTABLISHED as a convention; (5) total tissue death incidence independently estimable — ESTABLISHED, wide intervals; (6) partition stable rather than diurnal/dietary/age-dependent — FLAGGED, changes the estimand's form not its answerability; (7) no modality systematically missed because corpses clear faster than markers persist — CONTESTED, boundable only; (8) ADDED AT GATE 4 (adversary 1), not in the Gate 0-3 record: that physiological loss presents as marker-positive dying cells at all — modalities that leave no corpse (removal of a living cell by phagocytosis) cannot be scored by any in situ panel and would not land in a residual defined over detected dying cells; the reconciliation deficit against total turnover is the only place such deaths appear, and the entry must say so.

What would count as an answer: per-modality marker-positive prevalence per unit tissue with intervals, a reported multi-positive fraction and an explicit unclassified residual, for a declared tissue and a pre-declared panel with in-tissue sensitivity/specificity; plus, where clearance/persistence times are measured or bounded, conversion to per-modality incidence per day reconciled against an independent turnover total. Prevalence alone, with the clearance confound bounded and stated, is a partial but publishable answer and must not be inflated into incidence. A null in which no panel reaches classifying specificity in situ is also an answer, about the field's measurement capability.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 plus 27 new ones across three adversaries (9 each, all in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try); full lists in batches/2026-10-18-0945/UQ-20261018-20-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
- Gate 2 Q2 "what fraction of cell death in the normal body is apoptosis versus necroptosis ferroptosis proportion" -> only feature-by-feature modality tables plus a discrimination protocol (10.1002/cpz1.951, COULD NOT READ); no fraction.
- Gate 2 Q9 (method-owning negative) "deconvolution estimate proportions of cell death modalities from single-cell RNA-seq" -> generic cell-type deconvolution only; the mixture-estimation machinery has never been pointed at death modalities.
- Gate 2 Q10 homeostatic intestinal per-modality share -> only induced/pathological shedding models.
- A1 Q1 (phagocyte immunology) "phagoptosis most common form of cell death in the adult body ... proportion killed by primary phagocytosis" -> DIRECT HIT, Brown 2023 NRI (new prior P5); vocabulary Gate 2 never used.
- A1 Q8 (mouse genetics, answer-side) BAX/BAK/APAF1 residual non-apoptotic turnover -> loss-of-function literature asks whether a modality is required, never what share it carries.
- A2 Q4 (Potten/crypt-counting) -> BioNumbers 109230, a published apoptosis prevalence figure (1-10%) for normal mouse small intestine, secondhand and position-restricted; Gate 2 missed it.
- A2 Q2 / A3 Q2 (toxicologic pathology historical control data) -> lesion incidence per animal, not per-modality death counts (J Toxicol Pathol 37:109-126, read as abstract).
- A3 Q7 literal "relative contribution ... to tissue homeostasis" phrase hunt -> no source asks for the share; the flagship non-apoptotic-death therapeutic review (Hadian & Stockwell, NRDD 2023, read) contains no homeostatic share, no per-day rates and no statement that either is missing.
- A2/A3 German, Chinese and Japanese sweeps -> taxonomic explainers only, no shares.
Disguise ran in full: each adversary executed 9 of its required 8 new queries, so Disguise is verified-and-run, not unverified.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Sender R, Milo R, "The distribution of cellular turnover in the human body", Nat Med 27:45-48 (2021), doi 10.1038/s41591-020-01182-9 (read twice independently). Unit: cell type within a reference adult body. Endpoint: cells replaced per day, grams per day. Comparator: across cell types, blood vs non-blood. Estimand: total and per-cell-type turnover; no modality index.
P2. Samson AL, Murphy JM, "Mapping where and when necroptotic cell death occurs in disease", Cell Death Differ 31:833-835 (2024) (read). Unit: tissue region/cell population scored by IHC. Endpoint: necroptotic pathway protein and phospho-form expression — capacity, one modality. Comparator: normal vs diseased. Estimand: a qualitative spatial map; no frequency.
P3. Newbold A, Martin BP, Cullinane C, Bots M, "Measuring Apoptosis in Mammals In Vivo", Cold Spring Harb Protoc 2014(11):pdb.top070417 (read; author line and key sentence re-verified un-primed by adversary 3). Unit: cells in tissue sections. Endpoint: apoptosis-positive counts, one modality. Comparator: treated vs untreated. Estimand: detection of and change in apoptotic burden under intervention.
P5 (FOUND AT GATE 4, adversary 1, and now the nearest prior overall). Brown GC, "Cell death by phagocytosis", Nat Rev Immunol (2023), doi 10.1038/s41577-023-00921-6 (read, author-hosted PDF). Unit: cell population, whole body. Endpoint: abundance ranking of death forms derived from cell lifespans and turnover rates. Comparator: across forms of death in the mammalian body. Estimand: which form is most abundant — "cell death by phagocytosis represents the most common form of cell death in the body" — while stating that "the quantitative contribution of different forms of cell death to physiological turnover of neutrophils is still unclear". VERIFIED AND QUALIFIED on post-batch verification (print citation Nat Rev Immunol 24:91-102 (2024); 2023 is the online/DOI year; read from the author-hosted publisher-typeset PDF because nature.com is unreachable from this environment). Both quoted strings are the document's own, the second confirmed as a complete returned fragment. Three things the entry should carry. (a) The quoted "most common" sentence is the document's UNHEDGED, UNCITED formulation; two sentences later the same subsection says "cell death by phagocytosis appears to be the most abundant form of cell death in mammals", hedged and citing reference 22, which is the author's own earlier review (Brown, Vilalta & Fricker, Curr Mol Med 15:842-851, 2015) rather than an external measurement; the abstract gives a third scope, "the mammalian body". Three scopes for one idea, and the citation is a self-citation. (b) The basis is an inference the author draws from cited turnover figures — not a measured modality share, not a calculated one, and not a citation to anyone else's share figure; the premises are human erythrocyte and neutrophil turnover ("the death of two million erythrocytes per second in humans"; neutrophils "0.5-1 million cells per second"), and the document performs no arithmetic and states no denominator for total body cell death. (c) A per-modality share is a genuine NOT FOUND at full text, confirmed by a whole-document scan: the 25% figure in the passage is a share of host CELLS, not of deaths.
P4 (recorded, closest measured homeostatic PREVALENCE — "share" corrected on verification, see below): Bandyadka et al., Front Cell Death 4:1677498 (2025), 10.3389/fceld.2025.1677498 (read at full text): "20%-30% of mitotic spermatogonial cysts undergo spontaneous germ cell death under homeostatic conditions", predominantly non-apoptotic; Drosophila testis for the quantitative claim, per cyst, confirmed un-primed. FOUR CORRECTIONS from post-batch verification, none of which moves the verdict and three of which widen the distance to this candidate. (i) It is a REVIEW article, so this entry attributed a finding to a review: the 20%-30% carries no literature citation (the only parenthetical is "(Figure 3B)", a pointer to the review's own micrograph), is hedged "Imaging of fixed testis samples suggests that", and is stated with no n, no SD, SE or interval. (ii) "Predominantly" is UNQUANTIFIED — no per-modality share appears anywhere in the paper; the non-apoptotic direction rests on loss-of-function genetics ("loss of function of Drice and Dcp-1 failed to reduce levels of cell death", against a lysosomal-gene screen that did reduce dying-cyst counts), and Caspase-9/Dronc IS required in a non-catalytic role, so "caspase-independent" would be a misstatement. The paper therefore does not report a share, which is why this entry's label is corrected to prevalence. (iii) The paper carries TWO unreconciled denominators for one phenomenon: the body text says 20%-30% of CYSTS and the Figure 3A caption says "Approximately one-quarter of spermatogonia undergo GCD" — per cell. This entry's stated unit (cysts) matches the body text and is the defensible choice, but the paper does not reconcile the two. (iv) The figure is a FIXED-sample point prevalence, and the paper's only duration is a one-sided lower bound ("this germ cell death process is prolonged, taking more than 24 h from initiation to completion", citing Chiang et al. 2017) with no mitotic-phase residence time, so prevalence cannot be converted to incidence from this paper either — the nearest prior with the right question shape is blocked by exactly the conversion this candidate makes conditional. The mouse content (Section 6, mouse oogenesis) is real but structural and carries no competing percentage, so the number has not been mis-transplanted from a mammal.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs P1: supplies the denominator and declines the numerator; its only modality statement is a disposal-route split in Methods, and by adversary 3's arithmetic on its own Methods values that "about half ... shed" is a mass share (~45% of grams) and only ~13% of cell number, so it does not even partition the total it fixes.
- vs P2: endpoint is pathway-protein expression (capacity), not counted deaths; disease frame, one modality, no prevalence, no residual. Expression of MLKL in a cell is not a death of that cell.
- vs P3: single-modality by construction; its healthy baseline is a reference level, never an estimand; no panel calibration, no clearance conversion.
- vs P5: same comparative topic, different estimand and different regime — P5 ranks abundance whole-body from lifespan arithmetic, is dominated by circulating blood cells cleared in spleen/liver/marrow, reports no prevalence, no intervals, no residual, no per-modality clearance times, and says the quantitative split is unclear. It does, however, show the how-much question IS asked in print at whole-body scale and coarsely answered there; V1's whole-body framing does not survive it and the graded V2 per-tissue estimand does.
- vs P4: right question shape, far narrower object: one germ-cell population, invertebrate for the number, two-way contrast, prevalence not incidence, no reconciliation.

Novelty confidence: Medium (and narrowing; search record incomplete)
Grounds: 38 queries across lay, cell-death technical, nomenclature, historical tissue kinetics, quantitative pathology, toxicologic-pathology control data, fragmentomics, radiobiology/crypt counting, ultrastructure, intravital reporters, computational pathology, deconvolution, phagocyte immunology and three non-English lanes returned no per-modality partition for any healthy adult mammalian tissue. Held below High by three things: P2 shows the field already asking the adjacent where-and-when question in its own words; P5 shows the comparative how-much question asked and coarsely answered at whole-body scale in a vocabulary Gate 2 never searched; and the single-modality conversion literature (Bursch et al. 1990) was UNREAD at Gate 2 and at every adversary pass — NOW READ AT ABSTRACT LEVEL ON POST-BATCH VERIFICATION, which discharges this limb and does not change the grade; see the verification block below for what it says. In short: the index-to-rate conversion for apoptosis in rat liver already exists and has since 1990 (the abstract states "a simple fonnula is given to calculate the cell loss rate by apoptosis" — "fonnula" is the publisher page's own OCR damage, reproduced as served — and gives the missing factor as "The mean duration of the histological stages of apoptosis was found to be ~3 h", confirmed un-primed across three independent summarisation passes), but it is one modality in one tissue, its "normal liver" is CPA-induced hyperplastic liver regressing with apoptosis initiation pharmacologically blocked rather than untreated steady-state liver, and the formula's form, inputs, denominator and arithmetic are all in the paywalled body and remain unread. That is this entry's anchoring confirmed at first hand, not its partition supplied. Full citation corrected: Bursch W, Paffe S, Putz B, Barthel G, Schulte-Hermann R, "Determination of the length of the histological stages of apoptosis in normal liver and in altered hepatic foci of rats", Carcinogenesis 11(5):847-853, doi 10.1093/carcin/11.5.847 — five authors in that printed order, so this entry's "Bursch W. et al." is correct, and the page range is 847-853 rather than the single page first recorded. Earlier route failures stood at four independent attempts across the record and all three adversaries — no publisher or DOI route recovered, PMC hard-blocked, doi.org/10.1093/carcin/11.5.847 returned HTTP 429 with an instruction not to retry — as is the Br J Cancer commentary "What is an apoptotic index measuring?" (PMC2077230 only). Not Low: no opened source reports shares across modalities in a declared healthy mammalian tissue.
Asked-but-open: not as posed. The coarse whole-body form is asked and coarsely answered (P5), so it is not routed; the weaker single-modality qualitative form ("does necroptosis occur, and where, in normal tissue?") is asked and open (P2) but is not this question.

Significance — consequence: An apoptosis-majority result turns an asserted premise (P3) into a measurement with an interval and positions non-apoptotic modalities as reserve programmes whose healthy-tissue knockout phenotypes need another explanation. A substantial non-apoptotic share gives every such phenotype a direct reading it now lacks, moves the homeostatic/pathological line the field draws around necroptosis and ferroptosis, and gives on-target safety reasoning for RIPK1/MLKL/GPX4-directed drugs a baseline physiological rate. A null in which no panel reaches classifying specificity is consequential in itself: current claims about which modalities matter physiologically would then be ungroundable in counted deaths.
Significance — audience: the regulated-cell-death community and NCCD (prevalence endpoint alongside operational definitions); the efferocytosis/clearance community, for whom per-modality persistence times are the missing conversion factor; whole-body quantitative physiology (P1 fixes the total and assigns no modality); quantitative-pathology and spatial-omics method developers, who own panel calibration and point it at expression; cfDNA turnover accounting (adversary 2, eLife 89321), a second community working the same denominator without a modality index. Counter-indicator, sourced: the flagship therapeutic review on non-apoptotic death (Hadian & Stockwell, NRDD 2023) argues its whole case with no homeostatic share and no statement that one is missing, which is evidence the preclinical-safety audience does not currently treat the baseline as load-bearing.
Significance — fecundity: per-modality corpse-persistence times in vivo; whether the partition differs between tissues of similar turnover; diurnal, dietary and age dependence; whether non-apoptotic physiological deaths are immunologically silent; which clearance route takes which modality's corpses; compensatory substitution within the partition in knockout animals; a death-modality signature matrix for existing deconvolution machinery.
Significance — anchoring: the standing "is necroptosis/ferroptosis physiological or only pathological?" dispute; the modality-free accounting at P1; the old tissue-kinetics problem of what an apoptotic index measures (prevalence = incidence x persistence), generalised from one modality to a panel — with this correction from post-batch verification: the relation is this entry's own statement of the problem and is NOT attributed to any source read. The commentary whose title poses it, now pinned as Potten CS, "What is an apoptotic index measuring? A commentary", Br J Cancer 74(11):1743-1748 (1996), doi 10.1038/bjc.1996.624, single author, is COULD NOT READ on every route available here (nature.com serves a subscription preview with no abstract, the Christie repository record has an Abstract heading with no text under it, two further searches found no open copy, and the free full text is PMC2077230 behind this environment's PMC block). Not one word of its argument has been read, so no claim about what it argues — including that it states this relation or supplies a persistence time — has first-hand support. Inferring its answer from its title is precisely the move this ledger exists to catch. The relation itself is sound as the entry's own reasoning and is now independently exemplified by two sources that WERE read: Bursch 1990, which supplies the persistence term for apoptosis in rat liver and states that quantifying cell loss needs counts plus the duration of the visible stages; and Bandyadka 2025, whose fixed-sample prevalence cannot be converted because its duration term is a one-sided bound and its denominator time is absent; whether markers calibrated on induced death transfer to spontaneous death.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary-boundary and incentive gap with a measurement obstruction on top, sharpened at Gate 4. The field's unit of credit is a pathway demonstrated by loss of function, so prevalence in a healthy animal is nobody's endpoint (adversary 1's BAX/BAK sweep: the knockout literature asks whether a modality is required, never what share it carries; P3 shows the in vivo method literature organised around intervention contrasts). Ownership is split: the group holding the total assigns no modality, the group holding modality assays produces expression maps. The sharper form, supplied by adversary 1 and accepted here: when the how-much question IS asked (P5), it is answered by the lifespan/turnover route that never looks at a corpse, precisely because efferocytosis clears corpses fast and the per-modality persistence times needed to divide prevalence by have not been assembled. That explains silence about the corpse-counting method, not about the topic — a weaker and more honest mechanism than the record claimed. Adversary 2 adds a pre-emption-by-definition limb (apoptosis was introduced in 1972 as the tissue-kinetic mechanism OF physiological deletion), which is plausible but unsourced here: the 1972 paper could not be opened.

STATUS UNCHANGED BUT ITS GROUND REPLACED on post-batch verification: the NCCD has now been opened and read at PARTIAL level (Introduction, Fig. 1 legend, Box 1 "Operational definitions", and the modality sections through Parthanatos, where the converted text stops mid-sentence; entosis onward and the concluding remarks are unread). So the kill stays Partial, for a different and better reason than before. Two further findings cut toward the response: the article as read does not address fixed tissue sections, histology, IHC or in-situ detection at all, so the NCCD is SILENT on marker-based assignment in tissue rather than prohibitive of it, and silence is not a prohibition (the same correction this batch had to make on UQ-20261018-16); and every dependence claim and measurement encountered is at per-cell, per-culture or per-mouse-model level, with nothing framed as a tissue-level or population-level share, which is the aggregation gap this candidate is about rather than an argument against it. Collateral: Box 1 defines programmed cell death as a "Particular form of RCD that occurs in strictly physiological scenarios" which "does not relate to perturbations of homeostasis", which sources presupposition 4's convention; and "The precise role of ferroptosis in development and tissue homeostasis, however, remains to be fully elucidated" sources the anchoring dispute directly from the nomenclature committee. | Partial |
Nothing Unresolved on any attack from any adversary. Unverified (checks that did not run, carried as neither pass nor kill) — AS AT GATE 5: Bursch et al. 1990 and the Br J Cancer apoptotic-index commentary, unread after four route attempts, leaving the apoptosis conversion limb's novelty unverified; the NCCD 2018 recommendations, unopened, leaving attack 8's definitional ground unsourced. REVISED AFTER POST-BATCH VERIFICATION: Bursch 1990 is read at abstract level and that limb is discharged; the NCCD is read at PARTIAL level and attack 8's first limb is sourced while its exclusive limb is not, so the kill stays Partial. One item remains genuinely unverified: the Br J Cancer apoptotic-index commentary (now pinned as Potten 1996, doi 10.1038/bjc.1996.624) is unread on every route available in this environment, so nothing this entry says about its contents has first-hand support. It is carried as neither pass nor kill, and under this ledger's rule an unrun check caps the entry at Provisional and cannot reject it.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 (V2 makes the estimand statable and settleable; held off 3 by the untested transfer of induced-death marker calibration to spontaneous death, by mutual exclusivity being handled by declared convention rather than resolved, and by the absence of a pre-stated residual threshold above which the study has failed rather than answered) · Significance 3/3 (bidirectional consequence, informative null, named audiences of which two display the gap in print — tempered by the sourced counter-indicator at attack 6).

Strongest remaining objection: The question is asked and coarsely answered at the scale the canonical V1 statement uses. Brown GC, Nat Rev Immunol (2023), doi 10.1038/s41577-023-00921-6, asks which form of cell death predominates in the mammalian body and answers it — phagoptosis, "the most common form of cell death in the body" — in a vocabulary Gate 2 never searched; and that dominant term is the removal of cells that are still alive, which no in situ marker panel can score at all. So the per-tissue marker-calibrated estimand that survives is both narrower than the question as written and structurally blind to the modality a top-tier review calls the largest, with the reconciliation deficit as its only trace.
Promotion requires: this clause was rewritten after post-batch verification, which discharged two of the three reading requirements the Gate 5 version demanded and showed that version named no condition that would remove the close neighbour. DISCHARGED — Bursch et al. 1990 is read, and the answer to what it was being read for is yes, an index-to-rate conversion for apoptosis in a liver its own title calls normal has existed since 1990, one modality, one tissue, in pharmacologically manipulated tissue, with the formula itself still unread; and the NCCD is opened far enough to source attack 8's mechanistic-definition limb but not its exclusive limb. The Gate 5 version made the NCCD read a potential kill — "if only counterfactually, attack 8 regrades Unresolved and the entry is Rejected". THAT CONDITION DID NOT FIRE AND COULD NOT HAVE: the read is PARTIAL, it stops mid-sentence inside Parthanatos, and the decisive question is explicitly a could-not-read rather than a check that passed, so under this ledger's rule it caps the entry at Provisional and cannot reject it. What would settle it is narrow and now locatable: the concluding remarks of Galluzzi et al. 2018, pp. 486-541, fetched from the UCL Discovery mirror of the published PDF with an offset past Parthanatos. If they state that modality cannot be assigned without an intervention, attack 8 regrades Unresolved and the entry is Rejected; if they state no such rule, the kill stays Partial permanently and this route to rejection closes. THREE THINGS ARE NEEDED FOR PROMOTION, and the Gate 5 version named only the first two. (1) Novelty to High, which requires the close neighbour removed, not merely described. P5 (Brown 2023) is close in topic and distant in estimand, and this entry already argues that distance; what it has never done is run the search record in the vocabulary that found P5. So: the phagoptosis / primary-phagocytosis / entosis / cell-death-by-phagocytosis lane executed as a full Gate 2 record, plus the canonical question restated per declared tissue with the whole-body 330-billion framing dropped. If that completed record still returns no per-modality in situ prevalence for any declared healthy mammalian tissue, the neighbour is distant in the respect that matters and novelty goes to High; if it returns one, novelty goes to Low and the entry is Rejected at Gate 2. Either way the close-neighbour clause stops applying, which is what the Gate 5 version failed to provide — the same defect this ledger recorded on UQ-20261016-50. (2) Well-posedness to 3/3 needs all THREE of the things holding it at 2/3, not the two design repairs alone. The repairs — presupposition 8 with an explicit reading of the reconciliation deficit, and a pre-stated residual threshold above which the study has failed rather than answered — are statable on paper. The third is not: the transfer of induced-death marker calibration to spontaneous death is an empirical matter, and it has to be measured or bounded in the declared tissue, not declared. Until it is, well-posedness stays at 2/3 and Validated is unreachable whatever happens to novelty. (3) Significance is already 3/3 and is not a constraint. So the honest ceiling today is Provisional, and it is set by well-posedness rather than by novelty: even a High-novelty regrade with the neighbour removed leaves the calibration-transfer limb open. The Br J Cancer commentary, unread on every route here, is not on the promotion path either way — it bears on this entry's anchoring rhetoric, not on any score.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): locate a tissue in which a total turnover rate and at least one modality's corpse-persistence time are both already measured, and ask what the existing per-modality clearance-kinetics literature actually bounds there — not a counting experiment.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): not rejected, and a Provisional entry's own question is never routed; the coarse whole-body form is asked and coarsely answered by Brown 2023, so it is not routable either. ONE ROW ADDED ON POST-BATCH VERIFICATION, and it is not this entry's question. Brown 2023 poses, in print and of its own subject, a strictly narrower question and declares it open: "contribution of different forms of cell death to physiological turnover of neutrophils is still unclear" — quoted here as the complete fragment the reader returned; the full sentence, labelled as a reconstruction from two consecutive returned fragments, is "However, there is evidence of some contribution of apoptosis to the turnover of neutrophils45, and the quantitative contribution of different forms of cell death to physiological turnover of neutrophils is still unclear." One cell type rather than a declared tissue, no panel, no residual, no reconciliation; posed by the source, verbatim, and declared unanswered by the source itself. That meets the routing test and is recorded in ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Nothing else in the six verified sources qualifies: Bandyadka 2025 enumerates eight open questions in its own Open Questions section and every one is mechanistic or evolutionary, with none asking what fraction of physiological death runs through each modality; Sender & Milo note the absence of an ENERGETICS analysis, not of a modality breakdown, and must not be read as flagging this gap; the NCCD's "precise role of ferroptosis in development and tissue homeostasis ... remains to be fully elucidated" is a role question too vague to work as a problem; and the Potten commentary is unread, so its title's question cannot be routed on the strength of a title.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18): read by six independent fresh-context readers, one per source, each given the claim and its source but not this entry's reasoning. Status UNCHANGED at Provisional. It could not have gone up — well-posedness is 2/3 and the Validated line requires 3/3 — and the one route down, attack 8 regrading Unresolved on the NCCD, could not fire from a partial read whose decisive question is an explicit could-not-read. What changed is the ground under almost every claim, corrected in place above.

Sources read first-hand, with read level: Sender & Milo 2021 (full text via summariser, all nine Methods subsections); Brown 2023 (full text via summariser, author-hosted publisher-typeset PDF); Newbold et al. 2014 (ABSTRACT ONLY, body paywalled); Bandyadka et al. 2025 (full text via summariser); Bursch et al. 1990 (ABSTRACT ONLY, body paywalled); Galluzzi et al. 2018 / NCCD (PARTIAL, stops mid-sentence inside Parthanatos); Potten 1996 (COULD NOT READ — not one word). Five of six load-bearing sources moved from inferred or single-sourced to first-hand. No reader achieved a raw read: direct curl egress is refused at this environment's gateway for every external host tried, so every quotation above passed through the fetch summariser and its ~125-character cap, and no cut string has been completed. Where a reconstruction from consecutive fragments is reported, it is labelled as one.

The batch's signature defect, found here too. Three of this entry's claims were quotations or paraphrases clipped where the surrounding grammar changes the claim: Newbold's "clearance efficiency ... rather than the death rate", where the document says "the efficiency of this process" and never mentions the death rate; Sender & Milo's "assigns no death modality anywhere", contradicted by the entry's own next clause and by the Methods sentence that names apoptosis; and Brown's "most common form of cell death in the body", which is the document's own string but its unhedged, uncited formulation rather than the hedged one two sentences later that cites the author's own prior review. In each case the source is real, correctly identified and accurately quoted somewhere; the defect is in the grain, which is the same failure this ledger recorded on the 06:19 batch and the same reader-side error, not paper-side.

What the pass added rather than corrected. Bursch 1990 turns this entry's central methodological claim from the entry's own reasoning into a sourced fact: the conversion exists, for one modality, in one tissue, since 1990, and the persistence term it supplies is ~3 h in a liver whose "normal" is pharmacologically manipulated. Bandyadka 2025 supplies a second, independent instance of the same obstruction in a different phylum: a fixed-sample prevalence with a one-sided duration bound and no denominator time, so uninvertible. And the NCCD's silence on in-situ detection is more useful to this candidate than a prohibition would have been, because silence leaves the measurement open while the committee's own mechanistic definitions explain why nobody has made it.

Two readers hit route refusals and stopped: a classifier declined inspection of the egress proxy, and api.crossref.org refused CONNECT to curl in six separate readers' logs while answering the same readers through WebFetch. That is one mechanical cause behind six differently-worded per-host failures, and it is evidence about the fetcher rather than about any document. Recorded so no later reader re-derives it. One live trap is recorded for the same reason: nature.com/articles/6690758.pdf is returned by a title search for the Potten commentary and is NOT it — it is Ito et al., Br J Cancer 81(4):747-751 (1999), a 76-tumour human HCC study that defines an apoptotic index crisply and quotably as apoptotic cells per 1000. A reader who trusted the search result's title association could lift a clean "apoptotic index is per 1000 cells" quotation from it and attribute it to Potten.
