ID: UQ-20261021-05
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — critical/respiratory care and hospital medical-gas governance; health-systems surge capacity. Method-owning neighbours: medical-gas and building-services engineering (design flow, diversity factors), flow metrology, water-distribution pressure-dependent demand.
Question (canonical): On declared wards served by identified medical-gas pipeline legs, with leg flow and pressure logged at <=1 min, delivered flow measured at instrumented terminal units on a sampled subset of outlets, and per-patient-hour prescribed device and flowmeter setting from the EHR: (i) is delivered-minus-set flow at an outlet a function of EXOGENOUS leg load — concurrent draw by patients other than the index patient, as a fraction of that leg's engineering design flow, breakpoint pre-declared — and (ii) what share of within-patient variation in a pre-declared oxygenation endpoint (SpO2 time-in-target, FiO2 shortfall, device escalation) is attributable to that load, under within-patient contrasts and a negative-control leg? (V2; V1 and the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation are in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
- Lay: Is a patient's oxygen dose partly set by how much oxygen the rest of the hospital is using at that moment?
- Technical: Using pipeline flow/pressure telemetry as exposure and per-patient oxygenation as outcome, estimate the load-dependent delivery shortfall and its clinical footprint, with design flow as the pre-declared breakpoint.
Motivating gap: The telemetry exists (Leicester/IHEEM: 60 s BMS dashboard, ultrasonic meters, per-leg daily reports, alarm levels derived from copper pipe capacity) with no patient endpoint anywhere in it; the clinical literature treats the wall outlet as an infinite source. The worry is documented (NHS Wales EFA 2020-001, ECRI S0396, NHS Scotland SAN SC2103, AARC 2020). Found in this run: a national safety body has investigated one incident in which a measured pipeline pressure drop coincided with two desaturations, and could not attribute them (HSIB, P1). Post-batch verification establishes that the report poses no question about delivered flow against concurrent demand, so this is an adjacent unresolved attribution, not the candidate's question asked before it.
Presuppositions: P1 leg flow/pressure logged at usable resolution — established for >=1 trust, generalisability unverified. P2 per-patient-hour prescription retrievable — contested in the record; moved toward established by adversary #2's 2024 medRxiv read (two years of EMR device settings). P3 delivered flow measurable at a terminal unit — contested; instrumented-outlet route demonstrated by Davidson's flow-analyser rig. P4 regulated delivery can fall within the observed load range — contested, the premise most able to dissolve the question; survives as open. The supporting arithmetic is narrowed by verification: HSIB's 4.2 -> 3.1 bar is pipeline pressure in the HDU recorded during a Trust-run DELIBERATE Sunday pressure test, after patients had been moved to redistribute flow, and not during the incident. Same quantity as the 50 psi = 3.45 bar flowmeter calibration point, so the comparison stands as an existence proof that ward pipeline pressure can fall below calibration under a real hospital condition; it is not evidence about the incident, and it is not a measurement of delivered flow. P5 endpoint sampled fast enough — established only where continuous SpO2 exists. P6 exogenous load is not an acuity proxy — contested; the negative-control-leg answer is asserted, not evidenced.
What would count as an answer: a load-response curve of delivered-minus-set flow (secondary: FiO2 shortfall) against exogenous leg demand as a fraction of design flow, on instrumented terminal units in >=2 hospitals over >=1 high-demand period, plus the within-patient variance share from within-patient and negative-control contrasts. A flat curve reported with the minimum detectable shortfall answers it negatively, so both branches are reportable.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 in total — 11 at Gate 2, 9 per adversary, all Disguise sweeps executed. Full lists: batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-05-record.md and -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "hospital oxygen demand modelling COVID-19 exceeded pipeline capacity measured ward flow clinical consequence patients received less oxygen than prescribed" → the HSSIB investigation report (decisive hit, P1); "measured discrepancy between prescribed and delivered oxygen flow at bedside audit flowmeter set flow actual delivered" → only device error against its own setting, no load covariate (the "already computed" probe); "pressure-dependent demand / load-dependent delivery applied to medical-gas distribution, nodal pressure, patient outlet" → water-distribution machinery only, never transplanted to medical gas; adversary #2 "oxygen flowmeter internal pressure regulator output flow constant over inlet pressure range 3 to 4 bar ISO 15002" → no published measurement of flowmeter output against inlet pressure in either direction; adversary #2 "congestion externality other patients' concurrent demand shared hospital resource ... individual patient outcomes" → a mature congestion-externality literature that congests staff and beds, never a physical utility. COULD NOT READ: PMC8680427 — top hit in six queries across four vocabularies, unidentified after ~9 routes by three readers (PMC hard-blocked; NCBI idconv 429; curl ncbi/eutils CONNECT 403; Semantic Scholar PMCID CLIENT_ERROR; OmicsDI absent; EBI BioStudies 429). Also unopened (titles only): arXiv:2003.12349, MSF flow-splitter SOP, US11911567.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
- P1 HSSIB, "Oxygen issues during the COVID-19 pandemic", investigation report, recommendations 2021, https://www.hssib.org.uk/patient-safety-investigations/oxygen-issues-during-covid-19-pandemic/investigation-report/ — full text via summariser; unit = one HDU incident at one trust; exposure = hospital oxygen demand and MGPS performance in a surge, with a measured trust pressure test 4.2 -> 3.1 bar; endpoint = whether the desaturations were attributable to the pressure drop; comparator = none; estimand = a binary attribution, NOT reached (fragments: "unable to conclusively determine whether the desaturation"; "unable to identify whether the pressure drop in the HDU was responsible"). Clinical management explicitly scoped out; recommendations are governance and engineering only (R/2021/120, 132-135).
- P2 Graham HR et al., "Cost-effectiveness and sustainability of improved hospital oxygen systems in Nigeria", BMJ Global Health 7(8):e009278 (journal/volume from URL path, date from DOAJ — flagged) — unit = 12 hospitals; exposure = system capability (oximetry then solar oxygen); endpoints = screening/treatment coverage, cost per DALY; comparator = pre-intervention period; no telemetry, no demand linkage.
- P3 Davidson J, Gazzeta C, Torres LC, Jardim JR, Nascimento OA, "Precision and Accuracy of Oxygen Flow Meters Used at Hospital Settings", Respir Care 2012;57(7):1071-1075, doi 10.4187/respcare.01230 — FULL TEXT read by both adversaries (the record's abstract-only flag and its "incomplete byline" flag both corrected). Unit = flowmeter (n=91/11); reference = the set flow at 1/3/5/10 L/min; inlet pressure FIXED at the 50 psi calibration point via a reducing valve, never varied; "good precision and poor accuracy" (+22% at 5, +40% at 10 L/min). Its Introduction asserts gas pressure as an influencing factor but measures neither direction nor magnitude.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same subject, different object and estimand (patient-hour nested in patient and leg; continuous exogenous load against design flow; within-patient plus negative-control comparator; load-response function and variance share, against one unresolved binary attribution with no comparator). vs P2 — exposure is the existence of a system, not competing concurrent draw; endpoint is coverage and cost; contrast is between calendar periods. vs P3 — same measurand family but the reference is the device's own setting with pressure held at calibration; it supplies the candidate's noise floor, not its exposure-response. Near-misses not graded on: Chatburn & Branson, Respir Care 2022;67(8):1002 (abstract only — engineering estimation review); NHSE C0871; IHEEM/St Helier demand-management documents; a 2024 medRxiv preprint that computes per-patient oxygen delivery from EMR settings against facility procurement and conspicuously does not cross it with outcomes; US patent 12599734 (title only).
Novelty confidence: Medium for the V2 estimand — not disturbed: P1's unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand all differ from the candidate's, so it grounds no Low grade, and nothing opened in 29 queries measures delivered-minus-set flow against concurrent network load. The search record was INCOMPLETE on the record as it stands, which independently barred Validated. Post-batch verification closes one half of that: PMC8680427 is identified and read (see the verification block) and is a close neighbour on EXPOSURE — one hospital's pipeline failure, measured in bar at the wall outlets and at the pressure-reducing station and in LPM of reducing-valve capacity, against a headcount of patients concurrently drawing oxygen — carrying no measurement of delivered bedside flow against a prescribed setting. Three same-physics disguise neighbours (arXiv:2003.12349, the MSF flow-splitter SOP, US11911567) remain unopened, so the record is still incomplete and Medium-with-a-close-neighbour is where Gate 5 puts this entry in any case.
Significance — consequence: if delivery degrades with load, a flowmeter setting stops being a dose under surge: MGPS alarm thresholds currently derived from copper pipe capacity acquire a patient-outcome basis, demand-management plans gain a target leg and load instead of hospital-wide restriction, and an HTM revision would have an exposure-response to write design flow against. If flat through and beyond design flow with a stated detection bound, a concern that surge planning carries unquantified is retired and the regulated-delivery assumption becomes evidence rather than custom.
Significance — audience: critical-care and respiratory clinicians titrating to SpO2 targets; authorised persons and medical gas committees, who own the telemetry and have no patient endpoint; NHS England estates policy (HTM 02-01 — the claim that it is mid-revision could not be verified by adversary #2 and a 2021 recommendation read in 2026 is more likely closed); LMIC oxygen-system programmes sizing PSA plants, whose current exposure variable is capability, not concurrent load.
Significance — fecundity: is a leg's effective capacity a function of device mix (HFNC vs low-flow)? Does leg flow telemetry work as a leading indicator of deterioration clusters? Should alarm levels be clinically rather than hydraulically derived? Do oxygenation-target trials run through surges carry an unbounded exposure-measurement error?
Significance — anchoring: HSSIB's unresolved attribution and its finding that the guidance is outdated; the NHSE/I alert that some hospitals drew more than their MGPS design flow; "good precision and poor accuracy" as the metrological noise floor; the oxygenation-target literature's assumption that a prescribed setting is a delivered dose.
Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary coinciding with an instrument-ownership boundary — estates telemetry's endpoint is the pipe, the EHR's exposure is the prescription, and no actor owns the join; plus terminal-unit delivered flow is unlogged by default. Both adversaries accepted the mechanism but noted it is partly an answering-difficulty mechanism dressed as an asking one, and that the worry itself was voiced repeatedly in print. Judge's reading at Gate 5 was that the repeated voicing of the worry told against the candidate; that reading is withdrawn, because verification shows what was voiced is qualitative analogy and one unattributed incident, not the question. The mechanism stands as the adversaries left it: partly an answering-difficulty mechanism dressed as an asking one, which is a non-fatal objection and caps the entry here.

## Verification of the rejection ground at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Two fresh-context readers, each handed one claim and its source and neither handed any reviewer's reasoning. The verdict moved: Rejected to Provisional.

**The ground falls.** The rejection rested on HSIB having put the candidate's own lay formulation — does one patient's delivered oxygen depend on the rest of the hospital's concurrent draw, and does it show up in their saturations — to a real incident. A reader with the full report (128,114 characters) found that it does not pose that question in any form. What the report contains is (i) a twice-stated, explicitly unresolved attribution question about whether one measured pressure drop caused two desaturations in one HDU, and (ii) five governance recommendations to NHSE/I and the CQC. The general quantity appears only twice and in neither case as a question: as asserted qualitative physics (a hosepipe/sprinkler analogy; "reduces the potential pressure available to oxygen outlets later in the system") and as A/2021/041, a Trust action installing estate-level flow meters. The term "diversity factor" appears nowhere in the report. An analogy is not a posed question, and an incident the report could not attribute is not the candidate's estimand asked before it.

**Three defects underneath the ground, each of a kind this ledger has catalogued.**

1. *The body is misattributed.* The report's own front matter says HSIB, the Healthcare Safety Investigation Branch. HSSIB is the successor body that hosts the page. The name was taken from the host rather than from the front matter, in this entry and in both adversary logs. Corrected to HSIB throughout this block; the citation in the prior list still reads HSSIB and is corrected here rather than by rewriting it.
2. *Both quoted fragments are severed at the hinge.* "unable to identify whether the pressure drop in the HDU was responsible" is verbatim but cut at a disjunction: the sentence could not identify whether the pressure drop was responsible OR whether other clinical factors were. The cut turns an even-handed non-determination into what reads like an unproven but live pipeline hypothesis. "unable to conclusively determine whether the desaturation" drops its entire predicate, stopping before all three branches — pressure loss, reduction in oxygen flow, other factors in their care. The two formulations are also not interchangeable: only the Executive Summary version mentions FLOW, while para 2.26 says pressure drop and CLINICAL factors, and neither carries a citation. This is the clipped-quotation defect that was the signature of the 2026-10-18 09:45 batch, found here on the sentence the verdict turned on.
3. *The figures were cited for the wrong measurand and circumstance.* 4.2 and 3.1 are pipeline pressure in bar in the HDU, recorded by the Trust during a deliberate Sunday pressure test after patients had been moved to redistribute flow. They are not flow, not L/min, not bedside, not from the original incident, and not compared against any prescribed setting. Presupposition P4 above is narrowed accordingly rather than withdrawn, because the comparison with the 3.45 bar calibration point is between like quantities.

**One near-miss recorded so it is not re-litigated.** The report notes that a red-dot plan was not working and that capacity calculations did not account for uneven demand. Those are absences in the TRUST'S PLANNING, not an acknowledged knowledge gap about delivered flow, and reading them as a flag of this candidate's gap would have routed a question nobody posed. Against the non-finding's weight, note also that the report states it "has not explored the clinical management of patients requiring oxygen therapy in this report" while resting its non-determination on being unable to exclude other clinical factors: the alternative it cannot rule out is one it did not examine.

**PMC8680427 is identified, and the nine-route failure was a routing failure, not a missing source.** It is a Clinical Communication on one hospital's medical-gas pipeline failure (volume 65, issue 11, pages 834-836 per Crossref-registered metadata; the publisher's served full-text page prints no volume, issue or pages, and the affiliations are unrecoverable from it). Its measurements are system-side throughout: bar at the wall outlets and at the pressure-reducing station, LPM of reducing-valve capacity, set against a headcount of patients concurrently drawing oxygen. So it is a close neighbour on the candidate's EXPOSURE and carries no evidence on the candidate's endpoint, delivered bedside flow against the prescribed flowmeter setting. Two route facts worth keeping: a bare-string web search on "PMC8680427" is an active trap here, returning ten confident-looking hits of which none is this article (pubannotation pages keyed to different PMC ids, bioRxiv full-text tab fragments, PubChem RDF pages), and the NCBI ID Converter path answers JSON while 302-ing to a pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov path, so the standing "PMC is hard-blocked" fact — which covers ARTICLE pages — is almost certainly what made this identifier look unidentifiable. The earlier readers' finding is recorded as COULD NOT READ, never as NOT FOUND.

**No late Gate 4 is owed, and this is the reason.** What fell is the JUDGE's Gate 2 scope call, not an adversary's ground. Gate 4 ran twice on this candidate: adversary 1 returned all eight attacks Resolved, adversary 2 returned Resolved or Partial with nothing Unresolved, both ran their Disguise sweeps (9 queries each), and both recommended Provisional. The verdict is re-graded on the record that already exists and the entry says so, per the ledger's rule that a withdrawn ground forces a fresh Gate 4 only where the ground was an adversary's.

**Routing withdrawn.** The row drafted at Gate 5 for `ledger/routed-open-problems.md` is not appended, for two independent reasons: a Provisional entry's own question is never routed, since the ledger still claims it as un-asked; and HSIB does not pose it, so there is no asked-but-open source to route it on. A one-incident forensic attribution that a report could not reach, in a report that scoped out the clinical alternative it could not exclude, is not a problem the research run could pick up.

ID: UQ-20261021-06
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — nuclear engineering / evaluated nuclear data and criticality safety; secondary: statistical learning (held-out validation), measurement metrology

Question (canonical): For a declared set of evaluated and adjusted nuclear-data libraries, each classified in advance by the provenance regime through which integral experiments entered its production — (A) documented formal assimilation/adjustment with a retrievable benchmark set, covariances and sensitivity profiles, versus (B) documented expert-judgement feedback (accept/reject, or scaling a differential evaluation to make a named assembly's k_eff agree) with no refittable objective function — what is, in regime A, the signed leave-one-benchmark-out shift in C/E (in pcm and in units of each benchmark's own stated experimental uncertainty) and in the derived bias and bias uncertainty; in regime B, the association between a benchmark's documented use-in-production status and its C/E residual, adjusted for energy range, material and facility and labelled as an association; and, for a declared documented validation suite, the resulting change in the Upper Subcritical Limit under the bias/bias-uncertainty construction of ANSI/ANS-8.24?

Alternative formulations:
1. Are evaluated nuclear-data libraries validated on the same integral experiments that shaped them, and if the shared experiments are held out, how much larger do the bias and bias uncertainty used in criticality-safety margins become?
2. What is the leave-one-benchmark-out cross-validated C/E of current nuclear-data libraries, and does it differ from the in-sample C/E that licensing calculations rest on?
(V1, as intaken, asked for a leave-one-out shift across ENDF/B, JEFF and JENDL; it was reformulated once at Gate 1 because that estimand does not exist where integral feedback entered by expert judgement. V2 above is the scored version. Both versions are in the record.)

Motivating gap: Library release documentation presents C/E clustered near unity on criticality benchmarks that are themselves documented inputs to evaluation, and ANSI/ANS-8.24 converts that C/E distribution into a bias and bias uncertainty inside the Upper Subcritical Limit, so in-sample optimism would propagate into a licensing margin. Gate 2 confirmed the first half from a primary document (ENDF/B-VIII.1 release paper: ²³⁹Pu prompt-ν̄ "driven by lower criticality required for Pu solutions benchmarks"; scaling up to 0.1% to set Jezebel k_eff ≡ 1, the "Jezebel v5 'calibration'" recommended by CSEWG) and refuted the intake's claim that no held-out C/E study exists.

Presuppositions: (1) ICSBEP is an enumerable frame with retrievable specifications and published C/E — established by use; Handbook not opened. (2) At least one library used integral benchmarks in production — ESTABLISHED for ENDF/B-VIII.1; unsourced for JEFF/JENDL. (3) The adjustment is refittable with benchmarks held out — TRUE for regime A, CONFIRMED FALSE for regime B. (4) ICSBEP benchmarks not so correlated that leave-one-out is meaningless — CONTESTED; SG39 "Integral correlations have a strong impact on adjustments" flags without settling; SANDA D5.6 and arXiv:1602.04038 not opened. (5) Applicant ANS-8.24 validation populations overlap the evaluation population — UNSOURCED. (6) Apparent accuracy adequately summarised by a C/E distribution against stated uncertainties — defensible. (7) Bias and bias uncertainty enter the USL as ANS-8.24 prescribes, which the intake required be quoted from the standard — **UNVERIFIED; ANSI/ANS-8.24 is a paid standard and COULD NOT READ by the record or by either adversary.** OSTI 1215586's abstract corroborates the construction at secondary level only.

What would count as an answer: a signed number with an interval per (library, benchmark class), in pcm and in units of each benchmark's stated uncertainty, plus a recomputed bias and bias uncertainty and a ΔUSL for a declared validation suite; a demonstration that the shift lies inside the benchmarks' stated uncertainties is an equally complete answer; the regime-B association is the fallback form; "provenance not reconstructible from public documents" is a third admissible answer.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries in total — 11 at Gate 2 (cap reached), 9 by adversary 1, 9 by adversary 2, the adversaries' 18 all in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try. Full lists with per-query results: batches/2026-10-21-1233/UQ-20261021-06-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative:
- `over-fitting in nuclear data adjustment integral benchmarks` (Gate 2 q1, the mandated own-field title query) → returned the killing paper, EPJ Plus 10.1140/epjp/i2018-12361-x, on the first query; it was nearly discarded as a bare catalogue hit.
- `how many ICSBEP benchmarks were used in nuclear data library adjustment fraction number of integral experiments` (Gate 2 q9, the mandated fraction query) → no published per-library ICSBEP-fraction count; the only counts that exist are per-study (12 in-sample / 51 held-out).
- `ANSI/ANS-8.24 upper subcritical limit bias and bias uncertainty validation criticality safety benchmark selection` (Gate 2 q6) → four LANL Whisper/USL reports, NCSD and SRNS items; all USL methodology, none paired with held-out library performance.
- `"data leakage" OR "train/test split" OR "held-out benchmarks" nuclear data evaluation machine learning ICSBEP` (A1 q2, ML vocabulary) → no held-out ICSBEP study; surfaced SG45 9-Trkov (opened, silent on circularity).
- `integral data testing versus integral data adjustment circular reasoning CSEWG criticism compensating errors history` (A2 q7, CSEWG's own historical words) → Chadwick, "Notes on Calibration," CSEWG Nov 2006 (opened full deck): "Are we getting the right answer for the wrong reason?" — "yes, at some level"; "Does it matter? Possibly, away from calibration point."
- `TSURFER adjusted cross-section library should not be used for validation same experiments consistency chi-square SCALE` (A2 q4) → SCALE/TSURFER manual (opened, full reST source): hold-out consistency testing of a predicted bias is a prescribed guideline in the code that produces criticality-safety biases.

Unrun checks, recorded as unrun and not as clear: the field's own term for the phenomenon, "over calibration" (Rochman §3.1), was searched by nobody; ENDF/B-VIII.1 Section XIV; ANSI/ANS-8.24; NUREG/CR-6698 (ML013230504); SANDA D5.6; CIEMAT C/E synthesis; WPEC SG45 (VaNDaL); jackknife/LOO k_eff bias (A2 q8 returned items, none opened).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. **D. Rochman, E. Bauge, A. Vasiliev, H. Ferroukhi, S. Pelloni, A.J. Koning, J.Ch. Sublet, "Monte Carlo nuclear data adjustment via integral information," Eur. Phys. J. Plus 133:537 (2018), DOI 10.1140/epjp/i2018-12361-x.** FULL TEXT read three times independently (Gate 2 and both adversaries) via the PSI author offprint https://tendl.web.psi.ch/bib_rochman/epjp1800496-offprints.pdf. Unit: random TMC/TENDL-style file realisation (10,000 per isotope, ²³⁵U, ²³⁸U, ²³⁹Pu), scored per benchmark. Endpoint: C−E with ΔC, summarised as χ²/P. Comparator: prior average and nominal file 0. Estimand: in-sample fit versus fit on a held-out set. §8.3 "Predictive power" scores the adjusted files on 51 further criticality benchmarks "not included in the updating procedure" (18 hmf / 18 pmf / 7 imf / 3 mmf / 4 mcf / 1 icf) and finds "As observed, the best performances are obtained for the prior nominal file 0." The adjusted files score worse on both measures - verbatim, "The adjustment methods as well as the best random file lead to larger [chi-squared glyph] and biases." - and the authors bound their own conclusion twice: "Such conclusion is dependent on the selection of benchmarks and on the type of random files used, but it still demonstrates that an adjustment is firstly valid for a given number of systems, and that any use of the adjusted nuclear data outside this selection has to be checked.", followed immediately by "Such observations do not discard the advantages of the presented methods for the uncertainty reduction". (Quotations corrected at first hand post-batch: the earlier form clipped the file-0 sentence off its hedges and transliterated the chi-squared glyph as "chi2".)
2. **OECD/NEA WPNCS Subgroup 14, "Performance Benchmark for Error Recovery and Experimental Coverage," https://sg14.ornl.gov/** (page read in full at Gate 2; neither adversary re-opened it). Unit: synthetic exercise case, 4 fictitious experiments × declared assimilation subsets. Endpoint: posterior application k_eff and predicted application bias with uncertainty. Comparator: which experiments enter the assimilation. Estimand: the DA method's ability to recover an embedded error and predict application bias.
3. **G. Palmiotti, WPEC SG39, "Methods and approaches to provide feedback from nuclear and covariance data adjustment," https://www.oecd-nea.org/download/wpec/meeting2017/sg_meetings/WPEC-REP-SG39-G.Palmiotti.pdf** (read in full at Gate 2; neither adversary re-opened it). Unit: the adjustment exercise / named integral experiment. Endpoint: adjusted cross sections and covariances fed back to evaluated files. Comparator: pre- versus post-adjustment. Estimand: criteria for using adjustment results effectively.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
1. It does not differ on the question, only on the measurement. Rochman's manipulation (exclude benchmarks from the adjustment), frame (criticality benchmarks with measured k_eff) and comparison (in-sample versus held-out) are the candidate's regime-A limb, and the answer runs in the direction the candidate hypothesised. The candidate differs on unit (released adjusted libraries vs random-file ensembles), design (leave-one-out vs a single 12-in/51-out split) and endpoint (pcm-per-stated-σ, derived bias and bias uncertainty vs χ²/P) — a refinement of the same question, not a different object. Both adversaries weighed that difference and both still graded Disguise Unresolved. One correction in the candidate's favour, from adversary 2: the paper calls the 51 "a new set of criticality benchmarks" and does not state they are ICSBEP; the ICSBEP provenance is inferred from the class codes. It does not change the verdict, since the limb concerns held-out criticality benchmarks with measured k_eff, which these are.
2. SG14 varies which experiments enter the assimilation — structurally the candidate's manipulation — but has no held-out measured benchmark at all: the applications carry no measured values, so there is no C/E to shift. Synthetic, not ICSBEP; C/E and USL not mentioned.
3. Palmiotti is the field's methodological mandate document and makes no recommendation about independent validation sets, over-fitting, double counting or "bias in the bias," and reports no out-of-sample test. It is evidence that the recommendation layer is silent, not that the measurement is unpublished — Prior 1 published it.

Novelty confidence: Low

Significance — consequence: If large: every criticality-safety validation deriving a bias and bias uncertainty from a C/E population overlapping the evaluation's own integral inputs has an understated bias uncertainty and a non-conservative USL by a computable amount — a licensing quantity. If small: the worry retires. Deflated, because Prior 1 already answered the regime-A limb directionally, so that limb is "how much," not "whether"; the consequence now lives in the regime-B and ΔUSL limbs, which nothing opened connects to a margin.

Significance — audience: Real, named and already engaged: criticality-safety analysts and the ANSI/ANS-8 working groups who own ANS-8.24; the US NCSP (whose WANDA 2026 performance-assessment talk asks for "No significant regression in performance" with no numbers and no independence test); WPEC SG45 (VaNDaL) and SG46; WPNCS SG14, whose live exercise already manipulates which experiments enter assimilation. Adversary 2 showed the engagement cuts both ways: TSURFER's guidelines already prescribe a hold-out check of a predicted bias, and OSTI 1215586 is the criticality-safety community re-deriving the USL under a violated independence assumption — the audience is real and has already acted, which lowers the marginal value of an answer.

Significance — fecundity: Moderate. Opens: how to declare a correlation model for ICSBEP so leave-one-group-out is meaningful; whether evaluation provenance is reconstructible per isotope from release papers (partly, on the ENDF/B-VIII.1 read — the Jezebel scaling is stated outright); whether regime-B feedback is auditable at all.

Significance — anchoring: The compensating-errors problem ENDF/B-VIII.1 names in its own text ("compensating errors in individual reaction channel data may still play a consequential role in the prediction of criticality"); integral-experiment correlation (SG39, SANDA D5.6, arXiv:1602.04038); WPNCS SG14's error-recovery exercise; unrecognised-systematic-uncertainty work (arXiv:1911.01825, not opened).

Reason for silence: The record proposed a disciplinary boundary with an incentive gap — evaluation owns the adjustment and reports fit in χ² and C−E, criticality safety owns the USL and takes the library as given, neither owns the join. **Gate 4 broke this on both sides.** Evaluation side: Chadwick's CSEWG 2006 "Notes on Calibration" asks the generalization question in CSEWG's own room ("Are we getting the right answer for the wrong reason?" — "yes, at some level"), and the adjuster-versus-data-tester tension was a titled question forty years ago (Wagschal & Yeivin, "Why are data-testers afraid of adjustment?", 1985 — abstract-level read only, used solely for the existence and framing of the question). Criticality-safety side: the hold-out consistency test is in the SCALE manual's guidelines. Adversary 1 found the mechanism operating only in a weaker form — Kleedtke's CSEWG 2024 LANL deck has the ²³⁹Pu tuning target on slide 6 and the same assembly as a validation gain on slide 8 with no comment — which supports "not noticed here," close to the "no one thought of it" the LEDGER disallows. What survives is a narrower claim: the joined quantity (a held-out degradation propagated into an ANS-8.24 USL) has no venue and appears in nothing opened. That is an uncomputed number, not an unasked question.

Strongest remaining objection: Disguise. The primary limb is a disguised known — Rochman et al. 2018 §8.3 "Predictive power" asks and answers it in the candidate's own field and its own words, on 51 held-out criticality benchmarks scored against measured k_eff, with the answer in the hypothesised direction, and it surfaced on the very first query Gate 2 ran. **Which leg the verdict stands on:** a single leg, Rochman §8.3 — specifically that §8.3 is a held-out scoring against measured values and not a forward uncertainty propagation, and that the 51 benchmarks did not enter the weighting. That leg was read at full text and verified independently three times (Gate 2, A1, A2) from the PSI author offprint, including the front matter and Table 7's dependence on measured values. **What would survive if it fell:** not the Disguise kill. Priors 2 and 3 and the Wieselquist WANDA2026 deck each affirmatively lack held-out C/E, and TSURFER's hold-out test is inside the applicant's own GLLS adjustment — a different object from the library evaluation's integral feedback, and resting a kill on it would be exactly the scope transfer this ledger has lost batches to. ## Verification of the kill at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Two fresh-context readers: one handed the Rochman paper and the four strings this entry quotes from it, one sent on an independent sweep for the released-library and USL limb. **The verdict does not move — Rejected — and the ground it rests on is narrower than the entry stated.**

**The kill holds where it was read.** The paper's front matter is exactly as cited (all seven authors in order, Eur. Phys. J. Plus 133:537, 2018, DOI 10.1140/epjp/i2018-12361-x), section 8.3 genuinely is a held-out predictive test, and all four quoted strings are in it. The exercise: 12 benchmarks supplying 14 integral quantities enter the adjustment (Table 1), and the caption of Table 7 reads verbatim "51 benchmarks are used: 18 hmf, 18 pmf, 7 imf, 3 mmf, 4 mcf and 1 icf". A single in-set/out-set split, not a leave-one-out. So the candidate's primary limb — the shift when benchmarks are held out of a library's own integral-data adjustment, in the direction the candidate hypothesised — is asked and answered in the candidate's own field, which is what the Gate 2 grade turned on.

**Three scope corrections, and they matter for what this paper may be cited for.** (1) The unit is five individually named ENDF-6 files — the paper's own prior nominal file 0, its BMC, BFMC and Mocaba posteriors, and file 1834, the best member of its own random ensemble. **No released evaluated library is scored on the held-out set.** JEFF, JENDL and ENDF/B appear only in the introduction, in section 8.2.2 and in a remark about one ENDF/B-VIII reaction; the paper never says file 0 derives from a released library, only that it resembles what "one can find in a nuclear data library". Any claim of the form "adjusted data generalise worse than released libraries" is outside this paper's regime, and the paper is silent there rather than supportive. (2) The endpoint is an unthresholded mean bias in pcm — absolute 311 (file 0) against 627, 493, 470 and 423 — plus chi-squared per benchmark, with **no sampling uncertainty, no interval, no bias uncertainty, no area of applicability and no tolerance limit**. The strings "bias uncertainty", "upper subcritical limit", "USL", "subcritical", "ANSI", "ANS-8" and "8.24" do not occur, and no criticality-safety standard is cited; "criticality-safety" appears once, as one item in a list of application areas. So the paper cannot be cited for a criticality-safety bias in the ANSI/ANS-8.24 sense, and its silence on the USL is an absence, not a flag. (3) ICSBEP is named in sections 1 and 2.2 and Table 1 cites the handbook for the measured values, but section 8.3 says only "a new set of criticality benchmarks" and the Table 7 caption names no source — so the ICSBEP provenance of the 51 is an inference from the class codes, exactly as this entry already recorded.

**Two quotation defects in this entry, corrected above.** "larger chi2 and biases" was a transliteration rather than a quotation: the paper prints the chi-squared glyph, and the sentence's subject is "The adjustment methods as well as the best random file", which the fragment dropped. And the file-0 string was quoted away from its hedges — its own sentence opens "As observed," tying it to Table 7, the next sentence makes the conclusion dependent on the benchmark selection and the file type, and the sentence after that explicitly refuses the strong reading: "Such observations do not discard the advantages of the presented methods for the uncertainty reduction". The entry now carries the surrounding sentences. One further distinction worth keeping: the paper's own "no predictive power" remark is about the linear-combination method, which it excluded from the test, and is not a caution about validation.

**The residual limb is UNVERIFIED, not established as un-asked, and that is load-bearing.** The independent sweep could not settle whether the overlap question is posed for released libraries, because the two documents most likely to carry it — WPEC SG-22's "First conclusions" and the ENDF/B-VIII.0 release paper — were both robots-refused, and eleven further USL and bias-uncertainty documents (WPEC SG-33, SG-44, UACSA Phase IV, CSSG Response 2014-02, LA-UR-16-23533 among them) were identified and never opened. Under the ledger's rule an unrun check cannot pass a candidate and cannot kill it, so this limb neither rescues the entry nor adds to the kill: the rejection stands on the verified limb alone. One firm finding from the sweep is worth recording because it would otherwise be misread as this gap: the field's documented concern is non-independence AMONG validation benchmarks (NUREG/CR-7308 on repeated sensitivity across benchmarks), which is a different gap from overlap between the production set and the validation set, and any future hit on "benchmark non-independence" has to be checked for which of the two it is in. NUREG/CR-7308 also says that "significant challenges remain to be solved" before GLLSM-type adjustment can be used "directly for determining bias and bias uncertainty for NCS validation", and is silent on overlap as one of those challenges — silence, not a prohibition. That report was read in two windows only, so its absences are window-scoped.

**What would have to be true for this question to come back.** Not a re-grade on this record: a fresh Gate 0 intake, stated for released libraries whose integral-data use is documented from their own release papers, with the ANSI/ANS-8.24 text in hand for the USL limb, and the WPEC SG-22 and SG-33 conclusions read. As the Gate 5 judge said, the ΔUSL residue is a quantity not yet computed rather than a question not yet asked, and the sweep that would decide which it is has not been run.

ID: UQ-20261021-07
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — chemical/mechanical engineering (heat transfer, process plant design); secondary: industrial energy efficiency, reliability engineering, forecast verification

Question (canonical): V2 (Gate 1 reformulation, the one permitted; scored as canonical) — For a declared frame of in-service heat exchangers in one process-service class, with monitored duty, flows and inlet/outlet temperatures and retrievable design datasheets, what are the bias and spread of the distribution of realized fouling resistance over the tabulated fouling resistance used in that unit's design, under a propagated uncertainty budget with a stated detection floor; and, restricted to units whose surface area is verifiably fouling-allowance-controlled on the datasheet, what is the SIGNED area-sizing error implied by that distribution — excess installed area where the allowance over-predicted, deficit where it under-predicted?
V1 (intake, superseded) asked limb 2 one-sidedly ("excess area" only), presupposing the sign; both versions recorded per Gate 1 in batches/2026-10-21-1233/UQ-20261021-07-record.md.

Alternative formulations:
- Do the tabulated fouling factors designers take from standards predict the fouling that actually occurs, and by how much are exchangers consequently over- or under-sized?
- Treating the design fouling allowance as a prediction and the monitored thermal resistance as its outcome, what are the bias and spread of that prediction across a service class?

Motivating gap:
Design practice uses a standard's tabulated fouling resistance (TEMA the index case) as though it were the fouling the unit will experience, though the values ship with no distribution, uncertainty or provenance. Gate 2 correction: the provenance half is not a silence but a published observation in the candidate's own trade literature — Sloley (Chemical Processing 2023, full text): the TEMA values "were originally developed with very little, or perhaps even no data, to back up the values."; Aguirre (Chemical Processing 2006, full text): the originals represented "a combination of a fouling and safety factor".

Presuppositions:
1. A standard tabulates fouling resistances and designers use them as the allowance — ESTABLISHED from trade sources, but TEMA's own wording NOT QUOTED (standard not opened by the record or by either adversary; Unverified, not a kill).
2. Realized fouling resistance is identifiable from operating data given a clean reference — CONTESTED, and contested by the field: Sloley 2023, "the plant calculated fouling factor... includes the results of all errors and uncertainties."
3. The per-unit design allowance is retrievable from datasheets — CONTESTED; every empirical source found operates on a cooperating-operator archive, not a sample of the installed base.
4. A single lumped fouling resistance is the right measurand — CONTESTED, unaddressed by any source opened.
5. Fouling resistance within a run is stationary or has an estimable trajectory — CONTESTED, unaddressed.
6. Excess area is a meaningful counterfactual — CONTESTED and partly inverted (Sloley 2019: higher fouling shifts the heat-recovery optimum to higher capital), which is why V2 signs the limb.
7. Monitored duty is attributable to the exchanger, not to an upstream service change — CONTESTED, unaddressed.
Adversary 2 added a sourced mechanism against presupposition 3/limb 2: margin is composite and carried through interchangeable datasheet fields — Shilling, Rudy & Rudy (HEFC 2009, paper 48, full text) decompose it into correlation error, fouling resistance and operating uncertainty, with Example 1 "using zero fouling resistance with an additional 5 percent area".

What would count as an answer:
A per-service-class distribution of realized over tabulated fouling resistance with a propagated uncertainty budget and stated detection floor, plus the implied signed area-sizing error on the allowance-controlled subset. A ratio centred on 1 with modest spread vindicates the tables. A demonstration that routine plant instrumentation cannot identify the measurand at useful precision is also an answer.

It stands on PRIOR 4 (Shilling, Rudy & Rudy 2009, HEFC paper 48, read in full by adversary 2): design-margin theory applied to heat exchangers, authored inside HTRI, treating the fouling allowance as one of three probability-rated margin components with fouling resistance and area as interchangeable carriers of the same risk. That single leg defeats the record's distinguishing claim, its reason-for-silence mechanism and part of its fecundity claim, and it grounds the Unresolved Disguise that is fatal on its own. If it fell, the verdict would survive on the Gate 2 leg (PRIORS 1 and 2 — same author, same comparator, same quantity, point answer published, distribution announced), though that leg rests on abstracts nobody re-opened and would support Low only for limb 1. King 2007 is corroborative only (abstract, assertion without data) and nothing rests on it. If both the prior-4 and Sloley legs fell, PRIOR 3 alone would carry Medium, not Low, and the entry would then be Provisional at best — never Validated, since attacks 4 and 5 are Partial on the as-written measurand and limb 2 — and would need the full eight attacks re-run per the Gate 5 rule on withdrawn Gate 2 grounds.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): obtain HTRI F-2 and F-12 and the full texts of AIChE 2019 paper 166c and AIChE SWPTC 2018 paper 14c, to establish how much of limb 1 is already answered and whether the announced Monte Carlo distribution was ever published.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no. The row recommended at Gate 5 is WITHDRAWN on first-hand verification, on three independent grounds: the 2019 abstract's announced Monte Carlo is over fouling RATES comparing two modelling choices, not realized against tabulated RESISTANCE over a frame, so it does not show the candidate's question open; the form that is actually posed is answered, and answered rejections are never routed; and the two remarks that look like the field flagging the gap ("the accuracy of these TEMA values has been reconsidered"; "actual values ... can be either higher or lower than the resistances calculated") state that the error is unquantified without posing the measurement. Both adversaries add a fourth reason: the tabulated value is a bundled safety-and-uncertainty allowance, so scoring it as a point forecast is partly a category error. Checked by grep: ledger/routed-open-problems.md carries no row for this ID, and this line is a recommendation rather than a record of an append.

## Verification of the kill at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Three fresh-context readers: one on the two Sloley proceedings pages, one on the Shilling paper, one on an independent sweep for the distribution itself. **The verdict does not move — Rejected — but the strongest Low ground is withdrawn, the routing row is withdrawn, and four citation defects in this entry are corrected.**

**What survives.** The comparison is posed and point-answered in the candidate's own field and words. Both quoted strings are verbatim in the pages as served: from the 2019 abstract, "Operating data from four crude units supported the use of fouling factors at three times TEMA values."; from the 2018 abstract, "data from typical plants show the TEMA values are extremely low compared to experience in many units." Neither page declares a sampling frame or a service class, and neither reports any variance statistic. Shilling et al. 2009 was read in full and refutes the record's method-vocabulary claim more strongly than the entry needed: the paper does not merely rate the fouling allowance by probability, it makes the allowance contingent on that rating — "We propose to use a value for fouling resistance only if the risk level for fouling is high enough to justify it" — inside a named three-component decomposition of margin with a 1-5 probability ladder, a five-band money consequence scale and a matrix lookup to Low/Medium/High actions.

**The strongest Low ground falls on scope.** The entry graded novelty Low partly because "the distributional version is announced in prior 1's own abstract". It is not, in the candidate's regime: the announced Monte Carlo analysis is over fouling RATES and compares two MODELLING CHOICES (unit-average against a distribution), not realized against TABULATED fouling RESISTANCE over a frame of units, and the page reports none of its results. That announcement is silent in the candidate's regime rather than closing it. Both Sloley reads are also ABSTRACT ONLY behind an AIChE login wall, so whether either paper contains a distribution is UNREAD, not absent: a verdict that these papers lack one would exceed the read. The rejection therefore rests on the asked-and-point-answered comparison, which is visible in the abstracts themselves, and not on the stronger claim.

**The independent sweep found no distribution anywhere readable, and one address unresolved.** No readable source publishes a bias-and-spread, percentiles or a fitted distribution of realized against tabulated fouling resistance over a declared frame of in-service exchangers. Each candidate stops short in a nameable way: Bories & Patureaux give per-exchanger point values and a min-max range over eight named units without ever differencing them against TEMA; Zubair et al. fit a distribution to the wrong variable (time to a critical resistance) on laboratory data with assumed scatter; Awad's review carries the one large in-service dataset collapsed to category averages. The residual is HTRI Report F-2, member-restricted and read only as a catalogue entry, where the roughly 700-exchanger dataset lives; F-12 and the ESDU fouling items were never examined. That is COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND, and it is why nothing here is promoted to "never published". Non-English and thesis literature is effectively unswept.

**The routing row is WITHDRAWN, on three independent grounds.** (1) The source the row cited as showing the question open — the 2019 abstract's announced Monte Carlo — is in a different regime, as above. (2) The form that IS posed is ANSWERED: the 2018 abstract poses "what's normal" and answers it directionally, the 2019 abstract gives the multiplier, and an answered rejection is never routed. (3) The two remarks that look like the field flagging the gap do not pose it: "the accuracy of these TEMA values has been reconsidered" and "actual values of fouling resistances in any application can be either higher or lower than the resistances calculated" say the direction and size of the error are unknown, which is an acknowledgement that the bias is unquantified rather than a posed measurement; and the 2018 abstract's "Recent work has focused on probabilistic and statistical methods of evaluating fouling systems. Nevertheless, fouling factors remain in common use." points at other people's work. Both adversaries independently raised a fourth reason to withhold: the tabulated value is a deliberately bundled safety-and-uncertainty allowance ("thus representing a combination of a fouling and safety factor"), so scoring it as a point forecast is partly a category error, and routing a problem whose estimand is contested would hand the research run work under a false label. Checked by grep: ledger/routed-open-problems.md carries no row for this ID and none was added.

**Citation defects in this entry, corrected above.** (1) Shilling's author line and affiliation were both wrong: the front matter prints R.L. Shilling, M.P. RUDY and T.M. Rudy, and only Shilling is at HTRI — both Rudys are at ToMaRu Consulting, Warrenton, Virginia, with the work credited to HTRI's Exchanger Design Margin Task Force. "Paper 48" is a filename, not a printed designation; the printed pagination is 340-345. (2) "add 5% extra area" inverts when cut: the full cell reads "Do not apply fouling factor, but add 5% extra area", so the area REPLACES the fouling factor, and it is the LOW-risk row only of a three-row table. (3) The obsolescence string drops its hedge — the sentence opens "Many of these resistance values", not all, and its antecedent is the TEMA standards plus plant data, company standards and simple safety factors; it carries no citation, so it must not be sourced to Hays 1989 or Müller-Steinhagen 2000, which attach to the following sentence. (4) "not based on actual cases" is scoped by its own "Although" clause to the paper's two worked examples, not to the framework or to Table 1.

**Three further corrections that bear on how this entry may be cited.** The 2018 string is cut before "Nevertheless," and the sentence before it concedes that published fouling values "often lack basic information on many of the factors affecting fouling" — so quoted bare it reads as an empirical finding where the source advances a judgement over acknowledged gaps in the data. The 2019 sentence travels without the sentence that immediately qualifies it, "Fouling rates may vary dramatically from unit to unit and from exchanger to exchanger within the same unit.", and its "supported" is weaker than "established": the page assigns the multiplier's provenance to earlier literature work and the four units corroborate it. The 2019 page as served reads "at last three times higher", not "at least"; that damage is reproduced, not silently corrected. And on the area limb, the figures in circulation (20-50% excess surface for tubular exchangers, 15-25% for compact) are AS-DESIGNED margins computed from a tabulated resistance, uncited in the source that carries them and swinging 40% to 20% on one input choice in its worked example — they are not the share of installed area that realized fouling leaves unused, and that quantity appears genuinely unmeasured in everything read. Shilling itself marks the boundary the entry should state: "However, this tool has not yet been applied to the heat exchanger design process", so the probabilistic-margin vocabulary exists in the heat-exchanger literature as an introduction against a practice that did not use it, which is not the same as the practice using it.

ID: UQ-20261021-08
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — materials engineering / failure analysis and forensic engineering (TARGET field: its literature decides novelty, its community would act). Method transplanted from forensic statistics (black-box design, variance decomposition of inconclusives) and forensic psychology (contextual bias, linear sequential unmasking). Method-owning neighbours: forensic statistics; human factors in non-destructive evaluation.

Question (canonical): Under a forensic-style black-box design — specimens failed in the laboratory by mechanisms known by construction, a mechanism label set and an explicit inconclusive option fixed in advance, examiners working independently and blind both to the answer and to one another, and each specimen randomised across context arms declared in advance as either NON-DIAGNOSTIC (which side retained the examiner) or DIAGNOSTIC-BUT-MANIPULATED-IN-VERIDICALITY (a service-history narrative that is true, false, or withheld) — what are the false-attribution rate, the inconclusive rate and the inter-examiner reproducibility of expert fracture-mode and failure-mode determination in engineering failure analysis, and by how much does each context arm shift them relative to the no-context arm?

Alternative formulations:
- (lay / historical trigger) What is the error rate of a failure analyst, measured the way the forensic pattern disciplines were compelled to measure theirs after the 2009 National Academies report?
- (sharpest single limb) Is a fracture-mode determination reproducible across examiners, and is it invariant to the narrative handed to the examiner with the specimen?
- (method field's words) For the task "assign a failure mechanism from a fixed label set", what are the discipline's failure rate, inconclusive rate and examiner/item variance components under known ground truth, and what is the measured effect of context exposure?
- V1 (intake), superseded at Gate 1: same design with "task-irrelevant context (claimed service history, identity of the commissioning party)". Reformulated because service history is a legitimate input to mechanism determination, so V1 smuggled a contested presupposition (P8) and its context limb could be answered in favour of "bias" whatever the evidence showed. V2 splits the manipulandum into a non-diagnostic component (retaining side) and a diagnostic component whose veridicality, not relevance, is varied. Estimands unchanged.

Motivating gap: Forensic pattern disciplines were pushed into measuring examiner error against constructed ground truth. Engineering failure analysis performs the same epistemic operation — an expert assigning a category from pattern features on a physical specimen — and its determinations decide insurance claims, recalls, airworthiness directives and litigation. The field's own reliability work measures DETECTION (probability of detection, false-call rate in NDE), not ATTRIBUTION. Confirmed from both sides: the method field's current methodology paper enumerates the disciplines black-box studies have been run in and names no engineering field (P3', full text); the nearest engineering neighbour measures hit/miss POD and never asks for a mechanism (P1', full text). Sharpened by P2' (abstract level), in which the target field states the premise in its own words — fractographic evaluations "are influenced by human factors, such as subjectivity, and suffer from a lack of reproducibility" — while validating a model against "the expert consensus achieved in the round robin test", i.e. the consensus is the yardstick and its own accuracy is unmeasured. That circularity is what the design would break, and it is also the candidate's closest and least-verified neighbour.

Presuppositions:
- P1. Fracture/failure-mode attribution is a routine categorical expert task with a defined label set (fatigue, ductile overload, cleavage, SCC, hydrogen embrittlement, creep, wear). ASSERTED, NOT QUOTED from any opened handbook or standard — the intake's undertaking is unmet and recorded as unmet, not as a check that passed. Indirect support only: P2' operates a binary ductile/brittle partition (abstract level); VDI 3822 organises FractoDB (adversary 1, full text); ISO 15243:2017 standardises rolling-bearing damage/failure terms and causes (adversary 2, catalogue level, page not opened — support by analogy, different object).
- P2. Ground truth can be manufactured: specimens failed by a known mechanism. CONTESTED at the edges (mixed mode, sequence, environment); ambiguity handling must be pre-declared and independently adjudicated. Evidenced as routine apparatus for flaw PRESENCE in the adjacent field (P1', full text: three induced thermal fatigue cracks, signals extracted, removed and re-inserted at known locations, amplitudes "artificially altered"); never established for MECHANISM.
- P3. Enough practising examiners participate under blinding for usable precision. CONTESTED; volunteers are non-random, so the rates estimate the laboratory task among volunteers, not field performance of the profession. P1' sharpens the worry: its own sample was nine trainees, one excluded after 1290 false calls, eight analysed.
- P4. Laboratory specimens are informative about field specimens, which arrive corroded, worn, incomplete and already accompanied by context. CONTESTED; the transplant's weakest joint; stated as a scope limit, not argued away.
- P5. Context can be operationalised and randomised without unacceptable deception. CONTESTED AND HARDER UNDER V2: forensic black-box studies withhold context, they do not fabricate it; the false-history arm has no cited precedent and is the arm most likely to be struck by a review board. Fallback declared: the retained-side arm survives as the clean bias test.
- P6. Inconclusives can be analysed rather than discarded. CONTESTED AND EVIDENCED AS UNSETTLED (P3', full text: inconclusives apportioned by "the examiner variance divided by the total (examiner plus item) variance"; the method "may produce counterintuitive results in some edge cases"). The analysis plan must pre-commit; it cannot inherit a settled recipe.
- P7. An error rate, rather than a calibrated likelihood ratio, is the decision-relevant quantity. CONTESTED AND REINFORCED: P3' reports "failure rates" instead of false positive/negative error rates, so the method field is itself moving the target.
- P8 (added at Gate 1; the reason for the reformulation). Context in failure analysis separates into diagnostic and non-diagnostic components, so a bias arm is distinguishable from a legitimate-input arm. CONTESTED; the transplant's conceptual joint. If the separation fails, the diagnostic arm measures responsiveness to evidence (or credulity) rather than bias, and only the retained-side arm survives as a bias test.

What would count as an answer: A rate with a confidence interval in each design cell — false attribution, inconclusive, and an inter-examiner reproducibility statistic — plus the context effect as a difference in rates between each context arm and the no-context arm, from a pre-registered protocol in which ground truth is adjudicated independently of the examiners and the inconclusive treatment is pre-committed. A pre-registered null is an equally complete answer and is immediately usable by courts and accreditation bodies; the symmetry of usefulness between positive and null is a mark in the design's favour. A demonstration that single-mechanism ground truth cannot be constructed for the label set is a third admissible answer, reportable as a falsification of P2 (a finding about the design, not about examiners) — the discipline that stops the third branch functioning as rhetorical insurance.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries in total — 11 at Gate 2 (5 fetches), 9 by adversary 1 (8 Disguise + 1 prior check; 4 fetches, 1 refused by robots), 9 by adversary 2 (all in untried vocabularies; 4 fetches). No search call was refused anywhere. Full lists: batches/2026-10-21-1233/UQ-20261021-08-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative:

P1'. Virkkunen I, Haapalainen J, Papula S, Sarikka T, Kotamies J, Hänninen H, "Effect of Feedback and Variation on Inspection Reliability", 7th European-American Workshop on Reliability of NDE (DGZfP), 2017. acris.aalto.fi/ws/portalfiles/portal/17437784/ — FULL TEXT, re-verified by adversary 2 (all six authors and venue confirmed from front matter). Not used as priors, and why: the HFACS cause-coding inter-rater literature, the SSM/BAM NDT human-factors reports, the Charpy shear-fracture-appearance reliability papers and the fire-investigation bias studies were seen at snippet or title level only and nothing was opened, so none grounds a grade; FRACTESUS and the VAMAS/ceramics round robins reproduce measured values, not categorical attributions.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1' — endpoint differs decisively (detection of a flaw's presence vs attribution of the process that produced a failure); unit and estimand differ. The shared element is methodological and helps rather than pre-empts: ground truth by construction and arm randomisation are already routine, so the apparatus is not speculative. A POD study never asks what mechanism produced the flaw, so it cannot bound the candidate's quantity.
vs P2' — label set differs (binary appearance partition and a continuous ductile portion vs a multi-class mechanism set with an inconclusive option); reference differs and that is the crux (P2' takes expert consensus AS the yardstick; the candidate makes the examiner the object and the constructed mechanism the yardstick, the inversion that would let P2'-style models be validated non-circularly); no context manipulation anywhere in P2'. BUT the round robin is unread, so the reproducibility limb cannot be graded confidently against it.
vs P3' — same method, different discipline and object: source identity vs failure mechanism. The candidate inherits the inconclusive problem as a pre-registration requirement rather than a settled recipe, and inherits the failure-rate framing as a reason to report both quantities. Its enumeration of disciplines supplies the negative in the method-owning field's own vocabulary, which is the form the ledger requires.
vs P4' — substrate overlaps (fractured surfaces, blind examination, error-rate ambition); estimand does not (which object the piece came from vs which mechanism broke it). Clean distinction on endpoint.
vs the method-owning fields generally — the surviving negative must be stated narrowly and as a transplant: not "nobody has asked whether context shifts a categorical expert determination" (asked and repeatedly answered one discipline over, including for fire-cause determination), but "it has never been asked of failure-mechanism attribution, where the label set is a physical process rather than a source, and where the field's own automated-analysis work uses examiner consensus as its reference standard without having measured that consensus against constructed truth."

Novelty confidence: Medium, at the bottom of the band, and with a close neighbour that is unread. Not High: the target field has at least one multi-expert fracture-surface round robin (P2', paywalled), an organised body that "systematically carries out laboratory and round robin tests" on archived lab-made reference fractures (Bettge & Schmies 2023, full text), and a Charpy fracture-appearance reliability literature known only by title (OSTI 115531; OSTI/ORNL 1972570) — three unread neighbour families on the reproducibility/accuracy limb. Not Low: no near-duplicate was actually READ by any of the three agents, and 29 queries across the target field's own words, German, Japanese, ceramics/VAMAS, NDE human factors, accident-investigation and fire-investigation human factors, metrology/proficiency testing, implant retrieval, bearing-damage standards and the answer side returned no black-box or constructed-truth attribution study and no published false-attribution rate. Not Unverified: every required search ran; both adversaries completed their Disguise sweeps (8 and 9 new-vocabulary queries).
Legs of the grade: Leg 1 — P3's own enumeration of black-box disciplines, full text, with no engineering field among them (independently re-verified). Leg 2 — the mandated NDE neighbour measures detection, not attribution (full text), and the field's flagship interlaboratory programme measured values, not judgments (VAMAS record, full abstract). Leg 3 — nothing surfaced in 29 queries; an absence-of-evidence leg, the weakest, and the one the unread neighbours threaten. If any unread neighbour reports per-examiner accuracy or agreement for fracture-MODE assessment, the reproducibility limb drops to Low and the grade rests on Leg 1 alone, with only the constructed-truth and context-arm limbs surviving.

Significance — consequence: If the false-attribution rate is material and context-sensitive, every failure-analysis conclusion entering litigation, a recall decision or an airworthiness directive carries an error term that is unquantified and signed — a context effect biases rather than merely adds noise, so it cannot be dismissed as attenuation — and the remedies are already built one discipline over (blind verification, linear sequential unmasking, case-manager control of non-diagnostic context), none of which appear in failure-analysis practice or accreditation. If the answer is a null, the field gains a published rate with an interval under a named design that an expert can offer when asked what his discipline's error rate is. A third outcome, that single-mechanism truth cannot be constructed across the label set, would say that the categories are not cleanly instantiable even in the laboratory, which bears on the evidentiary weight they carry.

Significance — audience: (i) Failure-analysis practice and its venues (ASM International, J Fail Anal Prev), whose literature is a case literature. (ii) Accreditation bodies and ISO/IEC 17025 assessors: PT machinery exists for quantitative and chemical measurands and no scheme for mechanism attribution. (iii) Courts and retaining counsel: the 2009 NAS error-rate demand reshaped forensic pattern testimony and has not been pressed on engineering experts. (iv) Airworthiness and product-recall investigation bodies, whose determinations are single-examiner or small-panel and unblinded. (v) The NDE human-factors community (Aalto, BAM, SSM), who own the apparatus and are the likeliest party to run it. (vi) The DVM/DGM WG Fractography, which already runs systematic round robins on lab-made reference fractures.
HONEST QUALIFICATION (why significance is 2, not 3): no engineering body was found calling for this measurement; demand is inferred from the structure of the field's decisions, not evidenced in its words, and the field has a live incentive not to want the number. Adversary 2 sharpened this into revealed preference: the same community sustained five international round robins across ~40 laboratories over thirteen years and never selected mode attribution as a target. Capability is evidenced; demand is not.

Significance — fecundity: Is the error rate mechanism-dependent, with the hard cells predictable in advance (SCC vs corrosion fatigue; creep vs overload at temperature)? Does the inconclusive rate decompose into examiner and item variance as P3's model predicts when the classes are processes rather than sources — a test of that method outside the regime it was built in? Does a pre-specified unmasking order for instrumental evidence (SEM, EDS, hardness, metallography) change the rate, converting linear sequential unmasking into a laboratory workflow question? Is there an allegiance effect by retained side? And most directly: can automated fractography be calibrated against constructed truth instead of expert consensus, removing the circularity visible in P2'?

Significance — anchoring: (a) The 2009 NAS error-rate demand, which fell on disciplines defined by criminal prosecution rather than by task structure. (b) Admissibility of engineering expert testimony, where no discipline-level rate exists to cite. (c) A live circularity in automated fractography (P2', abstract). (d) NDE reliability's POD/false-call framework, with mature ground-truth-by-construction methodology (P1') and no attribution analogue. (e) The unsettled analysis of inconclusives in forensic statistics (P3', full text). (f) This ledger's UQ-20261017-43, whose Gate 4 rejection turned on estimating detection performance without ground truth; the candidate's answer is to manufacture the truth, on a different endpoint.

Reason for silence (strongest first): 1. A DISCIPLINARY BOUNDARY DRAWN BY LEGAL EXPOSURE RATHER THAN BY TASK STRUCTURE — black-box studies were compelled by a report about criminal forensics, in disciplines whose output convicts people; failure analysis performs the same operation in civil and regulatory practice, where no compelling event occurred. Evidenced: P3's enumeration (full text, re-verified) names no engineering field; and the one engineering-adjacent exception the adversaries found, context-bias experiments in fire-cause determination (Bieber 2012, abstract level; Portsmouth, title only), sits inside criminal forensics too, so it tests the boundary and does not breach it. 2. THE FIELD'S RELIABILITY VOCABULARY IS ALREADY OCCUPIED, so the question sounds answered — here "reliability" means POD and false-call rate, and a "round robin" means reproducibility of a measured value. Evidenced most cleanly by the VAMAS record (five round robins, ~40 laboratories, thirteen years, toughness values, no agreement figure) and by Swab & Quinn 2019 (full text, dynamic compression strength). A practitioner asked whether examiner reliability has been measured can answer yes, truthfully, and mean something else. 3. A PUBLICATION FORM WITH NO DENOMINATOR — a case literature validated by internal coherence; a rate requires an assembled population with known answers. 4.
