Well-posedness 3/3 (V2): the answer form is specified at estimand level (three rates with intervals per cell, an agreement statistic, arm differences against a no-context arm), every presupposition is established or explicitly flagged, the V1 defect that made the context limb unfalsifiable is removed, and the third admissible answer is declared as a falsification rather than a free pass. Three items are named as open rather than resolved, and both adversaries pushed on them: P1's label set is unquoted (the intake's unmet undertaking), the input modality is unspecified (adversary 1, attack 4c), and no agreement statistic or minimum detectable arm difference is declared (adversary 2, attack 5). None falsifies a presupposition; all are fixable in the question text, which is why the score holds at 3.
Significance 2/3: consequence is clear and symmetric between positive and null; audiences are specific, institutionally routed and now evidenced as equipped; fecundity is concrete and includes breaking a circularity in an adjacent active literature. Held at 2 because no engineering body's published call was found, the demand is inferred from decision structure rather than the field's words, and thirteen years of round robins in the same community never selected this target.

Strongest remaining objection: Three unread neighbours on the reproducibility/accuracy limb, all inside the target field or its standards estate — P2' (Herges et al. 2023, doi 10.1515/pm-2023-1042: a multi-expert fracture-surface round robin, COULD NOT READ by the record and both adversaries), the DVM/DGM WG Fractography's systematic round robins on archived lab-made reference fractures (existence in full text, outputs not located), and the Charpy fracture-appearance reliability papers (OSTI 115531; OSTI/ORNL 1972570, refused by robots). If any of them reports per-examiner accuracy or inter-examiner agreement for fracture-mode assessment, the reproducibility limb is a disguised known and the entry falls to Rejected on that limb. THE VERDICT STANDS ON THIS LEG — the Provisional cap is the "Medium novelty with a close neighbour" clause, and the leg is the unread P2'. WHICH WOULD SURVIVE IF IT FELL: adversary 2's dissolution leg, which needs no external source — the absolute false-attribution rate is a property of the specimen set the designer chose, not of the discipline, so even with every unread neighbour proved irrelevant the question shrinks to its within-set contrasts (context-arm difference and inter-examiner agreement) and the headline "error rate of failure analysis" is not an estimand about examiners. Adversary 1's second leg — that FractoDB's archived lab-made reference fractures contradict silence mechanism 4 — also survives independently, but it only narrows a silence mechanism and does not reach the novelty grade, which rests on P3's enumeration (Leg 1, full text, twice read). Note that the unread neighbours cannot kill the entry now: an unread paper grounds no grade in either direction, which is exactly why this is a cap and not a Rejection.
Promotion requires: (i) reading the P2' body, which post-batch verification established is reachable only offline — the publisher withholds it, OpenAlex confirms no open deposit exists, and five search routes plus the DGM media library returned nothing — so the route is interlibrary loan or a subscription to Practical Metallography 60(6) 352-362, or the corresponding author; the open 2025 Materials & Design paper by the same group (doi 10.1016/j.matdes.2025.114424) is the cheapest lead, since it may restate or cite the round robin, but anything from it must be attributed to it. What is needed from that body is the round robin's design: participant count, the examiners' task, the label set, and whether any reference beyond expert consensus was used. (ii) OSTI/ORNL 1972570 by a route other than the robots-refused biblio page (the servlets purl, an ORNL or NTRL mirror, info.ornl.gov) — still COULD NOT READ, so still neither passing nor killing. (iii) The DVM/DGM working-group round-robin outputs, which post-batch searching did NOT FIND as a published result; if a later pass confirms none exists, that absence is the candidate's novelty rather than a gap in the record. DISCHARGED post-batch: OSTI 115531 was opened and measures operator consistency in a continuous fracture-APPEARANCE value with no constructed truth, so it does not report fracture-MODE attribution accuracy and does not pre-empt the candidate. If (i) and (iii) return no per-examiner accuracy or inter-examiner agreement for mode attribution against constructed truth, novelty rises to a solid Medium and Disguise moves to Resolved; the entry can then be Validated once the question text also fixes the three specification gaps — quote the mechanism label set from an opened handbook or standard, declare the input modality and the masking of laboratory artefacts, and name the agreement statistic with a minimum detectable arm difference.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): read the three unread neighbours named above before designing anything — the promotion condition and the first step are the same act, which is the clearest sign the entry is not yet ripe.

Routing: ROUTE: no — the status is Provisional, so the ledger still claims this question as un-asked, and by construction a Provisional entry is not routed to the open-questions project. It is also not a rejection as already-asked: no near-duplicate was read by any of the three agents, so there is no source showing an asked-but-open problem to hand over. If the promotion check finds that a target-field round robin already measured examiner accuracy or reproducibility of fracture-mode attribution, the correct disposition is Rejected as a disguised known, which is also not routed; the only path to routing is a finding that the question is asked in the literature and still unanswered, which nothing in this record supports.

## Verification of the cap at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Two fresh-context readers, one per unread neighbour family. **The verdict does not move — Provisional — the cap is confirmed as a genuine COULD NOT READ, and two findings from the abstract run in the candidate's favour.**

**P2' is still unread, and the routes are now exhausted rather than untried.** The De Gruyter page serves the abstract, acknowledgements and references with the body behind "Licensed / Unlicensed Requires Authentication"; OpenAlex reports is_oa false, best_oa_location null and has_fulltext false, so no open deposit exists to find; five searches for an author preprint, a repository copy, a DVM or DGM proceedings version or the chair's publication list returned nothing; and the DGM media-library item is a JavaScript shell with no text. The remaining routes are offline ones this session cannot reach — interlibrary loan or a subscription to the journal issue, or the corresponding author. This is COULD NOT READ, explicitly not NOT FOUND, so the paper still neither passes nor kills the candidate and the Medium-with-a-close-neighbour cap stands exactly as the entry set it. The journal name, volume, issue and pages remain an inference from deposited metadata rather than from the article's own front matter.

**But the abstract settles the direction of comparison, and it runs the candidate's way.** The round robin exists — "the expert consensus achieved in the round robin test", and in the German abstract "im Ringversuch ermittelten Expertenkonsens" — and the acknowledgements thank fractography experts at AG der Dillinger Hüttenwerke plus university staff who took part in a fracture-surface analysis survey. What the paper scores, however, is the MODEL against the experts: "the results being in good agreement with the expert consensus". The experts are the reference standard, not the object of measurement. The only construction-known labels in sight — upper-shelf (ductile) and lower-shelf (brittle) reference regions, fixed by test temperature rather than by anyone's reading — label the MODEL's training database, while the human comparison happens on mixed fracture modes where the standard is reader consensus. That is the inversion this entry claimed as its distinction, now corroborated from the source's own abstract rather than argued. Two cautions: the abstract is written almost entirely in the future tense, so it reports no quantified result and must not be read as reporting one; and quoting "the expert consensus achieved in the round robin test" to support a claim that the round robin MEASURED expert performance would cut the phrase away from its clause, where it is only the provenance of the comparator.

**One of the three unread families is now read, and it does not pre-empt.** OSTI 115531 was opened: it measures operator-to-operator consistency in fracture APPEARANCE — a continuous percent-shear-type value on Charpy specimens, with no truth known by construction — and its agreement finding is ordinal rather than a statistic ("Results showed that agreement was greatest when operators are experienced..."). Every number in it belongs to sample size or transition-temperature comparison. Cited for fracture-MODE or failure-MECHANISM attribution it is silent, not supportive, and its one mode-sounding sentence ("unlike Charpy energy, fracture appearance tells how a specimen failed") is a motivating remark, not a result. Its front matter is thin — no authors, no date — with a same-titled Welding Journal record beside it, so no author or year may be transplanted between the two.

**The second family is NOT FOUND and the third is COULD NOT READ.** No DVM or DGM Fractography working-group round-robin RESULT publication surfaced in Practical Metallography or in a DVM report series; only a describing paper about an online image database, itself unreadable (two De Gruyter routes returned CLIENT_ERROR). So the working group cannot be cited for examiner-reliability data on this evidence. OSTI/ORNL 1972570 returned robots refusals with no front matter at all, and two plausible routes were left untried when the fetch cap was reached — existence neither confirmed nor refuted, and it must not be recorded as absent. Several attractive nuisances surfaced and are named here so a later pass does not mistake them: the DVM round robins on instrumented Charpy testing measure VALUES, and "Classification of fracture characteristics and fracture mechanisms using deep learning and topography data" (10.1515/pm-2022-1008) reports a MACHINE classifier's accuracy, not an examiner's.

**A search trap, recorded so a later reader does not fall into it.** Saarland repository handle 20.500.11880/40767 is returned by several queries naming the 2023 article but holds a DIFFERENT, open-access 2025 paper by an overlapping author set: Herges, Bachmann, Scholl & Mücklich, "An automated Machine Learning based approach for a reproducible and efficient evaluation of industrial Charpy V-notch specimens", Materials & Design 257, doi 10.1016/j.matdes.2025.114424. A checker could read that body and believe it had read this one. It is also the most promising lead for the round robin's design, since the same group may restate or cite it — but anything taken from it must be attributed to it, not folded into the 2023 citation.

ID: UQ-20261021-09
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — geotechnical/structural engineering (target field; its code committees would act). Instrument from InSAR geodesy; method vocabulary from screening-test (diagnostic-accuracy) and SHM/NDE methodology.
Question (canonical): On a building frame declared before any data pull in one EGMS-covered region, with the damage cut fixed in advance at Burland D>=2 (D>=3 as a pre-specified sensitivity arm) and the predictor declared as EGMS-derived within-footprint differential vertical velocity over the service observation window rather than as cumulative angular distortion since construction: (a) what are the sensitivity, specificity, ROC/AUC with intervals and — on a probabilistically drawn, independently verified sub-sample that fixes damage prevalence — the positive predictive value of exceeding each criterion's own limiting value, evaluated only for those criteria whose measurand the service supplies (Skempton–MacDonald delta/L; Burland–Wroth Delta/L under a declared inflection-point rule), with Boscardin–Cording reported as not evaluable for want of horizontal strain; and (b) how much of any shortfall is attributable to the rate-for-cumulative substitution, estimated on the subset also carrying bed-joint levelling? (This is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation, scored as canonical; V1 asked more loosely whether the Skempton–MacDonald / Burland–Wroth / Boscardin–Cording family discriminates damaged from undamaged buildings at population scale.)
Alternative formulations: Do the settlement-damage criteria embedded in geotechnical practice work when applied to every building in a region rather than to the few dozen case histories they were fitted on? / Over a declared building population, how well does satellite-measured differential settlement rate separate buildings with recorded damage from those without, at the thresholds practice actually uses?
Motivating gap: The criteria in daily use were fitted to small 1950s–1980s case-history sets because population-scale differential settlement was unmeasurable; a free continent-scale persistent-scatterer service makes the criterion evaluable as a screening test. Intake added that the InSAR-and-damage literature only draws risk maps, presupposing the discrimination. Gate 2 falsified that last clause, and it was the clause the candidate rested on.
Presuppositions: (1) EGMS supplies scatterer density sufficient for a within-footprint differential on a usable share of buildings — contested; Drougkas et al. IDW-interpolated 10 m grids to fill scatterer gaps, and the achieved frame is instrument-defined, not a sample of the stock. (2) The service's windowed roof-level vertical velocity maps onto cumulative foundation-level distortion — strongly contested; Prosperi et al. Sec. 5.2 attributes to Peduto et al. that satellite SRI values "may be lower" over a fixed 5-year window. (3) An independent, joinable building-level damage record exists at population scale — contested and unevidenced; all three priors used bespoke façade/levelling campaigns. (4) Damage has other causes, so this measures discrimination not attribution — established. (5) Each threshold has one stated definition — refuted for Boscardin–Cording, whose horizontal-strain input the product does not supply; Peduto et al. already computed Burland–Wroth at the original inflection-point definition. (6) The building, not the party-wall-joined terrace, is the right unit — contested and unresolved; Peduto et al. 2017 returned different damage ranges at the two units over the same area. (7) Damage and motion records share a period — flagged; V2's rate predictor declares the window.
What would count as an answer: Per-criterion sensitivity, specificity and ROC/AUC with intervals, plus PPV on a verification sub-sample that fixes prevalence, on a frame and measurand mapping declared before any data pull; the rate-for-cumulative substitution as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis against the levelling subset; Boscardin–Cording recorded as not evaluable rather than evaluated on a surrogate; a demonstrated inability to estimate reported as such. For the levelling instrument this answer substantially exists; for the EGMS rate predictor and for PPV it does not.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 13 at Gate 2 (cap was 11; the two-query overrun is recorded as an overrun of the shared budget, not a refusal — no call was refused), plus 8 Disguise queries from adversary 1 and 9 from adversary 2, all executed. Most informative: `InSAR-derived angular distortion predicts settlement-induced building damage validation survey` (mandatory own-field, own-words title query) → surfaced two of the three killing priors, including Peduto et al. 2019 full text; `receiver operating characteristic sensitivity specificity geotechnical threshold criterion building damage prediction` → the decisive prior, Prosperi et al. 2023; `Copernicus EGMS building damage assessment validation positive predictive value` → EGMS-and-buildings papers, none reporting PPV; `EGMS percentage of buildings covered measurement points fraction building stock persistent scatterer density Europe` (the "what fraction of X" limb) → the share of the building stock was not found published; `structural health monitoring ROC analysis of code damage threshold probability of detection false alarm settlement criterion population of buildings` (method-owning field) → POD/ROC of thresholds is mature in SHM and not applied to the settlement criteria, but this does not rescue the candidate because the ROC was run in the data-owning field. Adversary Disguise vocabularies not tried at Gate 2: Dutch funderingsschade, Italian, French retrait-gonflement insurance claims, NCB mining subsidence, tunnelling stage-2 screening, ML precision/recall (precision is PPV renamed), forecast-verification hit rate / false alarm ratio, Spanish Murcia, Chinese land subsidence, geodetic PSI-vs-levelling validation, answer-side EGMS service name. None returned a renamed equivalent of the residual estimand. Full lists: batches/2026-10-21-1233/UQ-20261021-09-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) Prosperi, Korswagen, Korff, Schipper, Rots, "Empirical fragility and ROC curves for masonry buildings subjected to settlements," J. Building Engineering 68 (2023) 106094 — https://repository.tudelft.nl/file/File_d05fb48c-e7b7-4fd1-b000-3963834114f2?preview=1 — READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT, opened independently by the record and by both adversaries. Unit = individual masonry building (386 Dutch, mainly pre-1950 terraced; 122 shallow, 264 piled); endpoint = surveyed damage, positive class pooling "light" and "moderate to severe"; comparator = four SRI parameters against one another, with Boscardin–Cording's 3.3 permille converted to a fragility probability; estimand = ROC/AUC discrimination plus a per-parameter optimal cut-off; instrument = 2003 bed-joint levelling, not InSAR. The paper's own words: "The relative rotation or angular distortion [46] beta". Verified absences: no numeric AUC/TPR/FPR/PPV in text, tables or captions, no prevalence, and Table 1 an empty TN/FP/FN/TP template. (2) Peduto, Korff, Nicodemo, Marchese, Ferlisi, "Empirical fragility curves for settlement-affected buildings … seven hundred masonry buildings in The Netherlands," Soils and Foundations 59 (2019) 380–397, DOI 10.1016/j.sandf.2018.12.009 — https://www.iris.unisa.it/bitstream/11386/4721876/2/Peduto%20et%20al_2019_S%26F.pdf — READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT (record); existence corroborated by adversary 1 (exact-title repository and author-list hits), content not re-verified by either adversary. 706 buildings, bespoke DInSAR/PSI (not EGMS), lognormal fragility for P(D>=d|IM), rotation theta = Deltarho/L and deflection ratio computed both simplified and at Burland and Wroth's inflection-point definition; no ROC, AUC, sensitivity, specificity or PPV. (3) Drougkas, Verstrynge, Van Balen, Shimoni, Croonenborghs, Hayen, Declercq, "Country-scale InSAR monitoring for settlement and uplift damage calculation in architectural heritage structures," Structural Health Monitoring (2020), DOI 10.1177/1475921720942120 — https://lirias.kuleuven.be/retrieve/582850 — READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT with named extraction damage (record); existence corroborated at five hosts by adversary 2, content re-verified by neither. 269,194 objects across Belgium, endpoint a calculated damage class not an observed one, six criteria models compared, own StaMPS processing with IDW-filled velocity grids; no classification statistics.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Prior 1 — differs on instrument (EGMS windowed rate vs bed-joint cumulative), on one metric (PPV, which Prior 1 cannot supply: non-random sample, prevalence not stated), and on treating the published limiting values themselves as classifiers rather than converting them to fragility probabilities. It does not differ on the central estimand: ROC discrimination of damaged vs undamaged Dutch masonry buildings by angular distortion is published. vs Prior 2 — asks for discrimination statistics where Prior 2 reports fragility parameters, and for a free continent-scale service where Prior 2 used bespoke PSI over four municipalities; but Prior 2 already performs the satellite-to-building-damage join at the candidate's unit at n = 706 with the Skempton–MacDonald measurand and with Burland–Wroth at its own inflection-point definition, so the "re-derive each threshold at its author's definition from satellite data" move is not new. vs Prior 3 — asks for validation where Prior 3 performs calculation; Prior 3 is the risk-map genre the motivating gap names and presupposes the discrimination at issue, but at 269k objects it is already the population-scale application, so the new-instrument framing is weaker than intaken.
Novelty confidence: Medium, with a close neighbour (re-graded from Low on first-hand verification, 2026-10-21 post-batch; see the verification block below). The neighbour is Prosperi et al. 2023, which works the same object with the same predictor and publishes its own ROC-optimised cut-offs, while printing no discrimination number anywhere and never scoring a published threshold as a classifier.
Significance — consequence: If the thresholds discriminate near chance on EGMS rates, code committees learn a daily-use criterion has no population-scale validity under that instrument; if they discriminate well, population screening is licensed and municipalities and insurers would act. But after Prior 1 either answer reads as an instrument result, not a criterion result: the criteria already have a published ROC under levelling with optimal cut-offs (beta 4.77 / 3.67 mm/m) of the same order as Boscardin–Cording's 3.3 mm/m. The consequential unknown has shifted from "do the criteria work" to "does the free service's rate carry the signal the criteria need."
Significance — audience: Real, identifiable and already engaged with this exact object: Eurocode 7 / national-annex serviceability committees; Dutch municipal asset managers and Belgian heritage agencies (the priors' own clients); subsidence insurers and the ESA business-applications ground-motion-underwriting services. Adversary 1 strengthened this with two unvalidated products now in use — Hammad and Stouthamer (EGU26-18341) feeding EGMS velocities through a TU Delft fragility curve to building-specific damage probabilities as a "decision-support and spatial planning tool", and Shahbazi et al. (IGARSS 2024) flagging "308 buildings … as vulnerable to damage" over Catalunya with only an internal uncertainty analysis. The engagement cuts both ways: it shows significance is not inflated, and it shows the question was reachable, which is why it was reached.
Significance — fecundity: A measured rate-vs-cumulative transfer function would make every published InSAR risk map interpretable as a screening instrument with a known error rate, open the question of what a criterion calibrated on population data rather than case histories looks like, and force the unit-of-analysis question for party-wall-joined terraces that Prior 2's companion paper raises implicitly.
Significance — anchoring: Scatterer-frame representativeness (Prior 3's IDW gap-filling); the Dutch foundation/subsidence-damage liability controversy; the standing mismatch between deterministic serviceability criteria and reliability-based code calibration.
Reason for silence: It was not silent, which is the finding. The only mechanism that survives explains the residue alone: the discrimination-metric vocabulary (ROC, POD, PPV) belongs to screening-test and SHM/NDE methodology while the data belong to geotechnics, so the metrics arrived late and incompletely — Prosperi et al. import ROC, define TPR and FPR, print an empty contingency template, and then report no AUC, sensitivity, specificity or prevalence. Secondary: EGMS became free and regularly updated only from 2022, after Priors 2 and 3 were processed. Adversary 2 read the same evidence as a question half-asked in that very paper, which weakens rather than supports a never-asked claim; adversary 1 reduced the silence to "not yet", three years after Prosperi, with the same group holding both datasets.

Strongest remaining objection: The question is one step from an analysis that has already been performed in print: Prosperi et al. 2023 runs a ROC analysis of surveyed damage against angular distortion over 386 Dutch masonry buildings and publishes optimal cut-offs of the same order as Boscardin-Cording's value, so the candidate's contribution is the part that paper leaves unreported (absolute discrimination statistics, a prevalence and therefore a PPV) and the part it never attempts (scoring the published limits themselves as classifiers, and doing it from a free continent-scale instrument). Adversary 2 read that same proximity as a question half-asked in Prosperi's own paper and left attack 7 Unresolved, which caps the entry. THE SUPERSEDED KILL, kept for the record: the Gate 5 rejection rested on three legs — Leg 1, Prosperi publishing the candidate's central estimand; Leg 2, Peduto et al. 2019 publishing the satellite-to-damage join with both measurand definitions; Leg 3, Drougkas et al. 2020 applying the criteria at population scale. Legs 1 and 2 were read at first hand post-batch and neither reports any discrimination statistic, and neither scores a published threshold as a classifier; Leg 3 was always a calculation rather than a validation, as this entry's own comparison said. The verification block gives the detail.
Promotion requires: (i) obtaining the absolute discrimination statistics behind Prosperi et al. 2023's eight ROC panels — the AUC values, and the coordinates of the plotted best-sensitivity points — from the authors or from a later paper by that group, since digitising the figure would be answering the question rather than grading it, and confirming that no later publication prints them; (ii) a dedicated sweep for any study that scores the Skempton-MacDonald, Burland-Wroth or Boscardin-Cording limiting values AS classifiers at their own authors' thresholds against surveyed damage, because Prosperi is not that check and its absence is what the candidate's novelty now rests on; (iii) closing the well-posedness gap at 2/3 by fixing which EGMS product the predictor is (decomposed vertical velocity or line-of-sight), over what window, and naming a joinable population-scale damage register with its ascertainment rule; and (iv) declaring the prevalence a PPV claim would assume, since no opened source supplies one. If (ii) returns nothing and (iii) is fixed, novelty is a solid Medium and attack 7 can be re-run on the narrowed question.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Read Prosperi et al. 2023 Fig. 8 and Table 5 against Peduto et al. 2019's per-building DInSAR dataset for the overlapping Schiedam cluster and establish whether the two instruments rank the same buildings — i.e. measure the rate-vs-cumulative transfer before proposing any population-scale screening study; no new data collection needed. (The record's claim that 262 cases appear in both datasets is unattributed and was flagged as unverified by adversary 2; it is not load-bearing.)

## Verification of the kill at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Two fresh-context readers, each handed one source and the claim made of it, neither handed any reviewer's reasoning. **The verdict moved: Rejected to Provisional.**

**Leg 1 falls.** Prosperi et al. 2023 was read in full at the TU Delft repository. It has ROC curves in its title, defines TPR and FPR in equations (2) and (3), plots eight ROC panels with the AUC shaded — and prints **not one absolute discrimination number**. No AUC value, no sensitivity, no specificity, no TPR or FPR, no PPV appears in its text, tables or figure captions; Table 1 is an empty symbolic TN/FP/FN/TP template with no counts; the "best sensitivity-pair" is a black dot whose coordinates are never given; no damage prevalence is stated, which forecloses PPV even in principle. The six percentages in its section 5.3 (14/14/7 shallow, 6/3/1 deep) are relative increases over differential settlement, ambiguous in the source between absolute percentage-point and relative differences, and Table 5's percentages are fragility-curve damage probabilities at the optimised threshold, not discrimination statistics. So the judge's Leg 1 — that the paper *publishes* the candidate's central estimand — does not hold. What holds is that the paper *performs* a ROC analysis and derives its own optimal cut-offs from it.

**And the deciding finding, which no pass had made explicit: the classical limits are never scored as classifiers.** Skempton–MacDonald [46] and Burland–Wroth [26] are cited for DEFINITIONS only and their limiting values are never evaluated, never even stated as numbers; Boscardin–Cording's 3.3 permille is run THROUGH the fragility curve to yield 5% (shallow) and 2% (deep), which is the opposite direction of travel from classification. No TPR or FPR is computed at 3.3 permille. On the question of whether anyone has scored the published settlement limits as damage classifiers on real buildings, this paper is silent rather than supportive of either answer, and it was the closest-looking candidate in the field.

**Leg 2 falls too.** Peduto, Korff, Nicodemo, Marchese & Ferlisi 2019 (Soils and Foundations 59:380–397) was read in full. The factual core the entry claimed holds exactly: 706 buildings, satellite displacement joined to surveyed damage at the individual-building unit, four Dutch municipalities, 180 shallow and 526 mainly-wooden-piled. But it reports fragility parameters and nothing resembling a diagnostic-test evaluation: ROC, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, false positives and confusion matrices are all absent, and its one use of the word "accuracy" means DInSAR measurement accuracy against levelling. Skempton–MacDonald is cited, not applied — its rotation is a DInSAR footprint profile slope, not an angular distortion between adjacent frame points — and Burland–Wroth is used at their definition only for D2/L2, with D1/L1 the paper's own simplified approach. Its instrument is bespoke TerraSAR-X PSI (2009–2014, SkyGeo), damage surveyed 2015–2016, exterior facades only, D4 and D5 merged, beta constrained by the authors; the European Ground Motion Service postdates it by three years, so it cannot be cited for what a free continent-scale service delivers.

**What the verdict now rests on.** Gate 4 is complete — two independent adversaries, both Disguise sweeps executed, nothing Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4 — and what fell is the JUDGE's Gate 2 call, not an adversary's ground, so no late Gate 4 is owed and the entry is re-graded on the existing record. Novelty is Medium with a close neighbour: Prosperi works the same object, the same buildings and the same predictor, and publishes optimised cut-offs (beta 4.77 and 3.67 mm/m) of the same order as the literature value, which is close even though it scores no published threshold and reports no discrimination number. Provisional, not Validated: adversary 2 left attack 7 (reason for silence) Unresolved, reading the same evidence as a question half-asked in Prosperi's own paper, and well-posedness stands at 2/3.

**Corrections to this entry's own record, none of which changes the verdict.** The claim that 262 Schiedam cases appear in both datasets was already flagged unverified and remains so; Prosperi's 262 Schiedam cases sit adjacent to 264 piled-foundation buildings and the paper never reconciles them, so the two numbers must not be read as the same group. Prosperi's instrument carries a stated directional bias — displacements "of only a few points are gathered at fixed, limited intervals with manual bed-joint levelling readings, thus suggesting that damage appears at higher values of distortion" — and its causal attribution is an assumption: "all the visual damage to the surveyed buildings was assumed to be caused by the settlements". Its bed-joint campaign (2003) predates the damage information by a decade. Satellite data is present in Prosperi only as discussion and as a comparison attributed to Peduto et al., so neither "this paper validates InSAR-derived distortions" nor "satellite data is absent from it" is right. Peduto's served text carries OCR damage in Table 3, so no rotation or deflection-ratio median should be quoted from this read.

**A briefing error of my own, recorded rather than hidden.** The verification brief for Leg 2 listed four candidate journals for Peduto et al. rather than quoting this entry's own citation, and the reader reported the venue as "misidentified in the claim as it was handed to me". The entry's citation was correct throughout — Soils and Foundations 59 (2019), five authors including Ferlisi. The defect was in the brief, not in the ledger. This is the third pass in which a brief written from something other than the entry's full citation manufactured a defect that does not exist.

ID: UQ-20261021-10
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — materials/chemical engineering (Li-ion battery recycling, hydro- and pyrometallurgy) as target field; secondary industrial ecology/LCA and recycling policy; method-owning field minerals-processing sampling theory (Gy, WCSB).
Question (canonical): For a declared region and window and a frame declared before any data pull, on one pre-declared crosswalk layer (cathode-active-material chemistry shares by mass of arriving battery mass, with black-mass element content reported as a separate second layer): (a) what is the measured arrival-composition distribution under a sampling protocol declared in advance and reported with its fundamental-sampling-error and grouping-and-segregation budget and detection limits; (b) over a declared literature frame of recycling-process and LCA studies that state an input composition, what is the distribution of *assumed* compositions on that same layer, with the non-stating excluded share reported as a primary result; and (c) what is the signed gap, and what does it do to those studies' recovery-efficiency and recycled-content figures when their own models are re-run on the measured composition? (Format = stratifier; state of health defined only on the intact-pack/module sub-stream, with the not-evaluable remainder's mass share reported.)
Alternative formulations: What is actually in the arriving stream and in the black mass made from it, and does the published process/LCA literature assume a feedstock the real stream does not supply? / Over a declared frame of published Li-ion recycling and LCA studies, what feedstock composition does each assume, and what is the signed gap to the composition measured at operating plants? (V1 at intake bundled chemistry, SoH, format and contamination as one endpoint with no crosswalk; V2 above is the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation and is what is scored.)
Motivating gap: Dense-how, empty-why. Thick literature on leaching routes, direct regeneration and separation trains, each stated for a particular input composition; mass-based recovery and recycled-content obligations (Reg. (EU) 2023/1542 as index instrument) assessed on assumed compositions; recovery chemistry-sensitive by stoichiometry (LiFePO4 contains no Ni or Co). Restated after Gate 2: an instrumented black-mass characterisation genre does exist (Dadé 2022; Bologna 2025; WCSB10), so "near-silent on what is arriving" is too strong for the material; what is absent is the frame, the variance budget, the coding of assumed compositions, and the comparison.
Presuppositions: (1) arrival composition measurable at plant scale under a declared protocol — partly established for the derived product, open for the stream; (2) a recycler or authority permits sampling or has published data — partly relieved (multi-supplier studies exist); statutory route now partly characterised: Reg. (EU) 493/2012 Annex I pt 3 requires each recycler to determine input-fraction composition at element/compound level, for lead-acid/Ni-Cd/"other" only, submitted to authorities, unpublished, and it may lawfully be based on placed-on-market composition rather than measured; (3) studies state assumed input composition explicitly enough to code — established on opened instances (Mohr 2020; Petzold 2025), frame share unknown; (4) composition comparably defined on both sides — contested, which is why V2 declares the crosswalk; (5) arrivals attributable to the declared region — contested and unrelieved (production scrap dominant today; black mass internationally traded; "arriving" gate not fixed in V2); (6) recovery outcomes composition-sensitive — stoichiometrically sound for element-specific targets, unverified for mass-based ones; (7) SoH measurable on arriving units — contested and NOT SEARCHED by Gate 2 or by either adversary.
What would count as an answer: A measured arrival distribution on the declared layer with its FSE/GSE components and detection limits; a coded distribution of assumed compositions over the declared frame with the excluded non-stating share as a primary result; and the signed gap propagated into those frame studies' own reported figures where their models are re-runnable, with the non-re-runnable share reported. Three outcomes are all full answers: a gap; no gap (which closes the worry and grants the existing literature an empirical warrant); or a demonstration that assumed compositions are not reported well enough to code (an answer about the literature, actionable for journals and LCI bodies). A documented failure to obtain sampling access, with fallback routes attempted, is an admissible negative about feasibility.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 (cap 11, min 8), plus 9 new by adversary 1 and 9 new by adversary 2 in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try = 29 distinct queries, 9 pages opened. Full lists: batches/2026-10-21-1233/UQ-20261021-10-record.md and ...-adversary-1.md, ...-adversary-2.md. Most informative: `characterization of end-of-life lithium-ion battery waste stream received at an industrial recycling plant composition` (own-field own-words title query → a characterisation-of-samples genre only; no stream-under-a-frame title) · `theory of sampling Gy ... battery black mass ... fundamental sampling error` (method-owner → mature named method, pointed at black mass once, with the strategy as an aim) · `share of lithium-ion battery recycling feedstock production scrap versus end-of-life batteries percentage` (mandatory quantity limb → Fraunhofer ISI projection publishes the *origin* split, ~50 kt/yr now to ~420 kt in 2030, no chemistry breakdown at all) · `metallurgical accounting feed grade reconciliation assumed versus measured plant feed assay` (A2 → assumed-vs-measured feed reconciliation with variance propagation is a mature named practice in minerals processing and has never been applied to battery feedstock; the best-aimed transplant query, clean in the target field) · `退役锂离子电池 回收 来料 成分 实测 分布 NMC LFP 占比` (A2, in the language of the largest arrival stream → process reviews only) · `Regulation 493/2012 recycling efficiency "input fraction" composition reporting` (A1 → the statutory return, opened) · `review life cycle assessment ... table of studies assumed cathode chemistry input composition` (A2 → Nanomaterials 15(16):1283 opened; codes boundaries, functional units and impact categories across studies, tabulates inventories by chemistry not by study, reports no measured gap). Unverified residue, recorded as unrun and not as passed: national statutory returns (UBA Altbatterien, ZVEI "Recycling-Batterien 2025", ARSO, Eurostat, the WKO/Commission recycling-efficiency annex) unopened by Gate 2 and by both adversaries; VTT "Identification of waste LIB cell chemistry", 化工进展 2023 42(5):2702, Zenodo 13644996, Vanderbruggen et al. 2021 unopened.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) Dadé, Wallmach, Laugier, "Detailed Microparticle Analyses ... into the Black Mass", Minerals 12(2):119, 2022, DOI 10.3390/min12020119 — read first-hand at the publisher by Gate 2 and by both adversaries; unit = microparticle aggregated to sample, three fine (<500 µm) black-mass samples from three unnamed suppliers after pyrolysis, dry shredding and sieving; endpoint = per-sample phase/cathode-type abundance plus harmful impurity phases; comparator = the samples against each other; estimand = each sample's composition as measured, not a population parameter; no frame, region, window, field protocol or variance budget. (2) Mohr, Peters, Baumann, Weil, "Toward a cell-chemistry specific life cycle assessment of lithium-ion battery recycling processes", J. Ind. Ecol. 24:1310–1322, 2020, DOI 10.1111/jiec.13021 — full text read at the KIT repository; unit = modelled cell by chemistry (NCA, NMC111, LFP, Na-ion); endpoint = life-cycle impacts per chemistry; estimand = chemistry-specific impacts at 1 kWh with a 1 kg-treated-cells reference quantity; assumed input constructed, not measured ("compositions ... retrieved from Peters and Weil (2018)"). (3) Donnelly, Pirrie, Power, Corfe et al., "The sampling and phase characterisation of black mass", TOS Forum 11:397–409 (WCSB10), 2022, DOI 10.1255/tosf.166 — ABSTRACT/METADATA ONLY (South Wales repository); full PDF COULD NOT READ at budget; unit = particle within two samples (one natural, one powdered); endpoint = phase and element identification incl. Li; no comparator stream; a pragmatic sampling strategy stated as an aim, not a delivered result. Adversary 2 aimed a query squarely at this item in the proceedings' own vocabulary and did not surface it, so Prior 3 is uncorroborated by any second read. Two near-neighbours added at Gate 4 and verified first-hand: Commission Regulation (EU) No 493/2012 (EUR-Lex full text — element-level, three battery categories, confidential, measurement not mandated); Petzold et al., Waste Management 207:115109, 2025 (full text — mixed-CAM black-mass TEA whose feed is built from "the market shares from Melin (2018) for 2025", lab-prepared, sensitivity run on marketing factors and electricity price, never on chemistry shares).
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Dadé — same material, different unit and estimand (stream parameter over a declared frame vs three delivered samples compared to each other) and no modelled comparator there; Dadé settles the instrument presupposition favourably and makes the *sampling* presupposition load-bearing, and concedes the bare alternative formulation "what is in the black mass" as substantially prior art. vs Mohr — the opposite side of the same comparison; limb (b) codes papers like this one across a frame rather than writing another, and Mohr demonstrates the assumed composition is an explicit parametrised inventory choice. vs Donnelly — same method community and material, two samples, no frame, and the protocol an aim rather than an executed variance budget; the candidate asks for that first objective and adds a comparison the paper never raises. vs 493/2012 — the statutory object is element/compound-level input composition for three legacy categories, confidential and lawfully assumable; the candidate's primary layer (Li-ion cathode-chemistry shares) is outside its scope entirely and its publication regime excludes the rest. vs Petzold 2025 — a codable instance of the assumed side, whose assumed mixture is a dated market-share forecast; it is the thing limb (c) would compare against, not the comparison.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If a gap: every recovery-efficiency and recycled-content figure computed on the assumed composition carries an unpriced sign and magnitude of error, asymmetric across target types — a shift toward LFP removes recoverable Ni and Co from the feed as stoichiometry, shrinking element-specific denominators while the mass-based denominator holds, and a train optimised on an NMC-dominant assumption is assessed against a feed it was not designed for; plant sized on an assumed Ni-Co grade is sized on a revenue line. If no gap: the worry closes and the existing process/LCA literature gains an empirical warrant it lacks. If assumed compositions cannot be coded: the finding relocates to the literature and the actionable object becomes a reporting requirement.
Significance — audience: (i) process designers and recyclers — flowsheet, sizing and feed-blending decisions; demand demonstrated by an existing commercial characterisation practice (Eramet's 260-phase database, vendor assay material) and by Petzold et al. 2025, an industry-academic TEA that parametrises a mixed feed on a 2018 forecast and never varies chemistry shares; (ii) LCA practitioners and inventory bodies — Mohr shows the assumed composition is a changeable parametrised choice, and the 2025 Nanomaterials review lists compositional variability and excluded upstream sorting among its reviewed literature's limitations; (iii) the standards community — verified first-hand: the SHERLOCK consortium (Pure Devices, phase VISION, MEET Münster, Öko-Institut, PTB, BAM, Fraunhofer ISC, with industry black-mass suppliers) exists to define standardized quality classes and a technical specification for DIN and ISO, two national metrology/materials-testing institutes among them; (iv) regulators implementing Reg. (EU) 2023/1542 — this leg stays unverified (neither the regulation nor its calculation guidance was opened by anyone), and significance does not need it.
Significance — fecundity: Whether black-mass price formation tracks assay or nameplate, and with what lag; whether chemistry-specific LCAs should be reweighted by the arrival mixture before policy appraisal, and what that does to published route rankings; whether a composition-conditional recovery target is better behaved than a fixed mass-based one; what sampling intensity a compliance assay needs to hold a stated false-declaration rate (the method-owning community's standard next question); whether the gap runs the other way, with processes designed for contamination the stream does not carry; and whether a production-scrap-dominant feed means today's arrival distribution carries almost no information about the 2035 end-of-life window, which would make the window declaration the most consequential part of the design.
Significance — anchoring: The stoichiometric tension between mass-based recovery obligations and an LFP-shifting mix; the reported origin inversion in the feedstock (production scrap now, end-of-life vehicles from ~2035, per a Fraunhofer ISI projection with scenario ranges); the occurrence of the phrase "an unspecified mixed battery waste stream" inside a peer-reviewed LCA paper, marking the assumed-input problem as already half-seen in the modelling literature; and the live black-mass characterisation standardisation gap, now verified as a funded DIN/ISO-routed effort scoped to assay and sample preparation rather than to stream sampling.
Reason for silence: Strongest and now sourced: the question was administratively closed by fiat. Since 2012 the EU has captured input-fraction composition as a confidential per-recycler compliance return (493/2012 Art. 3(4), Annex I pt 3), at element level, for three legacy battery categories, with lawful substitution of placed-on-market composition for measurement — so no research community needed to pose it and the data that would prompt it never entered the literature. Second: a disciplinary boundary separating method (sampling theory, WCSB venue) from material (battery/chemical engineering) from assumptions (industrial ecology/LCA) from target (recycling policy); evidenced by what was opened — the one characterisation paper verified cites exactly one representativity work (a sample-preparation citation to Vanderbruggen et al. 2021) and declares no protocol, and the one standards effort scopes itself to the assay and never reaches the modelling literature. Third: a missing standard, now being built, which places the candidate at the moment the comparison becomes expressible. Supporting: a new-instrument component (automated mineralogy with large phase databases, X-ray CT, LA-ICP-MS for Li; the studies using them are 2021–2025). Adversary 2 raises a rival mechanism that would deflate rather than support the finding — the modelling community treats chemistry as a scenario parameter, not a measurand, so there was no assumed mixture to be wrong about; no source was found that notices the comparison and declines it, so the chosen mechanism remains partly inferred.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3
Strongest remaining objection: Attack 4, crosswalk identifiability, Partial from both adversaries and unrelieved by anything opened — V2's primary layer (CAM chemistry shares by mass of arriving battery) may not be measurable as declared. It has three legs. Leg (i): the instrument the record relies on, and Gy particulate theory with it, operates on sieved <500 µm post-pyrolysis black mass, and back-conversion to arriving-battery mass needs per-chemistry and per-format yield factors no opened source supplies. Leg (ii): upstream of the shredder the stream is discrete units, for which the FSE framework is not the applicable theory, and V2 never fixes which gate "arriving" names. Leg (iii, adversary 2's dissolution line): most of the modelled frame states chemistry-conditional cases rather than a mixture, and V2's frame rules provide no class for them, so the signed gap may be near-vacuous over much of the frame. The hold-off-Validated stands on leg (i), which is the only leg both adversaries reached independently; if legs (i) and (ii) fell — say a declared yield-factor crosswalk were demonstrated — leg (iii) would survive on its own and still hold the entry below Validated, since it is a defect in the question's declared design rather than an interpretation of it. Note that none of these legs is a kill: every one is reasoning unsourced to a primary text, which under this ledger's own standard caps them at Partial, and this is why the entry is Provisional and not Rejected.
Promotion requires: Fixing V2 to name the plant gate "arriving" refers to, to declare the comparison component-wise per study, and to add a frame class for chemistry-conditional studies (which would lift well-posedness toward 3/3 by closing attacks 4, 5 and 8). Of the three unverified checks that bore on novelty, post-batch verification discharges one and reframes it: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2289 DOES carry a chemistry axis on the arriving side (Annex III F.5, "The quantity of batteries from a chemistry supplied to recycling"), but Article 1(4) ties it to the recycling-efficiency classes of Annex II, where "lithium-based" is one class, so the instrument is silent within lithium-ion and the gap is a GRANULARITY gap rather than an absence of any statutory chemistry axis; what remains on that check is opening an actual filed return, the 2026-02-20 corrigendum, and the UBA, ZVEI, Eurostat and ARSO returns, none of which may yet be cited as lacking cell-chemistry data. Also discharged: Minerals Engineering 169:106924 is "Automated mineralogy as a novel approach for the compositional and textural characterization of spent lithium-ion batteries" (Vanderbruggen, Gugala, Blannin, Bachmann, Serna-Guerrero & Rudolph), a characterisation study of one black-mass lot with no variance budget, so it is Dadé's representativity referent but not a protocol source. Still open: independently confirming Prior 3 (DOI 10.1255/tosf.166, full text COULD NOT READ) and the unopened narrow-limb-(a) residue (VTT "Identification of waste LIB cell chemistry", the 2023 Chinese-language item at 42(5):2702, Zenodo 13644996). If a filed return or a review turns out to publish arrival chemistry shares at cell-chemistry resolution, or to code assumed compositions across a frame, novelty falls.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Before any plant contact, read Vanderbruggen et al. 2021 and the WCSB10 proceedings forward to settle whether a stream protocol with a variance budget already exists, and open one statutory input-fraction return; if the protocol exists, the question collapses to limbs (b) and (c), which are desk work on the literature frame.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — status is Provisional, not rejected-as-asked, so the ledger still claims this question as un-asked and there is nothing to hand to the open-questions project. This line is a recommendation for whoever maintains ledger/routed-open-problems.md, not an action taken in this run.

## Verification of the priors and the unverified checks at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Three fresh-context readers: one on Dadé et al. 2022, one on the statutory question this entry named as unverified, one on the two sampling-protocol references. **The verdict does not move — Provisional — one novelty correction lands, the hold-off-Validated leg is strengthened, and the measurement limb is left open where the entry put it.**

**The statutory check is DISCHARGED, and it corrects this entry rather than confirming it.** Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2289 does make chemistry a mandatory reporting dimension on the arriving and treated side: Annex III item F.5 is literally "The quantity of batteries from a chemistry supplied to recycling". So nobody may say that no statutory instrument touches chemistry at arrival. But Article 1(4) ties that chemistry axis to the recycling-efficiency target classes, which Annex II shows to be lead-acid, lithium-based, nickel-cadmium and others — "lithium-based" is a single atom in that scheme. The instrument is therefore silent on shares WITHIN lithium-ion (NMC against LFP against LCO against NCA against LMO), which is the resolution this candidate asks about, and its element-level numbers are output-side recovery rates per material rather than an input assay. **The gap is a granularity gap, not the absence of a statutory chemistry axis, and this entry now says so in those terms.** Two limits on the strength of that finding: no filed return was opened, only the instrument prescribing the format, so publication is established as a prescribed obligation and not as an observed publication; and the item F.5 wording was read without its surrounding clause, which is exactly what distinguishes a published figure from a calculation denominator. The 2026-02-20 corrigendum was not opened. UBA was robots-refused and the ZVEI, Eurostat and Slovenian candidates are unexamined, so none of them may be cited as lacking cell-chemistry data.

**Dadé et al. 2022 holds descriptively and contradicts any population-level use of itself.** Front matter exact as cited. Three Black Masses from different unnamed suppliers and recyclers, after "treatments such as pyrolysis, dry shredding and sieving" — a non-exhaustive list, and dry shredding specifically — with per-sample phase and cathode-type abundances in mass percent recalculated from area on polished two-dimensional sections. Corrections: the "<500 µm" figure is an Introduction-level description of Black Mass in general, not a sieve cut applied to these three samples, so it was cut on the wrong side of its clause; the paper's representativity sentence is a general methodological point attributed to its reference [9], and its own two uses are uncited and hedged to two-dimensional sectioning against density segregation and to counting statistics over three million particles — none of which claims three samples represent a feedstock population; and "high statistical analytical precision" with r² > 0.99 is within-sample counting precision and assay agreement on the same material, not sampling uncertainty, with no variance, replicate or interval on any abundance. There is no sampling frame, region, time window, field protocol, tonnage or production-year information of any kind, lithium is inferred from stoichiometry rather than measured, and graphite and plastics come from external C/S analysis which the Conclusions flag as a gap. **This strengthens leg (i) of the crosswalk objection**, which is what holds the entry off Validated: the paper supplies no mass balance, no yield and no input inventory, so its measurand cannot be inverted to arriving-battery mass shares, and it explicitly declines process modelling. No LCA comparison appears anywhere in it.

**The sampling-protocol references are not what this entry called them, and the measurement limb stays open.** Minerals Engineering 169:106924 (2021) is "Automated mineralogy as a novel approach for the compositional and textural characterization of spent lithium-ion batteries" by Vanderbruggen, Gugala, Blannin, Bachmann, Serna-Guerrero & Rudolph — a characterisation study of one 9.6 kg black-mass lot (<1 mm, after vacuum pyrolysis, crushing and sieving) at particle level on grain mounts, with no sampling-variance mathematics at all: no fundamental sampling error, no heterogeneity invariant, no nominal sample mass, and a single generic Gy (1994) citation. It is Dadé's representativity referent, but it is not a sampling-protocol source, and citing it as one misnames what it is. A cut-grammar trap in it is worth recording: "the sampling procedure was carefully designed to obtain the most homogenous sample" ends "...for this characterization study", which is specimen preparation for one analysis rather than a sampling plan. DOI 10.1255/tosf.166 is a WCSB10 item on black-mass phase characterisation — "sampling" in the title, characterisation in the deposited abstract, also post-shredding — and its full text is COULD NOT READ, so any fundamental-sampling-error content in it is formally unverified. And on the independent question: at this search depth nothing publishes a declared variance budget for whole end-of-life cells, modules or packs at a plant gate, with the closest statistical work ("Overcoming Black Mass Variability", 2025) explicitly about black mass. So the narrow form of the measurement limb — a representative-sampling protocol with a variance budget for ARRIVING batteries rather than for black mass — is NOT FOUND rather than unread, which is where this entry already put it. The error pattern to guard throughout this literature is regime substitution: post-shredding black mass cited for pre-shredding plant-gate feedstock.

Status: Rejected — Gate 4, attack 1 (Triviality) Unresolved from both adversaries, with attack 4 (Presupposition failure) Unresolved from adversary 1 as an independent fatal leg.
Domain(s): AI architecture — model internals / residual-stream geometry; method-owning neighbour: low-precision inference, kernel and numeric-format design.

Question (canonical): Across k >= 3 independently seeded pretraining runs of one fixed recipe (identical architecture, data, data order and hyperparameters; differing only in the initialisation/dropout RNG stream), at >= 2 model scales, and on a pre-declared probe corpus with per-channel magnitude defined separately for each pre-declared token-position class (sequence-initial/BOS, delimiter, ordinary content), is the IDENTITY of the residual-stream channels carrying massive activations — the specific dimension indices, not their count, layer profile or magnitude distribution — reproduced across seeds beyond a declared null, measured as per-layer Jaccard overlap of the top-m index sets with CIs, re-derived at >= 3 thresholds drawn from the source literature's own rules and scored against both a uniform index-permutation null and a statistics-matched null (the same recipe's per-channel magnitude ranking at initialisation, and a run trained on a different corpus), and is the per-channel magnitude ORDERING preserved, measured as Spearman rho on the full d_model-length per-channel magnitude vector (primary) with the union of the seeds' top-m index sets as a pre-declared sensitivity arm?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the single Gate 1 reformulation, and the version graded. V1 as intaken (recorded, not graded): same question without the token-position classes, without the named nulls, and with "the per-channel magnitude ordering" left without a common support. The reformulation pinned the statistic, the position classes and the nulls; it changed no subject matter and weakened nothing.

Alternative formulations:
(1) When you train the same model twice, do the same few "hot" dimensions light up, or different ones?
(2) Is a transformer's outlier-channel layout a predictable property of the recipe that a numeric format or kernel can be designed around in advance, or is it per-checkpoint symmetry breaking that must be re-measured for every artifact?
(3) Is the residual-stream index of a massive-activation channel a recipe-level constant, an initialisation-level constant, or a per-run lottery ticket?

Motivating gap: anomaly mining on an index that is printed but never cross-checked. The literature does print specific dimension indices (Puccetti et al. Table 4; "dimension 2533" in arXiv:2605.06611) and a 45-run multi-seed pretraining suite does exist (PolyPythias), yet nothing opened at Gate 2 computes an agreement statistic over those index sets across seeds of one recipe, and the suite holding the runs performs no per-dimension activation analysis.

Presuppositions: P1 the residual-stream basis is privileged enough for channel-index identity to be a meaningful cross-seed quantity, with the record's load-bearing corollary that "the candidate needs NO cross-run matching step" because the basis is shared — STRUCK at Gate 4 (see attack 4). P2 massive-activation channels are individuable by a pre-declared threshold rule; contested, handled by a threshold arm spanning a magnitude rule and a functional-damage rule, since the literature's rules are not commensurable. P3 k >= 3 RNG-only replicas are obtainable at a scale where the phenomenon reproduces; partly established with a measured ceiling (PolyPythias gives 10 seeds per size but only to 410M, while the audience lives at 7B+). P4 data order can be held fixed while initialisation varies; the only public suite ANALYSES 45 runs that vary initialisation and batch composition jointly, but its Table 5 also releases three 160M "only parameters" runs (and three "only data" runs) that hold the other factor fixed, unanalysed, so the condition exists at 160M and V2 needs purpose-run seeds only above that. P5 "beyond chance" has a defensible null; CONTESTED and STRUCK in part — the at-initialisation matched null, read across seeds, is itself exchangeable and so coincides with the uniform null it was meant to be more stringent than. P6 quantization/kernel engineers would act on the answer; NOT EVIDENCED by the record and not improved at Gate 4.

What would count as an answer: k >= 3 (preferably >= 5) seed replicas of one recipe at >= 2 scales with data order held by a separate RNG stream; per-layer Jaccard overlap of the top-m index sets across all seed pairs with CIs, plus Spearman rho on the full per-channel magnitude vector, each computed per token-position class and scored against both nulls at >= 3 thresholds; and a pre-declared two-sided decision rule (overlap at null means the layout is seed-contingent and no format, kernel or shared calibration may bake it in; overlap near 1 means it is recipe-determined). NOT answers: within-model cross-layer persistence of a dominant dimension; cross-family index comparisons; overlap against a uniform permutation null alone; agreement across checkpoints of one run.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 web searches and 5 fetches at Gate 2, 9 searches and 4 fetches by adversary 1, 10 searches and 4 fetches by adversary 2 — 30 distinct queries in all, full lists in batches/2026-10-21-1833/UQ-20261021-11-record.md and the two adversary files. Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 1/3
Downgraded from the record's 3/3 and 2/3. Well-posedness: V2 pins unit, statistic, thresholds, scales and a two-sided decision rule, but P5's "statistics-matched" null is not distinct from the uniform null it was meant to be more stringent than, and no multiplicity rule covers layers x token classes x thresholds x nulls x scales, so the third reportable outcome is not decidable as written. The question is under-specified, not ill-posed, so this is not a Gate 1 rejection. Significance: the consequence argument requires the engineering branch to be undecided, and both adversaries find it decided by the same symmetry that kills attack 1; P6 remains inferred, with both bearing titles unopened by all three passes.

Strongest remaining objection: the permutation-gauge triviality argument (attack 1). The verdict stands on that leg alone. The candidate's two pre-declared limbs — per-layer Jaccard of top-m index sets, and Spearman rho on the full d_model magnitude vector — have a derivable a-priori value equal to the candidate's own uniform-permutation null, for any recipe with exchangeable initialisation over residual coordinates and a coordinatewise optimiser, which the served Pythia-160M config satisfies; the only physical escape anyone named is floating-point reduction order and GEMM/tensor-parallel tiling, and a result arising that way is a measurement of the kernel, not of the recipe. The leg is reached twice independently, by adversaries that did not see each other's logs, and is anchored for this object in a source adversary 2 opened and quoted ("permutation-only alignment is symmetry-incomplete for RMSNorm models"; "coordinate names are reproducible only relative to an explicit gauge") plus a consistency check against every cross-artifact index pair the record itself prints, all non-overlapping. If that leg fell — if a non-equivariant component of real recipes were shown to produce a shared index preference — the entry would NOT become Validated: adversary 1's attack 4 (Unresolved on its own, striking P1's load-bearing "needs NO cross-run matching step" as a conflation of rotation symmetry with permutation symmetry, and collapsing P5's matched null into the uniform one) is an independent fatal leg that would survive, since it is a claim about the record's presuppositions rather than about the answer; and attacks 3, 6, 7 and 8 (Unresolved from adversary 1, Partial from adversary 2) would cap the entry at Provisional at best. Both adversaries flag that their derivations are their own and not quoted theorems, so the honest standing of this rejection is: a complete, regime-checked, twice-reproduced derivation with its governing claim sourced to an opened primary paper in the candidate's own object class, which is the strongest sourcing an exact-symmetry kill can have short of a cited theorem.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): none for V2, which is rejected. For a verifier re-testing the kill, the one load-bearing check is step (1) of either derivation — that conjugating a permutation through embedding, Q/K/V, out-projection, MLP in/out, norm gains and biases, and unembedding leaves the computed function identical for the specific normalisation and positional scheme in play — followed by reading arXiv:2305.19268, the last unopened novelty risk.

Routing: ROUTE: no — this is not an asked-but-still-open problem, so no row belongs in ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The rejection is triviality: the primary endpoint is fixed at the candidate's own null by residual-coordinate permutation equivariance, and no source opened by any of the three passes publishes the candidate's number, so it is not an answered-elsewhere rejection either. The salvageable sibling both adversaries name independently — whether a run's final massive-activation index is already determined by that run's own at-initialisation per-channel magnitude ranking, and if so how early — belongs to the lottery-ticket / early-training-dynamics line and is a fresh intake for this ledger, not a routed open problem.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Seven fresh-context checkers, each handed one claim and the source it is made of and none of them this entry's reasoning. Notes: VERIFY-gauge-2606.31963.md, VERIFY-multirun-2605.06611.md, VERIFY-quant-at-scale-2305.19268.md, VERIFY-polypythias-2503.09543.md, VERIFY-puccetti-2205.11380.md, VERIFY-gurnee-2401.12181.md, VERIFY-equivariance-counterexample.md.

THE VERDICT STANDS AND THE KILL IS RESTATED ALONG A SEAM THIS BATCH DID NOT DRAW. The triviality argument has two halves and they have different evidential standing. Half A, that a decoder-only transformer is equivariant under a relabelling of residual coordinates, is now corroborated in print: arXiv:2403.00986v3 asserts it with algebra for a LayerNorm encoder, a single shared permutation and its transpose carried along the residual path with the norm weights permuted with it, though unnumbered, unproved and citing Stoica et al. 2024 for the norm handling. So the derivation is corroborated rather than cited to a theorem, and it must be stated as an ALGEBRAIC identity, not a bitwise one: reduction order over the hidden dimension is itself index-dependent and is examined by nobody, here or in the literature read. Half B, that exchangeable initialisation plus an elementwise optimiser puts the expected top-m overlap at the candidate's own uniform null, survived the attempt to break it only because NOBODY HAS LOOKED. No paper reports index recurrence across independently initialised runs of one recipe, and no paper reports the contrary either: every source that prints an index trains one seed per recipe, and the one fifty-run multi-seed suite measures no activations. Half B also predicts a MEAN, so a single shared index would not refute it. That is this rejection's one real vulnerability, recorded as such: an entire kill resting on an expectation nobody has measured, in a metric defined once at k = 10 and never evaluated across runs. arXiv:2511.01023 is named as the unopened item most likely to settle it.

THE LAST NOVELTY RISK IS DISCHARGED. arXiv:2305.19268 was read in full. It is the strongest demonstration that outlier dimensions follow from pre-training optimization rather than scale, by ablating four optimization factors and counting outliers per variant at 410M and 6B - and it never asks the candidate's question: the seed is not varied (the word never appears), each configuration is trained once, no index list is printed, and no overlap, intersection or rank correlation across runs is computed. It also takes no position on whether a channel layout can be shared, its own pipeline being calibration-free one-shot PTQ with vector-wise scales. Its Appendix B.3 observation that "the *same* dimension" recurs "across 20 random samples from the C4 validation set" is within-model across-INPUT and is not a partial answer; its outlier-count evidence belongs to 410M/6B, not to the 52B headline. Novelty Medium therefore stands with the entry's own named risk cleared rather than outstanding.

P4 IS STRONGER THAN THIS ENTRY SAID. PolyPythias is confirmed to contain no per-dimension or per-channel activation analysis of any kind, with none of the relevant vocabulary occurring in the full text, and "Outliers" in its title is confirmed to mean outlier RUNS under an explicit two-SD across-seed criterion on last-checkpoint accuracy. But its Table 5 releases three 160M "only parameters" runs and three "only data" runs, so a data-order-fixed condition does exist unanalysed at 160M; all 45 ANALYSED runs move both factors together, and footnote 3 must travel with any use of "data order", since batch composition is not a reordering. The 410M multi-seed ceiling stands, and Table 4's parameter statistics are not activation measurements.

CORRECTIONS TO CARRY. (i) The gauge paper (arXiv:2606.31963, sole author John Sweeney, v1 2026-06-30) is real and both quoted strings are verbatim, but both are ABSTRACT sentences: string 1 follows "Thus" from the premise that RMSNorm charts WITH GENERIC PER-CHANNEL GAIN have a signed-permutation gauge, and string 2 is the closing slogan scoped to "index-level interpretability claims" (served as "indexlevel", extraction damage). It DEFINES top-k overlap by activation magnitude at k = 10 in Appendix H and prints no value under that name; its Table 8 k = 10 counts are measured on gauge-transformed copies of ONE model. Its Table 4 "cross-seed" pairs are FINE-TUNING seeds off a shared base, not independent initialisations, and its permutation-recovery figures (91.1 +/- 8.7 transport-via-base against 60.3 +/- 32.6 endpoint) must carry that spread. Its only independent-initialisation measurement is "about 50%" sign mismatch on one 10M-parameter, 4-layer, d = 256 pair, in running prose, with Table 7 barriers 1.68 / 0.66 / 0.42 behind it and the percentages the author's own arithmetic; the author himself calls that row a small-scale sanity check. So it supports a GAUGE-RELATIVE claim about coordinate naming and is SILENT on how much two production-scale from-scratch runs share at the index level. Proposition 4.1 denies a canonical transport from function-level information; it is not a measurement. (ii) arXiv:2605.06611 has no section titled "5.2 Multi-run Consistency" - it is the "Multi-run Consistency" paragraph inside section 5.2 Experimental Results - and the two figures recorded above are both Dimension Disparity, not one of each; dimension 2533 belongs to a single pretrained Llama-2-7B while the four seeds are 152M from-scratch runs, and section 4.1's Kendall tau (mean 0.32, within one Llama-2-7B layer) is not a cross-seed index check. (iii) Puccetti's Table 4 sits in Appendix A under "The outliers identified for each model used in the paper" and prints bert-base-uncased 308/381 and multiberts-seed-1 218/674 verbatim; its thresholds are 2 SD for RoBERTa and 3 SD for BERT rather than a 2-3 SD band, and the five-fold damage condition is stated on MNLI specifically. Its three BERT-medium runs "started from the same initialization but were fed different data according to the tokenization schemes", and with one multiBERTs seed and a single aggregated row for those three the cross-run statistic was never computable from that design - a granularity gap for that family rather than an absence of runs. The paper nowhere notes the question, so it is SILENT, and its silence must not be cited as the field flagging the gap. (iv) Gurnee: cite Sec 4.1, carry the authors' own "no principled threshold" hedge wherever the 0.5 is quoted, and do not read the 1-5% as seed-to-seed variability; the design is confirmed as five models per architecture of one recipe differing in random seed, the paper's own term is "initialization universality", it frames the result as a BOUND on similarity under larger changes, and index plays no role in its matching. (v) arXiv:2307.12941 is Brown, Vyas and Bansal (2023-07-24), a real published opposite finding over per-layer neurons in vision CNNs and a ViT with an unstated run count; its privileged-basis finding is compatible with, and presupposed by, a permutation-only symmetry.

WHAT NOTHING MOVED. The absence at the centre of the entry held against all seven checks: no source opened by any of the three batch passes or by this one publishes a cross-seed massive-activation index overlap for one recipe, and the contrary measurement is equally absent.
