ID: UQ-20261021-12
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional — no fatal objection survives judging, but Disguise is incomplete and the record's own nominated load-bearing leg is dead by verified algebra.
Domain(s): AI architecture — post-training and reward modelling (target field: reward-model training, preference-data curation, RLHF/RLAIF pipeline design, RM benchmarking). Neighbours searched in their own vocabularies: paired-comparison statistics/psychometrics, econometrics (incidental parameters), metrology, learning-to-rank/metasearch, generalizability theory, RL advantage design.

Question (canonical): In reward models trained by the standard pairwise (Bradley-Terry) objective — whose likelihood depends only on reward differences within a prompt's comparison set, leaving the fitted reward identified only up to an additive function of the prompt — (i) what share of the variance in the scalar reward is that per-prompt offset, with CIs, for >= 3 released pairwise-trained reward models on >= 2 preference corpora, with the panel declared; (ii) is the between-prompt component reproducible across k re-fits with different seeds and permuted prompt order, or seed-contingent; and (iii) for each named shipped practice whose decision rule genuinely spans prompts, what is the decision-flip rate when the score is centred within prompt, computed under that practice's own stated decision rule, with a CI?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation (V1 presumed every named practice states a numeric threshold; two do not). Gate 5 narrows limb (iii) further, from "each named practice that compares or thresholds reward across prompts" to each such practice whose rule is not shift-invariant — see the strike list under Adversarial log.

Alternative formulations:
1. Is a reward model's number a utility you can compare between two different questions, or only within one?
2. Does the reward scale have an origin, or only an interval structure per prompt, and what has treating it as absolute done to concrete decisions?

Motivating gap (source method: presupposition inversion): The pairwise logistic likelihood is invariant to adding any function of the prompt to every response in that prompt's comparison set, so the fitted reward is identified only up to a per-prompt additive term, while some shipped practice reads the scalar as an absolute quality score across prompts. STRUCK AT GATE 5, clause (a): the record claimed the per-prompt form "was never written down in either literature" because the candidate's own field restated the constant as item-independent (Sun/Shen/Ton Prop. 24, "for a constant C does not depends on i" [served text, grammar as served]). Both adversaries independently falsified this from a primary source they opened — DPO (arXiv:2305.18290) Section 5.1 Definition 1 defines reward equivalence as "r(x, y) - r'(x, y) = f(x) for some function f", attaches Lemmas 1-2, and calls it "a well-known under-specification issue with the Plackett-Luce family of models". Reward Collapse (arXiv:2305.17608) Theorem 1 likewise writes "a function c(x) depending on x". What survives is narrower and is the real gap: the per-prompt term is written down, proved irrelevant to the KL-regularised policy optimum, and never measured or audited for cross-prompt uses.

Presuppositions:
P1 — Frame restricted to objectives invariant to per-prompt shifts (pairwise/BT); absolute-rating regression RMs and scale-pinning regularisers excluded or reported separately. ESTABLISHED analytically, and now confirmed in the field's own vocabulary (DPO Def. 1). LIVE CAVEAT, unverified in all three runs: ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1, one of the RMs used by the opened cross-prompt practice, is believed to be multi-objective absolute-rating regression plus gating, hence not purely shift-invariant.
P2 — Some shipped practice compares reward across prompts in a way the offset can change. STATUS REWRITTEN AT GATE 5. Of the four practices named: cross-prompt best-of-n allocation (AdaBoN, arXiv:2505.12050v3) and margin-based budget routing (Landesberg, arXiv:2603.12520 App. C) are EVIDENCED BUT SHIFT-INVARIANT, so they cannot flip; un-centred advantage computation is DROPPED (DPO Section 3 reports prior works normalise "such that Ex,y~D [r_phi(x, y)] = 0 for all x", and Lemma 2 covers the idealised optimum); report-card averaging remains UNEVIDENCED. One non-invariant practice is now evidenced, by adversary 2 and not by the record: RLHF Book ch. 10 presents global top-K selection over the pooled set ("Alternatively, we can select the top \(K\) prompt-completion pairs from the entire set") with no comparability discussion and no per-prompt normalisation — though it states no numeric cutoff and leaves the RM's training objective unspecified, so P1 compliance of that instrument is not established.
P3 — Within-prompt centring is estimable (>= 2 scored responses per prompt). True of standard corpora; stated as a frame restriction.
P4 — The decomposition is of the instrument's output, not of any true human utility.
P5 — "Unidentified by the loss" does not mean "arbitrary in the fitted model": a shared trunk may learn a systematic prompt offset. CONTESTED, and limb (ii) is the test. Neither adversary dented this.
P6 — Someone would act. Partly evidenced; see Significance — audience.

What would count as an answer: (i) a between-/within-prompt variance decomposition with CIs for >= 3 released pairwise-trained RMs on >= 2 preference corpora, with the panel declared (prompt set, responses per prompt, response-generating policy) — a ratio, hence invariant to affine rescaling of a model's whole reward; (ii) a re-fit of one architecture with k seeds and permuted prompt order, reporting whether the between-prompt component is stable (reproducible = learned difficulty signal; seed-contingent = noise in an unidentified direction); (iii) for each non-invariant cross-prompt practice, the decision-flip rate under within-prompt centring at that practice's own stated rule, with a CI. A CLEAN NEGATIVE COUNTS. NOT answers: within-prompt pairwise accuracy; reward-hacking results; calibration against human ratings; a theoretical restatement of BT identifiability with no decision-flip measurement.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries and 13 fetches across three runs — 11 + 5 at Gate 2, then 9 + 4 per adversary, both adversaries spending all 9 on Disguise in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try; no search or fetch was refused. Full lists in batches/2026-10-21-1833/UQ-20261021-12-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: "are reward model scores comparable across prompts" (own field, own words, the mandatory obvious-title query) → RM-evaluation papers only, no paper on cross-prompt comparability of the scalar; "variance decomposition reward model scores between-prompt within-prompt share of variance" → surfaced the closest hit of all three runs, Landesberg arXiv:2603.12520; the mandatory already-computed-quantity query ("normalizing reward model scores within prompt changes which responses selected... subtract prompt mean") → RM-bias papers only, none measuring a flip rate under per-prompt centring; DPO equivalence-class query (run independently by both adversaries) → arXiv:2305.18290, the premise-is-published hit; practitioner-vocabulary per-prompt-z-score query → RLHF Book ch. 10, the first source for the filtering limb; learning-to-rank "scale calibration" / metasearch "score normalization" queries → a mature structural neighbour surfaced BY TITLE ONLY and never opened in any of the three batch runs, OPENED AT VERIFICATION, where the exemplar turns out to be arXiv:2211.01494 (Bai et al., CIKM 2023) rather than the arXiv:2105.04651 the record named; ICC/psychometrics query → arXiv:2608.23641 "How much of a measured AI preference is the model, and how much is the instrument?", not opened in any batch run and OPENED AT VERIFICATION (see the verification block: it decomposes a self-report welfare battery, not a reward model or judge, and measures neither of the other two limbs).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
PRIOR 1 — Landesberg, "When LLM Judge Scores Look Good but Best-of-N Decisions Fail", arXiv:2603.12520. Read full text (chars 0-100,000 of 101,821) at Gate 2 and re-opened by adversary 2. Unit = prompt x candidate; endpoint = recovery of achievable selection gain and top-1 accuracy; comparator = random floor and oracle ceiling; estimand = fraction of selection gain recovered. NUMBER NAMED AND LOCATED: Table 3, caption "Variance decomposition of judge and oracle scores into between-context and within-context components (prompt is the context in this dataset)", rows "Between-context variance (prompt-level)" 74% (Judge) / 81% (Oracle) and "Within-context variance (candidate-level)" 26% / 19%; denominator = total variance of that score over the prompt x candidate panel. Instrument = GPT-5 absolute-rubric 0-100 judge, explicitly not a reward model, "no additional Bradley-Terry refit".
PRIOR 2 — Sun, Shen & Ton, "Rethinking Bradley-Terry Models in Preference-Based Reward Modeling", arXiv:2411.04991v1. Read full text at Gate 2 and by both adversaries. Unit = a preference pair; endpoint = golden-reward gain under best-of-N (N=500), order consistency, truncated KL risk; comparator = BT vs classification objectives, and same-prompt vs cross-prompt annotation; estimand = whether BT is a necessary objective choice.
PRIOR 3 — Raman, Asi & Kale, "AdaBoN: Adaptive Best-of-N Alignment", arXiv:2505.12050v3. Read full text at Gate 2 and by adversary 1. Unit = a batch of K=5 prompts at budget BK; endpoint = batch win rate vs uniform; comparator = uniform allocation at equal budget; estimand = P(adaptive beats uniform). RMs: RM-Mistral-7B, FsfairX-LLaMA3-RM-v0.1, ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1.
Supporting negative in the method-owning field: Fang et al., "Recent advances in the Bradley-Terry Model", arXiv:2601.14727v2 — a review, so nothing is attributed to it as a finding; it pins the indeterminacy globally with 1^T u = 0 "provided that H_n(E) is connected" and discusses decomposing the graph into disjoint subgraphs without addressing per-subgraph offsets.

Novelty — how this differs from each: Prior 1 is the only source printing a number of limb (i)'s shape, and that number belongs to an origin-fixed rubric judge, where a large between-prompt share is a property of an IDENTIFIED scale rather than of an unidentified nuisance; adversary 2 verified first-hand that the paper prints no reward-model variance share anywhere and never touches BT identifiability, shift invariance or per-prompt centring, and that its oracle is a pre-normalized reference score, never stated to be a BT reward model. It measures neither limb (ii) nor limb (iii), and its App. C routing result ("Margin-based routing captures almost none of the available gain (headroom ~92-101%)"; "random allocation is essentially as good as margin-only routing") is measured on a rubric judge's margins, so it motivates the candidate without being evidence about the candidate's instrument. Prior 2 asserts item-INDEPENDENCE, i.e. the opposite of a per-prompt shift, and prints no variance share or flip rate (verification adds that its Proposition 24 is a one-sided INEQUALITY s_i >= r_i - C conditional on the data coming from the BT model, not an identification up to a constant, and that the paper is silent on per-prompt versus global while its own C is a functional of the comparison pool); the residual leak the record flagged is CLOSED by both adversaries — its "cross-prompt" arm means annotating pairs drawn from different prompts, endpoint BoN golden-reward gain, with the finding "cross-prompt comparisons outperform same-prompt comparisons" and its MAGNITUDE NEVER PRINTED (figures only, described qualitatively), so by the published-is-not-performed rule it is not a known for limb (i) — but it does retire the record's fecundity line about deliberately collecting cross-prompt anchor comparisons, which it proposes, theorises and tests. Prior 3 is the candidate's target rather than its answer, and Gate 5 now finds it a target that cannot flip (see below). Where the record could not name a number for its own quantity it says so: no source NAMES a between-/within-prompt variance share for a pairwise-trained reward model. What the sources actually do is DEFINE the per-prompt term (DPO Def. 1), BOUND it (Reward Collapse Thm 1, c(x)), and MEASURE it on a different instrument (Landesberg, Table 3).

Novelty confidence: Medium, and narrowed. It holds for limbs (i) and (ii), which no opened source measures in any of the three runs. It does NOT extend to the premise: the per-prompt indeterminacy is a published, named result in the candidate's own field, so the identifiability observation may not be counted as part of this entry's novelty claim. Not High: the neighbour is close on the quantity's shape and on the decision critique, the cross-prompt practice the candidate would audit is itself published, and the learning-to-rank/metasearch per-query score-normalization literature — the structural analogue in the field that owns the method — was surfaced by title in three separate runs and opened in none of them; verification opened it, found neither limb measured there either, and found the premise exclusion confirmed a second time in that field's own words.

Significance — consequence: If the between-prompt share is large and seed-contingent, decisions taken on raw cross-prompt reward are partly reading a quantity the objective never pinned, and the fix is cheap and specific (centre per prompt, or pin the scale with cross-prompt anchor comparisons). If it is large but reproducible and monotone in a declared difficulty proxy, the finding inverts: the offset is a free, already-trained difficulty estimator and cross-prompt practice is licensed. If the share is small or flip rates are negligible at the practices' own rules, the question closes with a licence.
Significance — audience: (a) preference-data curation teams doing global top-K selection over a pooled set — EVIDENCED, from a source adversary 2 opened, and now the only named audience whose rule the offset can actually change; (b) adaptive-inference, allocation and routing authors — EVIDENCED as practice but REMOVED as audience, since their rules are shift-invariant and AdaBoN's authors chose win rate as their metric precisely "because the scalar outputs of RMs are often only meaningful comparatively"; (c) RL pipeline authors deciding whether to centre advantages — DROPPED, the canonical recipe already zeroes the per-prompt mean; (d) RM-benchmark maintainers — inferential only, and they already score within prompt, where the offset is invisible by construction. Audience (a) is real; the list the record gave was padded.
Significance — fecundity: Does the between-prompt component predict prompt difficulty, annotator disagreement, or the onset of reward over-optimisation? Does it explain part of RM-ensemble disagreement, and does it transfer to process reward models and verifiers, where cross-step comparisons are routine? How large a panel makes a flip rate of the observed size detectable? The cross-prompt-anchor-collection line is retired (already done in Prior 2).
Significance — anchoring: reward over-optimisation; the RM-benchmark-to-downstream generalisation gap; the "scalar reward is underspecified" strand in alignment theory; incidental parameters in econometrics; scale identifiability and anchor-item equating in psychometrics; per-query score calibration in learning-to-rank.

Reason for silence: The record's mechanism is STRUCK (see Motivating gap). The surviving mechanism, reconstructed and evidenced by adversary 2, is disciplinary attention rather than absence: the fact was written down and then retired for the uses the field cares about — Lemma 2 licenses ignoring f(x) for policy optimisation, the canonical recipe zeroes the per-prompt mean in the RL stage, and RM evaluation culture scores within prompt, where the offset cannot be seen. What was never audited is the cross-prompt side uses, which are engineering choices published without an identifiability check. Gate 4's own rule says a failed silence mechanism returns the novelty finding for inspection, which is one reason this entry is not Validated.

Dissolution | It dissolves into the injunction "then do not compare across prompts". | Limb (ii) points both ways and is not available from the invariance statement: a reproducible offset makes the injunction wrong and the offset useful; a seed-contingent one makes it right and the flip rate says what it cost. | A1 Partial (the canonical question dissolves in its decision-relevant limb); A2 Resolved.

GRADE CORRECTIONS AT GATE 5, stated so the mechanical rule is not applied to a mis-graded row. Adversary 1 returned Unresolved on attacks 1 and 4, which would be fatal. I verified its load-bearing arithmetic independently and it is CORRECT: under r → r + c_i, AdaBoN's KDE-estimated expected-max curve translates rigidly (Scott's-rule bandwidth depends on the sample sd, not its mean), so every marginal gain V_{i,a+1} - V_{i,a} is unchanged, the greedy path and final allocation are identical, and the batch win rate is unchanged because the sum of offsets cancels on both allocations; I reproduced this numerically to 4e-15. So the record's own nominated standing leg is dead and that finding stands. Both fatal grades nonetheless fall, on two grounds. First, scope: each rests on the further claim that no non-invariant practice is evidenced, and adversary 2 falsified that from a primary source it opened and quoted. Second, the LEDGER's own three-way definition: the candidate response adversary 1 graded Unresolved on attack 4 is described in its own row as plausible but unsourced ("such practice plausibly exists... but no source was opened"), which is Partial by definition, not Unresolved; and its attack-1 Unresolved is explicitly limb-scoped, conceding in the same row that limbs (i) and (ii) are genuinely unmeasured, so it does not establish that the question is answerable in a page. Adversary 1's Landesberg leg is weaker again: it did not open App. C and marked the leg as resting on the record's description; adversary 2 opened the paper and confirmed the App. C text but not the margin's within- or cross-prompt structure, so that leg is unverified in either direction. Hence no fatal Unresolved survives and the entry is not Rejected; the non-fatal Unresolveds on attacks 6 and 7, the Partial Disguise, and the two unopened leads cap it at Provisional.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 3/3 on V2 as narrowed: all three limbs name the evidence that would settle them, the share is a ratio and so comparable across models, the panel dependence is declared, and presuppositions are enumerated at their true evidential status. Limb (iii) is determinate rather than ill-posed on the invariant practices — its answer there is exactly 0 — but the practice list must be filtered for shift-invariance before the limb is posed, which is the narrowing recorded above. Strongest remaining objection: The verdict stands on adversary 1's shift-invariance result, which I verified independently — both cross-prompt practices the record actually evidenced decide on within-prompt differences, so limb (iii)'s flip rate is identically zero on each, including the leg the record itself nominated as the one it would stand on if the others fell, which means the question's entire decision relevance now rests on one rule (global top-K preference-data selection) that an adversary found and the record did not, in a practitioner reference that states no numeric cutoff and does not specify its reward model's training objective. If that leg fell — if some evidenced practice were shown to compare reward LEVELS across prompts — the next-strongest objection is the falsified premise: the per-prompt indeterminacy is published in the candidate's own field as DPO Definition 1 and called "a well-known under-specification issue", which strikes clause (a) of the Motivating gap and the record's whole Reason-for-silence mechanism and, under Gate 4's attack-7 rule, returns the novelty finding to Gate 2. Behind both, and surviving independently of either, is the Disguise gap: the learning-to-rank and metasearch per-query score-normalization literature was surfaced by title in all three runs and opened in none, and arXiv:2608.23641 ("How much of a measured AI preference is the model, and how much is the instrument?") was never opened.
Promotion requires: all four of — opening the learning-to-rank/metasearch per-query score-normalization neighbour and arXiv:2608.23641 and finding neither measures the limbs; re-posing limb (iii) only on cross-prompt rules checked for shift-invariance BEFORE they are named, with at least one P1-compliant BT-trained RM named for the global top-K filtering practice; striking the "never written down" clause and citing DPO Def. 1 and Lemmas 1-2 as the field's own statement of the premise; and demoting limb (i) to a panel-declared descriptive preliminary with limb (ii) carrying the novelty claim.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Seven fresh-context checkers, each handed one claim and its source and none of them this entry's reasoning. Notes: VERIFY-dpo-definition-1.md, VERIFY-landesberg-2603.12520.md, VERIFY-ltr-per-query-normalisation.md, VERIFY-preference-instrument-2608.23641.md, VERIFY-rlhf-book-global-topk.md, VERIFY-adabon-shift-invariance.md, VERIFY-sun-shen-ton-2411.04991.md.

STATUS UNCHANGED AT PROVISIONAL, with two of the four promotion conditions now discharged and the entry's central absence confirmed twice over.

CONDITION 1 IS DISCHARGED, IN THE ENTRY'S FAVOUR ON THE QUANTITY. Both named leads were opened. (a) The learning-to-rank and metasearch per-query score-normalization literature measures neither limb: no source there names a between- or within-QUERY variance share for a pairwise-trained ranker, and none prints a cross-query decision-flip rate under within-query centring, so the entry's closing absence now extends to a second field. The exemplar is a factual correction: arXiv:2211.01494 (Bai et al., CIKM 2023), not arXiv:2105.04651, and the neighbour is best described as stating the invariance and then PINNING the scale to an absolute regression target instead of centring, with NDCG and LogLoss as its endpoints. That field also states the premise in its own words - "the SoftmaxCE loss is translation-invariant", and PairwiseLogistic "mainly considers the pairwise score differences" (Sec. 3) - so the Gate 5 exclusion of the identifiability observation from the novelty claim is confirmed in TWO literatures, not one. (b) arXiv:2608.23641 is real and open: v1, single author Jason Hung, cs.AI, 2026-08-24, title verbatim. It PRINTS a variance decomposition (Table 5, captioned over five models, five instruments, 15 outcomes and five replicates: Outcome 0.1883 = 17.9% between; "Residual, across replicates" 0.3279 = 31.1% within; instrument effect 0.1963 = 18.6%), reports instrument dependence 0.876 with a leave-one-out range 0.777-0.934 against a null 95th percentile of 0.365, and a generalisability coefficient of 0.348 at five instruments by five replicates. But its instrument is NEITHER a pairwise reward model NOR an absolute-rating judge: it fits Thurstonian utilities to a model's own forced choices, Spearman-Karber switch points on intensity ramps and a log exchange rate, with the model under test as respondent about its own welfare, and no reward model or LLM judge appears in the paper at all. On the two other deciding questions it is plainly absent: the words seed, refit and re-fit do not occur, and flip and reversal do not occur, its centring being applied within each model-instrument slab at a stated cost of three zeroed variance components rather than a flip rate. So it is a METHODOLOGICAL ANALOGUE and is silent in the candidate's regime: it may be cited for method and must not be cited as evidence about reward-model score structure.

THE SHIFT-INVARIANCE LEG HOLDS, WITH ONE MANDATORY RESTATEMENT. AdaBoN's only cross-prompt operation is the greedy argmax over within-prompt marginal gains of the Eq. 2 expected-maximum curve in Algorithm 1; no threshold, pooled ranking, shared cutoff or between-prompt reward-level comparison appears in the rule or in either reported metric, and the KDE bandwidth is itself shift-invariant, so a per-prompt constant translates the whole curve rigidly and changes nothing. The restatement: this invariance is ENTAILED by the paper's stated rule, not REPORTED by it - the paper never states, proves or tests it, and its Proposition 3.1 proves concavity and monotonicity, a different property. The checker reproduced the derivation independently. So the entry's leg is a derivation on a published rule, which is legitimate, and the entry must say "the paper's rule implies" rather than "the paper shows".

THE SURVIVING AUDIENCE SURVIVES, WITH A LOCATOR FIX. The RLHF Book's global top-K rule is confirmed cross-prompt: the quoted string is verbatim, and the reading is forced by R_flat's stated length M x N, by the single global argsort in equation (8) and by a worked example that draws twice from one prompt and never from another. Corrections: the chapter is 9 under current numbering, not 10 (the entry's URL still resolves); the sentence should be cited together with equations (7), (8) and (15), since alone it is ambiguous about what "the entire set" ranges over; and the sentence the entry presents as adjacent is not. Two absences may be used as absences only: the passage states no numeric cutoff and names no reward-model objective, and it nowhere discusses cross-prompt comparability - silence, not a denial, and not the chapter identifying a gap.

THE PREMISE AND THE NEAREST NUMBER. DPO holds as recorded: Section 5.1 Definition 1, the equivalence in the form the entry quotes, Lemmas 1 and 2 attached with Lemma 2 giving the same optimal policy "under the constrained RL problem", the "well-known under-specification issue with the Plackett-Luce family of models" string verbatim, and the Section 3 normalisation sentence transcribed correctly. Three tightenings: attribute the "well-known" sentence to Lemma 1 and the Plackett-Luce family with the paper's own citation rather than to the indeterminacy at large; flag the Section 3 joint-expectation wording as the source's own incoherence; and state the absence in DEFINES / PROVES / NORMALISES-AWAY vocabulary, because not measuring f(x) is DPO's design rather than its oversight - the cancellation is why the method works. Landesberg holds on every string and figure: identity, the Table 3 caption verbatim, all six numbers, the Table 12 reference-label row and both Appendix C strings. Two scope points the entry must keep: the 74% and 81% belong to an absolute 0-100 rubric judge and to an upstream normalized reference scalar used as given, with the paper's only Bradley-Terry sentence declining to refit such a model, so neither may be read as a BT reward model's between-prompt share; and the gap in the quantity is a DEFINITION gap, since the paper prints the share and never prints its denominator or estimator.

SUN, SHEN AND TON: THE PUBLISHED-IS-NOT-PERFORMED FINDING IS CERTIFIED, WITH ONE REGION OUTSTANDING. The string "cross-prompt comparisons outperform same-prompt comparisons" is verbatim twice, in the Figure 4 caption and in Section 6.3, both unhedged and uncited, and in everything read the result is Figures 4, 5 and 6 only, with no table, percentage, win rate or axis value printed and Figure 6's relation given as "highly correlated" with no coefficient. Appendices D, E and F were not read, so the absence is certified for the main text and Appendices A-C only. Its measured endpoint is golden-reward improvement under best-of-N at N = 500; order consistency and truncated KL risk are DEFINED and BOUNDED, never measured. Its preference labels are simulated by open-source golden reward models, and its reward models are small heads on LLM embeddings rather than fine-tuned LLM reward models. Proposition 10/25 is not a variance share: expected absolute differences, on assumed oracle utilities, with the variance an assumption input.

WHAT WOULD STILL PROMOTE THIS ENTRY: conditions 2 and 4 of the Promotion line, unchanged - a P1-compliant Bradley-Terry-trained reward model named for the global top-K filtering practice, and limb (i) demoted to a panel-declared descriptive preliminary with limb (ii) carrying the novelty claim. Condition 3 was already satisfied at Gate 5 and condition 1 is satisfied by this pass.

Domain(s): AI architecture — the human-preference data layer (reward modelling, model-comparison adjudication). Method home: survey/official statistics (intra-interviewer correlation, Kish design effect, effective sample size). Neighbours: educational measurement (G-theory, MFRM), clinical measurement (ICC). Source method: cross-field transplant.
Question (canonical): On a pre-declared frame F of preference corpora carrying stable per-annotator identifiers (or a declared proxy: vendor, shift, guideline revision), under a pre-declared cross-classified Bradley-Terry/logistic model of the pairwise outcome with crossed random effects for annotator, annotator-cluster and item plus a linear-probability companion — (a) what are the variance components and the implied annotator-level and cluster-level intraclass correlations, on both declared scales, with CIs; (b) what Kish design effect and effective sample size N_eff do they imply when computed with the UNEQUAL cluster sizes actually present rather than an equal-cluster formula, with sensitivity to the cluster definition; and (c) holding total labels fixed and varying the number of distinct annotators, does reward-model accuracy (or a declared RLHF endpoint) track N_eff rather than N, against pre-registered bands (NULL Deff <= 1.1 / MODEST 1.1-2 / MATERIAL > 2)? [This is V1, the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V0 asked the same thing without declaring the ICC scale, the frame, the model or the bands, and for a binary outcome the latent-logistic and linear-probability ICCs are different numbers from one fit. Full V0 text and the reformulation note: batches/2026-10-21-1833/UQ-20261021-13-record.md.]
Alternative formulations: (1) If a dataset says it holds a million preference labels, how many independent judgments is that really? (2) Treat the annotator as the interviewer and the preference label as the interview: what is the intra-interviewer correlation and the interviewer design effect of a preference corpus?
Motivating gap: Official statistics will not publish a survey estimate without an intra-interviewer correlation and a design effect converting nominal N to N_eff; preference corpora are quoted in raw label counts and reward-model sample-size reasoning treats labels as independent. The quantity is defined and illustrated in the candidate's own field (Kopteva & Hlynianyi-Zhuk) and never estimated — "published is not performed". Deff is driven by cluster size as much as by rho, so the number, not the direction, is the question.
Presuppositions: P1 per-annotator ids (or proxy) recoverable for a non-trivial frame — PARTLY ESTABLISHED (PRISM, PluriHarms per arXiv:2606.27578 opened; Arena shipped an anonymized user id in the July 2023 release, adversary 1 S2 opened; HelpSteer2's paper never states that annotator identifiers are released, printing only annotators per sample, so it supports the objection in neither direction; OASST's export format does carry a per-rater id on each rating event while its documented released label is an average with a reviewer count, a granularity gap verification could not close; SHP publishes no rater identifier at all). P2 a crossed or partially crossed design exists — PARTLY ESTABLISHED, CONTESTED (PluriHarms 100 x 150 implies crossing; no rater-by-item cross-tabulation printed). What would count as an answer: (i) variance components (annotator, cluster, item, residual) from a crossed or partially crossed preference-labelling design on >= 2 corpora in F or one purpose-collected replication, with CIs on both declared scales; (ii) rho and Kish Deff on the clustering actually present, with sensitivity to the cluster definition, and N_eff reported beside the advertised N; (iii) the fixed-total-labels / varying-annotator-count arm reporting a reward-model endpoint against N versus N_eff. Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If rho is non-negligible the arithmetic is unforgiving, because Deff is driven by cluster size: at production cluster sizes a corpus advertised as a million pairs would be worth a small fraction of that in independent judgments, every independence-assuming interval on a reward-model evaluation would be too narrow, and the marginal label from an existing annotator would be worth less than one from a new annotator — inverting the cheapest way to buy data, from depth to breadth, and putting an N_eff beside the N on dataset cards. If rho is near zero, Deff near 1 and the subsampling arm flat, the field's unstated independence assumption is licensed for the first time: a publishable null. The asymmetry is the point. The live discount is that this consequence is stated at cluster sizes no corpus in F exhibits (see Strongest remaining objection).
Significance — audience: (1) teams buying annotation, who take the labels-per-annotator versus number-of-annotators decision today — the one documented decision here, and adversary 1's opened source (Liu et al., arXiv:2502.06387) names annotator heterogeneity and the unclear link between annotation quality and downstream performance as the standing open challenges; (2) leaderboard operators publishing intervals on preference votes, where voter-level clustering is a correction none applies, though at ~2.5 votes per user it would barely move Arena intervals unless heavy users dominate; (3) reward-model researchers reporting accuracy with independence-assuming intervals (demand inferred); (4) dataset publishers deciding whether to ship annotator ids, a zero-cost decision this question prices. Discounted honestly: the pluralistic-alignment community — PEBS's own venue — reads the same variance as structure to preserve, so for them the answer reframes rather than decides.
Significance — fecundity: whether Deff explains the reward-model data-scaling plateau; whether vendor-level clusters align with identifiable reward directions (a bridge to reward-hacking work); whether annotator-stratified purchasing beats random purchasing at fixed budget; whether direct-alignment pipelines (DPO/GRPO) inherit the same deflation; whether guideline revisions act as period effects across a time series of corpora; whether a judge-facet partition and an annotator-facet partition compose into a total pipeline design effect.
Significance — anchoring: the reward-model data-scaling plateau; the leaderboard-interval dispute (Chatbot Arena arXiv:2403.04132 and the "Leaderboard Illusion" exchange); the pluralistic-alignment debate over whether annotator variance is error or signal; Kopteva & Hlynianyi-Zhuk's explicitly unmade measurement; Kish's deff and the official-statistics convention of never publishing an estimate without one. Strongest remaining objection: The feasible frame and the significant regime do not overlap (adversary 2, attack 6, reinforced by adversary 1's attack 4(ii)). rho is estimable only where stable annotator ids exist, and there per-annotator cluster sizes run from about 2.5 (Arena) through 6 (PRISM, after its own filter) to 150 (PluriHarms), where even a material rho yields a Deff inside or barely above the pre-registered NULL/MODEST bands; every consequence the significance case rests on lives at cluster sizes two orders larger, and limb (b)'s own instruction to use the clustering actually present forbids the extrapolation. WHICH LEG THIS STANDS ON: the cluster-size mismatch alone, sourced to the record's own established P1/P5 facts plus PRIOR 3's printed illustration and adversary 1's arithmetic on the opened Arena release counts. It does NOT rest on the two unsourced technical legs — adversary 1's position-order identification argument and adversary 2's Kish-estimand-specificity argument — and would survive unaffected if both of those fell; conversely, if the cluster-size leg fell (F extended to a production-scale corpus), the position-order argument would remain as the next-strongest objection, since it attacks limb (a)'s estimand rather than its feasibility.
Promotion requires: extend F to include at least one corpus with production-scale per-annotator cluster sizes (or add a purpose-collected arm at n >= 500 labels per annotator) so limb (b) is answered in the regime its consequence claim lives in; pre-commit the primary scale and cluster definition for the bands; report the annotator-by-item component alongside the annotator intercept with the outcome coding declared, so a near-zero intercept ICC under randomized presentation cannot be read as a null on heterogeneity (noting Gate 1's single reformulation is already spent, so this must be a reporting specification inside V1's declared model, not a V2); and close the three read holes — arXiv:2608.15980, arXiv:2502.06387's appendices, and independent confirmation of arXiv:2606.27578 and arXiv:2604.11581 via publisher or abs routes.

STATUS UNCHANGED AT PROVISIONAL. The novelty cap holds for the reason given, one read hole is closed, one adversary's stated ground for a Partial is discharged, and the cluster-size facts the strongest objection rests on need four corrections without changing their direction.

THE NOVELTY CAP IS CONFIRMED, AND IT IS A DEFINITION-AND-ILLUSTRATION PRECEDENT. Every string this entry attributes to arXiv:2607.16195 is present and verbatim, and every characterisation of what the paper does holds: rho assumed and swept at 0, 0.1 and 0.2; the pilot measuring stylistic features of model outputs; no causal test; rater-level data proprietary. Two cautions from the checker. The paper does NOT explicitly recommend the variance-components estimation - implicit at most, with no explicit recommendation found at a full-PDF read level - so this entry must not credit it with proposing the measurement. And Deff = 20.9 with N_eff about 48 is computed from stipulated inputs on a hypothetical workforce of 1,000, so it must never be read as a characterisation of real annotator clustering. Gate 2's abstract-only read could not have reached Section 4.1 or 7.3, and none of the four illustrative-or-not-measured formulations is in the abstract.

THE READ HOLE IS CLOSED AND ONE PARTIAL LOSES ITS STATED GROUND. arXiv:2608.15980 was logged COULD NOT READ in the batch; it reads in full at the arXiv HTML rendering, and only the PDF route failed, which is a standing route lesson rather than a fact about the paper. On the deciding question it answers plainly in the negative: the word "variance" does not occur anywhere in it, nor intraclass, ICC, variance component, design effect, effective sample, random effect, mixed-effects, kappa or Krippendorff, so the pool-level variance share adversary 1 held open cannot be the reason for a Partial - the thing to be excluded is not in the source. What the paper does print sharpens this entry rather than closing it: item-level majority divergence and winner-reversal rates between an expert and a crowd pool (23.6% and 9.2% on MultiPref; 30.5% and 8.5% on MT-Bench), a per-model win-rate shift from -2.1 to +2.8 percentage points with SD 1.9pp across six models, an adjacent-pair difference at SD 2.6pp, a raw 50.1% disagreement between the two experts on a single MultiPref item, and P(at least one model displaced) rising from 0.28 at six models to 1.00 at thirty. It has no fixed-labels, varying-annotator-count arm and trains no reward model. And it corroborates this entry's access leg in its own words: of the four corpora it examined, two "cannot support this analysis at all" "purely because they discarded annotator identity".

THE CLUSTER-SIZE LEG: FOUR CORRECTIONS, SAME DIRECTION. (i) Arena's anonymized user id is confirmed present and printed twice, "33K cleaned conversations" is printed, and the user figure is printed as 13,383 in the card's statistics table while the card's own prose defines it as "13K unique IP addresses"; no per-user vote-count distribution is published anywhere, so about 2.5 votes per user is arithmetic on two printed totals over an IP-shaped denominator and must be carried as such, not as a dataset statistic. (ii) PRISM is stronger than recorded: it links each rating to a pseudonymous participant id and its Figure 1 PRINTS "Conversations / participant 5.7 +/- 1.0", restated in Section 4.2.1 as about six conversations with four models, over 1,500 participants and 8,011 conversations - so at least one corpus in the frame publishes the quantity, at more than twice Arena's derived value, with ratings per participant finer still and unlocated. (iii) HelpSteer2 cannot support the objection in either direction: it engaged approximately 1,000 US-based annotators through a vendor and prints only annotators per sample (at least three, up to five, the three most in agreement retained, 3.41 on average) over 21,362 samples; it never states that annotator identifiers are released, and silence is neither a release nor a prohibition. The implied per-annotator figure of about 73 labels is nowhere printed. (iv) OASST's export schema does carry a per-rater user_id on every rating, ranking and score event, while the documented released label is an aggregate ("quality": value 0.416, count 3) with a reviewer count and no rater identity on the value; whether the public files populate those events is unverified, so this is a granularity gap rather than a settled absence, and it is the one fact that could extend the frame. SHP publishes no rater identifier at all, so its per-rater clusters are undefined rather than small.

PEBS: THE GAP IS REAL AND THE MISMATCH IS WORSE THAN RECORDED. A paper that publishes between-rater variance components for a per-rater calibrator's slope and offset forms no intraclass correlation, no design effect and no effective sample size - all four phrases absent - and runs no arm varying the number of annotators at fixed labels. The internal inconsistency is stronger than this entry said: 23.2 matches neither 26.2 nor 115.7 on either reading, is printed as a bare tau-hat^2 with no subscript in Appendix A rather than in Section 3.6, and is nowhere reconciled; the same residual quantity carries two different symbols in two appendices, and one of them, 23.5, is a standard deviation. There is no table in Appendix B, so any citation of the form "Appendix B, Table N" would cite something that does not exist. The scope boundary is load-bearing: Eq. (3) models a 0-100 scalar RATING, with pairwise preferences entering only upstream inside a frozen reward model, while the paper's prose calls that scalar a preference score - so 26.2 and 115.7 are calibrator-parameter variances on a rating instrument and nothing else. The paper's own M of about 4 is asserted and never derived, and it is a worst-case maximum rather than an average cluster size.

MESSING: READ LEVEL UP, FACET LIMB CLOSED. The read was better than recorded - main body plus Appendices A-D and E.1-E.2, truncated inside E.3, with G-R unread - and 43.8% of Var(theta-hat) holds as printed, including its denominator, with the operational design N=141, V=5, M=3, H=3, R=8 and an Appendix C.5 contrast of 0.8% of per-observation variance. Every facet in its Table 2 and Eq. 1 is a machine configuration or a benchmark item or category; humans enter as ground truth, a per-vote agreement baseline and a nine-rater consensus comparator, never as a modelled facet, and its Table 5 maps G-theory's rater facet onto the model. So this entry's own candidate-outside verdict is confirmed at first hand.

RESIDUALS THIS PASS DID NOT CLOSE: arXiv:2502.06387's appendices; whether the released OASST files populate the rating events that carry rater ids; and ratings-per-participant for PRISM, finer than the printed conversations-per-participant.

ID: UQ-20261021-14

Status: Rejected — failed at Gate 2 (novelty Low; disguised known, asked and substantially answered in the candidate's own field); confirmed fatal at Gate 4 by adversary 1's Unresolved on attacks 1 and 2.
Domain(s): AI architecture — likelihood evaluation of non-autoregressive (masked-diffusion) LMs. Method home: variational inference / generative-model likelihood estimation (IWAE, bidirectional Monte Carlo sandwich bounds).

Question (canonical): For the open-weight masked-diffusion language models now released at 7–8B scale, how loose is the variational bound their reported perplexities are computed from — what is the gap, in nats per token, between the published bound and an unbiased or sandwiched estimate of the model's actual log-likelihood — and does closing that gap change the diffusion-versus-autoregressive comparisons those perplexities are used to support?
Reformulation note: one Gate 1 reformulation was taken (decompose the published-bound-minus-evaluable-likelihood difference into (a) variational slack against the model's own uniform-order marginal and (b) the change of scored distribution induced by a deterministic test-time unmasking policy, each in nats/token with MC standard errors). Gate 2 was run against the canonical form above, as the rules require; the reformulation is recorded, not substituted, and it does not rescue the candidate — its residue is narrower than a question.

Alternative formulations:
- When a diffusion language model reports a perplexity, how much of that number is the model and how much is the looseness of the bound?
- Are the likelihood figures in diffusion-LM release tables comparable with the exact likelihoods of autoregressive baselines, and if not, by how much is the diffusion model being penalised?

Motivating gap: masked-diffusion LMs crossed into open weights at 7–8B in 2025 (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B) and their release tables print a bound-derived likelihood beside AR baselines whose likelihood is exact by the chain rule — a one-sided bound against an exact value, biased in a known direction by an unknown magnitude. The motivating absence was UNVERIFIED at intake (the generating pass spent no query on it). Gate 2 executed it and the absence was an artefact of not searching: the gap claim is false as of 2026-03/2026-05.

Presuppositions: P1 a shipped masked-diffusion LM defines one normalised distribution whose log-likelihood exists — contested at intake, and measured as order-dependent since (Yao 2606.00997 prints UP TO 0.49 nats/token between a left-to-right order and a target-aware oracle order on one checkpoint, in its Abstract, Introduction and Appendix A.1 rather than in Section 4.2, which prints -3.00, -3.49 and "~0.5" (corrected at verification: this is a two-point worst-case range, not a spread over six orders); Deng & Thrun, NeurIPS 2026 poster 154353, verbatim: per-order log-probability rankings "disagree on most inputs"). P2 the published perplexities are bound-derived — CONFIRMED third-party (DUEL evaluates "LLaDA-8B-Base ... with sequence length L=2048"). P3 a tighter estimator is feasible at 7–8B with usable MC error — PARTLY: an exactly-evaluable alternative is feasible at 8B (DUEL), a genuine two-sided sandwich is demonstrated only at block-model scale (TUBE: "Our empirical study is limited to BM"), and no 8B work prints standard errors. P4 the comparisons rest on the likelihood numbers — CONFIRMED (DUEL's abstract: "the MDM–autoregressive perplexity gap shrinks by up to 32% on in-domain data and 82% on zero-shot benchmarks"). P5 the AR side is exact under matched tokenisation and byte-normalisation — NOT ESTABLISHED by anything any agent opened; it contaminates the candidate's numbers and DUEL's equally, so no verdict here rests on it. P6 someone would act — CONFIRMED; four groups did within 2026.

DUEL is real and open, a primary methods paper whose exactness result is its own (Theorem 4.3); its three authors are in the order recorded, the version is v2, Table 5's subject and all nine of its figures check out, both quoted strings are verbatim and locatable, and LLaDA-8B-Base with L = 2048 is confirmed in Appendix D.1. The kill's narrowness is confirmed exactly as the entry framed it: if the rejection needs only that the ELBO scores the wrong distribution and that DUEL's numbers are lower, it is fully supported; if it needed the difference SPLIT into variational slack against the uniform-order marginal versus the change of scored distribution, it is not supported, because the paper names that distinction in prose twice without numbers ("the variational gap... can be substantial"; "Delta_ELBO may overestimate the true gap") and prints only the combined difference and a gap-closed ratio, never computing an exact likelihood under the uniform ordering - so neither component number exists anywhere. Two further limits on what may be quoted from it: perplexity only, with no log base, no stated normalisation and no dispersion, so any nats- or bits-per-token restatement is the reader's arithmetic; and the one result in which a masked-diffusion model beats an autoregressive one (36.47 against 52.11 on AG News) is Table 7's 110M BD3-LM under a ground-truth oracle over 24 block permutations with a different AR comparator, not Table 5's 8B setting, where DUEL does not reach Llama3 in any column.

TUBE: SPINE HOLDS, THREE CORRECTIONS. Identity, author order and date are right; both quoted strings are verbatim; "BM" is the paper's own abbreviation for block models; the plus-or-minus figures are standard deviations over 10 ordering subsets, stated twice; the numbers are perplexities; and no shipped 7-8B checkpoint is evaluated anywhere, LLaDA and Dream appearing only as citations. (1) The paper prints NO parameter count, so the block-model scale this entry attributes to it must be cited to Arriola et al. (2025) and labelled as external. (2) It prints endpoints and a TUBE-against-ARM gap but no sandwich WIDTH, so the 0.72-2.47 perplexity widths remain the Gate 2 agent's arithmetic, as the entry already says. (3) Both quotations must carry their second halves: string 1's continuation DEFENDS the block-model-only scope rather than conceding it, and string 2's continuation holds a "we consider" qualifier that bounds "every configuration" to its Tables 2-3. Quoting either half alone overstates the paper in opposite directions.

YAO: ONE NUMBER DEFECT, CORRECTED ABOVE. The 0.49 is the paper's own figure and is printed, but not where the entry put it and not as the quantity the entry described: it is an upper bound between a left-to-right order and a target-aware oracle (Oracle min-q) order, printed in the Abstract, the Introduction and Appendix A.1, while Section 4.2 prints -3.00, -3.49 and "~0.5". Without the oracle qualifier the entry stated a worst-case probe as an operating-condition sensitivity, which the paper's own Finding 2 contradicts. Confirmed otherwise: the single-author short form is accurate, the regime is LLaDA-2.1-mini on C4 with 1,000 examples, a 32-token prefix, a 128-token continuation and block size 32, the parameter count is not stated, and the absence of any ELBO or autoregressive baseline in that section is total - "evidence lower bound" and "variational" occur nowhere in the paper, and its FORCED-AR arm is a reveal order on the same diffusion model rather than a causal AR model.

THE ONE RESIDUAL, HELD OPEN RATHER THAN CLOSED. arXiv:2510.24088 exists, is open and is what the entry says it is, by four authors at Yonsei University; its COULD NOT READ status is now a partial read rather than a failure to identify. But the deciding question - whether it prints an ELBO-versus-exact-likelihood gap, and at what scale - must not be closed in either direction: its tables, figures and appendix bodies were never served through any route tried, and the paper itself announces an appendix on evaluating NLL on a pretrained language model. It does apply its estimator to LLaDA, a released open-weights masked-diffusion model, so the shipped-checkpoint element holds in kind while "7-8B" is not served by this source. The honest ledger cell is COULD NOT READ at the grain asked, with the partial evidence recorded; a reader with fetch quota should read its tables directly.

Domain(s): AI architecture — evaluation methodology and model-lifecycle engineering (reproducibility of results obtained on retired closed model snapshots). Neighbour vocabularies: archival science, API deprecation/behavioural breaking changes, metrology, clinical assay bridging, ML backward compatibility (negative flips / prediction churn), official-statistics series breaks, satellite sensor intercalibration, psychometric equating, FDA substantial equivalence.
Question (canonical): Over an enumerated frame of published studies that applied a since-retired commercial model snapshot and released per-item outputs plus a recoverable configuration: (a) what is the per-item agreement between the archived predecessor outputs and freshly collected outputs from the vendor-designated successor named in dated vendor documentation, under the recorded configuration, stratified by task class, with a declared distance per output type, read against the predecessor's own archived run-to-run band; and (b) under a pre-declared rule mapping each paper's own stated claim and threshold onto a re-derivable decision on the same items, with inter-rater reliability on the mapping, what share of those studies' conclusions reverse, with a confidence interval — the excluded share and exclusion reasons being part of the answer?
Reformulation note: this is R1, the single Gate 1 reformulation; the intake V0 (which named neither comparator nor unit) is in the record.
Alternative formulations: When a vendor retires a model and points you at its replacement, is the replacement a substitute for the purposes of the papers that used the original? / At what rate does carrying a result forward from a retired snapshot to its designated successor fail?
Motivating gap: Silence mapping. Retirement is dense with how-answers (deprecation calendars, successor tables, migration guides) and the exposure has been censused (arXiv:2609.04699: 42% of 8,931 paper-model mentions exposed, median 538 days to retirement), while the intake claimed nobody asks whether the prescribed migration preserves the finding. Gate 2 narrowed that gap itself: arXiv:2510.25506 re-executes five studies' artifacts on later snapshots and names model deprecation as the chief cause of reproduction failure, so the question is in print in the candidate's own field; only the candidate's estimand was absent.
Presuppositions: P1 a non-trivial set of studies released per-item outputs (binding feasibility risk; only neighbouring number found is executability, 5 of 69 OpenAI-based ICSE/ASE articles, arXiv:2510.25506 Sec. 3.1/4.1/4.2 — not per-item output release). P2 a vendor-designated successor is identifiable from dated vendor text (flagged; the OpenAI deprecations page was never opened, in the record or by either adversary). P3 configuration is recoverable (contested; failed in practice for the studies 2510.25506 attempted). P4 "conclusion reverses" is operationalisable by a pre-declared claim-mapping rule with IRR (contested; no such rule exists anywhere in the record or the adversary sweeps). P5 successor-equivalence is the question worth answering rather than output archiving or weight escrow (weakened: 2510.25506 Sec. 5.1 treats deprecated-model use as "an issue exclusive to commercial models"). P6 reproducibility-policy bodies and auditors would act. P7 predecessor run-to-run variation must be separable via a negative control (flagged in the record as unsupplied — defeated, see below).
What would count as an answer: (i) the enumerated frame with excluded share and reasons; (ii) per-item predecessor-vs-successor agreement by task class with CIs and a declared distance per output type; (iii) a conclusion-level re-derivation under the pre-declared mapping with IRR, reporting a reversal rate with a CI; (iv) the predecessor-repeat negative control. Strongest remaining objection [SUPERSEDED AT VERIFICATION — the leg below fell on regime; the surviving objection and the promotion condition are stated after it]: Limb (a) is a measured known reached by an instrument-and-corpus swap. Behind it sits the claim-mapping rule of limb (b), which exists nowhere and whose inter-rater reliability measures agreement rather than validity, and then adversary 2's Unresolved attack 7: the record conceded in print that the composite is discussed in the candidate's own field, and the mechanism it offered explains why answering is hard rather than why nobody asked.
Promotion requires: all three of — an enumerated frame showing that a non-trivial number of retired-snapshot studies released per-item outputs with a recoverable configuration, since that is the binding feasibility risk and not a presupposition that can be declared; a pre-declared claim-mapping rule with its inter-rater reliability, specified as a reporting commitment inside R1 because Gate 1's single reformulation is already spent; and a reason-for-silence mechanism that explains the ABSENCE OF ASKING rather than the difficulty of answering, since the one offered was falsified by the method-owning field having measured limb (a)'s shape in its own vocabulary.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): enumerate how many retired-snapshot studies actually released per-item outputs with a recoverable configuration, before any measurement; that count decides whether the question is answerable in the regime its consequence claim lives in.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Six fresh-context checkers, each handed one claim and its source and none of them this entry's reasoning. Notes: VERIFY-chen-zaharia-zou.md, VERIFY-sheng-lu-2608.13607.md, VERIFY-icse-repro-2510.25506.md, VERIFY-annotator-sub-2602.11898.md, VERIFY-retirement-census-2609.04699.md, VERIFY-nber-w35110.md.

VERDICT REVERSED, Rejected to Provisional, because both halves of the Gate 2 grade fell at first hand.

HALF ONE, limb (a) as a measured known. Prior A is real, open, correctly attributed and readable at both routes the entry names, so Gate 2's failure to find it was a retrieval failure and not an absence. The repeat-run control the record said no source supplies DOES exist and IS printed - "running GPT-3.5 March twice yields a disagreement rate of 2.8%" and "running GPT-3.5 June twice yields disagreement rate of 7.0%", Section 3.4 body text, each returned whole - and that much of the kill stands. But those two figures cannot carry the rejection on four counts. They are point estimates with no interval, no repeat count and no stated uncertainty, so they are not a BAND. They cover GPT-3.5 on OpinionQA alone, with nothing for GPT-4 and nothing for the other seven evaluation sets. They are measured where the paper says "We set the temperature to be 0.1 to reduce output randomness", so they are a floor under a deliberately chosen test setting rather than an operating-condition spread. And decisively, the design is "one snapshotted in March 2023 and another in June 2023" of the SAME MODEL NAME, both live and queryable - which is why both could be queried at all. There is no predecessor, no vendor-designated successor and no retirement anywhere in it, and no API identifier strings appear in either version. On how a retired predecessor stands to its designated successor the paper is SILENT, and silence is not support. Secondary corrections from the same check: the USMLE pair (27.9% GPT-3.5, 12.2% GPT-4, Section 3.7) and the happy-numbers pair (67.6% GPT-4, 77.2% GPT-3.5, Section 3.2) hold as recorded; OpinionQA's 27% is the sentence and 27.5% is a Figure 8(a) label; the LangChain per-model pair is withdrawn above; the paper's only scope-limiting sentence is in Section 2.2, not its conclusions; and claim (e) is a clean absence - no share of published conclusions reversing, in either version, the unit of analysis being the item and "mismatch" being a definition rather than an evaluation.

Leg 2 could not take over, exactly as the entry itself predicted, and verification strengthened that on a second ground. Prior B's models are "all open-weight" because "these signals require white-box access to hidden states, attention weights, and output logits", so its object of study is not computable on a commercial API snapshot and the two regimes are disjoint by construction rather than merely different. It also runs at temperature 0 with a single greedy decode and deterministic flip labels, so it has no within-version repeat-run control and structurally cannot have one: run-to-run variance is removed by fiat, not measured. Its six NFR ranges, the entry's whole quantitative content for that prior, are now marked unconfirmed: the appendix carrying them was unreachable on both the arXiv HTML and PDF routes, which is COULD NOT READ and not absence, and its main-text table of confidence and likelihood-drift values is a trap a skimming reader can mistake for flip rates. The rate is conditional on the old-model-correct subset, so reading 55.2% as a share of MATH-full inflates it by roughly one over accuracy.

HALF TWO, limb (b) as asked-but-open. This is the half that also decides the routing row, and it fails the routing test's first half on both sources, as recorded in the Routing line above. Prior C's identity and all six recorded quantities verify verbatim, with three repairs: the rounded Pan interval is in Section 4.1 and not Table 1, whose bounds are 45.585 and 55.272; Zhou's 50% to 82.35% is an observed min-max for configuration P+A4 K=1, not a 95% interval, and sits beside a Table 1 cell reading 75.2 with bounds 53.10 and 81.49; and Pan's interval rests on 15 repetitions, not 30, because a $500 cost cap cut that study short. Its "an issue exclusive to commercial models" string is exact and in Section 5.1, where it classifies which impediment is proprietary to the commercial setting and is immediately followed by "We acknowledge that authors have little control over the deprecation of models." Its deprecated models were already withdrawn when the team started, so no old-model arm was ever measured: the old side of every comparison is the original paper's printed number, and the paper calls gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 "the current model" rather than a designated successor, treating the newer version as a confound needing different prompting. arXiv:2602.11898 ("Benchmark Illusion", Yang and Wang) is real and reads in full, and three of the entry's claims about it need correcting: the ">80%" belongs to Section 5.1's education case study, not 5.2, and that section's own printed figure is 84%, computed as a max-over-min spread across the eight annotator models (0.19 to 0.35) rather than a deviation from the published 0.44; "16-66%" is an abstract and introduction formulation whose body counterpart is 16-76% across all models and 16-38% above 60% accuracy; and the quoted phrase is "Two of the eight models we tested (Gemma-3-27B and Qwen-2.5-72B)", accurate in substance. Its manipulation is cross-family annotator substitution, with API volatility cited only to Barrie, Palmer and Spirling (2024) in its literature review, so it is silent on a deprecation-driven version swap.

WHAT THE RE-GRADE RESTS ON, AND WHY NO LATE GATE 4 IS OWED. What fell is the JUDGE's Gate 2 call, not an adversary's fatal ground: both adversaries ran all eight attacks on this candidate and their statuses on attacks 1, 2 and 4 are Partial or Resolved, with the only Unresolved on attack 7 from adversary 2. Gate 4 is therefore complete at the strict standard, nothing fatal survives, and the entry is re-graded on the existing record rather than sent back for a fresh Gate 4 - the rule this ledger has applied twice before. The cap is adversary 2's Unresolved attack 7 plus well-posedness 2/3, which blocks Validated independently.

CORRECTIONS TO THE SUPPORTING FIGURES. arXiv:2609.04699's census is real and its shape survives, but the printed in-scope figure is 41.6% (3,715 of 8,931 mentions, 730-day cutoff) rather than 42%; "median 538 days" is an abstract-announced figure whose body counterpart is a MEAN of 546 days over the retired-or-scheduled subset, with no dispersion reported; and the word "exposed" must go, the paper's construct being a vendor-retirement cutoff it labels "rapidly outdated" while it re-executes nothing. arXiv:2604.07530 drops from "second census" to directional corroboration on a different endpoint. NBER w35110's two headline numbers are verbatim, correctly located and re-derivable at the authors' own rounding, but "one county-level estimate flipping" overstates what Table 2 Panel B shows - four annotator-specific estimates, three insignificant and one significantly negative, the flip being which arm clears significance rather than a conclusion reversing - and the 3.6-fold figure must travel with the paper's own 1.9 under its composite specification, with 57% carried as "as low as", the band being 57-73%.

STILL TRUE AFTER THE PASS: no source found by any pass prints a share of published conclusions reversing on migration to a vendor-designated successor, with a denominator and an interval. That absence is now the entry's novelty claim rather than a routing ground.

Domain(s): Biology — comparative/organismal physiology and metabolic ecology (respirometry). Adjacent: measurement metrology, clinical indirect calorimetry, trait-data curation. Method-owning neighbour: impossible-value/internal-consistency detection in the published record (statcheck/GRIM/SPRITE) and process-systems data reconciliation.

Question (canonical): Over a frame of published animal respirometry studies declared before any data pull that report both O2 consumption and CO2 production (or an RQ/RER computed from them) for the same individuals or same declared group, with the unit fixed in advance as one reported value-pair at the finest grain the paper prints and the feasibility window fixed in advance at RQ 0.70-1.00 with pre-declared arms at the clinical 0.67-1.30 and at taxon/state exemptions (anaerobiosis, net lipogenesis, discontinuous gas exchange with CO2 storage, aquatic carbonate buffering, non-steady state): (i) what is the infeasible share, with a CI, by taxon, respirometry mode and decade, against a dual-gas denominator that is itself uncounted; (ii) per respirometry mode, derived from that mode's own computation, which error classes an infeasible RQ can and cannot identify, and only then what bound if any it places on the reported mass-specific metabolic rate; and (iii) under pre-declared exclusion and correction rules, does the refitted interspecific allometric exponent move beyond its published confidence interval? [Operative form is V2 = R1, the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V1 and the two changes R1 makes are in the record.]
Alternative formulations: Do the published metabolic rates that comparative physiology's scaling datasets rest on fail their own internal arithmetic check, and by how much? · Treating simultaneously reported VO2 and VCO2 as a redundant pair, what is the internal-inconsistency rate of the comparative respirometry literature, and what error floor does it place on interspecific metabolic-rate comparison?

Motivating gap: RQ is bounded by substrate stoichiometry (~0.70 fat to 1.00 carbohydrate), so a printed pair outside the window is a failed redundancy check. Comparative databases and the 2/3-vs-3/4 exponent dispute pool exactly these primary measurements, and no audit found computes the corpus's infeasible-RQ share or propagates it into pooled values. Carried forward from Gate 1: the intake's mechanism was inverted. In flow-through mode both rates are linear in STP-corrected flow, so a multiplicative flow error cancels in the ratio to first order; the check is blind to the dominant shared term and sensitive to per-channel span/zero and water-vapour asymmetry. That derivation is the generator's own algebra and all three adversaries declined to source it in either direction. PARTLY SOURCED AT VERIFICATION, and it narrows rather than falls: Withers (2001) is identified as Australian Journal of Zoology 49(4):445-461, doi 10.1071/ZO00057, and only its abstract is served. That abstract moves AGAINST the derivation's premise — it describes configurations in which one flow is measured and the other calculated from gas composition, notes that flow differs in parts of the excurrent circuit, and states that the equations vary with the configuration. So the cancellation is CONDITIONAL on a shared-flow, degree-one structure and is EXACT where that structure holds, rather than being a general property of flow-through respirometry. Limb (ii)'s demotion survives for the shared-flow case and does not generalise.

Presuppositions: (1) a non-trivial number of papers print both channels for the same animals — CONTESTED, the denominator is part of the answer (PRIOR 1's 202-paper aquatic frame never mentions VCO2/RQ); (2) aerobic catabolism confines steady-state RQ to ~0.70-1.00 — established for the three substrate classes, contested in the arms' taxa/states, and the institutional window is wider (AARC 0.67-1.3); (3) an infeasible RQ in the pre-declared strata indicates measurement error — CONTESTED, and the single most damaged presupposition after Gate 4 (see adversary 1, S1); (4) an RQ deviation bounds the VO2 error — PARTLY FALSE AS STATED, conceded inverted for shared terms, limb (ii) rewritten to ask identifiability first; (5) mode/calibration/humidity classifiable from published method text — PARTLY CONTESTED, and the only presupposition with direct quantitative evidence, pointing against the candidate (PRIOR 1 reporting prevalences 71%/12%/48% under Equipment and 15%/19% under Measurement conditions — re-sited at verification — and "more than 30%" silent on background respiration; denominator 202 papers except the MMR items at n = 123); (6) the interspecific fit is sensitive to a minority of bad points — CONTESTED; the bias path runs through mass-dependence of the error, predicted and untested.

What would count as an answer: a pre-registered audit with frame, window, unit and arms fixed before extraction, reporting (i) the infeasible share with a CI by taxon, mode and decade, with the dual-gas denominator and the unclassifiable share reported separately; (ii) a per-mode derivation of which error classes the check identifies, then any bound it places, carrying sources' own uncertainties; (iii) exponents refitted under pre-declared rules against the published interval. A near-zero share with exponents unmoved answers it negatively and is usable: an explicit measurement-error floor and a licence to pool, which nobody can currently issue.

Strongest remaining objection: the boundary coincidence (adversary 3, attack 4, leg b). The candidate's pre-declared lower bound of 0.70 IS the expected true value of the state that defines the corpus limb (iii) must refit: Genoud et al. 2018's SELECT criteria require postabsorptive, resting, thermoneutral measurement, in the very curation whose exponent (0.729 +/- 0.010 S.E., Table 1) carries the entry's one sourced stake. THE QUOTATION THAT CARRIED THIS LEG IS WITHDRAWN AS A MISQUOTATION BY CUT. The string "a respiratory quotient compatible with a postabsorptive state (i.e. approaching 0.7)" is verbatim, but the entry cut both ends: the governing clause is "measurements done on artiodactyls fasted for variable durations have shown that", the predicate is "can be reached well before starvation", and the content is attributed to Silver et al. 1969. The whole sentence is about how LONG a fast is needed in artiodactyls, not a statement that the corpus's modal true RQ sits at 0.7 — and verification confirms RQ is NOT a SELECT inclusion criterion at all (SELECT = E = 1 or 2 across thermoneutrality, rest, postabsorptive state, resting phase, adult and non-reproductive), with the abbreviation "RQ" occurring nowhere in the paper and no empirical RQ distribution printed anywhere in it. What survives is the textbook physiology, not this source: a corpus selected for postabsorptive rest does have an expected RQ near 0.70, so the boundary coincidence stands as a physiological argument while losing its citation. A one-sided bound placed at the modal true value makes the sub-0.70 share a function of the field's measurement noise about the bound rather than of any error in a reported rate, and no exemption arm can exempt the corpus's central operating state. THE LEGS, and which the objection stands on: it stands on this one. If it fell, two further legs would survive independently — adversary 1's Walsberg & Hoffman 2005 finding (doves at RER 0.58-0.69 and three kangaroo rats at 0.65-0.70) — WHICH FALLS AT VERIFICATION AS A SCOPE TRANSFER OF EXACTLY THE KIND THIS LEDGER KEEPS MAKING. The doves had rice ad libitum up to trial start and ran at RER 1.01-1.20 for the first four hours, so they were not postabsorptive; trials began between 13:00 and 15:00, the active phase for a diurnal species, so they were not at rest in the required sense; and thermoneutrality was never established at the 25 °C used. All three are states the candidate's declared strata exclude, so the finding does not damage P3 inside the candidate's core regime, and the entry's claim that it was "the better survivor" because it rests on printed primary numbers in the candidate's own taxa does not hold: the numbers are printed and primary, and the regime is wrong. Two further corrections to the same leg: the 0.4% is an ETHANOL-BURN CALIBRATION figure, not an accuracy claim for the animal trials, and "the extensive series of assumptions" attaches to the direct-versus-indirect calorimetry discrepancies rather than to the low RERs. And adversary 2's leg A, that the exponent datasets are O2-only and the screenable subset too small to move +/-0.01, which adversary 2 itself refused to score as a kill for want of an opened source. Neither survivor holds after verification: leg A was never scored for want of an opened source, and the Walsberg & Hoffman leg fails on regime. So the strongest objection now rests on the boundary coincidence as PHYSIOLOGY alone, with no opened source establishing it for this corpus — weaker than when it was graded, and still enough for the Partial it was graded at, since the physiological point itself is not in doubt.
VULNERABILITY OF THIS OBJECTION, recorded as the standing rule requires because the objection rests on something nobody has measured.
