## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Six fresh-context readers, briefed from the full citations this entry carries rather than from labels in the adversarial logs. No errors. **Verdict unchanged: Provisional.** The pass did not move the verdict and it moved almost everything under it: the strongest objection lost both of the legs it was resting on, and the entry's own promotion conditions had to be rewritten because three of the four were misframed.

**Genoud, Isler & Martin — the quotation is verbatim and the claim built on it is not.** *Biological Reviews* 93:404-438 (2018), doi 10.1111/brv.12350, opened in full. The string "a respiratory quotient compatible with a postabsorptive state (i.e. approaching 0.7)" is exactly in the paper. The entry cut both ends of its sentence. The governing clause is "measurements done on artiodactyls fasted for variable durations have shown that"; the predicate is "can be reached well before starvation"; the content is attributed to **Silver et al. 1969**. The sentence is about how long a fast must last in artiodactyls, not about where the corpus's modal RQ sits. This is the clipped-quotation defect, checked on both sides of the cut as the standing rule requires. Two further facts: **RQ is not a SELECT inclusion criterion** (SELECT is E = 1 or 2 across thermoneutrality, rest, postabsorptive state, resting phase, adult and non-reproductive), the abbreviation "RQ" occurs nowhere in the 35 pages, and **no empirical RQ distribution is printed anywhere in it**. Table 1's SELECT beta is confirmed at **0.729 ± 0.010** as the exponent of body mass, N = 549 species, mlO2/h against g — but the printed t-test is **against 0**, not against 3/4, so "intervals claimed to exclude both 3/4 and 2/3" was the record's reading, not the table's test. The paper's 1739 values / 817 species / 946 publications counts are real but span two sections, so they are not one reported triple.

**Walsberg & Hoffman 2005 — the named "better survivor" is itself a scope transfer.** This is the finding the entry singled out as the leg that would survive if the boundary coincidence fell, "because it rests on printed numbers from an opened primary source in the candidate's own taxa". The numbers are printed and primary. The regime fails on three counts, each from the paper's own methods: the doves had **rice ad libitum up to trial start** and ran at **RER 1.01-1.20 for the first four hours**, so they were not postabsorptive; trials began **between 13:00 and 15:00**, the active phase for a diurnal species; and **thermoneutrality was never established** at the 25 °C used. Every one of those is a state the candidate's declared strata exclude. Two corrections travel with it: the **0.4%** is an ethanol-burn calibration figure, not an accuracy claim for the animal trials, and "the extensive series of assumptions" attaches to the direct-versus-indirect calorimetry discrepancies, not to the low RERs. The authors offer **no mechanism** for a sub-0.70 RER and say anaerobic heat production would **exacerbate** their low cases — which is why promotion condition (c), written to require an arm set surviving "Walsberg & Hoffman 2005's mechanisms", was asking for something the source does not supply.

**The strongest objection, after both corrections.** It stands at Partial, where it was graded, but on narrower ground: the boundary coincidence survives as **physiology** — a corpus selected for postabsorptive rest does have an expected RQ near 0.70 — and no longer as a sourced claim about Genoud's curation. Adversary 2's leg A was never scored for want of an opened source and still is not. So the objection is weaker than when it was graded and the entry is not stronger, because Well-posedness 2/3 bars Validated on its own and the Medium-novelty cap is untouched.

**Price & Mager 2020 — found, fully cited, still unread, and probably not the paper the entry needs.** Price, E. R., & Mager, E. M. (2020), "Respiratory quotient: Effects of fatty acid composition", *Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A* 333(9):613-618, doi **10.1002/jez.2422**, PMID 33063463. The entry's record that "no publisher or DOI route surfaced" is **false** — both exist. It is COULD NOT READ for a different reason: closed access, with no open copy indexed. And its metadata (fish, DHA, stearic acid, polyunsaturated fatty acids) points to a fuel-molecule stoichiometry study rather than the cross-taxon compilation of published RQ values the entry needed it to be. The regime is **open**: no identified source prints the empirical spread about 0.70 for this corpus, so ground (1) of the vulnerability is harder to settle than the record implied.

**PRIOR 1 (Killen et al. 2021) — confirmed, with three corrections.** doi 10.1242/jeb.242522, read in full. It never mentions RQ, RER or VCO2; **CO2 occurs exactly once, in criterion 20's Description, and not about scrubbing** — the record's gloss was wrong. The denominator is 202 papers throughout **except the MMR items, where n = 123**. The **15% and 19%** belong to Measurement conditions, not Equipment, where the record placed them. The background-respiration figure is the paper's own "more than 30%". The granularity-gap reading holds: every number it prints is a reporting prevalence and none is an infeasible-RQ share. This also discharges half of the entry's own promotion condition (d), since PRIOR 1 has now been read by an agent other than the generator.

**Withers (2001) — identified, abstract only, and it narrows the derivation rather than falling it.** *Australian Journal of Zoology* 49(4):445-461, doi 10.1071/ZO00057. Only the abstract is served, and it moves against the derivation's premise: it describes configurations where one flow is measured and the other calculated from gas composition, notes that flow differs in parts of the excurrent circuit, and states that the equations vary with the configuration. So the first-order cancellation is **conditional on a shared-flow, degree-one structure, and exact where that structure holds** — not a general property of flow-through respirometry. Limb (ii)'s demotion survives for the shared-flow case and does not generalise. The derivation remains the generator's own algebra, now with its scope stated.

Domain(s): Biology — enzymology and quantitative biochemistry; adjacent: systems biology (enzyme-constrained models), kinetic-parameter curation.
Question (canonical): For a panel of enzymes purified by standard published routes and declared before any measurement, (a) what is the distribution of the catalytically active fraction of protein in each preparation — stoichiometric active-site titration or single-turnover burst amplitude against total protein measured by the same assay the source papers used, endpoint declared in advance — with per-enzyme and per-route variance components; and (b) what is the maximum share of the published between-report log10 kcat variance for those same enzymes that an active-fraction distribution of the measured magnitude could generate, under a declared exchangeability assumption, with the residual assigned to assay conditions after covariate adjustment?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation. V1 asked for an attribution of historical kcat spread to active fraction; the historical preparations no longer exist and were never titrated, so V1's estimand was unidentified. V2 is a bound conditional on a declared assumption. Full V1 text in ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0033/UQ-20261022-02-record.md.
Alternative formulations: When biochemistry writes kcat = Vmax/[E], how often is [E] the concentration of enzyme that actually works, and how much of the kcat literature's disagreement could that substitution account for? / Is the active fraction of a purified preparation a reproducible property of its purification route, and how large a share of the spread in published turnover numbers could its distribution generate?
Motivating gap: kcat is computed by dividing Vmax by a bulk total-protein concentration, presupposing that essentially every counted molecule is catalytically competent. Active-site titration exists because that is not guaranteed, and is rarely performed. The mechanism is named and then dropped without measurement in the candidate's own reproducibility literature (Prior 1) and in the kapp-vs-kcat literature (Prior 2), so the gap is ACKNOWLEDGED-BUT-UNQUANTIFIED rather than unnoticed. Newly consequential because kcat compilations are now training labels for ML predictors and parameters in enzyme-constrained genome-scale models.
Presuppositions: P1 kcat routinely computed from total not active enzyme (established as convention, unaudited here). P2 a competent/incompetent partition exists — CONTESTED; Prior 4 measures a continuous per-molecule activity distribution with no zero-activity class, so the partition is operational. P3 a stoichiometric titrant or burst assay exists for the panel's enzymes — a severe, non-random selection constraint (Prior 3 is a whole paper delivering one titrant for one family). P4 route-level reproducibility of active fraction — CONTESTED, unestimated anywhere. P5 published kcat spread not already fully explained by assay conditions — CONTESTED; no published attribution either way. P6 total-protein assays not themselves biased in a way that mimics the deficit — requires an orthogonal arm. P7 Michaelis-Menten adequate — assumed. P8 panel preparations exchangeable with the source papers' — CONTESTED, untestable from the panel; declared. P9 (added by adversary #1, absent from the record) inactive protein is kinetically inert, without which kcat_obs = f·kcat_true fails and Km moves. P10 (added by adversary #3, absent from the record, and the fatal one) the total-protein assay used by each source paper is recoverable from that paper.
What would count as an answer: a prospective panel with enzyme list, routes, titrant, titration endpoint and total-protein method declared in advance, reporting (a) the measured active-fraction distribution with per-enzyme and per-route variance components, each total-protein value cross-checked against one orthogonal quantitation; and (b) a variance budget giving the maximum share such a distribution could generate in the published between-report log10 kcat spread for the same enzymes, conditional on the declared exchangeability assumption, residual assigned to assay conditions. A fraction near 1 with small spread is an equally decisive answer.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Every load-bearing source was re-read by a fresh-context agent that did not write this entry, each briefed from the full citation this entry carries rather than from a label in an adversarial log. Six readers, no errors. **Verdict unchanged: Rejected.** The fatal leg was confirmed to the character; four corrections landed underneath it, and one non-fatal Unresolved fell.

**The fatal leg holds, and is now exact.** Halling, Fleming, Gurung, Straathof, Kastritis, Kettner, Rohwer, Schnell and Swainston, "An empirical analysis of enzyme function reporting for experimental reproducibility", *Biophysical Chemistry* 242 (2018) 22-27, was opened in full. Table 3 prints **45** in the column headed "Found in papers (%)" against the row **"No enzyme concentration"**. The denominator is **100 papers** — the 100 most recent at September 2017 (earliest 2008), drawn from the ten journals most represented in SABIO-RK. No uncertainty is carried with the 45, and the by-enzyme-family rate is not measured anywhere in the paper, which is the transfer limit adversary #3 declared for itself and verification confirms rather than closes.

**One supporting clause was a sign inversion.** The entry's attack-4 row added that "the protein-measurement method itself [was] flagged as a deficiency in Papers 2-4". The source says the opposite, verbatim: *"Since papers 2-4 do make clear the way protein concentration has been measured, their experiments are reproducible in this respect."* Withdrawn. The fatal row now rests on the 45% alone, which carries it.

**Two further Halling quotations were mis-sited, both in the candidate's favour.** (i) "STRENDA DB requires enzyme concentration (and also a statement on how this was measured)" is a **Table 1 cell commenting on Paper 8**, not the paper's prose statement of the norm. (ii) The active-site reach is a **reviewer's** point — "A reviewer has pointed out that the IUBMB Recommendations ... imply" — not the paper's own requirement. Since the reviewer's remark is the only place active-site concentration is reached for at all, re-siting it **widens** the granularity gap between the published standard and this candidate's grain rather than narrowing it. (iii) The audit's denominator is 100 papers over ten journals; "across 111 papers" aggregated it with a separate qualitative 11-paper two-journal set that prints no percentages. Corrected in three places.

**Adversary #1's non-fatal Unresolved (attack 5) falls.** The Gate 2 record and adversary #1 both asserted that limb (b)'s denominator — the between-report log10 kcat spread for one enzyme — has no published value. It does. Kroll, Engqvist, Heckmann and Lercher 2023, "Turnover number predictions for kinetically uncharacterized enzymes using machine and deep learning", *Nature Communications* 14:4139, print in the Discussion a mean deviation of **0.75 log10 units (5.7-fold)** between two kcat measurements of the **same enzyme-reaction pair** reported by different studies, and **0.52 log10 units (3.3-fold)** against the geometric mean of the remaining measurements. Limb (b) is therefore anchorable, and attack 5 drops from Unresolved to Partial.

**That miss is this batch's instance of the rule it was written for.** TurNuP was not an unsearched paper: **this entry's own adversary #3 surfaced it at search N4 and never opened it.** A prior nobody opened is not prior art, and a denominator nobody looked for is not an absence. It cost the entry a false Unresolved and gave the Gate 2 record a false negative; neither changed the verdict, which is luck, not method.

**Prior 3 (Sweeney et al., 10.1039/d0sc05380e) was misread in four ways, all of which make it a worse neighbour, not a better one.** The paper prints **no ratios**: it prints paired concentrations, so the 1.02 and 1.16 that exceed 1 are this ledger's own arithmetic (AOA 93/91, EPA 116/100). Its denominator is **activity-derived** — "Determined by declared activity measurements" — not vendor-listed nominal concentration and not total protein, so it is further from this candidate's measurand than the record said. Its four rows are **three alpha-amylases plus one yeast alpha-glucosidase**, not four members of one family. And the authors describe both >1 rows as "agreement was excellent", so the entry's use of them as an impossibility proof is the ledger's reading, not theirs.

**Bender et al. 1966** is real and correctly attributed: *J Am Chem Soc* **88:5890-5913** (the entry printed 5890 alone). It remains COULD NOT READ at every route tried, so the Disguise gap it holds open is UNVERIFIED, not Unresolved — it caps and does not reject — and "by active-site titration" stays an unverified gloss on its title.

**What verification did not settle.** The 100-paper source list and per-paper breakdown behind Table 3 were not served, so the rate inside the P3-constrained subset of titratable mechanistic families — the one number that could convert the general 45% into a rate inside this candidate's population, or fall it back to Partial — is still unmeasured by anyone. That remains the single unopened source most likely to overturn this rejection, exactly as the entry recorded before verification ran.

Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Validated blocked by Well-posedness 2/3 (Gate 5 requires 3/3) and by Partial statuses on attacks 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8; nothing Unresolved anywhere, so not Rejected. Verdict UNCHANGED at verification. The core gap STRENGTHENED (no replicate-level object exists anywhere in the benchmark as released) while the BROAD form of it DIED (Reeb/Rost 2020 asked it in print in March 2020); counts corrected, one sub-claim downgraded from a negative to an UNREAD.
Domain(s): Biology — protein science / functional genomics (variant-effect measurement and prediction). Method transplanted from psychometrics (Spearman 1904 correction for attenuation).
Question (canonical): On a pinned release of the ProteinGym substitution DMS benchmark (217 assays, ~2.7M missense variants), restricted to assays whose distributed raw pre-preprocessing files carry >=2 independently selected replicate measurements per variant — with the eligible share itself reported as a primary result — and under estimators declared before any data pull (primary: variant-level between-replicate reliability on the merged-score scale, Spearman-Brown stepped up to the k replicates merged into the released DMS_score; sensitivity arms: a rank-reliability analogue, an Enrich2/DiMSum per-variant-SE reliability, and a reliability-heteroscedasticity-stratified arm): (a) what is each eligible assay's own test-retest reliability, with bootstrap CIs; (b) when each published zero-shot predictor-assay rank correlation is disattenuated by that reliability, what share of the apparent headroom to perfect prediction (1 - rho_observed) is assay measurement error rather than model error, with its uncertainty; and (c) does the published ranking of predictors change, reported as Kendall tau between published and disattenuated orderings plus a count of pairwise reversals in a pre-declared top-k?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation. V1 (as intaken) left eligibility, estimator and the meaning of "share of headroom" to the analyst; V2 pins the frame, declares the estimator plus three arms, and makes the eligible share a reported result rather than an assumption. No change of subject.
Alternative formulations:
- A1: How good can a variant-effect predictor look against an assay that disagrees with itself, and where is the benchmark's real ceiling once the assay's own noise is removed?
- A2: Is the variant-effect-predictor leaderboard a ranking of models, or partly a ranking of which assays happen to have been measured precisely?
Motivating gap: These benchmarks score predictors by rank correlation against DMS values treated as the criterion, while measurement theory has held since Spearman (1904) that correlation with a noisy criterion is attenuated by the square root of the criterion's reliability. ProteinGym's evaluated per-assay files carry only mutant / mutated_sequence / DMS_score / DMS_score_bin (README read at full text, 26,106 bytes, via raw.githubusercontent.com); the replicate-bearing layer ships separately as substitutions_raw_DMS.zip (500MB) and is documented only as provenance, so it sits outside every scoring script's path. The only uncertainty ProteinGym publishes is a between-assay bootstrap SE on aggregates — a different quantity in the slot a reliability estimate would occupy.
Presuppositions:
1. A usable share of the 217 assays released independent replicate-level measurements — CONTESTED and decisive; UNVERIFIED by anything anyone opened. Adversary #2's first-hand parse of reference_files/DMS_substitutions.csv (217 rows, 46 columns — corrected at verification from 47, read in full) found no replicate column anywhere in the schema, exactly one ingested phenotype column per assay, and — CORRECTED AT VERIFICATION — **96 of 217** ingested columns named as aggregates or fits, not 74. The 74 is the **INDEL benchmark's assay count**, carried into this entry as if it were a substitution-benchmark tally; the two numbers are unrelated. The 217 assay rows draw on **94 distinct ingested column names**. That is the INGESTED layer, not an inventory of the raw files, and replicates_mean_brightness positively implies per-replicate columns beside it in at least some of them — a granularity finding, not a demonstration of absence. TWO FURTHER VERIFICATION RESULTS, pulling in opposite directions. The core gap STRENGTHENS: ProteinGym ships one scalar per variant — the evaluated files carry mutant, mutated_sequence, DMS_score and DMS_score_bin and nothing else — and there is **no replicate-level object anywhere in the benchmark as released** (the string "replicate" occurs twice in the whole repository, neither occurrence a field), so the reliability of the 217 assays is not auditable from the benchmark at all. And sub-claim (d) DOWNGRADES from a negative finding to an UNREAD: substitutions_raw_DMS.zip was refused at both routes tried, so what the raw layer contains is COULD NOT READ, not absent. Under the standing rule an unrun check caps and never rejects.
2. Replicates are independent at the level that actually attenuates the predictor-assay correlation (independent selections, not technical re-reads) — CONTESTED; per-assay, unresolved by anything opened. V2 makes it an eligibility criterion rather than a premise.
3. Disattenuation is applicable to rank correlations under a pre-declared estimator — partly established only; no canonical rank estimator exists.
4. Benchmark rankings are consequential enough that re-ranking changes behaviour — contested, not verified here.
5. Benchmark assay values are not derived from or filtered by predictor outputs — established by construction.
6. Reliability is roughly homogeneous across an assay's variant range, or heteroscedasticity is modelled — CONTESTED and unverified; hence the stratified arm.
What would count as an answer: Per-assay reliability coefficients with bootstrap CIs; disattenuated predictor-assay correlations under the pre-declared primary and its three arms; the share of residual variance attributable to assay error, with uncertainty; and the re-ranked leaderboard with Kendall tau plus top-k pairwise reversals. Uniformly high reliability answers it the other way (ceiling near 1, model error dominates, published ranking stands, pursuit of the last tenth of Spearman licensed). A small eligible share answers a different but reportable question: how much of a flagship benchmark's criterion layer is auditable at all.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Adversary #2's within-assay invariance result. Correcting by a per-assay reliability multiplies EVERY predictor's correlation against assay a by the same positive constant 1/sqrt(r_a), so within-assay ordering is exactly preserved, and limb (b) is then a deterministic function of limb (a) via share = (rho/sqrt(r) - rho)/(1 - rho). This holds for any estimator of the form rho/g(r_a) with g>0 and predictor-independent, which covers the declared primary and two of the three arms; only the heteroscedasticity-stratified arm escapes. VERIFIED AT VERIFICATION, and sharpened in three ways. The within-assay invariance is an EXACT identity, and sqrt(r_a) is not load-bearing in it: it holds for EVERY positive predictor-independent divisor, so no choice of reliability estimator rescues limb (c) at the single-assay level. The share expression is exact arithmetic on a denominator of 1 - rho, and it is UNBOUNDED ABOVE once rho > sqrt(r), so the reported "share of headroom that is measurement error" can exceed 1 — a well-posedness consequence the entry had not recorded and which belongs with the 2/3. And the invariance DOES NOT SURVIVE AGGREGATION: a two-assay counterexample with r = 1.00 against r = 0.64 reorders the cross-assay average, which is what ProteinGym's published ranking actually is. So limb (c)'s payoff is dead within an assay and genuinely open across assays, exactly as the entry's own vulnerability note predicted. It removes limb (c)'s advertised payoff at the single-assay level and defeats the model-developer audience claim outright. The objection rests on several legs and the Provisional standing is set by THIS one: it is exact, needs no retrieval, and cannot be defeated by opening a file. If it fell, two legs would survive independently — the unverified eligible share (adversary #2's parse of the 46-column curation table: no replicate field, and 96 of 217 ingested columns named as aggregates or fits — both figures corrected at verification, the 74 having been the INDEL benchmark's assay count) and the three-way identification problem (within-assay sampling noise, condition-specific true variance, model error; adversary #3, grounded in between-experiment rho of 0.21 to 0.93 and P1's median 0.54). VULNERABILITY OF THIS OBJECTION, recorded because nobody has measured it: the invariance result is an ALGEBRAIC identity in the estimator, not a bitwise or empirical finding, and it is silent on the quantity ProteinGym's published ranking actually is — a cross-assay average, whose re-weighting by 1/sqrt(r_a) has no a-priori ordering and which the objecting adversary itself concedes is a genuine open empirical question. No reported result anywhere bears on it; it follows from the correction's design. The single unopened source most likely to settle whether the aggregate reorders is substitutions_raw_DMS.zip together with ProteinGym's per-assay reference files, which would supply the r_a values the re-weighting needs; it was refused at both routes at verification and REMAINS the one unopened thing that matters. The second named source is now CLOSED: MIMAVE, Genome Biology 2024, DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03223-9, was opened in full at verification, names replicates nowhere, and is identical in substance to the preprint — so the appetite leg is settled against an appetite existing in the standard, and no preprint-to-published change may be invoked.
Promotion requires (REWRITTEN AT VERIFICATION): opening substitutions_raw_DMS.zip plus the per-assay reference files and reporting how many of the 217 assays carry >=2 independently selected replicate columns with independence adjudicated for that subset — still the first condition, and now the ONLY retrieval left, since the archive was refused again at verification and the benchmark as released carries no replicate-level object anywhere; restating limb (c) at the cross-assay aggregate level, where verification confirmed the ordering is NOT algebraically fixed (a two-assay counterexample at r = 1.00 against 0.64 reorders the average), and limb (b) as a three-way variance decomposition with a declared tie-break rule across arms; bounding the share expression, which verification found unbounded above once rho > sqrt(r) and which must not be reported as a share while it can exceed 1 — this plus a defended primary estimator is what lifts Well-posedness to 3/3; and stating the residue in the narrow form only, since the broad form is dead: measured, named and framed as the benchmark by Reeb/Rost in March 2020, but never quantified per assay, never applied as a correction, never used to re-rank. The MIMAVE condition is DISCHARGED (opened in full; no appetite for replicate-level agreement in either version). The FLIP2 body remains the one unrun check besides the archive.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): list the contents of substitutions_raw_DMS.zip against reference_files/DMS_substitutions.csv and count, per assay, the columns that are per-replicate rather than aggregated. Nothing beyond that count is needed to decide whether the question is measurable.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — status is Provisional, so the ledger still claims the composite as un-asked and the recommendation is no by construction. Noted for whoever revisits this entry: if it is later rejected, the generic limb is routable on P2 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.03.26.586797, Discussion: FLIP and ProteinGym "need to be corrected"), which is asked in print and unperformed; the composite is not.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Six fresh-context readers, briefed from the full citations this entry carries. No errors. **Verdict unchanged: Provisional.** The pass pushed hard in both directions: the artefact-level gap is larger than the entry claimed, and the question's broad form turns out to have been asked in print six years ago.

**The core gap strengthens.** ProteinGym's evaluated per-assay files carry one scalar per variant — mutant, mutated_sequence, DMS_score, DMS_score_bin — and there is **no replicate-level object anywhere in the benchmark as released**: the string "replicate" occurs twice in the entire repository and neither occurrence is a field. So the reliability of the 217 assays is not auditable from the benchmark as released, which is a stronger statement than the entry's "the evaluated files carry one merged score".

**Three counts were wrong, and one of them was a number from a different benchmark.** The curation table has **46** columns, not 47. **96 of 217** ingested columns are named as aggregates or fits, not 74 — and the 74 is the **INDEL benchmark's assay count**, which had been carried into this entry as a substitution-benchmark tally. The 217 assay rows draw on 94 distinct ingested column names. This is the recurring defect of a real number aimed at the wrong object, and it came in through an adversary's own arithmetic.

**Sub-claim (d) downgrades from a negative to an UNREAD.** substitutions_raw_DMS.zip was refused at both routes tried, so what the raw layer contains is COULD NOT READ. Under the standing rule that caps and never rejects, and it remains the single unopened thing that matters here.

**The broad form of the question is dead, and the narrow form is not.** Reeb & Rost 2020 (*BMC Bioinformatics* 21:107, doi 10.1186/s12859-020-3439-4) carries a Results subsection headed, verbatim, **"Experimental agreement sets the benchmark for prediction methods"**, and calls that agreement **"One proxy for an answer"**. The framing was therefore measured, named, and set up as the benchmark, in print, in this candidate's own field, in March 2020. The ledger must stop claiming the broad gap. What survives is narrower and must be stated in exactly these words: never **quantified** as a per-assay reliability, never **applied** as a correction, never **used to re-rank**.

**The algebra under the strongest objection holds, and extends three ways.** Within-assay invariance is an exact identity and sqrt(r_a) is not load-bearing — it holds for every positive predictor-independent divisor, so no estimator choice rescues limb (c) inside an assay. The share expression is exact arithmetic on a 1 - rho denominator and is **unbounded above once rho > sqrt(r)**, so the quantity limb (b) reports as a "share" can exceed 1; that is a well-posedness defect the entry had not recorded and it belongs with the 2/3. And the invariance **does not survive aggregation**: a two-assay counterexample at r = 1.00 against r = 0.64 reorders the cross-assay average, which is what ProteinGym's published ranking is. The entry's own vulnerability note had called this the genuine open empirical question; verification confirms it by construction.

**P1 (Livesey & Marsh 2023) — 0.54 is the wrong grain for the use it was put to.** The median 0.54 is **between-assay**, not between-replicate; "replicate" appears nowhere in the paper. It bounds alternate-forms agreement across differing conditions and cannot be read as a within-assay noise floor in either direction. Its denominator is deferred to Table EV3, still COULD NOT READ.

**P3 (arXiv:1809.10389) — holds, with its vocabulary and its direction corrected.** The word "reliability" is absent from the paper, so that label is this ledger's translation; Eq. 14 is a derived estimate rather than a definition; and sigma_DB sits in the **numerator**, so a narrower within-protein spread yields a **lower** ceiling — the opposite of what the entry's framing suggests. Its regime differs from the candidate's on five axes (unit, error source, correlation coefficient, object, and the absence of DMS), so it remains a dataset-level ceiling for pooled ddG and not a per-assay DMS reliability.

**MIMAVE — now opened, and the appetite leg is settled against it.** The Genome Biology 2024 version (doi 10.1186/s13059-024-03223-9) was served in full for the first time. Replicates are mentioned nowhere. The verb strengths are on record: "we urge" for raw counts, "we recommend" for pre-normalisation scores, "we strongly recommend" for raw reads. It is **identical in substance to arXiv 2306.15113**, so any force drawn from a preprint-to-published change is struck — there was no change. That discharges one of the entry's two promotion conditions.

**P2 (FLIGHTED) — all four sub-claims survive**, and it is this batch's cleanest published-is-not-performed case: it announces that FLIP and ProteinGym "need to be corrected to account for noise inherent in single-step selection", and what it actually performs is a label correction on its own 45 models over a GB1 four-site mRNA-display library, improving 37/45 and 41/45 by averages of +0.15 and +0.05. The recommendation is made; the candidate's measurement is not.

**What verification did not settle.** substitutions_raw_DMS.zip and the FLIP2 body. Everything else named in this entry has now been read first-hand.

Domain(s): Biology — translation fidelity, protein quality control, proteostasis. Adjacent: aggregation cell biology; biomanufacturing sequence-variant control; molecular evolution of coding sequences.

Question (canonical): Using single-molecule protein sequencing of full-length chains in an unstressed cell, what is the distribution of the number of amino-acid misincorporation errors per individual polypeptide molecule, does it depart from the site-independent (Poisson-binomial) null built from position- and codon-specific rates measured in the same cells — i.e. are errors clustered onto a minority of molecules over a window longer than one tryptic peptide — and what fraction of molecules carry two or more errors?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, and the version scored. V1 (intake) named a single-lambda Poisson null and claimed peptide-level MS cannot see co-occurrence at all; both were corrected from opened sources (per-site rates span orders of magnitude, so the null must be Poisson-binomial; two to four substitutions inside one tryptic peptide are detectable and were tested against the independence product under drug). Full text of both versions in ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0033/UQ-20261022-04-record.md.

Alternative formulations:
- Does mistranslation produce many slightly wrong proteins or a few badly wrong ones?
- Is the proteome's per-molecule error load site-independent, and what fraction of molecules carry two or more errors — measured, not inferred from the bulk rate?

Motivating gap: measured mistranslation is an aggregate ratio because the instrument has been bottom-up MS, whose unit of observation is the tryptic peptide. Three sourced parts: the canonical unstressed map (P3) runs no co-occurrence or Poisson-departure test and averages error rates within a protein; the stressed cluster study (P1) states its own clusters are "likely to supersede the length of average tryptic peptides", so the window is shorter than the object — verified verbatim and it HOLDS, with the scope stated: it is one hedged, streptomycin-specific clause carrying no number, so it establishes the direction of the mismatch and not its size; and the per-molecule quantity exists in print only as a prediction under assumed independence (P2).

Presuppositions: (1) single-molecule protein sequencing can read a full-length chain end to end with per-residue reading error far below the ~10^-3 translation signal — CONTESTED, and the one the verdict turns on; (2) errors are frequent enough to count per molecule at achievable throughput (lambda ~0.3 on a 300-mer) — CONTESTED; (3) sampled molecules are full-length mature products — CONTESTED; (4) degradation has not already removed multi-error molecules, and the estimand (errors per synthesised vs per surviving molecule) is left unchosen — CONTESTED; (5) the independent-error null with same-cell position- and codon-specific rates is the right comparator — established, and already a published construct; (6) bulk per-site frequency and per-molecule count are commensurable under (5); (7) "an error" is individuated identically by both instruments — stated in words, not operationalised.

What would count as an answer: a measured per-molecule error-count distribution with CI, tested against a pre-declared Poisson-binomial null from same-sample position- and codon-specific rates; known-sequence standards bounding instrument reading error; a stated detection limit for 2+ errors on one chain; the fraction of molecules with 2+ errors with uncertainty; and a declared estimand with respect to presupposition 4. A null-consistent distribution reported with power to exclude clustering above a declared effect size answers it negatively.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 38 web searches total — 11 at Gate 2, then 9 + 9 + 9 across three adversaries, with 8 new-vocabulary Disguise queries each from adversaries 1 and 3 and 6 new plus 3 partially overlapping from adversary 2, so Disguise was executed, not unverified. Most informative: "translation errors per polypeptide chain Poisson distribution clustered error-prone subpopulation" → surfaced P1, the only source that has ever tested co-occurrence against an independence product; "fluorosequencing single-molecule proteomics detect sequence variants per molecule amino acid substitution Edman" (method-owning field) → method and patent literature only, no application to error counting; "top-down proteomics intact mass proteoform amino acid misincorporation multiple substitutions on the same protein molecule" (run independently by two adversaries, the full-chain MS instrument Gate 2 never considered) → proteoform catalogues only, no misincorporation counting per intact molecule; '"statistical proteins" ambiguous translation proteome diversity CUG Candida albicans' → Gomes 2007, the vocabulary Gate 2 missed; '"phenotypic mutations" ... Willensdorfer Burger Nowak' → a whole population-genetics vocabulary for per-molecule error load that Gate 2 missed, all independence-assuming; "mistranslation errors per polypeptide overdispersion ... unstressed proteome test" → bioRxiv 2025.04.18.649569, the record's own unopened intake paper, opened by adversary 3 and found to run no co-occurrence test. Full lists: ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0033/UQ-20261022-04-record.md and the three adversary files in this directory.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Wohlgemuth I., Garofalo R., Samatova E., Günenç A.N., Lenz C., Urlaub H., Rodnina M.V., "Translation error clusters induced by aminoglycoside antibiotics", Nature Communications 12:1830 (2021). Read full text via the Göttingen repository mirror; existence independently corroborated by adversaries 1 and 2 (Göttingen record ID-86738, DOAJ, MPI-NAT project page, PanoramaWeb project title). Unit = tryptic peptide; endpoint = cluster error frequency; comparator = the independence product of per-position rates; estimand = observed/expected enrichment, up to 60,000-fold, plus a conditional next-error probability of 0.05–0.25. Condition = aminoglycoside-stressed or ram mutant; clusters reported absent in untreated ram cells. Three verification corrections: the 60,000-fold must NOT be set beside the Abstract's 10,000-fold as the same quantity (they are differently scoped and the entry's single figure invites the merge); the only no-drug cluster measurement in the paper is the untreated **ram mutant**, an error-prone mutant and not a wild-type baseline; and for untreated WILD-TYPE cells the paper reports nothing at all, because that sample is its false-positive filter rather than a measured condition. So P1 supplies no unstressed wild-type comparator, which widens the gap this candidate sits in.
P2. Landerer C., Pöhls J., Toth-Petroczy A., "Evolutionary impact of codon specific translation errors at the proteome scale", bioRxiv 2022.10.11.511697. Read full text by the record; existence independently confirmed by adversary 2's search return of the PDF with the exact title (adversary 1's Crossref check was rate-limited, adversary 3 corroborated only the group). Unit = codon/site summed to protein; comparator = none, independence is an assumption; estimand = probability of error-free translation, printing ">15% of all proteins contain at least one" error. CORRECTED AT VERIFICATION: that figure is INTRODUCTION-level, inherited and cited from other work and hedged with "imply" — it is not an output of P2's own model. This DEEPENS the gap rather than closing it: the one printed per-molecule number in P2 is not even P2's measurement.
P3. Mordret E., Dahan O., Asraf O., Rak R., Yehonadav A., Barnabas G.D., Cox J., Geiger T., Lindner A.B., Pilpel Y., "Systematic Detection of Amino Acid Substitutions in Proteomes...", Molecular Cell 75:427–441 (2019), doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2019.06.041. Read full text by the record; confirmed by adversary 2 from the Crossref metadata record. Unit = peptide/site; endpoint = dependent/base peptide intensity ratio, "around one misincorporation event per 1,000 translated residues"; estimand = per-site, per-codon frequency; protein-level operation an average.
Fourth prior added at Gate 4 by adversary 3 (vocabulary Gate 2 never entered): Gomes A.C. et al., "A genetic code alteration generates a proteome of high diversity in the human pathogen Candida albicans", Genome Biology 8:R206 (2007), read full text via link.springer.com. Figure 4c plots the per-molecule count distribution (0/1/2/3 leucines) for three-CUG genes under an explicit binomial model — OPENED AND CONFIRMED at verification, where adversary 3 could not read it. It is prior art FOR THE CONSTRUCT: a published per-molecule error-count distribution exists, and has since 2007. The regime differs sharply and that is what keeps novelty at Medium rather than dropping it: three pre-specified CUG sites in a single gene, under programmed sense-codon ambiguity rather than misincorporation, unit = peptide, and the distribution is computed under the binomial, not measured.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1, same comparator logic but a different regime on two legs — unstressed versus drug-stressed, and full-chain count distribution versus frequency ratio inside one peptide, a window P1's own authors flag as too short. vs P2, the candidate asks for the measurement P2 substitutes an assumption for; P2 predicts the quantity and does not measure it. vs P3, same cells and condition and the source of the null's per-site rates, but a per-site estimand on a unit that cannot carry a per-molecule count. vs Gomes 2007, a different error class on a peptide unit, with the count distribution plotted under a binomial null rather than observed.
On the published-is-not-performed check: no source opened by the record or by any of three adversaries names a MEASURED number for the candidate quantity. The nearest printed numbers are P2's ">15% carry at least one" — at verification an Introduction-level inherited citation hedged with "imply", not P2's own model output, so weaker still than the record treated it — and Gomes Figure 4c's binomial plot, which verification DID open: it is a genuine per-molecule 0/1/2/3 count distribution under an explicit binomial, so a published per-molecule count-distribution CONSTRUCT does exist, dated 2007. P2 and Gomes PREDICT; P1 MEASURES a different object (peptide-window enrichment under drug); P3 MEASURES per-site rates and averages them away. So the kill below does not rest on any source publishing the candidate quantity.

Novelty confidence: Medium — distinct, but P1 is close and Gate 4 showed the Gate 2 vocabulary sweep missed two further vocabularies in which the quantity is predicted. Not Low: nothing measures a per-molecule error-count distribution and nothing prints a 2+ fraction. Not High: the independence-versus-clustering question has been posed and answered in a neighbouring regime of the candidate's own literature.

Significance — consequence: if clustered, P2's ">15%" and its summed per-protein fitness burden both move, redistributing the same total error count onto fewer molecules and raising per-affected-molecule severity, the quantity that matters for aggregation seeding; and P1's processivity extends from drug-induced to constitutive. If independent, P2's assumption is licensed outside the stressed regime and per-molecule load becomes computable from bulk rates. Honest bound: at lambda ~0.3 the expected 2+ share is a few percent (adversary arithmetic, range 0.5–26% across the record's own rate spread), and no effect size that would matter is declared.
Significance — audience: proteostasis and aggregation modellers, whose load models take a bulk rate where thresholds are nonlinear; translation-fidelity groups, one of which has already quantified the conditional next-error probability under drug and stopped at the peptide window; biomanufacturing sequence-variant control — this third audience survived no adversary, resting only on the record's own negative search, and all three adversaries graded attack 6 Partial on it.
Significance — fecundity: does the error-prone state decay with distance along a chain; is the clustered subpopulation ribosome- or transcript-linked; does degradation preferentially clear multi-error molecules; do multi-error molecules seed aggregates at rates predicted from substitution count; does the distribution differ between abundant and scarce proteins.
Significance — anchoring: P1's unexplained processivity of misreading; the mistranslation-induced-misfolding constraint on coding-sequence evolution (title-level only in the record); P2's independence assumption as a live untested modelling convenience; proteostasis-collapse models framed on aggregate rates.

Reason for silence: an instrument boundary stated in the prior literature's own words, plus a disciplinary split — the community that measures fidelity reports site ratios and averages within proteins, while the community that uses per-molecule load obtains it by assuming independence, so the quantity is nobody's deliverable. Graded Resolved by adversary 1 and Partial by adversaries 2 and 3, who both held that the mechanism explains why nobody has ANSWERED better than why nobody ASKED: the proposition is explicitly asserted by P2, tested by P1 under drug, and computed by Gomes 2007 in an unstressed cell nineteen years ago without being tested.

(Well-posedness held at 2/3 by the unchosen synthesised-versus-surviving estimand and the un-operationalised cross-instrument individuation of "an error"; both were pressed by all three adversaries and neither was resolved. 2/3 independently bars Validated.)

Strongest remaining objection: the verdict stands on ONE leg — attack 4. The candidate's canonical wording conditions the question on single-molecule protein sequencing of full-length chains, and the enabling source, read first-hand by two adversaries at body-text level, does known-position classification among known candidates in a synthetic sequence background, publishes no de novo per-residue accuracy, no limit of detection and no false-positive rate for a substitution, and reaches 61% at 20-way only in simulation. ALL OF THAT NOW HOLDS OF THE VERSION OF RECORD TOO, opened at verification (Nature 633, p. 662): it prints none of the three numbers, and its Discussion forecloses the measurement in the authors' own voice. That leg depends on none of the others and would stand if every other leg fell; it is now empirically grounded in the reviewed text rather than in the preprint alone. If it fell, what survives caps the entry at Provisional rather than rejecting it: the algebraic identity under attack 8 (the count distribution alone cannot distinguish within-molecule processivity from between-molecule rate heterogeneity), well-posedness at 2/3, and Medium novelty with P1 as an admitted close neighbour. The disguise reading on which the candidate is P1's question with a condition-and-instrument swap was pressed by all three adversaries and came back Partial twice and Resolved once; it is the second most dangerous leg and it does not reject on its own.
Vulnerability of this rejection — recorded as required, because the kill rests partly on what nobody has measured: attack 4's evidential core is an ABSENCE IN PRINT plus adversary arithmetic, not a reported negative result. No source opened by any agent here publishes a de novo per-residue accuracy, a limit of detection, or a substitution false-positive rate for a native full-length chain, so the instrument's actual floor at the candidate's regime is itself an unmeasured quantity; the 2-to-3-order-of-magnitude shortfall is an extrapolation from classification accuracy in a synthetic background, i.e. a claim following from the published experiment's DESIGN rather than from a measurement of the thing the candidate needs. Distinguishing the kinds of ground in play: the attack-8 overdispersion result is an ALGEBRAIC identity (Var(N) = E[lambda] + Var(lambda), exact by construction and not falsifiable by any instrument), and so is the attack-1 cross-site covariance decomposition; the attack-4 instrument shortfall is EMPIRICAL AND UNMEASURED, not algebraic, and a single published number could overturn it. Single unopened source most likely to settle it: the peer-reviewed version of the multi-pass nanopore work, Nature 633 (2024), doi 10.1038/s41586-024-07935-7 — nobody here opened it (adversary 1 read only a preLights secondary; adversaries 2 and 3 read the bioRxiv preprint body with front matter not served; nature.com was never attempted), and its reviewed text and supplementary are the likeliest place for a limit of detection or false-positive rate to be printed. If it prints one that clears ~10^-4 per residue de novo on a native chain, this rejection should be reopened at Gate 4 rather than left standing. **RESOLVED AT VERIFICATION, AND THE REOPENING CONDITION IS NOT MET.** The version of record was opened in full at the NSF Public Access Repository mirror (par.nsf.gov) after nature.com failed both ways: it prints no de novo per-residue accuracy, no limit of detection and no substitution false-positive rate, and its Discussion states in the authors' own voice that "directly determining amino acid sequences from the nanopore signal (de novo sequencing) will be ... even more difficult". The rejection stands on read text rather than on an untested absence. One place is still unopened — the Supplementary Information — and it remains the only place such a number could now hide; the reopening condition transfers to it unchanged.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): establish the instrument floor before the biology — read known-sequence standard polypeptides to bound per-residue de novo reading error and the detection limit for two or more substitutions on one chain, then decide whether the ~10^-3 signal is separable at all.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — this is not an asked-but-open rejection. It fails at Gate 4 on presupposition failure, and no opened source poses the unstressed full-chain per-molecule question, so there is nothing to hand to the open-questions project. The adjacent question that WAS asked (are translation errors independent along a chain?) was answered for the aminoglycoside-stressed peptide-window regime by P1, which is recorded above as the close neighbour, not as a routing target. No row for ledger/routed-open-problems.md.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Five fresh-context readers, none of them the generator or an adversary, each briefed from the full citations this entry carries. No errors. **Verdict unchanged: Rejected** — and for the first time it rests on the document the entry itself named as the one that could overturn it.

**The reopening condition was tested and failed.** This entry recorded, before verification ran, that the peer-reviewed version of the multi-pass nanopore work was the single unopened source most likely to settle attack 4, and that a printed de novo per-residue figure clearing ~10^-4 on a native chain should reopen the rejection. nature.com refused both routes even though the article is open access; the **NSF Public Access Repository mirror** (`par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10560827`) served the full typeset article. It is Motone, Kontogiorgos-Heintz, Wee, Kurihara, Yang, Roote, Fox, Fang, Queen, Tolhurst, Cardozo, Jain and Nivala, **"Multi-pass, single-molecule nanopore reading of long protein strands"**, *Nature* **633**, p. 662 (2024), doi 10.1038/s41586-024-07935-7. Note the published title **drops** the preprint's "with single-amino acid sensitivity". It prints **no de novo per-residue accuracy, no limit of detection and no substitution false-positive rate**, and the Discussion forecloses the direction in the authors' own words: *"directly determining amino acid sequences from the nanopore signal (de novo sequencing) will be ... even more difficult"*. The absence is now an absence in the reviewed text, read first-hand, not an inference from a preprint.

**What the instrument does measure**, for the record and in its own units: pairwise discrimination 100%, 3-way 95%, 5-way 86%, 20-way **28%** against a 5.5% random-guess baseline, top-5 67% and top-8 81%; per-read whole-strand accuracy ~62% and 42% (HDKER) and ~51% and 21% (AVLIM) over engineered variable-region positions. The **61% is simulated**, in Supplementary Note 3, with Extended Data Fig. 7d captioned "Simulated effect of rereading...". Every construct is a designed PASTOR carrier; the titin item is an engineered 89-residue I27V15P variant, not a full-length native chain.

**Two corrections to the attack-4 row, one favouring the candidate.** The 20-way task does not classify "among KNOWN candidates": it "considers all possible amino acid classes", so the instrument is marginally better than this entry described — and still two to three orders short of what a count-per-chain estimand needs. And "published anywhere" was too strong: it is now scoped to the preprint main text and the version-of-record main text, both read, with the Supplementary Information the one unopened place.

**The preprint was misidentified in an adversary log.** It is bioRxiv **10.1101/2023.10.19.563182**, not 2025.04.18.649569, which is an unrelated mistranslation paper. The entry itself never carried the wrong identifier; the log did.

**P1 (Wohlgemuth et al. 2021) — sub-claim holds, three scope corrections.** The clause that the clusters are "likely to supersede the length of average tryptic peptides" is verbatim and stands, but it is one hedged, streptomycin-specific sentence with no number attached, so it establishes the direction of the window/object mismatch and not its magnitude. The paper's only no-drug cluster measurement is the untreated **ram mutant** — an error-prone mutant, not a wild-type baseline — and for untreated wild-type cells it reports nothing, because that sample serves as the false-positive filter. So P1 supplies no unstressed wild-type comparator at all, which widens rather than narrows the gap. Finally, the 60,000-fold enrichment must not travel beside the Abstract's 10,000-fold as though they were the same quantity.

**P2 (Landerer et al.) — the printed number is not the model's.** ">15% of all proteins contain at least one" error is **Introduction-level, inherited from cited work and hedged with "imply"**, not an output of P2's own proteome-scale model. The record treated it as the nearest published approach to the candidate quantity; it is weaker than that, and the gap is correspondingly deeper.

**Gomes 2007 — the figure was opened, and it is prior art for the construct.** Adversary 3 could not read Figure 4c's values; verification did. It is a genuine per-molecule **0/1/2/3** count distribution under an explicit binomial model. A published per-molecule error-count-distribution construct therefore exists and has since 2007, which is a real finding against this candidate's framing. It does not drop novelty below Medium, because the regime differs on every axis that matters: three pre-specified CUG sites in a single gene, programmed sense-codon ambiguity rather than misincorporation, a peptide unit, and a distribution computed under the binomial rather than measured against it.

**Net effect.** Nothing moved the verdict, and the rejection is stronger than it was: its fatal leg is now anchored in the version of record and in the authors' own statement of difficulty, rather than in a preprint plus arithmetic. Its remaining vulnerability has narrowed to one document — the Supplementary Information of Nature 633 — and the reopening condition transfers to it unchanged.

ID: UQ-20261022-05
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — REVERSED from Rejected at verification. Adversary 3's attack 4 rested on an identity conditional on a premise nobody had tested: that a dated datasheet yields ONE scalar stock concentration per catalogue number. The first sample of actual datasheets, taken by a fresh-context checker, contradicts it in 3 of 3 documents, and Leg B's two load-bearing claims are unsourced or false. With that ground withdrawn nothing is Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4; Gate 4 is complete (three adversaries, all eight attacks each, none skipped), so the entry is re-graded on the existing record and capped by adversary 1's Unresolved attack 5 on the same defect, plus well-posedness 2/3
Domain(s): Biology — experimental methods and research-reagent practice (immunoassays in cell and molecular biology). Adjacent: measurement metrology, reporting standards, meta-research.
Question (canonical): For a pre-declared panel of commercial research antibodies, each pinned to a catalogue number and a dated datasheet of record: (i) is the vendor-recommended working dilution for a named application predicted by the product's stated stock concentration, or by a measurable binding constant plus the nominal target abundance in the recommended sample type, under a comparison declared in advance; and (ii) across a pre-declared sample of published immunoassays using that panel, in what fraction is the mass-per-volume or molar antibody concentration in the incubation computable at all from the paper plus that datasheet, and among papers quoting the same nominal dilution for the same catalogue number, what is the spread in computed concentration? [R1, adopted at Gate 1; V0 superseded there for well-posedness — both versions in the record.]
Alternative formulations: (a) Where does "1:1000" come from — the antibody's biophysics, or the bottle's packaging? (b) Biology's most-used reagent class is specified by a dilution rather than a concentration: how often is the dose recoverable from the published record, and is the recommended dilution a property of the antibody at all?
Motivating gap: Methods sections specify antibodies by dilution, and a dilution is a dose only if stock concentration is known — which many products do not state. The titration how-to literature tells users to optimise empirically and is silent on where the vendor's figure came from. Claim driving the candidate: two papers both reporting "1:1000" may differ in dose by orders of magnitude.
Presuppositions: P1 datasheets state a recommended dilution and state/omit stock concentration recordably — not measured here; no datasheet was opened by the record or by any of three adversaries. P2 binding parameters obtainable for enough of the panel — contested, no survey of affinity-data availability found. P3 a polyclonal has a single meaningful affinity — contested, handled by stratification. P4 the selling vendor sets the figure — contested, OEM relabelling; Voskuil 2014 (read by adversary 3) notes the same clone sold "in known mg/ml concentration" and "without any specifications". P5 dose materially affects results — partly established; NordiQC CD8 run 54 (read) shows optimal IHC across a typical 1:25–1:200 range when retrieval/detection are adjusted, which bounds it in that regime. P6 antibodies individuable across papers — bounded by prior A: catalogue numbers missing in 32%/20% of papers, lot numbers in 1%. P7 printed stock concentration accurate — unchecked. P8 stock concentration varies enough for the packaging model to have variance to explain — contested, unchecked. P9 (added by adversaries, not in the record) the recommended dilution is a scalar at all — contradicted in practice: Rockland (read) states manufacturers "often give dilution ranges"; CST (read) states it recommends "a specific dilution or dilution range" and prints no stock concentration.
What would count as an answer: a pre-registered two-part study — (i) regression of log recommended dilution, one row per product x application, on stated stock concentration vs. binding constant plus nominal target abundance, format and vendor as covariates, variance partitioned; (ii) a paper x dated-datasheet join reporting the computability fraction with the identifier-coverage bound, and the spread in computed concentration at fixed nominal dilution.

Significance — consequence: if dose is usually unrecoverable and dilution tracks packaging, nominal dilution is not poolable across papers and the field's commonest reagent is dosed in a container property; if dilution tracks affinity and dose is recoverable, the concern closes.

Adversary 2 judged this Resolved on the strength of prior A being that audience writing to itself.

Significance — anchoring: research-antibody reproducibility literature; prior A's measured reporting gaps; the titration literature's silence on provenance; the absence of a concentration field from the reporting standards this run could read.

[SUPERSEDED AT VERIFICATION — the premise this objection is conditional on was tested for the first time and failed in every document sampled; see the verification section below. Kept verbatim because the ledger is append-only and because its own Vulnerability paragraph predicted exactly this outcome.] Strongest remaining objection (as written at Gate 5): limb (ii)'s "spread in computed concentration among papers quoting the same nominal dilution for the same catalogue number" is identically zero under the candidate's own operationalisation, and the motivating "orders of magnitude" claim lives in a comparison across catalogue numbers while the quantity actually posed is within one. THE VERDICT STANDS ON THIS LEG — adversary 3's attack 4 Leg A, corroborated independently by adversary 1's attack 5, which found the same defect and filed it in a non-fatal slot. WHICH LEG WOULD SURVIVE IF IT FELL: Leg B, that CST holds the recommended dilution constant as a product-sizing convention and tunes the vial concentration instead, printing no stock concentration at all, so limb (i)'s contest is degenerate on one side and undefined on the other. Leg B is sourced to a full read of the vendor's own post, but it is a vendor policy statement for one catalogue, not an evaluation, and all three adversaries graded their versions of it Partial at worst; on Leg B alone this entry would be Provisional with "re-specify limb (i)" as the promotion condition, not Rejected. THIS REJECTION'S OWN VULNERABILITY, recorded as the standing rule requires: Leg A rests on something nobody has measured. It is an ALGEBRAIC identity in the candidate's text — stated stock concentration times quoted dilution, one datasheet per catalogue number, therefore one value — and not a bitwise or empirical finding: no agent has computed concentrations over any paper corpus, no datasheet of record was opened by the record or by any of the three adversaries, and no source reports that such computed values coincide. The identity holds only if a dated datasheet yields a unique scalar stock concentration, and that is precisely what is unmeasured: two opened vendor sources state that recommendations and specifications come as RANGES or are absent (Rockland: manufacturers "often give dilution ranges"; CST prints no concentration), and a datasheet printing a range, a ">" bound, a lot-dependent value, or a lyophilised mass reconstituted at a laboratory-chosen volume would make the computed dose non-unique and the spread empirically nonzero. The single unopened source most likely to settle it: Weller M, "Quality Issues of Research Antibodies", Analytical Chemistry Insights 2016 — the one review squarely on research-antibody documentation quality, unopened by the record and by two adversaries only because opus4.kobv.de serves an Anubis bot interstitial to this reader; try the SAGE journal route rather than that repository PDF. A second-order vulnerability worth recording: the same defect was fatal only because adversary 3 filed it under attack 4 while adversary 1 filed it under attack 5, and the ledger's rule makes that filing decisive.
Strongest remaining objection (REWRITTEN AT VERIFICATION): limb (i) has no response variable for part of any panel that could be assembled. Sigma-Aldrich A2228 recommends a working CONCENTRATION range (0.5-1 ug/mL for Western blot) and no dilution at all, so for those products the quantity limb (i) asks to predict does not exist and the panel must either exclude them, which selects on documentation style, or carry a second response variable, which makes the two arms non-comparable. This is a specification defect, not a disguised known, and it is sourced to a datasheet a checker opened rather than to an inference. THE LEGS: it stands on this one. If it fell, what survives is adversary 1's Unresolved attack 5, which caps the entry at Provisional on its own.
Promotion requires: all three of — (a) limb (ii) re-specified as the DOCUMENT JOIN it actually is (catalogue page, which prints a dilution and no concentration, times lot certificate of analysis, which prints a concentration and no dilution, joined on a lot number that appears in about 1% of papers by prior A's own measure), with the within-product spread stated as a function of lot-CoA dispersion, which is measurable from published certificates; (b) limb (i)'s response variable defined so it exists for products recommending a concentration range and no dilution; (c) a declared datasheet-form frame, since the three documents sampled at verification gave three different forms and none a unique unconditional scalar. Well-posedness reaches 3/3 only with (b), and the Medium novelty cap holds independently until the three designated unopened priors are read.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): sample dated datasheets across vendors and product formats and record, for each, whether a stock concentration is printed and in what form — scalar, range, bound, lot-referred or absent. That one sample settles P1, P8 and the hinge of Leg A at once, and it is the step nobody in this record has taken.
Routing: ROUTE: no — not rejected as already-asked and not a disguised known. Disguise ran in full (27 fresh-vocabulary queries, 12 pages opened) and found no prior performing either measurement, so routed-open-problems.md is not the right destination; the rejection is for well-posedness at Gate 4, and an asked-but-open row would misdescribe it. A reformulated candidate that drops the within-product spread, replaces it with the across-product spread of computed dose at a fixed nominal dilution, and re-specifies limb (i) on working concentration with vendor convention as a named third category would be a new candidate requiring all eight attacks from scratch; it inherits nothing from this entry.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Three fresh-context checkers, each handed one claim and its source and none of them this entry's reasoning. Notes: VERIFY-datasheet-concentration-form.md, VERIFY-weller-2016-antibodies.md, VERIFY-blind-spots-westerns.md.

VERDICT REVERSED, Rejected to Provisional, because the fatal ground's premise was tested for the first time and failed. Leg A is an algebraic identity CONDITIONAL on a dated datasheet yielding one scalar stock concentration per catalogue number. Nobody in the batch had opened a datasheet. A checker opened three, across three formats, and 0 of 3 gave an unconditional scalar: Cell Signaling Technology prints an exact per-LOT value on a separately versioned certificate of analysis that carries no dilution ("Concentration: 36 ug/ml", product 5125 lot 8, "version 2025-04-11"); Sigma-Aldrich gives "~2 mg/mL" with a pointer to a lot or batch certificate; Synaptic Systems 266 011 gives a MASS (100 ug) reconstituted at a volume the laboratory chooses, so its "1 mg/ml" is the vendor's own arithmetic conditional on the user adding 100 ul. Three of the five forms the entry itself anticipated - range, lot-dependent, lyophilised mass - turned up in three pulls. n = 3, convenience-selected, so this is first evidence against the premise and not a frequency claim; the honest reading is that the rejection rested on an unmeasured premise with adverse first evidence, not on an established identity.

LEG B FAILS ON TWO OF ITS THREE CLAIMS. "CST adjusts the vial concentration instead" is nowhere on the CST post: the post holds the ASSAY COUNT constant, says "no matter the concentration", and attributes concentration variance to antibody activity, sensitivity, purity and vendor. The inverse-tuning mechanism was the entry's inference presented as the vendor's statement. And "CST prints no stock concentration" is true of the post and FALSE of the company, since CST's own lot certificate prints one - which contradicts attack 6's stronger wording that the convention "structurally cannot supply a concentration". What survives of Leg B is only that the post is undated, which was correctly recorded.

THE LEG-A REBUTTAL IS ITSELF REFUTED. Adversary 3 dismissed "the spread was meant to capture lot-to-lot variation" on the ground that it "needs lot data the frame excludes". Lot certificates are published and openable, and the checker opened one. So the within-product spread is a function of lot-CoA dispersion, which is measurable, and limb (ii) is not degenerate: two papers quoting the same nominal dilution of the same catalogue number compute different doses whenever they used different lots. That is why well-posedness is restored to 2/3 rather than left at 1/3.

A THIRD CATEGORY NOBODY IN THE BATCH NAMED, and it is now the entry's strongest objection: some vendors recommend a working CONCENTRATION range and no dilution at all (Sigma A2228, 0.5-1 ug/mL for Western blot), so limb (i)'s response variable is undefined for part of any panel - independent of the range problem adversary 2 filed, and a real specification gap rather than a kill.

QUOTATION AND SOURCING CORRECTIONS. (i) Rockland is quoted three times in this record as saying manufacturers "often give dilution ranges". The page serves "Often the manufacturer recommends dilution ranges compatible with other variables such as method,". Verb, number and qualifier all differ, so the quotation marks are withdrawn; the substance survives. The served segment also ends mid-clause at "such as method," and the tail was never obtained, so whether the sentence asserts that datasheet figures are themselves ranges is UNVERIFIED, and this record used the fragment as if it did. Adversary 2's Rockland titre quotations are verbatim, but it quoted only the polyclonal half and omitted the stronger ascites clause "1:1000-1:100,000". (ii) Both vendor sources DEFINE or ANNOUNCE and neither MEASURES: Rockland asserts that ranges are common and illustrates dilution arithmetic; CST announces a convention and claims in-house data while printing no titration curve, no dissociation constant, no distribution and no n.

WELLER 2016 IS NOW OPEN, AND IS USABLE FOR FRAMING ONLY. The two earlier failures were route-specific: the paper is open access and opens cleanly at the SAGE PDF route, so the opus4.kobv.de bot interstitial was a COULD NOT READ at one route and should never have propagated as an unreadable source. It supports the entry's framing - vendors "usually" state a protein or IgG concentration, and the review's point is that this substitutes for the quantity that matters, the concentration of ACTIVE antibody - and it supports nothing numeric: it prints no share of datasheets missing a concentration, no share of papers failing to state a dose, no data table of its own. It has no unit of analysis, endpoint, comparator or estimand; it is a single-author review whose output is an argument and a nine-item programme. Three attribution traps recorded so they are not re-run: its 44% and "less than 50%" are about whether an antibody named in a paper can be IDENTIFIED, not about concentration or dose, so they are a different gap; its ">75% nonspecific" is an unnamed company's unpublished test relayed from a comment on Baker 2015, with no reference number; and dose computability from paper plus datasheet is simply absent from it, which is silence and not a denial.

PRIOR A IS FULLY IDENTIFIED AND THE "AUTHORSHIP UNAVAILABLE" NOTE IS STRUCK. It is Kroon C, Breuer L, Jones L, An J, Akan A, Mohamed Ali EA, Busch F, Fislage M, Ghosh B, Hellrigel-Holderbaum M, Kazezian V, Koppold A, Moreira Restrepo CA, Riedel N, Scherschinski L, Urrutia Gonzalez FR, Weissgerber TL, "Blind spots on western blots", PLOS Biology 2022;20(9):e3001783, doi 10.1371/journal.pbio.3001783, Meta-Research Article, 12 September 2022. The complete 17-author byline is served on the publisher's typeset PDF, so the earlier "not served at any route" does not reproduce. Its 551 July-2021 papers and its 25% and 52% hold as printed, but three corrections travel with them: the DENOMINATORS "about 151 and 400" are supplied by this record and printed nowhere near the figures (the sentence states no n and the Figure 4 caption states none; 151 and 400 are the whole-sample field sizes), so they are withdrawn as asserted; the figures sit inside a primary-versus-secondary comparison whose other half is 58% and 72% for secondary antibodies, which should travel with them; and the paper contains no antibody concentration in mass or molar units and no computed dose anywhere, so the gap it leaves is an ABSENCE rather than a granularity gap, and it performs no datasheet join of any kind. One unresolved numeric tension in the source itself, flagged and not corrected: its consistency check reads "a random selection of 10% (n = 62) of papers from the sample" while 10% of 551 is 55.

WHAT NOTHING MOVED: the novelty grade. No source opened by the record, by any of the three adversaries, or by this pass performs either limb, and the Medium cap stands on prior A occupying the same corpus one granularity step away plus three designated priors still unopened. The rejection was never a novelty kill and the reversal is not a novelty finding.
