Domain(s): Medicine — laboratory medicine / clinical chemistry (target field). Adjacent vocabularies swept: metrology, EHR/biobank lab-data curation, quality-management/middleware, official-statistics selective editing, pharmaceutical OOS retest, regulated bioanalysis (ICH M10), semiconductor retest, German and Chinese own-field terms.

Question (canonical): In >=2 accredited clinical laboratories running different middleware vendors and different repeat rule sets, under a rule declared before any data pull for which runs count as the "first valid measurement", (a) per analyte, what share of released results is not the first valid measurement of that analyte on that specimen, decomposed by the rule that caused the replacement (rerun, dilution, delta-check repeat, critical-value repeat, cross-instrument confirmation); (b) how do the paired first-measurement and released-result distributions differ; and (c) recomputed on both substrates, do the reference-interval limits, the prevalence of threshold-crossing abnormality and the within-person monitoring delta differ by more than a materiality bound fixed in advance — with the share of candidate laboratories whose logs could not supply superseded measurements at all reported as a primary result?
Reformulation note: this is R1, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, adopted in the record and the version scored here; the intake version V0 asked the same (a)+(b)+(c) composite without the pre-declared rule, the materiality bound or the feasibility denominator. Gate 1's single reformulation is spent, so the narrowed limb-(c)-only question that survives the kill is not available as a repair inside this entry.

Alternative formulations:
- How much of what a laboratory reports is a second opinion it gave itself, and does that change the numbers everyone downstream computes from its results?
- What is the magnitude and direction of the within-laboratory selection effect that repeat-and-replace rules impose on the distribution of released results, and which released-result estimands are biased beyond a pre-declared materiality bound?

Motivating gap (as recorded, and as it stands after Gate 4): the own field audits repeats for whether the repeat confirms the original (cost/benefit frame), while reference intervals, EHR phenotype prevalence, biological variation and monitoring deltas are all computed on released results, i.e. on the output of a within-laboratory selection rule. The gap survives for limb (c). It does not survive as stated for limbs (a) and (b): the record's claim that "nobody has characterised this in this population or on this unit" is refuted by the source below, which the record's own queries returned three times (Q2, Q6, Q10) and never opened.

Presuppositions: P1 middleware/LIS retains superseded measurements retrievably — CONTESTED in the record, which opened zero instances of the document kind; adversary 2 then supplied two (a laboratory that reconstructed 701 superseded measurements with reason codes and both initial and final values; an open-source LIMS data model that persists a retracted analysis as its own object and creates the repeat as a new linked object). P1 therefore survives contact with the literature and is NOT the ground of this rejection; what remains unverified is narrower — no clinical analyser-middleware vendor audit-trail document was opened by the record or by either adversary, so R1's different-middleware-vendors clause still rests on zero instances of that specific document kind. P2 "first valid measurement" is rule-definable — established by instance (one laboratory operationalised it). P3 replacement decisions reconstructable from reason codes rather than undocumented discretion — supported by the same instance. P4 released results are the downstream substrate — asserted from extract structure, not from a source anyone opened; the OHDSI/OMOP form of it remains unopened by all three runs, while one opened paper shows five hospitals fitting delta-check limits to released results, which supports it indirectly. P5 the first-versus-released difference is not identically zero — now evidenced, not presupposed (significant initial-vs-final differences in 8 of 18 analytes).

What would count as an answer: per-analyte shares of released results that are not first valid measurements with the pre-declared rule, the rule-wise decomposition and the sensitivity arms, from >=2 laboratories on different middleware vendors; paired first-vs-released distributions; recomputation of the three named estimands on both substrates against the pre-fixed materiality bound; plus the share of candidate laboratories whose logs cannot supply superseded measurements. A null is a reportable answer. This field is unchanged by the verdict: the question is answerable, which is why it fails on novelty rather than on well-posedness.

Unit = initial/repeat run pair on one critical-value specimen (601 pairs); endpoint = initial-vs-repeat discrepancy against the CAP allowable-error limit; comparator = the initial run; estimand = proportion of pairs exceeding the limit, 4.0% (24/601). Regime = critical-value chemistry at one hospital, analytical confirmation benefit.
(Also load-bearing but not a prior formulation: Sciacovelli L. et al. (IFCC WG-LEPS), "Quality Indicators in Laboratory Medicine", Clin Chem Lab Med 2017;55(3):348-357, doi:10.1515/cclm-2016-0929, full text — the MQI set contains no indicator counting repeated, re-run, diluted or re-analysed results; the intra-analytical axis stops at IQC/EQA and transcription error. This closes the record's unresolved P4 as a granularity gap rather than an absence, and it cuts for the candidate, not against it.)

Novelty — how this differs from each: against prior 1, the differences are regime and design attributes only — >=2 laboratories on different middleware vendors rather than one site, a released-results denominator rather than tests performed, a pre-declared rule with sensitivity arms rather than one undeclared operationalisation, dilution and cross-instrument confirmation added as trigger classes, and distributional comparison rather than central tendency. Unit of analysis (a re-analysis of the same analyte on the same aliquot, replacing the initial value before release), endpoint family and estimand for limbs (a) and (b) are the same. That is a corpus-and-instrument swap with added design rigour on an asked-and-answered question, which this ledger rejects as a disguised known even where the exact variant is unmeasured. Limb (c) is genuinely untouched by prior 1: no reference-interval recomputation, no threshold-crossing prevalence, no monitoring delta, no feasibility census. Against prior 2, the same selection mechanism, correctly named and formally treated, but a different unit, instrument, repeat act and estimand — a close neighbour on mechanism, not a kill. Against prior 3, the estimand is run-to-run agreement on a selected critical subset in an analytical-confirmation frame, not the share of released results nor any population estimand.

Vulnerability of that rejection, as the batch left it (retained; the rejection is withdrawn): the kill rests on reported, printed results rather than on anything unmeasured — not an expected value at a null, not an equivariance or symmetry argument, not a claim following from a design. One limb of it is algebraic and is marked as such: the restatement of the share on a released-results denominator, 701/(95,757-701) = 0.74%, is an ALGEBRAIC derivation from two published numbers under two assumptions (one repeat per repeated test; all tests released), not a bitwise or empirical match to the candidate's quantity, and it inherits the paper's 2,051-test inconsistency. Promotion requires: all four of — (1) PMC8137285, "Termination of Repeat Testing in Chemical Laboratories Based on Practice Guidelines: Examining the Effect of Rule-Based Repeat Testing in a Transplantation Center", converted to its DOI and read, since it is the one returned-and-unopened title whose promise overlaps limb (a) in general chemistry and it is the open novelty risk the next pass should close first; (2) R1's materiality bound repaired, because it conditions on "each analyte's own clinical decision limit" and the per-analyte published quantity that actually exists is ALLOWABLE BIAS — the Ricós database prints B(%) for roughly 400 entries and a decision limit for none of them, and for the many routine analytes whose only threshold is the laboratory's own reference limit the reclassification component is CIRCULAR, limb (c) simultaneously claiming that limit moves — so the component must be restricted in advance to analytes with an externally fixed decision limit and a published allowable-bias figure; (3) the significance field corrected, striking audience (iv): the EuBIVAS methods draw samples under a dedicated ten-week protocol from 91 healthy volunteers, freeze them and measure duplicates "within the same instrument run for a single day", using no released patient results at all, so the flagship source feeding the EFLM biological-variation database is immune to this mechanism by design and the "most direct casualty" claim about it is false; (4) one middleware vendor data dictionary or audit-trail specification opened, to settle whether release status and superseded runs are recorded per run — three of the four runs on this candidate have now failed to open any such document, which is the single clause the whole feasibility leg turns on. Two standing limitations to carry rather than cure: where the replacement is a PROCEDURE SWITCH the first-measurement substrate is a value-selected mixture of measurement procedures, so limb (c)'s reference-limit component compares across procedures rather than detecting bias within one and survives cleanly only for same-procedure reruns and confirmation repeats (R1's rule-wise decomposition already supplies the stratification that separates them); and two of R1's five named replacement causes are empty classes at the nearest own-field site.

## Verification of this entry's sources, and the late Gate 4 it forced (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Five fresh-context checkers read this entry's load-bearing sources (`VERIFY-bhattarai-unit-and-scope.md`, `VERIFY-bhattarai-numbers.md`, `VERIFY-bhattarai-tables.md`, `VERIFY-uq06-limb-c-delta-check.md`, `VERIFY-uq06-other-priors.md`), the fatal ground fell, and two further cold adversaries then ran on the Gate 0-3 record (`UQ-20261022-06-adversary-3.md`, `UQ-20261022-06-adversary-4-attack4.md`). **Verdict REVERSED: Rejected to Provisional.**

**1. Why the kill fell. Prior 1 does not print the candidate's quantity, and the failure is worse than a subset failure.** In the checker's words: "it is a different numerator on a different denominator with only partial overlap." Bhattarai & Thapa define a repeat in Methods as "a re-analysis of the same analyte from the original sample aliquot performed before the initial result was reported", and explicitly EXCLUDE "Tests repeated on clinician's request after initial reporting or on a new sample". The overlap fails in **both** directions. The 701 **misses** new-sample repeats, post-report repeats, cross-instrument confirmation (no second analyser exists in the paper, capture is one analyser's logs, and every search term for it is NOT PRESENT) and delta-check repeats (the word "delta" appears nowhere). And the 701 **includes** a class the candidate explicitly excludes: where the first run was voided by an analyser error flag (37.09%), a QC failure or being out of linearity (9.55%) the released value IS the first *valid* measurement, which is "up to 46.6% of the 701". The denominator is tests **PERFORMED**, confirmed against "ordered" and "released" on direct question. And the paper prints the share **REPEATED**, not the share **REPLACED**: "the replacement share is printed nowhere". The entry's own algebraic restatement, 701/(95,757-701) = 0.74%, was marked as its own arithmetic and is now moot, because the numerator is the wrong class.

**2. The paper is also internally inconsistent in three ways, which is why its composition cannot be reconstructed.** Three mutually inconsistent corpus totals (95,757, 93,706 and 88,706 — Table 3's printed total does not match the sum of its own nine rows); two different repeat rates for one numerator (0.73% and 0.75%); and a Methods inclusion list that is not the same four categories as the Results decomposition ("quality control failure" appears only in Methods, "out of linearity" only in Results). So "the composition of the 701 cannot be reconstructed from what the paper prints". Separately, no confidence interval or standard error accompanies the 0.73%; its 0.5–5% comparison range is carried by a CAP Today trade column plus Niu 2013; and the rule-wise decomposition is figure-backed rather than table-backed, only n=311 being printed.

**3. What DID verify, and the read-fidelity caveat is retired.** Two further checkers read the paper's front matter, its verbatim abstract string, all 11 spot-checked Table 2 values, Table 4's eight significant analytes (AST, HbA1c, PPBS, serum albumin, serum sodium, urea, beta-hCG, triglycerides) and the article type (Original Article, cross-sectional observational). The entry's recorded worry that "no rendered table was seen" is therefore discharged: the tables are as described. The paper is real, correctly cited and accurately quoted. It is simply not prior art for this question, which is the [[ledger-prior-art-fit]] pattern and not a citation error.

**4. One genuine prior on MECHANISM, which the entry must cite against itself.** Manathunga et al., arXiv:2602.14877v1, section 2.3, opened on the first attempt, states verbatim that conditional repetition "induces selection on the measurement error". Any claim that the threshold-conditioning insight is un-asked must name this paper. It is silent on all three downstream quantities: "reference interval" is absent, "prevalence" appears only as attributed to another author, and "delta" only as a cross-validation statistic. Its own estimand is a variance decomposition on below-cutoff donor haemoglobin, with 22% female and 25% male variance shares over 100,000 Vitalant donor visits. Two scope traps to avoid on numbers from this cluster: the 94.6% and 93.1% agreement figures live strictly inside the **below-cutoff stratum** (17,195/18,173 and 114,840/123,379, on first readings, not released results); and Niu 2013's 4.0% (24/601) is **pooled**, and its own authors decline to conclude from it, citing 2.1% within the analytical measurement range against 41.4% outside it. Prior 3's "repeat" is patient-level recurrence across specimens, a different event, and two of its three numbers are printed without denominators while the third does not reconcile with the paper's own totals.

**5. Limb (c) survives on shallow evidence, and the shallowness cuts the candidate's way.** No opened source computes a monitoring delta, a delta-check limit or a reference change value on **both** released results and first measurements. The two best instances were opened and both compute on one basis only, and that basis is a between-specimen pair of released results: an eight-year routine LIS extract fitted for RCVs with no mention of reruns, repeats, duplicate measurements on one specimen or corrected results anywhere in its front matter, abstract, Methods or Results as served; and delta-check limits derived from 434,927 patient pairs with no such mention in its served abstract. In the checker's words this literature "takes the released result of each specimen as an atom ... It never opens the atom" — which establishes the limb's premise as live practice at scale while establishing nothing about the question, "and that cuts in the candidate's favour". The corrected- and amended-report literature exists as citations and none of it opened, so its numbers are not established; and it would in any case be a **unit swap**, counting reports altered AFTER release where the candidate concerns a measurement replaced BEFORE release, which by construction leaves no corrected report behind.

**6. The late Gate 4: adversary 3, all eight attacks, nothing Unresolved (RPRPPPRP).** Its decisive move was to open the Gate 2 record's own number-one unopened risk: **Starks et al., "Use of middleware data to dissect and optimize hematology autoverification", J Pathol Inform 2021;12(1):19, doi:10.4103/jpi.jpi_89_20**, read in full. That source is the best possible test of the three strongest kills, being a laboratory team with the middleware audit data publishing in a pathology-informatics journal — and it closes all three in the candidate's favour. **Triviality, Resolved:** what the middleware yielded them was instrument FLAG data, not numeric superseded results, which "required extensive data cleanup and manual review"; the paper prints an autoverification rate (87.8% of 16,073 orders before, 93.5% of 91,692 after) and a manual-review rate (10,314 of 132,432 specimens, 7.8%) and, in the fetch's words, "No percentage of specimens re-run with PLT-F is printed." The afternoon query was available to them and did not produce limb (a). **Combinatorial novelty, Resolved:** their dominant rule reflexes from impedance platelet count to fluorescent platelet count when PLT-I < 70 k/mm3 (8.0% of flags holding both the CBC and the WBC differential), so the replacement is not a redraw from the same error distribution but a **switch of measurement procedure chosen as a function of the value** — which Manathunga's single-device truncation correction does not cover and for which the regression-to-the-mean sign argument delivers neither direction nor magnitude. **Reason for silence, Resolved:** the paper exhibits the mechanism rather than asserting it, reading the log as workload and rule efficiency, computing no reference interval, no prevalence and no delta, and never once using the phrase "delta check". Attack 2 is Partial on documents rather than on reasoning: fifteen queries in six vocabularies Gate 2 never tried (pharmaceutical GMP out-of-specification retesting, econometric and survey-methodology measurement error, semiconductor and industrial retest, forensic and anti-doping confirmation analysis, screening-epidemiology confirmatory prevalence, biological-variation metrology) found no rename, but three plausible owners were returned and not opened, chief among them **PMC8137285**, which is now promotion condition (1).

**7. The late Gate 4: adversary 4, attack 4 alone, clause by clause, Partial.** It enumerated R1's conditioning clauses and tested each against a document it opened. The clause everyone expects to break the question — that analyser and middleware logs retain and expose superseded measurements — is genuinely **CONTESTED on primary sources**: 42 CFR §493.1291, read in full, attaches its duties to **reports** ("All test reports or records of the information on the test reports must be maintained", and (k)(3) "Maintain duplicates of the original report, as well as the corrected report"), so no retention duty attaches to an unreported measurement; the Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care's retention standard, 9th edition 2022, gives four years at Table 1 item 1.5 for "records of analysis", textually "records ... from which the result is derived", below the report's seven; and the one documented middleware pipeline purges to an off-site archive monthly. **But R1's canonical wording already converts exactly that clause into a reported primary quantity**, and the record's multi-leg note already makes the feasibility census standalone — which is the difference between a presupposition and a measurand, and R1 is on the right side of it. Two genuine dents survive and neither is fatal: two of R1's five named replacement causes (cross-instrument confirmation, delta-check repeat) are **empty classes** at the nearest own-field site and a third (dilution) is not sourced as log-attributable anywhere opened, so the decomposition will report zeros it did not anticipate; and the materiality bound's "the analyte's clinical decision limit" presupposes a definiteness that Ozarda (Biochemia Medica 2016;26(1), doi:10.11613/BM.2016.001, read in full) denies, decision limits being "defined by consensus and vary among different populations" — which binds the analyte list rather than the question. Six clauses are **Unverified** on its own reading, three of them load-bearing for the fallback leg: that the log identifies WHICH run was released; that per-analyte published allowable-bias figures exist (its attempt at that table was refused at the source, so could-not-read and not not-found); and durable patient linkage in a middleware extract. It ran only attack 4, so Provisional is the ceiling it can certify.

**8. Why not Validated.** Gate 5 requires novelty at or above Medium **with the complete search record**, and the record is not complete: adversary 3 names thirteen returned-and-unopened items across six vocabularies, adversary 4 names twelve, and three of adversary 4's unverified clauses are load-bearing. Gate 5 also names Medium novelty with a close neighbour as Provisional in its own right, and Manathunga is that neighbour on mechanism. Significance is 2/3 with one audience refuted. The four promotion conditions above are what would close it; none is expensive, and the first is a single identifier conversion away.

ID: UQ-20261022-07
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — capped by one non-fatal objection at Gate 4 (attack 7, adversary 3) and by Medium novelty with very close neighbours. AMENDED ON POST-BATCH VERIFICATION 2026-10-22: five fresh-context checkers read the five load-bearing sources. The verdict is unchanged, but attack 7's status moves from Unresolved toward Partial (its stated ground fails on its own adjectives, while two sourced silence mechanisms the record never stated were found), and limb 1's novelty narrows against a fifth prior nobody in the batch had seen (Baxi et al. 2018). See the verification block at the end of this entry; where that block and the body conflict, the block governs.
Domain(s): Medicine — randomised-trial methodology and clinical pharmacology (target field). Adjacent swept: estimand science (ICH E9(R1)), bioanalytical/analytical toxicology, pharmacodynamic adherence verification, nutrition-biomarker trials, econometric noncompliance, anti-doping retrospective reanalysis, nonclinical control-sample contamination.

Question (canonical): For a frame of completed placebo-controlled trials declared before any specimen is pulled (study class licensed or obtainable outside the trial's own prescribing channel during the enrolment window; scheduled-visit control-arm biospecimens retained; release permissible under the governing consent): what is the proportion of control-arm participant-visits at which the study class is detected by one pre-declared validated assay whose limit of detection and false-positive rate are reported and whose detection window is stated against the visit interval; what is that positivity's concordance with the same participant's protocol-recorded concomitant medication; and what is the signed difference between the trial's reported primary estimate and the estimate under one contamination-adjusted estimand declared before any assay result is seen — reported with the share of the declared frame whose governance refused release, so the denominator is auditable?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one reformulation permitted at Gate 1, scored as canonical. V1 (intake) asked the same object less tightly: "In randomised placebo-controlled trials of a drug class that is simultaneously obtainable outside the trial, what fraction of placebo-arm participants has the active class detectable in their own stored trial biospecimens at scheduled visits, and by how much does that measured off-protocol exposure attenuate the trial's estimated treatment effect?" V2 changes specification only: visit-level denominator, assay error characterisation, estimand pre-declaration, governance-refusal share as a reported quantity.

Alternative formulations:
- How many people in the placebo group are actually taking the real drug — measured in their blood rather than asked on a form — and what does that do to the trial's answer?
- Treating off-protocol exposure as a measurable contamination of the control condition, what is its assayed prevalence per visit and what is the effect estimate under one pre-declared contamination-adjusted estimand?

Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion. Trials verify adherence in the active arm biochemically and ascertain control-arm exposure by self-report on a concomitant-medication CRF — inverting the burden of proof exactly where the comparison lives. Rytgaard et al. (arXiv:2605.05859, 8 May 2026), building time-varying concomitant-medication estimands on LEADER, renders control-arm access to the study class as nil rather than as a quantity (clipped fragment; whether that is a modelling assumption or a descriptive claim is UNVERIFIED). Two sponsor protocols opened at Gate 4 (SOUL NCT03914326, STEP-HFpEF NCT04788511, tirzepatide NCT04311411) show the asymmetry in the documents themselves: drug-concentration sampling sits in a pharmacokinetics section while outside use of the class is prohibited by instruction and ascertained by eCRF review. The intake's blanket negative ("no study has assayed control-arm samples for the study class") was withdrawn at Gate 2 (iPrEx) and is further falsified at Gate 4 (ASCEND, below).

Presuppositions:
1. Scheduled-visit control-arm specimens exist and are releasable outside the original protocol. SPLIT. "Specimens exist": SUPPORTED by one opened protocol (NCT04311411 PK footnote exempts only the liraglutide arm; "Nonpharmacogenetic stored samples" unrestricted by arm). "Releasable": UNVERIFIED — zero consent forms, biobank policies or release SOPs opened by anyone. In SOUL the future-research series exists only under a separate optional consent scoped on its face to "biosamples for biomarkers and genetic analyses", with the biomarker row "Only applicable for the year two visit (V 12)"; the governing retention appendices (SOUL App. 7, STEP-HFpEF App. 6) COULD NOT BE READ.
2. An adequate assay exists for the class. SPLIT. ESTABLISHED for small-molecule ARVs (HPTN HRMS deck: "LOD = 2-20 ng/mL for all ARV drugs"). For the motivating class, STEP-HFpEF's flowchart carries a scheduled-visit row "Semaglutide plasma concentration (10.2)", so a validated measurement exists in this trial family — but which arm is sampled is UNVERIFIED (PK section truncated). Falsified for aspirin, where a ~20-minute half-life makes a drug assay impossible and the instrument clause collapses onto a pharmacodynamic marker.
3. Detection implies ingestion, not cross-reactivity or sample contamination. UNTESTED — no specificity source opened; the EMA guideline on test-substance contamination of control samples (CPMP/SWP/1094/04) was surfaced but not opened and is nonclinical.
4. Off-protocol exposure is non-zero somewhere in the frame. ESTABLISHED at Gate 4, where Gate 2 had it WEAKENED by iPrEx's out-of-regime zero: ASCEND prints placebo-arm biochemical positivity of "5/74 (7%)" overall and "4/9 (44%)" among placebo participants recorded as non-adherent.
5. Measured exposure can be carried into a pre-declared estimand without reopening the primary analysis. SUPPORTED by existence of machinery (Rytgaard et al.), not by demonstration.
6. Control-arm off-protocol use is not already captured adequately by CRF reporting. HALF-ESTABLISHED. Large assay-versus-self-report discordance is published for ARVs at enrolment ("45 (46.9%) of 96 'ARV naive' index participants ... were on ART", HPTN 052), but on pre-randomisation index participants in non-placebo designs.
7. The candidate's measurement has not been performed. FALSIFIED, and more sharply than Gate 2 recorded: not only iPrEx's qualitative zero but ASCEND's printed prevalence with denominators. What survives is the narrower claim stated under novelty.

What would count as an answer: For the pre-declared frame — the assayed prevalence of class-positive control-arm participant-visits with LOD and false-positive rate; the concordance of positivity with that participant's own CRF; and the primary estimate re-computed under one pre-declared contamination-adjusted estimand plus one sensitivity arm; all with the governance-refusal share reported so the denominator is auditable. A prevalence indistinguishable from the assay's false-positive rate is a clean negative, declared in advance to be an answer. An interval too wide to separate material from immaterial against a pre-declared margin is declared in advance to be an answer about feasibility and governance, not a null.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 38 distinct queries — 11 at Gate 2, 9 per adversary, all 27 adversary queries in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use; all three adversaries executed their Disguise sweeps in full. Full lists: ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0633/UQ-20261022-07-record.md and the three adversary files in that folder. Most informative:
- Record q10 (mandatory own-field, own-words obvious title): "unreported use of study drug among placebo recipients prevalence impact on efficacy estimate randomised trial drug levels measured" → only the ACTIVE-PLACEBO literature (Cochrane MR000055); the obvious title does not exist in the candidate's own field.
- Record q3 (mandatory already-computed-fraction query) → no published control-arm prevalence with a denominator surfaced; this miss is what Gate 4 corrected.

- Adversary-2 q5 "aspirin trial placebo group non-study aspirin use detected serum thromboxane B2 urinary 11-dehydro proportion of placebo participants" and adversary-3 D1 (same vocabulary, independently) → ASCEND urinary-thromboxane paper, P1 below. Two independent adversaries reached it from the pharmacodynamic-adherence-verification vocabulary that Gate 2 never swept.
- Adversary-1 A9, aimed at the answer form ("treatment effect re-estimated adjusting for drug concentration measured in placebo arm") → returned the record's own Simes/FIELD prior from four separate hosts and nothing nearer; positive evidence the attractor was correctly identified.
- Adversary-1 A7 (protocol/biobank regulatory vocabulary) → the two openable instances of the document kind presupposition 1 depends on.

Record q5/q10, adversary-1 A9, adversary-2 q8 and adversary-3 D3 were aimed there; the estimand and econometric literatures model control-arm uptake and ascertain it from records, never from assay.
- Residual retrieval gaps that bear on the grade, each a gap and not an absence: PMID 9160496 "Adjusting for noncompliance and contamination in randomized clinical trials" COULD NOT BE READ (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov served a reCAPTCHA interstitial — new route fact: the NCBI interstitial is not confined to PMC; no publisher route tried); the nutrition-contamination cluster (D-Health, D2d, SUN-D, omega-3 biostatus) unopened by both adversaries that nominated it as the likeliest home of a published limb-1-plus-limb-3 analogue; iPrEx Supplementary Fig. S5 (P3's denominator) unopened; three adjustment-methods PDFs (White Rose eprints 43/1/355, Birmingham sim.8958, NIHR 2001444) unopened.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Parish S, Buck G, Aung T, Mafham M, Clark S, Hill M, Collins R, Bowman L, Armitage J (ASCEND Study Collaborative Group). "Effect of low-dose aspirin on urinary 11-dehydro-thromboxane B2 in the ASCEND randomized controlled trial." Trials 2023;24:166. DOI 10.1186/s13063-023-07198-z. READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT (Oxford ORA version-of-record PDF), independently opened by two adversaries. Unit: one participant's mailed spot urine at a single occasion "a mean of 2 years after randomization", in a random sample of 152 (74 placebo) plus 198 purposively adherent (105 placebo) of 15,480 randomised. Endpoint: "effective suppression", U-TXM <1500 pg/mg creatinine. Comparator: aspirin 100 mg vs placebo. Estimand: proportion suppressed by allocated arm and adherence stratum. Instrument: competitive ELISA (AspirinWorks, Corgenix) for a thromboxane metabolite — a pharmacodynamic consequence of COX-1 inhibition, NOT a detection assay for the class; no LOD, no LOQ, no false-positive rate, cut-off justified by reference to a commercial kit's 510(k). NUMBER AND WHERE PRINTED: Results, first paragraph — "82% allocated aspirin versus 7% allocated placebo achieved effective suppression of U-TXM (Table 1)"; "Only 3% of participants adherent to placebo had effective suppression"; Table 1 placebo column — 5/74 (7%), 1/63 (2%), 4/105 (4%), 5/168 (3%), and non-adherent 4/9 (44%). Regime: aspirin obtainable over the counter, for the trial's own indication, throughout 2005-2017 conduct; specimens frozen; assay retrospective but inside the protocol, so no governance-release question arose.
P2. Rytgaard HCW, Fong E, Tarp JM, Gerds TA, van der Laan MJ, Ravn H. "Estimation of treatment effects in presence of differential use of post-randomization concomitant medication with time-to-event outcomes." arXiv:2605.05859, 8 May 2026. READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT (arXiv PDF); existence spot-checked by a second adversary. The METHOD-owning prior. Unit: participant with visit-indexed indicator Z_k = 1 "if the patient initiates or continues to use insulin at any time between visits k - 1 and k". Endpoint: LEADER three-component MACE at visit 8, "42 months after randomization" (the paper is internally inconsistent — section 2 defines cardiovascular death alone; reproduced as served). Comparator: liraglutide vs placebo. Estimand: risk differences under static, dynamic and stochastic time-varying interventions. Instrument: trial-recorded initiation/discontinuation dates; no assay. NUMBER IT PRINTS: of 5,171 not on insulin at baseline, "30% initiated insulin ... in the GLP1 arm whereas 47% initiated insulin in the placebo arm" — a control-arm drop-in prevalence with a denominator, for a DIFFERENT class, by record.
P3. Grant RM et al. "Preexposure Chemoprophylaxis for HIV Prevention in Men Who Have Sex with Men." NEJM 2010 (iPrEx). READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT via institutional mirror (kimirina.org PDF); Supplementary Appendix NOT read. Unit: matched seronegative control specimens inside a seroconversion case-control drug-level subgroup. Endpoint: drug detection as an exposure variable. Estimand: within-active-arm risk reduction conditional on detection. NUMBER FOR THE CANDIDATE'S LIMB: a zero without a denominator — "No drug was detected in any plasma or cell specimens from subjects in the placebo group"; the specimen count is referred to unread Fig. S5. Regime: TDF/FTC licensed for treatment but approved for prophylaxis nowhere, so the class was NOT obtainable for the trial's own indication.
(Simes et al., PLoS ONE 2010;5(1):e8580, FIELD — read in full at Gate 2 and spot-checked by an adversary — is demoted to fourth: same comparator structure and adjustment ambition, but the instrument is a clinic medication record and the adjusted exposures are OTHER classes; its printed "fibrate (6%)" is a share of patients on lipid-lowering therapy, not of the placebo arm, and must not be read as the candidate's fraction.)

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs P1 (ASCEND): this is the close neighbour, and it answers limb 1 in substance for one class. Differences, verified by read: instrument (pharmacodynamic surrogate with no LOD and no false-positive rate vs a detection assay for the class, with suppression attributable to other NSAIDs); grain (participant at one mailed occasion in a ~2% subsample vs control-arm participant-visits); limb 2 is DEFINED and never counted — Methods define non-adherence to include "or known to be taking non-study aspirin" and Figure 1 carries the category "Placebo aspirin, non-adherent (took non-study aspirin)", but no count is printed for it, which per the ledger's rule is a definition and a classification axis, not an evaluation; limb 3 is verified ABSENT, with no sentence on dilution or attenuation and the 12% primary-outcome reduction quoted from the main ASCEND report rather than re-estimated; limb 4 does not arise. For aspirin specifically the instrument difference is not available to the candidate (half-life ~20 minutes), so on that class the surviving difference is grain, error characterisation and limbs 2-3 only.
- vs P2 (Rytgaard et al.): the candidate is this estimand family applied to an intercurrent event the paper excludes by construction and ascertained by an instrument it does not use. It prints 47% control-arm drop-in for insulin; nobody prints the analogous figure for the study class by a detection assay at visit grain.
- vs P3 (iPrEx): performs the measurement and prints a qualitative zero with its denominator referred to an unread appendix; no prevalence, no concordance, no re-estimation, and obtained in a regime where the class was unobtainable for the trial's own indication, so it bounds nothing here.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds. Not High: limb 1 has demonstrably been measured and published twice on a control arm — qualitatively by P3, and with printed denominators by P1 in a class more freely obtainable than the motivating one — so the record's surviving sentence ("no source prints the control-arm fraction with a denominator") is falsified in substance and must be reworded to "by an assay that detects the study class, at participant-visit grain, with LOD and false-positive rate reported". Not Low: the record names P1's NUMBER and where it is printed, and that number is a pharmacodynamic surrogate at participant-occasion grain, which is an instrument gap plus a granularity gap rather than the candidate quantity; limb 2 is classified without a count in P1 (a definition, not an evaluation); and limb 3 is verified absent in P1 and found nowhere across 38 queries. The grade is Medium with a very close neighbour, which is itself a Provisional condition under Gate 5.

Significance — consequence: If assayed prevalence exceeds the assay's false-positive rate materially, placebo-controlled trials of a widely obtainable class carry a bias of known sign (toward the null) that is currently neither measured by a detection assay nor declared, and the estimand framework has no category for an intercurrent event ascertained by assay. If it is indistinguishable from the false-positive rate, the worry is retired on evidence and CRF ascertainment is licensed on measurement rather than assumption. The governance-refusal share measures, auditably, how much of the trial enterprise's own stored evidence is unavailable for methodological self-examination. Trimmed by Gate 4: the one printed magnitude in a maximally obtainable class is small (7% overall, 2-4% among placebo-adherent), which points toward immaterial, and the "neither measured nor declared" wording is falsified — ASCEND measured and declared it in a methods journal. No adversary converted those percentages into an attenuation, correctly declining to do its own arithmetic on a surrogate with no stated uncertainty, so the "signed, bounded correction" remains a promise rather than a demonstration.
Significance — audience: (i) the estimand community, which demonstrably builds time-varying interventions on control-arm concomitant medication in this exact trial family; (ii) regulators reading estimands under ICH E9(R1), where an assay-ascertained intercurrent event has no slot and the bias runs against the sponsor; (iii) biobank governance committees and IRBs, now documented rather than hypothetical — the opened protocols show a real optional-consent biobank object with a named scope; (iv) meta-analysts and HTA bodies pooling estimates from the availability window; (v) bioanalytical laboratories of the HPTN type, independently re-surfaced by an adversary in a vocabulary the record did not use. Access, not audience reality, is the pressure point: in every opened instance the sole custodian is the sponsor, the party with the least to gain.
Significance — fecundity: Makes askable what the contamination prior should be for other obtainable classes; whether assay-based control-arm monitoring belongs in protocols as design rather than audit; what consent language would license a contamination audit without reopening a primary analysis; whether measured attenuation reconciles any part of the trial-versus-real-world effect gap; and whether contamination tracks availability for the trial's own INDICATION rather than availability as a molecule. Gate 4 adds a sharper one: whether the control-arm figure, where it has been measured, is routinely reported as a comparator and then never carried — P1 and P3 both show that pattern.
Significance — anchoring: (a) the ICH E9(R1) intercurrent-event taxonomy, which classifies by what happened and not by how it was ascertained; (b) the drop-in and treatment-switching adjustment literature, which ascertains exposure from records throughout and whose single most on-point title here COULD NOT BE READ; (c) the active-placebo literature, which addresses the distinct presupposition of what the placebo CONTAINS; (d) the biochemical-verification tradition in smoking-cessation trials, and now the pharmacodynamic-adherence-verification tradition in cardiology, which is where the close neighbour was found; (e) the unexplained placebo-arm improvement anomaly in cardiometabolic and obesity trials.

Reason for silence: This field is the entry's weakest, and an adversary returned Unresolved on it. The record claimed a four-mechanism conjunction: disciplinary boundary (primary), incentive gap, governance friction, new availability regime. Three are contradicted by one opened instance. An academic trial-methodology group pre-specified a placebo-arm biochemical comparison, assayed frozen control-arm specimens and published the placebo-arm figure open-access in a trials-methodology journal, so "no one's remit spans them" is false and "the analysis has no natural funder" is false in that instance; and aspirin was obtainable outside the trial's prescribing channel, for the trial's own indication, throughout 2005-2017, so dating the testable regime to the 2023-2026 GLP-1 supply window is wrong as a general claim. Governance friction survives only for retrospective release, since P1 shows the measurement can be taken inside the protocol. The mechanism the surviving silence needs is a different one, which the adversary itself named: the control-arm number is a by-product of the adherence question, reported as a specificity comparator and then dropped — exactly the pattern in P1 (category defined, never counted, no dilution sentence) and P3 (one clause, never a prevalence). That mechanism is coherent and would explain silence on limbs 2 and 3, but it is a rewrite of the field rather than a response from the record, so the attack stands Unresolved and the ledger's clause bites: the novelty finding is suspect and the field must be rebuilt before promotion.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Three adversaries ran all eight attacks each on the Gate 0-3 record, none reading another's log; all three executed their Disguise sweeps (9 new-vocabulary queries each, 27 total), so Disguise is verified as executed and is not an unrun check. Statuses below are the worst returned by any adversary; full logs in ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0633/UQ-20261022-07-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md.
1 | Triviality — the three limbs are deducible: bound prevalence from prescription databases, get attenuation from a dilution formula; and the answer is now twice measured as small | The algebra takes prevalence as its input and that input is the unmeasured quantity; prescription databases do not cover compounded and telehealth supply; a binary per-visit detect supplies neither dose nor duration, which the time-varying estimand needs; P1 shows the input is not a scalar (7%, 3%, 2%, 4%, 44% for one arm in one table); limb 2 is derivable from no aggregate. The adversary that pressed the algebra flagged that it opened no primary source on contamination-induced attenuation and withdrew that leg from carrying a kill | Partial (Resolved by two of three)
2 | Disguise — a renamed known in contamination-of-the-control-group, drop-in, nutrition-biomarker, diverted-supply, econometric always-taker, anti-doping-reanalysis, nonclinical control-sample or pharmacodynamic-adherence vocabulary | 27 new-vocabulary queries. The pharmacodynamic-adherence vocabulary, unswept at Gate 2, publishes limb 1 with printed denominators (P1), so the record's surviving novelty sentence is falsified in substance. But P1's instrument is a surrogate with no LOD and no false-positive rate, its unit is a participant at one occasion in a small subsample, it prints no limb-2 count and limb 3 is verified absent; the EMA nonclinical guideline concerns animal-facility cross-contamination and was not opened, so it grounds nothing. One limb of three is a known question renamed; the conjunction is not | Partial — residual unverified fringe: PMID 9160496 COULD NOT BE READ, and the nutrition-contamination cluster both adversaries named as the likeliest home of a limb-1-plus-limb-3 analogue was not opened. Blocks Validated; does not kill
3 | Combinatorial novelty — bioanalytical chemistry x estimand methodology bolted together | A specific interface problem, named from opened documents: scheduled visits are months apart while a plasma assay sees days to weeks, so visit positivity is a snapshot while the estimand needs an indicator over the whole inter-visit interval ("initiates or continues to use ... at any time between visits k-1 and k"). V2's requirement that the detection window be stated against the visit interval shows the generator saw this. P1 further shows the existing control-arm instrument yields a threshold crossing with no dose, no timing and an uncharacterised false-positive rate — nothing the estimand machinery can consume | Resolved (all three)
4 | Presupposition failure — the question conditions on a releasable scheduled-visit control-arm specimen series, and on the measurement never having been made | No presupposition shown false; several tested in the candidate's favour. "Obtainable outside the trial's channel" holds and is instanced. "Specimens exist" is SUPPORTED by an opened protocol whose PK footnote exempts only one non-placebo arm. Presupposition 4 moves from WEAKENED to ESTABLISHED by P1's 7% and 4/9. Presupposition 7 is falsified but sits in the novelty rationale, not in the conditioning clauses. Against the candidate: in SOUL the releasable series exists only under a separate optional consent scoped to "biosamples for biomarkers and genetic analyses" with the biomarker row "Only applicable for the year two visit (V 12)" — a granularity gap against a visit-denominated question, and an obstacle (purpose outside the consent's stated scope) for which limb 4's "refused release" category has no slot | Partial (all three) — the release clause recorded as Unverified, not failed: zero consent forms, biobank policies or release SOPs opened by anyone, and the governing retention appendices COULD NOT BE READ
5 | Vagueness — pre-declared estimand, clean-negative condition and feasibility clause mean no evidence can embarrass the question; and the frame criterion is unquantified | V2 pins unit, instrument, error characterisation, threshold reporting, estimand and clean-negative condition, so within one declared protocol exactly one number is the answer and a stated margin decides materiality; P1's five numbers for one arm are a consequence of post hoc subgrouping, which pre-declaration forbids | Partial — two sourced residuals: the snapshot-to-interval bridging model is load-bearing and unconstrained, so two honest teams could pre-declare different estimands and report different signed differences from the same data; and with P1 in hand the unquantified availability criterion selects the answer (pick aspirin and limb 1 is already ~7%; pick GLP-1 and it is unmeasured)
6 | Significance inflation — the audiences are decorative; and the audience that holds the number did nothing with it | Three audiences tested and real: the performing party was independently re-surfaced in a vocabulary the record did not use, the method-owning group demonstrably builds these estimands in this trial family, and the governance audience is documented by opened protocols. P1's object was active-arm suppression and the placebo figure fell out as the comparator, so inaction at 7% for aspirin does not predict inaction where prevalence might be an order of magnitude larger | Partial — the consequence claim is falsified as worded and the only printed magnitude points toward immaterial; significance trimmed to 2/3
7 | Reason for silence — three of the four stated mechanisms are contradicted by one opened instance, and the testable regime is dated two decades late | The repair is a different mechanism than any the record states: the control-arm figure is a by-product of adherence verification, reported as a comparator and then dropped (the pattern in both P1 and P3). Coherent, and it would explain silence on limbs 2 and 3 | Unresolved (adversary 3; Partial from the other two) — a rewrite of the field rather than a response from it. Non-fatal, and the trigger for the Provisional ceiling

Per-visit positivity is a convolution of prevalence, dosing recency and detection window — P1's active-arm result is explicitly conditioned on a last tablet "more than 12 h before urine sampling" — so the question narrows under analysis rather than dissolving | Partial — on the one biobank instance opened, the live path converts a pharmacology question into a governance audit, a less significant question than the one scored; and the adjustment literature that would decide this attack was returned unopened by two adversaries

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection: One opened paper — Parish et al., Trials 2023;24:166, read in full and reached independently by two adversaries from a vocabulary Gate 2 never swept — publishes the candidate's limb-1 quantity with denominators ("82% allocated aspirin versus 7% allocated placebo achieved effective suppression of U-TXM"; Table 1 placebo cells 5/74, 5/168, 4/9) in a placebo-controlled trial of a class obtainable over the counter for the trial's own indication throughout its conduct, and in doing so contradicts three of the record's four reasons for silence and dates the testable regime two decades before the window the record claims made the question askable. This kill has three legs and they are not equally sourced: (a) the sweep gap in the pharmacodynamic-adherence-verification vocabulary; (b) limb 1 published with denominators; (c) the collapse of the disciplinary-boundary, incentive-gap and new-regime mechanisms. Legs (a) and (b) can be argued down, because the instrument is a pharmacodynamic surrogate and not a detection assay for the class, the grain is a participant at one mailed occasion rather than participant-visits, no LOD or false-positive rate is reported, limb 2 is defined and never counted, and limb 3 is verified absent. The leg the verdict stands on if those two fall is (c), which needs only the paper's existence and provenance and not the match of its instrument. Leg (c) is the one that cost the entry its promotion, and the record's own nominated standing leg — attenuation — is the leg that holds: no source anyone opened carries assay-measured control-arm study-class exposure into a re-estimated effect.
Promotion requires: all four of — (1) the reason-for-silence field rebuilt around the by-product-of-adherence-verification mechanism, with the disciplinary-boundary, incentive-gap and new-regime mechanisms withdrawn or restricted to the retrospective-release case, which is what would move attack 7 from Unresolved; (2) the novelty sentence reworded to "no source prints the control-arm fraction across scheduled PARTICIPANT-VISITS, by a PRE-DECLARED detection assay reporting both its LOD and its false-positive rate, with the detection window stated against the visit interval", with Parish et al. 2023 AND Baxi et al. 2018 entered as priors and Medium re-argued on that wording — verification falsified the "detects the study class" clause as the distinguishing one, because Baxi prints 1/41 by LC/MS/MS for the study drug itself with a stated LLOQ, so what remains unpublished is the grain plus the two assay-characterisation figures, not the class-detecting assay; (3) the two unverified Disguise residuals closed — PMID 9160496 read by a non-NCBI publisher route, and the nutrition-contamination cluster (D-Health, D2d, SUN-D, omega-3 biostatus) swept; (4) two or three actual consent forms or biobank release SOPs opened, plus the governing retention appendices (SOUL App. 7, STEP-HFpEF App. 6, via a mid-document fetch offset below 110,443 characters), to move presupposition 1's release clause off Unverified.

Vulnerability of the grounds that cap this entry (recorded because the ledger requires it): the Provisional ceiling rests partly on things nobody has measured, and the entry says so rather than letting them pass as results. (i) The triviality objection's second leg — that limb 3 follows from limb 1 by a dilution formula under non-differential contamination — is an ALGEBRAIC identity derived from a design, not a bitwise or empirical finding; the adversary that raised it opened no primary source on contamination-induced attenuation and withdrew the leg, and the attenuation it predicts has never been measured for this object in any source anyone opened. (ii) Attack 4's consent-scope leg rests on reading "biosamples for biomarkers and genetic analyses" as exhaustive of the consented purpose — an inference from a footnote about what a document permits, with the governing appendix unread; only its granularity leg (footnote n, a direct quotation fixing the biomarker series to one visit) stands on quoted text. (iii) Presupposition 1's release clause and presupposition 3's specificity premise are Unverified in both directions: zero instances of the governing document kind were opened across all four agents. The single unopened source most likely to settle the capping objection is PMID 9160496, "Adjusting for noncompliance and contamination in randomized clinical trials", which is the one directly on-point new title any agent surfaced, which bears on both the triviality algebra and attack 8, and which failed only on route (the NCBI reCAPTCHA interstitial, with no publisher host tried); the nutrition-contamination cluster is the next most likely, because it is where a published limb-1-plus-limb-3 analogue would sit if one exists.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open two or three actual consent forms and specimen-release policies from trials in the frame, before any assay question is raised, and see whether the document kind supports retrospective release at all — the cheapest check in the record, unopened by the generator and by all three adversaries, and the one whose failure would retire the question on feasibility rather than on novelty.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — status is Provisional, so the ledger still claims the question as un-asked and no row belongs in ledger/routed-open-problems.md; by construction a Provisional is never routed. This is a recommendation about what a later step should do, not a report of anything done to that file.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Five fresh-context checkers were each handed one claim and its source, with the entry's citations but not its reasoning. Logs: `VERIFY-uq07-silence-mechanism.md`, `VERIFY-parish-ascend-numbers.md`, `VERIFY-parish-instrument-grade.md`, `VERIFY-iprex-placebo-drug-levels.md`, `VERIFY-rytgaard-and-simes.md` in this folder. **Verdict unchanged: Provisional.** One attack status improves, one novelty limb narrows, and four quotations need repair.

**1. Attack 7 (reason for silence) moves from Unresolved toward Partial, and not for the reason the entry gives.** The attack's stated ground fails on its own adjectives: "pre-specified" is absent from Parish; "published two decades before the entry's claimed regime" is false of both publication dates (2018 and 2023); and "biochemical positivity for an over-the-counter class" describes no single source, since Parish's instrument does not detect the class and Baxi's class is not over the counter. So the strong conclusion drawn from it — that there is no credible reason for silence — is not supported. The weak form survives and needs none of those adjectives: two of the record's four stated mechanisms are contradicted by published instances ("no one's remit spans them" is false of two groups; "the analysis has no natural funder" is false, both figures being published open access by the trials' own investigators), and the record's dating of the testable regime to 2023–2026 is wrong as a general claim, the measurements having been taken on specimens from mid-2000s trials. **But two sourced mechanisms the record never stated now exist**, which is what an Unresolved attack 7 denied: Jacot et al. 2018 states that LC–MS/MS "can only be done on samples from the treatment group of a placebo-controlled study" and that measuring "adherence in both placebo and drug arms ... would better inform future trial designs" — the field treats the placebo arm as un-assayable in principle — and ICH E9(R1) names the intercurrent event across five strategies with no word for measuring it, so no guidance makes the measurement anyone's obligation. The ledger's rule that a missing silence mechanism makes the novelty finding itself suspect is therefore no longer triggered. The status change is conditional on the reason-for-silence field being rebuilt around these two mechanisms, which is promotion condition (1) and is unchanged.

**2. A fifth prior nobody in this batch had seen. Baxi et al. 2018** prints **1/41** by LC/MS/MS for the study drug itself, with a stated LLOQ, open access. It is in neither the Gate 0–3 record nor any of the three adversary logs, and it falsifies adversary 3's proposed novelty wording. What survives is narrower and is now promotion condition (2): the control-arm fraction across scheduled **participant-visits**, by a **pre-declared** assay reporting **both** its LOD and its false-positive rate, with the detection window stated against the visit interval. No source read by anyone prints a false-positive rate, and neither instance uses participant-visits.

**3. Parish et al. 2023 — the 7% is real, and it is the wrong number for a cap.** The 5/74 (7%) is printed, intention-to-treat, in the **random** sub-sample at U-TXM < 1500 pg/mg creatinine, so the purposive-sample objection does not reach it and any entry wording claiming no such quantity has been printed is refuted. But **4 of its 5 positives were already flagged non-adherent by the participant's own form** (4/9, 44%), so the 7% is overwhelmingly declared non-adherence rather than concealed exposure. A cap on *undetected* control-arm exposure belongs on the adherent-stratum cell: **1/63 (2%)** in the random sample, or **5/168 (3%)** pooled — and the pooled figure is mostly purposive and is not a prevalence. Both rest on 1 and 5 events with no uncertainty supplied by the source: the paper prints no confidence interval on the 7%. Two quotation repairs: the 82%/7% string must carry its opening clause **"During follow-up, in the intention-to-treat analysis of the random sample,"**, and the "Only 3%" figure must carry its denominator of 168 adherent placebo participants, 105 of them purposively selected. The paper also closes neither of the two things this entry's gap turns on: it prints no agreement measure against the participant's own form (the 1/63 discordance is the reader's subtraction, not the paper's figure), and it never re-estimates ASCEND's effect for the measured positivity — it cites the published 12% proportional reduction and infers sufficiency, which is an inference from a published effect, not an adjusted analysis.

**4. Parish's instrument grade holds on the source's own text, with two grounds requiring repair.** The analyte is "a stable metabolite of thromboxane A2" normalised to creatinine, so the instrument is a pharmacodynamic surrogate and the paper nowhere claims to detect aspirin or an aspirin metabolite — the entry's core distinction is the paper's own. The main text prints no LOD, no LOQ, no false-positive rate and no specificity figure, four separately checked absences whose only assay number is a duplicate reproducibility of 0.98; the threshold is named for a pharmacodynamic state ("effective suppression"), adopted by bare citation with the hedge "taken as"; the grain is one participant-sampling, not participant-occasion; and the paper characterises no false-positive mechanism at all, every mechanism it discusses running the other way, which strengthens the entry's defence beyond how the entry puts it. Repairs: **strike "other NSAIDs"** from the defence or source it elsewhere, Parish does not say it; **downgrade "pre-specified"** to "collected inside the trial's protocol and consent, assayed by the trial's own group" unless pre-specification is sourced from the protocol or the DAP, which touches attack 7(a) directly; and qualify the four absences as **main text, Supplementary Methods not opened**. On the release presupposition this paper is evidence neither way — the assay was run by the trial's own group on its own frozen aliquots under its own consent, and no release to an outside party occurred — so presupposition (iii) stays **Unverified**, unchanged.

**5. iPrEx — the quoted zero is verbatim, but it is omitted, not deferred, and it is a subgroup.** The string is genuine and is a whole sentence, reproduced with both flanking sentences, so it is not a grammar-at-the-cut misquotation. Two framings must change. The entry must not say the count is "deferred to Fig. S5": it is **omitted**, and Fig. S5 is cited for the matching scheme, so "deferred" implies a number that exists one hop away, which the read does not support. And the zero must not be treated as a trial-wide placebo-arm figure: its regime is a prespecified, site-matched, case-anchored **case–control subgroup**, where the zero is modest and the missing N is a reporting gap, whereas trial-wide it would be a much stronger claim the paper does not make. Sub-claim (d) is a clean **no**: the paper never re-estimates its 44% (95% CI 15 to 63) for placebo-arm exposure and never discusses placebo participants obtaining antiretrovirals outside the trial, and its conditional 92%/95% figures are a within-FTC–TDF contrast — so the chain of unprinted denominator to unexamined assumption to widely cited conditional efficacy, which is the substance of this entry, survives. One live uncertainty to carry honestly: the Supplementary Appendix was unreachable at nejm.org here and unreachable at PMC by routing policy, so **Fig. S5 is unchecked** and the entry may not assert that no denominator exists anywhere. Also carried forward as the source's own: a 22-of-43 versus 22/42 discrepancy, a "Serum"/plasma title mismatch, and front matter unverified at this mirror because it is the online-first version.

**6. Rytgaard cannot foreclose this candidate, because it assumes the candidate's premise away.** Source 1 is real, open and fully readable, and is a genuine methodological neighbour — an estimand-and-TMLE apparatus for differential post-randomisation use of a concomitant medication of **another** class. On control-arm access to the **study** class it is not merely silent: Section 3.1 **assumes the exposure to be zero** in the control arm ("the active treatment is not available") and Section 7 cites that absence as a virtue of the trial it analyses. If any part of this entry rested on Source 1 to dispose of the candidate, that rest is misplaced; the honest statement in the other direction is that the candidate's premise is exactly the assumption this paper leaves unexamined and unsourced. Its endpoint inconsistency is real and reproducible at both locations and is a defect in the paper itself. **Simes et al. is COULD NOT READ**, not NOT FOUND: the article exists and is open but would not serve through the one permitted route inside budget, so it must be carried as unverified, its (f) quotation must not be treated as confirmed, and a re-check should go to journals.plos.org alone on a fresh budget, one page at a time, reading the published Correction before quoting any figure.

**What verification did not reach, so the entry does not claim it.** Whether the measurement has ever been done pre-2000 (tuberculosis, hypertension, aspirin cardiology — all unreached); whether CONSORT or any FDA or EMA guidance mentions assay-measured control-arm exposure (CONSORT could not be read, the rest unchecked); and the nutrition-contamination cluster that adversary 3 named as the single most likely home of a limb-1-plus-limb-3 analogue, which neither the adversary nor the checker opened. The frequency question is therefore bounded by budget and is not answered in general.
