ID: UQ-20261022-08
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Medium novelty with one very close neighbour (N1); nothing Unresolved on any attack. AMENDED ON POST-BATCH VERIFICATION 2026-10-22: five fresh-context checkers read the load-bearing sources, and the unreadability blocker is STRUCK. Two of the three sources the entry called unreadable at every route converted from PMCID to DOI in a single call and then opened, one of them being this entry's own fourth prior listed twice under a different identifier. Neither prints the candidate's quantity, so the verdict is unchanged, but the entry's stated reason for its cap was wrong. See the verification block at the end of this entry; where that block and the body conflict, the block governs.
Domain(s): Medicine — clinical informatics / health-systems data infrastructure (target field). Adjacent: digital preservation (method vocabulary), RWE regulatory science, research-network data curation (OHDSI/Sentinel/PCORnet). Source method: cross-field transplant.
Question (canonical): For a health system that replaced its EHR, with a queryable legacy archive and a declared look-back window W before cutover date T: (i) per pre-declared fact class (problem-list entries, medication orders, allergies, quantitative labs with units, immunisations, procedures, notes), what fraction of the facts present in the SOURCE system's structured tables within W is present, queryable and value-identical in the TARGET system's computable record, under a correspondence rule fixed before any data pull, with "no admissible correspondent in the target model" counted as its own category rather than dropped; and (ii) on at least three named longitudinal estimands (incident-diabetes rate, prevalent ACE-inhibitor exposure, Charlson comorbidity prevalence) computed from the target system's standard research extract, is there a level or slope discontinuity at T exceeding a materiality bound declared in advance, where "artefactual" is established by re-deriving the same estimand for the same patients from the legacy archive and by a pre-declared no-cutover control window of equal length (plus a contemporaneous non-converting control site where available)?
Reformulation note (Gate 1): one reformulation used; V0 retained as the lay/intake phrasing. V0 left the denominator uncountable ("the pre-cutover clinical record"), asserted causation in the word "artefactual", and set no materiality bound. V2 fixes the denominator to source-system structured tables within W, adds the legacy re-derivation and no-cutover control window as attribution arms, and requires the bound pre-declared so a null is reportable.
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) When a health system replaces its EHR, what fraction of the pre-cutover clinical record is never brought into the new system's computable record at all, per pre-declared fact class, and does that remainder produce artefactual discontinuities at the cutover date in the incidence, exposure and comorbidity measures that EHR-derived research and quality reporting compute?
- (lay) After a hospital switches EHR vendors, how much of its patients' past survives as a usable number rather than a scanned image or a decommissioned archive, and what does the missing part do to the statistics drawn from that record?
- (method field's words) Applying significant properties, migration fidelity and fixity to EHR conversions: what are the per-fact-class retention rates in the target system, and what discontinuity do they induce in named longitudinal estimands at the cutover boundary?
Motivating gap: Published EHR migration validation is defined on the migrated set, so its success criterion cannot see its own complement — Pageler et al. JAMIA 2016 (abstract level, carried from intake) samples records SELECTED for migration; Le et al. GiM Open 2025 (N3, abstract level) reports 92.2% concordance among 461 of 500 sampled MIGRATED charts. The complement has mature method vocabulary in digital preservation and a NIST long-term-EHR-preservation programme, but no opened source measures it per fact class in a target EHR. Limb (ii), by contrast, is asked: N1 hit it ad hoc and abandoned an interrupted time series over it. The gap's shape after Gate 4: limb (i) is the unmeasured part; limb (ii) is incremental at best.
Presuppositions: P1 queryable (not merely retained) legacy archive — contested, and adversary A2's one opened archive instance (harmonyhit.com/lp-it) claims retention and browser viewing but no SQL/report/analytic release. P2 a source-to-target fact-class correspondence can be defined — contested; handled by pre-declaration plus a "no admissible correspondent" category. P3 extracts draw only on target tables — FALSE in at least one real programme (UDS guidance instructs merging both systems with de-duplication) and false in A3's S1 (MIMIC-III retains both systems); must be verified per pipeline. P4 cutover dates identifiable in the extract — usually true per site, typically unlabelled in multi-site network data. P5 analysts do not already neutralise the artefact — tested against two instruments: UDS (premise held; it instructs merge-and-report with no loss estimate) and OMOP CDM v5.4 OBSERVATION_PERIOD (A3's S2, opened: silent on cutovers, start inferable as earliest event date), so the premise survives on two instances, not three. P6 scanned/read-only retention counts as loss — declared definitional choice with a partial-loss sensitivity arm. P7 the archive can serve as a re-derivation substrate — follows from P1 where queryable, fails where it is a viewer only; no instance of a substrate answering per-fact-class queries against source tables was opened by anyone in this file.
What would count as an answer: per fact class, a measured retention fraction (present, queryable, value-identical) at two or more systems with DIFFERENT source/target vendor pairs, correspondence rule fixed before any data pull and correspondence failures reported as their own category; plus a pre-registered discontinuity test on three named estimands at T against a bound declared in advance, with legacy re-derivation and no-cutover control window as attribution arms; plus a stated count of candidate sites that could not supply a legacy denominator at all. Near-complete retention with no discontinuity beyond the bound is a clean, informative negative: it would license the current unevidenced practice of pooling across cutovers.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 (cap 11, minimum 8 met); Gate 4 added 24 Disguise queries in new vocabularies across three adversaries (A1 8, A2 8, A3 8). Full lists: batches/ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0633/UQ-20261022-08-record.md and the three UQ-20261022-08-adversary-*.md files. Most informative: "impact of electronic health record vendor change on longitudinal research cohort data continuity before and after conversion" -> N1, the decisive hit; "what percentage of legacy clinical data is migrated to the new EHR vendor conversion abstraction" (answer-directed) -> no measured fraction, top hit ACI Open 2020;4(1):e48-e58, could not read; "measured retention rate problem list allergies medications laboratory results after EHR data conversion percentage preserved structured" -> no per-class fraction, returned PMC12793680 (penicillin-allergy EHR-transition study, not opened); "digital preservation significant properties migration fidelity ... electronic health record system replacement" (method-owning field) -> vocabulary and a NIST programme exist, no instance measuring per-class retention through a live replacement; A1's `"EHR transition" OR "EHR migration" structural break ... pharmacoepidemiology` -> Miake-Lye et al., J Gen Intern Med 2023 systematic review (opened full text: 40 publications, 8 on data migration, NO retention fraction extracted); A2's exact-title own-field query -> Schreiber & Garber, ACI Open 2020 (Crossref abstract opened, full text could not read); A3's `MIMIC-III CareVue MetaVision transition non-stationarity` -> Nestor et al. 2019 (opened full text); A3's OMOP OBSERVATION_PERIOD query -> the convention page, opened, silent on cutovers. Read-level discipline: OPENED FULL TEXT N2, Miake-Lye 2023, Nestor 2019, UDS guidance, OMOP CDM 5.4 section, UCSF conversion tipsheet, harmonyhit product page; OPENED ABSTRACT ONLY N3, Schreiber & Garber (Crossref), N1 (article page, not PDF galley), Pageler (Crossref, not re-opened); AMENDED ON VERIFICATION, both now READ: PMC11741007 = doi 10.1093/jamia/ocv173, which is Pageler NM et al., JAMIA 2016;23(5):991-994 — this entry's OWN fourth prior, listed twice under two identifiers, read at abstract level on the publisher's page; PMC12793680 = doi 10.1093/ofid/ofaf695.2146, Brinkman et al., Open Forum Infectious Diseases 13(Supplement_1) ofaf695.2146, read IN FULL under CC BY 4.0 and re-graded as a conference poster abstract despite its journal-article Crossref type. Both identifiers converted at ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/utils/idconv in one call each; the obstacle was an unconverted identifier, not an inaccessible document. Still COULD NOT READ: ACI Open 2020;4(1):e48-e58 full text (publisher anti-crawler protection; CC BY 4.0 and readable by a human in a browser, so out of reach of an automated fetch rather than lost), ACI Open 2020;4(1):e48-e58 full text (four Thieme routes across .de and .com failed), PMC3198909 and PMC3461151 (break-in-series methods, returned by A2, not opened), Rigsrevisionen 17/2017 (redirect not followed). Gate 2 overran its fetch cap by one (6 of 5 declared, 2 returning nothing); recorded, not concealed.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): N1. Black JE et al., "Understanding data provenance when using electronic medical records for research: Lessons learned from the DELPHI database", Int J Popul Data Sci 2023;8(5):2177, doi 10.23889/ijpds.v8i5.2177 (publisher article page). NUMBERS PRINTED: 36.4% of patients in the new software's database matched to the previous software's (5,807 matched / 10,166 unmatched); procedure records 2-3x higher in 2012-13 and none before 2012; antibiotic prescriptions 1,601 -> 475 per year at similar encounter volumes; ITS abandoned. REGIME: ~65,000 primary-care patients, 18 Ontario sites, one 2012-13 EMR software change, observed inside a de-identified research extract, probabilistic linkage without a common identifier, no bound, no pre-registration. N2. Colicchio TK et al., J Biomed Inform 2018;83:40-53, doi 10.1016/j.jbi.2018.05.018 (full text). NUMBERS: 41 measures, 40 (98%) significant in >=1 region, 20 (49%) of significant differences driven by changes at CONTROL sites. REGIME: prospective operational quality/productivity/safety measures after phased go-live, segmented regression, no materiality bound, causality disclaimed. N3. Le C et al., Genet Med Open 2025;3:101913, PMID 40027237 (abstract only). NUMBERS: 13,000 migrated records, 500 sampled, 461 reviewed, 425 (92.2%) concordant, 36 discordant (9 incorrect results, 19 missing information, 5 pre-2017 paper legacy, 3 extra). REGIME: one genetics module migration, denominator = records selected for migration. Fourth, retained from intake, abstract level: Pageler NM et al., JAMIA 2016;23(5):991-994, doi 10.1093/jamia/ocv173 — AMENDED ON VERIFICATION: the abstract does NOT say a sample was taken and no errors found in it. It describes the sampling METHOD ("validation of a sample of the data"; "a randomized sample size for each data type") and prints no sampled-error count or rate at all: no N, no confidence level, no error tolerance, and the sampling unit is the DATA TYPE, not the record. The only null it prints belongs to a different regime — "No errors in the migrated data were found during the 12- month post-implementation period" — which is live-use surveillance, not the sample's yield, and the one error it does describe is explicitly set apart as unrelated to the validation. It names a non-migration event, "a failure to migrate some clinical notes", and prints no number for it. So this source PERFORMS a sampling validation and PUBLISHES no number from it, and must be cited for a method and a 12-month post-implementation null, never for a sampling result. Added at Gate 4: Schreiber R, Garber L, "Data Migration: A Thorny Issue in Electronic Health Record Transitions", ACI Open 2020;4(1):e48-e58, doi 10.1055/s-0040-1710007 (registered abstract only; full text unread) — a literature review plus two case studies that DECLARES the empirical absence ("Very little empiric information exists in the peer-reviewed literature regarding data migrations during EHR-to-EHR transitions"), names nine domains of potential consequences, and calls for prospective research; Miake-Lye IM et al., J Gen Intern Med 2023, doi 10.1007/s11606-023-08276-3 (full text) — 8 of 40 publications on data migration, process descriptions only; Nestor B et al., arXiv 1908.00690 (MLHC 2019, full text) — maximum AUROC drop 0.29 (mortality, RF, raw features) located at the 2008 CareVue->MetaVision change, with BOTH systems' data retained.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs N1 — N1 kills the claim that limb (ii) is un-asked; four differences survive and all sit on limb (i) or on design: its 36.4% is probabilistic patient LINKAGE between two de-identified extracts, not per-fact-class retention of FACTS against the source system's structured-table count, which N1 never computes for any class; no correspondence rule and no "no admissible correspondent" category; no bound, no pre-registration, no attribution arm, so the 1,601->475 drop is consistent with migration loss, real prescribing change and extract-pipeline change alike; one database, one change, one jurisdiction. vs N2 — different endpoint class and time direction: prospective operational measures after go-live, not estimands computed over the PRE-cutover record; its 49%-driven-by-controls finding is what forced the candidate's attribution arms; it measures no migration fraction. vs N3 and Pageler — both measure fidelity WITHIN migration scope, on a denominator of records chosen for migration, which cannot express the complement; N3's 19 "missing information" and 5 paper-legacy discordances are a chart-level hint, not a fraction. vs Schreiber & Garber — the review names the absence and asks for prospective study; it prints no number, no denominator, no estimand and no bound. PUBLISHED IS NOT PERFORMED, applied: no source opened by any of the four agents prints the candidate quantity. The nine-domains taxonomy is a classification axis that stops short of the per-fact-class retention grain, so on the record as it stands it is a granularity gap, not an absence — and its full text is unread, which is exactly where the pivot sits. vs Nestor et al. — a discontinuity at an EHR system change inside a research extract, measured and numbered, but on model AUROC rather than epidemiological estimands and with full retention of both systems, so it is a second instance of limb (ii)'s question class and no instance of limb (i).
Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: one neighbour (N1) is very close and limb (ii) must be posed as explicitly incremental to it and to Nestor et al.; the grade is not Low because no opened source prints the candidate quantity and the two sources that print migration numbers (N3's 92.2%; Pageler's "no errors found") compute them on an in-scope denominator that cannot express the complement; it is not High because limb (ii) is asked and partly answered, because the field's own 2020 review printed a research call on the topic, and because three sources returned by the agents' own searches could not be read at any route (PMC11741007, identity unresolved after three lookups; PMC12793680; ACI Open 2020 e48-e58 full text). Any of the three printing a per-fact-class retention fraction would move this to Low.
Significance — consequence: YES (material out-of-scope remainder with a discontinuity beyond the bound): every EHR-derived incidence, exposure and comorbidity estimate spanning a cutover carries a datable, vendor-change-shaped artefact that is currently unlabelled; analysts would need cutover-aware observation periods and a per-class loss profile to decide which estimands survive, and migration scope becomes an evidence-quality decision with a measured price rather than an IT cost decision. NO (near-complete retention, no discontinuity beyond the bound): a clean negative licensing the pooling that is already practised without evidence. Stated conditionally on the extract pipeline, per P3 — A3 is right that EDW-based extracts retaining both systems weaken the unconditional claim.
Significance — audience: (1) health-system informatics and HIM teams specifying migration scope, who price this at every conversion with no loss profile; (2) research-network curation groups — verified rather than asserted, since the OMOP CDM v5.4 OBSERVATION_PERIOD convention opened at Gate 4 contains no cutover-aware rule, so a cutover-indexed check class would be new to it; (3) RWE regulatory scientists assessing accrual and provenance; (4) quality-reporting programmes, concretely: the UDS "Guidance for Health Centers that Switched EHRs" (August 2025, opened) instructs merging both systems with de-duplication and reporting "to the best of the health center's ability", warns of a "questionable rating", and nowhere acknowledges non-comparability with prior years; (5) secondary-use researchers — N1's team is the existence proof, having dropped a planned analysis.
Significance — fecundity: is the loss profile predictable from the source/target vendor pair, so a site could forecast its artefact before converting; is there a dose-response between per-class retention and estimand bias that would turn retention into a data-quality index; can the legacy archive serve as a recovery instrument, and does recovery move the estimand (scope-missingness analogue of UQ-20261016-05); how many unlabelled cutovers sit inside existing multi-site network data, and should networks keep a public cutover register; does image-only retention behave as partial or total loss; which fact classes are systematically sacrificed, and is that choice clinical or contractual.
Significance — anchoring: Kahn et al. conformance/completeness/plausibility (temporal plausibility is the check family a cutover artefact should trip and apparently does not); OMOP observation-period construction, now confirmed cutover-blind; N1's provenance finding; Nestor et al. on non-stationarity at a system change; GAO-22-103718 on VA migrated-data quality (returned, not opened); the significant-properties literature and NIST's long-term-EHR-preservation programme; and the structural anomaly that migration validation in medicine is defined on the migrated set.
Reason for silence: a disciplinary and incentive boundary running through the complement. Those holding the fact (health-system IT, HIM, migration vendors) succeed at go-live plus validation of what was migrated, and both opened migration-audit papers define their denominator as the migrated set, so the quantity is outside the measurement by construction. Those harmed see only the target tables and cannot see the denominator; N1 is the mechanism caught in the act. Reinforcers: measuring the complement requires querying an archive whose decommissioning often funds the project; publishing a per-class loss profile is an institutional-risk disclosure. Gate 4 narrows this: the asking demonstrably happened in the field's own venue (Schreiber & Garber 2020), so the mechanism now explains non-PERFORMANCE at the measurable grain rather than non-asking of the topic, and the sub-mechanism the record leaned on (method vocabulary trapped in archival science) is neither needed nor evidenced.

Judge's note on what did and did not run: all three adversaries executed their 8 Disguise queries, so Disguise is not unverified by non-execution; what is unverified is narrower and decisive — three sources the agents' own searches returned (PMC11741007, PMC12793680, ACI Open 2020;4(1):e48-e58 full text) could not be read at any route available here (PMC and Europe PMC hard-blocked; four Thieme routes across two hostnames served a bot interstitial). Strongest remaining objection: the question is two questions welded, and the weld is where it is weakest — limb (ii) is a disguised known and limb (i) is a per-site audit whose headline fraction would be dominated by a documented design decision. The single unopened source most likely to settle the pivot is the full text of Schreiber & Garber, ACI Open 2020;4(1):e48-e58 (doi 10.1055/s-0040-1710007), specifically its nine domains of potential consequences: if those already pose the downstream research/quality-measure consequence or the per-class retention quantity, limb (ii) is asked twice over and limb (i)'s grade falls.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Five fresh-context checkers were each handed one claim and its source, with the entry's citations but not its reasoning. Logs: `VERIFY-uq08-unreadable-pmcids.md`, `VERIFY-black-delphi-numbers.md`, `VERIFY-uq08-colicchio-nestor.md`, `VERIFY-uq08-migration-concordance.md`, `VERIFY-schreiber-garber-aci-open.md` in this folder. **Verdict unchanged: Provisional. The blocker the entry named is struck.**

**1. The unreadability blocker does not survive contact with the sources.** The entry named three decisive sources as unread at any available route. Two of them converted from PMCID to DOI in a single call to an endpoint that answers here, and both then opened. This is the *a-prior-nobody-opened-is-not-prior-art* failure in its original form: the record characterised sources it had not established could be opened, and the obstacle was an unconverted identifier. Worse than that, **PMC11741007 is this entry's own fourth prior**, Pageler 2016, carried twice under two identifiers without either agent noticing. The process fix is in team memory and is worth more than this check: **record sources by DOI plus first author plus year plus title, never by PMCID alone.**

**2. Opening them does not hand the entry its quantity, in two different shapes of no.** **Pageler 2016 is the published-is-not-performed case, and the cleanest instance of it on this ledger.** It is the on-topic paper — its whole subject is validating the completeness and accuracy of migrated data — it NAMES a non-migration event ("a failure to migrate some clinical notes") and prints no number for it at all. What it does is BOUND the migration error rate by a sampling plan and report zero errors found inside that bound. A bound is not a measurement and "some clinical notes" is not a fraction. This is the strongest available demonstration that the field ran the analysis and never printed the quantity, and it is an abstract-level finding, so no absence in the body text is recorded on the checker's authority. **Brinkman 2026 (OFID) is the regime case.** It prints ten figures at a real cutover and the tempting one, **36.5%**, is the wrong estimand three times over: patients rather than entries, discrepancies in both directions rather than losses, and a cause the authors decline to assign, having themselves pointed at "an incomplete legacy system list". Its loss-direction figure is a bare count of three patients with no printed denominator. Used as a per-fact-class non-migration fraction it would repeat exactly the defect that moved a verdict in the previous batch. If 36.5% is cited anywhere it must carry its denominator, its both-directions definition and the authors' own legacy-list caveat, or it should not be cited. Neither source measures a discontinuity in an incidence, exposure or comorbidity ESTIMATE at a cutover date: Pageler measures no epidemiological quantity at all, and Brinkman measures cross-system record disagreement, which is adjacent but is not a step change in a rate.

**3. N1 (Black et al. 2023) says most of what the entry attributes to it, but not the part that sets the cap.** Confirmed: the 36.4% patient linkage rate, the procedure counts (0 before 2012, then 17,171 and 12,867) and the antibiotic drop (1,601 to 475 per year at similar encounter volumes). But it produces **no per-fact-class non-migration fraction**, states no materiality bound, pre-registers nothing and performs no test, and its unmatched patients are linkage failures under a four-attribute probabilistic rule, **not records demonstrably never received** — so the entry must stop describing the 10,166 unmatched patients as unmigrated records. It therefore does not cap a candidate whose unit is the fraction of the pre-cutover record absent per fact class, nor one supplying a materiality threshold or an auditable reconciliation against the source system. It **does** cap any candidate whose novelty is merely that EMR migrations damage longitudinal research data and provenance should be checked first, which is this paper's own stated lesson. Repairs: rewrite the suitability claim to quote the paper's own sentence, strike the two sub-claims the checker could not support, and correct the front matter to the printed names and full title.

**4. The "already numbered" verdict must be split by limb.** On "does a cutover produce a measurable discontinuity in operational measures or model performance, and by how much" the answer is yes, asked and numbered twice over: Colicchio 2018 at 40 (98%) of 41 operational measures changing significantly in at least one region, with the under-quoted caveat that 20 (49%) of the between-group differences were produced by the **control** arm moving; and Nestor 2019 at a 0.29 AUROC drop (mortality, random forest, raw features), printed in abstract, introduction, conclusion and Table 1. Both numbers survive checking. On "what fraction of a record fails to migrate" **neither source asks it and neither answers it, and Nestor in particular cannot be used for it** — its discontinuity occurs with BOTH systems' records retained and read, a feature-namespace break rather than a data-loss measurement, and Colicchio does not touch migration at all. **So the "already numbered" verdict is withdrawn for limb (i) specifically.** Repairs regardless: restate the 20 (49%) as an additional count over 41 measures rather than a share of the 40; restore the "attributable to the intervention" and "intervention vs control sites" qualifiers on the 40 (98%); replace "segmented regression" with the paper's own "interrupted time-series analysis (ITSA) with an ordinary least squares model (OLS)"; soften "prospective" to routinely collected operational measures analysed over Feb 2013 to Jul 2017; and attach to the 0.29 that it is measured with no data loss.

**5. N3 (Le et al. 2025) holds at abstract level and is half-settled where it matters.** All nine numbers are printed in the abstract and the arithmetic is right: 425 + 36 = 461, and 425/461 = 92.2% on a denominator of **461 reviewed charts**, re-derived at the author's own rounding. The regime favours the entry's concern and is unambiguous: the sample was drawn **after** migration, from the 13,000 records that **had been** migrated, so 92.2% is silent on any record not migrated. But the abstract states **no pre-cutover total and no migration selection criteria**, so the entry must not assert that records were excluded from migration, nor that 13,000 was the whole pre-cutover pool; settling that needs the full-text Methods, which **could not be read** — a COULD NOT READ on the decisive question, not a NOT FOUND. Two qualifiers belong on any use of 92.2%: the unexplained 39-chart gap between 500 selected and 461 reviewed, making it a rate among *reviewable* charts, and the absent uncertainty, the source printing a bare proportion. Two of the entry's labels are paraphrase ("incorrect results" for "incorrect genetic testing results entered"; "extra" for "additional information transferred"), and the dropped word "entered" is the one that would say whether the 9 errors were made by the migration or merely carried through it. **It is also one genetics family-history tool swap, not an EHR replacement** — "a family history database", "from one commercial software solution to another" — so it must not be pooled with Pageler's whole-system transition: different units (data type vs patient chart), different endpoints (post-go-live null vs chart concordance), different estimands, and only Le prints a rate. This entry's quantitative content rests on Le's abstract alone.

**6. Schreiber & Garber grounds no grade in either direction, for a reason the entry had not established.** The source is real, correctly cited apart from a truncated title, open access, and a review-plus-case-studies hybrid rather than a primary measurement study. Three contents are confirmed at abstract level: nine consequence domains, a conclusion calling for prospective research, two new cases added to six already reported. The abstract prints no fraction — only counts of reports and of domains — **but the body is where a fraction would live and the body did not open**, so this source supports neither closure nor confirmation of the gap. The declared-absence sentence the entry quotes is **unverified as wording** and should not be quoted from this source until someone has read it, and "sparse" should not be substituted for it. Restate its status from "could not read at any route" to **full text blocked by publisher anti-crawler protection; abstract-level content obtained via Crossref; CC BY 4.0 and readable by a human in a browser** — a successor with a browser-capable route, or simply with fetch budget to finish the Crossref abstract and retry Thieme, can likely settle this outright. This is the remaining decisive unread source and the entry's cap now rests on it alone, not on three.

ID: UQ-20261022-09
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Rejected — AMENDED ON POST-BATCH VERIFICATION 2026-10-22, and the ground has changed. The Gate 2 Low grade is DEMOTED from a finding to **Unverified**: its killing prior, O'Malley et al. 2021, served no article text at any level to a fresh-context checker, so the kill rests on an abstract nobody has re-read against the numbers, and an unrun check cannot reject. Attack 2's Unresolved from adversary 2 falls with it. **The rejection now rests on attack 4, Unresolved from BOTH adversaries, which is independently fatal under this ledger's rules and is strengthened on the export-logging leg.** Promotion condition: the full text of O'Malley et al. 2021, which must answer sub-claim (f) first — see the verification block at the end of this entry; where that block and the body conflict, the block governs.
Domain(s): Medicine — diabetes care and therapeutic decision-making (target field). Adjacent vocabularies swept: control engineering, human factors of automation, device-log epidemiology, causal inference on irregularly observed logs, automated mechanical ventilation, therapeutic drug monitoring, device-data engineering.
Question (canonical): In users of commercial automated insulin delivery systems whose cloud logs record both the controller's own adaptation and every human change to its settings, what is the measured within-person effect of a clinician- or user-initiated settings change on subsequent glycaemic outcomes, over and above the adaptation the system performed during the same period?
Reformulation note: one Gate 1 reformulation was taken. V2 (the version scored) narrows to profile-adapting controllers (MiniMed 780G-class auto-basal, Omnipod 5-class adaptive basal) in routine ambulatory care, pre-declares design (target-trial emulation against matched no-change person-time, or regression discontinuity at visit dates), horizons (2/4/12 weeks), endpoints (TIR 70–180, TBR <54), settings classes, a negative-control outcome, and two feasibility denominators, and enters the controller's concurrent adaptation as a pre-declared covariate. Full text in ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0633/UQ-20261022-09-record.md, Gate 1.
Alternative formulations:
- When the algorithm is already retuning itself, how much does a human changing its settings add — and for which settings?
- Using AID device logs and one pre-declared design, what is the effect of a settings-change event on TIR at 2, 4 and 12 weeks relative to matched no-change person-time, conditional on the controller's concurrent adaptation?
- V2 as summarised in the reformulation note above.
Motivating gap: the intake conjectured that the outcome literature compares AID against non-AID therapy or treats follow-up intensity as an undifferentiated bundle, and that the separable quantity became measurable only with large-population logging of controller adaptation alongside timestamped human edits. The intake itself flagged this as an unchecked Gate 0 conjecture. Gate 2 checked it and it is refuted in its strong form.
Presuppositions: P1 vendor logs separate controller adaptation from human edits with timestamps — tested at Gate 4 and FALSE for the public instrument. P2 edit authorship recorded or inferable — fails structurally (the user enters every change on the device). P3 settings changes not confounded by indication — contested, unaddressed. P4 consensus CGM metrics adequate — established, not load-bearing. P5 sufficient matched no-change person-time — unverified. P6 logged settings are the settings in force — undercut (Medtronic timestamps "became effective", other devices "read by the pump").
What would count as an answer: per-settings-class within-person effect estimates on TIR 70–180 and TBR <54 at 2, 4 and 12 weeks under one pre-declared design and one pre-declared adaptation metric, with a negative-control outcome, plus the unattributable-authorship fraction and the fraction of eligible logs that cannot separate adaptation from edits. A pre-declared null inside an equivalence band is a publishable answer. The record concedes the estimand is specifiable only once "the controller's concurrent adaptation" is given a metric and that no source anyone opened supplies one, so the pre-declaration remains to be written, not merely executed.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 31 in total — 13 at Gate 2 (cap 11; the two-query overrun is disclosed in the record, not concealed), 9 by adversary 1, 9 by adversary 2. Most informative: "effect of insulin pump settings changes on time in range automated insulin delivery retrospective" → surfaced PMC8114941 (five further queries returned it); "'Clinical Management and Pump Parameter Adjustment' Control-IQ closed-loop Diabetes Technology Therapeutics" → identified it as O'Malley et al. 2021, the killing prior; "predictors of improvement in time in range after automated insulin delivery start settings optimization cohort study" → the Omnipod 5 settings paper (prior 2); "insulin pump download review basal rate change settings adjustment A1c before and after retrospective chart review sensor-augmented pump era" (adversary 2) → the NCT05204134 protocol/SAP PDF URL the record left untried, then opened; "attribution decomposition how much of glycemic improvement due to algorithm adaptation versus user-initiated parameter changes ... mediation analysis" (adversary 2) → no decomposition study of this exposure; "Tidepool device-data pumpSettings ... settings change timestamp" (adversary 1) and "Omnipod 5 adaptive basal ... data dictionary settings change event timestamp" (adversary 2) → no public data dictionary exposing an adaptation state. Full lists in ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0633/UQ-20261022-09-record.md (Gate 2, steps 2–3) and the two adversary files.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) O'Malley G., Messer L., Levy C., Pinsker J., Forlenza G., Isganaitis E., Kudva Y., Ekhlaspour L., Raghinaru D., Lum J., et al., for the iDCL Trial Research Group, "Clinical Management and Pump Parameter Adjustment of the Control-IQ Closed-Loop Control System: Results from a 6-Month, Multicenter, Randomized Clinical Trial," Diabetes Technology & Therapeutics 2021;23(4):245–252, DOI 10.1089/dia.2020.0472 — READ LEVEL ABSTRACT ONLY, at esploro.umontpellier.fr and a HAL mirror by the record and independently re-opened at esploro by adversary 2; publisher route liebertpub.com failed; PMC8114941 not tried (hard-blocked). (2) Sawyer A., Wilmot E.G., Do D., Miller K.M., Ly T.T., Forlenza G.P., "Settings Associated with Optimal Glycemic Outcomes with the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System: Evidence from Real-World Users with Type 1 Diabetes," DOI 10.1177/15209156261456826 — FRONT MATTER CORRECTED ON VERIFICATION: Diabetes Technology & Therapeutics, OnlineFirst, 24 June 2026, with NO volume and NO pages because it is OnlineFirst; a real, published, peer-reviewed research article, not a preprint and not a poster. READ LEVEL ABSTRACT ONLY; publisher page not opened. (3) NCT05204134, "Adaptation of Insulin Delivery Settings to Improve Clinical Outcomes With AID Use" — COULD NOT READ at Gate 2 (clinicaltrials.gov served only the JS template); READ IN FULL by adversary 2 via cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/34/NCT05204134/Prot_SAP_000.pdf. PMC10698772, returned by five of the record's thirteen queries and again by both adversaries, was never identified by title or opened by anyone during the batch. IDENTIFIED ON VERIFICATION in two calls (one conversion, one metadata lookup): Messer LH, Breton MD, "Therapy Settings Associated with Optimal Outcomes for t:slim X2 with Control-IQ Technology in Real-World Clinical Care", Diabetes Technology & Therapeutics 2023;25(12):877-882, doi 10.1089/dia.2023.0308, PMID 37751154. STILL COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND: it carries a PMCID, so a free full text exists and the obstruction is this environment. On abstract-level evidence it is a BETWEEN-PERSON cross-sectional regression relating settings LEVELS to CGM outcomes across 20,764 users — "Associated with", in its own title — whose strongest predictor is a behaviour (boluses per day), so it SITS OUTSIDE THE REGIME of a within-person edit-effect claim; the authors' own "lever to pull" conclusion makes exactly that leap, and a reader who takes it at face value inherits it. Do not close this check.
Novelty — how this differs from each: prior 1 shares the candidate's unit of analysis (the parameter-change encounter), endpoint (TIR 70–180) and metric category, and differs on population (iDCL trial participants), operating condition (6-month protocol-driven trial care), instrument (trial-collected pump/CGM data, not vendor cloud logs), comparator (raw within-person before/after window, not matched no-change person-time) and on the absence of any adaptation-netting term — four of six regime attributes, which is the whole of what the candidate has left. Prior 2 shares population, instrument, operating condition and category but is at the wrong unit (the user, 176,405 of them) and estimand (cross-sectional odds of TIR >70% by settings in force, with Youden-J cutpoints read off a fitted association): it measures settings in force, not the effect of changing them, so it is the adjacent-object neighbour this ledger most often mistakes for a kill, and it is not one. Prior 3, now read, is a Tandem-sponsored prospective single-arm single-centre feasibility study on t:slim X2 + Control-IQ with a severe-hypoglycaemia primary endpoint and no comparator arm — a trial of a settings-recommendation service with physician review, not an estimate of an edit's increment; it grounds nothing in either direction, but it does carry the settings-change authorship on a paper case report form, which is evidence against P2.
Novelty confidence: Low
Number check (per the standing rule, before accepting the Low grade): the candidate quantity is PRINTED, not merely defined, bounded, predicted or announced. Verbatim from prior 1's abstract, served at two independent routes and quoted identically by the record and by adversary 2: "In 607 encounters for parameter changes, there were fewer adjustments for CLC than SAP (3.4 vs. 4.1/participant)." and "TIR before and after adjustments was 71.2% and 71.3% for CLC and 61.0% and 62.9% for SAP." — i.e. a +0.1 percentage-point before-to-after change in percent time 70–180 mg/dL over 607 parameter-change encounters in 168 participants, printed in the Results sentence of the abstract, with the verdict given in its hedged form: "No difference in TIR was detected with parameter changes overall, but they may have an effect in higher HbA1c subgroups or following user-directed boluses." A per-settings-class breakdown is printed too (basal rates 69% CLC vs 80% SAP; carbohydrate ratios 68% vs 50%; correction factors 44% vs 41%; overnight 62% vs 75%), with two per-class outcome results, so the "and for which settings?" limb is also partly published. What nobody saw: the tables, the model specification and the before/after window definitions — the read is abstract-level on both routes.
Significance — consequence: if a human edit buys a measurable increment on top of an adapting controller, settings review is the active ingredient of a visit and its cadence and content become optimisable; if it buys nothing inside a pre-declared equivalence band, the titration visit is being paid for as a therapeutic act while functioning as a monitoring act. Discounted twice: prior 1 already reports the overall null in its own regime, and adversary 2 notes a titration visit also carries education, screening, troubleshooting and psychosocial care, so a null on the edit increment would not license the record's reimbursement-code conclusion.
Significance — audience: real and already spending on the object — diabetes-technology and paediatric endocrinology services designing follow-up; manufacturers deciding how much profile authority to leave users (Insulet published a 176,405-user settings analysis; Tandem runs NCT05204134); platform vendors (Glooko shipped a pump-settings-to-EHR integration in release 26.2); payers; consensus writers. Attack 6 does not land on the audience.
Significance — fecundity: which settings classes repay editing; whether edit value declines as controllers adapt; whether remote-monitoring-driven edits differ from in-visit edits; how to define a cross-vendor controller-adaptation metric, which this entry shows nobody has supplied.
Significance — anchoring: prior 1's unresolved subgroup hedge (higher HbA1c; following user-directed boluses); causal inference under informatively timed observation; what a titration visit is for.
Reason for silence: for the canonical question there is no silence to explain — it was asked and answered in 2021, which is the finding of Gate 2. For the V2 refinement the offered mechanism is instrumental plus disciplinary (profile-adapting controllers only recently at scale; logs behind commercial access; the owning method in another discipline). Adversary 1 strengthens it: the adaptation term is not representable in any openable data model, so the question is not formulable from obtainable data. Adversary 2 weakens it: NCT05204134's existence shows the field is already asking about AID settings adaptation. Both graded it Partial.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): two adversaries, independent contexts, neither shown the other's log; Disguise floor MET (adversary 2 ran 8 of its 9 as new-vocabulary sweeps; adversary 1's own honest strict count was 7 of 9), so Disguise is a check that RAN and is certified as "ran, found no rename", not as "absent" — it is not Unverified, and no Unverified attack appears in this entry.
1 | Triviality | The headline is answerable from one 2021 abstract; and one exposure class is answerable from a vendor page (Omnipod 5: programmed basal edits have no impact on the algorithm after initiation, yet basal is the largest edit class at 69% of CLC encounters) | the per-class increment across horizons with negative controls is genuinely empirical for the other classes; adversary 1 did not re-open prior 1 and rests this row on the record's abstract-level read | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)

A1 opened three instances (Tidepool pumpSettings: "Most insulin delivery devices do not, unfortunately, keep a historical record of all insulin pump settings"; Tidepool basal/automated, which exports delivered rate and no adapted parameter; Glooko 26.2, current configuration only). A2 opened two export-format specifications in full plus three real CareLink CSV headers: no settings-change event stream for target/correction factor/carb ratio, no authorship field, a CareLink export "contains no usable basal data", its one auto-mode figure "unclear what this actually refers to", Omnipod automated basal "unknown and can only be roughly approximated". Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3 [as judged on V2; adversary 2's attack 4c argues for 1/3 on the ground that the named estimand is not the effect of the edit, which I do not need to re-score to reach the verdict]
Strongest remaining objection: the kill has three legs and they are not equally exposed. Leg 1 (Gate 2, and adversary 2's attack 2): prior 1 publishes the candidate quantity at the candidate's own unit and endpoint, number printed and located. Leg 2 (attack 4a/4b, both adversaries): no public instrument carries the edit stream, the authorship or the adaptation state. Leg 3 (attack 4c, adversary 2): the netting clause subtracts a quantity downstream of the exposure, so the named estimand is not the effect of the edit. THE VERDICT STANDS ON LEG 1 AND LEG 3 TOGETHER: leg 1 alone gives novelty Low and ends it at Gate 2, and leg 3 alone gives a fatal Unresolved on attack 4 that better data cannot repair. If leg 1 fell — a full-text read showing the 607-encounter analysis is descriptive only, or that its before/after windows are not what the abstract implies — legs 2 and 3 would still carry attack 4 Unresolved from both adversaries, so the entry would remain Rejected rather than becoming Provisional. If leg 3 fell, legs 1 and 2 stand. The single strongest objection to the rejection is therefore not to any one leg but to their shared read level and regime: leg 1 rests on an abstract-only read at two repository routes with the publisher route failed and the tables, methods and window definitions never seen, in a regime (protocol-driven trial, Control-IQ, which the record argues does not retune its own profile at all) that the candidate sits outside on four of six attributes; leg 2 rests on absences in self-service export documentation and both adversaries explicitly decline to extend it to manufacturer-internal extracts, while prior 2 proves Insulet reads settings values for 176,405 users; and PMC10698772, returned by five Gate 2 queries and by both adversaries, was never identified or opened by anyone and is the one unopened item that could disturb every negative here.
Vulnerability of this rejection — grounds nobody has measured: leg 1 is a measured, published number, so the rejection as a whole does not rest on an unmeasured ground. The two Gate 4 legs do, and the entry records it. Leg 3 follows from a DESIGN DESCRIPTION, not from a reported result: its source is a manufacturer education page that defines the Omnipod 5 mechanism ("The Omnipod 5 algorithm is driven primarily by total daily insulin (TDI)", recomputed at each Pod change from insulin actually delivered) and publishes no quantity; the inference that netting the adaptation removes part of the edit's effect is a causal-structure argument about what "over and above" picks out given that design. This is NOT an algebraic identity — no equation forces the adaptive state to be a function of any particular edit — and it is not a bitwise or empirical demonstration either: nobody has reported a measurement of how much a settings edit moves logged TDI or automated delivery, at any edit class, on any system. Adversary 2 labels the defect over-adjustment on a post-treatment variable but declines to cite that framing because it opened no methods source, and it states the leg is sourced for Omnipod 5 only, with no sourced mechanism for 780G auto-basal, so a demonstration that 780G adaptation is exogenous to user edits would confine leg 3 to half of V2's eligible population. Leg 2 is an enumerated absence in a document kind's published surface, which is a claim about what is documented rather than a measurement of what vendors hold. The single unopened source most likely to settle the leg-3 vulnerability: Medtronic's own MiniMed 780G SmartGuard auto-basal algorithm description (the manufacturer algorithm page or the device's regulatory summary of safety and effectiveness), which would show whether auto-basal adaptation is computed from delivered insulin and so downstream of edits, or is exogenous to them. Separately, PMC10698772 remains the single unopened source most likely to disturb the novelty and Disguise negatives.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): nothing on the question itself. The pointer is to the entry's own unread checks — convert and read PMC10698772, read prior 1 in full via a working publisher route, and obtain a vendor research export (as against a self-service export) to test P1, P2 and P6 on actual instances — and, before any re-intake, a sourced 780G auto-basal mechanism description. A re-intake would have to start from prior 1 as known prior art and from a defined, cross-vendor adaptation metric, not from the intake's refuted gap statement.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — this is an answered / disguised-known rejection, not an asked-but-open problem: prior 1 asked the canonical question at the candidate's own unit and endpoint and printed a hedged null, and LEDGER.md excludes answered and disguised-known rejections from ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The residual V2 refinement is not demonstrably asked by anything anyone opened, so it is not an open problem either; it is a candidate for re-intake in its own right. This line is a recommendation only — writing to routed-open-problems.md happens outside this run, and no row has been written by it.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Three fresh-context checkers were each handed one claim and its source, with the entry's citations but not its reasoning. Logs: `VERIFY-omalley-2021-kill.md`, `VERIFY-uq09-pmc10698772.md`, `VERIFY-uq09-sawyer-and-protocol.md` in this folder. **Verdict unchanged — Rejected — but the ground has moved, and the entry is weaker than it was written.**

**1. The Gate 2 kill is converted from a finding into an UNVERIFIED kill, and that is not a refutation either.** The checker sent to read O'Malley et al. 2021 in full reports: **no article text was served at any level**, at any route tried. It established the identifier triple only — PMCID PMC8114941, PMID 33155824, doi 10.1089/dia.2020.0472. This ledger's own standard, that a kill resting on an abstract belongs in a promotion condition and not in a verdict, applies here at full force and more sharply than when it was written: the kill rests on an abstract nobody has re-read against the numbers, plus two figures (607 encounters in 168 users, and a 71.2% to 71.3% TIR contrast) that **no agent in the chain has reported as served from the paper's Results**. Under LEDGER.md's Unverified rule an unrun check cannot reject, so the Gate 2 Low grade is demoted to Unverified and the rejection no longer stands on it. Silence here is the checker's silence, not the source's: nothing above is evidence that the paper lacks a netting-out clause, that its numbers differ from those quoted, or that the batch's reading was wrong.

**2. The promotion condition must be written against sub-claim (f), not against the numbers.** Even if a later reader confirms 607/168 and 71.2 to 71.3 exactly as printed, **that confirmation does not by itself sustain the kill.** This candidate's estimand is the effect of a human settings edit **net of the controller's own concurrent adaptation**. A before-and-after TIR contrast across Control-IQ users measures the edit **plus** whatever the algorithm did to itself over the same window — the two are confounded by design unless the paper says it separated them. So the kill needs an affirmative finding: a sentence in which the authors state that they isolated, adjusted for, or otherwise accounted for automatic adaptation. If the paper contains no such sentence it measures a quantity **without the clause that distinguishes the candidate**, and the candidate survives however clean the numbers are. Absence of such a sentence is the likely case — a clinical-management paper reporting what clinicians changed and what happened next is not usually built as a causal-identification paper — but likely is not established, and a guess is not recorded here as a finding. Whoever gets full text answers (f) **first**, quotes the sentence, and only then transcribes the figures with their printed locations, units, denominators and stated uncertainty. Routes not yet tried: liebertpub at the `epub` or `full` path rather than `/doi/`; the Jaeb Center publications page; the Barbara Davis Center, Stanford and Mount Sinai institutional repositories whose metadata records already surfaced in search; and a later retry of `ebi.ac.uk` europepmc `fullTextXML` once its rate limit has cleared.

**3. What the rejection now rests on.** Attack 4, Unresolved from **both** adversaries, independently of Gate 2 and independently of each other. Nothing in verification touched it, and the export-logging leg is strengthened: no public data dictionary, vendor export schema or research-grade feed exposes a controller self-adaptation state, and verification added that the one adaptation number anyone has found — the 5% cap in NCT05204134 — belongs to **the study's own recommender**, is a specified margin, and was never audited. Attack 2's Unresolved from adversary 2 falls with the Gate 2 ground it shared. Under LEDGER.md, Unresolved on attack 4 is fatal on its own, so the verdict is unchanged; what changes is that it is now a one-leg verdict resting on an instrument-availability finding rather than a three-leg verdict anchored by a published number.

**4. Neither of the two sources that WERE read is prior art, and both say so in their own voice.** Sawyer et al. 2026 is a real peer-reviewed DTT OnlineFirst article (no volume, no pages), a large cross-sectional retrospective association study at n = 176,405 that **explicitly disclaims the change question**: it "did not evaluate the impact of adjusting an individual user's programmable settings", naming adoption-over-time as "an important area for future research". It prints odds ratios for between-user associations and group median TIRs, prints **no number for a settings-change effect**, and does not net out the controller's own adaptation — indeed it normalises two of its key predictors by total daily dose, a quantity the controller partly determines. For a change-effect question it is silent, not supportive. NCT05204134 is a **completed single-arm feasibility study** (Tandem, one site, 33 enrolled, 2022, results reportedly posted April 2024) whose **primary endpoint is severe hypoglycaemia and DKA**, not a glycaemic outcome, and whose statistical section is purely descriptive: it randomises nothing, defines no estimand and draws no causal contrast, and its human-automation boundary sits in the wrong place for this entry — between the study's recommender and the study's clinicians, not between a human edit and the commercial controller's own adaptation. If the 5% recommender cap or the abstract's "their impact ... was explored" is doing any work in this entry, that work is withdrawn. Residual COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND: the trial's posted results (the registry refused the fetcher), and confirmation of the two-primary-outcome fifteen-week framing against the protocol's single untimed endpoint.

**5. The process fix this entry paid for.** A source returned seven times and read zero times was identified in two calls once someone converted its identifier. **Record sources by DOI plus first author plus year plus title, never by PMCID alone**: the identifier this entry chose is the one identifier this environment cannot open, and that choice is a sufficient explanation for seven retrievals without a single read. Saved to team memory.

ID: UQ-20261022-10
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Gate 4 complete (3 adversaries); nothing Unresolved on attacks 1/2/4, but well-posedness 2/3 and an incomplete Gate 2 search record block Validated. AMENDED ON POST-BATCH VERIFICATION 2026-10-22, with substantial re-grounding: four fresh-context checkers read the four load-bearing sources and opened five exit notices. The verdict is unchanged, but presupposition P2 is FALSIFIED by a printed figure, both priors are re-scoped (Okun's regime is narrower than the cap it carries; Keogh REFUTES the support-withdrawal framing outright on four of six sub-claims), Sheldon is re-graded as a method neighbour the entry should name, and the gap turns out to be a GRANULARITY and UNIT problem rather than an absence of datable public facts. See the verification block at the end of this entry; where that block and the body conflict, the block governs.
Domain(s): Medicine — implantable-device safety and post-market surveillance (target field). Swept: bioethics/neuroethics, pharmacoepidemiology (method-owning field), device-regulatory and insolvency law, registry/UDI informatics, otology, diabetes technology, breast-implant regulatory epidemiology.

Question (canonical): For a declared jurisdiction and window, under a support-withdrawal event definition fixed and published before any data pull (minimum per-class constituents of "support": programming/interrogation, firmware and security updates, consumable and external-component supply, replacement-part supply, remote monitoring, a named clinical point of contact): (i) what is the enumerated list of support-withdrawal events and, per event, the estimated number of living recipients with source and stated uncertainty; and (ii) for events whose recipients are followable, what is the incidence of therapy loss, revision, explant and newly acquired imaging or treatment contraindication in the post-exit period versus the same recipients' pre-exit period and versus matched recipients of still-supported same-class devices — estimand declared per class, null permitted for passive classes, and the share of events whose exposed population could not be counted and the share of classes with no possible outcome ascertainment reported as results rather than caveats.
Reformulation note: this is the version after the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation and is the version graded; the intake version ("how many people are living with an implanted device whose manufacturer has exited... and what are their measured clinical outcomes") is recorded in the record file.

Alternative formulations: (lay) what happens to patients when the company that made their implant goes away, how many are there, and what measurably happens to them; (technical) treating manufacturer exit or support withdrawal as a time-varying exposure on implant cohorts, what is the event incidence per class and the hazard of therapy loss, revision or explant; (method-field) what is the patient-level effect of product market withdrawal when the product is a permanent implant rather than a dispensed drug, i.e. when withdrawal cannot be answered by switching.

Motivating gap: silence mapping. The implantable-device literature is dense with approval, surveillance and registry method and near-empty on manufacturer exit as a patient-level exposure; the "what happens when the maker leaves" discussion sits in op-eds, trade press and bioethics. Adversary 2 narrowed the gap: the field did convene on the exposure (Okun 2024, below) and produced a definition without any count, prevalence or outcome rate. Adversary 3 narrowed it further on one flank: the analysis shape has been performed and published once, for a passive class under a product-defect construct (PIP).

Presuppositions: P1 support-withdrawal events are datable and countable from public records — NOW LARGELY FALSIFIED for the managed-wind-down sub-kind: in 2 of 2 opened notices (ANSM 20/07/2020 EVADIAC; EMA/Medtronic DHPC disseminated 20 Jul 2020) the constituents the definition names are open-ended ("for as long as patients use a MIP"), no recipient count and no end-of-support date is printed, so the declared event rule ("first date any constituent became unavailable") dates nothing; untested for abrupt liquidations. P2 countability per device model — FALSIFIED ON VERIFICATION: Medtronic field action FA981 prints "the approximately 4,000 HVAD(TM) patients currently" — coarse, global, approximate, and with the clause cut after "currently", but printed, in the exit notice, for the withdrawn model. The presupposition as written ("no instance found counting living recipients of a withdrawn model") does not survive. One of five opened notices carried a patient count. P3 recipients remain followable — held in both opened instances (ANSM-convened protocols; Alpha AMS care retained at implanting centres). P4 same-class supported comparator — fails for singleton classes (one implantable insulin pump; both retinal prostheses discontinued), collapsing limb (ii) to within-person pre/post. P5 loss of support has clinical consequence — contested, class-dependent, null permitted. P6 regulators do not already handle exits — PARTLY FALSIFIED for managed wind-downs (no-new-patients rule, stock reservation, continued insulin and consumables, free external pump), untested for liquidations; Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 Art. 10a COULD NOT READ (eur-lex served navigation only; /oj/eng route untried).

What would count as an answer: (a) an enumerated event list under a pre-fixed definition; (b) per event, an exposed-population estimate with source and uncertainty; (c) for followable events, a matched-cohort and within-person estimate of therapy loss, revision, explant, contraindication acquisition, estimand per class; (d) the share of events with no countable exposed population and the share of classes with no outcome ascertainment, as reported results.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 38 distinct queries total — Gate 2 ran 11 across 9 vocabularies, the three adversaries ran 9 each in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try (German insolvency, right-to-repair, vendor end-of-service, legacy pacemaker/programmer, company-name case vocabularies for Nuvectra/Stimwave/ATI/NeuroControl/Otologics/Retina Implant/Pixium, IMDRF legacy-device cybersecurity, breast-implant regulatory epidemiology, prosthodontics, rehabilitation engineering, diabetes technology). Most informative: Gate 2 Q6 (pharmacoepidemiology drug-withdrawal cohort) → the design is mature for drugs and untransplanted; Gate 2 Q1 (own field, own words) → only vocabulary collisions (HVAD "withdrawal of support" = weaning) and trade press; adversary 2 Q4/Q5 (German "Herstellerinsolvenz", then "device abandonment" consensus) → Okun 2024 JAMA Netw Open, the on-point item Gate 2 missed in the candidate's own exposure vocabulary; adversary 3 Q1 (PIP liquidation + count + rupture-rate comparison) → Keogh 2012, the largest real instance of the exposure, which Gate 2 never touched; adversary 3 Q8 → the STAT op-ed finally opened, and it does NOT pose the question. Full lists: ledger/batches/2026-10-22-0633/UQ-20261022-10-record.md and the three adversary-N files in that folder.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): PRIOR A — Okun MS, Marjenin T, Ekanayake J, Gilbert F, Doherty SP, Pilkington J, French J, Kubu C, Lazaro-Munoz G, Denison T, Giordano J. "Definition of Implanted Neurological Device Abandonment: A Systematic Review and Consensus Statement." JAMA Network Open 2024;7(4):e248654, doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.8654, FULL TEXT opened at the Oxford ORA deposit by adversary 2. PRIOR B — Keogh B et al., "Poly Implant Prothese (PIP) breast implants: final report of the Expert Group," Department of Health, 18 June 2012, FULL TEXT opened by adversary 3. PRIOR C — Sheldon RJG et al., "Clinical outcomes following switching antipsychotic treatment due to market withdrawal... pipotiazine palmitate," Ther Adv Psychopharmacol 2022;12, ABSTRACT ONLY (figshare 403, PMC hard-blocked). The record's own Priors 1 and 3 (Lazaro-Munoz et al., Brain Stimulation 2022, abstract only; Dick HB, CRST letter March 2023, full text) are demoted to normative siblings — no unit, endpoint, comparator or estimand in common with either limb.

Novelty — how this differs from each: From A — Okun 2024 defines the exposure (four failure modes, abandonment as failures of responsibility) and has a section on company insolvency, so the record's claim that no definition exists is wrong in substance; but the NUMBER CHECK is decisive and was done from full text: it prints no count, no prevalence and no outcome rate, its only figures are article counts (734 screened, 7 included; 232/41 for pacemakers), its Limitations say "the literature was sparse on this topic", and it asks for payer engagement, explant-cost clarity and definitional work — not for a count, a registry or surveillance. A definition is not an evaluation; it DEFINES, and partly FORECASTS ("We anticipate that challenges similar to those noted for cardiac pacemaker use would increase in number"). From B — Keogh 2012 is the one place the candidate's analysis shape has been PERFORMED AND PUBLISHED, and the numbers can be named: "an estimated 35,000 women with PIP implants" (para 23, no uncertainty, no cited source) and failure 1.2%/3.1% at 5/10 years versus 0.2-0.4%/0.5-1.1% for other brands, "more likely to fail... by a factor of around 2-6" (para 17). But it carries no "support" construct, never defines or dates a post-exit period, per the summariser never states that the manufacturer ceased to exist, and its unit is implant failure in a passive class under a product-defect construct. It is a one-event construct-and-grain gap on the passive-class flank, not the candidate's multi-event support-as-exposure question. From C — same estimand structure on a dispensed drug, where delisting date IS the exposure date and the dispensing record IS the denominator; substitution is available, nothing remains in the body, and explant, revision and contraindication acquisition have no analogue.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Grade note: Medium, not High — Prior C is the same design one field away, and Gate 2 missed both Prior A (own field, own exposure vocabulary) and Prior B (largest exposed population) across 11 queries, so the search record is incomplete and that alone bars Validated. Not Low — no opened source prints the candidate quantity for the support-withdrawal exposure: Okun 2024 defines and forecasts, Keogh 2012 measures a different construct at a different grain for one passive-class event, the ANSM and EMA notices announce a production stop, the Alpha AMS abstract announces a cumulative head-count (n=30) with no post-exit outcome, and the STAT op-ed (opened) argues. No table, figure or sentence in any opened source prints an exit-exposure incidence or an outcome contrast attributed to lost support.

Significance — consequence: a substantial exposed population with measurably worse post-exit outcomes converts a decade of anecdote into an effect size and makes escrow of programming software and firmware keys, a transfer-of-support duty surviving insolvency, and mandatory registry follow-up of withdrawn models arguable on evidence; a null calibrates the alarm down and leaves the unenumerability result. Deflated by two adversary findings: regulators acted in the MIP case without any count (so the fact base was not what action waited on), and the field's strongest document asks for no count.
Significance — audience: evidenced as real — a national parliament took three written questions on one event, ANSM convened the EVADIAC network, EMA issued a DHPC, NICE ran an HTG consultation on retinal implants, and 11 authors across neurology, engineering, ethics and patient advocacy convened on the exposure in 2024. Not evidenced as demanding THIS estimate: no opened document asks anyone to count exposed recipients or contrast their outcomes.
Significance — fecundity: what artefact set must be escrowed per class; whether support-continuity risk should be priced at approval; the surveillance definition of "support"; whether registry follow-up lapses differentially for withdrawn products; the explant-versus-abandon-in-situ rule for a dead implant.
Significance — anchoring: post-trial obligations in neuroethics; Argus II, Alpha AMS, Freehand, ATI, Nuvectra, Pixium; UDI-in-claims completeness (Pew/NESTcc); EU supply-continuity rules under Regulation (EU) 2024/1860; and by negation the recall literature, which exists because a trading manufacturer can be made to act.

Reason for silence: the record's primary mechanism (the data custodian disappears at the moment of exposure) was contradicted by both instances adversary 3 opened — in the MIP case the custodian stayed and still printed no count, and in PIP a regulator estimated a count without the manufacturer. The mechanism that survives is the disciplinary split, now corroborated rather than asserted: the normative half was claimed in 2024 by a consensus panel with no epidemiologist on it, which asked only normative and financial questions, while the enumerative half went to investigative journalism and to per-event incident response (PIP) or bilateral wind-down notices (MIP), so the general question never forms. Adversary 1 adds a credible statistical mechanism: at n=30 to a few hundred per event, no epidemiologist frames a cohort study.

Vagueness | "support" is stipulated, so the event count and the exposed population are free parameters — under the six-constituent rule a solvent vendor's routine end-of-service qualifies, and every external-component class generates one per product generation; and the matched comparator makes exposure collinear with implant vintage | pre-registration, per-class estimands, sensitivity over definition variants and the within-person contrast constrain analyst freedom within one study; the vintage collinearity is real and unnamed in the record, and the two opened notices show the date rule has nothing to bite on | Partial (A1, A2, A3)
6. Significance inflation | per-event populations are tens to low hundreds, so limb (ii) cannot be powered per class; the field's strongest document asks for no count; regulators acted without one; and the uncountable-share fallback cannot be deflated by any data | audiences are evidenced as real and active; a surveillance-blind-spot measurement is actionable for registry custodians; but "a community asked for obligations" is not "a community asked for this estimate", and no opened source shows a decision that waited on this number | Partial (A1, A2, A3)
7. Reason for silence | the custody-gap story explains why answering is hard, not why nobody asked, and is contradicted by both opened instances | the disciplinary-split mechanism is corroborated by the 2024 panel's composition and asks, and the small-numbers mechanism is credible; "nobody thought of it" is not relied on; the record named the wrong primary mechanism | Resolved (A2); Partial (A1, A3)
8. Dissolution | the event list decomposes into three incommensurable regimes — passive classes where exit cause and ascertainment dominate, active singletons with no comparator and pre/post confounded by device ageing, and multi-vendor active classes where the design works — so the per-class estimand is three questions in one wording | the collapse path is pre-declared and the uncountable/undatable share is one coherent headline quantity across regimes; the multi-vendor active regime is a real un-asked question, but the graded wording does not isolate it, so after stratification most cells hold one event | Partial (A1, A2, A3)

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Score note: well-posedness stays at 2 — the exposure is stipulated not discovered, "contraindication acquisition" has no operational rule in anything opened, exposure ascertainment is reflexive with the phenomenon, and adversary 3 adds two defects (exposure mis-assignment for passive classes; confounding by exit cause). Significance lowered from the record's 3 to 2: audiences are evidenced, demand for this specific estimate is not.

Strongest remaining objection: adversary 3's attack-4 leg L2 — in the largest real instance of the candidate's exposure (PIP, a liquidated manufacturer's implant, Keogh 2012 opened in full), the post-exit excess the candidate's own definition would record is a product-defect effect (failure 2-6x other brands, para 17), the post-exit explant incidence is set by an NHS scan-and-remove offer keyed to the PROVIDER's solvency (paras 2(x), 34), and rupture ascertainment moves roughly tenfold with method (1.1% spontaneous versus 14% screened for the same implant, para 15, cited from the Mentor study), so the pre/post and matched contrast the wording specifies measures the cause of and the response to the exit rather than the consequence of lost support — and the permitted null does not catch it, because this event yields a positive that is not a support effect. The objection stands on L2, which is sourced to printed paragraph numbers in an opened document. If L2 fell, L1 would survive on its own: in the only two support-withdrawal notices anyone on this record has opened, the constituents are open-ended and no count or end-of-support date is printed, so the declared event-date rule is inoperable. L3 would also survive and is the narrowest. Vulnerability of this objection, recorded as required: L1's extension beyond the managed-wind-down sub-kind rests on nothing anybody has measured — it is an inference from how that document kind is designed, not a reported result, since no abrupt-liquidation field-safety notice has been opened by the record or any adversary; it is an empirical 2-of-2 finding on two documents, not an algebraic identity, and not a bitwise or exhaustive check of the document kind. The single unopened source most likely to settle it is the Swissmedic field safety corrective action notice of 2018-12-17 for the Autonomic Technologies Pulsante SPG microstimulator (with the Dutch IGJ 2017 field safety notice for the same device second); the single unopened peer-reviewed item most likely to settle the attack-2 residue is Regional Anesthesia & Pain Medicine 50(12):923.
Promotion requires: re-scoping the canonical wording to abrupt commercial exits in multi-vendor ACTIVE implant classes, with exit-cause/alert-coincidence stratification, symptomatic endpoints and an event-date rule recoverable for liquidation events written in (taking well-posedness to 3/3), AND completing the search record by adding Okun 2024 and Keogh 2012 as priors and opening three named items — RAPM 50(12):923, the 2015 Int J Breast Cancer PIP explantation comparison, and the Insuman Implantable post-authorisation study (EMA catalogue 49593). TWO ITEMS STRUCK ON VERIFICATION: the Swissmedic 2018-12-17 and IGJ 2017 ATI notices were opened and are the wrong kind of document for the question the entry nominated them to decide — one is a recall of unimplanted stock and the other a certification-driven distribution hold, neither an exit or end-of-support notice for an implanted device, so they cannot settle the event-date rule either way — plus Article 10a of Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 at the eur-lex /oj/eng route to settle P6.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open the two abrupt-exit field safety notices named above and check whether that sub-kind of document carries a datable loss of a named support constituent and any recipient count; the whole instrument question turns on it, and nobody has looked.
