## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

Four fresh-context checkers were each handed one claim and its source, with the entry's citations but not its reasoning; the fourth opened five actual field safety and end-of-support notices. Logs: `VERIFY-okun-2024-abandonment.md`, `VERIFY-keogh-2012-pip.md`, `VERIFY-sheldon-pipotiazine.md`, `VERIFY-uq10-support-withdrawal-notices.md` in this folder. **Verdict unchanged: Provisional. More of this entry's reasoning changed on verification than on any other entry in this batch.**

**1. Okun 2024 holds as read, and its regime is narrower than the cap it carries.** On the full text the checker read, it prints **no** count, **no** prevalence, **no** incidence and **no** outcome rate; "prevalence" and "incidence" do not occur; the only person-numbers are one undenominated NeuroVista anecdote and the composition of the consensus panel. The "defines without evaluating" characterisation is accurate and, if anything, understated: the paper also relays no count or rate from its 7 included articles, and it **does not call for** enumeration or outcome measurement — "registry", "track", "surveillance", "incidence" and "prevalence" are all absent, and its forward-looking ask is for "guidelines, policies, and laws". Two qualifications now bear on the Medium cap. **Regime:** this source's regime is active implantable **neurotechnological** devices, DBS, VNS and SCS, with the **article** as its unit (734 screened, 7 included). Inside DBS/VNS/SCS the cap is well founded; pitched at implanted devices broadly, or at non-neurological implants, Okun 2024 is **silent in that regime rather than prior art in it**, and the cap would need another source to carry it. **Kind of anticipation:** a definition citation is not an evaluation. It anticipates *defining* abandonment and anticipates nothing about *measuring* it, so if this candidate's contribution is enumeration, prevalence or an outcome rate, this source does not touch it. One hazard for anyone rewriting the entry: do not let the surrounding insolvency discussion migrate into the definition, whose support clause is actor- and cause-agnostic ("Failure to fulfill reasonable responsibility for medical, technical, and/or financial support prior to the end of an implantable device's labeled lifetime") — manufacturer exit is the paper's motivating example, handled in the body, not a trigger enumerated in the definition.

**2. Keogh 2012 REFUTES the support-withdrawal framing on four of six sub-claims, and this is the sharpest finding of the batch.** The two numbers hold: "an estimated 35,000 women" is printed verbatim at paragraph 23 as the denominator of a 0.6% rupture rate over MHRA reports 2007–2009, and it counts women in the UK **estimated to have PIP implants**, that is recipients, not women still implanted and not a post-explantation residual, which the report never gives. "By a factor of around 2-6" is printed twice, in the Summary and at paragraph 17(i), backed by printed component rates (PIP 1.2% at 5 years and 3.1% at 10; other brands 0.2–0.4% and 0.5–1.1%) — but it is meaningful **only inside reported-adverse-event ascertainment**, the report itself saying the true rate is higher and that cross-brand comparison is not on "a truly comparable basis", and a separate 3–5 factor applies to local clinical signs and is a different claim. What refutes: the **construct** is product defect and manufacturing fraud ("the non-medical grade silicone illegally used by PIP", "after the discovery of the fraud in March 2010") and the report says **nothing** about PIP's insolvency or exit, its one "no longer in business" sentence concerning **private clinics'** aftercare obligations with the NHS backfilling consultation, scanning and removal — a payer and provider exit construct, not a device-support construct; **no post-exit period** is defined or measured, outcomes being indexed to time since implantation with the post-discovery era **excluded** as a reporting-bias confounder; there is **no support construct at all** — no programming, parts, external components or remote monitoring anywhere in the document, a passive gel prosthesis having nothing to withdraw, which makes it different **in kind** and not merely in degree; and there is **no matched comparison**, only aggregate unmatched "other brands" with market-share-asymmetric denominators and bias adjustment in place of matching. Net: good prior art for a product-defect mass-notification and aftercare-liability event, including the genuinely relevant point that a private provider's commercial exit can strand patients and shift aftercare onto a public system — and **not** prior art for a device-support-withdrawal question.

**3. Sheldon is prior art on METHOD, not on exposure, and the entry should name it as such.** It holds in its weak form: a real cohort, a market withdrawal as the exposure, hard clinical endpoints (discontinuation, acute care use) over a defined post-withdrawal window, in a named jurisdiction, on 137 patients in 2022. So the appeal to novelty must not rest on "nobody has measured clinical outcomes after a product left the market", because this paper did. It fails in the form that would sink the candidate: its estimand is **which of three available substitutes a patient received and how they fared**, which cannot be evaluated where substitution is impossible, and a result proved under substitution is silent, not supportive, outside it. Whether this entry's novelty survives therefore depends on whether its claim is pitched at the method or at the non-substitutable exposure; pitched at the method, this paper weakens it materially. Two things must not be recorded as settled: **anything numerical**, since the checker did not open the paper and the figures in hand are abstract-level, denominator-uncertain and interval-free; and **"no comparator"**, which is Unresolved and distinguishable in Methods only. A routing correction: the batch's confident "this journal is open access at journals.sagepub.com, try that directly" did not serve this reader — SAGE failed as well as figshare (403) and PMC (blocked), and a successor should start at `api.figshare.com/v2/articles/23488739` through WebFetch to recover the `ndownloader` link to the 287.82 kB PDF.

**4. Five exit notices opened, and the instrument question decomposes three ways.** Of the five documents opened, **3** are genuine exit, discontinuation or end-of-support notices for an implanted device or a constituent of one; the other 2 are a recall of unimplanted stock and a certification-driven distribution hold, and are the wrong kind of document for this question. **Holds and now extends beyond the regime it was formed in — open-ended constituents:** 3 of 3 implant-level notices leave the constituent list open, one on its face with "including" and "for example" plus "may require support for many years", one enumerating nothing, one naming two ending items and leaving software, technical support and troubleshooting unaddressed. The entry's recorded vulnerability, that this was an inference from how the document kind is designed rather than a reported result, is **partly discharged**: it is a reported result in 5 of 5 documents, and for the first time in an **abrupt commercial exit**, the sub-kind the entry listed as untested. **Holds for the implant, fails for the constituent — no end-of-support date:** 0 of 3 implant-level notices date the loss of any support constituent, while the one constituent-level notice dates it day-precise (Cochlear Kanso 1, 30 September 2025). So "no end-of-support date is printed" must be re-scoped to **whole-device exit notices**, and what this shows is not that the event-date rule is inoperable but that it is **mis-grained**: dates appear when the unit of the notice is a named constituent, which is the granularity the rule itself asks about. **Fails — no recipient count:** P2 is falsified, as recorded above. The proportions, reported as found and not as advice: carried a patient count 1 of 3 (1 of 5 overall); carried a dated end of support 1 of 3, and that date is for an external constituent, so for the implant itself 0 of 3; carried a dated commercial exit event 2 of 3 (one day-precise, one month-only); carried a closed constituent list 0 of 3; said something about clinical consequences or patient management 3 of 3, ranging from explant/exchange/continue guidance down to "there is nothing they need to do at this time" with no clinical risk statement.

**5. What this does to well-posedness, stated as a finding and not as a score.** The defect cited to hold well-posedness at 2/3 — that the declared event-date rule dates nothing — **survives for the implant-exit sub-kind**, and now has three documents under it rather than two, including the sub-kind the entry said was untested. But three of the surrounding supports move: the uncountability presupposition is falsified by a printed figure; the two documents the entry nominated as decisive are the wrong kind and cannot decide it; and the exit itself is datable and published, so "dates nothing" is accurate only about support constituents, never about the event. What the sources show is that the gap is a **granularity and unit problem** — notices date constituents when they name constituents, and date exits always — rather than the absence of datable public facts. Two of the five promotion items are therefore no longer useful and are struck above. Whether the remainder leaves the score at 2/3 or lifts it is a judgement for whoever rewrites the canonical wording, and this entry does not pre-empt it.

Strongest remaining objection: attack 4, on three legs, and the verdict stands on leg (a) alone — a leg reached independently by two adversaries that never saw each other's work. Leg (a), DEFINITIONAL and read from opened sources (adversary #1 raw, adversary #2 at code-search fragment level, and re-read byte-exact from the raw module by the post-batch verification pass): in ietf-ptp@2019-05-07.yang the description of `current-utc-offset` OPENS with "The offset between TAI and UTC" and runs in full "The offset between TAI and UTC when the epoch of the PTP system is the PTP epoch in units of seconds, i.e., when ptp-timescale is TRUE; otherwise, the value has no meaning." — the continuation is a condition of applicability, not a change of quantity, and if anything it STRENGTHENS this leg, since a field explicitly meaningless unless `ptp-timescale` is TRUE is even less assimilable to a UT1−UTC quantity. All four of the record's own instances carry the accumulated TAI−UTC offset or a bare flag rather than UT1−UTC (the accumulated TAI−UTC offset being 10 s plus accumulated leap seconds — 37 s at 1 Jan 2017 against 27 leap seconds inserted by then, which is THIS ENTRY'S OWN ARITHMETIC from linuxptp's printed `#define CURRENT_UTC_OFFSET  37 /* 1 Jan 2017 */`; no source opened prints the decomposition). IEEE Std 1588 itself was NOT read, being paywalled — COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND — so the announce-message instance rests on two named proxies: IEEE's own `ieee802-dot1as-gptp.yang`, whose same-named leaf is glossed "Offset from UTC (TAI - UTC). The offset is in units of seconds.", and linuxptp's `msg.h`/`ds.h`, which declare `Integer16 currentUtcOffset` on the wire and in `timePropertiesDS` with that 37 s default. V2's per-member estimand and the draft 3,600 s ceiling are both on |UT1−UTC|, the Earth-rotation residual, and not on the atomic-minus-civil integral offset TAI−UTC — so for that class the measurand has no referent, the record's worked cell is the conflation, and V2's taxonomy classifies the mechanism's SHAPE while never reporting which offset it carries. The frame in fact mixes AT LEAST THREE incommensurable offset kinds, not two — TAI−UTC, UT1−UTC, and UT1 − GPST, the third supplied by Steigenberger et al. (2022) — and a |UT1−UTC| ceiling fails to reach the first and the third alike. Leg (b), that the accumulated TAI−UTC offset is frozen under continuous UTC so the 3,600 s ceiling never reaches a TAI−UTC field, would NOT survive alone, and remains the ADVERSARY'S OWN INFERENCE: it follows from what "continuity" means rather than from any reported result. The post-batch pass obtained verbatim the operative parts of the only two documents that could have settled it, and they neither overturned nor established it — Resolution 4 (2022)'s operative part contains no occurrence of "TAI" at all, no "leap second", and no statement that leap seconds cease, every operative reference to a quantity being to "the difference (UT1-UTC)"; and CGPM-2026 Draft Resolution C never writes "UTC-TAI" or "TAI-UTC" in its operative part and says nothing there about the offset becoming constant, its only TAI content being a recital that UTC differs "from TAI only by an integral number of seconds". So leg (b) is an inference that SURVIVED a verbatim check of the only two documents that could have settled it — not a gap awaiting a document, and not document-supported either; it must not be re-labelled as document-supported. The two obvious targets are now exhausted, and what remains open is the CCTF's report to the 28th CGPM (COULD NOT READ in the post-batch pass) or the ITU-R TF.460 successor. Leg (b) is also exactly the step that slides between two quantities on the shared token "UTC", from a ceiling on the Earth-rotation residual |UT1−UTC| to the behaviour of the integral offset TAI−UTC. Leg (c), reach ("most of the frame"), would not survive alone either, and adversary #2's own Disguise return bears on it — but not as this entry formerly recorded, and the former wording is STRUCK: the claim that Steigenberger et al. establish a genuine UT1−UTC-carrying artifact class in GNSS broadcast navigation messages, the four-constellation parenthesis "(GPS CNAV, BeiDou, QZSS, IRNSS)" attached to that class, and the characterisation that the return "cuts in the candidate's favour", are all struck as unsupported by the paper. What the paper supports is narrower: Steigenberger et al. (GPS Solutions 26:50, 2022) establish a broadcast EARTH-ROTATION-PARAMETER class in four constellations — "ERPs are included in the GPS/QZSS CNAV and CNAV-2, BeiDou CNAV-1, CNAV-2 and CNAV-3," "as well as IRNSS NAV messages" — and evaluate its ΔUT1 to about 0.13 ms against IERS C04. It does NOT establish that those fields carry UT1−UTC: for GPS it reports that "∆UT1 = UT1 − UTC has been replaced by ∆UT1GPS = UT1 − GPST" from IS-GPS-200L/705G/800G (2020), because GPST "is a continuous time scale" that "avoids potential problems in the vicinity of leap second changes", and it states that "no details about the origin of the ERP data and the parameterization of the ERP prediction model are provided for BDS, QZSS, and IRNSS". The four words "UT1 − UTC" are verbatim in the paper and the clause they sit in says the OPPOSITE of what this entry used them for — a grammar-on-both-sides-of-the-cut failure inherited from adversary #2 and amplified here. The frame therefore gains four CANDIDATE members and no confirmed UT1−UTC members, and "larger than adversary #1's small" is now an UNSOURCED step in this entry rather than an adversary's concession. If (b) and (c) both fell, (a) would still bar V2 as graded, because every repair either adversary names is a different question and the one permitted reformulation is spent on V2.

One residual, declared and not inferred: the "unperformed" half rests on an absence check over slides 1-13 and 16-23 that was summariser-mediated rather than verbatim — enough for routing, not enough to use this entry as evidence that the GNSS community has done no such assessment. ## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What the pass was, and what each checker was sent to read.** Seven fresh-context checkers ran after the batch closed. Each was blind to the reviewers' reasoning and each was sent to re-read one load-bearing source first-hand. Checker 1 took ietf-ptp@2019-05-07.yang together with the record's other three P2 instances (the PTP announce-message `currentUtcOffset`, the NTP leap indicator, the Linux/C `tai_offset`), i.e. the definitional core of attack 4 leg (a). Checker 2 took Report ITU-R TF.2511-0 (10/2022), and section 6 in particular, this entry's own nominated single most-likely-to-settle source. Checker 3 took the CGPM resolution this entry cited for the |UT1−UTC| ceiling, plus the CGPM-2026 material behind the 3,600 s figure. **Leg (a) was re-tested first-hand and survived, which is why the verdict does not move.** The entry's quotation was a left-whole, right-cut string presented as the whole declaration, and that cut is the defect: the module's description OPENS with "The offset between TAI and UTC" and runs in full "The offset between TAI and UTC when the epoch of the PTP system is the PTP epoch in units of seconds, i.e., when ptp-timescale is TRUE; otherwise, the value has no meaning." The entry's prose now carries the full printed string and says the quoted words open the declaration. The continuation is a condition of applicability, not a change of quantity, so it does not reverse the leg and if anything strengthens it. The type is confirmed `type int16` with no `range` and no `units` substatement anywhere on the leaf, gated by `when "../current-utc-offset-valid='true'"`; no source opened prints 32,767 or any maximum, so the entry's labelling of that figure as its own arithmetic stays exactly as it was. All four instances check out in substance: three carry the accumulated TAI−UTC offset (the ietf-ptp leaf; the announce-message field, glossed by IEEE's own 802.1AS module as "Offset from UTC (TAI - UTC). The offset is in units of seconds." and carried in linuxptp as `Integer16 currentUtcOffset` with `#define CURRENT_UTC_OFFSET  37 /* 1 Jan 2017 */`; and the Linux `tai_offset`, which linuxptp assigns straight from the announce field into `tx.modes = ADJ_TAI` under the comment "/* Update TAI-UTC offset of the system clock if valid and traceable. */") and the fourth, NTP's leap indicator, is a bare two-bit warning flag — "LI Leap Indicator (leap): 2-bit integer warning of an impending leap second to be inserted or deleted" — with no magnitude field at all. NO instance carries UT1−UTC, and nothing in the five documents read offers a bridge; linuxptp's own shipped default of 37 s is more than forty times the IERS |DUT1| ceiling of 0.9 s, so a |UT1−UTC| bound applied to that field would reject the field's own default value.

**Claims struck.** Two, both in the Strongest-remaining-objection paragraph, both on Steigenberger et al. First, the claim that the paper establishes a genuine UT1−UTC-carrying artifact class in GNSS broadcast navigation messages, together with the four-constellation parenthesis "(GPS CNAV, BeiDou, QZSS, IRNSS)" attached to it. Second, the characterisation that the return "cuts in the candidate's favour". The paper's only UT1−UTC equation sits inside the sentence recording GPS moving away from it — "∆UT1 = UT1 − UTC has been replaced by ∆UT1GPS = UT1 − GPST", from IS-GPS-200L/705G/800G (2020), because GPST "is a continuous time scale" that "avoids potential problems in the vicinity of leap second changes" — and for the other three the paper's own disclaimer is "no details about the origin of the ERP data and the parameterization of the ERP prediction model are provided for BDS, QZSS, and IRNSS". The four words "UT1 − UTC" are verbatim in the paper and the clause they sit in says the opposite of what this entry used them for: a grammar-on-both-sides-of-the-cut failure inherited from adversary #2 and amplified here. What the paper does establish, and what the entry now says, is a broadcast earth-rotation-parameter class in four constellations — "ERPs are included in the GPS/QZSS CNAV and CNAV-2, BeiDou CNAV-1, CNAV-2 and CNAV-3," "as well as IRNSS NAV messages" — evaluated to about 0.13 ms against IERS C04, with no bit width, scale factor, LSB or range printed for any of them. The frame gains four candidate members and no confirmed UT1−UTC members, so "larger than adversary #1's small" is now recorded as an unsourced step in this entry rather than as an adversary's concession. One consequence runs the other way and is now in the prose: UT1 − GPST is a third offset kind that a |UT1−UTC| ceiling also fails to reach, so leg (a) is reinforced in shape and the entry says "at least three incommensurable offset kinds", not two.

**Claims narrowed.** The CGPM quantity language is narrowed throughout: the ceiling is on the magnitude of the Earth-rotation residual |UT1−UTC|, which Draft Resolution C asks the BIPM to "continue to monitor", and not on the atomic-minus-civil integral offset TAI−UTC; leg (b) is flagged in the prose as exactly the step that slides between the two on the shared token "UTC". Leg (b) itself is narrowed from "the one leg that a document could overturn" to an inference that survived a verbatim check of the only two documents that could have settled it: Resolution 4 (2022)'s operative part contains no occurrence of "TAI" at all, no "leap second", and no statement that leap seconds cease, every operative reference to a quantity being to "the difference (UT1-UTC)"; Draft Resolution C never writes "UTC-TAI" or "TAI-UTC" in its operative part, its only TAI content being the recital that UTC differs "from TAI only by an integral number of seconds". So leg (b) is neither overturned nor document-supported, and it is not to be re-labelled as document-supported. "Continuous without any future adjustment", which the entry had used as if operative, is a recital reporting an industrial-user requirement, and the prose now says so. The terminology "the LEAP COUNT" is replaced throughout by "the accumulated TAI−UTC offset": the field carries 10 s plus accumulated leap seconds, 37 s at 1 Jan 2017 against 27 leap seconds inserted by then, a decomposition labelled in the prose as this entry's own arithmetic because no source opened prints it. The TF.2511-0 read level is narrowed to "table of contents plus body through section 5.2; section 6 unread", and the entry's "no annexes, no tables" aside is corrected, the complete TOC in fact running sections 1-8 plus Annexes 1-4. Legs (b) and (c) are re-pointed: section 4, "Systems for dissemination of time signals", is where the per-format material lives and where the only DUT1 line anyone has read sits — 4.3.1, "contains the DUT1 (the offset between UT1 and UTC with a resolution of 0.1 s)", a quantisation step and not a maximum, served as a fragment whose subject was never delivered — while section 6, organised by impacted domain with only 6.1-6.5 naming radiocommunication services, stays right for leg (b), whose premise remains UNTESTED against this source. Rec. ITU-R TF.460 is named as the document where DUT1 encoding is actually specified, and named as a next source only: it was not read in this pass. Every "six" is narrowed to "six named devices (the page's prose says seven)", the device table naming six T-BCs from six vendors while the body prose of the same page says "seven Telecom Boundary Clocks" and the seventh is named nowhere. Seaman's "no maximum representable offset" limb is narrowed so it rests on the record rather than on silence: the paper does print ±0.9 s, the current UTC standard's bound on |DUT1|, cited as the threshold past which existing code is unvetted, with no artifact characterised against it; and the 90% figure is narrowed to the explicit counterfactual it is — "Even if 90% of the files identified using the current UTC search terms were to turn out not to require direct modification, the remaining file count would still represent four times as many files as were modified for Y2K." — neither the author's estimate nor a measurement. The note that 1312 and 11,600 are not co-located is added, 1312 sitting in a body sentence of "A BRIEF UTC INVENTORY OF IRAF" and 11,600 in the Table 1 caption, "The total number of source files searched is about 11,600."

**Claims strengthened, and claims confirmed outright.** The EANTC limb was understated in the entry's own favour and is now stated as what the document supports: the test PASSED. An emulated T-GM was "sending announce messages with the leap59 flag set to true, which is required to announce a negative leap second, and UTC Offset being set to 37", the chain was put into deliberate holdover with the T-GM link cut at 23:55:00 so each boundary clock had to process the event itself rather than forward a pre-digested Announce, and afterwards "all T-BCs showed that leap59 was set to false and that UTC Offset had been set to 36, the correct expected behaviour, as verified using the Calnex Paragon neo and the Keysight Time Sync Analyzer." That is a clean pass nowhere near any limit, which makes the entry's "every maximum in play is ALGEBRAIC" firmer rather than weaker. The entry's earlier rendering, "leap59 set to true and UTC Offset set to 37", was an unmarked elision of an intervening relative clause presented as verbatim, and it is replaced by the full printed string. The entry's note that EANTC carries no UT1−UTC value is confirmed and protected in the prose: the 37 is the PTP `currentUtcOffset`, which the page itself scopes with "leap seconds only affect UTC time, not TAI", so it is a value of a neighbouring field and not a small instance of the |UT1−UTC| magnitude the 3,600 s threshold governs. Novelty Medium is SUSTAINED, and the reason is sharper than the entry had it: Seaman's 1312 is a different quantity in a different unit at a prior stage of the same work — a lexical candidate count, 65.3% of it from the single term "Second" (857 of 1312, this entry's own arithmetic), whose own author says "this requires human review to comprehend the intent of the algorithms in each file" — and not a weaker measurement of the candidate's quantity. The pass also records, so that a later reader does not weaken the entry with it, that Seaman's two apparent internal mismatches both reconcile (the 90% sentence's denominator is files "modified for Y2K", about a third of the roughly 124 surveyed; and the "less than 1%" runs against a base that includes documentation while the 11,600 excludes it), so nothing here should lean on any claim that the paper is internally inconsistent.

**Citation corrections.** The largest is the CGPM citation, which was wrong twice over. There is no "CGPM Resolution 5 (2022)" about UTC: Resolution 5 of the 27th CGPM (2022) is "On the future redefinition of the second" (DOI 10.59161/CGPM2022RES5E), and the UTC resolution is Resolution 4 of the 27th CGPM (2022), "On the use and future development of UTC" (DOI 10.59161/CGPM2022RES4E). Nor does that resolution set a ceiling: it "decides that the maximum value for the difference (UT1-UTC) will be increased in, or before, 2035," and "requests that the CIPM consult with the ITU, and other organizations that may be impacted by this decision in order to … propose a new maximum value for the difference (UT1-UTC) that will ensure the continuity of UTC for at least a century," which is the opposite of fixing one; the strings "3600", "3 600" and "one hour" do not appear in it. The 3,600 s figure belongs to CGPM-2026 Draft Resolution C, "On the technical actions needed to ensure the continuity of UTC", in its operative sentence "the maximum value for the difference |UT1-UTC| will be 3 600 seconds (1 hour), ensuring the long-term continuity for UTC for several centuries", alongside "continuous UTC will become effective on 20 May 2027," — a draft before the 28th CGPM, served at version 4.0 and endorsed for update by Decision CIPM/115-05 (2026), which "fixes 20 May 2027 as the implementation date of the new maximum value". Every occurrence in the entry has been re-attributed and labelled a draft, and the resolution number, the verb and the attribution of the figure are all corrected. The other corrections: Report ITU-R TF.2511-0 is carried by its printed title, "Content and structure of time signals to be disseminated by radiocommunication systems and various aspects of current and potential future reference time scales, including their impacts and applications in radiocommunication", with institutional authorship (ITU-R, Radiocommunication Study Group 7) and no DOI issued — the entry carried no rival title string of its own, so nothing had to be dropped, but it is worth recording for a later pass that the commonly used short label "Impact of a continuous reference time scale on radiocommunication services" is approximately section 6's heading and not the report's title. Coleman is expanded to Michael J. Coleman, Naval Center for Space Technology, US Naval Research Laboratory, also listed as a member of the CCTF's Task Force on Continuous UTC, with the meeting given in full. The ICG document is carried by its own identifier ICG/REC/2025 and title, "Information on the work related to the proposed redefinition of UTC (revision of Recommendation 16-B (2016))", with "Recommendation C" marked as the filename label. The EANTC report takes its full printed title, "EANTC Transport & Cloud Networks Interop Test Report 2026", with corporate authorship and no DOI; the entry's caveat that its year came from the URL path is withdrawn, because 2026 is printed in the page body in the report's own title, and is replaced by the caveat that no publication date is printed anywhere read and that the hot-staging dates "From January 26 to February 6" carry no year. Seaman gains his first name and the front matter that arXiv:1112.0067 is v1 only, submitted 2011-12-01, with no DOI and no journal reference, so none should be sought. Steigenberger et al. gain their title, and the honest note that the publisher page as served truncates the author list at "et al." with an empty affiliations block, so positions 4-5 of the five-author citation are COULD NOT READ, neither confirmed nor contradicted.

**Routes that failed, recorded so a later pass does not repeat them.** `curl` to the TF.2511-0 PDF at itu.int returned "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" — a tool-scoped policy denial that was reported and not retried or routed around, while WebFetch reached the same URL; the consequence is that the PDF could not be put on disk for a local text extraction, which is the route most likely to deliver section 6. WebFetch on that PDF at offset 85000 and again at offset 115000 both terminated inside section 5.2, each reported as cut off mid-sentence, so paging further forward buys nothing: the extracted text itself ends there. WebFetch on the .docx edition returned a 13-character body, because the tool does not unpack Office zip containers, so the offset was never the issue; the .docx is a zip and `word/document.xml` can be read out of it directly. The ITU publication page carries no direct PDF link at all. `curl` to the RFC editor was refused with a CONNECT tunnel 403 while WebFetch succeeded on the same URL; `curl` to IEEE's grouper host was refused at the egress proxy with `connect_rejected`, so the 802.1AS module came through the summariser only. Crossref at `api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/s10291-022-01232-4` returned RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED on two separate calls, which is why the Steigenberger author list stands truncated. Springer served the article three times but never served Table 1 or Table 2, so those are unread rather than absent. On the Seaman and unoosa documents nothing failed at the host: what failed was a prompt — the summariser declined long consecutive verbatim passages twice for Seaman and declined a whole-document transcription for the ICG PDF, and in both cases re-requesting the load-bearing sentence or the operative clause as numbered consecutive sub-cap fragments succeeded. No search was refused by the classifier in any of the seven checks.

**What the pass did not reach.** IEEE Std 1588's own clause text (paywalled). The body of TF.2511-0 section 6, its section 7, its sections 5.3-8 generally and its four annexes — including Annex 4, the industry petition letter. Rec. ITU-R TF.460 in any form in this pass. Any standalone CCTF report on Draft Resolution C, and with it the one remaining place an operative statement about TAI−UTC under continuous UTC would live. The official combined PDF of the 27th CGPM resolutions and the authoritative French text of Resolution 4. The verbatim recitals of Resolution 4 and of Draft Resolution C. Slides 1-13 and 16-23 of the Coleman deck line by line. Steigenberger's tables, figures, affiliations and dates, and the four governing ICDs (IS-GPS-200L message type 32 / IS-GPS-800G, BDS-SIS-ICD B-CNAV-1/2/3, IS-QZSS-PNT-004, the IRNSS SPS ICD) where per-constellation referents and bit counts would actually be found. The twelve sibling EANTC test pages. RFC 5905 past Section 10. Nothing in that list is scored in either direction.

**The verdict did not move, and no late Gate 4 was owed.** The entry stays Rejected, on attack 4 leg (a) alone, exactly as graded. Leg (a) was re-tested first-hand on ietf-ptp@2019-05-07.yang by a byte-exact raw read, and both conditions the brief named for the kill falling came back FALSE: the definition is what the entry says it is (the quoted words open the declaration and nothing after the cut departs from TAI−UTC), and none of the named instances carries UT1−UTC (three carry the accumulated TAI−UTC offset, one is a bare two-bit flag). A fatal ground that survives first-hand re-testing of its own sources is not a withdrawn ground, and a late Gate 4 is owed only where the ground is withdrawn; so none ran, and none should. Nothing in this pass promotes anything, and nothing here is a promotion condition, this entry being Rejected. The corrections above are copy-edits, strikes and narrowings to a conclusion its own sources sustain — with one correction cutting against the entry's confidence rather than for it, since the CGPM citation failed in the half the entry treated as settled while the leg it expected a document to overturn survived instead.

**What closing each leg would now take (prose, because a Rejected entry carries no promotion conditions).** For leg (b): an operative paragraph, or an explicit statement in the CCTF's report to the 28th CGPM or in the ITU-R TF.460 successor, that names TAI−UTC under continuous UTC. The CIPM decision and the draft resolution are now closed as sources of such a statement; the CCTF report is COULD NOT READ and stays open. For leg (c): the four governing GNSS ICDs, read per constellation for whether the broadcast ΔUT1 is referenced to UTC or to the constellation's own system time, and for its bit count and scale factor — that is the only way the UT1−UTC subset of the frame becomes countable, and none of it is in Steigenberger et al. For the already-asked question, which is not the ground of this rejection: sections 6.1-6.16 and section 7 of TF.2511-0 from a text extraction that actually reaches them. Because those two sections are exactly where a tally of affected services would live and both are unread, a disguised known CANNOT BE RULED OUT, and this entry claims no presupposition failure on that sub-claim.

**What the routing row will say, exactly.** The Coleman row SURVIVES and is not withheld; the orchestrator appends it, and this entry's description of it is now true to the documents. The row records a PROVIDER-STATED, TOLERANCE-CONDITIONAL engineering assessment reported unperformed — not an open task posed by Coleman in his own voice, and not an assertion that the assessment is overdue now — carried by slide 14's first bullet under "GPS", on a slide headed "Answers from GNSS Providers" and under the framing line "Impacts of a new tolerance", as a verb-initial fragment with no printed subject: "Necessitate an engineering assessment of all GPS ground and on-orbit software models that presently assume that UT1 – UTC < 1.0 second." That sentence is a reconstruction from two fragments with the junction VERIFIED rather than inferred — a second, differently prompted fetch was asked what word follows "models", returned "that", matching the second fragment's opening token, and reported the bullet to be one sentence ending in a period, so two independent reads agree at the cut — and it is quoted exactly as printed, with the spaced en dash and "1.0 second" and with no absolute-value bars, the bars the entry formerly inserted being an inserted mathematical commitment the slide does not make. The row's QZSS leg reads as a self-declared limit on DUT1, which "needs to be within 64 seconds to avoid broadcast message format and ground control algorithm changes (a value of 1 minute or less might be preferred)", carrying both the ground-segment half and the second printed figure. The row's ICG leg reads that ICG/REC/2025 of 24 Oct 2025 asks for no inventory and prints no count — no "inventory", "survey" or "catalogue" anywhere, and no digit in the operative clause — while the document does print "increased in or before 2035" and "expected at CGPM 2026". The row carries one residual: the "unperformed" half rests on an absence check over slides 1-13 and 16-23 that was summariser-mediated rather than verbatim, which is enough for routing and not enough to use this entry as evidence that the GNSS community has done no such assessment. Nothing in this entry claims that any row exists in ledger/routed-open-problems.md, and this amendment writes nothing to it.

ID: UQ-20261022-12
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — well-posedness 2/3 and Medium novelty with two close neighbours; no attack Unresolved on any of three adversaries.
Domain(s): Other STEM — measurement science and standardisation (analytical chemistry, petroleum and materials testing). Method field: statistics of variance components (ISO 5725, ASTM E691/D6300).
Question (canonical): Over a frame F of (standard test method, material class) pairs declared before any data pull and admitted only when (a) two or more independent interlaboratory precision studies of the SAME designated method exist on materials matching a declared rule, and (b) each study's laboratory count p, material count m and replicate structure n are recoverable from a public or purchasable document, what is the distribution of log(R2/R1) of the two published reproducibility limits, and does its realized spread exceed the pair-specific spread implied by the sampling distribution of each study's own s_R at its own (p, m, n)? Pairs failing (b) are enumerated as a reported coverage gap rather than dropped.
[Adopted wording is the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation (R1 in the record); the Gate 0 intake wording V0 is listed below. Second limb: the joint distribution of (age of the study behind the precision statement, p, m) over an enumerated frame of currently active methods.]
Alternative formulations: (1) V0 intake wording — restricted to methods with two or more independent interlaboratory studies on comparable materials, is the published reproducibility limit R itself reproducible? (2) Is R a property of the test method, or of the laboratories, materials and decade that happened to be in its one interlaboratory study? (3) If the study behind a currently active precision statement were re-run today, by how much would r and R change, and in which direction?
Motivating gap: A published R is reused far outside its one study — accreditation uncertainty budgets, specification limits, PT scoring limits — while the study behind it is run once, with few laboratories, on the materials and instruments of its era. The intake framing ("nobody has tested this") is withdrawn by the record: the per-method version is a published International Standard (ISO 4259-3:2020, whose achieved arm is proficiency-testing data and not a second interlaboratory study) and ASTM D7372 (read at store-page level as D7372-12; the active version is D7372-25a) defines a published-vs-achieved index. What survives is the CROSS-METHOD aggregate: no source opened by the generator, by three adversaries or by the four post-batch checkers prints a cross-method distribution, ratio or aggregate of achieved against published precision. The SINGLE-METHOD version of that comparison is a different and much weaker claim and is NOT excluded here: NCHRP Web-Only Document 141's Chapters 2-3, which are exactly where a single-method achieved-vs-published comparison for AASHTO T 104 would be printed, COULD NOT BE READ.
Presuppositions: 1. Frame non-empty for a non-trivial number of methods — UNVERIFIED after 39 queries across four agents, and STILL UNVERIFIED after the post-batch pass, in which the pair-hunting checker located no candidate at all on a two-search, five-fetch budget; nobody has opened a single COMPLETED two-ILS pair (two work items show the pair-generating process, both studies planned). That is NOT FOUND within budget, which is not the same as shown empty: the primary artefacts (ASTM research reports sold separately, CEN and EI ILS reports, successive paid editions of one method) are paywalled and were unreachable, and an unfound document's silence is no more evidence than an unread one's. 2. Design fields (p, m, n, date) printed in the precision statement — PARTLY FALSIFIED AS TO MANDATORINESS, not as to presence (TAPPI T 1200 calls them "suggested"; two real statements carry none; ASTM D6300 §8.5.1 does not require them even in the research report; ASTM E177-14 §10.3.1 says a precision statement "should include, as a minimum" the listed elements, and the one mandatory "shall" found, §10.1.1.1, covers the repeatability and reproducibility standard deviations and does not mention the counts). The gloss must not slide from "not mandatory" to "not printed": §10.3.1.1 puts "(2) number of laboratories, (3) number of test results per laboratory per material" inside a prescribed minimum-content list, and all three of E177's model statements print laboratories, materials and replicates (Ex.5.1: "in eight laboratories with five materials, with each laboratory obtaining three test results for each material"). So the premise HOLDS for ASTM E177-14 and is UNTESTED for ISO 4259-1/-2, which govern the ISO-side petroleum statements and were not opened; and the E177 clause numbers and the scope of the §10.1.1.1 "shall" were read from a third-party hosted PDF, Section 10 only, so they need re-verification against an authentic copy before weight rests on them. Admissibility still leans on paywalled research reports; partly offset by secondary sources that do print year and p (doctorfire fire-test table). 3. "Comparable materials" declarable across studies years apart — contested, made conditional on a declared rule. 4. Design-implied dispersion of s_R computable — established by simulation (prior 3), not by an opened closed-form source. 5. Published R is the study's output, not committee-adjusted — CONTESTED on an opened document (ASTM WK91528). 6. Frame membership independent of outcome — CONTESTED on one opened document only, and more weakly than this batch first had it: ASTM WK89836's rationale routes the judgement into "requirements of ASTM D6300", not into any comparison with a previously published precision value, and WK67628's rationale gives a DESIGN reason (one material replaced by "differing material types") and is affirmative evidence the other way; not addressed in the record. 7. NOT presupposed: that R is unstable; ratios inside the design-implied interval would be a full answer.
What would count as an answer: the distribution of log(R2/R1) over the declared frame with each pair's own design-implied prediction interval overlaid, and a test of realized against design-implied spread, plus a decomposition of any excess into laboratory-population, material and era components where research reports allow; second limb, the (study age, p, m) census over active methods. A clean negative licenses current practice; a positive yields a measured inflation factor for uncertainty derived from published R.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 39 distinct queries — 12 at Gate 2, 9 per adversary, 27 of them in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use (AOAC/HorRat, ASTM PTP/TPI, German Ringversuch, French essais interlaboratoires, ISO 5725-6 F-test, AIAG gauge R&R, fire-safety engineering, clinical EQA/EP15, AASHTO PSP, ISO 21748, between-trial statistics). Full lists: batches/ledger/batches/2026-10-22-1233/UQ-20261022-12-record.md and the three adversary files. Most informative: "published ASTM precision statement compared with proficiency testing program results reproducibility optimistic petroleum" → ISO 4259-3:2020 (prior 2, the standardised per-method PT-achieved-against-published version); "survey of ASTM standard test methods how old are precision statements number of participating laboratories" → store pages only, second-limb census unmeasured at title level; ASTM "Test Performance Index" TPI across methods → D7372 store pages only, no cross-method TPI distribution; ASTM workitem rationale "new interlaboratory study" replace current precision → WK91528, WK89836, WK67628 (all opened); Horwitz "precision of precision" / "factor of two" → the record's named hinge c4ay02020k, opened at the articlehtml route; AASHTO re:source AMRL proficiency sample program precision estimates vs existing precision statements → six NCHRP web-only documents RETURNED, NOT OPENED at the time (the live residual risk; post-batch, one of them — NCHRP Web-Only Document 141 — has been read at front-matter and table-of-contents level, with its body COULD NOT BE READ, and the other five remain unopened).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): PRIOR 1 — Michael Thompson (2016), "The comparison between reproducibility standard deviations from collaborative trials and proficiency tests: a preliminary study from food analysis", Anal. Methods, 8 (4), 742-746, DOI 10.1039/C5AY02890F (read FULL TEXT, author version, four differently targeted passes; year, volume and pages taken from the RSC article landing page because the author version prints none — the earlier "2015/16" uncertainty is resolved and struck: issue year 2016, first published online 17 Dec 2015): unit = one FAPAS "qualifying test" (the paper's word, not "round"), drawn from 907 qualifying FAPAS tests in 2014, median 41 participants (minimum 27), per-region n not printed; endpoint = that test's robust reproducibility standard deviation divided by the Horwitz-function prediction at the analyte's concentration, except below mass fraction 10^-7, where the divisor is a flat constant relative standard deviation of 0.22; estimand = location and spread of that ratio; numbers printed, all in running text under range headings (the paper contains no tables, and none of the four numbers appears in a figure caption): median 1.01, SD 0.53 for 10^-7 to 10^-1 — a ratio to the fitted trend; median 1.16, SD 0.55 below 10^-7 — a ratio to the 0.22 CONSTANT, not to the Horwitz function. Novelty — how this differs from each: vs PRIOR 1 — different unit (a method-material pair with two studies of ONE designated method, vs a PT test whose participants are "usually free to use any analytical procedure or method that seems appropriate"), different comparator (the other study's own published R, vs — in the Horwitz region 10^-7 to 10^-1 only — a trend fitted to collaborative-trial statistics "based on statistics published between the 1930s and 1977" and checked against a "more recent (1990-2000) collection", and below 10^-7 a flat constant relative SD of 0.22, so the 1.16/0.55 pair is a ratio to a CONSTANT and only 1.01/0.53 is a ratio to the fitted trend; "across eras" is the paper's own printed content, while "across methods" is the reader's INFERENCE and not printed words — the paper does not state how many trials the function was fitted to). Prior 1's Conclusions ANNOUNCE AND ATTRIBUTE rather than measure: "Moreover, studies of collaborative trial statistics alone show considerable scatter of individual values around the Horwitz function and its modifications, about double the variation that could be attributed to the random variation inherent in small-number statistics.5" — the sentence carries reference marker 5 and is followed by "That alone would inject considerable variation into the scaled values considered in this paper", so the doubling enters as a cited explanation for this paper's own dispersion; the paper neither measures nor estimates it and prints NO number for it anywhere, and the nearby printed "a standard deviation of about 0.5" is this paper's own PT-to-Horwitz scatter, a different quantity. On intervals: no interval, standard error or ± is printed for any statistic; there are four bare 95%-confidence significance verdicts with no F, p or df, plus one qualitative mention of "wide confidence intervals". vs PRIOR 2 — a standardised per-method conformity procedure, not an evaluation: it DEFINES, at scope level and in the words "specifies the methodology" twice over, a PER-METHOD comparison between a method's PROFICIENCY-TESTING-ACHIEVED reproducibility standard deviation and that method's published reproducibility. An ILS-versus-ILS reading is not available — the scope names PT data twice ("using data from proficiency testing schemes (PTSs)", "achieved in PT programmes versus that published") — and that it publishes no distribution of achieved-against-published ratios is a SCOPE-LEVEL INFERENCE flagged COULD NOT READ at body level, not a confirmed absence; the definition-is-not-an-evaluation conclusion survives anyway, because its force comes from the document's self-description as a methodology and not from an empty-table check. A consequence that TIGHTENS this entry: once the achieved arm is identified as PT data, ISO 4259-3 is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of supplying promotion condition (i)'s pair — a PT round yields no second published R and no second (laboratories, materials, replicates) triple — so that standard is not where (i) gets satisfied and a pair hunt must be pointed at ILS reports instead. The candidate must be stated as "the cross-method aggregate is unpublished", never as "the question is unasked". vs PRIOR 3 — prediction vs measurement: prior 3 simulates the dispersion a design implies and prints no r, no R and no real study's counts.
NO SOURCE NAMES THE NUMBER. Across four agents and 39 queries, and across four post-batch checkers, nothing opened prints R2/R1 for any method, the distribution of log(R2/R1), or the second limb's joint distribution; and none of NCHRP Web-Only Document 141, ASTM D7372-12 or the ASTM Interlaboratory Studies Program material prints a distribution, ratio or aggregate comparing achieved precision against published precision ACROSS METHODS — for the ILS leaflet and web page that rests on a full read, for WOD 141 on the document's own stated subject (one method, AASHTO T 104) rather than on its unread body, and for D7372 on document kind, a guide that prescribes and prints no data. The SINGLE-METHOD comparison is a separate and unverified matter: WOD 141 Chapters 2-3 are where it would appear and COULD NOT BE READ, so nothing here licenses a claim that no achieved-vs-published comparison exists for any single method. Graded on what each source actually does: prior 1 MEASURES a different ratio on a different denominator — the fitted Horwitz trend in 10^-7 to 10^-1, a 0.22 constant below 10^-7 — and ANNOUNCES AND ATTRIBUTES the excess to its own reference 5 without printing any number for it; prior 2 and D7372 DEFINE procedures/indices; prior 3 PREDICTS by simulation; AMC TB 17 STATES a rule of thumb ("an estimated RSD_R could easily vary by ±30% relative", "about a half of the scatter") in prose with no printed derivation, and says of the within-method case only that values "vary somewhat". A definition is not an evaluation and an announcement is not a measurement, so no Low grade is available on this evidence; the per-method/aggregate distinction is a granularity gap, not an absence.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: inside the design-implied interval, current practice is licensed and uncertainty derived from published R keeps its warrant; outside it, that derivation is a biased procedure with a measurable inflation factor, and the excess decomposition tells committees whether the fix is re-study (era/population) or narrowing a precision statement's material scope.
Significance — audience: accreditation bodies and assessed laboratories deriving uncertainty from method-performance data; PT providers setting scoring SDs from published precision; standards committees deciding when a precision statement needs re-study (ASTM D02/D04/E11, ISO TC28, TAPPI, AOAC, AASHTO); specification writers and dispute arbitration. Demonstrated on opened documents, not asserted: ISO 4259-3 exists for the per-method PT-achieved-against-published version; ASTM WK89836 is a committee work item whose rationale reads, in full as served, "In a previous revision of D5442, it was found that the precision was unsatisfactory according to requirements of ASTM D6300. It is necessary to develop a new interlaboratory study." — so a new ILS is announced, though the work-item page served no Title and a blank Status, which leaves the entry's former "2024" dating UNCONFIRMED and leaves the item's attribution to D5442 resting on the rationale's own body alone; WK91528 is a ballot handling a precision statement that "does not match the cited precision listed in the research report"; AASHTO re:source derives precision statements from PT data.
Significance — fecundity: does R drift downward with calendar time (instrument improvement) or upward (laboratory-population widening); is drift predictable from technology class, licensing a published age discount; what p makes a precision statement stable to a stated tolerance (prior 3's simulation turned into a design rule with realized data); is r, being within-laboratory, more stable; should a precision statement carry a confidence interval or an expiry date rather than a point limit.
Significance — anchoring: uncertainty estimated from method-performance data (ISO 21748, returned and unopened by all four agents); the sampling behaviour of variance components; the Horwitz-function scatter literature; the petroleum precision-monitoring machinery; the reproducibility-crisis literature at its measurement-science end, where the object is a result's reproducibility and almost never a published dispersion estimate's.
Reason for silence: disciplinary ownership plus access, with an incentive component. The per-method question has an owner and a published procedure, so no insider experiences a gap; the aggregate has no owner, its inputs are frozen research reports held one committee at a time, and the design fields are not mandatory even there (D6300 §8.5.1; ASTM E177-14 §10.3.1 asks only that a precision statement "should include, as a minimum" the listed elements, and its one mandatory "shall", §10.1.1.1, covers the precision values and not the counts — though "not mandatory" is not "not printed", since E177's minimum-content list names the laboratory and test-result counts and all three of its model statements print them). Auditing committee-adopted numbers rewards no community. Weakened on the access half by adversary 3: ASTM's own Interlaboratory Studies Program holds research reports centrally and has had access all along — and its leaflet was returned three times and opened by nobody.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): three independent adversaries (fresh context, Gate 0-3 record only); all three executed their Disguise sweeps (8, 9 and 8 queries in new vocabularies), so Disguise is verified as RUN, not unverified.
