Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Outcome-based selection into the frame — SURVIVING, but narrowed to one leg and weaker than this batch first had it. The surviving leg is ASTM WK89836, whose rationale reads in full, as served: "In a previous revision of D5442, it was found that the precision was unsatisfactory according to requirements of ASTM D6300. It is necessary to develop a new interlaboratory study." The batch's shorter quotation of that sentence was cut on the left, and the CUT WAS THE DEFECT: it dropped the subject and made an outcome comparison look textual, when what the sentence actually does is route the judgement into "requirements of ASTM D6300" — D6300's own conformance criteria — and NOT into any comparison with a previously published precision value. Whether those requirements are design minima (p, n, degrees of freedom, outlier handling) or an outcome threshold is exactly what COULD NOT BE READ, so the outcome reading is an INTERPRETATION the sentence does not carry. The WK67628 leg is STRUCK from this objection: its rationale contains no outcome claim at all — "This change is to incorporate the precision and bias statement to be determined by an inter-laboratory study utilizing differing material types replacing the previous statement determined using a single material." Nothing failed there; the stated defect is in the DESIGN of the earlier study (one material) and the remedy is a design change, so that work item is affirmative evidence for DESIGN-based commissioning and now sits on the claim's side rather than the objection's. On the one surviving leg: IF the judgement were outcome-based, first studies with a low-by-chance s_R1 would be preferentially re-studied, log(R2/R1) would be shifted positive under the null, and zero-centred design-implied intervals would read a selection artefact as instability. This objection's own vulnerability, recorded because nobody has measured it: it follows from the DESIGN of the re-study trigger, not from any reported result — adversary 3 labels the shift "my own reasoning, not sourced", no opened page says whether the D6300 judgement is design-based (p or df minima) or outcome-based (achieved vs published), and no published R2/R1 exists against which the shift could be checked. A FRAMING DEFECT, independent of the reading: design-based and outcome-based do not exhaust the options. A third possibility is live — that ASTM D6300 specifies no re-study trigger at all, being a practice for how to plan, run and compute a precision study and addressed to subcommittees ("This practice is intended for use by D02 subcommittees in determining precision estimates and bias statements to be used in D02 test methods. Its procedures correspond with ISO 4259"), with the decision to commission a re-study sitting with the subcommittee and D02's procedural rules. If that is so, the question as posed has no answer in that document and the selection worry must be settled elsewhere. On the document that would settle it: only the 2003/04 D6300 text has been read in body, and in THAT edition there is no clause comparing new precision with previously published precision; the post-batch read of a later edition reached ASTM D6300-23a, "Standard Practice for Determination of Precision and Bias Data for Use in Test Methods for Petroleum Products, Liquid Fuels, and Lubricants", at STORE-PAGE level only — section 1 (Scope) and section 5 (Significance and Use), in which none of the strings "previously published", "published precision", "minimum", "laboratories", "degrees of freedom", "re-study", "restudy" or "compare" occurs — and D6300-23a is itself listed "Standard Historical", so the live designation remains unidentified. The entry therefore records NO finding of "no such clause in the current edition": sub-claim (b), whether the current edition compares newly determined precision with previously published precision, and sub-claim (c), whether it states design minima for p, n or degrees of freedom, are both COULD NOT CHECK, with no number served either way, and an unread section's silence scores for neither side. The nearest adequacy language the read did serve is a purpose statement and not a trigger — "ASTM test methods are frequently intended for use in the manufacture, selling, and buying of materials in accordance with specifications and therefore should provide such precision that when the test is properly performed by a competent operator, the results will be found satisfactory for judging the compliance of the material with the specification." — and it benchmarks precision against the specification the material is judged against, not against a previously published precision figure. The related C5 weakness is ALGEBRAIC, not empirical or bitwise: s_R^2 is a combination of two mean squares, so a chi-square interval at (p, m, n) is an approximation rather than an identity, and no primary source on its adequacy was opened by anyone. Which leg the verdict stands on: the Provisional stands on well-posedness 2/3 — the frame-non-empty presupposition is unverified after 39 queries and after the post-batch pair hunt, and the design-field premise is partly falsified on mandatoriness — and that leg would survive intact if both the selection objection and the Disguise residuals fell. The selection objection and the published-R-vs-research-report mismatch (WK91528) are the legs that would then matter; they wound the inferential limb and the decomposition, not the first-limb distribution.
Promotion requires: (i) ONE COMPLETED two-ILS pair opened by a NAMED ROUTE rather than by another blind search — either an ASTM research report obtained and read alongside the precision statement that cites it, or two successive paid editions of one ASTM or ISO method held side by side, or an EI/IP precision re-determination report — with both published R values, both (p, m, n) triples and each study's trigger recorded, and enough further pairs enumerated to show the frame non-trivial, which is the only thing that moves well-posedness to 3/3; this condition is WELL-POSED BUT NOT REACHABLE at two searches and five fetches, since the primary artefacts (ASTM research reports sold separately, CEN and EI ILS reports, successive paid editions of one method) sit behind paywalls, so it needs a budget that can clear a paywall or reach a library copy, and it must NOT be aimed at ISO 4259-3, which is structurally incapable of supplying it because a PT round yields no second published R and no second design triple; (ii) the frame declaration amended to record the re-study trigger per pair and stratify or restrict on it, converting selection from a presupposition into a measurand, and to declare whether a PT/PSP round counts as a study and what "realized spread" is taken about; (iii) the live ASTM D6300 designation identified and its body obtained by a legitimate route — a national adoption of the ISO 4259 family is cheapest, since D6300-23a states that its "procedures correspond with ISO 4259" — and the two COULD NOT CHECK sub-claims answered from printed text with section numbers: whether any clause compares newly determined precision with previously published precision, and whether minima for p, n and degrees of freedom are stated; (iv) NCHRP Web-Only Document 141 (DOI 10.17226/23020) Chapters 2 and 3 read, recording with number and units whether the AMRL-derived precision for AASHTO T 104 is set beside that method's published statement, since a SINGLE-METHOD achieved-vs-published precedent there is likely and unverified; (v) what ASTM D7372's listed section "PTP and Site Precision Comparisons" sets against what resolved — if it compares PT-achieved precision against a method's published precision, this entry's framing (though not its cross-method aggregate claim) needs rewriting — and the remaining five NCHRP/AMRL cluster documents opened, since nothing read so far makes the candidate routable; (vi) one ASTM research report read beside its own precision statement, so that the ratio's referent (published statement or study output) is fixed rather than hedged; and (vii) Thompson and Wood, DOI 10.1039/C4AY02020K — reference 5 of prior 1, COULD NOT READ on this pass — opened and checked for whether the "about double" collaborative-trial excess is quantified there, before the novelty grade rests on nobody having quantified it.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): enumerate, from one committee's public work-item and research-report indices, the designations that carry more than one archived precision research report, and record each pair's trigger — this tests the frame-non-empty and selection clauses before any ratio is computed.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — the entry is Provisional, so the ledger still claims the question as un-asked and it is not an already-asked open problem; the per-method version that IS asked belongs to ISO 4259-3 (PT-achieved against published) and ASTM D7372 and is not this question. Nothing read in the NCHRP/AMRL, D7372 or ASTM ILS cluster POSES the candidate's question either, so nothing there makes it routable: the nearest formulation is D7372 §1.1's hedged, addressed one — the guide, written "For the committees responsible for the test methods included in interlaboratory proficiency testing programs", "describes procedures for assessing industry's ability to perform test methods" "and for potentially identifying needs for method improvement" — which hands assessment to each method's own committee, method by method, and answers nothing. This line is a recommendation only, not a record of any action taken on routed-open-problems.md.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What the pass was, and what each checker was sent to read.** Four fresh-context checkers ran after the batch closed, each blind to the reviewers' reasoning and each required to re-read a load-bearing source first-hand. Checker 1 was sent to the current edition of ASTM D6300 and to the two ASTM work items on which the outcome-based-selection objection rests (WK89836, WK67628), to settle whether the re-study trigger is design-based or outcome-based; it used 6 WebFetch, three of which retrieved nothing, and 2 WebSearch, and declared the one-fetch budget overrun. Checker 2 was sent to the three titles nobody in the batch had opened — the NCHRP/AMRL proficiency-sample cluster, ASTM D7372, and the ASTM Interlaboratory Studies Program material — to test whether a cross-method achieved-against-published aggregate is already in print; 5 WebFetch, 2 WebSearch. Checker 3 was sent to Thompson (2016) for the four printed figures, the ratio's denominator, the test count and the "about double" sentence; 5 WebFetch, 1 WebSearch. Checker 4 was sent to ISO 4259-3:2020, then to hunt a completed two-ILS pair, then to test the premise that a precision statement's design counts are not mandatory; 5 WebFetch, 2 WebSearch.

**Read level reached for each source, with COULD NOT READ and COULD NOT CHECK kept distinct from NOT FOUND.** ASTM D6300-23a: STORE PAGE / SCOPE level only — section 1 (Scope) and section 5 (Significance and Use) in full, plus front matter; sections 6-14 and all annexes, which is where a comparison clause or design minima would live, were NOT READ, so no body text of any edition later than the 2003/04 text already in the record has been read by anyone in this chain. ASTM WK89836 and WK67628: FULL TEXT of the Rationale as served, each assembled from two consecutive segments with the junction checked, but with no Title and a blank Status served on either page. ASTM D7372-12: PARTIAL — Scope §1.1, an excerpt of Significance and Use, and the page's section list; the body is paywalled and COULD NOT READ. NCHRP Web-Only Document 141: PARTIAL — bibliographic front matter and the complete table of contents with page ranges; Chapters 1-3 (pp. 1-16) and Appendices A-N (pp. 18-115) COULD NOT BE READ, the NAP reader having served navigation, citation boilerplate and the TOC only. ASTM's Interlaboratory Studies Program leaflet: FULL TEXT in substance, partial verbatim; the programme web page: FULL TEXT. Thompson (2016): FULL TEXT of the author version over four differently targeted passes, plus a FULL RECORD of the front matter from the RSC landing page; the plotted figures themselves were not seen, since vector graphics are not served as text, so statements about Figs 1-8 rest on captions and running text. ISO 4259-3:2020: ABSTRACT / CATALOGUE level only, from two independent servers; the normative body, its annexes and any critical values were COULD NOT READ, and whether critical values exist there at all is COULD NOT CHECK. ASTM E177-14: PARTIAL — Section 10 and its worked examples only, from a third-party hosted PDF read through a summariser, with no front matter seen. ASTM E691, ISO 4259-1 and ISO 4259-2: NOT OPENED. Thompson and Wood, DOI 10.1039/C4AY02020K, in its role as reference 5 of prior 1: COULD NOT READ, budget exhausted on the primary document — explicitly not NOT FOUND. The completed two-ILS pair: NOT FOUND within a two-search budget — no candidate document was located, so nothing was opened and nothing was read at any level, and that is a fact about the budget and the paywalls, not evidence that no pair exists.

**Claims struck.** First, the WK67628 leg of the outcome-based-selection objection is struck from the objection outright and moved to the claim's support, because its rationale contains no outcome claim at all: "This change is to incorporate the precision and bias statement to be determined by an inter-laboratory study utilizing differing material types replacing the previous statement determined using a single material." Nothing failed; the stated defect is in the DESIGN of the earlier study (one material) and the remedy is a design change, which is affirmative evidence for design-based commissioning. The entry's old gloss that WK89836 and WK67628 "show precision statements being re-made because they failed" is struck with it. Second, the characterisation of nap.edu/read/23020 as the NCHRP cluster's lead CROSS-METHOD candidate is struck: by its own title it is a SINGLE-METHOD report, "Precision Estimates for AASHTO Test Method T 104, Determined Using AMRL Proficiency Sample Data", and the checker's read of what it could see reported "The material covers only T 104 ... The page doesn't present any aggregate across multiple test methods." It cannot be read as a cross-method candidate and no longer heads the condition. Third, "over 907 FAPAS rounds" is struck as the denominator of the two medians: 907 is the whole 2014 qualifying set across three mass-fraction regions — "The total number of qualifying tests was 907, encompassing a wide range of analyte types, matrices and mass fractions. The minimum number of laboratories participating in any of these tests was 27 and the median 41." — and no per-region n is printed, so neither pair is computed over 907. The entry now says "drawn from 907 qualifying FAPAS tests in 2014, median 41 participants (minimum 27), per-region n not printed". Fourth, the "2015/16" uncertainty over Thompson's year is struck as resolved: Anal. Methods, 2016, 8 (4), 742-746, first published online 17 Dec 2015; the author version prints no year, volume or pages, which is what produced the earlier hedge. Fifth, "IP 367 Part 3" is struck from the ISO 4259-3 citation line as unconfirmed — neither the ISO catalogue page nor the Swedish adoption page names IP 367. Sixth, the entry's former dating of WK89836 as a "2024 committee finding" is struck, because the work-item page served no Title and a blank Status; the rationale's own body is the only support for attributing the item to D5442.

**Claims narrowed.** The WK89836 leg is narrowed to what the sentence says. Printed in full: "In a previous revision of D5442, it was found that the precision was unsatisfactory according to requirements of ASTM D6300. It is necessary to develop a new interlaboratory study." That routes the judgement into "requirements of ASTM D6300" and NOT into a comparison with a previously published precision value; whether those requirements are design minima or an outcome threshold is exactly what could not be read, so the outcome reading the entry built on it is an interpretation the sentence does not carry. The NCHRP finding is narrowed to the CROSS-METHOD aggregate explicitly: none of the three titles prints a distribution, ratio or aggregate comparing achieved precision against published precision across methods, and that negative rests on a full read for the ILS material, on the document's own stated subject for WOD 141, and on document kind for D7372 — a guide that, in its own words, "describes procedures for assessing industry's ability to perform test methods" "and for potentially identifying needs for method improvement", and therefore prescribes rather than performs. The entry must not be read as claiming that no achieved-vs-published comparison exists for any single method; the single-method leg is live and unverified, because WOD 141 Chapters 2-3, "Results of Analysis and Estimates of Precision" (pp. 4-14) and "Conclusions and Recommendations" (pp. 15-16), are exactly where such a comparison would be printed and COULD NOT BE READ. Thompson's leg 1 is narrowed on the denominator: "Each standard deviation from FAPAS was scaled to (that is, divided by) the value predicted by the Horwitz function for the corresponding concentration of the analyte", but below 10^-7 the paper reports "a tendency for the observed relative reproducibility standard deviation to stabilise at a lower value, centred on 0.22 regardless of concentration" and "It was therefore used in this study to scale the RSDR values from the proficiency test statistics" — so the 1.16/0.55 pair is a ratio to a CONSTANT and only 1.01/0.53 is a ratio to the fitted trend. "Across eras" is kept because it is printed — the function is "based on statistics published between the 1930s and 1977", checked against "a more recent (1990-2000) collection of statistics" — while "across methods" is now marked as the reader's inference, not printed words, the paper nowhere stating how many trials the function was fitted to. "No confidence intervals anywhere" is narrowed to "no interval, standard error or ± printed for any statistic; four bare 95%-confidence significance verdicts with no F, p or df, plus one qualitative mention of 'wide confidence intervals'". The ISO 4259-3 claim is narrowed from an unqualified "per-method monitoring procedure" to a per-method procedure comparing a method's PROFICIENCY-TESTING-achieved reproducibility standard deviation against its published reproducibility, because the scope says PT data twice: "the regular monitoring of the test method precision achieved ... using data from proficiency testing schemes (PTSs) supported by the regular users of standard test methods" and "the statistical comparison of standard deviation under reproducibility conditions achieved in PT programmes versus that published". No leg of this entry was resting on an ILS-versus-ILS reading of that standard; the per-method achieved-against-published claim is kept with its achieved arm named as PT data. The (e) premise is narrowed in its gloss: "design counts are not mandatory" HOLDS for ASTM E177-14 on the modal verb — §10.3.1 asks that a statement "should include, as a minimum", and the only "shall" found, §10.1.1.1, covers the precision values and not the counts — but it must not slide into "not printed", since §10.3.1.1's prescribed minimum-content list names "(2) number of laboratories, (3) number of test results per laboratory per material" and all three of E177's model statements print labs, materials and replicates; the premise is marked holds for ASTM E177-14, untested for ISO 4259-1/-2.

**Claims confirmed, re-sourced or upgraded.** Thompson's four figures are confirmed exactly as the entry carried them, including which pair goes with which range, and all four sit in running text under range headings, the paper having no tables and none of the four numbers appearing in a figure caption: "The median observed value was 1.01 ... the dispersion of the scaled values was considerable, with a standard deviation of 0.53" for "Mass fractions between 10-7 and 10-1 (the 'Horwitz region')", and for "Mass fractions smaller than 10-7 (the 'low' region)" a trend "at an almost constant level, with a median of 1.16 and a standard deviation of 0.55". For completeness, the high region (greater than 10^-1) prints no median and no SD at all. Thompson's leg 2, that published is not performed, is UPGRADED: the Conclusions sentence reads "Moreover, studies of collaborative trial statistics alone show considerable scatter of individual values around the Horwitz function and its modifications, about double the variation that could be attributed to the random variation inherent in small-number statistics.5" — it carries reference marker 5 and is followed by "That alone would inject considerable variation into the scaled values considered in this paper", so the paper ANNOUNCES AND ATTRIBUTES the doubling as an explanation for its own dispersion rather than measuring or estimating it, and no number for it is printed anywhere; the nearby "a standard deviation of about 0.5" is this paper's own PT-to-Horwitz scatter and is a different quantity. ISO 4259-3's DEFINES half is re-sourced and strengthened: it is now confirmed from ISO's own catalogue page, iso.org/standard/65961.html, with word-for-word identical scope wording returned independently by the national adoption SS-EN ISO 4259-3:2020, so the entry's former weakness of resting on a reseller catalogue page is dropped, while "read at SCOPE level only" stays accurate because that is all ISO publishes free. The no-evaluation half is DEMOTED from verified to inferred: "publishes no distribution of achieved-against-published ratios" is a scope-level inference flagged COULD NOT READ at body level, not a confirmed absence, and the definition-is-not-an-evaluation conclusion survives because its force comes from the document's self-description as a methodology ("specifies the methodology", twice) and not from an empty-table check. A new consequence has been recorded that tightens the entry: once the achieved arm is identified as PT data, ISO 4259-3 is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of supplying promotion condition (i)'s pair, since a PT round yields no second published R and no second (laboratories, materials, replicates) triple, so that standard is not where (i) gets satisfied and a pair hunt belongs at ILS reports instead. A framing defect has been added that is independent of the reading: the entry treated design-based and outcome-based as exhausting the options, when a third is live — that D6300 specifies no re-study trigger at all, being a practice addressed to subcommittees ("This practice is intended for use by D02 subcommittees in determining precision estimates and bias statements to be used in D02 test methods. Its procedures correspond with ISO 4259"), in which case the question as posed has no answer in that document and the selection worry must be settled elsewhere. Finally, the pass records that nothing in the NCHRP/D7372/ILS cluster POSES the candidate's question, so nothing there makes it routable; the nearest is D7372 §1.1's hedged, addressed formulation, which hands assessment to each method's own committee, method by method.

**Quotation defects found and repaired.** One, and it is the kind that counts even though the quoted words were verbatim: the entry's "unsatisfactory according to requirements of ASTM D6300" was cut on the left, and the cut was the defect — it dropped "In a previous revision of D5442, it was found that the precision was", which supplies the subject and makes the comparator D6300's own requirements rather than a published precision value. As the entry carried it, the fragment read as support for an outcome comparison. The full printed sentence now stands in the entry's prose wherever the fragment appeared. Relatedly, the entry must not and no longer does record "no such clause in the current edition" of D6300: the read reached the store page, Scope and Significance and Use only, and recording an absence there would convert a scope-level read into a full-text finding. Within those two sections the checker could report at word level that none of "previously published", "published precision", "minimum", "laboratories", "degrees of freedom", "re-study", "restudy" or "compare" occurs, and the nearest adequacy language served is a purpose statement, not a trigger: "ASTM test methods are frequently intended for use in the manufacture, selling, and buying of materials in accordance with specifications and therefore should provide such precision that when the test is properly performed by a competent operator, the results will be found satisfactory for judging the compliance of the material with the specification." Sub-claims (b), whether the current edition compares newly determined precision with previously published precision, and (c), whether it states design minima for p, n or degrees of freedom, are marked COULD NOT CHECK, with no number served for either.

**Citation corrections.** Thompson is now cited in full: Michael Thompson (Birkbeck, University of London), 2016, "The comparison between reproducibility standard deviations from collaborative trials and proficiency tests: a preliminary study from food analysis", Anal. Methods, 8 (4), 742-746, DOI 10.1039/C5AY02890F — the entry previously carried a truncated title and no year, volume or pages. ISO 4259-3:2020 is now cited by its full title, "Petroleum and related products — Precision of measurement methods and results — Part 3: Monitoring and verification of published precision data in relation to methods of test", edition 1, published 2020-01, status "International Standard confirmed [90.93]", ICS 75.080, committee ISO/TC 28, with EN ISO 4259-3 confirmed via SS-EN ISO 4259-3:2020 and IP 367 Part 3 dropped. The NCHRP document is now cited as National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (2009), "Precision Estimates for AASHTO Test Method T 104, Determined Using AMRL Proficiency Sample Data", NCHRP Web-Only Document 141, Washington, DC: The National Academies Press, DOI 10.17226/23020, with no individual authors, since its front matter names none and any individual attribution would be invented. ASTM D7372 now carries an edition, D7372-12, "Standard Guide for Analysis and Interpretation of Proficiency Test Program Results", Committee D02, Subcommittee D02.94, with the active version named as D7372-25a and a note that the bare designation is ambiguous across -07, -12, -17, -21 and -25a. ASTM D6300 is named as D6300-23a, "Standard Practice for Determination of Precision and Bias Data for Use in Test Methods for Petroleum Products, Liquid Fuels, and Lubricants", with the warning that -23a is itself listed "Standard Historical", so the live designation is unidentified and "-20a, -23a or later" does not name it. Thompson and Wood is given as Anal. Methods, 2015, 7, 377-379, DOI 10.1039/C4AY02020K, with the identification of that reference-list entry as reference 5 of prior 1 made on year, volume and pagination match only and therefore unverified. ASTM's programme is recorded under both of the names its own sources use, "Interlaboratory Studies Program" on the leaflet and "Interlaboratory Study Program" on the web page. ASTM E177-14 is recorded with its provenance: a third-party hosted PDF, not ASTM's server, Section 10 only, with the clause numbers and the scope of the §10.1.1.1 "shall" taken from that copy and flagged for re-verification against an authentic copy before weight rests on them; ASTM E691, which governs ILS design and is cited by E177, was not opened, so any claim about mandatory ILS design reporting belongs to E691 and is unchecked. No DOI applies to any of the standards documents; the one DOI thrown up by the pair search, doi:10.3390/ndt2030011 on pavement density profiling, is a single study, not a pair, and is not used.

**Routes that failed, recorded so a later pass does not repeat them.** astm.org/d6300-23a.html returns HTTP 302 to store.astm.org/d6300-23a.html and the cross-host redirect comes back unfollowed; re-fetching at the store host works. ASTM work items are reliable at the long path membership-participation/technical-committees/workitems/workitem-wkNNNNN and only sometimes at the short /workitem-wkNNNNN path: the short path worked for WK67628 and returned a client error for WK89836, whose long path then succeeded. The D02 jurisdiction page (get-involved/technical-committees/committee-d02/subcommittee-d02/jurisdiction-d020102) returned a client error and nothing at all. nap.edu/read/23020 redirects to www.nationalacademies.org/read/23020/chapter, which must be followed manually, and neither that page nor .../chapter/3 served any body prose for Chapter 2; a PDF route or the per-page NAP reader was never attempted. The ISO Online Browsing Platform (iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:4259:-3:ed-1:v1:en) returns only a JavaScript stub for a client-rendered application, which is a tool failure and not a host block. GlobalSpec (standards.globalspec.com/std/14256098/en-iso-4259-3) failed at the site with a client error and nothing was retrieved. PMC and Europe PMC are hard-blocked here; Unpaywall was not used because its route requires a contact email address. Both ASTM pages carry a notice that use of ASTM standards and related intellectual property with AI is prohibited, and no checker attempted to defeat a paywall. One search surfaced a mirror of D6300-03, the edition already read, and no openly posted current edition — NOT FOUND at that budget, not non-existent.

**What the pass did not reach.** The body of any current ASTM D6300 edition, including the programme-planning sections and annexes where design minima or a comparison clause would sit, and the live designation itself. The body of ASTM D7372 and the referent of its listed section "PTP and Site Precision Comparisons", which remains unresolved and is not scored as cleared. NCHRP Web-Only Document 141 Chapters 1-3 and Appendices A-N, and the other five documents of the NCHRP/AMRL cluster. The normative body, annexes and any critical values of ISO 4259-3, and ISO 4259-1 and ISO 4259-2 entirely. ASTM E691, and E177's front matter. Thompson and Wood, DOI 10.1039/C4AY02020K, where the "about double" figure would have to be looked for. The IP 367 / EN ISO 4259 national adoptions. And, above all, a single completed two-ILS pair: the pair hunt spent its whole two-search budget and returned the machinery of precision work rather than any instance of it, which is NOT FOUND within budget and is not a finding that the frame is empty.

**Whether the verdict moved, and what happened to the conditions and the grade.** The verdict did NOT move: the entry STAYS PROVISIONAL, and well-posedness STAYS 2/3. Nobody has opened even one completed two-ILS pair, so the clause the question cannot live without is still unverified; and nothing the pass read shows the frame empty either, because the primary artefacts — ASTM research reports sold separately, CEN and EI ILS reports, successive paid editions of one method — are paywalled and were unreachable, and an unfound document's silence is no more evidence than an unread one's. The pass confirmed every fatal ground and every surviving status, and the net movement inside the entry is lateral: the strongest remaining objection is weaker than the batch had it, since its clearer leg (WK67628) runs the other way and its stronger-sounding leg (WK89836) rested on a mis-cut quotation, yet the objection is not refuted, because the document that would refute it is still unopened. On the promotion conditions, the pass rewrote the entry's single promotion-conditions line. Condition (i) is now ROUTE-NAMED rather than a blind search — an ASTM research report obtained and read alongside the precision statement citing it, or two successive editions of one ASTM or ISO method side by side, or an EI/IP precision re-determination — with the explicit note that it is well-posed but not reachable at two searches and five fetches and needs a budget that can clear a paywall or reach a library copy, and with ISO 4259-3 ruled out as its venue. The D6300 (b) and (c) sub-claims were converted from findings into that same line as a condition; the NCHRP conversions (WOD 141 Chapters 2-3, and the referent of D7372's "PTP and Site Precision Comparisons") were folded in beside them, as was the new condition that Thompson and Wood be opened before the novelty grade rests on nobody having quantified the collaborative-trial excess. Promotion condition (iii)'s cross-method leg SURVIVES on the reads achieved, narrowed to the cross-method aggregate. The novelty grade is UNCHANGED at Medium: the graded distinctions that hold it there were strengthened, not weakened — prior 1's announcement is now known to be an attribution to its reference 5 with no number printed anywhere, and prior 2's definitional character is now sourced from ISO's own catalogue page — while the one route that could have lowered it, reference 5 itself, could not be read, and an unread document's silence neither raises nor lowers the grade.

ID: UQ-20261022-13
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Medium novelty with a close in-field neighbour, in-field prior art (Sardina et al. 2017) that prints a directional, magnitude-dependent rapid-versus-catalogue structure but no same-agency vintage bias and no decision-flip share, and a document-kind premise whose latency half is now evidenced from a real trigger while its vintage-and-source half is COULD NOT READ
Domain(s): Other STEM — seismology and operational earthquake information (target field: NEIC/JMA/GeoNet-class reporting agencies, tsunami-warning and automated-response operators, parametric risk transfer/ILS). Method field: econometrics of statistical-agency data revisions (news-versus-noise, revision rationality on successive published vintages). Source method: cross-field transplant.
Question (canonical): For earthquakes with M >= M0 in a declared region and window, reading back from agency A's own versioned event history (or an archived snapshot series or dated bulletins) the magnitude m_tau that A had published at latency tau after origin, and fixing "final" as A's value m_D at a declared date D: (a) is the revision r = m_D - m_tau mean-zero (bias in magnitude units, with CI) and orthogonal to the settlement-instant information set (depth, region, station count/azimuthal gap, magnitude type, local time, m_tau itself), reported as a news-versus-noise decomposition; and (b) over the publicly documented population of parametric contracts and automated response thresholds keyed to A's published magnitude, how many trigger decisions flip under m_D rather than m_tau, with the sign of each flip and the money or action at stake?
Reformulation note: this is the Gate 1 reformulation (one permitted, both recorded). The intake version left tau, D, A and the contract frame unpinned, which left the estimand unstated rather than ill-posed; substance unchanged. Intake text in batches/ledger/batches/2026-10-22-1233/UQ-20261022-13-record.md.
Alternative formulations:
1. Are earthquake magnitude revisions news or noise?
2. Is the magnitude that settles a parametric earthquake contract a biased estimate of the magnitude the catalogue ends up with, and does the bias run towards or away from payout?
3. Intake version: treating the magnitude published at a fixed settlement latency as a forecast of the finally published magnitude, is that forecast efficient, and what share of keyed trigger decisions would have come out differently under the final magnitude?
Motivating gap: Parametric earthquake instruments and automated response rules settle on a named agency's reported magnitude as published at a named time, while the agency keeps revising that magnitude for days to weeks. A revision process designed for scientific accuracy is load-bearing for binary financial and emergency decisions. The mechanism is documented in a real case (Artemis, 19 Apr 2014: USGS "initially recorded it as a M7.5", "subsequently downgraded to a M7.2", with the MultiCat Mexico 2012 bond discussed "had the initial magnitude of 7.5 been maintained") and in a 2026 near-miss (USGS Mww 7.3 against a M7.4 Class B threshold). What is absent is any measurement OF THE TWO CANDIDATE QUANTITIES — a signed revision statistic over an agency's own successive published vintages, and a share of keyed decisions that flip under the later vintage. It is NOT the case that nothing directional has been measured on early earthquake magnitudes: Sardina, McCreery and Fryer (2017), Paper N° 193, 16WCEE, print over n=647 that 60% of PTWC rapid bulletin magnitudes ran high and 24% ran low against GCMT, that 68% of the Mw >= 7.6 events ran low, and that the sign flips at Mw ~ 7.45. That structure is cross-producer against an external catalogue, with no decision-flip share; it is not the candidate's quantity, but any claim that the directional question is unmeasured is struck.
Presuppositions:
- Vintage read-back (CONTESTED, now partly sourced): USGS retains origin product versions with updateTime ("Other versions remain available for review and comparison."), and for one large NEIC event the pt/at/us versions at 6/8/18 min are kept; but no `usauto` origin is kept, for 283 of 441 ComCat events of one day the earliest retained version was already reviewed, GeoNet keeps history 365 days only, and the one independent snapshot archive found begins 2026-07-05. Recoverable for tau from roughly 6-20 min onward on large NEIC events; not recoverable for the earliest automatic vintage, and unverified for JMA.
- Contract document kind (CONTESTED, SPLIT: latency half evidenced, vintage-and-source half COULD NOT READ): IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 prospectus supplement (dated 3 April 2024; Classes A and B earthquake, Class C Atlantic named storm; AIR as Event Calculation Agent) keys payout to "Earthquake Event Parameters provided by the applicable Earthquake Reporting Source", warns sources "may make available from time to time several different reports which may show different levels of accuracy", and uses "Primary Earthquake Reporting Source" and "Back-up Earthquake Reporting Source" as defined terms, so the contract does turn on an identified source. LATENCY HALF, read from the Overview and the "The Notes" summary (NOT from Annex A): the Earthquake Calculation Date is the LATER OF the first Business Day after a Notice of Applicable Event is delivered and "the first (1st) Business Day at least fourteen (14) calendar days after the Date of Occurrence of such Earthquake", so the fourteen days is a FLOOR on the stand-off and not a fixed reading date; the "Event Parameters Acquisition Period" is "the thirty (30) Business Days' period" beginning the first Business Day after the Calculation Date, extendable in increments of at least five Business Days. VINTAGE-AND-SOURCE HALF: the definitions of "Earthquake Reporting Source" and "Earthquake Event Parameters" were not served, no agency, catalogue or bulletin is named, and no magnitude type or vintage appears, so the entry does NOT assert that the annex specifies which published magnitude vintage it reads. The entry's earlier gloss that the supplement "makes the calculation agent's determination final and binding absent manifest error" is withdrawn as unsupported by any quotation on the verification read, which found no finality or post-Event-Report-revision clause in the served text and offers no quotation either way: that sub-claim is COULD NOT CHECK, not NOT FOUND, and is scored neither way. Annexes A-C are COULD NOT READ, not absent: the document names them. Consequence unchanged: tau is a window with a variable end that the study must impose, not read off the contract.
- A "final" magnitude (converted): fixed by declared rule (value as of D); a declared convention, not a world-claim.
- The binding agency is the one named in the contract (CONTESTED): for tsunami-warning operators the structure fits less cleanly, since the centres publish their own origins minutes before NEIC's, so their early value and their "final" belong to different producers.
- Power (CONTESTED, unverified): few large events, non-stationary network coverage and a changing magnitude pipeline may power only a bias test; declared in advance with the bias-only fallback.
- NOT presupposed: that revisions are biased or that any trigger flips. An unforecastable revision with zero flips is a full answer.
What would count as an answer: a regression of r = m_D - m_tau on the settlement-instant information set as a news-versus-noise decomposition, bias stated in magnitude units with CI; plus a tabulated count over the declared contract and threshold population of decisions that flip under m_D, with sign and stake. A clean negative is pre-registered as a full answer.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 41 documented queries — 14 at Gate 2 (cap was 11; the three-call overrun is recorded in the record, not hidden) plus 9, 9 and 9 across three adversaries, in tsunami-warning, network-operations, NEIC-historical (QED/PDE), Japanese (速報値/暫定値/確定値), Spanish, Italian, data-provenance, PAGER/impact-alert, weather-derivative settlement, ISDA correction-of-published-values, hydrology provisional-versus-approved, ag-econ index-insurance and cat-bond defined-terms vocabularies. Most informative: "fraction of earthquakes magnitude changed more than 0.2 units after review percentage revised magnitudes catalog quality study" -> no published share of events revised by any stated amount; "retrospective how many earthquake events would have triggered parametric cover under revised final magnitude instead of reported magnitude" -> nothing, only trigger-design papers and payout news; "real-time vintage database geophysical catalogue revisions news noise test applied outside macroeconomics" -> every return macroeconomic, no geophysical transplant; "automatic versus manually revised magnitude difference distribution seismic network analyst review systematic bias" -> catalogue-scale automatic-versus-reviewed work, no per-event vintage study; "気象庁 マグニチュード 速報値 暫定値 確定値 差 統計" -> JMA method-change notices and 験震時報 EEW papers, no provisional-versus-definitive statistic; GitHub code search for ""initial magnitude" "final magnitude" comcat superseded" -> 0 hits. Full lists in batches/ledger/batches/2026-10-22-1233/UQ-20261022-13-record.md and the three adversary files.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Lux, Angela I., et al. (2024), "Status and Performance of the ShakeAlert Earthquake Early Warning System: 2019-2023", Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America, DOI 10.1785/0120230259 — OPENED IN FULL, but the copy read is an author copy at that DOI (front matter prints volume "XX", issue "Number XX", pages 1-22), NOT the paginated version of record, so neither percentage is certified against the version of record and the entry carries no volume or pages. TWO units, not one: for the missed-event rate the unit is a ComCat catalogue earthquake (denominator 53, M>=4.5 within the West Coast reporting region / alerting boundary, 2019-2023); for the false-alert rate the unit is a ShakeAlert detection (denominator 95). Endpoint matched/missed/false against a matching criterion of "no matching catalog event within 100 km and 30 s of origin time"; comparator ComCat, treated as FIXED ground truth; estimand the operational detection and false-alarm performance of a deployed EEW system against a reference catalogue, judged against the Given et al. (2018) design target "No more than 1 out of 10 ComCat earthquakes above the target magnitude will be missed." Both percentages are printed ONLY in the CONCLUSIONS — the Abstract, Results and Table 1 carry the counts and no percentages — and both are given here as the full printed sentences, because the entry's earlier left-cut strings ("a missed event rate of 22.6%", "a false alert rate of 7.4%") dropped exactly the numerators and denominators at issue: "Missing 12 of the 53 earthquakes gives a missed event rate of 22.6%." and "a false alert rate of 7.4% for the real-time system (seven false alerts out of 95 M >=4.5 alerts)." The 12 is a COMPOSITE and is not Table 1's own "missed event" class, which counts 7: it is 7 undetected ComCat M>=4.5 events PLUS 5 events ShakeAlert did detect and characterise but whose magnitude estimate fell below the M 4.5 publication threshold, so any gloss implying ShakeAlert "failed to see 12 earthquakes" misdescribes 5 of them; the paper also carries a third, location-error-based "missed" class (three detected events with location error over 100 km). The 95 is not unambiguous: the Abstract, Results and Table 1 make it DETECTIONS with maximum magnitude estimate M>=4.5, the Conclusions sentence calls the same 95 "alerts" (published alerts are a strict subset — 41 of the 46 detected events), and the Figure 1 caption gives 87 for an apparently identical criterion. "Detections" is the defensible reading and is the one used here.
2. Collich, Rosillo, Martinez, Wald, Durante (2020), "Financial risk innovation: Development of earthquake parametric triggers for contingent credit instruments", DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-43708-4_1 — ABSTRACT ONLY (Springer chapter not opened). Unit: trigger/index design per event; endpoint payout as a function of magnitude, intensity and exposure; estimand index calibration; no revision statistic at abstract level.
3. Artemis, 19 Apr 2014, "M7.2 earthquake close to the trigger of MultiCat Mexico 2012 cat bond" — OPENED IN FULL; URL independently re-returned by adversary 2's search. n=1, no estimand, and it does not establish a realised flip.
Also weighed, found by the adversaries and since read: Sardina, V.; McCreery, C.; Fryer, G. (2017), "Compilation and analysis of two decades worth of tsunami bulletins issued by the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center", 16th World Conference on Earthquake Engineering (16WCEE 2017), Santiago, Chile, Paper N° 193, Registration Code S-B1463015136 — NO DOI, since 16WCEE proceedings papers are not DOI-registered, so the paper number plus registration code are the only identifiers. The entry's earlier label, "two decades of Pacific Tsunami Warning Center operations", is corrected: the title's object is the tsunami BULLETINS, which is what fixes the population. READ LEVEL: PARTIAL, not UNOPENED and not abstract-only — Abstract, the full section-heading list, all nine figure captions verbatim, Section 3.2 "Distribution of PTWC Magnitude Residuals" in detail with every residual statistic, count and percentage, Section 3.3 case examples, the threshold discussion and the numbered Conclusions; continuous verbatim text of no section was obtained. Population: "the 647 earthquakes under consideration in this study", PTWC bulletins 1998 to April 2016, collapsed to one preliminary value per event. Numerator: the magnitude "reported in the PTWC bulletins" — Mwp after about 2002, Ms before it, and for at least one case (2011 Japan) a JMA-sourced 7.9 — with no PTWC later bulletin value entering the comparison at all. Comparator: GCMT moment magnitude Mw, an EXTERNAL catalogue. What it prints: the aggregate figures are explicitly ABSOLUTE values — "The absolute values of these magnitude residuals have a mean of 0.19, a standard deviation of 0.16," and the sentence continues "and a median value of 0.2 magnitude units", followed by the authors' own hedge, "These general statistics, however, fall short of revealing some significant trends in the data." (The Abstract gives the same figure unsigned: "and 0.2 units for the magnitude residuals.") It also prints sign-resolved structure over the population: residual = PTWC bulletin magnitude minus GCMT Mw, so positive = overestimation; 391 overestimations (60% of 647), of which 379 of the 590 events with Mw < 7.6 (64%); 160 underestimations (24% of 647), of which 39 of the 57 events with Mw >= 7.6 (68%); an Andean South America subset n=48 with 22 (46%) underestimated by up to 0.8 units and 15 (31%) overestimated; and a sign crossover, "The black regression line in Fig. 6a intersects the Y=X line around Mw=7.45," the sentence continuing "where the data trend clearly shifts from mostly overestimations to underestimations." A magnitude-dependent Mwp correction formula is announced and applied (Conclusion 8; its coefficients came back garbled and are not reported here). NOT printed: any signed mean or median residual; any PTWC-first-bulletin-versus-PTWC-later-bulletin comparison; any share of alerts, warnings or threshold crossings that would change under the later magnitude. Benami, Ramanujan, Cecil (2025), "Rain check: how data details influence payout determinations in a U.S. rainfall index insurance program", Agricultural and Resource Economics Review (ABSTRACT ONLY; "payout determinations would differ in 13% of cases"); and the grey-literature earthquakes-feed repository (FULL TEXT of cited sections; 283 of 441 events' earliest retained version already reviewed, a dated mb 4.5 -> 4.4 revision one and 2.5 months after origin).
Novelty — how this differs from each: Lux grades an algorithm's seconds-scale internal estimate against the catalogue for a public-alerting endpoint, prints no bias statistic and, on a full read, runs no counterfactual on which alert decisions would have changed; its comparator is a reference catalogue treated as FIXED, not an agency's own successive published magnitudes, and it nowhere compares a preliminary published catalogue magnitude against a later revised one, nor discusses ComCat/ANSS revision at all. The near neighbour that must not be conflated with the candidate: Lux DOES report ShakeAlert's own successive real-time estimates inside a single event's alert sequence ("The first alert update from EPIC revised the magnitude estimate of M 3.8, with a final estimate of M 3.7."; "The EPIC magnitude increased to a final magnitude estimate of M 6.3."), each against a fixed ComCat value — and since ShakeAlert is a USGS product, "an agency's own successive estimates" is literally true of EPIC updates, which is exactly why the candidate's unit must stay worded as successive PUBLISHED magnitudes or the separation collapses on a technicality. Collich designs the trigger this candidate audits; designing an index is silent on whether its input is a rational forecast of its own final value. Artemis is n=1 journalism establishing that the mechanism bites, not an answer. Sardina et al. (2017) DOES print directional, magnitude-dependent early-magnitude structure over an earthquake population — 60% high, 24% low, 68% of Mw >= 7.6 low, sign flip at Mw ~ 7.45, plus a correction formula built on that structure — so the candidate cannot be distinguished from it by claiming the directional question is unmeasured. It is distinguished on three things instead: its numerator is a warning centre's rapid Mwp/Ms (plus one JMA value) rather than an agency's own earlier published value; its comparator is GCMT, an EXTERNAL catalogue, so nothing in it speaks to one agency's own successive published vintages; and it computes no decision-flip share, so the quantity that converts a bias into an operational cost is unmeasured there — its thresholds (7.6-7.8 regional warning, >= 7.9 expanding warning and watch, a 7.1 Pacific threat criterion) are a DEFINITION CITATION with single-event counterfactual narratives, not an evaluation. Its aggregate residual figures (mean 0.19, sd 0.16, median 0.2 magnitude units) are ABSOLUTE-value statistics, i.e. a spread and not a bias; the population also mixes magnitude types (Ms -> Mwp), carries an administrative 2002 automatic correction the authors themselves back out as a confound, and is selection-conditioned on a bulletin having been issued. Benami is a different peril and a different axis — dataset, grid resolution and reference-period choice, with no time dimension at all — so its 13% is not a vintage flip share. earthquakes-feed bounds what vintages can be recovered; it measures no revision statistic. The method-field negative (news-versus-noise, revision rationality, real-time vintage databases) returned only macroeconomic series across three independent passes, and was additionally checked in hydrology's provisional-versus-approved vocabulary with the same result; it rests on searches and on no opened source, so it is a search negative, not a proof.
PUBLISHED IS NOT PERFORMED — what no opened source names: not one source any gate opened prints (i) a signed bias, in magnitude units, of an agency's own successive published magnitude vintages at any latency, or (ii) a share of trigger or threshold decisions that flip under a later vintage, in any peril. Graded on what the sources actually do: Lux DEFINES AND MEASURES an adjacent quantity (missed/false alert rates for a different instrument, 12/53 and 7/95, Conclusions); Sardina et al. (2017) MEASURES a directional, magnitude-dependent rapid-versus-external-catalogue structure over n=647 (counts, shares and a sign crossover at Mw ~ 7.45) and separately BOUNDS the dispersion with ABSOLUTE-value statistics (mean 0.19, sd 0.16, median 0.2), and it ANNOUNCES AND APPLIES a magnitude-dependent correction — which, since fitting a correction to Mwp against GCMT is in substance a demonstration that the error is a predictable function of the early value, is adjacent to the efficiency finding and not nothing, but it is presented as CALIBRATION, with no test statistic, no standard errors, no out-of-sample check and garbled coefficients, so it does not MEASURE predictability as such; Shelly et al. (2022) MEASURES a cross-SCALE bias ("In our case study, we find that converted magnitudes can result in a systematic bias sometimes exceeding 0.5 magnitude units, a difference that typically corresponds to a factor of ~3 in seismicity rate.") on an axis with no time dimension; Corrette et al. (2020) ASSERTS without quantifying that PAGER estimates "improved as refined ShakeMaps with updated shaking estimates are incorporated", and grades PAGER LOSS estimates against observed losses; Benami MEASURES a sibling-peril flip share on a different axis; earthquakes-feed BOUNDS vintage recoverability; Collich DESIGNS the trigger; Artemis NARRATES one case. The candidate's two numbers — a SIGNED revision statistic over one agency's own successive published vintages, and a vintage decision-flip share — are unnamed by every opened source, so neither limb is a known at the level of published measurement; but the weaker claim that no directional early-magnitude structure has been measured over an earthquake population is struck, because Sardina et al. prints one.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: no opened source prints either candidate quantity, and both quantitative-limb queries returned nothing. Medium remains the grade, but the three reasons for not going higher no longer stand equally. Lux is still genuinely close in spirit on the decision-flip limb. Significance — consequence: If yes (biased and/or predictable revisions with flips), three things change: contracts settle on a later vintage or sharpen their revision mechanism; the agency attaches an uncertainty, not merely a status flag, to the value it knows is load-bearing at a named latency; and the ILS market gets a priceable basis-risk component currently attributed to hazard rather than to measurement. If no, current practice is licensed and the recurring near-miss argument is closed as tail noise.

Significance — anchoring: ILS basis-risk literature (names index-versus-loss gaps, not first-versus-final published-value gaps); seismological catalogue homogenisation (period- and definition-level, no per-event vintage object); the post-2011 rapid-Mw underestimation debate; and the macroeconometric real-time data programme, unused on this data type.
Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary plus an incentive gap, with a new-data component that the adversaries sourced rather than weakened: agency trails discard the earliest vintages, GeoNet history lapses at 365 days, several nodes keep only final origins, and the only independent snapshot archive begins 2026-07-05, so the vintage series genuinely could not be built until recently and is still partial. Two legs were weakened on opened sources, and one of them is now weakened further by a source read rather than searched: operational seismology does repeatedly ask "how good is the rapid estimate against the final" (tsunami centres, EEW, GEOFON), and Sardina et al. IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 prospectus supplement: **PARTIAL** — front matter, Overview, the "The Notes" summary and Additional Risk Factors; Annexes A, B and C and Appendices I, II and III are **COULD NOT READ**, strictly not NOT FOUND, because the document opened names all six of them. Sub-claim (e), on post-Event-Report and post-settlement revision, is **COULD NOT CHECK**, with no quotation offered either way. The IBRD CAR Chile 2023 prospectus was **NOT ATTEMPTED** on exhausted budget, which is not a negative finding.

**Claims struck.** First and most important, any version of this entry's weakest Disguise leg that asserted nobody has shown directional, magnitude-dependent early-magnitude bias over an earthquake population is struck from the entry's own prose, in the Motivating gap, in the "how this differs" paragraph, in PUBLISHED IS NOT PERFORMED, in adversary rows 1 and 2, and in the Strongest-remaining-objection paragraph. What settled it: over n=647, Sardina et al. print 391 overestimations (60%) and 160 underestimations (24%), with 39 of the 57 events at Mw >= 7.6 (68%) running low, and they print a sign crossover — "The black regression line in Fig. 6a intersects the Y=X line around Mw=7.45," continuing "where the data trend clearly shifts from mostly overestimations to underestimations." — plus a magnitude-dependent correction formula built on exactly that structure. Sardina et al. (2017) is now cited in the entry as prior art that already prints the rapid-versus-catalogue directional structure, and the entry says so in the same places where it formerly claimed the opposite. Second, the entry's own earlier response sentence "the PTWC work is cross-producer at minutes latency and serves no signed bias" is struck as a misstatement: it serves no signed *mean*, but it does serve sign-resolved population structure. Third, the SSA PAGER-accuracy item is struck from the promotion condition as **discharged**, and the entry now records why it was over-weighted: it is a 2020 SSA Annual Meeting **poster abstract** (Corrette, Marano, Engler, Jaiswal, Wald), not an SRL or BSSA article, and a one-paragraph meeting abstract is not the kind of document that prints a population statistic with a table. It prints **no percentage of any kind** — the only numbers on the page are 2010, 20 minutes, one hour and one order of magnitude — and what it grades is PAGER **loss** estimates against observed losses, not magnitudes, by residual and statistical analysis against a casualty and economic-loss database since 2010. Adversary 3's explicit demotion trigger, a share of decisions whose category changed between initial and final magnitude, therefore **does not fire** on it. The entry's former description of it as a possible "alert-category change count" source was inferred **from a title, not from the document**, and the entry now says that in those words. Fourth, the entry's gloss that the Mexico 2024 supplement "makes the calculation agent's determination final and binding absent manifest error" is withdrawn from the Contract-document-kind presupposition and from adversary rows 3, 4 and 6: the verification read found no finality, revision, amendment, restatement or correction clause in the served text and offers no quotation either way, so that sub-claim is COULD NOT CHECK and is scored neither way. Fifth, the Motivating gap's flat closing sentence "What is absent is any measurement" is struck and replaced by a sentence that names the two candidate quantities and concedes what has in fact been measured.

**Claims narrowed, and the two self-assessment corrections that run in both directions.** The efficiency limb was rewritten so that its numerator and comparator are explicit — same-agency successive **published vintages**, and/or a computed share of alerts or threshold crossings that flip under the later value — because the leg that survives is precisely the one Sardina et al. cannot occupy: its comparator is **GCMT, an external catalogue**, so nothing there speaks to one agency's own successive published vintages, and it computes no decision-flip share, so the quantity that converts a bias into an operational cost is unmeasured. Its thresholds (7.6-7.8 regional warning, >= 7.9 expanding warning and watch, a 7.1 Pacific threat criterion) are a **definition citation, not an evaluation**, illustrated with single-event counterfactuals. On the adjacent sub-claim the entry now states the position honestly in its own prose: fitting a magnitude-dependent correction to Mwp against GCMT is in substance a demonstration that the error is a predictable function of the early value, which is the efficiency finding — but it is presented as **calibration**, with no test statistic, no standard errors and no out-of-sample check, and the fitted coefficients came through garbled and are not reported; the paper **announces and applies** a correction, it does not **measure** predictability as such. The 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.2 figures are now stated as **absolute-value** statistics, i.e. a spread and not a bias, wherever they appear. Limb (b) was split in half. The **latency half is promoted to read**, evidenced from inside a real parametric earthquake trigger and cited to the **Overview and "The Notes"**, never to Annex A: a floor of "the first (1st) Business Day at least fourteen (14) calendar days after the Date of Occurrence of such Earthquake" — carried with its "later of" construction, because that string is the second limb of a two-limb test and a late Notice of Applicable Event pushes the date out, so fourteen days is a floor and not a fixed reading date — plus an Event Parameters Acquisition Period of "the thirty (30) Business Days' period" beginning the first Business Day after the Calculation Date and extendable in increments of at least five Business Days. The **vintage-and-source half remains unread**: the defined terms "Primary Earthquake Reporting Source" and "Back-up Earthquake Reporting Source" do exist in the document, so the contract does turn on an identified source, but their definitions were not served and no agency, catalogue, bulletin, magnitude type or vintage is named in what was read, and the entry accordingly does **not** assert that the annex specifies which published magnitude vintage it reads. Shelly et al. (2022) was converted from an open unknown into a sharpened, smaller condition: its regime is now fixed and is not the candidate's — cross-**scale** bias against an authors-computed coda Mw, M ~ 2-4, Oklahoma and Kansas, no time axis, no publication timestamps, no initial/final pair, no threshold, no decision — so the entry's worry that it "could carry per-event magnitude differences close enough to the candidate's bias limb to move novelty toward Low" is answered **at regime level**, per-event differences there being between scales where the candidate's are between vintages of one scale. The read was abstract-only, so the condition became a body check and not an opening. The two self-assessment corrections run in opposite directions and are both now in the prose: the entry **understated itself** in calling limb (b) unread, since its latency half is evidenced from a real trigger; and it **understated the obstacle** in treating the truncation as a bad route taken once, since the same prospectus was reopened from the **issuer's own host** and the whole served extraction was read end to end — 118,763 characters, bounded exactly — with the annexes still absent, which means that host does not serve annex text at all.

**Claims re-sourced and confirmed, and every citation correction.** Limb (a) on Lux et al. (2024) **holds**, with the three required wording changes made. Both percentages are cited to the **Conclusions**, because neither 22.6% nor 7.4% appears in the Abstract, the Results or Table 1 and a reader checking Table 1 would find counts and no percentages and conclude the citation was wrong. The composition of the 12 is given: 7 undetected ComCat M >= 4.5 events plus 5 events ShakeAlert did detect and characterise but whose magnitude estimate fell below the M 4.5 publication threshold — so 22.6% built on Table 1's own "missed" class would be 7/53, and any gloss implying ShakeAlert "failed to see 12 earthquakes" misdescribes 5 of them; the paper's third, location-error-based "missed" class is noted too. The two denominators are **split**: the former phrase "over 53 ComCat M>=4.5 in-region events with 95 detections" read as one population characterised two ways, where in fact 22.6% is per catalog earthquake (/53) and 7.4% is per detection (/95). The in-paper 95-versus-87 tension is flagged — the Conclusions call the 95 "alerts" while the Abstract, Results and Table 1 make it detections, published alerts being a strict subset at 41 of 46 detected events, and the Figure 1 caption gives 87 — so 95 is not presented as unambiguous. The read-level caveat about the author copy is carried. The separation the entry rests on survives: Lux's comparator is a reference catalog treated as **fixed**, not an agency's own successive published magnitudes, and the paper nowhere compares a preliminary published catalogue magnitude against a later revised one; the near neighbour that must not be conflated — ShakeAlert's own successive EPIC estimates inside one alert sequence — is now named in the entry, with the reason the candidate's unit must stay worded as successive *published* magnitudes or the separation collapses on a technicality. Two quotation defects were fixed as defects of the **cut**, not of the words. The entry's "a missed event rate of 22.6%" and "a false alert rate of 7.4%" were left-cut strings whose surrounding clauses carried exactly the numerators and denominators at issue; they are replaced by the full printed sentences, "Missing 12 of the 53 earthquakes gives a missed event rate of 22.6%." and "a false alert rate of 7.4% for the real-time system (seven false alerts out of 95 M >=4.5 alerts)." And on the Sardina side the checker identified the cut that would have been a misquotation had the entry made it: cutting at "these magnitude residuals have a mean of 0.19" would be verbatim and would drop the absolute-value operator that is the whole question, so the entry now carries the full sentence, "The absolute values of these magnitude residuals have a mean of 0.19, a standard deviation of 0.16," with its continuation "and a median value of 0.2 magnitude units" marked as such, together with the authors' own hedge, "These general statistics, however, fall short of revealing some significant trends in the data." Citation corrections, all now in the entry's front matter: Sardina, V.; McCreery, C.; Fryer, G. (2017), "Compilation and analysis of two decades worth of tsunami bulletins issued by the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center", 16WCEE 2017, Santiago, Chile, Paper N° 193, Registration Code S-B1463015136, **no DOI** because 16WCEE proceedings papers are not DOI-registered — and the entry's former label "two decades of Pacific Tsunami Warning Center operations" is not the title, whose object is the **bulletins**, which is what fixes the population; the ITAM Invenio mirror (record 18657) renders the title in title case with a trailing "(Ptwc)" and lists **no authors at all**, so it is a mirror hazard and must not be cited from, the author block of the paper itself being the source used here. "USGS pub 70230329" is a Publications Warehouse **index ID** for Shelly, David R., et al. (2022), "A big problem for small earthquakes: Benchmarking routine magnitudes and conversion relationships with coda-envelope-derived Mw in southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma", **Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America** 112(1), 210-225, DOI 10.1785/0120210115 — it is itself a BSSA, i.e. an SSA, article and not a USGS numbered-series report, which removes any force from reasoning that treated it as an in-house USGS operational report; the entry's former short title dropped the regime-fixing tail; and the author surname rendered "Gok" by the USGS record is near-certainly "Gök" in the BSSA front matter, flagged because the journal page could not be reached. The PAGER item has **no DOI, no volume and no pages**, as a meeting abstract has none, and the served rendering "John Presenting Corrette" is a scrape artifact of the page's "Presenting Author" label. Whether that abstract was also printed in an SRL meeting supplement is **not established**.

**Every route that failed, so a later pass does not repeat it.** On Sardina: WebFetch on `https://wcee.nicee.org/wcee/article/16WCEE/WCEE2017-193.pdf` (no `www`) returned `client_error` with nothing retrieved, while the **www** host served the same path three times — a path/host fault, not a block; `curl -L` on that URL failed with `curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` at the agent proxy, which is tool-scoped and was not routed around or probed further; ordered-consecutive-verbatim transcription of the Abstract and Section 3.2 was refused by the summariser as full-text reproduction; and the ITAM Invenio record page carries no direct PDF link and no author list, so it is usable only as a title and date cross-check. On Shelly: `https://doi.org/10.1785/0120210115` returned `client_error` with no redirect target, so the GeoScienceWorld article URL was never obtained; `curl https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70230329` failed with `curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` while WebFetch reached the same URL without trouble; and no open full text was found — the Warehouse record advertises an "Open Access Version: External Repository" link whose target was not in the served text, neither USGS record page carries a PDF link, and no repository URL was constructed by hand. On the PAGER item: verbatim transcription of the abstract body was refused on the roughly 125-character quotation cap, and no reconstruction was assembled from non-consecutive returns. On Lux: `pubs.geoscienceworld.org/ssa/bssa/article/114/4/1875/639301` returned `client_error`, so the volume, issue and page numbers implied by that path were never confirmed. On the prospectus: `thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/5cbd575a1d088a7f093b3e93bc996ba0-0340022024/original/ft2024-XS2799645788.pdf` at offset 160000 returned "Nothing left to read ... this page's text is 118763 characters long", a useful negative that bounds the served extraction exactly, while the offset-0 and offset-80000 passes both land in cover matter, Overview, "The Notes" and Additional Risk Factors, the offset-80000 pass terminating mid-sentence on the token "...Not"; the Annex A/B/C Final Terms and the definitions of "Earthquake Reporting Source" and "Earthquake Event Parameters" are not in the served text by either route. The Chile 2023 prospectus was not attempted on exhausted budget — not a failed route and not a negative finding. Three routes were named as unattempted and promising, and are now written into the promotion line: the Luxembourg Stock Exchange or other listing-venue filing of the same notes, which serves annexes as separate documents; the Mexican Ministry of Finance (SHCP) disclosure of the same transaction; and the Chile 2023 prospectus as the second instance that a premise about a **kind** of document requires.

**What the pass did not reach.** It did not reach continuous verbatim full text of Sardina et al., so the no-efficiency-test and no-decision-flip-share negatives are **partial-read** negatives, corroborated by the Abstract, the complete heading list, all nine figure captions and the Conclusions but not by a full-text read; the entry carries that caveat, and carries the instruction that if its disposition were ever to turn on the decision-flip negative alone, the PDF must be got onto disk and grepped first. It did not reach the fitted correction coefficients, which came back garbled. It did not reach Sardina's Sections 3.1 and 3.4 beyond caption level. It did not reach the body of Shelly et al., so that paper's case-study denominator is named but not numbered and no claim is made about what its tables print. It did not reach verbatim text of the PAGER abstract. It did not reach Lux's version of record. It did not reach the prospectus annexes, the definitions of "Earthquake Reporting Source" or "Earthquake Event Parameters", any named reporting agency, or any clause answering sub-claim (e); accordingly the entry now says **in those words** that its second limb has not been shown to describe a real decision, rather than implying the question is settled. It did not reach the Chile 2023 prospectus, so the document-kind premise still rests on one instance. No checker was sent to the econometric method canon, so the method-field negative on news-versus-noise and real-time vintage databases remains a **search** negative resting on no opened source, exactly as the entry already said. And 験震時報 vol. 67, the unresolved Seismica item and the NCEDC automatic-versus-reviewed poster remain returned and not opened.

**Whether the verdict moved, and why.** It did not. The entry stands at **Provisional**, narrowed. The document that could have moved it to Rejected came back PARTLY: it erodes one formulation of the novelty ground outright, but it does not print a signed mean, its comparator is an external catalogue rather than one agency's own successive published vintages, and it computes no decision-flip share, so it does not close the efficiency limb and does not support rejection. Everything else that was open stayed open at the level of COULD NOT READ or COULD NOT CHECK — the prospectus annexes, sub-claim (e), the Shelly body — and by this ledger's standing rule an unrun or unreadable check is neither a kill nor a clearance. No ground for the verdict was found false; one ground was found to be prior art on a formulation the entry had itself flagged as vulnerable, and the entry now concedes that formulation in its own prose instead of carrying it as a novelty claim. The scores are untouched at Well-posedness 3/3 and Significance 2/3, because no checker was sent to anything bearing on them.

**What the pass did to the promotion conditions and to the novelty grade.** The entry's single promotion-conditions line was rewritten rather than extended. The PAGER item was struck from it as discharged. "Opening WCEE2017-193.pdf and finding that it prints no bias" was replaced by a requirement of a different shape — that the entry carry a quantity of a **kind** Sardina et al. do not print: a signed mean over a stated population, a same-agency successive-published-vintage revision series, or a decision-flip rate — because the directional-structure version of that ground is now spent. "Opening USGS pub 70230329" was replaced by the far smaller and very likely negative check of reading the body of Shelly et al. (2022) far enough to confirm that its event tables carry no preliminary-versus-reviewed catalogue magnitude column. "Annex A of the Mexico 2024 supplement plus one further prospectus" was replaced by a condition that names the failure mode: a trigger annex opened from a route that **actually serves annex text**, with the definitions of "Earthquake Reporting Source" and "Earthquake Event Parameters" quoted together with a clause answering sub-claim (e), and with the three unattempted routes named so the issuer's own host is not tried again. The restatement of the canonical question with tau restricted to the contractual-latency class is retained unchanged. On novelty: **Medium is still the right grade and does not move**, but the entry now records that of the three grounds for not going higher, one is **spent** (the PAGER item, which was never the threat the entry took it for), one has **shrunk** (Shelly et al., from an unchecked in-field neighbour to a regime-excluded paper with an unread body), and the third is **partially read** and has become prior art on one formulation — so the entry's own statement of what holds LEG A open has been narrowed to the two things no opened source prints: a signed revision statistic over one agency's own successive published vintages, and a vintage decision-flip share.
