ID: UQ-20261022-14
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Rejected — Gate 4, attack 4 (presupposition failure), Unresolved from both adversaries independently and reached by each on documents it opened itself.
Domain(s): Other STEM — hydrology, geodesy, dam engineering. Instrument: SWOT wide-swath interferometric altimetry. Method-owning field: vertical-datum metrology (levelling, GNSS network survey).
Question (canonical): Over a declared frame of SWOT-observed reservoirs and lakes whose operator publishes both a water-level record and a documented datum (a named vertical datum, or a published conversion to one), and whose operating rule states a flood-pool, spillway-crest or freeboard threshold: (i) what is the distribution across the frame of the per-water-body residual r = (SWOT geoid-referenced water-surface elevation) minus (operator-reported level transformed to the same geopotential datum by the operator's OWN stated conversion), with its uncertainty; (ii) is r stationary over the mission record, tested for steps and trend against an independent local vertical-motion constraint where one exists; and (iii) within each water-body size class for which SWOT's stated WSE accuracy is smaller than the stated operating margin, for what share of the frame does |r| exceed that margin?
Reformulation note: the text above is V2, the single reformulation permitted at Gate 1. V1 asked for the offset between a level "in its own local datum" and the SWOT geoid-referenced elevation; it was withdrawn as an undecomposable mixture. V1 verbatim in the record. Gate 1's one reformulation is spent, which matters for the verdict below.
Alternative formulations:
- Do the water levels dam operators report mean what their operating rules assume they mean?
- Now that every reservoir's surface elevation can be measured in a global datum, how far out are the local gauge datums that flood operations, water accounting and dam-safety decisions run on, and are they drifting?
Motivating gap: SWOT-vs-gauge validation removes a per-water-body offset in its methods section before computing any metric and declines to investigate it (Koehn & Nielsen 2026, egusphere-2025-6366: "we remove the median offset between SWOT and the gauge on a per-lake-basis, before reporting any metric"; "investigating the origin of the removed offset lies beyond the scope of this study"). The offsets are printed but as nuisance residue, undecomposed, over frames chosen for altimeter validation, with no stationarity test and no comparison against any operating-rule threshold. The two fields that would own the decomposed quantity have each done one limb in another regime: altimetric detection of tide-gauge reference-level steps (Ray et al. 2023, J Geod, 10.1007/s00190-023-01800-7), and per-gauge datum harmonisation by GNSS campaign on one basin (USGS SIR 2016-5109).
Presuppositions: P1 operator records publish a stated or recoverable datum — CONTESTED; failed on 4 instances opened by the record and adversary 1 (TWDB portal, Grand River CA, USACE Kaw Lake, Hudson River – Black River Regulating District), TRUE on the one instance adversary 2 opened (USGS 07312109, "Diversion Lk nr Dundee, TX": "The Datum of the gage is 0.00 ft Above NGVD 29", and "To obtain reservoir water-surface elevations in NAVD 1988 add 0.82 feet to the NGVD 29 values." — both re-confirmed verbatim post-batch, with subject and direction intact; P1's own per-instance grading was not itself re-tested by any checker and stands as recorded). P2 SWOT WSE accuracy below the margins tested — UNVERIFIED; the mission reference document opened by adversary 1 states no accuracy requirement, and the 5.34 cm figure in the record is relative-change accuracy after offset removal. P3 operating rules state thresholds in the gauge's datum — CONTESTED, and NARROWED post-verification to the class it was actually tested on: every REAL-TIME LAKE-REPORT page opened prints threshold elevations with no datum (Kaw: Flood Control Pool 1044.50 ft, Top of Dam 1056.50 ft; confirmed verbatim first-hand — none of datum, NGVD, NAVD, msl, mean sea level or geoid appears anywhere on that page, elevations are labelled "(feet)" only, and the page's single footnote is about drainage area). The universal form this presupposition previously carried — "every rule page opened" — is FALSIFIED by one sentence of a document class nobody in the batch had opened: the Lockport Lock & Dam "WATER CONTROL MANUAL" (Appendix 1 to the Master Water Control Manual, Illinois Waterway Nine-Foot Channel, Chicago District, MAY 2024) prints, in section 4-01, "The maximum regulatory pool elevation of the CSSC is 583.0 feet NGVD", immediately followed by its equivalent in a second datum, "(+3.5 feet CCD at CRCW and O'Brien; + 5.0 feet at Wilmette)" — a threshold WITH its datum, co-occurring. P4 gauge-datum error separable from benchmark drift — CONTESTED; routine in the ocean regime, untransferred inland. P5 not presupposed: that offsets are large. P6 CONTESTED: that a geoid-referenced height is the right reference for an operational decision at all. P7 (the clause the verdict turns on, implicit in V2's wording) the operator's own stated conversion reaches SWOT's geopotential datum — FALSE on every operator document anyone opened, and re-tested first-hand after the batch, in the only form leg (a) needs: no operator document opened (USGS 07312109, Hudson River – Black River Regulating District, USACE Kaw Lake, and the newly opened Lockport water control manual) publishes a geoid model or a numeric conversion to a geopotential surface. Stated that way rather than as "nothing geoid-referenced", because the Hudson River – Black River Regulating District document does print the word: "NAVD 88 is compatible in principle with the Geoid", grounding NAVD 88 in "the Earth's observed gravity field" — a geoid reference with no model and no number.
What would count as an answer: per water body, r with uncertainty, a step-and-trend test over the mission record, and a flag of |r| against the declared margin; aggregated to a distribution and a share crossing margin by size class, plus the frame-construction yield. A small, stationary r is a full answer and would license the removal convention.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 29 distinct queries and 13 fetch attempts in total — 11 searches and 5 fetches at Gate 2, 9 and 4 by adversary 1, 9 and 4 (one a 302 route failure) by adversary 2; full lists in ledger/batches/2026-10-22-1233/UQ-20261022-14-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: the mandatory own-field title query ("comparison of SWOT water surface elevation with in situ gauge records lakes reservoirs validation") returned a dense cal-val genre and no datum-audit paper; the method-field query ("satellite altimetry used to detect errors in stream gauge vertical datum levelling benchmark") returned Ray et al. 2023, the ocean analogue of limb (ii); the mandatory share-of-X query ("share of reservoirs with incorrect gauge datum flood pool elevation dam safety survey error") returned no inventory-level share of any reservoir population; adversary 2's "SWOT water surface elevation compared reservoir operator reported pool elevation NAVD88 GEOID18" opened the record's own highest-risk unopened hit, and its South-Asian "reduced level / full reservoir level" query returned the one on-point population-scale paper nobody could read.

- Koehn & Nielsen (2026), "Evaluation of SWOT HR PIXC version D water level time series of small lakes", egusphere-2025-6366. Full text read via summariser. 37 gauged Danish lakes, 0.25-40 km2, national datum DVR90 against EGM2008, median unbiased RMSE 5.34 cm.

(2026), "Issues and potentials of multi-sensor water level monitoring: lesson learned at Recentino Lake, Italy", Int. Arch. Photogramm. Remote Sens. Spatial Inf. Sci. XLIX-M-1-2026, 19-26, 10.5194/isprs-archives-XLIX-M-1-2026-19-2026, published 02 July 2026, seven authors. P., Calmant Stéphane, Ghosh S., Dhote P. R., Sharma R., Chauhan P. THE BODY IS COULD NOT READ, NOT NOT FOUND — no methods, no tables, no figures, no datum section, no validation section. Established at that level: "around 29 geometrically complicated inland water bodies in India", 22 of them named reservoirs plus five lakes; retrievals checked against "observed gauge data"; a bias attributed to "geoid height of each reservoir" (a fragment cut on both sides, whose surrounding clause was never seen); instruments ERS-2, ENVISAT RA-2, SARAL-AltiKa and Sentinel-3A, so the paper is PRE-SWOT and published 2021.

Thakur et al. 2021 is the closest prior on limb (i)'s population axis — ~29 water bodies nationally, with a bias attributed to geoid height at each reservoir — but on nadir altimetry a mission generation before SWOT, and nothing readable establishes that its comparand is operator-published, that it prints a residual distribution rather than a scalar RMSE, that it tests stationarity, that it computes any share against FRL or a structural margin, or that it bridges frames by a conversion anyone owns.

Significance — consequence: non-stationary or large residuals identify structures operated against a mis-referenced gauge, biased assimilated levels, and datum error inherited by elevation-capacity volumes; small stationary residuals convert the removal convention from practice into a validated licence and make the SWOT-minus-gauge residual a gauge-health monitor; a collapsed frame yield is itself the finding.
Significance — audience: dam-safety regulators and owners, IJC-style boards (SIR 2016-5109 is the existence proof of paid demand on one basin), NOAA NGS and the NAPGD2022 transition, operational flood forecasting, reservoir water accounting, and the SWOT cal-val bias budget. Narrowed by P3 AS NARROWED, and the narrowing matters here: every REAL-TIME LAKE-REPORT page opened states thresholds with no datum, which is weak evidence that rules are read in gauge units by construction — but the one water control manual opened post-batch (Lockport, MAY 2024) labels its regulatory threshold with a datum and gives it in a second, so the inference holds for the real-time reporting class and NOT for rule documents generally; and the Hudson River – Black River Regulating District states of its own NGVD29-to-NAVD88 upgrade, in full, "Only the numerical value for the elevation changes; the depth and volume remain the same."
Significance — fecundity: whether offsets cluster by operator, construction era or original datum (a triage signature for unsurveyed structures); whether the residual's drift becomes a usable observable of reservoir-load subsidence and settlement; whether published storage volumes inherit the same offset; whether assimilation bias corrections are absorbing and hiding datum error; what a declared referencing margin in an operating rule should be, which no opened document contains.
Significance — anchoring: the NAVD88 to NAPGD2022 transition; the Rainy-Namakan and Lake Champlain harmonisation campaigns; the SWOT cal-val bias budget; the standing datum ambiguity in reservoir water accounting.
Reason for silence: a convention that consumes the measurand, sourced rather than asserted (the removal and the explicit refusal to investigate are both quoted from the validating paper's own methods and discussion); a new instrument (SWOT science orbit mid-2023), before which the operational version was answered by bespoke basin campaigns; and a three-way disciplinary split across datums, gauge records and margins, which the ocean analogue did not face because tide-gauge quality control sits inside one community. Adversary 2 added fresh evidence for the mechanism: a 2026 paper in the candidate's own regime measures the difference, attributes it partly to height-frame inconsistency, and leaves the cause "to be checked".

This rejection's own vulnerability (recorded per the operating rule, because part of the kill rests on what nobody has measured): the fatal clause has three legs of unequal standing. (a) EMPIRICAL and sound, and now re-tested first-hand after the batch by a checker blind to the adversaries' reasoning: that these specific operator documents publish no geoid model and no numeric conversion to a geopotential surface is read off the documents, not inferred — five instances in the batch, all failing, plus a sixth of a new and deliberately chosen kind, a USACE water control manual, which fails in the same direction while being datum-richer than any of the five (three datums in simultaneous use, an explicit printed per-project NGVD29-to-NAVD88 offset, and no use for a geoid). The escape route this entry nominated for itself has been walked and does not lead out. (b) UNMEASURED, and the UNIVERSAL QUANTIFIER IS STRUCK: the form "no operator publishes a conversion reaching EGM2008" is neither supported nor refuted by anything opened, and it is withdrawn from this entry. What the governing policy document licenses instead, now that it has been opened, is narrower and sourced to quotable sentences: USACE ER 1110-2-8160, "POLICIES FOR REFERENCING PROJECT ELEVATION GRADES TO NATIONWIDE VERTICAL DATUMS", Engineering and Design, Office of the Chief of Engineers, Department of the Army, 1 March 2009 (two pages, paragraphs 1-6, no appendix, no tables), creates NO requirement that would produce an operator-published conversion reaching a geopotential surface; it requires an INTERNALLY DOCUMENTED conversion reaching NAVD88. Paragraph 4: "the designed, constructed, and maintained elevation grades of projects shall be reliably and accurately referenced to a consistent nationwide framework, or vertical datum--i.e., the National Spatial Reference System (NSRS) or the National Water Level Observation Network (NWLON)... The current orthometric vertical reference datum within the NSRS in CONUS is the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88)" — ellipsis marked, and assembled by the checker from consecutive summariser segments — with reservoir pool stages in scope by name at 4c, which requires that "river or pool stages, and stream gages in inland flood risk and water control systems shall be accurately referenced to the NSRS (e.g., NAVD88)." Paragraph 6: "The relationship between these local (legacy) orthometric or hydraulic reference datums and the current nationwide frameworks ... must be accurately modeled, documented in O&M manuals, and be kept current". Note the hedging asymmetry and carry it the way the regulation prints it: the DOCUMENTATION is "must", while the transition away from legacy datums is only "Long-term effort should be programmed to transition from legacy reference datum grades to the NSRS." Note also that "publish", "published", "disseminate", "website", "report" and "share" are ALL ABSENT from the regulation, whose single occurrence of "public" is "This regulation is approved for public release; distribution is unlimited." What this entry MAY NOT say on that basis, and no longer says: that no operator publishes such a conversion. A requirements floor is not a survey — it enumerates no operators, prints no counts, applies to "all USACE commands" rather than to operators of this reservoir class generally, and is dated before the NSRS modernisation. Recorded so that nobody mis-cuts it: "geoid", "geopotential", "EGM", "ellipsoid" and "GPS" appear NOWHERE in the regulation, on either route; the only adjacent word is "orthometric", twice, both times an adjective on a levelling datum with no conversion verb, so quoting it as geoid language would be a verbatim-but-mis-cut misquotation. EM 1110-2-6056, offered as corroboration, was NOT REACHED within budget and must not be scored as checked in either direction. So leg (b) remains an argument from absence with a plausible explanation attached, and an argument from absence plus an explanation of the absence is still an argument from absence, which is NOT a kill. It still rests on 0 of 5 records opened in the batch (0 of 4 on the verifier's own independent, non-random reading), which is exactly the yield the question proposes to measure, so this entry's own admission that the kill partly presupposes the answer is NOT CURED by the regulation and stands as recorded. (c) SPLIT by verification into two halves that go opposite ways. (c-i) The DEFINITIONAL half HOLDS and is RE-SOURCED off trade press onto NGS's own words, so it no longer depends on GPS World: NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 72, "GEOID 18", Ahlgren, Scott, Zilkoski, Shaw and Paudel, May 2020, §2 Purpose — "Hybrid geoid models are created by constraining a gravimetric geoid model to published heights using GPS observations on leveled bench marks", and "The purpose of GEOID18 is to return a geoid height that is consistent with the published NAVD 88 orthometric heights on NGS Data Sheets" — with the mechanism at §4.1, "the residuals obtained in (1) are contaminated with a continental tilt and bias that is estimated and removed", together with NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 64, "Blueprint for 2022, Part 2: Geopotential Coordinates", National Geodetic Survey, 13 November 2017 (no individual authors printed), §5 for NGS's own definition of "hybrid geoid". ONE WORD NARROWED: NGS nowhere says GEOID18 "cannot close a geopotential comparison", and no NGS sentence read says it is not an equipotential surface or that the hybrid "inherits" or "absorbs" NAVD 88's distortions — NGS's framing is that the tilt and bias are "estimated and removed". That negative is THIS ENTRY'S INFERENCE from NGS's quoted construction and purpose, and is labelled as such from here on rather than presented as an NGS assertion; the inference is sound, and a reviewer who grants the construction must grant it, so the narrowing costs the attack nothing. (c-ii) The EVIDENTIAL half is STRUCK OUTRIGHT, not narrowed: the claim that nobody has stated the magnitude of the NAVD88-to-geopotential difference is FALSE, and it is falsified by the very document this entry recorded as never opened. NOS NGS 72 prints 56.2 cm (§6.1.1; Table 13 mean 56.22 cm over 32,357 bench marks in CONUS, Canada and Mexico) — "There is also a 56.2 cm bias present in the raw residuals, which is a mostly driven by the offset between the NAVD 88 datum and the W0 value for xGEOID19B" (the report's own grammatical slip preserved) — and the hedged, cited formulation "This agrees with one estimate for the separation, which puts NAVD 88 55 +/- 2 cm below the W0 = 62 636 856.0 m2/s2 surface (Bursa, et al 2004)."; and NOS NGS 64 §4, p. 8 prints "This revealed that NAVD 88 heights were, on average, biased by 50 centimeters in CONUS and were tilted about 1 meter from the Pacific Northwest to the Southeast of CONUS." The magnitude is therefore a RESOLVED CITATION rather than an open question, carried with the hedges NGS itself uses — "one estimate", +/- 2 cm — and anyone rounding to "about half a metre" must say which number was rounded: 56.2 cm is NGS's own residual mean against xGEOID19B's W0, 50 cm is NOS NGS 64's CONUS average against a 2017 EXPERIMENTAL geoid, and 55 +/- 2 cm is Bursa et al. 2004's estimate that NGS quotes as agreeing with its own. The only defensible residue of the struck claim is the much weaker "neither adversary stated a magnitude", which is a fact about the exchange and not about what is knowable, and which no longer supports treating the magnitude as open. THREE MARGIN WARNINGS for anyone citing a number off this leg: (i) the offset is NOT national — the same Table 13 that prints +56.22 cm for CONUS/Canada/Mexico prints MINUS 42.74 cm for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands (127 marks), so "a ~50 cm bias in NAVD 88" stated as a general property of the datum overreaches its source; (ii) the 2.4 m in NOS NGS 72's footnote 1 is the NAVD 88 tilt PLUS the IGS08-to-NAD83(2011) GEOMETRIC ellipsoid tilt combined, and must not be cited for leg (c) at all; (iii) the 1.27 cm and 1.39 cm figures are the hybrid model's FIT to the bench marks and are silent on datum separation. Provenance caution on the quotations themselves: every NGS string above came through a summariser with a ~125-character verbatim cap, and the two longest reconstructions — the §2 Purpose sentence (3 fragments) and footnote 1 (4 fragments) — must be re-verified against the PDF before they are quoted further. The one number attached to this leg, the 12.9 cm by which the mean-tide geoid exceeds the tide-free geoid at the equator, is NOT this entry's own algebra, and that provenance label is STRUCK: it is a PRINTED BULLET on slide 11 of the SWOT reference deck — "Mean-Tide Geoid height larger than Tide-Free Geoid height by 12.9 cm.", under the slide title "Difference Between Mean-Tide and Tide-Free Geoid Height" and the line "At equator:" — so the figure is confirmed and thereby strengthened, while the claim that the entry derived it is false and is replaced by the citation. It is an EQUATORIAL EXTREMUM of a latitude-dependent function, not a constant offset, and it remains a difference of static reference surfaces rather than an empirical discrepancy measured at any reservoir; it bounds nothing about any gauge. Both calls this entry recorded as unopened have since been made, and the nomination over-promised. USACE ER 1110-2-8160 — correctly titled "POLICIES FOR REFERENCING PROJECT ELEVATION GRADES TO NATIONWIDE VERTICAL DATUMS", 1 March 2009; the word is ELEVATION, not "evaluation", an error traceable to the asktop.net mirror's filename and hence to a citation assembled from a search listing rather than from front matter — was read in full (paragraphs 1-6) on two agreeing routes, one of them the host this entry cites, and it is two pages of policy with no numbers, no survey of practice and no enumeration of operators, so it constrains what operators are REQUIRED to publish and cannot settle a population claim about what they do publish. The primary NGS specification was also opened, and it settles leg (c)'s magnitude in the opposite direction from the one this entry expected, by printing it.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): the step this line used to propose, open ER 1110-2-8160 and one USACE water-control manual, HAS NOW BEEN TAKEN by the verification pass, and neither document produced an operator-published conversion reaching a geopotential surface — the regulation routes the legacy conversion into O&M manuals rather than into publication, and the one manual opened is three datums deep with no geoid in it. So that read did not reword the question into existence, and what remains is the two-stage audit (documentation yield, then residual). The next pointer is accordingly different: enumerate a DEFINED population — a named set of USACE districts' published water control manuals and gauge datum sheets, plus the non-USACE operators of this reservoir class the question wants to include, which ER 1110-2-8160 does not govern at all — and check each for a published conversion and its terminus, because until someone does that enumeration leg (b) has no denominator.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What the pass was, and what each checker was sent to read.** Six checkers ran, each in fresh context and each blind to the adversaries' reasoning, and each was sent to re-read one load-bearing source first-hand rather than to re-argue the entry. Checker 1 was sent to USACE ER 1110-2-8160, the regulation this entry nominated as the single unopened source most likely to settle legs (b) and (c) of the fatal attack, with EM 1110-2-6056 as a secondary. Checker 2 was sent to the three operator documents leg (a) names — the USGS monitoring-location page for 07312109, the Hudson River – Black River Regulating District "Vertical Datum Upgrade" document, and the USACE Tulsa District Kaw Lake water-control page — and then past them, deliberately, to a document of the class nobody in the batch had opened: a USACE water control manual. Checker 3 was sent to a primary NGS geoid specification, for both halves of leg (c). Checker 4 was sent to the SWOT reference documentation, for the mean-tide EGM2008 statement, the user-responsibility clause and the 12.9 cm figure. Checker 5 was sent to the ISPRS SWOT-versus-reservoir paper, for the "not available" sentence and the two numbers the entry set against each other. Checker 6 was sent to find, cite and test the Indian reduced-level/FRL population paper that the batch had only been able to describe.

**Read levels reached, keeping COULD NOT READ and COULD NOT CHECK strictly apart from NOT FOUND.** ER 1110-2-8160 was read at FULL TEXT of the regulation body, paragraphs 1-6, on two independent routes that agreed with each other, one of them the publications.usace.army.mil host this entry cites; the read is PARTIAL on one element only, the signature block, which neither route served, so the approving official cannot be named. EM 1110-2-6056 was NOT LOCATED within budget — two searches returned no link to it on any host — and that is neither a negative finding nor a COULD NOT READ: nothing is known about whether it exists under that number, and it must not be scored as checked in either direction. The USGS 07312109 page, the Hudson River – Black River Regulating District document and the USACE Kaw Lake page were each read at FULL TEXT of the served page. The Lockport Lock & Dam "WATER CONTROL MANUAL" (Appendix 1 to the Master Water Control Manual, Illinois Waterway Nine-Foot Channel, Upper Mississippi River Basin, Chicago District, MAY 2024, redacted public copy) was read PARTIAL — title page, "Pertinent Data", section 1-07, Table 3-1 and its note a, sections 4-01 and 4-02 — and the summariser reported its own input truncated, so every negative finding on that manual is a negative over the visible portion and not over the manual. Two further water control manuals, Keyhole Dam and Reservoir (Dec 2017) and Mathews Canyon & Pine Canyon Dams & Reservoirs (June 2022), are COULD NOT READ and not NOT FOUND: both exist at their URLs, nothing of either was read, and they are therefore silent in both directions and excluded from every count. NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 72, "GEOID 18" (May 2020), was read PARTIAL — front matter, §1, §2, §4.1, §6.1.1 with Table 13, §6.1.2 with Table 14, §7.1 with Table 15, §8 — with the gravimetric chain chapters, the regional chapters and the appendices NOT reached; the NGS "GEOID18 Technical Details" page was read at FULL TEXT; NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 64, "Blueprint for 2022, Part 2" (13 November 2017), was read PARTIAL at front matter, §4 pp. 8-10, §5 pp. 12-13 and §14.3 p. 38. No NAPGD2022- or GEOID2022-specific release document was reached at all: that is COULD NOT REACH ON BUDGET, silent in both directions. The SWOT reference deck was read at FULL TEXT on the five quoted pages (10, 11, 12, 15, 21) and at summary level elsewhere; the SWOT User Handbook and the L2_HR_RiverSP Product Description Document / ATBD are COULD NOT READ, explicitly not NOT FOUND, since the deck itself cites a handbook section. The ISPRS paper was read PARTIAL — abstract, Section 4, Section 5 and Table 3, with Sections 2-3, Tables 1-2, the figures and the reference list NOT reached — which is weaker than the "Full text read" this entry recorded, and the entry's source line has been corrected to PARTIAL accordingly. Thakur et al. 2021 was reached at ABSTRACT ONLY, and not even the abstract verbatim: the front matter was read directly off the IRD Horizon record, verbatim reproduction of the abstract was declined on copyright grounds, and what is held is a paraphrase plus three sub-125-character fragments. Its BODY is COULD NOT READ — no methods, no tables, no figures, no datum section, no validation section — and emphatically not NOT FOUND, since it is identified, cited by DOI, and reachable by routes nobody has yet spent.

**What was re-tested first-hand and HELD, which is the half of this pass that decides the verdict.** Leg (a) of attack 4's fatal clause — the operator's own stated conversion — was re-tested on all three named instances and on the document class this entry itself nominated as its best hope of a counterexample, and it survived every test. USGS 07312109 publishes "The Datum of the gage is 0.00 ft Above NGVD 29." and "To obtain reservoir water-surface elevations in NAVD 1988 add 0.82 feet to the NGVD 29 values.", with altitude datum "National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929" and altitude accuracy "0.1 feet", and names no geoid model; the entry's compression of that conversion preserved both magnitude and direction and is a fair compression, not a misquotation. The Hudson River – Black River Regulating District document publishes NGVD29-to-NAVD88 numbers only, worked out as "a water level for the Great Sacandaga Lake is 771.00 ft. and will be 770.12 in the NAVD 88 standard." and summarised as "Only the numerical value for the elevation changes; the depth and volume remain the same." The USACE Kaw Lake page names no datum at all, confirmed verbatim: none of datum, NGVD, NAVD, msl, mean sea level or geoid appears on it, its elevations are labelled "(feet)" only, its one "above" is relative ("1.45 ft ABOVE normal"), and its single footnote concerns drainage area. And the new kind held too: the Lockport Lock & Dam Water Control Manual, MAY 2024, Chicago District, reaches THREE datums in simultaneous use (NGVD 1929, NAVD 88 and CCD) and prints an explicit per-project offset under the header "Conversion from NGVD (1929) Datum to NAVD 1988 Datum by Project" — "Lockport Lock 0.00 feet NGVD = -0.30 feet NAVD 88" — and still reaches no geoid model and no geopotential surface in the portion read, with geoid, GEOID12B, GEOID18, EGM2008, mean sea level, orthometric and geopotential all reported absent from that portion. Four of four documents read publish no conversion reaching a geoid model. The checker declines to generalise past those four, since the sample was chosen partly by following this entry's own citations and is therefore not a random draw from any operator population. Also re-confirmed, cutting against the entry rather than for it: Table 3 of the ISPRS paper is a genuine dispersion summary of exactly the candidate's residual (SD 0.15 m, NMAD 0.12 m, RMSE 0.17 m, MAE 0.13 m, split by combined, ascending and descending orbit), which is prior art for a sliver of limb (i) at n=1 reservoir, with no stationarity test and no threshold comparison — so the entry's statement that limbs (ii) and (iii) are unoccupied in everything anyone opened survives.

**What was struck.** Four claims were struck from this entry's own prose, not merely noted. First, the universal quantifier in leg (b): "no operator publishes a conversion reaching EGM2008" is neither supported nor refuted by anything opened, and ER 1110-2-8160 cannot settle it, because a requirements floor is not a survey — it enumerates no operators, prints no counts, and applies to "all USACE commands" rather than to this reservoir class. Second, the "assigns the transformation to the data user" leg of the SWOT clause. The user-responsibility sentences do exist — p. 15, "If necessary, adjust independent data to use consistent reference static surface."; p. 21, "User may need to convert or transform one or both data sets to reach this common representation."; p. 21, "Users are responsible for determining the representations of their independent data to which SWOT is compared." — but the cut was the defect: read with the clause around it, what the user is made responsible for is determining the representations of their own data, not the transformation arithmetic, because the deck hands that over explicitly, giving the permanent-tide transformation in closed form on slide 10 with its constants ("Hperm = -0.31460 m, k2 = 0.3") and an error bound ("results with < 1.3 mm error"), and two worked conversion identities on slide 15 under "Examples:" with a pointer to a User Handbook section. Third, the "own algebraic consequence" label on the 12.9 cm: the figure is a printed bullet on slide 11 — "Mean-Tide Geoid height larger than Tide-Free Geoid height by 12.9 cm." — so the number is confirmed and strengthened while the provenance claim was false, and it has been replaced by the citation. Fourth, the number-pairing in the "Strongest remaining objection" paragraph: "the candidate frame shift flagged in that paper (-0.18 m) is larger than the residual it would explain (-0.08 m)" misstates its source and survives in no form, because the difference the -0.18 m is offered to explain is the -0.17 m UAV-DEM-minus-gauge difference at the single UAV epoch, and against that comparand the frame shift is the same size to within 0.01 m — which is why the authors propose it. The paper's own hedges are "(to be checked)", "which requires additional future checks" and "In case future checks on gauge height reference frame will confirm its present misalignment". Fifth and last, the evidential half of leg (c): the claim that nobody has stated the magnitude of the NAVD88-to-geopotential difference is false, and false on the very document this entry recorded as never opened.

**What was narrowed.** Presupposition P3 and adversary 1's cross-check C4 are both falsified as stated by a single sentence of the Lockport manual — "The maximum regulatory pool elevation of the CSSC is 583.0 feet NGVD", immediately followed by its equivalent in a second datum — and both are narrowed in the prose above to the real-time lake-report class they were actually tested on; the derived audience claim at Significance is narrowed with them. The "nothing geoid-referenced" clause is narrowed as applied to the Hudson River – Black River Regulating District, which does print "NAVD 88 is compatible in principle with the Geoid" and grounds NAVD 88 in "the Earth's observed gravity field" — a geoid reference with no model and no number — so the clause now reads "no geoid model and no numeric conversion to a geopotential surface", which is what leg (a) needs and what survives, and which the prose mention therefore cannot be used to embarrass. The definitional half of leg (c) is narrowed by one word: NGS nowhere says GEOID18 "cannot close a geopotential comparison", and no NGS sentence read says it is not an equipotential surface or that the hybrid "inherits" or "absorbs" NAVD 88's distortions, NGS's framing being that the tilt and bias are "estimated and removed", so that negative is labelled this entry's inference from NGS's quoted construction and purpose rather than an NGS assertion. The SWOT geoid clause regains its dropped scope hedge, "through Version D", stated twice in the deck, and the 12.9 cm is marked as an equatorial extremum of a latitude-dependent function rather than a constant offset. The uniqueness parenthetical "the only published SWOT-versus-reservoir-operator comparison" is reworded to "the only one found", since uniqueness could not be checked and was not tried. The Combinatorial-novelty line loses its juxtaposition of -0.18 m and -0.08 m: "beside" was literally true, both numbers being in the paper, but the juxtaposition carried the inference and the juxtaposition was this entry's, not the paper's; the seam survives without it, on the paper's own sequence of could-not-obtain, assumed RDN2008 + ITALGEO05, bridged to EGM2008 with a geoid-model difference of its own, and left to "future checks".

**What was re-sourced, and what the struck magnitude was replaced with.** The definitional half of leg (c) comes off trade press and onto NGS's own words: NOS NGS 72 §2 Purpose, "Hybrid geoid models are created by constraining a gravimetric geoid model to published heights using GPS observations on leveled bench marks" and "The purpose of GEOID18 is to return a geoid height that is consistent with the published NAVD 88 orthometric heights on NGS Data Sheets", with the mechanism at §4.1, "the residuals obtained in (1) are contaminated with a continental tilt and bias that is estimated and removed", corroborated by the Technical Details page's "the gravimetric geoid model is warped to fit the existing GPS on bench mark data using least squares collocation (Moritz, 1980)", and with NOS NGS 64 §5 supplying NGS's own definition of the term. The GPS World citation is gone. The struck evidential half becomes a resolved citation rather than a weakened claim: NOS NGS 72 §6.1.1 prints "There is also a 56.2 cm bias present in the raw residuals, which is a mostly driven by the offset between the NAVD 88 datum and the W0 value for xGEOID19B" (Table 13 mean 56.22 cm, 32,357 marks) and the hedged "This agrees with one estimate for the separation, which puts NAVD 88 55 +/- 2 cm below the W0 = 62 636 856.0 m2/s2 surface (Bursa, et al 2004).", while NOS NGS 64 §4 p. 8 prints "This revealed that NAVD 88 heights were, on average, biased by 50 centimeters in CONUS and were tilted about 1 meter from the Pacific Northwest to the Southeast of CONUS." The hedges travel with the numbers, and the entry now states which figure any rounding to "about half a metre" came from. Three margin warnings travel with them too, and are recorded in the prose above: the offset is not national, since the same Table 13 that prints +56.22 cm for CONUS, Canada and Mexico prints minus 42.74 cm for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands; the 2.4 m of footnote 1 is NAVD 88 tilt plus the IGS08-to-NAD83(2011) geometric ellipsoid tilt combined and must never be cited for leg (c); and the 1.27 cm and 1.39 cm figures are the hybrid's fit to the bench marks, silent on datum separation. For leg (b), the struck universal is replaced by what ER 1110-2-8160 actually licenses: paragraph 4's requirement of referencing to "a consistent nationwide framework, or vertical datum--i.e., the National Spatial Reference System (NSRS) or the National Water Level Observation Network (NWLON)", with "The current orthometric vertical reference datum within the NSRS in CONUS is the North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88)" and pool stages in scope by name at 4c, and paragraph 6's "must be accurately modeled, documented in O&M manuals, and be kept current" against the merely programmatic "Long-term effort should be programmed to transition from legacy reference datum grades to the NSRS." The regulation's silence on publication is itself sourced: "publish", "published", "disseminate", "website", "report" and "share" are absent, and its one "public" is "This regulation is approved for public release; distribution is unlimited."

**Citation corrections made.** ER 1110-2-8160's title is "POLICIES FOR REFERENCING PROJECT ELEVATION GRADES TO NATIONWIDE VERTICAL DATUMS": the entry's "evaluation" was wrong, traceable to the asktop.net mirror's filename and to the search-result title derived from it, which means the citation had been assembled from a listing rather than from front matter; the missing date, 1 March 2009, is added, and it matters, because a 2009 policy cannot speak to the reach of a datum chain in the NAPGD2022 era. "HRBRRD" is spelled out as the Hudson River – Black River Regulating District (New York), a state regulating district in the Adirondack and Hudson basins with no Red River connection; the source line handed to the checker had called it a Hulah/Red Rock or Red River basin authority page, and that is corrected. USGS 07312109 is identified as "Diversion Lk nr Dundee, TX", a USGS-published gage page, not the output of any basin authority. The SWOT statements are cited to their actual document, "SWOT Reference Frame, Geodetic Coordinates, Reference Surfaces, and Tides", NASA/JPL/Caltech, May 19, 2025 — a slide deck with no document number and no named authors, served from archive.podaac.earthdata.nasa.gov — and by slide-footer page number, rather than to the product description document, ATBD or user handbook, in none of which the verified statements appear. The ISPRS paper gains its title, its DOI (10.5194/isprs-archives-XLIX-M-1-2026-19-2026), its first author's forename (Alireza Hamoudzadeh), its seven-author count, its publication date, its UAV photogrammetric leg — whose omission from the entry's description is what left -0.18 m nowhere to live but the SWOT residual — and a read level corrected from "Full text read" to PARTIAL. The NGS sources are cited as NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 72, "GEOID 18", Ahlgren, Scott, Zilkoski, Shaw and Paudel, May 2020, and NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 64, "Blueprint for 2022, Part 2: Geopotential Coordinates", National Geodetic Survey, 13 November 2017, with no individual authors printed and no DOI on either, NOAA technical reports carrying none. Thakur et al. 2021 is cited in full for the first time anywhere in this batch: thirteen authors, "Water level status of Indian reservoirs: a synoptic view from altimeter observations", Advances in Space Research 68(2), 619-640, DOI 10.1016/j.asr.2020.06.015, with given names left as initials because the record prints initials and expanding them would be invention.

**Routes that failed, recorded so a later pass does not repeat them.** Both ER routes returned content and agreed, and nothing failed there; EM 1110-2-6056 was simply not located by two searches, and the publications.usace.army.mil engineer-manual index page was not attempted and is where a next checker should start. A curl to water.usace.army.mil returned "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" at the proxy with zero bytes, and was reported rather than circumvented — no TLS setting was changed and the proxy was not probed; WebFetch reached the same host, so the block is tool-scoped. The Keyhole Dam manual fetch reached the host but arrived as binary with no readable text layer, and the Mathews Canyon manual failed at its site with a client_error, the literal ampersand in its URL being the likely cause; both are COULD NOT READ. The podaac archive directory is not browsable and returned a client_error, so the handbook and PDD PDFs sitting beside the deck could not be enumerated; the earthdata catalogue page for L2_HR_RiverSP carries no handbook, PDD or ATBD link; and a targeted search for the PDD returned no such PDF. The deck's own internal pointer is unresolved: one pass served "section 11.3.1 of User Handbook" and another "User Handbook Sections 3.1.24 and 3.1.25", and neither should be quoted as settled. For the ISPRS paper, curl to the publisher PDF hit the same proxy 403; the publisher HTML full-text page resolved but served abstract content only; and on the final call the summariser declined to reproduce the two paragraphs at issue, substituting a statement of the pronoun antecedent plus one short quotation, so that one point rests on the summariser's reading rather than the checker's and should be re-checked against the PDF by anyone who needs it airtight. For Thakur et al., HAL failed identically on both the legacy hal-insu.archives-ouvertes.fr landing page and the current insu.hal.science file route, with an Anubis bot-protection interstitial and error code 9e4edb5b6b850c41, so HAL should not be budgeted as a full-text route from this environment at all; the ADS abstract page failed with robots_disallowed; the IRD Horizon record succeeded and is the only route that returned anything; and a re-request for ordered consecutive abstract segments was refused on copyright grounds, which is a second failure mode of the segment protocol distinct from fragment-junction risk. ScienceDirect PII S0273117720304178, the ResearchGate deposit and archive.iwmi.org are untried rather than failed, and the real IRD full text is restricted to an account or an emailed request, which this pass could not use.

**What the pass did not reach.** EM 1110-2-6056 was not located. The ER's signature block was not served, so its approving official is unnamed. Two water control manuals could not be read. The gravimetric chain chapters, regional chapters and appendices of NOS NGS 72 were not reached, nor §1-§3 and §6-§14.2 of NOS NGS 64, nor any NAPGD2022 or GEOID2022 release document. The SWOT User Handbook and the RiverSP PDD/ATBD could not be read, so this pass cannot say that SWOT nowhere supplies a national-datum bridge, only that the reference deck does not. Sections 2 and 3, Tables 1 and 2, the figures and the reference list of the ISPRS paper were not reached, and its uniqueness as a SWOT-versus-operator comparison was not checked and not attempted. The body of Thakur et al. 2021 was not reached by any route. Every NGS, ER and ISPRS quotation above arrived through a summariser with a roughly 125-character verbatim cap, so the longer ones are reconstructions from ordered consecutive fragments; two in particular — the NOS NGS 72 §2 Purpose sentence, three fragments, and footnote 1, four fragments — must be re-verified against the PDF before they are relied on as quotations.

**The verdict did not move, and no late Gate 4 was owed.** This entry stays Rejected, and it stays Rejected on leg (a) of attack 4's fatal clause alone, exactly as it declared. That leg was re-tested first-hand, by a checker who re-read the documents rather than the argument, on all three named instances and on the one document class this entry had itself nominated as its best hope of a counterexample — and it survived every one of those tests. A ground that survives verification of its own sources is not a withdrawn ground: no late Gate 4 was owed, because no late Gate 4 is owed for a ground that holds. Nothing here is promoted, and nothing is Validated. The threatened second, independent ground for rejection — that Thakur et al. 2021 might do the candidate's job over a population — is NOT ESTABLISHED, which is not the same as refuted: the paper's body was never opened, so attack 2 is held at Partial, neither promoted nor demoted, and promoting it on front matter and an abstract would repeat precisely the error this ledger is trying to stop. What did change is everything standing next to the fatal ground. Leg (b) loses its universal quantifier and remains an argument from absence with a plausible explanation attached, which is not a kill, and this entry's own admission that the kill partly presupposes the answer is not cured. Leg (c) splits, holding and re-sourced on the definitional side, struck on the evidential side. The SWOT clause survives only in its narrowed form, with the genuinely un-owned material reduced to two things: no national-levelling-datum bridge, and no supplied GeoidX field for the slide 15 identity, which is a schema the user must fill. Two presuppositions beside the fatal one are falsified as written and narrowed, and attack 5's stated reason is spent. And one finding runs against the entry's own grading: the documentation yield in the water-control-manual class is visibly higher than its five instances implied, which argues limb (i) is better posed than attack 5 allows — not that the fatal clause is wrong.

**Conditions this pass leaves open.** They are written here as prose, because a Rejected entry carries no promotion clause, and none of them would move this verdict while leg (a) stands. For leg (b), a real denominator: enumerate a defined population — a named set of USACE districts' published water control manuals and gauge datum sheets, plus the non-USACE operators of this reservoir class, whom ER 1110-2-8160 does not govern — and check each for a published conversion and its terminus. For leg (c), one narrow and precise question, worth a single fetch: whether NGS has since printed a NAVD88-to-NAPGD2022 figure for the datum AS RELEASED, rather than against xGEOID19B's W0 (2020) and the 2017 experimental geoid; it affects only the precision of the figure, not its sign or its order of magnitude. For the SWOT clause, a read of the SWOT User Handbook at the cited section — unresolved between "11.3.1" and "3.1.24/3.1.25" — establishing that no national-levelling-datum conversion is supplied there either; until that read happens the narrowed clause is supported on the deck but not closed. For attack 2, one successful fetch of the body of Thakur et al. 2021, whose validation tables and datum treatment would settle Disguise in one direction or the other: if that body prints a share of its ~29-body population exceeding Full Reservoir Level, or tests the residual's stationarity, against operator-published reduced levels, this entry acquires a second independent ground for rejection; if it prints neither, with table and figure numbers named, attack 2 resolves. And one defect this entry must keep carrying until that body is read: the Full Reservoir Level threshold is the BATCH'S INFERENCE and not the paper's text — "FRL" and "Full Reservoir Level" do not appear in its abstract — so it is legitimate as a flag and illegitimate as a property of the paper, and nothing in this entry may read as though the FRL comparison were a known fact.

ID: UQ-20261022-15
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Validated blocked independently at Gate 1 (Well-posedness 2/3, 3/3 required), at Gate 2 (Medium with a close neighbour), and by on-point sources that post-batch verification could read only in part or not at all (HITRAN2024 partial, MARVEL/IUPAC Part III partial, the ACE-FTS validation paper COULD NOT READ on four routes) — Unverified reads, not failed checks
Domain(s): Other STEM — molecular spectroscopy and atmospheric remote sensing. TARGET field: curators of shared line-parameter compilations (HITRAN/GEISA/ExoMol) and operational column-retrieval teams. METHOD field: provenance/citation-chain resolution and non-independence auditing of a reference corpus.
Question (canonical): For a declared frame of the six HITRAN-format line parameters (nu_ij, S_ij, gamma_air, gamma_self, n_air, delta_air) of the transitions carrying at least a declared share X of the Jacobian-weighted absorption in the fitting windows of a declared set of operational column retrievals, at a pinned compilation release: resolving each parameter's own per-parameter reference index to its primary source, and under a pre-declared independence rule scored at two strictness levels (R-strict: distinct apparatus AND calibration standard AND sample AND no shared author AND distinct theoretical method/fitting code, each criterion reported separately; R-weak: distinct publication only), what is (i) the count n of mutually independent primary determinations per parameter and whether they agree within stated uncertainties, (ii) the share of sensitivity-weighted parameter mass with n <= 1 at each strictness level, and (iii) for each parameter with n <= 1, which declared retrievals and ground networks actually read it, established from each retrieval's own documented spectroscopy source rather than assumed?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation and the scored version. V1 added a limb asking what share of the retrieval's spectroscopic error budget is a common-mode dependence on a single laboratory; V1's "mutually independent" and "share of the error budget" were undefined estimands. V1 is NOT scored here, and adversary 3 is explicit that on V1 attack 4 would be Unresolved (its clause P8 is FALSE on an opened source), i.e. V1 as worded is Rejected. The record's Domain, Motivating-gap and Significance (i) paragraphs still carry V1's framing; that mismatch is charged to significance below, not to attack 4.
Alternative formulations: (1) How independent are the world's greenhouse-gas measurements, given that they all read the same line list? (2) For the strongest contributors to a retrieval's sensitivity, what is the count of independent laboratory determinations behind the line intensity and the broadening coefficient, and how many missions share each one?
Motivating gap: compilation imperfection is reported repeatedly as an accuracy limit and an error term and, in what the record opened, never as a dependency structure. Anchor opened at intake: arXiv:2209.07464 (exoplanet regime only — "a hard accuracy wall around 0.5 to 1 dex", "the reported values often did not agree within their uncertainties") which does not count the primary determinations behind its parameters. The Earth-side anchor is abstract-level only. Adversary 3 weakens the gap as stated: HITRAN2020 Sec. 2.1.6 shows the curators themselves run a per-transition multi-source intercomparison and classify "a single datum for a transition" separately, and ABSCO v5.2 Table 1 states the per-band source for the flagship retrieval — so dependency structure IS reported at band level, just never aggregated or weighted.
Presuppositions: (1) per-parameter reference indices exist and resolve to primary sources — VERIFIED at format level by three independent reads (HITRAN2004 Table 2 "References for 3/6 critical parameters"; HITRAN2020 Sec. 2 "Uncertainty and reference indices are now given for all parameters in HITRAN except for the Einstein-A coefficients"; the .par `Iref` field at line[133:145] in three independent parsers), NOT VERIFIED at the record level — no index was resolved to a primary source by anyone in this batch, and none by post-batch verification either, which re-read both release papers and found no worked end-to-end trace in the windows it reached. Two hedges printed in HITRAN2024 (Gordon, Rothman, Hargreaves, Gomez, Bertin, Hill, Kochanov, Tan, Wcislo, Makhnev et al., "The HITRAN2024 molecular spectroscopic database", JQSRT 353 (2026) 109807, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2026.109807) Sec. 2 preamble dent even the format-level reading: the exclusion is parenthesised "(which usually share the same source and uncertainty as the intensities), lower-state energies, and quantum numbers", so the parameter-to-source mapping is not stated one-to-one even for the Einstein-A case; and the same preamble warns of its own coding that "the code 0 in Table 2 might lend itself to two different meanings". (2) "independent determination" is definable — CONTESTED, carried by declared rule R, and STRENGTHENED against the strict reading by post-batch verification; hybrid scaled-ab-initio values (HITRAN2020 Sec. 2.2.4, where "the UCL line intensities [137] of the 00031-00001 band were scaled by the factor of 1.1217 to match the line intensities measured by Birk et al. [153]" — a figure that is edition-specific and now SUPERSEDED, HITRAN2024 Sec. 2.2.2 having rescaled the same 00031-00001 band by 0.99314) and team-assigned uncertainty codes 1/2 have no defined n under R as written. A second, printed illustration now stands beside the hybrid: HITRAN2024 Sec. 2.4.1 states that "a MARVEL energy level analysis has been carried out using 91 published sources for 14N2 16O" — 91 published sources feeding ONE joint energy-level fit, a printed case where R-strict scores n=1 while 91 laboratories supplied the data, and it concerns a quantity (energy levels) that carries no reference index at all. (3) dominant parameters are identifiable — ESTABLISHED by use; no published per-transition Jacobian ranking was opened. (4) the declared missions read the compilation's shipped values — FALSE for the flagship ON ONE COMPILATION ONLY, on an opened source (ABSCO User Guide, Payne and Oyafuso, Jet Propulsion Laboratory/Caltech, revision date 25 February 2022, documenting the v5.2 ACOS/OCO-2/OCO-3 tables, Table 1: O2 from Payne 2021 with the Drouin et al. 2017 methodology, weak 1.61 µm CO2 from Devi 2016b, strong 2.06 µm CO2 from "Drouin (not yet published)", H2O from Toon 2018/ATM18; HITRAN appears in the document only as the CH4 line list, as netCDF gas/isotope indices, as superseded v5.1 H2O "HITRAN 2012" in Table 2, and in one reference entry). Post-batch verification NARROWS this: ABSCO reads a compilation as shipped, just a different one — the weak band's cross sections "were determined from the Devi et al. (2016) database, then subsequently scaled by a constant factor of 1.014", which leaves positions, widths, their temperature dependences, speed dependence and line mixing as that database ships them, and H2O reads ATM18 as shipped under one scalar. V2 limb (iii) makes readership a measurand, so attack 4 does not reach it. (5) shared provenance produces same-signed bias across missions — UNVERIFIED by every source anyone opened, and HELD UNVERIFIED by post-batch verification WITH ITS SOURCE LIST FOR THIS PRESUPPOSITION NOW EMPTY: the one document this entry had nominated to settle it (arXiv:2509.16419) was read in full and cannot settle it in either direction, and nothing else anyone opened argues it. It remains cut against, more weakly than this entry first said, by ABSCO's band-wide cross-section scale factors — four of the five atmospherically anchored, one a laboratory ratio. (6) concentration is NOT presupposed; n >= 3 with agreement throughout is pre-declared as a complete answer.
What would count as an answer: per parameter in the declared sensitivity-weighted set, n under R-strict and R-weak with primary sources named and agreement within stated uncertainties assessed; aggregated into the share of sensitivity-weighted parameter mass at n <= 1 under each rule; plus the readership map taken from each retrieval's own documentation. Three admissible complete answers pre-declared: (a) concentration with a ranked list; (b) a clean negative (n >= 3 with agreement throughout), which retires the worry; (c) "provenance not reconstructible from public documents" for a stated share of the frame.

Significance — consequence: the remeasurement-ranking limb is unconditionally actionable and needs only the count and the sensitivity weights; the line-shape and mixing parameters, which are single-source per band by design and are NOT empirically rescaled, are where airmass- and temperature-dependent residual biases live, so a weighted census would still rank them. The corroboration limb — that agreement between missions reading the same compilation stops counting as evidence — is the candidate's headline and is the part that did not survive: it needs presupposition 5, which nothing any adversary opened argues and which the one document nominated to settle it cannot settle; and ABSCO v5.2 shows the flagship team applying BAND-WIDE CROSS-SECTION scale factors (O2 0.76 µm 1.0048; weak 1.61 µm CO2 1.014 baked into the tables, then 0.994; strong 2.06 µm CO2 0.9875; H2O 0.981), i.e. treating a band-wide multiplicative scale as a tunable common mode without an independence count. Three corrections post-batch verification forces on that sentence: the document's own heading is "Scaling of absorption cross-sections", so only 1.014 is an intensity ratio in its words; only two of the five (1.014, 0.981) are in the shipped tables at all, the other three living in the Level-2 algorithm on top of an unscaled table; and the practice is not settled but dated by the document to v5.2 / L2 v11, which prints the contrary for the version before — "For version 10, the scaling factors applied within the Level 2 algorithm to ABSCO v5.1 tables were 1.000 and 1.004 for the weak and strong bands, respectively. However, for that version, no effort was made to account for the overall persistent bias of retrieved XCO2 through spectroscopic adjustments." A clean negative remains informative.
Significance — audience: real and sourced, which is an upgrade on the record's unfound absence. NIST spent a cavity ring-down campaign on a band it had identified as resting on one source and reported literature deviations of "-1.16 % to +0.33 %" against it (P2); PTB and partners commissioned a per-band literature census of intensity determinations for exactly these gases (P1); the EURAMET/PTB MetCTG project page was confirmed to exist. Counter-evidence to declare: that demand is for better band measurements, not for a per-line n, and the ensemble community is the one audience shown to assume unaudited independence (EMMA: "we expect relatively independent bias patterns", "EMMA relies on the assumption that it is unlikely that the majority of algorithms produce outliers in the same direction", with shared spectroscopy never discussed).
Significance — fecundity: whether an independence-adjusted spectroscopic covariance can replace a scalar uncertainty class in retrieval error budgets; whether a compilation should ship a dependency flag as a first-class field beside its reference and uncertainty indices; whether agreement between two determinations sharing a fitting code or a scaling reference is evidence at all (the R-strict/R-weak gap makes this measurable, and P3's scaled-to-measurement hybrids make it urgent); whether the same audit transfers to ExoMol/GEISA; whether the exoplanet and Earth regimes share single points of failure.
Significance — anchoring: Checa-Garcia et al. 2015's regionally correlated spectroscopy-induced XCH4 error exceeding 0.6%; P3's printed inter-determination discrepancies for the OCO-2/TCCON CO2 bands (NIST vs Zak ab initio "agree at the 0.06% level" for 30013-00001 but "a systematic discrepancy of about 1.1%" for 30012-00001, with DLR and Long et al. differing "outside of the stated uncertainties"); EMMA's unaudited independence assumption; arXiv:2209.07464's accuracy wall in the exoplanet regime; and the ledger's nuclear-data sibling UQ-20261021-06, where the analogous shared-data worry was a published known in that field.
Reason for silence: an incentive gap, not a conceptual boundary, and the record's stronger phrasing is withdrawn. Sourced mechanism: both routes to action bypass the count — the operational route sets per-mission band-wide cross-section scale factors, four of its five against atmospheric references and one (the weak CO2 band's 1.014) against a laboratory intensity ratio (ABSCO v5.2), and the laboratory route remeasures the key bands (NIST in P2, PTB in P1) — so the per-line census has no customer, and the curators already hold per-transition source multiplicity internally (P3 Sec. 2.1.6) without publishing it as a statistic. What is withdrawn: the record's claim that compilation imperfection is "never" reported as a dependency structure and that "nobody points the method at a line list" — band-level dependency statements are printed (ABSCO Table 1, P1) and BRASS has done database provenance resolution on an atomic line list. "No one thought of it" is not being offered.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: the verdict rests on three legs, and it is worth being explicit about which. Leg A, decisive and self-standing: Well-posedness is 2/3 where Validated requires 3/3, on grounds internal to the record — the headline share is a quantity under a convention whose R-strict/R-weak spread could be the whole result, presupposition 1 is verified only at format level (no reference index was resolved to a primary source by anyone in this batch, nor by post-batch verification, which re-read both release papers and found no worked end-to-end trace), and hybrid and team-assigned values have no defined n. Leg A would survive if both other legs fell. Leg B, real and sourced but at REDUCED STRENGTH after post-batch verification, and NO LONGER clearly "substantively the strongest objection": the flagship operational retrieval reads no HITRAN-frame parameter for O2 or CO2 (held narrowly) and applies BAND-WIDE CROSS-SECTION scale factors per band (ABSCO User Guide, Payne and Oyafuso, JPL/Caltech, rev. 25 February 2022, pp. 6-8 — corrected here from "pp. 5-8", page 5 carrying only "1 Introduction" and "1.1 Scope and Background" — with 0.981 repeated on p. 9: O2 1.0048; weak CO2 1.014 then 0.994; strong CO2 0.9875; H2O 0.981). Three strikes, one narrow hold and a page correction bear on that sentence. "Intensity" is STRUCK from "empirical intensity scale factors": the document's own heading is "Scaling of absorption cross-sections" and Table 1's row is "ABSCO scaling", only 1.014 is an intensity ratio in the document's words, 1.0048 is fit to a retrieved-surface-pressure bias "on the order of several hPa", and a single scalar per band is degenerate with continuum, collision-induced absorption, instrument line shape and radiometric gain. "From atmospheric references" is STRUCK as a universal and narrowed to 1.0048, 0.994, 0.9875 and 0.981: the weak band's 1.014 "represents a ratio between line intensities in the Devi et al. (2016) database and reference intensity measurements from our NIST ABSCO team members, described in Polyansky et al. (2015)", a LABORATORY-to-database ratio that TCCON only tests afterwards, and the strong band's v5.2 table is itself anchored to "the ab initio intensities reported in Zak (2016)" via Fleurbaey (2020) — the document draws no atmospheric-versus-laboratory contrast, this entry supplied it. The claim that the shared compilation is not the dependency the retrievals actually have is STRUCK in that broad form: ABSCO swaps one compilation for another and retunes one scalar per band, leaving positions, widths, temperature dependences, speed dependence and line mixing of the Devi et al. (2016) database and of ATM18 exactly as shipped — this entry's own concession that the line-shape and mixing parameters are NOT empirically rescaled belongs here, inside Leg B, and it is the whole weak-band parameter set except intensity. And a HITRAN line list IS shipped into both CO2 windows for CH4 — "CH4 tables using the HITRAN line list are now also available; they are computed over both CO2 spectral windows" — which undercuts Leg B's inference though not its narrow wording; hedged, because "now also available" states availability and operational use in L2 v11 was not established (published is not performed). What survives is an objection about ONE parameter (intensity), scaled per band by a single scalar, with one of four anchors laboratory, and with the determination-level overlap with HITRAN UNRESOLVED and now carried as a promotion condition — the document is SILENT, not negative, on whether its named sources are different DETERMINATIONS from HITRAN's for the same bands, and "not labelled HITRAN" is a citation-frame fact where Leg B needs a determination-level one. V2's census therefore survives as bookkeeping while the common-mode motivation is neither restored nor finally defeated. LEG A CARRIES THE VERDICT: it is decisive and self-standing, it rests only on the record's internals, and nothing in the post-batch pass touched it. Leg C, weakest: novelty is held at Medium by two close neighbours and by an on-point-title residue the pass shrank without clearing — HITRAN2024 and MARVEL/IUPAC Part III read in part, arXiv:2509.16419 read in full and found silent, MARVEL Parts I, II and IV unopened, and the ACE-FTS validation paper still COULD NOT READ. This is not a rejection, so no leg has to carry a kill.
Grounds resting on nothing anyone has measured, recorded as this verdict's own vulnerability: (i) presupposition 5 — that a shared parameter error produces same-signed bias across missions — is UNVERIFIED by every source any agent opened, in the batch and in post-batch verification alike; it is a design-and-mechanism argument on both sides, with nobody's reported result testing cross-mission sign, and its source list for this presupposition is now EMPTY. The nomination of arXiv:2509.16419 as "the single unopened source most likely to settle it" is STRUCK. The paper was read IN FULL and is refuted as a settler on three grounds verifiable in the document: there is no spectroscopic or line-parameter term in its error decomposition, the sole occurrence of "spectroscop" in the whole paper being a reference-list title (Hobbs et al., 2020) cited under a generic forward-model clause; there is no second standalone mission, ACOS-GOSAT v9.0 appearing only as an input to a fused product with no bias figure of its own and OCO-3 only in the abstract, introduction and references; and it states "In the decomposition shown in Eq. (21), it is assumed that all the terms are independent", so it cannot be read as having found correlated same-signed error. Opening it does NOT convert presupposition 5 from UNVERIFIED to refuted: the paper is silent on cross-mission common-mode under a regime that EXCLUDES the question — its "systematic" is defined as what "remain[s] unchanged when averaging observation errors within a single station/day coincidence" — and silence under an inapplicable regime is not negative evidence. One warning is carried here as a trap for a future reader: its Tables 2 and 3 DO print a column of same-signed negative biases, -0.1 to -0.31 ppm across products, and anyone skimming could cite that as "same-signed bias across missions"; it is same-signed bias across derivatives of ONE retrieval lineage against TCCON, the authors never interpret the sign, and the one row that breaks the pattern (+0.32 ppm, MEaSUREs OCO-2 Prior, ocean) is a prior rather than a retrieval. What would actually settle presupposition 5 is a different kind of document: a study that (i) grades two or more INDEPENDENT missions or retrieval algorithms, (ii) perturbs a NAMED spectroscopic or line parameter, and (iii) prints the sign and the correlation of the resulting bias per mission. The lead — UNOPENED, and flagged as a lead rather than a finding — is Hobbs et al. (2020), "Spectroscopic uncertainty impacts on OCO-2/3 retrievals", cited in arXiv:2509.16419 Sec. 3.2; its title scopes it to one instrument family, so it may not reach (i). (ii) Leg B's generalisation beyond the flagship: ABSCO's numbers are printed, and empirical for four of the five (the weak CO2 band's 1.014 being a laboratory-to-database ratio), but that mission-specific tables break sharing across ALL missions is an inference from two documented chains (OCO-2/OCO-3 and MkIV/TCCON) plus title-level knowledge of the SEOM-IAS TROPOMI databases; GOSAT, GOSAT-2, TanSat and MicroCarb were never checked. (iii) Adversary 1's selection-policy leg — "n=1 by construction" — is STRUCK in its universal form and survives only in a narrow one. This entry had it as an ALGEBRAIC consequence of a curation policy as worded, not a bitwise or empirical count; post-batch verification establishes something stronger, that the premise does not exist as a policy at all: a merge policy selecting a single source per parameter is NOT STATED in either HITRAN2020 or HITRAN2024 anywhere in the window read — no general rule in HITRAN2024's Sec. 1 or Sec. 2 preamble, and no sentence in either document saying one source is chosen per parameter. The sentence the leg rested on is narrower even than H2O-wide: H2-16-O transition frequencies, and only the discrepant ones, resolved by a two-criterion judgment. HITRAN2020's own averaging and scaling modes confirm the policy is not universal, and nobody has counted the share. HITRAN2024 (Gordon et al., JQSRT 353 (2026) 109807, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2026.109807), which this entry had called "the single unopened source most likely to settle it" and "the one document that would restate merge policy per molecule", is now PARTIALLY READ — front matter through Sec. 2.5; about 85 kB served; CH4, O2 and Sec. 3 onward COULD NOT READ — and found to state NO SINGLE-SOURCE MERGE POLICY: per-molecule source HANDLING yes (H2O Secs. 2.1.1-2.1.3, CO2 Secs. 2.2.2-2.2.4, O3 Sec. 2.3, N2O Secs. 2.4.1-2.4.3, CO Sec. 2.5), per-molecule single-source POLICY no, general policy no. Several of those per-molecule statements are explicitly TWO-SOURCE hybrids — an ab initio or variational list scaled to a named measurement, e.g. O3 variational intensities "scaled ... to agree with the experimental data from Birk et al." by a factor of 1.0073, and N2O's Huang et al. [169] intensities "scaled to agree with the lower J values in the JPL catalogue" — which cuts directly against n=1. The silence of the unread sections about CH4 and O2 is COULD NOT READ and must not be read as absence.
Promotion requires: all five of — (a) rewording so n counts determinations that EXIST for the parameter (alternative formulation 2) with the compilation's merge mode reported as a separate class and a declared convention for scaled-ab-initio and team-assigned values, which is what takes Well-posedness to 3/3; (b) re-basing the declared frame on what the declared retrievals actually read (ABSCO/ATM18/SEOM-IAS chains) and including at least one retrieval verified to read the compilation as shipped, or else dropping the corroboration consequence and re-scoring significance on the remeasurement-ranking limb alone; (c) one actual per-parameter reference index resolved end-to-end to a primary source, which is the only thing that would move presupposition 1 off format level and which remains ENTIRELY UNDISCHARGED, neither release paper carrying any worked end-to-end trace in the windows read; (d) the census checks, now PARTIALLY DISCHARGED WITH NO KILL and to be completed — HITRAN2024 (Gordon et al., JQSRT 353 (2026) 109807, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2026.109807) read front matter through Sec. 2.5 and found to print no census, and HITRAN2020 (Gordon et al., JQSRT 277 (2022) 107949, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2021.107949) likewise, so the Rejected branch does NOT fire on either, but (d) cannot be marked satisfied on them because both reads are partial and the unread remainder includes the later molecule sections and all of Sec. 3, which is COULD NOT READ and not NOT FOUND; arXiv:2509.16419v1 (Yadav et al., 2025, "An Error Model for Evaluating the Accuracy of Satellite-Based XCO2 Products", preprint, no DOI) read IN FULL and found to print no per-parameter and no sensitivity-weighted source count; MARVEL/IUPAC Part III (Tennyson et al., "IUPAC critical evaluation of the rotational-vibrational spectra of water vapor, Part III: Energy levels and transition wavenumbers for H2(16)O", JQSRT 117 (2013) 29-58, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2012.10.002) read at PARTIAL level and found to count transitions per source rather than sources per level, with Parts I, II and IV still UNOPENED so that the plural "reports" is not yet satisfied; and "Validation of the HITRAN 2016 and GEISA 2015 line lists using ACE-FTS solar occultation observations" still COULD NOT READ after four distinct failed routes (the HAL file, the HAL landing page and hal.science for insu-02237353, all three returning the same Anubis block with error code 9e4edb5b6b850c41, and ScienceDirect PII S002240731930425X, robots_disallowed), where what a checker would accept as a read of it is any route serving the article's own body text and front matter — an institutional or university repository copy or the authors' group page being the untried candidates, with no DOI to be constructed from the locators; if any of these documents, read further, prints a sensitivity-weighted or per-parameter source count, the entry goes to Rejected as a disguised known instead; and (e) resolving the determination-level question ABSCO leaves SILENT rather than negative — whether Devi et al. (2016) and the Payne (2021)/Drouin et al. (2017) O2 work are among HITRAN2020's adopted sources for the 1.61 µm CO2 and 0.76 µm O2 bands, and whether the 1.014 target (NIST, Polyansky et al. 2015) is HITRAN's own intensity lineage for that band — the routes to try being the HITRAN2020 CO2 section (Gordon et al., JQSRT 277 (2022) 107949, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2021.107949) and P1's own per-band tables, already in this entry, which print ABSCO 5.1's 30013-band intensities as "data from Ref. [78] rescaled by 1.4%", i.e. 1.014 may be a rescaling of a SHARED determination; if it resolves that way, LEG B INVERTS and the common-mode motivation is restored rather than defeated.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): the two reads this entry previously put first have since been made in part — HITRAN2024 through Sec. 2.5 and MARVEL/IUPAC Part III — and neither converted this entry's status, so the first step is now to resolve the ABSCO-versus-HITRAN determination-level overlap (promotion condition (e)), since that is the one check that could INVERT Leg B; then resolve a single parameter's reference index end-to-end for one dominant transition to establish whether the chain terminates in a primary source at all; and reach the later sections of HITRAN2024 by some route other than hitran.org/media/refs/HITRAN-2024.pdf, which serves only about 85 kB of text and truncates partway into Sec. 2.5. Do not take any of these steps here.
