## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What the pass was and what it was sent to read.** Five fresh-context checkers ran, each re-reading the load-bearing sources first-hand and blind to the reviewers' reasoning. Checker 1 was sent to the ABSCO v5.2 documentation for the five scale factors, their page range and the "reads no HITRAN-frame parameter" inference. Checker 2 was sent to arXiv:2509.16419, the document this entry had nominated as most likely to settle presupposition 5. Checker 3 was sent to HITRAN2024 and HITRAN2020 for the merge policy, the select/average/scale quotations, the 1.1217 factor, and whether either edition prints an aggregate source count. Checker 4 was sent to P1 (PriSpecTemp) and P2 (Fleurbaey et al.) for the transitions-per-source direction, the independence rule and the "only source" sentence. Checker 5 was sent to the MARVEL/IUPAC water task-group reports and the ACE-FTS HITRAN2016/GEISA2015 validation paper under promotion condition (d). One checker returned a flat NO — the only outright "the claim does not hold" of the batch — on the merge-policy claim. The verdict did NOT move: no census was found anywhere, so condition (d)'s Rejected branch did not fire, and Provisional stands for exactly the reasons it stood before, with Leg A untouched.

**The headline defect: a misquotation cut mid-clause.** The single most important correction of this batch lands on the HITRAN2020 selection-policy quotation this entry carried as "we chose the source that has the lowest uncertainty associated with it". The words are verbatim, but the cut is a misquotation by this ledger's own standard, because the surrounding clause changes its force in three ways at once. It drops the opening "In such cases,", which scopes the sentence to DISCREPANCY RESOLUTION; it drops the preceding "We also detected a small number of discrepancies in the transition frequencies", which scopes it to a minority of one parameter class of one molecule; and it drops the trailing "and also considered the type of experiment used to derive the value in the empirical line list", which makes it a TWO-CRITERION JUDGMENT rather than a selection rule. The entry's P3 paragraph now carries the full printed passage with the ellipsis marked, and says there that the cut was the defect. No one-source-per-parameter algebra can be run off the sentence as printed.

**What was struck.** Adversary 1's selection-policy leg is struck in its universal form, in the attack-5 row and in vulnerability (iii), not merely noted below them. A merge policy selecting a single source per parameter is NOT STATED AT ALL, as a policy, in HITRAN2020 or HITRAN2024, anywhere in the window read: no general rule in HITRAN2024's Sec. 1 or Sec. 2 preamble, and no sentence in either document saying one source is chosen per parameter. What survives is only the discrepancy-resolution procedure quoted above, for H2-16-O transition frequencies and only the discrepant ones — narrower even than H2O-wide. It cannot carry "the headline share measures curation policy rather than the world", because no stated policy of the required generality exists to do the measuring. This entry's existing hedge (algebraic, H2O-only, cut against by averaging and scaling) is CONFIRMED and has been strengthened on the two points the checker named. Also struck: the nomination of arXiv:2509.16419 as the source most likely to settle presupposition 5, refuted on three grounds verifiable in the document now that it has been read in full; the broad form of Leg B's inference, that the shared compilation is not the dependency the retrievals actually have, and with it the why-it-matters wording "reads no COMPILATION-frame parameter for O2 or CO2", since ABSCO reads the Devi et al. (2016) database and ATM18 as shipped under one scalar each; "intensity" from "empirical intensity scale factors"; and "from atmospheric references" as a universal.

**What was narrowed.** The ABSCO page citation goes from "pp. 5-8" to "pp. 6-8", page 5 carrying only "1 Introduction" and "1.1 Scope and Background". Leg B now says "band-wide cross-section scale factors", because the document's own heading is "Scaling of absorption cross-sections" and Table 1's row is "ABSCO scaling"; only 1.014 is an intensity ratio in the document's words, 1.0048 was fit to retrieved surface-pressure biases "on the order of several hPa", and only two of the five (1.014, 0.981) are in the shipped tables at all. "From atmospheric references" is narrowed to 1.0048, 0.994, 0.9875 and 0.981: the weak band's 1.014 "represents a ratio between line intensities in the Devi et al. (2016) database and reference intensity measurements from our NIST ABSCO team members, described in Polyansky et al. (2015)" — a LABORATORY-to-database ratio, with TCCON used only to test it afterwards — and the strong band's v5.2 table is anchored to "the ab initio intensities reported in Zak (2016)" via Fleurbaey (2020). The atmospheric-versus-laboratory contrast is this entry's own, not the document's, and is labelled as such. The "no HITRAN-frame parameter for O2 or CO2" half is HELD NARROWLY: HITRAN appears in the document only as the CH4 line list, as netCDF gas/isotope indices, as superseded v5.1 H2O ("HITRAN 2012", Table 2) and in one reference entry, and nowhere in the v5.2 O2 or CO2 parameter rows (O2 = Payne 2021 with the Drouin et al. 2017 methodology; weak CO2 = Devi 2016b; strong CO2 = "Drouin (not yet published)"; H2O = Toon 2018). Presupposition 4 is narrowed to one compilation only. Vulnerability (ii) now records that four of the five ABSCO numbers are empirical and one is a laboratory ratio. The provenance note on arXiv:2509.16419 is narrowed: the item was returned four times across two adversaries' sweeps and opened by nobody, and those four returns are recorded as TITLE-LEVEL MATCHES on "error model for satellite XCO2 products", NOT as independent corroboration — counting unopened returns as convergence is exactly the failure mode this narrowing exists to prevent. The MARVEL finding is narrowed to Part III (H2-16-O) only, so the plural "reports" in condition (d) is not yet satisfied in full.

**What was re-sourced, and the citation corrections.** HITRAN2024 is no longer carried as the bare filename "HITRAN-2024.pdf at hitran.org/media/refs/" but as Gordon, Rothman, Hargreaves, Gomez, Bertin, Hill, Kochanov, Tan, Wcislo, Makhnev et al., "The HITRAN2024 molecular spectroscopic database", JQSRT 353 (2026) 109807, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2026.109807. HITRAN2020 gains DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2021.107949, whose string carries 2021 although the volume year is 2022. The ABSCO source is now cited by its printed front matter — ABSCO User Guide, Payne and Oyafuso, Jet Propulsion Laboratory/Caltech, revision date 25 February 2022 — since it carries no printed version number and no DOI, "v5.2" living in the filename and in the body's scope sentence. arXiv:2509.16419 is carried as a v1 stat.AP preprint submitted 2025-09-19 with eleven authors, first author Yadav, and explicitly with NO DOI and no journal reference. MARVEL/IUPAC Part III is pinned to Tennyson et al., JQSRT 117 (2013) 29-58, DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2012.10.002. P1 gains its publisher and length; P2 gains its full printed title and Hélène Fleurbaey's forename. For the ACE-FTS paper no citation was invented: only two locators were obtained, from URLs rather than front matter, and they are labelled as locators.

**What was confirmed, with the quotations that settled it.** The five ABSCO figures are all printed, in the bands this entry assigns, and in the stated order for the weak band (1.014 baked in, then 0.994). Against P1, the "transitions per SOURCE, inverse of sources per transition" leg is confirmed and now anchored on printed column headings: every summary table is keyed "Reference"/"Ref." with "Number of transitions" as an attribute of the work, no independence rule appears anywhere, and "weighted" occurs only as other people's "global weighted fits of spectroscopic parameters" and as plotted "weighted averages". Against P2 the leg is confirmed too — intensities only, 20013 ← 00001 near 2.06 µm, 12C16O2, with line-shape parameters fitted but not reported — and this entry's gloss ("announces n=1 ... as motivation for a remeasurement") was already faithful to the hedged form, so the P2 problem was a quotation defect and not a reasoning defect. The three HITRAN2020 source-handling modes are all confirmed with locations (select Sec. 2.1.1, average Sec. 2.1.6, scale Sec. 2.2.4), and the attribution of 1.1217 to Sec. 2.2.4 and to the 00031-00001 band is exact. Neither HITRAN edition prints any aggregate count or distribution of sources per parameter in the windows read: both DEFINE the reference-index mechanism that would make the count computable and neither PERFORMS it. On the MARVEL leg nothing was struck: Part III counts measured TRANSITIONS PER SOURCE, settled by the Table 2 caption "A = number of assigned transitions in the original data source, V = number of transitions validated in this study", with per-level numbers appearing only as the aggregate "These transitions give rise to 18 486 validated energy levels" and as levels per vibrational band origin in Table 6. It does not count sources per level, which is the direction this candidate's quantity runs — the same inversion already charged against P1, so the read is consistent with this entry's reasoning rather than a correction to it, and no disguised known was found.

**Number hygiene, and a new illustration for presupposition 2.** The factor 1.1217 is now tagged HITRAN2020 Sec. 2.2.4 and FLAGGED SUPERSEDED: HITRAN2024 Sec. 2.2.2 rescaled the same 00031-00001 band by 0.99314 (served once by the checker and not re-verified at a clause junction). Against the strict reading of presupposition 2 — the "independent determination" definability contest — the HITRAN2024 MARVEL figure has been added beside the 1.1217 hybrid: "a MARVEL energy level analysis has been carried out using 91 published sources for 14N2 16O" (Sec. 2.4.1) is a printed case where R-strict scores n=1 while 91 laboratories supplied the data, and it concerns a quantity, energy levels, that carries no reference index at all. That number is a counter-illustration, not a census: its numerator is published sources feeding one isotopologue's energy-level fit, and it must not be allowed to drift into the candidate's quantity.

**A factual correction to this entry's history.** This entry twice treated the flagship's resetting of band scales as settled practice. The document dates it to v5.2 / L2 v11 and prints the contrary for the version before: "For version 10, the scaling factors applied within the Level 2 algorithm to ABSCO v5.1 tables were 1.000 and 1.004 for the weak and strong bands, respectively. However, for that version, no effort was made to account for the overall persistent bias of retrieved XCO2 through spectroscopic adjustments." The significance-consequence paragraph now carries that sentence. Noted there and in Leg B, undercutting Leg B's inference though not its narrow wording: a HITRAN line list IS shipped into both CO2 windows for CH4 — "CH4 tables using the HITRAN line list are now also available; they are computed over both CO2 spectral windows" — hedged, because "now also available" states availability and operational use in L2 v11 was not established.

**Read level reached for each source, with COULD NOT READ kept distinct from NOT FOUND.** ABSCO User Guide: PARTIAL, via the fetch summariser over a cached PDF in three passes, with Sec. 2.1 reconstructed from 47 consecutive numbered fragments and the cell text of Tables 1 and 2 PARAPHRASE only, the summariser having refused verbatim table reproduction; the PDF was never read raw. arXiv:2509.16419: FULL TEXT, in four passes, nothing COULD NOT READ. HITRAN2024: PARTIAL — front matter and author list, Sec. 1, the Sec. 2 preamble, Secs. 2.1-2.1.3 (H2O), Sec. 2.2 with 2.2.2-2.2.5 (CO2), Sec. 2.3 (O3), Secs. 2.4-2.4.4 (N2O) and the opening of Sec. 2.5 (CO); CH4, O2, NO, SO2, NH3, HNO3, OH, HF, HCl, every molecule section after CO, Sec. 3 onward including the cross-sections section, and the entire reference list are COULD NOT READ by the only route that served the document. HITRAN2020: PARTIAL — front matter, the Sec. 2 preamble, Sec. 2.1 with 2.1.1 and 2.1.6, Sec. 2.2 with 2.2.4, breaking off partway through Sec. 2.2.9; the remainder of Sec. 2.2, all molecule sections after CO2 and Secs. 3-7 with appendices are COULD NOT READ. P1: PARTIAL — complete front matter, the caption and full column headings of all seven tables, and targeted passages, but NOT a continuous read of all 24 pages, so the ABSENT findings on the n<=1 share and on the independence rule rest on a targeted query plus a complete inventory of the seven tables rather than on a line-by-line read. P2: PARTIAL — Introduction, front matter and scope statements; the experimental, fitting and results sections were not read continuously. MARVEL/IUPAC Part III: PARTIAL — front matter, the Table 2 caption and column definitions, sample rows, the aggregate level count, the Table 6 description, the admission criterion and the reweighting passages, but not the full body, not the full Table 2 and not the supplementary material; Parts I, II and IV were NOT OPENED, and their silence is not evidence. The ACE-FTS validation paper is a flat COULD NOT READ and its sub-claims are COULD NOT CHECK: not one word of its text, abstract or front matter was served, so nothing about it is cleared and nothing about it is impeached.

**Routes that failed, recorded so a later pass does not repeat them.** For the ACE-FTS paper, four distinct routes failed: the HAL file for insu-02237353, the HAL landing page, and hal.science/insu-02237353/document all returned the same Anubis bot-protection page with error code 9e4edb5b6b850c41, and ScienceDirect PII S002240731930425X failed at the site with robots_disallowed, which is the route this entry itself had suggested and which does not work from here; doi.org was never tried because no verified DOI was obtained and none was constructed. For HITRAN2020, the guessed path hitran.org/media/refs/HITRAN2020.pdf returned a site client_error with nothing retrieved; the correct filename carries a hyphen, HITRAN-2020.pdf. For HITRAN2024, hitran.org/media/refs/HITRAN-2024.pdf serves only 85,320 characters of extracted text and truncates partway into Sec. 2.5, so the later sections need a different route — the ScienceDirect article page for DOI 10.1016/j.jqsrt.2026.109807, or an institutional repository copy, neither tried. For P1, a direct curl to the PTB file store failed with a 403 CONNECT tunnel rejection at the agent proxy while the fetch tool reached the same URL on the next call, a tool-scoped failure, and the proxy was neither probed nor reconfigured. Internal content refusals, distinct from route failures: the summariser declined verbatim reproduction of ABSCO Tables 1 and 2 and of P2's Introduction on first request, and its roughly 125-character verbatim cap forced several passages into labelled reconstructions from ordered consecutive fragments.

**What the pass did NOT reach.** It did not resolve any per-parameter reference index end-to-end to a primary source, in either release paper. It did not establish whether Devi et al. (2016), Payne (2021) or Drouin's unpublished fit are among HITRAN2020's adopted sources for the same bands, which is the determination-level fact Leg B needs and which the ABSCO document leaves SILENT rather than negative. It did not open Hobbs et al. (2020), MARVEL/IUPAC Parts I, II and IV, the ACE-FTS paper, HITRAN2024's CH4, O2 and Sec. 3 onward, HITRAN2020 beyond Sec. 2.2.9, or any of ABSCO's own cited sources. It did not check GOSAT, GOSAT-2, TanSat or MicroCarb, so vulnerability (ii) is exactly where it was. It did not verify ABSCO's or P2's table cells verbatim. And it did not establish operational use of the HITRAN CH4 tables in OCO-2 L2 v11: published is not performed.

**Whether the verdict moved, and why not.** It did not. The entry remains Provisional. No census or per-parameter source count was found in any document read, so condition (d)'s Rejected branch did not fire and the disguised-known kill is not available; nothing read raises Well-posedness off 2/3, since no reference index was resolved to a primary source and the hybrid and team-assigned values still have no defined n — indeed presupposition 1 is slightly DENTED by two new hedges, the Einstein-A coefficients "usually" sharing the intensities' source and uncertainty "code 0 in Table 2" possibly bearing two meanings. What moved is the internal weighting of the grounds: Leg B is reduced to one parameter, one scalar per band, one of four anchors laboratory and an unresolved determination-level overlap, so it is no longer clearly the strongest objection, and Leg A — decisive, self-standing and untouched by this pass — now carries the verdict in the entry's own prose.

**What the pass did to the promotion conditions.** The single "Promotion requires" line now carries five conditions rather than four. Condition (a) is unchanged. Condition (b) is unchanged in substance, though Leg B's reduction makes its second branch (dropping the corroboration consequence) the likelier route. Condition (c) is recorded as ENTIRELY UNDISCHARGED and slightly harder, since neither release paper contains a worked end-to-end trace. Condition (d) is recorded as PARTIALLY DISCHARGED WITH NO KILL, source by source, with each read level and each failed route named, and with what a checker would accept as a read of the ACE-FTS paper stated; it is explicitly not marked satisfied, because the HITRAN reads are partial and the unread remainder includes later molecule sections and all of Sec. 3, and because MARVEL Parts I, II and IV are unopened. Condition (e) is NEW and is the decisive residue of the ABSCO check converted out of the findings into a condition: resolve whether ABSCO's named sources are the same determinations HITRAN adopts for the same bands, with the HITRAN2020 CO2 section and P1's per-band tables named as routes, and with the explicit note that if it resolves that way Leg B inverts and the common-mode motivation is restored rather than defeated.

**What the pass did to the novelty grade.** Novelty stays MEDIUM, with a close neighbour, capped rather than confirmed. Attack 2 (Disguise) is marginally RELIEVED rather than strengthened: the one newly opened on-point title, MARVEL/IUPAC Part III, tabulates the same inverted quantity already charged against P1. The unopened-title residue shrinks — one part of one series read, one preprint read in full and found silent, one release paper read in part — but it does not clear, and the grade cannot rise while P1 and P2 remain genuinely close and while HITRAN2024's later sections, MARVEL Parts I, II and IV and the ACE-FTS paper stay unread. The grade cannot fall to Low either: no opened source names the candidate's number, and the pass found nothing that does.

ID: UQ-20261022-16
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Medium novelty with a close neighbour that already builds the instrument (Awad et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.27268, no DOI printed), and five sources that could in principle carry the quantity still unopened by anybody; nothing Unresolved on any attack from either adversary.
Domain(s): AI architecture — the tokenizer/vocabulary layer and the inference-time sampling layer (model design + serving). Neighbours searched: NLP decoding/sampling theory, software-engineering dependability (the glitch-token line at FSE/ASE/AAAI), on-device inference efficiency, tokenization theory/canonicality, LLM security; adversaries added classifier-geometry, RL invalid-action masking, LLM billing/tokenization-multiplicity, Chinese, Japanese.
Source method: anomaly mining.

Question (canonical): For a pre-declared set of shipped open-weight LLM releases, a pre-declared prompt set, and a detector-defined set U of under-trained vocabulary items (reported SEPARATELY from the set R of tokenizer-unreachable items, since the two sets and their hazard meanings differ), under free self-conditioned generation: (i) what is the mean and upper-tail step-wise pre-truncation probability mass on U and on R; (ii) at what share of generation steps does at least one member of U (resp. R) remain inside the sampling support after the release's own declared default truncation rule is applied — with the arm defined per artifact from `generation_config.json`/model card, and an explicitly declared substitute arm recorded as such for releases that ship none; and (iii) what is the realised emission rate of members of U and of R per 10^6 generated tokens, against a null of a vocabulary subset matched on unigram frequency profile?
Reformulation note: this is Gate 1 version B, the single permitted reformulation, used for well-posedness only and widening no scope. Version A (recorded, superseded) fused U with R, left the shipped-default arm undefined for releases that ship none, and stated limb (iii) with no null. Both adversaries restated version B independently and both restatements match it.

Alternative formulations: (1) Are glitch tokens a live inference-side hazard or only an input-side one — how often do shipped default sampling configurations actually let an under-trained token through into output? (2) What is the measured leakage rate of the untrained region of an LLM's output vocabulary under the decoding settings the model is actually served with? (3) Version A as intaken: "In ordinary, non-adversarial generation from shipped open-weight LLMs, how much step-wise probability mass does the model place on its own under-trained or unreachable vocabulary items, what share of that mass survives the truncation sampler at the release's own default decoding settings, and what is the resulting emission rate per million generated tokens?"

Motivating gap: the detection literature establishes that shipped tokenizers carry items the model was effectively never trained on, and tests them by FEEDING THEM IN. STATED PRECISELY, because the strong form of this gap claim is refutable from one sentence of Land & Bartolo's Sec. 2.3: that literature DOES read the model's next-token output distribution — its own noun for the measured quantity is "output probability", and it prints "The rate of successful verification (p < 0.01)" over vocabulary items in its Fig. 3 caption — so the gap is NOT "nothing on the output side", it is the absence of any probability conditioned on a sampling truncation rule and of any rate at which such a token is emitted in ordinary generation. That symmetric arm — whether the model puts mass on them unprompted, and whether the shipped truncation rule already removes it — is measured by none of the eleven sources now opened at first hand (nine across the record and the two adversaries; GlitchCleaner and Sampling Adapters added by the post-batch verification pass), and the one 2026 paper that builds exactly the per-step support-membership instrument it needs points it at the opposite end of the distribution (legitimate human words being cut off). Intake's gap claim was title-level only; Gate 2 re-established it from full-text reads and narrowed it; the post-batch verification pass of 2026-10-22 re-read every load-bearing prior and narrowed it again.

Presuppositions:
- P1 shipped releases carry a non-trivial set U — ESTABLISHED at first hand three times over. Land, Sander & Bartolo, Max, 2024, "Fishing for Magikarp: Automatically Detecting Under-trained Tokens in Large Language Models", arXiv:2405.05417 = ACL Anthology 2024.emnlp-main.649, no DOI string seen and none asserted (record, full text): verified tokens "typically ranges between 5-50% of tested candidate tokens, corresponding to 0.1-1% of the total vocabulary size" — two denominators in one sentence, which must travel with their numbers — and the hedged Sec. 5 restatement is the one to prefer, "typically around 0.1-1% of the vocabulary consisting of severely under-trained tokens"; Table 1 with 24 open-weight rows, its #Confirmed column printed as confirmed/TESTED, not over vocabulary. The 0.1-1% numerator is tokens in the top 2% of the unembedding-geometry ranking that survive prompt verification, and it EXCLUDES by construction the paper's separate categories — "Unreachable: When no input string can result in the token id", "Partial UTF-8 sequences", "Special tokens" — and everything outside that 2% cut, the paper's indicators having "no definitive threshold". GlitchMiner — Wu, Zihui et al., 2026, "GlitchMiner: Mining Glitch Tokens in Large Language Models via Gradient-based Discrete Optimization", DOI 10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40693, Proc. AAAI 40(40):33998-34005, arXiv:2410.15052 preprint first posted 2024 (adversary 1, full text): Detected@2000 of 1839 for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 302 for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, a metric with no denominator at all ("Detected@N = Number of true glitch tokens among the top N predictions"). GlitchProber — Zhang, Zhibo et al., 2024, "GlitchProber: Advancing Effective Detection and Mitigation of Glitch Tokens in Large Language Models", DOI 10.1145/3691620.3695060, ASE '24, arXiv:2408.04905 (adversary 2, full text): a whole detect-plus-mitigate pipeline run on released artifacts, censusing "all the 32,000 tokens of the Llama2 model" and identifying "6,425 glitch tokens from the entire vocabulary". INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY FLAG carried forward unsmoothed: Land & Bartolo give three mutually inconsistent OLMo counts (Table 1 178/993; Sec. 2.4 "191 out of 49,575" and 175/993), so no single OLMo figure is load-bearing.
- P2 "under-trained" is detector-relative — CONTESTED, definitional, and converted by the question into per-detector reporting with >=2 detectors required. Confirmed at first hand that the detector families disagree by construction: Land & Bartolo's INDICATOR stage is weights-and-tokenizer-space only (cosine distance of unembedding rows to the mean unused-token embedding with the constant component removed, no forward passes) — narrowed after verification, because their separate VERIFICATION stage does run forward passes and reads what the paper itself calls an "output probability", so "weights-only" is true of the indicator and not of the pipeline; Li, Yuxi et al. 2024, "Glitch Tokens in Large Language Models: Categorization Taxonomy and Effective Detection", arXiv:2404.09894v3, FSE 2024 Research Papers track (no DOI established, and none asserted) define a glitch token behaviourally by failure of three proxy tasks; GlitchProber uses PCA+SVM over hooked activations; GlitchMiner uses gradient-guided search with entropy as the uncertainty measure.
- P3 releases declare a default decoding rule machine-readably — NOW EVIDENCED BY OPENED INSTANCES, and the news is a case-split, not a pass. Adversary 1 opened two `generation_config.json` files: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ships `do_sample: true, temperature: 0.7, top_p: 0.8, top_k: 20, repetition_penalty: 1.05`; Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 ships bos/eos and transformers_version only, i.e. NO declared sampler at all. Adversary 2 opened a third (openPangu-R-72B-2512): `do_sample: true, temperature: 1.0, top_p: 0.8, top_n_sigma: 0.05, top_k: -1` — a spread-dependent truncation rule outside the record's own arm list, with top_k explicitly disabled. Kind-level check is three instances where the standing rule wants two or three, so it holds; nine further real instances were returned and not opened. The clause is a reported quantity under the canonical wording's substitute-arm clause, so attack 4 does not reach it.
- P4 emitting such a token is behaviourally consequential — CONTESTED and deliberately not assumed; the question measures the consequence and a harmless emission is still an answer. The only consequence evidence opened anywhere is input-side (Li et al. Table 3 symptom distribution on tokens fed in).
- P5 MEASURAND EXEMPTION DECLARED. That this hazard rate is unquantified is the question's measurand; an attack that the rate may be zero is a prediction about the answer. Both adversaries accepted the exemption as declared rather than graded around.
- NEW, from both adversaries independently, not in the record: C5/C6 — the limb (iii) null is weakly identifying for R. If R is "never produced as a result of tokenizing text", then every member of R has unigram frequency identically zero in any tokenized corpus, so a frequency-matched control must be drawn from the same zero-frequency stratum U is mined from. Neither adversary could source this to anything it opened; both labelled it their own reasoning; both graded it short of a kill.

What would count as an answer: a per-model table over the pre-declared prompt set and the pre-declared per-detector sets U and R giving (i) mean and upper-tail step-wise pre-truncation mass; (ii) share of steps with any member inside the post-truncation support under the artifact's declared default rule; (iii) emission rate per 10^6 generated tokens against the frequency-matched null; plus sensitivity arms over >=2 detectors of different kinds and >=2 sampler settings. Decision rule: post-truncation support membership at or below round-off across models and settings establishes the pathology as input-side only; a non-zero rate names the models and prompt classes where it is live and implies the logit-mask fix. NOT an answer: a re-run of detection with no decoding stage; an adversarial-input study; a count of glitch tokens occurring in an INPUT corpus.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs PRIOR 1. Prior 1's numerator = word-context pairs all of whose constituent tokens survive the filter; denominator = 1,000 word-context pairs for the aggregate WCS, and 100 target words per model for the 22-57% erased figure — two different denominators, which must travel with their numbers. Candidate's numerator = generation steps at which >=1 member of U or R lies inside the post-truncation support, and emitted members of U per 10^6 GENERATED tokens. Prior 1's 100-item word list is drawn from the 10k-40k frequency band of the Google Web Trillion Word Corpus and dictionary-validated against the Moby Word Lists, and by construction contains no under-trained, unreachable or special-token artifact — LABELLED PRECISELY, after verification, as CONSTRUCTIVE EXCLUSION PLUS SILENCE AND NOT AS A TESTED NEGATIVE: the paper's only word filter removes "URLs, OCR errors, and technical metadata", it states no exclusion rule on training status, and the strings "under-trained", "undertrained", "glitch", "unused token", "SolidGoldMagikarp" and "Land" are ALL ABSENT from its full text, footnotes and bibliography, so it never speaks of such items and does not cite Land & Bartolo. The entry draws the exclusion as ITS OWN ENTAILMENT of the construction and does not attribute it to any scope statement of the paper's; in particular the purpose clause "ensuring that the WCS measures the reachability of legitimate human expressions" is governed by the CONTEXT MAPPING and speaks of expressions, not of vocabulary items, so it is not cited here as a word-list exclusion. It never measures mass, by its own disclaimer, printed whole: "Because the WCS focuses strictly on the total elimination of linguistic paths it does not account for this soft probabilistic erosion." And its steps are prefix-forced, so no self-conditioned emission rate can be read off it. NO NOVELTY IS CLAIMED HERE FOR AUDITING AT SHIPPED OR DOCUMENTED DEFAULT DECODING SETTINGS: that is Prior 1's headline Table 2, sourced from vendor model cards and HF generation configs for six models (with two rows near-defaults rather than defaults — Llama and DeepSeek at T=0.7, "the nearest evaluated temperature to the documented recommendations", against documented T=0.6 — and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 omitted for want of a single documented Top-p). The three axes that genuinely run opposite are endpoint (membership vs mass), population (dictionary mid-frequency words vs under-trained and unreachable items) and operating condition (forced path vs free self-conditioned generation) — not the decoding settings. The candidate is the same instrument pointed at the opposite tail with a mass endpoint added — a real difference in estimand and simultaneously the largest single discount on this entry's novelty. The prior's own Sec. 6.1 concedes the gap and even predicts its direction, "Consequently, our empirical results must be interpreted as a conservative lower bound on the true scale of word erosion", which is the strongest novelty warrant this source gives the candidate.
- vs PRIOR 2. Numerator = tokens failing the <1% test; denominator = tested candidate tokens (Table 1 prints #Confirmed as confirmed/tested) and, in a separate figure, total vocabulary. The candidate INHERITS this set definition as one detector — and Land & Bartolo 2024 is the obvious PRIOR-ART CITATION for the candidate's DEFINITION of its token class, including the exclusions that definition carries ("Unreachable: When no input string can result in the token id"; "Partial UTF-8 sequences ... can not be converted to a string by itself"; "Special tokens"), which the candidate must adopt or explicitly reject. NOTHING IN THIS ENTRY CLAIMS THAT NOBODY HAS COUNTED GLITCH TOKENS PER VOCABULARY: Land & Bartolo measured exactly that across 24 models, and that framing is struck wherever it could be read into this entry. What the candidate changes is the denominator entirely (steps and generated tokens). Its probability measurement is NOT a single p(t | prompt containing t): it is the maximum over three generated positions and then the maximum again over all three prompts, a max-of-maxes over nine positions, under crafted prompts (two repetition, one definition) each containing the token, and it is silent in both directions on unprompted mass. The same holds of GlitchMiner and GlitchProber, both opened by adversaries and both re-opened at FULL TEXT rather than abstract level by the verification pass: GlitchMiner prints denominator-free Detected@1000 and Detected@2000 counts ("Detected@N = Number of true glitch tokens among the top N predictions") and contains no greedy, temperature, sampling, max_new_tokens, generation_config, top-k or top-p setting at all, leaving its decoding strategy unstated; GlitchProber sets "we set the temperature to 0 to eliminate randomness and ensure consistency in the model's responses" with "All other configurations are default", and mitigates by rescaling MLP activations — Sec. 4.2.1, "Note that we only adjust the activation values of the MLP module and not the attention patterns", with the hedged companion sentence that is the one to quote, "By only adjusting MLP activation values, we aim to fix glitch tokens without introducing additional noise" — never by masking at the sampling step. These are vocabulary-item denominators; the gap to the candidate's step and generated-token denominators is a genuine granularity gap, not a framing difference. The near-miss number to guard against is GlitchProber's "6,425 glitch tokens" from "all the 32,000 tokens of the Llama2 model": a vocabulary-membership count that misses all of generation and counts the never-sampled tail at weight 1, exactly like a token the model emits constantly. Any percentage derived from it is derived arithmetic and not a figure that paper prints.
- vs PRIOR 3. PERFORMED AND NOT PUBLISHED, which is the finding about Prior 3 and the reason it does not demote the grade: it runs the nearest thing to limb (i) and prints no number under that quantity's own name. NARROWED BY THE VERIFICATION PASS, and this is the honest form. The core survives: no row, column, caption or sentence in the body text, in any table, or in any figure caption is labelled log Z, log Z-hat, canonicality rate or any percentage of noncanonical token sequences, and Figure 4 — "Log-canonicality rate vs. (tokenized) length, including 95% confidence intervals, for each model." — is the quantity's ONLY presentation, its caption carrying no number and the surrounding prose giving only shape ("for the Llama methods, the log-canonicality rate stabilizes after 256 tokens, but for the GPT-2 models, it continues decreasing"). BUT THE ENTRY'S FORMER WORDING, "appears only as a plotted curve in Fig. 4 against maximum length with no numeric value in the text", was right about LABELLING and understated about RECOVERABILITY, and is replaced: the paper's own prose licenses a subtraction — "For the global method, the change in the log-loss is independent of the dataset because log Z-hat is independent of the dataset" — Figure 3 prints both the Baseline and the Global columns, and differencing them yields a per-model scalar log2(Z-hat) of roughly 0.8-2.0 bits/string, agreeing across PTB and WikiText to within 0.1 bits in all six rows. THAT SUBTRACTION IS THE CHECKER'S OWN ARITHMETIC OVER SUMMARISER-RECONSTRUCTED FIGURE 3 CELLS AND IS NOT A FIGURE THE PAPER PRINTS; and the authors' own caveat runs against it, printed whole, "Thus, for practical reasons, our experiments with GPT-2 will be based on a limit length of 1024, but bear in mind that this means that the actual log-canonicality rate is likely to be much smaller, meaning the reduction in log-loss for GPT-2 is larger than Fig. 3 indicates." — so for GPT-2 the recoverable value OVERSTATES Z-hat. The quantity is in any case a property of the canonicalized l rather than of the shipped model under its own sampler. STRUCK AS A DEFECTIVE LEG: the entry formerly said "the only printed instance anywhere in the paper is one WikiText string in App. A where 'the conditional probability of the canonical tokenization is only 2.7%, and it is ranked 4th'". That 2.7% is a DIFFERENT ESTIMAND and not an instance of the rate — a per-string illustration the paper introduces as "an interesting example", conditional on one WikiText character string under GPT-2, renormalised over a "(partially enumerated)" set of that string's encodings, and a canonical-encoding share rather than a log-rate. The surviving form: the only percentage printed anywhere in the paper is that per-string illustration, which does not estimate the canonicality rate. BECAUSE THE SCALAR IS RECOVERABLE, this entry's grade no longer rests on the number being unprinted; it rests on the regime gap, which is the durable one — no sampler, no generation_config, no truncation rule anywhere in Prior 3, its only sample-space restriction being the 1024-token length cap. Emitting a member of R does render a string non-canonical, so R-emission is a subset of Prior 3's event class — a subset Prior 3 neither isolates nor counts, while most of its own numerator is legitimate words split the wrong way.

Novelty confidence: Medium, and the post-batch verification pass of 2026-10-22 left the grade exactly where it was. 29 distinct queries across the candidate's own words, the method-owning field's words, four neighbouring literatures and three non-English or historical vocabularies; eleven sources now opened at first hand, seven of them in full. THE RECORD CANNOT NAME THE CANDIDATE'S NUMBER ANYWHERE, and the grade rests on that rather than on an absence of search: for limb (ii) the nearest printed figures are Prior 1's WCS 0.059-0.230 over 1,000 word-context pairs, a different numerator class on a different denominator; for limb (i) Prior 3 prints no value under the quantity's own name, presents it only in Fig. 4, and leaves a per-model scalar recoverable by one subtraction from Fig. 3, all of it on sequences under a modified distribution with no sampler; for limb (iii) nothing was found by any agent. The printed figures that look like an answer and are not, each now checked at first hand. (a) Li et al. Table 5's glitch-token ratios of 3.39% (Alpaca-52k), 2.09% (ShareGPT-52k), 2.22% (ShareGPT-90k) — NARROWED, because all three are the AVERAGE ROW over seven model/tokenizer rows and not any single model's figure, the per-row Alpaca-52k spread running 1.26% (Text-Davinci-003, 55,009 of 4,366,838) to 6.68% (Vicuna-13b, 324,879 of 4,861,603), so the 55,009/4,366,838 pair this entry formerly juxtaposed with 3.39% is in fact the LOWEST of the seven rows and is not the arithmetic behind the leading figure — are occurrences in a pre-existing text corpus the paper tokenized, not tokens a model emitted. The first-hand argument for that, which replaces this entry's former "an INPUT corpus of human and assistant text" framing (a characterisation Sec. 3.2 does not make, which imported outside knowledge and conceded that part of the denominator is itself model-generated text): the denominator is corpus-tokens-under-THAT-ROW'S-TOKENIZER and demonstrably moves with the tokenizer on a fixed dataset — Alpaca-52k is 4,366,838 tokens under r50k_base against 4,861,603 under LlamaTokenizer — and NO Table 5 row couples an emitting model to its own glitch set under any stated decoding condition. "Glitch Ratio" is a bare column header the paper never defines in prose, the division identity is the checker's own arithmetic rather than the paper's formula, and the paper states no uncertainty on the three figures; its caption is printed misspelled, "Occurance of Glitch Tokens in Commonly Used Datasets". (b) Land & Bartolo's 0.1-1%, which is an UNWEIGHTED VOCABULARY COUNT SHARE — numerator = tokens in the top 2% of the unembedding-geometry ranking that survive prompt verification, with Unreachable, Partial UTF-8 sequences and Special tokens held in SEPARATE categories and therefore excluded; denominator = the total vocabulary — and which fails the overlap test in BOTH directions against every limb of the candidate: it misses everything decoding-time, and it includes statically under-trained tokens that carry negligible probability at every step. (c) Sampling Adapters' footnote 11, whose 0.001 tail mass is STIPULATED inside a clause opening "To see why, consider a simple example:", and its Figure 7, which is a percentage OF TOKENS ("percentage of tokens to which the adapter assigns non-zero probability") and not of mass — a sampler can zero 99% of the vocabulary while removing 0.1% of the mass, so coverage is silent on limb (i) rather than weak evidence for it. Not High, because Prior 1 is a 2026 paper that already performs per-step truncation-support auditing at documented shipped defaults on the same class of models, and that defaults arm is its headline Table 2, so the candidate is a redirection of a published method; and because five returns that could in principle carry the quantity are still unopened, down from eight after this pass closed three of them. Not Low, because no opened source prints any limb for U or R, and because the record's own named promotion check came back NEGATIVE where it was run: GlitchProber and GlitchMiner, the two the record said an adversary should open first, were opened at FULL TEXT and neither carries an emission rate or a post-truncation support share; and because the two returns this pass newly opened — GlitchCleaner and Sampling Adapters — carry neither either.

Significance — consequence: if post-truncation support membership and emission are non-negligible for some release/default pair, the fix is a logit mask over U union R in the serving stack — machinery that already exists — and the deliverable is a shippable list per tokenizer release rather than a research programme; it would also reclassify the glitch-token hazard from input-only to bidirectional, which matters because every mitigation proposed in that literature is training-side, adapter-side or activation-side and NONE IS SAMPLER-SIDE — the precise word, narrowed from "serving-side" after verification, since GlitchProber's fix does run at inference time on every forward pass and is deployable without retraining ("adaptively modifies the process of model calculation without altering the model parameters"), so "not serving-side" would mislead a reader in the opposite direction. Li et al. Sec. 8.3 "Glitch Token Mitigation" offers exactly four remedies — "the meticulous curation and refinement of training datasets", "the advancement of model architectures to be more discerning", "the implementation of rigorous post-training evaluations" and "feed-back loops and continuous learning mechanisms" — and the strings "logit", "mask", "masking", "blacklist", "banned", "serving" and "vocabulary pruning" do not occur anywhere in that paper, its only inference-adjacent words scoping the pipeline description, the input side and GlitchHunter's cluster sampling respectively; the checker's read of Sec. 8.3 is PARTIAL, the summariser having refused whole-section reproduction, so this is an enumeration of what IS proposed plus a whole-paper term-search negative and not an unqualified "never". GlitchProber rescales MLP activations in selected key layers without altering parameters; GlitchCleaner attaches gated LoRA branches to the MLP of selected later layers at "less than 0.1% additional parameters to the original model" and detects at temperature 0. Not one of the four touches the truncation step. If the answer is at or below round-off across models and settings, the output-side arm closes, the detection literature's input-side scoping is vindicated, and the on-device vocabulary-pruning line gains a direct argument that the under-trained region is free to drop. A negative is informative, which is what keeps this a question rather than an agenda.
Significance — audience: (a) serving-engine maintainers (vLLM/SGLang/TGI/HF generate), who own the truncation step and already expose the mask; (b) model release teams writing generation_config.json, whose declared defaults Awad et al. show are already being harvested by third parties; (c) the SE glitch-token line (Li et al. FSE 2024, arXiv:2404.09894v3; GlitchProber ASE 2024, DOI 10.1145/3691620.3695060; GlitchMiner AAAI 2026, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40693 — citation corrected, since it is AAAI 2026 and not FSE or ASE, its arXiv preprint dating from 2024; GlitchCleaner AAAI 2026, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v40i36.40321), whose cheapest SAMPLER-SIDE control is one they have not evaluated — now first-hand rather than inferred, since GlitchProber was opened and its mitigation touches MLP activations and never the sampling step, and since GlitchCleaner was opened by the verification pass and prints no emission-side, sampling-side or mass quantity of any kind; (d) red-team analysts, for whom a self-emitted anomalous token is a different threat object from an injected one. Discounted honestly: (a) and (b) act only if the number is non-trivial, so for them a null is a licence rather than a change, and leg (d) was tested by neither adversary. One opened pair makes the limb (ii) arm non-vacuous for a real artifact: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct both carries ~1.8k detected glitch tokens (GlitchMiner Table 2) and ships an explicit truncating sampler (its generation_config.json).
Significance — fecundity: does emission concentrate after special tokens, in code, in non-Latin scripts, at high temperature? Is emission rate a cheap behavioural detector of under-training, giving the disagreement between weights-only and behavioural detectors an external referee? Does instruction tuning suppress it, as Prior 1's 0.740 -> 0.728 base-to-instruct shift makes immediately askable? Does speculative decoding change the hazard, since the draft model's U differs from the target's? Does quantization inflate mass on near-zero-logit rows? Should a shipped tokenizer carry a declared emission-safe mask as part of its release contract?
Significance — anchoring: the detection literature's untested symmetric arm; the non-canonical-mass problem, where R-emission is a subset nobody isolates and the figure is presented only in Fig. 4 while a per-model scalar sits one subtraction from Fig. 3; the sampler-adapter literature's open question of what truncation actually removes — which the verification pass established at first hand, since Sampling Adapters works at the exact operating condition limb (i) concerns and still only DEFINES truncation as eliminating and reallocating mass, ASSUMES a tail mass in a footnote, and MEASURES divergences, entropy and a token count instead, its epsilon-smoothing discussion showing the authors met the zeroed support and smoothed past it rather than quantifying it; the on-device vocabulary-pruning line, which prunes by log-mass and would be told whether the under-trained region costs anything; Prior 1's own stated limitation that it audits membership and not soft probabilistic erosion; and, newly, the RL invalid-action-masking literature as a structural precedent for the same question shape on a different population.

Reason for silence: an instrument and discipline asymmetry, evidenced at first hand rather than asserted, and the strongest-evidenced field in this entry. The owning field's apparatus deletes the sampler by design and puts the token in the input: GlitchProber does both ("we set the temperature to 0 to eliminate randomness and ensure consistency in the model's responses", with "All other configurations are default", token inside a repetition template, no truncation rule anywhere, and a mitigation hedged in its own words at the MLP — "By only adjusting MLP activation values, we aim to fix glitch tokens without introducing additional noise"); GlitchMiner likewise prefills the token in the assistant turn and, read at full text, states no decoding strategy at all; GlitchCleaner, opened by the verification pass, detects with a fixed repeat prompt at temperature 0, which "produces identical outputs for the same input", and repairs with gated LoRA on the MLP, its one distributional instrument being a Wasserstein distance over ACTIVATIONS rather than over emissions; Land & Bartolo App. B and Li et al. both set temperature to zero for the same reason. The one source in the neighbouring field that does sit at the truncation step itself, Sampling Adapters, still measures divergences rather than removed mass, which makes its silence the most informative silence available here. From inside that apparatus the candidate's object is not hard to measure, it is invisible — there is no sampling step to audit. The per-step truncation-support audit against documented shipped defaults is a 2026 construction (Prior 1), built for coverage and diversity rather than hazard. Secondary mechanisms are weaker and both adversaries discounted them: the expectation-of-null incentive gap is a prediction about the answer, and adversary 2 gave it no weight; the data-availability mechanism (the declared-default arm only became machine-readable with generation_config.json) is real but subordinate. "No one thought of it" is not claimed. Adversary 2's residual stands: the measurement is cheap on open weights, so the disciplinary boundary carries the whole load — which the gate accepts, since a cheap measurement the owning field's instrument structurally cannot see is a disciplinary boundary.

Strongest remaining objection: the candidate is Prior 1's own published instrument redirected at the opposite tail, and the answer it would return is predictable from the design — detectors select items by anomalous unembedding geometry, so a shipped `top_k: 20, top_p: 0.8` keeps them out of the support by construction, making limbs (ii) and (iii) ~0 before anyone runs it. ## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What the pass was and who ran it.** Seven checkers ran, each in fresh context, each blind to the reviewers' reasoning and sent to re-read one load-bearing source or pair of sources first-hand rather than to re-argue the grade. Checker 1 was sent to Prior 1, Awad et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.27268, to test six sub-claims about whether the Word Coverage Score measures mass or membership. Checker 2 was sent to Prior 3, Vieira et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.07956, to test whether a numeric log-canonicality rate is printed anywhere. Checker 3 was sent to Prior 2, Land & Bartolo 2024, arXiv:2405.05417, to test the entry's three claims about what probability that paper measures and what sampler strings it lacks. Checker 4 was sent to resolve and open the item the entry carried as "How Many Glitch Tokens Hide in Popular LLMs?". Checker 5 was sent to open the two returns the entry listed as opened by nobody, GlitchCleaner and Sampling Adapters. Checker 6 was sent to Li et al. 2024, arXiv:2404.09894v3, to test whether its 3.39% / 2.09% / 2.22% are emission rates and whether its Sec. 8.3 proposes a serving-side mask. Checker 7 was sent to GlitchProber and GlitchMiner, the two documents the record itself had named as the first an adversary should open, to re-test the promotion check the entry records as run and negative. Every one of the three findings that would have sent novelty to Low came back negative on a first-hand read, so the Medium cap survives on genuine instrument overlap and on nothing weaker.

Domain(s): AI architecture — pretraining data layer and tokenizer front-end (corpus encoding, per-language loss, multilingual evaluation). Neighbours searched: Unicode standards (UAX #15), corpus linguistics / DH encoding repair, property-based and metamorphic testing, formal-language theory of tokenization, MT detokenization, crosslingual evaluation methodology.

Question (canonical): For T >= 6 shipped tokenizer configurations drawn by a rule fixed before any data pull (the most-downloaded open-weight multilingual base-model repositories carrying a distinct `tokenizer.json`/`tokenizer.model`), each pinned by repository revision hash, and one pinned, dated, script-stratified multilingual document sample: (a) what is the document-level and codepoint-level rate at which decode(encode(d)) != d, under exact string identity and under identity up to the configuration's own declared normalisation, with CIs; (b) how does that rate decompose by script and orthographic feature (normalisation class, combining mark, ZWJ, whitespace run), and what share is equivalence-preserving versus meaning-changing; (c) by mechanism (normaliser, control-character stripping, absent byte fallback, decoder whitespace rule); and (d) when per-language held-out loss is recomputed on the round-trip-stable subset versus the full sample, what share of one named published cross-language loss gap does the difference account for?
Reformulation note: this is version B, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation and the version graded. Version A asked the same thing with two floating denominators — no selection rule for "shipped tokenizer configurations" and no named published loss gap for limb (d). The object was not changed, so the reformulation does not escape the Gate 2 finding.

Alternative formulations:
1. Is tokenization actually lossless for the languages we evaluate — and if not, for which scripts is per-language perplexity computed against a corrupted target?
2. How much text can a shipped tokenizer not represent at all, and does that unrepresentable share track the languages where models are reported weakest?

Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion on the settled claim that subword tokenization is a lossless invertible encoding, which is what licenses reading per-language loss as a property of the model rather than of the encoder. The intake premise — that the tokenizer literature measures fertility, compression and cost parity but not round-trip fidelity — is FALSE as of 2026-08, and that is the Gate 2 finding rather than the candidate's motivation: TokEval (Meister 2026, *TokEval: A Tokenizer Evaluation Suite*, arXiv:2608.18062v3; sole author, no DOI, no venue, no journal-ref) carries a section headed "Encoding Fidelity" (§3.4) that names and interprets round-trip reconstruction — **Table 1, not §3.4, is the definitional site** — and **names three mechanisms by which the round trip may differ**, three of limb (c)'s four. The intake declared its own novelty check unrun, so the first check that ran on this limb went against it.

Presuppositions: P1 shipped configurations include irreversible preprocessing and/or omit byte fallback — established as a configuration fact at shipped level (TokSuite Table 2: TokenMonster "Ignores Unknowns", mBERT "[UNK]", i.e. at least two of 14 shipped tokenizers without byte fallback — **this leg rests on adversary #2's read ALONE**: v2 Table 2 was COULD NOT READ at both post-batch routes, the v2 conversion truncating inside the reference list and the v1 tail skipping it, so the post-batch checker neither confirms nor contradicts it; TokSuite v1 App. A, "A Tokenizer Processing Glossary", verbatim-confirmed post-batch and **partitioning the whitespace options into lossy and lossless** — NFKC "Note that this can result in lossy detokenization", Normalized Whitespace "This results in lossy detokenization and often stops the downstream model", against the Learned/Manual/Individual entries' "This results in whitespace being preserved and allows for lossless detokenization" — i.e. a configuration taxonomy that **defines and announces**, with no rate, no incidence and no observed instance; SentencePiece defaults `nmt_nfkc` and `remove_extra_whitespaces`), incidence unmeasured. P2 CONTESTED criterion choice (exact identity vs identity up to declared normalisation); version B reports both, and TokEval uses exact match plus CER only. P3 FLAGGED: the released config is the one trained and evaluated on; neither TokEval nor TokSuite nor Qtok pins revisions, which evidences non-practice rather than impossibility. P4 UNVERIFIED by any opened source: a dated script-stratified multilingual *document* sample; every per-language resource in the opened priors is sentence- or treebank-grained. P5 established (arXiv:2608.25089 treats crosslingual metric comparability as live). P6 MEASURAND EXEMPTION declared and honoured by both adversaries: "it is a known bug class" is not an admissible kill without an opened source printing a rate — and the kill here is not that.

What would count as an answer: rates at document and codepoint grain with CIs under both criteria, decomposed by mechanism and by script; the equivalence-preserving / meaning-changing split; and limb (d)'s share-of-gap figure. Clean negative: rates at or near zero for all scripts under both criteria, or non-zero but wholly equivalence-preserving and uncorrelated with per-language gaps. Explicit non-answer: a fertility or compression-ratio comparison. Well-posed on version B; residual softness is that the headline fraction is relative to whichever sample is pinned.

Towards Comparable Crosslingual Language Model Evaluation*, Yang et al. 2026, arXiv:2608.25089 (v1 2026-08-25, v2 2026-08-30; three authors, not four — Xiulin Yang, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox, Catherine Arnett; no DOI, no venue), abstract only at Gate 2 and **re-read post-batch at full served body**. Its abstract's cause list is **three items, not two**: "Our results show that several widely used normalized metrics introduce crosslinguistic biases rooted in tokenization, encoding, and orthographic differences", and §8 names "script properties, tokenization granularity, and vocabulary size". The third term must be carried with its gloss: in that paper **"encoding" means REPRESENTATION LENGTH** — the byte/character premium of Arnett et al. (2024), developed under §2.1's "Orthography and Encoding" paragraph with Khmer at about three bytes per character against one for Latin — **not lossy encoding**; "lossy", "lossless", "round-trip", "reversib", "corrupt", "detokeniz" and "reconstruct" appear nowhere in the served full text, and its remedy conditions comparability on semantic equivalence of the parallel text and on the choice of normalisation unit, not on whether each language's text survives its own encoder. So the bias it reports is metric-normalisation, orthographic and byte-length bias, **not corrupted targets**; *Don't Touch My Diacritics* arXiv:2410.24140, full text — case studies, denominator one sample sentence per language, no rate, no round trip; Geng et al. arXiv:2412.03160, full text via summariser — formal inverse-homomorphism result with no normaliser, no pre-tokeniser, no corpus.)

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- **From TokEval:** it does not differ on the core of limb (a). TokEval asks the candidate's lead question in the candidate's own field and own words, under the heading "Encoding Fidelity": §3.4 writes the round trip as x̂ = T⁻¹(T(x)) and names Reconstruction Exact Match, while **Table 1, not §3.4, defines it** — formula column "1[x̂ = x], averaged over corpus", interpretation column "Strict round-trip reconstruction rate", CER's formula column "Lev(x, x̂) / |x|_chars" — §3.4's own text saying only that Reconstruction Exact Match and CER "together characterize round-trip fidelity" and that "CER uses the canonical definition of the metric and can exceed 1 when x̂ is substantially longer than x", which is a **deferral** to a definition held elsewhere rather than a definition; it asserts the candidate's own premise in a colon-joined sentence whose whole printed form is "A tokenizer is not necessarily lossless: the round-trip reconstruction x̂ = T⁻¹(T(x)) may differ from the original due to Unicode normalization, UNK substitution, or whitespace handling." (the entry earlier carried only the left half, "A tokenizer is not necessarily lossless …", without ellipsis or colon); it **names three mechanisms by which the round trip may differ** — Unicode normalization, UNK substitution, or whitespace handling, in printed order, joined by the paper's own "or", with nothing closing the list, so it is not an enumeration of *the* causes; and supplies a joint reading rule ("High exact-match failure with near-zero CER indicates minor systematic changes"). The candidate's differences are a population swap (shipped, revision-pinned configs, against TokEval's 44/46 author-trained panel), a corpus and grain swap (real-world documents and codepoints, against texts in an unnamed per-language corpus that may be FLORES+ sentences), P2's second criterion, a per-script stratification where TokEval's fidelity metrics are stratified by nothing at all (the 2-/3-/4-byte stratification §3.4 does report belongs to the neighbouring **Character Split Rate**, not to Reconstruction Exact Match or CER), and limb (d). Under the ledger's own definitions that is a covariate/corpus/population swap on an asked question.
- **From TokSuite:** different endpoint entirely (downstream accuracy under perturbation, not encoder invertibility). It corroborates P1 at shipped level and does not reach the candidate's object. The one known near-miss, examined post-batch at full main text and recorded here so it is on the record as *examined and found insufficient* rather than unexamined: TokSuite §5 carries an XGLM robustness-versus-faithfulness trade-off — NFKC normalisation buys robustness at the cost that "the tokenizer cannot faithfully represent or generate the diverse Unicode formatting" — in the same paper that prints the pooled 0.21 non-English / 0.15 English relative drops, so the **ingredients** of the interface claim co-occur in one document. What is missing is the **join**: TokSuite never says the non-English/English gap is partly encoder unfaithfulness, never conditions any comparison on fidelity, and prints no fidelity quantity at all (the terms "round-trip", "reversib" and "reconstruct" do not occur in its served main text). Note also, so the entry's own sentence is not widened past its warrant: "TokSuite reports no per-language loss" and "no BPB" are both TRUE, but "no per-language model-quality quantity" would be FALSE — v1 App. B Table 5 carries per-language canonical-performance columns (ZH, EN, FA, IT, TR) and the v2 main text cites Table 9 for a per-language −0.11 on Turkish and Chinese, both accuracy-family, not loss.
- **From Qtok:** vocabulary-level byte coverage, not behaviour on input text; a per-script axis that stops at vocabulary composition, so it is a granularity gap relative to limb (b), not prior art on it.

Novelty confidence: Low

THE NUMBER CHECK, applied before accepting the Low grade: **the record cannot name the number, and the entry does not claim one.** No reconstruction-fidelity value is printed in any span any of the three agents could read, and post-batch re-testing at eight further fetches could name none either. **The route accounting is corrected here, and the earlier "five distinct routes" claim is struck as overstating their independence:** arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18062v3 and arxiv.org/html/2608.18062v3 resolve, through this proxy, to the same body of **exactly 91,211 characters** and terminate in the same place, part-way through footnote 11 inside Appendix A.3; ar5iv is a genuinely second rendering at 89,656 characters and terminates in the same stretch of A.3. **Three renderings, one truncation point, all of it upstream of every appendix table** — so the appendix tables are not past an offset someone failed to guess, they are past the end of the longest text any of these routes will serve. Within that limit: **Table 10** (a per-tokenizer intrinsic-metric results table that §5 cites for Gini and UTF-8 character split rate) is **COULD NOT READ**, and so are Tables 4, 5, 12, 14, 16, 18 — but the earlier framing of Tables 4 and 5 as *result* tables is struck: App. A.3 says "Table 4 gives an overview of the panel definitions and Table 5 specifies all tokenizers", i.e. panel definition and tokenizer roster, **metadata**, whose unreadability costs the ledger nothing. The real loss is **one** table, not three. **And one finding the batch left on the table, now recorded in the words the ledger requires: Tables 2 and 3 were read in FULL post-batch — all 14 numeric rows × 7 outcome columns and all 9 rows × 4 columns — and Reconstruction Exact Match and CER are NOT among their 14 and 9 intrinsic metrics. That is NOT FOUND in Tables 2 and 3, in those words, not COULD NOT READ**, and it is the single strongest fact in support of this rejection: the suite defines the metric and then does not put it through either of the two measurement instruments it built. The numbers printed nearby belong to other metrics — BPB 0.7116–0.7185 (val) and 2.618–2.657 (FLORES all), plus the qualitative "Tamil and Bengali have far higher BPB than German or Spanish" — and one of them must be fenced explicitly, because a later reader skimming for "a printed number about bytes and characters" will find it first: the printed 0.001 for the three SCRIPT-encoding tokenizers against "0.008 or more for every other tokenizer" (§5, citing Table 10) are **UTF-8 CHARACTER SPLIT RATES**, disjoint from round-trip reconstruction **in both directions** — a tokenizer can post a split rate of 0.000 and still fail to reconstruct its input (normalisation is the whole of that gap), and a byte-fallback BPE splits multi-byte characters constantly while reassembling them exactly. A split rate licenses no statement whatever about reconstruction. Adversary #2 searched the metric's own name specifically (query A2-2) and found no second paper reporting it. So, graded on what the source actually does: TokEval **defines it in Table 1, bounds CER there, names and interprets both in §3.4, schedules and announces them** and asserts its motivating premise; it does **not evaluate** the candidate quantity on shipped pinned configurations over a document corpus — nor, per the NOT FOUND recorded above, on its own panel in Tables 2 and 3. A definition citation is not an evaluation, and this entry does not treat it as one. The Low grade therefore rests on the formulation having been published, not on the quantity having been measured — which under this ledger's Definitions makes limb (a) **asked but unanswered**, i.e. an open problem to route rather than an un-asked question to admit.

Significance — consequence: If round-trip failure is non-trivial and script-skewed, published per-language gaps are partly a property of the encoder, and low-resource evaluations would have to report a fidelity figure alongside the score. If near zero or wholly equivalence-preserving, current practice is positively licensed. The consequence is now carried by limbs (b) and (d); limb (a)'s is pre-empted by TokEval's metric whatever its values are.
Significance — audience: Real and already auditing shipped tokenizers — Qtok audits 13, TokSuite trains 14 LMs to isolate tokenizer choice, TokEval ships a fidelity sanity module and a fairness Gini, arXiv:2608.25089 argues crosslingual metric validity. Both adversaries graded significance inflation Resolved or Partial on that evidence, while noting the same literature shrinks limb (a)'s marginal value because TokEval already hands this audience the metric.
Significance — fecundity: Whether meaning-changing loss concentrates in the scripts where models are reported weakest; whether a fidelity figure belongs in model cards; whether byte fallback should be mandatory rather than configurable; whether harnesses should refuse to score a language above a fidelity threshold.
Significance — anchoring: Crosslingual comparability (arXiv:2608.25089), tokenizer fairness and parity, byte-level UTF-8 validity (arXiv:2606.14122, returned but unopened), UAX #15 normalization stability, and this ledger's UQ-20261016-12 on post-freeze config drift, which supplies P3.

Reason for silence: Disciplinary boundary plus incentive, and it is partly expired — which is itself the finding and part of the kill. Round-trip correctness was owned on one side as a construction property by the formal and MT literature (Geng et al. "by construct, f_detok(f_tok(x)) = x"; SentencePiece's spec) and on the other as a bug class by library maintainers (huggingface/tokenizers issues #826, #1274, #1527, #1757; TokEval §3 still files "roundtrip fidelity" among 16 deterministic checks emitting pass/warn/fail severities), never as a measurand. The boundary broke in 2026-08 when an evaluation-suite paper promoted fidelity from a sanity check to a metric, which is exactly why the candidate's framing is out of date and why a Gate 2 that had run even one query would have caught it. Adversary #2's objection is accepted: the silence mechanism explains the past, not a live gap, and the fallback incentive mechanism for limbs (b)/(d) — that auditing the target text implicates the authors' own corpus pipeline — is asserted in the record with no source, with a competing untested explanation available (the field may have reframed the concern as byte-level UTF-8 validity or robustness to non-canonical tokenization, both returned and both unopened).

Strongest remaining objection: **MULTI-LEG KILL — the verdict stands on Leg 1 alone.** Leg 1 (load-bearing, read at full body by both adversaries at routes the record did not use, and **re-read post-batch at full text on two independent routes, HTML and PDF, which agree word for word**): TokEval §3.4 "Encoding Fidelity" and Table 1 publish the candidate's lead limb in the candidate's own field and own words two months before intake — metric defined **in Table 1** as 1[x̂ = x] averaged over corpus, glossed there "Strict round-trip reconstruction rate", named and interpreted in §3.4, scheduled in a suite explicitly meant to be run "over a user-specified text corpus", with three of limb (c)'s four mechanisms **named** in an open "due to … or" list, and the premise asserted in the whole printed sentence "A tokenizer is not necessarily lossless: the round-trip reconstruction x̂ = T⁻¹(T(x)) may differ from the original due to Unicode normalization, UNK substitution, or whitespace handling." The post-batch scope check on that sentence **comes back clean**: no scope-limiting opener, subject "A tokenizer" universally quantified and hedged only by "not necessarily", the clause **ASSERTS** the property rather than denying it or recording a move away from it, a sound subject on the left of the cut and a full stop on the right, and "not necessarily lossless" is itself the hedged formulation — the paper nowhere states a bare "tokenizers are lossy" — so the entry is carrying the right one. Limb (a) is that run on a swapped population and corpus. Leg 2 (whether TokEval's appendix prints the values) is COULD NOT READ at three renderings, materially at **one** table (Table 10; Tables 4 and 5 are panel and tokenizer definitions, immaterial), and is **explicitly not load-bearing**: if it came back empty the verdict would not change, because novelty fails on publication of the formulation, not on measurement of the quantity. Leg 3 (TokSuite App. A's "lossy detokenization" over 14 shipped tokenizers) corroborates P1 only. Leg 4 (Qtok) does not reach the candidate's object by its own admission. If Legs 2–4 all fell the kill would stand unchanged; **if Leg 1 fell the kill would collapse entirely**, and because Gate 2 rejected this candidate before Gate 4 in the ordinary sense, the entry would then need all eight attacks re-run from scratch rather than a re-judge — the two logs here were run under the standing rule that a Gate 2 rejection still draws adversaries, so that work exists and would be reusable.

THIS REJECTION'S OWN VULNERABILITY: the kill rests on something **nobody has measured**. It rests on what a document *announces and defines* — a metric specification and a suite's advertised scope — not on any reported result; no agent can name a single value of the candidate quantity from any source, and the quantity may well be unmeasured everywhere. The verdict is therefore a judgement that a published formulation forecloses un-askedness, which is a claim about design and priority, not about evidence. A second design-derived claim appears in the record and is correctly not load-bearing: Geng et al.'s inverse-homomorphism result is an **ALGEBRAIC identity** over abstract token maps on Σ*, proved with no normaliser, no pre-tokenisation regex and no UTF-8 validity condition; it is **not** a bitwise or empirical demonstration that any shipped, revision-pinned configuration round-trips real documents byte-for-byte, and the paper's own Appendix B concedes a shipped heuristic breaks it. Nobody has run the bitwise check on a shipped pinned config over a document corpus — which is exactly why the residue is routable rather than answered. Single unread source most likely to settle the vulnerability, with its accounting corrected: **TokEval's Table 10 alone** — the one unreadable table in this paper that could carry a reconstruction value, since §5 cites it for two other per-tokenizer metric values; the earlier framing of Tables 4–5 as *result* tables is **struck** (App. A.3: "Table 4 gives an overview of the panel definitions and Table 5 specifies all tokenizers" — metadata, immaterial) — reachable, if at all, **via the arXiv e-print LaTeX source for 2608.18062v3**, which carries table bodies as markup no HTML converter can truncate. That is the one untried route **of the right kind**. The rendered-PDF URL arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18062v3 is **struck as a candidate**: post-batch it served the identical 91,211-character text as the HTML and truncated at the same point, so it was right in kind and wrong in fact. Reading Table 10 would show whether a reconstruction value and per-language strata are printed, which decides whether limb (a) is asked-and-open (route it) or asked-and-answered (do not). **And the sentence this rejection was missing, which is about the kill's REACH and not its truth: this Unresolved rests WHOLLY on a DEFINITIONAL prior in a SINGLE UNVENUED PREPRINT with NO MEASUREMENT behind the metric.** The second adversary's own log records that its nine sweeps found no cross-field disguise at all, so no second document anywhere in the record carries the kill; and the post-batch read confirms the paper has no journal-ref, no venue and no comments field, with 44 of its 46 configurations author-trained ablations and the 2 off-the-shelf tokenizers unpinned. Given this ledger's history of reversing single-source kills on rejections, that fact belongs in the entry rather than in a checker's file.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): do not pursue version B. Re-intake the residue as a narrower candidate: limb (b) alone (per-script and per-orthographic-feature decomposition with the equivalence-preserving / meaning-changing split, a grain TokEval does not reach at all, its fidelity metrics being stratified by nothing and its 2-/3-/4-byte stratification belonging to the neighbouring Character Split Rate) plus limb (d) rebuilt as a within-document counterfactual — score d and decode(encode(d)) under the same model — rather than a stable-subset comparison, which adversary #1 showed conflates fidelity with selection on document type. **The kill's own source was re-tested and it survived.** The load-bearing sentence was reconstructed from three consecutive PDF fragments, served in order, verified at both junctions, and independently corroborated on the HTML route, which served the first and third fragments in the same words. Its whole printed form is: "A tokenizer is not necessarily lossless: the round-trip reconstruction x̂ = T⁻¹(T(x)) may differ from the original due to Unicode normalization, UNK substitution, or whitespace handling." The scope-setting-opener check **comes back clean**: there is no scope-limiting opener — no "In such cases,", no "At the time of writing,", no "For byte-level tokenizers," — the subject "A tokenizer" is universally quantified and hedged only by "not necessarily", and the clause **ASSERTS** the property rather than denying it or recording a move away from it, the material after the colon being the explanation of the opener and not a restriction on it. The grammar survives on both sides of the cut: the subject of "may differ" is "the round-trip reconstruction x̂ = T⁻¹(T(x))", which sits before the cut, and "whitespace handling." terminates the sentence with a full stop, so no fourth cause was clipped. "Not necessarily lossless" is itself the hedged formulation, and the paper nowhere states a bare "tokenizers are lossy", so the entry was carrying the right one. Authorship is confirmed from the front matter: **Clara Meister, sole author**, submitted 2026-08-18, v3 2026-09-09, cs.CL and cs.LG, no venue and no journal-ref; a summariser pass that rendered the experiments in the plural is summariser prose and was not taken as front matter.
