**What was struck from the entry's own prose.** First, "enumerates the causes of deviation" is **struck wherever it stood** — in the motivating gap, in the From-TokEval comparison, in the strongest-remaining-objection paragraph and in the routing row — and replaced by "names three mechanisms by which the round trip may differ": the paper writes "due to" and joins the three with "or", with nothing closing the list, so the old wording upgraded an open illustrative list into a closed taxonomy. Second, the claim that no value is printed "across five distinct routes" is **struck as an overstatement of route independence**: arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18062v3 and arxiv.org/html/2608.18062v3 resolve through this proxy to the same body of exactly 91,211 characters and terminate at the same point, mid-footnote 11 in Appendix A.3, while ar5iv is a second rendering of 89,656 characters terminating in the same stretch — three renderings, one truncation point, all upstream of every appendix table. Third, the description of Tables 4 and 5 as "appendix result tables" is **struck**: Appendix A.3 says "Table 4 gives an overview of the panel definitions and Table 5 specifies all tokenizers", so they are metadata — a panel definition and a tokenizer roster — and their unreadability costs the ledger nothing, because a roster could not print a metric value in the first place. The real loss is **one** table, not three, and the entry's inflation of it threefold is removed. Fourth, the rendered-PDF URL is **struck as a next route**; the one untried route of the right kind is the arXiv e-print LaTeX source for 2608.18062v3, which carries the table bodies as markup no HTML converter can truncate.

**Where a checker misdescribed this entry, the entry carries its own record.** Checker B's handed premise stated that the entry nominates "the PDF at arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18062v3" as its most promising untried route. **What was narrowed.** (i) "Section 3.4 defines Reconstruction Exact Match … plus a character error rate" is **true of the paper but false of §3.4**, and is rewritten throughout to "§3.4 names and interprets; Table 1 defines". §3.4's own text says only that "Reconstruction Exact Match and, as a graded complement, Character Error Rate (CER) together characterize round-trip fidelity", and, on CER, that it "uses the canonical definition of the metric and can exceed 1 when x̂ is substantially longer than x" — a **deferral** to a definition held elsewhere, not a definition. The definitional site is Table 1, whose formula and interpretation columns print "1[x̂ = x], averaged over corpus" / "Strict round-trip reconstruction rate" and "Lev(x, x̂) / |x|_chars" with the note that it "can exceed 1". (ii) The paraphrase of *Apples to Apples?* is narrowed to the paper's own **three-item** list, "crosslinguistic biases rooted in tokenization, encoding, and orthographic differences", where the entry had carried two and dropped "encoding"; the omission mattered, because "encoding" is the word a later reader would seize on to claim the interface limb occupied, so the entry now carries the gloss that in that paper "encoding" means **representation length** — the byte/character premium of Arnett et al. (2024), developed under §2.1's "Orthography and Encoding" with Khmer at about three bytes per character against one for Latin — and not lossy encoding. The terms "lossy", "lossless", "round-trip", "reversib", "corrupt", "detokeniz" and "reconstruct" occur nowhere in that paper's served full text. (iii) The byte-width stratification is narrowed to the metric it actually belongs to: §3.4 prints "Character Split Rate is stratified and reported by byte width (2-, 3-, 4-byte)", so the fidelity metrics are stratified **by nothing at all**, not "by byte width". (iv) P1's Table 2 leg is now marked as resting on **adversary #2's read alone**, because v2 Table 2 was COULD NOT READ at both of checker C's routes; the glossary leg of P1 is upgraded instead to verbatim confirmation. (v) The entry's true sentence "TokSuite reports no per-language loss" is fenced against widening: TokSuite does print per-language *accuracy-family* quantities (v1 App. B Table 5's ZH/EN/FA/IT/TR canonical-performance columns, and the −0.11 Turkish/Chinese relative drop the v2 main text attributes to Table 9), so a restatement as "nothing per-language" would be false.

**The quotation defect, and why the cut was the defect.** The entry quoted "A tokenizer is not necessarily lossless" as though it were a whole sentence the paper states. It is the **left half of a colon-joined sentence**, given with no ellipsis and with the colon dropped. The words are verbatim, and the cut is grammatically clean on the left with the meaning intact — the right half only supplies the mechanism — so this is a **presentational** misquotation rather than a substantive one; but it is still a defect, and the entry now carries the whole printed sentence where the half-sentence stood, with the half-quotation flagged as such. What is missing is the **join**: TokSuite never says the non-English/English gap is partly encoder unfaithfulness, never conditions any comparison on fidelity, and prints no fidelity quantity at all. On the checked claim itself, checker C's verdict is HOLD at better read levels than the record had: neither source conditions a cross-language comparison on round-trip fidelity, and neither attributes a loss gap to encoder provenance, so the rejection does **not** widen to cover limb (d).

**Citation corrections.** TokEval's front matter needed none — title, arXiv id and version, both dates and the sole authorship of Clara Meister all check out against the paper's own first page — and "preprint, no venue, no journal-ref" is added, because it bears on how much weight a kill may rest on it. TokSuite is now recorded by first author (Gül Sena Altıntaş), both version dates (v1 2025-12-23, v2 2026-07-06), full title and arXiv id, with no DOI and no venue. *Apples to Apples?* is corrected to **three authors, not four** — Xiulin Yang, Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox, Catherine Arnett; the v2 HTML renders an image placeholder that can be mistaken for a fourth name, and /abs settles it — and is recorded by first author, year, full title and arXiv id, with no DOI and no venue. Since none of the three papers carries a DOI, each is recorded by arXiv designation plus first author plus year plus title, never by a bare identifier.

**Routes that failed, so a later pass does not repeat them.** On TokEval: arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18062v3 at default span and offsets 40,000 and 70,000 serves the body and Tables 2 and 3 but never an appendix table, ending at 91,211 characters; arxiv.org/html/2608.18062v3 at offset 78,000 serves the references and A.1–A.3 prose and then ends, and at offset 100,000 returns no text at all ("this page's text is 91211 characters long"), a length probe and not a read; ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2608.18062 at default span and offset 62,000 reaches Tables 1, 2 and 3 (Table 3 in full) and at offset 90,000 returns no text (89,656 characters). On TokSuite: arxiv.org/html/2512.20757v2 truncates at 84,361 characters inside the reference list, and a read at offset 80,000 returned only the conclusion tail and the first five references, confirming truncation rather than a mis-set offset; v1 at offset 70,000 served Appendix A's glossary tail and Appendix B's Tables 4–6 but not v1's equivalent of the detailed benchmark-results appendix and not Table 2. On *Apples to Apples?*: Figures 2, 3 and 4 are images, so their per-language values are unreachable at the HTML route. Not attempted and therefore still open: arxiv.org/pdf/2608.18062v1, TokEval's v1/v2 HTML, **the TokEval e-print LaTeX source**, arxiv.org/e-print/2512.20757v2, and any repository page either paper may name — checker B calls a repository results dump **a guess**, having never reached a repository page and never confirmed from the front matter or A.1–A.3 that the paper names one. curl to arxiv.org was not attempted post-batch, so the entry's record of a tool-scoped proxy 403 there is neither confirmed nor disputed; WebFetch reached arxiv.org repeatedly, which is what a tool-scoped refusal would predict.

**What the pass did not reach.** The tail of TokEval's appendix and every one of its appendix tables, Table 10 above all, are **COULD NOT READ** and are scored neither way: Table 10 is a per-tokenizer intrinsic-metric results table that §5 cites for two other metric values, and whether it carries an Exact-match or CER column is unknown. TokSuite's v2 Table 2, Table 9 and detailed benchmark appendix are **COULD NOT READ**. *Apples to Apples?*'s per-language figure values are **COULD NOT READ**. Qtok, Geng et al., *Don't Touch My Diacritics* and the six returned-but-unopened sources were not re-checked by this pass at all and remain unchecked, not absent. Nothing in this pass establishes that limb (d)'s magnitude is non-negligible: that is precisely what no opened source measures, and no checker added a number to it.

**Did the verdict move? No — it HELD.** The verdict is **Rejected**, as it was before this pass, and the Unresolved on attack 2 survives re-testing of its own source at full text on two independent routes, with the scope check clean, the three mechanisms verbatim and in printed order, the authorship and dates confirmed, and the one quotation defect presentational. What changed is the entry's prose, not its verdict: three defects fixed in place, one leg strengthened by a NOT FOUND the batch had not recorded, two accounting errors corrected, one route nomination struck, and several citations completed.

**No late Gate 4 was owed, and why.** A late Gate 4 run is owed when a rejection's fatal ground is **withdrawn** — when the thing the kill stood on turns out not to be there, so that the candidate's attacks must be re-run against a record that no longer contains the kill. That did not happen here. The fatal ground is TokEval §3.4's publication of the candidate's lead limb, it was re-tested first-hand against its own source by a checker blind to the reviewers' reasoning, and **it survived**: the heading holds, the lossless sentence holds and holds in its hedged form, the three mechanisms hold verbatim, the authorship and both dates hold, and the only corrections are a locative narrowing (Table 1, not §3.4, defines), a framing narrowing ("names three mechanisms", not "enumerates the causes") and a presentational quotation fix. **A ground that survives verification of its own sources is not a withdrawn ground**, so nothing was reopened, no late Gate 4 was run on this entry, and none was owed. The verdict in this pass's brief was final and is not re-judged here.

**Separately: this is a SINGLE-SOURCE kill, and what that means for its reach.** The whole of attack 2's Unresolved rests on **one paper**. Adversary #2's own log records that its nine sweeps found **no cross-field disguise at all**, so no second document in the record carries the kill, and checker B's search of the metric's own name found no second paper reporting it. The kill therefore rests **wholly on a definitional prior, in a single unvenued preprint, with no measurement behind the metric** — no printed Reconstruction Exact Match value, no printed CER value, the metric absent from both of the paper's own measurement instruments, and an evidence base of 44 author-trained ablation tokenizers plus 2 unpinned off-the-shelf references. Given this ledger's history of reversing single-source kills on rejections, that is stated here in terms rather than left in a checker's file. The consequence is about **reach**, not truth: against a candidate whose contribution is to **raise the question or define the metric**, the kill lands squarely and this rejection is supported on its lead limb; against a candidate whose contribution is a **measured, corpus-named, script-stratified fidelity rate**, the kill **does not reach it**, because §3.4 measures nothing and stratifies nothing. This is recorded as prose and closes nothing: the entry is Rejected and this pass promotes no part of it. A future intake that brings a measured, corpus-named, script-stratified fidelity result would have to cite §3.4 and Table 1 as prior art for the definition and for the lossless observation, but the present kill would not by itself dispose of it. The routing row's own open edge runs the other way and is recorded above: if the arXiv e-print LaTeX source shows Table 10 carrying an Exact-match or CER column, limb (a) becomes asked and answered for the 39-tokenizer panel, the row must be withdrawn, and this rejection strengthens to a disguised known.

ID: UQ-20261022-18
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Provisional — Validated blocked by an incomplete Gate 2 search record and, in limb (ii)'s denominator, a two-grid ambiguity wherever a merge or pixel-shuffle step exists together with the absence of any family-neutral lattice convention; nothing Unresolved on any attack from either adversary.
Domain(s): AI architecture — multimodal model design (vision encoder, resize/tiling policy, projector). Method transplanted from imaging-performance metrology (ISO 12233 slanted-edge SFR) and visual psychophysics.

Question (canonical): For a pre-declared set of shipped vision-language models crossed with input modes (native resize; each dynamic-tiling / any-resolution setting), probed with synthetic targets (sine gratings; slanted edges) swept over spatial frequency expressed both in cycles per image and in cycles per encoder patch, crossed with Michelson contrast, orientation and phase, under a 2AFC readout with pre-declared low-frequency positive controls and an enforced chance level: (i) at what frequency does orientation-discrimination accuracy fall to a pre-declared 75%-correct criterion, and what is the contrast threshold as a function of frequency; (ii) what is the ratio of that cutoff to the nominal patch-Nyquist limit; (iii) is any above-cutoff correct responding attributable to resize-kernel aliasing rather than to true transmission; (iv) in a pre-registered out-of-sample comparison with the model x input-mode arm as the unit, does the per-arm cutoff explain variance in fine-detail task accuracy (small text, counting, dense-chart QA) beyond input pixel count and vision-token/patch count?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation; V1 ("end-to-end behavioural modulation transfer function ...") is recorded in the record and under Alternative formulations. V2 is the version graded.

Alternative formulations:
- V1 as submitted: what is the end-to-end behavioural modulation transfer function of a shipped VLM's image pathway, where does forced-choice reporting fall to chance, and does that cutoff predict fine-detail failures better than input resolution or patch count?
- What is the visual acuity and contrast-sensitivity limit of a VLM's image front-end, measured the way an imaging system's resolution is measured rather than by accuracy on natural images?
- If a VLM's vision stack is treated as an imaging chain and a test target is swept through it, where is its resolution limit, and how far do dynamic-tiling policies move it?

Motivating gap: imaging metrology characterises any chain by a frequency response before reporting task accuracy; VLM practice reports natural-image benchmark accuracy and nominal configuration (pixels, patch size, token count). The intake's premise that "VLM evaluation has no such instrument" was falsified at Gate 2 by arXiv:2508.10367 and the gap narrowed accordingly; it must be narrowed again on Gate 4 findings. Three groups have now asked the perceptual-limit question with three instruments — a frequency axis without an engineering axis (2508.10367), a pixel-size axis carrying a criterion-defined threshold that is printed per model (2606.07861: Eq. 3 defines RT_X, Table 1 prints mean RT50 in px for 18 models, 7.3 to 24.8, read at full text on the post-batch pass), and a pixels-per-glyph legibility axis with an uncriterioned knee and a measured patch-boundary effect (2402.07384, now published as a TMLR 2026 paper under a revised title) — and none prints a criterion-defined cutoff FREQUENCY, a cycles-per-patch quantity, an aliasing magnitude referred to a stated resize kernel, or a rival-predictor regression. The patch-boundary leg is no longer vacant and the entry no longer claims it is: 2402.07384 sweeps the target's offset against the patch grid and measures the effect, and the patch-lattice aliasing boundary is named in print as a confound to design around (IRIS, arXiv:2608.05122, Sec. 3.1, "the upper bound is kept below the patch-wise Nyquist frequency to avoid aliasing").

Presuppositions: P1 behavioural readout of the image pathway is possible (partly relieved by 2508.10367; prompt wording is a declared nuisance arm). P2 loss is organised by spatial frequency (weakly supported; still contested for orientation/phase discrimination). P3 per-arm preprocessing is recoverable — the record's cheapest unverified check, now TRUE and sourced independently by both adversaries from huggingface/transformers (image_processing_llava_next.py BICUBIC + image_grid_pinpoints; image_processing_qwen2_vl.py BICUBIC + smart_resize + patch_size 14 / merge_size 2), with the caveat that library defaults are not a checkpoint's preprocessor_config.json and the applied kernel is backend-dependent. That caveat is now partly closed: the post-batch pass opened the shipped checkpoint files themselves — llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf/preprocessor_config.json at FULL TEXT ("size": {"shortest_edge": 336}, "crop_size" 336x336, "do_center_crop": true, "resample": 3, "image_processor_type": "CLIPImageProcessor") and Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct/preprocessor_config.json at field level (patch_size 14, merge_size 2, temporal_patch_size 2, min_pixels 3136, max_pixels 12845056, and no "size" key at all) — so the per-arm pitch and bounds are recoverable from the checkpoint and not only from library defaults; the applied kernel remains backend-dependent. P4 a nominal patch-Nyquist limit exists per arm — CONTESTED, see Strongest remaining objection. P5 the fine-detail failures are real and reported — TRUE for small symbols and counting (2407.06581, re-read at full text from the PDF at the post-batch pass: the four-model mean is 58.57% over that paper's own 7-task synthetic suite, and that figure is an unweighted mean of unweighted task-column means — denominator 4 models x 8 Table 1 columns = 32 cells, NOT an accuracy over the 4,764-item question pool, with the 480-image overlapping-shapes task split across two columns and so carrying double weight (the cell arithmetic reproducing the printed headline is the checker's own); the weakest task columns are nested squares at 30.99% and single-coloured paths at 42.06% against random baselines of 25.00 and 33.33; the 2402.07384 size-quantile gaps 16.71%/21.83% on GQA/TextVQA for BLIP-2 and the 58-point location disparity for Qwen-VL-Chat were NOT reached by any checker at that pass and stand on adversary 2's read alone, scored neither way here); still NOT SOURCED for dense charts, and now positively confirmed that 2407.06581 contains no dense-chart task at all — its only chart is two 2-segment piecewise-linear functions deliberately spaced to be separable, and its real-world failures are a subway map, a musical score and a street map, so that paper is SILENT on dense charts rather than negative about them. P6 measurand exemption declared for the values in (i)-(iv) only, and not for "no frequency-resolved behavioural measurement exists", which is false.
Also falsified on a sourced read: the claim that the tiling map is content-dependent (adversary 2: select_best_resolution and smart_resize take only dimensions; corroborated at the post-batch pass from the shipped OpenGVLab/InternVL2_5-8B and OpenGVLab/InternVL3-8B configs, which print "dynamic_image_size": true, "min_dynamic_patch": 1, "max_dynamic_patch": 12 and "use_thumbnail": true — tiling fixed by dimensions, with a whole-image thumbnail tile added in the same forward pass), which removes one of the two stated grounds for spending the reformulation. The other ground (no intensity-linear output to Fourier-transform) stands.

What would count as an answer: per model x input mode, a response surface over the pre-registered sweep giving the 75%-correct 2AFC cutoff in both frequency units; its ratio to a correctly named nominal limit; a target-fixed, alias-specific manipulation separating aliasing from kernel-dependent blur; and an out-of-sample test of the cutoff against pixel count and patch count with the estimator, unit and power declared in advance. A counting negative: cutoffs sit at the nominal limit and carry no incremental predictive information. Not an answer: natural-image fine-detail accuracy with no frequency axis, or a cutoff measured under one tiling setting and reported as the model's cutoff.

Estimand = where legibility plateaus. The printed threshold is the number 8 and it is a RENDERING FONT SIZE: Sec. 4 defines quality as "the original sampling rate of an object (in pixels per inch, or pixels per vector graphic range)" and Sec. 4.1 operationalises it for the synthetic task "in terms of the font size used during text creation", "which correlates with the vertical pixel count of the text characters". The full printed sentence, Sec. 4.2, is "Remarkably, the threshold of a sampling rate of 8 is consistently observed across all MLLM models." — the earlier string cut the opening adverb, which scopes the clause as a cross-model observation rather than a derivation, and the Fig. 4 caption carries a different sentence ("from the sampling rate of 8 (marked as red), the image starts to become fully recognizable."), so the quotation may not be cited to the caption. NO accuracy criterion is declared for it: the support offered is "the performance stabilized with increasing sampling rate", a knee read off a curve, at a single fixed contrast on white, from an open-ended response with no alternative set, no chance level and no fitted psychometric function. Its denominator is one character's vertical extent in pixels — NOT the image, NOT the patch, NOT a degree of visual angle, there being no viewing geometry in the paper. The words Nyquist, spatial frequency, cycles per degree and cycles per patch do not appear, on two full passes. It tabulates patch sizes (Table 3: 14x14 for the four CLIP-family models and 30x30 for Fuyu-8B, with patch numbers 16x16 / 16x16 / 24x24 / 32x32 / 10x10) and in Sec. 4.5.1 amalgamates "every four adjacent 14 x 14 image patches" into a 28x28 patch. And it MEASURES a patch-lattice effect in Sec. 4.5.2, "Local Patch Boundary Cut" (Figs. 8-9, complete results in Appendix A), sweeping the target across the grid in separate vertical-cut and horizontal-cut conditions over "100 random numbers for each experiment", with the counter-intuitive direction printed in full as "Model's performance is lower when target objects remain undivided by patch boundaries." and restated in Sec. 5 as "MLLMs are good at recognizing small objects that are divided into more image tokens."; the one printed scalar is "Qwen-VL-Chat still presents an around 10 percent gap between different patch boundary cuts.", for one model, and everything else on that limb is plotted rather than tabulated.
2. Li L. (Lujun Li), Sleem L., Gentile N., Xu Y., Song Y., Wu W., State R., "The Last Visible Pixel: Probing Fine-Scale Perception in Vision-Language Models", arXiv:2606.07861v1, posted 5 June 2026, 25 pages, no DOI assigned (author list and order CONFIRMED at the post-batch pass). READ: FULL TEXT twice over — via the alphaxiv .md mirror by adversary 1 (summariser-mediated), and independently at the post-batch pass via ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2606.07861, which served the whole body including Table 1, Eq. 3, Secs. 1-5 and Appendices A, B and C.1 on the first attempt; abstract-only at Gate 2; COULD NOT READ at arxiv.org/html x3 and arxiv.org/pdf x2 across three agents, and arxiv.org/pdf returned RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED again at the post-batch pass. Appendix C.2 (Inference Settings) is cited in the served text but its body did not come through: COULD NOT READ, and nothing here rests on it. Unit = a model x task x rendered-target-size cell; 18 models, Table 1's leaderboard carrying 18 rows and Appendix A giving N=18 (the earlier read's "Table 6" is not confirmed and is withdrawn). Endpoint = strict exact-match accuracy on JSON-formatted answers over twelve subtasks split into perception and reasoning groups, with a separately reported JSON hallucination rate. Comparator = perception against reasoning over the same size sweep, which is SEVEN discrete levels — 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px — not a continuous or finely spaced ramp. Estimand = RT_X, defined at Eq. 3 in Sec. 3.3: "Given a target accuracy threshold X in (0,100), we define RT_X as the smallest target size at which the accuracy reaches X%:", with "RT_X = s_1 if Acc(s_1) >= X, and RT_X = s_max+1 if X is never reached." and "Smaller values indicate better fine-grained visual sensitivity." The entry's open residual — values located but not transcribed — is now CLOSED for the headline metric: Table 1, the "FineSightBench leaderboard", prints mean RT50 in px for all 18 models, 7.3 (Gemma-4-31B), 11.1, 13.1 (Gemini-2.5-Flash), 14.0 (GPT-4o), 14.8, 16.4, 17.7, 17.8, 18.9, 19.1, 19.2, 21.3, 22.0, 22.8, 22.9, 23.8, 24.3, 24.8 (Qwen3-VL-2B), reported at X = 50 only, on absolute strict-match accuracy with chance neither mentioned nor corrected for, under the censoring convention s_max+1 standing in for failure, and with no CIs, no error bars and no seeds anywhere in the table. Whether "mean RT50" averages all twelve subtasks or the perception subtasks only is not stated in the served caption — a residual on the read, not an asserted defect — and the earlier read's location of RT80 in Table 8 and of per-task values in Tables 7-8 was not re-confirmed at this pass. Names patch geometry qualitatively (16x16, 14x14 and 12x12 appear as Sec. 2 background and normalise no reported result) and hypothesises "recognition is bounded by the finest signal within a patch"; aliasing, Nyquist, spatial frequency and interpolation absent, the controlled variables being size, colour, category and position.
3. Hernández-Cámara P., Gómez-Villa A., Jaén-Lorites J. M., Vila-Tomás J., Laparra V., Malo J., "Contrast Sensitivity in Multimodal Large Language Models: A Psychophysics-Inspired Evaluation", arXiv:2508.10367v2, front-matter date 15 October 2025, no DOI located in the document. READ: FULL TEXT (Gate 2, and again at the post-batch pass in four passes over arxiv.org/html/2508.10367v2, all sections reached including Appendices A and B, with the contested points returned identically on two independent passes). Unit = a contrast-frequency-prompt cell, aggregated to one psychometric function per frequency per prompt and then to one CSF per model (8 open MLLMs at two nominal scales, plus CLIP and SigLIP2 in Appendix B). Endpoint = "we computed the proportion of affirmative responses (i.e., yes answers)", fitted with a Weibull cumulative distribution (Eq. 1), the threshold being "the contrast level corresponding to a 50% detection probability" and sensitivity its reciprocal (Eq. 2). The entry's earlier "responses not scored correct/incorrect" is STRUCK as too strong: it is the PSYCHOPHYSICAL endpoint that is never a correctness score, while a correctness score does appear, in Sec. 5 and throughout Fig. 6, as the downstream Imagenette classification accuracy the CSF is tested as a predictor OF ("Accuracy values are reported relative to performance on unaltered images."). Comparator = the human Standard Spatial Observer. Estimand = contrast-detection threshold vs frequency and its human-likeness; prints Pearson rho (shape agreement only, absolute scale excluded by construction) and RMSE (absolute sensitivity, units unstated) per model in Table 1, no cutoff frequency, and no printed NUMERIC per-model peak or cutoff — though it does argue from per-model peak sensitivity qualitatively (Sec. 5.2; Fig. 6 caption, "the largest accuracy reductions occur at frequencies where the model shows peak sensitivity") and plots the curves in Figs. 3 and 6, so the narrower true claim is that it reaches for a per-model frequency landmark and stops short of naming one. The only cpd figures printed anywhere are the stimulus range "logarithmically spaced between 0 and 32 cycles per degree (cpd)", the sampling resolution "64 pixels per degree, typical of modern displays", and the HUMAN "peak sensitivity around 4-6 cycles per degree (cpd)". The strings cutoff, cut-off, patch, Nyquist, alias, resize, tiling and interpolat are ABSENT from the whole text including appendices; "no patch-normalised quantity" therefore holds exactly as worded, but the paper does print resolution quantities — 256x256 px stimuli at 64 px/deg — and they are stimulus-side and display-referred, normalised to nothing about the model. Of the four irregularities flagged at Gate 2, three were re-checked: 25 vs 10 is CONFIRMED and stronger than Gate 2 put it, since Sec. 2.1's "we created 25 statistically independent samples for each frequency-contrast pair" stands against Sec. 2.2's "10 independently generated noise images" AND Sec. 2.3's "10 repeated stimulus presentations per condition", so 25 is the likelier stray and the trial denominator behind every psychometric fit is ambiguous by a factor of 2.5; the unnamed "proprietary model included for illustrative comparison" (Sec. 2.4) is CONFIRMED and is a dangling reference rather than a mere omission, Table 1 printing eight named rows and no proprietary row; and the Weibull item is RECLASSIFIED — a Weibull CDF needs no transform to be read at 50%, so this is not an internal inconsistency but an UNSTATED ASSUMPTION, Eq. 1 pinning P(0) = 0, i.e. a zero false-alarm rate, with no guess-rate or bias term under a 50% criterion on a yes/no task, which the paper's own Sec. 3.2 prompt-sensitivity result puts under strain. The fourth (a caption describing absent bolding) was not re-checked at this pass. Two genuine inconsistencies, then, not four — and its numbers still should not be transported, though the decisive obstacle is the regime rather than the bookkeeping: a frequency-collapsed pair of scalars over display-referred stimuli would print no patch-normalised cutoff even in a fully self-consistent version of this paper.
Also on record: Rahmanzadehgervi P., Bolton L., Taesiri M. R., Nguyen A. T., "Vision language models are blind", arXiv:2407.06581v4 (2024) — the entry's earlier "ACCV 2024" is UNVERIFIED by the post-batch read, which saw no venue line and no DOI in the front matter served to it (not contradicted, not confirmed). It sources the counting and small-symbol failures, and its resolution finding is NARROWER than the entry's earlier heading-level citation implied, on four axes. (1) It covers THREE of the paper's seven tasks — B.2 two touching circles, D.2 counting line intersections, F.2 counting the shapes in an Olympic-like logo (the correct labels are B.2/D.2/E.2/F.2, not the "0.B.2"/"0.E.2" the entry previously printed); Task 3 is rendered at a fixed 512 px and Task 5 at a fixed 1000 px, so for those two no sweep exists at all, and Tasks 6 and 7 do use several canvas sizes while appendices G and H analyse none. (2) The sweep is canvas size over {384, 769, 1155} px (B.1, F.1) and {384, 768, 1152} px (D.1): three points, a one-sided 3x range, every step upward, with NOTHING below 384 px. (3) The RESULT sentence governs, not the heading — "Based off these results, we conclude that VLMs' ability to see the intersection of two circles does not depend on the quality of the image." (B.2), with D.2's "Fig. 32 depicts that increasing the resolution in our plots does not help the VLMs see and count the intersections of 2D lines." and Fig. 37's "For most models, resolution (a) and colors (b) have minimal impact on performance.", a null asserted with an explicit exception class; and the best model IS the exception in two of the three experiments, with the sign flipping between them: "Sonnet-3.5 slightly performs worse at 769 and 1155px compared to 384px" (B.2) against "Sonnet-3.5 performs better as the image size increases (a)" (Fig. 37 caption). (4) NO per-resolution accuracy number is printed in B.2, D.2 or F.2 — the comparison exists only as plotted points in Fig. 20-left, Fig. 32-left and Fig. 37-a, which the checker could not read numerically — so no sentence of the form "X% at 384 px and Y% at 1155 px" can be sourced to this paper. Flagged as the CHECKER'S OWN INFERENCE from the construction wording ("rendered ... on a canvas of size C in {...}px") and not as anything the paper states: the sweep RE-RENDERS the scene at each canvas size rather than varying the pixels available for a fixed rendered detail, which is a different quantity from resolution in the sense limb (iv) needs. The paper manipulates NO contrast and NO spatial frequency anywhere — a confident negative from the complete A-through-I subsection inventory plus a keyword sweep, not a verified-exhaustive grep, and not a COULD NOT CHECK. The line-width effect HOLDS, and the entry carries BOTH of the paper's own formulations, which conflict: E.2, "Finding: the best performing model is affected by line width", whose body reads "Table 15 shows that the best VLM on the nested square task (Sonnet-3.5) is more accurate as line width increases." with printed numbers over 3/4/6 px — Sonnet-3.5 90.00 / 91.25 / 95.00, +5.00 points, and GPT-4o 58.75 / 56.25 / 52.50, -6.25 points, at 40 images per cell by the checker's own arithmetic from the task's 120 — against Table 15's own caption, "Line thickness has minimal effect on VLMs' performance, suggesting that visual attributes of shapes are not critical to VLMs when asked to count the shapes." Route note so a later pass does not repeat it: the arXiv HTML render of v4 is 83,598 characters, terminates inside Sec. 4 and carries NO appendix, so a checker working from it would record COULD NOT READ as NOT FOUND; arxiv.org/pdf/2407.06581v4 is the only route that serves B.2/D.2/E.2/F.2. Zhuang et al., arXiv:2602.02539 (abstract only) is the nearest per-vision-token capacity law.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
1. From 2402.07384 / TMLR 2026: a pixels-per-glyph legibility knee identified by inspection on free-form text recognition — the threshold is a rendering font size "which correlates with the vertical pixel count of the text characters", so no contrast axis (text on plain white), no orientation or phase variable, no declared criterion ("the performance stabilized with increasing sampling rate"), no alternative set and no chance floor, no tiling arm (each model at its own fixed native resolution, 224-448 px per Table 3), no aliasing magnitude, and explicitly no test of input resolution or token count as competing predictors (Appendix C: "it is unclear which factor plays the most important role") — Table 3 holds the ingredients, patch number and patch size and resolution per model, and no sentence regresses, correlates or otherwise contests the threshold against them; the nearest thing to it is the qualitative invariance observation across five models spanning 224-448 px and 10x10-32x32 patches, with no test statistic and no effect size, which if anything reports that the threshold does NOT vary with resolution or patch count. Its one per-patch quantity is a DESIGN parameter and not a measured frequency: "the maximum digit capacity for a single image patch, specifically setting at six digits for Fuyu-8B and three digits for the remaining models." A knee found by eye on a sampling-density axis and a criterion crossing on a frequency axis are different quantities, however much the word "threshold" is shared. What it DOES occupy is the patch-boundary leg: it put the patch-grid question inside the target field in Feb 2024 with patch sizes tabulated AND swept the boundary offset, with the counter-intuitive direction that uncut targets read worse, so the candidate can claim that leg only on the terms set out under the promotion conditions below.
2. From 2606.07861: RT_X is a criterion-based threshold, and it is printed per model for 18 models, but it sits on a pixel-SIZE axis for a complex target at a single contrast; it cannot separate a contrast-limited from a sampling-limited failure, cannot detect aliasing, is never divided by the patch pitch or expressed in any patch unit, and runs no predictor comparison — confirmed at full text on the post-batch pass, which found Sec. 2 treating input resolution as background only, Sec. 4.2 analysing failures against target size rather than input resolution, and Sec. 4.3 ablating scoring and decoding rather than resolution. Its reported instantiation is X = 50, not a 75%-correct 2AFC criterion; its readout is multi-way strict exact match with chance neither named nor corrected for; and Table 1 prints no CIs, error bars or seeds. A size threshold on a complex target is not a cutoff frequency in cycles per image or per encoder patch, and on this ledger a figure in the wrong unit is as wrong as a missing one. The paper also carries an internal tension that favours the candidate rather than killing it: its headline is UNCRITERIONED ("perception saturates around 12px" in the abstract, "in 12px, perception tasks are already close to saturation" in Sec. 4.1, "12 pixels" in Sec. 5) while the only threshold it defines puts 16 of its own 18 models above 12.0 px, median about 18.4 — the checker's own arithmetic on a table that prints no uncertainty, not a figure the paper states.
3. From 2508.10367: same instrument family, different measurand. Detection of bandpass noise at a 50%-"yes" criterion on a cycles-per-degree axis under a display-referred stimulus geometry (256x256 px at 64 px/deg), with no cutoff, no printed numeric per-model peak, and no mention of patch size, resize kernel, tiling, aliasing, interpolation or Nyquist anywhere in the full text including appendices; prediction tested on Imagenette under two perturbations — bandpass suppression in the Fourier domain and added frequency-specific noise, both calibrated to constant RMSE — on two models, InternVL3-2B and InternVL3-8B, never against resolution or patch count. Its numerator is "yes" responses with an unconstrained yes-bias that Eq. 1's P(0) = 0 does not model and its own Sec. 3.2 prompt-sensitivity result puts under strain; the candidate's is correct forced-choice orientation/phase trials. Recorded as the checker's OWN ARITHMETIC and not as the paper's: 64 px/deg puts the stimulus sampling Nyquist at exactly 32 cpd, the top of the paper's stated 0-32 cpd range, so the paper bounds its own stimuli at Nyquist silently in the generator and never for the model — which tells against anyone arguing that it implicitly handles sampling.

Novelty confidence: Medium — at the floor of Medium, and stated against the record's own pre-declared trigger, which is a LOW trigger and not a Reject trigger, and which has already FIRED. Gate 2 wrote that prior 2's full text would move the grade to Low if it "defines a criterion-based threshold"; adversary 1 read it and RT_X fires that disjunct, the post-batch pass confirmed the disjunct at full text with the per-model numbers now in hand, and 2402.07384 fires a second one Gate 2 never considered. The grade survives at Medium on the number test and on the unit test together: no opened source prints the candidate quantity. 2508.10367 prints rho and RMSE for a 50%-detection threshold, no cutoff and no numeric per-model peak; 2606.07861 prints mean RT50 in px for 18 models, 7.3 to 24.8, against a criterion defined at Eq. 3 — a threshold on target SIZE, never normalised to a patch and never set against resolution or token count; 2402.07384 prints the number 8 as a rendering font size, an uncriterioned legibility knee on a sampling-density axis. A criterion threshold in pixels of target size and a knee in pixels per glyph are an axis-and-unit gap, not the candidate's cutoff frequency, and three near-neighbours each one axis away compress the margin without closing it. What would move it to Low: any source printing a criterion-defined frequency cutoff, a cycles-per-patch quantity, or a cross-arm regression of a measured limit against pixel and token count. Two of the four returns nominated for that role are now OPENED and neither carries one — arXiv:2608.05122 (Mohan V. B., Naganoor V., Annadani Y., Hegde S., "IRIS: A Visual Cortex-Inspired Framework for Analyzing Orientation Selectivity in Vision Transformers", 2026, v2, cs.CV, no DOI and no venue, so a preprint and not a published prior) at FULL TEXT, whose only frequency number is a sub-Nyquist stimulus-generator cap over frozen-backbone ACTIVATIONS, and arXiv:2104.11222 (Parmar G., Zhang R., Zhu J.-Y., "On Aliased Resizing and Surprising Subtleties in GAN Evaluation", v3, 21 Jan 2022 — so the entry's implicit 2021 was the v1 year only) at PARTIAL, which prints FID/KID/PSNR deltas per resize implementation and no aliasing magnitude at all. arXiv:2606.03795 (spectral accessibility in vision representations) and arXiv:2503.23667 (OCR vs image resolution) remain UNOPENED, and are not scored either way. The one live route to Low the pass could not take is the TMLR camera-ready of 2402.07384, OpenReview D8MjYW8m35: COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND, and if it added a contrast or spatial-frequency analysis then limbs (i) and (ii) fall and this entry becomes a Reject. High is unavailable under any reading.

Significance — consequence: if the cutoff sits below the nominal limit and survives limb (iv), the fine-detail failures demonstrated in 2407.06581 (on its own 7-task synthetic suite, four closed API models of mid-2024) and thresholded in 2606.07861 — whose 12 px headline is uncriterioned while its criterion-defined mean RT50 runs 7.3 to 24.8 px across 18 models, median about 18.4, so "localised near 12 px" overstated what that paper pins down — become attributable per arm to pathway information loss rather than reasoning, and model-card figures are shown to be nominal; design attention moves to the resampling and tiling stages, and benchmark builders get an item-level admissibility test. If cutoffs sit at the nominal limit with no incremental predictive information, nominal reporting is vindicated — a clean negative made plausible by the published resolution nulls.
Significance — audience: evidenced on an opened source rather than on titles — 2402.07384 is a target-field group measuring a pixels-per-glyph legibility knee, patch-boundary alignment and target location across five MLLMs, tabulating patch sizes, and then naming the attribution problem limb (iv) addresses; and 2606.07861 is a second such group, now with a printed per-model criterion threshold (mean RT50, 18 models) that teams could use instead of a cutoff, which is why adversary 1's inflation objection stays open rather than resolved. Secondarily: resolution-policy teams (Res-Bench, CARES, Task-Aware Resolution Optimization, ICLR 2026 adaptive patching — titles only, opened by nobody), eval builders who cannot currently separate loss from reasoning, and the machine-psychophysics group that owns the instrument and has no engineering axis on it.
Significance — fecundity: cardinal-vs-oblique cutoff asymmetry as a signature of the patch lattice — unoccupied, and now POSITIVELY CHECKED as unoccupied at one level rather than merely unopened: IRIS (arXiv:2608.05122), the second adversary's nomination as the likeliest unopened carrier, was opened at full text and is genuinely the right KIND of document (a parametric orientation-by-spatial-frequency Gabor battery, 36 orientations and five log-spaced frequencies, over eight backbone families), and it prints NO cardinal-versus-oblique asymmetry on any axis for any of OpenCLIP, DeiT III, DINOv2, DINOv3, MAE, AIMv2, MetaCLIP or SigLIP 2, while its unit of analysis is the activation of an internal unit ("For all readout bases, responses are averaged over patch tokens to obtain a single response per stimulus.") and not model output, so it does not reach the candidate's measurand however much "orientation" its title carries; non-occupancy is therefore checked at the frozen-backbone-activation level and remains UNCHECKED at the shipped-VLM behavioural level, which no source opened by anyone touches. Also: phase-dependent anisotropy at tile seams; whether post-training moves the cutoff with the encoder frozen; whether a cutoff-matched pre-filter removes aliasing-driven errors with no model change; a scaling law of cutoff against vision-token budget, where this meets arXiv:2602.02539.
Significance — anchoring: 2407.06581's low-level failures, with its resolution null scoped to three of seven tasks over a one-sided 384-1155 px canvas range and its best model deviating in both directions, and its line-width effect carried in both of that paper's conflicting formulations; 2606.07861's perception/reasoning dissociation with no mechanism, and the internal tension between its uncriterioned 12 px headline and its own criterion-defined RT50 column; 2402.07384's measured patch-boundary effect, which is an interface phenomenon with no instrument and whose direction (uncut targets read worse) nobody has explained; 2508.10367's finding that models match the human CSF in shape or in scale but never both.

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary, in the sharper form the adversaries forced. The instrument belongs to imaging metrology and psychophysics, and both corroborated queries show metrology asking the predictive question of a CAMERA front-end, because that is what its charts attach to; psychophysics reached shipped MLLMs in 2025 but brought vision science's question (is the CSF human-like) and so never mentions resize kernels. The architecture community reports nominal configuration because that is what it sets and ships. The residue is specific, and the post-batch pass narrows it: it is the patch NORMALISATION that nobody owns, and the criterion on a FREQUENCY axis — a criterion-defined threshold as such is owned, by 2606.07861, on a pixel-size axis at one contrast (Eq. 3, RT50 for 18 models), so the entry can no longer say that nobody owns a criterion. Nor may it imply that the patch-lattice aliasing boundary is unremarked in print: IRIS Sec. 3.1 names patch-wise Nyquist as a real operating boundary for ViT grating stimuli and bounds its own stimuli below it. What stays unremarked is the magnitude. Adversary 2's correction stands and is recorded — 2402.07384 had both halves in hand in Feb 2024 (patch sizes tabulated, an uncriterioned pixels-per-glyph threshold printed, a patch-boundary effect measured) and did not join them, which is as consistent with low perceived payoff as with a boundary, and the published resolution nulls keep that explanation live. The secondary new-object mechanism (content-independent but dimension-driven dynamic tiling, roughly two years old, making the front end a non-trivial resampler) is intact and dated, but it excuses only the engineering normalisation, not behavioural probing, which 2508.10367 shows was feasible by 2025.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness is downgraded from the record's 3/3 on converging sourced findings from both adversaries, and the cap is HELD at 2/3 by the post-batch pass on four opened repositories, though for a narrower and partly different reason than the entry first gave: limbs (i), (iii) and (iv) are pinned, but limb (ii)'s denominator is ambiguous by a factor of two per axis wherever a merge or pixel-shuffle step exists — not universally, LLaVA-1.5-7B having one grid and exactly one defensible interval — the deeper obstacle being that the PRINCIPLED lattice differs by family, so that no population-wide denominator has a family-neutral justification; and limb (iii)'s wording conflates "above 0.5 cycles/patch" with "aliased". The question is not ill-posed — the repair is a declaration, not an argument — but the one permitted reformulation is already spent, so it cannot be made inside V2. Significance 2/3 stands: consequence, fecundity and anchoring are argued on opened sources, and the audience is now evidenced on an opened source rather than on titles, with the deduction kept for limb (iv)'s realistic power at tens of arms.

Strongest remaining objection: limb (ii)'s denominator is not one quantity wherever a merge or pixel-shuffle step exists. Confirmed at the post-batch pass from four opened repositories, three named families. Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct prints "patch_size": 14 and "spatial_merge_size": 2 as separate, co-equal fields in vision_config, marking neither lattice as "the" grid, and the Qwen2.5-VL technical report (arXiv:2502.13923v1, Sec. 2.1, read PARTIAL) prints "During both training and inference, the height and width of the input images are resized to multiples of 28" — so 2D-RoPE is indexed on the 14-px lattice while the language model receives tokens on the 28-px one. OpenGVLab/InternVL2_5-8B and OpenGVLab/InternVL3-8B both print "image_size": 448, vision "patch_size": 14 and "downsample_ratio": 0.5, giving 32x32 = 1024 patches per tile pre-shuffle against 16x16 = 256 post-shuffle (the products and quotients are the checker's own arithmetic; the configs print none of them), and they print IDENTICAL values on every grid-bearing field, so citing both is one test and not two. So "the nominal patch-Nyquist limit set by patch size and positional-encoding resolution" is ambiguous by exactly the factor that decides whether the headline reads "the cutoff sits far below nominal" or "at nominal" — but the entry's universal quantifier is STRUCK: llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf/preprocessor_config.json, read at FULL TEXT, carries no merge, pixel-shuffle, downsample or tiling field at all, so LLaVA-1.5-7B has ONE grid and one defensible interval. The second term is CORRECTED, not merely narrowed: the pitch is NOT undefined for the axial-RoPE family — it is printed twice, "patch_size": 14 and "spatial_patch_size": 14, with the 28-px resize rule in the report, and 2D-RoPE SELECTS the pre-merge lattice rather than dissolving it, so that leg's valence was inverted as the entry had written it. What is genuinely undefined for that family is the grid EXTENT — the preprocessor config has no "size" key at all and the only spatial bounds are min_pixels 3136 and max_pixels 12845056 — and the pitch in SOURCE-image coordinates, the resize scale being per-image. The dynamic-tiling leg is meanwhile stronger than the entry had it: InternVL's "use_thumbnail": true with "max_dynamic_patch": 12 puts the whole image into one additional 448-px tile in the same forward pass, so a single image carries several sampling intervals at once (up to 13 x 256 = 3328 tokens at mixed scales, the checker's arithmetic) and the interval is well defined only per (model, image, tile) — a factor of two is not a description of a multi-scale pyramid. The sharpest statement of the Gate 1 defect is therefore family-neutrality: the principled lattice differs by family — RoPE-indexed pre-merge for Qwen2.5-VL, post-pixel-shuffle for what InternVL's language model reads, a single lattice for LLaVA-1.5 — so no population-wide denominator has a family-neutral justification; and nothing opened MEASURES the quantity, the configs and the report defining and bounding the lattice while printing no cycles-per-patch or cycles-per-pixel figure of any kind. Kept strictly as read failures and not as findings: Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct was COULD NOT READ (one curl attempt refused at the proxy before any transfer, no WebFetch spent), which is not evidence that the 3B differs; LLaVA-1.5's patch_size is NOT in the file opened, so the 24x24 lattice at 14 px pitch is the checker's inference from the ViT-L/14 backbone, flagged as such rather than supplied from recollection, and it lives in llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf/config.json, unopened; the InternVL2.5 and InternVL3 technical reports were NOT READ, so their position-encoding schemes are asserted no further than the configs print. This objection has three legs and the verdict stands on the first only: (a) the printed-config two-grid ambiguity together with the family-neutrality obstacle, read directly from shipped configuration source, which survives alone; (b) the argument that the patch stage is not a sampling limit at all, which would survive the loss of (a) but is weaker and is flagged below; (c) the Disguise finding (2402.07384), which narrows novelty and occupies the patch-boundary leg without publishing any candidate quantity, and could not sustain the objection by itself.
Vulnerability of leg (b), recorded because it rests on nothing anybody has measured: both adversaries reach it by design-level reasoning, not from a reported result. A1 argues from modeling_clip.py that a Conv2d with kernel = stride = patch is a lossless re-blocking followed by a linear map; A2 counts 3 x 14 x 14 = 588 values into hidden_size 3584 from printed defaults and labels the arithmetic its own. That is an ALGEBRAIC identity about what a dimension-non-decreasing map can in principle preserve — not a bitwise or empirical demonstration, and explicitly not a claim about the trained weights. Whether the learned patch projection is full-rank, and how much sub-patch structure survives attention and the 4:1 token merge (2352 values into out_hidden_size 3584), is unmeasured by anything either adversary opened, and is close to what the candidate would itself measure. Single unopened source most likely to settle it: arXiv:2606.03795, "Beyond Compression: Quantifying Spectral Accessibility in Vision Representations", nominated by kind — a document that would print band-wise recoverability from vision-encoder representations — and from its title only. Leg (b) was NOT re-checked at the post-batch pass: no checker opened arXiv:2606.03795, and nothing any checker read measures sub-patch recoverability, so leg (b) stands exactly where the two adversaries left it, as design-level reasoning.
Promotion requires: all five of (1) one fetch of the TMLR camera-ready of the Feb-2024 prior — Zhang J., Hu J., Khayatkhoei M., Ilievski F. & Sun M. (2026), "Exploring Perceptual Limitations of Multimodal LLMs on Small Visual Objects", Transactions on Machine Learning Research, OpenReview D8MjYW8m35 — which is COULD NOT READ at the post-batch pass (openreview.net/pdf?id=D8MjYW8m35 returned a site client_error with nothing retrieved) and postdates the arXiv text by two years under a revised title, so that if it added a contrast or spatial-frequency analysis then limbs (i) and (ii) fall and this entry becomes a Reject; that fetch should happen before the entry is closed either way, and until it is made the camera-ready is scored neither way; (2) a re-graded novelty line that survives the record's own fired Low trigger on the number-and-unit test rather than by omission, with arXiv:2606.03795 opened — arXiv:2608.05122 was opened at full text at the post-batch pass and came back empty on the orientation limb, so that half of the old condition is discharged; (3) a DECLARED denominator for limb (ii), written into the entry text and naming all three of the lattice (e.g. cycles per pre-merge patch), the input size or resize policy, and the tiling-and-thumbnail policy for the InternVL members, with an explicit note that "pre-merge" degenerates to the only lattice for LLaVA-1.5 and that this is a declaration and not a measurement, since nothing opened prints any cycles-per-patch figure — and the positional-encoding term dropped not as "no PE grid" but as the grid EXTENT and source-pixel coordinate frame that are genuinely undefined for the native-resolution arms; (4) limb (iii) restated as a target-fixed, alias-specific manipulation with the applied kernel named per arm, promotable only on a printed aliasing MAGNITUDE referred to a stated resize kernel with its denominator — which neither IRIS nor arXiv:2104.11222 supplies, the latter printing only score deltas (FID 0.64 to 7.43 against PIL-bicubic, Table 1) — and, for its patch-boundary leg, claimable only by quantifying what 2402.07384 plots, i.e. a per-model boundary-phase effect with an interval, over more than 100 synthetic strings, outside rendered text on white; Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): the 2AFC pilot in (4) above, on two open-weight arms whose preprocessing is already printed in the sources both adversaries opened.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What ran, and what each checker was sent to read.** Six fresh-context checkers ran on this entry, each blind to the reviewers' reasoning and each required to re-read a load-bearing source first-hand rather than grade the entry's summary of it. The first was sent to arXiv:2402.07384 — the close prior Gate 2 never returned and adversary 2's moiré query found — to test the entry's three surface predicates (a printed threshold, tabulated patch sizes, a measured patch-boundary effect) and the candidate's four limbs against it; this was the highest-stakes check in the batch, since the entry's novelty margin rests on what that paper does and does not print. The second was sent to arXiv:2606.07861, "The Last Visible Pixel", to test the recorded read level and the claim that it prints no criterion and no per-model number. The third was sent to arXiv:2508.10367v2, the contrast-sensitivity paper, to test the no-cutoff / no-per-model-peak / no-patch-quantity claims, the endpoint claim, the Figure 6 prediction test and the four irregularities flagged at Gate 2. The fourth was sent to the appendix of arXiv:2407.06581v4, "Vision language models are blind", to read the resolution and line-width findings at body level rather than heading level, and to test P5 and the dense-chart carve-out. The fifth was sent to shipped configuration source for limb (ii)'s denominator — the factor-of-two assertion and the axial-RoPE assertion, taken separately. The sixth was sent to arXiv:2608.05122 (IRIS), named by the second adversary as the likeliest unopened carrier of the orientation limb, and to arXiv:2104.11222 on aliased resizing. Fetch budgets used were 7+1 search, 4, 4, 7 (a declared overrun of one, spent establishing that the arXiv HTML render carries no appendix), 6+1 search, and 5. No search was refused by the classifier anywhere, and no checker touched TLS settings or HTTPS_PROXY.

**Read levels reached, with COULD NOT READ kept strictly distinct from NOT FOUND.** arXiv:2402.07384v1 was reached at FULL TEXT from the PDF (front matter, Secs. 1-5, Tables 1-3, Figs. 1-13 captions, Appendices A-E, in two targeted passes), and its abs page at FULL; its TMLR camera-ready, OpenReview D8MjYW8m35, is COULD NOT READ, so its silence on contrast and spatial frequency is evidence in neither direction. arXiv:2606.07861v1 was reached at FULL TEXT through the ar5iv mirror, Appendix C.2 (Inference Settings) being the one subsection that did not come through and therefore COULD NOT READ. arXiv:2508.10367v2 was reached at FULL TEXT including Appendices A and B, with the contested sentences returned identically on an independent second pass licensed to answer ABSENT rather than construct a plausible sentence; its companion CCN 2025 abstract is COULD NOT READ, no URL having been in hand, and nothing rests on it. arXiv:2407.06581v4 was reached at PARTIAL from the PDF, heavy on the appendix — the complete A.1-to-I heading inventory, the full bodies of B.2, D.2, E.2 and F.2, the captions of Figs. 20, 32, 37, 45 and 46 and of Table 15, Table 15's numbers and Table 1's cells — while the numeric content of Fig. 20-left, Fig. 32-left and Fig. 37-a was NOT READ (they are raster plots) and Table 1's model-row labels render as glyphs, so the row-to-model assignment in that note is a MATCH and not a read. On the configuration side, llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf/preprocessor_config.json was reached at FULL TEXT; Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct's preprocessor_config.json at PARTIAL field level (the summariser declined verbatim whole-file reproduction) and its config.json at PARTIAL (vision_config plus rope fields); OpenGVLab/InternVL2_5-8B and OpenGVLab/InternVL3-8B at PARTIAL (eleven and nine requested fields); the Qwen2.5-VL technical report, arXiv:2502.13923v1, at PARTIAL (Secs. 2.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.2.1 and the Fig. 1 caption); Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct at COULD NOT READ, which is not evidence that the 3B differs; and llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf/config.json plus both InternVL technical reports NOT READ. IRIS, arXiv:2608.05122, was reached at FULL TEXT, summariser-mediated, over three routes that are one document surfaced three ways and must not be counted as corroboration; the HTML route served v1 while the current version is v2. arXiv:2104.11222 was reached at PARTIAL (front matter, Sec. 1, Sec. 3.1, Sec. 4.1 and Table 1, figure captions), one route, the stamp read being v3, 21 January 2022, so its appendix is COULD NOT CHECK rather than empty.

**The highest-stakes check: narrowed, not struck.** All three of the entry's surface predicates about arXiv:2402.07384 survive a full-text read — a threshold is printed, patch sizes are tabulated in Table 3, and a patch-boundary effect is measured in Sec. 4.5.2 with Figs. 8-9 and Appendix A — so the prior has been promoted in the body to the nearest NAMED prior under its real title, and the adversaries were right that this is a real neighbour. What does not survive is the inference the entry drew from them. The printed threshold is the number 8 as a RENDERING FONT SIZE, Sec. 4.1 operationalising the synthetic task's sampling rate "in terms of the font size used during text creation", "which correlates with the vertical pixel count of the text characters": a pixels-per-glyph legibility knee, read off a curve with no declared criterion — the support offered is "the performance stabilized with increasing sampling rate" — at a single fixed contrast on text "overlaid on plain white backgrounds", from an open-ended generated string scored by Gestalt Pattern Matching with no alternative set and no chance level. Its denominator is one character's vertical extent in pixels: not the image, not the patch, not a degree of visual angle, there being no viewing geometry in the paper. The words Nyquist, spatial frequency, cycles per degree and cycles per patch do not appear on two full passes. So limbs (i), (ii) and (iv) — a criterion-defined cutoff frequency, a cycles-per-patch quantity, and the cutoff tested against resolution and patch count as rival predictors — are ABSENT on a full-text read, not COULD NOT CHECK, and they remain this entry's live novelty; Table 3 holds the ingredients for limb (iv) and no sentence uses them that way. Limb (iii) is the one that moves: the patch-boundary sweep is substantially OCCUPIED, with the counter-intuitive direction that uncut targets read worse — "Model's performance is lower when target objects remain undivided by patch boundaries." — and one printed scalar, "Qwen-VL-Chat still presents an around 10 percent gap between different patch boundary cuts.", for one model over 100 random numbers per experiment, everything else being plotted. That limb has accordingly been taken out of the findings and written into the promotion conditions, and the motivating gap no longer claims the patch-boundary leg is vacant. Two quotation defects were fixed in the body: Gate 2's string cut the opening adverb of "Remarkably, the threshold of a sampling rate of 8 is consistently observed across all MLLM models.", which scopes the clause as a cross-model observation rather than a derivation, and the cut was the defect; and the entry cited that string to "Sec. 4.2 / Fig. 4 caption" when the caption carries a different sentence, "from the sampling rate of 8 (marked as red), the image starts to become fully recognizable." The patch-boundary quotation was likewise restored to its full printed form from the left-cut "performance is lower when target objects remain undivided by patch boundaries".

**The declined recommendation, recorded in full.** The checker on arXiv:2606.07861 reached that paper at FULL TEXT through the ar5iv mirror and recommended moving this entry to REJECTED, on the ground that the entry had set its own rejection test — that the full text printing a criterion-defined threshold per model would occupy the candidate's limbs — and that the paper satisfies it. That recommendation IS NOT ACCEPTED, for three reasons, two of which are misreadings of this entry's own record and the third of which the same check establishes against itself. First, the trigger is a LOW trigger, not a Reject trigger, and it had ALREADY FIRED before the pass began: the entry's novelty line records that Gate 2 wrote this prior's full text would move the GRADE TO LOW if it "defines a criterion-based threshold", that adversary 1 read it and RT_X fires that disjunct, and that the grade nonetheless survives at Medium on the number test because no opened source prints the candidate quantity. The entry books the trigger as fired; the checker read it as an unfired Reject condition. Second, the read level was already FULL TEXT: the entry records prior 2 as read at full text via the alphaxiv .md mirror by adversary 1, abstract-only at Gate 2, and COULD NOT READ at five arXiv routes — so the "one-fetch budget failure" charged against the entry is not what the entry records. What the entry DID record as not done is the TRANSCRIPTION of the RT50/RT80 values, and that is exactly the residual the check closed. Third, the measurand is different, as the check itself establishes: RT50 is a criterion threshold on a pixel-SIZE axis at a single contrast, and the same check confirms the paper has NO patch-unit normalisation, NO contrast or spatial-frequency axis, and NO comparison of a perceptual limit against input resolution or token count as rival predictors. A size threshold on a complex target is not a cutoff frequency in cycles per image or per encoder patch, and on this ledger a figure in the wrong unit is as wrong as a missing one. The checker erred on the first two points and the entry carries its own record rather than the checker's version; the entry's prose has nonetheless been corrected everywhere the check found it wrong.

**What that check does deliver, and the entry now carries.** The open residual is CLOSED. Table 1, the "FineSightBench leaderboard", prints mean RT50 in px for 18 models, 7.3 (Gemma-4-31B) to 24.8 (Qwen3-VL-2B), against the criterion defined at Equation 3 in Sec. 3.3 — "Given a target accuracy threshold X in (0,100), we define RT_X as the smallest target size at which the accuracy reaches X%:" — reported at X=50, on strict exact-match accuracy with no chance correction, under the censoring convention s_max+1, with no CIs, no error bars and no seeds in the table. The size sweep is seven discrete levels (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px), the author list and date are confirmed as the entry had them, and the entry's "Table 6" for the 18-model table is withdrawn in favour of Table 1. The entry's "localised near 12 px" is CORRECTED: the 12 px headline is uncriterioned in all three places it appears (abstract "perception saturates around 12px", Sec. 4.1 "in 12px, perception tasks are already close to saturation", Sec. 5 "12 pixels") while the paper's own RT50 values sit mostly well above it — 16 of 18 above 12.0, median about 18.4, the checker's own arithmetic on a table printing no error bars — an internal tension that favours the candidate rather than killing it, and which the anchoring line now names. The route that worked is recorded for later passes: ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/<arXiv id>, served on the first attempt after five arXiv routes had failed across three agents, with arxiv.org/pdf returning RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED again at this pass.

**Prior 1, the contrast-sensitivity paper: held, with three narrowings and one reclassification.** The claim holds on its load-bearing parts — no cutoff is printed, no numeric per-model peak is printed, the strings cutoff, cut-off, patch, Nyquist, alias, resize, tiling and interpolat are all absent from the full text including appendices, the psychophysical endpoint is the yes-proportion ("we computed the proportion of affirmative responses (i.e., yes answers).") and Figure 6 is as described. Narrowing one: "responses not scored correct/incorrect" is STRUCK, because Sec. 5 and the whole of Figure 6 run on classification accuracy ("Accuracy values are reported relative to performance on unaltered images."), so what is true is that the PSYCHOPHYSICAL endpoint is never a correctness score while correctness appears as the predicted variable. Narrowing two: "no per-model peak frequency" is narrowed to no printed NUMERIC per-model peak or cutoff, since the paper argues from per-model peaks qualitatively and makes them its central result ("the largest accuracy reductions occur at frequencies where the model shows peak sensitivity") and plots them in Figs. 3 and 6 — which sharpens the contrast with the candidate rather than weakening it. Narrowing three: "no patch-normalised quantity" survives as worded, but the entry now says that the paper does print resolution quantities, stimulus-side and display-referred (256x256 px at 64 px/deg), normalised to nothing about the model. The reclassification: the Weibull item is not an internal inconsistency, because reading a Weibull CDF at 50% requires no transform; it is an UNSTATED ASSUMPTION — Eq. 1 pins P(0) = 0, a zero false-alarm rate, with no guess-rate or bias term — and the paper's own Sec. 3.2 prompt-sensitivity result puts it under strain. Two of the remaining three irregularities are confirmed and strengthened: 10 appears in both Sec. 2.2 and Sec. 2.3 against the 25 of Sec. 2.1, so 25 is the likelier stray and the trial denominator behind every psychometric fit is ambiguous by a factor of 2.5; and the unnamed "proprietary model included for illustrative comparison" is a dangling reference, Table 1 printing eight named rows and no proprietary row. The fourth (a caption describing absent bolding) was NOT re-checked and is scored neither way. Both figures the record carries from Table 1 verify exactly (Qwen2.5VL-3B rho = 0.86; LLaVA-1.5-7B RMSE = 109.8) and the units are indeed unstated. One point added as the checker's OWN ARITHMETIC and not the paper's: 64 px/deg puts the stimulus sampling Nyquist at exactly 32 cpd, the top of the paper's stated range, so the paper bounds its own stimuli at Nyquist silently in the generator and never for the model.

**"Vision language models are blind": the resolution finding narrowed on four axes, and a heading replaced by a result sentence.** The entry had cited a heading as a result. The body is narrower in four separate ways, all now in the prose: the finding covers three of seven tasks (Tasks 3 and 5 are rendered at a fixed 512 px and 1000 px, so no sweep exists for them, and appendices G and H analyse none of the canvas sizes Tasks 6 and 7 do use); the sweep is {384, 769, 1155} px and {384, 768, 1152} px, a one-sided 3x range with nothing below 384 px; the best model is the exception in two of the three experiments with the sign flipping between them, "Sonnet-3.5 slightly performs worse at 769 and 1155px compared to 384px" in B.2 against "Sonnet-3.5 performs better as the image size increases (a)" in the Fig. 37 caption; and the sweep re-renders the scene at each canvas size rather than varying the pixels available for a fixed rendered detail, which is flagged in the entry as the CHECKER'S OWN INFERENCE from the construction wording and not as anything the paper states. The result sentence now replaces the heading — "Based off these results, we conclude that VLMs' ability to see the intersection of two circles does not depend on the quality of the image." — and Fig. 37's null is quoted with the words that scope it, "For most models, resolution (a) and colors (b) have minimal impact on performance.", a cut of which to "resolution ... have minimal impact on performance" would drop the exception class. NO per-resolution number is printed anywhere in B.2, D.2 or F.2: the comparison exists only as plotted points, so on resolution the paper measures the quantity and does not print it. The line-width effect HOLDS and the entry now carries BOTH of the paper's own formulations, which conflict — E.2's body, with Table 15's printed numbers (Sonnet-3.5 90.00 / 91.25 / 95.00 and GPT-4o 58.75 / 56.25 / 52.50 over 3/4/6 px, 40 images per cell by the checker's arithmetic), against Table 15's own caption, "Line thickness has minimal effect on VLMs' performance, suggesting that visual attributes of shapes are not critical to VLMs when asked to count the shapes." P5 holds with its regime spelled out, and 58.57% is now stated as an unweighted mean of task-column means over 32 cells rather than an accuracy over the 4,764-item pool. The dense-chart carve-out HOLDS and is strengthened from "unverified" to a positive confirmation that the paper contains no dense-chart task, so it is silent there rather than negative. The appendix labels are corrected from "0.B.2" and "0.E.2" to B.2 and E.2, and the entry's "ACCV 2024" is now marked UNVERIFIED by this read — not contradicted, not confirmed, no DOI having been printed in anything served.

**Limb (ii)'s denominator: cap held, finding narrowed, axial-RoPE leg struck and replaced.** Four repositories covering three named families were opened and the ambiguity is REAL in three of the four: Qwen2.5-VL-7B has a pre-merge 14 px grid against a post-merge 28 px one, with 2D-RoPE indexed on the 14-px lattice while the language model receives tokens on the 28-px one; InternVL2.5-8B and InternVL3-8B each give 32x32 = 1024 patches per tile pre-shuffle against 16x16 = 256 post-shuffle, and print identical values on every grid-bearing field, so citing both is one test and not two. But LLaVA-1.5-7B has ONE grid and exactly one defensible interval, so the entry's universal quantifier overshot and has been narrowed to "wherever a merge or pixel-shuffle step exists". The axial-RoPE leg was WRONG AS WRITTEN and on one point pointed the wrong way, and it is struck and replaced: the pitch is printed twice in vision_config and the 28-px resize rule is printed in the technical report, so it is not undefined; what is undefined is the grid EXTENT (no "size" key, only min_pixels / max_pixels) and the pitch in source-image coordinates; and 2D-RoPE SELECTS the pre-merge lattice rather than dissolving it, so for Qwen2.5-VL it is an argument FOR the 14-px denominator. In its place the entry now carries the family-neutrality obstacle, which is sharper and is what actually blocks promotion, together with a strengthened dynamic-tiling leg: InternVL's thumbnail plus up to twelve tiles means one image carries several intervals at once, so the interval is well defined only per (model, image, tile), and a factor of two does not describe a multi-scale pyramid. Nothing opened MEASURES the quantity — the configs and the report define and bound the lattice and print no cycles-per-patch or cycles-per-pixel figure — so the repair remains a declaration and the entry says so. Kept as read failures and not as findings: Qwen2.5-VL-3B was COULD NOT READ, and LLaVA-1.5's patch_size is not in the opened file, so the 24x24 lattice is flagged as the checker's inference from the ViT-L/14 backbone rather than supplied from recollection. The checker also notes, and the entry accepts, that two reviewers reading the same four config files is one document set examined twice and not two independent sources.

**The orientation limb, and the aliasing boundary.** The orientation limb — carried in this entry under limb (i)'s orientation and phase variables and in the fecundity line as cardinal-versus-oblique asymmetry, and labelled "limb (ii)" by the checker that tested it — is now positively checked rather than left as an unopened nomination. IRIS, arXiv:2608.05122, named by the second adversary as the most likely unopened carrier, was opened at full text and is genuinely the RIGHT KIND of document: a parametric orientation-by-spatial-frequency Gabor battery, 36 orientations and five log-spaced frequencies, over eight backbone families. The nomination was therefore justified by kind and not a guess, and it came back EMPTY: no cardinal-versus-oblique asymmetry on any axis for any of OpenCLIP, DeiT III, DINOv2, DINOv3, MAE, AIMv2, MetaCLIP or SigLIP 2. Its unit of analysis is the activation of an internal unit — "For all readout bases, responses are averaged over patch tokens to obtain a single response per stimulus." — and not model output, so it does not reach the candidate's measurand however much "orientation" its title carries, and all of its models are bare frozen backbones with no text output, no VQA and no captioning. Non-occupancy is accordingly now POSITIVELY CHECKED at the frozen-backbone-activation level and remains UNCHECKED at the shipped-VLM behavioural level, which no source anybody opened touches. One narrowing the entry has taken: it may no longer imply that the patch-lattice aliasing boundary is unremarked in print, because IRIS Sec. 3.1 names patch-wise Nyquist as a real operating boundary for ViT grating stimuli — "the upper bound is kept below the patch-wise Nyquist frequency to avoid aliasing" — which BOUNDS the mechanism as a confound to design around rather than measuring it; its only frequency number, 0.75*P/2 cycles per image, is a stimulus-generator cap with no criterion attached, and the band at and above patch-wise Nyquist, where a lattice-induced behavioural cutoff would have to live, is designed out of that experiment. arXiv:2104.11222 supplies no aliasing magnitude either, only FID/KID/PSNR deltas per resize implementation (FID 0.64 to 7.43 against PIL-bicubic, Table 1), round-trip PSNR being a reconstruction-fidelity proxy and not an aliasing magnitude. Limb (iii) therefore carries a promotion condition: promotable only on a printed aliasing magnitude referred to a stated resize kernel with its denominator. The three IRIS routes are not counted as corroboration; they are one document.

(2026), "Exploring Perceptual Limitations of Multimodal LLMs on Small Visual Objects", Transactions on Machine Learning Research, ISSN 2835-8856, OpenReview D8MjYW8m35, no DOI, with the arXiv:2402.07384v1 preprint (2024-02-12) named under its different title — the entry's "Zhang H." was wrong, the first author being Jiarui Zhang. arXiv:2606.07861 gains its full author list and v1 date and loses "Table 6" in favour of Table 1. arXiv:2508.10367v2 gains its six named authors and its front-matter date. arXiv:2407.06581v4 gains Bolton, Taesiri and Nguyen, loses the "0." prefix on its appendix labels, and has its venue marked unverified. One internal reference was also fixed: the novelty line's "prior 3's full text" named the wrong row, since the prior whose full text adversary 1 read and which prints RT_X is prior 2 in this entry's own numbering.
