ID: UQ-20261022-19
Date: 2026-10-22
Status: Rejected — Gate 2 (novelty Low, asked-but-open); independently fatal at Gate 4 (attack 2 Unresolved, adversary #2)
Domain(s): AI architecture — test-time compute, reasoning-model design and evaluation methodology

Question (canonical): Using a deployed model's thinking-budget dial as an exogenous manipulation on a fixed item set, how much of the reported accuracy-versus-reasoning-token relationship is a within-item causal dose-response and how much is between-item difficulty selection — and is a model capped at N reasoning tokens behaviourally equivalent to the same model naturally stopping at N?
Reformulation note: one Gate 1 reformulation was used and both versions are retained. The graded version splits the compound into (a) DECOMPOSITION — on a pinned item set, report the signed selection share (b_p − b_w)/b_p per difficulty stratum and per truncation convention, where b_w is the within-item slope of correctness on log reasoning tokens under forced budgets assigned WITHIN ITEM — randomly assigned or completely crossed, randomisation NOT being required and being the weaker of the two designs (the word "randomized" is struck from this entry's absence claim throughout; see the verification block) — and b_p the pooled slope on naturally emitted length over the same items; and (b) EQUIVALENCE — on items where the model naturally emits approximately N tokens, test correctness-distribution equivalence between forced-at-N and natural-at-N at a pre-declared margin.

Alternative formulations:
- Is the test-time-scaling curve a treatment effect or a selection artefact of item difficulty, and does a forced cap behave like a natural stop?
- Confounding by indication for inference compute: harder items draw longer traces and also fail more, so what share of the pooled accuracy-length slope is dose and what share is difficulty selection?

Motivating gap: intake claimed exogenous within-one-model budget variation "makes a separation available that was not available before", at read level "title + URL only; I opened nothing". The gap does not survive. Budget forcing has been an instrument since arXiv:2501.19393 (s1, Jan 2025); the within-item/between-item decomposition has been performed and printed for reasoning models on observed length; and the randomized within-item budget experiment is proposed in print, in the candidate's own field, by someone else. Post-batch verification sharpens the failure on one leg and narrows it on another: a SATURATED within-item forced-budget design is already PERFORMED — Zhou, Ling, Chen, Wang, Fan & Wang (2026), "When More Thinking Hurts: Overthinking in LLM Test-Time Compute Scaling", arXiv:2604.10739v1 (no DOI printed), §4.1.3, 32 budget levels from 500 to 16,000 tokens crossed with every problem across AIME 2024+2025, MATH-500 and GPQA Diamond — so the within-item DESIGN is not what is missing. A complete crossing identifies a within-item slope BETTER than randomisation, which is how one approximates a crossed design when saturation is unaffordable. What is missing is the REPORTED CONTRAST of the within-item slope against the pooled slope: one regression and one comparison.

Presuppositions:
- P1 the budget dial is exogenous — CONTESTED; measurand exemption declared by the candidate (dial failure is a reportable output), so not available as a presupposition kill. Not checked against provider documentation in Gate 2.
- P2 natural per-item trace length observable — TRUE (sourced): arXiv:2606.26502 uses a per-response `reasoning_token_length` field on six open-weight LRMs.
- P3 same items rerunnable at every budget, difficulty stable across repeats — TRUE (sourced): arXiv:2510.11713 reruns each sample at nine cut points; arXiv:2604.10739 at forced budgets.
- P4 an identifiable body of claims rests on the observational association — measurand exemption declared; partly answered against the candidate, since arXiv:2604.10739's headline curves are already forced-budget curves.
- P5 a capped run yields a scorable terminal answer, and conventions differ — CONTESTED and now sourced against the candidate's instrument: arXiv:2609.03633 (abstract) reports that an injected end-of-think token "does not always induce a clean answering phase", with the continuation "scaling with the reasoning tokens saved by early exit". Nominal dose is not delivered dose.
- Dial-as-numeric-token-cap (literal to the canonical wording) — FALSE for at least one major provider and UNVERIFIED for another: Gemini's current API documentation exposes categorical `thinking_level` and no numeric thinking budget, its only numeric control being a response-wide `max_output_tokens` hard cutoff returning "truncated or empty output"; arXiv:2510.11713 states closed "model APIs do not support mid-reasoning interruptions". The Anthropic `budget_tokens` page was returned by both adversaries and opened by neither.

What would count as an answer: on a pinned item set stratified by difficulty from held-out repeats, for M >= 3 models — (i) forced-budget dose-response with per-item repeats, with budgets assigned within item either at random or by complete crossing (a saturated crossing satisfies this leg and is the stronger design); (ii) the observational accuracy-versus-emitted-length curve on the SAME items; (iii) decomposition of the observational slope into within-item and between-item components, with the signed selection share per difficulty stratum and per truncation convention; (iv) a formal equivalence test of capped-at-N against naturally-N on the matched subset. Negative answer: within-item slope matches pooled and capped behaves like natural. Not an answer: another forced-budget-only scaling curve.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 27 distinct queries across the record and two adversaries — 11 at Gate 2, 9 by adversary #1 (7 of them Disguise), 8 by adversary #2 (all Disguise/presupposition vocabularies the record did not use); 13 fetch calls, 7 primary sources opened. Full lists in batches/2026-10-22-1833/UQ-20261022-19-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative:
- "within-item fixed effects decomposition pooled slope selection on difficulty reasoning tokens causal dose-response language model" (econometrics vocabulary) → arXiv:2606.26502, the decisive hit.
- "forced reasoning budget versus natural chain-of-thought length same items accuracy per token test-time scaling" (mandatory own-field own-words title query) → 2507.14417, 2604.10739, 2603.08462, 2508.17196, 2601.09855; no decomposition, no matched equivalence test.
- "what fraction of accuracy-length association explained by item difficulty reasoning LLM variance decomposition published estimate" (mandatory already-computed-quantity query) → no published signed selection share surfaced.
- "psychometrics within-person versus between-person response time accuracy decomposition speed-accuracy tradeoff item level" and, independently, speededness / response-signal-paradigm queries → the method family (Mundlak within-between; imposed versus self-paced administration) is mature outside AI, which is why the AI-side import was findable at all.
- `"Injected" "</think>" doesn't cleanly halt LRM reasoning arxiv` (adversary #2) → resolved the record's identifier-less aiweekly alert to arXiv:2609.03633.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. arXiv:2606.26502 (2026), "Humans Disengage, Reasoning Models Persist: Separating Difficulty Registration from Deliberation Allocation", Wang, Han-yu — SOLE AUTHOR, NO AFFILIATION PRINTED, submitted 25 Jun 2026, v5 dated 2026-09-13, no DOI printed (the identifier is the arXiv ID). The author line was read FIRST-HAND from the /abs front matter by the post-batch verification pass, on the one route this entry had left untried; the earlier "University of Hong Kong" is NOT available from that route and is struck rather than carried, since arXiv's /abs page for this paper lists no affiliation. FULL TEXT, PDF route, opened independently three times by the record and the two adversaries, plus /abs front matter and the v5 HTML body at verification. Unit = attempt/trial; endpoint = binary correctness on log deliberation; comparator = within-item against between-item slope, and LRMs against humans; estimand = within/between slopes via a Mundlak re-parameterisation. Regime: six open-weight thinking LRMs plus DeepSeek-V3 against humans on H-ARC (400 items / 4,091 trials), Cortes (86 / 20,052), INTUIT (144 / 1,536); no experimenter-set budget; instrument = OBSERVED duration under THREE operationalisations of one construct, not one — `reasoning_token_length` for the six thinking LRMs, `total_output_tokens` for the non-thinking DeepSeek-V3 baseline, and reaction time in seconds for the humans, regressions taking the log. The data are a REANALYSIS of the de Varda et al. (2025) release rather than the author's own runs, under "nominally greedy decoding" (the paper's own hedge), and "Repeated stochastic samples from one model are unavailable" — so the unperformedness of the proposed experiment is structural, not incidental.
2. arXiv:2604.10739 (2026), "When More Thinking Hurts: Overthinking in LLM Test-Time Compute Scaling", first author Shu Zhou. FULL TEXT, PDF route (record only; neither adversary re-opened it). Unit = per-item flip events and model-level accuracy per forced budget; estimand = accuracy decline and flip ratio against a forced budget; one truncation convention only (force-decoded end-of-thinking delimiter plus "Wait" injection); observational arm in §4.2.9/Appendix A only (312 of 560 samples, 78% MATH-500 Level 4–5).
3. arXiv:2512.07019, "Latency-Response Theory Model", first author Zhiyu Xu. FULL TEXT, PDF route. Unit = LLM–item response; estimand = joint latent ability and latent speed with a between-LLM correlation rho; a single fixed 10,240-token ceiling, not a varied dose.
Also opened and recorded so they are not mistaken for priors: arXiv:2510.11713 ("Are Large Reasoning Models Interruptible?", Wu et al., ICML 2026, full text to 100,000 of 108,357 characters) — hard interrupts at relative cut points 0.1–0.9 of each sample's own trace against its uninterrupted accuracy, not absolute-N against natural-at-N; arXiv:2609.03633 (Koh et al., ABSTRACT ONLY) — spurious CoT termination, no accuracy number, no matched design; Chatpatanasiri, Ratthachat (2026), "Reasoning-Aware IRT: Explainable Evaluation of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models", SOLE AUTHOR, NeurIPS 2026 poster 139400, OpenReview Szz5xYoydw, no arXiv ID and no DOI found at two searches — the intake's nominated nearest neighbour, identified at last by the post-batch verification pass (the record had recorded no identifier for it). READ LEVEL: ABSTRACT ONLY, from the poster page; PAPER LEVEL **COULD NOT READ**, with openreview.net/pdf, /attachment and /forum (a browser-verification interstitial) and two api2.openreview.net routes all failing — COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND. It DOES put a reasoning-budget responsiveness slope and an IRT item-difficulty parameter in ONE LIKELIHOOD ("We propose reasoning-aware IRT, an extension in which each model's effective ability depends on baseline ability, reasoning-budget responsiveness, and overthinking curvature"), so THIS ENTRY MAY NO LONGER ASSERT that nobody has computed a difficulty-adjusted token relationship, and the blunt form of the objection ("it only fits IRT to final accuracy") is FALSE. But its unit of analysis is the MODEL, not the item — the budget term attaches to "each model's effective ability" — no sentence says the same item appears at two or more budgets; whether the budget is MANIPULATED or OBSERVED is **COULD NOT CHECK** (the earlier "on observed budgets" is struck as an unestablished claim); and it DEFINES and ANNOUNCES ("quantified reasoning-token benefits") without printing any slope, share or variance decomposition reachable at this read level. Regime: 42 unnamed language models on LiveBench alone, compute range NOWHERE STATED, estimation by "multi-pass generalized EM with post-hoc initialization refinement". So it narrows this entry's remainder without reaching its estimand, and the remainder survives RESTRICTED TO THE WITHIN-ITEM MANIPULATED-DOSE FORM; arXiv:2603.10960 (Hariri et al.) — its "budget" is the number of sampled trials N, not reasoning tokens, so not a prior at all.

Novelty — how this differs from each: against PRIOR 1 the candidate's limb (b)/(iv) genuinely differs, and so do M >= 3 models, two truncation conventions and the per-stratum signed share; but limb (i) and the forced half of (iii) do NOT differ — they are the experiment PRIOR 1 proposes in print. Against PRIOR 2 the candidate differs in requiring matched items, a formal equivalence margin, M >= 3 models and a second convention; it does not differ in ASKING whether capping and natural stopping agree, which PRIOR 2 asks and then asserts affirmatively from unmatched side-by-side groups with two tables that disagree on overlapping ranges (12K+ natural 47.3% in Table 6 against 44.7% in Table 8). Against PRIOR 3 the candidate differs on every attribute.

QUANTITATIVE LIMB — the CONTRAST is not published (NARROWED post-verification: "nowhere published" overstated a two-part absence as a whole-cloth one, and is struck in that form), and the Low grade does not rest on it: no opened source prints the candidate's signed selection share, per stratum or otherwise, and none contrasts a within-item slope against a pooled between-item slope in either the forced-budget or the naturally-emitted vocabulary. What is printed is (a) PRIOR 1 §3.3 for HUMANS on H-ARC, "a within-item slope of +0.24 and a between-item slope of -0.54", denominator 4,091 trials on 400 items — a different population; (b) PRIOR 1 Table S2 for LRMs (pooled), within-item −0.234, with the sentence "Within-item and between-item slopes differ at p < .001 in both agent groups" — so the decomposition's EXISTENCE for LRMs is printed, while the between-item cell is COULD NOT READ at three independent passes (adversary #1 records a summariser-inferred −1.214 and refuses it; adversary #2 confirms the table is misaligned in the source), and the row carries no attempt/item/model counts; (c) PRIOR 1 Figure 4a's fall from +0.241 to +0.125, which is a covariate-adjustment attenuation, NOT a selection share; (d) PRIOR 2's descriptive "78% are Level 4-5". So the priors MEASURE the two ingredient slopes (one unreadably), DEFINE the comparison, and PROPOSE the forced-budget design — they do not ANSWER it. NARROWED, because THREE of the candidate's FOUR INGREDIENTS ARE ALREADY IN PRINT and only one regression and one comparison are missing: (1) the within-item forced-budget grid — Zhou, Ling, Chen, Wang, Fan & Wang (2026), arXiv:2604.10739v1, §§4.1.3–4.1.4, 32 budgets x every problem, "For each problem at each budget, we record" (served quotation, cut by the summariser and relied on for the DESIGN only, not for any result), temperature 0, no randomisation and no printed slope; (2) the POOLED coefficient on naturally emitted length — Su, Healey, Nakov & Cardie (2025), "Between Underthinking and Overthinking: An Empirical Study of Reasoning Length and Correctness in LLMs", arXiv:2505.00127v1 (no DOI printed), Table 1, Pearson −0.1626 to −0.7248 across R1-Preview and R1-Distill on GSM8K and MATH, UNITLESS and DENOMINATOR UNSTATED, the paper not saying whether the coefficients are pooled across questions or computed within question — the very distinction this entry turns on; (3) the WITHIN-ITEM curve on naturally emitted length as a PLOT WITH NO NUMBER — Su et al. 2025, §4.1 and Figure 1, 10 samples per question ranked by length, "we observe a consistent non-monotonic trend across models and datasets", no numeric within-item slope or correlation printed; and (4) a bin-matched capped-against-natural comparison — Zhou et al. 2026, §4.2.9 and Table 6, 54.2% natural against 53.8% forced in the 6–8K bin, "Natural long-reasoning samples exhibit similar accuracy decline patterns and flip ratios", matched by token RANGE rather than on items, with no equivalence bound and no power statement, and CONFOUNDED BY DIFFICULTY on the paper's own Appendix A ("These samples tend to be harder problems (78% are Level 4-5 on MATH-500 difficulty scale)"). Sub-claim (e) is therefore NO LONGER CARRIED AS WHOLLY OPEN: a capped-against-natural comparison at bin-matched length EXISTS — confounded, un-bounded and eyeballed, but PERFORMED. The grade rests on the question having been ASKED in print, which under this ledger's Definitions is sufficient and routes the question out rather than admits it.

Novelty confidence: Low
Multi-leg kill, with the surviving leg named:
- LEG 1 (the leg the verdict stands on): arXiv:2606.26502 §4.2 — a DISCUSSION subsection titled "The value of continued work", under §4 Discussion, with Limitations a SEPARATE subsection at §4.3, so the design is posed as forward-looking future work and not as a limitation and not as something performed — proposes the candidate's central design in print, in its own field, in its own words, quoted here as the FULL PRINTED SENTENCES: "To estimate the return to further model computation, we propose a randomized reasoning-budget experiment." / "We would randomly assign runs of the same model-item pairs to different token budgets, draw repeated responses under fixed sampling settings, and use a common procedure for eliciting a final answer when reasoning ends or the budget is reached." / "Holding model and item fixed, this intervention would measure how the chance of success changes with the opportunity for further computation." / "Hu (2026) recommends manipulating trace length while monitoring accuracy." Openers intact and carried: segment 4's opener "To estimate the return to further model computation," is a PURPOSE clause naming the estimand the author wants and does not have, and the main clause asserts a PROPOSAL, not a result; the modal "would" in the second sentence governs all three coordinated verbs and the dropped remainder only ADDS design detail, so neither of this entry's two earlier cuts changed the force of its sentence — both are safe cuts, now restored whole anyway because the first names the estimand. The displayed estimand follows in the paper's own text: "With B denoting the assigned token budget, the target is" [displayed expression]. The clauses ASSERT the proposal and record no move away from it; every verb describing the experiment in the passage is conditional or future ("can be tested", "would help test", "we propose", "We would randomly assign", "would measure", "would help describe", "would thus connect") and NOT ONE is past or present perfect. The Hu sentence is Wang's CHARACTERISATION of Hu and not a read of Hu — see the Hu citation under this rejection's own vulnerability. Verified at the PDF route by the record and by both adversaries, and re-verified FIRST-HAND at post-batch verification on two further routes the entry had left untried — arxiv.org/abs/2606.26502 for front matter and arxiv.org/html/2606.26502v5 for the body, four targeted fetches, zero failed routes — where every sentence quoted above is present verbatim in v5. Adversary #2 attacked this leg directly: the arxiv.org/html/2606.26502v1 route denied the proposal, denied the Hu citation, reported a non-existent subsection and served non-matching coefficients, and the PDF route restored all of it verbatim — a route failure, not a document failure. The leg survived a genuine break attempt.

Partial only because the LRM between-item cell is unreadable.
- LEG 3 (weakest, but STRENGTHENED at verification from "asserts" to "performs-weakly"): PRIOR 2 — Zhou, Ling, Chen, Wang, Fan & Wang (2026), arXiv:2604.10739v1 — §4.2.9/Table 6 asks the capped-versus-natural question and PERFORMS a bin-matched comparison of it (54.2% natural against 53.8% forced in the 6–8K bin, "Natural long-reasoning samples exhibit similar accuracy decline patterns and flip ratios"), but matched by token RANGE and not on items, with no equivalence bound, no power statement and no TOST — "similar" is an eyeball verdict — and confounded by difficulty on its own Appendix A, in the direction that would make capped and natural look alike for the wrong reason. Its bookkeeping is also unresolved: the natural subset is 312 samples with more than 8K natural tokens per Appendix A, yet Table 6 reports natural values for the 6–8K and 8–10K bins, which verification flagged as unexplained and COULD NOT RESOLVE without the raw table. So limb (b)/(iv) is PARTLY ANSWERED, not wholly open. If LEG 3 fell entirely, limb (b)/(iv) would be the candidate's one open limb and LEG 1 would still kill the entry.
Not Medium, because LEG 1 is the design itself rather than a distant neighbour. Not Unverified: 27 queries ran and seven primary sources were opened.

Significance — consequence: if the within-item slope diverges from the pooled slope, every per-token compute-efficiency comparison fitted on observational trace lengths is a mixture of dose and difficulty selection and cross-model tokens-per-point figures stop being comparable; if it does not, the published curves are strengthened and the cheaper observational fit is licensed. Both branches actionable, but discounted: PRIOR 1 already pins the LRM within-item sign as negative against a positive human one.
Significance — audience: real and identifiable — anyone fitting or quoting per-token efficiency comparisons, serving-cost planners setting default effort levels, and the evaluation-methodology community PRIOR 1 and PRIOR 3 already write for. Not inflated; both adversaries graded attack 6 Resolved.
Significance — fecundity: whether difficulty-adaptive truncation policies are tuned on a confounded signal; whether provider effort levels are comparable units; whether capped-natural non-equivalence is a property of the stopping circuit or of the elicitation convention.
Significance — anchoring: the inverse-scaling and overthinking anomalies (2507.14417, 2604.10739), the speed-accuracy decomposition tradition PRIOR 1 imports, and the interruptibility line (2510.11713).

Reason for silence: the offered mechanism is "new instrument" (the dial newly exposed as a deployment parameter). It FAILS. Budget forcing predates the dial (s1, Jan 2025); the within-between machinery is mature in psychometrics and was imported to LRMs by PRIOR 1; the randomized within-item budget experiment is proposed in print, a second work is cited (at SECOND HAND, Hu itself being unread) as recommending the manipulation, and a saturated within-item forced-budget grid has in fact been RUN by Zhou et al. 2026 without the contrast being reported. There is no silence to explain — the question is spoken and only its execution is missing. The surviving mechanism (serving cost plus a closed-model variant check no provider documents) is an incentive-and-access explanation for why it is UNPERFORMED, not for why it was unasked. Per Gate 4 attack 7 this sends the novelty finding back to Gate 2, which is where the entry dies.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

**What the pass did.** Four checkers ran on this entry, each in fresh context and each blind to the reviewers' reasoning, re-reading load-bearing sources at first hand. Checker 1 was sent to the posing paper and its front matter — arXiv:2606.26502, to test whether the two sentences this entry rests its kill on are actually printed there, whether the experiment is performed anywhere in it, and who the author is (6 WebFetch, 0 WebSearch). Checker 2 was sent to Hu (2026, PNAS), the single source the entry had nominated as most likely to overturn the routing recommendation, with instructions to separate "recommends" from "performs" (6 WebFetch, 3 WebSearch). Checker 3 was sent to test whether the candidate's own number is genuinely unpublished — whether anyone has run a within-item forced-budget design and reported the within-item slope against the pooled slope (5 WebFetch, 3 WebSearch). Checker 4 was sent to the intake's designated nearest neighbour, "Reasoning-Aware IRT", which the record carried with no identifier and no read above title level (7 WebFetch, 2 WebSearch).

**Read levels reached, with COULD NOT READ kept distinct from NOT FOUND.** arXiv:2606.26502 (Wang, Han-yu, 2026) was reached at FULL TEXT PLUS FRONT MATTER: /abs for the author block and /html/2606.26502v5 for the body in four targeted fetches, with ZERO FAILED ROUTES and no search needed. arXiv:2604.10739v1 (Zhou, Ling, Chen, Wang, Fan & Wang 2026), arXiv:2505.00127v1 (Su, Healey, Nakov & Cardie 2025) and arXiv:2607.21433v1 (Oladri, Jawahar & Mohamed 2026) were reached at PARTIAL — the summariser over full HTML, section and table numbers as the summariser reported them, with no raw HTML seen and no junction verified by the checker, and with verbatim quotation capped near 125 characters. (2026), PNAS 123(17), e2604554123, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2604554123 is **COULD NOT READ**: the article exists and its landing page is what the PNAS index returns for its exact printed title, and not one word of Hu's own text is held here. Chatpatanasiri, Ratthachat (2026), "Reasoning-Aware IRT", NeurIPS 2026 poster 139400, OpenReview Szz5xYoydw is ABSTRACT ONLY from the poster page, PAPER LEVEL **COULD NOT READ**. arXiv:2605.16938v1 (Hu, Yueqing & Wang, Tianhong 2026) is ABSTRACT ONLY and, worse, PARAPHRASE WITH NO VERBATIM STRING AT ALL. arXiv:2610.25768 ("Truncated Reasoning Under a Budget: Evaluating System-1 Models as Decision-makers") is **COULD NOT READ**, rate-limited twice at the target. Sub-claims (c), (d) and (e) on Hu are **COULD NOT CHECK** for want of any read; whether Chatpatanasiri's budget is manipulated or observed is **COULD NOT CHECK**; Zhou et al.'s Table 6 natural-subset bookkeeping is **COULD NOT RESOLVE** without the raw table. None of these scores for or against this entry.

**What was confirmed, at first hand and verbatim.** The kill survives. Both sentences this entry carries are present verbatim in Section 4.2 of arXiv:2606.26502 itself, not in an adversary's summary: "To estimate the return to further model computation, we propose a randomized reasoning-budget experiment." and "We would randomly assign runs of the same model-item pairs to different token budgets, draw repeated responses under fixed sampling settings, and use a common procedure for eliciting a final answer when reasoning ends or the budget is reached." The grammar survives this entry's earlier cuts on both sides — the dropped purpose clause names the estimand but leaves the verb "propose", and the modal "would" governs all three coordinated verbs, so the dropped remainder only adds design detail — and no scope-setting opener reverses either sentence. The entry nonetheless now carries both sentences WHOLE, since the first names the estimand the design is for. Every verb in the passage that describes the experiment is conditional or future and not one is past or present perfect. The design is posed in print WITH THE ESTIMAND WRITTEN OUT ("With B denoting the assigned token budget, the target is") and is UNPERFORMED: no budget condition, cap or truncation appears anywhere outside the §4.2 proposal, under "These quantities are treated as behavioural measures of generated duration under nominally greedy decoding", on a reanalysis of the de Varda et al. (2025) release where "Repeated stochastic samples from one model are unavailable", and §4.3 Limitations itself calls the design "The proposed budget experiment". One precision is recorded rather than dressed up: there is no printed sentence saying "we set no token budget", so the negative is an absence plus three positive sentences, not a single declarative denial. Asked by Wang in print, still open because nobody ran it.

**Claims struck.** The word "RANDOMIZED" is struck from this entry's absence claim, in the Reformulation note's definition of b_w, in the answer spec's leg (i), and in the routing row's estimand. This was the central defect. Zhou, Ling, Chen, Wang, Fan & Wang (2026), arXiv:2604.10739v1, §4.1.3, performs a SATURATED within-item forced-budget design — 32 budget levels from 500 to 16,000 tokens crossed with EVERY problem across AIME 2024+2025, MATH-500 and GPQA Diamond, at temperature 0, "For each problem at each budget, we record" (a served quotation cut by the summariser and relied on for the DESIGN only) — and a complete crossing identifies a within-item slope BETTER than randomisation, randomisation being how one approximates a crossed design when saturation is unaffordable. The entry as written set a bar the literature steps over by a superior route and then counted the step-over as an absence; it was true on a wording artefact. Rewritten as "no one has reported the within-item against the pooled slope", it is true for the right reason. Also struck: "University of Hong Kong" as PRIOR 1's affiliation, because arXiv's /abs page for the paper prints NO affiliation and an affiliation not available from the front matter must be marked absent rather than guessed; the "author not retrieved" flag on the routing row, now resolved; and "on observed budgets" as a description of Chatpatanasiri 2026, because whether its budget is manipulated or observed is COULD NOT CHECK and the entry may not score an unread fact.

**Claims narrowed.** "Nowhere published" is narrowed to the TWO-PART ABSENCE, because three of the four ingredients are already in print: the within-item forced-budget grid (Zhou et al. 2026, §§4.1.3–4.1.4); the POOLED coefficient on naturally emitted length (Su, Healey, Nakov & Cardie 2025, arXiv:2505.00127v1, Table 1, Pearson −0.1626 to −0.7248 across R1-Preview and R1-Distill on GSM8K and MATH, unitless, denominator unstated, and the paper does not say whether its coefficients are pooled or within-question — the very distinction this entry turns on); the WITHIN-ITEM curve on naturally emitted length as a PLOT WITH NO NUMBER (Su et al. 2025, §4.1 and Figure 1, "we observe a consistent non-monotonic trend across models and datasets"); and a bin-matched capped-against-natural comparison (Zhou et al. 2026, §4.2.9 and Table 6, 54.2% natural against 53.8% forced in the 6–8K bin, "Natural long-reasoning samples exhibit similar accuracy decline patterns and flip ratios", confounded by difficulty on its own Appendix A, "These samples tend to be harder problems (78% are Level 4-5 on MATH-500 difficulty scale)"). What is missing is ONE REGRESSION AND ONE COMPARISON. Consequently sub-claim (e) is no longer carried as wholly open: a capped-against-natural comparison at bin-matched length EXISTS — matched by token range rather than on items, with no equivalence bound, no power statement and no TOST, so "similar" is an eyeball verdict — but it is PERFORMED, and only the item-matched, margin-declared form is open. The entry's remainder on difficulty adjustment is narrowed too: Chatpatanasiri 2026 DOES put a reasoning-budget responsiveness slope and an IRT item-difficulty parameter in ONE LIKELIHOOD ("We propose reasoning-aware IRT, an extension in which each model's effective ability depends on baseline ability, reasoning-budget responsiveness, and overthinking curvature"), so this entry may no longer assert that nobody has computed a difficulty-adjusted token relationship, and the blunt form of that objection is FALSE. But its unit is the MODEL and not the item — the budget term attaches to "each model's effective ability" — no sentence says the same item appears at two or more budgets, and it DEFINES and ANNOUNCES ("quantified reasoning-token benefits") without printing any slope, share or variance decomposition reachable at abstract level, over a regime of 42 unnamed language models on LiveBench alone with the compute range NOWHERE STATED. The question therefore survives as asked-but-still-open RESTRICTED TO THE WITHIN-ITEM MANIPULATED-DOSE FORM, and the routing row now names that restricted estimand. Finally, PRIOR 1's instrument line is narrowed from one operationalisation to three of one construct — `reasoning_token_length` for the six thinking LRMs, `total_output_tokens` for DeepSeek-V3, reaction time in seconds for the humans.

Domain(s): AI architecture — context-length design decisions, serving-system design, long-context evaluation. Vocabularies searched: AI serving-trace characterization, long-context ML (RoPE/YaRN extension recipes), capacity and reliability engineering (headroom / demand exceedance / right-sizing), decision analysis (option value), LLM observability and error codes, RAG-vs-long-context, public prompt/agent corpora, plus Chinese- and Japanese-language sweeps.

Question (canonical): For >= 2 open-weight model families with >= 2 announced context-length increases, and for each announced step L_prev -> L_new, measured on a named, dated, public request-length corpus C stratified by workload class (chat, coding agent, document QA, long tool-trace agent) — (a) what is the exceedance share s = P(input length > L_prev | class, C) with CIs; (b) on the exceeding stratum only, what is the task-outcome difference between serving at L_new and truncating-or-compressing to L_prev, against a retrieval-augmented truncation baseline; (c) what is the serving cost per request at L_new versus L_prev on one engine at one version; and (d) what is the short-context delta between that family's pre- and post-extension checkpoints on one pinned harness?
Reformulation note: this is the Gate 1 reformulation, the version graded; the intake version ("the share of real production requests" for closed families, with open-weight checkpoints supplying the outcome experiment) is retained in the record. Gate 1's single reformulation allowance is therefore spent, which matters below: the repair offered against the fatal clause is a second reformulation.

Alternative formulations: (1) Is the announced context window ever the binding constraint for real traffic, and what did the last doubling buy per unit of serving cost? (2) Where is the knee in the context-length cost-benefit curve when measured against deployed request-length distributions rather than synthetic long-context benchmarks?

Motivating gap: a dense how-literature (position interpolation, RoPE base scaling, YaRN, ring/flash attention, KV compression) and mature capability-at-length instruments (needle probes, effective-length suites) over an empty why — no published quantity justifies any particular announced number. Three production-trace characterizations opened in full at Gate 2 all hold per-request input lengths and none relates a length to any model's announced maximum window. NARROWED on what the late Gate 4 opened: the nearest prior, which was only abstract-deep at Gate 2, DOES relate lengths to each serving model's own context limit — Fig. 17 uses that limit as the denominator of a utilization axis — so the gap as the record worded it is partly occupied, and what remains unoccupied is the pairing of a length with an ANNOUNCED window, which that paper never prints in tokens for any of its anonymised models.

The figure LABEL of arXiv:2608.00101 Fig. 17 PRINTS "median pre-compaction context utilization is 66%". The multi-peak reading — peaks near 50%, 65-66%, 80% and near 100% of the serving model's own (unprinted) limit, which the authors read as model-specific policies — is DESCRIBED in the paper and is carried here as a description of a figure, not as a quotation of a printed series, with no numeric share printed for the near-100% peak. Independently of that paper, the trigger is documented as a configured constant in two agent frameworks: Inspect AI's default `threshold` of 0.9, and AgentScope's `trigger_ratio x context_size` capped at 0.9 with a 60%-of-window agentic hint.
- STRUCK AS AN INDEPENDENT FATAL LEG, and retained only as the observation it is (it stood here as "NEW, in neither P1-P6 — C5 ENDOGENEITY") — request lengths on a served trace are an output of a window-aware policy, not an exogenous property of demand; a served request cannot exceed the limit of the model that served it, and in the agentic class it is compacted well below it. THE MEASURAND EXEMPTION REACHES THIS CLAUSE, so attack 4 does not. Limb (a) READS "(a) what is the exceedance share s = P(input length > L_prev | class, C) with CIs", under an opener scoping every limb to a "named, dated, public request-length corpus C stratified by workload class", and no demand term — not "latent demand", not "unmet demand", not "would have failed" — appears in limb (a) or in that scoping clause. The question REPORTS the share; it does not ASSUME that the share measures latent demand. The demand reading lives in the record's INFERENCE from s — Significance below and alternative formulation (1) — and in the exogeneity observation booked at the Scores line, not in the question; so this is a well-posedness and interpretation charge, it is booked once there, and it is not charged twice as a presupposition failure. WHAT IS SOURCED ON IT: the compaction MECHANISM, now documented outside arXiv:2608.00101 in two independent frameworks' own documentation — Inspect AI, "Compaction works by monitoring model input and executing when input tokens get close to the model's context window size", with "The default threshold is `0.9` (90% of the context window)"; AgentScope 2.0.10, "If total tokens exceed `trigger_ratio x context_size`, compression activates", capped at 0.9, with the agentic hint firing "once the input tokens exceed 60% of the model context size". BOTH DEFINE A POLICY AND MEASURE NOTHING: neither prints a share of requests, a share of sessions, a length distribution or any traffic quantity on any population. WHAT IS NOT SOURCED: no published evidence was found that an input-length distribution shifted after a window increase in a model family, so the load-bearing step of this objection is AN INFERENCE, sourced nowhere — and the one paper whose title suggested it might formalise the adaptation, Tirmazi, Markelon, Bishop, Mitzenmacher, "Context Compaction Theory", arXiv:2608.01326v1 (Tirmazi, 2026), was opened and came back negative on it ("Context rot pushes agents to do context compaction even before their state reaches the context window." is a claim about a compaction trigger and says nothing about a length distribution); record it as OPENED AND NEGATIVE so no later run nominates it. Note finally that the documented trigger fires at 60-90% of the window, so the sourced mechanism censors the measurand's support at THE SCAFFOLD'S OWN THRESHOLD and not at L_prev — which sharpens this entry's own point below that a share COMPACTED is not a share EXCEEDING, and makes the objection an argument about a scaffold constant, which a restatement can pin, rather than about the window, which it cannot. P1 covers representativeness and model-mixing; nothing in the record covers truncation of the measurand's own support, and that remains true as a gap in the record's framing without being a false premise of the question.

What would count as an answer: per class and per announced step — s with CIs on the named dated corpus; the outcome difference on the exceeding stratum at L_new versus truncated-or-compressed to L_prev against a retrieval-augmented truncation baseline; serving cost per request at both settings on one engine at one version; and the short-context delta between the family's pre- and post-extension checkpoints on one pinned harness. Pre-declared negative: exceedance of a few percent, no outcome gain over truncation-plus-retrieval, and a measurable short-context cost. NOT an answer: a synthetic long-context benchmark score at L_new, nor a mean prompt length (which is what the nearest marketplace prior prints and cannot be inverted into a tail share).

Novelty — how this differs from each: against 1, the numerator is harness-triggered compaction events (fired at 50-100% of an unprinted limit) over a denominator of SESSIONS or CALLS, for closed anonymised models with no announced doubling; the candidate's numerator is requests exceeding a named open-weight family's L_prev over a denominator of requests in one class on C. Overlap runs both ways: 1 INCLUDES compactions fired at 50% and 65% utilization, far below any limit, and MISSES every request in the L_prev < n < L_new band that never triggered compaction — the candidate's entire object — along with the chat, document-QA and non-coding tool-trace classes and the announced-window anchor; it also cannot contain a request exceeding the limit of the model serving it, so it cannot hold the candidate's object even in principle. A share COMPACTED is not a share EXCEEDING — and the scaffold documentation now sourced puts the gap between the two at a configured constant rather than a rounding error: Inspect AI fires at a default 0.9 of the window, AgentScope at `trigger_ratio x context_size` capped at 0.9 with a 60% hint, and this paper's own Fig. 17 label prints "median pre-compaction context utilization is 66%". Against 2, same traffic, different statistic, no anchor: a fourfold rise in a mean neither implies nor bounds P(input > L_prev), since a Pareto-ish mixture can quadruple its mean with the tail above 128k still empty; its one tail-adjacent sentence ("Requests involving code understanding, debugging, and code generation routinely exceed 20K input tokens") carries no denominator and "routinely" is not a quantity. Against 3, a generator for systems benchmarking versus an evaluation of a product decision; it states no threshold, and re-deriving its fitted parameters at a threshold it never states is the inverse of scoring that threshold.

QUANTITATIVE LIMB — the candidate's number is NOT published, and no leg of this verdict claims it is. What IS printed, and where: arXiv:2608.00101 Sec. 1 "Context compaction is triggered in 7.8% of sessions yet affects 44% of total tokens" and "dropping over 70% of prompt tokens" (two-fragment reconstruction); Sec. 6 "7.8% of all agent sessions undergo at least one compaction event, rising to 22.6% among long-context sessions" (>100K-token prompts), "Compaction is rare at the level of an individual call, occurring in just 0.5% of the time", "the median event drops 72.8% of prompt tokens"; Sec. 5.1/Fig. 10 "prompt tokens have a median of 68K tokens per call"; Table 6, captioned "Share of total daily volume attributed to sessions that contain at least one compaction event", printing 7.8% of sessions against 44.2% of total tokens, 37.1% of LLM calls and 38.9% of tool calls; Table 4's per-turn prompt tokens, median 227.6K, P75 654.0K, P90 1.50M, mean 582.5K; and Fig. 17, captioned "Distribution of compaction trigger points", whose figure label prints "median pre-compaction context utilization is 66%". THIS ENTRY'S NOVELTY WORDING IS NARROWED HERE, because a reader who meets 22.6% alongside a bare "no source prints the exceedance share" will read the entry as simply wrong: what is unprinted is THE SHARE OF REQUESTS, SESSIONS OR TURNS EXCEEDING A MODEL'S ANNOUNCED CONTEXT WINDOW, and the compaction figures above are carried as the near neighbours it must be distinguished from — the distinguishing reason being Fig. 17's trigger peaks near 50%, 65-66%, 80% and near 100% of each model's own limit, plus the fact that every model in the paper is anonymised so no announced window can be attached to any of them. On a FULL read of Section 6 there is still no share of requests, sessions or turns hitting an announced context limit and no numeric announced window anywhere in the paper, which is why the exceedance limb is NOT occupied and novelty stays Medium rather than falling to Low. Both adversaries asked directly for the missing pieces and recorded them ABSENT: no per-call percentile beyond the median, no share of all sessions that are long-context, no model's limit in tokens, no truncation-or-rejection rate. So the record's promotion-to-High condition comes back NEGATIVE (a compaction share IS printed) without making the candidate a known: the printed quantity is a different numerator on a different denominator for a different model population, and the compaction axis is a classification that stops short of the candidate's grain — a GRANULARITY GAP, not an absence. Separately, the heavy tail in arXiv:2608.13573 is an analysis PERFORMED and labelled "not shown", which does not make the quantity a known either. Internal inconsistencies in arXiv:2608.00101 (95T vs ~44.9T tokens; 13M vs 13.5M sessions; a per-turn prompt-token median given as 160.2K in text and 227.6K in Table 4) are reproduced as served by both adversaries, so none of its composite totals is leaned on here.

Significance — consequence: either direction changes a configured number. Negligible exceedance against real cost reclassifies announced context length as a positional variable and licenses right-sizing max_model_len below the announced number with quantified residual risk — and THIS is where the endogeneity objection now lands, having been struck above as a presupposition failure, because the licence to right-size reads s as demand and that reading needs an exogeneity clause the record never states, on corpora that are model-mixed and never record which window was in force; so what is discounted is the decision inference, not the measurement; material exceedance in the agent-trace class relocates the long-context frontier from million-token documents to hundred-thousand-token tool traces.
Significance — audience: scored 2 at Gate 3 and further discounted by attack 6 in both Gate 4 rounds, all four adversaries grading it Partial. The record's audience (1), operators setting the served window, is not the party that binds in the class most likely to bind — the operative knob is the client harness's compaction threshold, which belongs to agent-harness developers, a community the record does not name. Audience (2), long-context benchmark designers, is a real named practice to change. Audience (3), release decision-makers, is conceded weak by the record. Narrowed, not emptied.
Significance — fecundity: where the knee of the length cost-benefit curve sits per class; whether exceedance is growing fast enough to justify pre-provisioning; whether truncation-plus-retrieval dominates native long context at equal cost on real request tails; the right denominator for traffic-weighted long-context capability.
Significance — anchoring: the effective-versus-announced-length anomaly; the long-context-versus-RAG debate, argued on benchmarks and not on traffic tails; the finding that TTFT grows primarily with input length; the KV-memory wall.

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary coinciding with a data boundary, plus an incentive gap. All four adversaries graded this Partial across both Gate 4 rounds, and the counterexample in the record's own nearest prior was found independently in each round — the late pair adding that the vendor itself published the short-context limb, so the mechanism must explain two counterexamples and not one: arXiv:2608.00101 holds per-call input lengths, the truncation event itself and the KV-cost argument all at once and still never relates any of them to an announced window — so "nobody holds two of them at once" fails as stated. The surviving leg is authority rather than data: the party holding the lengths cannot change the model's window, so it optimises compaction instead of auditing the window. That is a mechanism, not "no one thought of it", and the unopened agent-trace releases suggest the boundary is now dissolving.
