Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 at Gate 5 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness was 3/3 as graded at Gate 1 and is re-scored to 2 here on what Gate 4 opened, not on a change of standard; the reasons are re-stated on the late Gate 4's record rather than the first round's. Limb (b) names an interventional measurement for which NO corpus opened in this batch publishes an outcome signal of any kind — the two content-retaining chat corpora included — and the only public corpora that can be cut to the coding-agent or long-tool-trace class publish no prompt text, so the limb has no instrument on the populations the question cares about. Limb (d)'s wording assumes a pre- and post-extension CHECKPOINT PAIR that the candidate's own flagship family does not supply at either of its announced steps. And the inference from s to "realized marginal value" requires an exogeneity clause the record never states: THE EXOGENEITY POINT IS BOOKED HERE AND ONLY HERE, with its mechanism sourced (Inspect AI's 0.9 default, AgentScope's 0.9 cap and 60% hint, Fig. 17's printed 66% median utilization) and its load-bearing magnitude unmeasured by anyone and not even signed, since compaction pushes observed lengths down while a larger window invites longer histories. Significance 2/3 stands, with the audience narrowed per attack 6. Neither score is the verdict's ground; attack 4 is.

Strongest remaining objection: THE GROUND HAS BEEN COMPLETELY REPLACED, and this paragraph is the replacement rather than a restatement. The first round's two legs no longer carry it. The CONTENT leg (A1's C3 with A2's C4) keeps its premise and loses its conclusion: content-stripping is verified six for six at the release artifacts, with the structural cause printed verbatim ("Due to customer privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR), we do not have visibility into the content of the prompts"), but "cannot be re-served" is false as a universal because WildChat-1M and LMSYS-Chat-1M each publish about a million real-traffic conversations WITH content, so that leg now stands only as a narrowed, enumerative premise about public SERVING TRACES. The ENDOGENEITY leg (A2's C5) is struck as a presupposition failure altogether, because the measurand exemption reaches it. THE REDUNDANCY CLAIM THAT STOOD HERE IS STRUCK: this entry used to say that either leg independently made attack 4 Unresolved "so the fatal grade does not depend on which leg a judge prefers", and on re-testing the grade DID depend on the leg and then on neither of them. What carries the verdict now are two clauses neither first-round adversary raised, returned independently by the two late Gate 4 adversaries on two DIFFERENT parts of the question. (1) THE OUTCOME-SIGNAL GAP (adversary 3's clause C6): limb (b) presupposes that the over-L_prev stratum can be re-served at L_new and at truncated-L_prev and SCORED, and no corpus opened in this batch publishes any finish reason, truncation flag, error status or task-success signal — while the only public corpus reaching the coding-agent / long-tool-trace class says of itself "The corpus contains no prompt or response text". C6 is ASSUMED and never reported (the record's own P2: "Not tested at Gate 2"), so the measurand exemption does not reach it. (2) THE CHECKPOINT-PAIR CLAUSE (adversary 4's clause 2), which strikes the Gate 1 reformulation's own load-bearing repair: limb (d) is written as the short-context delta between "the pre- and post-extension checkpoints of that family", and for the flagship family this entry names first that pair does not exist at either announced step — 32K to 128K is training-free DCA+YaRN on one set of weights, and the 1M models branch from "an intermediate version from Qwen2.5 Base models" rather than from the released 128K checkpoint. If BOTH new grounds fell — someone opens a content-retaining, outcome-labelled agent corpus, and a defender establishes a clean base-to-extended checkpoint pair for some family — attack 4 would drop to Partial on adversary 4's independent fallback (limb (a)'s estimand censored by client-side policy on model-mixed corpora that never record the in-force window) and the correct status would be Provisional, not Validated, since attacks 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 leave Partials across both rounds and novelty is Medium with a close neighbour.

THIS REJECTION'S OWN VULNERABILITY (recorded because part of it rests on what nobody has measured):
- The content leg's universal form DID NOT SURVIVE, and this bullet records a loss rather than a risk. It was an INDUCTION over opened instances, empirical and verbatim-sourced, and its universal form ("no public corpus carries both") was exactly the kind of negative this ledger has lost entries to — it then lost it: WildChat-1M and LMSYS-Chat-1M, two dataset cards nobody at Gate 4 round 1 had opened, publish about a million real-traffic conversations each with full utterance content, timestamps and turn indices. What survives is the narrowed premise, six for six on public SERVING TRACES, named instance by instance above, with "by design" documented for Mooncake, Azure and ServeGen and withheld from BurstGPT. Two of the three repairing candidates adversary 2 had named unopened have since been opened and both came back against the repair: the reported 301,000-session Copilot agent-trace release is `GitHubCopilotCodingAgentDataset2026` and is metadata-only, and TraceLab's coding-agent corpus is text-free per its AIPerf schema page. The single unopened source still most likely to settle the content joint: SWE-chat, "Coding Agent Interactions From Real Users in the Wild", arXiv:2604.20779 — if it supplies production coding-agent requests with full prompt text plus per-request token lengths, the joint flips for one workload class. The promised "sanitized traces" of arXiv:2608.00101 Sec. 12 were not released at reading, and "sanitized" in this literature has meant length-and-hash-only, so that one remains a guess rather than a lead; note separately that Sec. 12 is inside the span the post-batch checker records as COULD NOT READ, so nothing about it is re-confirmed here.
- The endogeneity leg is PART DESIGN ARGUMENT AND PART UNMEASURED COUNTERFACTUAL — and it is no longer a leg of the verdict at all, only a limitation booked at the Scores line and in Significance. Its three components must still be kept apart. (i) "A served request cannot exceed the limit of the model that served it" is true BY CONSTRUCTION of serving — a design/definitional truth, NOT an algebraic identity over published numbers and NOT an empirical finding; it bounds the support of the observable and nothing more. (ii) The compaction rates and the sub-limit trigger distribution ARE empirical and printed (arXiv:2608.00101 Sec. 6, now read in full three times over; its Fig. 17 LABEL prints "median pre-compaction context utilization is 66%", while the multi-peak description is a reading of a figure and is not leaned on quantitatively), and the mechanism is now additionally documented in two independent frameworks that DEFINE a policy and MEASURE nothing (Inspect AI, AgentScope). (iii) The load-bearing step — that the counterfactual length distribution under L_prev differs from the observed one by enough to void s — HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED BY ANYONE: no published evidence was found that an input-length distribution shifted after a window increase in a model family, nobody has observed one workload's length distribution under two window settings, and the bias is not even signed (compaction pushes observed lengths down while a larger window invites longer histories). So this follows from how harnesses are designed, not from a reported result, and it is labelled AN INFERENCE here. THE SOURCE THIS ENTRY NOMINATED TO SETTLE IT HAS BEEN OPENED AND CAME BACK AGAINST THE CANDIDATE: TraceLab, "Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving", was nominated here as a lead by kind and not as a settler; the late Gate 4 opened the SYFI TraceLab corpus at its NVIDIA AIPerf schema page and found a corpus that records per-round token counts, model and provider but "contains no prompt or response text", with tool-call arguments stripped and no outcome, finish-reason, error or truncation field — so it does not supply the measured endogeneity, and it supplies instead one of the two new fatal grounds. STRUCK, against the candidate: the banking of arXiv:2608.13573's input lengths being "broadly stable over the year" as "weak evidence against strong endogeneity". The printed statistic is a monthly MEDIAN "staying in the thousands of tokens" on a model-mixed platform with no window anchor printed anywhere in the paper, roughly two orders of magnitude below any plausible L_prev of 128k; it is SILENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS at that threshold, not weak evidence either way, and this entry must not weigh it. (For completeness, the apparent clash with that paper's Sec. 1 contribution line "Request characteristics shift toward longer inputs and shorter outputs" was checked and is not a contradiction: on the checker's paraphrase — the summariser refused consecutive-segment reproduction, so it is paraphrase and not quotation — that sentence is about the input/output balance, inputs stable while outputs shrink.)
- NEW GROUND ONE HAS ITS OWN VULNERABILITY, and it is a single unread page. Adversary 3's C6 is overturnable by opening `huggingface.co/datasets/skein-community/coding-agent-traces`: if that corpus retains message content and carries any outcome field, C6 flips to true for the coding-agent class and attack 4 drops from Unresolved to Partial. That adversary COULD NOT READ it — its fetch returned a site client_error and retrieved nothing of the page — which is COULD NOT READ and emphatically NOT NOT FOUND, and the adversary itself logged the nominee as a guess by kind-match on title and host rather than as a verified lead. Within C6, the two joints are not equally strong: "no corpus cuttable to the coding-agent class retains prompt text" is the leg it stands on, while "no corpus publishes an outcome field" is the weaker of the two, because an LLM judge could score outcomes post hoc IF content existed.
- NEW GROUND TWO HAS ITS OWN VULNERABILITY TOO, of a different kind. A defender may answer adversary 4's clause 2 by saying that Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M are both released and may simply be CALLED the pair; adversary 4 states that escape itself and answers that the verdict then stands on its clause 6, the censoring/identification fallback, which is untouched by how the checkpoints are labelled. Two further limits on that ground, recorded so it is not overread: the "at least two open-weight families" half of the premise is UNVERIFIED rather than established, because that adversary opened no Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek or Gemma source and says so; and its Table 4 and Table 6 readings are the fetch summariser's reading of tables, NOT a verbatim transcription, and are flagged as such rather than quoted as table text.
- None of these vulnerabilities rescues the candidate as worded. The two new grounds fail independently and on different limbs — one on limb (b)'s instrument, one on limb (d)'s own repair clause — and a repair of either requires a second reformulation that Gate 1's allowance no longer permits, since the single allowance was spent on the graded reformulation itself. All of them are named so that a later run can reopen the kill rather than inherit it, and so that the one unread page that could overturn the first ground is not mistaken for a page that was read and came back empty.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open `huggingface.co/datasets/skein-community/coding-agent-traces`, which the late Gate 4 COULD NOT READ (site client_error) and which is the single page that could overturn the first new ground, then arXiv:2604.20779 and FineServe 2607.19349, and decide from them whether any public corpus can carry limbs (a) and (b) on one population with a per-request serving limit AND an outcome signal recorded. TraceLab no longer belongs on that list: it has been opened, and its corpus carries no prompt or response text, no tool-call arguments and no outcome, finish-reason, error or truncation field. Separately, whichever family is proposed for limb (d) must be checked for an actual pre- and post-extension checkpoint pair before the limb is written, since the family this entry names first supplies none at either of its announced steps. Only then consider whether a re-anchored question about the compaction ceiling rather than the announced window is the version worth posing.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — a RECOMMENDATION only, for whoever maintains ledger/routed-open-problems.md; this run makes no change to that file. Reason, in one line: NOVELTY IS NOT THE GROUND, the ground is presupposition failure, and a presupposition failure is not a routable asked-but-still-open question. It is also not a disguised known. All four adversaries ran their Disguise sweeps in full and all four concluded novelty survives at Medium: 49 queries across more than ten vocabularies, plus Chinese- and Japanese-language sweeps, surfaced no source that poses this question, so there is no asked-and-open problem to hand to the research workstream. The nearest neighbour (arXiv:2608.00101) asks a different question about a different quantity and answers it, so it is not an open problem either.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-22)

This entry is the exception in its batch. Every other entry's verdict held on verification; this one's did not hold for the reasons it was given. Six fresh-context checkers re-read its load-bearing sources first-hand, blind to the reviewers' reasoning, and between them they removed both legs of the original fatal ground. The status is still Rejected and the fatal attack is still attack 4, but not one of the clauses the original kill rested on survives as an independent fatal leg. What follows is therefore a record of a re-rejection on new grounds, not a confirmation of the old one, and it is the only block in this batch that has to disclose a second Gate 4.

**WHAT FELL, and which parts of it fell.** The original kill (round 1, logs `UQ-20261022-20-adversary-1.md` and `-adversary-2.md` in this batch directory) rested on two legs, each graded Unresolved by one adversary, and the entry had additionally banked their redundancy. Both legs failed on verification, in different ways, and the redundancy claim failed with them.

Leg (b), ENDOGENEITY (adversary 2's clause C5: lengths are endogenous to the window they were served under, because the harness compacts against it, so s does not estimate the demand L_prev would have failed) FELL AS AN INDEPENDENT FATAL LEG, because the measurand exemption reaches it. The checker settled this from the entry's own printed text rather than from any source: limb (a) READS "(a) what is the exceedance share s = P(input length > L_prev | class, C) with CIs", under an opener scoping every limb to a "named, dated, public request-length corpus C stratified by workload class", and no demand term — not "latent demand", not "unmet demand", not "would have failed" — appears in limb (a) or in that scoping clause. The question REPORTS the share; it does not ASSUME that the share measures latent demand. The demand reading lives in the record's INFERENCE from s — the Significance consequence line and alternative formulation (1) — and in the exogeneity observation the Scores line now books, not in the question. Attack 4 does not reach a clause the question converts into a reported quantity, so the surviving content belongs in the well-posedness line and in Significance, charged once and not twice, which is where the body above now carries it. What is sourced on that leg and what is not was separated as well. The compaction MECHANISM is documented and quotable in two independent frameworks the entry had not cited: Inspect AI, "Compaction works by monitoring model input and executing when input tokens get close to the model's context window size", with "The default threshold is `0.9` (90% of the context window)"; and AgentScope 2.0.10, "If total tokens exceed `trigger_ratio x context_size`, compression activates", capped at 0.9, with the agentic hint firing "once the input tokens exceed 60% of the model context size". BOTH DEFINE A POLICY AND MEASURE NOTHING — neither prints a share of requests, a share of sessions, a length distribution or any traffic quantity on any population. What is NOT sourced is the step the objection needed: no published evidence was found that an input-length distribution shifted after a window increase in a model family, and the one paper whose title suggested it might formalise the adaptation — Tirmazi, H., Markelon, S., Bishop, A., Mitzenmacher, M., "Context Compaction Theory", arXiv:2608.01326v1 (Tirmazi, 2026) — was opened and came back negative, its nearest sentence being "Context rot pushes agents to do context compaction even before their state reaches the context window.", which is a claim about a compaction trigger and says nothing about a length distribution. So the load-bearing step of leg (b) IS AN INFERENCE, sourced nowhere, and the body above labels it one. Note also what the sourced mechanism actually censors: the documented trigger fires at 60-90% of the window, so it truncates the measurand's support at THE SCAFFOLD'S OWN THRESHOLD and not at L_prev, which sharpens this entry's own point that a share COMPACTED is not a share EXCEEDING and makes leg (b) an argument about a scaffold constant that a restatement could pin rather than about the window, which it could not.

Leg (a), CONTENT-STRIPPING (adversary 1's clause C3) KEPT ITS PREMISE AND LOST ITS CONCLUSION. The premise holds SIX FOR SIX on public serving traces, every one read at the release artifact rather than at a paper about it. Azure LLM Inference 2023 and 2024 carry an identical three-field `### Schema` table (TIMESTAMP / ContextTokens / GeneratedTokens) under a `### Prompt content` section whose first sentence reads in full "Due to customer privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR), we do not have visibility into the content of the prompts.", followed by the substitute practice, quoted whole because the cut matters: "We instead use the production traces to guide the input and output sizes, where we send the input prompt with the required number of tokens, and force the model to generate the corresponding number of output tokens for each request." ServeGen's `conversations/conversations_hashed.json` is described as "Input and output content are replaced with block hashes to preserve privacy, while structural characteristics are retained for analysis." The Chutes release behind "A Year in LLM Serving" publishes twelve content-free fields (`invocation_id`, `function_name`, `chute_id`, `user_id`, `rehash_round`, `instance_id`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `it`, `ot`, `ct`, `ttft`). GitHub Copilot Coding Agent Traces 2026 states, under the heading "### What it does **not** contain", "This release is metadata-only. It includes **no**: ... user prompts, model responses, or tool outputs" (ellipsis marked; the printed list also excludes source code, file paths, identifiers and real model names). BurstGPT's CSV header line is literally "Timestamp,Session ID,Elapsed time,Model,Request tokens,Response tokens,Total tokens,Log Type". And Mooncake's schema bullet reads "`input_length`: Number of input tokens. Raw text and tokens are not included for privacy protection.", with its closing enumeration "The trace files contain only anonymized timing, length, and remapped hash information. They are intended for reproducible simulation and evaluation of KV cache reuse behavior without exposing user content."

BUT THE "CANNOT BE RE-SERVED" CONCLUSION FELL AS A UNIVERSAL, and it fell to two dataset cards nobody at Gate 4's first round had opened. WildChat-1M — "WildChat is a collection of 1 million conversations between human users and ChatGPT", with the `conversation` field carrying every utterance's `content` plus `timestamp` and `turn` — and LMSYS-Chat-1M — "This dataset contains one million real-world conversations with 25 state-of-the-art LLMs.", conversation text in OpenAI API JSON format — each publish approximately one million REAL-TRAFFIC conversations WITH full content, freely downloadable, from which a length-defined stratum is cuttable, stratifiable by timestamp against a model era, re-servable and gradeable. The checker's own words on the consequence: "the kill as written would be reversed by one dataset card the adversaries did not open." Three narrowings follow and all three are carried in the body above. First, "EVERY public production request-length corpus" becomes EVERY CORPUS CHECKED, named instance by instance, because the leg is an enumerative generalization over named releases and not a proof that no such corpus exists. Second, "by design" belongs where it is documented — Mooncake, which states the reason three times in its own release documents, plus Azure and ServeGen, which state theirs — and comes OFF BurstGPT, which publishes no content and documents no reason at all; its README was grepped for `privac|anonym|GDPR|content|prompt text|personal|licen|de-identif` with zero matches, so for BurstGPT the absence is verified from the header while the design intent is not. Third, neither BurstGPT nor Mooncake publishes a context-window or max-length field or identifies the serving model's window: BurstGPT names only the families `ChatGPT`(GPT-3.5) and `GPT-4`, each of which shipped in several context variants, and Mooncake names no model at all, its "The block size is 512 tokens." being a KV paging granularity that must not be read as a window. That bears on limb (a) rather than limb (b): an exceedance share is computable on those corpora only under an externally supplied window assumption the artifacts do not license. One seam is flagged because a determined reader will probe it, and it does not break the leg: the synthetic trace in the Mooncake FAST'25 release, `FAST25-release/traces/synthetic_trace.jsonl`, is "constructed from public datasets", so the prompts under that one file are public somewhere — but the release publishes no join key, its `hash_ids` being "Remapped prefix block hashes", a renumbering, and a block identifier is not content; and the file is explicitly not production data, so it sits outside the leg's population anyway.

And THE REDUNDANCY CLAIM WAS REVERSED. The entry had said that either leg independently made attack 4 Unresolved "so the fatal grade does not depend on which leg a judge prefers". On re-testing the grade DID depend on the leg — the endogeneity checker recorded that the content leg "is untouched by me and is the only leg I find capable of carrying it" — and then, once the content checker removed that leg's universal conclusion, it depended on neither. Neither checker was wrong about its own read; together they left nothing standing. That sentence is struck in the body above.

**A LATE GATE 4 THEREFORE RAN.** Because the fatal ground fell rather than merely narrowing, Gate 4 was INCOMPLETE and could not be patched from the first round's logs: an entry cannot be rejected on a ground that two first-hand re-reads have dismantled, and the remaining Partials across attacks 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 do not carry a fatal grade. Gate 4 was re-run from scratch, late and separately, after the batch's other entries were settled.

**THE FORM OF THE LATE GATE 4, disclosed in full.** Two fresh-context adversaries, numbered 3 and 4 and written to this batch directory as `UQ-20261022-20-adversary-3.md` and `UQ-20261022-20-adversary-4.md`. Each was handed the Gate 0-3 record ALONE, with the prior Gate 4 grade declared VOID and NOT described to it — neither was told what the first round had killed on, so neither could inherit or merely re-dress it. Each was given the verification pass's established facts above as first-hand findings so that it need not re-fetch them and could spend its whole budget on new ground. Each ran all eight attacks at the strict standard, with the measurand exemption declared out loud rather than graded around, and each wrote its conditioning clauses out as a numbered list read literally off the Gate 1 reformulation. Neither was shown the other's log. Adversary 3 ran 9 Disguise queries (10 searches at cap, 4 fetches at cap, one of them item 10 for prior retrieval); adversary 4 ran 10 Disguise queries (10 searches at cap, 4 fetches at cap), all ten in vocabularies or targets no earlier run had used — error telemetry, a Chinese-language sweep, searching for the answer as a stated figure, cache/miss-ratio-curve capacity sizing, megapixel-race and specsmanship, a discourse exact-phrase chase, and the chat-corpus artifacts. No search call was refused in either run.

**BOTH RETURNED ATTACK 4 UNRESOLVED, INDEPENDENTLY, ON TWO DIFFERENT CLAUSES, AND NEITHER IS THE ORIGINAL KILL.** Both also returned a recommended verdict of Rejected. That the two cold readers converged on the same attack is not the same as their converging on the same defect: adversary 3 killed on limb (b)'s instrument, adversary 4 on limb (d)'s own repair clause, and each named the other's territory without resting on it. Neither raised content-stripping as a universal and neither raised endogeneity as a fatal presupposition; adversary 3 graded its own endogeneity clause C8 a contributing leg and said so, and adversary 4 carried its censoring clause as an independent fallback rather than as the kill.

**NEW GROUND ONE — adversary 3's clause C6, THE OUTCOME-SIGNAL GAP.** Limb (b) presupposes that the over-L_prev stratum of a public corpus can be re-served at L_new and at truncated-L_prev and SCORED. No corpus opened anywhere in this batch — the two content-retaining chat corpora included — publishes any finish reason, truncation flag, error status or task-success signal: Chutes' twelve fields include no status field at all, Azure's three include none, Copilot's `status` is per TOOL CALL only and not on the LLM call or the turn, and WildChat's nearest fields (`openai_moderation`, `detoxify_moderation`, `toxic`) grade SAFETY and not task success. And the only public corpus reaching the coding-agent / long-tool-trace class says so of itself. The SYFI TraceLab corpus, opened at its NVIDIA AIPerf schema page ("Profile with TraceLab Agentic Coding Traces", docs.nvidia.com), states "The corpus contains no prompt or response text." — a sentence whose opening words scope the whole corpus rather than a field or a subset, and which ASSERTS the absence — and lists its complete per-round field set (`session_id`, `round_index`, `input_tokens_total`, `prefix_tokens`, `newly_append_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`, `model`, `provider`, `user`, `project`, `timing_events[]`, `tools[]`, `first_input_event_type`), with tool-call arguments stripped and no outcome, finish-reason, error or truncation field anywhere in it. The page then says what a replay harness must do instead: "AIPerf synthesizes prompt content to the recorded token counts." Synthesised content has no task and no ground truth, so no outcome difference is measurable on it. The record pre-excludes the only other substitute in its own words — "NOT an answer: a synthetic long-context benchmark score at L_new" — and the generous reading, that limb (b) might use some corpus other than C, leaves the central limb with no named instrument at all, which is a well-posedness hole rather than a rescue. Crucially, C6 is ASSUMED by the wording and nowhere reported by it: the record's own P2 says outcome measurability was "Not tested at Gate 2", so the measurand exemption that saved leg (b) does NOT reach this clause. The single leg this ground stands on, stated as the adversary stated it: no public corpus cuttable to the coding-agent or long-tool-trace class retains prompt text. One point of this entry's own history belongs here. The earlier verification pass nominated TraceLab as a LEAD BY KIND that it had not opened, and said in terms that it was a lead and not a settler. The late pass opened it, and it came back against the candidate — supplying not the measured endogeneity the entry hoped for but one of the two new fatal grounds.

**NEW GROUND TWO — adversary 4's clause 2, THE CHECKPOINT-PAIR CLAUSE, which strikes the GATE 1 REFORMULATION ITSELF.** The reformulation's load-bearing repair was to restrict to open-weight families "so that the family supplying the thresholds also supplies the checkpoints", with limb (d) written as the short-context delta between "the pre- and post-extension checkpoints of that family". That is FALSE for the flagship family this entry names first, at BOTH of its announced steps, on the Qwen2.5-1M Technical Report (arXiv:2501.15383, Qwen Team, 2025, read in full via the publisher PDF). At the 32K to 128K step, Table 4 lists Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 14B-Instruct at a claimed 32K "extended to 128K with DCA+YaRN" — a TRAINING-FREE INFERENCE-TIME method applied to ONE set of weights — so no post-extension checkpoint exists for that step and the delta is zero by construction rather than by measurement. At the 128K to 1M step the 1M models were "developed based on Qwen2.5 models" from "an intermediate version from Qwen2.5 Base models" rather than from the released 128K checkpoint, so the comparison the report ALREADY PRINTS is a SIBLING-MODEL DIFFERENCE and not a cost attributable to the extension: Table 6 and Section 6.2 give 7B against 7B-1M as MMLU-Pro 56.3/54.3, MMLU-redux 75.4/74.8, GPQA 36.4/41.4, MATH 75.5/72.9, HumanEval 84.8/86.0, IFEval 71.2/73.0, with Section 6.2 stating the 1M models "maintain performance on short text tasks that is similar to the 128k versions" — non-monotone in both model sizes. Limb (d) is therefore, for the candidate's own named example, SIMULTANEOUSLY ALREADY PUBLISHED AND UNATTRIBUTABLE. And the wording assumes the checkpoint pair exists rather than reporting it, so the measurand exemption does not reach this clause either. That adversary's independent fallback, which this entry carries as a fallback and not as the kill, is its clause 6: limb (a)'s estimand is censored by client-side policy — the Copilot paper's Figure 17 label "median pre-compaction context utilization is 66%", Inspect AI's 0.9 default, AgentScope's cap at 0.9, and, as a mechanism statement with no share attached, Buckman's "In practice, people building tools around LLMs typically stop putting tokens into the context well before the stated limits." — on model-mixed corpora that never record which window was in force, so P(input > L_prev | class, C) does not identify how often L_prev would have bound.

**EACH NEW GROUND'S OWN VULNERABILITY.** New ground one is overturnable by ONE UNREAD PAGE: `huggingface.co/datasets/skein-community/coding-agent-traces`. If that corpus retains message content and carries any outcome field, C6 flips to true for the coding-agent class and attack 4 drops from Unresolved to Partial. Adversary 3 COULD NOT READ it — its WebFetch returned a site `client_error` and retrieved nothing of the page — and that is COULD NOT READ, emphatically NOT NOT FOUND; the adversary itself logged the nominee as a guess by kind-match on title and host rather than as a verified lead, and said so in those words. Within C6 the two joints are not equally strong: "no corpus cuttable to the coding-agent class retains prompt text" is the leg the ground stands on, while "no corpus publishes an outcome field" is the weaker, because an LLM judge could score outcomes post hoc IF content existed. New ground two is vulnerable in a different way. A defender may answer that Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M are both released and may simply be CALLED the pair; adversary 4 states that escape itself and answers that the verdict then stands on its clause 6, the censoring and identification fallback, which is untouched by how the checkpoints are labelled. Two further limits on that ground are recorded so it is not overread: the "at least two open-weight families" half of the premise is UNVERIFIED rather than established, because that adversary opened no Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek or Gemma source and says so; and its Table 4 and Table 6 readings are the fetch summariser's reading of tables, NOT a verbatim transcription, and are flagged as such rather than quoted as table text. Neither vulnerability rescues the candidate as worded: the two grounds fail independently and on different limbs, and a repair of either requires a second reformulation that Gate 1's single allowance, spent on the graded reformulation itself, no longer permits.

**UNDER THE GATE 4 RULE, THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED AND ITS REASON IS COMPLETELY REPLACED.** Attack 4 Unresolved from both independent adversaries is fatal, so the status stays Rejected and the attack stays attack 4. That is the whole of what is unchanged. The ground is new, it is held by two clauses neither first-round adversary raised, and the clauses the original kill rested on are gone — one struck as an independent fatal leg by the measurand exemption, one reduced to a narrowed enumerative premise about public serving traces whose universal conclusion is false. A reader who takes the unchanged status as a confirmation of the first round's reasoning will have read this entry backwards.

"Collapsed to a monthly MEAN" goes: the paper states no aggregation period for that metric and its stated default is weekly, "all time-series aggregates are computed on a weekly basis using UTC-normalized timestamps" (Section 2.5). The Section 4.3 quotation is COMPLETED, because the entry's version stopped at a comma: "Average prompt tokens per request have increased roughly fourfold from around 1.5K to over 6K, while completions have nearly tripled from about 150 to 400 tokens." **NOVELTY, which is not the ground, survives at Medium, and one sentence of this entry's was too strong to leave standing.** THE RECORD'S OWN STATED PROMOTION CONDITION FAILS, and two readers reached the same document independently to establish it — adversary 4 at the publisher PDF, `microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/ghcp_traces-6.pdf`, and the verification checker at the arXiv HTML with Section 6 read in full. The record had said that a published compaction rate for coding-agent sessions would be a partial figure on limb (a) for one workload class. That paper prints exactly that in its Section 6: "7.8% of all agent sessions undergo at least one compaction event, rising to 22.6% among long-context sessions" (those with >100K-token prompts), "Compaction is rare at the level of an individual call, occurring in just 0.5% of the time", plus Table 6's volume shares of 44.2% of total tokens, 37.1% of LLM calls and 38.9% of tool calls against 7.8% of sessions. So the promotion-to-High condition comes back NEGATIVE on the artifact the record itself named. On a FULL read of that section, however, there is still NO share of requests, sessions or turns hitting an ANNOUNCED context limit and NO numeric announced window anywhere in the paper — the limit appears only as the denominator of Figure 17's utilization axis, every model is anonymised, and the length axis stops at a `>120K` bin near a 128k window rather than at it — so the exceedance limb is NOT occupied and novelty stays Medium rather than falling to Low. What must change is this entry's wording: "no source prints the exceedance share" is NARROWED to "no source prints the share of sessions exceeding a model's ANNOUNCED context window", with those figures carried as the near neighbours it must be distinguished from and with Figure 17's trigger peaks near 50%, 65-66%, 80% and near 100% of each model's own limit as the stated reason they are not exceedance figures; a session that compacted at half its window never exceeded anything, and the measure simultaneously misses every session that reached the limit without compacting, so the two errors do not cancel into a bound. The adjacent corpus figure points the same way and is carried for the same reason: the SYFI TraceLab `session_compaction_counts` page prints "8.8% of the 8,058 sessions undergo at least one compaction", 4.4% for Claude against 17.4% for Codex, on a detector keyed to reductions of at least 64k tokens of which 79.2% are tool-initiated, and that two independent sources disagree (7.8% against 8.8%) is itself evidence the quantity tracks scaffold policy rather than the window. The condition this entry records in prose, rather than as a promotion clause, since it is Rejected: the candidate must state its threshold as the model's ANNOUNCED MAXIMUM WINDOW and its denominator as a NAMED REQUEST CLASS, because if it instead means "the point at which the agent compacts" the quantity is already published at 7.8 / 22.6 / 0.5% and novelty collapses to Low on this one paper. A second condition in the same register, on wording and not on novelty: if the ServeGen release or v3 publishes fitted per-workload input-length parameters, this entry's limb must be re-stated as "no published share and no published window pairing" rather than as "no computable share", since a share above an analyst-chosen threshold is still not a share above a model's announced window. A third: whichever family is proposed for limb (d) must be checked for an actual pre- and post-extension checkpoint pair before the limb is written, the family this entry names first supplying none at either announced step. And one note on this entry's own nomination discipline, which is worth saying because it cuts in the entry's favour: its nomination of the Copilot paper was justified BY KIND — a production-trace characterization paper is the right kind of document to carry a per-class threshold share — and it paid off, the kind being right and the quantity adjacent. Three of the six checkers recommended converting their residue to a promotion condition; because this entry is Rejected, every such condition is written as prose here and no line of this entry is a promotion requirement.

**ROUTING STAYS NO,** and the reason is one line: novelty is not the ground, the ground is presupposition failure, and a presupposition failure is not a routable asked-but-still-open question. No routing row is written for this entry, and `ledger/routed-open-problems.md` is unchanged by this pass.

**ONE THING IN THE BODY ABOVE THAT THIS BLOCK JUDGES WRONG AND DID NOT EDIT.** The seam flagged in P2 is attributed to ServeGen's `synthetic_trace.jsonl`. That file is MOONCAKE'S, not ServeGen's: `FAST25-release/traces/synthetic_trace.jsonl` in `kvcache-ai/Mooncake`, which the checker read at the release's own `FAST25-release/README.md` and which the release describes as "constructed from public datasets and uses Poisson-generated arrivals while preserving the order within multi-turn conversations". ServeGen's released tree holds `chunk-i-dataset.json`, `chunk-i-trace.csv`, `conversations/conversations_hashed.json` and `offline/`, and no file of that name; and the `hash_ids` that supply the no-join-key answer are Mooncake's field, documented as "Remapped prefix block hashes", not ServeGen's block hashes. The two reasons the seam does not break leg (a) are unaffected by the misattribution and hold for Mooncake exactly as the body states them. The substance is right, the owner is wrong, and the correction belongs with whoever next amends that line.

ID: UQ-20261023-01
Date: 2026-10-23
Status: Provisional — Gate 4 ran complete (three independent adversaries, no Unresolved on any attack); verified post-batch by seven fresh-context checkers, which struck and narrowed findings inside this entry and made one promotion clause untickable as written but did not move the verdict; Medium novelty with one live close neighbour still unread after eight routes
Domain(s): Biology — systems neuroscience; chronic high-density extracellular electrophysiology methodology. Neighbour vocabularies swept: multi-target tracking, record linkage, capture-recapture with misidentification, biometrics, panel-survey gross flows, psychometric test-retest, Utah-array/BMI single-unit stability, calcium-imaging cell registration, Chinese-language ephys.
Question (canonical): For >=2 published cross-day unit matchers at declared operating points, applied to chronic high-density extracellular recordings in which unit identity is labelled by at least one construction that does NOT use the functional response later used to measure tuning, (a) what are the matcher's false-match and split/merge rates, (b) what apparent change do those rates ALONE induce in >=2 published drift statistics under a declared null of zero true drift — the matching-error drift floor — and (c) do published drift magnitudes, matched on brain area and interval, exceed that floor? [This is V2, the Gate 1 reformulation, the single permitted one, and the version Gates 2-5 and the post-batch verification pass were run against; the original per-paper decomposition wording is recorded verbatim in ledger/batches/2026-10-23-0033/UQ-20261023-01-record.md.]
Alternative formulations: How much of representational drift is a bookkeeping error about which neuron is which? / What drift floor is implied by cross-day unit-matching error alone, and do published drift magnitudes exceed it?
Motivating gap: cross-day matchers declare operating points and name the confound in their own discussions; no paper carries a MEASURED matcher false-match rate into a reported drift statistic. NARROWED at verification — the earlier wording "nobody prices it into a drift estimate" is too broad and must not be used anywhere, because bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.13.652528 (2025), "Temporal coding carries more stable cortical visual representations than firing rate over time" (journal version Nature Communications s41467-025-62069-2; FIRST AUTHOR NOT ESTABLISHED, since both bioRxiv routes served text beginning at the Introduction with no author list, and no name may be filled in from a search-result title) stipulates a 10% per-day identity shuffle, reports that it "eroded the decoder performance significantly towards chance level", and concludes that the observed tuning drift "cannot be trivially explained by the possible existence of tracking errors". The defensible form is: no paper carries a measured matcher false-match rate into a reported drift statistic; at least one stipulates an identity-error rate and reports its effect on a decoder. Confirmed at full-text read level in both field-standard matchers. UnitMatch, full printed sentence restored at verification because this entry previously carried it with its scope-setting opener dropped: "For example, the slow decrease in AUC values that we observed across days could be explained either by a decrease in the quality of matching, or changes in functional properties of the units." — and the sentence immediately after it, which strengthens the gap by putting the question outside the paper's own estimand: "Therefore, unless there is reason to believe that the functional properties are constant[refs], it is prudent to exclude these properties from the criteria that determine the tracking of units, and only consider them as a possible validation[refs] or as a separate question[refs]." (inline reference superscripts replaced by [refs]; both strings are reconstructions assembled only from consecutive served fragments, fragment counts recorded in VERIFY-uq01-unitmatch-quotes.md). Presuppositions: (1) cross-day "same neuron" is well defined — CONTESTED; measurand exemption declared by the record and independently re-declared by all three adversaries, since the question scores a decision against a declared labelling and reports the labelling's failure as a result. (2) >=1 matcher reports or permits an error rate at a declared operating point — ESTABLISHED at full text (UnitMatch "probability is >0.5"; EMD "z=10 um"), FLAGGED as not ground-truth-measured. (3)/(R1) a function-independent cross-day identity labelling exists with non-trivial coverage — CONTESTED ON COVERAGE, not false, and NARROWED TO A TIMESCALE at verification: the missing thing is not label independence as such but label independence AT A CROSS-DAY TIMESCALE, because UnitMatch's own within-day waveform cross-validation on the first and second halves of a recording IS a published function-independent identity label ("matching probabilities were close to 1 for the same units measured in the first and second half of the recording"), and the SpikeForest ground-truth families (paired, synthetic and HYBRID_JANELIA — the last being a dataset INSIDE SpikeForest rather than a separate family, so counting them separately inflated the prior list; preprint DOI 10.1101/2020.01.14.900688, author list not read from front matter and therefore not asserted) supply tuning-free identity in abundance but only inside one recording of "(600, 1200, 2400 s)", ten to forty minutes. STRUCK at verification: the claim that UnitMatch's only function-independent check is WITHIN-day. That is FALSE — the acute probe-reinsertion control is CROSS-DAY and FUNCTION-INDEPENDENT, its labelling coming from a physical manipulation rather than from functional fingerprints, printed whole as "Reassuringly, when we applied UnitMatch to acute recordings, where the probe was reinserted daily and had negligible chance of finding the same unit, finding a match was rare (4.0 ± 2.8%, n = 18 pairs of consecutive days; Wilcoxon rank sum comparing chronic and acute: p < 10^-10; [Fig figS3])", with the qualifier this entry previously omitted standing immediately after it: "Note that this was when UnitMatch was pushed to find matches by pretending the probe was in the same location between the recording sessions." What survives the strike is narrower and still intact: the control is negative-class only (no positive class, hence no miss rate), its spread is median ± median absolute deviation over DAY-PAIRS rather than mean ± SD over unit-pairs (the per-pair denominator carried over from the preceding sentence is the checker's own inference, not a printed statement), and it is an acute preparation at an adversarial operating point — so it is not a chronic per-unit-pair rate. "Split halves" was this entry's phrase and not the paper's, which says "the average spatiotemporal spike waveform in the first and in the second half of the recording". Bimbard et al. 2025, eLife 13:RP98522, DOI 10.7554/eLife.98522's ISIH check is a validator and not a ground truth, in the paper's own words "These ISIHs were not used to match neurons across days", no sentence of that article contains "false positive" on a targeted negative search, and its nearest number is a within-day ceiling — "For two recordings on the same day, 50% of neurons were matched, suggesting an upper limit in neuron tracking with the method we used" — which is a matched fraction, not an error rate. The one positive-class function-independent label in print — continuity in 24/7 recording, Dhawale 2017 — is tetrodes, with coverage falling to 0.4%/1.7% of units at one month. NARROWED FURTHER: of the five candidate label families the Gate material listed, only ONE could in principle settle this — hybrid or simulated datasets injecting the SAME known units into real recordings from DIFFERENT DAYS — since opto-tagging and genetic/anatomical marking give a cell-TYPE or population label and not per-unit identity (a PV+ tag on Tuesday and a PV+ tag on Friday are the same label on possibly different neurons: the tag constrains a match, it does not certify one), and juxtacellular/intracellular ground truth and paired-recording designs are excluded by instrument, the pipette not being held across days. No instance of the settling kind was found — HYBRID_JANELIA injects "at randomly selected channels and time points" inside one trimmed 600-1200 s recording — and no specific unopened paper is nominated as being one, because nominating one would be a guess. (4) dropped by the reformulation. (5) matching errors approximately independent of tuning — NOT a presupposition but a measurand; the EMD paper expects dependence ("Coincidentally similar visual responses could potentially contribute to inaccurate assignment" — a string carried from Gate 2 and NOT among those the post-batch pass re-verified). CORRECTED at verification, and this entry must not inherit its earlier wording: the EMD paper nowhere expects tuning-INDEPENDENCE to fail. On a full read of v2, every relevant sentence expects tuning STABILITY to fail and offers tuning-independence as the remedy — Introduction, "When neuronal representations change, e.g., during learning or representational drift, neural activity statistics became less reliable"; Discussion, "The visual fingerprint similarity of matched neurons decreased to 60% after 40 days (see reference 7 supplement)"; and the hedged "This reduction in fraction of reference units might be partially due to representational drift as well as the fact that the set of active neurons are slightly different in each recording" — while the paper affirmatively CLAIMS tuning-independence: "We show the capability of our method to track neurons with no specific tuning preference (Figure S16)." The supported form of the point is that the paper expects its own functional validation label to thin with the gap, not that it expects tuning-independent tracking to fail. (6) drift is reported as a measurable statistic — ESTABLISHED weakly. (R2) published statistics recomputable or analytically perturbable — UNVERIFIED (no data-availability statement opened by anyone); two adversaries note an analytic perturbation needs only the rates and a one-day tuning distribution, so R2 is weaker than the record states. (R3) a zero-true-drift null is realisable — the record nominated this as the place to attack well-posedness and TWO adversaries independently found that it is not a claim about the world at all: the reformulation says "declared" null, so R3 is a stipulation for a propagation, not a surrogate that must exist. The record aimed Gate 4 at its own strongest point. (NEW, from adversary 1) direction of bias: misses and splits select a waveform-stable subset and push measured drift DOWN while false matches push it UP, so "floor" presupposes a one-signed bias; an answer must report both components.
What would count as an answer: measured false-match and split/merge rates for >=2 matchers at declared operating points against >=1 declared function-independent identity labelling with its coverage stated; a propagation under a declared zero-drift null giving the apparent change those rates alone produce in >=2 published drift statistics, with CIs; and a comparison against >=2 published drift magnitudes matched on area and interval. A CLEAN NEGATIVE — floor small relative to published drift at all plausible rates and all constructions — settles it the other way and retires the concern. Both branches are informative, which is what keeps it a question rather than an agenda.

Significance — consequence: if the floor is comparable to published drift magnitudes at plausible rates, part of the ephys drift literature's effect size is identity bookkeeping and drift papers acquire an obligatory matcher-error term, as imaging papers already report registration error rates; if it is small, the concern retires and ephys drift is strengthened. Either branch replaces an argument with a number — and the argument currently in print is the EMD paper's reassurance from a subset accuracy its own authors say does not generalise.
Significance — audience: (a) the matcher developers, who wrote the confound into their discussions and are the natural producers of the floor; (b) drift theorists fitting time constants to measured rates, which an instrument-limited rate would mis-set; (c) chronic high-density labs whose drift claims rest on matched units — STILL NOT ENUMERATED, though after verification it no longer rests on wholly unopened returns: a checker opened three papers from the consuming literature (Lu et al. 2025, PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0321830; Bimbard et al. 2025, eLife 13:RP98522; bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.13.652528) and NONE of the three is a drift paper consuming UnitMatch/EMD-matched high-density units — the one genuine UnitMatch consumer measures yield and signal rather than tuning — so zero members of the named class have been opened by anyone. Evidence the audience acts: Stevenson et al. 2011 shows this community letting a noise-floor correction overturn an apparent-change result and restating its conclusion to match.
Significance — fecundity: the same floor logic transfers to cross-day decoder-stability and "stable subset" claims, to separating cell death from drift, and to whether reported drift TIMESCALES are instrument-limited; it opens the import of track-purity / ID-switch metrics and latent-identity capture-recapture estimators into ephys, where four separate searches found no such import.
Significance — anchoring: the standing is-drift-real-or-recording-instability debate; UnitMatch's SCOPED ground-truth disclaimer, NARROWED at verification — "However, neither can be considered ground truth." is a TWO-REFERENT denial whose referents are fixed by the sentence before it ("The higher similarity between UnitMatch and manual curation is reassuring because the latter is generally regarded more highly than automated spike sorting."), i.e. UnitMatch's own output and manual curation, so it is not a blanket disclaimer and says nothing about the acute reinsertion control or the within-day waveform cross-validation; this entry therefore no longer calls it "the two matchers' explicitly disclaimed ground truth" and no longer reads it as disclaiming ground truth outright, an overreading that ran in this entry's own favour by reading two of the paper's own labellings out of existence; Dhawale 2017's unpriced CONJECTURE, RE-ANCHORED at verification — it is a hedged, cited, disjunctive conjecture about OTHER studies' contrasting findings rather than a concession about this paper's own measurement, and the authors do answer it qualitatively in their own data ("In our data set, we found discontinuous tracking over day-long gaps to be highly error-prone"), which is unnumbered in the text rather than unaddressed; and the imaging-registration-error literature that may already perform half of this operation on a different instrument.
Reason for silence: ownership and incentive boundary — SURVIVES AS THE ONLY LEG. The record offered three. Leg B (the propagation method lives in record linkage, capture-recapture and MOT, fields with no citation contact) is DAMAGED, and damaged twice as of verification: Stevenson et al. 2011 is a systems-neuroscience paper in this very measurement family that performs the propagation and prints the corrected floor, so the field owns a version of the method already and only the error term differs; and bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.13.652528, from inside the consuming drift literature, stipulates a 10% per-day identity shuffle and reports the induced change in decoder performance, which is the same shape of damage again, now on a tracked-unit dataset. Leg C ("the instrument is young; cross-day matching arrived 2023-2025") is FALSE on an opened source, and verification strengthened the falsity: Stevenson 2011's introduction already refers to prior work in the printed clause "By recording many trials from the same neurons over the course of several days, a number of studies have", and its Results conclude that the corrected within-session result "provide[s] statistical insights into previous findings of apparent instabilities" — so the floor logic was not merely available in 2011, it was already AIMED at the cross-day instability debate; cross-day same-unit tracking with functional comparison predates the Neuropixels matchers by over a decade and the question could have been asked in 2009-2012. Leg A stands and is sourced: the party that can measure the rate owns the tool and not the estimand, and would be publishing a number that discounts its own tool; the party that owns the estimand cites the matcher as a black box. The silence is therefore ~15 years long, not 2, explained by incentive alone. Adversary 3's contrary reading — that instrument youth is the credible mechanism because the consuming high-density drift literature is too thin to propagate into — is recorded and NOT adopted: it rests on that literature being unverified rather than on an opened source, while Leg C's falsity rests on a sentence read in full text.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-23)

**What ran, and what each checker was sent to read.** Seven fresh-context checkers ran on this entry after the batch closed, one per load-bearing prior or kill leg. Each was handed the claim and its sources but NOT the reviewers' reasoning, and each re-read its sources first-hand. VERIFY-uq01-sheintuch-fulltext was sent to Sheintuch et al. 2017 (Cell Reports 21(4):1102-1115, DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2017.10.013) to test whether the one document deciding the Disguise attack is really unread past its abstract. VERIFY-uq01-unitmatch-quotes was sent to Prior 1 (van Beest et al., UnitMatch, bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.10.12.562040) for its eight sub-claims: the quoted strings, the printed rates and their denominators, and the unopened Supplementary Fig. S3. VERIFY-uq01-emd-27pct was sent to Prior 2 (Yuan et al., eLife 92495) for the 27%, the 29% reference subset, the unit of analysis, and the sentence this entry said expects tuning-independence to fail. VERIFY-uq01-stevenson-floor was sent to Prior 3 (Stevenson et al. 2011, J Neurophysiol 106:764-774, DOI 10.1152/jn.00626.2010) for the two SD figures, the within-session regime and the absence of any cross-session identity treatment. VERIFY-uq01-dhawale-drift was sent to Dhawale et al. 2017 (eLife 6:e27702, DOI 10.7554/eLife.27702) for the routing note's three legs. VERIFY-uq01-drift-papers-enumerate was sent to turn the motivating gap's universal into a list of named, opened drift papers consuming matcher-matched units. VERIFY-uq01-independent-groundtruth was sent to the question of whether any published work supplies a cross-day unit-identity ground truth independent of the functional response, and whether a matcher has been scored against one.

**Read level reached, source by source, with COULD NOT READ kept distinct from NOT FOUND.** Sheintuch 2017: ABSTRACT ONLY, and even the abstract only as a summariser's paraphrase rather than verbatim; body, Results, Methods and Figure 6 all COULD NOT READ; front matter FULL but metadata-confirmed from the OpenAlex record keyed on the DOI, not read off the paper's first page. UnitMatch: bioRxiv MAIN TEXT read in full, with the absence of front matter and of all supplementary figures and captions from that document verified rather than assumed; Supplementary Fig. S3, the "Supplementary analyses" and Supplementary eqn 28 COULD NOT READ at three routes; the published Nature Methods version COULD NOT READ; the UCL Discovery eprint record METADATA ONLY. EMD: FULL TEXT of v2 (10.7554/eLife.92495.2), with v1 (10.7554/eLife.92495.1) spot-checked on six strings; the Version of Record (10.7554/eLife.92495.3) and the bioRxiv preprint NOT READ, which is COULD NOT READ and not a negative finding; Equation 3's formula served as an image and unreadable, its structure taken from the surrounding prose. Stevenson 2011: FULL TEXT of the main article from the authors' own lab copy, front matter confirmed; Supplemental Material and Supplemental Note COULD NOT READ. Dhawale 2017: PARTIAL — Discussion, the day-gap Results passage, the Figure 3 legend, front matter, and keyword probes of Methods; the legend of Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C, the full Materials and methods, the figure data and the PDF all COULD NOT READ, and the summariser stated outright that the supplement legend text "is not included in the content provided". Drift-paper enumeration: three documents opened PARTIAL (Lu et al. 2025; Bimbard et al. 2025; bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.13.652528, the last DEFICIENT IN FRONT MATTER); two COULD NOT READ (Nature Communications s41467-025-62069-2; Cell Reports PII S2211124725003183). Independent-ground-truth: three documents opened PARTIAL (UnitMatch; SpikeForest, preprint DOI 10.1101/2020.01.14.900688; the EMD body at bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.08.03.551724v3 with FULL front matter from the eLife reviewed-preprint page); no opto-tagged, genetic/anatomical-marking, standalone paired-recording, SHYBRID or density-based-tracking paper was opened at all, which that checker recorded as COULD NOT CHECK rather than as a negative finding.

**What was struck.** Three things. First, the claim that UnitMatch's only function-independent check is WITHIN-day is FALSE and is struck from the presuppositions: the acute probe-reinsertion control is cross-day and function-independent, its labelling coming from a physical manipulation, and it prints "Reassuringly, when we applied UnitMatch to acute recordings, where the probe was reinserted daily and had negligible chance of finding the same unit, finding a match was rare (4.0 ± 2.8%, n = 18 pairs of consecutive days; Wilcoxon rank sum comparing chronic and acute: p < 10^-10; [Fig figS3])." Second, "asked in print" is struck as to Dhawale 2017: no interrogative on this topic exists in anything read, and the nearest "question" wording is scoped by its own opener to longitudinal calcium imaging, so the row carries a conjecture about other studies and not an asked question. Third, the triviality identity's clause "it holds only under the tuning-independence the EMD paper's own sentence expects to fail" is struck and reversed, because the paper affirmatively claims tuning-independence — "We show the capability of our method to track neurons with no specific tuning preference (Figure S16)" — and expects tuning STABILITY, not tuning-independence, to fail. Where a checker struck a sub-claim that this entry's filed prose did not carry verbatim, the entry's nearest wording was corrected and the strike recorded rather than left standing below: the sub-claims about the "We thus looked for functional 'fingerprints'" quotation, the 31.3 ± 11.2% ellipsis, and the "plotted rather than printed" characterisation were in the cards handed to the checkers, and this entry carried only the related material, which has been corrected in place.

**What was narrowed, and the quotations that settled each narrowing.** The motivating gap's "nobody prices it into a drift estimate" is narrowed to "no paper carries a MEASURED matcher false-match rate into a reported drift statistic", because bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.13.652528 stipulates a 10% per-day identity shuffle that "eroded the decoder performance significantly towards chance level" and states that the drift "cannot be trivially explained by the possible existence of tracking errors". The ground-truth disclaimer is narrowed to its two referents, fixed by the sentence before it: "However, neither can be considered ground truth." The absence claim is narrowed to a TIMESCALE, because UnitMatch's own within-day half-split is a published function-independent identity label — "matching probabilities were close to 1 for the same units measured in the first and second half of the recording" — and SpikeForest's tuning-free families live inside one recording of "(600, 1200, 2400 s)". The EMD reference subset is narrowed from "a visual-receptive-field subset" to the paper's own joint criterion, "The pool of reference units is established with three criteria: 1) The visual response similarity score of the pair, as described above, is greater than 1 and their physical distance, both before and after drift correction, is smaller than 30um." "Non-generalising" is qualified, because the paper calls the subset selection-biased ("Because reference units must be detected in two datasets, they must be easily isolated") while separately claiming the model generalises ("The similar shape of the distribution and a 29% false positive rate suggest that this method can be generalized"). The claim about Fig. S3 is narrowed to COULD NOT READ at three further routes, with the main text citing S3 twice rather than once. "'Representational drift' never appears anywhere in it" is narrowed to the MAIN TEXT, with the supplement unenumerated and the search summariser-mediated rather than a byte-level grep. The candidate-label list is narrowed from five families to one. And Prior 3's regime leg is narrowed by the concession that Stevenson et al. aim their within-session floor at the cross-day debate — "By recording many trials from the same neurons over the course of several days, a number of studies have" and "provide[s] statistical insights into previous findings of apparent instabilities" — so the NUMERATOR difference, not the regime difference, now carries the weight.

**What was re-sourced, and what was confirmed.** Three quotations were re-sourced because the cut was the defect even though the words were verbatim. Dhawale's sentence is restored whole, with its second disjunct and its true subject: "Such contrasting findings could be due to systematic errors in unit tracking across discontinuous recording sessions, or the choice of statistical framework used to assess stability (Rokni et al., 2007; Stevenson et al., 2011)." UnitMatch's confound sentence is restored with its opener: "For example, the slow decrease in AUC values that we observed across days could be explained either by a decrease in the quality of matching, or changes in functional properties of the units." Stevenson's hedge is restored with its opener and both governed values: "With the use of this method, we found that the corrected SD for blocks of 40 trials was 0.4 +/- 1.1 deg and for blocks of 120 trials, was 1.8 +/- 2.5 deg, compatible with absolutely stable PDs." The EMD leg is re-sourced away from a v2-only phrase to strings present in both versions: "The false positive fraction for the set of all KSgood units is obtained by integration" and "We cannot simply extrapolate from the measured false positive rate of the reference units." What was CONFIRMED and needed no change: UnitMatch's ">0.5" probability rule and its unnumbered data-driven total-score threshold, both halves; the printed 31.3% and 4.0% figures themselves; the paper's own exclusion of functional properties from its matching criteria; the EMD unit of analysis, population and z = 10 um operating point; the EMD paper's lack of any validation against a non-functional label, enumerated as true over the one version read in full; every testable specific of Prior 3 including "Spike sorting was performed offline by manual cluster cutting."; and the central claim about Sheintuch 2017, namely that it is unread past its abstract and that what it does is UNKNOWN rather than absent.

**Where checkers flagged their own limits, and the one place this entry's record overrides a checker.** Several steps are the checkers' own inferences and are carried as such, not as source findings: that the median ± m.a.d. convention and the per-pair denominator carry over from UnitMatch's chronic sentence to its acute sentence is explicitly the checker's inference and not a printed statement; that a Monte-Carlo-derived arithmetic mismatch in the EMD paper's Bayes step (P(~H) printed as 0.73 where 1 - 0.29 = 0.71) is the checker's own arithmetic over summariser-served text, low confidence, and is relied on for nothing; that the absence of "representational drift" from UnitMatch rests on a summariser-mediated search rather than a grep, so a single sweep's silence is not absence; that the completion of the word "sessions" in the Dhawale reconstruction is attested by the server's own statement rather than inferred, with the junction disclosed; and that two checkers declined to assert author lines they had not reached in front matter rather than copying a short form in circulation. That is true of the claim card it was handed and false of this entry as filed, which records Priors 1-3 and the live unread neighbour by DOI, first author, year and title; its identifier resolutions are nonetheless adopted, since they are additions rather than corrections. Similarly, VERIFY-uq01-unitmatch-quotes reports this entry as carrying a full UnitMatch author list and VERIFY-uq01-drift-papers-enumerate reports "no front-matter error found in the entry's existing citations of PRIOR 1"; the two are not in conflict, because the impeached list was in the record material and not in the entry's prose, which carries only "van Beest et al." and continues to do so.

**Did the verdict move.** No. The verdict is Provisional and it did not move. Gate 5 returned Provisional on this entry and the verification pass did not disturb that: three adversaries ran, none reached Unresolved on any attack, and nothing this pass established changed that grading, so NO LATE GATE 4 WAS OWED ON THIS ENTRY AND NONE RAN. The reason Provisional stands is the reason the entry already gave — the document that would decide the Disguise attack has not been opened — and this pass strengthened the evidence for that fact rather than altering it. But the verdict not moving must not be read as nothing having changed: this pass struck three claims, narrowed about a dozen, re-sourced four quotations whose cuts were the defect, corrected the citations of four of the five load-bearing sources, and made one clause of the promotion condition untickable as written.

**What the pass did to the promotion conditions and to the novelty grade.** The promotion condition grew from three clauses to seven. Clause (1) is now explicit about the branch and names the untested cell.com PII as the first route to try. Clause (2) is unchanged. Clause (3) is restated to name the class of document that would close it, and is recorded as not tickable in its original form. Four clauses were added by conversion: UnitMatch's Fig. S3, "Supplementary analyses" and eqn 28 by a working route, with the advance note that S3 will probably settle the within-day numbers rather than a chronic cross-day rate; the EMD Version of Record and its three strings; the density-based longitudinal tracker plus at least one opto-tagged chronic recording paper read rather than inferred from a title-level null; and UnitMatch's front matter, for the impeached author list. One tier-B routability claim was converted out of the findings into a routing condition on Dhawale's Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C. The novelty grade is unchanged at Medium: one checker holds Medium by default because the test that could lower it did not run, one finds both grade-costing counterfactuals fail, one finds Prior 3 does not undercut the Medium allowance, and one finds the gap survives at the timescale it should have specified so the grade falls neither to Low nor to High. The single internal movement is that limb (b) drops a notch, because a stipulated-rate-to-statistic sensitivity analysis now exists inside the drift literature on a tracked-unit dataset; limb (a) is untouched.

**The motivating gap contained a universal that is FALSE on two opened instances.** Stated separately because it is the most consequential thing this pass found. The broad form of the gap's universal — that no paper in the consuming literature carries any term, correction, control or sensitivity analysis for matcher identity error — is FALSE, and it is false on the first papers anybody opens. INSTANCE ONE, with its number: Lu, Hung-Yun; Stealey, Hannah M.; Zhao, Yi; Barnett, Cole R.; Contreras-Hernandez, Enrique; Santacruz, Samantha R. (2025), "Long-term neuron tracking reveals balance of stability and plasticity in functional properties", PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0321830 (= bioRxiv 2025.03.14.643204 = PMC13313350), declares a 5% false-positive rate against a cross-channel null — "the 95th percentile of this null distribution, ensuring a false positive rate of 5%" — which is a threshold choice rather than a measured rate, but is unmistakably a control for matcher identity error. INSTANCE TWO, with its number: bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.13.652528 (2025), "Temporal coding carries more stable cortical visual representations than firing rate over time" (journal version Nature Communications s41467-025-62069-2; first author NOT ESTABLISHED), runs a 10% per-day identity-shuffle sensitivity analysis which "eroded the decoder performance significantly towards chance level" and concludes that the observed tuning drift "cannot be trivially explained by the possible existence of tracking errors". The narrow form of the universal — that no such paper carries an error-propagation term, a matcher error rate carried through into a drift statistic under a declared null — was NOT falsified, and its class is still empty of opened instances: the one genuine UnitMatch consumer opened, Bimbard et al. 2025 (eLife 13:RP98522, DOI 10.7554/eLife.98522), reports no tuning or representational change across days at all. CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: the THIRD CLAUSE of the promotion condition is NOT TICKABLE AS WRITTEN. As originally worded it asked for ">=3 named drift papers consuming UnitMatch/EMD-matched units checked for an error-propagation term, converting the motivating gap's universal from unverified to a stated absence over named instances", and that conversion cannot be performed: the broad universal cannot be converted to a stated absence because it is false on the two instances above, and the narrow universal cannot be converted because the checker who went looking opened three papers and none of them belongs to the named class. The clause stays open, and the reason it stays open is not that such papers are hard to read but that the first one anybody opens turns out not to measure tuning at all.

**The one document deciding the Disguise attack is STILL unread, after eight routes, five of them new.** Sheintuch L., Rubin A., Brande-Eilat N., Geva N., Sadeh N., Pinchasof O., Ziv Y. (2017), "Tracking the Same Neurons across Multiple Days in Ca2+ Imaging Data", Cell Reports 21(4):1102-1115, DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2017.10.013, PMID 29069591, remains unread past a paraphrased abstract. The eight failed routes, listed so a later pass does not repeat them, are: sciencedirect (robots_disallowed); cell.com fulltext at PII S2211-1247(17)31466-6 (client_error); cell.com action/showPdf at the same PII (robots_disallowed, a path-level refusal that would have failed on either PII); PMC5670033 (hard-blocked, and treated as an identifier rather than a route); core.ac.uk search on the quoted title (robots_disallowed, NEW); scholar.archive.org search on the quoted title (robots_disallowed, NEW); web.archive.org on the cell.com fulltext URL (SITE_BLOCKED at the target, "Access to this website has been blocked", NEW); and the Semantic Scholar graph API keyed on the DOI (client_error by WebFetch and CONNECT tunnel 403 by curl at the agent proxy, NEW — two tools, one route, both closed). OpenAlex and DOAJ SUCCEEDED but serve metadata and a paraphrased abstract only, which is why the entry's two abstract strings are consistent-but-not-verbatim-verified rather than confirmed. Three searches were spent and none produced a reachable copy. The untried routes worth taking, each with its kind stated: the publisher PDF at the other PII, https://www.cell.com/article/S2211124717314304/pdf, and its matching fulltext path, which is the right KIND of document to settle what Figure 6 and the Results do; and the Ziv lab publications page at weizmann.ac.il, which is the right kind to yield an author-hosted PDF link and the wrong kind to answer any sub-claim by itself. The academia.edu posting is a repost host, usable only as a file source and never as a citation. Until the body is open, "the paper does not propagate its error rate into a drift statistic" is UNENUMERATED and not a finding, and "calcium imaging only" is true over the title and an abstract paraphrase and unenumerated over the body.
