Significance — consequence: if removal moves the metric materially and the contrast moves, hypoglycaemia endpoints in CGM trials are measured with a ruler that is partly instrument artifact, and the asymmetry matters wherever arms differ in sleep posture, alarm-driven waking or sensor site — which is what automated-insulin-delivery arms differ in. The consensus definitions would then need an artifact clause they do not have: the quality gate in use is completeness, and an artifact passes it because the readings are present. This is now sourced rather than predicted, and on FOUR documents from THREE groups rather than one — the Sanofi SAP (NCT04075513) gates data on "At least 80% time of records per 24 hours (ie, 231 data points among the 288 recorded in 24 hours)", "No gap (missing data) lasting for a total of >= 2 hours per 24 hours besides the warm-up time for the sensor after insertion", "a minimum of 10 days (not necessarily consecutive) of useable CGM data", and "For any gap of less than 2 hours between two available CGM measurements, linear interpolation", while artifact, artefact, compression, outlier, implausible, invalid, unreliable, discard, sensor error and data quality are ALL ABSENT from it on two independent full-document sweeps ("pressure" occurs only as "Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)"; "aberrant" occurs once, in MOS Sleep scoring, not about glucose). The warm-up clause is an EXEMPTION from a completeness criterion, not an exclusion of readings, and reading it as an artifact rule would misread its direction. The gap this entry points at is accordingly NARROWER than "SAPs say nothing about the trace", which is false on that document: it is specifically artifact and signal-validity, missing from inside an otherwise detailed data-handling chapter. One near neighbour must travel with this or a later reader will flip it on a misreading: the PROMISE SAP (NCT03808376) Section 6.2 DOES pre-specify a point-level exclusion, but it is keyed to the REFERENCE measurement and not to the sensor trace — "Flagged reference measurement as indicated in source documentation (e.g., expired membrane, expired calibration, dilute sample)" plus intake deviations (hematocrit out of window, tetracycline/sorbitol/mannitol, recent DKA or severe hypoglycaemia), over a denominator of per-protocol PAIRED measurements that is neither all sensor readings nor the separately gated evaluable population ("a minimum of three paired glucose readings"). What it MISSES relative to this candidate: every sensor-trace artifact — compression lows, pressure drops, early-wear drift, dropout — none named anywhere in the document. What it INCLUDES that this candidate excludes: assay-side and eligibility-side defects of the YSI comparator. It is one word away and a different quantity: a NEAR NEIGHBOUR, not a counter-instance, and it would be equally a defect to say point-level exclusion machinery is absent from this document kind — it exists and it is pointed at the comparator. Also carried: inferring an absent RULE from an absent TERM is the checker's own inference and not a quotation, since a SAP could delegate artifact handling to a device data-processing SOP or a vendor export specification without using these words; nothing opened does so, and no search that could have settled it was run. If the answer is null (both arms shift together), the artifact is a nuisance on absolute burden rather than a bias on inference, which still bears on target attainment and label claims.
Significance — audience: consensus-metric and guideline writers who would have to decide whether an artifact clause belongs in the definition; regulators treating TBR as a safety endpoint; trial statisticians, who would gain a pre-specifiable sensitivity analysis. Softer on the documents than in the record, but less soft than the entry formerly had it, and the count "the one SAP opened" is now false: in the Sanofi SAP (NCT04075513) TBR<70 is an other secondary ("Percent time and mean hours per day with glucose <70 mg/dL (on all time [00:00 to 23:59]"), TBR<54 is tertiary/exploratory, no multiplicity adjustment is made on other secondary variables, and margins exist only on TIR and CV (10% relative each). The "essentially descriptive" quotation is NARROWED post-batch, because it was being leaned on too hard: the printed sentence is "The analysis of the safety variables will be essentially descriptive." — a flat assertion carrying the sponsor's OWN hedge "essentially" — and the SAME section is not CI-free, Section 2.4.5.1 analysing hypoglycaemia incidence with odds ratios and 95% CIs from logistic regression and hypoglycaemia rates as OVER-DISPERSED POISSON RATE RATIOS. What that SAP withholds from the hypoglycaemia endpoints is a MARGIN, not a confidence interval, and "hypoglycaemia gets no yardstick at all" would be too strong a reading. That cuts both ways and the direction matters: it weakens the rhetoric and STRENGTHENS the event-count limb of the yardstick defect below, because an odds ratio and a Poisson rate ratio are dimensionless ratio-scale quantities against which a percentage-point half-width is not comparable at all. Against that softness stands the frame instance opened post-batch: in DCLP3 the two metrics this candidate would recompute are ALPHA-PROTECTED key secondaries, not exploratory ones, which is the strongest printed statement of audience interest anyone on this entry has reached. ID: UQ-20261023-07
Date: 2026-10-23
Status: Provisional — the Gate 2 kill fell at full text on this entry's own pre-declared falsification condition, and a late Gate 4, run separately, returned Provisional from both cold readers with nothing Unresolved; what caps the entry is novelty at Medium with a VERY CLOSE NEIGHBOUR — the second-unit limb's question form is asked and answered in print in the candidate's own single-unit adult regime (Roubinian 2022, JCI Insight 152598) — so what is new is the exposure's identity, a recorded per-unit haemoglobin mass nobody has measured, and not the question's form.
Domain(s): Medicine — transfusion medicine / patient blood management. Swept also: component manufacturing and regulatory QC, metrology and per-unit dose prediction, reliability engineering, veterinary transfusion, exercise physiology (Hbmass), neonatology, platelet dosing, econometrics (IV / natural experiment), operations research (blood inventory).

Question (canonical): In adult inpatients transfused under a single-unit policy, what fraction of the between-episode variance in the post-transfusion haemoglobin increment is attributable to the measured haemoglobin mass of the specific red-cell unit issued, and does the probability of needing a second unit depend on which unit the patient happened to receive? Reformulation note: one reformulation was used at Gate 1 (V2), adding non-bleeding adult inpatients at a service with a documented single-unit-then-reassess policy, a declared 12-48 h sampling window, inventory issue order within the ABO/Rh- and specification-compatible pool as L2's assignment mechanism with a stated covariate-balance test, a 48-h second-unit hazard, and a third limb (c) asking the pre-declared change in the 48-h second-unit rate under mass-based issuing. V1 and V2 are both on the record; V2 is the version scored.

Alternative formulations:
- Is "one unit" a dose — how much of the variability in haemoglobin response sits in the bag rather than in the patient?
- If a blood service labelled each red-cell unit with its haemoglobin mass and issued by mass instead of by count, how many fewer second units would be needed to reach the same haemoglobin target? [This is the formulation Gate 2 believed Atilla 2017 had killed. At full text the kill FELL: Atilla labelled nothing, issued on a CALCULATED figure ("donor Hb level x 450 mL") under a fixed two- or three-unit order, and prints no second-unit quantity of any kind — so what it answers is a neighbour of this formulation and not this formulation. See Novelty and the verification block.]

Motivating gap: the single-unit policy presupposes that a unit is a reproducible dose, while regulatory quality monitoring sets only a MINIMUM haemoglobin content per unit on a sampled basis, so issued units span a range of haemoglobin mass (the MAGNITUDE of that spread is unconfirmed — see presupposition (2)) and the delivered dose is unmeasured at the bedside. Three limbs are graded separately because they do not share a fate: L1 variance share and slope on grams delivered; L2 which-unit dependence of the second-unit hazard under natural, un-selected variation; L3 the mass-based-issuing counterfactual.

Presuppositions: (1) per-unit Hb mass knowable for the units actually issued — ESTABLISHED AT ABSTRACT LEVEL ONLY on Epah 2022 (13 routinely collected features; adjusted R-squared > 0.9 and mean absolute error <= 1.43 g on an independent 2,637-unit cohort), confirmed by verification at the abstract as served and by nobody at full text: Epah is COULD NOT READ at full text for every reader who has touched this entry, at four distinct routes, and the gloss "donation/production/QC features" was served to no checker. It is a PREDICTION with ~1.1-1.4 g error, not an assay, so the canonical question's word "measured" is satisfied only if a predicted value counts and the error attenuates any variance share. Adversary 5 records that its own clause 3 for this presupposition survives LITERALLY only because Gate 1's repair softened "measured" to "recorded", so a calculated field counts — and that the only recorded instrument anyone has opened is donor capillary Hb times a CONSTANT volume (Atilla's Hemosoft field), "which carries no information about the unit's actual volume". (2) Between-unit Hb mass varies — DOWNGRADED FROM ESTABLISHED. The 38.5-79.9 g spread across 6,058 units WAS SERVED TO NOBODY: the verification checker reports that the range "was NOT in the abstract as served to me", does not contradict it, and records it as unconfirmed at its read level, and adversary 4 says the same figure "was not served at any read level anyone reached". So the figure that bears L1's weight is UNCONFIRMED rather than refuted — an unread check, not a negative finding — and it rests on one reader's rendering of one record; the magnitude of its consequence remains exempt as measurand. (3) A documented single-unit-then-reassess population exists — UNVERIFIED by all three readers; nothing opened contests it. (4) Unit-to-recipient linkage — UNVERIFIED; exists in research infrastructure (REDS-III). (5) A usable post-transfusion window — supported in a paediatric source (12-18 h), UNVERIFIED for adult inpatients. (6) Monotonic response to grams delivered, and the magnitude of the variance share — MEASURAND, exempt, declared by the record and accepted by both adversaries. (7) V2's new clause, that issue order within the compatible pool is prognosis-independent — CONTESTED and UNVERIFIED; the record argues against itself (oldest-compatible-first ties issued Hb mass to storage age; specification-directed units break the pool), adversary 2 argues the opposite from its own unsourced reasoning (Hb mass is fixed at manufacture, so FIFO would tie it to storage age only via a collection-date correlation it knows no mechanism for) and says plainly that the search which would ground that never ran. V2(b)'s identification rests entirely on this clause. The late cold pass left the clause where it was and added two more self-labelled opinions on it rather than a source: adversary 4 calls the record's FIFO worry "overstated in my judgement — MY OWN REASONING, NOT A SOURCE FINDING" and states that "the search that would have grounded this (a specification or storage study printing haemoglobin recovery over storage) was NOT RUN; I had no fetches left"; adversary 5 says "I opened nothing on issuing order" and "I did not run the search that would have grounded it either way". The clause is therefore still UNVERIFIED and is scored neither way.

What would count as an answer: a variance-components estimate partitioning between-episode increment variance into issued-unit Hb mass, recipient blood volume (with that estimator's own error propagated), pre-transfusion Hb, diagnosis and operator, from linked unit-measurement and recipient-outcome records; the slope of increment on grams delivered with a CI; a 48-h second-unit hazard as a function of issued Hb mass with a reported balance test; and a pre-declared counterfactual second-unit rate under mass-based issuing at the same target. A small share with a flat slope answers in the negative and retires the question. Adversary 2's unmet specification gap: V2 never names WHICH decomposition (sequential R-squared, ICC of a unit-level random effect, Shapley/LMG), so the headline number is under-identified; the slope is estimand-invariant whichever is chosen.

1. Atilla E, Toprak SK, Civriz Bozdag S, Topcuoglu P, Arslan O. "A Randomized Comparison of Hemoglobin Content-Based Versus Standard (Unit-Based) Red Blood Cell Transfusion Policy." Turk J Hematol 2017;34(3):244-249. DOI 10.4274/tjh.2015.0365 (= PMC5544044). Printed with diacritics as Erden Atilla, Selami Koçak Toprak, Sinem Civriz Bozdağ, Pervin Topçuoğlu, Önder Arslan; e-ISSN 1308-5263; single affiliation Ankara University Faculty of Medicine, Department of Hematology, Ankara, Turkey. READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT, opened by post-batch verification on 2026-10-23 in TWO FETCHES from the citation this entry already carried — the tjh.com.tr article page the record itself had reached carries the PDF link in plain sight; jag.journalagent.com then returned a 302 to pdf.journalagent.com, which served the PDF three times for three separate sweeps. NO ROUTE FAILED, and no host refused anything. THE ENTRY'S EARLIER "FULL TEXT OPENED BY NOBODY" IS STRUCK: it recorded three spent budgets as a property of the source. COULD NOT READ, and scored neither way: the numeric interior of Tables 1-3 and the plotted values behind Figure 1, which the summariser did not render. THE NUMBERS, at their printed locations. Body Results: "The rate of finding Hb content-matched pRBCs was 41.3% (38/92) and the rate of saving pRBC units" / "was 19.8% (38/192) in the study group" — so the 38 are the units NOT transfused, and the abstract's "In the study group totally, 38 units of pRBCs were transfused with a reduction of 19.8% (38/192) from the original order" contradicts it; the body is primary (it is the Results-section definition and it reconciles arithmetically), and the body's reading is the one this entry's wording already used. The next sentence scopes the figure from the other side: "In the case of no Hb content-matched units found in the study group, two pRBC units were given as ordered in the 54 episodes." p=0.125 is printed in the ABSTRACT and the DISCUSSION only, citing Figure 1 — "The rates of achieving targeted Hb were not statistically different in the control and study groups (p=0.125)" — and a dedicated sweep for the string "0.125" found NO occurrence in the Results section; it is a failure to reject with no power calculation and no per-arm attainment numerator or denominator in running text, and the paper's Conclusion overstates it as "we clearly demonstrated that the efficacy of Hb content-based transfusion is similar to that of unit-based transfusion", so the hedged Discussion formulation is the one to quote. Significantly higher Hb content in the study arm is printed in body Results, p<0.0001, Table 3 — of the CALCULATED content. Units: counts of pRBC units. Denominator: 192 units ORDERED in the study arm, never defined in Methods but reconstructable from the printed "Eighty-four of the 92 episodes in the study group were a 2-unit order and 8 were a 3-unit order" (84x2 + 8x3 = 192 is THE CHECKER'S OWN ARITHMETIC and not a printed number; the paper never prints the 154 units transfused that this implies). Unit of analysis: the transfusion episode — "A total of 178 transfusion episodes occurred in 89 patients, which were randomized into a control group (unit-based, n=86) and a study group (Hb content-based, n=92)" — so this entry's ~2.1 units per episode is confirmed by the paper's own printed order counts (2.09), not merely by division. A third, unrelated 38 is also printed, a PATIENT count ("38 patients had 2 or more episodes"), which anyone sweeping for "38" will hit. WHAT THE FULL TEXT CHANGED, all three in the paper's own words. The EXPOSURE is not a measured mass: "Total Hb content of each pRBC unit in the inventory was calculated as" / "\"donor Hb level x 450 mL\" automatically in Hemosoft" — a capillary finger-stick HemoCue donor haemoglobin scaled by a nominal constant, so the only quantity that varies between units is the DONOR's haemoglobin; no unit was assayed, collected volume does not enter the formula, the formula is in whole-blood terms while the issued product had 200-250 mL of plasma removed and 100 mL of SAGM added with no correction for processing loss, and NO UNIT WAS LABELLED — the figure lived in a blood-bank database field queried at order time. The POLICY is multi-unit throughout: "All patients received two pRBC units in 86 transfusion episodes as requested by the clinician in the control group", with 2-unit (84/92) or 3-unit (8/92) orders in the study arm, NO reassessment step anywhere in the protocol, and therefore NO second-unit quantity of any kind in the paper. The mass-based rule FIRED IN ONLY 41.3% (38/92) OF EPISODES, the arm reverting to control behaviour in the other 54. Further defects, all new at full text: no primary endpoint declared and no power calculation; 178 episodes from 89 patients (up to 7 each) analysed as independent with Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis and chi-square only, and NO MODEL OF ANY KIND; open-label with no sequence generation or allocation-concealment method stated; Table 1's "n=92" against 89 patients; "Successfully matched" / "Unsuccessfully matched" used as Table 2 headers and never defined. Atilla is nonetheless a genuine EVALUATION — it randomised an issuing policy and printed a units-saved figure with a null on attainment, not a definition and not an announcement — and is correctly named as the nearest prior on L3.

It is a JOINT fit, and NARROWED HERE: its printed covariate set also carries "Hours between pre-Tx measurement and Tx", "Hours between Tx and post-Tx measurement" and "Transfusion year" — measurement-process and secular-trend nuisance terms — so part of the 0.25 is bought by draw timing rather than by donor, component or recipient biology, and ONE MINUS 0.25 IS NOT A RESIDUAL ATTRIBUTABLE TO UNMEASURED UNIT BIOLOGY. This entry does not lean on the unexplained share as headroom for per-unit haemoglobin mass; that inference does not follow from this paper. A MEASURED PER-UNIT HAEMOGLOBIN MASS IS ABSENT from the exposure set, and the paper does not merely omit it: it ASSUMES a constant dose ("the same RBC dose (~89 grams Hgb per transfused unit)", Discussion) and records that even the nearest proxy was unavailable (future work "will need to normalize for donor hemoglobin levels to assess the impact of in vitro"). The unit-side variables present are proxies and are named as proxies: storage duration (four categories), whole blood collection, RBC additive solution AS-3 versus AS-1, gamma irradiation, male donor, donor age, donor Rh, donor ABO. Donor haemoglobin is not among them. No variance decomposition exists — the strings "variance", "random effect" and "intraclass" do not occur, and the Abstract's "estimated correlation of 0.5" is the GEE WITHIN-RECIPIENT WORKING CORRELATION, not a unit-versus-patient split, a different quantity one word away. No second-unit probability or hazard is reported, and that is FORECLOSED BY THE SINGLE-UNIT DESIGN rather than answered either way. INSTANCED as the rule requires: the negative on the exposure set is TRUE OVER THE INSTANCES THE CHECKER OPENED (Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Tables 1-6) and UNENUMERATED over Appendix Tables 1-10; the checker grades it true for a reason it labels "MY OWN REASONING, NOT A SOURCE FINDING" — that an appendix table of model coefficients cannot contain a variable the study never measured — and this entry carries it in those words rather than as a source finding. One further sentence, flagged because it is the one most likely to be misused in either direction: the Introduction's "Donor and component characteristics may impact rates of in-vitro hemolysis or the hemoglobin content of a unit of RBC" is a HEDGE ("may impact") and a DISJUNCTION asserting no measurement, so it cannot be cited for haemoglobin content alone, in support or in refutation, and this entry cites it for nothing.

Novelty — how this differs from each: from Atilla 2017, read at FULL TEXT, the gap is THREE AXES WIDE and not the single population swap Gate 2 scored it as. The EXPOSURE differs — Atilla's per-unit figure is "calculated as 'donor Hb level x 450 mL'" in a Hemosoft database field, a capillary donor haemoglobin scaled by a nominal constant with no unit assayed and no unit labelled, where the candidate's exposure is the recorded haemoglobin mass of the specific bag. The POLICY differs — "All patients received two pRBC units in 86 transfusion episodes ... in the control group", with 2- and 3-unit orders in the study arm and no reassessment step anywhere, where the candidate's regime is single-unit-then-reassess. The ENDPOINT differs — Atilla counts units trimmed off an order at issue, where the candidate asks a reassessment-triggered 48-h second-unit rate, and Atilla prints NO second-unit quantity of any kind. Atilla also SELECTS units to hit a per-patient target, removing exactly the natural, un-selected variation L1 and L2 are about, and its rule fired in only 41.3% of episodes. At full text, after five separate dedicated sweeps, it prints none of L1's or L2's quantities: no variance decomposition, no percent-variance-explained, no slope on grams delivered, no second-unit hazard, and no model of any kind (its one dose-response-adjacent result is an uncoefficiented correlation, p=0.001, on binary target attainment). So L1 and L2 are better established as open after a full-text read than this entry could claim from an abstract. STRUCK: the clause that "a population swap (single-unit policy instead of multi-unit ordering) on an answered question is a disguised known, not a new question" — the swap is not of population alone, and this entry's own pre-declared falsification condition for the leg was met in the paper's own words for BOTH arms. From Roubinian 2022 (JCI Insight 152598), which is now the nearest prior of all and is NOT Atilla: it occupies the candidate's population, its single-unit policy frame, its unit of analysis AND its 48-hour second-unit endpoint — 102,043 evaluable single-unit adult transfusion episodes in 46,705 patients across 12 US hospitals, 2013-01-01 to 2016-12-31, an episode defined as one unit from one donor with usable pre- and post-transfusion labs and no other RBC unit in between, with a logistic model for the odds of a subsequent transfusion within 48 hours (genotype subset 6,168 episodes in 5,354 patients). It prints conditional coefficients of determination of 0.54 (full cohort) and 0.47 (RBC-Omics subset) for the haemoglobin increment at Table 3 footnote A, and on the second-unit endpoint, for units from G6PD-deficient donors an odds ratio of 2.35 (95% CI 1.16-4.76), P = 0.017, n = 43, with mean additional units 1.14 (0.75-1.52) against 0.69 (0.65-0.73), P = 0.03; for SEC14L4 homozygous-recessive donors OR 1.54 (95% CI 1.03-2.30), P = 0.035, n = 247. What differs is the EXPOSURE and nothing structural: the paper states the unit's haemoglobin content was "Not directly measured or reported" and uses donor fingerstick haemoglobin and donor sex as PROXIES, its Results calling donor factors "predicted to increase the amount of hemoglobin in a unit" and its Discussion saying increments "correlated positively with factors associated with increased RBC unit mass". It prints no R-squared on the candidate's object, no ICC, no variance component and no slope on grams delivered, and the 0.54 is a JOINT CONDITIONAL R-squared absorbing the recipient random effect, not a share attributable to any exposure; it does not restrict to non-bleeding inpatients and carries issue location as a covariate, so OUTPATIENT episodes sit inside its denominator where the candidate says inpatients; and it adds donor SNP genotypes, a bilirubin outcome and a storage-age-by-irradiation interaction that the candidate excludes, as well as recipient blood volume entering only as BMI/sex/age adjustments rather than as an estimated term with its own error. From Roubinian 2019, the candidate sits inside its population and policy and outside its exposure set; its 0.25 is a joint fit on 27,384 24-hour episodes whose covariates include draw timing and transfusion year, and the paper ASSUMES a constant ~89 g per unit rather than measuring one, so it neither supplies L1's number nor forecloses it. From DeSimone 2023, the endpoint match is EXACT and not a loose resemblance — its secondary endpoint is additional RBC transfusion within 48 hours of the index event, the same window and event class as V2(b) — and the difference is in population and exposure: VLBW infants under a neonatal threshold protocol receiving WEIGHT-INDEXED ALIQUOTS in mL/kg, 567 episodes in 254 infants, with donor, component and recipient metadata none of which is grams, and no variance figure of any kind printed. STRUCK: the gloss "where one unit is a multiple of total blood volume rather than a ~10% increment", which is FALSE OF THIS PAPER — it does not transfuse whole units, and its component exposure is "Issued aliquot volume in mL/kg". The DIRECTION of the regime point survives, on a different mechanism (a neonatal weight-indexed aliquot is a far larger fractional exchange than an adult unit), but the only arithmetic offered for it — about 15 mL/kg against a neonatal blood volume of about 80 mL/kg, roughly 19% of circulating volume, versus a ~300 mL adult unit against ~5000 mL at about 6% — is THE CHECKER'S OWN ARITHMETIC ON TEXTBOOK FIGURES and not a number either paper printed; DeSimone's printed mean aliquot volume in mL/kg was not retrieved, the checker's budget having been spent, so this entry states the direction and claims no figure. From Saqlain 2022, a paper explicitly about red-cell concentrate characteristics and the increment, the candidate differs in the same place again: no concentrate haemoglobin content or mass measured or reported and unit volume not analysed, donor haemoglobin entering only as two categories (12-13 against 14-15 g/dl, increments 2.39 +/- 0.42 against 2.50 +/- 0.44 g/dl, p = 0.2200, Table IV, p. 1423), with no R-squared, no variance component, no ICC and no additional-transfusion endpoint, in 100 PAEDIATRIC recipients at one Lahore centre. Its 12-18 h post-transfusion draw does show that the candidate's window is one the field actually samples in. Adversary 5 flags its internal inconsistencies (a donor age band printed 31-44 in Table IV against 31-45 in the text; washing p < 0.0001 in the abstract against p < 0.001 in the Discussion) and says it "would not lean on its figures"; this entry does not lean on them either. From Epah 2022, the candidate's exposure is its output: it supplies the instrument and none of the answers.

Novelty confidence: Medium with a VERY CLOSE NEIGHBOUR — not Low, and not Medium clean. The Low grade is STRUCK: it was set on limb L3 and alternative formulation 2 by Atilla 2017 read at ABSTRACT level, and at full text that number's class does not match the candidate's (units ORDERED in a multi-unit arm, 38 units SAVED from initial orders, no reassessment endpoint and no second-unit quantity of any kind). What caps novelty now is a different document. THE CANDIDATE'S SECOND-UNIT LIMB AS A QUESTION FORM — does the chance of needing another unit depend on which unit the patient happened to receive, in adults, at 48 hours — IS ASKED AND ANSWERED IN PRINT IN THE CANDIDATE'S OWN FIELD AND OWN SINGLE-UNIT REGIME, affirmatively, on a unit-level attribute: Roubinian 2022, JCI Insight 2022;7(1):e152598, DOI 10.1172/jci.insight.152598, G6PD-deficient donor units OR 2.35 (95% CI 1.16-4.76). Adversary 4 states that V1's L2 AS ORIGINALLY WORDED WOULD HAVE BEEN KILLED BY THAT PAPER and that Gate 1's reformulation is precisely what saves it. So what survives is novelty ON THE EXPOSURE'S IDENTITY — recorded grams in the issued bag — AND NOT ON THE QUESTION'S FORM. Adversary 4's summary of the record as it now stands: "six groups' documents are now open across this record and not one measures the candidate's exposure." Both late cold readers placed novelty at Medium with a very close neighbour rather than at Medium clean, which under Gate 5's own wording is a PROVISIONAL CEILING; the two earlier adversaries had graded the pre-full-text record at "Medium with a close neighbour at best, not Low for the question as canonically worded" (adversary 1) and "does not reach Medium" (adversary 2). For L1 and L2 taken alone, nothing anyone has opened across the 29 queries plus the cold pass's 20 prints the variance share attributable to the issued unit's haemoglobin mass, the slope on grams delivered, or a second-unit hazard as a function of issued haemoglobin mass; the one nominated carrier that was opened (DeSimone 2023, now at full text) prints none of them, and the second nominated carrier (PMC10530070) turned out to be that same paper.

Significance — consequence: if a large share of between-episode increment variance sits in the bag, "one unit" is not a dose, the single-unit audit indicator is measuring an input whose own spread is unestablished here — the 38.5-79.9 g range that would make it "more than two-fold" was served to nobody, so this entry claims the direction and not the factor — and mass-labelling becomes a cheap auditable intervention; if the share is small with a flat slope, the convention is vindicated and the storage-and-donor-factor literature loses a candidate nuisance term. Both answers change something.
Significance — audience: blood services' quality and inventory functions (now a software decision, not a laboratory one, since Epah 2022 needs no new assay and reports a free, open-source web application — which removes the cost objection adversary 2 raised; both facts are ABSTRACT-SCOPED, and the abstract reached the verification checker only as a paraphrase); PBM committees and guideline writers who own the single-unit recommendation and its audit indicator; regulators who set a minimum rather than a target or tolerance; vein-to-vein research consortia who hold the linkage but not the grams.
Significance — fecundity: per-unit dose labelling as a design object; tolerance-based rather than minimum-based specification; variance-based rather than count-based transfusion audit; a re-reading of null storage-duration trials in which unlabelled dose heterogeneity was never modelled.
Significance — anchoring: the single-unit policy's own evidence base; the expected-versus-observed increment literature; the storage-lesion nulls; and this ledger's UQ-20261017-36 (nominal versus delivered inhaled dose).

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary with an incentive gap on each side — and verification narrowed the framing the mechanism can support. Per-unit Hb content is a regulator-facing, SAMPLED, pass/fail quantity against a minimum, so no service generated a content figure for the units it actually issued; a per-unit figure for every unit became obtainable only with a validated predictor published in 2022. The boundary is visible inside single papers: Epah 2022 computed content for 8,695 units (6,058 + 2,637, the checker's OWN ARITHMETIC on two printed abstract numbers) and published zero recipient outcomes at the abstract level that is all anyone has read, while DeSimone 2023 modelled increments and 48-hour additional transfusions on 567 episodes and never had the grams, and Roubinian 2022 modelled the increment and the 48-hour second unit on 102,043 episodes with the unit's haemoglobin content "Not directly measured or reported". But the mechanism explains a missing MEASUREMENT better than a missing QUESTION, and verification sharpened that against this entry in two ways. FIRST, THE FRAMING MUST CHANGE: ROUBINIAN 2019 NAMES THE GAP IN ITS OWN VOICE — its Discussion says future work "will need to normalize for donor hemoglobin levels to assess the impact of in vitro" and lists what that work would need, "including hemoglobin content, biochemical properties" — so the honest framing of limb L1 is "UNPERFORMED, AND FLAGGED AS FUTURE WORK BY ROUBINIAN ET AL. 2019", NOT "un-asked". Announced is not performed, so the question remains unanswered; but the stronger claim that nobody posed it is not true here, and only the measurement claim is. SECOND, THE CORROBORATION BASE IS THINNER THAN THIS ENTRY PRESENTED: DeSimone 2023 and Roubinian 2019 SHARE TWO AUTHORS — Nareg H. Roubinian and Colleen Plimier — and the same REDS-III linked vein-to-vein resource, and Roubinian 2022 is that same group a third time. ONE GROUP, three populations, not three independent supports. By the front matter the checkers resolved, the priors named here are FIVE GROUPS and not five independent efforts: Atilla/Arslan (Ankara), Roubinian/Plimier (REDS-III and REDS-IV-P, three papers), Epah/Schäfer (Frankfurt-Tübingen), Davenport (Michigan, sole author) and Saqlain (Lahore) — that tally is THIS ENTRY'S OWN ARITHMETIC on the checkers' front-matter reads, where adversary 4 counted six groups. Atilla's article, the same group's conference item and the Turkish thesis remain ONE group citing itself, counted once, and the DGTI-2022 congress item a search returned is Epah's own group's conference abstract, one document and not corroboration. So the mechanism this entry relies on is NOT "two independent teams modelled the increment and neither had the grams" but the sharper and simultaneously thinner one: THE ONE TEAM HOLDING THE UNIT-TO-RECIPIENT LINKAGE MODELLED THE INCREMENT THREE TIMES — adults, VLBW neonates, then adults with donor genotypes — AND NEVER HAD THE GRAMS. The programme has also been stated in print since at least 2005 ("Blood components should be labeled for content", Davenport R, sole author, Transfusion 2005;45(1):3-4, DOI 10.1111/j.1537-2995.2005.04323.x — front matter now resolved; text unread BY SPENT BUDGET and not by any failed route) and named in a 2022 title ("From Unit to Dose"), which is why adversary 2 graded this attack Partial and adversary 4 graded it Partial again.

Note what these discharges cannot do: well-posedness is 2/3 and Gate 1's single reformulation is SPENT, so this entry cannot reach Validated on them alone, and the novelty ceiling Roubinian 2022 sets — the question's FORM asked and answered in the candidate's own regime — is not a document-retrieval problem and is discharged by none of them.

Strongest remaining objection: NOT Atilla, and no longer that the bundle contains an answered question — the single leg the Rejected verdict stood on FELL at full text, on this entry's OWN pre-declared falsification condition. The strongest objection now is that THE SECOND-UNIT LIMB'S QUESTION FORM IS ALREADY ASKED AND ANSWERED IN THE CANDIDATE'S OWN REGIME AND ONLY THE EXPOSURE IS NEW. Roubinian 2022 (JCI Insight 2022;7(1):e152598, DOI 10.1172/jci.insight.152598), opened at full text independently by both cold readers and by nobody before them, asks in print — in adults, under a single-unit frame, at the same 48-hour window, with the episode as the unit of analysis — whether the chance of needing another unit depends on which unit the patient happened to receive, and answers it affirmatively on an attribute of the specific unit: 102,043 evaluable single-unit episodes in 46,705 patients at 12 hospitals, a logistic model for a subsequent transfusion within 48 hours, G6PD-deficient donor units OR 2.35 (95% CI 1.16-4.76), P = 0.017, n = 43, and SEC14L4 homozygous-recessive donor units OR 1.54 (95% CI 1.03-2.30), P = 0.035, n = 247. Adversary 4 states that V1's L2 AS ORIGINALLY WORDED WOULD HAVE BEEN KILLED BY THAT PAPER and that Gate 1's reformulation is precisely what saves it. So what survives is novelty on the EXPOSURE'S IDENTITY — a recorded per-unit haemoglobin mass, which that paper says was "Not directly measured or reported" and replaces with donor fingerstick haemoglobin and donor sex as proxies — AND NOT ON THE QUESTION'S FORM. That is a cap and not a kill for reasons both readers give: the paper prints no R-squared on the candidate's object, no ICC, no variance component and no slope on grams delivered; its 0.54 and 0.47 (Table 3 footnote A) are JOINT CONDITIONAL R-squareds absorbing the recipient random effect, so neither is a share attributable to any exposure; it does not restrict to non-bleeding inpatients and carries issue location as a covariate, so outpatient episodes sit inside its denominator where the candidate says inpatients; and on the exposure itself, in adversary 4's words, "six groups' documents are now open across this record and not one measures the candidate's exposure". The two legs the old verdict would have fallen back on are both weaker than it assumed, and neither becomes the strongest objection. The programme leg — that the framing is a named published programme (Epah 2022 "From Unit to Dose"; the 2005 Transfusion title) — does not survive as a kill on the canonical question, because Epah PREDICTS the exposure and ANNOUNCES a dosing application without measuring any recipient outcome at the abstract level that is all anyone has read, and an announcement is not an evaluation; the 2005 item is still text-unread by everyone, now with its front matter resolved (Davenport R, sole author). The triviality leg is explicitly algebraic and is self-labelled by two adversaries as THEIR OWN reasoning with the grounding search unrun, and one adversary refuted it by showing the two inputs sit in separate databases. What this entry therefore claims as un-asked is narrower than it claimed before: the variance attribution to a recorded per-unit haemoglobin mass, and the which-unit dependence AS A FUNCTION OF THAT EXPOSURE rather than as a question form.

Date: 2026-10-23
Status: Rejected — Gate 2 (novelty Low; disguised known on an asked-and-answered question), re-settled at a LATE and SEPARATE Gate 4 re-run after post-batch verification destroyed the original ground: fatal on adversary 4's attack-2 Unresolved, which stands on LaMotte et al. 1977, Public Health Reports 92(6):554–560, PMID 200968, read at FULL TEXT — a document nobody had opened — while the original Parsons-based ground is WITHDRAWN, not downgraded, and adversary 5 returned Provisional on the same record.
Domain(s): Medicine — laboratory medicine, accreditation and quality assurance. Adjacent vocabularies swept: forensic QA, regulated workplace drug testing, anti-doping metrology, environmental/ISO 17043 PT, TB smear-microscopy EQA, regulatory-inspection economics.
Question (canonical): For a pre-declared set of analytes and accredited clinical laboratories, what is the signed difference between a laboratory's error rate on declared external-quality-assessment samples and its error rate on identical material submitted blind through the routine patient workflow, and how much of any difference is attributable to declared-sample handling (senior-staff assignment, batching, repeat runs before reporting)? Reformulation note: one Gate 1 reformulation was taken and is recorded as R1 — same estimand, restricted to currently accredited general laboratories on automated analysers with retained middleware audit trails from >=2 vendors, analytes limited to those with documented commutability, scored against a reference-method-assigned target, with the share of blind specimens recognised by staff reported as a primary result and the difference decomposed against logged operator grade, repeat runs before release and time to report. R1 is graded here, and it is not a free repair: it adds two load-bearing feasibility premises (laboratory consent to covert submission; operator grade recoverable from middleware), the second of which the record labels its own inference with no search behind it.
Alternative formulations:
- Do clinical laboratories grade themselves on an exam they know they are sitting — what is the declared-versus-blind performance gap?
- Transplanting forensic science's blind quality-control programmes into clinical pathology: what would a blind EQA scheme have found that the declared scheme did not?
Motivating gap: blind proficiency specimens are a standing instrument in forensic QA and federally regulated workplace drug testing because declared samples are known to be handled differently; clinical accreditation and PT use declared samples. CORRECTED AT GATE 2: the transplant premise is false. The design is dormant own-field practice, and the earliest instance any reader has reached at FULL TEXT is 49 years old: CDC's 1977 blind-versus-mail-distributed comparison in US urine drug-screening laboratories (LaMotte et al. 1977, Public Health Reports 92(6):554–560), followed by CDC blind surveys of US clinical laboratories c. 1979–1982 and a paired open-versus-blind blood-lead experiment in Clinical Chemistry in 2001 (abstract-only at every route any reader has reached, and now verified paywalled at the publisher). The intake's load-bearing claim that the quantity "currently has no number attached to it anywhere in clinical medicine" is false as written for QUALITATIVE detection, where LaMotte 1977 prints paired per-drug counts in the same laboratories; for the candidate's own QUANTITATIVE class the claim is UNESTABLISHED rather than refuted, because the signed difference is printed nowhere any reader has reached.
Presuppositions: (1) material commutable with patient specimens and indistinguishable at intake — demonstrated in kind for three analyte classes (urine drug screens, LaMotte 1977, read at full text; blood lead, Parsons 2001, abstract level only; anti-doping urine), generality across a routine chemistry menu UNVERIFIED; (2) a governance route for covert submission without a fictitious patient identity — CONTESTED, and now sourced ONE WAY AND AGAINST the candidate: the only executed blind-submission protocol any reader has reached in full text achieved indistinguishability by routing samples through hospital administrators and methadone-centre officials and, in its 1975 arm, BY USING FICTITIOUS PATIENT IDENTITIES (LaMotte 1977), so the one documented instance of this document-kind satisfies the indistinguishability half by violating the no-fictitious-identity half. Adversary 4 labels the consenting-donor alternative that would satisfy both halves as ITS OWN REASONING, NOT A SOURCE FINDING, and names no instance of a clinical laboratory consenting to covert submission since CLIA '88; the nearest quantitative prior's requisition/ethics Methods remain unreadable at every route tried; (3) error scored against a participant-independent reference value — a declared design requirement that NEITHER prior meets (Parsons 2001 scored against CLIA '88 tolerance bands; LaMotte 1977 scored correct qualitative detection of a drug known to be present), so R1's own specification is unprecedented at the read level achieved; (4) that laboratories handle declared samples differently — MEASURAND EXEMPTION declared and applied by both adversaries; (5) concealment holds — MEASURAND (R1 reports the recognised share); (6) middleware retains operator grade, repeat-run count and time to report — UNVERIFIED, and literally absent in the one vendor document anyone opened (Data Innovations Instrument Manager inspection guide: operator identity and event timestamps present; rerun logging, retention period and operator grade/seniority NOT PRESENT on a second targeted sweep). Zero middleware specifications were opened across all three runs; that is an unrun check, not a premise that fails.
What would count as an answer: paired per-analyte error rates plus bias and imprecision on the SAME material in the SAME laboratories over the same period, declared versus blind, with confidence intervals; the recognised share of blind specimens; and the handling mechanism measured from middleware logs (operator grade, repeat runs before release, time to report) rather than inferred.

WHAT IS PRINTED AND WHAT IS NOT — and this entry's earlier statement that the paper prints the signed difference with units and denominators is WITHDRAWN: the abstract prints TWO RATES AND A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT and no signed difference. NO DENOMINATOR IS PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THE ABSTRACT: no N of blind results, no N of open results, no aliquot count per laboratory. Also printed: 13 of 22 laboratories (60%) exhibited a statistically significant difference between blind and open performance in phase 1 — a COUNT OF SIGNIFICANCE VERDICTS carrying no magnitude and no units, which establishes THAT a per-laboratory paired contrast was computed and does NOT show that its value was printed — and seven of 22 met the aggregate acceptability threshold under open testing but not under blind, two of those with gross discrepancies prompting further investigation. Methods, Results body and every table and figure remain unread at every route tried, so the numerator's exclusions, the target-assignment method, the requisition route, the ethics arrangement, any concealment audit, any bias/imprecision split and any per-laboratory SIGNED difference with its N are COULD NOT CHECK — unknown to every reader so far rather than absent from the paper, and the design (multiple aliquots of up to 72 pools against a two-sided criterion) is precisely the design that would support such tables.

A regulation ASSERTING a requirement — a definition, not an evaluation; it grounds audience and legal chill, and it does not ground the kill. READ LEVEL: FULL TEXT, in ONE FETCH, at stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/65385/cdc_65385_DS1.pdf, by adversary 4's own query T9 — a document listed as returned-not-opened by every reader before, and nominated BY KIND and left unopened for budget by the verification pass that named it. Regime: US laboratories performing urine drug-abuse screening for hospitals and methadone treatment centres (1973 arm, 22 laboratories; 1975 arm, nine per the text and "24 laboratories" per Table 3's heading — the paper is internally inconsistent here); unit of analysis = the DETECTION OPPORTUNITY (drug x sample x laboratory); operating condition = identical material sent twice, once mail-distributed and declared, once submitted through hospitals or methadone centres as ordinary patient specimens, with fictitious patient identities in the 1975 arm; threshold = correct qualitative detection of a drug known to be present. WHAT IT PRINTS, 1973 arm: barbiturates, mailed 110 of 110 opportunities detected against blind 110 opportunities with "only 79 correct detections" (31 missed); morphine, mailed "110 opportunities" with the drug "missed only once" against blind "111 opportunities" where "the drug was missed 41 times"; methadone, mailed 110 opportunities missed twice against blind "106 opportunities" missed 21 times; d-amphetamine, blind "82 opportunities" with "only 39 correct detections". Its summary sentence as served: "the laboratories detected a greater percentage of the drugs in the mailed samples than in the blind samples" — a clause that ASSERTS the gap. THE MISS-RATE DIFFERENCES OF APPROXIMATELY +28.2 PERCENTAGE POINTS (barbiturates), +36.0 (morphine) AND +18.0 (methadone) ARE ADVERSARY 4'S OWN ARITHMETIC ON THOSE PRINTED COUNTS, NOT PRINTED FIGURES, and the paper prints no confidence intervals, so no uncertainty can be carried through them. Adversary 4 checked the paper's internal consistency before leaning on it and found the 1975 arm cannot be decomposed from what it prints — the 1975 morphine blind counts (31 + 24 = 55) exceed the stated 45 opportunities, the 1975 methadone blind line as served contradicts the paper's own discussion, and the 1975 laboratory count differs between text and table heading — so it leans ONLY on the 1973 arm and on the design, and that honesty item travels with the figures. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not print the candidate's quantity. Its numerator class is MISSED QUALITATIVE DETECTION OPPORTUNITIES for a drug qualitatively present, not results falling outside a quantitative acceptability limit, and its denominator is detection opportunities, not results, not specimens, not laboratories; it does not measure the handling mechanism (the explanations it offers — staff reticence about reporting positives, routine specimens "processed en masse without strict quality controls" — are, in the paper's own framing, assumptions from laboratory directors' statements, not measurements); and it does not report the share of blind specimens recognised by staff. Both of R1's added limbs are genuinely absent here. WHAT IT SETTLES, at full text and under its own title rather than at an abstract: that the question was ASKED, DESIGNED, EXECUTED AND PUBLISHED 49 years ago in the candidate's own field, own country and own regulatory system — and that the MULTI-ANALYTE FRAMING this record treated as surviving novel residue is itself 1977 prior art in qualitative form.
Novelty — how this differs from each: from Parsons, the candidate generalises one analyte to a declared multi-analyte set, moves from UP TO 42 blood-lead-certified laboratories (phase 1 analysed on 22) to general accredited laboratories on modern automated/middleware platforms, adds bias and imprecision as separate estimands, adds a concealment audit, and adds the mechanism limb; it does not differ on the pairing, the submission design as characterised, or the sign, and it DOES differ on the unit and the printed quantity — Parsons's printed rates are pooled RESULT-LEVEL while the candidate's estimand is LABORATORY-LEVEL, a different quantity one word away, and Parsons prints no signed difference and no denominators at any read level anyone has reached. On a literal reading of R1 the two analyte sets are disjoint. From Boone, it differs in regime and in carrying a quantitative paired estimand; it does not differ in what it asks, though the sentence in which Boone poses anything is unread. From LaMotte 1977, it differs in analyte class and scoring (qualitative detection of a known-present drug versus results outside a quantitative acceptability band around a reference-method-assigned target), in era and platform, in adding bias and imprecision as separate estimands, in adding the concealment audit and in adding the mechanism decomposition; LaMotte in turn covers qualitative drug-of-abuse detection in 1970s screening laboratories, which R1's own restriction to routine quantitative analytes on automated analysers excludes outright. It does NOT differ from LaMotte in what it asks, in the pairing, in the submission design or in the sign. From the 1998 review, it differs by proposing to measure what the review lists as one member of a list of limitations and names, in one member of a list of suggestions, as "occasional use of 'blind' PT". The Quattrone/CSAFE forensic blind-PT paper, returned under two hosts by two runs, has now been opened by NOBODY across four readers and grounds no grade in either direction; its cited URL is DEAD post-migration (scholarship.law.upenn.edu/qc_articles/23 returns 302 to a repository search page answering "Sorry, no results found that match your criteria"), so a later pass needs a new locator rather than a retry of the citation's own route, and lib.dr.iastate.edu/csafe_pubs/74 has never been attempted.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: real but substantially pre-empted. If the gap is large and general, accreditors, EQA providers and payers cannot read declared-EQA performance as an estimate of patient-result quality, and the mechanism limb would name the handling practice to interdict. The intake's claim that a null would retire a suspicion with no number anywhere in clinical medicine is false, but it is false in a narrower way than this entry first recorded: what exists for blood lead is TWO POOLED RESULT-LEVEL RATES AND A P VALUE, not the candidate's laboratory-level signed difference, and what exists at full text is LaMotte 1977's paired per-drug QUALITATIVE detection counts. A null would bound the generalisability of those numbers, which is smaller.
Significance — audience: real and documentary, not inflated — CMS/CLIA and CLIAC, CAP and ISO 15189 accreditors, EQA/PT providers, and the forensic and anti-doping QA communities that already run covert arms. A regulator codified the concern (42 CFR 493.801), the field's flagship chemistry journal published the experiment, and an anti-doping accreditation regime pays for a double-blind arm today.
Significance — fecundity: moderate. Makes askable: what share of accreditation findings would change under blind submission; whether autoverification rules act differently on declared and blind material; whether the PT-referral prohibition has measurable handling effects.
Significance — anchoring: commutability literature; the EQA-versus-patient-sample validity debate; the ledger's UQ-20261022-06 (share of released results that is not the first valid measurement, from middleware logs), of which this mechanism limb is a declared-versus-blind stratification.
Reason for silence: there is no silence — dormancy with mechanisms. Disciplinary boundary (the two own-field precedents sit in public-health laboratory surveillance and blood-lead toxicology, literatures routine chemistry and accreditation science do not read, which is why the design looks foreign from inside the field); provider conflict of interest; legal chill from the PT-referral rule; specimen-identity and billing integrity. These explain non-UPTAKE of a published positive over 49 years, measured from LaMotte 1977 rather than from the 1998 recommendation. The gate asks why nobody ASKED, and nobody can answer that here because it was asked. Adversary 2 adds that these mechanisms cannot reach the anti-doping case at all — no patient, no requisition, no bill — and that system runs both arms anyway. Adversary 4 returned attack 7 UNRESOLVED on exactly this point, in its own terms: the record's answer offers a mechanism for non-REPETITION, and a mechanism for non-repetition cannot support an un-asked finding. In the course of that attack it SOURCED the part of the mechanism no verification checker could reach — 42 CFR 493.801(b)(1) and (b)(5) as quoted in DAB 1951, which require PT samples to be run "with the laboratory's regular patient workload … using the laboratory's routine methods" under an attestation "documenting that [PT] samples were tested in the same manner as patient specimens", with (b)(4) carrying revocation for referral — and concluded that it cuts FOR the candidate on dormancy, because a laboratory consenting to this study is consenting to a measurement of whether its own signed federal attestation is true. That is a real incentive-and-legal-exposure mechanism, and it explains a 49-year gap after a published positive rather than an absence of asking. ## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-23)

### What the pass did, and the headline

Three fresh-context checkers ran on this entry, one per load-bearing prior or kill leg, each handed the claim and its sources but NOT the reviewers' reasoning, and each blind to the others. Checker 1 (VERIFY-uq08-parsons-fulltext.md) was sent to Parsons et al. 2001 to establish, at first hand, whether it prints the candidate's primary estimand — the signed declared-minus-blind difference, with units and denominators, on the candidate's unit, endpoint, comparator and sign. Checker 2 (VERIFY-uq08-boone-1982.md) was sent to Boone et al. 1982 to establish whether it asks the candidate's question in the candidate's own field, and whether it prints an error rate for either arm. Checker 3 (VERIFY-uq08-review-and-corroborators.md) was sent to the 1998 own-field review behind PubMed 9448012 and to the three corroborative legs — the WADA EQAS deck, 42 CFR 493.801 and the Quattrone/CSAFE forensic paper — plus the group-independence sentence. The pass then forced a consequence it had no authority to settle: the leg this entry's Rejection stood on could not be established, so Gate 4 was incomplete, and Gate 4 was re-run late and separately. THE VERDICT DID NOT MOVE AND ITS REASON WAS REPLACED IN FULL. This entry stays Rejected, on a wholly new ground and a different document, and nothing below should be read as a confirmation of the original kill — the original kill is WITHDRAWN, not downgraded.

### Read level reached for each source, with COULD NOT READ kept strictly distinct from NOT FOUND

Parsons et al. 2001: ABSTRACT ONLY, plus front matter, at four routes by five readers; Materials and Methods, the Results body and every table and figure were never reached by anyone, and the publisher route is a verified paywall, so the shortfall is a route fact and not a budget fact. Boone et al. 1982: ABSTRACT ONLY, and only through an aggregator (RePEc/IDEAS), with front matter NEVER REACHED; three publisher paths returned a site-level client_error (ROUTE FAILURE) and doi.org rate-limited on a single unrepeated attempt (SPENT BUDGET), which the checker recorded as both rather than logging the paper unreadable. The 1998 review: ABSTRACT ONLY at pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9448012, with front matter NOT REACHED and the publisher never attempted — COULD NOT READ at the publisher, strictly distinct from NOT FOUND. WADA EQAS deck: FULL TEXT, whole deck (the slide count is the summariser's inference, page markers being inconsistent; the content is as served). 42 CFR 493.801: COULD NOT READ by the verification pass — one eCFR route tried, client_error, then budget gone — and then SOURCED at full text by adversary 4 through HHS DAB decision No. 1951. The Quattrone/CSAFE forensic paper: COULD NOT READ by all four readers, its URL dead. LaMotte et al. 1977: FULL TEXT, one fetch, by adversary 4 — the only document in this record read in full at first hand, and one that every earlier reader had listed unopened.

### 1. The original fatal leg is WITHDRAWN, not downgraded

The leg was that Parsons et al. 2001 prints the candidate's primary estimand with units and denominators, on the candidate's unit, endpoint, comparator and sign. Checker 1 re-tested it at first hand across eight fetches, including the publisher route the citation names, and it failed on the leg's own three terms. First, the SIGNED DIFFERENCE IT REQUIRES IS NOT PRINTED: what is printed is "We found that 17.7% of all blind PT results were classified as unacceptable compared with only 4.5% of open PT results", with P <0.001 from the OUP serving and NO DENOMINATORS ANYWHERE in the abstract, so the 13.2-percentage-point gap is the checker's own subtraction and any reader's, not a printed figure. Second, THE PRINTED RATES ARE RESULT-LEVEL POOLED where the candidate's estimand is LABORATORY-LEVEL — the quotation's own scoping words are "of all blind PT results" / "of open PT results" — a different quantity one word away. Third, THE ANALYTE IS BLOOD LEAD ALONE against the candidate's declared MULTI-ANALYTE SET, a mismatch checkable at any read level and sufficient on its own to demote the paper from match to near neighbour on regime. Because the leg is an EXISTENCE claim about what a document prints, the checker instanced it: over the instances opened — the OUP article-abstract page, the LVHN repository metadata record, the dbpia mirror — THE PREMISE IS FALSE; over the full text, which nobody in this record has opened, it is UNENUMERATED. It is unestablished, not refuted, and a leg that cannot be established cannot carry a Rejection. What survives of the paper is not trivial and the entry now says only that: a real paired open-versus-blind study in certified clinical laboratories on identical material, blind arm "disguised as routine patient specimens", printing two arm rates and a significance verdict plus the laboratory-level count "13 of 22 laboratories (60%) exhibited a statistically significant difference" — a count of significance verdicts that establishes THAT a per-laboratory paired contrast was computed and does not show that its VALUE was printed.

### 2. The entry's recorded read level on Parsons was INFLATED, and the paywall is now verified

This entry logged "abstract plus partial Methods/Results". Checker 1 reached ABSTRACT ONLY in eight fetches and recorded that if an earlier reader genuinely saw Methods or Results text, that route is unrecorded and should be recorded — and if not, the read level is inflated. No such route exists anywhere in this record, so the read level was inflated and has been corrected in the entry's own prose. One cold reader then tested the publisher route nobody had tested and found the paper PAYWALLED: "You do not currently have access to this article", the PDF marked "Subscribers Only". ABSTRACT-ONLY IS THEREFORE A ROUTE FACT AND NOT A BUDGET FACT, which also corrects checker 1's own hedge that its shortfall was partly a spent budget.

### 3. Both original adversaries' attack-2 Unresolved rested on that same abstract-level read

Adversary 1 and adversary 2 each returned attack 2 Unresolved against an abstract-level read of the ONE document the leg turned on — adversary 2 at the dbpia mirror, adversary 1 at academic.oup.com. THEIR AGREEMENT WAS NOT CORROBORATION: it was two readings of one abstract of one document from one author group, and the repeated appearance of that title across every search is one document surfacing many times, counted as title matches and never as corroboration. ### Did the verdict move

No. The verdict stays REJECTED, and its REASON IS REPLACED IN FULL. The original ground — Gate 2 plus attack-2 Unresolved from both original adversaries, all of it standing on Parsons et al. 2001 — is withdrawn, because the leg failed on its own three terms when re-tested at first hand and because both adversaries' agreement was two readings of one abstract. Adversary 5, on the same record, returned Provisional with nothing Unresolved, so the Rejection is a judgement on a split, decided by this ledger's rule that one Unresolved on attack 2 from any reader is fatal. Nothing here promotes anything, and no leg was re-graded by the amendment itself.

### Conditions that would close each leg, written as prose because this entry is Rejected

On the withdrawn Parsons leg, the remainder of checker 1's bearing was converted to a condition rather than a finding, and it is discharged by ONE fetch of the published full text — the OUP article-pdf for Clin Chem 47(2):322–330, or an interlibrary or institutional copy of that PDF, since only the Methods and Results tables themselves are the right KIND of document (the LVHN record is a metadata page with a truncated abstract and no PDF and is expressly NOT that kind) — checking three things: whether any table prints a per-laboratory SIGNED open-minus-blind difference with its N; whether Methods describe the blind specimens entering the ROUTINE PATIENT ACCESSIONING WORKFLOW indistinguishably or by a separate route; and whether a concealment audit and a bias/imprecision split exist. If those tables do print per-laboratory signed gaps, the first two failures partly reverse and that leg regains ground on the estimand, never on the analyte. On Boone, opening AJPH 72(12):1364–1368 by any non-PMC route would answer the arm numbers, the question sentence and the Methods route with printed figures, denominators and a quotation, after which that leg could be stated at full-text level. On the 1998 review, the publisher route nobody has tried would settle the attribution, the article-type label and — the single most decisive unopened check in this entry — whether its reference list enumerates any declared-versus-blind study in an analyte other than lead. Two cheaper checks would bear on R1 rather than on the priors: two or three real instrument-middleware audit-trail specifications, which must say what the trail retains per result and must print whether pre-release repeat runs, operator identity and release timestamps are retained; and any documented instance of a clinical laboratory consenting to covert submission since CLIA '88, a search adversary 4 states was NOT RUN.

Checker 3 closed its bearing by saying that striking the group-count sentence "does not touch the Parsons et al. 2001 leg on which the verdict actually stands, so it does not reverse the rejection". Domain(s): Medicine — diagnostic devices, screening programmes, regulatory science (autonomous AI diagnosis)

Question (canonical): For FDA-cleared autonomous diagnostic AI devices in routine deployment, what is the decision-flip rate when the same patient is re-imaged within the same visit by a different operator on the same camera model, and how does that intra-visit flip rate compare with the uncertainty margins on the sensitivity and specificity in the device's own clearance study? (Source method: new-instrument questions. Gate 1's reformulation allowance was recorded NOT USED; the narrower repair the record drafted is noted under "Suggested first step" and is a different question, not this one.)

Alternative formulations: (1) If the patient walked back in and was photographed again, would the autonomous device say the same thing? (2) Clearance measures accuracy against a reading centre under protocolised imaging; what is repeatability under deployment imaging, and does the flip rate exceed the margin the device was cleared on?

Motivating gap: a cleared device issues refer / do-not-refer / insufficient-quality with no human read, deployed in primary care where acquisition is by non-specialist staff rather than the clearance study's trained photographers; the patient receives one acquisition. The gap is FALSE as stated: the clearance file of a named device in this class contains the re-acquisition measurement, and for AEYE-DS the pivotal operators were themselves novices "who had not previously performed ocular imaging" (K221183, adversary 1 Source B), so the protocolised-vs-deployment premise is contested across devices.

Presuppositions: P1 autonomous devices in routine use at scale — class-level TRUE on two primary clearance files; the no-human-read wording is UNVERIFIED verbatim in every IFU opened ("indicated for use by healthcare providers to automatically detect"; K200667 also has the operator "working under supervision of a healthcare provider"). The verdict does not need it. P2 intra-visit re-acquisition feasible — TRUE, sourced (K200667 Cohort P1, 3 operator-camera pairings in which each of 3 operators was fixed to one of 2 units of one camera model, so NOT a crossed design and the operator contrast is confounded with camera unit; K221183 with ">= 8 minutes between successive imaging"). P3 deterministic output for a fixed image set — UNVERIFIED and unmeasured; no opened document re-runs identical images, so no file separates acquisition- from algorithm-induced flips. P4 flip is consequential, ungradable its own outcome — TRUE, sourced: OA = (PP+NN+UU)/N over negative/positive/ungradable. P5 clearance prints a stated uncertainty — TRUE, three instances, three different interval constructions (clustered bootstrap; exact binomial; pre-specified one-sided 97.5% lower limits). P6 operator, camera unit and device version recorded — TRUE inside the pre-market sub-study, UNVERIFIED in routine deployment logs. P7 flip rate and clearance margin commensurable — CONTESTED to FALSE (adversary 2, attack 4).

What would count as an answer: per named device, an intra-visit decision-flip rate with a CI, by output category, decomposed into acquisition- and algorithm-induced components (the latter from re-running identical images), from a pre-declared deployment cohort with a re-imaging fraction pre-declared independently of the first result, plus an explicit comparison with that device's clearance interval.

Real for the residual: if deployment flip rates exceed the pre-market inter-operator figure, the cleared accuracy is not the accuracy an individual patient receives.

Significance — audience: real and identifiable — FDA CDRH (whose own staff specified the precision study without measuring it), screening-programme commissioners deciding single vs double acquisition, vendors' labelling — but the audience's own channel already carries the number for one device family, and the ARVO 2026 review shows the community framing deployment as imageability and workflow governance rather than flip-rate-versus-CI. The audience would act on the residual, not on the question.

Significance — fecundity: the useful children are narrower than the parent — what share of flips is algorithmic (P3); whether a pre-market inter-operator agreement predicts a deployment one; why a precision study appears in some cleared AI device files (K200667, K223357, K221183) and not in others (K213037, whose summary describes none and never raises the subject at all, rather than recording an absence), a regulatory-consistency question in its own right.

Significance — anchoring: the complaint that AI clearances rest on retrospective or protocolised data; scan-rescan repeatability of deep-learning classifiers (arXiv 2305.14385; prostate-ADC test-retest work, search level only); the clinical-chemistry patient-reclassification-from-imprecision family; arXiv 2602.14877, which names and models conditional-repeat sequential testing bias for a continuous biomarker thresholded to a binary decision and states it "does not model categorical diagnostic tests directly".

Reason for silence: the record's mechanism was a document-channel boundary — the measurement lives in 510(k) grey literature that PubMed does not index, named in regulatory-metrology vocabulary the clinical vocabulary does not reach. Adversary 2 damaged it: a 2026 narrative review whose material is precisely FDA decision summaries plus real-world deployment studies reads that channel and still does not ask for the quantity. The surviving mechanism is an incentive-and-workflow gap: every repeat acquisition that occurs in deployment is outcome-dependent (ungradable → dilate → re-shoot; two independent Disguise sweeps returned only that pathway), and a flip-rate design requires deliberately re-imaging a patient AFTER an adequate first image, which no workflow or billing pathway rewards. That is an acceptable mechanism, and as applied to the canonical question the channel story is a disguise mechanism rather than a silence mechanism.
