Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection: the verdict stands on ONE leg — K200667's Table 13 prints 90.3% [95% CI 82.3% – 96.8%], 56/62, from the design printed in full as "3 operator-camera pairings consisting of 3 different operators using 2 different camera units of the same model (each operator operated a given camera unit)" — 62 EYES from 31 subjects at ONE of the two US primary-care sites, not 62 subjects across both, and an operator contrast confounded with camera unit — in the same FDA-hosted file as the clearance sensitivity and specificity with 95% CIs, those being from the enrichment-permitted accuracy cohort and so a different cohort, instrument and unit; read first-hand at the primary PDF by both adversaries and now a third time by a fresh-context checker who also opened the cells. If that leg fell the Disguise kill fails and the entry returns to Gate 2. The legs that would survive it falling: adversary 2's attack 4 (C7 non-commensurability), which depends only on the printed metric DEFINITIONS and the missing denominators in K223357, not on any number; and attack 2 as a method-family kill via CLSI EP12 plus K221183 — whose documentary half is now confirmed at first hand, K221183 printing the between-operator agreement at the FDA primary and the pivotal Prot/SAP section 9.10 announcing the R&R sub-study without a number, while CLSI EP12 itself was NOT re-read in the verification pass and is carried as the reviewers left it. The leg that would NOT survive is the arithmetic bridge. THIS REJECTION'S OWN VULNERABILITY, since it rests partly on something nobody has measured: "flip rate = 1 − OA" is an ALGEBRAIC identity — exact complementation of a printed proportion and its interval — not a bitwise or empirical demonstration that a different-operator pair flips at 9.7%; and Table 13's 56/62 is agreement across THREE operators over 62 eye-triplets, so 9.7% [3.2%, 17.7%] is an UPPER BOUND on the pairwise, different-operator flip rate the candidate actually asks for, by P(any of three pairs disagree) >= P(a given pair disagrees). That inequality follows from the design, not from a reported pairwise result, and its direction has now been checked at first hand and CONFIRMED (pairwise <= 1 minus OA: one-directional, assertoric, not an equality and not a sufficient condition). What does NOT survive is the premise behind the next clause. The pairwise figure is derivable from the printed 3x3x3 cells, and this entry's universal that NOBODY derived or even listed them was true over the instances the ledger had opened and is now FALSE: the cells have been served at the FDA-hosted primary this citation already names, all 27 of them are listed in the verification note for this entry, and the pairwise different-operator disagreement rate is 12/186 = 6.45% (the checker's own arithmetic, its grid confirmed against four printed statistics; that 186 is 186 operator-pair comparisons over 62 eyes and is NOT Table 10's 186 intra-operator eye pairs — the same integer over different numerator classes) against the triplet bound 6/62 = 9.68% — materially below it, by exactly the factor 2/3, which is the maximal looseness three-rater geometry permits. By this entry's own pre-declared trigger the quantitative leg therefore WEAKENS FROM A MATCH TO A BOUND. Table 13 moreover PRINTS pairwise different-operator agreements outright (APA 92.2%, ANA 95.8%, AUA 50.0%, with CIs), which is proved internally and independently of any cell reading because AUA is printed as 50.0% while the all-Ungradable cell is zero, so AUA cannot be a triple-concordance statistic on any reading; one table thus mixes metric families without flagging the change, and that undeclared mixture SUPPORTS attack 4's C7 non-commensurability leg rather than weakening it. The record of who did what at Gate 4 stands as written — adversary 1 flagged the gap and labelled it its own reasoning, adversary 2 did not reach it. Adversary 2's C7 leg is likewise explicitly its own reasoning, with the regulatory-statistics search that would have grounded it not run. The source nominated as most likely to settle the vulnerability, the cell-level contents of Table 13 in https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf20/K200667.pdf, IS NOW OPENED, and it converted the bound into the pairwise number. The record that "no summariser served Table 13's cells" was wrong about where the failure lay: the refusal, reproduced on a first fetch as "I can't reproduce the full table text or every cell under the 125-character quote limit", is a QUOTATION-CAP REFUSAL that dissolves on a transcription prompt, and a quotation-cap refusal recorded as an extraction failure is the same class of false absence as a spent budget recorded as a property of the source. The nomination was correct BY KIND: a filing carrying the joint cross-tabulation is the only kind of document that can settle a pairwise question, since the pairwise rate is not a function of OA or of the margins. K213037 (IDx-DR v2.3), opened by neither adversary and the sole basis for the claim that one cleared device has no precision study at all, is now opened too, and the quotation that was that claim's whole authority is struck as unsourced, the documentary silence surviving in the weaker form stated above. The pairwise cells DID show the different-operator flip rate materially below the triplet bound, so the quantitative leg HAS weakened to a bound rather than a match, exactly as this entry pre-declared — attack 2 still kills on study type, its method-family ground re-tested at first hand at the FDA primary and returned CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED, and attack 4 still kills on C7, which Table 13's undeclared mixture of metric families now reinforces, so the rejection holds.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not for this question, which is rejected. For the residual child — "what share of intra-visit re-acquisition flips is algorithm-induced rather than acquisition-induced, and does a patient-visit-level deployment flip rate match the eye-level inter-operator agreement printed in the device's pre-market precision study?" — K200667's Table 13 cells and K213037 are now both read at accessdata.fda.gov and reported in this entry's verification block, so the child starts from the measured pairwise 12/186 = 6.45% rather than from 1 minus OA; the kinds of document still unopened are an FDA decision summary or review memorandum (DEN180001, the original IDx-DR De Novo, is of that kind, and it is nominated BY KIND ONLY — NOT OPENED, with nothing asserted about its contents) and the "Repeatability and Reproducibility Study Protocol" that AEYE-DS-001 section 9.10 defers to, which has been seen listed nowhere public, so its availability is a GUESS and not a lead. Note too that this child carries unchecked presuppositions of its own (a deployed version can be re-fed its own stored image sets under one version; eye-level tables lift to the patient-visit via the worse-eye rule) which must be tested as hard as the original.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — this is a disguised known, not an asked-but-still-open problem: the quantity is performed and printed for two cleared device families in their public FDA clearance files, so nothing goes to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. This line is a recommendation only; any change to that file happens outside this run.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-23)

**What ran, and what each checker was sent to read.** Three fresh-context checkers ran on this entry, one per load-bearing prior or kill leg, each handed the claim and its sources but NOT the reviewers' reasoning. Checker 1 (note: VERIFY-uq09-k200667-table13.md) was sent to the cell-level body of Table 13 in FDA 510(k) summary K200667, "EyeArt", applicant Eyenuk, Inc., 510(k) Summary "Date Prepared: August 3, 2020" — the single unopened source this entry had nominated against its own stated vulnerability. Checker 2 (VERIFY-uq09-k213037.md) was sent to FDA 510(k) summary K213037, "IDx-DR v2.3", applicant Digital Diagnostics, Inc., 510(k) Summary prepared June 14 2022, decision date 06/17/2022 — the sole basis for this entry's counter-instance, plus the FDA 510(k) database record and the Innolitics mirror as a hypothesis test about where a quotation came from. Checker 3 (VERIFY-uq09-k221183-primary.md) was sent to FDA 510(k) summary K221183, "AEYE-DS", applicant AEYE Health Inc., clearance letter header November 10 2022, and to NCT04612868's posted "Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan" (Prot_SAP_000.pdf, protocol AEYE-DS-001 v3.4, sponsor AEYE Health Inc., 24 November 2021) — attack 2's method-family leg. All three primary sources are regulatory filings and are recorded here by report designation (K number) plus responsible party, printed date and trade name, because the ledger's author-plus-DOI template is INAPPLICABLE to them rather than merely unverified: a 510(k) summary has no author list, no journal or venue, no volume, no issue, no page range in the bibliographic sense and no DOI, and recording "could not confirm authors/DOI" against one would itself be a false absence. Checkers 1 and 3 returned "does the claim hold: partly" and "yes"; checker 2 returned "partly", its two legs splitting.

**Read level reached, source by source.** K200667: FULL TEXT at the FDA-hosted primary https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf20/K200667.pdf, including the 27-cell body of Table 13, over six fetches all returning 200, with budget unspent. K213037: FULL TEXT at the FDA primary https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf21/K213037.pdf on the FIRST fetch at the route this entry's own citation names, in three passes (front matter and performance, a dedicated term-by-term sweep, a located-quotation pass); FULL TEXT of the FDA 510(k) database record page; FULL TEXT of the Innolitics mirror, read only to test the quotation's origin. K221183: FULL TEXT at the FDA primary https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf22/K221183.pdf on the FIRST fetch, no redirect and no error, across two passes; the Innolitics mirror deliberately NOT fetched. NCT04612868: FULL TEXT of the registry record via the classic route; the Prot/SAP read PARTIAL — section 9.10 in full, title page, table of contents and targeted term sweeps across the whole document, with sections 1 to 9.9 and 10 to 11 NOT read in full. There is NO COULD NOT READ and NO COULD NOT CHECK anywhere in this pass: every sub-claim put to every checker was reached, and nothing below is a budget-induced absence. What is absent is absent on dedicated sweeps, which is a different thing and is labelled as NOT FOUND where it occurs.

**Did the verdict move? No.** The verdict was settled before this pass and is not re-judged here: Rejected, on attacks 1, 2 and 4 Unresolved, with attack 2 Unresolved from BOTH original adversaries independently. Attack 2's ground — the method-family kill — was re-tested at first hand at the FDA primary and came back CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED: K221183 prints the between-operator agreement at the primary rather than at a mirror, and prints intra-operator agreement besides, while the pivotal protocol's own section 9.10 announces the repeatability sub-study and prints no number. Because that ground survived verification of its own sources, NO LATE GATE 4 WAS OWED on this entry and none ran; a ground that survives verification of its own sources is not a withdrawn ground. Checker 1's recommended bearing went further than a bearing can go — it proposed converting the quantitative leg's sufficiency into a promotion condition — and that recommendation is recorded, not executed: it is a bearing on one leg and not a verdict, this entry is Rejected and carries no promotion-condition line, so the conditions the pass produced are written below as prose. What the pass did change is the entry's prose, in the places listed here.

**The gravest finding of this batch: an unsourced quotation, struck.** This entry presented K213037's 510(k) summary as "stating" the string 'Repeatability or reproducibility study: None described'. The string is ABSENT from the FDA primary PDF. The heading is absent; there is no precision, repeatability or reproducibility heading anywhere in the document to carry such a line, the printed headings being Submitter; Device; Device Description; Indications for Use; Predicate Device; Purpose of Submission; Comparison of Technological Characteristics with the Predicate Device; Performance Data; Conclusions, with Section VIII holding exactly two subsections, "A. Summary of Non-clinical Studies" (and one further heading, "Usability") and "B. Summary of Clinical Performance Testing". The distinctive three-word fragment "None described" is absent on a sweep aimed only at it. There is no field-and-value template of the "<study type>: None described" shape anywhere in the file. And the Innolitics mirror carries no such field and no such value either, its non-clinical rendering listing software documentation, hazard analysis, cybersecurity and a "Usability" subsection in agreement with the FDA text — so the error cannot be excused as a mirror artefact mistaken for FDA text. One targeted search located the string in no FDA document at all, returning only title matches, among them two ASTM listings of the same standard F1469 under different year suffixes, which count as title matches and never as corroboration; a single search's silence is not absence, so the honest status of the string is UNSOURCED: not in the cited document and not located in any document. It is therefore STRUCK from this entry's prose, in both places it stood (the nearest-prior paragraph and the fecundity line). It is NOT repaired by reattribution to a guessed document, and it is NOT converted into a promotion condition, because no condition turns an unlocated string into a citation. In its place the entry now carries the substantive restatement the checker supplied: K213037's 510(k) summary, decision date 06/17/2022, describes no repeatability, reproducibility or precision study; the terms repeatability, reproducibility, precision and variability do not appear in it on per-term sweeps (test-retest, agreement as a noun, and consistency are likewise absent, "operator" occurring three times); and Section VIII's only non-clinical performance content is the eleven-item software documentation list, verification and validation at unit, integration and system level, a risk analysis, a cybersecurity assessment, technical parameter characterization, an algorithm change protocol and a usability validation. The inference is NARROWED with it: what is established is a gap in the PUBLIC CLEARANCE SUMMARY, not an established absence of measurement, so the entry's "rather than a measured one" has become "rather than one this clearance summary reports" — published-is-not-performed, run backwards, was the entry's error here, and a 21 CFR 807.92 summary is applicant-selected and brief, so its silence is weak evidence about what was submitted and near-zero evidence about what was performed. The near-misses are now named rather than written off as "nothing at all": the usability validation, whose stated endpoint is operator TASK SUCCESS — "demonstrated that previously untrained" / "camera operators could capture four retinal images of sufficient quality following the imaging protocol" — and not between-operator agreement, and for which no number is printed at all, no operator count, no success rate, no denominator; and the Section VII user-interface change, "Updated to provide clear language of 'exam completed' after repeated imaging attempts have resulted in" / "an insufficient image quality output", which sits in a list of changes relative to the predicate, changes the wording the client displays, and neither asserts nor denies any quantity. The entry's bookkeeping is reversed on one point: this claim is no longer unopened by anybody, and it broke on its character-level leg while its substantive leg held in narrowed form. Checker 2 added one argument it labelled "MY OWN REASONING, NOT A SOURCE FINDING" — that a retrospective re-analysis of the predicate's fixed image set cannot measure acquisition-side repeatability even in principle — and said the protocol or SAP for the v2.3 validation that would have grounded it was not opened; it is recorded here in those words and is NOT carried into the entry's prose as a source finding.

**The quantitative leg: from a match to a bound, by the entry's own pre-declared trigger.** Everything descriptive and logical in the leg HOLDS, verbatim. Table 13 p. 21 prints "OA 90.3% [82.3% - 96.8%] (56/62)" under the caption "EyeArt reproducibility for mtmDR results with Canon CR-2 AF camera", narrated on p. 10 as "an inter-operator OA of 90.3% [95% CI: 82.3% - 96.8%] was achieved"; Table 10 p. 20's 93.9% [89.7% - 97.7%] (169/180) and its OA* row 90.9% [84.7% - 95.7%] (169/186) verify, as do sensitivity 92.9% [87.1% - 97.5%] (92/99) and specificity 85.6% [82.2% - 89.1%] (457/534) in Tables 3 and 8. The printed definitions on p. 19, under "For 3x3 contingency tables, the definitions are as follows:", give "Overall agreement (OA): (PP+NN+UU) / N", "Average Positive Agreement (APA): (2*PP) / (TP + PT)", "Average Negative Agreement (ANA): (2*NN) / (TN + NT)" and "Average Ungradable Agreement (AUA): (2*UU) / (TU + UT)", with Ungradable carried as a live third category whose UU counts toward OA's numerator. 1 minus OA is correctly characterised as an algebraic identity on a printed proportion and as a one-directional upper bound on the pairwise different-operator flip rate, not itself a measured pairwise result; the checker tested the logical form and not merely the characters, and confirmed the inequality's DIRECTION, pairwise <= 1 minus OA, both from the three-rater geometry and from the realised numbers. What FALLS is the entry's unspoken premise that the pairwise result is UNAVAILABLE from the file, and it falls two ways. First, the cells open at the primary the citation already names: the eight non-empty triplets are (N,N,N)=37, (P,P,P)=19, (N,P,N)=1, (P,P,N)=1, (N,N,P)=1, (P,N,P)=1, (U,N,U)=1 and (U,P,U)=1, summing to 62, from which the pairwise different-operator disagreement rate is 12/186 = 6.45% and pairwise agreement 174/186 = 93.55%. Both of those are THE CHECKER'S OWN ARITHMETIC and are labelled as such, not as something the source prints; the grid behind them was confirmed against four printed statistics rather than accepted, reproducing OA at 90.3%, APA at 92.1875% against a printed 92.2%, ANA at 95.7627% against a printed 95.8% and AUA at 50.0000% against a printed 50.0%. The structural reasoning that 12/186 sits at exactly 2/3 of 6/62 — that with three raters a disagreeing eye must have at least two disagreeing pairs, so average pairwise disagreement lies in [(2/3)(1-OA), (1-OA)], and that every one of the six discordant eyes here had exactly two of three pairs disagreeing, placing the realisation at the lower limit and making 1 minus OA loose by the maximal factor 3/2 — is likewise THE CHECKER'S OWN REASONING, not a source finding. Second, Table 13 PRINTS pairwise different-operator agreements directly: APA 92.2% [81.4% - 98.3%], ANA 95.8% [91.9% - 99.1%] and AUA 50.0% [21.5% - 78.5%], with confidence intervals. That these are pairwise is proved internally and independently of any cell reading, because AUA is printed as 50.0% while the all-Ungradable cell is zero, so on any triple-concordance reading AUA would be 0.0%, not 50.0%. The entry had fixed its own trigger in advance — "If the pairwise different-operator flip rate is materially below the triplet bound, the quantitative leg weakens from a match to a bound" — and 6.45% against 9.68% meets it, so the entry's prose now says the leg HAS weakened from a match to a bound. Table 13 therefore MIXES METRIC FAMILIES, a triplet statistic sitting above three pairwise statistics with no flagging of the change, and that undeclared mixture SUPPORTS attack 4's C7 non-commensurability leg rather than weakening it, which the entry's prose now states. Two further strikes follow from the same read: the entry's "no summariser served Table 13's cells" is corrected to a QUOTATION-CAP REFUSAL — reproduced on the checker's first fetch as "I can't reproduce the full table text or every cell under the 125-character quote limit" — which dissolved when the table was asked for as structured data and again when the literal text-layer token sequence was requested, and a quotation-cap refusal recorded as an extraction failure is the same class of false absence as a spent budget recorded as a property of the source; and the entry's universal that "nobody derived or even listed the 3x3x3 cells" was true over the instances the ledger had opened and is now FALSE, all 27 cells being listed in the checker's note.

**The regime description, wrong in three ways, now fixed.** Table 13's N=62 is 62 EYES from 31 subjects at ONE site — Cohort P1, settled numerically by Table 10's caption, "3 operators were to each provide one intra-operator pair per eye for a total of 186 eye pairs (3 intra-operator pairs x 31 subjects x 2 eyes/subject)", and by p. 10's "The reproducibility was measured in Cohort P1 by analyzing the agreement among the EyeArt results for each eye" — and NOT the 62 subjects of the two-site study, which the separate printed string "precision (repeatability and reproducibility) study on 62 subjects at 2 US primary care sites (31 subjects each)" scopes across both sites. The pairwise 186 is NOT Table 10's 186: Table 10's is 186 intra-operator eye pairs with protocol deviations counted as ungradable, while the checker's is 186 operator-pair comparisons over 62 eyes — the same integer over different numerator classes, Table 10's including repeat readings by the SAME operator that the checker's excludes, and the checker's including comparisons ACROSS operators that Table 10's excludes. And the operator contrast is CONFOUNDED WITH CAMERA UNIT by the clause this entry's own quotation cut: the printed sentence is "3 operator-camera pairings consisting of 3 different operators using 2 different camera units of the same model (each operator operated a given camera unit)", and the cut at "of the same model" was itself the defect, since the dropped parenthetical and the "operator-camera pairings" opener are the words that establish the confound; no C1/C2/C3-to-unit mapping is printed. The entry's prose now carries the full sentence in both places it had the short one, and the two consequential claims built on the short one are corrected: the entry no longer calls K200667 a "crossed 3 x 2" design, in the presuppositions, in the differences-from-prior-3 paragraph or in the attack 8 response. Any flip rate taken from this table is accordingly a per-eye rate across operator-and-camera pairings in a 31-subject precision cohort, so comparing it to the enrichment-permitted accuracy cohort's interval crosses cohort, instrument and unit — which the entry now says where it previously called limb 2 a plain subtraction within one file. The checker also noted that the p. 19 definitions sit beneath a TWO-rater template ("EyeArt result 1" / "EyeArt result 2") and are extended to three operators silently, and flagged as ITS OWN READING a probable typo in that legend, "TU=NU+PU+UN" where the Ungradable column marginal requires NU+PU+UU; it affects no printed value, and it is recorded here rather than in the entry's body. On uncertainty: the file prints 95% CIs and NOTHING ELSE — a dedicated second sweep found no occurrence of "performance goal", "endpoint", "acceptance criteri", "pre-specified", "primary analysis", "success criteri", "non-inferiority", "superiority", "lower bound", "lower confidence" or "powered", with "prespecified" occurring twice but not about accuracy — so the comparison limb 2 would make is against a printed interval, not an acceptance criterion, and the entry now says so.

**K221183 holds, and strengthens.** The figure is CONFIRMED AT THE FDA PRIMARY rather than at a mirror, character for character: "OA 97.73% (43/44) [88.19% ;99.60% ]", between-operator, 1 image per eye, in the section headed "Precision Study", in a table block headed "Between - Operator Reproducibility", from "imaged by three different novice operators, using two different Topcon NW400 fundoscopy devices", the operators being "Novice operators, who had not previously performed ocular imaging"; beside sensitivity 92.98% [83.30%; 97.24%] and specificity 91.36% [88.22%; 93.72%] in the "Clinical Performance Data" section of the same file, the sensitivity sentence opening "AEYE-DS correctly identified 53 of the 57 fully analyzable subjects with mtmDR+, thus the sensitivity was 92.98%". The entry's note that the FDA primary was not attempted is therefore STRUCK and replaced with the primary URL, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf22/K221183.pdf, and a one-fetch note: that was an UNATTEMPTED route, not a failed one, and no later reader should re-spend the call or discount the figures as mirror-only. The entry now also carries the printed SET rather than one of six values — between-operator 97.73% (43/44) and the LOWER 95.45% (42/44) [84.87%; 98.74%] at two images per eye, intra-operator 98.48% (130/132) [94.64%; 99.58%] and 96.97% (128/132) [92.47%; 98.82%], and between-device 98.48% (65/66) [91.90%; 99.73%] and 95.45% (63/66) [87.47%; 98.44%] — because an entry arguing that this vendor DID characterise repeatability is stronger for saying the file prints intra-operator agreement too, and because carrying only the higher of two between-operator values is a selection a reader cannot see from the entry. "In the same file" is correct and "in the same table" would have been wrong: two sections, three tables, and two different populations, 22 participants against 462. The related claim is confirmed at the exact section number the entry names: NCT04612868's posted "Study Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan" (Prot_SAP_000.pdf, AEYE-DS-001 v3.4, 2021-11-24, uploaded 2023-05-23, 1,776,272 bytes) section 9.10 "Repeatability & Reproducibility Testing" ANNOUNCES the sub-study in future modality — "will be performed", "will be used", "Full details of the study design and analysis will be provided in the Repeatability and Reproducibility Study Protocol" — and prints no percentage, no count and no confidence interval, its 10 repeats, three operators, two devices and half/half split being design parameters and not results; "97.73" does not occur anywhere in that protocol on a dedicated sweep, and "precision" does not occur in it at all. The registry's posted results independently corroborate the two clinical figures outside the 510(k) channel, sensitivity 92.98% (83.3 to 97.24) and specificity 91.36% (88.22 to 93.72) in 462 participants. One narrowing is absorbed into the entry: the Precision Study does NOT define its unit of analysis and does not say how 44, 66 and 132 are formed, its only unit noun being "image sets/diagnoses" in "12 image sets/diagnoses were obtained for each participant, for a total of 264 image sets/diagnoses in total", so the entry's earlier "per-eye (44 between-operator pairs)" is withdrawn and the fractions are carried as printed with no characterisation of the unit — the checker's observation that 44, 66 and 132 divide by 22 participants into 2, 3 and 6 comparisons each is ITS OWN ARITHMETIC and not a source finding, and the numerator class of the 43/44 is UNDEFINED IN THE SOURCE, so no exclusions and no overlap in either direction can be written for it. The existence claim behind the method-family framing is TRUE OVER THE ONE INSTANCE OPENED: one vendor file was opened, no other vendor's 510(k) summary was, so no sentence of the form "vendors generally print this" or "no other vendor prints this" may be written from this check in either direction.

Domain(s): Medicine — hospital pharmacy, nephrology/AKI, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical decision support. Question (canonical): In a cohort of hospital admissions with linked timestamped medication-administration and laboratory records, restricted to a pre-declared drug list whose labels state a renal dose threshold and a single full dose per indication (titrated drugs excluded by pre-declared rule) and to episodes in which the administered dose fell below the labelled full dose while measured clearance was below that drug's label threshold, then taking renal recovery as clearance returning above that same label threshold and staying above it for a declared interval (primary 24 h; sensitivity arms at 12 h and 48 h and a cystatin-C/measured-clearance arm): (a) what is the cumulative incidence of dose restoration to the labelled full dose as a function of time since recovery, with drug discontinuation, discharge and death as competing risks; (b) what share of episodes is never restored before the first of those events; (c) what is the exposure deficit, as administered over labelled full dose integrated across the post-recovery pre-event window, per drug class; (d) what share of non-restorations is documented-deliberate rather than undocumented; and (e) per contributing site, does the deployed renal dosing rule set contain any rule that fires on a dose below the labelled full dose at a clearance above the threshold? [This is V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, scored as canonical. V1 asked the same five limbs without fixing the recovery clock, the denominator of "intended exposure" or the integration window; V2 fixes each by stipulation and moves the rule-directionality limb from the motivating prose into a reported output. No limb was added or dropped. THREE one-sentence repairs are owed and are noted under Scores: the primary instrument should read "estimated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault where the label specifies an equation)" — not merely "estimated clearance", because two of the five labels opened post-batch name no estimating equation at all; limb (c)'s integral should say whether it is the integral of a ratio or the ratio of integrals; and the "pre-declared drug list" this clause restricts to must actually be ENUMERATED, with its exclusion rule widened beyond titration to the pathogen- and day-of-therapy-conditional dosing the opened labels print. None of the three changes a limb.]
Alternative formulations: Renal dosing is a ratchet — how often does the dose come back up when the kidneys do? / What exposure deficit do un-restored renal dose reductions create, and do deployed decision-support rule sets fire in only one direction?
Motivating gap: labels, nomograms, eGFR-equation debates, appropriateness audits and alert rule sets are dense with how-to for reducing a dose as kidney function falls and near-silent on the reverse transition. One leg of this gap was struck by the record itself and a second by adversary #2, and the entry is graded on what survives. Struck leg 1 (an unenumerated universal over deployed rule sets): the record's claim that alert logic fires on a dose too high and "by construction" not on a dose too low is false on the one rule set opened — Boussadi et al. built 962 rules with an under-dose branch keyed to the expert-panel dose for the patient's eGFR and log a real instance at a normal eGFR ("For 35: the pharmacist failed to detect an under dose with a normal eGFR rate"). Struck leg 2: the record's claim that "the vocabulary itself has only one direction in it" is falsified on a second opened source — Hughes et al. 2022 prints dosing advice keyed on improving and recovering function, and the full printed sentence, restored here because this entry had cut it at "review", is "Dose adjustments after 48 h were not recommended if renal function was improving to baseline at time of review to correct for any potential hyperfiltration with recovering function". That sentence is a CONDITIONAL, its modality is NORMATIVE local guidance rather than an observation of what anyone did, and its direction is an UNLOADING — the adjustment it withholds is the downward one — so the recovery-keyed vocabulary exists but is a reason to LEAVE a dose at full, never a trigger to raise a dose that had been cut. What survives, and is narrower and better evidenced, is that the recovery clock and the dose-adequacy classification exist in the same literature and in at least one case the same paper, and were never crossed.
Presuppositions: (P1) renal recovery is definable from routine data at a declared threshold — CONTESTED and declared; creatinine lags, definitions differ, a mid-period eGFR-equation switch can manufacture a crossing; handled by one primary rule plus three pre-declared sensitivity arms. (P2) the reduction was renal-attributable — CONTESTED and declared; restriction to label-threshold drugs and to doses below the labelled full dose at a sub-threshold clearance narrows it, residual confounding is a limitation not a fix. Adversary #1 adds that V2's dropping of V1's word "reduced" admits episodes that started low and never had a full dose, for which "restoration" is first escalation — a scope statement owed, not a false premise. (P3) an intended full dose is identifiable per patient — INSTANCED, and no longer unverified: five US FDA-format product labels were opened post-batch, and the premise is TRUE OVER THE INSTANCES OPENED on three of them. ZERBAXA (ceftolozane and tazobactam) for injection, Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, rev. 5/2026, SPL set id 70ac1d90-eff3-4f0b-9f46-5846c571b32f — threshold "Estimated CrCl (mL/min)" with the footnote "Estimated CrCl using the Cockcroft-Gault formula", full dose 1.5 g q8h for cIAI and cUTI and 3 g q8h for HABP/VABP. What would count as an answer: per pre-declared drug class — (i) the cumulative incidence function of restoration to the labelled full dose after documented recovery, estimated under discontinuation, discharge and death as competing risks, with intervals; (ii) the never-restored share at the first competing event; (iii) the exposure deficit as a fraction of labelled intended cumulative dose over the post-recovery window, with intervals; (iv) the documented-deliberate versus undocumented split from charted rationale; (v) a per-site inventory of whether any deployed rule can fire on a low dose at a recovered clearance, with "no rule set deployed" a permitted answer. (i)-(iii) repeated under the three recovery-definition arms. Negative answer stated in advance: a small deficit concentrated in documented deliberate decisions with restoration incidence rising steeply in 24-48 h. Positive answer: a large deficit dominated by undocumented omission. Same design produces either, so this is a question and not a thesis.

On that quantity the paper does not measure, bound, predict or announce. Adversary #2 flags that the article carries mutually inconsistent recovery denominators (105/106 and 106/107 in text and abstract against 96/97 and 100/101 in Table 2) and two P-value sets, and therefore leans only on the timing figure, which is printed once. Two further opened documents, recorded as what they do rather than as priors: Donnelly K et al., Crit Care 2011;15(Suppl 1):P218, DOI 10.1186/cc9638 (abstract is the document) BOUNDS the problem with a point-prevalence concordance rate, "2,004 (81.1%)" of 2,472 ICU antibiotic prescriptions correctly prescribed for renal function/RRT, plus per-unit items such as tazocin underdosed in mild renal failure (7.0%), and prints no time to adjustment and no exposure; the ISPOR 13th Annual Meeting 2008 presentation "Epidemiology and outcomes of patients with changes in renal function during hospitalization that may require drug dosage adjustment" (Gupta and colleagues, Cardinal Health; Value in Health 11(3); read by adversary #1 as a SUMMARISER SUMMARY of an abstract, not verbatim) DEFINES the denominator — 1,011,055 non-dialysis admissions with >= 2 creatinine values across 74 US hospitals, 79.2% unchanged, 11.6% worsened, 9.2% IMPROVED by >= 1 Cockcroft-Gault stratum — and PREDICTS a need ("potential dosage adjustment"), measuring no dosing action in either direction. Group count: the five documents come from five different institutions (Nijmegen/Den Bosch, Barcelona, London, Birmingham ICU audit, a US vendor analysis), so nothing here is one laboratory citing itself — and on the pair this entry leans on hardest that is now checked against the printed author lists rather than assumed. The two older priors are TWO INDEPENDENT GROUPS with ZERO author overlap: Hospital Clínic Barcelona (Rodriguez-Reyes, López-Suñé, Calvo-Cidoncha, Tuset-Creus, Codina-Jané, Soriano-Viladomiu) against Jeroen Bosch Hospital and Dutch academic co-authors (Eppenga, Wester, Derijks, Hoedemakers, Wensing, De Smet, Van Marum) — different countries, different institutions, different clinical questions. Neither printed list contains any author named Hughes; whether some OTHER author of the Hughes paper also appears on either list is COULD NOT CHECK on a spent budget, which is a limit of the check and not an absence, and it is not scored either way. Boussadi et al. (arXiv:1305.5665, Paris, read in full by the record) is a sixth and bears only on limb (e).
Novelty — how this differs from each: from (1) — protocol versus measurement, post-discharge community at two fixed visits versus a within-admission clock, counterfactual "a change would be needed" versus whether anyone actually restored the dose, point-in-time percentages versus a cumulative incidence under competing risks, and no never-restored share and no exposure deficit anywhere in it. From (2) — same setting and record kind, different quantity: its 62.5% is direction-ambiguous (the abstract never says whether improvements, deteriorations or both were counted, so it cannot be decomposed), point-in-time, single-drug, patient-unit, and its numerator includes the opposite transition (CrCl fell, dose not reduced) and patients never dose-reduced at all; it prints no timing, no competing risks, no deficit and no deliberateness split. From (3) — the closest of the three priors, and the one that most sharpens the grade: it measures recovery timing AND dose adequacy in the same cohort and NEVER CROSSES THEM. Its five-of-eleven count — of pharmacist corrections to maximum dosing, "escalation" being a word the paper itself never uses, absent on two dedicated sweeps — has a different time origin, 24 h post bacteraemia as printed in the sentence's own restored tail, and no upward adjustment in it is linked to renal function recovering; upward moves made by pharmacist review of an inappropriate initial prescription, the paper's own verb being "corrected", irrespective of renal trajectory, are not restorations; its population is GNB bacteraemia at a trust whose local policy is unadjusted dosing for the first 48 h, which is itself unusual. None of the five documents DEFINES time from recovery to restoration, a never-restored share under competing risks, or an exposure-deficit fraction; what they do is announce (Eppenga), bound (Donnelly), define a denominator and predict a need (ISPOR 2008), assert a direction-ambiguous non-adjustment rate (Rodriguez-Reyes) and assert a count of pharmacist corrections to maximum dosing inside 24 h of bacteraemia, unlinked to renal recovery (Hughes). A further document now belongs in this comparison as a NEIGHBOUR rather than a prior, because it has since been opened: Aldardeer NF et al. 2024, "Early Versus Late Antipseudomonal beta-Lactam Antibiotic Dose Adjustment in Critically Ill Sepsis Patients With Acute Kidney Injury: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study", Open Forum Infectious Diseases 2024;11(3):ofae059, DOI 10.1093/ofid/ofae059. It times only the DOWNWARD transition — its Methods stratify patients "according to the time to beta-lactam renal dose reduction", both arms being defined by the time to a REDUCTION from an initial full dose — so it differs from this question by direction, by which variable is the outcome (dose timing is its exposure and renal recovery its secondary outcome, the arrow reversed), by population and drug list, and by denominator object (patients, not dose reductions). Its two numbers that a keyword sweep would mistake for this question's are both disarmed on the paper's own text: the 38/224 (16.9%) "escalation" row, with HR 0.747 (95% CI .395-1.413) in Table 2, is defined in its Methods as a SPECTRUM switch, "switching patients from antibiotics with a lower spectrum of activity to antibiotics with a broader spectrum of activity", restricted by the row label to escalation needed to target culture in patients with gram-negative isolates; and the 48-hour AKI-recovery figures (70.7% L-BLA versus 47.6% E-BLA, P = .001) run the arrow backwards, dose timing predicting recovery rather than recovery predicting dose. No Low grade is available on anything opened.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: if the deficit is large and dominated by undocumented omission, it is a named, measured exposure loss in the drug classes where exposure-response is steepest, and the remedy is a mirror branch on an existing rule triggered by the clearance crossing rather than by the order — Boussadi shows the branch is buildable and that human reviewers miss under-doses even when it fires, so the finding would bear on alert placement and recipient, not only on whether to build one. If the deficit is small and concentrated in documented deliberate decisions, that closes a worry currently circulating as stewardship folklore without a number and licenses teams to stop looking, which is itself a resource decision. The limit is honest and was pressed by both adversaries: with the benefit limb out of scope, a positive answer is an exposure finding and not a harm finding.
Significance — audience: four communities with a concrete action — (1) antimicrobial stewardship teams, whose prospective audit-and-feedback worklists are built from rule outputs that surface over-dosing and spectrum; (2) clinical informaticists who own the renal dosing rule configuration, where the action is one rule and is cheap, auditable and testable; (3) anticoagulation and AF services, for whom DOAC under-dosing is already a quality measure but is measured cross-sectionally against label criteria rather than as a failure to revert — with a tension recorded rather than hidden, flagged by the label check: the one DOAC label opened (ELIQUIS apixaban, E.R. Squibb & Sons, rev. 4/2025) prints no adult renal dose threshold in clearance at all, so this entry's own inclusion rule cannot admit the drug this audience prescribes, and either the rule widens or this audience claim narrows; (4) AKI follow-up and nephrology pharmacy, who own the recovery event but not the medication ledger. Adversary #2 found the audience's problem already in print as policy rather than measurement: a real trust had to legislate trajectory-dependent dosing, in the full printed sentence "Dose adjustments after 48 h were not recommended if renal function was improving to baseline at time of review to correct for any potential hyperfiltration with recovering function" — normative guidance, and an unloading rather than a loading — with no measurement of the transition behind it.
Significance — fecundity: does the restoration hazard depend on who is on service, on whether a pharmacist or a prescriber made the cut, or on handover boundaries; is the deficit visible in outcomes once expressed as exposure rather than as an error count; do the same ratchets exist for non-renal reductions (hepatic, cytopenia, weight-based dosing after oedema resolves); and does the presence of a Boussadi-style under-dose branch measurably change the restoration hazard, a natural comparison limb (e) sets up.
Significance — anchoring: the augmented-renal-clearance underdosing literature, which asks the same exposure question from the other end of the clearance distribution and never meets the recovery event; the post-AKI drug-restart literature (RAS blockers), which treats the agent as binary and never the dose as continuous; the DOAC inappropriate-dosing quality measures, which count label discordance at a point in time; and therapeutic inertia, which owns the method for "a change that should have happened and did not" and has applied it only to initiation and up-titration.
Reason for silence: a disciplinary join, now the strongest of the three mechanisms the record proposed and the only one that survived Gate 4 intact. The record's mechanism (1), an asymmetric harm taxonomy in which an un-restored low dose generates no incident report and no ADE code, survives only weakly — adversary #1 corroborates it at title level (roughly 60 returned titles across eight registers are reduction-direction or appropriateness-framed) while adversary #2 falsifies its strong form on an opened source that prints recovery-keyed dosing advice — normative guidance whose direction is an unloading, so the vocabulary exists but withholds a reduction rather than restoring a cut dose. Mechanism (2), that the dominant cross-sectional audit design has no clock, is also weaker than stated: Hughes et al. HAS a clock inside a renal-dosing paper (median 3 days, IQR 2-5, defined as days from peak serum creatinine to a 1.5-fold reduction, denominator unstated). Mechanism (3) stands and is sharpened: the recovery clock and the dose-adequacy classification sit in the same literature and in at least one case the same paper, and nobody crossed them — recovery is owned by nephrology and critical care as an outcome, the medication ledger by pharmacy and informatics as orders, and the joining quantity belongs to neither. Per Gate 4's own rule, two of three mechanisms being dented is a reason to treat the novelty finding as suspect; that is one of the reasons this entry is Provisional rather than Validated. What is NOT claimed: that rule sets could not fire on recovery. They can, and one does.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): TWO adversaries ran, each on the Gate 0-3 record only and neither reading the other's log. DISGUISE WAS EXECUTED BY BOTH and is graded on its returns, not Unverified: adversary #1 ran 8 Disguise sweeps plus 1 lead-check (9/9 searches, 4/4 fetches) and adversary #2 ran 9 (9/9 searches, 4/4 fetches), in thirteen registers the Gate 2 record had not used. Both recommended Provisional. Nothing came back Unresolved from either. Statuses below are the worse of the two where they differ, with both named. Two curl calls per adversary were refused with "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" (tool-scoped, per the standing route fact) and both then answered through WebFetch; no route failed outright, and every COULD NOT READ in these logs is a spent fetch budget, stated as such. One later COULD NOT READ is NOT a budget and must not be read as one: the post-batch pass tried the Eppenga 2016 thesis and both of its routes failed, which is recorded in the verification block and distinguished there from NOT FOUND.

The nearest published count (Hughes, five of eleven dose-reduced β-lactams taken to maximum dosing by a pharmacist, Results text; the paper never uses the word "escalation") has its time origin 24 h post bacteraemia and links no upward adjustment to renal function recovering; the largest-scale document (ISPOR 2008, 1.01M admissions) stops at "may require" adjustment and measures no dosing action. STRUCK as it previously stood: no opened source bounds the never-restored share. Hughes prints no such figure — "restor" and "never" are both absent on dedicated sweeps and the paper is silent past 24 h — so it does not measure, bound, predict or announce that quantity, and the six-of-eleven complement means "not escalated within 24 h", not "never restored". Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 3/3 — V2 states in advance the recovery clock and its arms, the inclusion rule, the estimator with named competing risks, the deficit's numerator, denominator and window, the deliberateness instrument and both directions of answer, and the measurand exemption is declared out loud rather than smuggled. The grade is kept at 3/3 because the defects found are wording and not object — but there are now THREE of them, and the third is new. (i) "measured clearance" should read "estimated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault where the label specifies an equation)": the primary instrument as written is either unavailable in the conditioned data source or redundant with its own "where available" arm, and of the five labels opened two name no equation at all, so the flat word "estimated" is right in direction and under-specified. (ii) Limb (c)'s integral should say whether it is the integral of a ratio or the ratio of integrals. (iii) NEW well-posedness defect, from the label check, of the same repairable kind as the other two: the "pre-declared drug list" DOES NOT EXIST. The phrase and its variants occur ELEVEN times across this entry, the record and both adversary logs, and NOT ONE of them is followed by an enumeration, while the two drugs named most often in the record — vancomycin and allopurinol — are the titrated exemplars the rule EXCLUDES; so "pre-declared" is at present an announcement of a list and not a declaration of one, and neither adversary asked this question, both having tested only whether labels CAN satisfy the clause. The exclusion rule is also ONE-DIMENSIONAL: "titrated drugs excluded by pre-declared rule" handles therapeutic-drug-monitoring dosing and nothing else, where the opened labels produce two further conditioning dimensions that each give "the labelled full dose" more than one referent inside a single indication — PATHOGEN (meropenem cSSSI, 500 mg q8h against 1 g q8h, since "For P. aeruginosa, a dose of 1 gram every 8 hours is recommended") and DAY OF THERAPY (apixaban for DVT/PE, "10 mg taken orally twice daily for the first 7 days of therapy. After 7 days, the recommended dose is 5 mg taken orally twice daily."). The breaking case is instanced rather than hypothetical: a cSSSI episode on meropenem 500 mg q8h at a recovered clearance scores as a 50% exposure deficit if the denominator is read as 1 g and as fully restored if it is read as 500 mg. Each of the three is still a one-sentence repair that changes no limb, and the checker that found the third left the question of whether that still reads 3/3 to the grader rather than scoring it itself. The concession previously recorded here — that three agents had left zero labels opened, so limb (c)'s denominator was unverified at the document-kind level — is DISCHARGED: the denominator is verified at the document-kind level on three of the five labels now opened, on US labels only and not on SmPCs, which remain UNENUMERATED because none was opened. Validated is blocked by novelty, by the unenumerated Eppenga results leg and by the dented silence mechanisms, not by well-posedness. Significance 2/3 and not 3/3 — the audience and action are concrete and cheap and the question survives either answer, but the benefit limb is out of scope by design, so a positive answer is one inferential step short of compelling practice change, and two of the three silence mechanisms are dented.
Strongest remaining objection: NOT Disguise any more, and that is the change. The one document the verdict used to stand on has been opened. Aldardeer NF, Alshreef MM, Alharbi EA, Aljabri AK, Aljawadi MH, Almangour TA, Alobaili S, Alarifi MI, Alomari A, Alhammad AM. "Early Versus Late Antipseudomonal beta-Lactam Antibiotic Dose Adjustment in Critically Ill Sepsis Patients With Acute Kidney Injury: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study." Open Forum Infectious Diseases 2024;11(3):ofae059, pages 1-9, DOI 10.1093/ofid/ofae059 — returned by both adversaries' sweeps and opened by neither, now read at Abstract, Introduction, Methods including Definitions, Results including Secondary Outcomes, and Tables 1-3. It times only the DOWNWARD transition: Methods stratifies "according to the time to beta-lactam renal dose reduction" and excludes patients who "received the initial dose of beta-lactam adjusted for renal function", so every retained course runs full to reduced. It is therefore a NEIGHBOUR and not a disguised known, this entry does not fall to Rejected on it, and adversary #1's title reading turned out right on ground that was a guess until the read. What is now the strongest objection is the leg this entry had argued shut by design rather than by a read: whether the Eppenga 2015 protocol has since produced a results publication is UNENUMERATED, not settled — the first author's own 2016 PhD thesis is a document of exactly the right kind and would not open at either route tried (COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND), and registry record onderzoekmetmensen.nl/en/node/43767 is a second unopened instance of the right kind — so this entry does not close that leg and carries it as a promotion condition. Behind it stand novelty at Medium with a close neighbour, two of three silence mechanisms dented, and the new well-posedness defect under Scores: the pre-declared drug list is announced and never enumerated, and its exclusion rule covers titration only. The label premise is no longer a live objection at all: five US labels are open, the premise is instanced on three, and limb (c)'s document-kind concession is discharged, with SmPCs still unenumerated. The record's own previously strongest objection — that the never-restored share would be arithmetic about course length because recovery may fall after the drug stops — is ANSWERED, not open, but answered narrowly: Hughes et al. prints a median time to recovery of 3 days (IQR 2-5) in a bacteraemia-with-AKI cohort whose courses run longer, which establishes that the window is non-empty; it is time from peak creatinine to a 1.5-fold reduction with its denominator unstated, and it bounds nothing about the never-restored share.
Promotion requires: three things, the OFID fetch and the label fetches having both been done (the first closing Disguise on that document, the second closing limb (c)'s document-kind premise on US labels only and not on SmPCs, which stay unenumerated). First, the Eppenga results check, which must be settled by a read and not by a design argument: open W.L. Eppenga's 2016 PhD thesis (Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis, COULD NOT READ at both routes tried — WebFetch returned "[binary data]", curl returned "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" — so a third route is needed), or registry record onderzoekmetmensen.nl/en/node/43767, or a differently-titled results paper from this cohort; if any of them prints a share of medication changes made or not made after renal function improved, that prior becomes live and this entry must be re-graded. Second, enumerate the pre-declared drug list, which is announced eleven times across this entry and its logs and written down nowhere, and widen its exclusion rule beyond therapeutic drug monitoring to the pathogen- and day-of-therapy-conditional dosing the opened labels print. Third, the three one-sentence repairs under Scores: "estimated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault where the label specifies an equation)" for the primary instrument, the integral-of-a-ratio versus ratio-of-integrals wording for limb (c), and the list-and-exclusion-rule repair itself.
Vulnerability of this verdict (recorded as the rule requires, since it applies to grounds nobody has measured and not only to kills): the Provisional no longer rests on an unopened document — that document is open — and rests instead on an UNENUMERATED leg, on novelty at Medium beside a close neighbour, and on two of three dented silence mechanisms. First, adversary #2's dismissal of the Eppenga results publication as incapable of printing the quantity follows FROM A DESIGN — the 2015 protocol's medication limb is a counterfactual need measured post-discharge at two fixed visits — and not from any reported result; that worry is SUSTAINED, because a post-batch read confirmed the protocol half ("announces and does not measure") and could not reach the thesis half: the 2016 thesis at the Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis URL returned "[binary data]" through WebFetch and "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" with 0 bytes through curl, so it is COULD NOT READ rather than NOT FOUND, no route was worked around and no TLS setting was touched. It remains the single source most likely to settle this leg, with registry record 43767 a second unopened instance of the right kind. Second, adversary #2's claim that label thresholds are themselves defined on an estimated clearance was its own recollection with zero labels opened; over the five labels now opened it is true and explicit on one (Zerbaxa, "Estimated CrCl using the Cockcroft-Gault formula"), true only as a scoped fallback on one (meropenem, "When only serum creatinine is available"), unstated on two (Zosyn and Fresenius name "creatinine clearance" and no equation at all) and inapplicable on one (Eliquis, serum creatinine in mg/dL) — so the recollection was right in direction and too flat, which is why the Gate 1 repair's wording is corrected under Scores. Third, both magnitude dents under attack 6 are the adversaries' own arithmetic on single-centre figures, labelled as such by their authors, and one of the figures behind #2's dent was mis-transcribed in this entry and is corrected in that row. None of these three carried the Provisional; what carries it now is the unenumerated Eppenga leg together with novelty and the dented mechanisms. One identity to keep straight: the step from Hughes's 1.5-fold creatinine-fall recovery rule to V2's label-threshold clearance crossing is neither algebraic nor bitwise — it is an empirical comparability gap between two instruments, so the median-3-days figure BOUNDS the window's existence rather than measuring the candidate's own clock, and it is in any case a median time from peak creatinine to a partial (1.5-fold) fall, in an unstated denominator, rather than a time to restored baseline function. Second-order: this entry drew two adversaries as the rule requires, and the second closed the first's strongest killing point, which is the scrutiny working as intended rather than a softening.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): both of the steps previously named here have now been taken, by the post-batch verification pass rather than by the record or either adversary — DOI 10.1093/ofid/ofae059 was opened at academic.oup.com and prints no dose-increase timing or share conditioned on renal improvement in the sections read, and five US labels were opened, three of which print a single full dose per indication beside a clearance threshold. What is left as a first step is therefore: find a third route to W.L. Eppenga's 2016 thesis (or to registry record onderzoekmetmensen.nl/en/node/43767) and read it for a share of medication changes made or not made after renal function improved; open one EU or UK SmPC, since the label half of the premise is instanced only in the US FDA format; and write the drug list down.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ROUTE: no — the entry is Provisional, so by construction the ledger still claims this question as un-asked and there is nothing to hand to the open-questions project; a routable row needs a rejection on the ground that the question was asked and is still unanswered, which is not this verdict. No row is recommended for ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The disguised-known inversion that was the live risk here did not occur: the OFID check has been run and came back a neighbour. If a remaining check inverts the verdict — the Eppenga results leg is the only one that could — the right successor action would be a disguised-known rejection, which is also not routable.

## Verification of this entry's sources (post-batch, 2026-10-23)

**THE HEADLINE: THE DISGUISE HOLE CLOSES.** The one right-kind document that both adversaries' sweeps returned and neither opened has now been opened, and it is a NEIGHBOUR rather than a disguised known, so Disguise moves from Partial to clear as far as that document is concerned. Its citation, corrected from its own front matter, is Aldardeer NF, Alshreef MM, Alharbi EA, Aljabri AK, Aljawadi MH, Almangour TA, Alobaili S, Alarifi MI, Alomari A, Alhammad AM, "Early Versus Late Antipseudomonal beta-Lactam Antibiotic Dose Adjustment in Critically Ill Sepsis Patients With Acute Kidney Injury: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study", Open Forum Infectious Diseases 2024;11(3):ofae059, pages 1-9, published online 1 February 2024, DOI 10.1093/ofid/ofae059. The entry had carried the title stem, journal, year and DOI correctly and had dropped the subtitle, the ten authors, the volume, the issue and the article number; the subtitle is load-bearing because it declares the design the regime comparison turns on. The DECIDING FINDING is in Methods > Definitions, reconstructed by the checker from five consecutive fragments with every junction verified and nothing completed by inference: "After receiving the initial full dose of antipseudomonal beta-lactam upon sepsis recognition, participants were stratified into 2 groups according to the time to beta-lactam renal dose reduction. The early beta-lactam dose adjustment (E-BLA) group included patients who received a reduced renal dose of beta-lactam within the first 24 hours of sepsis recognition, while the late beta-lactam dose adjustment (L-BLA) group included patients who received a reduced renal dose of beta-lactam after 24 hours from sepsis recognition." The opening words SCOPE the entire stratification to the window after an initial unreduced dose and name the stratifier as the time to a REDUCTION; the logical form is a stipulative biconditional assigning patients to arms, not a necessary condition read as sufficient, not a hedged modality and not a disjunction, and because it exhausts both arms the reading that the paper times only the DOWNWARD transition survives each of those tests. The exclusion of patients who "received the initial dose of beta-lactam adjusted for renal function" guarantees the same thing from the other side. So adversary #1, who read the TITLE as timing the reduction, reached the right conclusion on ground that was a guess until this read, and the confirmation sits in a Methods subsection neither adversary opened.

**The two keyword traps in that paper, disarmed explicitly.** First, the 38/224 (16.9%) escalation row (12/84 in E-BLA, 26/140 in L-BLA), which recurs in Table 2 as a Cox covariate with HR 0.747 (95% CI .395-1.413) and 0.665 and 0.659 in two variant models, carries real numbers and would read to a sweep as an upward transition; the paper's own Methods define it as a SPECTRUM switch — "Escalation of antibiotic therapy was defined as switching patients from antibiotics with a lower spectrum of activity to antibiotics with a broader spectrum of activity" — and the Table 1 row label restricts it to escalation needed to target culture in patients with gram-negative isolates, so the word records a move AWAY from any dose reading. Second, the 48-hour AKI-recovery figures (70.7% versus 47.6%, P = .001; transient AKI 139/224, 62.1% overall) run the arrow backwards: dose timing is the exposure and renal recovery the outcome, where this question conditions the other way, so a dosing-conditioned recovery figure must not be read as a recovery-conditioned dosing figure. Dedicated per-term sweeps across the sections read found "de-escalat", "restor", "return to", "back-titrat", "titrat" and "resume" ABSENT; "increas" present six times and never as a dose increase (three of them KDIGO creatinine thresholds, which move in the direction of worsening function); "full dose"/"full doses" present four times and every one the INITIAL dose before reduction; and "reversal" only inside "the complete reversal of AKI within 48 hours", a reversal of the injury. The closure rests on the Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results and Tables 1-3 — the sections where a measured quantity would be printed — with the Discussion, Limitations and Conclusion UNREAD on a spent budget. The existence premise under test (that this paper prints an upward-transition quantity) is therefore FALSE OVER THE INSTANCE OPENED for those read sections and UNENUMERATED for the unread tail. The checker's argument that a Discussion in a paper of this design could only restate numbers already in the Results or Tables is labelled by its author as ITS OWN REASONING and not a finding, and it is carried here as that and nothing more; the document that would ground it is the OUP PDF or the PMC XML of the same DOI, which is one document under three identifiers (DOI 10.1093/ofid/ofae059 = PMID 38434610 = PMC10906704) and adds no independent corroboration, and the IDSA Science Speaks blog commentary that the search returned resolves to this same DOI and must never be graded in the paper's place.

**Whether the verdict moved, and why not.** It did not. The verdict is Provisional and stays Provisional. No late Gate 4 was owed and none ran, because Gate 4 ran twice with nothing Unresolved. What the pass changed is the REASON this entry is capped. Both adversaries held Disguise at Partial solely because one right-kind document was returned by both sweeps and opened by neither; that document is now open and the hole closes on it, and one of the two items under the single promotion line also closes, on US labels only and not on SmPCs. Against that, the pass REOPENED a check this entry had argued shut by design rather than by a read — whether the Eppenga 2015 protocol produced a results publication — and found one NEW well-posedness defect of the repairable kind, that the pre-declared drug list does not exist. The cap therefore now rests on the unenumerated Eppenga results leg, on novelty at Medium beside a close neighbour, and on two of three dented silence mechanisms, not on an unopened document.

**How many checkers ran and what each was sent to read.** Four fresh-context checkers, one per load-bearing prior or kill leg, each handed the claim and its sources but NOT the reviewers' reasoning. Checker 1 (note at batches/2026-10-23-0633/VERIFY-uq10-ofid-2024.md) was sent to the OFID 2024 paper, DOI 10.1093/ofid/ofae059, on the single question that decided the entry. **Read level reached, source by source, with COULD NOT READ kept distinct from NOT FOUND.** OFID ofae059: PARTIAL — front matter, Abstract, Introduction, all Methods subsections including Definitions, Results including Secondary Outcomes, and Tables 1-3, served by academic.oup.com; Discussion, Limitations and Conclusion COULD NOT READ, the served article body terminating at the Discussion's first two words, "This prospective", at every offset tried.
