Two further COULD NOT CHECK items, each a spent budget and not an absence: whether any author of the Hughes paper appears on either older prior's author list, and whether any EU or UK SmPC satisfies the premise, since no SmPC was opened.

**Hughes 2022: one leg strengthened, one narrowed, one struck, and two quotation repairs.** The 5-of-11 string holds, verbatim up to the glyph, in the Results running text under "Antimicrobial use" — no table and no figure, exactly as this entry said — and the denominator chain closes upward ("β-Lactam based therapy was prescribed in 97/105 cases", full licensed dosing "utilized in 86/97 cases (88.7%)", 86 + 11 = 97), so the denominator is 11 dose-reduced β-lactam courses and not 97, 105, 123, 647 or 608. Two repairs were owed and are made in the entry's own prose. The paper prints the Greek glyph, "β-lactams", so the entry's string was not literally verbatim as rendered; the glyph is now carried. And the entry's quotation STOPPED ONE CLAUSE EARLY, at "pharmacist", where the printed sentence continues "within the first 24 h post bacteraemia." The grammar was clean on both sides of that cut, which is why nothing flagged it, and THE CUT WAS THE DEFECT: the dropped adverbial is the trailing clause that fixes the time origin, which is this entry's own point. The time origin is the BACTERAEMIA and not renal recovery, and it is printed twice in the paper's own words — Methods, "Antibacterial treatment prescribed within the first 72 h from blood culturing was analysed in patients with acute kidney injury or failure (defined as AKI stage 2 or above)", and the restored tail, "post bacteraemia" — so this is established by a read rather than inferred, which strengthens the entry's reading that the five of eleven are pharmacist corrections of inappropriate initial reductions (the paper's own verb is "corrected") and not escalations triggered by recovering renal function. The narrowing: "it never links the escalation to renal function" was too strong and has been rewritten to "it never links an UPWARD adjustment to renal function recovering", because the Discussion does link dose adjustment to renal function twice — "Dose adjustments after 48 h were not recommended if renal function was improving to baseline at time of review to correct for any potential hyperfiltration with recovering function" and "Where renal function recovery was slow, dose adjustments based on the estimated renal function at 48 h were advised" — and an unqualified "never" was a hostage to a one-fetch rebuttal. The first of those sentences is a CONDITIONAL, its modality is NORMATIVE local guidance rather than an observation of what was done, and its direction is an UNLOADING: the adjustment withheld is the downward one, so improving renal function is a reason to leave a dose at full and never a trigger to raise a dose that had been cut. The median 3 days (IQR 2-5) holds verbatim, in Results under "Impact of AKI on patients' outcomes", and now travels with its two qualifications: it is time from PEAK creatinine to a 1.5-FOLD REDUCTION and not to restored baseline function, the paper reserving a stricter second definition of the same word for its 105/106 figure, and its denominator is NOT PRINTED, so the entry writes "unstated" rather than picking among 106, 112, 105 and a summariser-reported 96/97. STRUCK: any treatment of this paper as bounding the never-restored share. "restor" and "never" are both absent on dedicated sweeps, the paper is silent past 24 hours, and the six-of-eleven complement is the checker's own arithmetic meaning "not escalated within 24 h", not "never restored"; the entry's attack-8 row, which had said the dissolution worry was "now bounded on an opened source", is rewritten to claim only the weaker and sufficient point that the window is non-empty. Population refinements carried: "2016-2020" is four FISCAL years, April 2016 to March 2020; the unit is the episode, deduplicated to the first isolate within 30 days; urine output was "not routinely available", so KDIGO ran on its creatinine limb only; and the paper declares NO primary or secondary endpoint, so any endpoint language about it is imported. Source-side defects recorded rather than laundered: the Discussion's "typically corrected by a pharmacist within 24 h" overstates its own 5 of 11 (the checker's own arithmetic: 45.5%, under half), and the AKI stage >=2 subgroup is reported against at least four unreconciled denominators. One number in the entry was wrong and is corrected: "97/105 full-dose cases" conflated the 97 of 105 cases on β-lactam therapy with the 86 of 97 at full licensed dosing. Hughes's citation needed NO correction: the printed author order and initials match, and the absence of a page range is correct rather than an omission. A method limit the checker flagged in its own work, carried in its words: its first broad "improv" sweep reported sentences absent that an earlier pass had already surfaced, which is why the load-bearing strings were re-run on a dedicated sweep; single-swept absences in that note are weaker than double-swept ones.

**The two older priors.** On the congress abstract the claim holds on a full read, and three fixes are made in the entry's prose. The scope-setting opener "During treatment," is RESTORED to the quotation, because those are the words that confine the clause to the on-therapy window of mean 8.4 days; quoting from "16 patients" left the entry asserting the window rather than quoting it, and the cut happened to favour the entry, which is exactly why it had to be repaired. "16 of 46" is now labelled DERIVED, since the abstract prints "Forty-six patients were included" and prints 16 but prints no percentage joining them. The numeric collision is now named: the abstract's other sixteen, "Sixteen patients (34.8%) were admitted to the intensive care unit", makes 34.8% look like the CrCl-change share and it is not. Direction is NOT PRINTED anywhere, confirmed by a dedicated direction-term sweep rather than a broad one, so the ten non-adjustments pool un-made increases with un-made reductions. The gloss that "underdosed" is a renal-reduction artefact is STRUCK as an assertion available to this entry: the abstract defines underdosing solely as "any dose lower than the Summary of Product Characteristics recommended dose (based on CrCl)", states no mechanism, and leaves a competing non-renal explanation unadjudicated (ceftolozane/tazobactam's higher licensed pneumonia dose, respiratory being the commonest site at 43.5%), and the entry now says so where it reports those figures. One correction to the checker's framing, which the batch record requires be stated rather than inherited: the checker attributed that gloss to "the record", and on a sweep of this entry the gloss appears nowhere in the entry's own prose — the entry carried the point-in-time figures without any mechanism claim — so there was nothing in the entry to delete, and what has been added instead is the explicit statement that the abstract states no mechanism, which forecloses the gloss. The record file itself is read-only and was not edited. On the 2015 protocol, "announces and does not measure" is SETTLED BY A READ and the entry's characterisation of it is exact: "This study will provide data on changes in renal function in elderly patients after discharge from the hospital" records a promise, and the medication endpoint is explicitly counterfactual, "the percentages of patients in whom a change in the medication would be needed". Added: its 5% improvement and 15% deterioration figures are SAMPLE-SIZE ASSUMPTIONS fed into the power calculation and not findings, being the numbers in that document most easily mistaken for the quantity this question wants, and the protocol states no trial registration, so it offers no registry identifier to search by. But the other half of that limb is REOPENED against this entry: whether a results publication has appeared is UNENUMERATED, not settled. Nothing anyone read establishes that none exists; one search returned a candidate of exactly the right kind — W.L. Eppenga's own 2016 PhD thesis, same first author, same hospital, the year after the protocol, and a thesis is the kind of document that carries a cohort's results chapter with full tables — and that candidate would not open. Writing "no results paper exists" would be an unenumerated universal from one sweep's silence, and writing "a results paper exists" would be the mirror defect, so the entry closes the leg in neither direction and carries it on the single promotion line. On that half, the objection that the check was argued shut by design rather than by a read IS SUSTAINED, not because the design argument is wrong but because it was doing work a read has not done. One structural point in this entry's favour that it did not previously claim is now claimed: the two older priors are TWO INDEPENDENT GROUPS with ZERO author overlap — Hospital Clínic Barcelona against Jeroen Bosch Hospital and Dutch academic co-authors — so this claim is not a case of one group citing itself; whether the Hughes paper shares any author with either is COULD NOT CHECK on a spent budget, and neither printed list contains anyone named Hughes.

**The label premise, now instanced on five US labels.** The premise is TRUE OVER THE INSTANCES OPENED on ZERBAXA (Merck Sharp & Dohme, rev. 5/2026), ZOSYN (Baxter Healthcare, rev. 5/2026) and PIPERACILLIN AND TAZOBACTAM (Fresenius Kabi USA, rev. 6/2015) — two labelers concordant on the threshold and on both full doses eleven years apart, which is the positive finding for limb (c)'s denominator having one referent per molecule across labelers. It is HALF-MET on MEROPENEM (Xellia, rev. 4/2021): threshold yes, unique full dose no for cSSSI. It FAILED on ELIQUIS (E.R. Squibb & Sons, rev. 4/2025): no adult clearance threshold at all, the trigger being serum creatinine >= 1.5 mg/dL inside a 2-of-3 rule over a disjunctive set, in the wrong units and with the inequality the opposite sign to a clearance floor, and Section 8.6 stating "No dose adjustment is recommended for patients with renal impairment, including those with ESRD on dialysis" for the other indications. Consequently P3's "ZERO product labels or SmPCs were opened by the record or by either adversary" is no longer true of this ledger and has been rewritten; the second item under the single promotion line CLOSES, on US labels only and not on SmPCs, which remain unenumerated; and the concession under Scores that limb (c)'s denominator is unverified at the document-kind level is DISCHARGED. The adversaries' shared reading of the clause as a satisfiable existence claim is vindicated on opened documents rather than on the shape of the clause. But the defect RELOCATES rather than disappearing, and this pass logs ONE NEW well-posedness defect of the same repairable kind as the two already carried. The "pre-declared drug list" DOES NOT EXIST: on three greps, labelled by their author as the checker's own greps and not a source finding, the phrase and its variants occur eleven times across the entry, the record and both adversary logs and NOT ONE is followed by an enumeration, every drug named in the record is an example of something else, and the two named most often — vancomycin and allopurinol — are the titrated exemplars the rule EXCLUDES; "pre-declared" is at present an announcement of a list rather than a declaration of one, and neither adversary asked this, both having tested only whether labels CAN satisfy the clause. The exclusion rule is also ONE-DIMENSIONAL, handling therapeutic-drug-monitoring dosing only, where the opened labels produce two further conditioning dimensions that each give "the labelled full dose" more than one referent inside a single indication: PATHOGEN, on meropenem for cSSSI, 500 mg q8h against 1 g q8h, since "For P. aeruginosa, a dose of 1 gram every 8 hours is recommended"; and DAY OF THERAPY, on apixaban for DVT/PE, "10 mg taken orally twice daily for the first 7 days of therapy. After 7 days, the recommended dose is 5 mg taken orally twice daily." The breaking case is INSTANCED rather than hypothetical: a cSSSI episode on meropenem 500 mg q8h at a recovered clearance scores as a 50% exposure deficit if the denominator is read as 1 g and as fully restored if it is read as 500 mg. Meropenem also cuts the other way in one respect worth keeping: its Table 1 expresses the reduced doses relatively ("One-half recommended dose"), which makes the full dose the explicitly named referent of the reduction. A tension the checker flags, marked by its author as its own inference from quoted label text rather than a source finding, is now recorded in the entry: this entry's audience (3) is anticoagulation and AF services, whose drug the pre-declared rule cannot admit, so the significance claim and the inclusion rule are in tension on the one DOAC label opened. Two further corrections carried from this check: the Gate 1 wording repair "measured clearance" to "estimated clearance" is right in direction but too flat, and should read "estimated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault where the label specifies an equation)", because over five labels the equation is named unconditionally on one, named only as a scoped fallback on one ("When only serum creatinine is available"), unstated on two and inapplicable on one; and the Zerbaxa label's only ranges are DURATIONS ("4 to 14 days"), so a cut dropping the word "days" would manufacture a dose range out of a course length. The checker states plainly what it is not saying, and the entry repeats it: it is not saying that labels generally print a single full dose per indication — five labels in one jurisdiction and one format are five labels, two of them complicated the premise, and a larger sample would likely complicate it further.

**Citation corrections made, gathered in one place.** The OFID 2024 paper gained its subtitle, its ten authors in printed order, volume 11, issue 3, article number ofae059 and pages 1-9. The EJHP 2019 congress abstract gained its six printed authors and its abstract DOI 10.1136/ejhpharm-2019-eahpconf.222, its page locator corrected from "A102.2" to the printed A102 (the ".2" being the BMJ sub-locator and not a printed page), its title set in the printed title case, a note that there is no issue number because it is a supplement, and a note that the BMJ front matter prints "Rodriguez-Reyes" unaccented where the EAHP congress page prints "Rodríguez-Reyes". The BMC Nephrology 2015 protocol gained its full seven-author list in printed order, a note that "95" is an ARTICLE NUMBER and not a page and that there is no issue number, and the fact that it states no trial registration. Hughes 2022 needed no front-matter correction, only the glyph and the restored clause. The five labels are recorded by the only front matter their document kind has — issuing authority (US Food and Drug Administration, hosted on DailyMed), labeler or packager, revision date and SPL set id — and asking a label for authors, journal, volume, pages or a DOI is a category error that this pass did not manufacture around.

**Routes that failed, so a later pass does not repeat them.** doi.org/10.1093/ofid/ofae059 returned 302 to academic.oup.com/ofid/article/11/3/ofae059/7596145 and the cross-host redirect was handed back rather than followed, which is a hop and not a failure; the OUP article HTML succeeded but its served body terminates at "This prospective" at the default offset and at offsets 24000 and 60000, so the truncation is in the served document and not in the window, and each table is duplicated in the page source, which is why the offsets land where they do. The PMC ID-converter URL returned a 302 to the hard-blocked PMC host and was not followed; pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10906704 served a reCAPTCHA interstitial ("Checking your browser before accessing...") rather than the article, which is the declared hard block behaving as declared. No institutional PDF mirror was attempted, on a spent budget, which is why the OFID tail is COULD NOT READ. Unpaywall was deliberately skipped because its contact-email parameter would put a personal identifier in a query string. For the Eppenga 2016 thesis, the Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis PDF URL reached the host through WebFetch but the summariser received no extractable text and reported "[binary data]", and the same URL through curl returned "curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403" with HTTP 000 and zero bytes; the proxy was not routed around and no TLS setting was touched, so a third route is needed. Nothing failed on doi.org/10.1093/jacamr/dlac080 (one 302, then the article), on the EJHP PDF, on the Springer protocol PDF, or on any of the five DailyMed pages. Routes that WORKED and are worth reusing: DailyMed drugInfo.cfm?setid=... serves a full label through WebFetch in one call, fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=... also works, and search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=<name> returns the setid list when no search budget is left. One trap recorded for the congress abstract: the EAHP congress page for 4CPS-073 does not contain the string "62.5", which is a fact about that page's rendering and not about the abstract, which prints "(n=10, 62.5%)" plainly at the BMJ route — anyone sweeping only the EAHP page would file a false absence. Repeated title returns are not corroboration: the OFID paper filled four of nine result slots in one search as two PMC URL forms, a PMID-routed PMC URL and a blog commentary, which is one document plus one restatement of it.

**What the pass did NOT reach.** The OFID paper's Discussion, Limitations and Conclusion, on a spent budget and a truncated served body — COULD NOT READ, so the existence premise is unenumerated for that tail. Every SmPC: no EMA product information and no medicines.org.uk entry was opened, so on SmPCs the label premise is UNENUMERATED and no claim is made about what section 4.2 Posology contains. The Eppenga 2016 thesis and the registry record 43767, both instances of the right kind, the first COULD NOT READ and the second unopened. Whether any author of the Hughes paper appears on either older prior's author list — COULD NOT CHECK. The Aarau 2023 CDS thesis, still unopened, as it was at Gate 4. The record's own side-claim that no full paper exists behind the congress abstract, which was not re-tested and remains unverified in both directions. The final characters of four of the five label pages, beyond a 100,000-character coverage ceiling, the unread tails being package and NDC blocks. The unenumerated drug list could not be checked as a fraction at all, because there is no denominator to divide by, which is itself the finding; against the drugs this entry names anywhere, four molecules and five labels were checked, and vancomycin, allopurinol, enoxaparin, dabigatran, metformin and quinolones as a class were not reached.

**What this block did not change, and why.** The verdict, which was settled before this amendment and is not re-judged here, and the scores, which the label checker explicitly left to the grader when it declined to re-score 3/3 itself. The adversaries' recorded Partial statuses, which are a historical record of what each adversary graded on the Gate 0-3 record and are annotated rather than overwritten, with the closure recorded beside them. The record and both adversary logs, the four verification notes and every other ledger file, all of which are read-only to this amendment; where a checker's bearing described something as sitting in "the record", this block says so and leaves that file alone. And the five limbs of the canonical question, none of which is added, dropped or rewritten here: the three repairs owed are wording repairs, and the enumeration of the drug list is work for whoever answers the question, not a change of what is asked.

ID: UQ-20261023-11
Date: 2026-10-23
Status: Provisional — Gates 0-3 pass with novelty Medium; Validated blocked twice over, at Gate 1 (well-posedness 2/3) and at Gate 4 (attack 7 Unresolved, adversary #2). No fatal objection: attacks 1, 2 and 4 are Resolved or Partial in all three adversary logs, none Unresolved. Post-batch verification (five fresh-context checkers, 35 fetches, 4 searches, 0 errors) left the class and every grade exactly where they were and moved the GROUND of the Gate 1 cap: presupposition 1's un-instantiated-kind leg STRIKES on two live FDSN availability instances opened and a third found false, while promotion condition (ii) holds NARROWED TO ITS IMS/ANSS LEG; the entry's own declared Low trigger remains UNFIRED AND UNVERIFIED, not cleared, because neither Kvaerna & Ringdal paper has been read by anybody, and an unrun check caps this entry at Provisional without ever rejecting it.

Domain(s): Other STEM — observational seismology and monitoring-network engineering (target field: network operators, CTBTO/IDC and NDCs, PSHA catalogue builders; EEW operators were listed here too and the post-batch pass struck that audience claim from Significance, so they are named only as a field the method vocabulary touches, not as an audience this entry claims). Method vocabulary from reliability engineering (common-cause failure / beta factor) and power-system common-mode-and-dependent outage analysis. Source method: anomaly mining.

Question (canonical): For one declared seismic network N over one declared window W, with the station frame fixed by rule (channels whose FDSN epoch covers >=90% of W), the reference fixed as a NAMED published capability or completeness product for N on a declared magnitude scale, and the grid enumerated at clustering window w in {15 min, 1 h, 6 h}, margin dM in {0.2, 0.3, 0.5} magnitude units and duration T in {1, 3, 6, 12} h — estimate from per-channel availability records and a declared model mapping the up-channel set at t to a realized threshold field: (a) the share of downtime station-hours falling in multi-station coincident clusters in excess of a per-station independent (Poisson/renewal) null, at each w, with a permutation interval; (b) the paired probabilities of an interval of >=T h in which the realized threshold exceeds the named reference by >=dM, computed once under the independent null and once under the measured joint downtime process, reported as a ratio over the (dM, T) grid; and (c) the share of realized-threshold variance attributable to correlated versus independent downtime under a declared variance decomposition.
This is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation (V1 and the reasons for the repair are in batches/2026-10-23-1233/UQ-20261023-11-record.md, Gate 0). V1 left dM, T and w undeclared and presupposed a unique "published capability map"; V2 enumerates the grid, states the frame as a rule, and requires the reference to be a named document.

Alternative formulations:
- Do seismic stations go dark together, and if so how much does that inflate the chance of a detection blind window compared with the independent-availability picture behind published capability maps?
- From per-channel FDSN/ANSS availability records for a declared network and window: (a) a beta-factor-style common-cause downtime fraction, and (b) the distribution of realized-minus-reference detection-threshold excursions and their durations.

Motivating gap: the field computes realized, time-resolved detection capability operationally (prior A: CTBTO/NORSAR threshold monitoring, estimates every 10 s, hourly averages and hourly worst case per adversary #1's S3), and governs station availability per station against a 98% DAU floor (prior B), and joins neither to the other as a statistic. Cui & Atkinson 2016 DECLINED to model outages for want of data — the narrowed form, replacing the entry's earlier reading that it identified outages as a source of bias. The printed sentence in full, p. 854, section "METHODOLOGY FOR ESTIMATING AND MAPPING Mc", a single parenthetical Note in Methods (reconstruction from four fragments across three independent reads, every junction separately verified): "(Note: we know the operational start and stop dates for each station, and make the assumption that they were operating continuously during this time, ignoring any occasional outages that may have occurred, because we do not have this level of detailed information.)" The entry's earlier two-string rendering was a cut quotation and the cut was the defect: it dropped the operative verb "make the assumption" and the reason clause "because we do not have this level of detailed information", which is what turns the clause from an assertion about outages into an assumption made for want of data, hedged over outages that "may have occurred"; the two strings are two clauses of ONE sentence and therefore one support, not two. The paper has no Limitations, Caveats or Conclusions section, its Discussion (pp. 859-863) never returns to the point, and "outage" occurs once in the whole paper, so this is a nobody-has-the-data gap, which is still a gap but carries no measured bias. The entry's "not character-verified" flag is LIFTED. The gap is not that realized capability is invisible; it is that no opened source turns the realized series into a population of excursions or tests whether downtime is coincident.

Presuppositions: (1) per-channel availability records retrievable at resolution finer than w=15 min and T=1 h — THE UN-INSTANTIATED-KIND LEG IS STRUCK, because the post-batch pass opened the three endpoints nobody had opened and the kind is now instantiated. TRUE OVER TWO LIVE INSTANCES: NCEDC (net BK, station CMB, location 00, channel BHZ) returns per-channel spans with 0.1 ms stamps across an arbitrary chosen week, and RESIF (net G, station SSB, locations 00 and 10, BHZ) returns microsecond stamps with three printed interruptions. FALSE OVER THE THIRD, and the counter-instance is what decides the kind: SCEDC (net CI, station PASC, BHZ) returns ONE row per channel whose Earliest and Latest are exactly the requested window endpoints, with "TimeSpans NA" and an empty Quality column, so no gap of any length is resolvable from it. Two readings of the printed stamps are the checker's OWN ARITHMETIC and not source findings, and both cut against a naive use of these records: the resolvable 186.05 s interval between two NCEDC D-quality rows is NOT an outage, because a Q row covers the identical week continuously and the rows are one channel partitioned by the Quality key; and RESIF's three 0.050001 s interruptions are ONE-SAMPLE tears at the printed SampleRate of 20.0 (1/20.0 = 0.05 s). The entry's claim that the two spec reads "settle the document kind" is STRUCK as an over-claim: SCEDC's own landing page lists only net, sta, loc, cha, start, end, asset, format and nodata, naming neither mergegaps nor show, and its /query returns extent-shaped single rows, so the specification binds implementations to its response shape no more than it "binds no network and names no holdings". Novelty — how this differs from each: THE NUMBER TEST, run on every one of them, and no source names any of the candidate's three numbers. A supplies the instrument and none of the statistics — now VERIFIED rather than assumed, by a second reader's three prompted reads one of which was a dedicated number sweep: it DEFINES and DISPLAYS the realized threshold, carries per-station availability as a CATEGORICAL COLOUR CLASS ONLY ("Colour of Station Symbols Represents Data Availability During the Analyzed Time Interval", with no numeric colour scale and no numeric tick labels served), and ANNOUNCES outages as one unquantified member of driver disjunctions ("The IMS event detection threshold varies by time because of factors such as station outages"). The only percentage sign in the entire document is the "90%" of its criterion; it prints no downtime statistic, no availability percentage and no exceedance frequency, count or distribution, so Low trigger (ii) is NOT in play from prior A. Its two printed durations are now verbatim and both are attributed, in their own sentences, to ARRIVING SIGNAL: "As seismic phases and the associated coda from large earthquakes reach the different IMS stations, the network event detection capability is generally reduced. For these four sites the M 6.5 Jan Mayen earthquake caused the IMS event detection threshold to significantly increase for about half an hour after the event origin." and "The main event and the aftershock sequence caused a significant reduction in IMS event detection capability for several hours." Citing either as outage-driven would transfer a duration across panels AND cite a three-or-more-member driver disjunction for one of its members — the scope transfer the entry warned of, now confirmed with its mechanism named and with no counter-instance in either panel; "significantly" is unquantified in both and the poster prints no magnitude-unit size for either excursion. Its comparator is a USER PARAMETER, "a baseline time interval selected by the user", instanced as "The average detection thresholds for June 2025", and it names no published capability product anywhere because it carries NO references or bibliography section at all, which STRENGTHENS the "against a named published reference" leg. Its 10-second estimation cadence and its "Hourly maps with the average and worst-case event" are two distinct cadences and must not be conflated in either direction. Its method paper 4828, now read at full text by three independent readers with dedicated outage sweeps, prints NEITHER product the entry previously attributed to it: the per-station "percentages of successfully recorded and processed data" are ANNOUNCED in a figure-discussion bullet of Sect. 7.1's "Analysis results" whose own opener is "The second set of results (see example in Section 7.2, Figure 7 .2.3)", and NO per-station percentage value appears on any page of 4828 (three readers, three sweeps, no station code with a number); its only downtime statement in its own words is qualitative — "several of the stations were out of operation for all or part of the time." Its outage attribution is one cited member of a three-cause list whose cited member is itself a disjunction that does not separate station from IDC processing outages: "Variation from hour to hour of the average detection capability is primarily caused by longer station or processing outages" (that sentence's tail, naming increased background noise and long-duration signals from large events, is paraphrase-confirmed and NOT verbatim — a summariser refusal about the checker's request shape, not a property of the document), and its subject is the hour-to-hour variation of the Fig. 7.2.4 product printed in the section 4828 does not contain. The Discussion's hedged, listed formulation is the one to cite: "Changes in data quality at the IDC caused by communications problems, station outages or other data errors", one bullet in a list of four factors. So: an announcement and an unquantified authorial attribution with no number, no denominator and no study period, no fraction, no duration distribution, no simultaneity statement; and its independence sentence, located in the Method and not the Discussion, is about DETECTION probability rather than availability — "We assume that the probability of detection is statistically independent among the stations in the network." B MEASURES a different numerator on a different denominator: stations clearing 98% DAU — "% of stations with DAU > 98% are overall stable since 2013 (~73%)", where the ~73% is the level of a series and carries no year of its own, and "Continuous increase of % of stations with DAU above 98% DAU (> 90% in 2022)", doubled "DAU" as printed — a count of stations over stations, against the candidate's downtime station-hours in coincident clusters over all downtime station-hours. The entry's "per year" is STRUCK: it is not printed, the poster saying only that results are presented on a yearly basis and never that DAU is computed per year. Its cause taxonomy and DAU stop at the per-station marginal, and the gap is WIDER than the entry argued rather than narrower: DAU's own numerator and denominator are undefined anywhere on the poster (the only definition served is "Data Availability Unauthenticatied (DAU) is the metric used to quantify station Data Loss (DL).", misspelling as printed, plus "DAU computed from cdtools", with no formula and no computation period), no station counts are printed for any population so even ~73% and >90% have no absolute base, and the poster is internally inconsistent at its own boundary, printing ">" in the bullet against "⩾" in the chart legend. No coincidence, simultaneity or multi-station concept appears anywhere in it, by a keyword sweep AND a dedicated concept sweep, with the residue that figure interiors (Severity Matrix cells, chart data series) were served as labels and captions rather than images. This is a GRANULARITY GAP short of the candidate's grain, not an absence. C DECLINES the quantity in its own words for want of data — the narrowed form — at inter-configuration-period resolution over seven periods ("1985-1989, 1990-1999, 2000-2006, 2007-2009, 2010, 2011-2013, and 2014-2015", verbatim as the record lists them), with operational start and stop dates as its only availability input and D4 "calculated from the station configuration for the applicable time period"; the refinement is that the start/stop dates are known at DAY resolution and it is the D4/Mc mapping that collapses to the seven periods, so the paper does not lack finer station data, its mapped quantity does. The second coarsening the entry missed, and should carry: "We consider the stations that have been operating since the beginning of each time period" is a SELECTION rule, so stations added mid-period are excluded from that period too, independently of outages. One datum that cuts the other way on C's silence about multi-station structure: D4 uses the fourth-nearest station because Alberta practice was to catalog events detected on four or more stations (paraphrase, not served verbatim) — a cataloguing practice, not a coincidence statistic, and silent on simultaneous downtime. Sect. 4.4 prints, hedged: "Our simulations suggest an increase of below 0.05 units m_b for this percentage of operational PS stations when compared to a fully deployed and operational network.", whose "this percentage" is the immediately preceding sentence, "At the current status, 44 out of the 50 (88 %) planned stations of the PS network are certified and operational." Sect. 6 prints the same substance in different words and by numeral rather than anaphor: "The current status of the network (44 operational PS stations) only leads to an increase of less than 0.05 units m_b, when compared to the detection capability of a fully operational network (50 PS stations)." CITATION CORRECTION: "below" is Sect. 4.4's word ONLY — Sect. 6 says "less than" — so the entry's earlier attribution of that one verbatim string to "Sect. 4.4 and Sect. 6" was wrong on the word, and a reader checking Sect. 6 for "below" will not find it. The 50% figure, with its cut at the comma repaired, reads in full: "Assuming a station outage of 50 % the magnitude threshold on average increases around 0.2 units m_b, with a further increase of around 0.2 when considering only 30 % operational PS stations." — two cumulative removal levels, the second 0.2 printed bare without units, so the continuation REINFORCES "only near 50%" instead of qualifying it; this is the rare cut that does not change the claim it carried, and it is repaired anyway. Significance — consequence: if the common-cause excess is large, every capability and completeness product inherits an optimism that no amount of per-station compliance reporting can reveal, because the governed unit is the station marginal while the failure mode is the joint, and mitigation changes category from adding stations to diversifying telemetry, power and firmware. If it is about zero, the field gains a published null it does not have and threshold monitoring can be read as per-station-independent in availability. Deflated by Gaebler & Ceranna, with the aggregation now stated because it is what makes the deflation global-only: at a GLOBAL GRID MEAN over 259200 cells, under UNIFORM RANDOM removal, over 100 draws whose averaging the paper does not print and whose spread it reports nowhere, and on the authors' own hedge "Our simulations suggest", for the IMS globally the smallest margin in the grid (0.2 m_b) is reached only near 50% random loss and the current 12% shortfall (6 of 50 planned; the paper itself frames 44 as the current status against 50 planned) costs under 0.05 m_b — so the stakes are bounded globally and live regionally, where a clustered loss of the three governing stations is not a global-average effect, a regional rider that rests on no printed number in that paper and is doing real work. Two directions the entry did not carry and now does. The paper declares its own estimate CONSERVATIVE against REB magnitudes, so true thresholds may be LOWER, which makes the published reference pessimistic and would make a realized-minus-reference excursion SMALLER — cutting the same way as the deflation. And promotion condition (iii) and this deflation are THE SAME MOVE rather than two independent ones: pinning the realized model to this paper's recipe makes the definitional offset zero by construction and then lets the paper's own Sect. 4.4 numbers bound V2(b) in V2's own units (the checker's OWN REASONING over the recipe it verified, not a source finding), so they must not be scored twice in opposite directions, and only V2's undeclared SPATIAL QUANTIFIER keeps the deflation from being decisive.
Significance — audience: CTBTO/IDC and NDCs, who fund and run both halves as separate products and whose 98% DAU floor is the governance instrument that would be re-specified; BGR/NDC capability authors, who already run outage simulations inside capability papers and would act on whether random removal is the right model; PSHA catalogue builders, for whom an availability-conditioned Mc is the deliverable. THE EEW AUDIENCE CLAIM IS STRUCK, not merely weakened: clause C5 moved from contested to settled at one instance and it moved against this entry, SCEDC stating a deliberate backfill delay whose stated purpose is "to allow gaps in the archive to be filled" and returning `Updated` = NA, with no opened instance distinguishing channel-up from data-received, so an FDSN-derived availability record is an archive holding rather than operational status at time t and supplies no quantity an alerting SLA could use. No opened document shows a capability product changing a decision, and the Operational Manual citation is secondhand AND hedged at its only attribution — though the three Manuals are now three named instances (CTBT/WGB/TL-11,17/15/REV.7, /16-REV.7, /17-REV.7) rather than a nominated kind, none of them opened by anybody.
Significance — fecundity: a beta factor for monitoring networks, portable to infrasound, hydroacoustic, GNSS, magnetometer and gravimeter networks; whether diversity rather than station count is the design variable; whether bulletin non-detections should be reweighted by realized availability; whether a capability map should be replaced by a capability exceedance curve; whether coda-driven and downtime-driven degradation have separable duration distributions; whether the alpha-factor generalisation applies once three or more stations share a cause.
Significance — anchoring: threshold monitoring and the quantity it displays without summarising; the NORSAR outage-versus-below-threshold ambiguity in REB non-detections; time-dependent Mc; per-station availability governance; CCF/beta-factor modelling and power-system CMD analysis, both untransplanted here; ledger entries UQ-20261018-06 and UQ-20261022-13.

Reason for silence: THE RECORD'S PRIMARY LEG FAILED, and it was the leg the record itself nominated to stand on. It claimed availability and capability are owned by separate units that "neither report the other's unit" and that the coincidence statistic needs the two records joined. Two adversaries contradicted that on documents they opened, and the 4828 half of that contradiction is CORRECTED AND NARROWED here, because the sentence this entry previously carried was false as printed in three ways. The true sentence: 4828's "Analysis results" section CROSS-REFERENCES, in two adjacent bullets, a per-station recorded-data display and an hourly average/worst-case capability map, BOTH PRINTED IN THE COMPANION SECTION 7.2; and its own "Initial IDC implementation" feature list names, as adjacent bullets under the lead-in "The initial IDC implementation comprises the following main features:", "Hourly summaries of station availability and background noise levels" and "Hourly average and worst-case global capability maps". What is struck: 4828 prints no hourly realized threshold series at all (its hourly objects are a geographic map pair for the single hour 10:00 to 11:00 on 1998/05/11, and its only multi-hour trace is Fig. 7.1.6's single day), it prints no per-station percentage value, and the two objects are two different figures (7.2.3 and 7.2.4) in a section report 4828 does not contain and nobody has opened — so adversary #2's "in one product" is FALSE, and "in one section" is true only of the two cross-referencing bullets, never of the printed products. The strings the kill quotes DO exist, as cross-referencing sentences in Sect. 7.1's Analysis results, not as a published join of values. The kill's CONCLUSION survives, at ANNOUNCEMENT LEVEL ONLY and at a location the kill does not cite: the IDC feature list shows one system emitting both halves in 1998, so the unit-of-governance boundary is still weakened — but what is demonstrated is that both products were ANNOUNCED as outputs of one implementation, not that any values were joined on a page, and by this entry's own standard elsewhere ("A supplies the instrument and none of the statistics") this leg is of the same kind as prior A, one document earlier. The "two independent readers at full text" support also reads stronger than it is: three readers have now read the SAME PDF and found the same cross-references, the figures the leg leans on have been seen by nobody, and adversary #1's "figure contents not served" was a property of a figure absent from the file — three readers of one document is one document. And Gaebler & Ceranna 2021 Sect. 4.4 reports capability degradation in m_b as a function of the percentage of operational PS stations (adversary #3, full text; confirmed post-batch by a second reader at the named locations). The units have been joined, in 1998 and again in 2021, under the very independence assumption the candidate interrogates. What survives is narrower and weaker: the join exists as a display, an attribution and a random-removal simulation, and the STATISTIC was never required of anyone. Two replacement mechanisms were offered, both labelled by their authors as own reasoning rather than source findings — an incentive gap (the published IMS sensitivity looked immaterial, so testing the independence assumption looked pointless) and a new-data mechanism (standardized per-channel gap spans became exchangeable only with the FDSN availability spec, v1.0, 2019-06-27). The second is the better one and the record never invoked it; the post-batch pass confirms it is STILL UNSOURCED, and narrows what 4828 can do to it. 4828 contains no sentence that could source it: nothing in it discusses the exchange, reporting or standardization of availability or gap information between institutions, and it never says how the system learns a station is down or how missing data are handled. Against the mechanism's STRONG form 4828 is a counter-instance, because the IDC was already emitting "Hourly summaries of station availability and background noise levels" in 1998, two decades before the spec; its NARROW form (per-channel, sub-15-minute, standard-form exchangeability across institutions) is untouched, since an hourly summary at one data centre is none of those three things. The kind of document that could source the narrow form is an FDSN working-group or data-centre document, or a motivation section in the spec itself; no instance was opened, so that is a WORK ITEM and not a lead. The record's secondary leg (the series is consumed as a display, not accumulated into a histogram) is close to "no one thought of it", which the protocol does not accept; its tertiary vocabulary leg the record already called weaker than it looks, and Marouani & Shapira 1991 shows the reliability framing of seismic-network detection failure was published 35 years ago (on an abstract-only read; its body is unopened by anybody).

ID: UQ-20261023-12
Date: 2026-10-23
Status: Provisional — Validated blocked at Gate 1 (well-posedness 2/3, standing on reasons (b) and (c)) and by Medium novelty; no Unresolved attack from any of three adversaries, so not Rejected.
Domain(s): Other STEM — metrology and measurement-systems engineering (calibration-interval analysis, test-and-measurement fleet management). Method fields searched: biostatistics (informative visit times), reliability/inspection policy, survey methodology, econometrics (endogenous sampling), legal metrology, nuclear I&C drift analysis.
Question (canonical): In at least one real field-instrument fleet whose calibration-management records hold, per calibration event, the instrument model, the scheduled due date (or the recall interval in force, from which it is derivable), the actual calibration date, and a numeric as-found deviation per calibrated characteristic together with that characteristic's tolerance limit — is the arrival time for calibration independent of the as-found deviation state after conditioning on elapsed time since the previous calibration, instrument model and a usage proxy; and, expressed as the change in days and as a percentage of the current interval in the interval that meets a declared end-of-period in-tolerance target, what are the sign and size of the bias that any such dependence imparts to the estimated in-tolerance-probability-versus-elapsed-time curve from which calibration intervals are set?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation, scored as canonical. V1 (recorded, superseded) asserted the record-field premise as settled; V2 moves it into the question as an explicit scope condition on the fleet, admits the in-force recall interval for a stored due date, and names the tolerance limit and the conditioning set. Full V1 text and the test of V2's own new presuppositions: batches/2026-10-23-1233/UQ-20261023-12-record.md.
Alternative formulations: (1) Are instruments brought in for calibration early because somebody already suspected them, and if so by how much is the out-of-tolerance-rate-versus-interval curve the interval policy rests on wrong? (2) Treating arrival for calibration as a potentially informative inspection time, how large is the outcome-dependent-sampling bias in reliability-based calibration-interval analysis, in days of the interval meeting a declared end-of-period in-tolerance target?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion. Reliability-based calibration-interval analysis estimates P(in tolerance | elapsed time) from the as-found results of returned instruments and sets the interval where that curve crosses a declared target; it presupposes that an as-found observation at elapsed time t is a draw from the drift distribution at t, i.e. arrival timing non-informative. No document that any reader has opened and reported asserts that presupposition, denies it, or tests it — NARROWED post-batch from an unenumerated universal, because as written it ranged over roughly a dozen documents nobody opened and over logs nobody read. ENUMERATED over the three instances a fresh-context checker re-opened and swept for exactly this: NRC ML13303B093 TRUE (it never mentions arrival timing, reason for calibration or selection bias, and both of its interval bounds carry printed non-arrival reasons); NRC ML003677584 TRUE but recorded as the NEAR MISS, since it asserts the GENUS (selection bias, doubly hedged) and is silent on the SPECIES (arrival timing), with no whole-word "overdue", "late", "early", "out of interval" or "unscheduled" anywhere in either attachment, and its one time-axis sentence, "it is unacceptable to exclude data simply because it is old data", POINTS AWAY FROM excluding on timing; DTIC AD0669904 TRUE OVER THE LEGIBLE TEXT and UNENUMERABLE over Section IV.G and the whole of Table 4, which are COULD NOT READ from OCR destruction (not NOT FOUND) and are precisely where a scheduled-versus-non-scheduled condition comparison would sit. **What the pass was, and what each checker was sent to read.** Five fresh-context checkers ran on this entry, each blind to the reviewers' reasoning and each instructed to re-read the load-bearing sources first-hand. Check 2, on whether the nuclear and Navy regimes already assert, deny or test the presupposition, was sent to the three documents behind three single-reader kills — NRC ML13303B093, NRC ML003677584 and DTIC AD0669904 — and deliberately read neither this entry, nor the record, nor any adversary log, so that every quotation in it comes from a document it opened itself. **The verdict did not move, and no grade moved.** The status stays PROVISIONAL, well-posedness stays 2/3 and Significance stays 2/3; novelty confidence stays MEDIUM. What changed is what the Provisional stands on. The entry's CENTRAL NEGATIVE WAS CONFIRMED ON DEDICATED SWEEPS: Castrup 2005 "prints no out-of-tolerance rate against elapsed time anywhere" is true over the document at full text by a second reader on a dedicated single-target sweep, with its one table and all three figures enumerated and every occurrence of "%" in the paper accounted for as a declared confidence level (90%, 80%, 95%) and "out-of-tolerance" occurring four times with no number attached to any of them — as well-established as a single-document universal gets, with the one caveat now carried in the entry that §2.1 does assert the dependence in words and names "an end of period (EOP) percent in-tolerance criterion", so the negative is about printed numbers only. And two of the named unopened returns that capped attack 2 were opened and both SUPPORT the Disguise grade rather than threatening it: NIST TN 2146 applies the RP-1 method to real electronic calibration records and names no selection-bias concept and no reason-keyed rule, and EPRI MTA-MA-019 "contains no statement of which historical calibration data are included or excluded ... no rule keyed to the reason for a calibration ... and no rule keyed to outlier status or interval length." What fell is decoration and counting, and all of it has been carried into the entry's own prose above rather than left standing with a note below.

**What was struck.** FOUR strikes. (1) NOVELTY GROUND (d)'s MIDDLE CLAUSE, which also reverses in direction: "ILAC-G24:2022 cl. 6.6 now shows RP-1 is the NORMATIVE REFERENCE for exactly this method, sharpening it from likely pre-emptor to cited authority" is false on the document as served, three ways — there is no normative references clause at all ("The document has no separate normative references clause. Domain(s): Other STEM — computational thermodynamics / CALPHAD assessment. Target field deciding novelty: materials thermodynamics (Calphad, J. Phase Equilib. Diffus.). Method-owning fields engaged: statistical model comparison / evaluation-protocol sensitivity; nuclear-data adjustment-vs-validation; crystallography's free-R discipline.
Question (canonical): For a declared frame of systems each carrying two or more independently published CALPHAD assessments whose full parameter sets are retrievable, and on one commonly digitised experimental corpus with every datum attributed to its source study: (a) what is the Kendall tau between the ordering of the competing assessments by their apparent residual, recomputed on the pooled corpus under one pre-declared common metric, and their ordering by leave-one-study-out predictive residual under that same metric; (b) what is the distribution of the predictive-minus-apparent gap, in the metric's units and as a ratio; and (c) in how many systems, and which, does the top-ranked assessment change?
Reformulation note: this is R1, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, adopted in the record. V0 asked whether the ordering "by their own reported fit" survives held-out evaluation; the one assessment paper opened (arXiv:2601.11899, read in full) prints no fit statistic at all, so the V0 ordering does not exist and V0 was ill-posed. R1 replaced reported fit with a recomputed apparent residual. The repair is what the rejection turns on: it never declared whether the held-out evaluation re-fits, and post-batch verification established, on two aimed sweeps of both answer-protocols, that the record is silent in BOTH directions — no re-fitting step (re-fit / re-optimise / re-estimate / adjust / tune / calibrate / train: zero occurrences in either version) and no statement anywhere that the parameter set is fixed or frozen, with no fold aggregation declared either. From two-way silence no identity follows; what follows is an undeclared operation, and the rejection now rests on what that undeclared operation leaves limb (b) with rather than on a forced identity.
Alternative formulations: (1) Do competing thermodynamic descriptions of the same alloy system change places when scored on experimental studies they were not fitted to? (2) What is the out-of-sample penalty of a published CALPHAD assessment — the free-R analogue of a thermodynamic description — and does it reorder assessments relative to their apparent agreement?

**The old ground, taken apart in three places.** The entry wrote against itself, "If the algebraic leg fell, nothing here would reject the entry and it would stand Provisional", and the leg fell on its own terms. FIRST, the universal is false as written. The identity is EXACT under pooled, datum-equal aggregation and FALSE under mean-over-folds, where the gap equals exactly `-(1/n) * sum_k (n_k - n/K)(r_k - rbar)` — minus the equal-weight-over-studies covariance between study SIZE and study RESIDUAL — which is zero only if all studies are the same size or size is uncorrelated with residual, and which takes either sign. THIS IS THE CHECKER'S OWN ARITHMETIC, verified numerically by it, and it is not a document finding: on its worked counter-example of two attributed studies of 100 and 10 data (n = 110, K = 2), assessment A with per-study residuals 1.0 and 10.0 scores apparent 1.8182 and fold-mean 5.5000, assessment B with 2.0 and 2.0 scores 2.0000 both ways, so the apparent ordering A-ahead-of-B inverts to B-ahead-of-A, Kendall tau is -1 rather than +1, limb (c)'s change count is 1 rather than 0, and the gaps are {+3.6818, 0.0000} in metric units and {3.025, 1.000} as ratios; a third row with residuals 10.0 and 1.0 reverses the sign, gap -3.6818, ratio 0.599. The fold-mean is the form in which the standard reference literature DEFINES every cross-validation estimator, read at full text by that checker: Arlot, S. & Celisse, A., "A survey of cross-validation procedures for model selection", DOI 10.1214/09-SS054, arXiv:0907.4728v1 (27 Jul 2009), §4.2.2 equation (9), "LbCV(A; Dn; (I(t)j) for j = 1..B) := (1/B) × sum over j = 1..B of LbH-O(A; Dn; I(t)j)", prefaced "In brief, CV consists in averaging several hold-out estimators of the risk corresponding to different splits of the data" and universally quantified by the authors' own next sentence, "All existing CV estimators of the risk are of the form (9)", with each hold-out term internally normalised by its own validation size at §4.2.1 equation (8), "(1/nv) × ...". The equation numbers are the arXiv v1's, not necessarily the published version's. Why the entry's intuition misfired is printed in the same source: under leave-one-OBSERVATION-out the two aggregations coincide, because §4.3.1 equation (10)'s `LbLOO(A; Dn) = (1/n) × sum over j = 1..n of γ(A(D(-j)n); ξj)` is simultaneously a fold-mean and a datum-mean, whereas leave-one-STUDY-out has validation sets of size n_k > 1 and in general unequal. A dedicated second sweep of that document returned, in terms, that "Leave-one-group-out" does not appear, that "group" does not appear as a term for CV, and that "The document never states that validation sets must have the same size, or that unbalanced splits cause a problem or bias" — a two-sweep absence of a WARNING, not of the formula, while §4.3.2's V-fold is set up on "subsamples of approximately equal ardinality n/V" and §5.1.2's result is stated under the explicit condition "When the Aj s have exatly the same size n/V" (both transcribed as served, OCR garbling included and not silently repaired). SECOND, a hedge had been cut. Adversary #1's sentence reads "summed over folds, predictive residual equals apparent residual (up to fold weighting), the gap is identically zero and tau is identically 1 by construction, for every system, regardless of the data" — and "(up to fold weighting)" names exactly the loophole the arithmetic exploits; the entry adopted adversary #3's bare version and dropped the parenthetical with the grammar clean on both sides of the cut. Significance — consequence: if the exceedance fraction is materially above zero, the G.827x and substation/synchrophasor limits are specified against a budget the disturbance environment routinely overruns, and resilience (holdover class, assisted PRTC, terrestrial backup) is being sized from test conditions; if it is bounded near zero with stated power, the current limits are licensed and the protective mechanism is shown to work.
Significance — audience: ITU-T SG15 Q13, which owns the limits limb 2 scores against; IEEE PSRC and IEC TC57; the NASPI Time Synchronization Task Force, which commissioned exactly this shape of study for another epoch class; telecom sync operators and utility protection engineers, who would act through holdover-class procurement and alarm thresholds. The earlier count of "three independent groups" is CORRECTED to two for the 26 Jan 2016 epoch: NIST contributes two documents (Lombardi's CGSIC deck and Yao et al., Lombardi second author, the same monitored population) and Chronos two (P1 and Curry, the same group citing itself), while Cao and Veitch is on a DIFFERENT epoch, the December 2016 leap second, and has never been read past its abstract.
Significance — fecundity: whether multi-constellation capability reduces delivered error under real disturbance or only changes the failure mode; whether the MTIE alarm thresholds that fired in P1 detect the errors that matter; whether standard limits should carry an exposure-conditioned term; and the inverse, whether a fleet of delivered-error logs is itself an interference detector.
Significance — anchoring: the GNSS-timing resilience debate, which currently prices vulnerability from test conditions; the unquantified half of the 26 Jan 2016 post-mortem; NASPI's leap-second work, which left the fraction limb unprinted; legal metrology's in-service conformance surveillance, which has the method and not the instrument class.
Reason for silence: a sourced disclosure convention plus a disciplinary boundary. The acting community's own flagship fleet report publishes "without identifying either device vendors or models nor the affected companies" (P2 Section 1) and the NIST deck likewise names no makes or models, so the two join keys are removed at publication; the only model-resolved record is a vendor's own support estate. The method — surveying a deployed instrument population for exceedance of a maximum permissible error — is named and mature in legal metrology, whose scope excludes infrastructure clocks. Adversary #2 sharpens rather than settles this: on the corrected count TWO groups published FOUR different partial versions within three years (NIST twice with Lombardi on both; Chronos twice, the same group citing itself), so asking was cheap and what nobody took was the step of naming the limit; A2 labels that inference as its own reasoning rather than a source finding, with the grounding search unrun, and that honest label is the only reason the three-group step could be corrected here. The newly opened NIST paper reinforces the disclosure mechanism rather than weakening it: Yao et al. also prints that its receivers are "not identified by make or model".

Promotion requires: (i) an IN-FRAME operator or utility in-service monitoring report carrying a per-unit delivered-TE series at ≥ 1 sample/15 min over ≥ 30 days against a NAMED independent reference, for units under one of the enumerated limits — named unopened instance of that kind: Larvick (BPA/PNNL), "Complementary Precise Timing Distribution in a Transmission Utility Environment", NASPI, 15 Apr 2026, https://www.naspi.org/sites/default/files/2026-04/8-2_Larvick-PNNL_1.pdf, which this ledger's own intake already carries with ePRTC GPS/caesium, "Mean TE was ~ 452.7 ns", "Alarm logs showed 85 holdover events" and a cited ±1 µs synchrophasor target, and which fails ONLY the epoch limb ("NO GNSS-disturbance test"), and which NOBODY IN THIS LEDGER HAS OPENED; and (ii) the synchrophasor standard's OWN NORMATIVE CLAUSE — IEC-IEEE 60255-118-1 (or IEEE C37.118.1) opened and recorded as to whether it prints a numeric time limit with its measurand and point of application, or only the 1 % TVE criterion — STILL UNOPENED BY ANYBODY, its paywall never tested, so no paywall error is on record and its silence is evidence in neither direction.

Domain(s): Other STEM — civil and structural engineering. Decision surface: structural-reliability code calibration (EN 1990 / ASCE 7 / AASHTO LRFD reference periods) and LCA/EPD reference service life. Vocabularies searched across three agents: US highway-bridge English, US utility-depreciation English, Eurocode-reliability English, wind-energy asset registers, German/Danish register English, Japanese 架替え bridge administration, Highway-Research-Board-era English, Spanish vida útil, Dutch performance-age asset management, actuarial competing risks, AASHTO code-drafting history.

Question (canonical): For a cohort named before any data pull from an enumerable infrastructure asset register carrying per-unit commissioning and removal dates (or removal dates reconstructible to a stated resolution) and a recorded or reconstructible removal reason: (i) what is the realized service-life distribution — median, quartiles and P(reaching the declared design working life) — estimated with left truncation and right censoring handled and the denominator stated; (ii) under a cause partition fixed by a stated generating rule rather than a list, what share of removals falls in the class the design working life encodes versus each non-structural class, with an agreement statistic from an adjudicated sub-sample and the unclassifiable share reported; and (iii) what is the lifetime failure probability implied by the code's target reliability when integrated over the realized service-life distribution rather than over the nominal reference period, reported as a change in the implied reliability index, together with the same figure under the reading that the reference period is only a normalising convention of the load statistics (which should return no change)?
Reformulation note: this is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation the pipeline permits. V1 (intake wording) named no cohort and gave the cause set as a non-exhaustive, non-disjoint LIST; V2 names a cohort and states a generating RULE (structural class = exactly those recorded reasons whose satisfaction would have been prevented by greater design resistance; residue to an explicit unclassifiable class). The record chose the rule option over the enumeration option and says so.

Alternative formulations:
- Do bridges actually leave service because they wore out, or for reasons the design working life has nothing to do with — and in what proportion?
- What is the realized in-service duration of a declared asset population against its code-declared design working life, decomposed by removal cause, and what does the mismatch do to the lifetime failure probability implied by the code's target reliability?

Motivating gap: silence mapping — a literature dense with how-answers about service life (designing to a 50- or 100-year design working life, remaining-useful-life estimation, life-extension justification) and, per the intake, empty of the why-question about departure from service. THE GAP STATEMENT IS FALSE AS WRITTEN and did not survive its first on-point query in the candidate's own field and words (record Q1), nor the adversaries' native-language sweeps. The intake ran one search, returned nine items and opened none.

So the code text is still unread by everyone, and this clause is scored in neither direction. Adversary 1's recollection that AASHTO defines design life as the basis of the statistical derivation of transient loads is unsourced in its own log, and the one code-practice document it did open (Caltrans BDP ch.1, June 2024) uses "design life" six times in running text and never defines it. 6. MEASURAND EXEMPTION, declared and applied by both adversaries: a finding that realized life matches the declared life, or that removals ARE dominated by the design limit state, answers the question rather than falsifying a premise. Adversary 2 notes in passing that Xie's Dutch mean (80.2 years against an expected 60–80) runs OPPOSITE to the motivating direction, and correctly declines to score that against the question — though the post-batch pass establishes that in Xie 2017 the 80.2 years is ANNOUNCED and not measured: no denominator, no sample size and no stated link to the 219 projects appears anywhere in the portion served.

What would count as an answer: three deliverables for the named cohort. (i) A competing-risks survival estimate — median, quartiles, P(reaching the declared design working life) — with left truncation and right censoring handled and the denominator stated. (ii) A cause-attribution table under V2's generating rule, with an agreement statistic from an adjudicated sub-sample and the unclassifiable share. (iii) Lifetime failure probability implied by the code's target reliability integrated over the realized distribution rather than the nominal reference period, as a change in implied reliability index, plus the same figure under the normalising-convention reading (pre-declared: no change). NOT an answer: a survivor curve alone; an average service life by plant account; a reliability recalibration over an assumed service-life distribution. The record's own TRIVIALITY GUARD, retained here but NARROWED by the post-batch pass and no longer load-bearing in the form the record wrote it: over the one depreciation-study instance anybody has now opened, limb (i) is routine only in an ACCOUNTING sense on vintage DOLLAR balances. Iowa curves and average service lives are printed account by account (Account 331.00 T&D mains, 75-R4, 75 years, summary pp. III-4/5), but on plant-account vintage dollar balances by the retirement rate method, with an accounting retirement of a book balance as the event, dollars of exposure as the denominator, no unit count, no cause of retirement, and left truncation and right censoring never named — handled instead under the names "experience band", "placement band", "exposures" and "stub survivor curve", the last of which IS right censoring under another name. Routine in that sense does NOT strip a per-unit survival limb out of a novelty question, and P2's own Introduction says so from inside this entry's own citation set: "problem arises from using depreciation service life to represent replacement cycle". The annual-to-reference-period conversion remains textbook. So the candidate still turns mainly on (ii) and (iii), but the guard no longer carries limb (i) out of the question by itself, and a kill on limb (ii) alone can carry a Rejection only in this narrowed form.

Significance — consequence: If realized life is materially shorter than the declared design working life AND removals are dominated by non-structural causes, then (a) a lifetime failure probability computed over a 50- or 100-year reference period is computed over an exposure that does not occur, bearing on whether current partial factors carry an unintended conservatism, and (b) a reference service life longer than the realized one understates everything normalised by it in LCA/EPD, propagating into procurement thresholds. If realized life matches and the design limit state dominates, the codes' implicit reading is vindicated — a publishable closure under the declared measurand exemption. Force of this limb depends ENTIRELY on presupposition 5, unchecked by all three agents.

Significance — audience: CEN/TC250/SC10 (EN 1990) and the JCSS Probabilistic Model Code committee; ASCE 7 load committees; EN 15978/15804 PCR writers; state DOT and national asset-management offices. The owner-side audience is demonstrably real and already acting, on three independent instruments: a national questionnaire programme run five times since 1967 (P1), a national asset owner commissioning the object directly (P3, supervised from Rijkswaterstaat — which is also why P3 is not an independent population: one group reporting its own register), and a US national survey with agency reason records from five states (Bektaş/NCHRP — ANNOUNCED in (b)'s abstract, which names the states as Utah, Michigan, California, Pennsylvania and Florida and was served as PARAPHRASE, while the report body is COULD NOT READ, so the survey's existence is announced and its measure is not printed at any read level reached). Significance — fecundity: makes askable (a) what design working life would equalise nominal and realized exposure for a class; (b) whether design-life-extension investment pays when the modal exit is functional; (c) differential obsolescence across asset classes sharing one code; (d) whether the convention reading is testable empirically at all.

Significance — anchoring: the early-replacement anomaly named in the Bektaş group's own later chapter title; the long-standing LCA sensitivity to assumed lifespan; and the treatment of existing structures in structural reliability, where remaining working life is assumed rather than estimated from realized exits.

Reason for silence: the record's mechanism — a disciplinary boundary running along the instruments (depreciation engineering owns realized exit distributions and has no reason to attribute them to limit states; code calibration owns the reference period and takes it as given), plus an incentive gap in that no committee is rewarded for proposing relaxed factors — is CONTRADICTED for limbs (i) and (ii) and survives only for limb (iii). Infrastructure engineers crossed the boundary in Japan in 1967 and every decade since, in the Netherlands via a national owner (one group reporting its own register, through a thesis read only to Chapter 2 and a source document nobody can address), and in the US — where the crossing is one group across three identifiers read at abstract level, i.e. one unread project, plus P2's Weibull on the NBI 1930 cohort, which attributes no cause at all. Per the gate's own rule, a failed silence mechanism makes the novelty finding suspect in the direction of LESS novelty, which is the direction this verdict already runs.

Its opening words scope it as a definitional clarification and the clause ASSERTS the distinction; but its regime is design-stage cost optimisation on generic designed members with the working life fixed at n = 50 y and the reference period at 1 or 50 y, no asset register and no measured exits, so it DEFINES and optimises a target index (β_opt(n=50) ≈ 3.3–3.7 at Cstr/C1 = 50, ρ = 2–9, read off Fig. 2, §4.2) and measures no realized service-life distribution — and that reader says expressly that this does NOT kill, because V2 reports limb (iii) under both readings with the convention arm's answer pre-stated, so by the measurand exemption the clause is a reported quantity and attack 4 does not reach it. **Where a checker erred, and what this entry carries instead.** A checker's report is evidence, not an instruction, and two of them disagreed about the same fact. VERIFY-15-xie-2017-and-rws-2016b.md writes in its bearing that P1's "表-2.2 cells no agent has seen verbatim and whose printed percentage column disagrees with its printed counts (50.0% vs 688/1,342 = 51.3%, unresolved)". That checker ERRED by inheriting a caveat two other checkers had already dissolved: VERIFY-15-crosswalk-premises.md got the cells to serve on a transcription-style request, so "cells never seen verbatim" was a property of the earlier request and not of the table, and VERIFY-15-p1-table-verbatim.md located the 50.0 as a within-material-column percentage in a cross-tab, in a column the claim never uses. This entry therefore carries the CORRECTION — the cells serve, what remains unseen is only the 上部構造/下部構造 sub-row counts, and the percentage caveat is resolved and struck — and not that checker's version. The record itself erred twice more: it nominated ks044402.pdf and ks044403.pdf as "the untried route here" without checking their KIND, when a cover page and a preface could never have settled the question (the TOC is ks044404.pdf, a fifth file ks044401.pdf exists, and the body chapters are in files the record never names); and it recorded "I CANNOT NAME A PRINTED REALIZED-LIFE CURVE OR AVERAGE-SERVICE-LIFE FIGURE FROM ANY OF THEM" after zero fetches, which one fetch falsified six times over. Both corrections are in the prose above. Two checkers disclosed going one fetch over their allowances, and those disclosures are carried rather than laundered, including the consequence the over-spending checker named itself: that its ground A rests on one instance rather than two or three.

**A late and separate Gate 4 WAS owed, and it ran.** This entry is REJECTED and its fatal ground did NOT survive at the grade it was given, so a late and separate Gate 4 was owed. Its form, disclosed: two cold readers, logs at UQ-20261023-15-adversary-3.md and UQ-20261023-15-adversary-4.md in this batch's folder, each handed the Gate 0–3 record only and the numbered facts the verification pass had established at first hand, each running all eight attacks on its own budget (9 and 10 Disguise queries respectively), and neither told what the earlier Gate 4 concluded. Cold reader 3 returned Provisional with nothing Unresolved; cold reader 4 returned Unresolved on attacks 2, 4 and 5 and a verdict of Rejected. By the rule stated over readers this is a Rejection on a SPLIT, and it is recorded as such rather than as a concurrence.

**The asymmetry that makes this entry unusual.** The TABLE verified EXACTLY and the GRADE built on it did not. On the table: the seven printed counts sum to 1,342, three of the seven top-level cells close against their printed sub-rows, and NOT ONE of the four failure modes this entry had pre-declared for that table was met — the table does exist at a table number and prints replacement counts by reason; the denominator IS 1,342 bridges; the counts ARE those seven integers, which is now the best-corroborated part of the whole entry; and the fourth mode, a percentage column implying a different denominator, is MET IN LETTER and VOID IN FORCE, because the percentages are within-material-type column percentages, at least one served 合計-column value is a visible duplication artifact, and this entry's share rests on the count column and its own division and never on a printed percentage. On the grade: the step from NILIM's administrative reason classes to the candidate's resistance counterfactual was performed once, by one reader, under a reading of the damage class that the printed sub-rows contradict — seven of its nine sub-rows are durability and material-deterioration mechanisms and one is defined by the explicit exclusion of load capacity (「凍害、中性化、塩害等の耐荷力不足以外の要因で床版が損傷する全てのケースに該当する」) — so the honest printed-cell spread is 4.5% to 25.0%, a factor of 5.5, rather than the two points inside it that the kill used. Both corroborating legs fell with the grade: the clause claiming corroboration in a second independent population at full text is a citation to an UNREAD source, the Dutch figures being a secondary report of a document nobody has identified let alone opened; and the "15% to 30%" unidentifiable share is in NONE of the three documents opened, sits in a different paper from the one this entry cited it to, and is scoped by its own opening words to the PRIOR literature rather than to this group's own result.

**The new ground, and the two caveats its reader stated in its own words.** The new ground is attack 4 and not attack 2. Gate 1's one permitted repair defines the structural class as "exactly those recorded reasons whose satisfaction would have been prevented by greater design resistance, everything else is non-structural", while the code the question measures against encodes deterioration inside its design working life, so the repair's own rule sends the code's durability-driven removals to the NON-structural class — which on the only register whose per-reason cells are printed is 201 of 1,342 removals. Cold reader 4's supporting read of Ichikawa, Takeda & Tamakoshi 2008 (土木技術資料 50-5:10-13, Figure 5) is at full text and shows that block durability-dominated, with 鋼材の腐食 at 49.2% of steel n=59 and 塩害によるコンクリート桁の破損 at 51.5% of PC n=33 — shares of material-type sub-counts and NOT of 1,342. The cold reader's own two caveats are carried in its words: EN 1990 itself was not opened, the fragments being a secondary reproduction from a training manual; and one step of the argument is its own reading rather than a source finding.

**Did the verdict move, and why.** It did NOT move: the entry is Rejected, as it was. What moved is the ground. The original ground is DOWNGRADED rather than confirmed — attack 2 narrows from Unresolved to Partial — and the verdict now rests on a wholly new ground that a cold reader found, on a split with the other cold reader returning Provisional. Nothing here promotes anything to Validated, and well-posedness at 2/3 blocks that independently of any Gate 4 outcome.
